# .github/workflows/collabskus-release.yml
#
# Builds self-contained Ladybird binaries on every push to master.
# Linux  → AppImage  (x86_64)
# macOS  → zipped .app bundle (arm64)
# Publishes a GitHub Release tagged build-YYYYMMDD-<short sha>.
#
# Fixes applied vs previous version:
#   - Removed ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test (caused 504 timeout; not needed on ubuntu-24.04)
#   - ubuntu-24.04 already ships gcc-14; clang-21 comes from LLVM apt directly
#   - vcpkg bootstrap script is Meta/Utils/build_vcpkg.py (not Meta/BuildVcpkg.py)
#   - macOS: explicit brew link for llvm@21 so clang-21 is actually on PATH
#   - Updated all actions to Node 24-compatible versions (v5+)
#   - Linux: added -Wl,--start-group/--end-group linker flags to fix circular
#     dependency between liblagom-unicode and liblibunicode_rust.a
#   - macOS: replaced dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with a direct rustup call to
#     avoid "detected conflict: bin/cargo-clippy" on macos-15 runners that ship
#     with Rust + clippy pre-installed; rustup update stable installs nothing new
#     when the component already exists, sidestepping the conflict entirely.

name: collabskus Build & Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  LLVM_VERSION: 21

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
jobs:

  # ── Linux x86_64 → AppImage ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build-linux:
    name: Build Linux (x86_64)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip3 install pyyaml requests six

      - name: Install apt dependencies
        run: |
          # ── LLVM apt repo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
          curl -fsSL https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key \
            | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/llvm-snapshot.gpg
          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm-snapshot.gpg] \
            http://apt.llvm.org/noble/ llvm-toolchain-noble-${LLVM_VERSION} main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list

          # ── Kitware (CMake 3.30+) ──────────────────────────────────────────
          wget -qO - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc \
            | gpg --dearmor \
            | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] \
            https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ noble main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list

          sudo apt-get update -y

          # ubuntu-24.04 ships gcc-14 and g++-14 natively — no PPA needed
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            autoconf \
            autoconf-archive \
            automake \
            bison \
            build-essential \
            ccache \
            cmake \
            curl \
            fonts-liberation2 \
            g++-14 \
            gcc-14 \
            git \
            clang-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            clang++-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            clang-tools-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            lld-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            libdrm-dev \
            libgl1-mesa-dev \
            libegl1-mesa-dev \
            libpulse-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            libstdc++-14-dev \
            libxkbcommon-dev \
            libtool \
            nasm \
            ninja-build \
            patchelf \
            pkg-config \
            tar \
            unzip \
            zip

          sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/clang   clang   /usr/bin/clang-${LLVM_VERSION}   100
          sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/clang++ clang++ /usr/bin/clang++-${LLVM_VERSION} 100
          sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/lld     lld     /usr/bin/lld-${LLVM_VERSION}     100

          cmake --version
          clang --version
          ninja --version

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Install Qt 6.9
        uses: jurplel/install-qt-action@v4
        with:
          version: '6.9.0'
          target: 'desktop'
          arch: 'gcc_64'

      - name: Configure (Distribution preset)
        run: |
          cmake --preset Distribution -B Build \
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$Qt6_DIR" \
            -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,--start-group" \
            -DCMAKE_STATIC_LINKER_FLAGS="" \
            -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,--start-group"

      - name: Install wasm-tools
        run: |
          VERSION=1.243.0
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasm-tools/releases/download/v${VERSION}/wasm-tools-${VERSION}-x86_64-linux.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local/bin \
              "wasm-tools-${VERSION}-x86_64-linux/wasm-tools"
          wasm-tools --version

      - name: Bootstrap vcpkg
        run: python3 Meta/Utils/build_vcpkg.py

      - name: Configure (Distribution preset)
        run: |
          # -Wl,--start-group/--end-group resolves the circular dependency between
          # liblagom-unicode (C++ side) and liblibunicode_rust.a (Rust side): the
          # Rust archive calls back into C symbols that are defined in a static lib
          # that appears earlier on the link line.  GNU ld resolves this with a
          # group; lld accepts the same flags.
          cmake --preset Distribution -B Build \
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-${LLVM_VERSION} \
            -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,--start-group" \
            -DCMAKE_STATIC_LINKER_FLAGS="" \
            -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,--start-group"

      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build
        run: cmake --build . --parallel $(nproc)

      - name: Install into staging prefix
        run: cmake --install Build --strip --prefix ${{ github.workspace }}/AppDir/usr

      - name: Download linuxdeploy + Qt plugin
        run: |
          wget -q https://github.com/linuxdeploy/linuxdeploy/releases/download/continuous/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage
          wget -q https://github.com/linuxdeploy/linuxdeploy-plugin-qt/releases/download/continuous/linuxdeploy-plugin-qt-x86_64.AppImage
          chmod +x linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage linuxdeploy-plugin-qt-x86_64.AppImage

      - name: Write desktop entry and icon
        run: |
          mkdir -p AppDir/usr/share/applications AppDir/usr/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps
          cat > AppDir/usr/share/applications/ladybird.desktop <<'DESKTOP'
          [Desktop Entry]
          Name=Ladybird
          Exec=Ladybird %u
          Icon=ladybird
          Type=Application
          Categories=Network;WebBrowser;
          MimeType=text/html;text/xml;application/xhtml+xml;x-scheme-handler/http;x-scheme-handler/https;
          DESKTOP
          ICON_SRC=$(find Build -name "*.png" 2>/dev/null | grep -i ladybird | head -1 || true)
          if [ -n "$ICON_SRC" ]; then
            cp "$ICON_SRC" AppDir/usr/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps/ladybird.png
          else
            python3 -c "
          import base64
          open('AppDir/usr/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps/ladybird.png','wb').write(
            base64.b64decode('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwADhQGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==')
          )"
          fi

      - name: Build AppImage
        env:
          QMAKE: /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmake6
        run: |
          COMMIT_SHORT="${GITHUB_SHA::8}"
          TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%d)"
          export VERSION="${TIMESTAMP}-${COMMIT_SHORT}"
          ./linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage --appdir AppDir --plugin qt --output appimage
          APPIMAGE=$(ls Ladybird*.AppImage 2>/dev/null | head -1 || ls *.AppImage | head -1)
          FINAL="Ladybird-${VERSION}-linux-x86_64.AppImage"
          mv "$APPIMAGE" "$FINAL"
          echo "APPIMAGE_PATH=${FINAL}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "RELEASE_TAG=build-${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Upload Linux artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: linux-appimage
          path: ${{ env.APPIMAGE_PATH }}
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Save release tag
        run: echo "${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}" > release-tag.txt

      - name: Upload release tag artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: release-tag
          path: release-tag.txt
          retention-days: 7

  # ── macOS arm64 → zipped .app bundle ──────────────────────────────────────
  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS (arm64)
    runs-on: macos-15

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip3 install pyyaml requests six

      - name: Install Homebrew dependencies
        run: |
          brew update
          brew install \
            autoconf \
            autoconf-archive \
            automake \
            bash \
            ccache \
            coreutils \
            libtool \
            llvm@${LLVM_VERSION} \
            nasm \
            ninja \
            pkg-config \
            qt \
            unzip

      - name: Link llvm@21 and add to PATH
        run: |
          # Unlink any conflicting llvm version first, then link ours
          brew unlink llvm 2>/dev/null || true
          brew link --force --overwrite llvm@${LLVM_VERSION}
          LLVM_BIN="$(brew --prefix llvm@${LLVM_VERSION})/bin"
          echo "${LLVM_BIN}" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          # Verify immediately
          "${LLVM_BIN}/clang" --version
          "${LLVM_BIN}/clang++" --version

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        # macos-15 runners ship with Rust + clippy pre-installed. Using
        # dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable causes "detected conflict: bin/cargo-clippy"
        # because the action unconditionally tries to add the clippy component.
        # Instead, we call rustup directly: `rustup update stable` refreshes the
        # toolchain without touching components that are already present, and
        # `rustup default stable` ensures cargo/rustc on PATH are the stable ones.
        run: |
          rustup update stable
          rustup default stable
          rustc --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Install wasm-tools
        run: |
          VERSION=1.243.0
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasm-tools/releases/download/v${VERSION}/wasm-tools-${VERSION}-aarch64-macos.tar.gz" \
            | tar -xz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local/bin \
              "wasm-tools-${VERSION}-aarch64-macos/wasm-tools"
          wasm-tools --version

      - name: Bootstrap vcpkg
        run: python3 Meta/Utils/build_vcpkg.py

      - name: Configure (Distribution preset)
        run: |
          LLVM_BIN="$(brew --prefix llvm@${LLVM_VERSION})/bin"
          cmake --preset Distribution -B Build \
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="${LLVM_BIN}/clang" \
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="${LLVM_BIN}/clang++"

      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build
        run: cmake --build . --parallel $(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu)

      - name: Install into staging prefix
        run: cmake --install Build --strip --prefix ${{ github.workspace }}/Install

      - name: Bundle and zip .app
        run: |
          COMMIT_SHORT="${GITHUB_SHA::8}"
          TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%d)"
          VERSION="${TIMESTAMP}-${COMMIT_SHORT}"

          APP_BUNDLE=$(find Install -name "*.app" -maxdepth 5 | head -1)
          if [ -z "$APP_BUNDLE" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: no .app found under Install/:"
            find Install | head -40
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Found bundle: $APP_BUNDLE"

          FRAMEWORKS="$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$FRAMEWORKS"

          VCPKG_LIB="Build/vcpkg_installed/arm64-osx/lib"
          [ -d "$VCPKG_LIB" ] && cp -n "$VCPKG_LIB"/*.dylib "$FRAMEWORKS/" 2>/dev/null || true

          LOCAL_LIB="Build/lib"
          [ -d "$LOCAL_LIB" ] && cp -Rn "$LOCAL_LIB"/. "$FRAMEWORKS/" 2>/dev/null || true

          for EXE in "$APP_BUNDLE/Contents/MacOS"/*; do
            [ -f "$EXE" ] || continue
            install_name_tool -add_rpath "@executable_path/../Frameworks" "$EXE" 2>/dev/null || true
          done

          ARCHIVE="Ladybird-${VERSION}-macos-arm64.zip"
          cd "$(dirname "$APP_BUNDLE")"
          zip -r --symlinks "${{ github.workspace }}/${ARCHIVE}" "$(basename "$APP_BUNDLE")"
          echo "MACOS_ARCHIVE=${{ github.workspace }}/${ARCHIVE}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Upload macOS artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: macos-app
          path: ${{ env.MACOS_ARCHIVE }}
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Publish Release ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release:
    name: Publish Release
    needs: [build-linux, build-macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    if: always() && (needs.build-linux.result == 'success' || needs.build-macos.result == 'success')

    steps:
      - name: Download Linux AppImage
        if: needs.build-linux.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: linux-appimage
          path: dist/

      - name: Download macOS app
        if: needs.build-macos.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: macos-app
          path: dist/

      - name: Download release tag
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: release-tag
          path: .

      - name: Read release tag
        run: echo "RELEASE_TAG=$(cat release-tag.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: List dist
        run: ls -lh dist/

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
          name: "Ladybird ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}"
          body: |
            ## Ladybird Browser — automated build

            **Commit:** [`${{ github.sha }}`](${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }})
            **Branch:** `${{ github.ref_name }}`
            **Built at:** ${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}

            ### Assets
            | File | Platform |
            |------|----------|
            | `*.AppImage` | Linux x86-64 — self-contained, no install needed |
            | `*.zip` | macOS arm64 — drag `.app` to `/Applications` |

            ### Linux usage
            ```bash
            chmod +x Ladybird-*.AppImage
            ./Ladybird-*.AppImage
            ```

            ### macOS usage
            Unzip, drag `Ladybird.app` to `/Applications`.
            First launch: right-click → Open to bypass Gatekeeper (unsigned build).

            > ⚠️ Unofficial pre-alpha builds from
            > [collabskus/ladybird](https://github.com/collabskus/ladybird),
            > tracking [LadybirdBrowser/ladybird](https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird).
          files: dist/*
          make_latest: true
          fail_on_unmatched_files: false

FILE: .github/workflows/dev-container.yml
# This workflow builds a docker image with the Dev Container CLI (https://github.com/devcontainers/cli)
#
name: 'Build Dev Container Image'
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/**'
      - 'vcpkg.json'
  schedule:
    # https://crontab.guru/#0_0_*_*_1
    - cron:  '0 0 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read
  # Push images to GHCR.
  packages: write

jobs:
  build:
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1

      - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v4.8.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build Base Dev Container Image
        uses: devcontainers/ci@v0.3.1900000450
        with:
          imageName: ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-devcontainer
          imageTag: base,latest
          push: always

FILE: .github/workflows/js-and-wasm-artifacts.yml
name: Package the js repl as a binary artifact

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      reference_to_build:
        description: 'Branch, tag or commit hash to build'
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}
  CCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ccache

jobs:
  build-and-package:
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.runner_labels) }}
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
    name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}, ${{ matrix.arch }}
    container: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.container) }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os_name: ['Linux']
        arch: ['x86_64']
        toolchain: ['Clang']
        package_type: ['Linux-x86_64']
        runner_labels: ['["blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404"]']
        container: [&ci_container '{"image":"ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-ci:2026.11.21"}']

        include:
          - os_name: 'macOS'
            arch: 'arm64'
            toolchain: 'Clang'
            package_type: 'macOS-arm64'
            runner_labels: '["blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26"]'
            container: 'null'

          - os_name: 'Linux'
            arch: 'arm64'
            toolchain: 'Clang'
            package_type: 'Linux-aarch64'
            runner_labels: '["blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404-arm"]'
            container: *ci_container

    steps:
      - name: Checkout LadybirdBrowser/ladybird
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.reference_to_build }}

      - name: 'Determine build commit hash'
        id: build-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: "Set up environment"
        id: 'setup'
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup
        with:
          os: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          build_preset: 'Distribution'

      - name: Restore Caches
        uses: $/.github/actions/cache-restore
        id: 'cache-restore'
        with:
          os: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          toolchain: ${{ matrix.toolchain }}
          cache_key_extra: 'LibJS and LibWasm Artifacts'
          ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
          sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
          vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}

      - name: Create build directory Ubuntu
        run: |
          cmake --preset Distribution \
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang \
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
            -DENABLE_GUI_TARGETS=OFF
        if: ${{ matrix.os_name == 'Linux' }}

      # FIXME: Add the following flag back when vcpkg supports Universal binaries:
      #        -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="x86_64;arm64"
      #
      #        See: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/discussions/19454
      - name: Create build directory macOS
        run: |
          cmake --preset Distribution \
            -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET="12.0" \
            -DENABLE_GUI_TARGETS=OFF
        if: ${{ matrix.os_name == 'macOS' }}

      - name: Build js
        working-directory: Build/distribution
        run: |
          ninja js

      - name: Build wasm
        working-directory: Build/distribution
        run: |
          ninja wasm

      - name: Package js and wasm
        working-directory: Build/distribution
        run: |
          cpack

          # Inject the COMMIT file for older builds (before commit 5c5de0e30e04).
          for package in ladybird-*.tar.gz; do
            if ! tar -tzf "${package}" | grep -qx COMMIT; then
              echo "${{ steps.build-commit.outputs.sha }}" > COMMIT
              gunzip "${package}"
              tar --append --file="${package%.gz}" COMMIT
              gzip "${package%.gz}"
              rm COMMIT
            fi
          done

      - name: Save Caches
        uses: $/.github/actions/cache-save
        with:
          arch: 'Lagom'
          ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
          ccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.ccache_primary_key }}
          sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
          sccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.sccache_primary_key }}
          vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}
          vcpkg_cache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.vcpkg_cache_primary_key }}

      - name: Sanity-check the js repl
        shell: bash
        run: |
          path="Build/distribution/ladybird-js-${{ matrix.package_type }}.tar.gz"
          if [ -f "${path}" ]; then
            tar -xvzf "${path}"
            bin/js -c "console.log('Hello, World\!');" > js-repl-out.txt
            if ! grep -q "\"Hello, World\!\"" js-repl-out.txt; then
              echo "Sanity check failed: \"Hello, World\!\" not found in output."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Sanity-check the wasm repl
        shell: bash
        run: |
          path="Build/distribution/ladybird-wasm-${{ matrix.package_type }}.tar.gz"
          if [ -f "${path}" ]; then
            tar -xvzf "${path}"
            bin/wasm -e run_sanity_check -w "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/CI/ci-sanity-check.wasm" > wasm-repl-out.txt
            if ! grep -q "Hello, World\!" wasm-repl-out.txt; then
              echo "Sanity check failed: Hello, World\! not found in output."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Upload js package
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ladybird-js-${{ matrix.package_type }}
          path: Build/distribution/ladybird-js-*.tar.gz
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload wasm package
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ladybird-wasm-${{ matrix.package_type }}
          path: Build/distribution/ladybird-wasm-*.tar.gz
          retention-days: 7

FILE: .github/workflows/js-and-wasm-benchmarks.yml
name: 'JS benchmarks'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Package the js repl as a binary artifact']
    branches: [master]
    types: [completed]

jobs:
  js-benchmarks:
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.runner_labels) }}
    if: ${{ github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}, ${{ matrix.arch }}
    container: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.container) }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os_name: ['Linux']
        arch: ['x86_64']
        package_type: ['Linux-x86_64']
        runner_labels: ['["ubuntu-24.04-internal", "js-benchmarks", "self-hosted"]']
        container: ['{"image":"ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-ci:2026.11.21"}']

        include:
          - os_name: 'macOS'
            arch: 'arm64'
            package_type: 'macOS-arm64'
            runner_labels: '["macos-26", "js-benchmarks", "self-hosted"]'
            container: 'null'

    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: 'Checkout LadybirdBrowser/js-benchmarks'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: LadybirdBrowser/js-benchmarks
          path: js-benchmarks
          ref: master

      - name: 'Determine js-benchmarks commit hash'
        id: js-benchmarks-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd js-benchmarks
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: 'Download JS repl artifact'
        uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v28
        with:
          run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: ladybird-js-${{ matrix.package_type }}
          path: js-repl

      - name: 'Extract JS repl'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd js-repl
          tar -xvzf ladybird-js-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz

      - name: 'Determine JS repl build commit hash'
        id: js-build-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          commit_hash=$(cat js-repl/COMMIT)
          echo "sha=${commit_hash}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: 'Download wasm repl artifact'
        uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v28
        with:
          run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: ladybird-wasm-${{ matrix.package_type }}
          path: wasm-repl
          if_no_artifact_found: warn

      - name: 'Extract wasm repl'
        if: ${{ hashFiles('wasm-repl/*.tar.gz') != '' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd wasm-repl
          tar -xvzf ladybird-wasm-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz

      - name: 'Run the benchmarks'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd js-benchmarks
          python3 -m venv .venv
          source .venv/bin/activate
          python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

          run_options='--iterations=3'

          js_path="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/js-repl/bin/js"
          run_options="${run_options} --executable=${js_path}"

          wasm_path="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/wasm-repl/bin/wasm"
          if [ -x "${wasm_path}" ]; then
              run_options="${run_options} --wasm-executable=${wasm_path}"
          else
              echo "Wasm repl not found; skipping wasm benchmarks."
          fi

          if [ "${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
              # Upstream was run manually; we might run into failing benchmarks as a result of older builds.
              run_options="${run_options} --continue-on-failure"
          fi

          ./run.py ${run_options}

      - name: 'Save results as an artifact'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: js-benchmarks-results-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: js-benchmarks/results.json
          retention-days: 90

      - name: 'Call webhook'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo '{
              "commit": "${{ steps.js-build-commit.outputs.sha }}",
              "benchmarks_commit": "${{ steps.js-benchmarks-commit.outputs.sha }}",
              "os": "${{ matrix.os_name }}",
              "arch": "${{ matrix.arch }}",
              "artifact": "js-benchmarks-results-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}",
              "artifact_run_id": "${{ github.run_id }}"
          }' > request.json
          curl \
              --fail \
              --silent \
              --show-error \
              --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              --header "X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=$(openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac '${{ secrets.JS_BENCHMARKS_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}' request.json | cut -d' ' -f2)" \
              --data-binary '@request.json' \
              '${{ secrets.JS_BENCHMARKS_WEBHOOK_URL }}'

FILE: .github/workflows/lint-commits.yml
name: Lint Commit Messages

on: [pull_request_target]

# Make sure to update Meta/lint-commit.sh to match this script when adding new checks!
# (… but don't accept overlong 'fixup!' commit descriptions.)

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'

    steps:
      - name: Lint PR commits
        uses: actions/github-script@v9.0.0
        with:
          script: |
            const excludedBotIds = [
              49699333,  // dependabot[bot]
            ];
            const rules = [
              {
                pattern: /^[^\r]*$/,
                error: "Commit message contains CRLF line breaks (only unix-style LF linebreaks are allowed)",
              },
              {
                line: 2,
                pattern: /^$/,
                error: "Empty line between commit title and body is missing",
              },
              {
                line: 1,
                pattern: /^(?!Merge branch )/,
                error: "Commit is a git merge commit, use the rebase command instead",
              },
              {
                line: 1,
                pattern: /^(Revert "|\S+: )/,
                error: "Missing category in commit title (if this is a fix up of a previous commit, it should be squashed)",
              },
              {
                line: 1,
                pattern: /^\S.*?: [A-Z0-9]/,
                error: "First word of commit after the subsystem is not capitalized",
              },
              {
                line: 1,
                pattern: /[^.]$/,
                error: "Commit title ends in a period",
              },
              {
                pattern: /^(.{0,72}|\s*[a-z]+:\/\/([a-z0-9\-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}(:\d+)?(\/[a-zA-Z_0-9@#:;%+.~?&=\-]+)*)$/,
                error: "Commit message lines are too long (maximum allowed is 72 characters, except for URLs on their own line)",
              },
              {
                pattern: /^(?!Signed-off-by: )/,
                error: "Commit body contains a Signed-off-by tag",
              },
            ];

            const { repository, pull_request } = context.payload;

            // NOTE: This maxes out at 250 commits. If this becomes a problem, see:
            // https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v18#pulls-list-commits
            const opts = github.rest.pulls.listCommits.endpoint.merge({
              owner: repository.owner.login,
              repo: repository.name,
              pull_number: pull_request.number,
            });
            const commits = await github.paginate(opts);

            const errors = [];
            for (const { sha, commit: { message }, author } of commits) {
              if (author !== null && excludedBotIds.includes(author.id)) {
                continue;
              }
              let commitErrors = [];
              message.split("\n").forEach((line, index) => {
                for (const { line: ruleLine, pattern, error } of rules) {
                  if (ruleLine !== undefined && ruleLine !== index + 1) {
                    continue;
                  }
                  if (!pattern.test(line)) {
                    commitErrors.push(error);
                  }
                }
              });
              if (commitErrors.length > 0) {
                const title = message.split("\n")[0];
                commitErrors = [...new Set(commitErrors)];  // remove duplicates
                errors.push([`${title} (${sha}):`, ...commitErrors].join("\n  "));
              }
            }

            if (errors.length > 0) {
              core.setFailed(`One or more of the commits in this PR do not match the code submission policy:\n\n${errors.join("\n")}`);
            }

FILE: .github/workflows/macos-accessibility-tests.yml
name: macOS accessibility tests

# The macOS AX tests need an unlocked GUI (Aqua) login session, and an Accessibility grant for the process tree the
# runner starts. Blacksmith's macOS machines have both, but a few of them still boot screen-locked — so the AX preflight
# below fails at once on a locked session. The tests don't build Ladybird themselves. Instead, they re-use the Ladybird
# the Sanitizer build already built: packed with Meta/package-macos-test-bundle.py, and uploaded to a machine of its own
# that just runs the tests. That takes a few minutes, so a rerun after a locked boot doesn't wait for a rebuild.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner_labels:
        description: 'JSON array of the labels selecting the runner, e.g. ["blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26"]'
        required: true
        type: string
      artifact_name:
        description: 'The artifact holding ladybird-app-bundle.tar.gz, as the build job uploaded it'
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  CI:
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.runner_labels) }}
    # The harness and the pip install run pull-request code, so the job's token is read-only and the checkout doesn't
    # leave it behind in .git/config for them to read.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # The bundle is the Sanitizer build's, so a report from Ladybird or one of its helpers goes to the diagnostics
    # directory, which the last step uploads. The test step creates the directory before anything can write there.
    env:
      ASAN_OPTIONS: log_path=${{ github.workspace }}/ax-diagnostics/asan.log
      UBSAN_OPTIONS: log_path=${{ github.workspace }}/ax-diagnostics/ubsan.log

    steps:
      # The harness, its fixtures and the diagnostic probe come from the checkout; the app comes from the build job.
      # The build jobs check out the moving refs/pull/N/merge ref, for a fresher master under the code they build. This
      # job only needs the harness, so it takes the default checkout: the merge commit the run was created for, which
      # stays put while the build job runs — and still exists once a PR has picked up a conflict, when GH drops the
      # merge ref, and a checkout of it fails.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Every step below that touches the macOS Accessibility API — the session probe, the TCC grant, the preflight, the
      # harness and the diagnostic probe — does it through PyObjC from the python3 on PATH. And no python3 on a hosted
      # runner image ships PyObjC — Apple's /usr/bin/python3 included. actions/setup-python puts its interpreter first
      # on PATH, so this is the one they all find. Quartz is for the session-state probe.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: 3.12

      - name: Install PyObjC
        run: pip3 install pyobjc-framework-ApplicationServices pyobjc-framework-Cocoa pyobjc-framework-Quartz

      - name: Download the packaged app bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.artifact_name }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ladybird-app-bundle

      # run_tests.sh and diagnose.py both take the app from LADYBIRD_BINARY.
      - name: Unpack the app bundle
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/ladybird-app-bundle
        run: |
          tar -xzf ladybird-app-bundle.tar.gz
          echo "LADYBIRD_BINARY=${PWD}/Ladybird.app/Contents/MacOS/Ladybird" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Try to wake a display and clear the lock UI. And print the session state before and after — so a remedy that
      # doesn't work is visible, rather than inferred. (A few of Blacksmith's macOS runners still boot with the session
      # screen-locked and no active displays, which is what breaks the accessibility tests: macOS withholds a window's
      # accessibility representation while the session is locked — so AXFocusedWindow answers with the application
      # element itself and no AXWebArea is reachable under it. The window is real — the window server reports one
      # on-screen — and the engine renders the page fine headlessly. So, the lock is the only thing in the way.)
      - name: Wake the macOS session for the accessibility tests
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          py=""
          for candidate in python3 /usr/bin/python3 /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3; do
            if command -v "${candidate}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "${candidate}" -c "import Quartz" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              py="${candidate}"
              break
            fi
          done
          session_state() {
            if [ -z "${py}" ]; then
              echo "  (no python3 with Quartz on this runner; cannot read session state)"
              return 0
            fi
            "${py}" - <<'SESSEOF'
          import re

          from Quartz import CGGetActiveDisplayList
          from Quartz import CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary

          err, _displays, count = CGGetActiveDisplayList(16, None, None)
          print("  active displays : err=%s count=%s" % (err, count))
          session = CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary() or {}
          print("  screen locked   : %s" % ("YES" if session.get("CGSSessionScreenIsLocked") else "no"))
          print("  session dict    : %s" % re.sub(r"\s+", " ", repr(dict(session)))[:300])
          SESSEOF
          }

          echo "=== session state BEFORE ==="
          session_state

          # Stop the screen saver arming again mid-job, and keep the display and machine awake for the run.
          defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver idleTime -int 0 || true
          sudo pmset -a displaysleep 0 sleep 0 disksleep 0 || true

          # Dismiss the lock UI if a screen saver is what put it up. A bare killall with no match exits non-zero,
          # which would abort this step under bash -e, so tolerate that.
          killall ScreenSaverEngine 2>/dev/null || true

          # Assert user activity and keep a display awake for the rest of the job. This wakes a slept display; on its
          # own it won't clear a session lock. That's why it runs alongside the steps above rather than instead of them.
          nohup caffeinate -u -d -i -t 7200 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          caffeinate -u -t 1 || true

          sleep 3
          echo "=== session state AFTER ==="
          session_state

      # Report the GUI session state before anything depends on it. Accessibility is mediated by WindowServer. So, a
      # runner without one denies every grant — however the TCC database is written. And that's the difference between a
      # runner which can host these tests, and one that can't. This just reports; it doesn't fail: Each probe tolerates
      # a non-match — which matters under "bash -e", where a bare pgrep that finds nothing would abort the step.
      - name: Report macOS GUI session state
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          echo "launchctl managername : $(launchctl managername 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
          if pgrep -x WindowServer >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "WindowServer          : running"
          else
            echo "WindowServer          : absent"
          fi
          if pgrep -x loginwindow >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "loginwindow           : running"
          else
            echo "loginwindow           : absent"
          fi
          echo "console user          : $(stat -f%Su /dev/console 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
          # TCC attributes an Accessibility request to the responsible process — the top-level launcher that owns the
          # process tree, not the process calling the API — so this names the binary a grant must cover.
          /usr/bin/python3 - << 'RESPEOF'
          import ctypes, os, subprocess

          libc = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib")
          try:
              fn = libc.responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid
              fn.argtypes, fn.restype = [ctypes.c_int], ctypes.c_int
              responsible = fn(os.getpid())
          except AttributeError:
              responsible = -1
          if responsible <= 0:
              print("responsible process   : unavailable")
          else:
              exe = subprocess.run(["ps", "-p", str(responsible), "-o", "comm="],
                                   capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
              print("responsible process   : {} (pid {})".format(exe or "unknown", responsible))
          RESPEOF

      - name: Check macOS SIP/TCC state
        run: |
          csrutil status || true
          SYSTEM_TCC=/Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db
          if [ -f "$SYSTEM_TCC" ]; then
            sudo ls -l "$SYSTEM_TCC" || true
            echo "--- existing kTCCServiceAccessibility entries ---"
            sudo sqlite3 "$SYSTEM_TCC" \
              "SELECT service, client, client_type, auth_value FROM access WHERE service = 'kTCCServiceAccessibility';" \
              2>&1 || echo "(could not query)"
          else
            echo "(system TCC.db doesn't exist)"
          fi

      # We only do this on non-self-hosted runners, which are fresh VMs. This rewrites the system TCC DB. And that's not
      # something we want to do on a self-hosted machine. A self-hosted machine gets its grant from whoever set it up.
      - name: Grant Accessibility to the responsible process
        if: ${{ !contains(inputs.runner_labels, 'self-hosted') }}
        run: |
          if ! csrutil status | grep -qi "disabled"; then
            echo "::warning::SIP is enabled on this runner. Can't write to TCC.db."
            exit 0
          fi
          # Grant Accessibility by writing the system TCC database directly: tccutil is broken here and MDM/PPPC
          # profiles are off-limits — so direct SQL is the only lever.
          #
          # The client that has to be granted is the *responsible* process — not the process that calls the API. TCC
          # walks up from the requesting process to the top-level launcher owning the tree — and attributes the request
          # to *that* binary. (It's the same rule that makes you grant Accessibility to your terminal app — rather than
          # to each shell script you want to run.) For a workflow step, the responsible process is whatever agent the
          # runner provider used to start the runner. So, it differs between providers — even on a byte-identical image.
          # And granting bash or python3 on its own accomplishes nothing.
          #
          # So, resolve it at run time — instead of hard-coding any provider's agent path. And grant the rest of the
          # ancestry and the interpreters alongside it — so the grant holds however the tree gets attributed.
          #
          # tccd must be restarted afterwards. It caches the database and watches only MDMOverrides.plist, not TCC.db.
          # So, a direct write stays invisible until the daemons are bounced. 'launchctl kickstart -k' does that
          # reliably; 'killall tccd' does not dependably relaunch the root-owned system instance.
          #
          # Columns: client_type=1 (path), auth_value=2 (allowed), auth_reason=4, auth_version=1, csreq=<blob>.
          # The rest default (boot_uuid defaults to 'UNUSED'). INSERT OR REPLACE keeps it idempotent.
          SYSTEM_TCC=/Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db
          CLIENTS=$(mktemp "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/tcc-clients.XXXXXX")
          REQ_BIN=$(mktemp "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/tcc-csreq.XXXXXX")

          # The responsible process, then every ancestor up to launchd — so the grant covers whichever of them the
          # kernel attributes this tree to.
          /usr/bin/python3 - >> "$CLIENTS" << 'ANCESTRYEOF'
          import ctypes, os, subprocess


          def executable(pid):
              out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "comm="], capture_output=True, text=True)
              return out.stdout.strip()


          def parent(pid):
              out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "ppid="], capture_output=True, text=True)
              text = out.stdout.strip()
              return int(text) if text.isdigit() else 0


          libc = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib")
          try:
              fn = libc.responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid
              fn.argtypes, fn.restype = [ctypes.c_int], ctypes.c_int
              responsible = fn(os.getpid())
          except AttributeError:
              responsible = -1
          if responsible > 0:
              print(executable(responsible))

          pid = os.getppid()
          while pid > 1:
              print(executable(pid))
              pid = parent(pid)
          ANCESTRYEOF

          # The preflight and run_tests.sh both use the active python3, which is the actions/setup-python one, and is
          # where we install PyObjC. So, it needs the grant as much as the system interpreters do. TCC records a client
          # by the path it was launched from — which for a symlinked Homebrew bash or a PATH-resolved python3 is not the
          # same as its realpath. So, record both forms.
          for client in "$(command -v python3 || true)" "${BASH:-$(command -v bash || true)}" \
                        /bin/bash /usr/bin/python3 /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3; do
            [ -n "$client" ] || continue
            echo "$client" >> "$CLIENTS"
            /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,sys; print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$client" >> "$CLIENTS" 2>/dev/null || true
          done

          sort -u "$CLIENTS" -o "$CLIENTS"
          # Read the list on fd 3: sudo below would otherwise consume the loop's stdin and cut it short.
          while IFS= read -r client <&3; do
            [ -n "$client" ] || continue
            [ -e "$client" ] || continue
            # codesign prints the designated requirement as 'designated => ...', or as a commented '# designated
            # => cdhash H"..."' for ad-hoc-signed binaries (Homebrew's bash, the downloaded Python). Accept both,
            # then compile it to the binary csreq blob that tccd stores and matches against. A client with no
            # derivable requirement still gets a row, with a NULL csreq, which is what the runner image's own
            # pre-provisioned rows carry.
            req=$(codesign -d -r- "$client" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^#* *designated => //p')
            csreq_sql=NULL
            csreq_note="none"
            if [ -n "$req" ] && printf '%s' "$req" | /usr/bin/csreq -r- -b "$REQ_BIN" 2>/dev/null; then
              csreq_sql="readfile('$REQ_BIN')"
              csreq_note="compiled"
            fi
            echo "=== Granting Accessibility to $client (csreq: $csreq_note) ==="
            sudo sqlite3 "$SYSTEM_TCC" \
              "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO access (service, client, client_type, auth_value, auth_reason, auth_version, csreq) VALUES ('kTCCServiceAccessibility', '$client', 1, 2, 4, 1, $csreq_sql);"
          done 3< "$CLIENTS"
          rm -f "$CLIENTS" "$REQ_BIN"

          echo "=== Accessibility entries after grant ==="
          sudo sqlite3 "$SYSTEM_TCC" \
            "SELECT client, auth_value, CASE WHEN csreq IS NULL THEN 'NULL' ELSE 'len=' || length(csreq) END FROM access WHERE service = 'kTCCServiceAccessibility' ORDER BY client;"
          # Bounce both the system and per-user tccd, so the next AX request reads these rows fresh (see note above).
          sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.apple.tccd.system || true
          launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/com.apple.tccd" || true

      - name: Verify macOS GUI session + Accessibility (AX preflight)
        run: |
          fail=0
          session=$(launchctl managername 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
          echo "launchctl managername : ${session}"
          if [ "${session}" != "Aqua" ]; then
            echo "::error title=AX preflight: no GUI session::The accessibility tests need a GUI (Aqua) login session, but this runner is in the '${session}' session. Fix: Run as a LaunchAgent under an auto-logged-in user (not a root LaunchDaemon), with screen-lock and display-sleep disabled."
            fail=1
          fi
          # An Aqua session type is not the same as a live GUI. Accessibility is mediated by WindowServer — so a runner
          # without one denies every request, no matter how the TCC DB is written. Report that here — so a failure below
          # says which of the two is missing. Each probe tolerates a non-match: this runs under "bash -e", where a bare
          # pgrep that finds nothing would abort the step.
          if pgrep -x WindowServer >/dev/null 2>&1; then window_server=running; else window_server=absent; fi
          if pgrep -x loginwindow >/dev/null 2>&1; then login_window=running; else login_window=absent; fi
          console_user=$(stat -f%Su /dev/console 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
          echo "WindowServer          : ${window_server}"
          echo "loginwindow           : ${login_window}"
          echo "console user          : ${console_user}"
          py=""
          for candidate in python3 /usr/bin/python3 /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3; do
            if command -v "${candidate}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "${candidate}" -c "import ApplicationServices" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              py="${candidate}"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -n "${py}" ]; then
            echo "probed interpreter    : ${py}"
            echo "responsible shell     : ${BASH:-unknown}"
            trusted=$("${py}" -c "from ApplicationServices import AXIsProcessTrusted as t; print('yes' if t() else 'no')" 2>/dev/null || echo "error")
            echo "AXIsProcessTrusted    : ${trusted}"
            if [ "${trusted}" != "yes" ]; then
              if [ "${window_server}" != "running" ]; then
                echo "::error title=AX preflight: no WindowServer::AXIsProcessTrusted() returned '${trusted}' and WindowServer is not running, so this runner has no live GUI session. Accessibility grants are inert without one, whatever the TCC database holds, so this is a runner property and not something the workflow can grant its way out of."
              else
                echo "::error title=AX preflight: no Accessibility access::AXIsProcessTrusted() returned '${trusted}' while WindowServer is running, so the TCC grant itself did not take. Fix: Restore the Accessibility grant for Python on this runner."
              fi
              fail=1
            fi
            # A screen-locked session passes every check above — but macOS withholds each window's accessibility
            # representation while the session is locked, so every test would fail. The wake step above tries to clear
            # the lock. So if the lock's still there, fail here, with an error that names the runner. But if the lock
            # state can't be read, just warn: The checks above already fail a runner with no GUI session, which is when
            # CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary() returns null.
            locked=$("${py}" -c "from Quartz import CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary as s; d = s(); print('unknown' if d is None else 'yes' if d.get('CGSSessionScreenIsLocked') else 'no')" 2>/dev/null || echo "error")
            echo "screen locked         : ${locked}"
            if [ "${locked}" = "yes" ]; then
              echo "::error title=AX preflight: session screen-locked::Runner ${RUNNER_NAME} booted with its session screen-locked, and waking it didn't clear the lock. macOS withholds each window's accessibility representation while the session is locked, so the accessibility tests can't run on this runner. Rerunning the job usually lands it on an unlocked runner."
              fail=1
            elif [ "${locked}" != "no" ]; then
              echo "::warning title=AX preflight: lock state unknown::Couldn't read if the session is screen-locked (got '${locked}'), so the accessibility tests run without that check."
            fi
          else
            echo "::error title=AX preflight: no PyObjC::No python3 with PyObjC found, so the accessibility tests cannot run on this runner."
            fail=1
          fi
          if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "AX preflight FAILED: this runner isn't set up to run the macOS accessibility tests (see the annotated errors above)."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${locked}" = "no" ]; then
            echo "AX preflight OK: GUI (Aqua) session unlocked, and Accessibility access present."
          else
            echo "AX preflight OK: GUI (Aqua) session and Accessibility access present, but the lock state is unknown."
          fi

      # When Ladybird never surfaces a populated AXWebArea, every test-class run waits out its full startup timeout. At
      # the 60s default, that's 20 classes times 60s: 1200s. That's past this step's timeout. And unittest only prints
      # tracebacks in its end-of-run summary. So, the harness's diagnosis (the AX surface dump plus Ladybird's stderr)
      # would be generated but then thrown away. Thus, we cap the per-class wait — so the whole suite stays inside the
      # timeout, and that summary always prints. Once warm, the Sanitizer bundle populates the web area in about 5s, and
      # the warm-up launch in run_tests.sh eats the cold first-launch cost. So, when the tests pass, this costs nothing.
      - name: Test - macOS AX testing
        timeout-minutes: 10
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ax-diagnostics
          Tests/LibWeb/AccessibilityBridgeMac/run_tests.sh
        env:
          LADYBIRD_AX_STARTUP_TIMEOUT: 20

      # Diagnostic probe for the runner-dependent failure mode of the step above: if Ladybird stays alive but never
      # surfaces a populated AXWebArea, and its stderr stays empty. A healthy Release Ladybird also writes nothing to
      # stderr (NSLog and os_log only reach the unified log). So, the probe collects the evidence saying what the app's
      # actually doing. For details on what it collects, see the Tests/LibWeb/AccessibilityBridgeMac/diagnose.py source.
      - name: Diagnose - macOS AX testing environment
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        env:
          LADYBIRD_AX_DIAG_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/ax-diagnostics
          LADYBIRD_AX_DIAG_WAIT: 25
        run: |
          py=""
          for candidate in python3 /usr/bin/python3 /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3; do
            if command -v "${candidate}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "${candidate}" -c "import ApplicationServices" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              py="${candidate}"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "${py}" ]; then
            echo "no python3 with PyObjC on this runner; skipping the probe"
            exit 0
          fi
          "${py}" Tests/LibWeb/AccessibilityBridgeMac/diagnose.py
          # The probe shuts its own Ladybird down; this catches anything the test step or the probe left behind.
          pkill -9 -f "${RUNNER_TEMP}/ladybird-app-bundle/" 2>/dev/null || true

      # A sanitizer report from any process the two steps above launched is in ax-diagnostics/ (the job's ASAN_OPTIONS
      # and UBSAN_OPTIONS). So, the upload below keeps it. Print it here too — as the build jobs do.
      - name: Sanitizer Output
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          log_output=$(find ax-diagnostics \( -name 'asan.log.*' -o -name 'ubsan.log.*' \) -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$log_output" ]; then
            echo "No sanitizer issues found."
          else
            echo "$log_output"
            echo "Sanitizer errors happened while running the accessibility tests; see the Test step above."
          fi

      - name: Upload macOS AX diagnostics
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ax-diagnostics-${{ fromJSON(inputs.runner_labels)[0] }}
          path: ax-diagnostics/
          retention-days: 0
          if-no-files-found: ignore

FILE: .github/workflows/merge-conflict-labeler.yml
name: 'Label PRs with merge conflicts'
on:
  # PRs typically get conflicted after a push to the branch they target.
  push:
    branches: [master, 'release/*']

  # If a PR is (re)opened or updated, recheck all PRs for conflicts and update their labels.
  # NOTE: This runs against the target branch, not the PR branch.
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  auto-labeler:
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'

    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - uses: eps1lon/actions-label-merge-conflict@v3.1.0
        with:
          commentOnDirty: >
            Your pull request has conflicts that need to be resolved before it can be reviewed and merged. Make sure to
            [rebase](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ElRzTuYln0M) your branch onto its target branch.
          dirtyLabel: 'conflicts'
          repoToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          retryAfter: 15
          retryMax: 3

FILE: .github/workflows/nightly-lagom.yml
name: Nightly Lagom

on:
  # Automatically run at the end of every day.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * *'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # CI matrix - runs the job in build-and-test.yml with different configurations.
  Lagom:
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
    name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}, ${{ matrix.arch }}, ${{ matrix.build_preset }}, ${{ matrix.toolchain }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os_name: ['Linux']
        arch: ['arm64']
        build_preset: ['Sanitizer']
        toolchain: ['Clang']
        clang_plugins: [false]
        runner_labels: ['["blacksmith-16vcpu-ubuntu-2404-arm"]']
        container: ['{"image":"ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-ci:2026.11.21","options":"--ulimit core=1"}']

        include:
          - os_name: 'Windows'
            arch: 'x86_64'
            build_preset: 'Sanitizer'
            toolchain: 'ClangCL'
            clang_plugins: false
            runner_labels: '["blacksmith-16vcpu-windows-2025"]'
            container: 'null'

    secrets:
      VCPKG_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: >-
        ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
            && secrets.VCPKG_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID || '' }}
      VCPKG_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: >-
        ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
            && secrets.VCPKG_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY || '' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml
    with:
      toolchain: ${{ matrix.toolchain }}
      os_name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
      runner_labels: ${{ matrix.runner_labels }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      build_preset: ${{ matrix.build_preset }}
      clang_plugins: ${{ matrix.clang_plugins }}
      container: ${{ matrix.container }}

  Release:
    if: github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird'
    name: Build Release

    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      artifact-metadata: write

    uses: ./.github/workflows/build-release.yml

FILE: .github/workflows/web-benchmarks.yml
name: 'Web benchmarks'

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]

env:
  LADYBIRD_SOURCE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}
  CCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ccache

jobs:
  web-benchmarks:
    # A run takes longer on each runner than master usually goes between pushes, and the runners are the ones that the
    # PR benchmark runs (bench-pr.yml) queue for. So only the newest push waits for each platform's runner: A push
    # replaces the job still waiting for the previous one, and lets the job in progress finish. Each platform has a
    # group of its own, so neither waits for the other's runner.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # A run takes a quarter of an hour, and half an hour at the most. A job that hangs holds its platform's runner, and
    # each push meanwhile replaces the job waiting behind it, so the history skips every push until the job ends.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.runner_labels) }}
    if: ${{ github.repository == 'LadybirdBrowser/ladybird' }}
    name: ${{ matrix.os_name }}, ${{ matrix.arch }}
    container: ${{ fromJSON(matrix.container) }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os_name: ['Linux']
        arch: ['x86_64']
        runner_labels: ['["ubuntu-24.04-internal", "web-benchmarks", "self-hosted"]']
        container: ['{"image":"ghcr.io/ladybirdbrowser/ladybird-ci:2026.11.21"}']

        include:
          - os_name: 'macOS'
            arch: 'arm64'
            runner_labels: '["macos-26", "web-benchmarks", "self-hosted"]'
            container: 'null'

    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: 'Checkout ladybird'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}

      - name: 'Determine ladybird commit hash'
        id: ladybird-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "sha=${{ github.sha }}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: 'Checkout LadybirdBrowser/web-benchmarks'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: LadybirdBrowser/web-benchmarks
          path: web-benchmarks
          ref: master

      - name: 'Determine web-benchmarks commit hash'
        id: web-benchmarks-commit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd web-benchmarks
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      - name: 'Set Up Environment'
        id: 'setup'
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup
        with:
          os: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          toolchain: 'Clang'
          build_preset: 'Distribution'

      - name: 'Restore Caches'
        uses: $/.github/actions/cache-restore
        id: 'cache-restore'
        with:
          os: ${{ matrix.os_name }}
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          toolchain: 'Clang'
          cache_key_extra: 'Distribution'
          ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
          sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
          vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}

      - name: 'Assign Build Parameters'
        id: 'build-parameters'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ${{ matrix.os_name == 'Linux' }} ; then
            echo "host_cc=clang" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "host_cxx=clang++" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif ${{ matrix.os_name == 'macOS' }} ; then
            echo "host_cc=$(xcrun --find clang)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "host_cxx=$(xcrun --find clang++)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: 'Create Build Environment'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          cmake --preset Distribution -B Build \
            -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=${{ env.pythonLocation }}/bin/python \
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cc }} \
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${{ steps.build-parameters.outputs.host_cxx }}

      - name: 'Build'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}/Build
        run: cmake --build . --target ladybird

      # vcpkg's install log names a port that failed to build, but the port's own logs hold the error.
      - name: 'Collect the logs of vcpkg ports that failed to build'
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          out=vcpkg-failure-logs
          mkdir -p "$out"
          find Build -name vcpkg-manifest-install.log | while read -r install_log; do
            sed -n 's/^error: building \([^:[]*\).*/\1/p' "$install_log" | sort -u | while read -r port; do
              mkdir -p "$out/$port"
              find Build -path "*/buildtrees/$port/*.log" -exec cp {} "$out/$port"/ \; || true
            done
            cp "$install_log" "$out"/
          done || true

      - name: 'Save the logs of vcpkg ports that failed to build'
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: vcpkg-failure-logs-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: vcpkg-failure-logs/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30

      - name: 'Save Caches'
        uses: $/.github/actions/cache-save
        with:
          arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          ccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.ccache_path }}
          ccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.ccache_primary_key }}
          sccache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.sccache_path }}
          sccache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.sccache_primary_key }}
          vcpkg_cache_path: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.vcpkg_cache_path }}
          vcpkg_cache_primary_key: ${{ steps.cache-restore.outputs.vcpkg_cache_primary_key }}

      - name: 'Run the benchmarks'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd web-benchmarks
          python3 -m venv .venv
          source .venv/bin/activate
          python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

          if [ "${{ matrix.os_name }}" = "macOS" ]; then
            executable="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/bin/Ladybird.app/Contents/MacOS/Ladybird"
          else
            executable="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/Build/bin/Ladybird"
          fi

          ./run.py --iterations=3 --executable="${executable}"

      - name: 'Save results as an artifact'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: web-benchmarks-results-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: web-benchmarks/results.json
          retention-days: 90

      - name: 'Call webhook'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo '{
              "commit": "${{ steps.ladybird-commit.outputs.sha }}",
              "benchmarks_commit": "${{ steps.web-benchmarks-commit.outputs.sha }}",
              "os": "${{ matrix.os_name }}",
              "arch": "${{ matrix.arch }}",
              "artifact": "web-benchmarks-results-${{ matrix.os_name }}-${{ matrix.arch }}",
              "artifact_run_id": "${{ github.run_id }}"
          }' > request.json
          curl \
              --fail \
              --silent \
              --show-error \
              --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              --header "X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=$(openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac '${{ secrets.JS_BENCHMARKS_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}' request.json | cut -d' ' -f2)" \
              --data-binary '@request.json' \
              '${{ secrets.JS_BENCHMARKS_WEBHOOK_URL }}'

import os

import ycm_core

DIR_OF_THIS_SCRIPT = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
SOURCE_EXTENSIONS = [".cpp", ".c"]

database = ycm_core.CompilationDatabase(os.path.join(DIR_OF_THIS_SCRIPT, "Build/ladybird"))


def is_header_file(filename):
    extension = os.path.splitext(filename)[1]
    return extension in [".h", ".hxx", ".hpp", ".hh"]


def find_corresponding_source_file(filename):
    if is_header_file(filename):
        basename = os.path.splitext(filename)[0]
        for extension in SOURCE_EXTENSIONS:
            replacement_file = basename + extension
            if os.path.exists(replacement_file):
                return replacement_file
    return filename


def Settings(**kwargs):  # noqa: N802
    if kwargs["language"] != "cfamily":
        return {}
    # If the file is a header, try to find the corresponding source file and
    # retrieve its flags from the compilation database if using one. This is
    # necessary since compilation databases don't have entries for header files.
    # In addition, use this source file as the translation unit. This makes it
    # possible to jump from a declaration in the header file to its definition
    # in the corresponding source file.
    filename = find_corresponding_source_file(kwargs["filename"])

    compilation_info = database.GetCompilationInfoForFile(filename)
    if not compilation_info.compiler_flags_:
        return {}

    return {
        "flags": list(compilation_info.compiler_flags_),
        "include_paths_relative_to_dir": DIR_OF_THIS_SCRIPT,
        "override_filename": filename,
    }

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2020, the SerenityOS developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#pragma once

#include <AK/Concepts.h>
#include <AK/Find.h>
#include <AK/Iterator.h>

namespace AK {

template<typename TEndIterator, IteratorPairWith<TEndIterator> TIterator>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool all_of(
    TIterator const& begin,
    TEndIterator const& end,
    auto const& predicate)
{
    constexpr auto negated_predicate = [](auto const& pred) {
        return [&](auto const& elem) { return !pred(elem); };
    };
    return !(find_if(begin, end, negated_predicate(predicate)) != end);
}

template<IterableContainer Container>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool all_of(Container&& container, auto const& predicate)
{
    return all_of(container.begin(), container.end(), predicate);
}

}

#if USING_AK_GLOBALLY
using AK::all_of;
#endif

#pragma once

[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool any_of(
    TIterator const& begin,
    TEndIterator const& end,
    auto const& predicate)
{
    return find_if(begin, end, predicate) != end;
}

FILE: AK/Array.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2020, the SerenityOS developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Iterator.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Span.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/TypedTransfer.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>

namespace AK {

namespace Detail {

// This type serves as the storage of 0-sized `AK::Array`s. While zero-length `T[0]`
// is accepted as a GNU extension, it causes problems with UBSan in Clang 16.
template<typename T>
struct EmptyArrayStorage {
    T& operator[](size_t) const { VERIFY_NOT_REACHED(); }
    constexpr operator T*() const { return nullptr; }
};

}

template<typename T, size_t Size>
struct Array {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    using ValueType = T;

    // This is a static function because constructors mess up Array's POD-ness.
    static Array from_span(ReadonlySpan<T> span)
    {
        Array array;
        VERIFY(span.size() == Size);
        TypedTransfer<T>::copy(array.data(), span.data(), Size);
        return array;
    }

    static constexpr Array from_repeated_value(T const& value)
    {
        Array array;
        array.fill(value);
        return array;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T const* data() const { return __data; }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T* data() { return __data; }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr size_t size() const { return Size; }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr ReadonlySpan<T> span() const { return { __data, Size }; }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr Span<T> span() { return { __data, Size }; }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T const& at(size_t index) const
    {
        VERIFY(index < size());
        return __data[index];
    }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T& at(size_t index)
    {
        VERIFY(index < size());
        return __data[index];
    }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T const& first() const { return at(0); }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T& first() { return at(0); }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T const& last() const
    requires(Size > 0)
    {
        return at(Size - 1);
    }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T& last()
    requires(Size > 0)
    {
        return at(Size - 1);
    }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool is_empty() const { return size() == 0; }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T const& operator[](size_t index) const { return at(index); }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T& operator[](size_t index) { return at(index); }

    template<typename T2, size_t Size2>
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(Array<T2, Size2> const& other) const { return span() == other.span(); }

    using ConstIterator = SimpleIterator<Array const, T const>;
    using Iterator = SimpleIterator<Array, T>;

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr ConstIterator begin() const { return ConstIterator::begin(*this); }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr Iterator begin() { return Iterator::begin(*this); }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr ConstIterator end() const { return ConstIterator::end(*this); }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr Iterator end() { return Iterator::end(*this); }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator ReadonlySpan<T>() const { return span(); }
    [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator Span<T>() { return span(); }

    constexpr size_t fill(T const& value)
    {
        for (size_t idx = 0; idx < Size; ++idx)
            __data[idx] = value;

        return Size;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T max() const
    requires(requires(T x, T y) { x < y; })
    {
        static_assert(Size > 0, "No values to max() over");

        T value = __data[0];
        for (size_t i = 1; i < Size; ++i)
            value = AK::max(__data[i], value);
        return value;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] constexpr T min() const
    requires(requires(T x, T y) { x > y; })
    {
        static_assert(Size > 0, "No values to min() over");

        T value = __data[0];
        for (size_t i = 1; i < Size; ++i)
            value = AK::min(__data[i], value);
        return value;
    }

    bool contains_slow(T const& value) const
    {
        return first_index_of(value).has_value();
    }

    Optional<size_t> first_index_of(T const& value) const
    {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < Size; ++i) {
            if (__data[i] == value)
                return i;
        }
        return {};
    }

    Conditional<Size == 0, Detail::EmptyArrayStorage<T>, T[Size]> __data;
};

template<typename T, typename... Types>
Array(T, Types...) -> Array<T, sizeof...(Types) + 1>;

namespace Detail {

template<typename T, size_t... Is>
constexpr auto integer_sequence_generate_array([[maybe_unused]] T const offset, IntegerSequence<T, Is...>) -> Array<T, sizeof...(Is)>
{
    return { { (offset + Is)... } };
}

}

template<typename T, T N>
constexpr auto iota_array(T const offset = {})
{
    static_assert(N >= T {}, "Negative sizes not allowed in iota_array()");
    return Detail::integer_sequence_generate_array<T>(offset, MakeIntegerSequence<T, N>());
}

namespace Detail {

template<typename T, size_t N, size_t... Is>
constexpr auto to_array_impl(T (&&a)[N], IndexSequence<Is...>) -> Array<T, sizeof...(Is)>
{
    return { { move(a[Is])... } };
}

}

template<typename T, size_t N>
constexpr auto to_array(T (&&a)[N])
{
    return Detail::to_array_impl(move(a), MakeIndexSequence<N>());
}

}

#if USING_AK_GLOBALLY
using AK::Array;
using AK::iota_array;
using AK::to_array;
#endif

#pragma once

#include <AK/Span.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>

namespace AK {

enum class AssertionFailureKind : u8 {
    Verification,
    Assertion,
    RustPanic,
};

using AssertionFailureCallback = void (*)(AssertionFailureKind, char const*);

// Called for fatal assertions after the test handler, before formatting or
// backtrace generation. The callback must not allocate or trigger assertions.
void set_assertion_failure_callback(AssertionFailureCallback);

struct AssertionBacktraceFrame {
    FlatPtr address; // The enclosing physical frame's address for inline entries.
    StringView symbol;
    StringView filename;
    u32 line;
    u32 column;
    bool is_inline;
};

constexpr size_t maximum_assertion_backtrace_frames = 128;

using AssertionBacktraceCallback = void (*)(ReadonlySpan<AssertionBacktraceFrame>);

// Receive the same resolved frames used by terminal backtraces, before formatting.
// Views are valid only during the callback. The callback must not allocate.
void set_assertion_backtrace_callback(AssertionBacktraceCallback);

// Bounded, thread-local panic text. A recovered panic is not considered active.
// Suitable for the native crash handler after the Rust panic hook has run.
char const* current_rust_panic_message();

}

extern "C" void ladybird_rust_panic(u8 const*, size_t, u8 const*, size_t, u32, u32, bool (*)());
extern "C" void ladybird_rust_panic_hook_returned();
extern "C" void ladybird_rust_panic_may_abort();
extern "C" void ladybird_rust_panic_will_abort();

FILE: AK/Assertions.cpp
/*

 *
