// AK string data is immutable, and its reference count and cached metadata are atomic.
// The fly-string table synchronizes interning and destruction across threads.
// A raw string is never zero, which is what lets `Option` of an owner stay one word, the same as
// `AK::Optional<AK::Utf16String>`.
#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Debug)]
struct OwnedUtf16String {
    raw: NonZeroUsize,
}

impl OwnedUtf16String {
    #[inline]
    const fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            raw: NonZeroUsize::new(SHORT_STRING_FLAG).unwrap(),
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    unsafe fn from_raw(raw: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            raw: NonZeroUsize::new(raw).expect("raw AK strings are never zero"),
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
        let this = std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(self);
        this.raw.get()
    }

    #[inline]
    fn raw_word(&self) -> &usize {
        // SAFETY: NonZeroUsize has the same layout as usize.
        unsafe { &*std::ptr::from_ref(&self.raw).cast::<usize>() }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn as_units(&self) -> Utf16StringUnits<'_> {
        // SAFETY: This owner keeps the raw string alive for the returned lifetime.
        unsafe { utf16_string_units(self.raw_word()) }
    }
}

impl Clone for OwnedUtf16String {
    #[inline]
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: This owner keeps the raw string alive while adding a reference.
        unsafe { reference_utf16_string(self.raw.get()) };
        // SAFETY: The new reference is transferred to the returned owner.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw(self.raw.get()) }
    }
}

impl Drop for OwnedUtf16String {
    #[inline]
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This object owns one reference to its raw string.
        unsafe {
            release_utf16_string_with(self.raw.get(), |raw| ladybird_utf16_string_unref(raw));
        }
    }
}

/// A one-word Rust owner for the same storage as `AK::Utf16String`.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct Utf16String(OwnedUtf16String);

/// A one-word Rust owner for the same interned storage as `AK::Utf16FlyString`.
#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Utf16FlyString(OwnedUtf16String);

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<OwnedUtf16String>() == size_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<OwnedUtf16String>() == align_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Utf16String>() == size_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<Utf16String>() == align_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Utf16FlyString>() == size_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<Utf16FlyString>() == align_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Option<Utf16String>>() == size_of::<usize>());
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Option<Utf16FlyString>>() == size_of::<usize>());

const _: fn() = || {
    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_sync::<Utf16String>();
    assert_send_sync::<Utf16FlyString>();
};

macro_rules! impl_utf16_string_owner {
    ($name:ident) => {
        impl $name {
            /// Adopts an existing C++ ownership reference without changing its count.
            ///
            /// # Safety
            ///
            /// `raw` must be a valid `AK::Utf16String` raw representation for which
            /// the caller owns one reference. The reference must not be released
            /// separately after this call.
            #[inline]
            pub unsafe fn from_raw_owned(raw: usize) -> Self {
                // SAFETY: The caller transfers a valid ownership reference.
                Self(unsafe { OwnedUtf16String::from_raw(raw) })
            }

            /// Retains a borrowed raw `AK::Utf16String` reference.
            ///
            /// # Safety
            ///
            /// `raw` must be a valid, nonzero raw representation that remains live for this call.
            #[inline]
            pub unsafe fn from_raw_borrowed(raw: usize) -> Self {
                // SAFETY: The caller keeps the string alive while adding a reference.
                unsafe { reference_utf16_string(raw) };
                // SAFETY: The new reference is transferred to the returned owner.
                unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
            }

            /// Transfers this owner's existing reference to the caller.
            #[inline]
            pub fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
                self.0.into_raw()
            }

            /// Returns the shared one-word identity without transferring ownership.
            #[inline]
            pub fn raw_identity(&self) -> usize {
                self.0.raw.get()
            }

            /// Borrows the shared Latin-1 or UTF-16 character storage directly.
            #[inline]
            pub fn as_units(&self) -> Utf16StringUnits<'_> {
                self.0.as_units()
            }

            /// Borrows UTF-16 storage, widening Latin-1 only when a UTF-16 slice is needed.
            pub fn to_utf16(&self) -> std::borrow::Cow<'_, [u16]> {
                match self.as_units() {
                    Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => {
                        units.iter().map(|&unit| u16::from(unit)).collect()
                    }
                    Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(units),
                }
            }

            /// Returns whether the string has no code units.
            #[inline]
            pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
                self.length_in_code_units() == 0
            }

            /// Returns the number of UTF-16 code units, which is the number of bytes of Latin-1 storage.
            #[inline]
            pub fn length_in_code_units(&self) -> usize {
                match self.as_units() {
                    Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => units.len(),
                    Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => units.len(),
                }
            }
        }

        impl Default for $name {
            #[inline]
            fn default() -> Self {
                Self(OwnedUtf16String::empty())
            }
        }

        impl Clone for $name {
            #[inline]
            fn clone(&self) -> Self {
                Self(self.0.clone())
            }
        }
    };
}

impl_utf16_string_owner!(Utf16String);
impl_utf16_string_owner!(Utf16FlyString);

impl Utf16String {
    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation and initializes its storage from UTF-8.
    pub fn from_utf8(string: &str) -> Self {
        if string.is_ascii() {
            return Self::from_ascii_without_validation(string.as_bytes());
        }

        // SAFETY: The string remains alive for the duration of the call.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_string_from_utf8(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) };
        // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }

    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation and initializes its storage from UTF-16, with one byte per
    /// code unit if none is above U+00FF.
    pub fn from_utf16(string: &[u16]) -> Self {
        let is_ascii = string.iter().all(|code_unit| *code_unit <= 0x7f);
        if is_ascii || string.iter().all(|code_unit| *code_unit <= 0xff) {
            if is_ascii && string.len() < size_of::<usize>() {
                let mut bytes = [0; size_of::<usize>() - 1];
                for (index, code_unit) in string.iter().enumerate() {
                    bytes[index] = *code_unit as u8;
                }
                return Self::from_short_ascii(&bytes[..string.len()]);
            }

            let result = Self::create_uninitialized(string.len(), StorageKind::one_byte(is_ascii));
            let storage = result.long_storage();
            for (index, code_unit) in string.iter().enumerate() {
                // SAFETY: The allocation has space for exactly `string.len()` Latin-1 bytes.
                unsafe { storage.add(index).write(*code_unit as u8) };
            }
            return result;
        }

        let result = Self::create_uninitialized(string.len(), StorageKind::Utf16);
        // SAFETY: The source and destination are non-overlapping and the allocation has space for
        // exactly `string.len()` UTF-16 code units.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(string.as_ptr(), result.long_storage().cast(), string.len()) };
        result
    }

    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation from ASCII bytes.
    #[inline]
    pub fn from_ascii(string: &[u8]) -> Self {
        assert!(string.is_ascii(), "an ASCII string holds ASCII bytes");
        Self::from_ascii_without_validation(string)
    }

    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation from Latin-1 bytes, one per code unit.
    pub fn from_latin1(string: &[u8]) -> Self {
        if string.is_ascii() {
            return Self::from_ascii_without_validation(string);
        }

        let result = Self::create_uninitialized(string.len(), StorageKind::Latin1);
        // SAFETY: The source and destination are non-overlapping and the allocation has space for
        // exactly `string.len()` Latin-1 bytes.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(string.as_ptr(), result.long_storage(), string.len()) };
        result
    }

    pub fn to_ascii_lowercase(&self) -> Self {
        match self.as_units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) => Self::from_ascii(&units.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => Self::from_latin1(&units.to_ascii_lowercase()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => Self::from_utf16(
                &units
                    .iter()
                    .map(|&code_unit| match u8::try_from(code_unit) {
                        Ok(byte) => u16::from(byte.to_ascii_lowercase()),
                        Err(_) => code_unit,
                    })
                    .collect::<Vec<u16>>(),
            ),
        }
    }

    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation from the Latin-1 bytes of `pieces` one after the other, which
    /// add up to `length` bytes, copying each piece into the string's storage directly. `is_ascii` tells whether
    /// every byte is ASCII.
    pub fn from_latin1_concatenation<'a>(
        length: usize,
        is_ascii: bool,
        pieces: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a [u8]>,
    ) -> Self {
        if is_ascii && length < size_of::<usize>() {
            let mut bytes = [0; size_of::<usize>() - 1];
            let mut byte_count = 0;
            for piece in pieces {
                bytes[byte_count..byte_count + piece.len()].copy_from_slice(piece);
                byte_count += piece.len();
            }
            assert_eq!(byte_count, length, "the pieces add up to the length of the string");
            return Self::from_ascii(&bytes[..length]);
        }

        let result = Self::create_uninitialized(length, StorageKind::one_byte(is_ascii));
        let storage = result.long_storage();
        let mut byte_count = 0;
        for piece in pieces {
            assert!(
                piece.len() <= length - byte_count,
                "the pieces add up to the length of the string"
            );
            // SAFETY: The allocation has space for `length` Latin-1 bytes, of which `byte_count` are written, and the
            // piece fits in the rest.
            unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(piece.as_ptr(), storage.add(byte_count), piece.len()) };
            byte_count += piece.len();
        }
        assert_eq!(byte_count, length, "the pieces add up to the length of the string");
        // SAFETY: Every byte of the allocation is written.
        let bytes = unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(storage.cast_const(), length) };
        assert_eq!(bytes.is_ascii(), is_ascii, "an ASCII string holds ASCII bytes");
        result
    }

    /// Creates a string in AK's native representation of `length` ASCII bytes, which `fill` writes into the string's
    /// storage directly.
    pub fn from_ascii_with(length: usize, fill: impl FnOnce(&mut [u8])) -> Self {
        if length < size_of::<usize>() {
            let mut bytes = [0; size_of::<usize>() - 1];
            fill(&mut bytes[..length]);
            return Self::from_ascii(&bytes[..length]);
        }

        let result = Self::create_uninitialized(length, StorageKind::Ascii);
        // SAFETY: The allocation has space for exactly `length` ASCII bytes, which are zeroed before they are lent out.
        let storage = unsafe {
            std::ptr::write_bytes(result.long_storage(), 0, length);
            crate::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(result.long_storage(), length)
        };
        fill(storage);
        assert!(storage.is_ascii(), "an ASCII string holds ASCII bytes");
        result
    }

    #[inline]
    fn from_ascii_without_validation(string: &[u8]) -> Self {
        if string.len() < size_of::<usize>() {
            return Self::from_short_ascii(string);
        }

        let result = Self::create_uninitialized(string.len(), StorageKind::Ascii);
        // SAFETY: The source and destination are non-overlapping and the allocation has space for
        // exactly `string.len()` ASCII bytes.
        unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(string.as_ptr(), result.long_storage(), string.len()) };
        result
    }

    #[inline]
    fn from_short_ascii(string: &[u8]) -> Self {
        assert!(string.len() < size_of::<usize>());
        let mut bytes = [0; size_of::<usize>()];
        let tag = ((string.len() as u8) << SHORT_STRING_BYTE_COUNT_SHIFT) | SHORT_STRING_FLAG as u8;
        #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
        {
            bytes[0] = tag;
            bytes[1..][..string.len()].copy_from_slice(string);
        }
        #[cfg(target_endian = "big")]
        {
            bytes[size_of::<usize>() - 1] = tag;
            bytes[..string.len()].copy_from_slice(string);
        }
        // SAFETY: The constructed word is AK's short-string representation and owns no allocation.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(usize::from_ne_bytes(bytes)) }
    }

    fn create_uninitialized(length: usize, kind: StorageKind) -> Self {
        assert!(length < UNKNOWN_CODE_POINT_LENGTH as usize);
        let has_latin1_storage = kind != StorageKind::Utf16;
        let unit_size = if has_latin1_storage { 1 } else { size_of::<u16>() };
        assert!(
            size_of::<Utf16StringDataHeader>()
                .checked_add(
                    length
                        .checked_mul(unit_size)
                        .expect("UTF-16 string allocation size overflow")
                )
                .is_some()
        );
        // SAFETY: C++ returns a fully initialized native string owner with trailing storage sized
        // for `length` units. The caller initializes that storage before publishing the owner.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_string_create_uninitialized(length, has_latin1_storage) };
        if kind == StorageKind::Latin1 {
            // SAFETY: The new string is the address of its data, which starts with this header and is not shared yet.
            let header = unsafe { &*std::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<Utf16StringDataHeader>(raw) };
            header.flags.fetch_or(CONTAINS_NON_ASCII, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        // SAFETY: The allocator transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn long_storage(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        assert!(has_long_storage(self.raw_identity()));
        std::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<u8>(self.raw_identity())
            .wrapping_add(size_of::<Utf16StringDataHeader>())
    }
}

impl Utf16String {
    pub fn well_formed_from_utf16(string: &[u16]) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_string_to_well_formed(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) };
        // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }
}

/// Gives the memory the calling thread freed back to the system. The allocator otherwise keeps it until the thread
/// allocates again, so a thread that made large transient allocations calls this once it goes idle.
pub fn release_unused_allocator_memory() {
    // SAFETY: Takes no arguments, and any thread may call it.
    unsafe { ladybird_release_unused_allocator_memory() }
}

/// Adds a function that a thread pool calls on a thread that goes idle (see `release_idle_thread_memory()`). It gives
/// back the memory that the calling thread keeps outside the allocator for its next jobs, and does nothing on a thread
/// that keeps none. Adding a function a second time does nothing.
pub fn add_idle_thread_memory_release(release: extern "C" fn()) {
    // SAFETY: Any thread may add a function, which stays valid for as long as the process runs.
    unsafe { ladybird_add_idle_thread_memory_release(release) }
}

/// Calls all the functions added with `add_idle_thread_memory_release()` on the calling thread.
pub fn release_idle_thread_memory() {
    // SAFETY: Takes no arguments, and any thread may call it.
    unsafe { ladybird_release_idle_thread_memory() }
}

/// Maps in, in one go, the pages of the room `vector` has past its elements for `additional` more, for writes about to
/// fill it: a vector a large write grows into fresh memory then takes its pages at once rather than a fault at a time.
/// Where the system cannot, the writes map them in as they come.
pub fn populate_room_for_write<T>(vector: &mut Vec<T>, additional: usize) {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    {
        unsafe extern "C" {
            fn madvise(address: *mut core::ffi::c_void, length: usize, advice: core::ffi::c_int) -> core::ffi::c_int;
            fn getpagesize() -> core::ffi::c_int;
        }
        const MADV_POPULATE_WRITE: core::ffi::c_int = 23;
        let room = vector.spare_capacity_mut();
        let length = additional.min(room.len());
        let room = &mut room[..length];
        let (start, end) = (
            room.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
            room.as_mut_ptr() as usize + size_of_val(room),
        );
        // SAFETY: Takes no arguments.
        let page_size = unsafe { getpagesize() } as usize;
        let (start, end) = (start.next_multiple_of(page_size), end / page_size * page_size);
        if start < end {
            // SAFETY: The pages lie in unused capacity the vector owns, and mapping them in changes nothing the vector
            //         reads. It only fails where the kernel is too old to know the advice, which leaves the faults to
            //         the first writes.
            unsafe { madvise(start as *mut core::ffi::c_void, end - start, MADV_POPULATE_WRITE) };
        }
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
    let _ = (vector, additional);
}

pub fn validate_utf16(string: &[u16]) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
    unsafe { ladybird_utf16_validate(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) }
}

/// The number of bytes of the UTF-8 encoding of a well-formed UTF-16 string.
pub fn utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(string: &[u16]) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
    unsafe { ladybird_utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) }
}

/// Writes the UTF-8 encoding of a well-formed UTF-16 string to the start of `output`, which need not be initialized,
/// and returns the number of bytes it wrote, which are initialized afterwards.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `string` must be well-formed UTF-16, and `output` must have room for its UTF-8 encoding, which is
/// utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(string) bytes.
pub unsafe fn convert_valid_utf16_to_utf8(string: &[u16], output: &mut [MaybeUninit<u8>]) -> usize {
    debug_assert!(validate_utf16(string));
    debug_assert!(output.len() >= utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(string));
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that the string is well-formed and that the output has room for its encoding.
    unsafe { ladybird_convert_valid_utf16_to_utf8(string.as_ptr(), string.len(), output.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>()) }
}

pub fn append_utf16_as_utf8_up_to_unpaired_surrogate(output: &mut Vec<u8>, string: &[u16]) -> usize {
    let mut valid_code_units = 0;
    // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
    unsafe { ladybird_utf16_validate_prefix(string.as_ptr(), string.len(), &raw mut valid_code_units) };
    assert!(valid_code_units <= string.len());

    output.reserve(3 * valid_code_units);
    // SAFETY: The first `valid_code_units` code units are well-formed UTF-16, of which every code unit becomes at most
    // three bytes of UTF-8, and the output has room for them past its length.
    unsafe {
        let written = ladybird_convert_valid_utf16_to_utf8(
            string.as_ptr(),
            valid_code_units,
            output.as_mut_ptr().add(output.len()),
        );
        output.set_len(output.len() + written);
    }
    valid_code_units
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DecimalExponentialForm {
    pub sign: bool,
    pub fraction: u64,
    pub exponent: i32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RemoveTrailingZeroes {
    No,
    Yes,
}

#[inline]
pub fn convert_to_decimal_exponential_form(
    value: f64,
    remove_trailing_zeroes: RemoveTrailingZeroes,
) -> DecimalExponentialForm {
    assert!(value.is_finite());
    let mut form = DecimalExponentialForm {
        sign: false,
        fraction: 0,
        exponent: 0,
    };
    let convert = match remove_trailing_zeroes {
        RemoveTrailingZeroes::Yes => ladybird_convert_to_decimal_exponential_form,
        RemoveTrailingZeroes::No => ladybird_convert_to_decimal_exponential_form_with_trailing_zeroes,
    };
    // SAFETY: The outputs live for the duration of the call.
    unsafe {
        convert(
            value,
            &raw mut form.sign,
            &raw mut form.fraction,
            &raw mut form.exponent,
        );
    }
    form
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Base64Alphabet {
    Base64,
    Base64Url,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum LastChunkHandling {
    Loose,
    Strict,
    StopBeforePartial,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Base64DecodeError {
    ExtraBits,
    InputRemainder,
    InvalidCharacter,
    InvalidData,
}

pub struct Base64DecodeResult {
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub read: usize,
    pub error: Option<Base64DecodeError>,
}

fn raw_units(string: Utf16StringUnits<'_>) -> (*const u8, usize, bool) {
    match string {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => (bytes.as_ptr(), bytes.len(), true),
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => (units.as_ptr().cast(), units.len(), false),
    }
}

pub fn decode_base64(
    input: Utf16StringUnits<'_>,
    alphabet: Base64Alphabet,
    last_chunk_handling: LastChunkHandling,
    max_length: Option<usize>,
) -> Base64DecodeResult {
    let (data, length, has_latin1_storage) = raw_units(input);
    let capacity = max_length.unwrap_or_else(|| {
        // SAFETY: The string's storage remains alive for the duration of the call.
        unsafe { ladybird_size_required_to_decode_base64(data, length, has_latin1_storage) }
    });

    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
    let mut output_length = capacity;
    let mut read = 0;
    // SAFETY: The string's storage remains alive for the duration of the call, and the output has room for
    // `capacity` bytes, of which the call writes the first `output_length`.
    let error = unsafe {
        ladybird_decode_base64_into(
            data,
            length,
            has_latin1_storage,
            alphabet == Base64Alphabet::Base64Url,
            last_chunk_handling as u8,
            bytes.as_mut_ptr(),
            &raw mut output_length,
            &raw mut read,
        )
    };
    assert!(output_length <= capacity);
    // SAFETY: The call initialized the first `output_length` bytes.
    unsafe { bytes.set_len(output_length) };

    let error = match error {
        0 => None,
        1 => Some(Base64DecodeError::ExtraBits),
        2 => Some(Base64DecodeError::InputRemainder),
        3 => Some(Base64DecodeError::InvalidCharacter),
        _ => Some(Base64DecodeError::InvalidData),
    };
    Base64DecodeResult { bytes, read, error }
}

pub fn encode_base64(input: &[u8], alphabet: Base64Alphabet, omit_padding: bool) -> Utf16String {
    // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
    let raw = unsafe {
        ladybird_encode_base64_to_utf16(
            input.as_ptr(),
            input.len(),
            alphabet == Base64Alphabet::Base64Url,
            omit_padding,
        )
    };
    // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
    unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(raw) }
}

impl Utf16FlyString {
    /// Creates a string through AK's authoritative UTF-8 fly-string table.
    pub fn from_utf8(string: &str) -> Self {
        if let Some(raw) = utf16_short_string_raw(string) {
            // SAFETY: Short strings own no allocation or reference count.
            return Self(unsafe { OwnedUtf16String::from_raw(raw) });
        }

        // SAFETY: The string's storage remains alive for the duration of the call.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_fly_string_from_utf8(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) };
        // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }

    /// Creates a string through AK's authoritative UTF-16 fly-string table.
    pub fn from_utf16(string: &[u16]) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The slice remains alive for the duration of the call.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_fly_string_from_utf16(string.as_ptr(), string.len()) };
        // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }

    /// Mirrors the AK::Utf16FlyString constructor from a Utf16String: the fly string with the contents of `string`,
    /// which is the storage of `string` itself if AK's fly-string table has no equal string yet.
    pub fn from_utf16_string(string: &Utf16String) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The string keeps its storage alive for the duration of the call, which adds a reference of its own.
        let raw = unsafe { ladybird_utf16_fly_string_from_utf16_string(string.raw_identity()) };
        // SAFETY: The constructor transfers one ownership reference.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(raw) }
    }
}

/// Returns AK's one-word representation for a short ASCII string.
pub const fn utf16_short_string_raw(string: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let bytes = string.as_bytes();
    if bytes.len() >= size_of::<usize>() {
        return None;
    }

    let mut raw = (bytes.len() << SHORT_STRING_BYTE_COUNT_SHIFT) | SHORT_STRING_FLAG;
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < bytes.len() {
        if !bytes[index].is_ascii() {
            return None;
        }
        #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
        {
            raw |= (bytes[index] as usize) << ((index + 1) * 8);
        }
        #[cfg(target_endian = "big")]
        {
            raw |= (bytes[index] as usize) << ((size_of::<usize>() - index - 1) * 8);
        }
        index += 1;
    }
    Some(raw)
}

impl PartialEq for Utf16String {
    #[inline]
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        // Mirrors AK::Utf16StringBase::operator==(): the same word is the same string, and short strings, whose
        // characters are in the word itself, are equal only if their words are.
        let (left, right) = (self.raw_identity(), other.raw_identity());
        if left == right {
            return true;
        }
        if left & SHORT_STRING_FLAG != 0 && right & SHORT_STRING_FLAG != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        match (self.as_units(), other.as_units()) {
            (
                Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left),
                Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(right) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(right),
            ) => left == right,
            (Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(left), Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right)) => left == right,
            (Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left), Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right))
            | (Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(right), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(left) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(left)) => {
                left.len() == right.len() && left.iter().zip(right).all(|(left, right)| u16::from(*left) == *right)
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Eq for Utf16String {}

impl PartialEq<str> for Utf16String {
    fn eq(&self, other: &str) -> bool {
        match self.as_units() {
            // NB: The UTF-8 of an ASCII string is its ASCII bytes.
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) => units == other.as_bytes(),
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => units.iter().map(|&unit| u16::from(unit)).eq(other.encode_utf16()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => units.iter().copied().eq(other.encode_utf16()),
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq<&str> for Utf16String {
    fn eq(&self, other: &&str) -> bool {
        *self == **other
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Utf16String {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let string = match self.as_units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => {
                units.iter().map(|&unit| char::from(unit)).collect::<String>()
            }
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => String::from_utf16_lossy(units),
        };
        std::fmt::Debug::fmt(&string, formatter)
    }
}

impl std::hash::Hash for Utf16String {
    fn hash<H: std::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        // Equal strings can be kept in different storage, so the code units are hashed as UTF-16 whichever it is.
        match self.as_units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => {
                state.write_usize(units.len());
                for &unit in units {
                    state.write_u16(u16::from(unit));
                }
            }
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => {
                state.write_usize(units.len());
                for &unit in units {
                    state.write_u16(unit);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq for Utf16FlyString {
    #[inline]
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.raw_identity() == other.raw_identity() || (self.is_empty() && other.is_empty())
    }
}

impl Eq for Utf16FlyString {}

impl std::hash::Hash for Utf16FlyString {
    #[inline]
    fn hash<H: std::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.raw_identity().hash(state);
    }
}

impl From<Utf16FlyString> for Utf16String {
    #[inline]
    fn from(string: Utf16FlyString) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: `into_raw` transfers the existing reference to this owner.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(string.into_raw()) }
    }
}

impl From<&Utf16FlyString> for Utf16String {
    #[inline]
    fn from(string: &Utf16FlyString) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The source owner keeps the raw string alive while adding a reference.
        unsafe { reference_utf16_string(string.raw_identity()) };
        // SAFETY: The new reference is transferred to this owner.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_owned(string.raw_identity()) }
    }
}

#[inline]
fn has_long_storage(raw: usize) -> bool {
    raw != 0 && raw & SHORT_STRING_FLAG == 0
}

/// Adds an ownership reference to a raw `AK::Utf16String` representation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `raw` must be zero, a valid short string, or a live long string allocation.
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn reference_utf16_string(raw: usize) {
    if !has_long_storage(raw) {
        return;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `raw` points to a live long string allocation.
    let header = unsafe { &*std::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<Utf16StringDataHeader>(raw) };
    let result = header
        .reference_count
        .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |count| {
            (count != 0).then(|| count.checked_add(1)).flatten()
        });
    assert!(result.is_ok(), "invalid UTF-16 string reference count");
}

/// Releases an ownership reference to a raw `AK::Utf16String` representation.
/// Calls `release_last` when C++ must perform the potentially final release.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `raw` must be zero, a valid short string, or a live long string allocation
/// for which the caller owns one reference. `release_last` must perform the
/// release-ordered decrement and acquire fence required before destruction.
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn release_utf16_string_with(raw: usize, release_last: impl FnOnce(usize)) {
    if !has_long_storage(raw) {
        return;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `raw` points to a live long string allocation.
    let header = unsafe { &*std::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<Utf16StringDataHeader>(raw) };
    loop {
        let reference_count = header.reference_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        assert!(reference_count != 0, "invalid UTF-16 string reference count");
        if reference_count == 1 {
            // The callback performs the final release decrement and acquire fence.
            release_last(raw);
            return;
        }
        if header
            .reference_count
            .compare_exchange_weak(
                reference_count,
                reference_count - 1,
                Ordering::Release,
                Ordering::Relaxed,
            )
            .is_ok()
        {
            return;
        }
    }
}

/// Decodes the storage referenced by a raw `AK::Utf16String` representation.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `raw` must remain at a stable address for the returned lifetime. Its value
/// must be zero, a valid short string, or a live long string allocation that
/// remains alive for the returned lifetime.
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn utf16_string_units(raw: &usize) -> Utf16StringUnits<'_> {
    if *raw == 0 {
        return Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(&[]);
    }

    if !has_long_storage(*raw) {
        let bytes = raw.to_ne_bytes();
        #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
        let tag = bytes[0];
        #[cfg(target_endian = "big")]
        let tag = bytes[size_of::<usize>() - 1];
        let length = usize::from(tag >> SHORT_STRING_BYTE_COUNT_SHIFT);
        assert!(length < size_of::<usize>());

        let pointer = std::ptr::from_ref(raw).cast::<u8>();
        #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
        // SAFETY: A short string stores its bytes after the tag byte.
        let pointer = unsafe { pointer.add(1) };

        // SAFETY: The short-string bytes are stored inline in `raw` and `length`
        // is constrained to the remaining bytes in the word.
        return Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(pointer, length) });
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `raw` points to a live long string allocation.
    let header = unsafe { &*std::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<Utf16StringDataHeader>(*raw) };
    let length = header.length_in_code_units as usize;
    let storage = std::ptr::from_ref(header)
        .cast::<u8>()
        .wrapping_add(size_of::<Utf16StringDataHeader>());
    let flags = header.flags.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if flags & HAS_UTF16_STORAGE == 0 {
        // SAFETY: Long Latin-1 storage starts immediately after the header and contains `length` bytes.
        let units = unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(storage, length) };
        if flags & CONTAINS_NON_ASCII == 0 {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units)
        } else {
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units)
        }
    } else {
        // SAFETY: Long UTF-16 storage starts immediately after the aligned header and contains
        // `length` u16 code units.
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(storage.cast::<u16>(), length) })
    }
}

// SAFETY: These write the sine and cosine through the two pointers, and have no other effects.
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn ladybird_math_sincos(x: f64, sin_value: *mut f64, cos_value: *mut f64);
    fn ladybird_math_sincosf(x: f32, sin_value: *mut f32, cos_value: *mut f32);
}

macro_rules! define_math_functions {
    (
        unary: [$($unary:ident => $unary_f64:ident, $unary_f32:ident;)*]
        binary: [$($binary:ident => $binary_f64:ident, $binary_f32:ident;)*]
    ) => {
        pub trait Float: Copy {
            $(
                #[doc(hidden)]
                fn $unary(x: Self) -> Self;
            )*
            $(
                #[doc(hidden)]
                fn $binary(x: Self, y: Self) -> Self;
            )*
            #[doc(hidden)]
            fn sincos(x: Self) -> (Self, Self);
        }

        impl Float for f64 {
            $(
                #[inline]
                fn $unary(x: f64) -> f64 {
                    $unary_f64(x)
                }
            )*
            $(
                #[inline]
                fn $binary(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64 {
                    $binary_f64(x, y)
                }
            )*
            #[inline]
            fn sincos(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
                let (mut sin_value, mut cos_value) = (0.0, 0.0);
                // SAFETY: Both pointers are to locals that outlive the call.
                unsafe { ladybird_math_sincos(x, &raw mut sin_value, &raw mut cos_value) };
                (sin_value, cos_value)
            }
        }

        impl Float for f32 {
            $(
                #[inline]
                fn $unary(x: f32) -> f32 {
                    $unary_f32(x)
                }
            )*
            $(
                #[inline]
                fn $binary(x: f32, y: f32) -> f32 {
                    $binary_f32(x, y)
                }
            )*
            #[inline]
            fn sincos(x: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
                let (mut sin_value, mut cos_value) = (0.0, 0.0);
                // SAFETY: Both pointers are to locals that outlive the call.
                unsafe { ladybird_math_sincosf(x, &raw mut sin_value, &raw mut cos_value) };
                (sin_value, cos_value)
            }
        }

        $(
            #[inline]
            pub fn $unary<T: Float>(x: T) -> T {
                T::$unary(x)
            }
        )*
        $(
            #[inline]
            pub fn $binary<T: Float>(x: T, y: T) -> T {
                T::$binary(x, y)
            }
        )*
    };
}

define_math_functions! {
    unary: [
        acos => ladybird_math_acos, ladybird_math_acosf;
        asin => ladybird_math_asin, ladybird_math_asinf;
        atan => ladybird_math_atan, ladybird_math_atanf;
        cbrt => ladybird_math_cbrt, ladybird_math_cbrtf;
        cos => ladybird_math_cos, ladybird_math_cosf;
        cosh => ladybird_math_cosh, ladybird_math_coshf;
        exp => ladybird_math_exp, ladybird_math_expf;
        exp2 => ladybird_math_exp2, ladybird_math_exp2f;
        expm1 => ladybird_math_expm1, ladybird_math_expm1f;
        log => ladybird_math_log, ladybird_math_logf;
        log10 => ladybird_math_log10, ladybird_math_log10f;
        log1p => ladybird_math_log1p, ladybird_math_log1pf;
        log2 => ladybird_math_log2, ladybird_math_log2f;
        sin => ladybird_math_sin, ladybird_math_sinf;
        sinh => ladybird_math_sinh, ladybird_math_sinhf;
        tan => ladybird_math_tan, ladybird_math_tanf;
        tanh => ladybird_math_tanh, ladybird_math_tanhf;
    ]
    binary: [
        atan2 => ladybird_math_atan2, ladybird_math_atan2f;
        hypot => ladybird_math_hypot, ladybird_math_hypotf;
        pow => ladybird_math_pow, ladybird_math_powf;
    ]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hypot_does_not_overflow_for_large_finite_arguments() {
        assert_eq!(
            hypot(
                f64::from_bits(0x765f_ffff_ffff_fffe),
                f64::from_bits(0x74bf_ffff_ffff_ffff)
            ),
            1.5744403932561433e262
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sincos_matches_sin_and_cos() {
        for x in [0.5f64, 1.0, 3.0, 1.0e10] {
            assert_eq!(sincos(x), (sin(x), cos(x)));
        }
        assert_eq!(sincos(0.5f32), (sin(0.5f32), cos(0.5f32)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn inverse_hyperbolic_functions() {
        assert_eq!(acosh(1.0), 0.0);
        assert!(acosh(0.5).is_nan());
        assert_eq!(asinh(-0.0).to_bits(), (-0.0f64).to_bits());
        assert_eq!(atanh(1.0), f64::INFINITY);
        assert!((asinh(1.0) - 0.881_373_587_019_543).abs() < 1e-15);
        assert!((acosh(2.0) - 1.316_957_896_924_816_6).abs() < 1e-15);
        assert!((atanh(0.5) - 0.549_306_144_334_054_9).abs() < 1e-15);
    }
}

//! The inverse hyperbolic functions for f64, which LLVM libc does not have yet. These are built on its log and log1p.

use super::{log, log1p};
use core::f64::consts::LN_2;

fn high_word(x: f64) -> i32 {
    (x.to_bits() >> 32) as i32
}

/// acosh(x) = log(x + sqrt(x * x - 1)), computed as:
///  - log(x) + ln2, if x is large;
///  - log(2x - 1 / (sqrt(x * x - 1) + x)), if x > 2;
///  - log1p(t + sqrt(2t + t * t)) with t = x - 1, otherwise.
pub fn acosh(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let high = high_word(x);
    // x < 1
    if high < 0x3ff0_0000 {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    // x > 2^28
    if high >= 0x41b0_0000 {
        // x is Infinity or NaN
        if high >= 0x7ff0_0000 {
            return x + x;
        }
        return log(x) + LN_2;
    }
    if x == 1.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    // 2^28 > x > 2
    if high > 0x4000_0000 {
        let t = x * x;
        return log(2.0 * x - 1.0 / (x + (t - 1.0).sqrt()));
    }
    // 1 < x <= 2
    let t = x - 1.0;
    log1p(t + (2.0 * t + t * t).sqrt())
}

/// asinh(x) = sign(x) * log(|x| + sqrt(x * x + 1)), computed as:
///  - x, if 1 + x * x = 1;
///  - sign(x) * (log(|x|) + ln2), if |x| is large;
///  - sign(x) * log(2|x| + 1 / (|x| + sqrt(x * x + 1))), if |x| > 2;
///  - sign(x) * log1p(|x| + x^2 / (1 + sqrt(1 + x^2))), otherwise.
pub fn asinh(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let high = high_word(x);
    let magnitude_high = high & 0x7fff_ffff;
    // x is Infinity or NaN
    if magnitude_high >= 0x7ff0_0000 {
        return x + x;
    }
    // |x| < 2^-28
    if magnitude_high < 0x3e30_0000 {
        return x;
    }
    let magnitude = x.abs();
    let w = if magnitude_high > 0x41b0_0000 {
        // |x| > 2^28
        log(magnitude) + LN_2
    } else if magnitude_high > 0x4000_0000 {
        // 2^28 >= |x| > 2
        log(2.0 * magnitude + 1.0 / ((x * x + 1.0).sqrt() + magnitude))
    } else {
        // 2 >= |x| >= 2^-28
        let t = x * x;
        log1p(magnitude + t / (1.0 + (1.0 + t).sqrt()))
    };
    if high > 0 { w } else { -w }
}

/// atanh(x) = 0.5 * log((1 + x) / (1 - x)), computed for |x| as:
///  - 0.5 * log1p(2|x| / (1 - |x|)), if |x| >= 0.5;
///  - 0.5 * log1p(2|x| + 2|x| * |x| / (1 - |x|)), otherwise.
pub fn atanh(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let magnitude = x.abs();
    // |x| > 1, or x is NaN
    if magnitude.is_nan() || magnitude > 1.0 {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    if magnitude == 1.0 {
        return if x > 0.0 { f64::INFINITY } else { f64::NEG_INFINITY };
    }
    // |x| < 2^-28
    if high_word(magnitude) < 0x3e30_0000 {
        return x;
    }
    let t = if magnitude < 0.5 {
        let twice = magnitude + magnitude;
        0.5 * log1p(twice + twice * magnitude / (1.0 - magnitude))
    } else {
        0.5 * log1p((magnitude + magnitude) / (1.0 - magnitude))
    };
    if x >= 0.0 { t } else { -t }
}

//! The process's perf map, `/tmp/perf-PID.map`, which tells `perf` what generated code is where. Every code generator
//! in the process writes it through here.

use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::io::Write;

/// Appends a line for `size` bytes of code at `address` called `name` to the perf map.
///
/// NB: The line goes out in one write to a file opened for appending, so lines that threads write at the same time
///     never interleave, whichever copy of this crate they go through, and no lock is needed.
pub fn write_perf_map_entry(address: usize, size: usize, name: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let line = format!("{address:x} {size:x} {name}\n");
    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .append(true)
        .open(format!("/tmp/perf-{}.map", std::process::id()))?;
    let written = file.write(line.as_bytes())?;
    if written != line.len() {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(
            std::io::ErrorKind::WriteZero,
            "a short write to the perf map",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/*

//! Ranges of address space of a process's own, with memory that comes straight from the system and goes back to it.

use core::ffi::CStr;
use core::num::NonZeroUsize;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// What the system does for a region. Addresses and sizes are multiples of the page size.
#[cfg(all(unix, not(miri)))]
mod system {
    use core::ffi::CStr;
    use core::ptr::NonNull;

    pub fn page_size() -> usize {
        // SAFETY: sysconf() has no preconditions.
        let size = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
        usize::try_from(size).expect("the page size is positive")
    }

    /// Maps `size` bytes that nothing can access, at `address` in place of what is mapped there, or anywhere if it is
    /// null.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Unless `address` is null, the range must be inside a mapping from `reserve()` that nothing reads or writes.
    unsafe fn map_inaccessible(address: *mut libc::c_void, size: usize, name: &CStr) -> *mut libc::c_void {
        let fixed = if address.is_null() { 0 } else { libc::MAP_FIXED };
        // SAFETY: A new mapping at an address of the system's choosing has no preconditions, and the caller keeps the
        //         contract for a mapping in place of another.
        let mapping = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                address,
                size,
                libc::PROT_NONE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANON | libc::MAP_NORESERVE | fixed,
                -1,
                0,
            )
        };
        assert_ne!(mapping, libc::MAP_FAILED, "mapping address space for a column failed");
        // NB: The name tells the memory of columns apart in /proc/<pid>/smaps. A kernel that cannot name mappings
        //     fails the call, which changes nothing.
        #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
        // SAFETY: The range is the mapping made above, and the kernel copies the name.
        unsafe {
            libc::prctl(
                libc::PR_SET_VMA,
                libc::PR_SET_VMA_ANON_NAME as libc::c_ulong,
                mapping.addr() as libc::c_ulong,
                size as libc::c_ulong,
                name.as_ptr(),
            );
        }
        #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
        let _ = name;
        mapping
    }

    /// Reserves `size` bytes of address space, which is no memory yet.
    pub fn reserve(size: usize, name: &CStr) -> NonNull<u8> {
        // SAFETY: The address is null.
        let mapping = unsafe { map_inaccessible(core::ptr::null_mut(), size, name) };
        NonNull::new(mapping.cast()).expect("no mapping is at address zero")
    }

    /// Makes a range memory that can be read and written. The memory holds zeros.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be inside a mapping from `reserve()`, and not be memory already.
    pub unsafe fn commit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        let result = unsafe { libc::mprotect(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "the system has no memory for a column");
    }

    /// Gives the memory of a range back to the system. The range stays reserved.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be inside a mapping from `reserve()`, and nothing may read or write it until `commit()`.
    pub unsafe fn decommit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize, name: &CStr) {
        // NB: A new mapping in place of the pages drops them at once on every Unix. Advice to the kernel either leaves
        //     the pages for it to take later, or is not the same call everywhere.
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        unsafe { map_inaccessible(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, name) };
    }

    /// Gives the address space of a mapping back.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `base` and `size` must be those of a mapping from `reserve()` that nothing uses anymore.
    pub unsafe fn release(base: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        let result = unsafe { libc::munmap(base.as_ptr().cast(), size) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "unmapping the address space of a column failed");
    }
}

/// What the system does for a region. Addresses and sizes are multiples of the page size.
#[cfg(all(windows, not(miri)))]
mod system {
    use core::ffi::{CStr, c_void};
    use core::ptr::NonNull;

    const MEM_COMMIT: u32 = 0x1000;
    const MEM_RESERVE: u32 = 0x2000;
    const MEM_DECOMMIT: u32 = 0x4000;
    const MEM_RELEASE: u32 = 0x8000;
    const PAGE_NOACCESS: u32 = 0x01;
    const PAGE_READWRITE: u32 = 0x04;

    #[link(name = "kernel32")]
    unsafe extern "system" {
        fn VirtualAlloc(address: *mut c_void, size: usize, allocation_type: u32, protect: u32) -> *mut c_void;
        fn VirtualFree(address: *mut c_void, size: usize, free_type: u32) -> i32;
    }

    pub fn page_size() -> usize {
        4096
    }

    /// Reserves `size` bytes of address space, which is no memory yet.
    pub fn reserve(size: usize, _name: &CStr) -> NonNull<u8> {
        // SAFETY: A reservation at an address of the system's choosing has no preconditions.
        let base = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(core::ptr::null_mut(), size, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS) };
        NonNull::new(base.cast()).expect("reserving address space for a column failed")
    }

    /// Makes a range memory that can be read and written. The memory holds zeros.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be inside a reservation from `reserve()`, and not be memory already.
    pub unsafe fn commit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        let result = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) };
        assert!(!result.is_null(), "the system has no memory for a column");
    }

    /// Gives the memory of a range back to the system. The range stays reserved.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be inside a reservation from `reserve()`, and nothing may read or write it until `commit()`.
    pub unsafe fn decommit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize, _name: &CStr) {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        let result = unsafe { VirtualFree(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, MEM_DECOMMIT) };
        assert_ne!(result, 0, "giving the memory of a column back failed");
    }

    /// Gives the address space of a reservation back.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `base` must come from `reserve()`, and nothing may use the reservation anymore.
    pub unsafe fn release(base: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
        let result = unsafe { VirtualFree(base.as_ptr().cast(), 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
        assert_ne!(result, 0, "releasing the address space of a column failed");
    }
}

/// Miri has no way to change what a page allows, so one allocation that holds zeros stands in for a region there.
#[cfg(miri)]
mod system {
    use core::ffi::CStr;
    use core::ptr::NonNull;
    use std::alloc::{Layout, alloc_zeroed, dealloc, handle_alloc_error};

    pub fn page_size() -> usize {
        4096
    }

    fn layout(size: usize) -> Layout {
        Layout::from_size_align(size, page_size()).expect("the size of a region is a multiple of its alignment")
    }

    pub fn reserve(size: usize, _name: &CStr) -> NonNull<u8> {
        // SAFETY: A region is at least a page, so the layout has a size.
        let base = unsafe { alloc_zeroed(layout(size)) };
        NonNull::new(base).unwrap_or_else(|| handle_alloc_error(layout(size)))
    }

    pub unsafe fn commit(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {}

    pub unsafe fn decommit(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize, _name: &CStr) {}

    pub unsafe fn release(base: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes what `reserve()` allocated with this layout.
        unsafe { dealloc(base.as_ptr(), layout(size)) };
    }
}

/// A range of address space of which the first `committed` bytes are memory that can be read and written. The rest is
/// reserved: nothing else gets mapped there, and it takes no memory. A region takes its address space when it first
/// gets memory, so one that is never used costs the system nothing.
pub(crate) struct Region {
    /// Where the address space of the region is, once it has some.
    base: Option<NonNull<u8>>,
    reserved: usize,
    committed: usize,
    name: &'static CStr,
}

/// What a region without address space says it starts at: an address that is not null, with nothing there.
const NO_BASE: NonNull<u8> = NonNull::without_provenance(NonZeroUsize::new(4096).unwrap());

impl Region {
    /// Where the region starts, which is a multiple of 4096. A region with no memory may have nothing there.
    pub(crate) fn base(&self) -> NonNull<u8> {
        self.base.unwrap_or(NO_BASE)
    }

    /// How many bytes of address space the region has.
    pub(crate) fn reserved(&self) -> usize {
        self.reserved
    }

    /// Whether the region has taken its address space.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn has_address_space(&self) -> bool {
        self.base.is_some()
    }

    /// How many bytes of the region are memory. They are its first ones.
    pub(crate) fn committed(&self) -> usize {
        self.committed
    }

    /// A region of at least `size` bytes, none of them memory yet.
    pub(crate) fn new(size: usize, name: &'static CStr) -> Self {
        let reserved = size
            .max(1)
            .checked_next_multiple_of(system::page_size())
            .expect("a region fits in the address space");
        Self {
            base: None,
            reserved,
            committed: 0,
            name,
        }
    }

    /// Makes at least the first `size` bytes memory. What was memory before keeps its contents.
    pub(crate) fn commit(&mut self, size: usize) {
        assert!(size <= self.reserved, "a region does not grow past what it reserved");
        let committed = size.next_multiple_of(system::page_size());
        if committed <= self.committed {
            return;
        }
        let base = *self
            .base
            .get_or_insert_with(|| system::reserve(self.reserved, self.name));
        // SAFETY: Both sizes are multiples of the page size and at most `reserved`, so the range is the part of the
        //         reservation from where its memory ends.
        unsafe { system::commit(base.add(self.committed), committed - self.committed) };
        self.committed = committed;
    }

    /// Gives the memory past the first `size` bytes back to the system.
    pub(crate) fn decommit_past(&mut self, size: usize) {
        if size >= self.committed {
            return;
        }
        let kept = size.next_multiple_of(system::page_size());
        if kept >= self.committed {
            return;
        }
        let base = self.base.expect("a region with memory has address space");
        // SAFETY: The range is the end of the memory of the reservation, and `committed` shrinks to leave it out, so
        //         nothing reads or writes it until commit() makes it memory again.
        unsafe { system::decommit(base.add(kept), self.committed - kept, self.name) };
        self.committed = kept;
    }
}

impl Drop for Region {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let Some(base) = self.base else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The reservation is this region's, which nothing can use once it is dropped.
        unsafe { system::release(base, self.reserved) };
    }
}

// SAFETY: A region owns its mapping, and no thread has a special tie to a mapping.
unsafe impl Send for Region {}

/// The size of a page of memory.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn page_size() -> usize {
    system::page_size()
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Lists of rows of many types in one block of memory that comes straight from the system.
//!
//! A `RowBlock` holds lists, one after the other, in a `Column` of words. A list is rows of one plain type that are
//! next to each other. Adding a list gives a `RowList`, which is small and plain itself, so that rows can hold the
//! lists of other rows. The block gives the rows of a list back as a slice, with no decoding. A data structure of
//! many lists is one piece of memory this way: it is written from start to end, it is read where it is, and all of
//! it goes back to the system at one time.

use core::ffi::CStr;
use core::fmt;
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::mem::MaybeUninit;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};

use crate::column::Column;

/// A block has no room for a list, or cannot hold lists at all (see `RowBlock::can_hold_lists()`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RowBlockFull;

/// A list of rows of type `T` in a `RowBlock`. The block that the list was added to gives its rows.
pub struct RowList<T> {
    /// The index of the word of the block at which the first row starts.
    start: u32,
    len: u32,
    /// The number of the block that holds the rows, or 0 for a list with no rows.
    block: u32,
    // NB: Invariant in `T`: copies of a list write and read the same rows, so a list must not change its type.
    rows: PhantomData<fn(T) -> T>,
}

impl<T> RowList<T> {
    /// A list with no rows. All blocks have it.
    pub const fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            start: 0,
            len: 0,
            block: 0,
            rows: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn len(self) -> usize {
        self.len as usize
    }

    pub fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }
}

impl<T> Clone for RowList<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<T> Copy for RowList<T> {}

impl<T> Default for RowList<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::empty()
    }
}

// NB: Lists are equal if they are the same rows of the same block.
impl<T> PartialEq for RowList<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        (self.start, self.len, self.block) == (other.start, other.len, other.block)
    }
}

impl<T> Eq for RowList<T> {}

impl<T> fmt::Debug for RowList<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "RowList({} rows at word {})", self.len, self.start)
    }
}

/// The number that the next block gets. Numbers start at 1 and are never used again.
static NEXT_BLOCK: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(1);

/// A number that no block has had, or 0 when all the numbers are used.
fn new_block_number() -> u32 {
    NEXT_BLOCK
        .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |number| number.checked_add(1))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Lists of rows of many types, one after the other, in memory that stays where it is.
///
/// A block that is cleared keeps its memory for the lists that are added next; `trim()` gives memory back. The lists
/// of a block are only good for that block, and only until it is cleared: the block panics when it is asked for the
/// rows of another list.
pub struct RowBlock {
    words: Column<MaybeUninit<u64>>,
    /// Which block this is since it was made or cleared, or 0 for a block that cannot hold lists. The lists of the
    /// block have the number, and no other list has it.
    number: u32,
}

impl RowBlock {
    /// A block that holds up to `limit` bytes of rows. It takes no memory and no address space before it has a list.
    /// `name` shows up for its memory in /proc/<pid>/smaps on Linux.
    pub fn new(limit: usize, name: &'static CStr) -> Self {
        Self {
            words: Column::new((limit / size_of::<u64>()).min(u32::MAX as usize), name),
            number: new_block_number(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether lists can be added. A process can make or clear a block about four thousand million times. After
    /// that, blocks hold no lists.
    pub fn can_hold_lists(&self) -> bool {
        self.number != 0
    }

    /// How many bytes of memory the block has taken from the system.
    pub fn memory(&self) -> usize {
        self.words.memory()
    }

    /// How many bytes the lists of the block fill.
    pub fn bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.words.len() * size_of::<u64>()
    }

    /// Drops all lists. The block keeps its memory.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.words.clear();
        // NB: This makes the lists that were added so far lists of no block.
        self.number = new_block_number();
    }

    /// Gives memory back to the system: all that is past the lists and past the room for `keep` bytes.
    pub fn trim(&mut self, keep: usize) {
        self.words.trim(keep / size_of::<u64>());
    }

    /// Adds `rows` as a list, if the block has room for them.
    pub fn try_add<T: Copy + Send + Sync + 'static>(&mut self, rows: &[T]) -> Result<RowList<T>, RowBlockFull> {
        const {
            // NB: The rows of a list start at a word.
            assert!(size_of::<T>() != 0 && align_of::<T>() <= align_of::<u64>());
        }
        if rows.is_empty() {
            return Ok(RowList::empty());
        }
        if self.number == 0 {
            return Err(RowBlockFull);
        }
        let len = u32::try_from(rows.len()).map_err(|_| RowBlockFull)?;
        let start = self.words.len();
        let end = start + size_of_val(rows).div_ceil(size_of::<u64>());
        self.words
            .try_resize(end, MaybeUninit::uninit())
            .map_err(|_| RowBlockFull)?;
        let words = &mut self.words[start..end];
        // SAFETY: `words` has room for the bytes of `rows`, and `rows` is not part of the block, which is borrowed
        //         mutably. The words may hold any bytes, also the padding of the rows.
        unsafe {
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                rows.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(),
                words.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>(),
                size_of_val(rows),
            );
        }
        Ok(RowList {
            // NB: new() keeps the count of words in 32 bits.
            start: start as u32,
            len,
            block: self.number,
            rows: PhantomData,
        })
    }

    /// The words that hold the rows of `list`. Panics if the list is not a list of this block.
    fn words_of<T>(&self, list: RowList<T>) -> core::ops::Range<usize> {
        assert!(list.block == self.number, "the list is a list of this block");
        let start = list.start as usize;
        start..start + (list.len as usize * size_of::<T>()).div_ceil(size_of::<u64>())
    }

    /// The rows of `list`. Panics if the list is not a list of this block.
    pub fn rows<T: Copy + Send + Sync + 'static>(&self, list: RowList<T>) -> &[T] {
        if list.is_empty() {
            return &[];
        }
        let words = &self.words[self.words_of(list)];
        // SAFETY: A list with rows has the number of the block only if try_add::<T>() of this block returned it, or a
        //         copy of it, since the block was last cleared: the fields of a list are private, and no two blocks
        //         have the same number between two clears. So `words` starts with `len` rows of type `T` that
        //         try_add() copied there, at an address that is aligned for `T`, and only a mutable borrow of the
        //         block changes them.
        unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(words.as_ptr().cast::<T>(), list.len as usize) }
    }

    /// The rows of `list`, to change them. Panics if the list is not a list of this block.
    pub fn rows_mut<T: Copy + Send + Sync + 'static>(&mut self, list: RowList<T>) -> &mut [T] {
        if list.is_empty() {
            return &mut [];
        }
        let range = self.words_of(list);
        let words = &mut self.words[range];
        // SAFETY: As in rows(), and the mutable borrow of the block is the only access to the rows. Rows are plain
        //         values, so each value that is written there is a row of type `T` again.
        unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(words.as_mut_ptr().cast::<T>(), list.len as usize) }
    }
}

impl fmt::Debug for RowBlock {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "RowBlock({} bytes)", self.bytes())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
    struct Row {
        flag: bool,
        value: Option<u32>,
        inner: RowList<u16>,
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_of_many_types_share_a_block() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        assert_eq!(block.memory(), 0);
        let bytes = block.try_add(&[1u8, 2, 3]).unwrap();
        let halves = block.try_add(&[500u16, 600]).unwrap();
        let rows = block
            .try_add(&[
                Row {
                    flag: true,
                    value: None,
                    inner: halves,
                },
                Row {
                    flag: false,
                    value: Some(9),
                    inner: RowList::empty(),
                },
            ])
            .unwrap();
        let none = block.try_add::<u64>(&[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(block.rows(bytes), [1, 2, 3]);
        assert_eq!(block.rows(none), []);
        assert_eq!(block.rows(rows).len(), 2);
        let first = block.rows(rows)[0];
        assert!(first.flag);
        assert_eq!(block.rows(first.inner), [500, 600]);
        block.rows_mut(rows)[1].value = Some(10);
        block.rows_mut(halves)[0] = 501;
        assert_eq!(block.rows(rows)[1].value, Some(10));
        assert_eq!(block.rows(halves), [501, 600]);
        assert_eq!(block.rows(bytes), [1, 2, 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rows_stay_in_place_while_a_block_grows() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(1 << 24, c"test");
        let first = block.try_add(&[7u64]).unwrap();
        let address = block.rows(first).as_ptr();
        let values: Vec<u32> = (0..100_000).collect();
        let lists: Vec<_> = (0..8).map(|_| block.try_add(&values).unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(block.rows(first).as_ptr(), address);
        assert!(lists.iter().all(|list| block.rows(*list) == values));
        assert!(block.bytes() >= 8 * 400_000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_full_block_takes_no_list() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(64, c"test");
        let list = block.try_add(&[1u64; 8]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(block.try_add(&[1u8]), Err(RowBlockFull));
        assert_eq!(block.try_add::<u8>(&[]), Ok(RowList::empty()));
        assert_eq!(block.rows(list), [1; 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "the list is a list of this block")]
    fn a_block_gives_no_rows_for_a_list_of_another_block() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(1 << 12, c"test");
        let mut other = RowBlock::new(1 << 12, c"test");
        let list = block.try_add(&[true, false]).unwrap();
        other.try_add(&[7u8, 7]).unwrap();
        let _ = other.rows(list);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "the list is a list of this block")]
    fn a_cleared_block_gives_no_rows_for_its_old_lists() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(1 << 12, c"test");
        let list = block.try_add(&[true, false]).unwrap();
        block.clear();
        block.try_add(&[7u8, 7]).unwrap();
        let _ = block.rows(list);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cleared_block_keeps_its_memory_until_it_is_trimmed() {
        let mut block = RowBlock::new(1 << 24, c"test");
        block.try_add(&[0u8; 300_000]).unwrap();
        let memory = block.memory();
        assert!(memory >= 300_000);
        block.clear();
        assert_eq!(block.bytes(), 0);
        assert_eq!(block.memory(), memory);
        block.trim(0);
        assert_eq!(block.memory(), 0);
        let list = block.try_add(&[5u32]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(block.rows(list), [5]);
    }
}

#[must_use = "if unused, the scope guard is dropped immediately"]
pub struct ScopeGuard<F: FnMut()> {
    callback: F,
}

impl<F: FnMut()> ScopeGuard<F> {
    pub fn new(callback: F) -> Self {
        Self { callback }
    }
}

impl<F: FnMut()> Drop for ScopeGuard<F> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        (self.callback)();
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]

        let mut call_count = 0;
        {
            let _guard = ScopeGuard::new(|| call_count += 1);
        }
        assert_eq!(call_count, 1);
    }
}

//! Slices over arrays that C++ lends. An empty AK container lends a null pointer, which
//! `std::slice::from_raw_parts` forbids even for an empty slice.

/// The `length` values at `data`, where `data` may be null if `length` is zero.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Unless `length` is zero, `data` must meet the requirements of `std::slice::from_raw_parts` for
/// the lifetime `'a`.
#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn slice_from_raw_parts<'a, T>(data: *const T, length: usize) -> &'a [T] {
    // NB: Testing the pointer rather than the length lets the compiler drop the test where the
    //     pointer comes from a reference, as on the hot interpreter paths.
    if data.is_null() {
        assert!(length == 0, "a non-empty slice from a null pointer");
        return &[];
    }
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(data, length) }
}

/// The `length` values at `data`, mutably, where `data` may be null if `length` is zero.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Unless `length` is zero, `data` must meet the requirements of `std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut`
/// for the lifetime `'a`.
#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn slice_from_raw_parts_mut<'a, T>(data: *mut T, length: usize) -> &'a mut [T] {
    // NB: Testing the pointer rather than the length lets the compiler drop the test where the
    //     pointer comes from a reference, as on the hot interpreter paths.
    if data.is_null() {
        assert!(length == 0, "a non-empty slice from a null pointer");
        return &mut [];
    }
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(data, length) }
}

/// The values an AK `ReadonlySpan<T>` lends for `'a`, laid out as one, so that C++ passes its span by value.
///
/// Only C++ makes one, under the contract of [`slice_from_raw_parts`] for `'a`, and Rust from a borrowed slice, so
/// reading the values is safe.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Span<'a, T> {
    data: *const T,
    size: usize,
    lent: std::marker::PhantomData<&'a [T]>,
}

impl<T> Clone for Span<'_, T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<T> Copy for Span<'_, T> {}

impl<T> Default for Span<'_, T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(&[])
    }
}

impl<'a, T> Span<'a, T> {
    pub fn new(values: &'a [T]) -> Self {
        Self {
            data: values.as_ptr(),
            size: values.len(),
            lent: std::marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_slice(self) -> &'a [T] {
        // SAFETY: The span lends `size` values at `data` for 'a, as the type says.
        unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts(self.data, self.size) }
    }
}

/// The values an AK `Span<T>` lends for `'a`, mutably, laid out as one, so that C++ passes its span by value.
///
/// Only C++ makes one, under the contract of [`slice_from_raw_parts_mut`] for `'a`, and Rust from a borrowed slice,
/// so reaching the values is safe.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct SpanMut<'a, T> {
    data: *mut T,
    size: usize,
    lent: std::marker::PhantomData<&'a mut [T]>,
}

impl<'a, T> SpanMut<'a, T> {
    pub fn new(values: &'a mut [T]) -> Self {
        Self {
            data: values.as_mut_ptr(),
            size: values.len(),
            lent: std::marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn into_slice(self) -> &'a mut [T] {
        // SAFETY: The span lends `size` values at `data` for 'a, mutably, as the type says.
        unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts_mut(self.data, self.size) }
    }
}

/*
