//! The bounds of the native stack of the calling thread.

/// The lowest address of the stack of this thread, or `None` if that cannot be told.
pub fn lowest_address_of_this_thread() -> Option<usize> {
    // NB: Asking for the stack of the main thread reads /proc/self/maps on Linux.
    thread_local! {
        static LOWEST_ADDRESS: Option<usize> = thread_stack_lowest_address();
    }
    LOWEST_ADDRESS.with(|lowest_address| *lowest_address)
}

/// The address that the stack can only go `bytes` below where it is now.
pub fn limit_for_budget(bytes: usize) -> usize {
    let marker = 0u8;
    (&raw const marker as usize).saturating_sub(bytes)
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    // SAFETY: The attributes live for the calls, and are destroyed once initialized.
    unsafe {
        let mut attributes: libc::pthread_attr_t = std::mem::zeroed();
        if libc::pthread_getattr_np(libc::pthread_self(), &raw mut attributes) != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut address = std::ptr::null_mut();
        let mut size = 0;
        let result = libc::pthread_attr_getstack(&raw const attributes, &raw mut address, &raw mut size);
        libc::pthread_attr_destroy(&raw mut attributes);
        (result == 0).then_some(address as usize)
    }
}

#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)] // The other platforms' versions can fail.
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    // SAFETY: These only read the stack of the calling thread.
    unsafe {
        let thread = libc::pthread_self();
        let top = libc::pthread_get_stackaddr_np(thread) as usize;
        Some(top - libc::pthread_get_stacksize_np(thread))
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)] // The other platforms' versions can fail.
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    unsafe extern "system" {
        fn GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(low_limit: *mut usize, high_limit: *mut usize);
        fn SetThreadStackGuarantee(stack_size_in_bytes: *mut u32) -> i32;
    }
    let (mut low_limit, mut high_limit) = (0, 0);
    let mut stack_guarantee = 0;
    // SAFETY: These only read the limits of the stack of the calling thread. A guarantee of 0 asks for the current one
    //         without changing it.
    unsafe {
        GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(&raw mut low_limit, &raw mut high_limit);
        SetThreadStackGuarantee(&raw mut stack_guarantee);
    }
    // The stack overflows before reaching its low limit by the size reserved for handling that overflow.
    Some(low_limit + stack_guarantee as usize)
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos", windows)))]
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    None
}

FILE: AK/Rust/src/string_conversions.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

pub trait UnsignedInteger: Copy {
    const ZERO: Self;

    fn checked_mul_add(self, radix: u32, digit: u32) -> Option<Self>;
}

macro_rules! impl_unsigned_integer {
    ($($type:ty),*) => {
        $(
            impl UnsignedInteger for $type {
                const ZERO: Self = 0;

                fn checked_mul_add(self, radix: u32, digit: u32) -> Option<Self> {
                    self.checked_mul(<$type>::try_from(radix).ok()?)?
                        .checked_add(<$type>::try_from(digit).ok()?)
                }
            }
        )*
    };
}

impl_unsigned_integer!(u8, u16, u32, u64, usize);

/// Parses `input` as an unsigned integer made only of radix-`radix` digits, with no sign, whitespace or prefix.
/// Returns `None` if `input` is empty, holds anything else, or does not fit in `T`.
pub fn parse_ascii_digits<T: UnsignedInteger>(input: &[u8], radix: u32) -> Option<T> {
    if input.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    input.iter().try_fold(T::ZERO, |value, &byte| {
        value.checked_mul_add(radix, char::from(byte).to_digit(radix)?)
    })
}

FILE: AK/Rust/src/utf16_view.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! A borrowed string of code units, as `AK::Utf16View` is in C++.

/// A borrowed string of code units, in either of the two forms `AK::Utf16String` stores them in: one byte per code
/// unit, all of them below U+0100, or UTF-16.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum Utf16View<'a> {
    Latin1(&'a [u8]),
    Utf16(&'a [u16]),
}

impl PartialEq for Utf16View<'_> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        match (self, other) {
            (Self::Latin1(a), Self::Latin1(b)) => a == b,
            (Self::Utf16(a), Self::Utf16(b)) => a == b,
            (Self::Latin1(narrow), Self::Utf16(wide)) | (Self::Utf16(wide), Self::Latin1(narrow)) => {
                narrow.len() == wide.len() && narrow.iter().zip(wide.iter()).all(|(&a, &b)| u16::from(a) == b)
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq<str> for Utf16View<'_> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &str) -> bool {
        self.code_units().eq(other.encode_utf16())
    }
}

impl PartialEq<&str> for Utf16View<'_> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &&str) -> bool {
        *self == **other
    }
}

impl<'a> Utf16View<'a> {
    pub fn code_units(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u16> + 'a {
        let (narrow, wide): (&[u8], &[u16]) = match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => (code_units, &[]),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => (&[], code_units),
        };
        narrow.iter().copied().map(u16::from).chain(wide.iter().copied())
    }

    /// The code units as ASCII bytes, if that is all they are.
    pub fn as_ascii(self) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) if code_units.is_ascii() => Some(code_units),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn eq_ignore_ascii_case(self, other: &str) -> bool {
        self.len() == other.len() && self.starts_with_ignore_ascii_case(other)
    }

    /// Whether this starts with `prefix`, which must be ASCII, in any mix of ASCII upper and lower case.
    pub fn starts_with_ignore_ascii_case(self, prefix: &str) -> bool {
        debug_assert!(prefix.is_ascii());
        self.len() >= prefix.len()
            && self.code_units().zip(prefix.bytes()).all(|(code_unit, byte)| {
                u8::try_from(code_unit).is_ok_and(|code_unit| code_unit.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&byte))
            })
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.len(),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.len(),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    pub fn to_utf16(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
        let mut code_units = Vec::with_capacity(self.len());
        self.append_to(&mut code_units);
        code_units
    }

    pub fn append_to(&self, output: &mut Vec<u16>) {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => output.extend(code_units.iter().copied().map(u16::from)),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => output.extend_from_slice(code_units),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn code_units(input: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        input.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn views_compare_by_code_unit_whatever_form_they_are_in() {
        let wide = code_units("caf\u{e9}");
        let narrow = Utf16View::Latin1(b"caf\xe9");
        let wide = Utf16View::Utf16(&wide);
        assert_eq!(narrow, wide);
        assert_eq!(narrow, "caf\u{e9}");
        assert_ne!(narrow, "cafe");
        assert_ne!(wide, "caf");
        assert_eq!(wide.to_utf16(), code_units("caf\u{e9}"));
        assert_eq!(narrow.len(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn views_compare_with_ascii_in_any_case() {
        assert!(Utf16View::Latin1(b"Text/HTML").eq_ignore_ascii_case("text/html"));
        assert!(!Utf16View::Latin1(b"Text/HTML5").eq_ignore_ascii_case("text/html"));
        assert!(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("-//W3C//dtd html")).starts_with_ignore_ascii_case("-//w3c//DTD"));
        assert!(!Utf16View::Latin1(b"-//W3").starts_with_ignore_ascii_case("-//w3c//DTD"));
        assert!(!Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("\u{212a}")).eq_ignore_ascii_case("k"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_one_byte_ascii_views_are_ascii_bytes() {
        assert_eq!(Utf16View::Latin1(b"div").as_ascii(), Some(b"div" as &[u8]));
        assert_eq!(Utf16View::Latin1(b"d\xefv").as_ascii(), None);
        assert_eq!(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("div")).as_ascii(), None);
    }
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The WaiterLists of a process, which Atomics.wait, Atomics.notify and their WebAssembly counterparts use: one list of
//! all that wait, in the order the agents began to wait, under one lock, with a condition variable per agent. The
//! WaiterList of an address is what has that address in this list.
//!
//! A word has one address in a process, as every agent shares one mapping of it, and it never has waiters in another
//! process, as shared memory stays in its agent cluster, and an agent cluster stays in its process. Having a condition
//! variable per agent means that a notify wakes the agents it took off the list, and that an interrupt wakes its agent,
//! and nobody else.
//!
//! Blocking and asynchronous waits share the list, so notifications select both kinds in their registration order.
//! Asynchronous completions run after releasing the lock, and can register or notify another wait.

use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use core::time::Duration;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError};
use std::time::Instant;

/// Core::AtomicWaitResult.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AtomicWaitResult {
    Woken,
    NotEqual,
    TimedOut,
    Interrupted,
}

/// The word of a shared typed array element that Atomics.wait waits on, which is 4 or 8 bytes wide.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum WaitWord<'a> {
    Word32(&'a AtomicU32),
    Word64(&'a AtomicU64),
}

impl WaitWord<'_> {
    /// The address of the word, which is what the WaiterList of a location is found by: a 4-byte and an 8-byte view of
    /// the same location share it.
    fn address(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            WaitWord::Word32(word) => word.as_ptr().addr(),
            WaitWord::Word64(word) => word.as_ptr().addr(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the word equals `expected`, by a sequentially-consistent read, which matches the memory model's read for
    /// the wait comparison.
    fn equals(self, expected: u64) -> bool {
        match self {
            WaitWord::Word32(word) => word.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == expected as u32,
            WaitWord::Word64(word) => word.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == expected,
        }
    }
}

/// The node of one agent in the WaiterLists. An agent has one thread, so it is in one list at most.
pub struct AgentWaiter {
    condition: Condvar,
    is_interrupted: AtomicBool,
    /// Set by the notify that took the agent off its list.
    was_notified: AtomicBool,
}

impl AgentWaiter {
    pub fn new() -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            condition: Condvar::new(),
            is_interrupted: AtomicBool::new(false),
            was_notified: AtomicBool::new(false),
        })
    }

    /// Whether interrupt() was called.
    pub fn is_interrupted(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_interrupted.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }

    /// Whether the agent is on the list of a word, waiting for a notify. Any thread may call this.
    pub fn is_waiting(self: &Arc<Self>) -> bool {
        lists()
            .iter()
            .any(|waiting| matches!(&waiting.waiter, Waiter::Blocking(waiter) if Arc::ptr_eq(waiter, self)))
    }

    /// Ends the wait of this agent with AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted, and every later one at once. Any thread may call
    /// this. The agent loses its place in its list, which does not matter, as it never comes back.
    pub fn interrupt(&self) {
        self.is_interrupted.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        // NB: A waiter looks at the flag and goes to sleep with the lock held, so this cannot go past it.
        let _lists = lists();
        self.condition.notify_one();
    }
}

struct Waiting {
    address: usize,
    waiter: Waiter,
}

enum Waiter {
    Blocking(Arc<AgentWaiter>),
    Async(Arc<AsyncWaiter>),
}

pub struct AsyncWaiter {
    completion: Box<dyn Fn(AtomicWaitResult) + Send + Sync>,
}

impl AsyncWaiter {
    pub fn new(completion: impl Fn(AtomicWaitResult) + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Arc<Self> {
        Arc::new(Self {
            completion: Box::new(completion),
        })
    }
}

type Lists = VecDeque<Waiting>;

fn lists() -> MutexGuard<'static, Lists> {
    static LISTS: Mutex<Lists> = Mutex::new(VecDeque::new());
    LISTS.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

fn remove(lists: &mut Lists, waiter: &Arc<AgentWaiter>) {
    lists.retain(|waiting| !matches!(&waiting.waiter, Waiter::Blocking(other) if Arc::ptr_eq(other, waiter)));
}

/// Puts `waiter` on the list of the word unless it holds something else than `expected`, and sleeps until a notify takes
/// it off, its interrupt comes, or `timeout` passes.
pub fn atomic_wait(
    word: WaitWord<'_>,
    expected: u64,
    timeout: Option<Duration>,
    waiter: &Arc<AgentWaiter>,
) -> AtomicWaitResult {
    let address = word.address();
    // NB: A deadline too far away to express is no deadline.
    let deadline = timeout.and_then(|timeout| Instant::now().checked_add(timeout));

    // NB: The word is compared with the lock held, so a notify that follows a store to it finds this waiter on the list
    //     if the comparison did not see the store.
    let mut lists = lists();
    if waiter.is_interrupted() {
        return AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted;
    }
    if !word.equals(expected) {
        return AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual;
    }
    waiter.was_notified.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
    lists.push_back(Waiting {
        address,
        waiter: Waiter::Blocking(Arc::clone(waiter)),
    });

    // NB: The condition variable can wake for no reason, so only what the wake left behind counts. A notify that came
    //     along with the timeout already counted this waiter, so it wins.
    loop {
        if waiter.is_interrupted() {
            remove(&mut lists, waiter);
            return AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted;
        }
        if waiter.was_notified.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return AtomicWaitResult::Woken;
        }
        let Some(deadline) = deadline else {
            lists = waiter.condition.wait(lists).unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
            continue;
        };
        let remaining = deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
        if remaining.is_zero() {
            remove(&mut lists, waiter);
            return AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut;
        }
        lists = waiter
            .condition
            .wait_timeout(lists, remaining)
            .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
            .0;
    }
}

/// Takes the first `max_count` agents off the list of the word, wakes them, and returns how many there were.
pub fn atomic_notify(word: &AtomicU32, max_count: usize) -> usize {
    let address = word.as_ptr().addr();
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut asynchronous = Vec::new();
    {
        let mut lists = lists();
        lists.retain(|waiting| {
            if waiting.address != address {
                return true;
            }
            if let Waiter::Blocking(waiter) = &waiting.waiter
                && waiter.is_interrupted()
            {
                return false;
            }
            if count == max_count {
                return true;
            }
            count += 1;
            match &waiting.waiter {
                Waiter::Blocking(waiter) => {
                    waiter.was_notified.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    waiter.condition.notify_one();
                }
                Waiter::Async(waiter) => asynchronous.push(Arc::clone(waiter)),
            }
            false
        });
    }
    for waiter in asynchronous {
        (waiter.completion)(AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
    }
    count
}

/// Compares and registers under the same lock as synchronous waits and notifications.
/// None means the waiter was registered; Some is an immediate result.
pub fn atomic_wait_async(
    word: WaitWord<'_>,
    expected: u64,
    immediate_timeout: bool,
    waiter: &Arc<AsyncWaiter>,
) -> Option<AtomicWaitResult> {
    let mut lists = lists();
    if !word.equals(expected) {
        return Some(AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual);
    }
    if immediate_timeout {
        return Some(AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut);
    }
    lists.push_back(Waiting {
        address: word.address(),
        waiter: Waiter::Async(Arc::clone(waiter)),
    });
    None
}

/// Removes a registration if a notification has not already removed it.
pub fn cancel_async_waiter(waiter: &Arc<AsyncWaiter>) -> bool {
    let mut lists = lists();
    let old_length = lists.len();
    lists.retain(|waiting| !matches!(&waiting.waiter, Waiter::Async(other) if Arc::ptr_eq(other, waiter)));
    lists.len() != old_length
}

pub fn timeout_async_waiter(waiter: &Arc<AsyncWaiter>) {
    if cancel_async_waiter(waiter) {
        (waiter.completion)(AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize;

    /// Long enough for a thread that was just started to get to sleep.
    const TIME_TO_SLEEP: Duration = Duration::from_millis(30);

    fn wait(word: &AtomicU32, expected: u64, timeout: Option<Duration>, waiter: &Arc<AgentWaiter>) -> AtomicWaitResult {
        atomic_wait(WaitWord::Word32(word), expected, timeout, waiter)
    }

    fn waiters_of(word: &AtomicU32) -> usize {
        let address = word.as_ptr().addr();
        lists().iter().filter(|waiting| waiting.address == address).count()
    }

    fn wait_for_waiters(word: &AtomicU32, count: usize) {
        while waiters_of(word) != count {
            std::thread::yield_now();
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn asynchronous_waits_compare_before_testing_zero_timeout() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(1);
        let waiter = AsyncWaiter::new(|_| panic!("an immediate result must not dispatch"));
        assert_eq!(
            atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 0, true, &waiter),
            Some(AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 1, true, &waiter),
            Some(AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut)
        );
        assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, usize::MAX), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn blocking_and_asynchronous_waits_share_fifo_order() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let results = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let first_results = Arc::clone(&results);
        let first = AsyncWaiter::new(move |result| first_results.lock().unwrap().push((1, result)));
        assert_eq!(atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 0, false, &first), None);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let blocking = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new()));
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 2);
            let last_results = Arc::clone(&results);
            let last = AsyncWaiter::new(move |result| last_results.lock().unwrap().push((3, result)));
            assert_eq!(atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 0, false, &last), None);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
            assert_eq!(*results.lock().unwrap(), vec![(1, AtomicWaitResult::Woken)]);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
            assert_eq!(blocking.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
            assert_eq!(results.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
            timeout_async_waiter(&last);
            assert_eq!(
                *results.lock().unwrap(),
                vec![(1, AtomicWaitResult::Woken), (3, AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut)]
            );
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, usize::MAX), 0);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn asynchronous_notification_and_timeout_complete_once() {
        for _ in 0..50 {
            let word = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));
            let completions = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
            let results = Arc::clone(&completions);
            let waiter = AsyncWaiter::new(move |result| results.lock().unwrap().push(result));
            assert_eq!(atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 0, false, &waiter), None);
            let barrier = Arc::new(std::sync::Barrier::new(2));
            let notifier_barrier = Arc::clone(&barrier);
            let notifier_word = Arc::clone(&word);
            let notifier = std::thread::spawn(move || {
                notifier_barrier.wait();
                atomic_notify(&notifier_word, 1)
            });
            barrier.wait();
            timeout_async_waiter(&waiter);
            let notified = notifier.join().unwrap();
            let expected = if notified == 1 {
                AtomicWaitResult::Woken
            } else {
                AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut
            };
            assert_eq!(*completions.lock().unwrap(), [expected]);
            assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 0);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_removes_waiters_without_resolving_them() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let waiter = AsyncWaiter::new(|_| panic!("a canceled wait must not dispatch"));
        assert_eq!(atomic_wait_async(WaitWord::Word32(&word), 0, false, &waiter), None);
        assert!(cancel_async_waiter(&waiter));
        timeout_async_waiter(&waiter);
        assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, usize::MAX), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn notifies_wake_waiters_of_a_word_that_did_not_change() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let waiter = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new()));
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 1);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
            assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_word_that_differs_is_not_waited_on() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(1);
        assert_eq!(
            wait(&word, 0, Some(Duration::ZERO), &AgentWaiter::new()),
            AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual
        );
        // NB: Only the low half of a 4-byte word's expected value counts.
        assert_eq!(
            wait(&word, 0x1_0000_0001, Some(Duration::ZERO), &AgentWaiter::new()),
            AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut
        );
        let wide_word = AtomicU64::new(0x1_0000_0000);
        assert_eq!(
            atomic_wait(WaitWord::Word64(&wide_word), 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new()),
            AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_change_of_the_word_wakes_nobody() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let waiter = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, Some(Duration::from_millis(100)), &AgentWaiter::new()));
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 1);
            word.store(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn waits_time_out_and_leave_the_list() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let start = Instant::now();
        assert_eq!(
            wait(&word, 0, Some(Duration::from_millis(20)), &AgentWaiter::new()),
            AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut
        );
        assert!(start.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(20));
        assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn notifies_wake_in_the_order_of_the_waits_and_count_what_they_wake() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let wake_order = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            for index in 0..4 {
                let word = &word;
                let wake_order = &wake_order;
                scope.spawn(move || {
                    let result = wait(word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new());
                    assert_eq!(result, AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
                    wake_order.lock().unwrap().push(index);
                });
                wait_for_waiters(&word, index + 1);
            }
            for index in 0..4 {
                assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
                while wake_order.lock().unwrap().len() != index + 1 {
                    std::thread::yield_now();
                }
            }
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 0);
        });
        assert_eq!(*wake_order.lock().unwrap(), vec![0, 1, 2, 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn notifies_wake_no_more_than_they_are_asked_to() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            for _ in 0..3 {
                scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new()));
            }
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 3);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 0), 0);
            assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 3);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 2), 2);
            assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 1);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, usize::MAX), 1);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn views_of_both_widths_share_a_list() {
        let word = AtomicU64::new(0);
        // SAFETY: The low half of the word is a valid 4-byte word, as this is little-endian.
        let low_half = unsafe { AtomicU32::from_ptr(word.as_ptr().cast()) };
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let waiter = scope.spawn(|| atomic_wait(WaitWord::Word64(&word), 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new()));
            wait_for_waiters(low_half, 1);
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(low_half, 1), 1);
            assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupts_end_waits_with_and_without_a_timeout() {
        for timeout in [None, Some(Duration::from_secs(600))] {
            let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
            let agent = AgentWaiter::new();
            std::thread::scope(|scope| {
                let waiter = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, timeout, &agent));
                wait_for_waiters(&word, 1);
                agent.interrupt();
                assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
            });
            assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 0);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn notifies_pass_over_interrupted_agents_that_did_not_leave_yet() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let interrupted_agent = AgentWaiter::new();
        let waiting_agent = AgentWaiter::new();
        // NB: The lock stops the interrupted agent from leaving, as if its thread did not run yet.
        let mut held_lists = lists();
        let address = word.as_ptr().addr();
        for waiter in [&interrupted_agent, &waiting_agent] {
            held_lists.push_back(Waiting {
                address,
                waiter: Waiter::Blocking(Arc::clone(waiter)),
            });
        }
        interrupted_agent.is_interrupted.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        drop(held_lists);
        assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
        assert!(waiting_agent.was_notified.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
        assert!(!interrupted_agent.was_notified.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
        assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupted_agents_do_not_wait_again() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let agent = AgentWaiter::new();
        agent.interrupt();
        assert_eq!(wait(&word, 0, None, &agent), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
        assert_eq!(wait(&word, 1, None, &agent), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupts_reach_waits_that_are_just_starting() {
        for _ in 0..2000 {
            let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
            let agent = AgentWaiter::new();
            std::thread::scope(|scope| {
                let waiter = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &agent));
                agent.interrupt();
                assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
            });
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn interrupts_leave_the_other_waiters_of_a_word_alone() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let interrupted_agent = AgentWaiter::new();
        let woken = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let first = scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &interrupted_agent));
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 1);
            let second = scope.spawn(|| {
                let result = wait(&word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new());
                woken.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                result
            });
            wait_for_waiters(&word, 2);
            interrupted_agent.interrupt();
            assert_eq!(first.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
            std::thread::sleep(TIME_TO_SLEEP);
            assert_eq!(woken.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
            assert_eq!(waiters_of(&word), 1);
            // NB: The interrupted agent gave its place up, so nothing is lost to it.
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
            assert_eq!(second.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_agent_that_a_notify_counts_wakes_whatever_the_order_on_the_list() {
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let waiters: Vec<_> = (0..64)
                .map(|_| scope.spawn(|| wait(&word, 0, None, &AgentWaiter::new())))
                .collect();
            wait_for_waiters(&word, waiters.len());
            for _ in 0..waiters.len() {
                assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
            }
            assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 0);
            for waiter in waiters {
                assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
            }
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn many_agents_can_wait_on_one_word_and_be_interrupted_one_by_one() {
        // NB: More agents than the 31 interrupt slots that the futex path had.
        let word = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let agents: Vec<_> = (0..64).map(|_| AgentWaiter::new()).collect();
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            // NB: One at a time, as a notify wakes the first on the list, which the loop below expects to be this order.
            let waiters: Vec<_> = agents
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(index, agent)| {
                    let word = &word;
                    let waiter = scope.spawn(move || wait(word, 0, None, agent));
                    wait_for_waiters(word, index + 1);
                    waiter
                })
                .collect();
            for (index, (agent, waiter)) in agents.iter().zip(waiters).enumerate() {
                if index % 2 == 0 {
                    agent.interrupt();
                    assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted);
                } else {
                    assert_eq!(atomic_notify(&word, 1), 1);
                    assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), AtomicWaitResult::Woken);
                }
            }
        });
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Memory for code generated at run time on Windows x86-64, which the JITs of LibJS and LibWasm share.
//!
//! A chunk of code is reserved as a whole and its pages are committed as code is written to them, so that only pages
//! holding code count against the system's commit limit. Code is never writable and executable at once.
//!
//! Windows walks stacks with unwind tables, not frame pointers, and takes code without a table entry for a leaf
//! function. A walk through generated code would read a return address from the middle of a frame and derail, and the
//! dispatch of an exception is such a walk, which has to get to the base of the thread for the process's unhandled
//! exception filter to run. All generated code keeps a frame pointer, so one entry can describe a whole range of it
//! however many functions the range holds, and the start of the range, where its prologue is. A walk from the prologue
//! of another function of the range takes the frame pointer of the function's caller for the function's, which skips
//! the caller but stays on track if the caller's frame is laid out the same way. Code that native code calls, which
//! keeps no frame pointer on Windows, has to start a range.

use core::ffi::c_void;

/// The page size on Windows x86-64.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;

/// How much of the start of a chunk `add_unwind_info()` writes to, which code must stay out of.
pub const UNWIND_INFO_SIZE: usize = 64;

/// The most ranges of code a chunk can have.
const MAX_UNWIND_RANGES: usize = 2;

const MEM_COMMIT: u32 = 0x1000;
const MEM_RESERVE: u32 = 0x2000;
const MEM_RELEASE: u32 = 0x8000;
const PAGE_NOACCESS: u32 = 0x01;
const PAGE_READWRITE: u32 = 0x04;
const PAGE_EXECUTE_READ: u32 = 0x20;

const UNWIND_INFO_VERSION: u8 = 1;
const UWOP_PUSH_NONVOL: u8 = 0;
const UWOP_SET_FPREG: u8 = 3;
const RBP: u8 = 5;

#[link(name = "kernel32")]
unsafe extern "system" {
    fn VirtualAlloc(address: *mut c_void, size: usize, allocation_type: u32, protect: u32) -> *mut c_void;
    fn VirtualFree(address: *mut c_void, size: usize, free_type: u32) -> i32;
    fn VirtualProtect(address: *mut c_void, size: usize, protect: u32, old_protect: *mut u32) -> i32;
    fn GetCurrentProcess() -> *mut c_void;
    fn FlushInstructionCache(process: *mut c_void, address: *const c_void, size: usize) -> i32;
    fn RtlAddFunctionTable(table: *const RuntimeFunction, entry_count: u32, base_address: u64) -> u8;
    fn RtlDeleteFunctionTable(table: *const RuntimeFunction) -> u8;
}

/// Reserves address space for a chunk of `size` bytes, or returns null if there is none. Nothing of it can be accessed
/// before `make_writable()`.
pub fn reserve(size: usize) -> *mut u8 {
    // SAFETY: A reservation at an address of the system's choosing has no preconditions.
    unsafe { VirtualAlloc(core::ptr::null_mut(), size, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS).cast() }
}

/// Gives back the chunk at `base`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `base` must come from `reserve()`, and nothing may use the chunk anymore, which has no unwind info registered.
pub unsafe fn release(base: *mut u8) {
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
    let result = unsafe { VirtualFree(base.cast(), 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
    assert_ne!(result, 0, "releasing generated code memory failed");
}

/// Makes the pages of a range writable and not executable, committing the ones that were not committed. Returns whether
/// that worked, which only fails when the system is out of commit, and then leaves the pages as they were.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be inside a chunk from `reserve()`, and no code may run in its pages until `make_executable()`.
pub unsafe fn make_writable(address: *mut u8, size: usize) -> bool {
    // NB: Committing pages that are committed already keeps their contents and sets their protection.
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
    !unsafe { VirtualAlloc(address.cast(), size, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) }.is_null()
}

/// Makes the pages of a range executable and not writable, and has the processor see what was written to them. Returns
/// whether that worked, which only fails when the system is out of kernel memory.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be inside a chunk from `reserve()`, and all its pages must be committed.
pub unsafe fn make_executable(address: *mut u8, size: usize) -> bool {
    let mut old_protect = 0;
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
    unsafe {
        VirtualProtect(address.cast(), size, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, &raw mut old_protect) != 0
            && FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), address.cast(), size) != 0
    }
}

/// How the code of a range sets up its frames, which is all a stack walk needs to know about it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameLayout {
    /// `push rbp; mov rbp, rsp`: rbp points at the saved rbp.
    RbpAtSavedRbp,
    /// `push rbp; lea rbp, [rsp + 16]`: rbp points 8 bytes above the return address.
    RbpAboveReturnAddress,
}

/// A range of the code of a chunk, in bytes from the chunk's base.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CodeRange {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
    pub frame_layout: FrameLayout,
}

/// `RUNTIME_FUNCTION`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct RuntimeFunction {
    begin_address: u32,
    end_address: u32,
    unwind_info_address: u32,
}

/// `UNWIND_INFO` with its two unwind codes, which come in the reverse order of what they undo.
#[repr(C, align(4))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct UnwindInfo {
    version_and_flags: u8,
    size_of_prologue: u8,
    code_count: u8,
    frame_register_and_offset: u8,
    set_frame_register: [u8; 2],
    push_frame_register: [u8; 2],
}

impl UnwindInfo {
    const fn new(frame_layout: FrameLayout) -> Self {
        let (size_of_prologue, offset_in_units_of_16) = match frame_layout {
            // NB: 1 byte for the push, and 3 for the mov or 5 for the lea.
            FrameLayout::RbpAtSavedRbp => (4, 0),
            FrameLayout::RbpAboveReturnAddress => (6, 1),
        };
        Self {
            version_and_flags: UNWIND_INFO_VERSION,
            size_of_prologue,
            code_count: 2,
            frame_register_and_offset: RBP | (offset_in_units_of_16 << 4),
            set_frame_register: [size_of_prologue, UWOP_SET_FPREG],
            push_frame_register: [1, UWOP_PUSH_NONVOL | (RBP << 4)],
        }
    }
}

/// What `add_unwind_info()` writes to the start of a chunk. Entries of the table are in the order of their addresses,
/// and only the entries in use are registered.
#[repr(C)]
struct ChunkUnwindInfo {
    table: [RuntimeFunction; MAX_UNWIND_RANGES],
    rbp_at_saved_rbp: UnwindInfo,
    rbp_above_return_address: UnwindInfo,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ChunkUnwindInfo>() <= UNWIND_INFO_SIZE);

/// Tells the system how to walk through the ranges of code of the chunk at `base`, and how they are laid out. A range's
/// first bytes are taken for its prologue, so `start` should be where a function's prologue is, or inside the first
/// `UNWIND_INFO_SIZE` bytes of the chunk, where no code runs. Returns whether that worked, which only fails when the
/// system is out of commit or kernel memory.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `base` must come from `reserve()` and have no unwind info yet, the ranges must be in order and inside the chunk, and
/// no code may run in the chunk's first page while this runs.
pub unsafe fn add_unwind_info(base: *mut u8, ranges: &[CodeRange]) -> bool {
    assert!(!ranges.is_empty() && ranges.len() <= MAX_UNWIND_RANGES);
    assert!(ranges.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0].end <= pair[1].start));
    let info = base.cast::<ChunkUnwindInfo>();
    let mut table = [RuntimeFunction {
        begin_address: 0,
        end_address: 0,
        unwind_info_address: 0,
    }; MAX_UNWIND_RANGES];
    for (entry, range) in table.iter_mut().zip(ranges) {
        *entry = RuntimeFunction {
            begin_address: range.start,
            end_address: range.end,
            unwind_info_address: match range.frame_layout {
                FrameLayout::RbpAtSavedRbp => core::mem::offset_of!(ChunkUnwindInfo, rbp_at_saved_rbp),
                FrameLayout::RbpAboveReturnAddress => core::mem::offset_of!(ChunkUnwindInfo, rbp_above_return_address),
            } as u32,
        };
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract, and no code goes in the chunk's first bytes.
    unsafe {
        if !make_writable(base, UNWIND_INFO_SIZE) {
            return false;
        }
        info.write(ChunkUnwindInfo {
            table,
            rbp_at_saved_rbp: UnwindInfo::new(FrameLayout::RbpAtSavedRbp),
            rbp_above_return_address: UnwindInfo::new(FrameLayout::RbpAboveReturnAddress),
        });
        make_executable(base, UNWIND_INFO_SIZE)
            && RtlAddFunctionTable(&raw const (*info).table[0], ranges.len() as u32, base as u64) != 0
    }
}

/// Undoes `add_unwind_info()` for the chunk at `base`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The chunk must have unwind info, and stay mapped for the duration of the call.
pub unsafe fn delete_unwind_info(base: *mut u8) {
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract.
    let result = unsafe { RtlDeleteFunctionTable(base.cast::<RuntimeFunction>()) };
    assert_ne!(result, 0, "deleting the unwind info of generated code failed");
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// `CONTEXT`.
    #[repr(C, align(16))]
    struct Context([u8; 1232]);

    impl Context {
        const RSP_OFFSET: usize = 0x98;
        const RIP_OFFSET: usize = 0xf8;

        fn register(&mut self, offset: usize) -> &mut u64 {
            // SAFETY: The offsets are of 8-byte aligned registers in the structure.
            unsafe { &mut *self.0.as_mut_ptr().add(offset).cast::<u64>() }
        }
    }

    #[link(name = "kernel32")]
    unsafe extern "system" {
        fn RtlCaptureContext(context: *mut Context);
        fn RtlLookupFunctionEntry(pc: u64, image_base: *mut u64, history: *mut c_void) -> *const RuntimeFunction;
        fn RtlVirtualUnwind(
            handler_type: u32,
            image_base: u64,
            pc: u64,
            function: *const RuntimeFunction,
            context: *mut Context,
            handler_data: *mut *mut c_void,
            establisher_frame: *mut u64,
            context_pointers: *mut c_void,
        ) -> *mut c_void;
    }

    const CHUNK_SIZE: usize = 1 << 20;
    const CODE_OFFSET: usize = PAGE_SIZE;

    const FRAME_COUNT: usize = 32;

    /// `extern "C" fn(callback, frames)` with a `push rbp; mov rbp, rsp` frame, which calls `callback(frames)` in it.
    const RBP_AT_SAVED_RBP_CODE: &[u8] = &[
        0x55, // push rbp
        0x48, 0x89, 0xe5, // mov rbp, rsp
        0x48, 0x81, 0xec, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, // sub rsp, 256
        0x48, 0x89, 0xc8, // mov rax, rcx
        0x48, 0x89, 0xd1, // mov rcx, rdx
        0xff, 0xd0, // call rax
        0x48, 0x89, 0xec, // mov rsp, rbp
        0x5d, // pop rbp
        0xc3, // ret
    ];

    /// `extern "C" fn(callback, frames)` with a `push rbp; lea rbp, [rsp + 16]` frame, which calls `callback(frames)`
    /// in it.
    const RBP_ABOVE_RETURN_ADDRESS_CODE: &[u8] = &[
        0x55, // push rbp
        0x48, 0x8d, 0x6c, 0x24, 0x10, // lea rbp, [rsp + 16]
        0x48, 0x81, 0xec, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, // sub rsp, 256
        0x48, 0x89, 0xc8, // mov rax, rcx
        0x48, 0x89, 0xd1, // mov rcx, rdx
        0xff, 0xd0, // call rax
        0x48, 0x8d, 0x65, 0xf0, // lea rsp, [rbp - 16]
        0x5d, // pop rbp
        0xc3, // ret
    ];

    fn function_entry_of(pc: usize) -> *const RuntimeFunction {
        let mut image_base = 0;
        // SAFETY: Looking up a function has no preconditions.
        unsafe { RtlLookupFunctionEntry(pc as u64, &raw mut image_base, core::ptr::null_mut()) }
    }

    /// Walks the stack like the dispatch of an exception does, into `frames`.
    extern "C" fn capture_frames(frames: *mut [usize; FRAME_COUNT]) {
        let mut context = Context([0; 1232]);
        // SAFETY: The caller passes frames of its own, and the walk stays on the stack as long as the unwind info is
        //         right.
        unsafe {
            RtlCaptureContext(&raw mut context);
            for frame in (*frames).iter_mut() {
                let pc = *context.register(Context::RIP_OFFSET);
                if pc == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                *frame = pc as usize;
                let mut image_base = 0;
                let function = RtlLookupFunctionEntry(pc, &raw mut image_base, core::ptr::null_mut());
                if function.is_null() {
                    let stack_pointer = *context.register(Context::RSP_OFFSET);
                    *context.register(Context::RIP_OFFSET) = *(stack_pointer as *const u64);
                    *context.register(Context::RSP_OFFSET) = stack_pointer + 8;
                    continue;
                }
                let mut handler_data = core::ptr::null_mut();
                let mut establisher_frame = 0;
                RtlVirtualUnwind(
                    0,
                    image_base,
                    pc,
                    function,
                    &raw mut context,
                    &raw mut handler_data,
                    &raw mut establisher_frame,
                    core::ptr::null_mut(),
                );
            }
        }
    }

    type Callback = extern "C" fn(*mut [usize; FRAME_COUNT]);

    /// The code at `code` calling `capture_frames()`, in a function a walk has to come back through.
    #[inline(never)]
    fn call_generated_code(code: *const u8) -> [usize; FRAME_COUNT] {
        let mut frames = [0; FRAME_COUNT];
        // SAFETY: The code is a function of this type.
        let code: extern "C" fn(Callback, *mut [usize; FRAME_COUNT]) = unsafe { core::mem::transmute(code) };
        code(capture_frames, &raw mut frames);
        // NB: Keeps this from turning into a tail call, which would leave this function out of the walk.
        core::hint::black_box(frames)
    }

    /// Runs `code` in a chunk that describes it with `frame_layout`, and checks that a walk from inside it gets back to
    /// its caller.
    fn check_walk_through(code: &[u8], frame_layout: FrameLayout) {
        let base = reserve(CHUNK_SIZE);
        assert!(!base.is_null());
        // SAFETY: The chunk was just reserved, and nothing runs in it until the code is written and executable.
        unsafe {
            assert!(add_unwind_info(
                base,
                &[CodeRange {
                    start: 0,
                    end: CHUNK_SIZE as u32,
                    frame_layout,
                }],
            ));
            let code_start = base.add(CODE_OFFSET);
            assert!(make_writable(code_start, code.len()));
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), code_start, code.len());
            assert!(make_executable(code_start, code.len()));

            let frames = call_generated_code(code_start);
            let code_range = code_start as usize..code_start as usize + code.len();
            let index = frames
                .iter()
                .position(|frame| code_range.contains(frame))
                .expect("the walk goes through the generated code");
            let caller = frames[index + 1];
            assert_ne!(caller, 0, "the walk ends at the generated code");
            assert_eq!(
                function_entry_of(caller),
                function_entry_of(call_generated_code as *const () as usize),
                "the walk does not continue in the caller of the generated code"
            );

            delete_unwind_info(base);
            release(base);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_through_frames_with_rbp_at_saved_rbp() {
        check_walk_through(RBP_AT_SAVED_RBP_CODE, FrameLayout::RbpAtSavedRbp);
    }

    #[test]
    fn walks_through_frames_with_rbp_above_return_address() {
        check_walk_through(RBP_ABOVE_RETURN_ADDRESS_CODE, FrameLayout::RbpAboveReturnAddress);
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_contents_when_making_committed_pages_writable_again() {
        let base = reserve(CHUNK_SIZE);
        assert!(!base.is_null());
        // SAFETY: The chunk was just reserved, and no code runs in it.
        unsafe {
            assert!(make_writable(base, PAGE_SIZE));
            base.write(0x5a);
            assert!(make_executable(base, PAGE_SIZE));
            assert!(make_writable(base, PAGE_SIZE));
            assert_eq!(base.read(), 0x5a);
            base.write(0xa5);
            assert_eq!(base.read(), 0xa5);
            release(base);
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Memory for many small tables of words that live and die one by one.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::CStr;

use crate::region::Region;

/// A fixed number of 32-bit words in memory that comes straight from the system, and goes back to it when the chunk
/// is dropped.
///
/// An owner of many tables keeps them in a few chunks, each table in a range of words it hands out, so the tables
/// are no blocks of the heap. Everything that holds a part of a chunk shares the chunk, so the words can be read
/// and written through a shared reference, on the one thread that has the chunk.
pub struct WordChunk {
    region: Region,
    len: usize,
}

impl WordChunk {
    /// A chunk of `len` words, which are zero. `name` shows up for its memory in /proc/<pid>/smaps on Linux.
    pub fn new(len: usize, name: &'static CStr) -> Self {
        let size = len
            .checked_mul(size_of::<u32>())
            .expect("a chunk fits in the address space");
        let mut region = Region::new(size, name);
        // NB: A page of the chunk takes memory when it is first written, not here.
        region.commit(size);
        Self { region, len }
    }

    pub fn words(&self) -> &[Cell<u32>] {
        // SAFETY: The region has memory for `len` words from its base on, which is a multiple of 4096 and so aligned
        //         for them. The memory holds zeros until a word is set, so every word has a value. A `Cell<u32>` is laid
        //         out like a `u32`, and nothing refers to the words other than as cells. The region keeps the
        //         memory for as long as the chunk lives, and a chunk is not `Sync`, so the cells stay on the thread
        //         that has it.
        unsafe { crate::slice_from_raw_parts(self.region.base().as_ptr().cast(), self.len) }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn words_are_zero_until_they_are_set() {
        let chunk = WordChunk::new(100_000, c"test");
        let words = chunk.words();
        assert_eq!(words.len(), 100_000);
        assert!(words.iter().all(|word| word.get() == 0));
        words[0].set(1);
        words[99_999].set(2);
        // NB: Every view of the chunk is of the same words.
        assert_eq!(chunk.words()[0].get(), 1);
        assert_eq!(chunk.words()[99_999].get(), 2);
        assert_eq!(chunk.words()[1].get(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_chunk_may_hold_no_word() {
        let chunk = WordChunk::new(0, c"test");
        assert!(chunk.words().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn moves_to_another_thread() {
        let chunk = WordChunk::new(16, c"test");
        chunk.words()[3].set(7);
        let chunk = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            chunk.words()[4].set(8);
            chunk
        })
        .join()
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(chunk.words()[3].get(), 7);
        assert_eq!(chunk.words()[4].get(), 8);
    }
}

/*

//! A fixed-size set of small integers that keeps its words in a zone (see `Zone`).

use crate::Zone;
use crate::ZoneVec;

/// A fixed-size set of small integers, whose words are in a zone (see `Zone`).
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ZoneBitSet<'z> {
    // NB: A set of up to 64 integers fits in one word and takes no memory of the zone.
    first_word: u64,
    extra_words: ZoneVec<'z, u64>,
    len: usize,
}

impl Clone for ZoneBitSet<'_> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            first_word: self.first_word,
            extra_words: self.extra_words.clone(),
            len: self.len,
        }
    }

    fn clone_from(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.first_word = other.first_word;
        // NB: This keeps the memory of the words where they fit.
        self.extra_words.assign(&other.extra_words);
        self.len = other.len;
    }
}

impl<'z> ZoneBitSet<'z> {
    /// An empty set that can hold the integers `0..len`, with its words in `zone`.
    pub fn new_in(len: usize, zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            first_word: 0,
            extra_words: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, len.div_ceil(64).saturating_sub(1), zone),
            len,
        }
    }

    /// Takes all elements out. The set keeps its memory.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.first_word = 0;
        self.extra_words.fill(0);
    }

    /// The exclusive upper bound of the integers this set can hold.
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, index: usize) -> bool {
        assert!(index < self.len, "bit {index} out of range {}", self.len);
        let word = if index < 64 {
            self.first_word
        } else {
            self.extra_words[index / 64 - 1]
        };
        word & (1 << (index % 64)) != 0
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, index: usize) {
        assert!(index < self.len, "bit {index} out of range {}", self.len);
        if index < 64 {
            self.first_word |= 1 << index;
        } else {
            self.extra_words[index / 64 - 1] |= 1 << (index % 64);
        }
    }

    pub fn remove(&mut self, index: usize) {
        assert!(index < self.len, "bit {index} out of range {}", self.len);
        if index < 64 {
            self.first_word &= !(1 << index);
        } else {
            self.extra_words[index / 64 - 1] &= !(1 << (index % 64));
        }
    }

    pub fn insert_range(&mut self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>) {
        for index in range {
            self.insert(index);
        }
    }

    /// Adds every element of `other`. Returns whether this set changed.
    pub fn union_with(&mut self, other: &ZoneBitSet<'_>) -> bool {
        assert_eq!(self.len, other.len, "union of differently sized sets");
        let first_word = self.first_word | other.first_word;
        let mut changed = first_word != self.first_word;
        self.first_word = first_word;
        for (word, other_word) in self.extra_words.iter_mut().zip(other.extra_words.iter()) {
            let new_word = *word | other_word;
            changed |= new_word != *word;
            *word = new_word;
        }
        changed
    }

    /// Removes every element of `other`.
    pub fn subtract(&mut self, other: &ZoneBitSet<'_>) {
        assert_eq!(self.len, other.len, "difference of differently sized sets");
        self.first_word &= !other.first_word;
        for (word, other_word) in self.extra_words.iter_mut().zip(other.extra_words.iter()) {
            *word &= !other_word;
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.first_word == 0 && self.extra_words.iter().all(|word| *word == 0)
    }

    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.first_word.count_ones() as usize
            + self
                .extra_words
                .iter()
                .map(|word| word.count_ones() as usize)
                .sum::<usize>()
    }

    /// The elements in increasing order.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> + '_ {
        std::iter::once(&self.first_word)
            .chain(self.extra_words.iter())
            .enumerate()
            .flat_map(|(word_index, word)| {
                let mut bits = *word;
                std::iter::from_fn(move || {
                    if bits == 0 {
                        return None;
                    }
                    let bit = bits.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                    bits &= bits - 1;
                    Some(word_index * 64 + bit)
                })
            })
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for ZoneBitSet<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter.debug_set().entries(self.iter()).finish()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn empty_and_single_word_sets_clone_without_losing_bits() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        for len in [0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 128, 129] {
            let mut set = ZoneBitSet::new_in(len, &zone);
            assert_eq!(set.capacity(), len);
            assert!(set.iter().next().is_none());
            if len > 0 {
                set.insert(len - 1);
            }
            let mut cloned = ZoneBitSet::new_in(130, &zone);
            cloned.clone_from(&set);
            assert_eq!(cloned, set);
            assert_eq!(cloned.count(), usize::from(len > 0));
            set.subtract(&cloned);
            assert!(set.is_empty());
            assert_eq!(set.union_with(&cloned), len > 0);
            assert!(!set.union_with(&cloned));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_set_in_a_zone_inserts_removes_and_iterates_across_words() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        assert_eq!(ZoneBitSet::new_in(64, &zone).capacity(), 64);
        assert_eq!(zone.used(), 0);
        let mut set = ZoneBitSet::new_in(130, &zone);
        assert!(set.is_empty());
        for index in [0, 63, 64, 129] {
            set.insert(index);
        }
        assert_eq!(set.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0, 63, 64, 129]);
        assert_eq!(set.count(), 4);
        let mut other = ZoneBitSet::new_in(130, &zone);
        other.insert_range(0..2);
        other.insert(129);
        assert!(other.union_with(&set));
        assert!(!other.union_with(&set));
        assert_eq!(other.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0, 1, 63, 64, 129]);
        other.subtract(&set);
        assert_eq!(other.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [1]);
        set.remove(63);
        assert!(!set.contains(63) && set.contains(64));
        let copy = set.clone();
        other.clone_from(&set);
        set.clear();
        assert!(set.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(copy, other);
        assert_eq!(format!("{copy:?}"), "{0, 64, 129}");
    }
}

//! Maps and sets that keep their entries in a zone (see `Zone`).
//!
//! A `ZoneMap` keeps its entries next to each other in a list of its zone, in the order in which they were added,
//! and finds them through a table of indices into that list. So a compile makes no block of the heap for a map, and
//! the order in which a map gives its entries back does not depend on the hash of a key: what a compile does with
//! the entries of a map is the same on each run.

use core::fmt;
use core::hash::BuildHasher;
use core::hash::BuildHasherDefault;
use core::hash::Hash;

use crate::Zone;
use crate::ZoneVec;

use crate::fast_hash::FastHasher;

/// A map from `K` to `V` in a zone. Keys and values are plain data (see `ak::ZoneVec`).
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ZoneMap<'z, K, V> {
    /// The entries, in the order in which they were added. An entry that is removed gives its place to the last one.
    entries: ZoneVec<'z, (K, V)>,
    /// Where the entries are: for each slot, 0 or one more than the index of an entry. The entry of a key is in the
    /// first slot that is free from the home slot of the key on, in the order of the slots, which wraps around. The
    /// count of slots is a power of two, or 0 for a map that never had an entry.
    slots: ZoneVec<'z, u32>,
}

/// The fewest slots of a map that has entries.
const MIN_SLOTS: usize = 8;

impl<'z, K: Hash + Eq, V> ZoneMap<'z, K, V> {
    /// A map with no entries, which takes no memory before it has one.
    pub fn new_in(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            slots: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
        }
    }

    /// A map with no entries and room for `capacity` of them.
    pub fn with_capacity_in(capacity: usize, zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        let mut map = Self {
            entries: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(capacity, zone),
            slots: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
        };
        if capacity != 0 {
            map.slots.resize(Self::slots_for(capacity), 0);
        }
        map
    }

    /// A map of the entries that `entries` gives. For a key that comes more than one time, the last value stays.
    pub fn from_iter_in(entries: impl IntoIterator<Item = (K, V)>, zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        let mut map = Self::new_in(zone);
        map.extend(entries);
        map
    }

    /// How many slots keep `count` entries at most three quarters full.
    fn slots_for(count: usize) -> usize {
        (count * 4).div_ceil(3).next_power_of_two().max(MIN_SLOTS)
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.is_empty()
    }

    /// Drops all entries. The map keeps its memory.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.entries.clear();
        self.slots.fill(0);
    }

    /// The home slot of `key`. The map has slots.
    fn home(&self, key: &K) -> usize {
        let hash = BuildHasherDefault::<FastHasher>::default().hash_one(key);
        // NB: The hash ends with a multiplication, so its high bits depend on all the bits of the key.
        (hash >> (u64::BITS - self.slots.len().trailing_zeros())) as usize
    }

    /// The slot and the index of the entry of `key`.
    fn find(&self, key: &K) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
        if self.slots.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let mask = self.slots.len() - 1;
        let mut slot = self.home(key);
        loop {
            let entry = self.slots[slot] as usize;
            if entry == 0 {
                return None;
            }
            if self.entries[entry - 1].0 == *key {
                return Some((slot, entry - 1));
            }
            slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
        }
    }

    /// Puts the entry at `index` in the first free slot from its home on.
    fn place(&mut self, index: usize) {
        let mask = self.slots.len() - 1;
        let mut slot = self.home(&self.entries[index].0);
        while self.slots[slot] != 0 {
            slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
        }
        // NB: A list of a zone holds fewer than 2^32 elements.
        self.slots[slot] = index as u32 + 1;
    }

    /// Adds an entry for `key`, which has none.
    fn add(&mut self, key: K, value: V) {
        if (self.entries.len() + 1) * 4 > self.slots.len() * 3 {
            let count = Self::slots_for(self.entries.len() + 1).max(self.slots.len() * 2);
            self.slots.clear();
            self.slots.resize(count, 0);
            for index in 0..self.entries.len() {
                self.place(index);
            }
        }
        self.entries.push((key, value));
        self.place(self.entries.len() - 1);
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &K) -> Option<&V> {
        let (_, index) = self.find(key)?;
        Some(&self.entries[index].1)
    }

    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, key: &K) -> Option<&mut V> {
        let (_, index) = self.find(key)?;
        Some(&mut self.entries[index].1)
    }

    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &K) -> bool {
        self.find(key).is_some()
    }

    /// Makes `value` the value of `key`, and returns the value that `key` had.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: K, value: V) -> Option<V> {
        match self.find(&key) {
            Some((_, index)) => Some(core::mem::replace(&mut self.entries[index].1, value)),
            None => {
                self.add(key, value);
                None
            }
        }
    }

    /// Takes the entry of `key` out, and returns its value. The entry that was added last takes its place in the
    /// order of the entries.
    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &K) -> Option<V> {
        let (slot, index) = self.find(key)?;
        // Free the slot, and move each entry after it that was pushed away from its home back toward it, so that
        // every entry stays in the first free slot from its home on.
        let mask = self.slots.len() - 1;
        let mut hole = slot;
        let mut next = (hole + 1) & mask;
        while self.slots[next] != 0 {
            let home = self.home(&self.entries[self.slots[next] as usize - 1].0);
            // NB: The entry can move to the hole unless its home is after the hole on the way to its slot.
            if (next.wrapping_sub(home) & mask) >= (next.wrapping_sub(hole) & mask) {
                self.slots[hole] = self.slots[next];
                hole = next;
            }
            next = (next + 1) & mask;
        }
        self.slots[hole] = 0;
        let last = self.entries.len() - 1;
        if index != last {
            let (last_slot, _) = self.find(&self.entries[last].0).expect("each entry has a slot");
            self.slots[last_slot] = index as u32 + 1;
        }
        Some(self.entries.swap_remove(index).1)
    }

    /// The entry of `key`, to add it if the map has none.
    pub fn entry(&mut self, key: K) -> Entry<'_, 'z, K, V> {
        let found = self.find(&key).map(|(_, index)| index);
        Entry { map: self, key, found }
    }

    /// The entries, in the order in which they were added.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = (&K, &V)> + DoubleEndedIterator + '_ {
        self.entries.iter().map(|(key, value)| (key, value))
    }

    pub fn iter_mut(&mut self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = (&K, &mut V)> + '_ {
        self.entries.iter_mut().map(|(key, value)| (&*key, value))
    }

    pub fn keys(&self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &K> + DoubleEndedIterator + '_ {
        self.entries.iter().map(|(key, _)| key)
    }

    pub fn values(&self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &V> + DoubleEndedIterator + '_ {
        self.entries.iter().map(|(_, value)| value)
    }

    pub fn values_mut(&mut self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &mut V> + '_ {
        self.entries.iter_mut().map(|(_, value)| value)
    }
}

impl<K: Hash + Eq, V> Extend<(K, V)> for ZoneMap<'_, K, V> {
    fn extend<I: IntoIterator<Item = (K, V)>>(&mut self, entries: I) {
        for (key, value) in entries {
            self.insert(key, value);
        }
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Debug, V: fmt::Debug> fmt::Debug for ZoneMap<'_, K, V> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_map()
            .entries(self.entries.iter().map(|(key, value)| (key, value)))
            .finish()
    }
}

/// The place of a key in a map, which has an entry or gets one (see `ZoneMap::entry()`).
pub struct Entry<'a, 'z, K, V> {
    map: &'a mut ZoneMap<'z, K, V>,
    key: K,
    /// The index of the entry of the key, if it has one.
    found: Option<usize>,
}

impl<'a, K: Hash + Eq, V> Entry<'a, '_, K, V> {
    /// The value of the key, which is `value` if the key had none.
    pub fn or_insert(self, value: V) -> &'a mut V {
        self.or_insert_with(|| value)
    }

    /// The value of the key, which is what `make` returns if the key had none.
    pub fn or_insert_with(self, make: impl FnOnce() -> V) -> &'a mut V {
        let index = match self.found {
            Some(index) => index,
            None => {
                self.map.add(self.key, make());
                self.map.entries.len() - 1
            }
        };
        &mut self.map.entries[index].1
    }

    /// The value of the key, which is the default value if the key had none.
    pub fn or_default(self) -> &'a mut V
    where
        V: Default,
    {
        self.or_insert_with(V::default)
    }
}

/// A set of `K` in a zone. It gives its elements back in the order in which they were added.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ZoneSet<'z, K> {
    map: ZoneMap<'z, K, ()>,
}

impl<'z, K: Hash + Eq> ZoneSet<'z, K> {
    /// A set with no elements, which takes no memory before it has one.
    pub fn new_in(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            map: ZoneMap::new_in(zone),
        }
    }

    /// A set of the elements that `elements` gives.
    pub fn from_iter_in(elements: impl IntoIterator<Item = K>, zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        let mut set = Self::new_in(zone);
        set.extend(elements);
        set
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.map.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.map.is_empty()
    }

    /// Drops all elements. The set keeps its memory.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.map.clear();
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, element: &K) -> bool {
        self.map.contains_key(element)
    }

    /// Adds `element`, and returns whether the set did not have it.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, element: K) -> bool {
        self.map.insert(element, ()).is_none()
    }

    /// Takes `element` out, and returns whether the set had it. The element that was added last takes its place in
    /// the order of the elements.
    pub fn remove(&mut self, element: &K) -> bool {
        self.map.remove(element).is_some()
    }

    /// The elements, in the order in which they were added.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &K> + DoubleEndedIterator + '_ {
        self.map.keys()
    }
}

impl<K: Hash + Eq> Extend<K> for ZoneSet<'_, K> {
    fn extend<I: IntoIterator<Item = K>>(&mut self, elements: I) {
        for element in elements {
            self.insert(element);
        }
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Debug> fmt::Debug for ZoneSet<'_, K> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_set()
            .entries(self.map.entries.iter().map(|(key, _)| key))
            .finish()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_map_finds_what_was_added() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 24, c"test");
        let mut map = ZoneMap::new_in(&zone);
        assert!(map.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(zone.used(), 0);
        assert_eq!(map.get(&1_u64), None);
        for key in 0..10_000_u64 {
            // NB: Keys that differ only in their high bits, like the bits of boxed values.
            assert_eq!(map.insert(key << 48 | 7, key), None);
        }
        assert_eq!(map.len(), 10_000);
        for key in 0..10_000_u64 {
            assert_eq!(map.get(&(key << 48 | 7)), Some(&key));
            assert!(!map.contains_key(&(key << 48 | 6)));
        }
        assert_eq!(map.insert(5 << 48 | 7, 99), Some(5));
        *map.get_mut(&(6 << 48 | 7)).unwrap() += 1;
        assert_eq!(map.get(&(5 << 48 | 7)), Some(&99));
        assert_eq!(map.get(&(6 << 48 | 7)), Some(&7));
        assert_eq!(map.len(), 10_000);
        map.clear();
        assert!(map.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(map.get(&7), None);
        assert_eq!(map.insert(7, 1), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_map_gives_its_entries_back_in_the_order_they_were_added() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        let keys = [900_u32, 3, 77, 1 << 30, 0, 12];
        let mut map = ZoneMap::from_iter_in(keys.iter().map(|key| (*key, key.count_ones())), &zone);
        assert!(map.keys().copied().eq(keys));
        assert!(map.iter().all(|(key, ones)| key.count_ones() == *ones));
        for ones in map.values_mut() {
            *ones += 1;
        }
        assert!(map.values().copied().eq(keys.iter().map(|key| key.count_ones() + 1)));
        let copy = map.clone();
        map.insert(5, 0);
        assert_eq!(copy.len(), keys.len());
        assert_eq!(copy.get(&5), None);
        assert_eq!(
            format!("{:?}", ZoneMap::from_iter_in([(1, 'a'), (0, 'b')], &zone)),
            "{1: 'a', 0: 'b'}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_map_removes_entries() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 24, c"test");
        let mut map = ZoneMap::with_capacity_in(16, &zone);
        let mut model = std::collections::HashMap::new();
        // NB: A sequence that does not repeat for a long time, in place of random numbers.
        let mut state = 0x9e37_79b9_u32;
        for round in 0..20_000_u32 {
            state = state.wrapping_mul(1_664_525).wrapping_add(1_013_904_223);
            let key = (state >> 16) % 512;
            if state & 3 == 0 {
                assert_eq!(map.remove(&key), model.remove(&key));
            } else {
                assert_eq!(map.insert(key, round), model.insert(key, round));
            }
            assert_eq!(map.len(), model.len());
        }
        for key in 0..512 {
            assert_eq!(map.get(&key), model.get(&key));
        }
        let mut entries = map.iter().map(|(key, value)| (*key, *value)).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        entries.sort_unstable();
        let mut expected = model.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        expected.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(entries, expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_entry_adds_a_value_one_time() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        let mut map = ZoneMap::new_in(&zone);
        *map.entry("a").or_insert(1) += 10;
        *map.entry("a").or_insert(1) += 10;
        *map.entry("b").or_insert_with(|| 5) += 1;
        *map.entry("c").or_default() += 2;
        assert_eq!(map.entry("b").or_insert_with(|| unreachable!()), &6);
        assert!(
            map.iter()
                .map(|(key, value)| (*key, *value))
                .eq([("a", 21), ("b", 6), ("c", 2)])
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_set_has_each_element_one_time() {
        let zone = Zone::new(1 << 20, c"test");
        let mut set = ZoneSet::from_iter_in([4_u8, 9, 4, 1], &zone);
        assert_eq!(set.len(), 3);
        assert!(set.contains(&9));
        assert!(!set.contains(&5));
        assert!(!set.insert(1));
        assert!(set.insert(5));
        assert!(set.iter().copied().eq([4, 9, 1, 5]));
        assert!(set.remove(&4));
        assert!(!set.remove(&4));
        assert!(set.iter().copied().eq([5, 9, 1]));
        assert_eq!(format!("{set:?}"), "{5, 9, 1}");
        let copy = set.clone();
        set.clear();
        assert!(set.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(copy.len(), 3);
    }
}
