//! The records of a chunk with what placing them and hashing tile content read of each, and how the records of a chunk
//! are placed in a raster space: the record ranges they are binned into tiles as, with the reach of each.

use super::{ContentHash, ContentHasher, EffectHashScope, TileKeyingOfRasterSpace};
use crate::display_list::builder::{
    HEADER_SIZE, bounding_rect_computed_from_payload, for_each_command, has_inline_clip_in_its_own_space, read_command,
};
use crate::display_list::commands::{
    ContextRef, DisplayListCommandRun, DisplayListCommandType, EffectNodeIndex, FillRect, FillRectWithRoundedCorners,
    FillRoundedRectRing,
};
use crate::display_list::nested_records::{
    NestedRecordsRole, for_each_command_including_nested, for_each_nested_record_span, span_bytes,
};
use crate::display_list::reach::Reach;
use crate::display_list::storage::{ChunkIndexInList, ListChunk, RunIndexInChunk};
use crate::display_list::summary::{command_blend, live_content_of};
use crate::display_list::window_server_placement::RoundedRect;
use libgfx_rust::{Color, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, CornerRadii, IntRect};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The record draws live content, such as a caret or a scroll bar, itself or in a record nested in it, whose look the
/// frame decides. The frame state of the list hashes that of every such record that is in a band.
pub(super) const FRAME_STATE_LIVE_CONTENT: u8 = 1 << 0;
pub(super) const FRAME_STATE_SPACES_OF_INLINE_CLIPS: u8 = 1 << 1;
pub(super) const FRAME_STATE_SAMPLED_BACKGROUND_COLOR: u8 = 1 << 2;

/// A top-level record of a chunk, with what placing it and hashing tile content read of it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct ChunkRecord {
    pub(crate) offset: u32,
    pub(crate) end_offset: u32,
    pub(crate) run_index: RunIndexInChunk,
    pub(crate) bounding_rect: IntRect,
    draws_something: bool,
    pub(super) frame_state_read_flags: u8,
    pub(super) can_lower_destination_alpha: bool,
    // Record bytes hold no offset into the chunk, so a record hashes alike wherever it is.
    pub(super) content_hash_of_bytes: ContentHash,
}

impl ChunkRecord {
    pub(super) fn reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list(&self) -> bool {
        self.frame_state_read_flags & FRAME_STATE_LIVE_CONTENT != 0
    }
}

/// The index of a top-level record in the `RecordTable` of its chunk.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct RecordIndexInChunk(pub u32);

/// The top-level records of a chunk, by run, with what hashing tile content needs of each.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecordTable {
    records: Vec<ChunkRecord>,
    first_record_index_of_each_run: Vec<RecordIndexInChunk>,
    run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list_by_run_index: Vec<bool>,
}

fn frame_state_read_flags_of_record(
    header: &crate::display_list::commands::DisplayListCommandHeader,
    payload: &[u8],
    record_bytes: &[u8],
) -> u8 {
    let mut flags = 0;
    if header.inline_clip_count != 0 && has_inline_clip_in_its_own_space(header, payload) {
        flags |= FRAME_STATE_SPACES_OF_INLINE_CLIPS;
    }
    for_each_command_including_nested(record_bytes, &mut |command_type, _, payload| {
        if live_content_of(command_type, payload).is_some() {
            flags |= FRAME_STATE_LIVE_CONTENT;
        }
        if !background_color_animation_effect_of(command_type, payload).is_none() {
            flags |= FRAME_STATE_SAMPLED_BACKGROUND_COLOR;
        }
    });
    flags
}

// Records nested in a group, a pattern tile or a mask draw into a layer of their own; only those of a vector image draw
// straight into the destination.
fn record_can_lower_destination_alpha(command_type: DisplayListCommandType, payload: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if command_blend(command_type, payload).is_some_and(|(operator, _)| operator.lowers_destination_alpha()) {
        return true;
    }
    let mut can_lower = false;
    for_each_nested_record_span(command_type, payload, |role, span| {
        if role == NestedRecordsRole::VectorImage {
            for_each_command(span_bytes(payload, span), |header, _, payload| {
                can_lower |= record_can_lower_destination_alpha(header.command_type, payload);
            });
        }
    });
    can_lower
}

pub(super) fn background_color_animation_effect_of(
    command_type: DisplayListCommandType,
    payload: &[u8],
) -> EffectNodeIndex {
    match command_type {
        DisplayListCommandType::FillRect => read_command::<FillRect>(payload).background_color_animation_effect,
        DisplayListCommandType::FillRectWithRoundedCorners => {
            read_command::<FillRectWithRoundedCorners>(payload).background_color_animation_effect
        }
        _ => EffectNodeIndex::NONE,
    }
}

impl RecordTable {
    pub fn new(records_of_chunk: &[u8], command_runs: &[DisplayListCommandRun]) -> Self {
        let mut records = Vec::new();
        let mut first_record_index_of_each_run = Vec::with_capacity(command_runs.len() + 1);
        let mut run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list_by_run_index = Vec::with_capacity(command_runs.len());
        for (run_index, run) in command_runs.iter().enumerate() {
            let first_record_index_of_run = records.len();
            first_record_index_of_each_run.push(RecordIndexInChunk(first_record_index_of_run as u32));
            let run_bytes = &records_of_chunk[run.offset as usize..(run.offset + run.size) as usize];
            for_each_command(run_bytes, |header, offset_in_run, payload| {
                let offset = run.offset + offset_in_run as u32;
                let end_offset = offset + (HEADER_SIZE + payload.len()) as u32;
                let record_bytes = &records_of_chunk[offset as usize..end_offset as usize];
                let mut hasher = ContentHasher::new();
                hasher.write_bytes(record_bytes);
                let bounding_rect = bounding_rect_computed_from_payload(header, payload);
                records.push(ChunkRecord {
                    offset,
                    end_offset,
                    run_index: RunIndexInChunk(run_index as u32),
                    bounding_rect: bounding_rect.unwrap_or_default(),
                    draws_something: !header.command_type.is_compositor_metadata()
                        && bounding_rect.is_some_and(|rect| !rect.is_empty()),
                    frame_state_read_flags: frame_state_read_flags_of_record(header, payload, record_bytes),
                    can_lower_destination_alpha: record_can_lower_destination_alpha(header.command_type, payload),
                    content_hash_of_bytes: hasher.finish(),
                });
            });
            run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list_by_run_index.push(
                records[first_record_index_of_run..]
                    .iter()
                    .any(ChunkRecord::reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list),
            );
        }
        first_record_index_of_each_run.push(RecordIndexInChunk(records.len() as u32));
        Self {
            records,
            first_record_index_of_each_run,
            run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list_by_run_index,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list(&self, run_index: RunIndexInChunk) -> bool {
        self.run_reads_frame_state_hashed_for_the_list_by_run_index[run_index.0 as usize]
    }

    pub(crate) fn record(&self, index: RecordIndexInChunk) -> &ChunkRecord {
        &self.records[index.0 as usize]
    }

    pub(crate) fn records_in(&self, indices: std::ops::Range<RecordIndexInChunk>) -> &[ChunkRecord] {
        &self.records[indices.start.0 as usize..indices.end.0 as usize]
    }

    pub(crate) fn record_indices_of_run(&self, run_index: RunIndexInChunk) -> std::ops::Range<RecordIndexInChunk> {
        let run_index = run_index.0 as usize;
        self.first_record_index_of_each_run[run_index]..self.first_record_index_of_each_run[run_index + 1]
    }

    pub(crate) fn record_indices_between_offsets(
        &self,
        begin_offset: u32,
        end_offset: u32,
    ) -> std::ops::Range<RecordIndexInChunk> {
        let first = self.records.partition_point(|record| record.offset < begin_offset);
        let end = self.records.partition_point(|record| record.offset < end_offset);
        RecordIndexInChunk(first as u32)..RecordIndexInChunk(end as u32)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(super) struct DeviceAlignedFill {
    pub(super) rect: RoundedRect,
    pub(super) unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring: Option<RoundedRect>,
    pub(super) content_hash_except_rects: ContentHash,
    pub(super) color: Color,
    pub(super) draws_recorded_color_with_source_over: bool,
}

/// The index of a range in the `record_ranges` of a `ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct PlacedRecordRangeIndex(pub u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(super) struct PlacedRecordRange {
    pub(super) run_index: RunIndexInChunk,
    pub(super) first_record_index: RecordIndexInChunk,
    pub(super) end_record_index: RecordIndexInChunk,
    pub(super) begin_offset: u32,
    pub(super) end_offset: u32,
    pub(super) reach: Reach<IntRect>,
    pub(super) context: ContextRef,
    pub(super) is_spread_by_no_filter: bool,
    pub(super) device_aligned_fill: Option<DeviceAlignedFill>,
}

/// The ranges of a run: those it is binned as, from `first_binned_range_index` up to the range of the whole run.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub(super) struct PlacedRecordRangesOfRun {
    pub(super) first_binned_range_index: PlacedRecordRangeIndex,
    pub(super) whole_run_range_index: PlacedRecordRangeIndex,
    pub(super) reach_of_binned_ranges: Reach<IntRect>,
}

/// What the records of a chunk hold in one raster space, as the geometry of the space places the visual contexts of
/// the chunk's runs it holds: the record ranges the records are binned into tiles as, the reach of each, and the
/// content hash of what each draws. A chunk caches its latest placements for every list that names it.
pub struct ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace {
    placement_inputs_hash: ContentHash,
    pub(super) record_ranges: Vec<PlacedRecordRange>,
    pub(super) ranges_of_each_run: Vec<PlacedRecordRangesOfRun>,
}

impl ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace {
    pub fn placement_inputs_hash(&self) -> ContentHash {
        self.placement_inputs_hash
    }
}

impl TileKeyingOfRasterSpace<'_> {
    fn place_record_range(
        &self,
        chunk: &ListChunk,
        run_index: RunIndexInChunk,
        record_indices: std::ops::Range<RecordIndexInChunk>,
        reach: Reach<IntRect>,
    ) -> PlacedRecordRange {
        let table = chunk.record_table();
        let context = chunk.runs()[run_index.0 as usize].context;
        let is_spread_by_filters = !self
            .list
            .filters_of_effects()
            .nearest_spreading_effect_at_or_above(context.effect)
            .is_none();
        let is_one_record = (record_indices.start.0..record_indices.end.0).len() == 1;
        PlacedRecordRange {
            run_index,
            first_record_index: record_indices.start,
            end_record_index: record_indices.end,
            begin_offset: table.record(record_indices.start).offset,
            end_offset: table.record(RecordIndexInChunk(record_indices.end.0 - 1)).end_offset,
            reach,
            context,
            is_spread_by_no_filter: !is_spread_by_filters,
            device_aligned_fill: is_one_record
                .then(|| self.device_aligned_fill_of_record(chunk, table.record(record_indices.start), context))
                .flatten(),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn device_aligned_fill_of_record(
        &self,
        chunk: &ListChunk,
        record: &ChunkRecord,
        context: ContextRef,
    ) -> Option<DeviceAlignedFill> {
        let (header, payload) = chunk.record_at(record.offset);
        if header.inline_clip_count != 0 || header.has_inline_transform {
            return None;
        }
        let mut hasher = ContentHasher::new();
        hasher.write_u32(header.command_type as u32);
        let color;
        let draws_recorded_color_with_source_over;
        let (rect, corner_radii, unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring) = match header.command_type {
            DisplayListCommandType::FillRect => {
                let fill = read_command::<FillRect>(payload);
                hasher.write_u32(fill.color.0);
                hasher.write_u32(fill.compositing_and_blending_operator as u32);
                hasher.write_u32(fill.background_color_animation_effect.0);
                color = fill.color;
                draws_recorded_color_with_source_over = fill.compositing_and_blending_operator
                    == CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal
                    && fill.background_color_animation_effect.is_none();
                (fill.rect, CornerRadii::default(), None)
            }
            DisplayListCommandType::FillRectWithRoundedCorners => {
                let fill = read_command::<FillRectWithRoundedCorners>(payload);
                hasher.write_u32(fill.color.0);
                hasher.write_u32(fill.background_color_animation_effect.0);
                color = fill.color;
                draws_recorded_color_with_source_over = fill.background_color_animation_effect.is_none();
                (fill.rect, fill.corner_radii, None)
            }
            DisplayListCommandType::FillRoundedRectRing => {
                let ring = read_command::<FillRoundedRectRing>(payload);
                hasher.write_u32(ring.color.0);
                color = ring.color;
                draws_recorded_color_with_source_over = true;
                for width in ring.widths_within_rect() {
                    hasher.write_i32(width);
                }
                (ring.rect, ring.corner_radii, Some(ring.unfilled_inner_rect()?))
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring = match unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring {
            Some(unfilled_inner_rect) => Some(RoundedRect::device_aligned_of(
                &self.geometry.world,
                context.spatial,
                unfilled_inner_rect.to_float(),
                &CornerRadii::default(),
            )?),
            None => None,
        };
        Some(DeviceAlignedFill {
            rect: RoundedRect::device_aligned_of(
                &self.geometry.world,
                context.spatial,
                rect.to_float(),
                &corner_radii,
            )?,
            unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring,
            content_hash_except_rects: hasher.finish(),
            color,
            draws_recorded_color_with_source_over,
        })
    }

    fn place_runs_of_chunk(
        &self,
        chunk: &ListChunk,
        run_indices: &[RunIndexInChunk],
        placement_inputs_hash: ContentHash,
    ) -> ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace {
        let table = chunk.record_table();
        let mut record_ranges = Vec::new();
        let mut ranges_of_each_run = vec![PlacedRecordRangesOfRun::default(); chunk.runs().len()];
        for &run_index in run_indices {
            let run = &chunk.runs()[run_index.0 as usize];
            let record_indices_of_run = table.record_indices_of_run(run_index);
            let run_reach = self.reach_of_content_within(run.ink_bounds.to_float(), run.context);
            let first_binned_range_index = PlacedRecordRangeIndex(record_ranges.len() as u32);
            let mut reach_of_binned_ranges = Reach::Nothing;
            if run_reach != Reach::Nothing {
                if !self.geometry.world.draw_matrix(run.context.spatial).is_2d_affine() {
                    record_ranges.push(self.place_record_range(
                        chunk,
                        run_index,
                        record_indices_of_run.clone(),
                        run_reach,
                    ));
                    reach_of_binned_ranges = run_reach;
                } else {
                    for record_index in
                        (record_indices_of_run.start.0..record_indices_of_run.end.0).map(RecordIndexInChunk)
                    {
                        let record = table.record(record_index);
                        if !record.draws_something {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let record_reach = self.reach_of_content_within(record.bounding_rect.to_float(), run.context);
                        if record_reach == Reach::Nothing {
                            continue;
                        }
                        record_ranges.push(self.place_record_range(
                            chunk,
                            run_index,
                            record_index..RecordIndexInChunk(record_index.0 + 1),
                            record_reach,
                        ));
                        reach_of_binned_ranges = reach_of_binned_ranges.united(record_reach);
                    }
                }
            }
            let whole_run_range_index = PlacedRecordRangeIndex(record_ranges.len() as u32);
            record_ranges.push(self.place_record_range(chunk, run_index, record_indices_of_run, run_reach));
            ranges_of_each_run[run_index.0 as usize] = PlacedRecordRangesOfRun {
                first_binned_range_index,
                whole_run_range_index,
                reach_of_binned_ranges,
            };
        }
        ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace {
            placement_inputs_hash,
            record_ranges,
            ranges_of_each_run,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn placement_of_runs_of_chunk(
        &self,
        chunk_index: ChunkIndexInList,
        run_indices: &[RunIndexInChunk],
    ) -> Arc<ChunkPlacedInRasterSpace> {
        let chunk = self.list.display_list.chunk(chunk_index);
        let mut hasher = ContentHasher::new();
        for &run_index in run_indices {
            hasher.write_u32(run_index.0);
            hasher.write_content_hash(self.context_content_hash(
                chunk.runs()[run_index.0 as usize].context,
                EffectHashScope::WhatPlacingReads,
            ));
        }
        let placement_inputs_hash = hasher.finish();
        let (placement, newly_placed) = chunk.find_or_make_placement(placement_inputs_hash, || {
            self.place_runs_of_chunk(chunk, run_indices, placement_inputs_hash)
        });
        if newly_placed {
            self.chunks_placed.set(self.chunks_placed.get() + 1);
        }
        placement
    }
}

//! Works out what a tile holds over a part of its cell from its records, without rastering it.

use super::{
    BandBoundToListAndGeometry, BandTileKeys, KeyedTile, TileKeyingOfList, TileKeyingOfRasterSpace, TileReplayItem,
};
use crate::display_list::commands::{ClipMode, ClipNodeIndex, ContextRef, EffectNodeIndex};
use crate::display_list::effect_geometry::nearest_effects_at_or_above_where;
use crate::display_list::window_server_placement::RoundedRect;
use crate::visual_context::{ClipData, ClipNode, ClipNodeData, EffectNodeData};
use libgfx_rust::{Color, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, FloatRect, IntRect};
use std::collections::HashSet;

/// What a tile holds over a part of its cell, as its records tell without rastering it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TileCoverage {
    /// Every pixel of one color, which a raster gives exactly: the clear color of its layer, or an opaque one.
    OneColor(Color),
    /// Every pixel opaque, of more than one color.
    Opaque,
    Unknown,
}

impl TileCoverage {
    pub fn is_opaque(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            TileCoverage::OneColor(color) => color.alpha() == 255,
            TileCoverage::Opaque => true,
            TileCoverage::Unknown => false,
        }
    }

    fn under_plain_fill_of(self, color: Color) -> Self {
        match color.alpha() {
            255 => TileCoverage::OneColor(color),
            0 => self,
            _ if self.is_opaque() => TileCoverage::Opaque,
            _ => TileCoverage::Unknown,
        }
    }

    fn under_content_other_than_plain_fill(self, content_can_lower_destination_alpha: bool) -> Self {
        if self.is_opaque() && !content_can_lower_destination_alpha {
            TileCoverage::Opaque
        } else {
            TileCoverage::Unknown
        }
    }
}

/// The clips, and the effects whose output clips, a walk for the coverage of a tile found to leave its area unclipped,
/// so that walks of chains that share nodes stop where they meet.
#[derive(Default)]
struct WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped {
    clips: HashSet<ClipNodeIndex>,
    effects: HashSet<EffectNodeIndex>,
}

enum WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea {
    DrawsNothing,
    CoversItWith(Color),
}

impl RoundedRect {
    fn covers(&self, area: FloatRect) -> bool {
        self.rect.contains_rect(area) && !self.rounded_corner_reaches_into(area)
    }

    fn misses(&self, area: FloatRect) -> bool {
        self.rect.intersected(area).is_empty()
    }
}

impl TileKeyingOfList<'_> {
    /// Whether the effects that tiles apply at and around `effect` are plain groups.
    fn effects_applied_in_tiles_are_plain_groups(&self, effect: EffectNodeIndex) -> bool {
        if effect.is_none() {
            return true;
        }
        let nearest = self
            .nearest_composited_or_not_plain_effect_by_effect_index
            .get_or_init(|| {
                nearest_effects_at_or_above_where(self.tree, |effect, node| {
                    self.compositor_composites(effect)
                        || !matches!(&node.data, EffectNodeData::Effects(effects)
                            if effects.opacity == 1.0
                                && effects.filter.is_none()
                                && effects.backdrop_filter.is_none()
                                && effects.blend_mode == CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Normal)
                })
            })[effect.0 as usize];
        nearest.is_none() || self.compositor_composites(nearest)
    }

    /// Whether an effect that tiles apply at or around `effect` blends in a way that can lower the alpha below it.
    fn effects_applied_in_tiles_can_lower_destination_alpha(&self, effect: EffectNodeIndex) -> bool {
        if effect.is_none() {
            return false;
        }
        let nearest = self
            .nearest_composited_or_alpha_lowering_effect_by_effect_index
            .get_or_init(|| {
                nearest_effects_at_or_above_where(self.tree, |effect, node| {
                    self.compositor_composites(effect)
                        || matches!(&node.data, EffectNodeData::Effects(effects)
                            if effects.blend_mode.lowers_destination_alpha())
                })
            })[effect.0 as usize];
        !nearest.is_none() && !self.compositor_composites(nearest)
    }
}

impl TileKeyingOfRasterSpace<'_> {
    fn effect_chain_applied_in_tiles(&self, effect: EffectNodeIndex) -> impl Iterator<Item = EffectNodeIndex> {
        let tree = self.list.tree;
        std::iter::successors((!effect.is_none()).then_some(effect), move |effect| {
            Some(tree.effect_nodes[effect.0 as usize].parent).filter(|parent| !parent.is_none())
        })
        .take_while(|&effect| !self.list.compositor_composites(effect))
    }

    fn clip_node_leaves_area_unclipped(&self, node: &ClipNode, area_in_device_pixels: FloatRect) -> bool {
        let ClipNodeData::Rect(ClipData {
            rect,
            corner_radii,
            mode: ClipMode::Intersect,
        }) = &node.data
        else {
            return false;
        };
        !node.clips_everything
            && RoundedRect::device_aligned_of(&self.geometry.world, node.spatial, *rect, corner_radii)
                .is_some_and(|rect| rect.covers(area_in_device_pixels))
    }

    fn clip_chain_leaves_area_unclipped(
        &self,
        clip: ClipNodeIndex,
        area_in_device_pixels: FloatRect,
        known: &mut WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped,
    ) -> bool {
        let tree = self.list.tree;
        let mut clips_walked = Vec::new();
        let mut clip = clip;
        while !clip.is_none() && !known.clips.contains(&clip) {
            let node = &tree.clip_nodes[clip.0 as usize];
            if !self.geometry.clip_is_left_to_composite(clip)
                && !self.clip_node_leaves_area_unclipped(node, area_in_device_pixels)
            {
                return false;
            }
            clips_walked.push(clip);
            clip = node.parent;
        }
        known.clips.extend(clips_walked);
        true
    }

    fn output_clips_of_effects_applied_in_tiles_leave_area_unclipped(
        &self,
        effect: EffectNodeIndex,
        area_in_device_pixels: FloatRect,
        known: &mut WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped,
    ) -> bool {
        let mut effects_walked = Vec::new();
        for effect in self.effect_chain_applied_in_tiles(effect) {
            if known.effects.contains(&effect) {
                break;
            }
            if !self.clip_chain_leaves_area_unclipped(
                self.list.effect_clips.output_clip(effect),
                area_in_device_pixels,
                known,
            ) {
                return false;
            }
            effects_walked.push(effect);
        }
        known.effects.extend(effects_walked);
        true
    }

    fn context_applies_no_clip_or_effect_within(
        &self,
        context: ContextRef,
        area_in_device_pixels: FloatRect,
        known: &mut WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped,
    ) -> bool {
        let backface_culled = self
            .geometry
            .world
            .backface_culled
            .get(context.spatial.0 as usize)
            .copied()
            .unwrap_or(false);
        !backface_culled
            && self.list.effects_applied_in_tiles_are_plain_groups(context.effect)
            && self.clip_chain_leaves_area_unclipped(context.clip, area_in_device_pixels, known)
            && self.output_clips_of_effects_applied_in_tiles_leave_area_unclipped(
                context.effect,
                area_in_device_pixels,
                known,
            )
    }

    fn what_one_fill_item_does_within_area(
        &self,
        bound_band: &BandBoundToListAndGeometry,
        item: TileReplayItem,
        area_in_device_pixels: FloatRect,
        known: &mut WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped,
    ) -> Option<WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea> {
        let TileReplayItem::PlacedRecordRange {
            chunk_index,
            range_index,
        } = item
        else {
            return None;
        };
        let range = bound_band.placed_record_range(chunk_index, range_index);
        let fill = range.device_aligned_fill.as_ref()?;
        // The inner rect's corners curve only within the outer rect's corners.
        let area_is_inside_unfilled_inner_rect = fill.rect.covers(area_in_device_pixels)
            && fill
                .unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring
                .is_some_and(|unfilled_inner_rect| unfilled_inner_rect.covers(area_in_device_pixels));
        if (fill.rect.misses(area_in_device_pixels) || area_is_inside_unfilled_inner_rect)
            && range.is_spread_by_no_filter
        {
            return Some(WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea::DrawsNothing);
        }
        let fill_covers_area = fill.rect.covers(area_in_device_pixels)
            && fill
                .unfilled_inner_rect_of_ring
                .is_none_or(|unfilled_inner_rect| unfilled_inner_rect.misses(area_in_device_pixels));
        (fill_covers_area
            && fill.draws_recorded_color_with_source_over
            && self.context_applies_no_clip_or_effect_within(range.context, area_in_device_pixels, known))
        .then_some(WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea::CoversItWith(fill.color))
    }

    fn item_can_lower_destination_alpha(&self, bound_band: &BandBoundToListAndGeometry, item: TileReplayItem) -> bool {
        let chunk = self.list.display_list.chunk(item.chunk_index());
        self.records_of_item(bound_band, item).iter().any(|record| {
            let context = chunk.runs()[record.run_index.0 as usize].context;
            record.can_lower_destination_alpha
                || self
                    .list
                    .effects_applied_in_tiles_can_lower_destination_alpha(context.effect)
        })
    }

    /// What a raster of `tile` holds over `area` of its cell, in the device pixels of the space, as its replay items
    /// tell in paint order from `clear_color`, the color its layer's surface starts as.
    pub fn coverage_of_tile(
        &self,
        band_tile_keys: &BandTileKeys,
        tile: &KeyedTile,
        area: IntRect,
        clear_color: Color,
    ) -> TileCoverage {
        let bound_band = &band_tile_keys.bound_band;
        if self.list.replays_every_record_into_every_tile || area.is_empty() {
            return TileCoverage::Unknown;
        }
        // Fills are walked in list order, which depth-sorted planes are not replayed in.
        if self.list.tree_sorts_planes_by_depth
            && tile
                .replay_items_in_paint_order
                .iter()
                .any(|&item| self.root_of_context_sorting_item_by_depth(bound_band, item).is_some())
        {
            return TileCoverage::Unknown;
        }
        let area_in_device_pixels = area.to_float();
        let mut known_to_leave_area_unclipped = WhatLeavesAreaOfTileUnclipped::default();
        let mut coverage = TileCoverage::OneColor(clear_color);
        for &item in &tile.replay_items_in_paint_order {
            if matches!(item, TileReplayItem::PlacedRecordRange { .. })
                && bound_band.reach_of_item(item).part_of(area).is_empty()
            {
                continue;
            }
            coverage = match self.what_one_fill_item_does_within_area(
                bound_band,
                item,
                area_in_device_pixels,
                &mut known_to_leave_area_unclipped,
            ) {
                Some(WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea::DrawsNothing) => coverage,
                Some(WhatOneFillDoesWithinArea::CoversItWith(color)) => coverage.under_plain_fill_of(color),
                None => coverage
                    .under_content_other_than_plain_fill(self.item_can_lower_destination_alpha(bound_band, item)),
            };
            if coverage == TileCoverage::Unknown {
                break;
            }
        }
        coverage
    }
}

/*

use libgfx_rust::IntRect;
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

pub const TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS: i32 = 1024;
pub const TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS: i32 = 512;
/// How far past its part of a cell a tile holds what lies around it, so that a tile shown scaled or at a fraction of a
/// pixel blends its edges with the pixels of the tiles beside it instead of repeating its own edge.
pub const TILE_BORDER_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS: i32 = 1;
const MAXIMUM_CELLS_CONTENT_IS_FOLLOWED_INTO_ONE_BY_ONE: u64 = 4096;

/// A cell of the tile grid of a layer's raster space, which starts at the space's origin.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct TileCoord {
    pub column: i32,
    pub row: i32,
}

impl TileCoord {
    pub const fn new(column: i32, row: i32) -> Self {
        Self { column, row }
    }

    /// The cell that holds the device pixel at `x` and `y`.
    pub const fn of_pixel(x: i32, y: i32) -> Self {
        Self::new(
            x.div_euclid(TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS),
            y.div_euclid(TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS),
        )
    }

    pub const fn cell_rect(self) -> IntRect {
        IntRect::new(
            self.column * TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
            self.row * TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
            TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
            TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
        )
    }
}

/// `part_of_cell` with the border its tile holds around it.
pub const fn with_tile_border(part_of_cell: IntRect) -> IntRect {
    let border = TILE_BORDER_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS;
    part_of_cell.inflated_edges(border, border, border, border)
}

impl Ord for TileCoord {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
        (self.row, self.column).cmp(&(other.row, other.column))
    }
}

impl PartialOrd for TileCoord {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
        Some(self.cmp(other))
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for TileCoord {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "({},{})", self.column, self.row)
    }
}

/// The cells from a first to a last column and from a first to a last row. It holds no cell where a last column or row
/// comes before the first.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct CellRange {
    pub first_row: i32,
    pub last_row: i32,
    pub first_column: i32,
    pub last_column: i32,
}

impl Default for CellRange {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::NONE
    }
}

impl CellRange {
    pub const NONE: Self = Self {
        first_row: 0,
        last_row: -1,
        first_column: 0,
        last_column: -1,
    };

    /// The cells that `rect` reaches into.
    pub fn touched_by(rect: IntRect) -> Self {
        if rect.is_empty() {
            return Self::NONE;
        }
        let first = TileCoord::of_pixel(rect.x, rect.y);
        let last = TileCoord::of_pixel(rect.right() - 1, rect.bottom() - 1);
        Self {
            first_row: first.row,
            last_row: last.row,
            first_column: first.column,
            last_column: last.column,
        }
    }

    /// The cells at most `distance` columns and `distance` rows away from `center`.
    pub fn around(center: TileCoord, distance: i32) -> Self {
        Self {
            first_row: center.row.saturating_sub(distance),
            last_row: center.row.saturating_add(distance),
            first_column: center.column.saturating_sub(distance),
            last_column: center.column.saturating_add(distance),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.last_row < self.first_row || self.last_column < self.first_column
    }

    /// The rect its cells cover, which is empty where it holds no cell.
    pub fn rect(self) -> IntRect {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return IntRect::default();
        }
        TileCoord::new(self.first_column, self.first_row)
            .cell_rect()
            .united(TileCoord::new(self.last_column, self.last_row).cell_rect())
    }

    pub fn row_count(self) -> u64 {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return 0;
        }
        (i64::from(self.last_row) - i64::from(self.first_row) + 1) as u64
    }

    pub fn cell_count(self) -> u64 {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return 0;
        }
        self.row_count() * (i64::from(self.last_column) - i64::from(self.first_column) + 1) as u64
    }

    pub fn holds_every_cell_of(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        other.is_empty()
            || (self.first_row <= other.first_row
                && other.last_row <= self.last_row
                && self.first_column <= other.first_column
                && other.last_column <= self.last_column)
    }

    pub fn contains(self, coord: TileCoord) -> bool {
        (self.first_row..=self.last_row).contains(&coord.row)
            && (self.first_column..=self.last_column).contains(&coord.column)
    }

    pub fn contains_range(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        other.is_empty()
            || (self.first_row <= other.first_row
                && other.last_row <= self.last_row
                && self.first_column <= other.first_column
                && other.last_column <= self.last_column)
    }

    pub fn intersected(self, other: Self) -> Self {
        let intersection = Self {
            first_row: self.first_row.max(other.first_row),
            last_row: self.last_row.min(other.last_row),
            first_column: self.first_column.max(other.first_column),
            last_column: self.last_column.min(other.last_column),
        };
        if intersection.is_empty() {
            return Self::NONE;
        }
        intersection
    }

    /// Its cells, row by row.
    pub fn coords(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = TileCoord> {
        let columns = self.first_column..=self.last_column;
        (self.first_row..=self.last_row)
            .flat_map(move |row| columns.clone().map(move |column| TileCoord::new(column, row)))
    }
}

/// The cells that `rect` reaches into, row by row. A caller bounds `rect` first, since a rect far larger than the
/// viewport reaches into a great many cells; to find what a map holds within a rect of any size, it uses
/// `entries_within` or `for_each_entry_within`.
pub fn tile_coords_touching(rect: IntRect) -> impl Iterator<Item = TileCoord> {
    CellRange::touched_by(rect).coords()
}

/// Whether content within `rect` reaches too many cells to be followed into each of them, and is taken to reach every
/// cell it can instead.
pub fn reaches_too_many_cells_to_follow_one_by_one(rect: IntRect) -> bool {
    tile_count_touching(rect) > MAXIMUM_CELLS_CONTENT_IS_FOLLOWED_INTO_ONE_BY_ONE
}

/// How many cells `rect` reaches into.
pub fn tile_count_touching(rect: IntRect) -> u64 {
    CellRange::touched_by(rect).cell_count()
}

// A map is looked up row by row where the range has no more rows than the map has entries, and walked whole otherwise,
// so that a range of many more cells than the map holds costs no more than the map.
fn looks_up_rows_of_range<V>(cells: &BTreeMap<TileCoord, V>, range: CellRange) -> bool {
    range.row_count() <= cells.len() as u64
}

fn first_and_last_coord_of_row(range: CellRange, row: i32) -> std::ops::RangeInclusive<TileCoord> {
    TileCoord::new(range.first_column, row)..=TileCoord::new(range.last_column, row)
}

/// The entries of `cells` within `range`, row by row. It costs no more than the rows of `range` or the entries of
/// `cells`, whichever are fewer, and not the cells of `range`.
pub fn entries_within<V>(cells: &BTreeMap<TileCoord, V>, range: CellRange) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&TileCoord, &V)> {
    let looks_up_rows = looks_up_rows_of_range(cells, range);
    let rows_looked_up = (looks_up_rows && !range.is_empty()).then(|| {
        (range.first_row..=range.last_row).flat_map(move |row| cells.range(first_and_last_coord_of_row(range, row)))
    });
    let entries_walked = (!looks_up_rows).then(|| cells.iter().filter(move |(coord, _)| range.contains(**coord)));
    rows_looked_up
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .chain(entries_walked.into_iter().flatten())
}

/// Visits the entries of `cells` within `range`, row by row, at the cost `entries_within` has.
pub fn for_each_entry_within<V>(
    cells: &mut BTreeMap<TileCoord, V>,
    range: CellRange,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(TileCoord, &mut V),
) {
    if range.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    if !looks_up_rows_of_range(cells, range) {
        for (coord, value) in cells.iter_mut().filter(|(coord, _)| range.contains(**coord)) {
            visit(*coord, value);
        }
        return;
    }
    for row in range.first_row..=range.last_row {
        for (coord, value) in cells.range_mut(first_and_last_coord_of_row(range, row)) {
            visit(*coord, value);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_rect_touches_the_cells_it_reaches_into_row_by_row() {
        let coords: Vec<TileCoord> = tile_coords_touching(IntRect::new(
            TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS - 6,
            10,
            TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS + 44,
            TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS - 6,
        ))
        .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            coords,
            [
                TileCoord::new(0, 0),
                TileCoord::new(1, 0),
                TileCoord::new(2, 0),
                TileCoord::new(0, 1),
                TileCoord::new(1, 1),
                TileCoord::new(2, 1),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rect_ending_on_a_cell_edge_does_not_touch_the_next_cell() {
        let coords: Vec<TileCoord> = tile_coords_touching(IntRect::new(
            0,
            0,
            TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
            2 * TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
        ))
        .collect();
        assert_eq!(coords, [TileCoord::new(0, 0), TileCoord::new(0, 1)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cells_left_of_and_above_the_origin_have_negative_coords() {
        let coords: Vec<TileCoord> =
            tile_coords_touching(IntRect::new(-1, -TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS - 1, 2, 1)).collect();
        assert_eq!(coords, [TileCoord::new(-1, -2), TileCoord::new(0, -2)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_rect_touches_no_cell() {
        assert_eq!(tile_coords_touching(IntRect::new(10, 10, 0, 20)).count(), 0);
        assert!(CellRange::touched_by(IntRect::new(10, 10, 0, 20)).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(CellRange::default(), CellRange::NONE);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_entries_within_a_range_are_alike_whether_rows_are_looked_up_or_every_entry_is_walked() {
        let held: BTreeMap<TileCoord, u32> = [(-3, -2), (0, 0), (1, 0), (5, 0), (0, 1), (2, 7), (9, 9)]
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, (column, row))| (TileCoord::new(column, row), index as u32))
            .collect();
        let ranges = [
            CellRange::touched_by(IntRect::new(
                0,
                0,
                2 * TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
                2 * TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
            )),
            CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(0, 0), 3),
            CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(4, 4), 1 << 20),
            CellRange::touched_by(IntRect::new(-(1 << 28), -(1 << 28), 1 << 29, 1 << 29)),
            CellRange::NONE,
        ];
        for range in ranges {
            let expected: Vec<(TileCoord, u32)> = held
                .iter()
                .filter(|(coord, _)| range.contains(**coord))
                .map(|(coord, value)| (*coord, *value))
                .collect();
            let found: Vec<(TileCoord, u32)> = entries_within(&held, range)
                .map(|(coord, value)| (*coord, *value))
                .collect();
            assert_eq!(found, expected);
            let mut visited = Vec::new();
            for_each_entry_within(&mut held.clone(), range, |coord, value| visited.push((coord, *value)));
            assert_eq!(visited, expected);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_window_around_a_cell_holds_the_cells_at_most_its_distance_away() {
        let window = CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(10, -4), 2);
        assert_eq!(window.cell_count(), 25);
        assert!(window.contains(TileCoord::new(8, -6)) && window.contains(TileCoord::new(12, -2)));
        assert!(!window.contains(TileCoord::new(13, -4)));
        assert!(window.contains_range(CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(11, -3), 1)));
        assert!(!window.contains_range(CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(12, -4), 1)));
        assert_eq!(
            window.intersected(CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(13, -4), 1)),
            CellRange::touched_by(IntRect::new(
                12 * TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
                -5 * TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
                TILE_WIDTH_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS,
                3 * TILE_HEIGHT_IN_DEVICE_PIXELS
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            window.intersected(CellRange::around(TileCoord::new(20, 0), 1)),
            CellRange::NONE
        );
    }
}

//! Checks a display list tape that comes from another process before anything reads it. A tape that passes has
//! well formed records, valid enum and bool bytes, and spans inside their payloads, so the typed reads that replay,
//! damage and the player make of it are sound. The tape of a page and that of a 2D canvas each hold only the
//! commands of their own kind.

use super::builder::{COMMAND_ALIGNMENT, HEADER_SIZE, bounding_rect_computed_from_payload, read_header};
use super::commands::*;
use libgfx_rust::filter::Filter;
use libgfx_rust::{
    CapStyle, Color, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, GlyphRunOrientation, GradientInterpolationMethod,
    GradientInterpolationType, HueInterpolationMethod, IntRect, InterpolationColorSpace, JoinStyle, LineStyle,
    MaskKind, Orientation, PolarColorSpace, RectangularColorSpace, ScalingMode, ShouldAntiAlias, WindingRule,
};
use std::mem::{align_of, offset_of, size_of};

pub type ValidationError = &'static str;

const RUN_SIZE: usize = size_of::<DisplayListCommandRun>();

// An enum that a tape stores as its raw discriminant.
trait TapeEnum {
    const SIZE: usize;
    fn is_valid(raw: i64) -> bool;
}

macro_rules! tape_enum {
    ($name:ident as $repr:ty { $($variant:ident),+ $(,)? }) => {
        impl TapeEnum for $name {
            const SIZE: usize = size_of::<$repr>();
            fn is_valid(raw: i64) -> bool {
                // A variant added to the enum does not compile here until it is listed.
                fn _every_variant_is_listed(value: $name) {
                    match value {
                        $($name::$variant => {})+
                    }
                }
                $(raw == $name::$variant as $repr as i64)||+
            }
        }
    };
}

tape_enum!(InlineClipKind as u8 { Rect, RoundedRect, Path });
tape_enum!(ClipMode as u8 { Intersect, Difference });
tape_enum!(PathPaintKind as u8 { Color, PaintStyle });
tape_enum!(DisplayListPaintStyleType as u8 { None, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, Pattern });
tape_enum!(DisplayListGradientSpreadMethod as u8 { Pad, Repeat, Reflect });
tape_enum!(Canvas2DPaintKind as u8 {
    Color,
    LinearGradient,
    RadialGradient,
    ConicGradient,
    Pattern,
});
tape_enum!(Canvas2DPatternRepetition as u8 { Repeat, RepeatX, RepeatY, NoRepeat });
tape_enum!(WindingRule as i32 { Nonzero, EvenOdd });
tape_enum!(LineStyle as u8 { Solid, Dotted, Dashed });
tape_enum!(ScalingMode as i32 { None, Bilinear, BilinearMipmap, NearestNeighbor });
tape_enum!(MaskKind as i32 { Alpha, Luminance });
tape_enum!(ShouldAntiAlias as u8 { Yes, No });
tape_enum!(InterpolationColorSpace as i32 { LinearRGB, SRGB });
tape_enum!(CapStyle as i32 { Butt, Round, Square });
tape_enum!(JoinStyle as i32 { Miter, Round, Bevel });
tape_enum!(Orientation as i32 { Horizontal, Vertical });
tape_enum!(GlyphRunOrientation as i32 { Horizontal, Vertical, VerticalCounterclockwise });
tape_enum!(GradientInterpolationType as u8 { Rectangular, Polar });
tape_enum!(RectangularColorSpace as u8 {
    Srgb,
    SrgbLinear,
    DisplayP3,
    DisplayP3Linear,
    A98Rgb,
    ProphotoRgb,
    Rec2020,
    Lab,
    Oklab,
    Xyz,
    XyzD50,
    XyzD65,
});
tape_enum!(PolarColorSpace as u8 { Hsl, Hwb, Lch, Oklch });
tape_enum!(HueInterpolationMethod as u8 { Shorter, Longer, Increasing, Decreasing });

impl TapeEnum for CompositingAndBlendingOperator {
    const SIZE: usize = size_of::<i32>();
    fn is_valid(raw: i64) -> bool {
        i32::try_from(raw).ok().and_then(Self::from_i32).is_some()
    }
}

// The bytes of one command payload. Offsets are relative to the payload start, where the command struct begins.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Payload<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
}

impl Payload<'_> {
    fn u8_at(self, offset: usize) -> u8 {
        self.bytes[offset]
    }

    fn u32_at(self, offset: usize) -> u32 {
        u32::from_ne_bytes(self.bytes[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    fn u64_at(self, offset: usize) -> u64 {
        u64::from_ne_bytes(self.bytes[offset..offset + 8].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    fn i32_at(self, offset: usize) -> i32 {
        i32::from_ne_bytes(self.bytes[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    fn f32_at(self, offset: usize) -> f32 {
        f32::from_ne_bytes(self.bytes[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    fn bool_at(self, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
        if self.u8_at(offset) > 1 {
            return Err("Display list command has an invalid bool");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn enum_at<E: TapeEnum>(self, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
        let raw = match E::SIZE {
            1 => i64::from(self.u8_at(offset)),
            4 => i64::from(self.i32_at(offset)),
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        if !E::is_valid(raw) {
            return Err("Display list command has an invalid enum value");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // A span of opaque bytes, which must lie inside the payload.
    fn span_at(self, offset: usize) -> Result<(usize, usize), ValidationError> {
        let start = self.u32_at(offset + offset_of!(DisplayListDataSpan, offset)) as usize;
        let size = self.u32_at(offset + offset_of!(DisplayListDataSpan, size)) as usize;
        if start.checked_add(size).is_none_or(|end| end > self.bytes.len()) {
            return Err("Display list span exceeds its command payload");
        }
        Ok((start, size))
    }

    // A span that holds a serialized filter graph, which the player builds without checking it.
    fn filter_span_at(self, offset: usize) -> Result<Filter, ValidationError> {
        let (start, size) = self.span_at(offset)?;
        Filter::deserialize(&self.bytes[start..start + size]).ok_or("Display list command has a malformed filter")
    }

    // A span of `T` values, which the player reads in place.
    fn array_span_at<T>(self, offset: usize) -> Result<usize, ValidationError> {
        let (start, size) = self.span_at(offset)?;
        if !size.is_multiple_of(size_of::<T>()) || !start.is_multiple_of(align_of::<T>()) {
            return Err("Display list array span is not a whole number of aligned values");
        }
        Ok(size / size_of::<T>())
    }
}

// Collects the nested record spans of one payload, which must not overlap each other, the command struct or the
// tail entries. Each nested byte then belongs to one record stream, and checking every stream stays linear.
struct NestedSpans<'a> {
    payload: Payload<'a>,
    struct_size: usize,
    entries_offset: usize,
    spans: Vec<(usize, usize)>,
}

impl NestedSpans<'_> {
    fn add(&mut self, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
        let (start, size) = self.payload.span_at(offset)?;
        if size == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if !start.is_multiple_of(COMMAND_ALIGNMENT) || !size.is_multiple_of(COMMAND_ALIGNMENT) {
            return Err("Nested display list records are not aligned");
        }
        if start < self.struct_size || start + size > self.entries_offset {
            return Err("Nested display list records overlap their command");
        }
        if self
            .spans
            .iter()
            .any(|&(other_start, other_size)| start < other_start + other_size && other_start < start + size)
        {
            return Err("Nested display list records overlap each other");
        }
        self.spans.push((start, size));
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn validate_color_stops(payload: Payload, offset: usize, must_have_stops: bool) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    let colors = payload.array_span_at::<Color>(offset + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientColorStops, colors))?;
    let positions = payload.array_span_at::<f32>(offset + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientColorStops, positions))?;
    payload.bool_at(offset + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientColorStops, repeating))?;
    if colors != positions {
        return Err("Display list gradient has a different number of colors and positions");
    }
    if must_have_stops && colors == 0 {
        return Err("Display list gradient has no color stops");
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_interpolation_method(payload: Payload, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    payload
        .enum_at::<GradientInterpolationType>(offset + offset_of!(GradientInterpolationMethod, interpolation_type))?;
    payload
        .enum_at::<RectangularColorSpace>(offset + offset_of!(GradientInterpolationMethod, rectangular_color_space))?;
    payload.enum_at::<PolarColorSpace>(offset + offset_of!(GradientInterpolationMethod, polar_color_space))?;
    payload
        .enum_at::<HueInterpolationMethod>(offset + offset_of!(GradientInterpolationMethod, hue_interpolation_method))
}

fn validate_optional_at(payload: Payload, offset: usize, has_value_offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    payload.bool_at(offset + has_value_offset)
}

fn validate_paint_style(
    payload: Payload,
    offset: usize,
    paint_kind_offset: usize,
    nested: &mut NestedSpans,
) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    payload.enum_at::<PathPaintKind>(paint_kind_offset)?;
    let style_type_offset = offset + offset_of!(DisplayListPaintStyle, paint_style_type);
    payload.enum_at::<DisplayListPaintStyleType>(style_type_offset)?;
    let gradient = offset + offset_of!(DisplayListPaintStyle, gradient);
    validate_optional_at(
        payload,
        gradient + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientPaintStyle, gradient_transform),
        offset_of!(OptionalAffineTransform, has_value),
    )?;
    payload.enum_at::<DisplayListGradientSpreadMethod>(
        gradient + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientPaintStyle, spread_method),
    )?;
    payload.enum_at::<InterpolationColorSpace>(gradient + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientPaintStyle, color_space))?;
    validate_color_stops(
        payload,
        gradient + offset_of!(DisplayListGradientPaintStyle, color_stops),
        false,
    )?;
    validate_optional_at(
        payload,
        offset + offset_of!(DisplayListPaintStyle, pattern_transform),
        offset_of!(OptionalAffineTransform, has_value),
    )?;
    let pattern_tile = offset + offset_of!(DisplayListPaintStyle, pattern_tile);
    let paints_pattern = payload.u8_at(paint_kind_offset) == PathPaintKind::PaintStyle as u8
        && payload.u8_at(style_type_offset) == DisplayListPaintStyleType::Pattern as u8;
    if paints_pattern {
        nested.add(pattern_tile)
    } else {
        payload.span_at(pattern_tile).map(|_| ())
    }
}

// The runs must split the glyphs exactly, since the player hands each run the glyphs that follow the previous run.
fn validate_canvas_2d_glyph_runs(payload: Payload) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    const MISMATCH: ValidationError = "Canvas glyph runs do not cover their glyphs";

    let run_count = payload.array_span_at::<Canvas2DGlyphRun>(offset_of!(Canvas2DDrawGlyphRuns, runs))?;
    let glyph_count = payload.array_span_at::<DisplayListGlyph>(offset_of!(Canvas2DDrawGlyphRuns, glyphs))?;
    let (runs_start, _) = payload.span_at(offset_of!(Canvas2DDrawGlyphRuns, runs))?;
    let mut remaining_glyphs = glyph_count as u64;
    for run in 0..run_count {
        let run_offset = runs_start + run * size_of::<Canvas2DGlyphRun>();
        let run_glyph_count = payload.u64_at(run_offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DGlyphRun, glyph_count));
        remaining_glyphs = remaining_glyphs.checked_sub(run_glyph_count).ok_or(MISMATCH)?;
    }
    if remaining_glyphs != 0 {
        return Err(MISMATCH);
    }
    if !payload
        .f32_at(offset_of!(Canvas2DDrawGlyphRuns, horizontal_scale))
        .is_finite()
    {
        return Err("Canvas glyph runs have a horizontal scale that is not finite");
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_canvas_2d_paint(payload: Payload, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    payload.enum_at::<Canvas2DPaintKind>(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DPaint, kind))?;
    payload.enum_at::<Canvas2DPatternRepetition>(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DPaint, pattern_repetition))?;
    payload.bool_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DPaint, pattern_has_image))?;
    validate_color_stops(payload, offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DPaint, color_stops), false)?;
    validate_optional_at(
        payload,
        offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DPaint, pattern_transform),
        offset_of!(OptionalAffineTransform, has_value),
    )
}

fn validate_canvas_2d_compositing(payload: Payload, offset: usize) -> Result<(), ValidationError> {
    payload.span_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, filter))?;
    payload.bool_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, has_filter))?;
    if payload.u8_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, has_filter)) != 0 {
        // A canvas filter comes from CSS filter functions, which draw no images, so the player has none to give it.
        let filter = payload.filter_span_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, filter))?;
        let mut draws_an_image = false;
        filter.for_each_image_frame_id(&mut |_| draws_an_image = true);
        if draws_an_image {
            return Err("Canvas 2D stream command has a filter that draws an image");
        }
    }
    // The player turns the global alpha into a byte, which only a value from 0 to 1 converts to.
    let global_alpha = payload.f32_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, global_alpha));
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&global_alpha) {
        return Err("Canvas 2D stream command has a global alpha outside 0 to 1");
    }
    payload.enum_at::<CompositingAndBlendingOperator>(
        offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, compositing_and_blending_operator),
    )?;
    payload.bool_at(offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, has_shadow))?;
    let shadow_offset = offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DCompositing, shadow);
    let shadow_offset_x = payload.f32_at(shadow_offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DShadow, offset_x));
    let shadow_offset_y = payload.f32_at(shadow_offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DShadow, offset_y));
    let shadow_blur = payload.f32_at(shadow_offset + offset_of!(Canvas2DShadow, blur));
    if !shadow_offset_x.is_finite() || !shadow_offset_y.is_finite() || !(shadow_blur.is_finite() && shadow_blur >= 0.0)
    {
        return Err("Canvas 2D stream command has a shadow with an offset or blur that is not finite or is negative");
    }
    Ok(())
}
