//! The framing of the WebGL command stream: how a struct and the data that belongs to it become the bytes of a record
//! or of a synchronous call, and back.

use core::mem::size_of;
use core::ptr;

use super::vocabulary::{CommandType, SyncCallType};

/// Records start at multiples of this many bytes, and so does the data that follows a struct, counted from the start
/// of the struct.
pub const RECORD_ALIGNMENT: usize = 16;

/// What precedes the struct of a record and of a request: its type as a `u16`, two unused bytes, and the number of
/// bytes that follow the header as a `u32`.
pub const HEADER_SIZE: usize = 8;
pub const HEADER_PAYLOAD_SIZE_OFFSET: usize = 4;

/// `size` bytes that start `offset` bytes after the start of the struct that has the span as a field.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct DataSpan {
    pub offset: u32,
    pub size: u32,
}

impl DataSpan {
    pub const EMPTY: Self = Self { offset: 0, size: 0 };

    pub fn following<S: WireStruct>(data: InlineData<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset: const { offset_of_data_following_struct(size_of::<S>()) },
            // NB: Data of 4 GiB or more has no span. It has no `FramedSize` either, so the recorder refuses what it
            //     would be sent in, and the size that stands in for the real one here is never sent.
            size: u32::try_from(data.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
        }
    }
}

const fn offset_of_data_following_struct(struct_size: usize) -> u32 {
    let offset = struct_size.next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT);
    assert!(offset <= u32::MAX as usize);
    offset as u32
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The type is `repr(C)`, made of numbers, booleans and [`DataSpan`]s, and has no byte that is not part of a field.
/// `BOOL_FIELD_OFFSETS` lists where its booleans are.
pub unsafe trait WireStruct: Copy + 'static {
    /// A struct is built from it, so that the bytes that the C ABI leaves unused between its fields, which are fields
    /// of their own here, do not have to be named.
    const ZEROED: Self;
    const BOOL_FIELD_OFFSETS: &'static [usize] = &[];

    fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: Per the contract of the trait every byte of the struct is initialized.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(ptr::from_ref(self).cast::<u8>(), size_of::<Self>()) }
    }

    /// The struct that a payload starts with. None where the payload is shorter than the struct, or where it has
    /// another byte than 0 or 1 for a boolean.
    fn read_from(payload: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
        if payload.len() < size_of::<Self>() || Self::BOOL_FIELD_OFFSETS.iter().any(|&offset| payload[offset] > 1) {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: The bytes are as many as the struct has, and per the contract of the trait and the check above they
        //         are a value of it.
        Some(unsafe { ptr::read_unaligned(payload.as_ptr().cast::<Self>()) })
    }
}

pub trait Command: WireStruct {
    const TYPE: CommandType;
}

pub trait SyncRequest: WireStruct {
    const TYPE: SyncCallType;
    type Reply: SyncReply;
}

/// # Safety
///
/// Every bit pattern is a value of the type.
pub unsafe trait SyncReply: WireStruct {
    fn from_reply_bytes(reply: &[u8]) -> Self {
        assert!(
            reply.len() >= size_of::<Self>(),
            "the reply to a WebGL call is shorter than its struct"
        );
        // SAFETY: The bytes are as many as the struct has, and per the contract of the trait any bytes are a value
        //         of it.
        unsafe { ptr::read_unaligned(reply.as_ptr().cast::<Self>()) }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum InlineData<'a> {
    /// No bytes take no room at all, not even for the alignment of what would follow.
    Bytes(&'a [u8]),
    /// The stream has a NUL after the bytes.
    NulTerminated(&'a [u8]),
}

impl InlineData<'_> {
    pub const NONE: Self = Self::Bytes(&[]);

    pub fn len(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Bytes(bytes) => bytes.len(),
            Self::NulTerminated(bytes) => bytes.len() + 1,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `destination` is valid for writes of `self.len()` bytes that do not overlap the data.
    unsafe fn write_to(self, destination: *mut u8) {
        let (Self::Bytes(bytes) | Self::NulTerminated(bytes)) = self;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides room for the bytes, and for the terminator after them.
        unsafe {
            ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), destination, bytes.len());
            if matches!(self, Self::NulTerminated(_)) {
                destination.add(bytes.len()).write(0);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn payload_layout_size(struct_size: usize, inline_data_size: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    match inline_data_size {
        0 => Some(struct_size),
        inline_data_size => struct_size
            .checked_next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT)?
            .checked_add(inline_data_size),
    }
}

/// There is none for a struct with 4 GiB of data or more, as the header says in a `u32` how many bytes follow it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct FramedSize {
    size_with_header: usize,
    size_after_header: u32,
}

impl FramedSize {
    fn with_size_after_header(size_after_header: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(Self {
            size_with_header: HEADER_SIZE.checked_add(size_after_header)?,
            size_after_header: u32::try_from(size_after_header).ok()?,
        })
    }

    /// A record is padded to the alignment of records as a whole.
    fn of_record(struct_size: usize, inline_data_size: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        let size_with_header = HEADER_SIZE
            .checked_add(payload_layout_size(struct_size, inline_data_size)?)?
            .checked_next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT)?;
        Self::with_size_after_header(size_with_header - HEADER_SIZE)
    }

    /// What follows the header of a request is padded to the alignment of records.
    fn of_sync_request(struct_size: usize, inline_data_size: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        let size_after_header =
            payload_layout_size(struct_size, inline_data_size)?.checked_next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT)?;
        Self::with_size_after_header(size_after_header)
    }
}

pub fn padded_record_size(struct_size: usize, inline_data_size: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    FramedSize::of_record(struct_size, inline_data_size).map(|size| size.size_with_header)
}

/// Writes a header, a struct and its data, and zeroes what is left of the size, so that no byte of the stream is one
/// that happened to be in memory.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `size` is that of the struct with the data, and `destination` is valid for writes of as many bytes, which overlap
/// neither the struct nor the data.
unsafe fn write_framed(
    destination: *mut u8,
    size: FramedSize,
    type_number: u16,
    payload: &[u8],
    inline_data: InlineData<'_>,
) {
    let mut header = [0; HEADER_SIZE];
    header[..2].copy_from_slice(&type_number.to_ne_bytes());
    header[HEADER_PAYLOAD_SIZE_OFFSET..].copy_from_slice(&size.size_after_header.to_ne_bytes());

    let mut written = HEADER_SIZE + payload.len();
    // SAFETY: The caller provides the bytes of the size, and every write below stays inside the layout that
    //         payload_layout_size() computes, which the size covers.
    unsafe {
        ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(header.as_ptr(), destination, HEADER_SIZE);
        ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(payload.as_ptr(), destination.add(HEADER_SIZE), payload.len());
        if !inline_data.is_empty() {
            let inline_data_offset = HEADER_SIZE + payload.len().next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT);
            ptr::write_bytes(destination.add(written), 0, inline_data_offset - written);
            inline_data.write_to(destination.add(inline_data_offset));
            written = inline_data_offset + inline_data.len();
        }
        ptr::write_bytes(destination.add(written), 0, size.size_with_header - written);
    }
}

pub struct Record<'a> {
    command_type: CommandType,
    payload: &'a [u8],
    inline_data: InlineData<'a>,
    size: FramedSize,
}

impl<'a> Record<'a> {
    pub fn new(command_type: CommandType, payload: &'a [u8], inline_data: InlineData<'a>) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(Self {
            command_type,
            payload,
            inline_data,
            size: FramedSize::of_record(payload.len(), inline_data.len())?,
        })
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size.size_with_header
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `destination` is valid for writes of `self.size()` bytes that overlap neither the struct nor the data.
    pub unsafe fn write_to(&self, destination: *mut u8) {
        // SAFETY: The caller provides the bytes of the record, whose size is that of the struct with the data.
        unsafe {
            write_framed(
                destination,
                self.size,
                self.command_type as u16,
                self.payload,
                self.inline_data,
            );
        }
    }

    pub fn append_to(&self, commands: &mut Vec<u8>) {
        let record_offset = commands.len();
        assert!(record_offset.is_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT));
        commands.resize(record_offset + self.size(), 0);
        // SAFETY: The vector was just grown by the size of the record, and it owns its bytes.
        unsafe { self.write_to(commands.as_mut_ptr().add(record_offset)) };
    }

    pub fn encoded(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        self.append_to(&mut bytes);
        bytes
    }
}

/// False, with no request in `request_bytes`, when the stream cannot carry the request.
#[must_use]
pub fn encode_sync_request<R: SyncRequest>(
    request_bytes: &mut Vec<u8>,
    request: &R,
    inline_data: InlineData<'_>,
) -> bool {
    request_bytes.clear();
    let Some(size) = FramedSize::of_sync_request(size_of::<R>(), inline_data.len()) else {
        return false;
    };
    request_bytes.resize(size.size_with_header, 0);
    // SAFETY: The vector has the size of the request, and it owns its bytes.
    unsafe {
        write_framed(
            request_bytes.as_mut_ptr(),
            size,
            R::TYPE as u16,
            request.as_bytes(),
            inline_data,
        );
    }
    true
}

pub fn read_header(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<(u16, usize)> {
    let header: &[u8; HEADER_SIZE] = bytes.first_chunk()?;
    let type_number = u16::from_ne_bytes([header[0], header[1]]);
    let size_after_header = u32::from_ne_bytes(*header[HEADER_PAYLOAD_SIZE_OFFSET..].first_chunk()?);
    Some((type_number, usize::try_from(size_after_header).ok()?))
}

/// The records of a stream of commands, each as its type and its payload.
pub fn records(bytes: &[u8]) -> Records<'_> {
    Records { bytes }
}

pub struct Records<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
}

impl<'a> Iterator for Records<'a> {
    type Item = Result<(CommandType, &'a [u8]), &'static str>;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
        if self.bytes.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let bytes = core::mem::take(&mut self.bytes);
        let Some((type_number, payload_size)) = read_header(bytes) else {
            return Some(Err("Truncated WebGL command header"));
        };
        let Some(command_type) = CommandType::from_number(type_number) else {
            return Some(Err("Invalid WebGL command type"));
        };
        let Some((payload, rest)) = bytes[HEADER_SIZE..].split_at_checked(payload_size) else {
            return Some(Err("Truncated WebGL command payload"));
        };
        self.bytes = rest;
        Some(Ok((command_type, payload)))
    }
}

/// The type and the payload of a synchronous request.
pub fn decode_sync_request(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(SyncCallType, &[u8]), &'static str> {
    let (type_number, payload_size) = read_header(bytes).ok_or("Truncated WebGL sync call header")?;
    let call_type = SyncCallType::from_number(type_number).ok_or("Invalid WebGL sync call type")?;
    let payload = &bytes[HEADER_SIZE..];
    if payload.len() != payload_size {
        return Err("Truncated WebGL sync call payload");
    }
    Ok((call_type, payload))
}

/// Where the data that follows the struct of a reply is, as [`encode_reply`] lays it out.
pub fn reply_data_spans<R: WireStruct, const N: usize>(sizes: [usize; N]) -> [DataSpan; N] {
    let mut end_of_previous_data = size_of::<R>();
    sizes.map(|size| {
        let offset = end_of_previous_data.next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT);
        end_of_previous_data = offset + size;
        DataSpan {
            offset: u32::try_from(offset).expect("the data of a reply starts in its first 4 GiB"),
            size: u32::try_from(size).expect("the data of a reply is less than 4 GiB"),
        }
    })
}

/// A reply: its struct, and each piece of data that is not empty at the next multiple of the alignment, padded to the
/// alignment as a whole.
pub fn encode_reply<R: WireStruct>(reply: &R, data: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = reply.as_bytes().to_vec();
    for data in data.iter().filter(|data| !data.is_empty()) {
        bytes.resize(bytes.len().next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT), 0);
        bytes.extend_from_slice(data);
    }
    bytes.resize(bytes.len().next_multiple_of(RECORD_ALIGNMENT), 0);
    bytes
}

pub fn resolve_data_span(reply: &[u8], span: DataSpan) -> &[u8] {
    let start = span.offset as usize;
    start
        .checked_add(span.size as usize)
        .and_then(|end| reply.get(start..end))
        .expect("a span of the reply to a WebGL call lies inside the reply")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::vocabulary::{commands, sync_calls};
    use super::*;

    fn record(command_type: CommandType, payload: &[u8], inline_data: InlineData<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
        let record = Record::new(command_type, payload, inline_data).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            Some(record.size()),
            padded_record_size(payload.len(), inline_data.len())
        );
        // NB: The bytes that a record is written over are not zero, as those of a reused buffer are not.
        let mut bytes = vec![0xAA; record.size()];
        // SAFETY: The vector has the size of the record.
        unsafe { record.write_to(bytes.as_mut_ptr()) };
        bytes
    }

    fn header(type_number: u16, payload_size: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut header = Vec::new();
        header.extend_from_slice(&type_number.to_ne_bytes());
        header.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0]);
        header.extend_from_slice(&payload_size.to_ne_bytes());
        header
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_is_a_header_and_a_struct_padded_to_the_alignment() {
        let command = commands::Viewport {
            x: 1,
            y: 2,
            width: 3,
            height: 4,
        };
        let bytes = record(CommandType::Viewport, command.as_bytes(), InlineData::NONE);
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(bytes[..8], header(CommandType::Viewport as u16, 24));
        assert_eq!(bytes[8..24], *command.as_bytes());
        assert_eq!(bytes[24..], [0; 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_data_of_a_record_follows_its_struct_at_the_alignment() {
        let data = [7u8; 5];
        let command = commands::Uniform1fv {
            location: 9,
            count: 1,
            value: DataSpan::following::<commands::Uniform1fv>(InlineData::Bytes(&data)),
        };
        assert_eq!(command.value, DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 5 });
        let bytes = record(CommandType::Uniform1fv, command.as_bytes(), InlineData::Bytes(&data));
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(bytes[..8], header(CommandType::Uniform1fv as u16, 24));
        assert_eq!(bytes[8..24], *command.as_bytes());
        assert_eq!(bytes[24..29], data);
        assert_eq!(bytes[29..], [0; 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_bytes_between_a_struct_and_its_data_are_zero() {
        let command = commands::Enable { cap: u32::MAX };
        let bytes = record(CommandType::Enable, command.as_bytes(), InlineData::Bytes(&[1]));
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(bytes[8..12], [0xFF; 4]);
        assert_eq!(bytes[12..24], [0; 12]);
        assert_eq!(bytes[24], 1);
        assert_eq!(bytes[25..], [0; 7]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_data_takes_no_room() {
        let command = commands::Uniform1fv {
            location: 9,
            count: 0,
            value: DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 0 },
        };
        let bytes = record(CommandType::Uniform1fv, command.as_bytes(), InlineData::Bytes(&[]));
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(bytes[..8], header(CommandType::Uniform1fv as u16, 24));
        assert_eq!(bytes[24..], [0; 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_string_is_followed_by_a_nul() {
        let name = InlineData::NulTerminated(b"position");
        assert_eq!(name.len(), 9);
        let command = commands::RequestExtensionANGLE {
            name: DataSpan::following::<commands::RequestExtensionANGLE>(name),
        };
        assert_eq!(command.name, DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 9 });
        let bytes = record(CommandType::RequestExtensionANGLE, command.as_bytes(), name);
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 48);
        assert_eq!(bytes[24..33], *b"position\0");
        assert_eq!(bytes[33..], [0; 15]);

        let empty_name = InlineData::NulTerminated(b"");
        let bytes = record(CommandType::RequestExtensionANGLE, command.as_bytes(), empty_name);
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(bytes[24..], [0; 8]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_are_appended_one_after_the_other() {
        let mut commands = Vec::new();
        let enable = commands::Enable { cap: 1 };
        let viewport = commands::Viewport {
            x: 1,
            y: 2,
            width: 3,
            height: 4,
        };
        Record::new(CommandType::Enable, enable.as_bytes(), InlineData::NONE)
            .unwrap()
            .append_to(&mut commands);
        Record::new(CommandType::Viewport, viewport.as_bytes(), InlineData::NONE)
            .unwrap()
            .append_to(&mut commands);
        assert_eq!(commands.len(), 16 + 32);
        assert_eq!(commands[..8], header(CommandType::Enable as u16, 8));
        assert_eq!(commands[16..24], header(CommandType::Viewport as u16, 24));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_request_is_a_header_and_a_payload_padded_to_the_alignment() {
        // NB: The replayer rejects a request whose payload is shorter than its struct, and the struct of a request
        //     without arguments is one byte in C++.
        let mut request_bytes = vec![0xAA; 64];
        assert!(encode_sync_request(
            &mut request_bytes,
            &sync_calls::GetErrorRequest::ZEROED,
            InlineData::NONE,
        ));
        assert_eq!(request_bytes.len(), 24);
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[..8], header(SyncCallType::GetError as u16, 16));
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[8..], [0; 16]);

        let name = InlineData::NulTerminated(b"color");
        let request = sync_calls::GetAttribLocationRequest {
            program: 3,
            name: DataSpan::following::<sync_calls::GetAttribLocationRequest>(name),
        };
        assert!(encode_sync_request(&mut request_bytes, &request, name));
        assert_eq!(request_bytes.len(), 8 + 32);
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[..8], header(SyncCallType::GetAttribLocation as u16, 32));
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[8..20], *request.as_bytes());
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[24..30], *b"color\0");
        assert_eq!(request_bytes[30..], [0; 10]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_stream_carries_what_its_header_can_count() {
        const FOUR_GIB: usize = 1 << 32;

        // The largest record: 8 bytes of header, 16 of struct, and data up to the last multiple of the alignment
        // that leaves what follows the header countable.
        let largest_data_size = FOUR_GIB - 8 - 16;
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(16, largest_data_size), Some(FOUR_GIB));
        assert_eq!(
            FramedSize::of_record(16, largest_data_size),
            Some(FramedSize {
                size_with_header: FOUR_GIB,
                size_after_header: u32::MAX - 7
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(16, largest_data_size + 1), None);
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(16, FOUR_GIB), None);
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(16, usize::MAX), None);
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(16, usize::MAX - 16), None);
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(usize::MAX, 0), None);
        assert_eq!(padded_record_size(usize::MAX, 1), None);

        // The largest request: what follows its header is padded on its own.
        assert_eq!(
            FramedSize::of_sync_request(16, FOUR_GIB - 16 - 16),
            Some(FramedSize {
                size_with_header: FOUR_GIB - 8,
                size_after_header: u32::MAX - 15
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(FramedSize::of_sync_request(16, FOUR_GIB - 16 - 15), None);
        assert_eq!(FramedSize::of_sync_request(16, usize::MAX), None);
        assert_eq!(FramedSize::of_sync_request(1, 0).unwrap().size_with_header, 8 + 16);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_reply_starts_with_its_struct() {
        let mut reply = Vec::new();
        reply.extend_from_slice(&5i32.to_ne_bytes());
        reply.extend_from_slice(&[16, 0, 0, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0]);
        reply.extend_from_slice(&[0; 4]);
        reply.extend_from_slice(b"abc");
        let decoded = sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply::from_reply_bytes(&reply);
        assert_eq!(decoded.length, 5);
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(&reply, decoded.info_log), b"abc");
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(&reply, DataSpan { offset: 19, size: 0 }), b"");
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "shorter than its struct")]
    fn a_reply_that_is_shorter_than_its_struct_is_not_read() {
        sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply::from_reply_bytes(&[0; 11]);
    }

    #[test]
    #[should_panic(expected = "lies inside the reply")]
    fn a_span_that_leaves_the_reply_is_not_resolved() {
        resolve_data_span(&[0; 16], DataSpan { offset: 12, size: 5 });
    }

    #[test]
    fn records_are_read_as_they_are_written() {
        let mut commands = Vec::new();
        let enable = commands::Enable { cap: 7 };
        let data = [1u8, 2, 3];
        let uniform = commands::Uniform1fv {
            location: 9,
            count: 1,
            value: DataSpan::following::<commands::Uniform1fv>(InlineData::Bytes(&data)),
        };
        Record::new(CommandType::Enable, enable.as_bytes(), InlineData::NONE)
            .unwrap()
            .append_to(&mut commands);
        Record::new(CommandType::Uniform1fv, uniform.as_bytes(), InlineData::Bytes(&data))
            .unwrap()
            .append_to(&mut commands);

        let read: Vec<_> = records(&commands).collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(read[0].0, CommandType::Enable);
        assert_eq!(commands::Enable::read_from(read[0].1), Some(enable));
        assert_eq!(read[1].0, CommandType::Uniform1fv);
        assert_eq!(commands::Uniform1fv::read_from(read[1].1), Some(uniform));
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(read[1].1, uniform.value), data);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_that_the_stream_does_not_hold_is_rejected() {
        assert_eq!(
            records(&header(0, 0)[..7]).next(),
            Some(Err("Truncated WebGL command header"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            records(&header(u16::MAX, 0)).next(),
            Some(Err("Invalid WebGL command type"))
        );
        let mut truncated = header(CommandType::Enable as u16, 8);
        truncated.extend_from_slice(&[0; 7]);
        let mut read = records(&truncated);
        assert_eq!(read.next(), Some(Err("Truncated WebGL command payload")));
        assert_eq!(read.next(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_struct_is_read_only_with_booleans_that_are_true_or_false() {
        let command = commands::BufferData {
            has_data: true,
            ..commands::BufferData::ZEROED
        };
        let mut bytes = command.as_bytes().to_vec();
        assert_eq!(commands::BufferData::BOOL_FIELD_OFFSETS, [16]);
        assert_eq!(commands::BufferData::read_from(&bytes), Some(command));
        bytes[16] = 2;
        assert_eq!(commands::BufferData::read_from(&bytes), None);
        assert_eq!(commands::BufferData::read_from(&bytes[..31]), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_request_is_read_as_it_is_written() {
        let name = InlineData::NulTerminated(b"color");
        let request = sync_calls::GetAttribLocationRequest {
            program: 3,
            name: DataSpan::following::<sync_calls::GetAttribLocationRequest>(name),
        };
        let mut request_bytes = Vec::new();
        assert!(encode_sync_request(&mut request_bytes, &request, name));
        let (call_type, payload) = decode_sync_request(&request_bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(call_type, SyncCallType::GetAttribLocation);
        assert_eq!(sync_calls::GetAttribLocationRequest::read_from(payload), Some(request));
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(payload, request.name), b"color\0");

        request_bytes.push(0);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_sync_request(&request_bytes),
            Err("Truncated WebGL sync call payload")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_sync_request(&header(u16::MAX, 0)),
            Err("Invalid WebGL sync call type")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_reply_holds_its_data_where_its_spans_say() {
        let info_log = b"abc";
        let [span] = reply_data_spans::<sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply, 1>([info_log.len()]);
        assert_eq!(span, DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 3 });
        let reply = sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply {
            length: 3,
            info_log: span,
        };
        let bytes = encode_reply(&reply, &[info_log]);
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32);
        assert_eq!(sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply::from_reply_bytes(&bytes), reply);
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(&bytes, span), info_log);
        assert_eq!(bytes[19..], [0; 13]);

        let [empty, second] = reply_data_spans::<sync_calls::GetShaderInfoLogReply, 2>([0, 5]);
        assert_eq!(empty, DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 0 });
        assert_eq!(second, DataSpan { offset: 16, size: 5 });
        let bytes = encode_reply(&reply, &[b"", b"hello"]);
        assert_eq!(resolve_data_span(&bytes, second), b"hello");
        assert_eq!(encode_reply(&sync_calls::GetErrorReply::ZEROED, &[]).len(), 16);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompositing/Scrolling/AsyncScrollingState.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGfx/Point.h>
#include <LibWebCommon/Page/AsyncScrollNodeStableID.h>

namespace Compositing {

using AsyncScrollOperationID = u64;

struct AsyncScrollOffset {
    Web::AsyncScrollNodeStableID stable_node_id;
    Gfx::FloatPoint compositor_scroll_offset;
    // The most recent nonzero delta of a relative scroll in each axis, such as a wheel or panning scroll. Absolute
    // scrolls, such as dragging a scrollbar thumb, leave it as it is.
    Gfx::FloatPoint last_relative_scroll_delta;
    // The scale the visual viewport was zoomed to, which only its scroll node reports.
    Optional<float> visual_viewport_scale;
    // The last of the main thread's scroll requests for the box that the compositor applied before it reported this.
    u64 applied_scroll_request_id { 0 };
    // How many times the compositor had scrolled the box for user input of its own when it reported this.
    u64 user_input_scroll_count { 0 };

    void merge_later_scroll(AsyncScrollOffset const& later)
    {
        compositor_scroll_offset = later.compositor_scroll_offset;
        applied_scroll_request_id = later.applied_scroll_request_id;
        user_input_scroll_count = later.user_input_scroll_count;
        if (later.visual_viewport_scale.has_value())
            visual_viewport_scale = later.visual_viewport_scale;
        if (later.last_relative_scroll_delta.x() != 0)
            last_relative_scroll_delta.set_x(later.last_relative_scroll_delta.x());
        if (later.last_relative_scroll_delta.y() != 0)
            last_relative_scroll_delta.set_y(later.last_relative_scroll_delta.y());
    }
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompositing/Scrolling/ScrollSnapSelection.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibCompositing/Export.h>
#include <LibCompositing/Forward.h>
#include <LibWebCommon/PixelUnits.h>

// What scroll snap position selection is asked and answers, on the main thread and in the compositor process alike.
// The selection is libcompositing_rust's scrolling::scroll_snap_selection. Everything here is in CSS pixels.

namespace Compositing {

// The box a snap area belongs to, which identifies the area across relayouts and across processes. A node's unique ID
// is never reused, so an area removed from the document keeps an identity no live area ever takes again and is no
// longer a snap area the container can be returned to.
struct SnapAreaIdentity {
    Web::UniqueNodeID node_id {};
    // 0 for the element's own box; otherwise the pseudo-element the box is generated for, plus one.
    u8 pseudo_element_type { 0 };

    bool operator==(SnapAreaIdentity const&) const = default;

    bool is_valid() const { return node_id.value() != 0; }
    bool is_pseudo_element() const { return pseudo_element_type != 0; }
};

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap-1/#scroll-types
struct COMPOSITING_API SnapSelectionStrategy {
    enum class Type : u8 {
        // An absolute scroll, or any other operation with only an intended end position.
        EndPosition,
        // A relative scroll with only an intended direction, such as a mouse wheel step or an arrow key press.
        Direction,
        // A relative scroll with both an intended direction and end position, such as scrollBy().
        EndPositionAndDirection,
    };

    Type type { Type::EndPosition };
    // The scroll offset the operation travels from; a snap position with `scroll-snap-stop: always` must not be
    // passed over on the way from there to the selected snap position.
    Optional<Web::CSSPixelPoint> start_offset {};
    // The net offset change the operation's input produced; an axis the operation did not travel in selects no snap
    // position.
    Web::CSSPixelPoint displacement {};
    // Snap positions short of this offset in the direction of travel are not selected; it defaults to the start
    // offset.
    Optional<Web::CSSPixelPoint> starting_positions_boundary {};
};

// The snap areas a scroll container is snapped to in each axis, so that it can be re-snapped to those same snap areas
// after a content change.
struct SnappedAreas {
    Vector<SnapAreaIdentity> x;
    Vector<SnapAreaIdentity> y;

    bool is_empty() const { return x.is_empty() && y.is_empty(); }
};

struct SnapDestination {
    Web::CSSPixelPoint position;
    // Whether a snap position was selected in each axis; an axis whose snap positions are all ineligible for the
    // scroll keeps the destination it was given.
    bool snapped_x { false };
    bool snapped_y { false };
    // Whether snap position selection ran in each axis. An axis the scroll did not travel in is not evaluated, and
    // whatever snap area the container is snapped to there remains snapped.
    bool evaluated_x { false };
    bool evaluated_y { false };
    SnappedAreas snapped_areas {};
};

}

#include <LibCompositing/RustFFI.h>
#include <LibCompositing/Scrolling/SmoothScrollAnimation.h>

namespace Compositing {

SmoothScrollAnimation::SmoothScrollAnimation(Gfx::FloatPoint start_offset, Gfx::FloatPoint destination_offset, double pixels_per_css_pixel, ScrollAnimationKind kind)
    : m_animation(RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_create(start_offset, destination_offset, pixels_per_css_pixel, kind))
{
}

SmoothScrollAnimation::~SmoothScrollAnimation()
{
    RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_destroy(m_animation);
}

SmoothScrollAnimation::SmoothScrollAnimation(SmoothScrollAnimation&& other)
    : m_animation(exchange(other.m_animation, nullptr))
{
}

SmoothScrollAnimation& SmoothScrollAnimation::operator=(SmoothScrollAnimation&& other)
{
    if (this != &other) {
        RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_destroy(m_animation);
        m_animation = exchange(other.m_animation, nullptr);
    }
    return *this;
}

ScrollAnimationKind SmoothScrollAnimation::kind() const
{
    return RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_kind(m_animation);
}

SmoothScrollAnimation::Sample SmoothScrollAnimation::sample(AK::Duration elapsed) const
{
    Sample sample;
    sample.complete = RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_sample(m_animation, elapsed.to_nanoseconds(), &sample.offset);
    return sample;
}

void SmoothScrollAnimation::retarget(Gfx::FloatPoint destination_offset, AK::Duration elapsed)
{
    RustFFI::smooth_scroll_animation_retarget(m_animation, destination_offset, elapsed.to_nanoseconds());
}

}

// A scroll the compositor started for user input of its own: the main thread registers it as a user scroll in
// flight. A scroll started for a step of a gesture is owed the scrollend event by that gesture, which continues
// from the offset its steps have asked for; a scroll started for the end of a gesture settles the gesture. The
// selection of a scroll that snapped along no axis carries only the destination. Repeated reports for the same
// operation update its accumulated input without starting another animation.
struct StartedUserScroll {
    Web::AsyncScrollNodeStableID stable_node_id;
    AsyncScrollOperationID operation_id { 0 };
    Web::CSSPixelPoint initial_scroll_offset;
    Web::CSSPixelPoint unsnapped_scroll_destination;
    Web::CSSPixelPoint relative_scroll_delta;
    SnapDestination selection;
    bool settles_gesture { false };
    bool is_absolute_scroll { false };
    Optional<ScrollAnimationKind> animation_kind;
};

    AfterDispatch,

    Vector<Web::AsyncScrollNodeStableID> scroll_chain;

// Blocking wheel event listeners hold a wheel step back from the compositor until the page has dispatched it. A step
// that the page dispatched and did not cancel has nothing left to wait for.

    NotYetDispatched,
    DispatchedAndNotCanceled,
};

// A later keyboard step continues from the destination of a smooth scroll the user started, rather than from its
// presented offset.
enum class SmoothScrollInitiator : u8 {
    Programmatic,
    UserInput,
};

// The main thread allocates the ids of the scrolls it requests from here up, so that they never meet the ids the
// compositor allocates for scrolls of its own.
inline constexpr AsyncScrollOperationID first_operation_id_the_main_thread_requests = AsyncScrollOperationID { 1 } << 63;

// An instant scroll by a distance from wherever the box is. Each scroll folded into it clamps the box to the scroll range
// it had, which leaves the box at clamp(offset + delta, lower_bound, upper_bound) in each axis.
struct RequestedRelativeScroll {
    Gfx::FloatPoint delta;
    Gfx::FloatPoint lower_bound { -AK::Infinity<float>, -AK::Infinity<float> };
    Gfx::FloatPoint upper_bound { AK::Infinity<float>, AK::Infinity<float> };

    void then(RequestedRelativeScroll const& later)
    {
        lower_bound = {
            AK::clamp(lower_bound.x() + later.delta.x(), later.lower_bound.x(), later.upper_bound.x()),
            AK::clamp(lower_bound.y() + later.delta.y(), later.lower_bound.y(), later.upper_bound.y()),
        };
        upper_bound = {
            AK::clamp(upper_bound.x() + later.delta.x(), later.lower_bound.x(), later.upper_bound.x()),
            AK::clamp(upper_bound.y() + later.delta.y(), later.lower_bound.y(), later.upper_bound.y()),
        };
        delta.translate_by(later.delta);
    }

    Gfx::FloatPoint applied_to(Gfx::FloatPoint offset) const
    {
        return {
            AK::clamp(offset.x() + delta.x(), lower_bound.x(), upper_bound.x()),
            AK::clamp(offset.y() + delta.y(), lower_bound.y(), upper_bound.y()),
        };
    }
};

// A smooth scroll that the main thread requests, from wherever the box is once the request's instant scroll is done.
struct RequestedSmoothScroll {
    AsyncScrollOperationID operation_id { 0 };
    // Where the scroll goes, or how far it goes from wherever the box is.
    Gfx::FloatPoint destination_offset;
    bool destination_is_relative { false };
    // What a relative scroll clamps the box to, as each scroll folded into it clamps the box to the scroll range it
    // had.
    Gfx::FloatPoint relative_lower_bound { -AK::Infinity<float>, -AK::Infinity<float> };
    Gfx::FloatPoint relative_upper_bound { AK::Infinity<float>, AK::Infinity<float> };
    ScrollAnimationKind animation_kind { ScrollAnimationKind::SmoothScroll };
    SmoothScrollInitiator initiator { SmoothScrollInitiator::Programmatic };
    // User input that heads the user input scroll of the same operation somewhere else, rather than starting another.
    bool retargets_operation { false };
    // For the scroll that settles a user's gesture, the count of the box's scrolls for the compositor's own user input
    // that the main thread had heard of. User input the compositor took since carries the gesture on instead.
    Optional<u64> settled_user_input_scroll_count;

    RequestedRelativeScroll relative_scroll() const
    {
        VERIFY(destination_is_relative);
        return { destination_offset, relative_lower_bound, relative_upper_bound };
    }

    // A later scroll of the same operation goes on from where this one was headed.
    void fold_later(RequestedSmoothScroll const& later)
    {
        VERIFY(later.operation_id == operation_id);
        auto earlier = *this;
        *this = later;
        retargets_operation |= earlier.retargets_operation;
        if (!later.destination_is_relative)
            return;
        if (!earlier.destination_is_relative) {
            destination_offset = later.relative_scroll().applied_to(earlier.destination_offset);
            destination_is_relative = false;
            return;
        }
        auto folded = earlier.relative_scroll();
        folded.then(later.relative_scroll());
        destination_offset = folded.delta;
        relative_lower_bound = folded.lower_bound;
        relative_upper_bound = folded.upper_bound;
    }
};

// What the main thread asks of the compositor for one scrolling box, carried with the frame it changed the box in. A
// request aborts the box's smooth scrolls, jumps the box to an offset, then starts a smooth scroll of it, in that
// order. The compositor marks the offsets it reports for the box with the id of the last request it applied to it.
struct ScrollRequest {
    Web::AsyncScrollNodeStableID stable_node_id;
    u64 request_id { 0 };
    Optional<Gfx::FloatPoint> jump_offset;
    // The scale the visual viewport jumps to along with its offset.
    Optional<float> visual_viewport_scale;
    // A relative scroll after the jump. For the viewport, it can move the visual viewport's position in the page, which
    // the visual viewport takes as much of as it can before the layout viewport takes the rest.
    Optional<RequestedRelativeScroll> relative_scroll;
    bool relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first { false };
    // Whether the instant scroll is the main thread's response to user input, rather than a script's or its own.
    bool instant_scroll_is_for_user_input { false };
    Optional<RequestedSmoothScroll> smooth_scroll;
    // Whether the request scrolls for input that ends the momentum scrolling the box, such as a key.
    bool takes_over_from_momentum { false };

    // A request made later in the same frame aborts the smooth scroll of this one, which never got under way.
    void fold_later(ScrollRequest const& later)
    {
        request_id = later.request_id;
        takes_over_from_momentum |= later.takes_over_from_momentum;
        if (later.jump_offset.has_value() || later.relative_scroll.has_value())
            instant_scroll_is_for_user_input = later.instant_scroll_is_for_user_input;
        if (later.jump_offset.has_value()) {
            jump_offset = later.jump_offset;
            if (later.visual_viewport_scale.has_value())
                visual_viewport_scale = later.visual_viewport_scale;
            relative_scroll = later.relative_scroll;
            relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first = later.relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first;
        } else if (later.relative_scroll.has_value()) {
            // A box is scrolled by distances of one kind: the viewport by its position in the page, the rest by offset.
            if (relative_scroll.has_value()) {
                VERIFY(relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first == later.relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first);
                relative_scroll->then(later.relative_scroll.value());
            } else {
                relative_scroll = later.relative_scroll;
                relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first = later.relative_scroll_moves_visual_viewport_first;
            }
        }
        if (smooth_scroll.has_value() && later.smooth_scroll.has_value() && smooth_scroll->operation_id == later.smooth_scroll->operation_id)
            smooth_scroll->fold_later(later.smooth_scroll.value());
        else
            smooth_scroll = later.smooth_scroll;
    }
};

enum class VisualContextNodeKind : u8 {
    Spatial,
    Effect,
};

// A node of the visual context tree that the name of a layer mentions, with the element whose box owns it. The

    u64 visual_context_tree_structural_epoch { 0 };

// AD-HOC: Wheel events carry no gesture phase information, so a wheel gesture is considered finished once no input of
//         it has moved a scrolling box for this long. The side that scrolled the gesture's steps decides when its
//         input ran out: the compositor reports the end of a gesture whose steps it chained, and the main thread
//         settles the gesture on that report, or after this delay for the steps it scrolled itself.
inline constexpr AK::Duration user_scroll_settle_delay = AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(500);

struct PausedDebuggerOverlayState {
    Optional<String> font_family;
    Optional<PausedDebuggerOverlayAction> hovered_action;

    bool operator==(PausedDebuggerOverlayState const&) const = default;
};

// The controls stay present while they are hidden, so that they fade out.
struct PictureInPictureControlsState {
    bool shown { false };
    Optional<PictureInPictureControl> hovered_control;

    bool operator==(PictureInPictureControlsState const&) const = default;
};

struct CompositorLayersOverlayState {
    Optional<String> font_family;
    Vector<u64> hidden_layer_ids;
    // The layers the overlay shows the tiles of.
    Vector<u64> selected_layer_ids;
    Optional<u64> hovered_layer_id;
    // Each new value zeroes the counts of tiles rastered.
    u64 raster_count_reset_generation { 0 };

    bool operator==(CompositorLayersOverlayState const&) const = default;
};

// What the browser draws over a context's page, on top of anything the page draws, with each overlay the view has
// present. The browser handles their input before the page sees any of it.
struct UIOverlays {
    Optional<PausedDebuggerOverlayState> paused_debugger;
    Optional<PictureInPictureControlsState> picture_in_picture_controls;
    Optional<CompositorLayersOverlayState> compositor_layers;

    bool operator==(UIOverlays const&) const = default;
};

// Which of an overlay's buttons the pointer is over, and which it pressed. A press acts once it is released over that
// same button.
template<typename Action>
class OverlayPointerState {
public:
    struct Outcome {
        bool hover_changed { false };
        Optional<Action> activated_action;
    };

    Outcome handle_mouse_event(Web::MouseEvent const& event, Optional<Action> action_under_pointer)
    {
        auto previously_hovered_action = m_hovered_action;
        Optional<Action> activated_action;

        switch (event.type) {
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseMove:
            m_hovered_action = action_under_pointer;
            if ((event.buttons & Web::UIEvents::MouseButton::Primary) == Web::UIEvents::MouseButton::None)
                m_pressed_action.clear();
            break;
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseLeave:
            reset();
            break;
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseDown:
            if (event.button == Web::UIEvents::MouseButton::Primary)
                m_pressed_action = action_under_pointer;
            break;
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseUp:
            if (event.button == Web::UIEvents::MouseButton::Primary) {
                if (m_pressed_action == action_under_pointer)
                    activated_action = m_pressed_action;
                m_pressed_action.clear();
            }
            break;
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseCancel:
            m_pressed_action.clear();
            break;
        case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseWheel:
            break;
        }

        return { m_hovered_action != previously_hovered_action, activated_action };
    }

    void reset()
    {
        m_hovered_action.clear();
        m_pressed_action.clear();
    }

    Optional<Action> hovered_action() const { return m_hovered_action; }
    bool is_pressing() const { return m_pressed_action.has_value(); }

private:
    Optional<Action> m_hovered_action;
    Optional<Action> m_pressed_action;
};

}

#include <LibCompositing/Video/VideoFrameHold.h>

namespace Compositing {

RefPtr<VideoFrameHold> VideoFrameHold::hold_current_frame(NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage> page, Media::VideoSinkHandle sink_handle, ReleaseThroughCompositor release_through_compositor)
{
    auto generation = page->hold_current_generation();
    if (!generation.has_value())
        return nullptr;
    return adopt_ref(*new VideoFrameHold(move(page), sink_handle, generation.value(), move(release_through_compositor)));
}

RefPtr<VideoFrameHold> VideoFrameHold::hold_frame_of_generation(NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage> page, Media::VideoSinkHandle sink_handle, u64 generation, ReleaseThroughCompositor release_through_compositor)
{
    if (!page->hold_generation(generation))
        return nullptr;
    return adopt_ref(*new VideoFrameHold(move(page), sink_handle, generation, move(release_through_compositor)));
}

VideoFrameHold::VideoFrameHold(NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage> page, Media::VideoSinkHandle sink_handle, u64 generation, ReleaseThroughCompositor release_through_compositor)
    : m_page(move(page))
    , m_sink_handle(sink_handle)
    , m_generation(generation)
    , m_release_through_compositor(move(release_through_compositor))
{
}

VideoFrameHold::~VideoFrameHold()
{
    if (!m_was_sent_to_compositor && m_page->release_hold_if_current(m_generation) == VideoFramePresentationPage::ReleaseResult::Released)
        return;
    if (m_release_through_compositor)
        m_release_through_compositor(m_sink_handle, m_generation);
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompositing/Video/VideoFramePresentationPage.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibCompositing/Video/VideoFramePresentationPage.h>
#include <LibIPC/Decoder.h>
#include <LibIPC/Encoder.h>
#include <LibMediaCodecs/Limits.h>

namespace Compositing {

static_assert(__atomic_always_lock_free(sizeof(u64), nullptr));

static constexpr size_t max_compare_exchange_attempts_before_assuming_a_misbehaving_peer = 64;

ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage>> VideoFramePresentationPage::create()
{
    auto buffer = TRY(Core::AnonymousBuffer::create_with_size(sizeof(SharedState)));
    new (buffer.data<void>()) SharedState;
    return create(move(buffer));
}

ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage>> VideoFramePresentationPage::create(Core::AnonymousBuffer buffer)
{
    if (!buffer.is_valid() || buffer.size() < sizeof(SharedState))
        return Error::from_string_literal("Invalid video frame presentation page buffer");
    return adopt_nonnull_ref_or_enomem(new (nothrow) VideoFramePresentationPage(move(buffer)));
}

VideoFramePresentationPage::VideoFramePresentationPage(Core::AnonymousBuffer buffer)
    : m_buffer(move(buffer))
    , m_shared_state(reinterpret_cast<SharedState*>(m_buffer.data<void>()))
{
}

u64 VideoFramePresentationPage::pack(GenerationAndHolds value)
{
    VERIFY(value.generation <= retired_generation);
    VERIFY(value.hold_count <= max_hold_count);
    return (value.generation << 16) | value.hold_count;
}

VideoFramePresentationPage::GenerationAndHolds VideoFramePresentationPage::unpack(u64 word)
{
    return { .generation = word >> 16, .hold_count = word & max_hold_count };
}

// Every change to the word is a read-modify-write, and it guards no other data, so nothing needs ordering.

VideoFramePresentationPage::GenerationAndHolds VideoFramePresentationPage::replace_generation(u64 new_generation)
{
    return unpack(word().exchange(pack({ .generation = new_generation, .hold_count = 0 }), AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed));
}

u64 VideoFramePresentationPage::current_generation() const
{
    return unpack(word().load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed)).generation;
}

Optional<u64> VideoFramePresentationPage::hold_current_generation()
{
    return hold(OptionalNone {});
}

bool VideoFramePresentationPage::hold_generation(u64 generation)
{
    return hold(generation).has_value();
}

Optional<u64> VideoFramePresentationPage::hold(Optional<u64> required_generation)
{
    auto expected = word().load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (size_t attempt = 0; attempt < max_compare_exchange_attempts_before_assuming_a_misbehaving_peer; attempt++) {
        auto current = unpack(expected);
        if (current.generation == retired_generation || current.hold_count == max_hold_count)
            return {};
        if (required_generation.has_value() && current.generation != required_generation.value())
            return {};
        auto held = pack({ .generation = current.generation, .hold_count = current.hold_count + 1 });
        if (word().compare_exchange_strong(expected, held, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed))
            return current.generation;
    }
    return {};
}

void VideoFramePresentationPage::publish_presented_frame(PresentedFrame const& presented_frame)
{
    m_shared_state->presented_frame.store(presented_frame);
}

Optional<VideoFramePresentationPage::PresentedFrame> VideoFramePresentationPage::presented_frame() const
{
    auto presented_frame = m_shared_state->presented_frame.read();
    if (!presented_frame.has_value())
        return {};
    if (presented_frame->width > Media::MAX_VIDEO_FRAME_DIMENSION || presented_frame->height > Media::MAX_VIDEO_FRAME_DIMENSION)
        return {};
    return presented_frame;
}

VideoFramePresentationPage::ReleaseResult VideoFramePresentationPage::release_hold_if_current(u64 generation)
{
    auto expected = word().load(AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (size_t attempt = 0; attempt < max_compare_exchange_attempts_before_assuming_a_misbehaving_peer; attempt++) {
        auto current = unpack(expected);
        if (current.generation != generation)
            return ReleaseResult::NotCurrent;
        if (current.hold_count == 0)
            return ReleaseResult::NotHeld;
        auto released = pack({ .generation = current.generation, .hold_count = current.hold_count - 1 });
        if (word().compare_exchange_strong(expected, released, AK::MemoryOrder::memory_order_relaxed))
            return ReleaseResult::Released;
    }
    return ReleaseResult::NotHeld;
}

}

namespace IPC {

template<>
ErrorOr<void> encode(Encoder& encoder, NonnullRefPtr<Compositing::VideoFramePresentationPage> const& page)
{
    return encoder.encode(page->buffer());
}

template<>
ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<Compositing::VideoFramePresentationPage>> decode(Decoder& decoder)
{
    return Compositing::VideoFramePresentationPage::create(TRY(decoder.decode<Core::AnonymousBuffer>()));
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompositing/Video/VideoFramePresentationPage.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Atomic.h>
#include <AK/Error.h>
#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/RefCounted.h>
#include <AK/SeqLock.h>
#include <AK/SharedMemoryValue.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <LibCompositing/Export.h>
#include <LibCore/AnonymousBuffer.h>
#include <LibIPC/Forward.h>

namespace Compositing {

// The generation and its hold count share one word, so a hold is either counted before the Compositor replaces the
// generation, or fails and is retried on the new one.
class COMPOSITING_API VideoFramePresentationPage : public RefCounted<VideoFramePresentationPage> {
public:
    static constexpr u64 retired_generation = (1ull << 48) - 1;
    static constexpr u64 max_hold_count = (1ull << 16) - 1;

    static ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage>> create();
    static ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<VideoFramePresentationPage>> create(Core::AnonymousBuffer);

    Core::AnonymousBuffer const& buffer() const { return m_buffer; }

    struct GenerationAndHolds {
        u64 generation { 0 };
        u64 hold_count { 0 };
    };

    GenerationAndHolds replace_generation(u64 new_generation);

    u64 current_generation() const;
    Optional<u64> hold_current_generation();

    enum class ReleaseResult : u8 {
        Released,
        NotCurrent,
        NotHeld,
    };
    ReleaseResult release_hold_if_current(u64 generation);

    struct PresentedFrame {
        u64 generation { 0 };
        u64 presented_frame_count { 0 };
        u64 dropped_frame_count { 0 };
        SharedMemoryValue<AK::Duration> media_time;
        SharedMemoryValue<MonotonicTime> presentation_time;
        u32 width { 0 };
        u32 height { 0 };
        bool frame_is_up_to_date { false };
    };
    void publish_presented_frame(PresentedFrame const&);
    Optional<PresentedFrame> presented_frame() const;
    bool hold_generation(u64 generation);

private:
    struct SharedState {
        Atomic<u64> word;
        SeqLock<PresentedFrame> presented_frame;
    };

    VideoFramePresentationPage(Core::AnonymousBuffer);

    Optional<u64> hold(Optional<u64> required_generation);

    static u64 pack(GenerationAndHolds);
    static GenerationAndHolds unpack(u64);

    Atomic<u64>& word() const { return m_shared_state->word; }

    Core::AnonymousBuffer m_buffer;
    SharedState* m_shared_state { nullptr };
};

}

namespace IPC {

template<>
COMPOSITING_API ErrorOr<void> encode(Encoder&, NonnullRefPtr<Compositing::VideoFramePresentationPage> const&);

template<>
COMPOSITING_API ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<Compositing::VideoFramePresentationPage>> decode(Decoder&);

}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompress/GenericZlib.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2025, Altomani Gianluca <altomanigianluca@gmail.com>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibCompress/GenericZlib.h>

#include <zlib.h>

namespace Compress {

static Error handle_zlib_error(int ret)
{
    switch (ret) {
    case Z_ERRNO:
        return Error::from_errno(errno);
    case Z_NEED_DICT:
        // Z_NEED_DICT if the input data needed a dictionary
        return Error::from_string_literal("zlib data needs dictionary");
    case Z_DATA_ERROR:
        // Z_DATA_ERROR if the input data was corrupted
        return Error::from_string_literal("zlib data error");
    case Z_STREAM_ERROR:
        // Z_STREAM_ERROR if the parameters are invalid, such as a null pointer to the structure
        return Error::from_string_literal("zlib stream error");
    case Z_VERSION_ERROR:
        // Z_VERSION_ERROR if the zlib library version is incompatible with the version assumed by the caller
        return Error::from_string_literal("zlib version mismatch");
    case Z_MEM_ERROR:
        // Z_MEM_ERROR if there was not enough memory
        return Error::from_errno(ENOMEM);
    default:
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
    }
}

GenericZlibDecompressor::GenericZlibDecompressor(AK::FixedArray<u8> buffer, MaybeOwned<Stream> stream, z_stream* zstream)
    : m_stream(move(stream))
    , m_zstream(zstream)
    , m_buffer(move(buffer))
{
}

ErrorOr<z_stream*> GenericZlibDecompressor::new_z_stream(int window_bits)
{
    auto zstream = new (nothrow) z_stream {};
    if (!zstream)
        return Error::from_errno(ENOMEM);

    // The fields next_in, avail_in, zalloc, zfree and opaque must be initialized before by the caller.
    zstream->next_in = nullptr;
    zstream->avail_in = 0;
    zstream->zalloc = nullptr;
    zstream->zfree = nullptr;
    zstream->opaque = nullptr;

    if (auto ret = inflateInit2(zstream, window_bits); ret != Z_OK)
        return handle_zlib_error(ret);

    return zstream;
}

GenericZlibDecompressor::~GenericZlibDecompressor()
{
    inflateEnd(m_zstream);
    delete m_zstream;
}

ErrorOr<Bytes> GenericZlibDecompressor::read_some(Bytes bytes)
{
    m_zstream->avail_out = bytes.size();
    m_zstream->next_out = bytes.data();

    if (m_zstream->avail_in == 0) {
        auto in = TRY(m_stream->read_some(m_buffer.span()));
        m_zstream->avail_in = in.size();
        m_zstream->next_in = m_buffer.data();
    }

    auto ret = inflate(m_zstream, Z_NO_FLUSH);

    if (ret != Z_OK && ret != Z_STREAM_END && ret != Z_BUF_ERROR)
        return handle_zlib_error(ret);

    // We got Z_BUF_ERROR (no progress was possible), no more input, stream is EOF and no output was produced.
    // There is no way to get out of this loop, error out.
    if (ret == Z_BUF_ERROR && m_zstream->avail_in == 0 && m_stream->is_eof() && bytes.size() == m_zstream->avail_out)
        return Error::from_string_literal("No decompression progress on EOF stream");

    if (ret == Z_STREAM_END) {
        inflateReset(m_zstream);
        if (m_zstream->avail_in == 0)
            m_eof = true;
    }

    return bytes.slice(0, bytes.size() - m_zstream->avail_out);
}

ErrorOr<size_t> GenericZlibDecompressor::write_some(ReadonlyBytes)
{
    return Error::from_errno(EBADF);
}

bool GenericZlibDecompressor::is_eof() const
{
    return m_eof;
}

bool GenericZlibDecompressor::is_open() const
{
    return m_stream->is_open();
}

void GenericZlibDecompressor::close()
{
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibCompress/GenericZlib.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2025, Altomani Gianluca <altomanigianluca@gmail.com>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/ByteBuffer.h>
#include <AK/FixedArray.h>
#include <AK/MaybeOwned.h>
#include <AK/MemoryStream.h>
#include <AK/Stream.h>

extern "C" {
typedef struct z_stream_s z_stream;
}

namespace Compress {

class GenericZlibDecompressor : public Stream {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(GenericZlibDecompressor);

public:
    ~GenericZlibDecompressor() override;

    virtual ErrorOr<Bytes> read_some(Bytes) override;
    virtual ErrorOr<size_t> write_some(ReadonlyBytes) override;
    virtual bool is_eof() const override;
    virtual bool is_open() const override;
    virtual void close() override;

protected:
    GenericZlibDecompressor(AK::FixedArray<u8>, MaybeOwned<Stream>, z_stream*);

    static ErrorOr<z_stream*> new_z_stream(int window_bits);

private:
    MaybeOwned<Stream> m_stream;
    z_stream* m_zstream;

    bool m_eof { false };

    AK::FixedArray<u8> m_buffer;
};

template<class T>
ErrorOr<ByteBuffer> decompress_all(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    auto input_stream = make<AK::FixedMemoryStream>(bytes);
    auto deflate_stream = TRY(T::create(MaybeOwned<Stream>(move(input_stream))));
    return TRY(deflate_stream->read_until_eof(4096));
}

}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use std::io::{self, Write};

use brotli::CompressorWriter;
use flate2::Compression;
use flate2::write::{DeflateEncoder, GzEncoder, ZlibEncoder};

use crate::Format;

/// The size of the buffer that the brotli encoder compresses into before it writes to its output.
const BROTLI_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 4096;
/// The quality and the window size that brotli uses by default.
const BROTLI_QUALITY: u32 = 11;
const BROTLI_WINDOW_BITS: u32 = 22;

/// The encoder of a format, which writes what it compresses to a buffer that it keeps, until it finishes.
enum Encoder {
    Brotli(Box<CompressorWriter<Vec<u8>>>),
    Zlib(ZlibEncoder<Vec<u8>>),
    Deflate(DeflateEncoder<Vec<u8>>),
    Gzip(GzEncoder<Vec<u8>>),
    Finished,
}

/// Compresses data that arrives in pieces, giving what it has compressed after each one.
pub struct Compressor {
    encoder: Encoder,
}

impl Compressor {
    pub fn new(format: Format) -> Self {
        let encoder = match format {
            Format::Brotli => Encoder::Brotli(Box::new(CompressorWriter::new(
                Vec::new(),
                BROTLI_BUFFER_SIZE,
                BROTLI_QUALITY,
                BROTLI_WINDOW_BITS,
            ))),
            Format::Zlib => Encoder::Zlib(ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default())),
            Format::Deflate => Encoder::Deflate(DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default())),
            Format::Gzip => Encoder::Gzip(GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default())),
        };
        Self { encoder }
    }

    /// Compresses the next bytes of the data, returning what the encoder output, which can be nothing.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// If the compressor has finished.
    pub fn compress(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let output = match &mut self.encoder {
            Encoder::Brotli(encoder) => {
                encoder.write_all(bytes)?;
                encoder.get_mut()
            }
            Encoder::Zlib(encoder) => {
                encoder.write_all(bytes)?;
                encoder.get_mut()
            }
            Encoder::Deflate(encoder) => {
                encoder.write_all(bytes)?;
                encoder.get_mut()
            }
            Encoder::Gzip(encoder) => {
                encoder.write_all(bytes)?;
                encoder.get_mut()
            }
            Encoder::Finished => panic!("a compressor compresses nothing after it finishes"),
        };
        Ok(core::mem::take(output))
    }

    /// Finishes the compressed data, returning the rest of what the encoder output.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// If the compressor has finished.
    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        match core::mem::replace(&mut self.encoder, Encoder::Finished) {
            // NB: The brotli encoder finishes the compressed data when it gives up its output.
            Encoder::Brotli(encoder) => Ok(encoder.into_inner()),
            Encoder::Zlib(encoder) => encoder.finish(),
            Encoder::Deflate(encoder) => encoder.finish(),
            Encoder::Gzip(encoder) => encoder.finish(),
            Encoder::Finished => panic!("a compressor finishes once"),
        }
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use core::fmt;

use brotli::{BrotliDecompressStream, BrotliResult, BrotliState, HeapAlloc, HuffmanCode};
use flate2::{Decompress, FlushDecompress, Status};

use crate::Format;

type BrotliDecoder = BrotliState<HeapAlloc<u8>, HeapAlloc<u32>, HeapAlloc<HuffmanCode>>;

/// The decoder of a format.
enum Decoder {
    Brotli(Box<BrotliDecoder>),
    // zlib, raw deflate and gzip, which zlib-rs decodes.
    Flate(Decompress),
}

/// How much the output of a decoder grows by while it decompresses.
const OUTPUT_GROWTH: usize = 16 * 1024;

/// The window that gzip data is decoded with, the largest that the format allows.
const GZIP_WINDOW_BITS: u8 = 15;

/// What decompressing some input gave: the output, and how many bytes at the end of the input the decoder did not
/// consume, which it leaves only once it has reached the end of the compressed data.
pub struct Decompressed {
    pub output: Vec<u8>,
    pub unconsumed_input: usize,
}

/// The input is not data of the format, with the decoder's description of why.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DecompressionFailed(String);

impl fmt::Display for DecompressionFailed {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str(&self.0)
    }
}

/// Decompresses data that arrives in pieces, giving all that it can decompress of each one.
pub struct Decompressor {
    decoder: Decoder,
    has_reached_end: bool,
}

impl Decompressor {
    pub fn new(format: Format) -> Self {
        let decoder = match format {
            // NB: new_strict() decodes RFC 7932 brotli only, without its large window extension.
            Format::Brotli => Decoder::Brotli(Box::new(BrotliDecoder::new_strict(
                HeapAlloc::default(),
                HeapAlloc::default(),
                HeapAlloc::default(),
            ))),
            Format::Zlib => Decoder::Flate(Decompress::new(true)),
            Format::Deflate => Decoder::Flate(Decompress::new(false)),
            Format::Gzip => Decoder::Flate(Decompress::new_gzip(GZIP_WINDOW_BITS)),
        };
        Self {
            decoder,
            has_reached_end: false,
        }
    }

    /// Whether the decoder has reached the end of the compressed data.
    pub fn has_reached_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_reached_end
    }

    /// Decompresses the next bytes of the data, giving all the output that the decoder can make of them and of what it
    /// kept of the bytes before them. Bytes after the end of the compressed data are left unconsumed.
    pub fn decompress(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> Result<Decompressed, DecompressionFailed> {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let unconsumed = if self.has_reached_end {
            input
        } else {
            match &mut self.decoder {
                Decoder::Brotli(decoder) => decompress_brotli(decoder, input, &mut output, &mut self.has_reached_end)?,
                Decoder::Flate(decoder) => decompress_flate(decoder, input, &mut output, &mut self.has_reached_end)?,
            }
        };
        Ok(Decompressed {
            output,
            unconsumed_input: unconsumed.len(),
        })
    }
}

/// Returns the input that the decoder did not consume.
fn decompress_brotli<'a>(
    decoder: &mut BrotliDecoder,
    input: &'a [u8],
    output: &mut Vec<u8>,
    has_reached_end: &mut bool,
) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecompressionFailed> {
    let mut available_in = input.len();
    let mut input_offset = 0;
    let mut total_out = 0;
    loop {
        let mut output_offset = output.len();
        output.resize(output_offset + OUTPUT_GROWTH, 0);
        let mut available_out = OUTPUT_GROWTH;
        let result = BrotliDecompressStream(
            &mut available_in,
            &mut input_offset,
            input,
            &mut available_out,
            &mut output_offset,
            output,
            &mut total_out,
            decoder,
        );
        output.truncate(output_offset);
        match result {
            BrotliResult::NeedsMoreOutput => {}
            BrotliResult::NeedsMoreInput => return Ok(&input[input_offset..]),
            BrotliResult::ResultSuccess => {
                *has_reached_end = true;
                return Ok(&input[input_offset..]);
            }
            BrotliResult::ResultFailure => return Err(DecompressionFailed(format!("{:?}", decoder.error_code))),
        }
    }
}

/// Returns the input that the decoder did not consume.
fn decompress_flate<'a>(
    decoder: &mut Decompress,
    mut input: &'a [u8],
    output: &mut Vec<u8>,
    has_reached_end: &mut bool,
) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecompressionFailed> {
    loop {
        output.reserve(OUTPUT_GROWTH);
        let total_in = decoder.total_in();
        let status = decoder
            .decompress_vec(input, output, FlushDecompress::None)
            .map_err(|error| DecompressionFailed(error.to_string()))?;
        let consumed = usize::try_from(decoder.total_in() - total_in).expect("the decoder consumed some of the input");
        input = &input[consumed..];
        match status {
            Status::StreamEnd => {
                *has_reached_end = true;
                return Ok(input);
            }
            // NB: The decoder stops when it runs out of input or of room for its output, and fails to make progress
            //     with BufError, so it has given all it can of this input once it stops short of both.
            Status::Ok if !input.is_empty() || output.len() == output.capacity() => {}
            Status::Ok | Status::BufError => return Ok(input),
        }
    }
}

//! Streaming compression and decompression of brotli, zlib, raw deflate and gzip data, with flate2 on zlib-rs and
//! with brotli.

mod compressor;
mod decompressor;

pub use compressor::Compressor;
pub use decompressor::{Decompressed, DecompressionFailed, Decompressor};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Format {
    /// RFC 7932
    Brotli,
    /// RFC 1950
    Zlib,
    /// RFC 1951
    Deflate,
    /// RFC 1952
    Gzip,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

FILE: Libraries/LibCompress/Rust/src/tests.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use crate::{Compressor, Decompressor, Format};

const FORMATS: [Format; 4] = [Format::Brotli, Format::Zlib, Format::Deflate, Format::Gzip];

fn compress(format: Format, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut compressor = Compressor::new(format);
    let mut compressed = compressor.compress(data).unwrap();
    compressed.extend(compressor.finish().unwrap());
    compressed
}

fn sample_data() -> Vec<u8> {
    (0..100_000u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8 ^ (i / 1000) as u8).collect()
}

#[test]
fn round_trip_in_one_piece() {
    let data = sample_data();
    for format in FORMATS {
        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(&compress(format, &data)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decompressed.output, data, "{format:?}");
        assert_eq!(decompressed.unconsumed_input, 0, "{format:?}");
        assert!(decompressor.has_reached_end(), "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn round_trip_in_pieces() {
    let data = sample_data();
    for format in FORMATS {
        let mut compressor = Compressor::new(format);
        let mut compressed = Vec::new();
        for piece in data.chunks(777) {
            compressed.extend(compressor.compress(piece).unwrap());
        }
        compressed.extend(compressor.finish().unwrap());

        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        for piece in compressed.chunks(13) {
            let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(piece).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(decompressed.unconsumed_input, 0, "{format:?}");
            output.extend(decompressed.output);
        }
        assert_eq!(output, data, "{format:?}");
        assert!(decompressor.has_reached_end(), "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn gives_all_the_output_of_each_piece() {
    let data = vec![b'a'; 1_000_000];
    for format in FORMATS {
        let compressed = compress(format, &data);
        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(&compressed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decompressed.output.len(), data.len(), "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn leaves_input_after_the_end_unconsumed() {
    let data = b"Ladybird";
    for format in FORMATS {
        let mut compressed = compress(format, data);
        compressed.extend([0, 1, 2]);

        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(&compressed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decompressed.output, data, "{format:?}");
        assert_eq!(decompressed.unconsumed_input, 3, "{format:?}");
        assert!(decompressor.has_reached_end(), "{format:?}");

        let after_end = decompressor.decompress(&[3, 4]).unwrap();
        assert!(after_end.output.is_empty(), "{format:?}");
        assert_eq!(after_end.unconsumed_input, 2, "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn does_not_reach_the_end_of_truncated_input() {
    let data = sample_data();
    for format in FORMATS {
        let compressed = compress(format, &data);
        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(&compressed[..compressed.len() - 1]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decompressed.unconsumed_input, 0, "{format:?}");
        assert!(!decompressor.has_reached_end(), "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn fails_on_corrupt_input() {
    for format in FORMATS {
        let mut compressed = compress(format, &sample_data());
        let middle = compressed.len() / 2;
        compressed[middle] ^= 0xff;
        compressed[middle + 1] ^= 0xff;

        let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(format);
        assert!(decompressor.decompress(&compressed).is_err(), "{format:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_gzip_stream_has_one_member() {
    let mut compressed = compress(Format::Gzip, b"one");
    let second_member = compress(Format::Gzip, b"two");
    compressed.extend(&second_member);

    let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(Format::Gzip);
    let decompressed = decompressor.decompress(&compressed).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(decompressed.output, b"one");
    assert_eq!(decompressed.unconsumed_input, second_member.len());
}

#[test]
fn rejects_brotli_large_window() {
    // "Hello World", compressed with the large window extension and a window of 25 bits.
    let compressed = [17, 25, 20, 0, 2, 72, 101, 108, 108, 111, 32, 87, 111, 114, 108, 100, 3];
    let mut decompressor = Decompressor::new(Format::Brotli);
    assert!(decompressor.decompress(&compressed).is_err());
}

#include <AK/Try.h>
#include <LibCore/AnonymousBuffer.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS)
#    include <mach/mach.h>
#    include <mach/mach_vm.h>
#endif

namespace Core {

ErrorOr<AnonymousBuffer> AnonymousBuffer::create_with_size(size_t size)
{
    auto fd = TRY(Core::System::anon_create(size, O_CLOEXEC, Core::System::AllowSealing::Yes));
    return create_from_anon_fd(fd, size);
}

ErrorOr<AnonymousBuffer> AnonymousBuffer::create_from_anon_fd(int fd, size_t size)
{
    auto impl = TRY(AnonymousBufferImpl::create(fd, size));
    return AnonymousBuffer(move(impl));
}

ErrorOr<AnonymousBuffer> AnonymousBuffer::snapshot() const
{
    return snapshot(0, size());
}

ErrorOr<AnonymousBuffer> AnonymousBuffer::snapshot(size_t offset, size_t size) const
{
    if (!is_valid())
        return Error::from_string_literal("Cannot snapshot an invalid anonymous buffer");

    if (offset > this->size() || size > this->size() - offset)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Anonymous buffer snapshot range is out of bounds");

    bool is_size_sealed = false;

#if defined(F_ADD_SEALS) && defined(F_GET_SEALS) && defined(F_SEAL_GROW) && defined(F_SEAL_SHRINK) && defined(F_SEAL_SEAL)
    static constexpr auto REQUIRED_SEALS = F_SEAL_GROW | F_SEAL_SHRINK;

    auto seals = TRY(Core::System::fcntl(fd(), F_GET_SEALS, static_cast<uintptr_t>(0)));

    if ((seals & REQUIRED_SEALS) != REQUIRED_SEALS && !(seals & F_SEAL_SEAL)) {
        TRY(Core::System::fcntl(fd(), F_ADD_SEALS, REQUIRED_SEALS));
        seals |= REQUIRED_SEALS;
    }

    is_size_sealed = (seals & REQUIRED_SEALS) == REQUIRED_SEALS;
#endif

    TRY(validate_backing_size());

    auto copy = TRY(create_with_size(size));
    if (size == 0)
        return copy;

    if (is_size_sealed) {
        bytes().slice(offset, size).copy_to({ copy.data<u8>(), copy.size() });
        return copy;
    }

#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS)
    // POSIX shared memory descriptors reject pread() on macOS. Copy through Mach so a concurrent truncation is reported
    // as an error instead of raising SIGBUS while reading the mapping directly.
    mach_vm_size_t copied_size = 0;

    auto result = mach_vm_read_overwrite(mach_task_self(),
        reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(data<u8>() + offset), size,
        reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(copy.data<void>()), &copied_size);

    if (result != KERN_SUCCESS || copied_size != size)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Failed to snapshot anonymous buffer");
#else
    // Unlike bytes().copy_to(), pread() reports a concurrent truncation as a short read instead of raising SIGBUS
    // while reading the unsealed mapping.
    size_t copied_size = 0;

    while (copied_size < size) {
        auto bytes_read = ::pread(fd(), copy.data<u8>() + copied_size, size - copied_size, static_cast<off_t>(offset + copied_size));
        if (bytes_read < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return Error::from_errno(errno);
        }

        if (bytes_read == 0)
            return Error::from_string_literal("Anonymous buffer was truncated while being snapshotted");
        copied_size += static_cast<size_t>(bytes_read);
    }
#endif

    return copy;
}

ErrorOr<void> AnonymousBuffer::validate_backing_size() const
{
    if (!is_valid())
        return Error::from_string_literal("Cannot validate the backing store of an invalid anonymous buffer");

#if defined(AK_OS_LINUX)
    // Sealed first, or the holder could shrink it after the check.
    auto seals = TRY(Core::System::fcntl(fd(), F_GET_SEALS, static_cast<uintptr_t>(0)));
    if (!(seals & F_SEAL_SHRINK))
        TRY(Core::System::fcntl(fd(), F_ADD_SEALS, F_SEAL_SHRINK));
#endif

    auto file_status = TRY(Core::System::fstat(fd()));
    if (file_status.st_size < 0 || static_cast<u64>(file_status.st_size) < size())
        return Error::from_string_literal("Anonymous buffer is smaller than its claimed size");
    return {};
}

void AnonymousBuffer::populate_for_reading() const
{
    if (!is_valid() || size() == 0)
        return;
    auto* data = const_cast<void*>(m_impl->data());
#if defined(AK_OS_LINUX) && defined(MADV_POPULATE_READ)
    // Kernels before 5.14 refuse this advice.
    (void)madvise(data, size(), MADV_POPULATE_READ);
#else
    (void)madvise(data, size(), MADV_WILLNEED);
#endif
}

ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<AnonymousBufferImpl>> AnonymousBufferImpl::create(int fd, size_t size)
{
    void* data = nullptr;
    // POSIX mmap rejects a zero length with EINVAL, so leave m_data null for zero-size buffers.
    if (size > 0) {
        data = mmap(nullptr, round_up_to_power_of_two(size, PAGE_SIZE), PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
        if (data == MAP_FAILED) {
            auto error = Error::from_errno(errno);
            close(fd);
            return error;
        }
    }
    auto impl_or_error = AK::adopt_nonnull_ref_or_enomem(new (nothrow) AnonymousBufferImpl(fd, size, data));
    if (impl_or_error.is_error()) {
        close(fd);
        if (data != nullptr)
            munmap(data, round_up_to_power_of_two(size, PAGE_SIZE));
    }
    return impl_or_error;
}

AnonymousBufferImpl::~AnonymousBufferImpl()
{
    if (m_fd != -1) {
        auto rc = close(m_fd);
        VERIFY(rc == 0);
    }
    if (m_data) {
        auto rc = munmap(m_data, round_up_to_power_of_two(m_size, PAGE_SIZE));
        VERIFY(rc == 0);
    }
}

AnonymousBufferImpl::AnonymousBufferImpl(int fd, size_t size, void* data)
    : m_fd(fd)
    , m_size(size)
    , m_data(data)
{
}

}

/*
