#include <AK/ByteBuffer.h>
#include <AK/ScopeGuard.h>
#include <LibCrypto/OpenSSL.h>
#include <LibCrypto/PK/EC.h>
#include <openssl/core_names.h>
#include <openssl/ec.h>
#include <openssl/evp.h>
#include <openssl/param_build.h>

namespace Crypto::PK {

static ErrorOr<char const*> curve_name(size_t scalar_size)
{
    switch (scalar_size) {
    case 32:
        return "P-256";
    case 48:
        return "P-384";
    case 66:
        return "P-521";
    default:
        return Error::from_string_literal("Unsupported EC curve");
    }
}

static ErrorOr<OpenSSL_PKEY> public_key_from_coordinates(ReadonlyBytes x, ReadonlyBytes y)
{
    if (x.size() != y.size())
        return Error::from_string_literal("EC coordinates have different sizes");
    auto const* group = TRY(curve_name(x.size()));
    auto octets = TRY(ByteBuffer::create_uninitialized(1 + x.size() + y.size()));
    octets[0] = 0x04;
    octets.overwrite(1, x.data(), x.size());
    octets.overwrite(1 + x.size(), y.data(), y.size());

    auto* builder = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_new());
    ScopeGuard const free_builder = [&] { OSSL_PARAM_BLD_free(builder); };
    OPENSSL_TRY(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_utf8_string(builder, OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_GROUP_NAME, group, 0));
    OPENSSL_TRY(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_octet_string(builder, OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_PUB_KEY, octets.data(), octets.size()));
    auto* params = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param(builder));
    ScopeGuard const free_params = [&] { OSSL_PARAM_free(params); };

    auto ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY_CTX::wrap(EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_name(nullptr, "EC", nullptr)));
    OPENSSL_TRY(EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init(ctx.ptr()));
    EVP_PKEY* key_pointer = nullptr;
    if (EVP_PKEY_fromdata(ctx.ptr(), &key_pointer, EVP_PKEY_PUBLIC_KEY, params) != 1)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Invalid EC public key");
    auto key = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY::wrap(key_pointer));

    auto check_ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY_CTX::wrap(EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey(nullptr, key.ptr(), nullptr)));
    if (EVP_PKEY_public_check(check_ctx.ptr()) != 1)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Invalid EC public key");
    return key;
}

ErrorOr<bool> ecdsa_verify(ReadonlyBytes x, ReadonlyBytes y, ReadonlyBytes digest, ReadonlyBytes r, ReadonlyBytes s)
{
    auto key = TRY(public_key_from_coordinates(x, y));
    if (r.size() != x.size() || s.size() != x.size())
        return false;

    auto* signature_object = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(ECDSA_SIG_new());
    ScopeGuard const free_signature_object = [&] { ECDSA_SIG_free(signature_object); };
    auto* r_value = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(BN_bin2bn(r.data(), r.size(), nullptr));
    auto* s_value = BN_bin2bn(s.data(), s.size(), nullptr);
    if (!s_value || ECDSA_SIG_set0(signature_object, r_value, s_value) != 1) {
        BN_free(r_value);
        BN_free(s_value);
        return Error::from_string_literal("Failed to build the ECDSA signature");
    }

    u8* signature = nullptr;
    ScopeGuard const free_signature = [&] { OPENSSL_free(signature); };
    auto signature_size = i2d_ECDSA_SIG(signature_object, &signature);
    if (signature_size <= 0)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Failed to encode the ECDSA signature");

    auto ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY_CTX::wrap(EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey(nullptr, key.ptr(), nullptr)));
    OPENSSL_TRY(EVP_PKEY_verify_init(ctx.ptr()));
    auto result = EVP_PKEY_verify(ctx.ptr(), signature, signature_size, digest.data(), digest.size());
    if (result == 1)
        return true;
    if (result == 0)
        return false;
    OPENSSL_TRY(result);
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

}

#include <AK/ScopeGuard.h>
#include <LibCrypto/OpenSSL.h>
#include <LibCrypto/PK/RSA.h>
#include <openssl/bn.h>
#include <openssl/core_names.h>
#include <openssl/evp.h>
#include <openssl/param_build.h>

namespace Crypto::PK {

// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017#section-3.1
// [...] the RSA public exponent e is an integer between 3 and n - 1 [...]
// NB: An odd e above 1 is at least 3.
static bool public_exponent_is_valid(BIGNUM const* n, BIGNUM const* e)
{
    return BN_is_odd(e) && !BN_is_one(e) && BN_cmp(e, n) < 0;
}

static OSSL_PARAM const pkcs1_parameters[] {
    OSSL_PARAM_utf8_string(OSSL_SIGNATURE_PARAM_PAD_MODE, const_cast<char*>(OSSL_PKEY_RSA_PAD_MODE_PKCSV15), sizeof(OSSL_PKEY_RSA_PAD_MODE_PKCSV15) - 1),
    OSSL_PARAM_END,
};

ErrorOr<bool> rsa_pkcs1_verify(ReadonlyBytes modulus, ReadonlyBytes public_exponent, Hash::HashKind hash_kind, ReadonlyBytes message, ReadonlyBytes signature)
{
    // NB: The builder reads each BIGNUM when it builds the parameters, so the BIGNUMs must outlive it.
    BIGNUM* n = nullptr;
    BIGNUM* e = nullptr;
    OSSL_PARAM_BLD* builder = nullptr;
    OSSL_PARAM* params = nullptr;
    ScopeGuard const free_parameters = [&] {
        OSSL_PARAM_free(params);
        OSSL_PARAM_BLD_free(builder);
        BN_free(n);
        BN_free(e);
    };
    n = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(BN_bin2bn(modulus.data(), modulus.size(), nullptr));
    e = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(BN_bin2bn(public_exponent.data(), public_exponent.size(), nullptr));
    builder = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_new());
    OPENSSL_TRY(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_BN(builder, OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_RSA_N, n));
    OPENSSL_TRY(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_push_BN(builder, OSSL_PKEY_PARAM_RSA_E, e));
    params = OPENSSL_TRY_PTR(OSSL_PARAM_BLD_to_param(builder));

    auto key_ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY_CTX::wrap(EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_name(nullptr, "RSA", nullptr)));
    OPENSSL_TRY(EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init(key_ctx.ptr()));
    EVP_PKEY* key_pointer = nullptr;
    OPENSSL_TRY(EVP_PKEY_fromdata(key_ctx.ptr(), &key_pointer, EVP_PKEY_PUBLIC_KEY, params));
    auto key = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY::wrap(key_pointer));

    if (!public_exponent_is_valid(n, e))
        return false;
    auto check_ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_PKEY_CTX::wrap(EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_pkey(nullptr, key.ptr(), nullptr)));
    if (EVP_PKEY_public_check(check_ctx.ptr()) != 1)
        return false;
    if (signature.size() != static_cast<size_t>(EVP_PKEY_get_size(key.ptr())))
        return false;

    auto ctx = TRY(OpenSSL_MD_CTX::create());
    OPENSSL_TRY(EVP_DigestVerifyInit_ex(ctx.ptr(), nullptr, TRY(Hash::openssl_digest_name(hash_kind)), nullptr, nullptr, key.ptr(), pkcs1_parameters));
    auto result = EVP_DigestVerify(ctx.ptr(), signature.data(), signature.size(), message.data(), message.size());
    if (result == 1)
        return true;
    if (result == 0)
        return false;
    OPENSSL_TRY(result);
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The libraries that link this crate link OpenSSL, but a crate's unit tests link no such library. With the
//! `link-openssl` feature, this links OpenSSL's libcrypto itself: the one the build system passes in
//! LADYBIRD_OPENSSL_CRYPTO_LIBRARY, or else one that a build directory has, or else the system's.

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn main() {
    println!("cargo::rerun-if-env-changed=LADYBIRD_OPENSSL_CRYPTO_LIBRARY");
    if env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_LINK_OPENSSL").is_none() {
        return;
    }

    let library = env::var_os("LADYBIRD_OPENSSL_CRYPTO_LIBRARY")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .or_else(find_in_build_directories);
    let Some(library) = library else {
        println!("cargo::rustc-link-lib=dylib=crypto");
        return;
    };
    println!("cargo::rerun-if-changed={}", library.display());

    let windows = env::var("CARGO_CFG_WINDOWS").is_ok();
    let file_name = library
        .file_name()
        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
        .expect("library file name");
    let stem = file_name.split('.').next().expect("library name");
    let name = if windows {
        stem
    } else {
        stem.strip_prefix("lib").unwrap_or(stem)
    };
    let kind = if file_name.ends_with(".a") { "static" } else { "dylib" };

    // NB: Cargo only lets binaries it runs find shared libraries that are in its target directory, so the library
    //     and the files it loads from at runtime are linked or copied there.
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR"));
    let directory = library.parent().expect("library directory");
    let mut runtime_directories = vec![directory.to_path_buf()];
    if windows && let Some(prefix) = directory.parent() {
        runtime_directories.push(prefix.join("bin"));
    }
    for runtime_directory in runtime_directories {
        let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(&runtime_directory) else {
            continue;
        };
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            let entry_name = entry.file_name();
            let Some(entry_name) = entry_name.to_str() else {
                continue;
            };
            if entry_name.starts_with(&format!("{stem}.")) || (windows && entry_name.starts_with(&format!("{stem}-"))) {
                place(&entry.path(), &out_dir.join(entry_name));
            }
        }
    }
    // The linker looks for the library by its plain name, which the one picked may not have, such as libcrypto.so.3
    // with no libcrypto.so next to it.
    if !windows && kind == "dylib" {
        let extension = if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() == Ok("macos") {
            "dylib"
        } else {
            "so"
        };
        place(&library, &out_dir.join(format!("{stem}.{extension}")));
    }
    println!("cargo::rustc-link-search=native={}", out_dir.display());
    println!("cargo::rustc-link-lib={kind}={name}");
}

// The vcpkg triplets that hold libraries for the target, such as x64-linux-dynamic for x86_64 Linux.
fn is_triplet_for_target(triplet: &str) -> bool {
    let arch = match env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").as_deref() {
        Ok("x86_64") => "x64",
        Ok("aarch64") => "arm64",
        Ok("x86") => "x86",
        Ok("arm") => "arm",
        _ => return false,
    };
    let os = match env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() {
        Ok("macos") => "osx".to_owned(),
        Ok(os) => os.to_owned(),
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    triplet == format!("{arch}-{os}") || triplet.starts_with(&format!("{arch}-{os}-"))
}

// The libcrypto of the vcpkg dependencies of a build directory for the target, such as Build/release.
fn find_in_build_directories() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let workspace = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("../../..")
        .canonicalize()
        .ok()?;
    let mut candidates = Vec::new();
    for build in fs::read_dir(workspace.join("Build")).ok()?.flatten() {
        let Ok(triplets) = fs::read_dir(build.path().join("vcpkg_installed")) else {
            continue;
        };
        for triplet in triplets.flatten() {
            if !triplet.file_name().to_str().is_some_and(is_triplet_for_target) {
                continue;
            }
            for name in ["libcrypto.so", "libcrypto.dylib", "libcrypto.a", "libcrypto.lib"] {
                let path = triplet.path().join("lib").join(name);
                if path.exists() {
                    candidates.push(path);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    candidates.sort();
    candidates.into_iter().next()
}

fn place(source: &Path, destination: &Path) {
    let _ = fs::remove_file(destination);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    let placed = std::os::unix::fs::symlink(source, destination);
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let placed = fs::copy(source, destination).map(|_| ());
    placed.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("Placing {} in {}: {error}", source.display(), destination.display()));
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The few DER structures that Web Crypto exports or checks. Each one is written into a single buffer of its final size,
//! so that no partial copy of a private key is left behind, which OpenSSL's encoders do leave.
//! Object identifiers are given as the contents of their DER encoding.

pub(crate) const INTEGER: u8 = 0x02;
pub(crate) const BIT_STRING: u8 = 0x03;
pub(crate) const OCTET_STRING: u8 = 0x04;
pub(crate) const OBJECT_IDENTIFIER: u8 = 0x06;
pub(crate) const SEQUENCE: u8 = 0x30;
pub(crate) const NULL: [u8; 2] = [0x05, 0x00];

/// The tag and definite length that start an element of `length` content bytes.
pub(crate) fn header(tag: u8, length: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut header = vec![tag];
    if length < 0x80 {
        header.push(length as u8);
    } else {
        let bytes = length.to_be_bytes();
        let leading_zeros = bytes.iter().take_while(|&&byte| byte == 0).count();
        header.push(0x80 | (bytes.len() - leading_zeros) as u8);
        header.extend_from_slice(&bytes[leading_zeros..]);
    }
    header
}

/// An element of the given tag and contents, the contents given in parts.
pub(crate) fn element(tag: u8, contents: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let length = contents.iter().map(|part| part.len()).sum();
    let header = header(tag, length);
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + length);
    output.extend_from_slice(&header);
    for part in contents {
        output.extend_from_slice(part);
    }
    output
}

/// The object identifier of the given DER contents.
pub(crate) fn object_identifier(contents: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    element(OBJECT_IDENTIFIER, &[contents])
}

fn algorithm_identifier(algorithm: &[u8], parameters: Option<&[u8]>) -> Vec<u8> {
    element(
        SEQUENCE,
        &[&object_identifier(algorithm), parameters.unwrap_or_default()],
    )
}

/// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017#appendix-A.1.2
pub(crate) fn rsa_private_key(integers: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<u8> {
    // RSAPrivateKey ::= SEQUENCE {
    //     version           Version,
    //     modulus           INTEGER,  -- n
    //     publicExponent    INTEGER,  -- e
    //     privateExponent   INTEGER,  -- d
    //     prime1            INTEGER,  -- p
    //     prime2            INTEGER,  -- q
    //     exponent1         INTEGER,  -- d mod (p-1)
    //     exponent2         INTEGER,  -- d mod (q-1)
    //     coefficient       INTEGER,  -- (inverse of q) mod p
    //     otherPrimeInfos   OtherPrimeInfos OPTIONAL
    // }
    // NB: The integers are unsigned and have no leading zeros, so a zero byte keeps one whose top bit is set positive.
    let version = [INTEGER, 1, 0];
    let prefixes: Vec<Vec<u8>> = integers
        .iter()
        .map(|integer| {
            let needs_zero = integer.first().is_none_or(|&byte| byte & 0x80 != 0);
            let mut prefix = header(INTEGER, integer.len() + usize::from(needs_zero));
            if needs_zero {
                prefix.push(0);
            }
            prefix
        })
        .collect();
    let mut contents: Vec<&[u8]> = vec![&version];
    for (prefix, integer) in prefixes.iter().zip(integers) {
        contents.push(prefix);
        contents.push(integer);
    }
    element(SEQUENCE, &contents)
}

/// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-4.1
pub(crate) fn subject_public_key_info(algorithm: &[u8], parameters: Option<&[u8]>, public_key: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let bit_string = element(BIT_STRING, &[&[0], public_key]);
    element(SEQUENCE, &[&algorithm_identifier(algorithm, parameters), &bit_string])
}

/// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5208#section-5
pub(crate) fn private_key_info(algorithm: &[u8], parameters: Option<&[u8]>, private_key: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let version = [INTEGER, 1, 0];
    let private_key_header = header(OCTET_STRING, private_key.len());
    element(
        SEQUENCE,
        &[
            &version,
            &algorithm_identifier(algorithm, parameters),
            &private_key_header,
            private_key,
        ],
    )
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2024-2025, Altomani Gianluca <altomanigianluca@gmail.com>
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! EC keys of the NIST prime curves. A key given by its coordinates or scalar is on the curve whose coordinates have
//! that size: 32 bytes for P-256, 48 for P-384 and 66 for P-521.

use core::ffi::{CStr, c_int};

use crate::der;
use crate::key::{HandleTag, Key, KeyDecodeError, KeyHandle, KeyPair, SecretBytes, StoredKey};
use crate::openssl::{self, ParamBuilder, Pkey, end_parameter, octet_string_parameter, utf8_parameter};
use crate::{CryptoError, EcCurve, KeyAlgorithm, sys};

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct EcPublicKey {
    key: Pkey,
    curve: EcCurve,
}

pub(crate) struct EcPrivateKey {
    key: Pkey,
    curve: EcCurve,
}

impl EcCurve {
    fn from_scalar_size(scalar_size: usize) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        match scalar_size {
            32 => Ok(Self::P256),
            48 => Ok(Self::P384),
            66 => Ok(Self::P521),
            _ => Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Unsupported EC curve")),
        }
    }

    fn scalar_size(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::P256 => 32,
            Self::P384 => 48,
            Self::P521 => 66,
        }
    }

    /// The name of the curve's group, as OpenSSL takes it.
    fn name(self) -> &'static CStr {
        match self {
            Self::P256 => c"P-256",
            Self::P384 => c"P-384",
            Self::P521 => c"P-521",
        }
    }

    fn nid(self) -> c_int {
        match self {
            Self::P256 => sys::NID_X9_62_PRIME256V1,
            Self::P384 => sys::NID_SECP384R1,
            Self::P521 => sys::NID_SECP521R1,
        }
    }

    /// The contents of the DER encoding of the curve's object identifier.
    fn oid(self) -> &'static [u8] {
        match self {
            // secp256r1, 1.2.840.10045.3.1.7
            Self::P256 => &[0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0xce, 0x3d, 0x03, 0x01, 0x07],
            // secp384r1, 1.3.132.0.34
            Self::P384 => &[0x2b, 0x81, 0x04, 0x00, 0x22],
            // secp521r1, 1.3.132.0.35
            Self::P521 => &[0x2b, 0x81, 0x04, 0x00, 0x23],
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_oid(oid: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
        [Self::P256, Self::P384, Self::P521]
            .into_iter()
            .find(|curve| curve.oid() == oid)
    }

    /// The arcs of the curve's object identifier, as a stored key gives them.
    fn arcs(self) -> &'static [u32] {
        match self {
            Self::P256 => &[1, 2, 840, 10045, 3, 1, 7],
            Self::P384 => &[1, 3, 132, 0, 34],
            Self::P521 => &[1, 3, 132, 0, 35],
        }
    }
}

/// The coordinates of the public point of `key`, a key on `curve`.
fn coordinates(key: &Pkey, curve: EcCurve) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), CryptoError> {
    let coordinate = |name| -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
        let number = key.number(name).ok_or(CryptoError::Backend)?;
        Ok(number.to_padded(curve.scalar_size())?.into_vec())
    };
    Ok((coordinate(c"qx")?, coordinate(c"qy")?))
}

fn uncompressed_point(key: &Pkey, curve: EcCurve) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let (x, y) = coordinates(key, curve)?;
    let mut octets = Vec::with_capacity(1 + x.len() + y.len());
    octets.push(0x04);
    octets.extend_from_slice(&x);
    octets.extend_from_slice(&y);
    Ok(octets)
}

impl EcPublicKey {
    /// A public key from its SEC 1 encoding, uncompressed or compressed.
    pub(crate) fn from_octets(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        let scalar_size = match data.first() {
            None => return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Empty EC point")),
            Some(0x04) if data.len() % 2 == 1 => (data.len() - 1) / 2,
            Some(0x02 | 0x03) => data.len() - 1,
            Some(_) => return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Unsupported EC point format")),
        };
        let curve = EcCurve::from_scalar_size(scalar_size)?;
        let invalid = |_| CryptoError::Invalid("Invalid EC public key");
        let params = [
            utf8_parameter(c"group", curve.name()),
            octet_string_parameter(c"pub", data),
            end_parameter(),
        ];
        let key = Pkey::from_data(c"EC", sys::EVP_PKEY_PUBLIC_KEY, &params).map_err(invalid)?;
        if !openssl::check_key(&key, false, false).map_err(invalid)? {
            return Err(invalid(CryptoError::Backend));
        }
        Ok(Self { key, curve })
    }

    fn from_coordinates(x: &[u8], y: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        if x.len() != y.len() {
            return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("EC coordinates have different sizes"));
        }
        let mut octets = Vec::with_capacity(1 + x.len() + y.len());
        octets.push(0x04);
        octets.extend_from_slice(x);
        octets.extend_from_slice(y);
        Self::from_octets(&octets)
    }

    fn coordinates(&self) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), CryptoError> {
        coordinates(&self.key, self.curve)
    }

    fn to_uncompressed(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
        uncompressed_point(&self.key, self.curve)
    }
}

impl EcPrivateKey {
    fn generate(curve: EcCurve) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        let params = [utf8_parameter(c"group", curve.name()), end_parameter()];
        Ok(Self {
            key: Pkey::generate(c"EC", &params)?,
            curve,
        })
    }

    /// The key of the private value `d`, whose public key, when given, must be the one `d` gives.
    fn from_scalar(d: &[u8], public_key: Option<&EcPublicKey>) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        let curve = EcCurve::from_scalar_size(d.len())?;
        let point =
            openssl::ec_public_point(curve.nid(), d)?.ok_or(CryptoError::Invalid("EC private key is out of range"))?;
        if let Some(public_key) = public_key
            && public_key.to_uncompressed()? != point
        {
            return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("EC public key does not match the private key"));
        }

        let mut builder = ParamBuilder::new()?;
        builder.push_utf8(c"group", curve.name())?;
        builder.push_number(c"priv", d, true)?;
        builder.push_octets(c"pub", &point)?;
        let params = builder.build()?;
        Ok(Self {
            key: Pkey::from_data(c"EC", sys::EVP_PKEY_KEYPAIR, &params)?,
            curve,
        })
    }

    fn coordinates(&self) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), CryptoError> {
        coordinates(&self.key, self.curve)
    }

    fn to_uncompressed(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
        uncompressed_point(&self.key, self.curve)
    }

    fn public_key(&self) -> Result<EcPublicKey, CryptoError> {
        EcPublicKey::from_octets(&self.to_uncompressed()?)
    }

    fn d_bytes(&self) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
        let d = self.key.number(c"priv").ok_or(CryptoError::Backend)?;
        d.to_padded(self.curve.scalar_size())
    }
}

// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5915#section-3
fn encode_private_key(d: &[u8], parameters: Option<EcCurve>, public_point: Option<&[u8]>) -> Vec<u8> {
    let version = [der::INTEGER, 1, 1];
    let d_header = der::header(der::OCTET_STRING, d.len());
    let parameters = parameters.map(|curve| der::element(0xa0, &[&der::object_identifier(curve.oid())]));
    let public_key = public_point.map(|point| der::element(0xa1, &[&der::element(der::BIT_STRING, &[&[0], point])]));
    der::element(
        der::SEQUENCE,
        &[
            &version,
            &d_header,
            d,
            parameters.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
            public_key.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),
        ],
    )
}

/// The private key `key` of a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo with the named curve `curve`, whose privateKey is `encoded`.
pub(crate) fn parse_private_key_info(curve: EcCurve, key: Pkey, encoded: &[u8]) -> Result<KeyHandle, CryptoError> {
    let scalar_size = curve.scalar_size();
    let d = key
        .number(c"priv")
        .ok_or(CryptoError::Backend)?
        .to_padded(scalar_size)?;
    let private_key = EcPrivateKey::from_scalar(&d, None)?;
    let uncompressed = private_key.to_uncompressed()?;
    let mut compressed = uncompressed[..=scalar_size].to_vec();
    compressed[0] = 0x02 | (uncompressed.last().copied().unwrap_or_default() & 1);

    // NB: OpenSSL accepts BER, and a privateKey of any width. The parameters and the public key are optional, and the
    //     public key may be compressed, so the encoding must be the DER encoding of the key in one of those forms.
    for parameters in [None, Some(curve)] {
        for public_point in [None, Some(uncompressed.as_slice()), Some(compressed.as_slice())] {
            let mut candidate = encode_private_key(&d, parameters, public_point);
            let matches = candidate == encoded;
            crate::key::clear(&mut candidate);
            if matches {
                return Ok(KeyHandle(Key::EcPrivate(private_key)));
            }
        }
    }
    Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Invalid ECPrivateKey"))
}

/// The public key of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo, whose subjectPublicKey is the SEC 1 encoding of the point.
pub(crate) fn parse_subject_public_key(encoded: &[u8]) -> Result<KeyHandle, CryptoError> {
    Ok(KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(EcPublicKey::from_octets(encoded)?)))
}

fn public_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> &EcPublicKey {
    match &key.0 {
        Key::EcPublic(public_key) => public_key,
        _ => panic!("The key is not an EC public key"),
    }
}

fn private_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> &EcPrivateKey {
    match &key.0 {
        Key::EcPrivate(private_key) => private_key,
        _ => panic!("The key is not an EC private key"),
    }
}

pub fn ec_generate_key_pair(curve: EcCurve) -> Result<KeyPair, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = EcPrivateKey::generate(curve).map_err(|_| CryptoError::Backend)?;
    let public_key = private_key.public_key()?;
    Ok(KeyPair {
        public_key: KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(public_key)),
        private_key: KeyHandle(Key::EcPrivate(private_key)),
    })
}

pub fn ec_sign(key: &KeyHandle, digest: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = private_key(key);
    openssl::ecdsa_sign(&private_key.key, digest, private_key.curve.scalar_size())
}

pub fn ec_verify(key: &KeyHandle, digest: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> Result<bool, CryptoError> {
    let public_key = public_key(key);
    if signature.len() != public_key.curve.scalar_size() * 2 {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    openssl::ecdsa_verify(&public_key.key, digest, signature)
}

pub fn ec_public_key_scalar_size(key: &KeyHandle) -> usize {
    public_key(key).curve.scalar_size()
}

pub fn ec_key_from_coordinates(x: &[u8], y: &[u8], d: Option<&[u8]>) -> Option<KeyHandle> {
    let public_key = EcPublicKey::from_coordinates(x, y).ok()?;
    let Some(d) = d else {
        return Some(KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(public_key)));
    };
    let private_key = EcPrivateKey::from_scalar(d, Some(&public_key)).ok()?;
    Some(KeyHandle(Key::EcPrivate(private_key)))
}

pub fn ec_parse_raw_public_key(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<KeyHandle> {
    Some(KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(EcPublicKey::from_octets(bytes).ok()?)))
}

// NB: Every EC key is a valid key for its own curve, since building it checks that.
pub fn ec_key_is_valid(curve: EcCurve, key: &KeyHandle) -> bool {
    let key_curve = match &key.0 {
        Key::EcPublic(public_key) => public_key.curve,
        Key::EcPrivate(private_key) => private_key.curve,
        _ => panic!("The key is not an EC key"),
    };
    key_curve == curve
}

pub fn ec_export_der(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = match &key.0 {
        Key::EcPublic(public_key) => {
            return Ok(der::subject_public_key_info(
                KeyAlgorithm::Ec.oid(),
                Some(&der::object_identifier(public_key.curve.oid())),
                &public_key.to_uncompressed()?,
            ));
        }
        Key::EcPrivate(private_key) => private_key,
        _ => panic!("The key is not an EC key"),
    };
    let parameters = der::object_identifier(private_key.curve.oid());
    // NB: The ECPrivateKey has its public key and not its parameters, which the PrivateKeyInfo already has.
    let public_point = private_key.to_uncompressed()?;
    let encoded = SecretBytes::new(encode_private_key(&private_key.d_bytes()?, None, Some(&public_point)));
    Ok(der::private_key_info(
        KeyAlgorithm::Ec.oid(),
        Some(&parameters),
        &encoded,
    ))
}

pub fn ec_export_uncompressed(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    public_key(key).to_uncompressed()
}

pub fn ec_export_public_coordinates(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), CryptoError> {
    match &key.0 {
        Key::EcPublic(public_key) => public_key.coordinates(),
        Key::EcPrivate(private_key) => private_key.coordinates(),
        _ => panic!("The key is not an EC key"),
    }
}

pub fn ec_export_private_scalar(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    Ok(private_key(key).d_bytes()?.into_vec())
}

pub fn ec_compute_coordinate(key: &KeyHandle, public_key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = private_key(key);
    let peer = self::public_key(public_key);
    if private_key.curve != peer.curve {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("EC keys are on different curves"));
    }
    openssl::derive(&private_key.key, &peer.key, true)
}

pub(crate) fn public_key_for_private_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> Option<KeyHandle> {
    let Key::EcPrivate(private_key) = &key.0 else {
        return None;
    };
    Some(KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(private_key.public_key().ok()?)))
}

impl EcPublicKey {
    /// The stored form of the key: its coordinates.
    pub(crate) fn stored(&self) -> StoredKey {
        let (x, y) = self.coordinates().expect("OpenSSL gives an EC key's coordinates");
        StoredKey::new(HandleTag::EcPublic, vec![SecretBytes::new(x), SecretBytes::new(y)])
    }
}

impl EcPrivateKey {
    /// The stored form of the key: its private value, then its public key's coordinates.
    pub(crate) fn stored(&self) -> StoredKey {
        let (x, y) = self.coordinates().expect("OpenSSL gives an EC key's coordinates");
        StoredKey::new(
            HandleTag::EcPrivate,
            vec![
                self.d_bytes().expect("OpenSSL gives an EC key's private value"),
                SecretBytes::new(x),
                SecretBytes::new(y),
            ],
        )
    }
}

/// The key that a stored handle of an EC tag holds.
pub(crate) fn decode_stored(
    tag: HandleTag,
    buffers: &[&[u8]],
    parameters: Option<&[u32]>,
    has_public_key: bool,
) -> Result<KeyHandle, KeyDecodeError> {
    let invalid = |_| KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents;
    match tag {
        HandleTag::EcPublic => Ok(KeyHandle(Key::EcPublic(
            EcPublicKey::from_coordinates(buffers[0], buffers[1]).map_err(invalid)?,
        ))),
        HandleTag::EcPrivate => {
            let public_key = if has_public_key {
                Some(EcPublicKey::from_coordinates(buffers[1], buffers[2]).map_err(invalid)?)
            } else {
                None
            };
            let private_key = EcPrivateKey::from_scalar(buffers[0], public_key.as_ref()).map_err(invalid)?;
            // NB: A stored key may have its own curve's parameters, and may not have its public key.
            if parameters.is_some_and(|parameters| parameters != private_key.curve.arcs()) {
                return Err(KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents);
            }
            Ok(KeyHandle(Key::EcPrivate(private_key)))
        }
        _ => Err(KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents),
    }
}

use super::{CryptoError, EcCurve, KeyHandle, MlDsaSize, MlKemSize, OkpCurve, der, ec, ml, rsa};
use crate::key::SecretBytes;
use crate::openssl::{self, Pkey};

/// The algorithm of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo or PrivateKeyInfo.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KeyAlgorithm {
    Rsa,
    Ec,
    Okp(OkpCurve),
    MlDsa(MlDsaSize),
    MlKem(MlKemSize),
}

impl KeyAlgorithm {
    const ALL: [Self; 12] = [
        Self::Rsa,
        Self::Ec,
        Self::Okp(OkpCurve::X25519),
        Self::Okp(OkpCurve::X448),
        Self::Okp(OkpCurve::Ed25519),
        Self::Okp(OkpCurve::Ed448),
        Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa44),
        Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa65),
        Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa87),
        Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem512),
        Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem768),
        Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem1024),
    ];

    /// The contents of the DER encoding of the algorithm's object identifier.
    pub(crate) fn oid(self) -> &'static [u8] {
        match self {
            // rsaEncryption, 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1
            Self::Rsa => &[0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01],
            // id-ecPublicKey, 1.2.840.10045.2.1
            Self::Ec => &[0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0xce, 0x3d, 0x02, 0x01],
            // id-X25519, id-X448, id-Ed25519 and id-Ed448, 1.3.101.110 to 1.3.101.113
            Self::Okp(OkpCurve::X25519) => &[0x2b, 0x65, 0x6e],
            Self::Okp(OkpCurve::X448) => &[0x2b, 0x65, 0x6f],
            Self::Okp(OkpCurve::Ed25519) => &[0x2b, 0x65, 0x70],
            Self::Okp(OkpCurve::Ed448) => &[0x2b, 0x65, 0x71],
            // id-ml-dsa-44, id-ml-dsa-65 and id-ml-dsa-87, 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.17 to 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.19
            Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa44) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x03, 0x11],
            Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa65) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x03, 0x12],
            Self::MlDsa(MlDsaSize::MlDsa87) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x03, 0x13],
            // id-alg-ml-kem-512, id-alg-ml-kem-768 and id-alg-ml-kem-1024, 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.4.1 to 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.4.3
            Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem512) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x04, 0x01],
            Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem768) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x04, 0x02],
            Self::MlKem(MlKemSize::MlKem1024) => &[0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x04, 0x03],
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_oid(oid: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::ALL.into_iter().find(|algorithm| algorithm.oid() == oid)
    }
}

/// A SubjectPublicKeyInfo or PrivateKeyInfo.
pub struct KeyInfo {
    algorithm: Option<KeyAlgorithm>,
    has_parameters: bool,
    named_curve: Option<EcCurve>,
    material: KeyMaterial,
}

pub enum KeyMaterial {
    /// The key of an RSA or EC structure, or of an ML-DSA or ML-KEM PrivateKeyInfo, which is parsed with the structure.
    Key(KeyHandle),
    /// The subjectPublicKey or privateKey contents of the other structures.
    Raw(SecretBytes),
    /// The privateKey of an ML-DSA or ML-KEM PrivateKeyInfo in the expandedKey form, which has no key.
    MlExpandedKey,
}

/// The contents of the DER OCTET STRING at the start of `data`, and whether it takes all of `data`.
pub fn parse_octet_string(data: &[u8]) -> Result<(&[u8], bool), CryptoError> {
    let invalid = || CryptoError::Invalid("Invalid OCTET STRING");
    let (&tag, rest) = data.split_first().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    let (&first_length_byte, mut rest) = rest.split_first().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if tag != der::OCTET_STRING {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let length = if first_length_byte & 0x80 == 0 {
        usize::from(first_length_byte)
    } else {
        let count = usize::from(first_length_byte & 0x7f);
        if count == 0 || count > size_of::<usize>() || rest.len() < count {
            return Err(invalid());
        }
        let (length_bytes, after) = rest.split_at(count);
        rest = after;
        length_bytes
            .iter()
            .fold(0, |length, &byte| (length << 8) | usize::from(byte))
    };
    let header_length = data.len() - rest.len();
    if rest.len() < length {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    // NB: DER gives each length a single encoding, which is the one this writes.
    if data[..header_length] != der::header(der::OCTET_STRING, length) {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("OCTET STRING is not in DER"));
    }
    Ok((&rest[..length], header_length + length == data.len()))
}

/// The DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo at the start of `data`, and whether it takes all of `data`.
pub fn parse_subject_public_key_info(data: &[u8]) -> Result<(KeyInfo, bool), CryptoError> {
    let parsed = openssl::parse_subject_public_key_info(data).map_err(CryptoError::Invalid)?;
    let key_info = KeyInfo::new(false, parsed.algorithm, SecretBytes::new(parsed.raw_key), parsed.key)?;
    Ok((key_info, parsed.consumed == data.len()))
}

/// The DER PrivateKeyInfo at the start of `data`, and whether it takes all of `data`.
pub fn parse_private_key_info(data: &[u8]) -> Result<(KeyInfo, bool), CryptoError> {
    let parsed = openssl::parse_private_key_info(data).map_err(CryptoError::Invalid)?;
    let key_info = KeyInfo::new(true, parsed.algorithm, parsed.raw_key, parsed.key)?;
    Ok((key_info, parsed.consumed == data.len()))
}

impl KeyInfo {
    // NB: OpenSSL decodes the RSA and EC keys of either structure, so those keys are taken from it.
    fn new(
        is_private: bool,
        algorithm: openssl::AlgorithmIdentifier,
        raw_key: SecretBytes,
        key: Option<Pkey>,
    ) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        let named_curve = algorithm.curve.as_deref().and_then(EcCurve::from_oid);
        let has_parameters = algorithm.has_parameters();
        let algorithm = KeyAlgorithm::from_oid(&algorithm.oid);
        let material = match algorithm {
            Some(KeyAlgorithm::Rsa) => {
                let key = key.expect("OpenSSL decodes RSA keys");
                KeyMaterial::Key(if is_private {
                    rsa::from_private_key(key)
                } else {
                    rsa::from_public_key(key)
                })
            }
            Some(KeyAlgorithm::Ec) => {
                let curve = named_curve.ok_or(CryptoError::Invalid("Unsupported EC parameters"))?;
                KeyMaterial::Key(match key {
                    Some(private_key) if is_private => ec::parse_private_key_info(curve, private_key, &raw_key)?,
                    _ => ec::parse_subject_public_key(&raw_key)?,
                })
            }
            Some(algorithm @ (KeyAlgorithm::MlDsa(_) | KeyAlgorithm::MlKem(_))) if is_private => {
                match ml::parse_private_key(algorithm, &raw_key)? {
                    Some(private_key) => KeyMaterial::Key(private_key),
                    None => KeyMaterial::MlExpandedKey,
                }
            }
            _ => KeyMaterial::Raw(raw_key),
        };
        Ok(Self {
            algorithm,
            has_parameters,
            named_curve,
            material,
        })
    }

    pub fn into_material(self) -> KeyMaterial {
        self.material
    }

    /// The algorithm the structure names, if it is one of those that Web Crypto supports.
    pub fn algorithm(&self) -> Option<KeyAlgorithm> {
        self.algorithm
    }

    /// Whether the structure's AlgorithmIdentifier has parameters.
    pub fn has_parameters(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_parameters
    }

    /// The curve the structure's parameters name, if they name P-256, P-384 or P-521.
    pub fn named_curve(&self) -> Option<EcCurve> {
        self.named_curve
    }
}

use crate::ec::{self, EcPrivateKey, EcPublicKey};
use crate::ml::{self, MlDsaPublicKey, MlKemPublicKey, MlPrivateKey};
use crate::rsa::{self, RsaPrivateKey, RsaPublicKey};
use crate::sys;
use crate::{OkpCurve, OkpKey, okp_key_from_raw};

pub struct KeyHandle(pub(crate) Key);

pub(crate) enum Key {
    Secret(SecretBytes),
    OkpPublic(OkpKey),
    OkpPrivate(OkpKey),
    MlDsaPublic(MlDsaPublicKey),
    MlKemPublic(MlKemPublicKey),
    MlPrivate(MlPrivateKey),
    EcPublic(EcPublicKey),
    EcPrivate(EcPrivateKey),
    RsaPublic(RsaPublicKey),
    RsaPrivate(RsaPrivateKey),
}

/// The tag of a stored key, which says what its buffers hold. The values are part of the stable storage serialization
/// format (Web::Crypto::HandleTag).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum HandleTag {
    Secret = 0,
    RsaPublic = 1,
    RsaPrivate = 2,
    EcPublic = 3,
    EcPrivate = 4,
    MlDsaPublic = 5,
    MlDsaPrivate = 6,
    MlKemPublic = 7,
    MlKemPrivate = 8,
    OkpPublic = 9,
    OkpPrivate = 10,
}

impl HandleTag {
    const ALL: [Self; 11] = [
        Self::Secret,
        Self::RsaPublic,
        Self::RsaPrivate,
        Self::EcPublic,
        Self::EcPrivate,
        Self::MlDsaPublic,
        Self::MlDsaPrivate,
        Self::MlKemPublic,
        Self::MlKemPrivate,
        Self::OkpPublic,
        Self::OkpPrivate,
    ];

    /// The number of buffers that a key of this tag stores. An EC private key stores one, followed by its public key's
    /// two when it has its public key.
    pub fn buffer_count(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Secret
            | Self::EcPrivate
            | Self::MlDsaPublic
            | Self::MlKemPublic
            | Self::OkpPublic
            | Self::OkpPrivate => 1,
            Self::RsaPublic | Self::EcPublic => 2,
            Self::MlDsaPrivate | Self::MlKemPrivate => 3,
            Self::RsaPrivate => 8,
        }
    }
}

impl TryFrom<u8> for HandleTag {
    type Error = KeyDecodeError;

    fn try_from(value: u8) -> Result<Self, KeyDecodeError> {
        Self::ALL
            .get(usize::from(value))
            .copied()
            .ok_or(KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents)
    }
}

/// The stored form of a key: its tag and its buffers. An EC private key's buffers are its private value and its public
/// key's coordinates.
pub struct StoredKey {
    pub tag: HandleTag,
    buffers: Vec<SecretBytes>,
}

impl StoredKey {
    pub(crate) fn new(tag: HandleTag, buffers: Vec<SecretBytes>) -> Self {
        Self { tag, buffers }
    }

    pub fn buffers(&self) -> &[SecretBytes] {
        &self.buffers
    }
}

/// Bytes that are cleared when they are dropped.
pub struct SecretBytes(Vec<u8>);

impl SecretBytes {
    pub(crate) fn new(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Self(bytes)
    }

    pub(crate) fn truncate(&mut self, length: usize) {
        self.0.truncate(length);
    }

    /// Appends `bytes`, which must fit in the capacity reserved so that no partial copy is left behind by a reallocation.
    pub(crate) fn extend_from_slice(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        assert!(self.0.len() + bytes.len() <= self.0.capacity());
        self.0.extend_from_slice(bytes);
    }

    pub fn into_vec(mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
        core::mem::take(&mut self.0)
    }
}

impl core::ops::Deref for SecretBytes {
    type Target = [u8];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl core::ops::DerefMut for SecretBytes {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8] {
        &mut self.0
    }
}

impl Drop for SecretBytes {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        clear_allocation(&mut self.0);
    }
}

/// Overwrites `bytes` with zeros in a way the compiler does not remove.
pub(crate) fn clear(bytes: &mut [u8]) {
    // SAFETY: The pointer and length come from a live mutable slice.
    unsafe { sys::OPENSSL_cleanse(bytes.as_mut_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) };
}

/// Overwrites all of the allocation of `bytes` with zeros, including what lies past its length.
pub(crate) fn clear_allocation(bytes: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    // SAFETY: The pointer and capacity describe the vector's allocation.
    unsafe { sys::OPENSSL_cleanse(bytes.as_mut_ptr().cast(), bytes.capacity()) };
}

pub struct KeyPair {
    pub public_key: KeyHandle,
    pub private_key: KeyHandle,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum KeyDecodeError {
    InvalidComponents,
}

impl KeyHandle {
    pub fn from_secret_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        Self(Key::Secret(SecretBytes::new(bytes.to_vec())))
    }

    pub fn secret_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match &self.0 {
            Key::Secret(bytes) => bytes,
            _ => panic!("The key is not a secret key"),
        }
    }

    pub fn to_stored(&self) -> StoredKey {
        match &self.0 {
            Key::Secret(bytes) => StoredKey::new(HandleTag::Secret, vec![SecretBytes::new(bytes.to_vec())]),
            Key::OkpPublic(key) => key.stored(HandleTag::OkpPublic),
            Key::OkpPrivate(key) => key.stored(HandleTag::OkpPrivate),
            Key::EcPublic(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::EcPrivate(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::RsaPublic(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::RsaPrivate(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::MlDsaPublic(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::MlKemPublic(key) => key.stored(),
            Key::MlPrivate(key) => key.stored(),
        }
    }

    /// The key that a stored form holds, as `to_stored()` gives it. An OKP key's curve is not stored with it.
    pub fn from_stored(
        tag: HandleTag,
        buffers: &[&[u8]],
        ec_parameters: Option<&[u32]>,
        has_ec_public_key: bool,
        okp_curve: Option<OkpCurve>,
    ) -> Result<Self, KeyDecodeError> {
        let is_ec_private_key = tag == HandleTag::EcPrivate;
        let expected = tag.buffer_count() + if has_ec_public_key { 2 } else { 0 };
        if buffers.len() != expected || (!is_ec_private_key && (ec_parameters.is_some() || has_ec_public_key)) {
            return Err(KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents);
        }
        match tag {
            HandleTag::Secret => Ok(Self::from_secret_bytes(buffers[0])),
            HandleTag::OkpPublic | HandleTag::OkpPrivate => {
                let curve = okp_curve.ok_or(KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents)?;
                okp_key_from_raw(curve, tag == HandleTag::OkpPrivate, buffers[0])
                    .map_err(|_| KeyDecodeError::InvalidComponents)
            }
            HandleTag::RsaPublic | HandleTag::RsaPrivate => rsa::decode_stored(tag, buffers),
            HandleTag::EcPublic | HandleTag::EcPrivate => {
                ec::decode_stored(tag, buffers, ec_parameters, has_ec_public_key)
            }
            HandleTag::MlDsaPublic | HandleTag::MlDsaPrivate | HandleTag::MlKemPublic | HandleTag::MlKemPrivate => {
                ml::decode_stored(tag, buffers)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The error of an operation: an input that it rejects, for the reason given, or a failure of OpenSSL.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum CryptoError {
    Invalid(&'static str),
    Backend,
}

impl CryptoError {
    pub fn message(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Invalid(reason) => reason,
            Self::Backend => "The cryptographic operation failed",
        }
    }
}

pub struct Argon2Inputs<'a> {
    pub password: &'a [u8],
    pub nonce: &'a [u8],
    pub memory: u32,
    pub passes: u32,
    pub parallelism: u32,

    pub associated_data: Option<&'a [u8]>,

pub fn fill_with_random(bytes: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), CryptoError> {
    openssl::fill_with_random(bytes)
}

impl ShaHashKind {
    /// The name of the digest, as OpenSSL takes it.
    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> &'static CStr {
        match self {
            Self::Sha1 => c"SHA1",
            Self::Sha256 => c"SHA2-256",
            Self::Sha384 => c"SHA2-384",
            Self::Sha512 => c"SHA2-512",
            Self::Sha3_256 => c"SHA3-256",
            Self::Sha3_384 => c"SHA3-384",
            Self::Sha3_512 => c"SHA3-512",
        }
    }
}

pub fn sha_digest(kind: ShaHashKind, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    openssl::digest(kind.name(), data)
}

pub fn hash_digest_size(kind: ShaHashKind) -> usize {
    match kind {
        ShaHashKind::Sha1 => 20,
        ShaHashKind::Sha256 | ShaHashKind::Sha3_256 => 32,
        ShaHashKind::Sha384 | ShaHashKind::Sha3_384 => 48,
        ShaHashKind::Sha512 | ShaHashKind::Sha3_512 => 64,
    }
}

pub fn hmac_sign(kind: ShaHashKind, key: &[u8], message: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let params = [utf8_parameter(c"digest", kind.name()), end_parameter()];
    openssl::mac(c"HMAC", key, message, hash_digest_size(kind), &params)
}

pub fn hkdf_derive_key(
    kind: ShaHashKind,
    salt: &[u8],
    key: &[u8],
    info: &[u8],
    length: u32,
) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    let params = [
        utf8_parameter(c"digest", kind.name()),
        octet_string_parameter(c"key", key),
        octet_string_parameter(c"salt", salt),
        octet_string_parameter(c"info", info),
        end_parameter(),
    ];
    let mut derived = SecretBytes::new(vec![0; length as usize]);
    openssl::kdf(c"HKDF", &params, &mut derived)?;
    Ok(derived)
}

pub fn pbkdf2_derive_key(
    kind: ShaHashKind,
    password: &[u8],
    salt: &[u8],
    iterations: u32,
    length: u32,
) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    // NB: OpenSSL's PBKDF2 takes the iteration count and the lengths as int.
    let fits_in_int = |value: usize| c_int::try_from(value).is_ok();
    if ![iterations as usize, password.len(), salt.len(), length as usize]
        .into_iter()
        .all(fits_in_int)
    {
        return Err(CryptoError::Backend);
    }
    let mut iterations: c_uint = iterations;
    // NB: Web Crypto does not impose SP 800-132's lower bounds on the salt, iterations and key length, which OpenSSL
    //     checks unless asked for PKCS #5 behaviour.
    let mut pkcs5 = 1;
    let params = [
        utf8_parameter(c"digest", kind.name()),
        octet_string_parameter(c"pass", password),
        octet_string_parameter(c"salt", salt),
        uint_parameter(c"iter", &mut iterations),
        openssl::int_parameter(c"pkcs5", &mut pkcs5),
        end_parameter(),
    ];
    let mut derived = SecretBytes::new(vec![0; length as usize]);
    openssl::kdf(c"PBKDF2", &params, &mut derived)?;
    Ok(derived)
}

pub fn cshake_validate_parameters(output_length: u32) -> Result<(), CryptoError> {
    if !output_length.is_multiple_of(8) {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("SHAKE output length must be a multiple of 8 bits"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

// https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-185.pdf
fn left_encode(output: &mut Vec<u8>, value: u64) {
    let bytes = value.to_be_bytes();
    let leading_zeros = bytes.iter().take_while(|&&byte| byte == 0).count().min(bytes.len() - 1);
    output.push((bytes.len() - leading_zeros) as u8);
    output.extend_from_slice(&bytes[leading_zeros..]);
}

// https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-185.pdf
fn encode_string(output: &mut Vec<u8>, string: &[u8]) {
    left_encode(output, string.len() as u64 * 8);
    output.extend_from_slice(string);
}

pub fn cshake_digest(
    kind: CShakeKind,
    data: &[u8],
    output_length: u32,
    customization: Option<&[u8]>,
    function_name: Option<&[u8]>,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    cshake_validate_parameters(output_length)?;
    let mut output = vec![0; (output_length / 8) as usize];
    cshake(
        kind,
        data,
        function_name.unwrap_or_default(),
        customization.unwrap_or_default(),
        &mut output,
    )?;
    Ok(output)
}

fn cshake(
    kind: CShakeKind,
    data: &[u8],
    name: &[u8],
    customization: &[u8],
    output: &mut [u8],
) -> Result<(), CryptoError> {
    // If N = "" and S = "", return SHAKE128(X, L) (or SHAKE256(X, L) for cSHAKE256).
    if name.is_empty() && customization.is_empty() {
        let shake = match kind {
            CShakeKind::CShake128 => c"SHAKE128",
            CShakeKind::CShake256 => c"SHAKE256",
        };
        return openssl::extendable_output(shake, &[data], output);
    }

    // Else return KECCAK[256](bytepad(encode_string(N) || encode_string(S), 168) || X || 00, L) for cSHAKE128, or
    // KECCAK[512](bytepad(encode_string(N) || encode_string(S), 136) || X || 00, L) for cSHAKE256.
    // NB: OpenSSL's KECCAK-KMAC digests are KECCAK[c](M || 00, L), the function that KMAC builds on.
    let (rate, keccak_name) = match kind {
        CShakeKind::CShake128 => (168, c"KECCAK-KMAC-128"),
        CShakeKind::CShake256 => (136, c"KECCAK-KMAC-256"),
    };
    let mut prefix = Vec::new();
    left_encode(&mut prefix, rate as u64);
    encode_string(&mut prefix, name);
    encode_string(&mut prefix, customization);
    prefix.resize(prefix.len().div_ceil(rate) * rate, 0);
    openssl::extendable_output(keccak_name, &[&prefix, data], output)
}

pub fn timing_safe_compare(left: &[u8], right: &[u8]) -> bool {
    left.ct_eq(right).into()
}

pub fn kmac_validate_parameters(output_length: u32, customization: Option<&[u8]>) -> bool {
    // OpenSSL's KMAC implementation rejects longer outputs and customization strings.
    const MAXIMUM_OUTPUT_LENGTH: u32 = 0xFF_FFFF / 8;
    const MAXIMUM_CUSTOMIZATION_LENGTH: usize = 512;

    output_length != 0
        && output_length.is_multiple_of(8)
        && output_length / 8 <= MAXIMUM_OUTPUT_LENGTH
        && customization.is_none_or(|customization| customization.len() <= MAXIMUM_CUSTOMIZATION_LENGTH)
}

// https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/#kmac-operations-sign
pub fn kmac_sign(
    kind: KmacKind,
    key: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    output_length: u32,
    customization: Option<&[u8]>,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    if !kmac_validate_parameters(output_length, customization) {
        return Err(CryptoError::Backend);
    }
    let name = match kind {
        KmacKind::Kmac128 => c"KMAC-128",
        KmacKind::Kmac256 => c"KMAC-256",
    };
    let output_size = (output_length / 8) as usize;
    let mut size = c_uint::try_from(output_size).map_err(|_| CryptoError::Backend)?;
    let mut params = vec![uint_parameter(c"size", &mut size)];
    if let Some(customization) = customization {
        params.push(octet_string_parameter(c"custom", customization));
    }
    params.push(end_parameter());
    openssl::mac(name, key, message, output_size, &params)
}

pub fn argon2_validate_parameters(nonce: &[u8]) -> Result<(), CryptoError> {
    // OpenSSL's Argon2 implementation rejects shorter salts.
    const MINIMUM_NONCE_LENGTH: usize = 8;

    if nonce.len() < MINIMUM_NONCE_LENGTH {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Argon2 nonce must be at least 8 bytes"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Argon2 with inputs that `argon2_validate_parameters()` accepts.
pub fn argon2_derive_key(kind: Argon2Type, inputs: &Argon2Inputs<'_>) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    let name = match kind {
        Argon2Type::Argon2d => c"ARGON2D",
        Argon2Type::Argon2i => c"ARGON2I",
        Argon2Type::Argon2id => c"ARGON2ID",
    };
    // NB: OpenSSL takes version 0x13, the only version Web Crypto allows, and one thread when none are given.
    let mut output = SecretBytes::new(vec![0; inputs.tag_length as usize]);
    let (mut passes, mut lanes, mut memory) = (inputs.passes, inputs.parallelism, inputs.memory);
    let mut size = c_uint::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| CryptoError::Backend)?;
    let mut params = vec![
        octet_string_parameter(c"pass", inputs.password),
        octet_string_parameter(c"salt", inputs.nonce),
        uint_parameter(c"iter", &mut passes),
        uint_parameter(c"lanes", &mut lanes),
        uint_parameter(c"memcost", &mut memory),
        uint_parameter(c"size", &mut size),
    ];
    if let Some(secret) = inputs.secret_value {
        params.push(octet_string_parameter(c"secret", secret));
    }
    if let Some(associated_data) = inputs.associated_data {
        params.push(octet_string_parameter(c"ad", associated_data));
    }
    params.push(end_parameter());
    openssl::kdf(name, &params, &mut output)?;
    Ok(output)
}

enum AesMode {
    Cbc,
    Ctr,
    Gcm,
    Ocb,
    Kw,
}

fn aes_cipher(mode: AesMode, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Cipher, CryptoError> {
    let ciphers = match mode {
        AesMode::Cbc => [sys::EVP_aes_128_cbc, sys::EVP_aes_192_cbc, sys::EVP_aes_256_cbc],
        AesMode::Ctr => [sys::EVP_aes_128_ctr, sys::EVP_aes_192_ctr, sys::EVP_aes_256_ctr],
        AesMode::Gcm => [sys::EVP_aes_128_gcm, sys::EVP_aes_192_gcm, sys::EVP_aes_256_gcm],
        AesMode::Ocb => [sys::EVP_aes_128_ocb, sys::EVP_aes_192_ocb, sys::EVP_aes_256_ocb],
        AesMode::Kw => [sys::EVP_aes_128_wrap, sys::EVP_aes_192_wrap, sys::EVP_aes_256_wrap],
    };
    let getter = match key.len() {
        16 => ciphers[0],
        24 => ciphers[1],
        32 => ciphers[2],
        _ => return Err(CryptoError::Backend),
    };
    Ok(Cipher::from_static(getter))
}

/// Encrypts or decrypts `input` whole with a context set up with the cipher, key and IV.
fn cipher(
    encrypt: bool,
    cipher: Cipher,
    key: &[u8],
    iv: Option<&[u8]>,
    input: &[u8],
    allow_key_wrapping: bool,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let mut context = CipherContext::create()?;
    if allow_key_wrapping {
        context.allow_key_wrapping();
    }
    context.init(encrypt, Some(cipher), Some(key), iv)?;
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    // NB: Key wrapping takes its input whole.
    let result = if allow_key_wrapping {
        context.update_whole(input, &mut output)
    } else {
        context.update(input, &mut output)
    };
    // NB: OpenSSL writes a plaintext out before it checks its padding.
    result
        .and_then(|()| context.finalize(&mut output))
        .inspect_err(|_| key::clear_allocation(&mut output))?;
    Ok(output)
}

pub fn aes_cbc_cipher(encrypt: bool, key: &[u8], input: &[u8], iv: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    const IV_LENGTH: usize = 16;

    let aes = aes_cipher(AesMode::Cbc, key)?;
    if iv.len() != IV_LENGTH {
        return Err(CryptoError::Backend);
    }
    cipher(encrypt, aes, key, Some(iv), input, false)
}

/// Increments only the low `counter_length` bits of the counter block, modulo 2^counter_length, as the standard
/// incrementing function of NIST SP 800-38A Appendix B.1 does.
pub fn aes_ctr_cipher(
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    input: &[u8],
    counter: &[u8],
    counter_length: u8,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let counter_block: [u8; 16] = counter.try_into().map_err(|_| CryptoError::Backend)?;
    if counter_length == 0 || counter_length > 128 {
        return Err(CryptoError::Backend);
    }

    // The native cipher increments the whole block, so split the input where the low bits wrap around.
    let mask = u128::MAX >> (128 - u32::from(counter_length));
    let mut block = u128::from_be_bytes(counter_block);
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    let mut remaining = input;
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        let blocks_until_wrap = (mask - (block & mask)).checked_add(1);
        let segment_length = match blocks_until_wrap.and_then(|blocks| blocks.checked_mul(16)) {
            Some(bytes) if bytes < remaining.len() as u128 => bytes as usize,
            _ => remaining.len(),
        };
        let (segment, rest) = remaining.split_at(segment_length);
        output.extend_from_slice(&SecretBytes::new(aes_ctr_cipher_whole_block_counter(
            encrypt,
            key,
            segment,
            &block.to_be_bytes(),
        )?));
        remaining = rest;
        block &= !mask;
    }
    Ok(output)
}

fn aes_ctr_cipher_whole_block_counter(
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    input: &[u8],
    counter: &[u8],
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let aes = aes_cipher(AesMode::Ctr, key)?;
    cipher(encrypt, aes, key, Some(counter), input, false)
}

pub fn aes_kw_cipher(wrap: bool, key: &[u8], input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let aes = aes_cipher(AesMode::Kw, key)?;
    cipher(wrap, aes, key, None, input, true)
}

/// Encrypts `input`, giving the ciphertext followed by a tag of `tag_length` bytes, or decrypts such a ciphertext.
fn aead(
    cipher: Cipher,
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    iv: &[u8],
    additional_data: &[u8],
    tag_length: usize,
    input: &[u8],
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let (input, tag) = if encrypt {
        (input, None)
    } else {
        let split_index = input
            .len()
            .checked_sub(tag_length)
            .ok_or(CryptoError::Invalid("Ciphertext too short"))?;
        let (ciphertext, tag) = input.split_at(split_index);
        (ciphertext, Some(tag))
    };

    let mut context = CipherContext::create()?;
    context.init(encrypt, Some(cipher), None, None)?;
    context.set_iv_length(iv.len())?;
    // NB: In OCB mode the tag length can only be set before the IV is; otherwise a default length is used.
    let ocb_ciphers = [sys::EVP_aes_128_ocb, sys::EVP_aes_192_ocb, sys::EVP_aes_256_ocb].map(Cipher::from_static);
    if ocb_ciphers.contains(&cipher) {
        context.set_tag_length(tag_length)?;
    }
    context.init(encrypt, None, Some(key), Some(iv))?;
    if let Some(tag) = tag {
        context.set_tag(tag)?;
    }
    context.add_additional_data(additional_data)?;

    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() + tag_length);
    // NB: OpenSSL writes a plaintext out before it checks its tag, and a failed finalization does not count the
    //     bytes it wrote.
    context
        .update(input, &mut output)
        .and_then(|()| context.finalize(&mut output))
        .inspect_err(|_| key::clear_allocation(&mut output))?;
    if encrypt {
        output.extend_from_slice(&context.tag(tag_length)?);
    }
    Ok(output)
}

/// AES-GCM encryption, giving the ciphertext followed by a tag of `tag_length` bytes, or decryption of such a
/// ciphertext.
pub fn aes_gcm_cipher(
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    input: &[u8],
    iv: &[u8],
    additional_data: &[u8],
    tag_length: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let cipher = aes_cipher(AesMode::Gcm, key)?;
    aead(cipher, encrypt, key, iv, additional_data, tag_length, input)
}

pub fn aes_ocb_cipher(
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    input: &[u8],
    iv: &[u8],
    additional_data: &[u8],
    tag_length: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let tag_length_bytes = tag_length / 8;
    if !(1..=16).contains(&tag_length_bytes) {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("Invalid AES-OCB tag length"));
    }
    let cipher = aes_cipher(AesMode::Ocb, key).map_err(|_| CryptoError::Invalid("Invalid AES-OCB key length"))?;
    aead(cipher, encrypt, key, iv, additional_data, tag_length_bytes, input)
}

pub fn chacha20_poly1305_cipher(
    encrypt: bool,
    key: &[u8],
    iv: &[u8],
    input: &[u8],
    additional_data: &[u8],
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    const KEY_SIZE: usize = 32;
    const NONCE_SIZE: usize = 12;
    const TAG_SIZE: usize = 16;

    if key.len() != KEY_SIZE {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("ChaCha20-Poly1305 key must be 32 bytes"));
    }
    if iv.len() != NONCE_SIZE {
        return Err(CryptoError::Invalid("ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce must be 12 bytes"));
    }
    aead(
        Cipher::from_static(sys::EVP_chacha20_poly1305),
        encrypt,
        key,
        iv,
        additional_data,
        TAG_SIZE,
        input,
    )
}

impl OkpCurve {
    /// The name of the curve's key type, as OpenSSL takes it.
    fn name(self) -> &'static CStr {
        match self {
            Self::Ed25519 => c"ED25519",
            Self::Ed448 => c"ED448",
            Self::X25519 => c"X25519",
            Self::X448 => c"X448",
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct OkpKey {
    curve: OkpCurve,
    key: Pkey,
}

impl OkpKey {
    /// The stored form of the key: its raw public or private key.
    pub(crate) fn stored(&self, tag: HandleTag) -> StoredKey {
        let bytes = if tag == HandleTag::OkpPrivate {
            self.key.raw_private_key()
        } else {
            self.key.raw_public_key().map(SecretBytes::new)
        };
        StoredKey::new(tag, vec![bytes.expect("OpenSSL gives an OKP key's raw key")])
    }

    fn public_key(&self) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        Ok(Self {
            curve: self.curve,
            key: Pkey::from_raw_public_key(self.curve.name(), &self.key.raw_public_key()?)?,
        })
    }
}

fn okp_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> &OkpKey {
    match &key.0 {
        Key::OkpPublic(key) | Key::OkpPrivate(key) => key,
        _ => panic!("The key is not an OKP key"),
    }
}

pub fn okp_generate_key_pair(curve: OkpCurve) -> Result<KeyPair, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = OkpKey {
        curve,
        key: Pkey::generate(curve.name(), &[end_parameter()])?,
    };
    Ok(KeyPair {
        public_key: KeyHandle(Key::OkpPublic(private_key.public_key()?)),
        private_key: KeyHandle(Key::OkpPrivate(private_key)),
    })
}

pub fn okp_key_from_raw(curve: OkpCurve, is_private: bool, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<KeyHandle, CryptoError> {
    Ok(KeyHandle(if is_private {
        Key::OkpPrivate(OkpKey {
            curve,
            key: Pkey::from_raw_private_key(curve.name(), bytes)?,
        })
    } else {
        Key::OkpPublic(OkpKey {
            curve,
            key: Pkey::from_raw_public_key(curve.name(), bytes)?,
        })
    }))
}

/// The raw public key of an OKP public key, or of the public key of an OKP private key.
pub fn okp_raw_public_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    okp_key(key).key.raw_public_key()
}

pub fn okp_raw_private_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    okp_key(key).key.raw_private_key()
}

pub fn okp_compute_coordinate(private_key: &KeyHandle, public_key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<SecretBytes, CryptoError> {
    let private_key = okp_key(private_key);
    if !matches!(private_key.curve, OkpCurve::X25519 | OkpCurve::X448) {
        return Err(CryptoError::Backend);
    }
    openssl::derive(&private_key.key, &okp_key(public_key).key, false)
}

pub fn okp_sign(private_key: &KeyHandle, message: &[u8], context: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    let OkpKey { curve, key } = okp_key(private_key);
    match curve {
        OkpCurve::Ed25519 => openssl::digest_sign(key, None, &[end_parameter()], message),
        OkpCurve::Ed448 => openssl::digest_sign(key, None, &openssl::context_string_parameters(context), message),
        OkpCurve::X25519 | OkpCurve::X448 => Err(CryptoError::Backend),
    }
}

// NB: The y-coordinates of the points of order 1, 2, 4 and 8, which Web Crypto's verify operation returns false for
//     when the public key or the signature's R is one. The sign bit of x is ignored.
const SMALL_ORDER_ED25519_Y_COORDINATES: [[u8; 32]; 7] = [
    // y = 0, order 4
    [
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    ],
    // y = 1, the identity
    [
        0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
        0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
    ],
    // Order 8
    [
        0x26, 0xe8, 0x95, 0x8f, 0xc2, 0xb2, 0x27, 0xb0, 0x45, 0xc3, 0xf4, 0x89, 0xf2, 0xef, 0x98, 0xf0, 0xd5, 0xdf,
        0xac, 0x05, 0xd3, 0xc6, 0x33, 0x39, 0xb1, 0x38, 0x02, 0x88, 0x6d, 0x53, 0xfc, 0x05,
    ],
    // Order 8
    [
        0xc7, 0x17, 0x6a, 0x70, 0x3d, 0x4d, 0xd8, 0x4f, 0xba, 0x3c, 0x0b, 0x76, 0x0d, 0x10, 0x67, 0x0f, 0x2a, 0x20,
        0x53, 0xfa, 0x2c, 0x39, 0xcc, 0xc6, 0x4e, 0xc7, 0xfd, 0x77, 0x92, 0xac, 0x03, 0x7a,
    ],
    // y = p - 1, order 2
    [
        0xec, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff,
        0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x7f,
    ],
    // y = p, a non-canonical 0
    [
        0xed, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff,
        0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x7f,
    ],
    // y = p + 1, a non-canonical 1
    [
        0xee, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff,
        0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x7f,
    ],
];

fn is_small_order_ed25519_point(point: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let Some((&last, rest)) = point.split_last() else {
        return false;
    };
    SMALL_ORDER_ED25519_Y_COORDINATES
        .iter()
        .any(|y| rest == &y[..31] && last & 0x7f == y[31])
}

pub fn okp_verify(
    public_key: &KeyHandle,
    signature: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    context: &[u8],
) -> Result<bool, CryptoError> {
    let OkpKey { curve, key } = okp_key(public_key);
    if *curve == OkpCurve::Ed25519
        && (is_small_order_ed25519_point(&key.raw_public_key()?)
            || signature.get(..32).is_some_and(is_small_order_ed25519_point))
    {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    match curve {
        OkpCurve::Ed25519 => openssl::digest_verify(key, None, &[end_parameter()], message, signature),
        OkpCurve::Ed448 => openssl::digest_verify(
            key,
            None,
            &openssl::context_string_parameters(context),
            message,
            signature,
        ),
        OkpCurve::X25519 | OkpCurve::X448 => Err(CryptoError::Invalid("The algorithm does not sign")),
    }
}

pub fn okp_export_der(key: &KeyHandle) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
    match &key.0 {
        Key::OkpPublic(public_key) => public_key.key.public_key_info(),
        Key::OkpPrivate(OkpKey { curve, key }) => {
            // https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8410#section-7
            // CurvePrivateKey ::= OCTET STRING
            let private_key = SecretBytes::new(der::element(der::OCTET_STRING, &[&key.raw_private_key()?]));
            Ok(der::private_key_info(
                KeyAlgorithm::Okp(*curve).oid(),
                None,
                &private_key,
            ))
        }
        _ => panic!("The key is not an OKP key"),
    }
}

pub fn public_key_for_private_key(key: &KeyHandle) -> Option<KeyHandle> {
    if let Key::OkpPrivate(private_key) = &key.0 {
        return Some(KeyHandle(Key::OkpPublic(private_key.public_key().ok()?)));
    }
    ml::public_key_for_private_key(key)
        .or_else(|| ec::public_key_for_private_key(key))
        .or_else(|| rsa::public_key_for_private_key(key))
}
