#pragma once

#include <AK/AtomicRefCounted.h>
#include <AK/ByteString.h>
#include <AK/IPv4Address.h>
#include <AK/IPv6Address.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/String.h>
#include <AK/Variant.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibDNS/Export.h>
#include <LibDNS/Types.h>

namespace DNS {

// RFC 4035, 4.3. Determining Security Status of Data.
enum class SecurityStatus : u8 {
    Secure,
    Insecure,
};

class DNS_API LookupResult : public AtomicRefCounted<LookupResult> {
public:
    using Address = Variant<IPv4Address, IPv6Address>;

    struct Record {
        Messages::ResourceType type;
        u32 ttl { 0 };
        Optional<Address> address;
        // The record's data, as `dns` prints it.
        String text;
    };

    LookupResult(ByteString name, Vector<Record> records, Optional<SecurityStatus> security_status)
        : m_name(move(name))
        , m_records(move(records))
        , m_security_status(security_status)
    {
    }

    ByteString const& name() const { return m_name; }
    Vector<Record> const& records() const { return m_records; }
    bool is_empty() const { return m_records.is_empty(); }

    Vector<Address> cached_addresses() const
    {
        Vector<Address> addresses;
        for (auto const& record : m_records) {
            if (record.address.has_value())
                addresses.append(*record.address);
        }
        return addresses;
    }

    bool has_cached_addresses() const
    {
        return any_of(m_records, [](auto const& record) { return record.address.has_value(); });
    }

    // Whether DNSSEC validation was attempted, with the result being Secure or Insecure.
    bool was_dnssec_validated() const { return m_security_status.has_value(); }
    bool is_dnssec_validated() const { return m_security_status == SecurityStatus::Secure; }

private:
    ByteString m_name;
    Vector<Record> m_records;
    Optional<SecurityStatus> m_security_status;
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibDNS/Resolver.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2024, Ali Mohammad Pur <mpfard@serenityos.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/Atomic.h>
#include <AK/ScopeGuard.h>
#include <AK/TemporaryChange.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <LibCore/EventLoop.h>
#include <LibCore/Socket.h>
#include <LibCore/Timer.h>
#include <LibDNS/Resolver.h>
#include <LibThreading/ThreadPool.h>
#include <RustFFI.h>

namespace DNS {

// What outlives the resolver: work on a thread pool worker, and calls deferred to the event loop.
struct Resolver::Shared : public AtomicRefCounted<Shared> {
    Atomic<bool> alive { true };
};

struct Resolver::Connection {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    Variant<NonnullOwnPtr<Core::UDPSocket>, NonnullOwnPtr<StreamConnection>> socket;
    ByteBuffer receive_buffer {};
};

static u64 now_ms()
{
    return static_cast<u64>(MonotonicTime::now().milliseconds());
}

static FFI::FfiBytes ffi_bytes(StringView string)
{
    return { reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(string.characters_without_null_termination()), string.length() };
}

static FFI::FfiBytes ffi_bytes(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    return { bytes.data(), bytes.size() };
}

static StringView string_view(FFI::FfiBytes bytes)
{
    return { reinterpret_cast<char const*>(bytes.data), bytes.length };
}

static Core::SocketAddress socket_address(FFI::FfiAddress const& address)
{
    if (address.is_ipv6)
        return { IPv6Address { address.octets }, address.port };
    return { IPv4Address { address.octets[0], address.octets[1], address.octets[2], address.octets[3] }, address.port };
}

static LookupResult::Address ip_address(FFI::FfiAddress const& address)
{
    if (address.is_ipv6)
        return IPv6Address { address.octets };
    return IPv4Address { address.octets[0], address.octets[1], address.octets[2], address.octets[3] };
}

static FFI::FfiAddress ffi_address(LookupResult::Address const& address)
{
    FFI::FfiAddress result {};
    address.visit(
        [&](IPv4Address const& v4) {
            result.is_ipv6 = false;
            auto octets = v4.to_u32();
            memcpy(result.octets, &octets, sizeof(octets));
        },
        [&](IPv6Address const& v6) {
            result.is_ipv6 = true;
            memcpy(result.octets, v6.to_in6_addr_t(), sizeof(result.octets));
        });
    return result;
}

static void append_string(void* context, FFI::FfiBytes bytes)
{
    *static_cast<String*>(context) = MUST(String::from_utf8(string_view(bytes)));
}

static NonnullRefPtr<LookupResult const> take_lookup_result(FFI::LookupResult const* result)
{
    ScopeGuard release = [&] { FFI::dns_lookup_result_release(result); };

    String name;
    FFI::dns_lookup_result_name(result, append_string, &name);

    Vector<LookupResult::Record> records;
    auto count = FFI::dns_lookup_result_record_count(result);
    records.ensure_capacity(count);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        auto record = FFI::dns_lookup_result_record(result, i);
        String text;
        FFI::dns_lookup_result_record_text(result, i, append_string, &text);
        records.unchecked_append({
            .type = static_cast<Messages::ResourceType>(record.rtype),
            .ttl = record.ttl,
            .address = record.has_address ? Optional<LookupResult::Address> { ip_address(record.address) } : OptionalNone {},
            .text = move(text),
        });
    }

    Optional<SecurityStatus> security_status;
    switch (FFI::dns_lookup_result_security_status(result)) {
    case FFI::FfiSecurityStatus::NotValidated:
        break;
    case FFI::FfiSecurityStatus::Secure:
        security_status = SecurityStatus::Secure;
        break;
    case FFI::FfiSecurityStatus::Insecure:
        security_status = SecurityStatus::Insecure;
        break;
    }

    return adopt_ref(*new LookupResult(name.to_byte_string(), move(records), security_status));
}

Resolver::Resolver()
    : m_shared(adopt_ref(*new Shared))
{
    m_resolver = FFI::dns_resolver_create(now_ms(), [](void*) { return Core::Socket::is_ipv6_globally_reachable(); }, nullptr);
    m_tick_timer = Core::Timer::create_single_shot(AK::Duration::zero(), [this] {
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_tick(m_resolver, now_ms());
        run_actions();
    });
}

Resolver::~Resolver()
{
    m_shared->alive.store(false);
    m_tick_timer->stop();
    m_connections.clear();
    FFI::dns_resolver_destroy(m_resolver);
}

void Resolver::set_server(Optional<Server> server)
{
    if (!server.has_value()) {
        FFI::dns_resolver_set_server(m_resolver, FFI::FfiServerTransport::None, {}, 0, now_ms());
    } else {
        auto transport = server->transport == ServerTransport::TLS ? FFI::FfiServerTransport::Tls : FFI::FfiServerTransport::Udp;
        FFI::dns_resolver_set_server(m_resolver, transport, ffi_bytes(server->host), server->port, now_ms());
    }
    run_actions();
}

void Resolver::set_stream_connector(StreamConnector connector)
{
    m_stream_connector = move(connector);
}

void Resolver::set_remote_system_resolver(RemoteSystemResolver resolver)
{
    m_remote_system_resolver = move(resolver);
}

void Resolver::set_loopback_domains(Vector<ByteString> const& domains)
{
    Vector<FFI::FfiBytes> ffi_domains;
    for (auto const& domain : domains)
        ffi_domains.append(ffi_bytes(domain));
    FFI::dns_resolver_set_loopback_domains(m_resolver, ffi_domains.data(), ffi_domains.size());
}

void Resolver::reset_connection()
{
    FFI::dns_resolver_reset_connection(m_resolver, now_ms());
    run_actions();
}

NonnullRefPtr<Resolver::ResultPromise> Resolver::lookup(ByteString name, Messages::Class class_, Vector<Messages::ResourceType> desired_types, LookupOptions options)
{
    Vector<u16> types;
    for (auto type : desired_types)
        types.append(to_underlying(type));

    auto promise = ResultPromise::construct();
    auto id = FFI::dns_resolver_lookup(m_resolver, ffi_bytes(name), to_underlying(class_), types.data(), types.size(), options.validate_dnssec_locally, options.query_aaaa_without_global_ipv6, now_ms());
    m_lookups.set(id, promise);

    // A lookup the resolver can answer at once, from the cache or because the name needs no lookup, settles before
    // this returns.
    TemporaryChange starting { m_lookup_being_started, Optional<u64> { id } };
    run_actions();
    return promise;
}

NonnullRefPtr<Resolver::ResultPromise> Resolver::lookup(ByteString name, Messages::Class class_, LookupOptions options)
{
    return lookup(move(name), class_, Vector { Messages::ResourceType::A, Messages::ResourceType::AAAA }, options);
}

void Resolver::run_actions()
{
    // The outer call drains actions queued by callbacks below.
    if (m_running_actions)
        return;
    TemporaryChange running { m_running_actions, true };

    FFI::FfiAction action {};
    while (FFI::dns_resolver_take_action(m_resolver, &action)) {
        // NB: What the action points to is only valid until the next call on the resolver, so it gets copied first.
        switch (action.kind) {
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::Connect:
            connect(action.connection, to_underlying(action.connect_kind), socket_address(action.address), string_view(action.server_name));
            break;
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::Write:
            write(action.connection, { action.bytes.data, action.bytes.length });
            break;
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::Close:
            // Defer destruction: the connection may be inside its own callback.
            if (auto connection = m_connections.take(action.connection); connection.has_value())
                Core::deferred_invoke([connection = connection.release_value()] { });
            break;
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::SystemResolve:
            resolve_with_system_resolver(action.request, string_view(action.name), action.ipv6);
            break;
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::CancelSystemResolve:
            cancel_system_resolution(action.request);
            break;
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::LookupSucceeded:
        case FFI::FfiActionKind::LookupFailed: {
            ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<LookupResult const>> result = Error::from_string_literal("DNS lookup failed");
            if (action.kind == FFI::FfiActionKind::LookupSucceeded) {
                result = take_lookup_result(action.result);
            } else {
                // NB: The message lives as long as the process does; the detail goes away with the action.
                if (action.error_detail.length > 0)
                    dbgln("DNS: {}: {}", string_view(action.error), string_view(action.error_detail));
                result = Error::from_string_view(string_view(action.error));
            }
            auto promise = m_lookups.take(action.lookup);
            if (!promise.has_value())
                break;
            auto settle = [promise = promise.release_value(), result = move(result)] mutable {
                if (result.is_error())
                    promise->reject(result.release_error());
                else
                    promise->resolve(result.release_value());
            };
            // Nobody waits on a promise that lookup() has yet to return, so it can settle right away. Otherwise,
            // callers hear back from the top of the event loop, not from inside whatever made the lookup settle.
            if (action.lookup == m_lookup_being_started)
                settle();
            else
                Core::deferred_invoke(move(settle));
            break;
        }
        }
    }

    schedule_tick();
}

void Resolver::schedule_tick()
{
    auto wait = FFI::dns_resolver_next_deadline(m_resolver, now_ms());
    if (wait < 0) {
        m_tick_timer->stop();
        return;
    }
    m_tick_timer->restart(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(wait));
}

void Resolver::connect(u64 connection, u8 kind, Core::SocketAddress const& address, ByteString const& server_name)
{
    auto fail_later = [this, shared = m_shared, connection](Error error) {
        Core::deferred_invoke([this, shared, connection, error = ByteString::formatted("{}", error)] {
            if (!shared->alive.load())
                return;
            FFI::dns_resolver_on_connect_failed(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(error), now_ms());
            run_actions();
        });
    };

    if (kind == to_underlying(FFI::FfiConnectKind::Udp)) {
        auto socket_or_error = Core::UDPSocket::connect(address);
        if (socket_or_error.is_error())
            return fail_later(socket_or_error.release_error());
        auto socket = socket_or_error.release_value();
        // NB: A closed connection goes away from the top of the event loop, so its callbacks can outlive the resolver.
        socket->on_ready_to_read = [this, connection, shared = m_shared] {
            if (!shared->alive.load())
                return;
            auto it = m_connections.find(connection);
            if (it == m_connections.end())
                return;
            auto& socket = *it->value->socket.get<NonnullOwnPtr<Core::UDPSocket>>();
            auto& buffer = it->value->receive_buffer;
            while (true) {
                auto readable = socket.can_read_without_blocking();
                if (readable.is_error() || !readable.value())
                    break;
                auto datagram = socket.read_some(buffer);
                if (datagram.is_error()) {
                    FFI::dns_resolver_on_connect_failed(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(ByteString::formatted("{}", datagram.error())), now_ms());
                    break;
                }
                // Core treats an empty read as EOF and stops notifying us, so this socket is done even on UDP.
                if (datagram.value().is_empty()) {
                    FFI::dns_resolver_on_eof(m_resolver, connection, now_ms());
                    break;
                }
                FFI::dns_resolver_on_received(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(datagram.value()), now_ms());
                if (!m_connections.contains(connection))
                    break;
            }
            run_actions();
        };
        socket->set_notifications_enabled(true);
        m_connections.set(connection, make<Connection>(move(socket), MUST(ByteBuffer::create_uninitialized(NumericLimits<u16>::max()))));

        // A UDP socket has nothing to wait for.
        Core::deferred_invoke([this, shared = m_shared, connection] {
            if (!shared->alive.load())
                return;
            FFI::dns_resolver_on_connected(m_resolver, connection, now_ms());
            run_actions();
        });
        return;
    }

    if (!m_stream_connector)
        return fail_later(Error::from_string_literal("No way to connect a stream to the DNS server"));

    auto security = kind == to_underlying(FFI::FfiConnectKind::Tls) ? StreamSecurity::TLS : StreamSecurity::None;
    auto stream_or_error = m_stream_connector(address, server_name, security);
    if (stream_or_error.is_error())
        return fail_later(stream_or_error.release_error());

    auto stream = stream_or_error.release_value();
    // NB: A closed connection goes away from the top of the event loop, so its callbacks can outlive the resolver.
    stream->on_connected = [this, connection, shared = m_shared] {
        if (!shared->alive.load())
            return;
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_connected(m_resolver, connection, now_ms());
        run_actions();
    };
    stream->on_data = [this, connection, shared = m_shared](ReadonlyBytes bytes) {
        if (!shared->alive.load())
            return;
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_received(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(bytes), now_ms());
        run_actions();
    };
    stream->on_eof = [this, connection, shared = m_shared] {
        if (!shared->alive.load())
            return;
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_eof(m_resolver, connection, now_ms());
        run_actions();
    };
    stream->on_error = [this, connection, shared = m_shared](Error error) {
        if (!shared->alive.load())
            return;
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_connect_failed(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(ByteString::formatted("{}", error)), now_ms());
        run_actions();
    };
    m_connections.set(connection, make<Connection>(move(stream)));
}

void Resolver::write(u64 connection, ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    auto it = m_connections.find(connection);
    if (it == m_connections.end())
        return;
    it->value->socket.visit(
        [&](NonnullOwnPtr<Core::UDPSocket>& socket) {
            if (auto result = socket->write_until_depleted(bytes); result.is_error()) {
                auto error = ByteString::formatted("{}", result.error());
                Core::deferred_invoke([this, shared = m_shared, connection, error] {
                    if (!shared->alive.load())
                        return;
                    FFI::dns_resolver_on_connect_failed(m_resolver, connection, ffi_bytes(error), now_ms());
                    run_actions();
                });
            }
        },
        [&](NonnullOwnPtr<StreamConnection>& stream) {
            stream->write(bytes);
        });
}

// A system lookup the resolver may give up on: then the remote resolver forgets it, and a worker skips it.
struct Resolver::SystemRequest {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    struct Abandoned : public AtomicRefCounted<Abandoned> {
        Atomic<bool> value { false };
    };

    CancelRemoteSystemResolution cancel_remote_resolution;
    NonnullRefPtr<Abandoned> abandoned { adopt_ref(*new Abandoned) };
};

void Resolver::set_system_resolution_timeout_for_testing(AK::Duration timeout)
{
    FFI::dns_resolver_set_system_resolver_timeout(m_resolver, timeout.to_milliseconds());
}

void Resolver::cancel_system_resolution(u64 request)
{
    auto system_request = m_system_requests.take(request);
    if (!system_request.has_value())
        return;
    (*system_request)->abandoned->value.store(true);
    if (auto& cancel = (*system_request)->cancel_remote_resolution)
        cancel();
}

void Resolver::resolve_with_system_resolver(u64 request, ByteString name, bool ipv6)
{
    auto family = ipv6 ? Core::Socket::AddressFamily::IPv6Only : Core::Socket::AddressFamily::IPv4Only;
    auto& system_request = *m_system_requests.ensure(request, [] { return make<SystemRequest>(); });
    auto answer = [this, shared = m_shared, request](SystemResolution resolution) {
        if (!shared->alive.load())
            return;
        // An answer to a lookup the resolver gave up on is dropped.
        if (!m_system_requests.remove(request))
            return;
        Vector<FFI::FfiAddress> addresses;
        if (!resolution.is_error()) {
            for (auto const& address : resolution.value())
                addresses.append(ffi_address(address));
        }
        FFI::dns_resolver_on_system_resolved(m_resolver, request, !resolution.is_error(), addresses.data(), addresses.size(), now_ms());
        run_actions();
    };

    if (m_remote_system_resolver) {
        // The remote resolver answers later, never from inside this call; still, nothing here relies on that.
        system_request.cancel_remote_resolution = m_remote_system_resolver(name, family, [answer = move(answer)](SystemResolution resolution) mutable {
            Core::deferred_invoke([answer = move(answer), resolution = move(resolution)] mutable {
                answer(move(resolution));
            });
        });
        return;
    }

    // Run blocking getaddrinfo() on a worker.
    Threading::ThreadPool::for_name_resolution().submit([name = move(name), family, abandoned = system_request.abandoned, event_loop = Core::EventLoop::current_weak(), answer = move(answer)] mutable {
        // A lookup given up on while it waited in the queue is not made, so the worker goes on to the next one.
        if (abandoned->value.load())
            return;
        auto resolution = Core::Socket::resolve_host(name, Core::Socket::SocketType::Stream, family);
        auto origin_event_loop = event_loop->take();
        if (!origin_event_loop.is_alive())
            return;
        origin_event_loop->deferred_invoke([answer = move(answer), resolution = move(resolution)] mutable {
            answer(move(resolution));
        });
    });
}

}

namespace FFI {

struct DnsResolver;

// A byte stream to a DNS server that someone else connects, such as over TLS. It must not block: it reports what
// happens through its callbacks, from the event loop it was made on.
class DNS_API StreamConnection {
public:
    virtual ~StreamConnection() = default;

    virtual void write(ReadonlyBytes) = 0;

    // Once connected, and done with the TLS handshake if there is one.
    Function<void()> on_connected;
    Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)> on_data;
    Function<void()> on_eof;
    Function<void(Error)> on_error;
};

enum class StreamSecurity : u8 {
    None,
    TLS,
};

using StreamConnector = Function<ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<StreamConnection>>(Core::SocketAddress const&, ByteString const& server_name, StreamSecurity)>;

// A stub resolver. It never blocks: sockets, timers and the system resolver all report back through the event loop.
class DNS_API Resolver {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Resolver);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Resolver);

public:
    struct LookupOptions {
        bool validate_dnssec_locally { false };
        // Asks the system resolver for AAAA records even when no global IPv6 route exists, as a host on the local
        // network may still be reachable over IPv6.
        bool query_aaaa_without_global_ipv6 { false };

        static LookupOptions default_() { return {}; }
    };

    enum class ServerTransport : u8 {
        // UDP, asked again over TCP when a response comes back truncated.
        UDP,
        // RFC 7858 DNS over TLS.
        TLS,
    };

    struct Server {
        // A host name, which the system resolver looks up, or an address.
        ByteString host;
        u16 port { 0 };
        ServerTransport transport { ServerTransport::UDP };

        bool operator==(Server const&) const = default;
    };

    using ResultPromise = Core::Promise<NonnullRefPtr<LookupResult const>>;

    using SystemResolution = ErrorOr<Vector<LookupResult::Address>>;
    // Resolves a name to the addresses of one family somewhere else, such as in another process, and calls back on the
    // thread that asked, once it has them.
    // Forgets a lookup handed to the remote resolver, whose answer, if any comes, is then dropped.
    using CancelRemoteSystemResolution = Function<void()>;
    using RemoteSystemResolver = Function<CancelRemoteSystemResolution(ByteString const&, Core::Socket::AddressFamily, Function<void(SystemResolution)>)>;

    Resolver();
    ~Resolver();

    // Without a server, every name goes to the system resolver.
    void set_server(Optional<Server>);

    // Where streams to the server come from: DNS over TLS, and TCP for responses too large for UDP.
    void set_stream_connector(StreamConnector);

    // Once set, the system resolver's lookups go to the remote resolver, rather than to getaddrinfo() on a thread pool.
    void set_remote_system_resolver(RemoteSystemResolver);

    // Names within these domains resolve to loopback, as names within "localhost" do.
    void set_loopback_domains(Vector<ByteString> const&);

    // How long the system resolver may take to answer, for tests that cannot wait for it.
    void set_system_resolution_timeout_for_testing(AK::Duration);

    // Drops the connection, everything in flight on it, and everything cached.
    void reset_connection();

    NonnullRefPtr<ResultPromise> lookup(ByteString name, Messages::Class, Vector<Messages::ResourceType> desired_types, LookupOptions = LookupOptions::default_());
    NonnullRefPtr<ResultPromise> lookup(ByteString name, Messages::Class = Messages::Class::IN, LookupOptions = LookupOptions::default_());

private:
    struct Shared;
    struct Connection;
    struct SystemRequest;

    void run_actions();
    void schedule_tick();
    void connect(u64 connection, u8 kind, Core::SocketAddress const&, ByteString const& server_name);
    void write(u64 connection, ReadonlyBytes);
    void resolve_with_system_resolver(u64 request, ByteString name, bool ipv6);
    void cancel_system_resolution(u64 request);

    FFI::DnsResolver* m_resolver { nullptr };
    NonnullRefPtr<Shared> m_shared;
    HashMap<u64, NonnullRefPtr<ResultPromise>> m_lookups;
    HashMap<u64, NonnullOwnPtr<Connection>> m_connections;
    HashMap<u64, NonnullOwnPtr<SystemRequest>> m_system_requests;
    StreamConnector m_stream_connector;
    RemoteSystemResolver m_remote_system_resolver;
    RefPtr<Core::Timer> m_tick_timer;
    Optional<u64> m_lookup_being_started;
    bool m_running_actions { false };
};

}

use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?);
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src");

    cbindgen::generate(manifest_dir).map_or_else(
        |error| match error {
            cbindgen::Error::ParseSyntaxError { .. } => {}
            e => panic!("{e:?}"),
        },
        |bindings| {
            let header_path = out_dir.join("RustFFI.h");
            bindings.write_to_file(&header_path);
        },
    );

    Ok(())
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use libcrypto_rust::{RsaSignaturePadding, ShaHashKind};

use crate::message::{Algorithm, DigestType, Dnskey, DomainName, Ds, Nsec3, Nsec3HashAlgorithm};

pub(super) fn is_supported_algorithm(algorithm: Algorithm) -> bool {
    matches!(
        algorithm,
        Algorithm::RSASHA1
            | Algorithm::RSASHA1NSEC3SHA1
            | Algorithm::RSASHA256
            | Algorithm::RSASHA512
            | Algorithm::ECDSAP256SHA256
            | Algorithm::ECDSAP384SHA384
            | Algorithm::ED25519
    )
}

pub(super) fn is_supported_digest_type(digest_type: DigestType) -> bool {
    matches!(digest_type, DigestType::SHA1 | DigestType::SHA256 | DigestType::SHA384)
}

// RFC 4034, 2.1.1. The Flags Field / 2.1.2. The Protocol Field.
// If bit 7 has value 0, then the DNSKEY record holds some other type of DNS public key and MUST NOT be used to
// verify RRSIGs that cover RRsets.
// The Protocol Field MUST have value 3, and the DNSKEY RR MUST be treated as invalid during signature verification
// if it is found to be some value other than 3.
pub(super) fn is_usable_zone_key(key: &Dnskey) -> bool {
    key.is_zone_key() && key.protocol == 3 && !key.is_revoked()
}

fn without_leading_zeros(bytes: &[u8]) -> &[u8] {
    let start = bytes.iter().position(|byte| *byte != 0).unwrap_or(bytes.len());
    &bytes[start..]
}

// RFC 3110, 3. RSA/SHA1 SIG Resource Records.
// The size of "n", including most and least significant bits (which will be 1) MUST be not less than 512 bits and not
// more than 4096 bits.
// We do not trust RSA keys with a modulus shorter than 1024 bits, nor spend time on ones longer than 8192 bits or with a
// public exponent longer than 33 bits. A signature by such a key never validates, so data signed only with one fails
// validation, unlike data signed with an unsupported algorithm, which is Insecure.
const MIN_RSA_MODULUS_BITS: usize = 1024;
const MAX_RSA_MODULUS_BITS: usize = 8192;
const MAX_RSA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT_BITS: usize = 33;

fn bit_length(bytes: &[u8]) -> usize {
    let bytes = without_leading_zeros(bytes);
    bytes
        .first()
        .map_or(0, |first| bytes.len() * 8 - first.leading_zeros() as usize)
}

pub(super) fn verify_signature(key: &Dnskey, signed_data: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> bool {
    match key.algorithm {
        Algorithm::RSASHA1 | Algorithm::RSASHA1NSEC3SHA1 | Algorithm::RSASHA256 | Algorithm::RSASHA512 => {
            let hash = match key.algorithm {
                Algorithm::RSASHA256 => ShaHashKind::Sha256,
                Algorithm::RSASHA512 => ShaHashKind::Sha512,
                _ => ShaHashKind::Sha1,
            };
            let Some(components) = key.rsa_public_key_components() else {
                return false;
            };
            let (modulus, exponent) = (
                without_leading_zeros(components.modulus),
                without_leading_zeros(components.exponent),
            );
            if !(MIN_RSA_MODULUS_BITS..=MAX_RSA_MODULUS_BITS).contains(&bit_length(modulus))
                || bit_length(exponent) > MAX_RSA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT_BITS
            {
                return false;
            }
            let Some(public_key) = libcrypto_rust::rsa_key_from_components(false, &[modulus, exponent]) else {
                return false;
            };
            libcrypto_rust::rsa_verify(hash, &public_key, RsaSignaturePadding::Pkcs1, signed_data, signature)
                .unwrap_or(false)
        }
        Algorithm::ECDSAP256SHA256 | Algorithm::ECDSAP384SHA384 => {
            // RFC 6605, 4. DNSKEY and RRSIG Resource Records for ECDSA.
            // ECDSA public keys consist of a single value, called "Q" in FIPS 186-3.  In DNSSEC keys, Q is a simple bit
            // string that represents the uncompressed form of a curve point, "x | y".
            // The two integers, both of which have length n bits, are concatenated to form "r | s".
            let (scalar_size, hash) = if key.algorithm == Algorithm::ECDSAP256SHA256 {
                (32, ShaHashKind::Sha256)
            } else {
                (48, ShaHashKind::Sha384)
            };
            if key.public_key.len() != scalar_size * 2 || signature.len() != scalar_size * 2 {
                return false;
            }
            let mut point = Vec::with_capacity(1 + key.public_key.len());
            point.push(0x04);
            point.extend_from_slice(&key.public_key);
            let Some(public_key) = libcrypto_rust::ec_parse_raw_public_key(&point) else {
                return false;
            };
            let Ok(digest) = libcrypto_rust::sha_digest(hash, signed_data) else {
                return false;
            };
            libcrypto_rust::ec_verify(&public_key, &digest, signature).unwrap_or(false)
        }
        Algorithm::ED25519 => {
            let Ok(public_key) =
                libcrypto_rust::okp_key_from_raw(libcrypto_rust::OkpCurve::Ed25519, false, &key.public_key)
            else {
                return false;
            };
            libcrypto_rust::okp_verify(&public_key, signature, signed_data, &[]).unwrap_or(false)
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ds_digest(owner: &DomainName, key: &Dnskey, digest_type: DigestType) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    // RFC 4034, 5.1.4. The Digest Field.
    // digest = digest_algorithm( DNSKEY owner name | DNSKEY RDATA);
    // DNSKEY RDATA = Flags | Protocol | Algorithm | Public Key.
    let mut input = owner.canonicalized().to_wire().ok()?;
    key.write_wire(&mut input);
    let hash = match digest_type {
        DigestType::SHA1 => ShaHashKind::Sha1,
        DigestType::SHA256 => ShaHashKind::Sha256,
        DigestType::SHA384 => ShaHashKind::Sha384,
        _ => return None,
    };
    libcrypto_rust::sha_digest(hash, &input).ok()
}

pub(super) fn ds_matches_key(owner: &DomainName, ds: &Ds, key: &Dnskey) -> bool {
    if ds.key_tag != key.calculated_key_tag() || ds.algorithm != key.algorithm {
        return false;
    }
    ds_digest(owner, key, ds.digest_type).is_some_and(|digest| digest == ds.digest)
}

// RFC 5155, 5. Calculation of the Hash.
// IH(salt, x, 0) = H(x || salt), and
// IH(salt, x, k) = H(IH(salt, x, k-1) || salt), if k > 0
pub(super) fn nsec3_hash(name: &DomainName, params: &Nsec3) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if params.hash_algorithm != Nsec3HashAlgorithm::SHA1 {
        return None;
    }

    let mut input = name.canonicalized().to_wire().ok()?;
    input.extend_from_slice(&params.salt);
    let mut hash = libcrypto_rust::sha_digest(ShaHashKind::Sha1, &input).ok()?;
    for _ in 0..params.iterations {
        hash.extend_from_slice(&params.salt);
        hash = libcrypto_rust::sha_digest(ShaHashKind::Sha1, &hash).ok()?;
    }
    Some(hash)
}

/*

use std::cmp::Ordering;

use super::crypto::nsec3_hash;
use super::rrset::VerifiedRRSet;
use crate::message::{DomainName, Nsec, Nsec3, Nsec3HashAlgorithm, RecordData, ResourceType};

// RFC 9276, 3.2. Recommendation for Validating Resolvers.
// Validating resolvers MAY return an insecure response to their clients when processing NSEC3 records with
// iterations larger than 0.
pub(super) const MAX_NSEC3_ITERATIONS: u16 = 100;

// A SHA-1 hash is 160 bits: 20 octets, or 32 characters of Base32hex.
const SHA1_HASH_LENGTH: usize = 20;
const SHA1_HASH_BASE32HEX_LENGTH: usize = 32;

// RFC 4648, 7. Base 32 Encoding with Extended Hex Alphabet.
fn base32hex_decode(input: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 5 / 8);
    let mut bits: u32 = 0;
    let mut bit_count = 0;
    for &ch in input {
        let value = match ch {
            b'0'..=b'9' => ch - b'0',
            b'A'..=b'V' => ch - b'A' + 10,
            b'a'..=b'v' => ch - b'a' + 10,
            _ => return None,
        };
        bits = bits << 5 | u32::from(value);
        bit_count += 5;
        if bit_count >= 8 {
            output.push((bits >> (bit_count - 8)) as u8);
            bit_count -= 8;
        }
    }
    Some(output)
}

trait TypeBitMap {
    fn has_type(&self, rtype: ResourceType) -> bool;
}

impl TypeBitMap for Nsec {
    fn has_type(&self, rtype: ResourceType) -> bool {
        Nsec::has_type(self, rtype)
    }
}

impl TypeBitMap for Nsec3 {
    fn has_type(&self, rtype: ResourceType) -> bool {
        Nsec3::has_type(self, rtype)
    }
}

// RFC 6840, 4.1. Clarifications on Nonexistence Proofs.
// An "ancestor delegation" NSEC RR (or NSEC3 RR) is one with:
// o  the NS bit set,
// o  the Start of Authority (SOA) bit clear, and
// o  a signer field that is shorter than the owner name of the NSEC RR, or the original owner name for the NSEC3 RR.
// Ancestor delegation NSEC or NSEC3 RRs MUST NOT be used to assume nonexistence of any RRs below that zone cut, which
// include all RRs at that (original) owner name other than DS RRs, and all RRs below that owner name regardless of
// type.
fn is_ancestor_delegation(record: &dyn TypeBitMap, original_owner: &DomainName, zone: &DomainName) -> bool {
    record.has_type(ResourceType::NS) && !record.has_type(ResourceType::SOA) && !original_owner.eq_ignore_case(zone)
}

// The last record in a chain wraps around to the first one, so it covers both the names after its owner and the
// names before the first owner. Neither endpoint is covered: those names exist.
fn is_within_interval(after_owner: bool, before_next: bool, wraps: bool) -> bool {
    if wraps {
        after_owner || before_next
    } else {
        after_owner && before_next
    }
}

struct NsecRecord<'a> {
    owner: &'a DomainName,
    nsec: &'a Nsec,
    zone: &'a DomainName,
    ttl: u32,
}

impl NsecRecord<'_> {
    fn matches(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        self.owner.eq_ignore_case(name)
    }

    // RFC 4035, 5.4. Authenticated Denial of Existence.
    // If the requested RR name would appear after an authenticated NSEC RR's owner name and before the name listed
    // in that NSEC RR's Next Domain Name field according to the canonical DNS name order defined in [RFC4034], then
    // no RRsets with the requested name exist in the zone.
    fn covers(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        if !self.zone.is_ancestor_or_equal_of(name) {
            return false;
        }
        // An ancestor delegation NSEC says nothing about the names below its owner, and neither does one at a DNAME.
        // RFC 6840, 4.1. Clarifications on Nonexistence Proofs.
        // An NSEC or NSEC3 RR with the DNAME bit set MUST NOT be used to assume the nonexistence of any subdomain of
        // that NSEC/NSEC3 RR's (original) owner name.
        if self.owner.is_ancestor_or_equal_of(name)
            && (is_ancestor_delegation(self.nsec, self.owner, self.zone) || self.nsec.has_type(ResourceType::DNAME))
        {
            return false;
        }
        let after_owner = self.owner.canonical_cmp(name) == Ordering::Less;
        let before_next = name.canonical_cmp(&self.nsec.next_domain_name) == Ordering::Less;
        // RFC 4034, 4.1.1. The Next Domain Field.
        // The value of the Next Domain Name field in the last NSEC record in the zone is the name of the zone apex
        // (the owner name of the zone's SOA RR).
        let wraps = self.nsec.next_domain_name.canonical_cmp(self.owner) != Ordering::Greater;
        is_within_interval(after_owner, before_next, wraps)
    }
}

struct Nsec3Record<'a> {
    owner_hash: Vec<u8>,
    nsec3: &'a Nsec3,
    zone: &'a DomainName,
    ttl: u32,
}

impl Nsec3Record<'_> {
    fn matches(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        nsec3_hash(name, self.nsec3).is_some_and(|hash| hash == self.owner_hash)
    }

    fn covers(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        if !self.zone.is_ancestor_or_equal_of(name) {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(hash) = nsec3_hash(name, self.nsec3) else {
            return false;
        };
        let after_owner = self.owner_hash < hash;
        let before_next = hash < self.nsec3.next_hashed_owner_name;
        // RFC 5155, 3.1.7. Next Hashed Owner Name.
        // The value of the Next Hashed Owner Name field in the last NSEC3 RR in the zone is the same as the hashed
        // owner name of the first NSEC3 RR in the zone in hash order.
        let wraps = self.nsec3.next_hashed_owner_name <= self.owner_hash;
        is_within_interval(after_owner, before_next, wraps)
    }
}

fn nsec_records(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet]) -> impl Iterator<Item = NsecRecord<'_>> {
    rrsets
        .iter()
        .filter(|verified| verified.rrset.rtype == ResourceType::NSEC)
        .flat_map(|verified| {
            verified
                .rrset
                .records
                .iter()
                .filter_map(move |record| match &record.data {
                    RecordData::Nsec(nsec) => Some(NsecRecord {
                        owner: &record.name,
                        nsec,
                        zone: &verified.zone,
                        ttl: verified.ttl,
                    }),
                    _ => None,
                })
        })
}

// Every NSEC3 record that could take part in a proof, regardless of its iteration count.
fn nsec3_records_with_any_iterations(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet]) -> impl Iterator<Item = Nsec3Record<'_>> {
    rrsets
        .iter()
        .filter(|verified| verified.rrset.rtype == ResourceType::NSEC3)
        .flat_map(|verified| {
            verified.rrset.records.iter().filter_map(move |record| {
                let RecordData::Nsec3(nsec3) = &record.data else {
                    return None;
                };
                // RFC 5155, 8.1 / 8.2: unknown hash types and unknown flags are ignored.
                if nsec3.hash_algorithm != Nsec3HashAlgorithm::SHA1 || (nsec3.flags & !Nsec3::FLAG_OPT_OUT) != 0 {
                    return None;
                }
                let first_label = record.name.labels.first()?;
                if !record.name.parent().eq_ignore_case(&verified.zone) {
                    return None;
                }
                // Both ends of the span have to be SHA-1 hashes, or comparing them to one means nothing.
                if first_label.len() != SHA1_HASH_BASE32HEX_LENGTH
                    || nsec3.next_hashed_owner_name.len() != SHA1_HASH_LENGTH
                {
                    return None;
                }
                let owner_hash = base32hex_decode(first_label)?;
                Some(Nsec3Record {
                    owner_hash,
                    nsec3,
                    zone: &verified.zone,
                    ttl: verified.ttl,
                })
            })
        })
}

fn nsec3_records(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet]) -> impl Iterator<Item = Nsec3Record<'_>> {
    nsec3_records_with_any_iterations(rrsets).filter(|record| record.nsec3.iterations <= MAX_NSEC3_ITERATIONS)
}

// RFC 5155, 8.3. Closest Encloser Proof.
// In order to verify a closest encloser proof, the validator MUST find the longest name, X, such that
// o  X is an ancestor of QNAME that is matched by an NSEC3 RR present in the response.  This is a candidate for the
//    closest encloser, and
// o  The name one label longer than X (but still an ancestor of -- or equal to -- QNAME) is covered by an NSEC3 RR
//    present in the response.
struct ClosestEncloserProof {
    closest_encloser: DomainName,
    next_closer_opt_out: bool,
}

fn nsec3_closest_encloser_proof(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet], name: &DomainName) -> Option<ClosestEncloserProof> {
    let mut previous_covered = false;
    let mut previous_opt_out = false;
    for labels in (1..=name.labels.len()).rev() {
        let sname = name.suffix(labels);
        let mut covered = false;
        // RFC 5155, 3.1.2.1. Opt-Out Flag.
        // If the Opt-Out flag is clear, the NSEC3 record covers zero unsigned delegations.
        // So any covering record without the flag rules out an unsigned delegation, whatever order they come in.
        let mut all_opt_out = true;
        for record in nsec3_records(rrsets) {
            if record.matches(&sname) {
                // Once the closest encloser has been discovered, the validator MUST check that the NSEC3 RR that has
                // the closest encloser as the original owner name is from the proper zone.  The DNAME type bit must
                // not be set and the NS type bit may only be set if the SOA type bit is set.
                if !previous_covered
                    || record.nsec3.has_type(ResourceType::DNAME)
                    || (record.nsec3.has_type(ResourceType::NS) && !record.nsec3.has_type(ResourceType::SOA))
                {
                    return None;
                }
                return Some(ClosestEncloserProof {
                    closest_encloser: sname,
                    next_closer_opt_out: previous_opt_out,
                });
            }
            if record.covers(&sname) {
                covered = true;
                all_opt_out &= record.nsec3.is_opt_out();
            }
        }
        previous_covered = covered;
        previous_opt_out = covered && all_opt_out;
    }
    None
}

fn nsec_closest_encloser(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet], name: &DomainName) -> Option<DomainName> {
    // The closest encloser is the longest ancestor of the name that exists. Every ancestor of an NSEC's owner and
    // next name exists, so the longest suffix the name shares with either side of a covering NSEC is it.
    nsec_records(rrsets)
        .filter(|record| record.covers(name))
        .map(|record| {
            name.common_suffix_length(record.owner)
                .max(name.common_suffix_length(&record.nsec.next_domain_name))
        })
        .max()
        .map(|shared| name.suffix(shared))
}

// RFC 8198, Appendix B. Procedure for Determining ENT vs. NXDOMAIN with NSEC.
// If the next domain name is a subdomain of the given name, you have an ENT.  Otherwise, you have an NXDOMAIN.
fn nsec_proves_empty_non_terminal(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet], name: &DomainName) -> bool {
    nsec_records(rrsets).any(|record| {
        record.covers(name)
            && name.is_ancestor_or_equal_of(&record.nsec.next_domain_name)
            && !name.eq_ignore_case(&record.nsec.next_domain_name)
    })
}

pub(super) fn has_excessive_nsec3_iterations(rrsets: &[VerifiedRRSet]) -> bool {
    nsec3_records_with_any_iterations(rrsets).any(|record| record.nsec3.iterations > MAX_NSEC3_ITERATIONS)
}

/// What a denial proof establishes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Denial {
    Proven,
    /// RFC 5155, 9.2. Use of the AD Bit.
    /// The AD bit, as defined by [RFC4035], MUST NOT be set when returning a response containing a closest (provable)
    /// encloser proof in which the NSEC3 RR that covers the "next closer" name has the Opt-Out bit set.
    /// An unsigned delegation may exist in the span, so the denial is only Insecure.
    OptOut,
}

pub(super) struct DenialProofs<'a> {
    pub rrsets: &'a [VerifiedRRSet],
}

impl DenialProofs<'_> {
    /// How long every record the proofs could rest on stays valid.
    pub fn ttl(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.rrsets.iter().map(|rrset| rrset.ttl).min()
    }

    pub fn proves_name_error(&self, name: &DomainName) -> Option<Denial> {
        // A name that owns an NSEC record, or is an empty non-terminal, exists.
        if nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name))
            || nsec_proves_empty_non_terminal(self.rrsets, name)
        {
            return None;
        }

        // RFC 4035, 5.4. Authenticated Denial of Existence.
        // To prove the non-existence of an RRset, the resolver must be able to verify both that the queried RRset does
        // not exist and that no relevant wildcard RRset exists.
        if let Some(closest_encloser) = nsec_closest_encloser(self.rrsets, name)
            && self.proves_wildcard_absent(&closest_encloser)
        {
            return Some(Denial::Proven);
        }

        // RFC 5155, 8.4. Validating Name Error Responses.
        // A validator MUST verify that there is a closest encloser proof for QNAME present in the response and that
        // there is an NSEC3 RR that covers the wildcard at the closest encloser.
        if let Some(proof) = nsec3_closest_encloser_proof(self.rrsets, name)
            && self.proves_wildcard_absent(&proof.closest_encloser)
        {
            return Some(if proof.next_closer_opt_out {
                Denial::OptOut
            } else {
                Denial::Proven
            });
        }

        None
    }

    pub fn proves_wildcard_absent(&self, closest_encloser: &DomainName) -> bool {
        let wildcard = closest_encloser.with_label_prepended("*");
        nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.covers(&wildcard))
            || nsec3_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.covers(&wildcard))
    }

    /// Returns how long the proof holds, if there is one.
    pub fn proves_next_closer_absent(&self, name: &DomainName, closest_encloser_label_count: usize) -> Option<u32> {
        // RFC 4035, 5.3.4 / RFC 5155, 8.8. Validating Wildcard Answer Responses.
        // Validators MUST verify that there is an NSEC3 RR that covers the "next closer" name to QNAME present in the
        // response.  This proves that QNAME itself did not exist and that the correct wildcard was used to generate the
        // response.
        if closest_encloser_label_count >= name.labels.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let next_closer = name.suffix(closest_encloser_label_count + 1);
        // An NSEC can span an empty non-terminal, which exists all the same.
        let nsec_ttl = if nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(&next_closer))
            || nsec_proves_empty_non_terminal(self.rrsets, &next_closer)
        {
            None
        } else {
            nsec_records(self.rrsets)
                .filter(|record| record.covers(&next_closer))
                .map(|record| record.ttl)
                .max()
        };
        let nsec3_ttl = nsec3_records(self.rrsets)
            .filter(|record| record.covers(&next_closer))
            .map(|record| record.ttl)
            .max();
        nsec_ttl.max(nsec3_ttl)
    }

    pub fn proves_no_data(&self, name: &DomainName, rtype: ResourceType) -> Option<Denial> {
        // RFC 4035, 5.4. Authenticated Denial of Existence.
        // If the requested RR name matches the owner name of an authenticated NSEC RR, then the NSEC RR's type bit map
        // field lists all RR types present at that owner name, and a resolver can prove that the requested RR type does
        // not exist by checking for the RR type in the bit map.
        // RFC 4035, 5.2: A security-aware resolver MUST use the parent NSEC RR when attempting to prove that a DS RRset
        // does not exist.
        let bitmap_denies = |record: &dyn TypeBitMap, owner: &DomainName, zone: &DomainName| {
            if record.has_type(rtype) || record.has_type(ResourceType::CNAME) {
                return false;
            }
            if rtype == ResourceType::DS && record.has_type(ResourceType::SOA) {
                return false;
            }
            rtype == ResourceType::DS || !is_ancestor_delegation(record, owner, zone)
        };

        if nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name) && bitmap_denies(record.nsec, name, record.zone))
        {
            return Some(Denial::Proven);
        }

        // An empty non-terminal owns no RRsets at all.
        if nsec_proves_empty_non_terminal(self.rrsets, name) {
            return Some(Denial::Proven);
        }

        // RFC 5155, 8.5. Validating No Data Responses, QTYPE is not DS.
        // The validator MUST verify that an NSEC3 RR that matches QNAME is present and that both the QTYPE and the CNAME
        // type are not set in its Type Bit Maps field.
        if nsec3_records(self.rrsets)
            .any(|record| record.matches(name) && bitmap_denies(record.nsec3, name, record.zone))
        {
            return Some(Denial::Proven);
        }

        // Wildcard No Data: the name does not exist, but a wildcard does, and it lacks the type.
        // RFC 5155, 8.7. Validating Wildcard No Data Responses.
        let wildcard_denies = |closest_encloser: &DomainName| {
            let wildcard = closest_encloser.with_label_prepended("*");
            nsec_records(self.rrsets)
                .any(|record| record.matches(&wildcard) && bitmap_denies(record.nsec, &wildcard, record.zone))
                || nsec3_records(self.rrsets)
                    .any(|record| record.matches(&wildcard) && bitmap_denies(record.nsec3, &wildcard, record.zone))
        };
        if let Some(closest_encloser) = nsec_closest_encloser(self.rrsets, name)
            && wildcard_denies(&closest_encloser)
        {
            return Some(Denial::Proven);
        }

        let proof = nsec3_closest_encloser_proof(self.rrsets, name)?;
        // RFC 5155, 8.5. Validating No Data Responses, QTYPE is not DS (as corrected by erratum 3441).
        // If there is no NSEC3 RR present that matches QNAME, then the validator MUST verify a closest provable
        // encloser proof for the QNAME.  The validator MUST verify that the Opt-Out bit is set in the NSEC3 RR that
        // covers the "next closer" name to the delegation name. This test covers the case where the response is due
        // to an Empty Non-Terminal derived from an insecure delegation covered by an Opt-Out NSEC3 RR.
        if proof.next_closer_opt_out {
            return Some(Denial::OptOut);
        }
        wildcard_denies(&proof.closest_encloser).then_some(Denial::Proven)
    }

    pub fn proves_insecure_delegation(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        // RFC 4035, 5.2. Authenticating Referrals.
        // If the validator authenticates an NSEC RRset that proves that no DS RRset is present for this zone, then there
        // is no authentication path leading from the parent to the child.
        // RFC 5155, 8.9. Validating Referrals to Unsigned Subzones.
        // If there is an NSEC3 RR present in the response that matches the delegation name, then the validator MUST
        // ensure that the NS bit is set and that the DS bit is not set in the Type Bit Maps field of the NSEC3 RR.  The
        // validator MUST also ensure that the NSEC3 RR is from the correct (i.e., parent) zone.  This is done by
        // ensuring that the SOA bit is not set in the Type Bit Maps field of this NSEC3 RR.
        let is_unsigned_delegation = |record: &dyn TypeBitMap| {
            record.has_type(ResourceType::NS)
                && !record.has_type(ResourceType::DS)
                && !record.has_type(ResourceType::SOA)
        };

        if nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name) && is_unsigned_delegation(record.nsec)) {
            return true;
        }
        if nsec3_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name) && is_unsigned_delegation(record.nsec3)) {
            return true;
        }

        // If there is no NSEC3 RR present that matches the delegation name, then the validator MUST verify a closest
        // provable encloser proof for the delegation name.  The validator MUST verify that the Opt-Out bit is set in the
        // NSEC3 RR that covers the "next closer" name to the delegation name.
        nsec3_closest_encloser_proof(self.rrsets, name).is_some_and(|proof| proof.next_closer_opt_out)
    }

    pub fn proves_name_exists_without_delegation(&self, name: &DomainName) -> bool {
        let is_not_a_cut =
            |record: &dyn TypeBitMap| !record.has_type(ResourceType::NS) && !record.has_type(ResourceType::DS);
        nsec_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name) && is_not_a_cut(record.nsec))
            || nsec3_records(self.rrsets).any(|record| record.matches(name) && is_not_a_cut(record.nsec3))
    }
}
