}

#[test]
fn reset_fails_whats_in_flight_and_forgets_the_cache() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let cached = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    harness.answer_udp();
    assert!(harness.result(cached).is_ok());

    let in_flight = harness.lookup("example.org");
    harness.resolver.reset_connection(harness.now);
    harness.drain();
    assert_eq!(harness.error(in_flight), "DNS connection was reset");
    assert_eq!(harness.resolver.cached_entry_count(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn expired_addresses_are_not_mistaken_for_a_negative_answer() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let first = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    harness.answer_udp();
    assert!(harness.result(first).is_ok());

    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(301);
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
}

// ---- The system resolver ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn system_requests(harness: &mut Harness) -> (SystemRequestId, Option<SystemRequestId>) {
    let requests = std::mem::take(&mut harness.system);
    let a = requests
        .iter()
        .find(|(_, _, family)| *family == AddressFamily::V4)
        .expect("A side")
        .0;
    let aaaa = requests
        .iter()
        .find(|(_, _, family)| *family == AddressFamily::V6)
        .map(|request| request.0);
    (a, aaaa)
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_waits_briefly_for_ipv6_after_ipv4() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    assert!(harness.done.is_empty());
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup).len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_goes_ahead_with_ipv4_when_ipv6_takes_too_long() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    harness.advance(IPV6_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    // The late side still lands in the cache.
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    let again = harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(again).len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_waits_for_ipv4_after_ipv6() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    harness.advance(IPV6_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert!(harness.done.is_empty());
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup).len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_goes_ahead_with_ipv6_when_ipv4_takes_too_long() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (_, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    harness.advance(IPV4_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup), vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_skips_ipv6_when_ipv6_is_unreachable() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    harness.ipv6_reachable.set(false);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    assert_eq!(aaaa, None);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    // On request, and for local names, the AAAA side goes ahead anyway.
    let options = LookupOptions {
        query_aaaa_without_global_ipv6: true,
        ..LookupOptions::default()
    };
    harness.lookup_with("example.org", &[ResourceType::A, ResourceType::AAAA], options);
    assert!(system_requests(&mut harness).1.is_some());
    harness.lookup("printer.local");
    assert!(system_requests(&mut harness).1.is_some());
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_looks_up_ipv6_again_once_ipv6_is_reachable() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    harness.ipv6_reachable.set(false);
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, _) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));

    harness.ipv6_reachable.set(true);
    harness.now += IPV6_REACHABILITY_CHECK_INTERVAL;
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (_, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    assert!(aaaa.is_some());
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_failure_fails_the_lookup() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Err("nope".to_owned()));
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Err("nope".to_owned()));
    assert_eq!(harness.error(lookup), "Could not resolve to IPv4 or IPv6 address");
}

// ---- DNSSEC ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Answers every query the resolver sends from the signed test zones, until nothing more goes out.
fn serve_signed_zones(harness: &mut Harness, server: &mut crate::dnssec::tests::Server) {
    loop {
        let writes = harness.take_writes();
        if writes.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        for (connection, query) in writes {
            let query = Message::from_wire(&query).unwrap();
            let mut response = server.answer(&query.questions[0]);
            response.header.id = query.header.id;
            harness.receive(connection, &response.to_wire().unwrap());
        }
    }
}

fn dnssec_harness(server: &crate::dnssec::tests::Server) -> Harness {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    harness.resolver.set_trust_anchors(vec![server.root_ds()]);
    harness
        .resolver
        .set_wall_clock(harness.now, u64::from(crate::dnssec::tests::NOW));
    harness
}

const VALIDATE: LookupOptions = LookupOptions {
    validate_dnssec_locally: true,
    query_aaaa_without_global_ipv6: false,
};

#[test]
fn validated_lookup_is_secure() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    server.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&server);
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);

    let result = harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(result.security_status, Some(SecurityStatus::Secure));
    assert_eq!(result.addresses(), vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 1))]);

    let again = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(
        harness.result(again).as_ref().unwrap().security_status,
        Some(SecurityStatus::Secure)
    );
}

#[test]
fn validated_lookup_in_an_unsigned_zone_is_insecure() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(true);
    server.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&server);
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("host.unsigned.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);
    assert_eq!(
        harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap().security_status,
        Some(SecurityStatus::Insecure)
    );
}

#[test]
fn validated_lookup_with_the_wrong_trust_anchor_fails() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    server.start();
    let mut other = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    other.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&other);
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);
    assert_eq!(harness.error(lookup), "DNSSEC validation failed");
}

#[test]
fn unvalidated_cache_entries_do_not_serve_validated_lookups() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    server.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&server);
    harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);

    // The unvalidated answer is cached, and serves unvalidated lookups.
    let cached = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.result(cached).as_ref().unwrap().security_status, None);

    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    assert!(!harness.writes.is_empty());
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);
    assert_eq!(
        harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap().security_status,
        Some(SecurityStatus::Secure)
    );
}

#[test]
fn lookup_for_no_types_settles_at_once() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap().records.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.connects.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn server_name_looked_up_with_the_system_resolver_stays_out_of_the_cache() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dns.quad9.net");
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    for (request, _, family) in std::mem::take(&mut harness.system) {
        let address = match family {
            AddressFamily::V4 => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(9, 9, 9, 9)),
            AddressFamily::V6 => IpAddr::V6("2620:fe::fe".parse().unwrap()),
        };
        harness.system_resolved(request, Ok(vec![address]));
    }
    assert_eq!(harness.connects.len(), 1);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    harness.take_writes();

    // Looking up the server's own name goes to the server, rather than coming from what the system resolver said.
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("dns.quad9.net", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(!harness.done.contains_key(&lookup));
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn server_names_get_the_same_special_handling_as_other_names() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("localhost.");
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.connects[0].address.ip().is_loopback());

    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dnsresolverabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz234567abcdefghijklmn.onion");
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.connects.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.result(lookup).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn lookup_fails_when_no_random_query_id_can_be_had() {
    let mut resolver = Resolver::new(Box::new(|| true), Box::new(|| None));
    let now = Instant::now();
    resolver.set_server(
        Some(ServerConfig {
            host: "127.0.0.1".to_owned(),
            port: 53,
            transport: ServerTransport::Udp,
        }),
        now,
    );
    let lookup = resolver.lookup(
        "example.com",
        Class::IN,
        &[ResourceType::A],
        LookupOptions::default(),
        now,
    );
    let mut failure = None;
    while let Some(action) = resolver.take_action() {
        if let Action::LookupDone { lookup: done, result } = action {
            assert_eq!(done, lookup);
            failure = result.err();
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(failure.unwrap().to_string(), "Could not pick a random DNS query ID");
}

#[test]
fn port_zero_is_the_default_port_of_the_transport() {
    for (transport, port) in [(ServerTransport::Udp, 53), (ServerTransport::Tls, 853)] {
        let mut harness = Harness::new(Some(ServerConfig {
            host: "192.0.2.53".to_owned(),
            port: 0,
            transport,
        }));
        harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(harness.connects[0].address.port(), port);
    }
}
#[test]
fn queries_for_names_that_differ_only_in_label_boundaries_are_kept_apart() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    harness.take_writes();

    let dotted_label = DomainName {
        labels: vec![b"a.b".to_vec(), b"example".to_vec()],
    };
    let two_labels = DomainName::from_string("a.b.example");
    for (index, name) in [dotted_label, two_labels].iter().enumerate() {
        let waiter = QueryWaiter::Validation(index as u64);
        harness
            .resolver
            .query(name, ResourceType::DS, Class::IN, true, waiter, harness.now);
    }
    harness.drain();
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn zero_ttl_answers_are_not_served_from_the_cache() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let connection = harness.connects[0].connection;
    harness.connected(connection);
    let (_, query) = harness.take_writes().remove(0);
    let response = respond(&query, |response| {
        for answer in &mut response.answers {
            answer.ttl = 0;
        }
    });
    harness.receive(connection, &response);
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn cache_hits_only_return_the_requested_types() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let both = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    harness.answer_udp();
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(both).len(), 2);

    let only_a = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(only_a), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_starts_over_once_a_grace_window_result_has_expired() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let first = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, stalled_aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    harness.advance(IPV6_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(first), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    // The AAAA side never answers. While the A record is fresh, it serves.
    let joined = harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(joined), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    harness.advance(Duration::from_secs(u64::from(SYSTEM_RESOLVER_SYNTHETIC_TTL_SECONDS)));
    let later = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    assert!(!harness.done.contains_key(&later));

    // The answer to the abandoned resolution changes nothing for the new one.
    harness.system_resolved(stalled_aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    assert!(!harness.done.contains_key(&later));
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(later), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);
}

fn soa(ttl: u32, minimum: u32) -> ResourceRecord {
    ResourceRecord {
        name: DomainName::from_string("example.com"),
        rtype: ResourceType::SOA,
        class: Class::IN,
        ttl,
        data: RecordData::Soa(crate::message::Soa {
            mname: DomainName::from_string("ns.example.com"),
            rname: DomainName::from_string("hostmaster.example.com"),
            minimum,
            ..crate::message::Soa::default()
        }),
        raw: None,
    }
}

// Answers A queries with an address that lives for 300 seconds, and AAAA queries with no data.
fn answer_without_aaaa(harness: &mut Harness, authority: Option<&ResourceRecord>) {
    for (connection, query) in harness.take_writes() {
        let response = respond(&query, |response| {
            let rtype = response.questions[0].rtype;
            response
                .answers
                .retain(|answer| answer.rtype == rtype && rtype == ResourceType::A);
            response.authorities.extend(authority.cloned());
            response.header.authority_count = u16::try_from(response.authorities.len()).unwrap();
        });
        harness.receive(connection, &response);
    }
}

#[test]
fn negative_answers_are_cached_for_as_long_as_the_soa_says() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let first = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    answer_without_aaaa(&mut harness, Some(&soa(3600, 5)));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(first), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());

    // The address is still fresh, but that there is none for IPv6 no longer holds.
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(5);
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
    let only_a = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(only_a), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);
}

#[test]
fn negative_answers_without_an_soa_are_not_cached() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    answer_without_aaaa(&mut harness, None);

    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn negative_answers_behind_an_alias_last_no_longer_than_the_alias() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example.com", &[ResourceType::AAAA], LookupOptions::default());
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    let (connection, query) = harness.take_writes().remove(0);
    let response = respond(&query, |response| {
        response.answers = vec![ResourceRecord {
            name: DomainName::from_string("www.example.com"),
            rtype: ResourceType::CNAME,
            class: Class::IN,
            ttl: 5,
            data: RecordData::Cname(DomainName::from_string("cdn.example.com")),
            raw: None,
        }];
        response.authorities.push(soa(300, 300));
        response.header.authority_count = 1;
    });
    harness.receive(connection, &response);
    assert!(harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap().addresses().is_empty());

    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(5);
    harness.lookup_with("www.example.com", &[ResourceType::AAAA], LookupOptions::default());
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_only_looks_up_the_requested_address_families() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let only_aaaa = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::AAAA], LookupOptions::default());
    let requests = std::mem::take(&mut harness.system);
    assert_eq!(requests.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(requests[0].2, AddressFamily::V6);
    harness.system_resolved(requests[0].0, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(only_aaaa), vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]);

    let tlsa = harness.lookup_with("_443._tcp.example.com", &[ResourceType::TLSA], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.error(tlsa), "The system resolver can only look up addresses");
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_failures_are_not_cached_as_missing_addresses() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let first = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (a, _) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Err("temporary failure".to_owned()));
    assert!(harness.result(first).is_err());

    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert_eq!(harness.system.len(), 1);
}

fn system_resolver_answers_say_nothing_about_types_it_was_not_asked_about() {

#[test]
fn system_resolver_finding_no_addresses_is_the_same_answer_before_and_after_caching() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let first = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (a, _) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![]));
    assert!(harness.addresses(first).is_empty());

    let cached = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.addresses(cached).is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_answers_from_before_a_reset_stay_out_of_the_cache() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let before = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);

    harness.resolver.set_server(
        Some(ServerConfig {
            host: "127.0.0.1".to_owned(),
            port: 53,
            transport: ServerTransport::Udp,
        }),
        harness.now,
    );
    harness.drain();
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]));
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![]));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(before), vec![IpAddr::V4(A_ADDRESS)]);

    // The configured server answers from now on.
    let after = harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(!harness.done.contains_key(&after));
    assert_eq!(harness.connects.len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn record_lifetimes_start_when_their_answer_arrives() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    let writes = harness.take_writes();
    let ttl_10 = |response: &mut Message| {
        for answer in &mut response.answers {
            answer.ttl = 10;
        }
    };

    let (connection, a_query) = &writes[0];
    harness.receive(*connection, &respond(a_query, ttl_10));
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(8);
    let (connection, aaaa_query) = &writes[1];
    harness.receive(*connection, &respond(aaaa_query, ttl_10));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup).len(), 2);

    // The A record has 2 seconds left, not 10.
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(2);
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn zero_ttl_answers_reach_the_lookup_that_fetched_them_alongside_later_ones() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    let writes = harness.take_writes();
    let zero_ttl = |response: &mut Message| {
        for answer in &mut response.answers {
            answer.ttl = 0;
        }
    };
    let (connection, a_query) = &writes[0];
    harness.receive(*connection, &respond(a_query, zero_ttl));
    harness.now += Duration::from_millis(5);
    let (connection, aaaa_query) = &writes[1];
    harness.receive(*connection, &respond(aaaa_query, |_| {}));
    assert_eq!(harness.addresses(lookup).len(), 2);

    // The cache only has the AAAA record to offer.
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.take_writes().len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn validated_record_lifetimes_start_when_the_answer_arrived() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    server.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&server);
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);

    // The answer comes in at once, and what validating it takes comes in much later.
    let (connection, query) = harness.take_writes().remove(0);
    let query = Message::from_wire(&query).unwrap();
    let mut response = server.answer(&query.questions[0]);
    response.header.id = query.header.id;
    harness.receive(connection, &response.to_wire().unwrap());
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(250);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);
    assert!(harness.result(lookup).is_ok());

    // The A record's 300 seconds count from when it arrived.
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(51);
    harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::A], VALIDATE);
    assert!(!harness.writes.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn query_ids_are_found_when_random_ones_keep_colliding() {
    let mut resolver = Resolver::new(Box::new(|| true), Box::new(|| Some(7)));
    let now = Instant::now();
    resolver.set_server(
        Some(ServerConfig {
            host: "127.0.0.1".to_owned(),
            port: 53,
            transport: ServerTransport::Udp,
        }),
        now,
    );
    resolver.lookup(
        "a.example",
        Class::IN,
        &[ResourceType::A],
        LookupOptions::default(),
        now,
    );
    resolver.lookup(
        "b.example",
        Class::IN,
        &[ResourceType::A],
        LookupOptions::default(),
        now,
    );
    let mut ids = resolver.in_flight_by_id.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    ids.sort_unstable();
    assert_eq!(ids, vec![7, 8]);
}

#[test]
fn server_is_reached_at_its_other_addresses_when_one_fails() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dns.quad9.net");
    let first = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let requests = std::mem::take(&mut harness.system);
    // The IPv6 side answers first, so its address comes first.
    for (request, _, family) in requests.iter().rev() {
        let address = match family {
            AddressFamily::V4 => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(9, 9, 9, 9)),
            AddressFamily::V6 => IpAddr::V6("2620:fe::fe".parse().unwrap()),
        };
        harness.system_resolved(*request, Ok(vec![address]));
    }
    assert_eq!(harness.connects[0].address, "[2620:fe::fe]:853".parse().unwrap());
    harness
        .resolver
        .on_connect_failed(harness.connects[0].connection, "unreachable".to_owned(), harness.now);
    harness.drain();
    assert!(harness.result(first).is_err());

    // The next attempt goes to the IPv4 address, still verifying the certificate for the server's name.
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.connects.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(harness.connects[1].address, "9.9.9.9:853".parse().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(harness.connects[1].server_name, "dns.quad9.net");
}

fn server_v6() -> IpAddr {
    IpAddr::V6("2620:fe::fe".parse().unwrap())
}

fn server_v4() -> IpAddr {
    IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(9, 9, 9, 9))
}

#[test]
fn server_addresses_that_come_in_after_connecting_started_are_tried_too() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dns.quad9.net");
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![server_v6()]));
    harness.advance(IPV4_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert_eq!(harness.connects.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(harness.connects[0].address.ip(), server_v6());

    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![server_v4()]));
    harness
        .resolver
        .on_connect_failed(harness.connects[0].connection, "unreachable".to_owned(), harness.now);
    harness.drain();

    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(harness.connects[1].address.ip(), server_v4());
}

#[test]
fn server_name_is_looked_up_again_once_all_its_addresses_failed() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dns.quad9.net");
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    for (request, _, family) in std::mem::take(&mut harness.system) {
        let address = if family == AddressFamily::V4 {
            server_v4()
        } else {
            server_v6()
        };
        harness.system_resolved(request, Ok(vec![address]));
    }
    for attempt in 0..2 {
        if attempt > 0 {
            harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
        }
        let connection = harness.connects.last().unwrap().connection;
        harness
            .resolver
            .on_connect_failed(connection, "unreachable".to_owned(), harness.now);
        harness.drain();
    }
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());

    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    assert_eq!(harness.system.len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn server_name_lookups_from_before_a_server_change_do_not_serve_the_new_server() {
    let mut harness = Harness::tls("dns.quad9.net");
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![server_v6()]));
    harness.advance(IPV4_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert_eq!(harness.connects.len(), 1);

    // Only the port changes, while the IPv4 side of the server's name is still being looked up.
    let server = ServerConfig {
        host: "dns.quad9.net".to_owned(),
        port: 8853,
        transport: ServerTransport::Tls,
    };
    harness.resolver.set_server(Some(server), harness.now);
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (new_a, new_aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![server_v4()]));

    // The new server gets the addresses of its own lookup.
    harness.system_resolved(new_aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![server_v6()]));
    harness.system_resolved(new_a, Ok(vec![server_v4()]));
    let connect = harness.connects.last().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(connect.address.port(), 8853);
    let connection = connect.connection;
    harness
        .resolver
        .on_connect_failed(connection, "unreachable".to_owned(), harness.now);
    harness.drain();
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let addresses: Vec<IpAddr> = harness
        .connects
        .iter()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|connect| connect.address.ip())
        .collect();
    assert!(addresses.contains(&server_v4()) && addresses.contains(&server_v6()));
}

#[test]
fn late_udp_answers_do_not_count_once_a_question_moved_to_tcp() {
    let mut harness = Harness::udp();
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let udp = harness.connects[0].connection;
    harness.connected(udp);
    let (_, query) = harness.take_writes().remove(0);
    let truncated = respond(&query, |response| {
        response.header.options.set_is_truncated(true);
        response.answers.clear();
    });
    harness.receive(udp, &truncated);
    let tcp = harness.connects[1].connection;
    harness.connected(tcp);
    let (_, tcp_query) = harness.take_writes().remove(0);

    // A full answer over UDP that shows up late is not the one asked for now.
    let late = respond(&query, |response| response.answers.truncate(1));
    harness.receive(udp, &late);
    assert!(!harness.done.contains_key(&lookup));

    harness.receive(tcp, &frame(&respond(unframe(&tcp_query), |_| {})));
    assert!(harness.result(lookup).is_ok());
}

#[test]
fn system_resolver_family_that_never_answers_is_given_up_on() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let lookup = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    // The A side's answer gets lost. The AAAA side finds nothing, which starts no grace window.
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![]));
    assert_eq!(
        harness.resolver.next_deadline(),
        Some(harness.now + SYSTEM_RESOLVER_TIMEOUT)
    );

    harness.advance(SYSTEM_RESOLVER_TIMEOUT);
    assert_eq!(harness.error(lookup), "Could not resolve to IPv4 or IPv6 address");
    assert_eq!(harness.resolver.next_deadline(), None);

    assert!(harness.resolver.system_requests.is_empty());
    assert!(harness.cancelled.contains(&a));

    // That the A side never answered says nothing about whether there are IPv4 addresses.
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert_eq!(harness.system.len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn late_system_resolver_answers_do_not_replace_newer_cached_addresses() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    let both = harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, stalled_aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 1))]));
    harness.advance(IPV6_RESOLUTION_DELAY);
    assert!(harness.result(both).is_ok());

    // A later IPv4-only lookup finds a newer address.
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(10);
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (a, _) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 2))]));

    // The first lookup's IPv6 side finishes now: its addresses join the cache, its older IPv4 one does not.
    harness.system_resolved(stalled_aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    let cached = harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    let mut addresses = harness.addresses(cached);
    addresses.sort();
    assert_eq!(
        addresses,
        vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 2)), IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]
    );
}

#[test]
fn resolutions_finishing_within_their_grace_window_keep_newer_cached_addresses() {
    let mut harness = Harness::new(None);
    harness.lookup("example.com");
    let (a, aaaa) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 1))]));

    harness.now += Duration::from_millis(20);
    harness.lookup_with("example.com", &[ResourceType::A], LookupOptions::default());
    let (newer_a, _) = system_requests(&mut harness);
    harness.system_resolved(newer_a, Ok(vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 2))]));

    // The first resolution's IPv6 side finishes before its grace window ends.
    harness.now += Duration::from_millis(20);
    harness.system_resolved(aaaa.unwrap(), Ok(vec![IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]));
    let cached = harness.lookup("example.com");
    assert!(harness.system.is_empty());
    let mut addresses = harness.addresses(cached);
    addresses.sort();
    assert_eq!(
        addresses,
        vec![IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(192, 0, 2, 2)), IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST)]
    );
}

#[test]
fn validated_negative_answers_last_no_longer_than_their_proof() {
    let mut server = crate::dnssec::tests::make_server(false);
    server.expire_example_signatures_in(2);
    server.start();
    let mut harness = dnssec_harness(&server);
    let lookup = harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::AAAA], VALIDATE);
    harness.connected(harness.connects[0].connection);
    serve_signed_zones(&mut harness, &mut server);
    let result = harness.result(lookup).as_ref().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(result.security_status, Some(SecurityStatus::Secure));
    assert!(result.records.is_empty());

    harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::AAAA], VALIDATE);
    assert!(harness.writes.is_empty());

    // The SOA allows longer, but the proof's signatures run out.
    harness.now += Duration::from_secs(2);
    harness.lookup_with("www.example", &[ResourceType::AAAA], VALIDATE);
    assert!(!harness.writes.is_empty());
}

FILE: Libraries/LibDNS/Rust/src/transport.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! A DNS connection that never waits or performs I/O. The socket owner supplies received bytes and sends queued output.
//! Streams carry plaintext here; the embedder handles TLS and reports connection only after the handshake.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::fmt;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    Udp,
    Stream,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error {
    TimedOut,
    Closed,
    Socket(String),
    FrameTooLarge,
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::TimedOut => write!(f, "Connecting to the DNS server timed out"),
            Error::Closed => write!(f, "The DNS server closed the connection"),
            Error::Socket(error) => write!(f, "DNS server connection failed: {error}"),
            Error::FrameTooLarge => write!(f, "DNS message is too large for a TCP frame"),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum State {
    Connecting,
    Ready,
    Failed(Error),
}

pub struct Connection {
    kind: Kind,
    state: State,
    deadline: Instant,
    // Streams only: bytes of a frame whose end has not arrived yet.
    incoming: Vec<u8>,
    // Messages that arrived complete.
    messages: VecDeque<Vec<u8>>,
    // Datagrams for UDP; for streams, bytes to write in order.
    outgoing: VecDeque<Vec<u8>>,
    // Messages to send once the connection is up.
    pending: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
}

impl Connection {
    /// Initially connecting, with the given timeout.
    pub fn new(kind: Kind, now: Instant, timeout: Duration) -> Self {
        Self {
            kind,
            state: State::Connecting,
            deadline: now + timeout,
            incoming: Vec::new(),
            messages: VecDeque::new(),
            outgoing: VecDeque::new(),
            pending: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self) -> Kind {
        self.kind
    }

    pub fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        self.state == State::Ready
    }

    pub fn is_connecting(&self) -> bool {
        self.state == State::Connecting
    }

    pub fn error(&self) -> Option<&Error> {
        match &self.state {
            State::Failed(error) => Some(error),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The connection timeout deadline, only while connecting.
    pub fn deadline(&self) -> Option<Instant> {
        (self.state == State::Connecting).then_some(self.deadline)
    }

    pub fn on_tick(&mut self, now: Instant) {
        if self.deadline().is_some_and(|deadline| now >= deadline) {
            self.fail(Error::TimedOut);
        }
    }

    pub fn on_connected(&mut self) {
        if self.state != State::Connecting {
            return;
        }
        self.state = State::Ready;
        for message in std::mem::take(&mut self.pending) {
            if let Err(error) = self.send_now(message) {
                self.fail(error);
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn on_socket_error(&mut self, error: String) {
        self.fail(Error::Socket(error));
    }

    /// The peer closed its side of a stream.
    pub fn on_eof(&mut self) {
        if self.error().is_none() {
            self.fail(Error::Closed);
        }
    }

    /// For UDP, `bytes` is one datagram. For streams, it is whatever the socket read.
    pub fn on_received(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        if self.error().is_some() {
            return;
        }
        match self.kind {
            Kind::Udp => self.messages.push_back(bytes.to_vec()),
            Kind::Stream => {
                self.incoming.extend_from_slice(bytes);
                self.take_frames();
            }
        }
    }

    /// Queues a message to the server, to go out once the connection is up.
    pub fn send(&mut self, message: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), Error> {
        match &self.state {
            State::Failed(error) => Err(error.clone()),
            State::Connecting => {
                if self.kind == Kind::Stream && message.len() > usize::from(u16::MAX) {
                    return Err(Error::FrameTooLarge);
                }
                self.pending.push(message);
                Ok(())
            }
            State::Ready => self.send_now(message),
        }
    }

    pub fn take_message(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        self.messages.pop_front()
    }

    /// The next datagram, or the next bytes of the stream, to write to the socket.
    pub fn take_outgoing(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        self.outgoing.pop_front()
    }

    fn send_now(&mut self, message: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if self.kind == Kind::Udp {
            self.outgoing.push_back(message);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // RFC 1035, 4.2.2. TCP usage.
        // The message is prefixed with a two byte length field which gives the message length, excluding the two
        // byte length field.
        let length = u16::try_from(message.len()).map_err(|_| Error::FrameTooLarge)?;
        let mut framed = Vec::with_capacity(message.len() + 2);
        framed.extend_from_slice(&length.to_be_bytes());
        framed.extend_from_slice(&message);
        self.outgoing.push_back(framed);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn fail(&mut self, error: Error) {
        self.state = State::Failed(error);
        self.pending.clear();
        self.outgoing.clear();
    }

    fn take_frames(&mut self) {
        // NB: The bytes of complete frames go all at once, rather than moving what follows each one forward.
        let mut consumed = 0;
        while let Some(length) = self.incoming[consumed..]
            .first_chunk::<2>()
            .map(|length| usize::from(u16::from_be_bytes(*length)))
        {
            let start = consumed + 2;
            if self.incoming.len() < start + length {
                break;
            }
            self.messages.push_back(self.incoming[start..start + length].to_vec());
            consumed = start + length;
        }
        self.incoming.drain(..consumed);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn udp_sends_datagrams_once_connected() {
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Udp, Instant::now(), Duration::from_secs(5));
        connection.send(vec![1, 2, 3]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(connection.take_outgoing(), None);
        connection.on_connected();
        assert_eq!(connection.take_outgoing(), Some(vec![1, 2, 3]));
        connection.on_received(&[4, 5]);
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), Some(vec![4, 5]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_frames_and_reassembles() {
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Stream, Instant::now(), Duration::from_secs(5));
        connection.on_connected();
        connection.send(vec![0xAA, 0xBB]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(connection.take_outgoing(), Some(vec![0, 2, 0xAA, 0xBB]));

        connection.on_received(&[0, 3, 1]);
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), None);
        connection.on_received(&[2, 3, 0, 1]);
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), Some(vec![1, 2, 3]));
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), None);
        connection.on_received(&[9]);
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), Some(vec![9]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_takes_every_frame_of_one_read() {
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Stream, Instant::now(), Duration::from_secs(5));
        connection.on_connected();
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        for frame in 0..100u8 {
            bytes.extend_from_slice(&[0, 1, frame]);
        }
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&[0, 2, 7]);
        connection.on_received(&bytes);
        for frame in 0..100u8 {
            assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), Some(vec![frame]));
        }
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), None);
        connection.on_received(&[8]);
        assert_eq!(connection.take_message(), Some(vec![7, 8]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_rejects_oversized_messages() {
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Stream, Instant::now(), Duration::from_secs(5));
        assert_eq!(connection.send(vec![0; 70_000]), Err(Error::FrameTooLarge));
    }

    // A server that accepts the connection and never finishes the handshake.
    #[test]
    fn connecting_times_out() {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Stream, start, Duration::from_secs(5));
        connection.send(vec![1]).unwrap();
        connection.on_tick(start + Duration::from_secs(4));
        assert!(connection.is_connecting());
        connection.on_tick(start + Duration::from_secs(5));
        assert_eq!(connection.error(), Some(&Error::TimedOut));
        assert_eq!(connection.take_outgoing(), None);
        assert_eq!(connection.send(vec![1]), Err(Error::TimedOut));
    }

    #[test]
    fn eof_fails_the_connection() {
        let mut connection = Connection::new(Kind::Stream, Instant::now(), Duration::from_secs(5));
        connection.on_connected();
        connection.on_eof();
        assert_eq!(connection.error(), Some(&Error::Closed));
    }
}

#include <LibDNS/Types.h>
#include <RustFFI.h>

namespace DNS::Messages {

static void store_string(void* context, FFI::FfiBytes bytes)
{
    *static_cast<String*>(context) = MUST(String::from_utf8({ reinterpret_cast<char const*>(bytes.data), bytes.length }));
}

String to_string(ResourceType type)
{
    String name;
    FFI::dns_resource_type_name(to_underlying(type), store_string, &name);
    return name;
}

Optional<ResourceType> resource_type_from_string(StringView name)
{
    u16 type = 0;
    if (!FFI::dns_resource_type_from_name({ reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(name.characters_without_null_termination()), name.length() }, &type))
        return {};
    return static_cast<ResourceType>(type);
}

}

// Listing from IANA https://www.iana.org/assignments/dns-parameters/dns-parameters.xhtml#dns-parameters-4.
enum class ResourceType : u16 {
    Reserved = 0,    // [RFC6895]
    A = 1,           // a host address [RFC1035]
    NS = 2,          // an authoritative name server [RFC1035]
    MD = 3,          // a mail destination (OBSOLETE - use MX) [RFC1035]
    MF = 4,          // a mail forwarder (OBSOLETE - use MX) [RFC1035]
    CNAME = 5,       // the canonical name for an alias [RFC1035]
    SOA = 6,         // marks the start of a zone of authority [RFC1035]
    MB = 7,          // a mailbox domain name (EXPERIMENTAL) [RFC1035]
    MG = 8,          // a mail group member (EXPERIMENTAL) [RFC1035]
    MR = 9,          // a mail rename domain name (EXPERIMENTAL) [RFC1035]
    NULL_ = 10,      // a null RR (EXPERIMENTAL) [RFC1035]
    WKS = 11,        // a well known service description [RFC1035]
    PTR = 12,        // a domain name pointer [RFC1035]
    HINFO = 13,      // host information [RFC1035]
    MINFO = 14,      // mailbox or mail list information [RFC1035]
    MX = 15,         // mail exchange [RFC1035]
    TXT = 16,        // text strings [RFC1035]
    RP = 17,         // for Responsible Person [RFC1183]
    AFSDB = 18,      // for AFS Data Base location [RFC1183][RFC5864]
    X25 = 19,        // for X.25 PSDN address [RFC1183]
    ISDN = 20,       // for ISDN address [RFC1183]
    RT = 21,         // for Route Through [RFC1183]
    NSAP = 22,       // for NSAP address, NSAP style A record (DEPRECATED) [RFC1706][Moving TPC.INT and NSAP.INT infrastructure domains to historic]
    NSAP_PTR = 23,   // for domain name pointer, NSAP style (DEPRECATED) [RFC1706][Moving TPC.INT and NSAP.INT infrastructure domains to historic]
    SIG = 24,        // for security signature [RFC2536][RFC2931][RFC3110][RFC4034]
    KEY = 25,        // for security key [RFC2536][RFC2539][RFC3110][RFC4034]
    PX = 26,         // X.400 mail mapping information [RFC2163]
    GPOS = 27,       // Geographical Position [RFC1712]
    AAAA = 28,       // IP6 Address [RFC3596]
    LOC = 29,        // Location Information [RFC1876]
    NXT = 30,        // Next Domain (OBSOLETE) [RFC2535][RFC3755]
    EID = 31,        // Endpoint Identifier [Michael_Patton][http://ana-3.lcs.mit.edu/~jnc/nimrod/dns.txt]
    NIMLOC = 32,     // Nimrod Locator [1][Michael_Patton][http://ana-3.lcs.mit.edu/~jnc/nimrod/dns.txt]
    SRV = 33,        // Server Selection [1][RFC2782]
    ATMA = 34,       // ATM Address "[ ATM Forum Technical Committee, "ATM Name System, V2.0", Doc ID: AF-DANS-0152.000, July 2000. Available from and held in escrow by IANA.]"
    NAPTR = 35,      // Naming Authority Pointer [RFC3403]
    KX = 36,         // Key Exchanger [RFC2230]
    CERT = 37,       // CERT [RFC4398]
    A6 = 38,         // A6 (OBSOLETE - use AAAA) [RFC2874][RFC3226][RFC6563]
    DNAME = 39,      // DNAME [RFC6672]
    SINK = 40,       // SINK [Donald_E_Eastlake][draft-eastlake-kitchen-sink]
    OPT = 41,        // OPT [RFC3225][RFC6891]
    APL = 42,        // APL [RFC3123]
    DS = 43,         // Delegation Signer [RFC4034]
    SSHFP = 44,      // SSH Key Fingerprint [RFC4255]
    IPSECKEY = 45,   // IPSECKEY [RFC4025]
    RRSIG = 46,      // RRSIG [RFC4034]
    NSEC = 47,       // NSEC [RFC4034][RFC9077]
    DNSKEY = 48,     // DNSKEY [RFC4034]
    DHCID = 49,      // DHCID [RFC4701]
    NSEC3 = 50,      // NSEC3 [RFC5155][RFC9077]
    NSEC3PARAM = 51, // NSEC3PARAM [RFC5155]
    TLSA = 52,       // TLSA [RFC6698]
    SMIMEA = 53,     // S/MIME cert association [RFC8162]
    HIP = 55,        // Host Identity Protocol [RFC8005]
    NINFO = 56,      // NINFO [Jim_Reid]
    RKEY = 57,       // RKEY [Jim_Reid]
    TALINK = 58,     // Trust Anchor LINK [Wouter_Wijngaards]
    CDS = 59,        // Child DS [RFC7344]
    CDNSKEY = 60,    // DNSKEY(s) the Child wants reflected in DS [RFC7344]
    OPENPGPKEY = 61, // OpenPGP Key [RFC7929]
    CSYNC = 62,      // Child-To-Parent Synchronization [RFC7477]
    ZONEMD = 63,     // Message Digest Over Zone Data [RFC8976]
    SVCB = 64,       // General-purpose service binding [RFC9460]
    HTTPS = 65,      // SVCB-compatible type for use with HTTP [RFC9460]
    SPF = 99,        // [RFC7208]
    UINFO = 100,     // [IANA-Reserved]
    UID = 101,       // [IANA-Reserved]
    GID = 102,       // [IANA-Reserved]
    UNSPEC = 103,    // [IANA-Reserved]
    NID = 104,       // [RFC6742]
    L32 = 105,       // [RFC6742]
    L64 = 106,       // [RFC6742]
    LP = 107,        // [RFC6742]
    EUI48 = 108,     // an EUI-48 address [RFC7043]
    EUI64 = 109,     // an EUI-64 address [RFC7043]
    NXNAME = 128,    // NXDOMAIN indicator for Compact Denial of Existence [draft-ietf-dnsop-compact-denial-of-existence-04]
    TKEY = 249,      // Transaction Key [RFC2930]
    TSIG = 250,      // Transaction Signature [RFC8945]
    IXFR = 251,      // incremental transfer [RFC1995]
    AXFR = 252,      // transfer of an entire zone [RFC1035][RFC5936]
    MAILB = 253,     // mailbox-related RRs (MB, MG or MR) [RFC1035]
    MAILA = 254,     // mail agent RRs (OBSOLETE - see MX) [RFC1035]
    ANY = 255,       // A request for some or all records the server has available [RFC1035][RFC6895][RFC8482]
    URI = 256,       // URI [RFC7553]
    CAA = 257,       // Certification Authority Restriction [RFC8659]
    AVC = 258,       // Application Visibility and Control [Wolfgang_Riedel]
    DOA = 259,       // Digital Object Architecture [draft-durand-doa-over-dns]
    AMTRELAY = 260,  // Automatic Multicast Tunneling Relay [RFC8777]
    RESINFO = 261,   // Resolver Information as Key/Value Pairs [RFC9606]
    WALLET = 262,    // Public wallet address [Paul_Hoffman]
    CLA = 263,       // BP Convergence Layer Adapter [draft-johnson-dns-ipn-cla-07]
    IPN = 264,       // BP Node Number [draft-johnson-dns-ipn-cla-07]
    TA = 32768,      // DNSSEC Trust Authorities "[Sam_Weiler][Deploying DNSSEC Without a Signed Root.  Technical Report 1999-19, Information Networking Institute, Carnegie Mellon University, April 2004.]"
    DLV = 32769,     // DNSSEC Lookaside Validation (OBSOLETE) [RFC8749][RFC4431]
};
DNS_API String to_string(ResourceType);
DNS_API Optional<ResourceType> resource_type_from_string(StringView);

// Listing from IANA https://www.iana.org/assignments/dns-parameters/dns-parameters.xhtml#dns-parameters-2.
enum class Class : u16 {
    IN = 1, // the Internet [RFC1035]
    CH = 3, // the CHAOS class [Moon1981]
    HS = 4, // Hesiod [Dyer1987]
};

#    include <sys/statvfs.h>

#    if !defined(AK_OS_IOS) && defined(AK_OS_BSD_GENERIC)
#        include <sys/disk.h>
#    elif defined(AK_OS_LINUX)
#        include <fcntl.h>
#        include <linux/fs.h>
#        include <sys/syscall.h>
#        include <unistd.h>
#    endif
#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS)
#        include <copyfile.h>
#        include <stdio.h>
#    endif
#endif

// On Linux distros that use glibc `basename` is defined as a macro that expands to `__xpg_basename`, so we undefine it
#if defined(AK_OS_LINUX) && defined(basename)
#    undef basename
#endif

namespace FileSystem {

static ErrorOr<struct stat> stat_path(StringView path)
{
    return Core::File::stat(path);
}

static ErrorOr<struct stat> stat_fd(int fd)
{
    return Core::File::fstat(fd);
}

// LibFileSystem is the portable home for path operations, so it is the one place
// (outside LibCore's own backends) still allowed to reach for platform primitives.
// On Windows these forward to the CRT for now.
// FIXME: Nativize the Windows half (DeleteFileW etc.) and map both platforms'
//        errors into a portable taxonomy.
#ifdef AK_OS_WINDOWS
static ErrorOr<void> remove_file(StringView path)
{
    ByteString path_string = path;
    if (::_unlink(path_string.characters()) < 0)
        return Error::from_syscall("unlink"sv, errno);
    return {};
}

static ErrorOr<void> remove_directory(StringView path)
{
    ByteString path_string = path;
    if (::_rmdir(path_string.characters()) < 0)
        return Error::from_syscall("rmdir"sv, errno);
    return {};
}
#else
static ErrorOr<void> remove_file(StringView path)
{
    return Core::System::unlink(path);
}

static ErrorOr<void> remove_directory(StringView path)
{
    return Core::System::rmdir(path);
}
#endif

ErrorOr<ByteString> current_working_directory()
{
    return Core::System::getcwd();
}

ErrorOr<ByteString> absolute_path(StringView path)
{
#ifndef AK_OS_WINDOWS
    if (exists(path))
        return real_path(path);
#endif

    if (LexicalPath::is_absolute_path(path))
        return LexicalPath::canonicalized_path(path);

    auto working_directory = TRY(current_working_directory());
    return LexicalPath::absolute_path(working_directory, path);
}

#ifndef AK_OS_WINDOWS
ErrorOr<ByteString> real_path(StringView path)
{
    ByteString dep_path = path;
    char* real_path = realpath(dep_path.characters(), nullptr);
    ScopeGuard free_path = [real_path]() { free(real_path); };

    if (!real_path)
        return Error::from_syscall("realpath"sv, errno);

    return ByteString { real_path, strlen(real_path) };
}
#else
// NOTE: real_path on Windows does not resolve symlinks
ErrorOr<ByteString> real_path(StringView path)
{
    return absolute_path(path);
}
#endif

bool exists(StringView path)
{
    return !stat_path(path).is_error();
}

bool exists(int fd)
{
    return !stat_fd(fd).is_error();
}

bool is_regular_file(StringView path)
{
    auto st_or_error = stat_path(path);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISREG(st.st_mode);
}

bool is_regular_file(int fd)
{
    auto st_or_error = stat_fd(fd);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISREG(st.st_mode);
}

bool is_directory(StringView path)
{
    auto st_or_error = stat_path(path);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);
}

bool is_directory(int fd)
{
    auto st_or_error = stat_fd(fd);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);
}

#ifdef AK_OS_WINDOWS
bool is_link(StringView path)
{
    ByteString string_path = path;
    auto attr = GetFileAttributes(string_path.characters());
    if (attr == INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES)
        return false;
    return attr & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT;
}
#else
bool is_link(StringView path)
{
    auto st_or_error = Core::System::lstat(path);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISLNK(st.st_mode);
}

bool is_link(int fd)
{
    auto st_or_error = Core::System::fstat(fd);
    if (st_or_error.is_error())
        return false;
    auto st = st_or_error.release_value();
    return S_ISLNK(st.st_mode);
}

ErrorOr<void> copy_file(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path, struct stat const& source_stat, Core::File& source, PreserveMode preserve_mode)
{
    auto destination_or_error = Core::File::open(destination_path, Core::File::OpenMode::Write, 0666);
    if (destination_or_error.is_error()) {
        if (destination_or_error.error().code() != EISDIR)
            return destination_or_error.release_error();

        auto destination_dir_path = ByteString::formatted("{}/{}", destination_path, LexicalPath::basename(source_path));
        destination_or_error = TRY(Core::File::open(destination_dir_path, Core::File::OpenMode::Write, 0666));
    }
    auto destination = destination_or_error.release_value();

    if (source_stat.st_size > 0)
        TRY(destination->truncate(source_stat.st_size));

    Array<u8, 64 * KiB> buffer;
    while (true) {
        auto bytes = TRY(source.read_some(buffer));
        if (bytes.is_empty())
            break;
        TRY(destination->write_until_depleted(bytes));
    }

    auto my_umask = umask(0);
    umask(my_umask);
    // NOTE: We don't copy the set-uid and set-gid bits unless requested.
    if (!has_flag(preserve_mode, PreserveMode::Permissions))
        my_umask |= 06000;

    if (auto result = Core::System::fchmod(destination->fd(), source_stat.st_mode & ~my_umask); result.is_error())
        if (result.error().is_errno() && result.error().code() != ENOTSUP)
            return result.release_error();

    if (has_flag(preserve_mode, PreserveMode::Ownership))
        if (auto result = Core::System::fchown(destination->fd(), source_stat.st_uid, source_stat.st_gid); result.is_error())
            if (result.error().is_errno() && result.error().code() != ENOTSUP)
                return result.release_error();

    if (has_flag(preserve_mode, PreserveMode::Timestamps)) {
        struct timespec times[2] = {
#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
            source_stat.st_atimespec,
            source_stat.st_mtimespec,
#    else
            source_stat.st_atim,
            source_stat.st_mtim,
#    endif
        };
        TRY(Core::System::utimensat(AT_FDCWD, destination_path, times, 0));
    }
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> move_file(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path, PreserveMode preserve_mode)
{
    auto maybe_error = Core::System::rename(source_path, destination_path);
    if (!maybe_error.is_error())
        return {};

    if (!maybe_error.error().is_errno() || maybe_error.error().code() != EXDEV)
        return maybe_error;

    auto source = TRY(Core::File::open(source_path, Core::File::OpenMode::Read));

    auto source_stat = TRY(Core::System::fstat(source->fd()));

    TRY(copy_file(destination_path, source_path, source_stat, *source, preserve_mode));

    return Core::System::unlink(source_path);
}

// Copies the file, with its permissions and, where the platform can, its extended attributes, to a destination that
// fails with EEXIST if a file is already there. The destination is private to the user until the copy is complete.
static ErrorOr<void> copy_to_new_file(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path)
{
    auto source = TRY(Core::File::open(source_path, Core::File::OpenMode::Read));
    auto source_stat = TRY(Core::System::fstat(source->fd()));
    auto destination = TRY(Core::File::open(destination_path, Core::File::OpenMode::Write | Core::File::OpenMode::MustBeNew, 0600));

    auto result = [&]() -> ErrorOr<void> {
#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS)
        if (::fcopyfile(source->fd(), destination->fd(), nullptr, COPYFILE_DATA | COPYFILE_XATTR) < 0)
            return Error::from_syscall("fcopyfile"sv, errno);
#    else
        Array<u8, 64 * KiB> buffer;
        while (true) {
            auto bytes = TRY(source->read_some(buffer));
            if (bytes.is_empty())
                break;
            TRY(destination->write_until_depleted(bytes));
        }
#    endif
        return Core::System::fchmod(destination->fd(), source_stat.st_mode & 07777);
    }();

    // NB: A failed copy removes the file it created, but not another that has taken its place since.
    if (result.is_error()) {
        auto created = Core::System::fstat(destination->fd());
        auto at_destination = Core::System::lstat(destination_path);
        if (!created.is_error() && !at_destination.is_error()
            && created.value().st_dev == at_destination.value().st_dev && created.value().st_ino == at_destination.value().st_ino)
            (void)Core::System::unlink(destination_path);
    }
    return result;
}

ErrorOr<void> rename_without_replacing(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path)
{
    ByteString source { source_path };
    ByteString destination { destination_path };
#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS)
    if (::renamex_np(source.characters(), destination.characters(), RENAME_EXCL) == 0)
        return {};
    if (errno != ENOTSUP)
        return Error::from_syscall("renamex_np"sv, errno);
#    elif defined(AK_OS_LINUX) && defined(SYS_renameat2)
    if (::syscall(SYS_renameat2, AT_FDCWD, source.characters(), AT_FDCWD, destination.characters(), RENAME_NOREPLACE) == 0)
        return {};
    if (errno != EINVAL && errno != ENOSYS)
        return Error::from_syscall("renameat2"sv, errno);
#    endif

    // NB: Linking fails when the destination exists, and is left for file systems that cannot rename without replacing.
    //     One that cannot link either gets a copy in a destination file created only if none exists.
    if (auto result = Core::System::link(source_path, destination_path); result.is_error()) {
        if (result.error().is_errno() && result.error().code() == EEXIST)
            return result.release_error();
        TRY(copy_to_new_file(destination_path, source_path));
    }

    // NB: The file is at its destination now, and a source left behind is only an extra copy of it.
    (void)Core::System::unlink(source_path);
    return {};
}

#endif // !AK_OS_WINDOWS

#ifdef AK_OS_WINDOWS
ErrorOr<void> move_file(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path, PreserveMode)
{
    // NOTE: Unlike POSIX rename(), MoveFileExW is not guaranteed to replace an existing
    //       destination atomically. MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED provides the cross-volume
    //       copy-and-delete fallback that the POSIX implementation does by hand.
    auto wide_source_path = TRY(to_wide_string(source_path));
    auto wide_destination_path = TRY(to_wide_string(destination_path));
    if (!MoveFileExW(wide_source_path.data(), wide_destination_path.data(), MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED))
        return Error::from_windows_error();
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> rename_without_replacing(StringView destination_path, StringView source_path)
{
    auto wide_source_path = TRY(to_wide_string(source_path));
    auto wide_destination_path = TRY(to_wide_string(destination_path));
    if (MoveFileExW(wide_source_path.data(), wide_destination_path.data(), 0))
        return {};
    auto error = GetLastError();
    if (error == ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS || error == ERROR_FILE_EXISTS)
        return Error::from_errno(EEXIST);
    return Error::from_windows_error(error);
}
#endif

ErrorOr<void> remove(StringView path, RecursionMode mode)
{
    if (mode == RecursionMode::Allowed && is_directory(path)) {
        auto di = Core::DirIterator(path, Core::DirIterator::SkipParentAndBaseDir);
        if (di.has_error())
            return di.error();

        while (di.has_next())
            TRY(remove(di.next_full_path(), RecursionMode::Allowed));

        TRY(remove_directory(path));
    } else {
        TRY(remove_file(path));
    }

    return {};
}

ErrorOr<off_t> size_from_stat(StringView path)
{
    auto st = TRY(stat_path(path));
    return st.st_size;
}

ErrorOr<DiskSpace> compute_disk_space(LexicalPath const& path)
{
#if defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
    ULARGE_INTEGER free_bytes;
    ULARGE_INTEGER total_bytes;

    if (!GetDiskFreeSpaceExA(path.string().characters(), &free_bytes, &total_bytes, nullptr))
        return Error::from_windows_error();

    return DiskSpace {
        .free_bytes = free_bytes.QuadPart,
        .total_bytes = total_bytes.QuadPart,
    };
#else
    struct statvfs stats {};

    if (::statvfs(path.string().characters(), &stats) != 0)
        return Error::from_syscall("statvfs"sv, errno);

    return DiskSpace {
        .free_bytes = stats.f_bavail * stats.f_frsize,
        .total_bytes = stats.f_blocks * stats.f_frsize,
    };
#endif
}

}

};
