namespace Gamepad {

static constexpr int GAMEPAD_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 8;

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-standard-gamepad
// Type     Index   Location
// Button   0       Bottom button in right cluster
//          1       Right button in right cluster
//          2       Left button in right cluster
//          3       Top button in right cluster
//          4       Top left front button
//          5       Top right front button
//          6       Bottom left front button
//          7       Bottom right front button
//          8       Left button in center cluster
//          9       Right button in center cluster
//          10      Left stick pressed button
//          11      Right stick pressed button
//          12      Top button in left cluster
//          13      Bottom button in left cluster
//          14      Left button in left cluster
//          15      Right button in left cluster
//          16      Center button in center cluster
static Array<Variant<SDL_GamepadButton, SDL_GamepadAxis>, 17> const standard_gamepad_button_layout {
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_SOUTH,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_EAST,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_WEST,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_NORTH,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_SHOULDER,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_SHOULDER,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFT_TRIGGER,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_RIGHT_TRIGGER,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_BACK,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_START,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_STICK,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_STICK,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_UP,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_DOWN,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_GUIDE,
};

static Array<SDL_GamepadButton, 11> const non_standard_gamepad_button_layout {
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC1,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_PADDLE1,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_PADDLE1,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_PADDLE2,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_LEFT_PADDLE2,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_TOUCHPAD,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC2,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC3,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC4,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC5,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_MISC6,
};

// axes     0       Horizontal axis for left stick (negative left/positive right)
//          1       Vertical axis for left stick (negative up/positive down)
//          2       Horizontal axis for right stick (negative left/positive right)
//          3       Vertical axis for right stick (negative up/positive down)
static Array<SDL_GamepadAxis, 4> const standard_gamepad_axes_layout {
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFTX,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFTY,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_RIGHTX,
    SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_RIGHTY,
};

static constexpr char const* VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD_NAME = "Ladybird Virtual Gamepad";

static SDLCALL bool record_received_dual_rumble_effect(void* user_data, u16 low_frequency_rumble, u16 high_frequency_rumble)
{
    auto* device = static_cast<SDLGamepadSource::Device*>(user_data);
    device->received_dual_rumble_effects.append({ low_frequency_rumble, high_frequency_rumble });
    return true;
}

static SDLCALL bool record_received_trigger_rumble_effect(void* user_data, u16 left_rumble, u16 right_rumble)
{
    auto* device = static_cast<SDLGamepadSource::Device*>(user_data);
    device->received_trigger_rumble_effects.append({ left_rumble, right_rumble });
    return true;
}

SDLGamepadSource::SDLGamepadSource(IgnoreSystemGamepads ignore_system_gamepads)
    : m_ignore_system_gamepads(ignore_system_gamepads)
{
}

SDLGamepadSource::~SDLGamepadSource()
{
    if (m_poll_timer)
        m_poll_timer->stop();

    // NB: A virtual joystick that outlives its device would call back into freed memory.
    for (auto handle : m_devices.keys())
        remove_device(handle);

    if (m_sdl_initialized)
        SDL_QuitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_GAMEPAD);
}

bool SDLGamepadSource::start()
{
    if (m_sdl_initialized)
        return true;

#if defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
    // Initialize COM in the multithreaded model before SDL gets a chance to initialize it apartment-threaded, which
    // would add a high overhead to calls across threads. If another component already chose a model, keep it.
    (void)CoInitializeEx(0, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
#endif

    // Without this, SDL turns SIGINT and SIGTERM into quit events that nothing handles.
    SDL_SetHint(SDL_HINT_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS, "1");

    if (!SDL_Init(SDL_INIT_GAMEPAD)) {
        dbgln("Failed to initialize SDL3: {}", SDL_GetError());
        return false;
    }

    m_sdl_initialized = true;
    return true;
}

void SDLGamepadSource::set_polling(bool polling)
{
    // Tests look at their gamepads when they ask.
    if (!polling || !m_sdl_initialized || m_ignore_system_gamepads == IgnoreSystemGamepads::Yes) {
        if (m_poll_timer)
            m_poll_timer->stop();
        return;
    }

    if (!m_poll_timer)
        m_poll_timer = Core::Timer::create_repeating(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GAMEPAD_POLL_INTERVAL_MS), [this] { poll(); });
    m_poll_timer->start();
}

void SDLGamepadSource::poll()
{
    if (!m_sdl_initialized)
        return;

    SDL_Event event;
    while (SDL_PollEvent(&event))
        handle_sdl_event(event);

    Vector<Web::Gamepad::GamepadState> changed_states;
    for (auto& entry : m_devices) {
        auto& device = *entry.value;
        if (!device.connected)
            continue;
        // Compare freshly read state, since SDL suppresses some input events, such as a guide button release shortly
        // after its press.
        read_current_state(device, m_scratch_state);
        if (m_scratch_state == device.last_state)
            continue;
        device.last_state = m_scratch_state;
        changed_states.append(device.last_state);
    }

    if (on_gamepad_states_changed)
        on_gamepad_states_changed(move(changed_states));
}

void SDLGamepadSource::handle_sdl_event(SDL_Event const& event)
{
    switch (event.type) {
    case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_ADDED:
        device_connected(event.gdevice.which);
        break;
    case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_REMOVED:
        device_disconnected(event.gdevice.which);
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
}

void SDLGamepadSource::device_connected(u32 sdl_joystick_id)
{
    auto* device = device_for_sdl_joystick_id(sdl_joystick_id);

    if (!device) {
        if (m_ignore_system_gamepads == IgnoreSystemGamepads::Yes)
            return;

        auto* sdl_gamepad = SDL_OpenGamepad(sdl_joystick_id);
        if (!sdl_gamepad) {
            dbgln("Failed to open gamepad: {}", SDL_GetError());
            return;
        }

        auto handle = m_next_handle++;
        auto new_device = make<Device>();
        new_device->sdl_joystick_id = sdl_joystick_id;
        new_device->sdl_gamepad = sdl_gamepad;
        new_device->description = build_description(handle, sdl_joystick_id, sdl_gamepad);
        device = new_device.ptr();
        m_devices.set(handle, move(new_device));
    }

    if (device->connected)
        return;
    read_current_state(*device, device->last_state);
    device->connected = true;
    if (on_gamepad_connected)
        on_gamepad_connected(device->description, device->last_state);
}

void SDLGamepadSource::device_disconnected(u32 sdl_joystick_id)
{
    auto* device = device_for_sdl_joystick_id(sdl_joystick_id);
    if (!device)
        return;
    auto handle = device->description.handle;
    remove_device(handle);
    if (on_gamepad_disconnected)
        on_gamepad_disconnected(handle);
}

void SDLGamepadSource::remove_device(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle)
{
    auto removed_device = m_devices.take(handle);
    if (!removed_device.has_value())
        return;
    auto& device = **removed_device;

    SDL_CloseGamepad(device.sdl_gamepad);
    if (device.virtual_sdl_joystick) {
        SDL_CloseJoystick(device.virtual_sdl_joystick);
        SDL_DetachVirtualJoystick(device.sdl_joystick_id);
    }
}

void SDLGamepadSource::rumble(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle, u16 low_frequency_magnitude, u16 high_frequency_magnitude, u32 duration_ms)
{
    // https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_RumbleGamepad
    // "Each call to this function cancels any previous rumble effect, and calling it with 0 intensity stops any
    // rumbling."
    if (auto device = m_devices.get(handle); device.has_value())
        SDL_RumbleGamepad((*device)->sdl_gamepad, low_frequency_magnitude, high_frequency_magnitude, duration_ms);
}

void SDLGamepadSource::rumble_triggers(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle, u16 left_magnitude, u16 right_magnitude, u32 duration_ms)
{
    // https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_RumbleGamepadTriggers
    // "Each call to this function cancels any previous trigger rumble effect, and calling it with 0 intensity stops
    // any rumbling."
    if (auto device = m_devices.get(handle); device.has_value())
        SDL_RumbleGamepadTriggers((*device)->sdl_gamepad, left_magnitude, right_magnitude, duration_ms);
}

Optional<Web::Gamepad::VirtualGamepad> SDLGamepadSource::create_virtual_gamepad()
{
    if (!start())
        return {};

    auto device = make<Device>();

    Vector<i32> buttons;
    Vector<i32> triggers;
    for (auto const& standard_gamepad_button : standard_gamepad_button_layout) {
        standard_gamepad_button.visit(
            [&](SDL_GamepadButton button) { buttons.append(button); },
            [&](SDL_GamepadAxis axis) { triggers.append(axis); });
    }

    Vector<i32> axes;
    for (auto const standard_gamepad_axis : standard_gamepad_axes_layout)
        axes.append(standard_gamepad_axis);

    SDL_VirtualJoystickDesc virtual_joystick_desc {};
    SDL_INIT_INTERFACE(&virtual_joystick_desc);

    virtual_joystick_desc.type = SDL_JOYSTICK_TYPE_GAMEPAD;
    virtual_joystick_desc.naxes = axes.size() + triggers.size();
    virtual_joystick_desc.nbuttons = buttons.size();

    u32 button_mask = 0;
    for (auto const button : buttons)
        button_mask |= 1 << button;

    virtual_joystick_desc.button_mask = button_mask;

    u32 axis_mask = 0;
    for (auto const axis : axes)
        axis_mask |= 1 << axis;

    for (auto const trigger : triggers)
        axis_mask |= 1 << trigger;

    virtual_joystick_desc.axis_mask = axis_mask;

    virtual_joystick_desc.name = VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD_NAME;
    virtual_joystick_desc.userdata = device.ptr();
    virtual_joystick_desc.Rumble = record_received_dual_rumble_effect;
    virtual_joystick_desc.RumbleTriggers = record_received_trigger_rumble_effect;

    auto sdl_joystick_id = SDL_AttachVirtualJoystick(&virtual_joystick_desc);
    if (sdl_joystick_id == 0) {
        dbgln("Failed to attach virtual joystick: {}", SDL_GetError());
        return {};
    }

    auto* sdl_joystick = SDL_OpenJoystick(sdl_joystick_id);
    auto* sdl_gamepad = SDL_OpenGamepad(sdl_joystick_id);
    if (!sdl_joystick || !sdl_gamepad) {
        dbgln("Failed to open virtual gamepad: {}", SDL_GetError());
        if (sdl_gamepad)
            SDL_CloseGamepad(sdl_gamepad);
        if (sdl_joystick)
            SDL_CloseJoystick(sdl_joystick);
        SDL_DetachVirtualJoystick(sdl_joystick_id);
        return {};
    }

    auto handle = m_next_handle++;
    device->sdl_joystick_id = sdl_joystick_id;
    device->sdl_gamepad = sdl_gamepad;
    device->description = build_description(handle, sdl_joystick_id, sdl_gamepad);
    device->virtual_sdl_joystick = sdl_joystick;
    m_devices.set(handle, move(device));

    return Web::Gamepad::VirtualGamepad { handle, move(buttons), move(axes), move(triggers) };
}

void SDLGamepadSource::set_virtual_gamepad_button(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle, i32 button, bool down)
{
    auto* device = virtual_device(handle);
    if (!device)
        return;
    SDL_SetJoystickVirtualButton(device->virtual_sdl_joystick, button, down);
    poll();
}

void SDLGamepadSource::set_virtual_gamepad_axis(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle, i32 axis, i16 value)
{
    auto* device = virtual_device(handle);
    if (!device)
        return;
    SDL_SetJoystickVirtualAxis(device->virtual_sdl_joystick, axis, value);
    poll();
}

void SDLGamepadSource::disconnect_virtual_gamepad(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle)
{
    if (virtual_device(handle))
        remove_device(handle);
}

Vector<Web::Gamepad::ReceivedDualRumbleEffect> SDLGamepadSource::virtual_gamepad_received_rumble_effects(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle)
{
    if (auto* device = virtual_device(handle))
        return device->received_dual_rumble_effects;
    return {};
}

Vector<Web::Gamepad::ReceivedTriggerRumbleEffect> SDLGamepadSource::virtual_gamepad_received_trigger_rumble_effects(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle)
{
    if (auto* device = virtual_device(handle))
        return device->received_trigger_rumble_effects;
    return {};
}

SDLGamepadSource::Device* SDLGamepadSource::device_for_sdl_joystick_id(u32 sdl_joystick_id)
{
    for (auto& entry : m_devices) {
        if (entry.value->sdl_joystick_id == sdl_joystick_id)
            return entry.value.ptr();
    }
    return nullptr;
}

SDLGamepadSource::Device* SDLGamepadSource::virtual_device(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle)
{
    auto device = m_devices.get(handle);
    if (!device.has_value() || !(*device)->virtual_sdl_joystick)
        return nullptr;
    return *device;
}

Web::Gamepad::GamepadDescription SDLGamepadSource::build_description(Web::Gamepad::GamepadHandle handle, u32 sdl_joystick_id, SDL_Gamepad* sdl_gamepad) const
{
    Web::Gamepad::GamepadDescription description;
    description.handle = handle;

    if (auto const* name = SDL_GetGamepadNameForID(sdl_joystick_id))
        description.id = String::from_utf8_with_replacement_character(StringView { name, strlen(name) });

    SDL_PropertiesID sdl_gamepad_properties = SDL_GetGamepadProperties(sdl_gamepad);
    description.supports_dual_rumble = SDL_GetBooleanProperty(sdl_gamepad_properties, SDL_PROP_GAMEPAD_CAP_RUMBLE_BOOLEAN, /* default_value= */ false);
    description.supports_trigger_rumble = SDL_GetBooleanProperty(sdl_gamepad_properties, SDL_PROP_GAMEPAD_CAP_TRIGGER_RUMBLE_BOOLEAN, /* default_value= */ false);

    bool has_standard_mapping = true;

    for (size_t canonical_index = 0; canonical_index < standard_gamepad_button_layout.size(); ++canonical_index) {
        bool has_input = standard_gamepad_button_layout[canonical_index].visit(
            [&](SDL_GamepadButton button) {
                return SDL_GamepadHasButton(sdl_gamepad, button);
            },
            [&](SDL_GamepadAxis axis) {
                return SDL_GamepadHasAxis(sdl_gamepad, axis);
            });

        if (!has_input) {
            has_standard_mapping = false;
            continue;
        }

        bool is_digital = standard_gamepad_button_layout[canonical_index].has<SDL_GamepadButton>();
        description.buttons.append({
            .canonical_index = static_cast<u32>(canonical_index),
            .logical_minimum = 0,
            // Buttons are binary inputs with SDL.
            // "Trigger axis values range from 0 (released) to SDL_JOYSTICK_AXIS_MAX (fully pressed) when reported by
            // SDL_GetGamepadAxis(). Note that this is not the same range that will be reported by the lower-level
            // SDL_GetJoystickAxis()."
            .logical_maximum = is_digital ? i16(1) : i16(SDL_JOYSTICK_AXIS_MAX),
        });
    }

    for (auto const non_standard_gamepad_button : non_standard_gamepad_button_layout) {
        if (!SDL_GamepadHasButton(sdl_gamepad, non_standard_gamepad_button))
            continue;
        description.buttons.append({
            .canonical_index = {},
            .logical_minimum = 0,
            .logical_maximum = 1,
        });
    }

    for (size_t canonical_index = 0; canonical_index < standard_gamepad_axes_layout.size(); ++canonical_index) {
        if (!SDL_GamepadHasAxis(sdl_gamepad, standard_gamepad_axes_layout[canonical_index])) {
            has_standard_mapping = false;
            continue;
        }
        description.axes.append({
            .canonical_index = static_cast<u32>(canonical_index),
            .logical_minimum = SDL_JOYSTICK_AXIS_MIN,
            .logical_maximum = SDL_JOYSTICK_AXIS_MAX,
        });
    }

    description.has_standard_mapping = has_standard_mapping;
    return description;
}

void SDLGamepadSource::read_current_state(Device const& device, Web::Gamepad::GamepadState& state) const
{
    state.handle = device.description.handle;
    state.axis_values.clear_with_capacity();
    state.button_values.clear_with_capacity();

    for (auto const standard_gamepad_axis : standard_gamepad_axes_layout) {
        if (SDL_GamepadHasAxis(device.sdl_gamepad, standard_gamepad_axis))
            state.axis_values.append(SDL_GetGamepadAxis(device.sdl_gamepad, standard_gamepad_axis));
    }

    for (auto const& standard_gamepad_button : standard_gamepad_button_layout) {
        standard_gamepad_button.visit(
            [&](SDL_GamepadButton button) {
                if (SDL_GamepadHasButton(device.sdl_gamepad, button))
                    state.button_values.append(SDL_GetGamepadButton(device.sdl_gamepad, button) ? 1 : 0);
            },
            [&](SDL_GamepadAxis axis) {
                if (SDL_GamepadHasAxis(device.sdl_gamepad, axis))
                    state.button_values.append(SDL_GetGamepadAxis(device.sdl_gamepad, axis));
            });
    }

    for (auto const non_standard_gamepad_button : non_standard_gamepad_button_layout) {
        if (SDL_GamepadHasButton(device.sdl_gamepad, non_standard_gamepad_button))
            state.button_values.append(SDL_GetGamepadButton(device.sdl_gamepad, non_standard_gamepad_button) ? 1 : 0);
    }
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/BlockAllocator.cpp
/*

 * Copyright (c) 2025, Ryszard Goc <ryszardgoc@gmail.com>

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#include <AK/Assertions.h>
#include <AK/Checked.h>
#include <AK/Mutex.h>
#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <AK/Try.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapRegion.h>

extern "C" {
GC_API FlatPtr js_heap_region_base = 0;
}

namespace GC {

static_assert(FFI::CHUNK_SIZE % HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE == 0);
static_assert(HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE % FFI::CHUNK_SIZE == 0);
static_assert(HEAP_REGION_HIGH_GUARD_SIZE % FFI::CHUNK_SIZE == 0);

// Every block of every heap is in one process-wide region, which this reserves at an address aligned to its size, so
// that a cell's offset in the region is its address modulo the region's size. LibGC's Rust core commits the region's
// chunks and hands out its blocks, see block_pool.rs.
class HeapRegion {
public:
    static constexpr size_t size = HEAP_REGION_SIZE;

    HeapRegion()
    {
        static_assert(sizeof(FlatPtr) >= sizeof(u64));
        Checked<size_t> reservation_size = size;
        reservation_size += size;
        VERIFY(!reservation_size.has_overflow());

        auto* reservation = MUST(Core::System::reserve_address_space(reservation_size.value(), Core::System::MemoryTag::GarbageCollector));
        auto reservation_start = reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(reservation);
        auto aligned_start = align_up_to(reservation_start, size);
        auto reservation_end = reservation_start + reservation_size.value();
        auto head_size = aligned_start - reservation_start;
        auto tail_size = reservation_end - (aligned_start + size);

#if !defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
        if (head_size != 0)
            MUST(Core::System::release_address_space(reservation, head_size));
        if (tail_size != 0)
            MUST(Core::System::release_address_space(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned_start + size), tail_size));
#else
        // VirtualFree with MEM_RELEASE can only release the complete
        // reservation, so keep the inaccessible head and tail on Windows.
        (void)head_size;
        (void)tail_size;
#endif

        m_base = aligned_start;
        VERIFY(m_base % size == 0);
        // NB: The guards at either end of the region are never committed.
        FFI::rust_gc_heap_region_init(reinterpret_cast<u8*>(m_base), HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE, size - HEAP_REGION_HIGH_GUARD_SIZE - FFI::CHUNK_SIZE);
        publish_base(m_base);
    }

    static void register_base_copy(HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration& registration)
    {
        MutexLocker locker(base_copies_mutex());
        registration.m_next = exchange(s_base_copies, &registration);
        if (js_heap_region_base)
            *registration.m_copy = js_heap_region_base;
    }

    FlatPtr start() const { return m_base; }
    FlatPtr end() const { return start() + size; }

private:
    static void publish_base(FlatPtr base)
    {
        MutexLocker locker(base_copies_mutex());
        js_heap_region_base = base;
        for (auto* registration = s_base_copies; registration; registration = registration->m_next)
            *registration->m_copy = base;
    }

    // NB: Static initialization registers copies, possibly before that of this file has run, so the list starts out
    //     constant-initialized and its mutex is set up on first use.
    static Mutex& base_copies_mutex()
    {
        static AK::NeverDestroyed<Mutex> mutex;
        return *mutex;
    }

    static constinit inline HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration* s_base_copies { nullptr };

    FlatPtr m_base { 0 };
};

static HeapRegion& heap_region()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<HeapRegion> region;
    return *region;
}

void BlockAllocator::wake_decommit_worker_async()
{
    FFI::rust_gc_wake_decommit_worker();
}

#pragma once

#include <AK/Badge.h>
#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>

namespace GC::FFI {

struct BlockPool;

}

namespace GC {

enum class DeferDecommit {
    No,
    Yes,
};

// The blocks of one type of cell in all heaps, see CellAllocatorDescriptorBase::block_allocator(). The pool itself, the
// heap region's chunks and the thread that gives the pages of freed blocks back to the system are LibGC's Rust core.
class GC_API BlockAllocator {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(BlockAllocator);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(BlockAllocator);

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    BlockAllocator();
    ~BlockAllocator();

    void* allocate_block(char const* name);
    void deallocate_block(void*, DeferDecommit = DeferDecommit::Yes);

    size_t block_count();

    // How many blocks are back in the pool after their pages went back to the system. Tests wait on it.
    size_t returned_block_count_for_testing();

    // Gives the pages of the free blocks back to the system right away, rather than leaving them for the system to take
    // when it runs short of memory. For a heap that went away, whose blocks may never be reused.
    void return_freed_blocks_to_system();

    static FlatPtr heap_region_start();
    static FlatPtr heap_region_end();
    // The end of the part of the region that chunks have been committed from so far. No block starts at or above it.
    static FlatPtr heap_region_committed_end();

    // Wake the global decommit worker so it processes any deferred madvise
    // work that's piled up. Call this at the end of a GC sweep.
    static void wake_decommit_worker_async();

    // How long a block can sit unused before its pages go back to the system. Tests make it short to see this happen.
    // Returns the age it replaces.
    static AK::Duration set_cold_block_age_for_testing(AK::Duration);

    FFI::BlockPool const* rust_pool(Badge<CellAllocator>) const { return m_pool; }

private:
    FFI::BlockPool const* m_pool { nullptr };
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/BitCast.h>
#include <AK/BuiltinWrappers.h>
#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapRegion.h>
#include <LibGC/Internals.h>
#include <RustFFI.h>

// NB: Only LibGC's own sources include this, since RustFFI.h is generated in its build directory.

namespace GC {

static_assert(FFI::BLOCK_SIZE == HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE);

// What the heap knows about each block lives in the block's descriptor, outside the heap region, so that nothing in a
// block can change it: the heap and the type of the block, and the mark bits of its cells. The descriptor of a block
// is at the index of the block in the region, in a table that LibGC's Rust core reserves once.
extern GC_API FFI::BlockDescriptor* const g_block_descriptors;

ALWAYS_INLINE FFI::BlockDescriptor& block_descriptor_for(void const* address)
{
    return g_block_descriptors[(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(address) - heap_region_base()) / HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE];
}

// A cell's bit in the bitmaps of its block's descriptor is its offset in its block divided by the cell size, which
// tells the cells apart since they are a cell size apart.
// OPTIMIZATION: Dividing by the cell size is slow, so the offset is multiplied by 2^32 / cell size, rounded up, and
//               shifted right by 32. For offsets and cell sizes up to 2^14, the rounding error never reaches the next
//               whole number.
ALWAYS_INLINE size_t cell_index(FFI::BlockDescriptor const& descriptor, void const* cell)
{
    auto offset = static_cast<u64>(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(cell) & (HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE - 1));
    return static_cast<size_t>((offset * descriptor.cell_index_magic) >> 32);
}

ALWAYS_INLINE u64 cell_bit(size_t index) { return static_cast<u64>(1) << (index % 64); }

// Marking sets mark bits from several threads at once, so every access is atomic. Outside of marking, nothing else
// writes them, so relaxed accesses are enough.
ALWAYS_INLINE bool is_marked(FFI::BlockDescriptor const& descriptor, void const* cell)
{
    auto index = cell_index(descriptor, cell);
    return __atomic_load_n(&descriptor.marked[index / 64], __ATOMIC_RELAXED) & cell_bit(index);
}

ALWAYS_INLINE bool is_marked(void const* cell)
{
    return is_marked(block_descriptor_for(cell), cell);
}

ALWAYS_INLINE void set_marked(void const* cell)
{
    auto& descriptor = block_descriptor_for(cell);
    auto index = cell_index(descriptor, cell);
    __atomic_fetch_or(&descriptor.marked[index / 64], cell_bit(index), __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}

// A cell is allocated from when it is handed out until the sweep or a move frees its slot. While an allocator has taken
// a run of free cells of a block to hand them out, they all count as allocated, see CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells. Only
// the thread that owns the block's heap reads and writes these bits.
ALWAYS_INLINE bool is_allocated(FFI::BlockDescriptor const& descriptor, size_t index)
{
    return descriptor.allocated[index / 64] & cell_bit(index);
}

ALWAYS_INLINE u32 allocated_cell_count_of(FFI::BlockDescriptor const& descriptor)
{
    u32 count = 0;
    for (auto word : descriptor.allocated)
        count += popcount(word);
    return count;
}

// The cell that `address` points into, if it is an allocated cell of a block of `heap`. The address must be within the
// committed part of the heap region, where every block has a descriptor.
ALWAYS_INLINE void* allocated_cell_containing(void const* heap, FlatPtr address, size_t cells_offset)
{
    auto const& descriptor = block_descriptor_for(bit_cast<void const*>(address));
    if (__atomic_load_n(&descriptor.heap, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != heap)
        return nullptr;
    auto block = address & ~(HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE - 1);
    if (address - block < cells_offset)
        return nullptr;
    auto offset_in_cells = static_cast<u64>(address - block - cells_offset);
    auto index = static_cast<size_t>((offset_in_cells * descriptor.cell_index_magic) >> 32);
    if (index >= descriptor.cell_count)
        return nullptr;
    auto cell = block + cells_offset + index * descriptor.cell_size;
    if (!is_allocated(descriptor, cell_index(descriptor, bit_cast<void const*>(cell))))
        return nullptr;
    return bit_cast<void*>(cell);
}

}

static_assert(sizeof(GCCellTypeInfo) == sizeof(CellTypeInfo));
static_assert(alignof(GCCellTypeInfo) == alignof(CellTypeInfo));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, cell_size) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, cell_size));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, alignment) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, alignment));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, kind) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, kind));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, visit_edges) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, visit_edges));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, finalize) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, finalize));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, destroy) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, destroy));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, external_memory_size) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, external_memory_size));
static_assert(offsetof(GCCellTypeInfo, class_name) == offsetof(CellTypeInfo, class_name));
static_assert(sizeof(CellKind) == sizeof(uint8_t));

static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_OTHER == to_underlying(CellKind::Other));
static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_OBJECT == to_underlying(CellKind::Object));
static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_PRIMITIVE_STRING == to_underlying(CellKind::PrimitiveString));
static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_SYMBOL == to_underlying(CellKind::Symbol));
static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_BIGINT == to_underlying(CellKind::BigInt));
static_assert(GC_CELL_KIND_ACCESSOR == to_underlying(CellKind::Accessor));

static_assert(GC_CELL_STATE_LIVE == to_underlying(Cell::State::Live));
static_assert(GC_CELL_STATE_DEAD == to_underlying(Cell::State::Dead));

static_assert(sizeof(NanBoxedValue) == sizeof(uint64_t));

static_assert(IsSame<decltype(PrimitiveStorageHandle::index), u32>);
static_assert(IsSame<decltype(PrimitiveStorageHandle::generation), u32>);
static_assert(GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_INVALID_OFFSET == PrimitiveStorage::invalid_offset);

static constexpr GCPrimitiveStorageHandle encode_primitive_storage_handle(PrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return (static_cast<u64>(handle.generation) << GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_HANDLE_GENERATION_SHIFT) | handle.index;
}

static constexpr PrimitiveStorageHandle decode_primitive_storage_handle(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return {
        .index = static_cast<u32>(handle),
        .generation = static_cast<u32>(handle >> GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_HANDLE_GENERATION_SHIFT),
    };
}

static_assert(encode_primitive_storage_handle({ .index = 0x01234567, .generation = 0x89abcdef }) == 0x89abcdef01234567);
static_assert(decode_primitive_storage_handle(0x89abcdef01234567).index == 0x01234567);
static_assert(decode_primitive_storage_handle(0x89abcdef01234567).generation == 0x89abcdef);
static_assert(decode_primitive_storage_handle(GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE).generation == 0);

class CAPICellAllocator final : public CellAllocatorDescriptorBase {
public:
    CAPICellAllocator(CellTypeInfo const& type_info, StringView class_name, void const* foreign_type)
        : CellAllocatorDescriptorBase(type_info, class_name, foreign_type)
    {
        set_trace_thread(TraceThread::AnyThread);
    }

    ~CAPICellAllocator()
    {
        // NB: The address of a descriptor without a foreign type names the type of its blocks, so it may never be reused.
        VERIFY(foreign_type());
        release_index();
    }
};

struct CAPI {
    static_assert(offsetof(ForeignCell, m_word_owned_by_the_foreign_implementation) == 0);
    static_assert(offsetof(ForeignCell, m_identity_hash_state) == offsetof(Cell, m_identity_hash_state));
    static_assert(offsetof(ForeignCell, m_state) == offsetof(Cell, m_state));
    static_assert(offsetof(ForeignCell, m_cell_kind) == offsetof(Cell, m_cell_kind));
    static_assert(offsetof(Cell, m_identity_hash_state) == IdentityHashState::offset);
    static_assert(IdentityHashState::offset == FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET);
    static_assert(IdentityHashState::hashed == FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED);
    static_assert(IdentityHashState::moved == FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED);

    static void get_layout(GCLayout& layout)
    {
        layout = {
            .cell_state_offset = offsetof(Cell, m_state),
            .cell_kind_offset = offsetof(Cell, m_cell_kind),
            .min_cell_size = HeapBlock::min_possible_cell_size,
            .max_cell_size = HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE - sizeof(HeapBlock),
            .max_cell_alignment = max_cell_alignment,
            .cell_type_info_size = sizeof(CellTypeInfo),
            .weak_impl_pointer_offset = WeakImpl::value_offset(),
            .free_cell_next_offset = HeapBlock::freelist_next_offset(),
            .free_cell_link_mask = HeapBlock::freelist_link_mask,
            .local_cursor_offset = offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, cursor),
            .local_end_offset = offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, end),
            .local_cell_size_offset = offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, cell_size),
            .heap_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc_offset = offsetof(Heap, m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc),
            .heap_gc_bytes_threshold_offset = offsetof(Heap, m_gc_bytes_threshold),
            .heap_total_allocated_bytes_offset = offsetof(Heap, m_total_allocated_bytes),
            .block_size = HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE,
            .block_foreign_type_offset = offsetof(HeapBlockBase, m_foreign_type),
            .heap_region_offset_mask = HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK,
            .primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask = PrimitiveStorage::cage_offset_mask,
            .visitor_marker_offset = static_cast<uint32_t>(Cell::Visitor::marker_offset()),
            .identity_hash_state_offset = FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET,
            .identity_hash_hashed = FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED,
            .identity_hash_moved = FFI::IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED,
        };
    }

    static Cell* allocate_cell(Heap& heap, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor)
    {
        auto* cell = heap.allocate_cell(descriptor);
        heap.mark_if_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(*cell);
        return cell;
    }

    static Cell* allocate_storage_cell(Heap& heap, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor)
    {
        auto* cell = heap.allocate_cell(descriptor, Heap::TriggersCollection::No);
        heap.mark_if_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(*cell);
        return cell;
    }

    static_assert(sizeof(Heap::m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc) == sizeof(size_t));
    static_assert(sizeof(Heap::m_gc_bytes_threshold) == sizeof(size_t));
    static_assert(sizeof(Heap::m_total_allocated_bytes) == sizeof(size_t));

    // Foreign code reads and writes the head of the list, the cursor and the end as plain pointers.
    static_assert(sizeof(Ptr<Cell>) == sizeof(Cell*));
    static_assert(offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, free_list) == 0);
    static_assert(sizeof(FlatPtr) == sizeof(void*));
    static CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells* local_free_cells(Heap& heap, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor) { return heap.cell_allocator_for(descriptor).local_free_cells({}); }
    static void set_foreign_context(Heap& heap, void* context) { heap.m_foreign_context = context; }
    static void* foreign_context(Heap& heap) { return heap.m_foreign_context; }
    static void defer_gc(Heap& heap) { heap.defer_gc(); }
    static void undefer_gc(Heap& heap) { heap.undefer_gc(); }
    static void deferral_state(Heap& heap, size_t*& deferrals, bool*& collect_when_deferrals_end)
    {
        deferrals = &heap.m_gc_deferrals;
        collect_when_deferrals_end = &heap.m_should_gc_when_deferral_ends;
    }
    static StackInfo const& stack_info(Heap const& heap) { return heap.m_stack_info; }
    static FFI::IdentityHashes** identity_hashes(Heap& heap) { return &heap.m_identity_hashes; }
    static bool will_move(Cell const& cell)
    {
        auto* evacuation = cell.heap().m_evacuation;
        return evacuation && FFI::rust_gc_evacuation_will_move(evacuation, &cell);
    }
    static void record_slot(Heap& heap, void const* slot, FFI::RecordedSlotKind kind)
    {
        if (heap.m_evacuation)
            FFI::rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot(heap.m_evacuation, slot, kind);
    }
};

}

using namespace GC;

static Heap& as_heap(GCHeap* heap) { return *reinterpret_cast<Heap*>(heap); }
static Heap const& as_heap(GCHeap const* heap) { return *reinterpret_cast<Heap const*>(heap); }
static Cell* from_gc_cell(GCCell* cell) { return reinterpret_cast<Cell*>(cell); }
static GCCell* as_gc_cell(Cell* cell) { return reinterpret_cast<GCCell*>(cell); }
static Cell::Visitor& as_visitor(GCVisitor* visitor) { return *reinterpret_cast<Cell::Visitor*>(visitor); }
static WeakImpl* as_weak_impl(GCWeakImpl* impl) { return reinterpret_cast<WeakImpl*>(impl); }
static GCWeakImpl* as_gc_weak_impl(WeakImpl* impl) { return reinterpret_cast<GCWeakImpl*>(impl); }
static PrimitiveStorage::ZeroFillNewBytes as_zero_fill_new_bytes(bool zero_fill) { return zero_fill ? PrimitiveStorage::ZeroFillNewBytes::Yes : PrimitiveStorage::ZeroFillNewBytes::No; }

static void store_primitive_storage_layout(PrimitiveStorage const& storage, PrimitiveStorageHandle handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    if (!out_layout)
        return;
    auto layout = storage.layout(handle);
    *out_layout = { .offset = layout.offset, .size = layout.size, .capacity = layout.capacity };
}

static bool store_created_primitive_storage(PrimitiveStorage const& storage, ErrorOr<PrimitiveStorageHandle> handle_or_error, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle* out_handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    if (handle_or_error.is_error()) {
        *out_handle = GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE;
        return false;
    }
    *out_handle = encode_primitive_storage_handle(handle_or_error.value());
    store_primitive_storage_layout(storage, handle_or_error.value(), out_layout);
    return true;
}

static bool store_resized_primitive_storage(PrimitiveStorage const& storage, ErrorOr<void> result, PrimitiveStorageHandle handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    if (result.is_error())
        return false;
    store_primitive_storage_layout(storage, handle, out_layout);
    return true;
}

GCHeap* gc_heap_create(GCGatherRootsCallback gather_roots, void* context, bool become_thread_default)
{
    auto* heap = new Heap(
        [gather_roots, context](HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot>& roots) {
            Detail::RootGatheringVisitor visitor { roots, HeapRoot::Type::VM };
            gather_roots(context, reinterpret_cast<GCVisitor*>(static_cast<Cell::Visitor*>(&visitor)));
        },
        become_thread_default ? Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::Yes : Heap::BecomeThreadDefault::No);
    CAPI::set_foreign_context(*heap, context);
    return reinterpret_cast<GCHeap*>(heap);
}

void gc_heap_destroy(GCHeap* heap)
{
    delete &as_heap(heap);
}

void gc_heap_collect_garbage(GCHeap* heap, int collection_type, bool print_report)

    VERIFY(collection_type == GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_GARBAGE || collection_type == GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_EVERYTHING);
    auto type = collection_type == GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_EVERYTHING ? Heap::CollectionType::CollectEverything : Heap::CollectionType::CollectGarbage;
    as_heap(heap).collect_garbage(type, print_report);
}

GCAllocator* gc_allocator_create(GCCellTypeInfo const* type_info, char const* name, size_t name_length, void const* foreign_type)
{
    VERIFY(type_info->visit_edges);
    VERIFY(type_info->cell_size >= HeapBlock::min_possible_cell_size);
    VERIFY(type_info->cell_size <= HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE - sizeof(HeapBlock));
    VERIFY(type_info->alignment <= max_cell_alignment);
    VERIFY(type_info->cell_size % type_info->alignment == 0);
    auto* allocator = new CAPICellAllocator(*reinterpret_cast<CellTypeInfo const*>(type_info), StringView { name, name_length }, foreign_type);
    return reinterpret_cast<GCAllocator*>(allocator);
}

void gc_allocator_destroy(GCAllocator* allocator)
{
    delete reinterpret_cast<CAPICellAllocator*>(allocator);
}

    reinterpret_cast<CAPICellAllocator*>(allocator)->set_movable();
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_allocate(size_t size, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle* out_handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    auto& storage = PrimitiveStorage::the();
    return store_created_primitive_storage(storage, storage.try_allocate(size, as_zero_fill_new_bytes(zero_fill)), out_handle, out_layout);
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_reserve(size_t size, size_t capacity, bool zero_fill, size_t guard_size, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle* out_handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    auto& storage = PrimitiveStorage::the();
    return store_created_primitive_storage(storage, storage.try_reserve(size, capacity, as_zero_fill_new_bytes(zero_fill), guard_size), out_handle, out_layout);
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_resize(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle, size_t new_size, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    auto& storage = PrimitiveStorage::the();
    auto decoded_handle = decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle);
    return store_resized_primitive_storage(storage, storage.try_resize(decoded_handle, new_size, as_zero_fill_new_bytes(zero_fill)), decoded_handle, out_layout);
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_reserve_capacity(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle, size_t new_capacity, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    auto& storage = PrimitiveStorage::the();
    auto decoded_handle = decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle);
    return store_resized_primitive_storage(storage, storage.try_reserve(decoded_handle, new_capacity), decoded_handle, out_layout);
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_resize_and_reserve(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle, size_t new_size, size_t new_capacity, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout)
{
    auto& storage = PrimitiveStorage::the();
    auto decoded_handle = decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle);
    return store_resized_primitive_storage(storage, storage.try_resize_and_reserve(decoded_handle, new_size, new_capacity, as_zero_fill_new_bytes(zero_fill)), decoded_handle, out_layout);
}

void gc_primitive_storage_free(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    PrimitiveStorage::the().free(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

bool gc_primitive_storage_is_valid(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().is_valid(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

size_t gc_primitive_storage_offset(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().offset(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

size_t gc_primitive_storage_size(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().size(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

size_t gc_primitive_storage_capacity(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().capacity(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

size_t gc_primitive_storage_committed_size(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().committed_size(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}

uint8_t* gc_primitive_storage_data(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle handle)
{
    return PrimitiveStorage::the().data(decode_primitive_storage_handle(handle));
}
}

#pragma once

#include <LibGC/Export.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

// A C interface to LibGC for cell types that are defined outside of C++.
//
// A foreign cell type describes itself with a GCCellTypeInfo, which LibGC dispatches through exactly as it does for
// C++ cells. The foreign side owns the whole cell: gc_heap_allocate_cell() hands out uninitialized storage, and the
// caller writes every byte of the cell, including the header fields at the offsets reported by gc_get_layout(),
// before anything that can collect garbage runs: another allocation, external memory accounting, undeferring,
// an explicit collection, or a return to the event loop.
//
// The first word of a cell, which holds the vtable pointer of a C++ cell, belongs to the foreign side. LibGC never
// reads it, but -fsanitize=vptr instrumentation of LibGC does, so that sanitizer cannot be used with foreign cells.
//
// Like the rest of LibGC, every heap in a process must be used from the same thread.

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct GCHeap GCHeap;
typedef struct GCCell GCCell;
typedef struct GCVisitor GCVisitor;
typedef struct GCAllocator GCAllocator;
typedef struct GCRoot GCRoot;
typedef struct GCWeakImpl GCWeakImpl;

typedef void (*GCCallback)(void* context);

// Called whenever the heap gathers its roots. Every cell passed to root_visitor is kept alive by this collection.
// root_visitor only accepts cells and values, not possible values, and the callback must not allocate.
typedef void (*GCGatherRootsCallback)(void* context, GCVisitor* root_visitor);

enum {
    GC_CELL_KIND_OTHER = 0,
    GC_CELL_KIND_OBJECT = 1,
    GC_CELL_KIND_PRIMITIVE_STRING = 2,
    GC_CELL_KIND_SYMBOL = 3,
    GC_CELL_KIND_BIGINT = 4,
    GC_CELL_KIND_ACCESSOR = 5,
};

enum {
    GC_CELL_STATE_LIVE = 0,
    GC_CELL_STATE_DEAD = 1,
};

enum {
    GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_GARBAGE = 0,
    GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_EVERYTHING = 1,
};

// Mirrors GC::CellTypeInfo. visit_edges is required; every other function may be null.
typedef struct GCCellTypeInfo {
    uint32_t cell_size;
    uint32_t alignment;
    uint8_t kind;
    void (*visit_edges)(GCCell*, GCVisitor*);
    void (*finalize)(GCCell*);
    void (*destroy)(GCCell*);
    size_t (*external_memory_size)(GCCell const*);
    char const* (*class_name)(GCCell const*, size_t* length);
} GCCellTypeInfo;

// Everything a foreign implementation of cells needs to agree on with this build of LibGC.
typedef struct GCLayout {
    uint32_t cell_state_offset;
    uint32_t cell_kind_offset;
    uint32_t min_cell_size;
    uint32_t max_cell_size;
    uint32_t max_cell_alignment;
    uint32_t cell_type_info_size;
    uint32_t weak_impl_pointer_offset;
    // For code that allocates cells from local free lists itself, see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list().
    uint32_t free_cell_next_offset;
    uint32_t free_cell_link_mask;
    // Where the cursor, the end and the cell size of the cells an allocator bumps through are, relative to the head
    // of its local free list (see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list()).
    uint32_t local_cursor_offset;
    uint32_t local_end_offset;
    uint32_t local_cell_size_offset;
    uint32_t heap_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc_offset;
    uint32_t heap_gc_bytes_threshold_offset;
    uint32_t heap_total_allocated_bytes_offset;
    // A cell's block starts at the cell's address rounded down to a multiple of block_size, and holds the foreign
    // type the cell's allocator was created with at block_foreign_type_offset.
    uint32_t block_size;
    uint32_t block_foreign_type_offset;
    uint64_t heap_region_offset_mask;
    uint64_t primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask;
    // Where a GCVisitor keeps a pointer to the marker it marks for, which is null in visitors that do not mark. Code that
    // visits can hand cells to the marker directly, with gc_marker_visit_cell() and gc_marker_visit_values().
    uint32_t visitor_marker_offset;
    // Where a cell keeps the state of its identity hash, and the bits of that state (see gc_cell_identity_hash()).
    uint32_t identity_hash_state_offset;
    uint8_t identity_hash_hashed;
    uint8_t identity_hash_moved;
} GCLayout;

// The caller passes the size of its GCLayout, which must match LibGC's, so that a mirror that drifted is caught before
// anything is written to it.
GC_API void gc_get_layout(GCLayout*, size_t layout_size);

// The base of the region all cells are allocated from, which NaN-boxed cell pointers are relative to. Reserves the
// region on first use.
GC_API uintptr_t gc_heap_region_base(void);
GC_API uintptr_t gc_primitive_storage_cage_base(void);

GC_API GCHeap* gc_heap_create(GCGatherRootsCallback, void* context, bool become_thread_default);
// Finalizes and destroys every remaining cell. Roots created with gc_root_create() must be destroyed first. The final
// collection also runs every sweep callback and pending post-GC task, with gc_heap_is_collecting_everything() true,
// so their contexts must stay valid until this returns; nothing they allocate then is destroyed.
GC_API void gc_heap_destroy(GCHeap*);
GC_API void gc_heap_collect_garbage(GCHeap*, int collection_type, bool print_report);
// Collects garbage without scanning the stack, so only the roots the heap knows of keep cells alive, and cells may move.
// The caller must hold no cell that it did not root.
GC_API void gc_heap_collect_garbage_without_scanning_the_stack(GCHeap*);
// Whether LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING is set, see Heap::moves_everything().
GC_API bool gc_heap_moves_everything(void);
// See Heap::set_moves_everything_for_testing().
GC_API void gc_heap_set_moves_everything_for_testing(GCHeap*, bool);
GC_API bool gc_heap_is_collecting_everything(GCHeap const*);
// Whether the heap gathers its roots and marks the live cells for a collection now, rather than for a graph dump.
GC_API bool gc_heap_is_marking_for_collection(GCHeap const*);
// Whether the collection that runs is there to give memory back to the system, for a process that is short of it.
GC_API bool gc_heap_is_returning_memory_to_system(GCHeap const*);
GC_API void gc_heap_defer_gc(GCHeap*);
GC_API void gc_heap_undefer_gc(GCHeap*);
GC_API void gc_heap_deferral_state(GCHeap*, size_t** deferrals, bool** collect_when_deferrals_end);
GC_API bool gc_heap_should_collect_on_every_allocation(GCHeap const*);
GC_API void gc_heap_set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(GCHeap*, bool);
GC_API void gc_heap_set_incremental_sweep_enabled(GCHeap*, bool);
GC_API void gc_heap_uproot_cell(GCHeap*, GCCell*);
// The bounds of the stack of the thread that created the heap; base is the lowest address.
GC_API void gc_heap_stack_bounds(GCHeap const*, uintptr_t* base, uintptr_t* top);
GC_API void gc_heap_enqueue_post_gc_task(GCHeap*, GCCallback, void* context);
// Runs during every collection after marking and finalization and before dead cells are swept, when weak holders can
// drop the cells that did not survive. There is no way to unregister a sweep callback, and it also runs when the heap
// is destroyed.
GC_API void gc_heap_register_sweep_callback(GCHeap*, GCCallback, void* context);
GC_API void gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory(GCHeap*, size_t);
GC_API void gc_heap_did_free_external_memory(GCHeap*, size_t);

// The type info and the name must outlive the allocator, and the allocator must outlive every heap it allocated from.
// The blocks of the allocator hold foreign_type, which also names the type of the cells for the whole process:
// allocators with the same foreign_type and cell size share a pool of blocks, across all heaps, and blocks never leave
// their pool. Different types must have different ones. An allocator without one has a pool of its own, and must never
// be destroyed.
GC_API GCAllocator* gc_allocator_create(GCCellTypeInfo const*, char const* name, size_t name_length, void const* foreign_type);
GC_API void gc_allocator_destroy(GCAllocator*);
// Cells of allocators created here may be traced on any thread while the collector marks, as long as the thread that
// owns their heap is stopped. This has the cells of an allocator traced only on that thread instead, for types whose
// visit_edges() or external_memory_size() reach state that is not their own. It must be called before the allocator
// allocates a cell.
GC_API void gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only(GCAllocator*);
// Lets collections move the cells of the allocator to other blocks of it, in collections that do not scan the stack. A
// cell moves as a bytewise copy, its old slot is freed without destroying it, and every slot that marking visited
// through gc_marker_visit_member(), gc_marker_visit_values(), gc_marker_visit_owned_values(),
// gc_marker_visit_interior_pointer() or gc_marker_visit_self_pointer() is rewritten. A cell that something visits by
// value, through gc_marker_visit_cell() or as a root, or that gc_marker_pin_cell() pins, stays where it is. So a type
// may only be movable if everything that keeps its address without visiting it as a slot either pins it or forgets it
// (see gc_cell_will_move()). It must be called before the allocator allocates a cell.
GC_API void gc_allocator_set_movable(GCAllocator*);

// Returns uninitialized storage for one cell.
GC_API GCCell* gc_heap_allocate_cell(GCHeap*, GCAllocator*);
// Like gc_heap_allocate_cell(), for cells that other cells keep their storage in instead of malloc memory: it never
// collects garbage, so storage can grow while its owner is between states nothing may observe, and callers can hold on
// to anything across the growth. It still counts towards the next collection, which the next allocation that may
// collect starts.
GC_API GCCell* gc_heap_allocate_storage_cell(GCHeap*, GCAllocator*);
// Each allocator takes the free cells of one block at a time into the heap, as a local free list of the cells that were
// freed and a range of cells that were never allocated, so that allocating is usually popping that list or bumping
// the cursor of that range, and code that allocates cells itself (like the Rust heap) does either inline:
// - The list is a list of dead cells of one block, linked through the word at free_cell_next_offset. Cells are in the
//   heap region, where anything may have been corrupted, so only the bits of a link under free_cell_link_mask count:
//   the next cell is at those bits within the block of the cell holding the link, that is, the cell's address with
//   the bits under free_cell_link_mask replaced by the link's. The list is empty when the bits of its head under
//   free_cell_link_mask are all zero (a null head, or the start of a block, where the last link leads).
// - Once the list is empty, cells come from the range: the cursor, the end and the cell size are pointer-sized words
//   at local_cursor_offset, local_end_offset and local_cell_size_offset from the head of the list. While the cursor is
//   below the end, the cell at the cursor is free, and taking it advances the cursor by the cell size. These words are
//   outside the heap region.
// - Before taking a cell of N bytes (the cell size of the allocator), such code checks that the heap's
//   allocated_bytes_since_last_gc + N stays within its gc_bytes_threshold, and allocates through the heap otherwise
//   (which may collect garbage). After taking it, it adds N to allocated_bytes_since_last_gc and total_allocated_bytes;
//   storage cells (see gc_heap_allocate_storage_cell()) skip the check but add N to both as well. These
//   are size_t fields of the heap, at the offsets gc_get_layout() reports.
// - It then writes every byte of the cell, as after gc_heap_allocate_cell().
// Returns where the head of the allocator's list in the heap is, which stays valid as long as the heap. The list and
// the range are always empty while the heap collects on every allocation. Returns null if cells must always be
// allocated through the heap, as in builds that poison free cells for AddressSanitizer.
GC_API GCCell** gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list(GCHeap*, GCAllocator*);
// The context that the heap of the cell was created with, as code that only has a cell finds the rest of its runtime.
GC_API void* gc_cell_heap_context(GCCell const*);
// The type info the cell's block was allocated with.
GC_API GCCellTypeInfo const* gc_cell_type_info(GCCell const*);
// Whether the last collection marked the cell. Only meaningful from the end of marking until the cell is swept, as in a
// sweep callback.
GC_API bool gc_cell_is_marked(GCCell const*);
// Whether the collection in progress moves the cell once marking is done, as a sweep callback may ask. A cache that keeps
// cells by address without visiting them drops such a cell, as if it died.
GC_API bool gc_cell_will_move(GCCell const*);
// Whether the collection in progress may move cells.
GC_API bool gc_heap_is_moving_cells(GCHeap const*);
// What a slot handed to gc_heap_record_slot() holds.
enum {
    // A NaN-boxed value, which may hold a cell.
    GC_RECORDED_SLOT_VALUE = 0,
    // A raw pointer to the start of a cell, or null.
    GC_RECORDED_SLOT_CELL_POINTER = 1,
};
// Has the collection in progress rewrite a slot that marking did not visit through it if its cell moves, as it rewrites
// the slots marking visited. Holders that keep cells without keeping them alive or in place, like weak maps, hand over
// the slots of the cells that survived from a sweep callback, once they forgot those that died. The cell must be marked,
// and nothing may free, move or write the slot until the collection is over. Does nothing if no cell moves.
GC_API void gc_heap_record_slot(GCHeap*, void const* slot, int kind);
// A 32-bit hash of the cell's identity, which stays the same while the cell lives, wherever the collector moves it.
// Hashing a cell for the first time sets the "hashed" bit of the byte at identity_hash_state_offset; while the "moved"
// bit is clear, the hash is the cell's compressed address, so code may compute it inline (see GC::identity_hash()) and
// call this only for cells whose "moved" bit is set.
GC_API uint32_t gc_cell_identity_hash(GCCell const*);

GC_API GCRoot* gc_root_create(GCCell*);
GC_API void gc_root_destroy(GCRoot*);
GC_API GCCell* gc_root_cell(GCRoot const*);

// Weak references are returned with one reference already taken, which the caller releases with
// gc_weak_impl_unref(). The pointer lives at weak_impl_pointer_offset and becomes null once the cell is collected.
GC_API GCWeakImpl* gc_heap_create_weak_impl(GCHeap*, GCCell*);
GC_API GCWeakImpl* gc_weak_impl_null(void);
GC_API void gc_weak_impl_ref(GCWeakImpl*);
GC_API void gc_weak_impl_unref(GCWeakImpl*);

GC_API void gc_visitor_visit_cell(GCVisitor*, GCCell*);
GC_API void gc_visitor_visit_cells(GCVisitor*, GCCell* const*, size_t count);
GC_API void gc_visitor_visit_values(GCVisitor*, uint64_t const*, size_t count);
// Visits a NaN-boxed value that is reachable only while key is, such as a WeakMap entry's. A collection that moves cells
// keeps both where they are.
GC_API void gc_visitor_visit_ephemeron(GCVisitor*, GCCell* key, uint64_t const* value);

// The marker a marking GCVisitor points to (see GCLayout::visitor_marker_offset), which these hand cells to directly.
typedef struct GCMarker GCMarker;
// Visits the cell by value, which keeps it from moving.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_cell(GCMarker*, GCCell*);
// Visits the values, whose slots a collection that moves cells rewrites if they are in a cell.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_values(GCMarker*, uint64_t const*, size_t count);
// Visits values in memory that the cell being visited owns outside the heap, whose slots a collection that moves cells
// rewrites where they are, like those in cells. Nothing may free, move or write that memory until the collection is
// over: no finalizer, destructor or sweep callback may touch it.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_owned_values(GCMarker*, uint64_t const*, size_t count);
// Visits the cell that the compressed pointer in the slot points to, if it is not null. A collection that moves cells
// rewrites the slot if it is in a cell, and keeps the cell where it is otherwise.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_member(GCMarker*, uint32_t const* slot);
// Visits a cell that the pointer in the slot points into, past its start, like the values of storage a cell keeps.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_interior_pointer(GCMarker*, uintptr_t const* slot, GCCell* cell);
// Notes a pointer in the slot to somewhere in the cell that holds it, up to one past its end, which a collection that
// moves the cell keeps pointing into the copy.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_self_pointer(GCMarker*, uintptr_t const* slot);
// Keeps the cell from moving without keeping it alive, for a weak reference that the collector cannot update.
GC_API void gc_marker_pin_cell(GCMarker*, GCCell const*);
// Marks value once key is marked, like gc_visitor_visit_ephemeron(), without keeping either from moving. The holder must
// hand the slots of both to gc_heap_record_slot() if the entry survives the collection.
GC_API void gc_marker_visit_ephemeron_without_pinning(GCMarker*, GCCell* key, GCCell* value);

// Primitive storage holds byte buffers inside the cage that starts at gc_primitive_storage_cage_base(), so that the
// interpreter can reach any of their bytes as a cage offset masked with primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask. Like the
// heap, primitive storage is not thread-safe, and every call must come from the thread that uses the heap.
//
// A handle crosses this interface as one 64-bit word: the generation of its table entry in the high 32 bits and the
// index of that entry in the low 32 bits. Generations start at 1, so GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE never names
// storage. Freeing storage moves its entry to the next generation, after which every function treats the old handle
// as naming no storage.
typedef uint64_t GCPrimitiveStorageHandle;

#define GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE ((GCPrimitiveStorageHandle)0)
#define GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_HANDLE_GENERATION_SHIFT 32
#define GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_INVALID_OFFSET SIZE_MAX

// Where storage is in the cage and how large it is. An owner may keep the layout at hand, since only creating and
// resizing the storage change it.
typedef struct GCPrimitiveStorageLayout {
    size_t offset;
    size_t size;
    size_t capacity;
} GCPrimitiveStorageLayout;

// The functions that create storage write its handle to *out_handle and return true, or write
// GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE and return false when the cage or the system is out of memory. With zero_fill, the
// first size bytes start out zero; without it, their contents are unspecified. The functions that create or resize
// storage also write its new layout to *out_layout when they succeed, unless out_layout is null.
//
// Storage of size bytes, which may share pages with other small storage.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_allocate(size_t size, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle* out_handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout);
// Storage of size bytes in a reservation of its own: capacity bytes followed by guard_size inaccessible bytes, both
// rounded up to whole pages. Only the pages the size covers are committed. Fails if size is greater than capacity.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_reserve(size_t size, size_t capacity, bool zero_fill, size_t guard_size, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle* out_handle, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout);
// Maps the first size bytes of the shared memory object behind fd into the cage. The mapping keeps the memory alive by
// itself, so the caller keeps ownership of fd and may close it at any time. Fails if size is 0. Growing the storage
// would replace the mapping with private memory, so shared storage keeps its size.

// The resizing functions return false and leave the storage as it was if the handle names no storage or memory runs
// out. Within the capacity, the storage stays where it is; beyond it, the bytes move to new storage, which changes the
// offset and the data pointer.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_resize(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle, size_t new_size, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout);
// Grows the capacity to at least new_capacity, moving the storage into a reservation of its own if it has to grow.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_reserve_capacity(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle, size_t new_capacity, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout);
// Sets the size and grows the capacity to at least new_capacity, moving the storage at most once. Fails if new_size
// is greater than new_capacity.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_resize_and_reserve(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle, size_t new_size, size_t new_capacity, bool zero_fill, GCPrimitiveStorageLayout* out_layout);
// Does nothing if the handle names no storage.
GC_API void gc_primitive_storage_free(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);

// For a handle that names no storage, the offset is GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_INVALID_OFFSET, the sizes are 0 and the data
// pointer is null.
GC_API bool gc_primitive_storage_is_valid(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);
// The offset of the first byte from gc_primitive_storage_cage_base().
GC_API size_t gc_primitive_storage_offset(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);
GC_API size_t gc_primitive_storage_size(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);
GC_API size_t gc_primitive_storage_capacity(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);
// The bytes from the offset on that are backed by memory.
GC_API size_t gc_primitive_storage_committed_size(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);
GC_API uint8_t* gc_primitive_storage_data(GCPrimitiveStorageHandle);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#pragma once

#include <AK/Array.h>

namespace GC {

template<typename T>
class Weak;

// A capture whose type the GC does not trace has to hold no cell edges at all. An owning or counted pointer is one if what
// it points to is, which a type declares with GC_UNTRACED_CAPTURE(). A raw pointer is never one of these, as it may point
// into a cell, such as at a mixin of one.
template<typename T>
struct IsUntracedCapture : FalseType { };

template<typename T>
requires(IsArithmetic<T> || IsEnum<T>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<T> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
requires(requires { typename T::HoldsNoCellEdges; })
struct IsUntracedCapture<T> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Empty> : TrueType { };

template<typename R, typename... Args>
struct IsUntracedCapture<R (*)(Args...)> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::String> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::Utf16String> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::FlyString> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::Utf16FlyString> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::ByteString> : TrueType { };

template<size_t inline_capacity>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::Detail::ByteBuffer<inline_capacity>> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Weak<T>> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::WeakPtr<T>> : TrueType { };

template<typename T, typename X, typename... Options>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::DistinctNumeric<T, X, Options...>> : IsUntracedCapture<T> { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::Duration> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::MonotonicTime> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::UnixDateTime> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::JsonValue> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::JsonObject> : TrueType { };

template<>
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::JsonArray> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::RefPtr<T>> : IsUntracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::NonnullRefPtr<T>> : IsUntracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::OwnPtr<T>> : IsUntracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsUntracedCapture<AK::NonnullOwnPtr<T>> : IsUntracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Optional<T>> : IsUntracedCapture<T> { };

template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Vector<T, inline_capacity>> : IsUntracedCapture<T> { };

template<typename T, size_t size>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Array<T, size>> : IsUntracedCapture<T> { };

template<typename... Ts>
struct IsUntracedCapture<Variant<Ts...>> {
    static constexpr bool value = (IsUntracedCapture<Ts>::value && ...);
};

template<typename T>
struct IsTracedCapture;

// Every part of a capture is either traced or holds no cell edges, so nothing a function captures can keep a cell
// that the GC does not see.
template<typename T>
consteval bool is_capturable()
{
    // NB: A type that holds no cell edges may be incomplete here, which asking whether it is traced would not allow.
    if constexpr (IsUntracedCapture<T>::value)
        return true;
    else
        return IsTracedCapture<T>::value;
}

template<typename T>
inline constexpr bool IsCapturable = is_capturable<T>();

template<typename T>
struct IsTracedCapture {
    static constexpr bool value = IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T> || (!IsCellLike<T> && requires(T& value, Cell::Visitor& visitor) { value.visit_edges(visitor); });
};

template<typename T>
struct IsTracedCapture<Ref<T>> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
struct IsTracedCapture<Ptr<T>> : TrueType { };

template<typename T>
struct IsTracedCapture<Optional<T>> {
    static constexpr bool value = IsCapturable<T>;
};

template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
struct IsTracedCapture<Vector<T, inline_capacity>> {
    static constexpr bool value = IsCapturable<T>;
};

template<typename T, size_t size>
struct IsTracedCapture<Array<T, size>> {
    static constexpr bool value = IsCapturable<T>;
};

template<typename... Ts>
struct IsTracedCapture<Variant<Ts...>> {
    static constexpr bool value = (IsCapturable<Ts> && ...);
};

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsTracedCapture<AK::RefPtr<T>> : IsTracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
requires(!IsCellLike<RemoveCV<T>>)
struct IsTracedCapture<AK::NonnullRefPtr<T>> : IsTracedCapture<RemoveCV<T>> { };

template<typename T>
inline constexpr bool IsRoot = false;

template<typename T>
inline constexpr bool IsRoot<Root<T>> = true;

template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
inline constexpr bool IsRoot<RootVector<T, inline_capacity>> = true;

// Visits a member of a value type, such as a generated dictionary, from its visit_edges(). Every member must be traced or
// hold no cell edges, so that the value can be captured by a GC::Function.
// NB: A root member would keep what it names alive for as long as the function lives, even through a cycle back to the
//     function, so a value with one isn't capturable.
template<typename Visitor, typename T>
void visit_capture_member(Visitor& visitor, T const& member)
{
    static_assert(!IsRoot<T>, "A captured value can't hold a root");
    static_assert(IsCapturable<T>, "A member of a captured value must be traced, or hold no cell edges");
    if constexpr (!IsUntracedCapture<T>::value) {
        static_assert(IsVisitable<T>::value, "A traced member of a captured value must be visitable");
        visitor.visit(member);
    }
}

}

#include <LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h>

namespace GC {

StringView class_name_of(Cell const& cell)
{
    if (cell.state() != Cell::State::Live)
        return "FreelistEntry"sv;
    auto const& type_info = cell.type_info();
    if (type_info.class_name) {
        size_t length = 0;
        auto const* characters = type_info.class_name(&cell, &length);
        return { characters, length };
    }
    return HeapBlock::from_cell(&cell)->cell_allocator().class_name().value_or("Cell"sv);
}

bool Cell::is_marked() const
{
    return GC::is_marked(this);
}

#pragma GCC diagnostic push
#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Winvalid-offsetof"
size_t Cell::Visitor::marker_offset()
{
    return offsetof(Visitor, m_marker);
}
#pragma GCC diagnostic pop

void GC::Cell::Visitor::visit(NanBoxedValue const& value)
{
    if (!value.is_cell())
        return;
    // NB: The value is visited through its slot, which a collection that moves cells rewrites if it is in a cell.
    if (m_marker) {
        gc_marker_visit_values(m_marker, reinterpret_cast<uint64_t const*>(&value), 1);
        return;
    }
    visit_cell(value.as_cell());
}

void GC::Cell::Visitor::visit_ephemeron(Cell&, NanBoxedValue const& value)
{
    visit(value);
}

}

#pragma once

namespace Detail {

// Whether a value of the type holds a pointer to a cell, as far as Cell::Visitor::ignore() checks.
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer : FalseType { };
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<T*> {
    static constexpr bool value = IsBaseOf<Cell, RemoveCV<T>> || IsBaseOf<ForeignCell, RemoveCV<T>>;
};
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<Ptr<T>> : TrueType { };
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<Ref<T>> : TrueType { };
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<Member<T>> : TrueType { };
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<NonnullMember<T>> : TrueType { };
template<typename T>
struct HoldsCellPointer<Optional<T>> : HoldsCellPointer<T> { };
template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity, FastLastAccess fast_last_access>
struct HoldsCellPointer<Vector<T, inline_capacity, fast_last_access>> : HoldsCellPointer<T> { };
template<typename T, typename Traits, bool IsOrdered>
struct HoldsCellPointer<HashTable<T, Traits, IsOrdered>> : HoldsCellPointer<T> { };
template<typename K, typename V, typename KeyTraits, typename ValueTraits, bool IsOrdered>
struct HoldsCellPointer<HashMap<K, V, KeyTraits, ValueTraits, IsOrdered>> {
    static constexpr bool value = HoldsCellPointer<K>::value || HoldsCellPointer<V>::value;
};

}

template<typename T>
struct IsVisitable;

#if defined(AK_COMPILER_CLANG)
#    define GC_ALLOW_CELL_DESTRUCTOR [[clang::annotate("ladybird::allow_cell_destructor")]]
#    define GC_VISITS_THROUGH_FOREIGN_IMPLEMENTATION [[clang::annotate("ladybird::visits_through_foreign_implementation")]]
