#define GC_CELL(class_, base_class)                \
public:                                            \
    using Base = base_class;                       \
    virtual StringView class_name() const override \
    {                                              \
        return #class_##sv;                        \
    }                                              \
    friend class GC::Heap;                         \
    friend struct GC::CellTypeThunks;

#define GC_CELL_WITH_CUSTOM_CLASS_NAME(class_, base_class) \
public:                                                    \
    using Base = base_class;                               \
    friend class GC::Heap;                                 \
    friend struct GC::CellTypeThunks;

// A coarse class tag stored in every cell header. It lets a holder of a cell pointer confirm what
// the cell really is with a single byte compare, without reading a vtable. Only the classes a
// JS::Value can point at need their own kind; everything else stays Other.
enum class CellKind : u8 {
    Other,
    Object,
    PrimitiveString,
    Symbol,
    BigInt,
    Accessor,
};

class GC_API Cell {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Cell);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Cell);

public:
    // Heap::allocate() copies this into the header of every cell it creates. A class that a
    // JS::Value can point at overrides it, and its subclasses inherit the override.
    static constexpr CellKind cell_kind_for_class = CellKind::Other;

    virtual ~Cell() = default;

    CellKind cell_kind() const { return m_cell_kind; }

    // Whether the last collection marked the cell, which it keeps in the descriptor of the cell's block. Only meaningful
    // from the end of marking until the cell's block is swept.
    bool is_marked() const;

    enum class State : bool {
        Live,
        Dead,
    };

    State state() const { return m_state; }
    void set_state(State state) { m_state = state; }

    virtual StringView class_name() const = 0;

    class GC_API Visitor {
    public:
        void visit(Cell* cell)
        {
            if (cell)
                visit_cell(*cell);
        }

        void visit(Cell& cell)
        {
            visit_cell(cell);
        }

        void visit(Cell const* cell)
        {
            visit(const_cast<Cell*>(cell));
        }

        void visit(Cell const& cell)
        {
            visit(const_cast<Cell&>(cell));
        }

        void visit(ForeignCell* cell);
        void visit(ForeignCell& cell);
        void visit(ForeignCell const* cell);
        void visit(ForeignCell const& cell);

        template<typename T>
        void visit(Ptr<T> cell)
        {
            if (cell)
                visit_cell(*as_cell(const_cast<RemoveConst<T>*>(cell.ptr())));
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(Ref<T> cell)
        {
            visit_cell(*as_cell(const_cast<RemoveConst<T>*>(cell.ptr())));
        }

        // Members are visited through their slot, which a collection that moves cells rewrites.
        template<typename T>
        void visit(Member<T> const& slot)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof(slot) == sizeof(u32));
            if (m_marker) {
                gc_marker_visit_member(m_marker, reinterpret_cast<u32 const*>(&slot));
                return;
            }
            if (slot)
                visit_member_cell(slot.ptr());
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(NonnullMember<T> const& slot)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof(slot) == sizeof(u32));
            if (m_marker) {
                gc_marker_visit_member(m_marker, reinterpret_cast<u32 const*>(&slot));
                return;
            }
            visit_member_cell(slot.ptr());
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(ReadonlySpan<T> span)
        requires(!IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T> && IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            for (auto& value : span)
                visit(value);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(ReadonlySpan<T> span)
        requires(IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T>)
        {
            visit_values(ReadonlySpan<NanBoxedValue>(span.data(), span.size()));
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(Span<T> span)
        requires(!IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T> && IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            for (auto& value : span)
                visit(value);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(Span<T> span)
        requires(IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T>)
        {
            visit_values(ReadonlySpan<NanBoxedValue>(span.data(), span.size()));
        }

        template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
        void visit(Vector<T, inline_capacity> const& vector)
        requires(!IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T> && IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            for (auto& value : vector)
                visit(value);
        }

        template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
        void visit(Vector<T, inline_capacity> const& vector)
        requires(IsBaseOf<NanBoxedValue, T>)
        {
            visit_values(ReadonlySpan<NanBoxedValue>(vector.span().data(), vector.size()));
        }

        template<typename T, size_t size>
        void visit(Array<T, size> const& array)
        requires(IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            visit(array.span());
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(HashTable<T> const& table)
        requires(IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            for (auto& value : table)
                visit(value);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(OrderedHashTable<T> const& table)
        requires(IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            for (auto& value : table)
                visit(value);
        }

        template<typename K, typename V, typename T>
        void visit(HashMap<K, V, T> const& map)
        {
            for (auto& it : map) {
                if constexpr (requires { visit(it.key); })
                    visit(it.key);
                if constexpr (requires { visit(it.value); })
                    visit(it.value);
            }
        }

        template<typename K, typename V, typename T>
        void visit(OrderedHashMap<K, V, T> const& map)
        {
            for (auto& it : map) {
                if constexpr (requires { visit(it.key); })
                    visit(it.key);
                if constexpr (requires { visit(it.value); })
                    visit(it.value);
            }
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(T const& value)
        requires(!IsCellLike<T> && requires(T& visitable) { visitable.visit_edges(*this); })
        {
            const_cast<T&>(value).visit_edges(*this);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(AK::RefPtr<T> const& value)
        requires(requires(RemoveConst<T>& visitable) { visitable.visit_edges(*this); })
        {
            if (value)
                visit(*value);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(AK::NonnullRefPtr<T> const& value)
        requires(requires(RemoveConst<T>& visitable) { visitable.visit_edges(*this); })
        {
            visit(*value);
        }

        template<typename T>
        void visit(Optional<T> const& optional)
        requires(IsVisitable<T>::value)
        {
            if (optional.has_value())
                visit(optional.value());
        }

        void visit(NanBoxedValue const& value);

        template<typename... Ts>
        void visit(Variant<Ts...> const& variant)
        requires((IsVisitable<Ts>::value || ...))
        {
            variant.visit([&](auto const& value) {
                if constexpr (requires { visit(value); })
                    visit(value);
            });
        }

        // Allow explicitly ignoring a member in a visit_edges implementation instead of just not using it. A pointer to a
        // cell that nothing visits goes stale once the cell moves, so a weak reference to a cell has to be a GC::Weak.
        template<typename T>
        void ignore(T const&)
        requires(!Detail::HoldsCellPointer<T>::value)
        {
        }

        // Visits a value that is reachable only while key is, such as a WeakMap entry's. Only marking tells them apart.
        // The caller must drop its entries whose key died, or the next collection reads a freed key.
        virtual void visit_ephemeron(Cell& key, NanBoxedValue const& value);

        static size_t marker_offset();

    protected:
        template<typename T>
        ALWAYS_INLINE void visit_member_cell(T* cell)
        {
            auto* mutable_cell = as_cell(const_cast<RemoveConst<T>*>(cell));
            // A compressed pointer must name the start of its cell.
            ASSERT(static_cast<void const*>(mutable_cell) == static_cast<void const*>(cell));
            visit_cell(*mutable_cell);
        }

        // NB: A marking visitor hands edges to its marker directly, rather than through its own visit_impl().
        ALWAYS_INLINE void visit_cell(Cell& cell)
        {
            if (m_marker) {
                gc_marker_visit_cell(m_marker, reinterpret_cast<GCCell*>(&cell));
                return;
            }
            visit_impl(cell);
        }

        ALWAYS_INLINE void visit_values(ReadonlySpan<NanBoxedValue> values)
        {
            if (m_marker) {
                if (!values.is_empty())
                    gc_marker_visit_values(m_marker, reinterpret_cast<uint64_t const*>(values.data()), values.size());
                return;
            }
            visit_impl(values);
        }

        // The marker of the collection that a marking visitor marks for, and null in every other visitor. Foreign
        // implementations find it at GCLayout::visitor_marker_offset.
        GCMarker* m_marker { nullptr };

        virtual void visit_impl(Cell&) = 0;
        virtual void visit_impl(ReadonlySpan<NanBoxedValue>) = 0;
        virtual ~Visitor() = default;
    };

    MUST_UPCALL virtual void visit_edges(Visitor&) { }

    // This will be called on unmarked objects by the garbage collector in a separate pass before destruction.
    MUST_UPCALL virtual void finalize() { }

    virtual size_t external_memory_size() const { return 0; }

    ALWAYS_INLINE Heap& heap() const { return HeapBlockBase::from_cell(this)->heap(); }
    ALWAYS_INLINE CellTypeInfo const& type_info() const { return HeapBlockBase::from_cell(this)->type_info(); }

protected:
    Cell() = default;

private:
    friend class Heap;
    friend struct CAPI;

    void set_cell_kind(CellKind kind) { m_cell_kind = kind; }

    // NB: Holds the state of the cell's identity hash, see identity_hash().
    [[maybe_unused]] u8 m_identity_hash_state { 0 };
    State m_state { State::Live };
    CellKind m_cell_kind { CellKind::Other };
};

// A cell whose type is implemented outside of C++ and allocated through LibGC/CAPI.h, such as a cell of the Rust
// LibJS runtime. Its header is laid out like a Cell's, except that the first word belongs to the foreign
// implementation instead of holding a vtable pointer. C++ code names these cells through types that derive from
// ForeignCell and add neither fields nor virtual functions, so that a pointer to such a type is the foreign cell
// itself. LibGC dispatches through the type info of a cell's block, never through a vtable, so Ptr, Ref, Root, Weak
// and visitors treat these types like subclasses of Cell. Only the foreign implementation creates and destroys them.
class ForeignCell {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(ForeignCell);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(ForeignCell);

public:
    ForeignCell() = delete;
    ~ForeignCell() = delete;

    CellKind cell_kind() const { return m_cell_kind; }
    bool is_marked() const { return as_cell(this)->is_marked(); }
    Cell::State state() const { return m_state; }

    ALWAYS_INLINE Heap& heap() const { return HeapBlockBase::from_cell(as_cell(this))->heap(); }
    ALWAYS_INLINE CellTypeInfo const& type_info() const { return HeapBlockBase::from_cell(as_cell(this))->type_info(); }

private:
    friend struct CAPI;

    [[maybe_unused]] void const* m_word_owned_by_the_foreign_implementation;
    // NB: As in Cell.
    [[maybe_unused]] u8 m_identity_hash_state;
    Cell::State m_state;
    CellKind m_cell_kind;
    // The foreign implementation lays its fields out right after the header. Naming these bytes keeps GCC from
    // placing a field of a derived type in the tail padding, where it would overlap them without changing the size.
    [[maybe_unused]] u8 m_tail_owned_by_the_foreign_implementation[sizeof(void*) - sizeof(u8) - sizeof(Cell::State) - sizeof(CellKind)];
};

inline void Cell::Visitor::visit(ForeignCell* cell)
{
    if (cell)
        visit_impl(*as_cell(cell));
}

inline void Cell::Visitor::visit(ForeignCell& cell)
{
    visit_impl(*as_cell(&cell));
}

inline void Cell::Visitor::visit(ForeignCell const* cell)
{
    visit(const_cast<ForeignCell*>(cell));
}

inline void Cell::Visitor::visit(ForeignCell const& cell)
{
    visit(const_cast<ForeignCell&>(cell));
}

template<typename T>
struct IsVisitable {
    static constexpr bool value = requires(Cell::Visitor& visitor, T const& value) { visitor.visit(value); };
};

GC_API StringView class_name_of(Cell const&);

// Where a cell keeps the state of its identity hash, and the bits of that state. CAPI.cpp checks them against the cell
// header and the Rust side.
namespace IdentityHashState {

static constexpr size_t offset = 8;
static constexpr u8 hashed = 1 << 0;
static constexpr u8 moved = 1 << 1;

}

// The hash of a cell's identity, which stays the same while the cell lives, wherever the collector moves it. Tables that
// are keyed by cells that may move hash them with this. See gc_cell_identity_hash().
ALWAYS_INLINE u32 identity_hash(void const* cell)
{
    // NB: The fast path of gc_cell_identity_hash(), for cells that did not move since they were first hashed.
    auto* state = static_cast<u8*>(const_cast<void*>(cell)) + IdentityHashState::offset;
    if (!(*state & IdentityHashState::moved)) [[likely]] {
        *state |= IdentityHashState::hashed;
        return compress(cell);
    }
    return gc_cell_identity_hash(static_cast<GCCell const*>(cell));
}

// The hash of a cell that a table which holds it weakly keys by, or of null once the cell is gone. A cell defined
// outside of C++ may move, which keeps its identity hash but not its address, see WeakBlock::update_moved_cells().
template<typename T>
ALWAYS_INLINE unsigned weak_key_hash(T const* cell)
{
    if constexpr (IsBaseOf<ForeignCell, T>)
        return cell ? u32_hash(identity_hash(cell)) : 0;
    else
        return Traits<T const*>::hash(cell);
}

inline StringView class_name_of(ForeignCell const& cell)
{
    return class_name_of(*as_cell(&cell));
}

}

#include <AK/Badge.h>
#include <AK/HashMap.h>
#include <AK/Mutex.h>
#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>

namespace GC {

struct BlockPoolKey {
    void const* type { nullptr };
    size_t cell_size { 0 };

    bool operator==(BlockPoolKey const&) const = default;
};

}

template<>
struct AK::Traits<GC::BlockPoolKey> : public DefaultTraits<GC::BlockPoolKey> {
    static unsigned hash(GC::BlockPoolKey const& key) { return pair_int_hash(ptr_hash(key.type), u64_hash(key.cell_size)); }
};

namespace GC {

// Descriptors are shared by the heaps of all threads, so they keep no per-heap state. Each has an index instead, which
// keeps the tables of the heaps dense: the indices of descriptors that went away are used again.
struct DescriptorIndices {
    Mutex mutex;
    size_t next_index { 0 };
    Vector<size_t> free_indices;
};

static DescriptorIndices& descriptor_indices()
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<DescriptorIndices> indices;
    return *indices;
}

CellAllocatorDescriptorBase::CellAllocatorDescriptorBase(CellTypeInfo const& type_info, StringView class_name, void const* foreign_type)
    : m_type_info(type_info)
    , m_class_name(class_name)
    , m_foreign_type(foreign_type)
{
    auto& indices = descriptor_indices();
    MutexLocker locker { indices.mutex };
    m_index = indices.free_indices.is_empty() ? indices.next_index++ : indices.free_indices.take_last();
}

void CellAllocatorDescriptorBase::release_index()
{
    auto& indices = descriptor_indices();
    MutexLocker locker { indices.mutex };
    indices.free_indices.append(m_index);
}

// A block that was used for a type stays with that type for as long as the process lives, whichever heap had it. So a
// stale pointer into the region can only ever find a cell of the type it was made for, at the same offsets. Heaps die
// while the process lives, so this has to hold across heaps: the pools outlive them, and a new heap reuses the blocks.
//
// A foreign type names the type for the whole process, while its descriptors come and go with the heaps. A descriptor
// without one lives as long as the process, as C++ ones do, so its own address does. The cell size tells the size
// classes of a foreign type apart, whose blocks do not fit each other.
BlockAllocator& CellAllocatorDescriptorBase::block_allocator() const
{
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<Mutex> mutex;
    static AK::NeverDestroyed<HashMap<BlockPoolKey, NonnullOwnPtr<BlockAllocator>>> pools;

    BlockPoolKey key { m_foreign_type ? m_foreign_type : this, cell_size() };
    MutexLocker locker { *mutex };
    return *pools->ensure(key, [] { return make<BlockAllocator>(); });
}

void CellAllocator::initialize_block(void* context, void* block)
{
    auto& allocator = *static_cast<CellAllocator*>(context);
    HeapBlock::initialize(block, allocator.m_heap, allocator);
}

// Frees the slot of a cell for LibGC's Rust core: runs its destructor first if it died, and marks it dead.
void CellAllocator::free_cell(void* context, void* address, bool destroy)
{
    auto& allocator = *static_cast<CellAllocator*>(context);
    auto* cell = static_cast<Cell*>(address);
    VERIFY(cell->state() == Cell::State::Live);
    if (auto* destroy_cell = allocator.type_info().destroy; destroy && destroy_cell) {
        allocator.m_heap.will_destroy_swept_cell({});
        destroy_cell(cell);
        allocator.m_heap.did_destroy_swept_cell({});
    }
    cell->set_state(Cell::State::Dead);

#ifdef HAS_ADDRESS_SANITIZER
    // NB: The header of a free cell, where its state is, stays accessible.
    auto after_header = round_up_to_power_of_two(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(cell) + HeapBlock::min_possible_cell_size, 8);
    VERIFY(after_header - reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(cell) <= allocator.cell_size());
    ASAN_POISON_MEMORY_REGION(reinterpret_cast<void*>(after_header), allocator.cell_size() - (after_header - reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(cell)));
#endif
}

CellAllocator::CellAllocator(Heap& heap, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor)
    : m_descriptor(descriptor)
    , m_block_allocator(descriptor.block_allocator())
    , m_heap(heap)
{
    m_local.cell_size = cell_size();
    FFI::AllocatorConfig config {
        .heap_region_base = heap_region_base(),
        .heap = &heap,
        .type_info = &type_info(),
        .pool = m_block_allocator.rust_pool({}),
        .local = reinterpret_cast<FFI::LocalFreeCells*>(&m_local),
        .cells_offset = static_cast<u32>(HeapBlock::cells_offset()),
        .cell_size = static_cast<u32>(cell_size()),
        .traced_on_owner_thread_only = descriptor.trace_thread() == TraceThread::OwnerThreadOnly,
        .movable = descriptor.is_movable(),
        .context = this,
        .initialize_block = initialize_block,
        .free_cell = free_cell,
    };
    m_allocator = FFI::rust_gc_allocator_create(&config);
}

CellAllocator::~CellAllocator()
{
    FFI::rust_gc_allocator_destroy(m_allocator);
}

static_assert(sizeof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells) == sizeof(FFI::LocalFreeCells));
static_assert(__builtin_offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, cursor) == __builtin_offsetof(FFI::LocalFreeCells, cursor));
static_assert(__builtin_offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, end) == __builtin_offsetof(FFI::LocalFreeCells, end));
static_assert(__builtin_offsetof(CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells, cell_size) == __builtin_offsetof(FFI::LocalFreeCells, cell_size));

Cell* CellAllocator::allocate_cell_slow(Heap& heap)
{
    if (!m_list_node.is_in_list())
        heap.register_cell_allocator({}, *this);

    // NB: A heap that collects on every allocation hands out single cells, as code that bumps through runs itself
    //     would take cells from them without collecting.
    bool can_sweep = heap.is_incremental_sweep_active() && !heap.is_gc_deferred();
    FFI::SweepStats stats {};
    // NB: The time spent sweeping goes into how far the heap grows before the next collection, see
    //     Heap::next_growth_factor().
    auto start_ns = can_sweep ? MonotonicTime::now().nanoseconds() : 0;
    auto* cell = static_cast<Cell*>(FFI::rust_gc_allocator_allocate(m_allocator, can_sweep, heap.should_collect_on_every_allocation(), &stats));
    if (stats.swept_blocks)
        heap.did_sweep_blocks_for_allocation({}, stats.swept_blocks, MonotonicTime::now().nanoseconds() - start_ns);
    ASAN_UNPOISON_MEMORY_REGION(cell, cell_size());
    return cell;
}

void CellAllocator::give_back_local_free_list(Badge<Heap>)
{
    FFI::rust_gc_allocator_give_back_local_free_cells(m_allocator);
}

size_t CellAllocator::block_count() const
{
    return FFI::rust_gc_allocator_block_count(m_allocator);
}

HeapBlock* CellAllocator::block_at(size_t index) const
{
    return static_cast<HeapBlock*>(FFI::rust_gc_allocator_block_at(m_allocator, index));
}

bool CellAllocator::is_local_block(HeapBlock const& block) const
{
    return FFI::rust_gc_allocator_local_block(m_allocator) == &block;
}

bool CellAllocator::has_blocks_pending_sweep() const
{
    return FFI::rust_gc_allocator_has_blocks_pending_sweep(m_allocator);
}

}

#pragma once

#include <AK/IntrusiveList.h>
#include <AK/IterationDecision.h>
#include <AK/NeverDestroyed.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/CellTypeInfo.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>

#ifdef HAS_ADDRESS_SANITIZER
#    include <sanitizer/asan_interface.h>
#endif

// The default allocator, which isolates different Cell types from being allocated in the same blocks.
#define GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(ClassName)    \
    using gc_allocator_marker = ClassName; \
    static GC::TypeIsolatingCellAllocator<ClassName> cell_allocator

#define GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(ClassName) \
    GC::TypeIsolatingCellAllocator<ClassName> ClassName::cell_allocator { #ClassName##sv }

namespace GC::FFI {

struct Allocator;

}

namespace GC {

// Which threads may trace the cells of an allocator while the collector marks. C++ cells are only traced on the thread
// that owns their heap.
enum class TraceThread : u8 {
    OwnerThreadOnly,
    AnyThread,
};

class GC_API CellAllocatorDescriptorBase {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(CellAllocatorDescriptorBase);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(CellAllocatorDescriptorBase);

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    Optional<StringView> class_name() const { return m_class_name; }
    CellTypeInfo const& type_info() const { return m_type_info; }
    size_t cell_size() const { return m_type_info.cell_size; }
    void const* foreign_type() const { return m_foreign_type; }
    TraceThread trace_thread() const { return m_trace_thread; }
    void set_trace_thread(TraceThread trace_thread) { m_trace_thread = trace_thread; }

    // Whether collections may move the cells to other blocks of their allocator, see gc_allocator_set_movable(). Only
    // allocators of cells defined outside of C++ are ever movable.
    bool is_movable() const { return m_movable; }
    void set_movable() { m_movable = true; }

    // Where each heap keeps its allocator for this descriptor, see Heap::cell_allocator_for().
    size_t index() const { return m_index; }

    // The blocks of the type of this descriptor, for every heap of the process and for as long as the process lives.
    BlockAllocator& block_allocator() const;

protected:
    CellAllocatorDescriptorBase(CellTypeInfo const& type_info, StringView class_name, void const* foreign_type = nullptr);

    // A descriptor that goes away while the process lives must call this, so that its index does not go to waste. No
    // heap may have an allocator for it any more.
    void release_index();

private:
    CellTypeInfo const& m_type_info;
    Optional<StringView> m_class_name;
    void const* m_foreign_type { nullptr };
    size_t m_index { 0 };
    TraceThread m_trace_thread { TraceThread::OwnerThreadOnly };
    bool m_movable { false };
};

// The cells of one type in one heap. LibGC's Rust core keeps the allocator's blocks, hands out their free cells in runs
// and sweeps them, see allocator.rs. This keeps the run that cells are allocated from inline.
class GC_API CellAllocator {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(CellAllocator);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(CellAllocator);

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    CellAllocator(Heap&, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase&);
    ~CellAllocator();

    CellAllocatorDescriptorBase const& descriptor() const { return m_descriptor; }
    Optional<StringView> class_name() const { return m_descriptor.class_name(); }
    size_t cell_size() const { return m_descriptor.cell_size(); }
    CellTypeInfo const& type_info() const { return m_descriptor.type_info(); }
    void const* foreign_type() const { return m_descriptor.foreign_type(); }

    // Cells come from a run of free cells that the allocator took from one
    // of its blocks (the local block) at once, so allocating is usually just
    // bumping a cursor.
    //
    // Invariants of the local free cells:
    // - They are free cells of the local block, whose allocated bits are set
    //   while they are out, see BlockDescriptor.h.
    // - The local block is never pending incremental sweep: they come from
    //   swept or new blocks only, and are handed back to their block whenever
    //   a collection starts. So cells from them never need marking.
    // - The list is always empty, which its head being null says. It is only
    //   there for code that allocates from it itself, which still checks it,
    //   see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list().
    // - The cells from the cursor up to the end are cell_size apart. There
    //   are none when the cursor is at the end.
    struct LocalFreeCells {
        Ptr<Cell> free_list;
        FlatPtr cursor { 0 };
        FlatPtr end { 0 };
        FlatPtr cell_size { 0 };
    };

    ALWAYS_INLINE Cell* allocate_cell(Heap& heap)
    {
        if (m_local.cursor < m_local.end) [[likely]] {
            auto* cell = bit_cast<Cell*>(m_local.cursor);
            m_local.cursor += m_local.cell_size;
            ASAN_UNPOISON_MEMORY_REGION(cell, cell_size());
            return cell;
        }
        return allocate_cell_slow(heap);
    }

    // Hands the local free cells back to the local block.
    void give_back_local_free_list(Badge<Heap>);

    // For code that allocates from the local free cells itself, see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list().
    LocalFreeCells* local_free_cells(Badge<CAPI>) { return &m_local; }

    template<typename Callback>
    IterationDecision for_each_block(Callback callback)
    {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < block_count(); ++i) {
            if (callback(*block_at(i)) == IterationDecision::Break)
                return IterationDecision::Break;
        }
        return IterationDecision::Continue;
    }

    size_t block_count() const;
    bool is_local_block(HeapBlock const&) const;
    bool has_blocks_pending_sweep() const;

    IntrusiveListNode<CellAllocator> m_list_node;
    using List = IntrusiveList<&CellAllocator::m_list_node>;

    IntrusiveListNode<CellAllocator> m_sweep_list_node;
    using SweepList = IntrusiveList<&CellAllocator::m_sweep_list_node>;

    BlockAllocator& block_allocator() { return m_block_allocator; }
    FFI::Allocator* rust_allocator(Badge<Heap>) { return m_allocator; }

private:
    friend class HeapBlock;

    HeapBlock* block_at(size_t index) const;
    Cell* allocate_cell_slow(Heap&);
    static void initialize_block(void* context, void* block);
    static void free_cell(void* context, void* cell, bool destroy);

    CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& m_descriptor;
    LocalFreeCells m_local;
    BlockAllocator& m_block_allocator;
    Heap& m_heap;
    FFI::Allocator* m_allocator { nullptr };
};

template<typename T>
class GC_API TypeIsolatingCellAllocator final : public CellAllocatorDescriptorBase {
public:
    using CellType = T;

    explicit TypeIsolatingCellAllocator(StringView class_name)
        : CellAllocatorDescriptorBase(cell_type_info_for<T>, class_name)
    {
    }
};

// Heap::allocate<T>() takes every cell from T::cell_allocator, and a subclass of T must declare an allocator of its own,
// so a cell that came from T::cell_allocator is exactly a T. This identifies a cell's type without reading its vtable.
inline bool cell_was_allocated_from(Cell const& cell, CellAllocatorDescriptorBase const& descriptor)
{
    return &HeapBlock::from_cell(&cell)->cell_allocator().descriptor() == &descriptor;
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/CellTypeInfo.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>

namespace GC {

// NB: Cells defined outside C++ keep 16-byte values in them, which some platforms align to less than 16 bytes.
constexpr size_t max_cell_alignment = max<size_t>(16, __BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT__);

struct CellTypeInfo {
    u32 cell_size { 0 };
    u32 alignment { 0 };
    CellKind kind { CellKind::Other };
    void (*visit_edges)(Cell*, Cell::Visitor*) { nullptr };
    void (*finalize)(Cell*) { nullptr };
    void (*destroy)(Cell*) { nullptr };
    size_t (*external_memory_size)(Cell const*) { nullptr };
    char const* (*class_name)(Cell const*, size_t* length) { nullptr };
};

struct CellTypeThunks {
    template<typename T>
    static void visit_edges(Cell* cell, Cell::Visitor* visitor)
    {
        static_cast<T*>(cell)->T::visit_edges(*visitor);
    }

    template<typename T>
    static void finalize(Cell* cell)
    {
        static_cast<T*>(cell)->T::finalize();
    }

    template<typename T>
    static void destroy(Cell* cell)
    {
        static_cast<T*>(cell)->T::~T();
    }

    template<typename T>
    static size_t external_memory_size(Cell const* cell)
    {
        return static_cast<T const*>(cell)->T::external_memory_size();
    }

    static char const* class_name(Cell const* cell, size_t* length)
    {
        auto name = cell->class_name();
        *length = name.length();
        return name.characters_without_null_termination();
    }

    template<typename T>
    static constexpr bool overrides_finalize()
    {
        return !IsSame<decltype(&T::finalize), void (Cell::*)()>;
    }

    template<typename T>
    static constexpr bool overrides_external_memory_size()
    {
        return !IsSame<decltype(&T::external_memory_size), size_t (Cell::*)() const>;
    }

    template<typename T>
    static constexpr CellTypeInfo info()
    {
        static_assert(alignof(T) <= max_cell_alignment);
        // A free cell holds a link to the next one, so a cell that can be allocated must have room for that after its
        // header.
        static_assert(__is_abstract(T) || sizeof(T) >= sizeof(Cell) + sizeof(FlatPtr), "A cell must be at least as large as a free cell");
        return {
            .cell_size = static_cast<u32>(sizeof(T)),
            .alignment = static_cast<u32>(alignof(T)),
            .kind = T::cell_kind_for_class,
            .visit_edges = &visit_edges<T>,
            .finalize = overrides_finalize<T>() ? &finalize<T> : nullptr,
            .destroy = &destroy<T>,
            .external_memory_size = overrides_external_memory_size<T>() ? &external_memory_size<T> : nullptr,
            .class_name = &class_name,
        };
    }
};

template<typename T>
inline constexpr CellTypeInfo cell_type_info_for = CellTypeThunks::info<T>();

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/CompressedPointer.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Assertions.h>
#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapRegion.h>

namespace GC {

// A compressed cell pointer is the cell's offset into the heap region in units of the 8-byte cell alignment. A u32 then
// covers the whole region, so decoding never leaves it whatever the 32 bits are. Null compresses to 0.
static constexpr u32 COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT = 3;
static_assert((static_cast<u64>(1) << (32 + COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT)) == HEAP_REGION_SIZE);

// Every compressed pointer below this decodes into the low guard, so it is never a cell.
static constexpr u32 MIN_COMPRESSED_CELL_POINTER = HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT;

// OPTIMIZATION: The region is aligned to its size, so the low 32 bits of a cell's address shifted right by 3 are its
//               compressed pointer, which takes no load of the base. Null stays 0.
ALWAYS_INLINE u32 compress(void const* cell)
{
    auto address = reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr>(cell);
    ASSERT(!cell || address - heap_region_base() < HEAP_REGION_SIZE);
    ASSERT(address % (1 << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) == 0);
    return static_cast<u32>(address >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT);
}

// Decodes a compressed pointer that is not null.
//
// Makes the compressed pointer live up to this point, and the decoded address from this point on. The conservative
// stack scan recognizes a cell by its address or by its compressed pointer in either half of a word, but not by its
// unshifted offset, which the compiler could otherwise keep instead while either is held across an allocation.
ALWAYS_INLINE FlatPtr decompress_nonnull(u32 compressed, FlatPtr heap_region_base = GC::heap_region_base())
{
    auto address = heap_region_base + (static_cast<FlatPtr>(compressed) << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT);
    // NB: The assembly is empty. It only has the compiler put the compressed pointer and the address in registers here.
    asm("" : "+r"(address) : "r"(compressed));
    return address;
}

ALWAYS_INLINE FlatPtr decompress(u32 compressed)
{
    if (!compressed)
        return 0;
    return decompress_nonnull(compressed);
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/CrossHeapMember.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Ali Mohammad Pur <ali@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibGC/CrossHeapMember.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>

namespace GC {

void CrossHeapMemberBase::reset(Cell* cell)
{
    auto* new_heap = cell ? &HeapBlockBase::from_cell(cell)->heap() : nullptr;
    if (m_registered_heap == new_heap) {
        m_cell = cell;
        return;
    }

    if (m_registered_heap)
        m_registered_heap->did_destroy_cross_heap_member({}, *this);
    m_cell = cell;
    m_registered_heap = new_heap;
    if (m_registered_heap)
        m_registered_heap->did_create_cross_heap_member({}, *this);
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/CrossHeapMember.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Ali Mohammad Pur <ali@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/Internals.h>

namespace GC {

// A strong reference from a cell on one heap to a cell on another heap in the same HeapGroup.
class GC_API CrossHeapMemberBase {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(CrossHeapMemberBase);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(CrossHeapMemberBase);

public:
    Cell* cell_base() const { return static_cast<Cell*>(m_cell); }

    void detach_from_heap(Badge<Heap>)
    {
        m_registered_heap = nullptr;
        m_cell = nullptr;
    }

protected:
    explicit CrossHeapMemberBase(Cell* cell)
    {
        reset(cell);
    }

    ~CrossHeapMemberBase()
    {
        reset(nullptr);
    }

    void reset(Cell* cell);

    void* m_cell { nullptr }; // Not a member of "this" heap.
    Heap* m_registered_heap { nullptr };
};

template<typename T>
class CrossHeapMember final : public CrossHeapMemberBase {
public:
    CrossHeapMember()
        : CrossHeapMemberBase(nullptr)
    {
    }

    explicit CrossHeapMember(T* cell)
        : CrossHeapMemberBase(as_cell(cell))
    {
    }

    CrossHeapMember& operator=(T* cell)
    {
        reset(as_cell(cell));
        return *this;
    }

    T* ptr() const { return static_cast<T*>(m_cell); }
    T* operator->() const { return ptr(); }
    explicit operator bool() const { return m_cell != nullptr; }

    // Called by the holder heap.
    void visit(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const
    {
        if (m_cell)
            visitor.visit(cell_base());
    }
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/ExternalEntityTable.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/BuiltinWrappers.h>
#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibGC/Export.h>

namespace GC {

struct ExternalEntityTableHandle {
    static constexpr u32 invalid_index = NumericLimits<u32>::max();

    u32 index { invalid_index };
    u32 generation { 0 };

    bool is_valid() const { return index != invalid_index && generation != 0; }
};

struct ExternalEntityTableTag {
    static constexpr u8 bit_count = 16;
    static constexpr u8 set_bit_count = bit_count / 2;
    static constexpr u16 tag_count = 12870;

    u16 value { 0 };

    constexpr bool is_balanced() const { return popcount(value) == set_bit_count; }
    constexpr bool operator==(ExternalEntityTableTag const&) const = default;
};

constexpr ExternalEntityTableTag balanced_external_entity_table_tag(u16 ordinal)
{
    VERIFY(ordinal < ExternalEntityTableTag::tag_count);

    u16 matching_tag = 0;
    for (u32 candidate = 0; candidate <= NumericLimits<u16>::max(); ++candidate) {
        if (popcount(candidate) != ExternalEntityTableTag::set_bit_count)
            continue;
        if (matching_tag == ordinal)
            return { static_cast<u16>(candidate) };
        ++matching_tag;
    }

    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

class GC_API ExternalEntityTable {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(ExternalEntityTable);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(ExternalEntityTable);

protected:
    ExternalEntityTable() = default;

    ALWAYS_INLINE ExternalEntityTableHandle allocate_entry(ExternalEntityTableTag tag)
    {
        VERIFY(tag.is_balanced());

        u32 index;
        if (m_free_entry_indices.is_empty()) {
            VERIFY(m_entries.size() < ExternalEntityTableHandle::invalid_index);
            index = static_cast<u32>(m_entries.size());
            m_entries.append({});
        } else {
            index = m_free_entry_indices.take_last();
        }

        auto& entry = m_entries[index];
        VERIFY(!entry.allocated);
        entry.allocated = true;
        entry.tag = tag;
        return { index, entry.generation };
    }

    ALWAYS_INLINE bool is_valid(ExternalEntityTableHandle handle, ExternalEntityTableTag expected_tag) const
    {
        return entry_for(handle, expected_tag) != nullptr;
    }

    ALWAYS_INLINE void free_entry(ExternalEntityTableHandle handle, ExternalEntityTableTag expected_tag)
    {
        auto* entry = const_cast<Entry*>(entry_for(handle, expected_tag));
        if (!entry)
            return;

        entry->allocated = false;
        ++entry->generation;
        if (entry->generation == 0)
            ++entry->generation;
        m_free_entry_indices.append(handle.index);
    }

private:
    struct Entry {
        u32 generation { 1 };
        ExternalEntityTableTag tag;
        bool allocated { false };
    };

    ALWAYS_INLINE Entry const* entry_for(ExternalEntityTableHandle handle, ExternalEntityTableTag expected_tag) const
    {
        if (!handle.is_valid() || handle.index >= m_entries.size())
            return nullptr;
        auto& entry = m_entries.data()[handle.index];
        if (!entry.allocated || entry.generation != handle.generation || entry.tag != expected_tag)
            return nullptr;
        return &entry;
    }

    Vector<Entry> m_entries;
    Vector<u32> m_free_entry_indices;
};

}

#pragma once

namespace Detail {

// A cell captured by reference is held as a Ref, and handed to the callable as a reference again.
template<typename T>
struct CapturedCellReference {
    Ref<T> cell;

    T& get() { return *cell; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(cell); }
};

// A cell captured by pointer is held as a Ptr, and handed to the callable as a pointer again.
template<typename T>
struct CapturedCellPointer {
    T* cell;

    T*& get() { return cell; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(Ptr<T> { cell }); }
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedValue {
    static_assert(IsCapturable<T>, "A GC::Function capture must be traced, or hold no cell edges");
    // NB: A value is copied into the function. A polymorphic one may be part of a larger object, such as the mixin of a
    //     cell captured as *this, and the function would act on a copy of it.
    static_assert(!__is_polymorphic(T), "A GC::Function can't capture a polymorphic value, which would be copied out of the object it is part of");

    T value;

    T& get() { return value; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const
    {
        if constexpr (!IsUntracedCapture<T>::value) {
            static_assert(IsVisitable<T>::value, "A traced GC::Function capture must be visitable");
            visitor.visit(value);
        }
    }
};

// A root that a function captures stops being a root, and is traced through the function instead. A function holding a
// root would keep what the root names alive for as long as the function lives, even through a cycle back to itself.
template<typename T>
struct CapturedRoot {
    CapturedRoot(Root<T> const& root)
        : cell(root.ptr())
    {
    }

    Ptr<T> cell;

    Ptr<T>& get() { return cell; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(cell); }
};

template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
struct CapturedRootVector {
    static_assert(IsCapturable<T>, "A GC::Function capture must be traced, or hold no cell edges");

    CapturedRootVector(RootVector<T, inline_capacity>&& vector)
        : elements(move(static_cast<Vector<T, inline_capacity>&>(vector)))
    {
    }

    CapturedRootVector(RootVector<T, inline_capacity> const& vector)
        : elements(vector)
    {
    }

    Vector<T, inline_capacity> elements;

    Vector<T, inline_capacity>& get() { return elements; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(elements); }
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedRootStorage {
    using Type = void;
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedRootStorage<Root<T>> {
    using Type = CapturedRoot<T>;
};

// A member of a cell is held as a pointer of its own, so that a function can name it as it is.
template<typename T>
struct CapturedMember {
    CapturedMember(Member<T> const& member)
        : cell(member.ptr())
    {
    }

    Ptr<T> cell;

    Ptr<T>& get() { return cell; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(cell); }
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedNonnullMember {
    CapturedNonnullMember(NonnullMember<T> const& member)
        : cell(*member)
    {
    }

    Ref<T> cell;

    Ref<T>& get() { return cell; }
    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const { visitor.visit(cell); }
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedRootStorage<Member<T>> {
    using Type = CapturedMember<T>;
};

template<typename T>
struct CapturedRootStorage<NonnullMember<T>> {
    using Type = CapturedNonnullMember<T>;
};

template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
struct CapturedRootStorage<RootVector<T, inline_capacity>> {
    using Type = CapturedRootVector<T, inline_capacity>;
};

template<typename T>
struct CaptureStorage {
    using Type = CapturedValue<RemoveCVReference<T>>;
};

template<typename T>
requires(!IsSame<typename CapturedRootStorage<RemoveCVReference<T>>::Type, void>)
struct CaptureStorage<T> {
    using Type = typename CapturedRootStorage<RemoveCVReference<T>>::Type;
};

template<typename T>
requires(IsLvalueReference<T> && IsCellLike<RemoveCVReference<T>>)
struct CaptureStorage<T> {
    using Type = CapturedCellReference<RemoveReference<T>>;
};

template<typename T>
requires(IsPointer<RemoveCVReference<T>> && IsCellLike<RemoveCV<RemovePointer<RemoveCVReference<T>>>>)
struct CaptureStorage<T> {
    using Type = CapturedCellPointer<RemovePointer<RemoveCVReference<T>>>;
};

template<size_t index, typename T>
struct CaptureSlot {
    T capture;
};

template<typename Indices, typename... Captures>
struct CaptureBox;

// The captures of a function, outside the GC heap.
template<size_t... indices, typename... Captures>
struct CaptureBox<IndexSequence<indices...>, Captures...> : CaptureSlot<indices, Captures>... {
    template<typename... Values>
    explicit CaptureBox(Values&&... values)
        : CaptureSlot<indices, Captures> { Captures { forward<Values>(values) } }...
    {
    }

    template<typename Callable, typename R, typename... Args>
    R invoke(Args&&... args)
    {
        return Callable {}(static_cast<CaptureSlot<indices, Captures>&>(*this).capture.get()..., forward<Args>(args)...);
    }

    void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor) const
    {
        (static_cast<CaptureSlot<indices, Captures> const&>(*this).capture.visit_edges(visitor), ...);
    }
};

template<size_t count, typename T>
struct DropParameters;

template<typename R, typename... Args>
struct DropParameters<0, R(Args...)> {
    using Type = R(Args...);
};

template<size_t count, typename R, typename First, typename... Rest>
requires(count > 0)
struct DropParameters<count, R(First, Rest...)> {
    using Type = typename DropParameters<count - 1, R(Rest...)>::Type;
};

// The type of a callable when it is given its captures, which also covers a callable that takes them as auto&.
template<typename Callable, typename... Captures>
struct CallableTypeWithCaptures {
    using Type = EquivalentFunctionType<Callable>;
};

template<typename Callable, typename... Captures>
requires(sizeof...(Captures) > 0 && requires { &Callable::template operator()<RemoveReference<decltype(declval<Captures&>().get())>...>; })
struct CallableTypeWithCaptures<Callable, Captures...> {
    using Type = EquivalentFunctionType<decltype(&Callable::template operator()<RemoveReference<decltype(declval<Captures&>().get())>...>)>;
};

// NB: A function is made in one library and called from another, so its signature is the hash of the mangled name of
//     its type, which every compiler and library spells the same. How a compiler spells the type differs: GCC, for one,
//     spells it as it was first written in each source file. Types of the same name with internal linkage, such as
//     those in an anonymous namespace, share one signature.
template<typename T>
inline u64 const function_signature = [] {
    u64 hash = 0xcbf29ce484222325;
    for (auto const* character = typeid(T).name(); *character; ++character) {
        hash ^= static_cast<u8>(*character);
        hash *= 0x100000001b3;
    }
    return hash;
}();

template<typename Callable>
concept CapturesNothing = __is_empty(Callable) && IsConstructible<Callable>;

template<typename Indices, typename... Values>
struct CaptureReferences;

template<size_t... indices, typename... Values>
struct CaptureReferences<IndexSequence<indices...>, Values...> : CaptureSlot<indices, Values&&>... {
    explicit CaptureReferences(Values&&... values)
        : CaptureSlot<indices, Values&&> { forward<Values>(values) }...
    {
    }

    template<typename Box>
    void make_box(void* storage)
    {
        new (storage) Box(static_cast<Values&&>(static_cast<CaptureSlot<indices, Values&&>&>(*this).capture)...);
    }
};

}

// What a function captures, as named by GC::captures(). It refers to the values until the function moves or copies them
// into its box, so it lives only as long as the expression that makes the function.
template<typename... Values>
struct CaptureList : Detail::CaptureReferences<MakeIndexSequence<sizeof...(Values)>, Values...> {
    using Detail::CaptureReferences<MakeIndexSequence<sizeof...(Values)>, Values...>::CaptureReferences;
};

template<typename... Values>
CaptureList<Values...> captures(Values&&... values)
{
    return CaptureList<Values...> { forward<Values>(values)... };
}

template<typename R, typename... Args>
struct FunctionOperationsFor : FunctionOperations {
    R (*invoke)(void* box, Args...) { nullptr };
};

template<typename T>
class Function;

template<typename R, typename... Args>
class Function<R(Args...)> final : public Cell {
    GC_CELL(Function, Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(Function);

public:
    using Operations = FunctionOperationsFor<R, Args...>;

    template<typename Callable, typename... Values>
    static Ref<Function> create(Heap& heap, CaptureList<Values...>&& captures, Callable&&)
    {
        static_assert(Detail::CapturesNothing<RemoveCVReference<Callable>>, "A GC::Function callable takes what it uses from its captures, and captures nothing itself");
        using Callback = RemoveCVReference<Callable>;
        using Box = Detail::CaptureBox<MakeIndexSequence<sizeof...(Values)>, typename Detail::CaptureStorage<Values>::Type...>;

        static_assert(alignof(Box) <= FunctionTable::box_alignment);

        if constexpr (sizeof...(Values) == 0) {
            auto cell = heap.allocate<Function>();
            cell->m_handle = heap.function_table().allocate(CaptureOperations<Callback, Box>::operations, 0).handle;
            return cell;
        } else {
            // NB: A collection waits until the function holds its box. Until then, the captured values may be where a
            //     conservative scan of the stack doesn't look, such as the storage of a temporary Vector of cells.
            DeferGC defer_gc { heap };
            auto cell = heap.allocate<Function>();
            auto allocation = heap.function_table().allocate(CaptureOperations<Callback, Box>::operations, sizeof(Box));
            captures.template make_box<Box>(allocation.box);
            cell->m_handle = allocation.handle;
            return cell;
        }
    }

    R operator()(Args... args) const
    {
        auto const& slot = heap().function_table().slot(m_handle);
        VERIFY(*slot.operations->signature == Detail::function_signature<R(Args...)>);
        // NB: The box is outside the heap, so nothing the callable holds points into this cell. This pointer is kept
        //     live across the call, where the conservative scan of the stack finds it, so that a collection the callable
        //     runs after dropping the last reference to its function does not destroy the box under it.
        ScopeGuard keep_alive = [this] { asm volatile("" : : "r"(this) : "memory"); };
        return static_cast<Operations const&>(*slot.operations).invoke(slot.box, forward<Args>(args)...);
    }

    Function const& function() const { return *this; }

    // NB: The captured values die when the cell is swept, not when it is finalized, so that the finalizer of another dead
    //     cell can still call this function.
    GC_ALLOW_CELL_DESTRUCTOR virtual ~Function() override
    {
        if (!m_handle.is_valid())
            return;
        auto& table = heap().function_table();
        auto const& slot = table.slot(m_handle);
        slot.operations->destroy(slot.box);
        table.free(m_handle);
        m_handle = {};
    }

private:
    Function() = default;

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        if (!m_handle.is_valid())
            return;
        auto const& slot = heap().function_table().slot(m_handle);
        slot.operations->visit_edges(slot.box, visitor);
    }

    template<typename Callback, typename Box>
    struct CaptureOperations {
        static constexpr Operations operations {
            {
                .signature = &Detail::function_signature<R(Args...)>,
                .visit_edges = [](void* box, Visitor& visitor) {
                    if (box)
                        static_cast<Box const*>(box)->visit_edges(visitor); },
                .destroy = [](void* box) {
                    if (box)
                        static_cast<Box*>(box)->~Box(); },
            },
            [](void* box, Args... args) -> R {
                if constexpr (IsSame<Box, Detail::CaptureBox<IndexSequence<>>>)
                    return Callback {}(forward<Args>(args)...);
                else
                    return static_cast<Box*>(box)->template invoke<Callback, R>(forward<Args>(args)...);
            },
        };
    };

    FunctionTableHandle m_handle;
};

// Makes a function of a callable that takes everything it uses from its captures. The values named by GC::captures()
// come first among the callable's parameters, followed by the function's own.
// NB: No template argument can be given for the leading pack, so a function type given explicitly selects the overload
//     below instead of being taken as the type of the first capture.
template<int&... ExplicitArgumentBarrier, typename... Values, typename Callable, typename T = typename Detail::DropParameters<sizeof...(Values), typename Detail::CallableTypeWithCaptures<RemoveCVReference<Callable>, typename Detail::CaptureStorage<Values>::Type...>::Type>::Type>
static Ref<Function<T>> create_function(Heap& heap, CaptureList<Values...>&& captures, Callable&& callable)
{
    return Function<T>::create(heap, move(captures), forward<Callable>(callable));
}

// The same, for a callable whose type does not name the function type, such as one that takes its own parameters as auto.
template<typename T, typename... Values, typename Callable>
requires(IsFunction<T>)
static Ref<Function<T>> create_function(Heap& heap, CaptureList<Values...>&& captures, Callable&& callable)
{
    return Function<T>::create(heap, move(captures), forward<Callable>(callable));
}

// Makes a function of a callable that captures nothing.
template<typename Callable, typename T = EquivalentFunctionType<RemoveCVReference<Callable>>>
static Ref<Function<T>> create_function(Heap& heap, Callable&& function)
{
    static_assert(Detail::CapturesNothing<RemoveCVReference<Callable>>, "A GC::Function callable captures nothing; name what it uses with GC::captures() and take it as parameters");
    return Function<T>::create(heap, CaptureList<> {}, forward<Callable>(function));
}

template<typename R, typename... Args>
GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(Function<R(Args...)>);

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/FunctionTable.h
/*

#pragma once

#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/NonnullOwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/Export.h>
#include <LibGC/ExternalEntityTable.h>

namespace GC {

using FunctionTableHandle = ExternalEntityTableHandle;

// What a GC::Function does with the box that holds its captures. Each kind of function has one static instance. The
// signature identifies the function type it was made for, so a handle that names another function's entry is caught
// before its box is invoked as the wrong type.
struct FunctionOperations {
    u64 const* signature { nullptr };
    void (*visit_edges)(void* box, Cell::Visitor&) { nullptr };
    void (*destroy)(void* box) { nullptr };
};

// The parts of every GC::Function that live outside the GC heap: the operations of its callable and the box that
// holds what it captured. A function cell holds only a handle to its entry, so the cell holds no pointer at all.
class GC_API FunctionTable : private ExternalEntityTable {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(FunctionTable);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(FunctionTable);

public:
    // A box this small is kept in its entry, which saves allocating one for most functions.
    static constexpr size_t inline_box_capacity = 48;
    static constexpr size_t box_alignment = 16;

    struct Slot {
        FunctionOperations const* operations { nullptr };
        void* box { nullptr };
        alignas(box_alignment) u8 inline_box[inline_box_capacity];
    };
    static_assert(sizeof(Slot) == 64);

    struct Allocation {
        FunctionTableHandle handle;
        void* box { nullptr };
    };

    FunctionTable() = default;

    // Reserves an entry with room for a box of box_size bytes, which the caller then constructs in place. The box keeps
    // its address until the entry is freed, also while the table grows, as a callable may make functions as it runs.
    ALWAYS_INLINE Allocation allocate(FunctionOperations const& operations, size_t box_size)
    {
        auto handle = allocate_entry(tag);
        if (handle.index == m_chunks.size() * slots_per_chunk)
            m_chunks.append(make<Chunk>());
        auto& slot = slot_at(handle.index);
        slot.operations = &operations;
        if (box_size == 0)
            slot.box = nullptr;
        else if (box_size <= inline_box_capacity)
            slot.box = slot.inline_box;
        else
            slot.box = kmalloc(box_size);
        VERIFY(!box_size || slot.box);
        return { handle, slot.box };
    }

    ALWAYS_INLINE Slot const& slot(FunctionTableHandle handle) const
    {
        VERIFY(is_valid(handle, tag));
        return const_cast<FunctionTable&>(*this).slot_at(handle.index);
    }

    // Releases the entry of a function whose box has been destroyed.
    ALWAYS_INLINE void free(FunctionTableHandle handle)
    {
        VERIFY(is_valid(handle, tag));
        auto& slot = slot_at(handle.index);
        if (slot.box && slot.box != slot.inline_box)
            kfree(slot.box);
        slot.operations = nullptr;
        slot.box = nullptr;
        free_entry(handle, tag);
    }

private:
    static constexpr auto tag = balanced_external_entity_table_tag(1);
    static constexpr size_t slots_per_chunk = 256;

    struct Chunk {
        AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;
        Slot slots[slots_per_chunk];
    };

    ALWAYS_INLINE Slot& slot_at(u32 index) { return m_chunks[index / slots_per_chunk]->slots[index % slots_per_chunk]; }

    Vector<NonnullOwnPtr<Chunk>> m_chunks;
};

}

namespace GC {

static constexpr size_t GC_MIN_BYTES_THRESHOLD { 32 * 1024 * 1024 };

// The share of running time we want to spend collecting. A cycle costs its mark and sweep time and lasts as long as it
// takes to allocate its budget, so meeting this share takes a budget of allocation_rate * cost * (1 - u) / u.
static constexpr double GC_TARGET_TIME_FRACTION { 0.1 };

// A heap that allocates steadily is collected from the idle timer once its garbage reaches this share of its live
// size (or GC_MIN_BYTES_THRESHOLD, whichever is more), well before the allocation threshold. Nobody waits for those
// collections, but they are not free either, so marking for them may take at most GC_STEADY_TIME_FRACTION of the
// running time. See idle_gc_on_timer().
static constexpr double GC_STEADY_GROWTH_FACTOR { 0.25 };
static constexpr double GC_STEADY_TIME_FRACTION { 0.02 };

// Growth factors relative to live cell bytes. The minimum lets the heap triple between collections, which is where a
// page that allocates slowly ends up. A lower minimum would save more memory, but marking pauses the page for as long
// as it takes to mark everything alive, and it would do so more often while the page is busy.
static constexpr double GC_MIN_GROWTH_FACTOR { 2 };
static constexpr double GC_MAX_GROWTH_FACTOR { 8 };

// The maximum factor goes down to the minimum as the live heap, counting the memory its cells own outside it, grows
// from the first size to the second. Letting a large heap grow by the maximum factor would add gigabytes of garbage.
static constexpr size_t GC_LARGE_HEAP_START_BYTES { 128 * 1024 * 1024 };
static constexpr size_t GC_LARGE_HEAP_END_BYTES { 512 * 1024 * 1024 };

// OPTIMIZATION: A program that allocates fast and keeps little alive gains from a budget far above the maximum factor,
//               so the maximum never limits a budget below this.
static constexpr size_t GC_MAX_BUDGET_FLOOR_BYTES { 256 * 1024 * 1024 };

// NB: Memory that cells own outside the heap (array buffer contents, decoded images) is mostly large, long-lived data,
//     and allocating more cells does not grow it. Letting it grow the threshold by the growth factor makes a page with
//     1 GiB of such memory allocate gigabytes of cells between collections, so it only grows the threshold by a tenth.
static constexpr size_t GC_EXTERNAL_GROWTH_FACTOR_NUMERATOR { 1 };
static constexpr size_t GC_EXTERNAL_GROWTH_FACTOR_DENOMINATOR { 10 };

// The share of the threshold that may be allocated before the sweep that follows a collection has to be done. Until a
// block is swept, its dead cells keep their slots and whatever memory they own outside the heap, and a program that
// keeps the event loop busy gives the sweep timer no chance to run, so allocation pays for the sweep as it goes.
static constexpr size_t GC_SWEEP_ALLOCATION_SHARE_DENOMINATOR { 4 };

static constexpr int GC_INCREMENTAL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 16;
static constexpr int GC_INCREMENTAL_SWEEP_SLICE_MS = 5;

// The idle GC timer ticks at this interval while the mutator is allocating; IdleCollectionPolicy decides on each tick
// whether to proactively collect. See idle_gc_on_timer().
static constexpr int GC_IDLE_GC_INTERVAL_MS = 4000;

// The shortest time from hearing of an abandoned object graph to collecting it. Whatever replaces the graph, like the
// next page, gets this long to settle, and a burst of abandoned graphs, like closing a window of tabs, shares one
// collection.
static constexpr int GC_ABANDONED_OBJECT_GRAPH_MIN_DELAY_MS = 1000;

// How long after a collection the thread gives the memory that its allocator holds back to the system, unless another
// collection comes first. The allocator only looks for memory to give back when the thread allocates, so what an idle
// thread freed, or what other threads freed of its memory, would stay. The delay keeps this away from a thread that is
// busy, and leaves time for the work that a collection starts on other threads, like compressing source text.
static constexpr int GC_ALLOCATOR_MEMORY_RELEASE_DELAY_MS = 5000;

// Compaction moves at most this many bytes of cells per collection. Moving cells out of nearly empty blocks costs about
// 3 ms per MiB on a desktop machine, half of it to copy the cells and take their new slots, and half to rewrite what
// points at them. Only a heap that went quiet compacts, so nobody waits for the pause, and as the emptiest blocks go
// first, a budget like this one frees most of what can be freed in one collection.
static constexpr size_t GC_COMPACTION_BUDGET_BYTES { 8 * MiB };

// A heap that went quiet compacts in collections of their own, one after another, as long as each frees at least this
// much and at least this much is left to recover.
// NB: While a page is busy, the holes that compaction would close are the room that the page fills again before the
//     next collection, which comes after GC_MIN_BYTES_THRESHOLD of allocation at least. Compacting then frees blocks
//     that the page needs again a few seconds later. Once the page is quiet, the heap would keep its holes for good.
static constexpr size_t GC_COMPACTION_MIN_RECOVERABLE_BYTES { 1 * MiB };

// Every thread that runs a VM has a heap of its own, and all but the main thread may come and go.
AK_TLS_INITIAL_EXEC static thread_local constinit Heap* s_the = nullptr;

namespace {

// LIBGC_LOG_LEVEL controls how much detail collect_garbage() prints:
//   0 (default) - silent.
//   1           - per-GC report with totals and per-phase timing breakdown.
//   2+          - everything in level 1, plus a full block allocator dump.
i32 read_libgc_log_level()
{
    char const* env = getenv("LIBGC_LOG_LEVEL");
    if (!env || !*env)
        return 0;
    return atoi(env);
}

i32 libgc_log_level()
{
    static i32 const level = read_libgc_log_level();
    return level;
}

// LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING=1 has every collection that may move cells (one that does not scan the stack) evacuate every
// block of cells defined outside of C++, moving each cell that can move to another slot. This tests that moving cells
// is safe, and its report tells what keeps cells from moving.
bool libgc_move_everything()
{
    static bool const value = [] {
        char const* env = getenv("LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING");
        return env && *env && atoi(env) != 0;
    }();
    return value;
}

// LIBGC_COMPACT=0 turns compaction off, so that collections never move cells unless LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING asks them to.
bool libgc_compact()
{
    static bool const value = [] {
        char const* env = getenv("LIBGC_COMPACT");
        return !env || !*env || atoi(env) != 0;
    }();
    return value;
}

}

// What a collection that moves cells did, for its report.
struct CompactionStats {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    enum PinReason : u8 {
        ByValueEdge,
        ByValueRoot,
        NonMovableAllocator,
        PinReasonCount,
    };

    struct Counts {
        size_t cells { 0 };
        size_t bytes { 0 };

        void add(size_t cell_size)
        {
            ++cells;
            bytes += cell_size;
        }
    };

    bool active { false };
    size_t evacuated_blocks { 0 };
    // The evacuated blocks that no cell stays in, which the sweep that follows lets go of.
    size_t freed_blocks { 0 };
    // What selection expected to recover and move, see rust_gc_compaction_select().
    size_t recoverable_bytes { 0 };
    size_t bytes_to_move { 0 };
    // The blocks that compaction could have freed as well, but that would have gone over the budget.
    size_t blocks_left_by_budget { 0 };
    Counts moved;
    Array<Counts, PinReasonCount> pinned;
    size_t recorded_slots { 0 };
    size_t rewritten_slots { 0 };
    i64 select_us { 0 };
    i64 copy_us { 0 };
    i64 fix_up_us { 0 };
    i64 release_us { 0 };
    HashMap<ByteString, Array<Counts, PinReasonCount>> pinned_by_type;
};

namespace {

// Per-phase timings recorded during a single collect_garbage() call. We keep
// these per thread (instead of threading more parameters through the GC's
// internal helpers) since a heap only collects on its own thread, guarded by
// m_collecting_garbage.
struct PhaseTimings {
    // Top-level phases.
    i64 gather_roots_us { 0 };
    i64 mark_live_cells_us { 0 };
    i64 finalize_unmarked_cells_us { 0 };
    i64 sweep_weak_blocks_us { 0 };
    i64 prune_weak_containers_us { 0 };
    i64 sweep_callbacks_us { 0 };
    i64 sweep_dead_cells_us { 0 };

    // gather_roots() subphases.
    i64 gather_embedder_roots_us { 0 };
    i64 gather_conservative_roots_us { 0 };
    i64 gather_explicit_roots_us { 0 };

    // gather_conservative_roots() subphases.
    i64 conservative_register_scan_us { 0 };
    i64 conservative_stack_scan_us { 0 };
    i64 conservative_cell_lookup_us { 0 };

    // mark_live_cells() subphases.
    i64 mark_initial_visit_us { 0 };
    i64 mark_bfs_us { 0 };
    i64 mark_clear_uprooted_us { 0 };
    size_t mark_threads { 0 };

    // sweep_dead_cells() subphases. Only populated for CollectEverything;
    // normal collections defer sweep to the incremental sweeper.
    i64 sweep_block_iteration_us { 0 };
    i64 sweep_block_reclassify_us { 0 };
    i64 sweep_update_threshold_us { 0 };
};
thread_local PhaseTimings g_phase_timings;

// Stats gathered during sweep_dead_cells() and consumed by the report printer
// in collect_garbage().
struct SweepStats {
    size_t collected_cells { 0 };
    size_t live_cells { 0 };
    size_t collected_cell_bytes { 0 };
    size_t live_cell_bytes { 0 };
    size_t live_external_bytes { 0 };
    size_t freed_block_count { 0 };
};
thread_local SweepStats g_sweep_stats;

struct IncrementalSweepBatchStats {
    size_t blocks_swept { 0 };
    i64 elapsed_us { 0 };
    bool forced { false };
};

struct IncrementalSweepStats {
    bool should_report { false };
    size_t total_blocks { 0 };
    Vector<IncrementalSweepBatchStats> batches;
    Core::ElapsedTimer timer { Core::TimerType::Precise };
};

IncrementalSweepStats& incremental_sweep_stats()
{
    // NB: Free each thread's batches when that thread exits.
#ifdef AK_COMPILER_CLANG
    AK_IGNORE_DIAGNOSTIC("-Wexit-time-destructors", static thread_local IncrementalSweepStats stats)
#else
    static thread_local IncrementalSweepStats stats;
#endif
    return stats;
}

thread_local bool g_next_incremental_sweep_should_report { false };

// What started the collection in progress, for its report.
thread_local CollectionTrigger g_collection_trigger { CollectionTrigger::Explicit };

StringView collection_trigger_name(CollectionTrigger trigger)
{
    switch (trigger) {
    case CollectionTrigger::Explicit:
        return "explicit"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::Allocation:
        return "allocation"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::IdlePolicy:
        return "idle policy"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::SteadyBudget:
        return "steady budget"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::AbandonedObjectGraph:
        return "abandoned object graph"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::Compaction:
        return "compaction"sv;
    case CollectionTrigger::DeferralEnded:
        return "deferral ended"sv;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

// Set by collect_garbage() while a reported collection is in flight. Used by
// the GC's helpers to decide whether they should record subphase timings.
thread_local bool g_recording_phase_timings { false };

void print_compaction_summary(CompactionStats const& stats)
{
    auto pinned_bytes = [&](CompactionStats::PinReason reason) { return human_readable_size(stats.pinned[reason].bytes); };
    dbgln("Compaction: {} source blocks, {} freed; moved {} of {} expected; pinned {} by edge, {} by root, {} non-movable; {} recoverable before; {} slots recorded, {} rewritten; select {} us, compaction {} us (copy {}, fix up {}, release {})",
        stats.evacuated_blocks, stats.freed_blocks, human_readable_size(stats.moved.bytes), human_readable_size(stats.bytes_to_move),
        pinned_bytes(CompactionStats::ByValueEdge), pinned_bytes(CompactionStats::ByValueRoot),
        pinned_bytes(CompactionStats::NonMovableAllocator),
        human_readable_size(stats.recoverable_bytes), stats.recorded_slots, stats.rewritten_slots, stats.select_us,
        stats.select_us + stats.copy_us + stats.fix_up_us + stats.release_us, stats.copy_us, stats.fix_up_us, stats.release_us);
}

void print_gc_report(i64 total_us, size_t live_block_count, bool scan_stack, size_t marked_cell_bytes, u64 allocated_bytes, CompactionStats const& stats)
{
    auto const& t = g_phase_timings;
    auto const& s = g_sweep_stats;

    auto pct = [&](i64 part_us) -> double {
        if (total_us <= 0)
            return 0.0;
        return 100.0 * static_cast<double>(part_us) / static_cast<double>(total_us);
    };

    dbgln("Garbage collection report");
    dbgln("=================================================================");
    dbgln("Totals:");
    dbgln("       Time spent: {} us", total_us);
    dbgln("     Stack scanned: {}", scan_stack ? "yes"sv : "no"sv);
    dbgln("          Trigger: {}", collection_trigger_name(g_collection_trigger));
    dbgln("     Marked cells: {}", human_readable_size(marked_cell_bytes));
    dbgln("  Allocated since: {}", human_readable_size(allocated_bytes));
    dbgln("       Live cells: {} ({})", s.live_cells, human_readable_size(s.live_cell_bytes));
    dbgln("    Live external: {}", human_readable_size(s.live_external_bytes));
    dbgln("  Collected cells: {} ({})", s.collected_cells, human_readable_size(s.collected_cell_bytes));
    dbgln("      Live blocks: {} ({})", live_block_count, human_readable_size(live_block_count * HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE));
    dbgln("     Freed blocks: {} ({})", s.freed_block_count, human_readable_size(s.freed_block_count * HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE));
    dbgln("");
    dbgln("Phase breakdown (us, % of total):");
    dbgln("  gather_roots                  {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.gather_roots_us, pct(t.gather_roots_us));
    dbgln("    embedder roots              {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.gather_embedder_roots_us, pct(t.gather_embedder_roots_us));
    dbgln("    conservative roots          {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.gather_conservative_roots_us, pct(t.gather_conservative_roots_us));
    dbgln("      register scan             {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.conservative_register_scan_us, pct(t.conservative_register_scan_us));
    dbgln("      stack scan                {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.conservative_stack_scan_us, pct(t.conservative_stack_scan_us));
    dbgln("      cell lookup               {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.conservative_cell_lookup_us, pct(t.conservative_cell_lookup_us));
    dbgln("    explicit roots              {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.gather_explicit_roots_us, pct(t.gather_explicit_roots_us));
    dbgln("  mark_live_cells               {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.mark_live_cells_us, pct(t.mark_live_cells_us));
    dbgln("    clear uprooted              {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.mark_clear_uprooted_us, pct(t.mark_clear_uprooted_us));
    dbgln("    initial visit               {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.mark_initial_visit_us, pct(t.mark_initial_visit_us));
    dbgln("    BFS marking                 {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.mark_bfs_us, pct(t.mark_bfs_us));
    dbgln("      marking threads           {:>10}", t.mark_threads);
    dbgln("  finalize_unmarked_cells       {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.finalize_unmarked_cells_us, pct(t.finalize_unmarked_cells_us));
    dbgln("  sweep_weak_blocks             {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_weak_blocks_us, pct(t.sweep_weak_blocks_us));
    dbgln("  prune_weak_containers         {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.prune_weak_containers_us, pct(t.prune_weak_containers_us));
    dbgln("  sweep_callbacks               {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_callbacks_us, pct(t.sweep_callbacks_us));
    if (t.sweep_dead_cells_us > 0) {
        dbgln("  sweep_dead_cells              {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_dead_cells_us, pct(t.sweep_dead_cells_us));
        dbgln("    block iteration             {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_block_iteration_us, pct(t.sweep_block_iteration_us));
        dbgln("    block reclassify            {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_block_reclassify_us, pct(t.sweep_block_reclassify_us));
        dbgln("    update threshold            {:>10} us ({:>5.1f}%)", t.sweep_update_threshold_us, pct(t.sweep_update_threshold_us));
    }
    if (stats.active) {
        auto print_counts = [](StringView label, CompactionStats::Counts const& counts) {
            dbgln("  {:<27} {:>10} cells ({})", label, counts.cells, human_readable_size(counts.bytes));
        };
        dbgln("");
        dbgln("Compaction:");
        dbgln("  evacuated blocks            {:>10}", stats.evacuated_blocks);
        dbgln("  freed blocks                {:>10}", stats.freed_blocks);
        print_counts("moved"sv, stats.moved);
        print_counts("pinned: by-value edge"sv, stats.pinned[CompactionStats::ByValueEdge]);
        print_counts("pinned: by-value root"sv, stats.pinned[CompactionStats::ByValueRoot]);
        print_counts("pinned: non-movable type"sv, stats.pinned[CompactionStats::NonMovableAllocator]);
        dbgln("  recorded slots              {:>10}", stats.recorded_slots);
        dbgln("  rewritten slots             {:>10}", stats.rewritten_slots);
        dbgln("  select                      {:>10} us", stats.select_us);
        dbgln("  copy                        {:>10} us", stats.copy_us);
        dbgln("  fix up                      {:>10} us", stats.fix_up_us);
        dbgln("  release                     {:>10} us", stats.release_us);
        if (!stats.pinned_by_type.is_empty()) {
            struct Entry {
                ByteString name;
                Array<CompactionStats::Counts, CompactionStats::PinReasonCount> counts;
                size_t bytes;
            };
            Vector<Entry> entries;
            for (auto const& it : stats.pinned_by_type) {
                size_t bytes = 0;
                for (auto const& counts : it.value)
                    bytes += counts.bytes;
                entries.append({ it.key, it.value, bytes });
            }
            quick_sort(entries, [](auto const& a, auto const& b) { return a.bytes > b.bytes; });
            dbgln("  top types by pinned bytes (edge / root / non-movable):");
            for (size_t i = 0; i < min<size_t>(entries.size(), 25); ++i) {
                auto const& entry = entries[i];
                dbgln("    {:<40} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10}", entry.name,
                    human_readable_size(entry.counts[CompactionStats::ByValueEdge].bytes),
                    human_readable_size(entry.counts[CompactionStats::ByValueRoot].bytes),
                    human_readable_size(entry.counts[CompactionStats::NonMovableAllocator].bytes));
            }
        }
    }
    dbgln("=================================================================");
}

void record_incremental_sweep_batch(size_t blocks_swept, i64 elapsed_us, bool forced)
{
    if (!incremental_sweep_stats().should_report || blocks_swept == 0)
        return;
    incremental_sweep_stats().batches.append({
        .blocks_swept = blocks_swept,
        .elapsed_us = elapsed_us,
        .forced = forced,
    });
}

void print_incremental_sweep_report(size_t live_cell_bytes, size_t live_external_bytes, size_t next_gc_bytes_threshold)
{
    if (!incremental_sweep_stats().should_report)
        return;

    size_t swept_blocks = 0;
    i64 batch_time_us = 0;
    i64 shortest_batch_us = NumericLimits<i64>::max();
    i64 longest_batch_us = 0;
    for (auto const& batch : incremental_sweep_stats().batches) {
        swept_blocks += batch.blocks_swept;
        batch_time_us += batch.elapsed_us;
        shortest_batch_us = min(shortest_batch_us, batch.elapsed_us);
        longest_batch_us = max(longest_batch_us, batch.elapsed_us);
    }

    if (incremental_sweep_stats().batches.is_empty())
        shortest_batch_us = 0;

    dbgln("Incremental sweep report");
    dbgln("=================================================================");
    dbgln("Totals:");
    dbgln("        Wall time: {} us", incremental_sweep_stats().timer.elapsed_time().to_microseconds());
    dbgln("       Batch time: {} us", batch_time_us);
    dbgln("          Batches: {}", incremental_sweep_stats().batches.size());
    dbgln("    Swept blocks: {} / {} ({})", swept_blocks, incremental_sweep_stats().total_blocks, human_readable_size(swept_blocks * HeapBlock::BLOCK_SIZE));
    dbgln("     Live cells: {}", human_readable_size(live_cell_bytes));
    dbgln("  Live external: {}", human_readable_size(live_external_bytes));
    dbgln("  Next threshold: {}", human_readable_size(next_gc_bytes_threshold));
    dbgln("");
    dbgln("Batch timings:");
    dbgln("  Shortest batch: {} us", shortest_batch_us);
    dbgln("   Longest batch: {} us", longest_batch_us);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < incremental_sweep_stats().batches.size(); ++i) {
        auto const& batch = incremental_sweep_stats().batches[i];
        dbgln("    #{:>3}: {:>5} blocks in {:>8} us{}", i + 1, batch.blocks_swept, batch.elapsed_us, batch.forced ? " (forced)"sv : ""sv);
    }
    dbgln("=================================================================");
}

class ScopedPhaseTimer {
public:
    ScopedPhaseTimer(bool enabled, i64& out_microseconds)
        : m_out_microseconds(out_microseconds)
        , m_enabled(enabled)
    {
        if (m_enabled)
            m_timer.start();
    }
    ~ScopedPhaseTimer()
