    auto blocks_due = static_cast<size_t>(static_cast<double>(m_blocks_to_sweep) * static_cast<double>(allocated) / static_cast<double>(allowance));
    // NB: Once every block is due, the sweep goes on until it finds nothing left to sweep, which finishes it.
    auto is_ahead = [&] { return m_blocks_swept >= blocks_due && blocks_due < m_blocks_to_sweep; };
    if (is_ahead())
        return;

    size_t blocks_swept = 0;
    auto start_time = MonotonicTime::now();
    while (!is_ahead()) {
        if (sweep_next_block()) {
            record_incremental_sweep_batch(blocks_swept, (MonotonicTime::now() - start_time).to_microseconds(), false);
            finish_incremental_sweep();
            return;
        }
        ++blocks_swept;
    }
    record_incremental_sweep_batch(blocks_swept, (MonotonicTime::now() - start_time).to_microseconds(), false);
}

void Heap::start_incremental_sweep_timer()
{
    if (!m_incremental_sweep_timer) {
        m_incremental_sweep_timer = Core::Timer::create_repeating(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_INCREMENTAL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS), [this] {
            sweep_on_timer();
        });
    }
    m_incremental_sweep_timer->start();
}

void Heap::stop_incremental_sweep_timer()
{
    if (m_incremental_sweep_timer)
        m_incremental_sweep_timer->stop();
}

void Heap::sweep_on_timer()
{
    if (!m_incremental_sweep_active)
        return;

    if (is_gc_deferred())
        return;

    size_t blocks_swept = 0;
    bool finished_sweep = false;
    auto start_time = MonotonicTime::now();
    auto deadline = start_time + AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_INCREMENTAL_SWEEP_SLICE_MS);
    while (MonotonicTime::now() < deadline) {
        if (sweep_next_block()) {
            auto elapsed = MonotonicTime::now() - start_time;
            record_incremental_sweep_batch(blocks_swept, elapsed.to_microseconds(), false);
            finish_incremental_sweep();
            finished_sweep = true;
            break;
        }
        ++blocks_swept;
    }

    if (blocks_swept > 0 && !finished_sweep) {
        auto elapsed = MonotonicTime::now() - start_time;
        record_incremental_sweep_batch(blocks_swept, elapsed.to_microseconds(), false);
        dbgln_if(INCREMENTAL_SWEEP_DEBUG, "[sweep] Timer slice: {} blocks in {}ms",
            blocks_swept, elapsed.to_milliseconds());
    }
}

void Heap::start_idle_gc_timer()
{
    if (!m_idle_gc_timer) {
        m_idle_gc_timer = Core::Timer::create_repeating(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_IDLE_GC_INTERVAL_MS), [this] {
            idle_gc_on_timer();
        });
    }
    m_idle_collection_policy.reset(m_total_allocated_bytes);
    m_idle_gc_timer->start();
}

void Heap::idle_gc_on_timer()
{
    // Leave an in-progress incremental sweep alone; it is already reclaiming memory. A GC deferral means now is not a
    // safe time to collect. In both cases we reconsider on the next tick.
    if (m_incremental_sweep_active || is_gc_deferred())
        return;

    // NB: Only a heap whose outermost event loop turns hold no cells ever runs a collection that moves them, so no other
    //     heap looks for blocks to compact.
    bool may_reduce_memory = libgc_compact() && !m_moves_everything && m_outermost_event_loop_turn_holds_no_cells;
    IdleCollectionPolicy::SteadyBudget steady_budget {
        .bytes = max(static_cast<size_t>(static_cast<double>(m_marked_cell_bytes) * GC_STEADY_GROWTH_FACTOR), GC_MIN_BYTES_THRESHOLD),
        .ns_since_last_collection = MonotonicTime::now().nanoseconds() - m_last_collection_end_ns,
        .min_ns_between_collections = static_cast<i64>(static_cast<double>(m_mark_duration_ns) * (1 - GC_STEADY_TIME_FRACTION) / GC_STEADY_TIME_FRACTION),
    };
    auto decision = m_idle_collection_policy.evaluate(m_total_allocated_bytes, m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc, m_gc_bytes_threshold, steady_budget);
    switch (decision) {
    case IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision::KeepWaiting:
        // NB: A heap that went quiet with little garbage still has the holes that its last sweep left, which
        //     compacting collections close.
        if (may_reduce_memory && !m_compacted_since_activity && m_idle_collection_policy.last_tick_was_quiet()
            && !Core::ThreadEventQueue::current().has_pending_events()) {
            m_reducing_memory = true;
            schedule_compaction_if_worthwhile();
        }
        return;
    case IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision::Park:
        // Nothing left to collect; the next allocation will re-arm the timer.
        m_idle_gc_timer->stop();
        return;
    case IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision::Collect:
    case IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision::CollectSteadyBudget:
        // NB: Whatever the event loop has queued, like input or a task, goes first, and the next tick looks again.
        //     What has not reached the queue yet, like a message still in its socket, waits for the collection. It
        //     waits for one tick at most, so that a queue that is never empty does not hold off the collection and the
        //     watchdog for good.
        if (!m_idle_collection_postponed && Core::ThreadEventQueue::current().has_pending_events()) {
            m_idle_collection_postponed = true;
            return;
        }
        // A heap that went quiet gives back what it can, compacting after this collection, see
        // schedule_compaction_if_worthwhile().
        m_reducing_memory = may_reduce_memory && m_idle_collection_policy.last_tick_was_quiet();
        m_compacted_since_activity = false;
        m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc = 0;
        collect_garbage_from_timer(decision == IdleCollectionPolicy::Decision::Collect ? CollectionTrigger::IdlePolicy : CollectionTrigger::SteadyBudget);
        m_idle_gc_timer->stop();
        return;
    }
}

void Heap::limit_gc_bytes_threshold_for_abandoned_object_graph()
{
    // The threshold came from a live size that still counts the abandoned objects. Left alone, whatever comes next
    // could allocate that whole budget on top of them.
    m_gc_bytes_threshold = min(m_gc_bytes_threshold, m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc + GC_MIN_BYTES_THRESHOLD);
}

void Heap::did_abandon_object_graph()
{
    VERIFY(is_on_owner_thread());
    limit_gc_bytes_threshold_for_abandoned_object_graph();

    if (m_abandoned_object_graph_state == AbandonedObjectGraphState::WaitingToCollect)
        return;
    m_abandoned_object_graph_state = AbandonedObjectGraphState::WaitingToCollect;

    if (!m_abandoned_object_graph_timer) {
        m_abandoned_object_graph_timer = Core::Timer::create_single_shot(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_ABANDONED_OBJECT_GRAPH_MIN_DELAY_MS), [this] {
            on_abandoned_object_graph_timer();
        });
    }

    // Marking pauses everything, so a heap that is expensive to mark waits longer. After this long, one marking pause
    // makes up the share of running time we want to spend collecting.
    auto marking_cost_budget_ns = static_cast<double>(m_mark_duration_ns) * (1 - GC_TARGET_TIME_FRACTION) / GC_TARGET_TIME_FRACTION;
    m_abandoned_object_graph_timer->restart(max(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_ABANDONED_OBJECT_GRAPH_MIN_DELAY_MS), AK::Duration::from_nanoseconds(static_cast<i64>(marking_cost_budget_ns))));
}

void Heap::on_abandoned_object_graph_timer()
{
    if (m_abandoned_object_graph_state == AbandonedObjectGraphState::WaitingToReleaseMemory) {
        m_abandoned_object_graph_state = AbandonedObjectGraphState::None;
        ak_kmalloc_collect();
        return;
    }

    // A collection now would have to finish the sweep in one go, and a deferral means now is not a safe time to
    // collect.
    if (m_incremental_sweep_active || is_gc_deferred()) {
        m_abandoned_object_graph_timer->restart();
        return;
    }

    m_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc = 0;
    collect_garbage_from_timer(CollectionTrigger::AbandonedObjectGraph);
}

void Heap::collect_garbage_from_timer(CollectionTrigger trigger)
{
    TemporaryChange trigger_change { g_collection_trigger, trigger };
    // A timer fires from the event loop. In its outermost turn the only frames on the stack are the event loop's and the
    // embedder's, so if the embedder vouches for its own, there is no root to find there. Words that only look like a
    // cell pointer are still there, and some never change, so scanning them could keep a cell alive for good. A nested
    // event loop has its caller's frames further up the stack, and those need the scan.
    if (m_outermost_event_loop_turn_holds_no_cells && !Core::ThreadEventQueue::current().is_processing_nested()) {
        collect_garbage_without_scanning_the_stack();
        return;
    }
    collect_garbage();
}

void Heap::collect_garbage_and_return_memory_to_system()
{
    // NB: A collection that has to wait for a deferral to end still lets go of as much as this one would. What it
    //     frees goes back to the system some seconds later, as after any other collection.
    if (is_gc_deferred()) {
        m_should_gc_when_deferral_ends = true;
        m_should_return_memory_when_deferral_ends = true;
        return;
    }
    {
        TemporaryChange change { m_is_returning_memory_to_system, true };
        collect_garbage();
        finish_pending_incremental_sweep();
    }
    for (auto& allocator : m_all_cell_allocators)
        allocator.block_allocator().return_freed_blocks_to_system();
    ak_kmalloc_collect();
}

void Heap::schedule_release_of_abandoned_object_graph_memory()
{
    // NB: A timer, since a sweep can finish in the middle of any allocation, and the allocator can't be collected from
    //     everywhere.
    m_abandoned_object_graph_timer->restart(AK::Duration::zero());
}

void Heap::schedule_release_of_allocator_memory()
{
    if (!m_allocator_memory_release_timer) {
        m_allocator_memory_release_timer = Core::Timer::create_single_shot(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(GC_ALLOCATOR_MEMORY_RELEASE_DELAY_MS), [] {
            ak_kmalloc_collect();
            FFI::rust_gc_marker_release_unused_helper_memory();
        });
    }
    m_allocator_memory_release_timer->restart();
}

void Heap::defer_gc()
{
    ++m_gc_deferrals;
}

void Heap::undefer_gc()
{
    VERIFY(m_gc_deferrals > 0);
    --m_gc_deferrals;

    if (m_gc_deferrals || !m_should_gc_when_deferral_ends)
        return;

    // NB: A destructor that a block sweep runs can end a deferral of its own, e.g. the one around constructing a cell
    //     it allocates. For the reason will_allocate() gives, no collection may start there, so the request waits for
    //     a deferral that ends outside the sweep.
    if (m_block_sweeps_in_progress > 0)
        return;

    {
        TemporaryChange change { m_is_returning_memory_to_system, m_should_return_memory_when_deferral_ends };
        TemporaryChange trigger { g_collection_trigger, CollectionTrigger::DeferralEnded };
        collect_garbage();
    }
    m_should_gc_when_deferral_ends = false;
    m_should_return_memory_when_deferral_ends = false;
}

void Heap::uproot_cell(Cell* cell)
{
    m_uprooted_cells.append(cell);
}

WeakImpl* Heap::create_weak_impl(void* ptr)
{
    // Once weak pointers to dead cells have been cleared, one that is created to a dead cell, e.g. by a finalizer of
    // this or another heap, must be null as well, or nothing would clear it before the cell is swept.
    if (m_weak_pointers_to_dead_cells_are_cleared && !static_cast<Cell*>(ptr)->is_marked())
        return &WeakImpl::the_null_weak_impl;

    if (m_usable_weak_blocks.is_empty()) {
        auto* weak_block = WeakBlock::create();
        m_usable_weak_blocks.append(*weak_block);
    }

    auto* weak_block = m_usable_weak_blocks.first();
    auto* new_weak_impl = weak_block->allocate(static_cast<Cell*>(ptr));
    if (!weak_block->can_allocate()) {
        m_full_weak_blocks.append(*weak_block);
    }

    return new_weak_impl;
}

}

#pragma once

#include <AK/Badge.h>
#include <AK/Function.h>
#include <AK/HashTable.h>
#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/NonnullOwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>

#include <AK/RefPtr.h>
#include <AK/StackInfo.h>

#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibCore/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/CrossHeapMember.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/FunctionTable.h>

namespace GC {

// What started a collection, for its report.
enum class CollectionTrigger : u8 {
    Explicit,
    Allocation,
    IdlePolicy,
    SteadyBudget,
    AbandonedObjectGraph,
    Compaction,
    DeferralEnded,
};

struct CompactionStats;

namespace FFI {

struct EvacuationSet;
struct IdentityHashes;

}

struct StackFrameInfo {
    String label;
    size_t size_bytes { 0 };
};

class GC_API Heap {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Heap);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Heap);

    friend class HeapGroup;

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    enum class BecomeThreadDefault {
        No,
        Yes,
    };

    explicit Heap(AK::Function<void(HashMap<Cell*, GC::HeapRoot>&)> gather_embedder_roots, BecomeThreadDefault = BecomeThreadDefault::Yes);
    ~Heap();

    // The default heap of the calling thread.
    static Heap& the();
    static void set_default_heap_for_testing(Heap&);

    template<typename T, typename... Args>
    Ref<T> allocate(Args&&... args)
    {
        return construct_cell<T>(allocate_cell<T>(), forward<Args>(args)...);
    }

    // Like allocate(), but takes the cell from the given allocator instead of T's own. This lets one C++ type keep
    // several kinds of objects apart, each in blocks of its own.
    template<typename T, typename... Args>
    Ref<T> allocate_with_descriptor(TypeIsolatingCellAllocator<T>& descriptor, Args&&... args)
    {
        return construct_cell<T>(allocate_cell(descriptor), forward<Args>(args)...);
    }

    enum class CollectionType {
        CollectGarbage,
        CollectEverything,
    };

    // NB: NEVER_INLINE so that each entry point keeps a frame of its own: setjmp() only captures the registers as
    //     they are in the frame it runs in, and the frames below become the scan's floor. The definitions are
    //     NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS so that the capture buffer stays on the real stack rather than ASan's fake one.
    NEVER_INLINE void collect_garbage(CollectionType = CollectionType::CollectGarbage, bool print_report = false);

    // Collects garbage and gives the memory that this frees back to the system before it returns. Otherwise the sweep
    // happens bit by bit after a collection, and the freed memory goes back to the system some time after that. For a
    // process that is short of memory now.
    void collect_garbage_and_return_memory_to_system();

    // Collects without taking any root from the stack or the registers, so no stale or lookalike word there keeps a
    // cell alive. Only safe where every cell the stack refers to is rooted some other way, as in the outermost turn of
    // the event loop.
    void collect_garbage_without_scanning_the_stack();

    // Tells the heap that no frame on the stack of the outermost turn of this thread's event loop holds the only
    // reference to a cell. The collections that the heap starts from its own timers then leave the stack out when they
    // run in that turn. Only the embedder can promise this, since those frames include its own, like main().
    void set_outermost_event_loop_turn_holds_no_cells(bool value) { m_outermost_event_loop_turn_holds_no_cells = value; }
    NEVER_INLINE AK::JsonObject dump_graph();

    // A cell on a retaining path, which reaches the next one through a field it visits. The cell is live until the next
    // garbage collection at least.
    struct RetainingPathStep {
        Ptr<Cell> cell;
        StringView class_name;
    };
    struct RetainingPath {
        HeapRoot root;
        // The first step is the root cell, and the last is the target.
        Vector<RetainingPathStep> steps;
    };
    // The shortest path from a root to each reachable cell that is_target accepts, for at most max_paths of them.
    NEVER_INLINE Vector<RetainingPath> find_retaining_paths(AK::Function<bool(Cell&)> const& is_target, size_t max_paths);
    static String describe_root(HeapRoot const&);

    // A heap belongs to the thread that created it: the collector only scans that thread's stack, and nothing in the heap
    // is synchronized. That thread has to destroy it as well. Collections and destruction verify this, allocation and
    // rooting are debug assertions.
    bool is_on_owner_thread() const { return pthread_equal(m_owner_thread, pthread_self()); }

    bool should_collect_on_every_allocation() const { return m_should_collect_on_every_allocation; }
    // This is true for any CollectEverything cycle, not only heap teardown.
    bool is_collecting_everything() const { return m_collecting_garbage && m_current_collection_type == CollectionType::CollectEverything; }
    // Whether a collection that marks the live cells runs, as opposed to one that only sweeps or a graph dump.
    bool is_marking_for_collection() const { return m_collecting_garbage && m_current_collection_type == CollectionType::CollectGarbage; }

    // Whether collect_garbage_and_return_memory_to_system() runs, so that what hangs off the heap can let go of more
    // than it does in other collections.
    bool is_returning_memory_to_system() const { return m_is_returning_memory_to_system; }

    // Whether the collection in progress may move cells, which only a collection that does not scan the stack does.
    bool is_moving_cells() const { return m_evacuation; }

    // Whether LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING has every collection that does not scan the stack move every cell it can, which
    // test runners use to collect without scanning the stack where they safely can.
    static bool moves_everything();
    // Has the collections of this heap that do not scan the stack move every cell they can, or not, as
    // LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING does for every heap, for tests of moving cells.
    void set_moves_everything_for_testing(bool moves_everything) { m_moves_everything = moves_everything; }

    void set_incremental_sweep_enabled(bool enabled) { m_incremental_sweep_enabled = enabled; }
    void set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(bool);

    void did_create_root(Badge<RootImpl>, RootImpl&);
    void did_destroy_root(Badge<RootImpl>, RootImpl&);

    void did_create_root_vector(Badge<RootVectorBase>, RootVectorBase&);
    void did_destroy_root_vector(Badge<RootVectorBase>, RootVectorBase&);

    void did_create_root_hash_map(Badge<RootHashMapBase>, RootHashMapBase&);
    void did_destroy_root_hash_map(Badge<RootHashMapBase>, RootHashMapBase&);
    void did_create_root_hash_table(Badge<RootHashTableBase>, RootHashTableBase&);
    void did_destroy_root_hash_table(Badge<RootHashTableBase>, RootHashTableBase&);

    void did_create_cross_heap_member(Badge<CrossHeapMemberBase>, CrossHeapMemberBase&);
    void did_destroy_cross_heap_member(Badge<CrossHeapMemberBase>, CrossHeapMemberBase&);

    void did_create_weak_container(Badge<WeakContainer>, WeakContainer&);
    void did_destroy_weak_container(Badge<WeakContainer>, WeakContainer&);

    void enable_stats();
    void add_stats(AK::JsonObject&) const;

    // Per allocator: its blocks, its live cells and bytes, and per class the live cells and the edges to cells they
    // visit. Finishes any pending sweep first.
    AK::JsonObject census();

    void register_sweep_callback(AK::Function<void()>);

    void register_cell_allocator(Badge<CellAllocator>, CellAllocator&);

    void uproot_cell(Cell* cell);
    void uproot_cell(ForeignCell* cell) { uproot_cell(as_cell(cell)); }

    bool is_gc_deferred() const { return m_gc_deferrals > 0; }

    FunctionTable& function_table() { return m_function_table; }
    bool is_incremental_sweep_active() const { return m_incremental_sweep_active; }

    // Sweeps the block now if the incremental sweep has yet to, as the sweep timer would.
    void sweep_block(HeapBlock&);

    // Whether `cell` points at a cell of this heap that is allocated: one that the sweep did not free yet. Code that keeps
    // pointers to cells that may have died since uses this to tell them apart from live ones.
    bool is_live_cell(Cell const*) const;

    // How many blocks the heap has, for all types of cells.
    size_t block_count() const;

    void did_sweep_blocks_for_allocation(Badge<CellAllocator>, size_t swept_blocks, i64 duration_ns);

    // A sweep runs the destructors of dead cells between these, see will_allocate().
    void will_destroy_swept_cell(Badge<CellAllocator>) { ++m_block_sweeps_in_progress; }
    void did_destroy_swept_cell(Badge<CellAllocator>) { --m_block_sweeps_in_progress; }

    template<typename Callback>
    void for_each_block(Callback callback)
    {
        for (auto& allocator : m_all_cell_allocators) {
            if (allocator.for_each_block(callback) == IterationDecision::Break)
                return;
        }
    }

    void enqueue_post_gc_task(AK::Function<void()>);

    WeakImpl* create_weak_impl(void*);

    void did_allocate_external_memory(size_t);
    void did_free_external_memory(size_t);

    // Tells the heap that a large graph of objects, such as a page that went away, has likely just become garbage.
    // Nothing about allocation shows that, so this brings the next collection forward, and hands what that collection
    // frees back to the system once it has been swept. It never collects from here, since the graph is often still on
    // the caller's stack.
    void did_abandon_object_graph();

private:
    friend struct CAPI;
    friend class CellAllocator;
    friend class HeapBlock;
    friend class MarkingVisitor;
    friend class DeferGC;

    void defer_gc();
    void undefer_gc();

    void dump_allocators();
    void finish_stats_collection();

    template<typename T, typename... Args>
    Ref<T> construct_cell(Cell* memory, Args&&... args)
    {
        defer_gc();
        new (memory) T(forward<Args>(args)...);
        auto* cell = static_cast<T*>(memory);
        cell->set_cell_kind(T::cell_kind_for_class);
        mark_if_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(*cell);
        undefer_gc();
        return *cell;
    }

    CellAllocator& cell_allocator_for(CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor)
    {
        auto index = descriptor.index();
        if (index < m_cell_allocators_by_descriptor_index.size()) [[likely]] {
            if (auto* allocator = m_cell_allocators_by_descriptor_index[index].ptr()) [[likely]]
                return *allocator;
        }
        return create_cell_allocator(descriptor);
    }
    CellAllocator& create_cell_allocator(CellAllocatorDescriptorBase&);

    template<typename T>
    Cell* allocate_cell()
    {
        static_assert(requires { cell_allocator_for(T::cell_allocator).allocate_cell(*this); }, "GC cell type must declare its own allocator using GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(ClassName)");
        static_assert(IsSame<T, typename decltype(T::cell_allocator)::CellType>,
            "GC cell allocator type mismatch");

        return allocate_cell(T::cell_allocator);
    }

    // Shared by allocate<T>() and any allocation whose cell type is only known through its allocator descriptor.
    // Cells that other cells keep their storage in never collect garbage, but count towards the next collection (see
    // gc_heap_allocate_storage_cell()).
    enum class TriggersCollection {
        No,
        Yes,
    };
    Cell* allocate_cell(CellAllocatorDescriptorBase& descriptor, TriggersCollection triggers_collection = TriggersCollection::Yes)
    {
        VERIFY(!m_collecting_garbage);
        will_allocate(descriptor.cell_size(), triggers_collection);
        return cell_allocator_for(descriptor).allocate_cell(*this);
    }

    // Cells allocated during incremental sweep in a block that the sweep has yet to finish must be marked so that it
    // keeps them. Sweeping a block clears its marks once it is done, so swept and new blocks need nothing.
    void mark_if_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(Cell& cell)
    {
        if (m_incremental_sweep_active) [[unlikely]]
            mark_cell_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(cell);
    }
    void mark_cell_allocated_during_incremental_sweep(Cell&);

    // Marking makes every block pending sweep again, which local free lists
    // must never be in, so every collection does this once it has finished the
    // pending sweep, whose destructors may take new local free lists.
    void give_back_local_free_lists();

    void will_allocate(size_t, TriggersCollection = TriggersCollection::Yes);
    void update_allocation_rate();
    double next_growth_factor(size_t live_cell_bytes);
    void update_gc_bytes_threshold();
    void limit_gc_bytes_threshold_for_abandoned_object_graph();

    enum class IncludeIncomingCrossHeapMembers {
        No,
        Yes,
    };
    // Where the conservative scan starts: every frame from stack_floor up, plus the callee-saved registers as captured
    // at the entry point. The floor lands just below the entry point's frame, so the caller's registers that its
    // prologue spilled are covered by the stack scan and the ones it left alone by the capture.
    struct ConservativeScanOrigin {
        FlatPtr stack_floor { 0 };
        ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> callee_saved_registers;
        bool scan_stack { true };
    };

    // NB: NEVER_INLINE so that these stay below their entry point's frame, and so that __builtin_frame_address(0)
    //     yields a floor that leaves out their own frames -- which is what keeps the collection's large locals from
    //     being scanned.
    NEVER_INLINE void run_collection(ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> callee_saved_registers, CollectionType, bool print_report, bool scan_stack = true);
    NEVER_INLINE AK::JsonObject build_graph(ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> callee_saved_registers);
    NEVER_INLINE Vector<RetainingPath> build_retaining_paths(ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> callee_saved_registers, AK::Function<bool(Cell&)> const& is_target, size_t max_paths);

    void gather_roots(ConservativeScanOrigin const&, HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot>&, Vector<StackFrameInfo>* out_stack_frames = nullptr, IncludeIncomingCrossHeapMembers = IncludeIncomingCrossHeapMembers::Yes);
    bool should_move_cells(CollectionType, bool scan_stack) const;
    void begin_evacuation();
    void evacuate();
    void end_evacuation();
    Cell* allocate_destination_for_moved_cell(CellAllocator&);
    void schedule_collection_that_moves_cells();
    void schedule_compaction_if_worthwhile();
    static void mark_live_cells_across(ReadonlySpan<Heap* const>, HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot>& roots);
    void clear_weak_pointers_to_dead_cells(bool report);
    void run_post_mark_phases(bool report);
    void gather_conservative_roots(ConservativeScanOrigin const&, HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot>&, Vector<StackFrameInfo>* out_stack_frames = nullptr);
    void mark_live_cells(HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot>& roots);
    void finalize_unmarked_cells();

#pragma once

#include <LibGC/Export.h>

namespace GC {

// A thread that runs beside the heap's own thread, but never on its behalf, forbids itself heap access: the collector
// only scans its own thread's stack and never waits for other threads, so a cell another thread allocates, roots or
// collects is one it races with. Allocation and rooting on such a thread are debug assertions, collection is a
// verification failure.
GC_API void forbid_heap_access_on_this_thread();
GC_API bool heap_access_is_forbidden_on_this_thread();

}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2020-2024, Andreas Kling <andreas@ladybird.org>

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h>
#include <LibGC/CellAllocator.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapBlock.h>

#ifdef HAS_ADDRESS_SANITIZER
#    include <sanitizer/asan_interface.h>
#endif

namespace GC {

static_assert(HeapBlock::min_possible_cell_size >= FFI::MIN_CELL_SIZE);

FFI::BlockDescriptor* const g_block_descriptors = FFI::rust_gc_block_descriptor_table(HEAP_REGION_SIZE);

#pragma GCC diagnostic push
#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Winvalid-offsetof"
size_t HeapBlock::cells_offset()
{
    // NB: The cells start at the largest alignment that a cell may have, which is more than 16 bytes in builds for some
    //     CPUs.
    static_assert(offsetof(HeapBlock, m_storage) == round_up_to_power_of_two(112, max_cell_alignment));
    // NB: A block counts its cells from its size, and the Rust core from this offset, so the two have to match.
    static_assert(sizeof(HeapBlock) == offsetof(HeapBlock, m_storage));
    return offsetof(HeapBlock, m_storage);
}
#pragma GCC diagnostic pop

void HeapBlock::initialize(void* block, Heap& heap, CellAllocator& cell_allocator)
{
    new (block) HeapBlock(heap, cell_allocator);
}

HeapBlock::HeapBlock(Heap& heap, CellAllocator& cell_allocator)
    : HeapBlockBase(heap, cell_allocator.type_info(), cell_allocator.foreign_type())
    , m_cell_allocator(cell_allocator)
    , m_cell_size(cell_allocator.cell_size())
    , m_cell_count((BLOCK_SIZE - sizeof(HeapBlock)) / m_cell_size)
{
    VERIFY(m_cell_size >= min_possible_cell_size);
    ASAN_POISON_MEMORY_REGION(m_storage, BLOCK_SIZE - sizeof(HeapBlock));
}

bool HeapBlock::is_pending_sweep() const
{
    return block_descriptor_for(this).pending_sweep;
}

bool HeapBlock::is_being_swept() const
{
    return block_descriptor_for(this).being_swept;
}

u32 HeapBlock::allocated_cell_count() const
{
    return allocated_cell_count_of(block_descriptor_for(this));
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/HeapBlock.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2020, Andreas Kling <andreas@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#pragma once

#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/CellTypeInfo.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/Internals.h>

namespace GC {

// The header of a block of cells. LibGC's Rust core creates blocks and keeps track of which of their cells are
// allocated, in the block's descriptor, see BlockDescriptor.h. The header is only what C++ reads from a cell's block.
class GC_API HeapBlock : public HeapBlockBase {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(HeapBlock);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(HeapBlock);

public:
    using HeapBlockBase::BLOCK_SIZE;

    // Fills in the header of a block that an allocator just took.
    static void initialize(void* block, Heap&, CellAllocator&);

    size_t cell_size() const { return m_cell_size; }
    size_t cell_count() const { return m_cell_count; }

    // The offset of the link to the next cell in a free cell, and the bits of a link that count, for code that pops
    // free lists itself, see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list(). The allocator hands out runs of cells only, so the
    // lists it hands out are empty.
    static constexpr size_t freelist_next_offset();
    static constexpr FlatPtr freelist_link_mask = BLOCK_SIZE - 1;

    // How far into a block its first cell is.
    static size_t cells_offset();

    // Whether the incremental sweep has yet to sweep the block, or is
    // sweeping it right now. Cells allocated in such a block during the
    // sweep must be marked so that the sweep keeps them.
    bool is_pending_sweep() const;
    bool is_being_swept() const;

    // How many cells of the block are allocated. The cells of a run that an allocator took from the block to hand out
    // count as allocated too, see CellAllocator::LocalFreeCells.
    u32 allocated_cell_count() const;

    static HeapBlock* from_cell(Cell const* cell)
    {
        return static_cast<HeapBlock*>(HeapBlockBase::from_cell(cell));
    }

    CellAllocator& cell_allocator() { return m_cell_allocator; }

private:
    HeapBlock(Heap&, CellAllocator&);

    struct FreelistEntry final : public Cell {
        GC_CELL(FreelistEntry, Cell);

        FlatPtr next { 0 };
    };

    CellAllocator& m_cell_allocator;
    u32 m_cell_size { 0 };
    // NB: Computed once, since dividing by the cell size is slow.
    u32 m_cell_count { 0 };
    // NB: Pads the header to the size that sets how many cells of each size a block holds, see cells_offset().
    [[maybe_unused]] u8 m_reserved[72];
    [[maybe_unused]] alignas(max_cell_alignment) u8 m_storage[];

public:
    static constexpr size_t min_possible_cell_size = sizeof(FreelistEntry);
};

constexpr size_t HeapBlock::freelist_next_offset()
{
    return __builtin_offsetof(FreelistEntry, next);
}

}

template<>
inline constexpr bool AllocatedWithCustomAllocator<GC::HeapBlock> = true;

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/HeapGroup.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Ali Mohammad Pur <ali@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/TemporaryChange.h>
#include <LibCore/ElapsedTimer.h>
#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibGC/HeapGroup.h>
#include <setjmp.h>

namespace GC {

HeapGroup::~HeapGroup()
{
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->m_group = nullptr;
}

void HeapGroup::add(Heap& heap)
{
    VERIFY(!heap.m_group);
    heap.m_group = this;
    m_heaps.append(&heap);
}

void HeapGroup::remove(Heap& heap)
{
    VERIFY(heap.m_group == this);
    heap.m_group = nullptr;
    m_heaps.remove_first_matching([&](auto* entry) { return entry == &heap; });
}

NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS void HeapGroup::collect_garbage(bool print_report)
{
    jmp_buf registers;
    setjmp(registers);
    ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> captured_registers { reinterpret_cast<FlatPtr const*>(registers), sizeof(jmp_buf) / (sizeof(FlatPtr)) };
    run_collection(captured_registers, print_report);
}

void HeapGroup::run_collection(ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> callee_saved_registers, bool print_report)
{
    Heap::ConservativeScanOrigin origin {
        .stack_floor = bit_cast<FlatPtr>(__builtin_frame_address(0)),
        .callee_saved_registers = callee_saved_registers,
    };

    // Defer all member heaps' collections until the last one, so that cross-heap edges are visible to the mark phase.
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps) {
        VERIFY(!heap->m_collecting_garbage);
        if (heap->m_gc_deferrals) {
            heap->m_should_gc_when_deferral_ends = true;
            return;
        }
    }

    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->finish_pending_incremental_sweep();
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps) {
        VERIFY(!heap->is_incremental_sweep_active());
        heap->give_back_local_free_lists();
        heap->m_collecting_garbage = true;
    }
    ScopeGuard unset_collecting = [&] {
        for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
            heap->m_collecting_garbage = false;
    };

    HashMap<Cell*, HeapRoot> roots;
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->gather_roots(origin, roots, nullptr, Heap::IncludeIncomingCrossHeapMembers::No);

    Heap::mark_live_cells_across(m_heaps, roots);

    // Weak pointers may point across heaps, so clear them in every heap before any heap runs its finalizers.
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->clear_weak_pointers_to_dead_cells(print_report);
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->run_post_mark_phases(print_report);
    for (auto* heap : m_heaps)
        heap->m_weak_pointers_to_dead_cells_are_cleared = false;

    for (auto* heap : m_heaps) {
        Core::ElapsedTimer measurement_timer { Core::TimerType::Precise };
        measurement_timer.start();
        heap->sweep_dead_cells(print_report, measurement_timer);
    }
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/HeapRegion.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGC/Export.h>

namespace GC {

// 32 GiB is what a 32-bit cell offset in units of the 8-byte cell alignment can address. It is the same on every target,
// and small enough for the second region-sized reservation used to align its base to fit in the user address space of
// Sv39 RISC-V, 39-bit AArch64, and the application ranges of the sanitizers.
static constexpr size_t HEAP_REGION_SIZE = 32ull * GiB;
static_assert(is_power_of_two(HEAP_REGION_SIZE));
static constexpr size_t HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK = HEAP_REGION_SIZE - 1;

// The bottom of the region is reserved but never committed, so no cell has an offset below 4 GiB. A compressed cell
// pointer below 512 Mi then never decodes to a cell. That keeps small integers from looking like one, and also the low
// half of a pointer to memory less than 512 MiB into any mapping aligned to 4 GiB or more, such as this region itself.
// Such low halves are all over the stack, so a smaller guard has the conservative scanner keep cells alive for them.
static constexpr size_t HEAP_REGION_LOW_GUARD_SIZE = 4ull * GiB;

// The top of the region is reserved but never committed either. Decoding any offset lands inside the region, and this
// keeps a field access through the decoded address from reaching memory past the end of the reservation.
static constexpr size_t HEAP_REGION_HIGH_GUARD_SIZE = 2ull * MiB;

}

extern "C" GC_API FlatPtr js_heap_region_base;

namespace GC {

// A copy of the heap region base outside LibGC, which LibGC fills in when it reserves the region, or when the copy is
// registered if that happens later. Either way that is before any cell exists, and the base never changes after that.
// A registration lasts for the rest of the process, like the shared objects that hold them, which are never unloaded.
class GC_API HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration);

public:
    explicit HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration(FlatPtr& copy);

private:
    friend class HeapRegion;

    FlatPtr* m_copy { nullptr };
    HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration* m_next { nullptr };
};

namespace Detail {

// OPTIMIZATION: Every shared object keeps a hidden copy of the base, which a decode reads with one PC-relative load.
//               Reading js_heap_region_base from outside LibGC takes a GOT load first.
class HeapRegionBaseCopy {
public:
    FlatPtr base() const { return m_base; }

private:
    // NB: Static storage starts out zeroed, so the base is 0 until registering it fills it in, also for anything that
    //     reads it before this is constructed.
    FlatPtr m_base { 0 };
    HeapRegionBaseCopyRegistration m_registration { m_base };
};

// NB: Every translation unit that decodes includes this header, so the copy of its shared object is constructed and
//     registered before the dynamic initialization of anything that it defines after including it. No cell exists
//     before the region does, so the copy holds the base by the time anything decodes a cell pointer.
#if defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
inline HeapRegionBaseCopy heap_region_base_copy;
#else
[[gnu::visibility("hidden")]] inline HeapRegionBaseCopy heap_region_base_copy;
#endif

}

ALWAYS_INLINE FlatPtr heap_region_base()
{
    return Detail::heap_region_base_copy.base();
}

}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

#pragma once

#include <AK/NumericLimits.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>

namespace GC {

// Decides, once per idle-timer tick, whether the heap should be proactively collected. See Heap::idle_gc_on_timer().
//
// The GC heap is never completely silent in practice: event-loop housekeeping (queuing an HTML task and so on) keeps a
// small allocation trickle going even on an idle page. So instead of waiting for zero allocation, we watch for the
// mutator transitioning out of an active phase: a tick whose allocation rate has dropped below 1/low_rate_divisor of
// the peak rate seen so far this episode. The rate-drop trigger is gated on enough uncollected garbage having piled up
// to be worth marking the whole live heap. A tick that allocates next to nothing is a quiet one, which collects once
// a few MiB of garbage are there, however large the heap and its threshold: nobody waits for a quiet heap, and what
// the garbage holds goes back to the system long before the threshold would have come. The watchdog bounds how long
// garbage can sit when neither trigger fires, e.g. on a heap that allocates too slowly to clear the gates.
//
// A heap that allocates steadily never shows a quiet tick and only shows a rate drop by accident, and its allocation
// threshold can sit far above its live size. So once the garbage reaches a steady budget, we collect even though the
// mutator is still busy, as long as enough time has passed since the last collection for marking to stay a small share
// of the running time.
class IdleCollectionPolicy {
public:
    enum class Decision : u8 {
        KeepWaiting,         // No collection yet; leave the idle timer running.
        Park,                // Nothing left to collect; stop the timer until allocation resumes.
        Collect,             // Collect now.
        CollectSteadyBudget, // Collect now, because the garbage reached the steady budget.
    };

    // When a heap that keeps allocating has piled up enough garbage to collect it anyway.
    struct SteadyBudget {
        size_t bytes { NumericLimits<size_t>::max() };
        // How long it has been since the last collection, and how long it must be at least before this one.
        i64 ns_since_last_collection { 0 };
        i64 min_ns_between_collections { 0 };
    };

    // Begins a fresh episode. `total_allocated_bytes` is the heap's monotonic allocation counter.
    void reset(u64 total_allocated_bytes)
    {
        m_total_allocated_at_last_check = total_allocated_bytes;
        m_peak_delta = 0;
        m_tick_count = 0;
        m_last_tick_was_quiet = false;
    }

    // Evaluates one idle-timer tick. `total_allocated_bytes` is the monotonic allocation counter, `garbage_bytes` is
    // the amount allocated since the last collection, `gc_threshold` is the allocation-driven GC threshold, and
    // `steady_budget` says when garbage is worth collecting while the heap is still allocating.
    Decision evaluate(u64 total_allocated_bytes, size_t garbage_bytes, size_t gc_threshold, SteadyBudget steady_budget)
    {
        if (garbage_bytes == 0)
            return Decision::Park;

        auto delta = total_allocated_bytes - m_total_allocated_at_last_check;
        m_total_allocated_at_last_check = total_allocated_bytes;
        m_peak_delta = max(m_peak_delta, delta);

        bool rate_dropped = delta * low_rate_divisor < m_peak_delta;
        m_last_tick_was_quiet = delta <= quiet_tick_bytes;
        bool watchdog_elapsed = ++m_tick_count >= watchdog_ticks;
        bool enough_garbage = garbage_bytes >= gc_threshold / min_garbage_divisor;
        bool enough_garbage_for_a_quiet_heap = garbage_bytes >= quiet_min_garbage_bytes;

        if ((rate_dropped && enough_garbage) || (m_last_tick_was_quiet && enough_garbage_for_a_quiet_heap) || watchdog_elapsed)
            return Decision::Collect;
        if (garbage_bytes >= steady_budget.bytes && steady_budget.ns_since_last_collection >= steady_budget.min_ns_between_collections)
            return Decision::CollectSteadyBudget;
        return Decision::KeepWaiting;
    }

    // Evaluates one idle-timer tick for a heap that never collects on a steady budget.
    Decision evaluate(u64 total_allocated_bytes, size_t garbage_bytes, size_t gc_threshold)
    {
        return evaluate(total_allocated_bytes, garbage_bytes, gc_threshold, SteadyBudget {});
    }

    // Whether the last tick that was evaluated allocated next to nothing.
    bool last_tick_was_quiet() const { return m_last_tick_was_quiet; }

    // A tick counts as a rate drop when its allocation is below 1/low_rate_divisor of the episode's peak.
    static constexpr u64 low_rate_divisor = 4;
    // The rate-drop trigger only fires once garbage reaches gc_threshold / min_garbage_divisor.
    static constexpr size_t min_garbage_divisor = 16;
    // A tick that allocates at most this much is a quiet one, and a quiet tick collects once this much is garbage.
    static constexpr u64 quiet_tick_bytes = 1 * MiB;
    static constexpr size_t quiet_min_garbage_bytes = 2 * MiB;
    // The watchdog forces a collection after this many ticks regardless of the rate or the gate.
    static constexpr u32 watchdog_ticks = 15;

private:
    u64 m_total_allocated_at_last_check { 0 };
    u64 m_peak_delta { 0 };
    u32 m_tick_count { 0 };
    bool m_last_tick_was_quiet { false };
};

}

#include <LibGC/Forward.h>

namespace GC {

class GC_API HeapBlockBase {
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(HeapBlockBase);
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(HeapBlockBase);

public:
    static constexpr size_t BLOCK_SIZE = 16 * KiB;
    static HeapBlockBase* from_cell(Cell const* cell)
    {
        return reinterpret_cast<HeapBlockBase*>(bit_cast<FlatPtr>(cell) & ~(BLOCK_SIZE - 1));
    }

    Heap& heap() { return m_heap; }
    CellTypeInfo const& type_info() const { return *m_type_info; }

    // What the foreign implementation that created the block's allocator says the type of its cells is.
    void const* foreign_type() const { return m_foreign_type; }

protected:
    HeapBlockBase(Heap& heap, CellTypeInfo const& type_info, void const* foreign_type)
        : m_heap(heap)
        , m_type_info(&type_info)
        , m_foreign_type(foreign_type)
    {
    }

    Heap& m_heap;
    CellTypeInfo const* m_type_info { nullptr };
    void const* m_foreign_type { nullptr };

private:
    friend struct CAPI;
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/Member.h
/*

#pragma once

#include <AK/Format.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <AK/Traits.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>
#include <LibGC/CompressedPointer.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>

namespace GC {

// Member and NonnullMember are the types of cell pointers stored in cells, and in storage that cells visit. They hold a
// compressed pointer in 32 bits. Locals, parameters and return values keep using the full-width Ptr and Ref, which
// members convert to implicitly. Like Ptr and Ref, members only hand out a raw pointer through ptr().
//
// A member holds the address of the T it points to, so T must start with its cell, which the conservative scanner
// requires of a compressed pointer it finds on the stack: it only recognizes cell starts.

template<typename T>
class Member;

template<typename T>
class NonnullMember;

namespace Detail {

// Every store of a member goes through this hook, where a generational or moving collector will record the slot. It is
// empty for now, so it compiles to nothing.
ALWAYS_INLINE void member_write_barrier([[maybe_unused]] void const* slot, [[maybe_unused]] u32 compressed)
{
}

template<typename T>
ALWAYS_INLINE u32 compress_cell(T* cell)
{
    return compress(static_cast<void const*>(cell));
}

template<typename T>
concept IsMember = IsSpecializationOf<T, Member> || IsSpecializationOf<T, NonnullMember>;

}

template<typename T>
class Member {
public:
    constexpr Member() = default;

    Member(nullptr_t) { }

    Member(T* cell)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(cell))
    {
    }

    Member(T& cell)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(&cell))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(U* cell)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(U& cell)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(&cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(Ptr<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(Ref<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    // OPTIMIZATION: Constructing a member from another copies its u32 and nothing else, which also has members passed
    //               and returned in registers. Only stores into existing members go through the write barrier.
    Member(Member const&) = default;
    Member(Member&&) = default;

    template<typename U>
    Member(Member<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(NonnullMember<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(U* foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(foreign_cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(U& foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(&foreign_cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(Ptr<U> const& foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(foreign_cell.ptr())))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member(Ref<U> const& foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(foreign_cell.ptr())))
    {
    }

    Member& operator=(Member const& other)
    {
        set_compressed(other.m_compressed);
        return *this;
    }

    template<typename U>
    Member& operator=(U&& other)
    requires(requires { Member(forward<U>(other)); })
    {
        set_compressed(Member(forward<U>(other)).m_compressed);
        return *this;
    }

    T* ptr() const { return reinterpret_cast<T*>(decompress(m_compressed)); }

    RETURNS_NONNULL T* operator->() const
    {
        ASSERT(m_compressed);
        return reinterpret_cast<T*>(decompress_nonnull(m_compressed));
    }

    [[nodiscard]] T& operator*() const
    {
        ASSERT(m_compressed);
        return *reinterpret_cast<T*>(decompress_nonnull(m_compressed));
    }

    explicit operator bool() const { return m_compressed != 0; }
    bool operator!() const { return m_compressed == 0; }

    Ref<T> as_nonnull() const
    {
        VERIFY(m_compressed);
        return *reinterpret_cast<T*>(decompress_nonnull(m_compressed));
    }

    template<typename U>
    operator Ptr<U>() const
    requires(IsConvertible<T*, U*> || IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<T, U>)
    {
        return Ptr<U>(ptr());
    }

    u32 compressed() const { return m_compressed; }

private:
    template<typename U>
    friend class Member;

    ALWAYS_INLINE void set_compressed(u32 compressed)
    {
        Detail::member_write_barrier(this, compressed);
        m_compressed = compressed;
    }

    u32 m_compressed { 0 };
};

template<typename T>
class NonnullMember {
public:
    NonnullMember() = delete;

    NonnullMember(T& cell)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(&cell))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember(U& cell)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(&cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember(Ref<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    NonnullMember(NonnullMember const&) = default;
    NonnullMember(NonnullMember&&) = default;

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember(NonnullMember<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(static_cast<T*>(other.ptr())))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember(U& foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(&foreign_cell)))
    {
    }

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember(Ref<U> const& foreign_cell)
    requires(IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<U, T>)
        : m_compressed(Detail::compress_cell(as_cell(foreign_cell.ptr())))
    {
    }

    NonnullMember& operator=(NonnullMember const& other)
    {
        set_compressed(other.m_compressed);
        return *this;
    }

    template<typename U>
    NonnullMember& operator=(U&& other)
    requires(requires { NonnullMember(forward<U>(other)); })
    {
        set_compressed(NonnullMember(forward<U>(other)).m_compressed);
        return *this;
    }

    RETURNS_NONNULL T* ptr() const { return reinterpret_cast<T*>(decompress_nonnull(m_compressed)); }

    RETURNS_NONNULL T* operator->() const { return ptr(); }

    [[nodiscard]] T& operator*() const { return *ptr(); }

    operator T&() const { return *ptr(); }

    template<typename U>
    operator Ref<U>() const
    requires(IsConvertible<T*, U*> || IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<T, U>)
    {
        return Ref<U>(*ptr());
    }

    template<typename U>
    operator Ptr<U>() const
    requires(IsConvertible<T*, U*> || IsForeignCellConvertibleToCell<T, U>)
    {
        return Ptr<U>(ptr());
    }

    operator bool() const = delete;
    bool operator!() const = delete;

    u32 compressed() const { return m_compressed; }

private:
    template<typename U>
    friend class NonnullMember;

    ALWAYS_INLINE void set_compressed(u32 compressed)
    {
        Detail::member_write_barrier(this, compressed);
        m_compressed = compressed;
    }

    u32 m_compressed;
};

// The byte offset of a member in a cell, for code that loads the field directly and so has to know that it holds a
// compressed pointer.
struct MemberOffset {
    size_t value { 0 };
};

template<typename FieldType>
constexpr auto field_offset(size_t offset)
{
    if constexpr (Detail::IsMember<FieldType>)
        return MemberOffset { offset };
    else
        return offset;
}

// The offset of a field of a cell, as a MemberOffset if the field is a member, and as a size_t otherwise.
#define GC_FIELD_OFFSET(Type, field) ::GC::field_offset<RemoveCV<decltype(Type::field)>>(offsetof(Type, field))

namespace Detail {

// Whether a member of T that holds `compressed` points to `other`, as a comparison of T* with U* would tell.
template<typename T, typename U>
ALWAYS_INLINE bool member_points_to(u32 compressed, U const* other)
{
    if constexpr (IsConvertible<U*, T const*>) {
        // OPTIMIZATION: Compressing the other pointer is a shift, where decoding the member would load the base.
        return compressed == compress(static_cast<T const*>(other));
    } else if constexpr (IsConvertible<T*, U const*>) {
        return static_cast<U const*>(reinterpret_cast<T const*>(decompress(compressed))) == other;
    } else {
        // A cell compared to a type that names foreign cells, which shares its address.
        return compressed == compress(other);
    }
}

}

// OPTIMIZATION: Two members point to the same cell exactly when their compressed pointers are equal, so comparing them
//               decodes neither.
template<typename T, typename U>
requires(Detail::IsMember<T> && Detail::IsMember<U>)
inline bool operator==(T const& a, U const& b)
{
    return a.compressed() == b.compressed();
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(Member<T> const& a, Ptr<U> const& b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b.ptr());
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(Member<T> const& a, Ref<U> const& b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b.ptr());
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(NonnullMember<T> const& a, Ptr<U> const& b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b.ptr());
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(NonnullMember<T> const& a, Ref<U> const& b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b.ptr());
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(Member<T> const& a, U const* b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b);
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(NonnullMember<T> const& a, U const* b)
{
    return Detail::member_points_to<T>(a.compressed(), b);
}

template<typename T>
inline bool operator==(Member<T> const& member, nullptr_t)
{
    return !member;
}

}
