//! The descriptors of the heap's blocks.
//!
//! A block holds cells of one type and one size. What the collector knows about a block is in its descriptor, which
//! lives outside the heap region: the heap and the type of the block, and which of its cells are allocated and which
//! are marked. So nothing that writes to a cell, or past it, can change what the collector does with the block. The
//! descriptor of a block is at the block's index in the region in a table of descriptors, which is reserved once for the
//! whole region and only backed by memory where blocks are.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::OnceLock;

use crate::evacuation::Evacuation;
use crate::os;

pub const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;

/// The smallest cell, which has room for the link of a free cell after the header of a cell.
pub const MIN_CELL_SIZE: usize = 24;

/// A cell's bit in the bitmaps of its block is its offset in the block divided by its size, which the smallest cells
/// take the most bits for.
pub const CELL_BITMAP_WORDS: usize = 11;

const _: () = assert!(CELL_BITMAP_WORDS == (BLOCK_SIZE / MIN_CELL_SIZE + 1).div_ceil(64));

/// What the collector knows about a block. LibGC's C++ side fills it in when it creates the block, and empties it when
/// the block goes away.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct BlockDescriptor {
    /// The heap the block belongs to, or null while there is no block.
    pub heap: *mut c_void,
    /// The CellTypeInfo of the block's cells.
    pub type_info: *const c_void,
    pub cell_size: u32,
    /// ceil(2^32 / cell_size): the offset of a cell in its block times this, shifted right by 32, is its mark bit.
    pub cell_index_magic: u32,
    /// Whether the block's cells may only be traced on the thread that owns their heap, as C++ cells must.
    pub traced_on_owner_thread_only: bool,
    /// Whether a collection may move the block's cells to other blocks of their allocator.
    pub movable: bool,
    /// Whether a collection evacuated the block and could not empty it because something pinned some of its cells.
    /// Compaction leaves the block alone until one of the cells it kept dies.
    pub kept_by_pins: bool,
    pub reserved: u8,
    /// How many cells fit in the block, after its header.
    pub cell_count: u16,
    /// The index of the first cell of the block, see cell_index(). Its cells have the indices from this one on.
    pub first_cell_index: u16,
    /// What a collection that evacuates the block knows about its cells, and null in every other collection. Marking
    /// reads it for every cell it visits, to pin the cells of evacuated blocks that something visits by value.
    pub evacuation: *mut Evacuation,
    /// One bit for each cell, which marking sets atomically, see mark_word().
    pub marked: [UnsafeCell<u64>; CELL_BITMAP_WORDS],
    /// One bit for each cell that is allocated: set when a cell is handed out, and when an allocator takes the free
    /// cells of the block to hand out itself, until it gives back the ones it did not hand out. Only the thread that
    /// owns the heap reads and writes them.
    pub allocated: [u64; CELL_BITMAP_WORDS],
    /// Where the block is in its allocator's list of blocks.
    pub list_index: u32,
    /// Whether the incremental sweep has yet to sweep the block.
    pub pending_sweep: bool,
    /// Whether a sweep is sweeping the block right now, which a destructor it calls may be in the middle of.
    pub being_swept: bool,
    /// Whether the block is on its allocator's list of blocks with free cells.
    pub usable: bool,
    /// Rounds the descriptor up to 256 bytes, four whole cache lines in the table.
    pub reserved2: [u8; 33],
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<BlockDescriptor>() == 256);

impl BlockDescriptor {
    pub fn heap(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        // SAFETY: A reference is a valid pointer.
        unsafe { heap_of_descriptor(self) }
    }

    /// A word of the mark bits, which other threads may set while marking runs.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn mark_word(&self, word: usize) -> &AtomicU64 {
        // SAFETY: The word is in an UnsafeCell, so writing to it through a shared reference is fine, and it is only
        //         ever accessed atomically while other threads may access it.
        unsafe { AtomicU64::from_ptr(self.marked[word].get()) }
    }

    /// The evacuation state of the block, if a collection evacuates it.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn evacuation(&self) -> Option<&Evacuation> {
        // SAFETY: The field is only accessed atomically while other threads may read it, only written while no marker
        //         runs, and the evacuation outlives the collection's use of it.
        unsafe {
            AtomicPtr::from_ptr((&raw const self.evacuation).cast_mut())
                .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
                .as_ref()
        }
    }

    /// The index of the cell at `address` in the block, which is also the index of its mark bit. Cells are a cell size
    /// apart, so the offsets of their starts divided by the cell size tell them apart.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn cell_index(&self, address: usize) -> CellIndex {
        CellIndex((((address & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1)) as u64 * u64::from(self.cell_index_magic)) >> 32) as usize)
    }

    /// The start of the cell that `address` points into, for a block whose cells start `cells_offset` bytes into it.
    pub fn cell_containing(&self, address: usize, cells_offset: usize) -> usize {
        let block = address & !(BLOCK_SIZE - 1);
        let offset_in_cells = (address & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1)) - cells_offset;
        // NB: As for the mark bit index, multiplying by the magic and shifting right by 32 divides offsets below 2^14 by
        //     the cell size exactly.
        let index = ((offset_in_cells as u64 * u64::from(self.cell_index_magic)) >> 32) as usize;
        block + cells_offset + index * self.cell_size as usize
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn mark_bit(&self, address: usize) -> (&AtomicU64, u64) {
        let index = self.cell_index(address).0;
        (self.mark_word(index / 64), 1 << (index % 64))
    }

    pub fn is_marked(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        let (word, bit) = self.mark_bit(address);
        word.load(Ordering::Relaxed) & bit != 0
    }

    /// Sets the mark bit of the cell at `address`, and returns whether it was clear.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn mark(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        let (word, bit) = self.mark_bit(address);
        // NB: A bit that is set already costs no atomic read-modify-write, which would take the word's cache line from
        //     the other threads that set bits in it.
        if word.load(Ordering::Relaxed) & bit != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        word.fetch_or(bit, Ordering::Relaxed) & bit == 0
    }

    /// Like mark(), for a thread that no other thread sets mark bits concurrently with.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn mark_exclusive(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        let (word, bit) = self.mark_bit(address);
        let value = word.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        if value & bit != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        word.store(value | bit, Ordering::Relaxed);
        true
    }
}

/// The index of a cell in its block, which marks and other per-cell bits of the block are indexed by.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CellIndex(pub usize);

/// The most cells a block has, and so the most bits that per-cell bitmaps of a block need.
pub const MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK: usize = CELL_BITMAP_WORDS * 64;

struct Table {
    descriptors: NonNull<BlockDescriptor>,
    count: usize,
}

// SAFETY: The table is only ever read through, and its descriptors are accessed atomically where threads share them.
unsafe impl Send for Table {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl Sync for Table {}

static TABLE: OnceLock<Table> = OnceLock::new();

/// The table of block descriptors, see rust_gc_block_descriptor_table().
pub fn descriptor_table() -> NonNull<BlockDescriptor> {
    TABLE.get().expect("the table of block descriptors exists").descriptors
}

/// The descriptor of the block that `address` is in, for an address in the heap region at `heap_region_base`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `address` must be in a block of the region, whose descriptor is backed by memory.
#[inline(always)]
pub unsafe fn descriptor_for<'a>(heap_region_base: usize, address: usize) -> &'a BlockDescriptor {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes an address in a block, whose descriptor is in the table.
    unsafe {
        descriptor_table()
            .add((address - heap_region_base) / BLOCK_SIZE)
            .as_ref()
    }
}

/// Sets the evacuation state of the block that `address` is in, which only a collection that is not marking may do.
///
/// NB: This writes through a pointer from the table rather than through a reference to the descriptor, which would let
///     the compiler assume that the descriptor does not change.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for descriptor_for().
pub unsafe fn set_evacuation_of_block(heap_region_base: usize, address: usize, evacuation: *mut Evacuation) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes an address in a block, whose descriptor is in the table, and the field is only accessed
    //         atomically while other threads may read it.
    unsafe {
        let descriptor = descriptor_table()
            .add((address - heap_region_base) / BLOCK_SIZE)
            .as_ptr();
        AtomicPtr::from_ptr(&raw mut (*descriptor).evacuation).store(evacuation, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

/// The heap of a block, read without borrowing its descriptor. The thread of another heap may be filling in the other
/// fields of the descriptor of a block that it takes, which a reference to the descriptor would assume do not change.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `descriptor` must point to a descriptor in the table that is backed by memory.
#[inline(always)]
pub unsafe fn heap_of_descriptor(descriptor: *const BlockDescriptor) -> *mut c_void {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a valid descriptor, and the field is only ever accessed atomically while other threads
    //         may read it.
    unsafe { AtomicPtr::from_ptr((&raw const (*descriptor).heap).cast_mut()) }.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

/// The descriptor of the block that `address` is in, if that block belongs to `heap`, which only the calling thread
/// changes, so nothing changes the descriptor while the reference is in use.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for descriptor_for().
#[inline(always)]
pub unsafe fn descriptor_of_heap<'a>(
    heap_region_base: usize,
    address: usize,
    heap: *const c_void,
) -> Option<&'a BlockDescriptor> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes an address in a block, whose descriptor is in the table.
    let descriptor = unsafe { descriptor_table().add((address - heap_region_base) / BLOCK_SIZE) };
    // SAFETY: As above.
    if unsafe { heap_of_descriptor(descriptor.as_ptr()) }.cast_const() != heap {
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: As above, and only the calling thread changes the descriptor of a block of the heap.
    Some(unsafe { descriptor.as_ref() })
}

/// Reserves the table of block descriptors for a heap region of `region_size` bytes, the first time it is called, and
/// returns it. The descriptor of the block at offset N of the region is at index N / BLOCK_SIZE.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_gc_block_descriptor_table(region_size: usize) -> *mut BlockDescriptor {
    TABLE
        .get_or_init(|| {
            let count = region_size / BLOCK_SIZE;
            let descriptors = os::reserve_zeroed(count * size_of::<BlockDescriptor>())
                .expect("reserve the table of block descriptors");
            Table {
                descriptors: descriptors.cast(),
                count,
            }
        })
        .descriptors
        .as_ptr()
}

/// Makes sure that the `count` descriptors from `first_index` on are backed by memory, before blocks are created there.
pub fn commit_descriptors(first_index: usize, count: usize) {
    let table = TABLE.get().expect("the table of block descriptors exists");
    assert!(
        first_index + count <= table.count,
        "the blocks are within the heap region"
    );
    // SAFETY: The descriptors are within the reserved table.
    unsafe {
        os::commit_reserved_zeroed(
            table.descriptors.add(first_index).cast(),
            count * size_of::<BlockDescriptor>(),
        );
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Compaction policy: which blocks a collection that may move cells evacuates.
//!
//! Cells only move within their allocator, so each allocator is looked at on its own. Its blocks are taken emptiest
//! first, as long as the live cells of the blocks taken still fit into the free slots of the blocks left. Then every
//! block that fits is a block that the collection frees, unless something pins one of its cells. Of the blocks that fit
//! in all allocators, the ones that move the fewest bytes go first, since each frees one block, until moving the next
//! one would go over the budget. A block that an earlier collection could not empty because something pinned some of
//! its cells is not taken again until one of the cells it kept dies, since evacuating it again would only move the
//! cells that moved into it since.

use crate::block::BLOCK_SIZE;
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

/// A block of a movable allocator, as the allocator knows it before the collection marks.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct CompactionCandidate {
    pub block: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
    /// Which allocator the block belongs to. The blocks of an allocator come one after another.
    pub allocator: u32,
    /// The cells of the block that are allocated: at least the ones that are alive. A block whose count the allocator
    /// does not know counts as full.
    pub live_cells: u32,
    pub cell_count: u32,
    pub cell_size: u32,
    /// Whether an earlier collection could not empty the block because of pinned cells, see
    /// BlockDescriptor::kept_by_pins. Its free slots still take the cells of other blocks.
    pub kept_by_pins: bool,
    /// Set for the blocks the collection evacuates.
    pub selected: bool,
}

/// What selection found.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CompactionSelection {
    /// How many bytes of blocks compaction could free in these allocators if it moved every cell it had to, which is
    /// the blocks each allocator has beyond the fewest that its live cells fit in.
    pub recoverable_bytes: usize,
    /// The blocks whose live cells fit into the free slots of their allocator's other blocks, which compaction frees
    /// unless something pins their cells. The ones over the budget are left for another collection.
    pub fitting_blocks: usize,
    pub selected_blocks: usize,
    /// The bytes of the live cells of the selected blocks, which move unless pinned.
    pub bytes_to_move: usize,
}

/// Selects the blocks to evacuate, moving at most `budget_bytes` of cells, and says how much could be recovered.
fn select(candidates: &mut [CompactionCandidate], budget_bytes: usize) -> CompactionSelection {
    let mut selection = CompactionSelection::default();
    // The blocks that fit, of all allocators, by index into the candidates.
    let mut fitting = Vec::new();
    let mut start = 0;
    while start < candidates.len() {
        let allocator = candidates[start].allocator;
        let end = start
            + candidates[start..]
                .iter()
                .take_while(|candidate| candidate.allocator == allocator)
                .count();
        let blocks = &candidates[start..end];
        debug_assert!(blocks.iter().all(|block| block.cell_count == blocks[0].cell_count));
        let cell_count = blocks[0].cell_count as usize;

        let live_cells: usize = blocks.iter().map(|block| block.live_cells as usize).sum();
        let fewest_blocks = live_cells.div_ceil(cell_count);
        selection.recoverable_bytes += (blocks.len() - fewest_blocks) * BLOCK_SIZE;

        let mut by_live_cells: Vec<usize> = (start..end).collect();
        by_live_cells.sort_by_key(|&index| candidates[index].live_cells);
        let mut free_cells_elsewhere = blocks.len() * cell_count - live_cells;
        let mut cells_to_move = 0;
        for index in by_live_cells {
            let block = &candidates[index];
            let live = block.live_cells as usize;
            // NB: A full block frees nothing that its cells would not take elsewhere.
            if live >= cell_count {
                break;
            }
            if block.kept_by_pins {
                continue;
            }
            let free = cell_count - live;
            if cells_to_move + live > free_cells_elsewhere - free {
                break;
            }
            cells_to_move += live;
            free_cells_elsewhere -= free;
            fitting.push(index);
        }
        start = end;
    }

    let bytes_of = |candidate: &CompactionCandidate| candidate.live_cells as usize * candidate.cell_size as usize;
    selection.fitting_blocks = fitting.len();
    if budget_bytes == 0 {
        return selection;
    }
    // NB: A stable sort keeps the blocks of an allocator emptiest first, so the ones within budget fit as well.
    fitting.sort_by_key(|&index| bytes_of(&candidates[index]));
    for index in fitting {
        let bytes = bytes_of(&candidates[index]);
        if selection.bytes_to_move + bytes > budget_bytes {
            break;
        }
        selection.bytes_to_move += bytes;
        selection.selected_blocks += 1;
        candidates[index].selected = true;
    }
    selection
}

/// Selects the blocks of `candidates` that a collection evacuates, as the module comment says, moving at most
/// `budget_bytes` of cells. A budget of 0 only tells how much could be recovered.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `candidates` must point to `count` candidates, the blocks of each allocator one after another.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_compaction_select(
    candidates: *mut CompactionCandidate,
    count: usize,
    budget_bytes: usize,
) -> CompactionSelection {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        if count == 0 {
            return CompactionSelection::default();
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller passes count candidates.
        select(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(candidates, count) }, budget_bytes)
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn candidate(allocator: u32, live_cells: u32) -> CompactionCandidate {
        CompactionCandidate {
            block: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            allocator,
            live_cells,
            cell_count: 100,
            cell_size: 64,
            kept_by_pins: false,
            selected: false,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_the_emptiest_blocks_whose_cells_fit_elsewhere() {
        let mut candidates = [candidate(0, 10), candidate(0, 50), candidate(0, 20), candidate(0, 90)];
        let selection = select(&mut candidates, usize::MAX);
        // 170 live cells fit in 2 blocks of 4. The blocks with 10 and 20 fit into the free slots of the others.
        assert_eq!(selection.recoverable_bytes, 2 * BLOCK_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(selection.fitting_blocks, 2);
        assert_eq!(selection.selected_blocks, 2);
        let selected: Vec<bool> = candidates.iter().map(|candidate| candidate.selected).collect();
        assert_eq!(selected, [true, false, true, false]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_nothing_from_full_allocators() {
        let mut candidates = [candidate(0, 100), candidate(0, 95), candidate(1, 100)];
        let selection = select(&mut candidates, usize::MAX);
        assert_eq!(selection.recoverable_bytes, 0);
        assert_eq!(selection.selected_blocks, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn skips_blocks_kept_by_pins_but_fills_them() {
        let mut candidates = [candidate(0, 10), candidate(0, 20), candidate(0, 50)];
        candidates[0].kept_by_pins = true;
        let selection = select(&mut candidates, usize::MAX);
        assert_eq!(selection.fitting_blocks, 2);
        let selected: Vec<bool> = candidates.iter().map(|candidate| candidate.selected).collect();
        assert_eq!(selected, [false, true, true]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_to_the_budget_with_the_cheapest_blocks_first() {
        let mut candidates = [candidate(0, 30), candidate(0, 5), candidate(1, 10), candidate(1, 10)];
        let selection = select(&mut candidates, 15 * 64);
        assert_eq!(selection.fitting_blocks, 2);
        assert_eq!(selection.selected_blocks, 2);
        assert_eq!(selection.bytes_to_move, 15 * 64);
        let selected: Vec<bool> = candidates.iter().map(|candidate| candidate.selected).collect();
        assert_eq!(selected, [false, true, true, false]);
    }
}

//! Evacuation: a collection that does not scan the stack may move the live cells out of some blocks, into free slots of
//! other blocks of the same allocator.
//!
//! An edge that marking visits through its slot can be updated once its target moves, while an edge visited by value
//! pins its target. Marking pins the cells of evacuated blocks that something visits by value, or that are roots, and
//! records the slots that point into evacuated blocks. After marking, a cell of an evacuated block moves if its
//! allocator is movable and nothing pinned it. Each cell that moves gets a free slot of another block first, then every
//! recorded slot that points at one is rewritten where it is, and only then is each cell copied bytewise to its new
//! slot, with its slots rewritten already, and its old slot freed without being destroyed. Cells move before the sweep,
//! so a dead cell's slot is never taken, and the sweep that follows destroys the dead cells once the collection is
//! over.
//!
//! The collector finds slots in cells, in the heap region: a slot elsewhere, like in malloc memory that a cell owns,
//! could be freed or moved by the finalizers and sweep callbacks that run between marking and moving, so the visit of
//! such a slot pins its target instead. The exception is memory that a live cell owns and that nothing frees, moves or
//! writes until the collection is over, whose values the cell visits as owned values (see
//! rust_gc_marker_visit_owned_values()). Holders of weak references, whose memory changes as they forget the cells that
//! died, hand their slots over once they did, before cells move (see rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot()).

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};

use crate::block::{
    BLOCK_SIZE, BlockDescriptor, CELL_BITMAP_WORDS, CellIndex, MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK, descriptor_for, descriptor_of_heap,
    set_evacuation_of_block,
};
use crate::identity_hash::{CompressedAddress, IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET, identity_hashes_of};
use crate::marker::COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT;
use crate::os;
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

/// Zero-filled room for `capacity` values of `T`, mapped from the system and given back to it as a whole when dropped,
/// for what a collection that moves cells keeps until it is over. Only the pages that are written to take memory.
///
/// NB: A compacting collection needs a burst of memory that it frees all at once. Malloc would keep those pages for
///     later and hand them out among long-lived allocations, which then keep them in the process.
struct MappedArray<T> {
    pointer: NonNull<T>,
    capacity: usize,
}

impl<T> MappedArray<T> {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// All-zero bytes must be a valid `T`.
    unsafe fn new_zeroed(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let capacity = capacity.max(1);
        let size = capacity * size_of::<T>();
        let pointer = os::reserve_zeroed(size).expect("map memory for a collection that moves cells");
        // SAFETY: The range is all of what reserve_zeroed() just returned.
        unsafe { os::commit_reserved_zeroed(pointer, size) };
        Self {
            pointer: pointer.cast(),
            capacity,
        }
    }

    fn get(&self, index: usize) -> &T {
        assert!(index < self.capacity);
        // SAFETY: The index is in bounds, and every value is valid from the start, as new_zeroed() requires.
        unsafe { self.pointer.add(index).as_ref() }
    }
}

impl<T> Drop for MappedArray<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The range is all of the reservation, which goes away with this.
        unsafe { os::release(self.pointer.cast(), self.capacity * size_of::<T>()) };
    }
}

/// How many slots a chunk of recorded slots has room for: 1 MiB of address space.
const RECORDED_SLOTS_PER_CHUNK: usize = 128 * 1024;

/// The slots one marker records, in chunks of mapped memory (see MappedArray).
pub struct RecordedSlots {
    /// The chunks, the one being filled last.
    chunks: Vec<MappedArray<RecordedSlot>>,
    /// Where the next slot goes in the last chunk, and the end of that chunk; both null before the first chunk.
    next: *mut RecordedSlot,
    end: *mut RecordedSlot,
}

impl Default for RecordedSlots {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            chunks: Vec::new(),
            next: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            end: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        }
    }
}

impl RecordedSlots {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn push(&mut self, slot: RecordedSlot) {
        if self.next == self.end {
            self.add_chunk();
        }
        // SAFETY: The last chunk has room at next, which stays within it.
        unsafe {
            self.next.write(slot);
            self.next = self.next.add(1);
        }
    }

    #[cold]
    fn add_chunk(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: A RecordedSlot is an integer.
        let chunk = unsafe { MappedArray::<RecordedSlot>::new_zeroed(RECORDED_SLOTS_PER_CHUNK) };
        self.next = chunk.pointer.as_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The chunk has room for its capacity.
        self.end = unsafe { self.next.add(chunk.capacity) };
        self.chunks.push(chunk);
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.chunks.is_empty()
    }

    /// The recorded slots, chunk by chunk.
    fn slices(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &[RecordedSlot]> {
        let last = self.chunks.len().wrapping_sub(1);
        self.chunks.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, chunk)| {
            let length = if index == last {
                // SAFETY: next is in the last chunk.
                unsafe { self.next.offset_from(chunk.pointer.as_ptr()) as usize }
            } else {
                chunk.capacity
            };
            // SAFETY: The first length slots of the chunk were written.
            unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(chunk.pointer.as_ptr(), length) }
        })
    }
}

/// Why a cell of an evacuated block stays where it is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum PinReason {
    Unpinned = 0,
    /// Something visited the cell by value rather than through a slot the collector can update.
    Edge = 1,
    /// The cell is a root, which roots hand over by value.
    Root = 2,
}

/// What a collection that evacuates a block knows about the block's cells. All zeros is nothing pinned or moved yet.
pub struct Evacuation {
    pinned_by_edge: [AtomicU64; CELL_BITMAP_WORDS],
    pinned_by_root: [AtomicU64; CELL_BITMAP_WORDS],
    /// The compressed address each cell that moved moved to, by cell index, and 0 for the cells that did not.
    forwarding: [AtomicU32; MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK],
}

impl Evacuation {
    /// Pins the cell at `address` of the block this evacuates, which markers may do from several threads at once.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn pin(&self, descriptor: &BlockDescriptor, address: usize, reason: PinReason) {
        let index = descriptor.cell_index(address).0;
        let bits = match reason {
            PinReason::Root => &self.pinned_by_root,
            _ => &self.pinned_by_edge,
        };
        let word = &bits[index / 64];
        let bit = 1u64 << (index % 64);
        // NB: As with mark bits, a bit that is set already costs no read-modify-write.
        if word.load(Ordering::Relaxed) & bit == 0 {
            word.fetch_or(bit, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }

    /// Whether the cell at `address` of the block this evacuates is pinned, for whatever reason.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_pinned(&self, descriptor: &BlockDescriptor, address: usize) -> bool {
        let index = descriptor.cell_index(address).0;
        let bit = 1u64 << (index % 64);
        (self.pinned_by_root[index / 64].load(Ordering::Relaxed)
            | self.pinned_by_edge[index / 64].load(Ordering::Relaxed))
            & bit
            != 0
    }

    pub fn pin_reason(&self, index: CellIndex) -> PinReason {
        let bit = 1u64 << (index.0 % 64);
        if self.pinned_by_root[index.0 / 64].load(Ordering::Relaxed) & bit != 0 {
            return PinReason::Root;
        }
        if self.pinned_by_edge[index.0 / 64].load(Ordering::Relaxed) & bit != 0 {
            return PinReason::Edge;
        }
        PinReason::Unpinned
    }

    fn forwarding(&self, index: CellIndex) -> Option<CompressedAddress> {
        let compressed = self.forwarding[index.0].load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        (compressed != 0).then_some(CompressedAddress(compressed))
    }
}

/// The kinds of slots that marking records, which differ in how they hold the address of their target.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(usize)]
pub enum SlotKind {
    /// A 32-bit compressed cell pointer, 0 for null, like GC::Member.
    Member = 0,
    /// A NaN-boxed value, which may hold a cell.
    Value = 1,
    /// A raw pointer into a cell, at the cell or past its start, as an object keeps to its property storage.
    InteriorPointer = 2,
    /// A raw pointer into the cell that holds it, as an object keeps to its inline property storage. It may point one
    /// past the end of the cell's own fields, at the start of the next cell, which only its holder tells apart.
    SelfPointer = 3,
}

const SLOT_KIND_MASK: usize = 3;

/// The address of a slot that marking recorded, with its kind in the low bits. Every slot is at least 4-aligned.
///
/// NB: The address is kept as an integer, so that a slot costs one word in the chunks that markers fill on several
///     threads. Recording a slot exposes its provenance, which pointer() picks up again.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecordedSlot(usize);

impl RecordedSlot {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn new(slot: *const u8, kind: SlotKind) -> Self {
        let address = slot.expose_provenance();
        debug_assert!(address & SLOT_KIND_MASK == 0, "slots are at least 4-aligned");
        Self(address | kind as usize)
    }

    pub fn address(self) -> usize {
        self.0 & !SLOT_KIND_MASK
    }

    /// The slot, with the provenance that new() exposed.
    fn pointer<T>(self) -> *mut T {
        core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut(self.address())
    }

    pub fn kind(self) -> SlotKind {
        match self.0 & SLOT_KIND_MASK {
            0 => SlotKind::Member,
            1 => SlotKind::Value,
            2 => SlotKind::InteriorPointer,
            _ => SlotKind::SelfPointer,
        }
    }
}

/// Where the collector finds what it needs to move cells and fix up slots.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct EvacuationLayout {
    pub heap_region_base: usize,
    /// How far into a block its first cell is.
    pub block_cells_offset: u32,
    /// As in MarkerLayout.
    pub value_is_cell_pattern: u64,
    pub value_offset_mask: u64,
}

/// The blocks a collection evacuates, and the slots its marking recorded.
pub struct EvacuationSet {
    layout: EvacuationLayout,
    heap: *mut c_void,
    /// The evacuated blocks, and their evacuations at the same indices.
    blocks: Vec<usize>,
    evacuations: MappedArray<Evacuation>,
    slots: Vec<RecordedSlots>,
    /// The slots handed over after marking, see rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot().
    slots_recorded_after_marking: RecordedSlots,
}

impl EvacuationSet {
    pub(crate) fn add_recorded_slots(&mut self, slots: RecordedSlots) {
        if !slots.is_empty() {
            self.slots.push(slots);
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn is_in_heap_region(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        (address.wrapping_sub(self.layout.heap_region_base) as u64) <= self.layout.value_offset_mask
    }

    /// Every recorded slot, chunk by chunk.
    fn all_slots(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &[RecordedSlot]> {
        self.slots
            .iter()
            .chain(core::iter::once(&self.slots_recorded_after_marking))
            .flat_map(RecordedSlots::slices)
    }

    /// The evacuation of the live block that `address` is in, with its descriptor.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn evacuation_of(&self, address: usize) -> Option<(&BlockDescriptor, &Evacuation)> {
        if !self.is_in_heap_region(address) {
            return None;
        }
        // SAFETY: The address is in the region, whose descriptors are backed by memory wherever a block ever was, and
        //         read as zero elsewhere.
        let descriptor = unsafe { descriptor_of_heap(self.layout.heap_region_base, address, self.heap) }?;
        Some((descriptor, descriptor.evacuation()?))
    }

    fn decompress(&self, compressed: CompressedAddress) -> usize {
        self.layout.heap_region_base + ((compressed.0 as usize) << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT)
    }

    /// A pointer to `address` in the heap region, whose provenance rust_gc_heap_region_init() exposed.
    fn heap_region_pointer(address: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut(address)
    }

    /// Where the cell that starts at `cell` moved to, if it moved.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn forwarding_address(&self, cell: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let (descriptor, evacuation) = self.evacuation_of(cell)?;
        evacuation
            .forwarding(descriptor.cell_index(cell))
            .map(|to| self.decompress(to))
    }

    /// Rewrites a slot that marking recorded to point where its target moves, and returns whether it did. Cells are only
    /// copied once their slots are rewritten, so the slot is still where marking found it, and the copy of a cell that
    /// moves gets the rewritten slots.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The slot must be in a live cell that has not moved yet, or in memory that such a cell owns, and hold what its
    /// kind says.
    unsafe fn fix_up(&self, slot: RecordedSlot) -> bool {
        let base = self.layout.heap_region_base;
        let address = slot.address();
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a slot of a live cell.
        unsafe {
            match slot.kind() {
                SlotKind::Member => {
                    let slot = slot.pointer::<u32>();
                    let compressed = slot.read();
                    if compressed == 0 {
                        return false;
                    }
                    let Some(to) = self.forwarding_address(self.decompress(CompressedAddress(compressed))) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    slot.write((to >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32);
                }
                SlotKind::Value => {
                    let slot = slot.pointer::<u64>();
                    let value = slot.read();
                    if value & self.layout.value_is_cell_pattern != self.layout.value_is_cell_pattern {
                        return false;
                    }
                    let mask = self.layout.value_offset_mask;
                    let Some(to) = self.forwarding_address(base + (value & mask) as usize) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    slot.write((value & !mask) | ((to - base) as u64 & mask));
                }
                SlotKind::InteriorPointer => {
                    let slot = slot.pointer::<*mut u8>();
                    let pointer = slot.read().addr();
                    let Some((descriptor, _)) = self.evacuation_of(pointer) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    let cell = descriptor.cell_containing(pointer, self.layout.block_cells_offset as usize);
                    let Some(to) = self.forwarding_address(cell) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    slot.write(Self::heap_region_pointer(to).wrapping_add(pointer - cell));
                }
                SlotKind::SelfPointer => {
                    let Some((descriptor, _)) = self.evacuation_of(address) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    let holder = descriptor.cell_containing(address, self.layout.block_cells_offset as usize);
                    let Some(to) = self.forwarding_address(holder) else {
                        return false;
                    };
                    let slot = slot.pointer::<*mut u8>();
                    let pointer = slot.read().addr();
                    // NB: The pointer may point one past the holder's fields, at the start of the next cell.
                    if pointer.wrapping_sub(holder) > descriptor.cell_size as usize {
                        return false;
                    }
                    slot.write(Self::heap_region_pointer(to).wrapping_add(pointer - holder));
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

/// Starts the evacuation state of a collection of `heap`, which evacuates up to `block_count` blocks that it adds, and
/// owns their evacuations.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_create(
    layout: EvacuationLayout,
    heap: *mut c_void,
    block_count: usize,
) -> *mut EvacuationSet {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(EvacuationSet {
        layout,
        heap,
        blocks: Vec::with_capacity(block_count),
        // SAFETY: All zeros is an evacuation that pinned and moved nothing.
        evacuations: unsafe { MappedArray::new_zeroed(block_count) },
        slots: Vec::new(),
        slots_recorded_after_marking: RecordedSlots::default(),
    }))
}

/// Has the collection evacuate the block at `block`, which must belong to the set's heap. Must be called before marking.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and `block` a live block of its heap that the set does not have yet. The set must have room for
/// it, see rust_gc_evacuation_create().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_add_block(set: *mut EvacuationSet, block: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
    let set = unsafe { &mut *set };
    let address = block.addr();
    debug_assert!(address & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1) == 0);
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live block.
    let descriptor = unsafe { descriptor_for(set.layout.heap_region_base, address) };
    debug_assert!(descriptor.heap() == set.heap && descriptor.evacuation().is_none());
    let evacuation = set.evacuations.get(set.blocks.len());
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live block, and no marker runs yet.
    unsafe {
        set_evacuation_of_block(
            set.layout.heap_region_base,
            address,
            core::ptr::from_ref(evacuation).cast_mut(),
        );
    }
    set.blocks.push(address);
}

/// Why a live cell of an evacuated block was pinned.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and `cell` a cell of one of its blocks.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_pin_reason(set: *const EvacuationSet, cell: *const c_void) -> PinReason {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
    let set = unsafe { &*set };
    let (descriptor, evacuation) = set
        .evacuation_of(cell.addr())
        .expect("the cell is in an evacuated block");
    evacuation.pin_reason(descriptor.cell_index(cell.addr()))
}

/// How many marked cells of an evacuated block were pinned, by reason.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PinnedCells {
    pub by_edge: usize,
    pub by_root: usize,
}

/// Finds the cells of an evacuated block that move once marking is done: the marked ones that nothing pinned. Writes
/// their addresses to `cells`, returns how many there are, and adds the marked cells that are pinned to `pinned`. Only
/// the mark bits are read, so the dead cells and the free slots of the block are never touched.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, `block` one of its blocks whose cells start `block_cells_offset` bytes into it and whose marks
/// are the ones marking left, and `cells` must have room for MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK addresses.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_cells_to_move(
    set: *const EvacuationSet,
    block: *const c_void,
    cells: *mut *mut c_void,
    pinned: *mut PinnedCells,
) -> usize {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set, room for the cells, and a live count.
        let (set, cells, pinned) = unsafe {
            (
                &*set,
                ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(cells, MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK),
                &mut *pinned,
            )
        };
        let (descriptor, evacuation) = set.evacuation_of(block.addr()).expect("the block is evacuated");
        let cell_size = descriptor.cell_size as usize;
        let cells_offset = set.layout.block_cells_offset as usize;
        // NB: A cell's mark bit is its offset in the block divided by the cell size, see BlockDescriptor::cell_index().
        let first_bit = cells_offset / cell_size;
        let mut count = 0;
        for word_index in 0..CELL_BITMAP_WORDS {
            let mut bits = descriptor.mark_word(word_index).load(Ordering::Relaxed);
            while bits != 0 {
                let bit = word_index * 64 + bits.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                bits &= bits - 1;
                let cell = block.addr() + cells_offset + (bit - first_bit) * cell_size;
                debug_assert!(descriptor.cell_index(cell).0 == bit);
                match evacuation.pin_reason(CellIndex(bit)) {
                    PinReason::Unpinned => {
                        cells[count] = block.with_addr(cell).cast_mut();
                        count += 1;
                    }
                    PinReason::Edge => pinned.by_edge += 1,
                    PinReason::Root => pinned.by_root += 1,
                }
            }
        }
        count
    })
}

/// A cell to move, from its slot to a free slot of another block of its allocator.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CellMove {
    pub from: *mut c_void,
    pub to: *mut c_void,
}

/// Notes where each cell moves to, before anything moves. The slots of both are `cell_size` bytes.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and the moves name live, unpinned cells of its blocks and free slots of the same allocators
/// outside its blocks, each once.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_forward_cells(
    set: *mut EvacuationSet,
    moves: *const CellMove,
    count: usize,
    cell_size: usize,
) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set, and count moves.
        let (set, moves) = unsafe { (&*set, ak::slice_from_raw_parts(moves, count)) };
        for cell_move in moves {
            let (from, to) = (cell_move.from.addr(), cell_move.to.addr());
            let (descriptor, evacuation) = set.evacuation_of(from).expect("the cell is in an evacuated block");
            debug_assert!(descriptor.cell_size as usize == cell_size);
            debug_assert!(set.evacuation_of(to).is_none(), "no cell moves into an evacuated block");
            let index = descriptor.cell_index(from);
            debug_assert!(evacuation.forwarding(index).is_none());
            evacuation.forwarding[index.0].store((to >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    });
}

/// Copies each cell to the slot it moves to, once its slots and the slots that point at it are rewritten. Both slots
/// are `cell_size` bytes.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_evacuation_forward_cells(), with the same moves.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_move_cells(
    set: *mut EvacuationSet,
    moves: *const CellMove,
    count: usize,
    cell_size: usize,
) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set, and count moves.
        let (set, moves) = unsafe { (&mut *set, ak::slice_from_raw_parts(moves, count)) };
        let mut identity_hashes = None;
        for cell_move in moves {
            let (from, to) = (cell_move.from.addr(), cell_move.to.addr());
            // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell and a free slot of the same size, which do not overlap.
            unsafe {
                core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(cell_move.from.cast::<u8>(), cell_move.to.cast::<u8>(), cell_size);
                let state = cell_move.to.cast::<u8>().add(IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET);
                if state.read() != 0 {
                    let table = identity_hashes.get_or_insert_with(|| identity_hashes_of(set.heap));
                    state.write(table.did_move(
                        state.read(),
                        CompressedAddress((from >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32),
                        CompressedAddress((to >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    });
}

/// Rewrites every slot that marking recorded and that points at a cell that moves, and returns how many it rewrote.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, every cell that moves has to be forwarded and none copied yet, and the cells that held recorded
/// slots must still be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_fix_up_slots(set: *mut EvacuationSet) -> usize {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
        let set = unsafe { &*set };
        let mut rewritten = 0;
        for slots in set.all_slots() {
            for &slot in slots {
                // SAFETY: The slot was recorded in a live cell or in memory that one owns, which the caller makes sure is
                //         still live and where it was.
                if unsafe { set.fix_up(slot) } {
                    rewritten += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        rewritten
    })
}

/// How many slots marking recorded.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_recorded_slot_count(set: *const EvacuationSet) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
    unsafe { &*set }.all_slots().map(<[RecordedSlot]>::len).sum()
}

/// What a slot handed to rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot() holds.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RecordedSlotKind {
    /// A NaN-boxed value, which may hold a cell.
    Value = 0,
    /// A raw pointer to the start of a cell, or null.
    CellPointer = 1,
}

/// Records a slot that marking did not visit, which the collection then rewrites like the slots marking recorded, for
/// holders that keep cells without keeping them alive or in place: the keys of weak maps, the targets of weak
/// references. They hand over the slots of the cells that survived once they forgot those that died.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and its marking done. The slot must hold what `kind` says, in memory that nothing frees, moves or
/// writes until the collection is over, and its cell, if it has one, must be marked.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot(
    set: *mut EvacuationSet,
    slot: *const c_void,
    kind: RecordedSlotKind,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set, and a slot that holds what its kind says.
    let set = unsafe { &mut *set };
    let (target, kind) = match kind {
        RecordedSlotKind::Value => {
            // SAFETY: See above.
            let value = unsafe { slot.cast::<u64>().read() };
            if value & set.layout.value_is_cell_pattern != set.layout.value_is_cell_pattern {
                return;
            }
            (
                set.layout.heap_region_base + (value & set.layout.value_offset_mask) as usize,
                SlotKind::Value,
            )
        }
        // SAFETY: See above.
        RecordedSlotKind::CellPointer => (unsafe { slot.cast::<usize>().read() }, SlotKind::InteriorPointer),
    };
    // NB: Only slots of cells that may move need rewriting.
    if set.evacuation_of(target).is_some() {
        set.slots_recorded_after_marking
            .push(RecordedSlot::new(slot.cast(), kind));
    }
}

/// Where the cell at `cell` moved to, or null if it did not move.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_forwarding_address(
    set: *const EvacuationSet,
    cell: *const c_void,
) -> *mut c_void {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
    let set = unsafe { &*set };
    match set.forwarding_address(cell.addr()) {
        Some(address) => EvacuationSet::heap_region_pointer(address).cast(),
        None => core::ptr::null_mut(),
    }
}

/// Ends the evacuation state of a collection: its blocks are no longer evacuated.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and nothing may use it after. Its blocks must all still be its heap's, which they are until
/// the sweep that follows the collection, the only thing that lets go of a block.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_destroy(set: *mut EvacuationSet) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set, which it gives up.
    let set = unsafe { Box::from_raw(set) };
    for (index, block) in set.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        // SAFETY: The block is still the heap's, as the caller makes sure, so only this thread changes its descriptor.
        let descriptor = unsafe { descriptor_for(set.layout.heap_region_base, *block) };
        assert!(
            descriptor.heap() == set.heap
                && descriptor
                    .evacuation()
                    .is_some_and(|current| core::ptr::eq(current, set.evacuations.get(index))),
            "an evacuated block stays its heap's until its evacuation ends"
        );
        // SAFETY: The block is the heap's, and no marker runs.
        unsafe { set_evacuation_of_block(set.layout.heap_region_base, *block, core::ptr::null_mut()) };
    }
}

/// Whether the collection will move the cell at `cell`: once marking is done, a live cell of an evacuated block moves if
/// its allocator is movable and nothing pinned it. Caches that hold cells weakly drop such a cell as if it died.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `set` must be live, and its marking done.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_evacuation_will_move(set: *const EvacuationSet, cell: *const c_void) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live set.
    let set = unsafe { &*set };
    let Some((descriptor, evacuation)) = set.evacuation_of(cell.addr()) else {
        return false;
    };
    descriptor.movable
        && descriptor.is_marked(cell.addr())
        && evacuation.pin_reason(descriptor.cell_index(cell.addr())) == PinReason::Unpinned
}

/*

//! Identity hashes: a 32-bit hash of each cell that stays the same for as long as the cell lives, wherever the
//! collector moves it.
//!
//! A cell's identity hash is its compressed address at the time it is first hashed. Two bits of the header byte that
//! LibGC leaves free tell where the hash is: in an unhashed cell nowhere yet, in a hashed cell in the cell's address, and
//! in a cell that was hashed and then moved in the side table of its heap. Hashing an unhashed cell sets "hashed", so
//! that the collector knows to keep its hash when it moves the cell: under the copy's address in the side table, with
//! "moved" set on the copy. A copy that moves again has its entry rekeyed, and the entry of a cell that died is dropped
//! when the sweep frees its slot.
//!
//! Every hash of a cell's identity goes through identity_hash(), or through the inline copies of its fast path in C++
//! (GC::identity_hash()) and in LibJS's runtime, which hand the cells that moved to it.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::hash::{BuildHasherDefault, Hasher};
use std::collections::HashMap;

use crate::block::{BLOCK_SIZE, descriptor_for};
use crate::marker::COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT;

/// Where a cell keeps its identity hash state, the header byte that LibGC leaves free.
pub const IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET: usize = 8;
/// Set once the cell has been hashed, so its identity hash must survive moves.
pub const IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED: u8 = 1 << 0;
/// Set on a hashed cell that moved since it was hashed, whose hash is then in the side table of its heap.
pub const IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED: u8 = 1 << 1;

/// A cell's compressed address, which keys the side table.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct CompressedAddress(pub u32);

/// An identity hash.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IdentityHash(pub u32);

/// OPTIMIZATION: The keys are compressed addresses, whose low bits differ the most, so a multiplication spreads them
///               well enough for the table.
#[derive(Default)]
struct CompressedAddressHasher(u64);

impl Hasher for CompressedAddressHasher {
    fn finish(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        for &byte in bytes {
            self.0 = (self.0 ^ u64::from(byte)).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
        }
    }

    fn write_u32(&mut self, value: u32) {
        self.0 = u64::from(value).wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15).rotate_left(32);
    }
}

/// The side table of a heap: the identity hashes of the hashed cells that moved, by their current address.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct IdentityHashes {
    hashes: HashMap<CompressedAddress, IdentityHash, BuildHasherDefault<CompressedAddressHasher>>,
}

impl IdentityHashes {
    /// Notes that a cell with identity hash state `state` moved from `from` to `to`, and returns the state of the copy.
    pub fn did_move(&mut self, state: u8, from: CompressedAddress, to: CompressedAddress) -> u8 {
        if state & IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED == 0 {
            return state;
        }
        let hash = if state & IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED != 0 {
            self.hashes
                .remove(&from)
                .expect("a cell that moved since it was hashed has an entry")
        } else {
            IdentityHash(from.0)
        };
        self.hashes.insert(to, hash);
        state | IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED
    }

    /// Drops the entry of a cell that moved since it was hashed, whose slot is freed.
    fn forget(&mut self, address: CompressedAddress) {
        self.hashes
            .remove(&address)
            .expect("a cell that moved since it was hashed has an entry");
        // NB: The table gives its room back once most of its entries are gone, and keeps enough to grow again without
        //     shrinking and growing over and over.
        if self.hashes.capacity() > 64 && self.hashes.len() < self.hashes.capacity() / 4 {
            self.hashes.shrink_to(self.hashes.len() * 2);
        }
    }

    fn get(&self, address: CompressedAddress) -> IdentityHash {
        *self
            .hashes
            .get(&address)
            .expect("a cell that moved since it was hashed has an entry")
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Where a LibGC heap keeps its side table, which CAPI.cpp defines.
    fn gc_heap_identity_hashes(heap: *mut c_void) -> *mut *mut c_void;
}

/// The tests of this crate link without CAPI.cpp, and none of their cells is hashed.
#[cfg(test)]
mod capi_for_tests {
    use core::ffi::c_void;

    #[unsafe(no_mangle)]
    extern "C" fn gc_heap_identity_hashes(_: *mut c_void) -> *mut *mut c_void {
        unreachable!("no cell of the tests is hashed")
    }
}

/// The side table of `heap`, which this creates if it has none yet.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `heap` must be a live LibGC heap, used on this thread.
pub unsafe fn identity_hashes_of<'a>(heap: *mut c_void) -> &'a mut IdentityHashes {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live heap, whose table only its thread uses.
    unsafe {
        let slot = gc_heap_identity_hashes(heap).cast::<*mut IdentityHashes>();
        if (*slot).is_null() {
            *slot = Box::into_raw(Box::default());
        }
        &mut **slot
    }
}

/// Destroys a side table that rust_gc_identity_hash() or the mover created.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `table` must be null or a table that nothing uses any more.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_identity_hashes_destroy(table: *mut IdentityHashes) {
    if !table.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a table this crate created and nothing uses.
        drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(table) });
    }
}

/// The identity hash of the cell at `cell`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell, of a heap that this thread uses.
#[inline]
pub unsafe fn identity_hash(heap_region_base: usize, cell: *const c_void) -> IdentityHash {
    let state = cell.cast::<u8>().cast_mut().wrapping_add(IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET);
    let compressed = CompressedAddress((cell.addr() >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32);
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell, whose header has the state byte, and which only this thread touches.
    unsafe {
        let value = state.read();
        if value & IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED == 0 {
            if value & IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED == 0 {
                state.write(value | IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED);
            }
            return IdentityHash(compressed.0);
        }
        let heap = descriptor_for(heap_region_base, cell.addr()).heap();
        identity_hashes_of(heap).get(compressed)
    }
}

/// identity_hash(), for C++ and for LibJS's runtime, whose inline fast paths hand it the cells that moved.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for identity_hash().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_cell_identity_hash(heap_region_base: usize, cell: *const c_void) -> u32 {
    debug_assert!(
        cell.addr() & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1) != 0,
        "a cell is never at the start of its block"
    );
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell.
    unsafe { identity_hash(heap_region_base, cell) }.0
}

/// Whether the cell at `cell` moved since it was hashed, so that the side table of its heap has an entry for it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be an allocated cell.
pub unsafe fn has_moved_since_hashed(cell: usize) -> bool {
    // NB: Cells are in the heap region, whose provenance rust_gc_heap_region_init() exposed.
    let state = core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<u8>(cell + IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET);
    // SAFETY: The caller passes an allocated cell, whose header has the state byte.
    unsafe { state.read() & IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED != 0 }
}

/// Drops the entry of the cell at `cell` from the side table of `heap`, as the sweep frees the cell's slot, which the
/// next cell there must not inherit.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `heap` must be a live LibGC heap, used on this thread, and `cell` a cell of it that has_moved_since_hashed().
pub unsafe fn forget_identity_hash(heap: *mut c_void, cell: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live heap.
    unsafe { identity_hashes_of(heap) }.forget(CompressedAddress((cell >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32));
}
