//! Marking: from the roots, every cell of the heaps being collected that can be reached gets its mark bit set, and its
//! edges visited.
//!
//! The thread that collects marks alone at first. If cells are left after a few thousand, the helper threads of the
//! pool join in, each with a marker of its own: a cell's mark bit is set atomically, so the marker that sets it is the
//! one that visits its edges, and markers that run out of cells steal them from the others. The cells that markers have
//! yet to visit are kept as 32-bit compressed pointers.
//!
//! A cell's edges are visited through the visit_edges() of the type its block was created for, which gets the visitor
//! of the marker, which hands the cells it finds straight back to the marker. The cells of some blocks may only be
//! visited on the thread that collects, as C++ cells must, so helpers hand those to it.

use core::cell::{Cell, UnsafeCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::Barrier;

use crossbeam_deque::{Injector, Steal, Stealer, Worker};

use crate::block::{BLOCK_SIZE, BlockDescriptor, descriptor_table, heap_of_descriptor};
use crate::evacuation::{EvacuationSet, PinReason, RecordedSlot, RecordedSlots, SlotKind};
use crate::pool::{Pool, PoolGuard};
use crate::rust_panic::abort_on_panic;

pub(crate) const COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT: u32 = 3;

/// How many cells the thread that collects marks alone before the helpers join in, which takes about as long as waking
/// them. Collections that mark fewer are done before then.
const CELLS_TO_MARK_BEFORE_HELPERS: usize = 4096;

/// Where the marker finds what it needs in LibGC's cells, type infos and NaN-boxed values.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct MarkerLayout {
    pub heap_region_base: usize,
    /// The state of a cell, a u8 that is cell_state_live while the cell is live.
    pub cell_state_offset: u32,
    pub cell_state_live: u8,
    /// `void (*)(Cell*, Visitor*)`.
    pub type_info_visit_edges_offset: u32,
    /// `size_t (*)(Cell const*)`, which may be null.
    pub type_info_external_memory_size_offset: u32,
    /// The bits that are all set in a NaN-boxed value that holds a cell, whose bits under value_offset_mask are then the
    /// cell's offset into the heap region.
    pub value_is_cell_pattern: u64,
    pub value_offset_mask: u64,
}

/// Creates the visitor of a marker, a Cell::Visitor that hands what it visits to the marker, on the marker's thread.
pub type CreateVisitor = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, marker: *mut Marker) -> *mut c_void;
pub type DestroyVisitor = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void);

#[repr(C)]
pub struct MarkRequest {
    pub layout: MarkerLayout,
    /// The heaps whose cells this marks. Cells of other heaps are neither marked nor visited.
    pub heaps: *const *const c_void,
    pub heap_count: usize,
    pub roots: *const *const c_void,
    pub root_count: usize,
    /// Whether the heaps are large enough for helpers to be worth waking, should the collecting thread not finish
    /// alone soon.
    pub parallel: bool,
    pub context: *mut c_void,
    pub create_visitor: CreateVisitor,
    pub destroy_visitor: DestroyVisitor,
    /// Arrays of heap_count entries, which this sets to the bytes of the cells it marked in each heap, and the bytes
    /// that they own outside the heap.
    pub marked_cell_bytes: *mut usize,
    pub marked_external_bytes: *mut usize,
    /// Set to the number of threads that marked.
    pub threads_used: usize,
    /// The evacuation state of a collection that moves cells, which gets the slots marking records, or null.
    pub evacuation: *mut EvacuationSet,
}

type VisitEdges = unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void);
type ExternalMemorySize = unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void) -> usize;

/// What every marker of one collection shares.
struct Job<'a> {
    layout: MarkerLayout,
    descriptors: NonNull<BlockDescriptor>,
    heaps: &'a [*const c_void],
    markers: Vec<Marker>,
    stealers: Vec<Stealer<u32>>,
    /// The cells that only the thread that collects may visit the edges of.
    owner_queue: Injector<u32>,
    /// How many markers mark in this round; 1 until the helpers join in.
    participants: AtomicUsize,
    /// The markers that found no work, see Marker::run_round().
    idle_markers: AtomicUsize,
    round_done: Barrier,
    /// Whether the markers go for another round, which the owner decides once a round is done.
    another_round: AtomicBool,
    context: *mut c_void,
    create_visitor: CreateVisitor,
    destroy_visitor: DestroyVisitor,
}

// SAFETY: Each marker is only used by its own thread while markers run. The thread that collects reads all of them
//         while every other marker waits at a barrier or is done. The rest is either immutable or synchronized.
unsafe impl Sync for Job<'_> {}

/// One thread's marker. The first is the one of the thread that collects (the owner).
///
/// Marking reenters the marker: a cell's visit_edges() hands the cells it finds back to the marker that visits it. So
/// a marker is only ever used through shared references.
pub struct Marker {
    job: Cell<*const Job<'static>>,
    is_owner: bool,
    /// Whether other markers may set mark bits at the same time.
    shared: Cell<bool>,
    queue: Worker<u32>,
    /// The owner's cells that only it may visit, which no other marker can steal. Once helpers mark too, the owner
    /// visits these first: they are what only it can do, while the other markers take the rest.
    owner_only_queue: Worker<u32>,
    visitor: Cell<*mut c_void>,
    marked_cell_bytes: Box<[Cell<usize>]>,
    marked_external_bytes: Box<[Cell<usize>]>,
    /// Ephemerons whose key was not marked yet when they were visited.
    pending_ephemerons: UnsafeCell<Vec<PendingEphemeron>>,
    /// The slots that point into evacuated blocks, which a collection that moves cells rewrites.
    recorded_slots: UnsafeCell<RecordedSlots>,
}

/// An ephemeron whose key was not marked yet when it was visited, with compressed addresses.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct PendingEphemeron {
    key: u32,
    value: u32,
    /// Whether marking the value pins it, see Marker::visit_ephemeron().
    pins_value: bool,
}

impl Job<'_> {
    #[inline(always)]
    fn compress(&self, address: usize) -> u32 {
        ((address - self.layout.heap_region_base) >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn decompress(&self, compressed: u32) -> usize {
        self.layout.heap_region_base + ((compressed as usize) << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT)
    }

    /// The descriptor of the block of a cell of the heaps being collected.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn descriptor(&self, address: usize) -> &BlockDescriptor {
        self.descriptor_in_domain(address)
            .expect("the cell is in a heap being collected")
            .1
    }

    /// The index among the heaps being collected of the heap of the block that `address` is in, and the block's
    /// descriptor, if it is one of them. Only then is the descriptor borrowed, as the descriptor of a block of another
    /// heap may change meanwhile, see heap_of_descriptor().
    #[inline(always)]
    fn descriptor_in_domain(&self, address: usize) -> Option<(usize, &BlockDescriptor)> {
        let index = (address - self.layout.heap_region_base) / BLOCK_SIZE;
        // SAFETY: Every cell is in a block of the region, whose descriptor is in the table.
        let descriptor = unsafe { self.descriptors.add(index) };
        // SAFETY: As above.
        let heap = unsafe { heap_of_descriptor(descriptor.as_ptr()) }.cast_const();
        let heap_index = if self.heaps.len() == 1 {
            (self.heaps[0] == heap).then_some(0)
        } else {
            self.heaps.iter().position(|&candidate| candidate == heap)
        }?;
        // SAFETY: The block belongs to a heap being collected, which is stopped, so nothing changes its descriptor but
        //         the mark bits, which are atomic.
        Some((heap_index, unsafe { descriptor.as_ref() }))
    }

    /// Whether `address` is in the heap region, and so in a cell, since the collector only records slots in cells.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn is_in_heap_region(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        (address.wrapping_sub(self.layout.heap_region_base) as u64) <= self.layout.value_offset_mask
    }
}

impl Marker {
    fn job(&self) -> &Job<'static> {
        // SAFETY: The job outlives its markers' use.
        unsafe { &*self.job.get() }
    }

    /// Sets the mark bit of the cell at `address` if it is in one of the heaps being collected, and queues the cell if
    /// that was news, which this returns. This is a visit by value, which pins the cell if its block is evacuated.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn mark(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        self.mark_pinned(address, PinReason::Edge)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn mark_pinned(&self, address: usize, reason: PinReason) -> bool {
        let job = self.job();
        let Some((_, descriptor)) = job.descriptor_in_domain(address) else {
            return false;
        };
        if let Some(evacuation) = descriptor.evacuation() {
            evacuation.pin(descriptor, address, reason);
        }
        self.mark_in(descriptor, address)
    }

    /// Marks the cell at `address`, which a slot at `slot` points to. If the cell's block is evacuated, the slot is
    /// recorded, so that it can be rewritten once the cell moves, or the cell pinned if the slot is not in a cell. A
    /// cell that is pinned already, as roots are before marking starts, stays where it is, so its slots are left out.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn mark_through_slot(&self, slot: RecordedSlot, address: usize) {
        self.mark_through_slot_of::<false>(slot, address);
    }

    /// Like mark_through_slot(), and if `SLOT_IS_OWNED`, the slot is recorded even outside the heap region, as it is in
    /// memory that a live cell owns and that stays where it is until the collection is over (see visit_owned_values()).
    #[inline(always)]
    fn mark_through_slot_of<const SLOT_IS_OWNED: bool>(&self, slot: RecordedSlot, address: usize) {
        let job = self.job();
        let Some((_, descriptor)) = job.descriptor_in_domain(address) else {
            return;
        };
        if let Some(evacuation) = descriptor.evacuation()
            && !evacuation.is_pinned(descriptor, address)
        {
            if SLOT_IS_OWNED || job.is_in_heap_region(slot.address()) {
                // SAFETY: Only this marker's thread touches its recorded slots while it marks.
                unsafe { &mut *self.recorded_slots.get() }.push(slot);
            } else {
                evacuation.pin(descriptor, address, PinReason::Edge);
            }
        }
        self.mark_in(descriptor, address);
    }

    /// Pins the cell at `address` without marking it, for a weak reference that the collector cannot update.
    fn pin(&self, address: usize) {
        let job = self.job();
        let Some((_, descriptor)) = job.descriptor_in_domain(address) else {
            return;
        };
        if let Some(evacuation) = descriptor.evacuation() {
            evacuation.pin(descriptor, address, PinReason::Edge);
        }
    }

    /// Records a slot that points into the cell that holds it, if that cell's block is evacuated.
    fn visit_self_pointer(&self, slot: *const usize) {
        let job = self.job();
        if !job.is_in_heap_region(slot.addr()) {
            return;
        }
        if let Some((_, descriptor)) = job.descriptor_in_domain(slot.addr())
            && descriptor.evacuation().is_some()
        {
            // SAFETY: Only this marker's thread touches its recorded slots while it marks.
            unsafe { &mut *self.recorded_slots.get() }.push(RecordedSlot::new(slot.cast(), SlotKind::SelfPointer));
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn mark_in(&self, descriptor: &BlockDescriptor, address: usize) -> bool {
        let job = self.job();
        let newly_marked = if self.shared.get() {
            descriptor.mark(address)
        } else {
            descriptor.mark_exclusive(address)
        };
        if newly_marked {
            // NB: The cell's edges are visited soon, as the queue is a stack.
            #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
            // SAFETY: Prefetching has no effect on memory.
            unsafe {
                core::arch::x86_64::_mm_prefetch(address as *const i8, core::arch::x86_64::_MM_HINT_T0);
            }
            let compressed = job.compress(address);
            if descriptor.traced_on_owner_thread_only && self.shared.get() {
                if self.is_owner {
                    self.owner_only_queue.push(compressed);
                } else {
                    job.owner_queue.push(compressed);
                }
            } else {
                self.queue.push(compressed);
            }
        }
        newly_marked
    }

    /// Marks the cells of the values in `values`, which are slots.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn visit_values(&self, values: &[u64]) {
        self.visit_values_of::<false>(values);
    }

    /// Marks the cells of the values in `values`, which are slots in memory outside the heap region that the cell
    /// being visited owns, and that nothing frees, moves or writes until the collection is over. A collection rewrites
    /// them where they are, like slots in cells, rather than pinning their cells.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn visit_owned_values(&self, values: &[u64]) {
        self.visit_values_of::<true>(values);
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn visit_values_of<const SLOTS_ARE_OWNED: bool>(&self, values: &[u64]) {
        let layout = &self.job().layout;
        for value in values {
            let bits = *value;
            if bits & layout.value_is_cell_pattern == layout.value_is_cell_pattern {
                self.mark_through_slot_of::<SLOTS_ARE_OWNED>(
                    RecordedSlot::new(core::ptr::from_ref(value).cast(), SlotKind::Value),
                    layout.heap_region_base + (bits & layout.value_offset_mask) as usize,
                );
            }
        }
    }

    /// Marks the cell a compressed pointer at `slot` points to, if it is not null.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn visit_member(&self, slot: *const u32) {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live slot.
        let compressed = unsafe { slot.read() };
        if compressed != 0 {
            let address = self.job().decompress(compressed);
            self.mark_through_slot(RecordedSlot::new(slot.cast(), SlotKind::Member), address);
        }
    }

    /// Marks `value` once `key` is marked. If `pins`, the key and the value stay where they are, as their holder visits
    /// them by value. Otherwise the holder hands their slots to the collection once marking is done (see
    /// rust_gc_evacuation_record_slot()), and only cells pinned by others stay where they are.
    fn visit_ephemeron(&self, key: usize, value: usize, pins: bool) {
        let job = self.job();
        if pins {
            self.pin(key);
        }
        // NB: Keys outside the heaps being collected are never marked here, so their values stay reachable.
        if job
            .descriptor_in_domain(key)
            .is_none_or(|(_, descriptor)| descriptor.is_marked(key))
        {
            self.mark_value_of_ephemeron(value, pins);
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: Only this marker's thread touches its pending ephemerons while it marks.
        unsafe { &mut *self.pending_ephemerons.get() }.push(PendingEphemeron {
            key: job.compress(key),
            value: job.compress(value),
            pins_value: pins,
        });
    }

    /// Marks the value of an ephemeron whose key is marked, and returns whether that was news.
    fn mark_value_of_ephemeron(&self, value: usize, pins: bool) -> bool {
        if pins {
            return self.mark(value);
        }
        let job = self.job();
        let Some((_, descriptor)) = job.descriptor_in_domain(value) else {
            return false;
        };
        self.mark_in(descriptor, value)
    }

    fn find_work(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        let job = self.job();
        if self.is_owner
            && let Some(cell) = self.owner_only_queue.pop()
        {
            return Some(cell);
        }
        loop {
            let mut retry = false;
            if self.is_owner {
                match job.owner_queue.steal_batch_and_pop(&self.owner_only_queue) {
                    Steal::Success(cell) => return Some(cell),
                    Steal::Retry => retry = true,
                    Steal::Empty => {}
                }
            }
            if let Some(cell) = self.queue.pop() {
                return Some(cell);
            }
            if self.shared.get() {
                for stealer in &job.stealers {
                    match stealer.steal_batch_and_pop(&self.queue) {
                        Steal::Success(cell) => return Some(cell),
                        Steal::Retry => retry = true,
                        Steal::Empty => {}
                    }
                }
            }
            if !retry {
                return None;
            }
        }
    }

    fn has_visible_work(&self) -> bool {
        let job = self.job();
        (self.is_owner && !job.owner_queue.is_empty()) || job.stealers.iter().any(|stealer| !stealer.is_empty())
    }

    /// Visits the edges of a marked cell, and counts the cell and the memory it owns outside the heap.
    fn visit_edges_of(&self, compressed: u32) {
        let job = self.job();
        let layout = &job.layout;
        let address = job.decompress(compressed);
        let (heap_index, descriptor) = job
            .descriptor_in_domain(address)
            .expect("only cells of the heaps being collected are marked");
        if !self.is_owner && descriptor.traced_on_owner_thread_only {
            job.owner_queue.push(compressed);
            return;
        }
        // NB: Cell addresses are in the heap region, whose provenance rust_gc_heap_region_init() exposed.
        let cell = core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<c_void>(address);
        // SAFETY: The cell is in a block of a heap being collected, which no thread changes meanwhile.
        if unsafe { cell.cast::<u8>().add(layout.cell_state_offset as usize).read() } != layout.cell_state_live {
            return;
        }
        let marked_cell_bytes = &self.marked_cell_bytes[heap_index];
        marked_cell_bytes.set(marked_cell_bytes.get() + descriptor.cell_size as usize);
        let type_info = descriptor.type_info.cast::<u8>();
        // SAFETY: The type info of a block outlives it, and the layout says where its functions are.
        let (external_memory_size, visit_edges) = unsafe {
            (
                type_info
                    .add(layout.type_info_external_memory_size_offset as usize)
                    .cast::<Option<ExternalMemorySize>>()
                    .read(),
                type_info
                    .add(layout.type_info_visit_edges_offset as usize)
                    .cast::<VisitEdges>()
                    .read(),
            )
        };
        if let Some(external_memory_size) = external_memory_size {
            // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the type whose function this is.
            let size = unsafe { external_memory_size(cell) };
            let marked_external_bytes = &self.marked_external_bytes[heap_index];
            marked_external_bytes.set(marked_external_bytes.get().saturating_add(size));
        }
        // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the type whose function this is, which may be visited on this thread, and
        //         the visitor is this marker's.
        unsafe { visit_edges(cell, self.visitor.get()) };
    }

    /// Visits the edges of at most `limit` cells, on this thread alone, and returns whether no cell was left.
    fn drain_alone(&self, mut limit: usize) -> bool {
        while limit != 0 {
            let Some(cell) = self.find_work() else {
                return true;
            };
            self.visit_edges_of(cell);
            limit -= 1;
        }
        self.queue.is_empty() && self.owner_only_queue.is_empty() && self.job().owner_queue.is_empty()
    }

    /// Visits edges until no marker has cells left.
    fn run_round(&self) {
        let job = self.job();
        loop {
            while let Some(cell) = self.find_work() {
                self.visit_edges_of(cell);
            }

            // NB: A marker only queues cells while it is not idle, and only the owner takes from the owner queue. So
            //     once every marker is idle and the owner queue is empty, no cell is left anywhere.
            job.idle_markers.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            let mut waits = 0u32;
            loop {
                if self.has_visible_work() {
                    job.idle_markers.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                    break;
                }
                if job.idle_markers.load(Ordering::SeqCst) == job.participants.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
                    && job.owner_queue.is_empty()
                {
                    return;
                }
                // NB: A marker that waits long yields, rather than take the time of a thread it shares a core with.
                waits += 1;
                if waits < 1024 {
                    core::hint::spin_loop();
                } else {
                    std::thread::yield_now();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Marks the values of the pending ephemerons of every marker whose key was marked since, into this marker, which
    /// must be the owner's. Returns whether that marked any.
    fn mark_values_of_reached_ephemerons(&self) -> bool {
        let job = self.job();
        let mut marked_a_value = false;
        for marker in &job.markers {
            // SAFETY: Every other marker waits at the barrier or is done.
            let pending = unsafe { &mut *marker.pending_ephemerons.get() };
            pending.retain(|ephemeron| {
                let key = job.decompress(ephemeron.key);
                if !job.descriptor(key).is_marked(key) {
                    return true;
                }
                marked_a_value |= self.mark_value_of_ephemeron(job.decompress(ephemeron.value), ephemeron.pins_value);
                false
            });
        }
        marked_a_value
    }

    fn create_visitor(&self) {
        let job = self.job();
        // SAFETY: The marker outlives its visitor.
        let visitor = unsafe { (job.create_visitor)(job.context, core::ptr::from_ref(self).cast_mut()) };
        self.visitor.set(visitor);
    }

    fn destroy_visitor(&self) {
        let job = self.job();
        // SAFETY: The visitor was created for this marker, which is done with it.
        unsafe { (job.destroy_visitor)(job.context, self.visitor.get()) };
    }
}

/// What every marker runs once the helpers joined in, with its index; the owner's is 0.
fn mark_in_parallel(job: &Job<'static>, index: usize) {
    let marker = &job.markers[index];
    marker.shared.set(true);
    if index != 0 {
        marker.create_visitor();
    }
    loop {
        marker.run_round();
        job.round_done.wait();
        // NB: Marking can reach the key of a pending ephemeron, so the owner looks at those between rounds, and the
        //     markers go again while that marks more.
        if index == 0 {
            job.idle_markers.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);
            let another_round = marker.mark_values_of_reached_ephemerons();
            job.another_round.store(another_round, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
        job.round_done.wait();
        if !job.another_round.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            break;
        }
    }
    if index != 0 {
        marker.destroy_visitor();
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `data` must be a live Job, and `index` a marker of it that runs nowhere else.
unsafe fn mark_in_parallel_from_pool(data: *const (), index: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live job.
    let job = unsafe { &*data.cast::<Job<'static>>() };
    abort_on_panic(|| mark_in_parallel(job, index));
}

/// Marks the cell a visitor visits, which must be the start of a cell.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `marker` must be the marker the visitor was created for, on its thread, and `cell` a cell.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(marker: *mut Marker, cell: *const c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.mark(cell.addr());
}

/// Marks the cells of the NaN-boxed values a visitor visits.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(), with `count` values at `values`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_values(marker: *mut Marker, values: *const u64, count: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker and count values.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_values(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(values, count) });
}

/// Marks the cells of the NaN-boxed values a visitor visits in memory that the cell being visited owns outside the heap
/// region, as slots the collector can update.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_values(), and the values must be in memory that the cell being visited owns, which
/// nothing frees, moves or writes until the collection is over: no finalizer, destructor or sweep callback touches it.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_owned_values(marker: *mut Marker, values: *const u64, count: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker and count values.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_owned_values(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(values, count) });
}

/// Marks the cell that the compressed pointer at `slot` points to, if it is not null, as a slot the collector can update.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(), and `slot` must hold a compressed cell pointer or 0.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_member(marker: *mut Marker, slot: *const u32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker and slot.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_member(slot);
}

/// Marks `cell`, which the pointer at `slot` points into, as a slot the collector can update.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(), and `slot` must hold a pointer into `cell`, past its start.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_interior_pointer(
    marker: *mut Marker,
    slot: *const usize,
    cell: *const c_void,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.mark_through_slot(RecordedSlot::new(slot.cast(), SlotKind::InteriorPointer), cell.addr());
}

/// Notes that the pointer at `slot` points into the cell that holds the slot, which keeps it right if that cell moves.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(), and `slot` must be in a cell being visited, and point into it, up to one past
/// its end.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_self_pointer(marker: *mut Marker, slot: *const usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_self_pointer(slot);
}

/// Keeps `cell` from moving, without marking it, for a weak reference the collector cannot update.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_pin_cell(marker: *mut Marker, cell: *const c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.pin(cell.addr());
}

/// Marks a cell that is reachable only while `key` is, such as a WeakMap entry's value, once the key is marked. Both
/// stay where they are, as their holder visits them by value.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_cell(), and `key` and `value` must be cells.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_ephemeron(marker: *mut Marker, key: *const c_void, value: *const c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_ephemeron(key.addr(), value.addr(), true);
}

/// Like rust_gc_marker_visit_ephemeron(), for a holder that keeps neither cell from moving: once marking is done, and
/// before cells move, it hands the slots of the key and the value of each entry that survived to the collection.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// As for rust_gc_marker_visit_ephemeron().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_visit_ephemeron_without_pinning(
    marker: *mut Marker,
    key: *const c_void,
    value: *const c_void,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live marker.
    unsafe { &*marker }.visit_ephemeron(key.addr(), value.addr(), false);
}

/// Has the threads that help mark give back the memory they no longer use, see Pool::release_unused_memory().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_release_unused_helper_memory() {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        if let Some(pool) = Pool::the() {
            pool.release_unused_memory();
        }
    });
}

/// Marks every cell of the heaps that the roots reach, and adds up the bytes they take.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The request must be valid as its fields describe. Nothing else may use the heaps until this returns.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_gc_marker_mark(request: *mut MarkRequest) {
    abort_on_panic(|| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a valid request.
        let request = unsafe { &mut *request };
        // SAFETY: The caller passes heap_count heaps.
        let heaps = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(request.heaps, request.heap_count) };
        // SAFETY: The caller passes root_count roots.
        let roots = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(request.roots, request.root_count) };
        mark(request, heaps, roots);
    });
}

fn mark(request: &mut MarkRequest, heaps: &[*const c_void], roots: &[*const c_void]) {
    let pool = if request.parallel { Pool::the() } else { None };
    let marker_count = pool.map_or(0, Pool::helper_count) + 1;
    let mut job = Job {
        layout: request.layout,
        descriptors: descriptor_table(),
        heaps,
        markers: Vec::with_capacity(marker_count),
        stealers: Vec::with_capacity(marker_count),
        owner_queue: Injector::new(),
        participants: AtomicUsize::new(1),
        idle_markers: AtomicUsize::new(0),
        round_done: Barrier::new(marker_count),
        another_round: AtomicBool::new(false),
        context: request.context,
        create_visitor: request.create_visitor,
        destroy_visitor: request.destroy_visitor,
    };
    for index in 0..marker_count {
        let queue = Worker::new_lifo();
        job.stealers.push(queue.stealer());
        job.markers.push(Marker {
            job: Cell::new(core::ptr::null()),
            is_owner: index == 0,
            shared: Cell::new(false),
            queue,
            owner_only_queue: Worker::new_lifo(),
            visitor: Cell::new(core::ptr::null_mut()),
            marked_cell_bytes: (0..heaps.len()).map(|_| Cell::new(0)).collect(),
            marked_external_bytes: (0..heaps.len()).map(|_| Cell::new(0)).collect(),
            pending_ephemerons: UnsafeCell::new(Vec::new()),
            recorded_slots: UnsafeCell::new(RecordedSlots::default()),
        });
    }
    // NB: The job lives on this stack until every marker is done with it, so the markers may point at it as if it lived
    //     forever.
    let job_pointer = (&raw const job).cast::<Job<'static>>();
    for marker in &job.markers {
        marker.job.set(job_pointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: See job_pointer.
    let job = unsafe { &*job_pointer };
    let owner = &job.markers[0];
    owner.create_visitor();
    for &root in roots {
        owner.mark_pinned(root.addr(), PinReason::Root);
    }

    // NB: Collections that mark few cells are done before helpers could have started.
    let mut threads_used = 1;
    let mut done_alone = owner.drain_alone(CELLS_TO_MARK_BEFORE_HELPERS);
    let helpers: Option<PoolGuard> = if done_alone {
        None
    } else {
        pool.and_then(Pool::try_acquire)
    };
    match helpers {
        Some(helpers) => {
            threads_used = marker_count;
            job.participants.store(marker_count, Ordering::SeqCst);
            // SAFETY: mark_in_parallel_from_pool() takes the job and the index of a helper's marker, which runs nowhere
            //         else.
            unsafe {
                helpers.run(mark_in_parallel_from_pool, job_pointer.cast(), || {
                    mark_in_parallel(job, 0);
                });
            };
        }
        None => {
            // NB: Another heap may be using the helpers, so this one marks alone.
            loop {
                if !done_alone {
                    owner.drain_alone(usize::MAX);
                }
                if !owner.mark_values_of_reached_ephemerons() {
                    break;
                }
                done_alone = false;
            }
        }
    }
    owner.destroy_visitor();

    for heap_index in 0..heaps.len() {
        let mut cell_bytes = 0usize;
        let mut external_bytes = 0usize;
        for marker in &job.markers {
            cell_bytes += marker.marked_cell_bytes[heap_index].get();
            external_bytes = external_bytes.saturating_add(marker.marked_external_bytes[heap_index].get());
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller passes arrays of heap_count entries.
        unsafe {
            request.marked_cell_bytes.add(heap_index).write(cell_bytes);
            request.marked_external_bytes.add(heap_index).write(external_bytes);
        }
    }
    request.threads_used = threads_used;

    // SAFETY: The caller passes null or a live evacuation set, which nothing else uses meanwhile.
    if let Some(evacuation) = unsafe { request.evacuation.as_mut() } {
        for marker in &job.markers {
            // SAFETY: Every marker is done.
            evacuation.add_recorded_slots(core::mem::take(unsafe { &mut *marker.recorded_slots.get() }));
        }
    }
}

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The virtual memory operations the collector needs: reserving zero-filled address space that is only backed by
//! memory where it is touched, committing the chunks of the heap region that C++ reserved, and handing the pages of
//! unused blocks back to the system while keeping them committed.

use core::ptr::NonNull;

#[cfg(unix)]
mod platform {
    use core::ptr::NonNull;

    // Tags the heap's memory on macOS, as Core::System does, so that tools like vmmap show it apart from malloc.
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    const MEMORY_TAG: i32 = 241 << 24;
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
    const MEMORY_TAG: i32 = -1;

    pub fn reserve_zeroed(size: usize) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
        // SAFETY: An anonymous mapping that the kernel places anywhere touches no existing memory.
        let address = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                size,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS | libc::MAP_NORESERVE,
                MEMORY_TAG,
                0,
            )
        };
        if address == libc::MAP_FAILED {
            return None;
        }
        NonNull::new(address.cast())
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be all of a reservation that reserve_zeroed() returned, which nothing uses any more.
    pub unsafe fn release(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a whole reservation that nothing uses.
        let result = unsafe { libc::munmap(address.as_ptr().cast(), size) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "munmap() failed");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be within memory that reserve_zeroed() returned.
    pub unsafe fn commit_reserved_zeroed(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {
        // NB: Anonymous mappings are backed by zeroed pages as they are first touched.
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be reserved address space that holds nothing yet.
    pub unsafe fn commit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the range is reserved, so mapping over it replaces nothing else.
        let mapped = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                address.as_ptr().cast(),
                size,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS | libc::MAP_FIXED,
                MEMORY_TAG,
                0,
            )
        };
        assert!(mapped != libc::MAP_FAILED, "commit a chunk of the heap region");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory.
    pub unsafe fn populate(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: This only fails if the kernel is too old to know it, which leaves the faults to the first touches.
        #[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the range is committed memory.
        unsafe {
            libc::madvise(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, libc::MADV_POPULATE_WRITE);
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android")))]
        let _ = (address, size);
    }

    /// Whether the range is made of whole pages. Advice applies to whole pages, and where a page is larger than a
    /// block, as on systems with 64 KiB pages, it also holds other blocks, which may be in use.
    fn is_whole_pages(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) -> bool {
        static PAGE_SIZE: std::sync::OnceLock<usize> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
        let page_size = *PAGE_SIZE.get_or_init(|| {
            // SAFETY: Reading a system configuration value has no preconditions.
            let page_size = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
            usize::try_from(page_size).expect("the page size is known")
        });
        address.as_ptr().addr().is_multiple_of(page_size) && size.is_multiple_of(page_size)
    }

    fn madvise(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize, advice: i32, what: &str) {
        // SAFETY: Every caller passes committed memory whose contents nothing needs, or that it is about to use again.
        let result = unsafe { libc::madvise(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, advice) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "{what} failed");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
    pub unsafe fn discard(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: Where pages hold more than one block, the pages of a free block stay as they are.
        if !is_whole_pages(address, size) {
            return;
        }
        // NB: macOS has a paired protocol for this, which its accounting of resident memory understands.
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_FREE_REUSABLE, "madvise(MADV_FREE_REUSABLE)");
        // NB: MADV_FREE keeps the pages mapped until the kernel needs them, so a block reused before then takes no
        //     page fault.
        #[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android", target_os = "freebsd"))]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_FREE, "madvise(MADV_FREE)");
        #[cfg(not(any(
            target_os = "macos",
            target_os = "linux",
            target_os = "android",
            target_os = "freebsd"
        )))]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_DONTNEED, "madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
    pub unsafe fn return_to_system(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: As in discard().
        if !is_whole_pages(address, size) {
            return;
        }
        #[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_DONTNEED, "madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)");
        // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
        #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android")))]
        unsafe {
            discard(address, size);
        }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory that was discarded, or that mark_reusable() was called on.
    pub unsafe fn reuse(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_FREE_REUSE, "madvise(MADV_FREE_REUSE)");
        #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
        let _ = (address, size);
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory that holds nothing yet.
    pub unsafe fn mark_reusable(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: So that reuse() pairs with this when the blocks of a new chunk are handed out.
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        madvise(address, size, libc::MADV_FREE_REUSABLE, "madvise(MADV_FREE_REUSABLE)");
        #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
        let _ = (address, size);
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod platform {
    use core::ptr::NonNull;
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
        MEM_COMMIT, MEM_RELEASE, MEM_RESERVE, MEM_RESET, PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_READWRITE, VirtualAlloc, VirtualFree,
        VirtualUnlock,
    };

    pub fn reserve_zeroed(size: usize) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
        // NB: Windows has no lazily committed memory that does not count towards the commit limit, so this reserves
        //     only, and commit_reserved_zeroed() commits what is used.
        // SAFETY: Reserving address space that the system places anywhere touches no existing memory.
        let address = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(core::ptr::null(), size, MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_NOACCESS) };
        NonNull::new(address.cast())
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be all of a reservation that reserve_zeroed() returned, which nothing uses any more.
    pub unsafe fn release(address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a whole reservation that nothing uses.
        let released = unsafe { VirtualFree(address.as_ptr().cast(), 0, MEM_RELEASE) };
        assert!(released != 0, "VirtualFree(MEM_RELEASE) failed");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be within memory that reserve_zeroed() returned.
    pub unsafe fn commit_reserved_zeroed(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: Committing pages that are committed already leaves their contents alone.
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the range is reserved.
        let committed = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) };
        assert!(!committed.is_null(), "commit the table of block descriptors");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be reserved address space that holds nothing yet.
    pub unsafe fn commit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the range is reserved.
        let committed = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE) };
        assert!(!committed.is_null(), "commit a chunk of the heap region");
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory.
    pub unsafe fn populate(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {}

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
    pub unsafe fn discard(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // NB: DiscardVirtualMemory() validates its range with VirtualQuery(), which makes the kernel check every page in
        //     the run of identical pages that starts at the block. All chunks are committed back to back in one
        //     reservation, so that run is the whole committed heap. MEM_RESET drops the contents without that walk, and
        //     VirtualUnlock() on pages that are not locked takes them out of the working set right away.
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the contents are unused.
        let reset = unsafe { VirtualAlloc(address.as_ptr().cast(), size, MEM_RESET, PAGE_READWRITE) };
        assert!(!reset.is_null(), "VirtualAlloc(MEM_RESET) failed");
        // SAFETY: As above.
        unsafe { VirtualUnlock(address.as_ptr().cast(), size) };
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
    pub unsafe fn return_to_system(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
        // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
        unsafe { discard(address, size) }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory.
    pub unsafe fn reuse(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {}

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The range must be committed memory.
    pub unsafe fn mark_reusable(_address: NonNull<u8>, _size: usize) {}
}

pub fn reserve_zeroed(size: usize) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
    platform::reserve_zeroed(size)
}

/// Gives back all of a reservation that reserve_zeroed() returned.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be all of a reservation that reserve_zeroed() returned, which nothing uses any more.
pub unsafe fn release(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::release(address, size) }
}

/// Backs a range of memory that reserve_zeroed() returned with memory, if it was not already.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be within memory that reserve_zeroed() returned.
pub unsafe fn commit_reserved_zeroed(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The caller's guarantee is the platform's.
    unsafe { platform::commit_reserved_zeroed(address, size) }
}

/// Commits a range of address space that the heap region reserved, which reads as zero until it is written.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be reserved address space that holds nothing yet.
pub unsafe fn commit(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::commit(address, size) }
}

/// Faults the pages of a committed range in at once, where the system can do that, which costs a fraction of faulting
/// them in one by one.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be committed memory.
pub unsafe fn populate(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::populate(address, size) }
}

/// Lets the system take back the pages of a committed range when it runs short of memory. Until then, they keep their
/// contents and cost no fault when they are written again.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
pub unsafe fn discard(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::discard(address, size) }
}

/// Gives the pages of a committed range back to the system right away, where the system can tell that apart from
/// discard().
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be committed memory whose contents nothing needs any more.
pub unsafe fn return_to_system(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::return_to_system(address, size) }
}

/// Tells the system that a range that discard() or mark_reusable() was called on is in use again.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be committed memory.
pub unsafe fn reuse(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::reuse(address, size) }
}

/// Marks a freshly committed range as unused, so that reuse() pairs with it as it does with discard().
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The range must be committed memory that holds nothing yet.
pub unsafe fn mark_reusable(address: NonNull<u8>, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Forwarded from the caller.
    unsafe { platform::mark_reusable(address, size) }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/Rust/src/pool.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The threads that help the thread that owns a heap mark it. They live as long as the process, and wait for the next
//! collection in between, so a collection does not pay for creating them.

use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard, OnceLock, PoisonError};

/// The most threads that mark a heap, the thread that owns it included, unless LIBGC_MARKER_THREADS asks for another
/// number. Marking is bound by memory accesses, so more threads than this gain little.
const DEFAULT_MAX_THREADS: usize = 8;

/// The threads that mark a heap, the thread that owns it included.
pub(crate) fn thread_count() -> usize {
    static COUNT: OnceLock<usize> = OnceLock::new();
    *COUNT.get_or_init(|| {
        if let Some(count) = std::env::var("LIBGC_MARKER_THREADS")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())
        {
            return count.clamp(1, 64);
        }
        std::thread::available_parallelism()
            .map_or(1, usize::from)
            .min(DEFAULT_MAX_THREADS)
    })
}

/// What a collection hands the helpers: a function they each call with the data and their index, from 1 up.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Task {
    run: unsafe fn(data: *const (), index: usize),
    data: *const (),
}

// SAFETY: The thread that hands out a task keeps its data alive and waits for every helper to be done with it.
unsafe impl Send for Task {}

struct State {
    /// Goes up by one for every task, which tells the helpers that a new one is there.
    generation: u64,
    task: Option<Task>,
    /// The helpers that have yet to finish the current task.
    helpers_left: usize,
}

pub(crate) struct Pool {
    /// The helpers that started, which is set once before the pool is used.
    helper_count: AtomicUsize,
    state: Mutex<State>,
    task_available: Condvar,
    helpers_done: Condvar,
    /// Held while a collection uses the helpers. Heaps of other threads collect on their own meanwhile.
    in_use: Mutex<()>,
    /// Whether the helpers ran a task since they last gave their unused memory back, see release_unused_memory().
    ran_since_release: AtomicBool,
}

fn lock<T>(mutex: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    mutex.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

impl Pool {
    /// The pool of the process, which is created on first use. There is none if only one thread marks.
    pub(crate) fn the() -> Option<&'static Pool> {
        static POOL: OnceLock<Option<&'static Pool>> = OnceLock::new();
        *POOL.get_or_init(|| {
            let helper_count = thread_count() - 1;
            if helper_count == 0 {
                return None;
            }
            let pool: &'static Pool = Box::leak(Box::new(Pool {
                helper_count: AtomicUsize::new(0),
                state: Mutex::new(State {
                    generation: 0,
                    task: None,
                    helpers_left: 0,
                }),
                task_available: Condvar::new(),
                helpers_done: Condvar::new(),
                in_use: Mutex::new(()),
                ran_since_release: AtomicBool::new(false),
            }));
            // NB: A helper that cannot start, as when the process has as many threads as it may, leaves marking to the
            //     ones that did, or to the thread that owns the heap alone.
            let started = (1..=helper_count)
                .take_while(|&index| {
                    std::thread::Builder::new()
                        .name("GC marker".into())
                        .spawn(move || pool.run_helper(index))
                        .is_ok()
                })
                .count();
            if started == 0 {
                return None;
            }
            pool.helper_count.store(started, Ordering::Relaxed);
            Some(pool)
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn helper_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.helper_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// Takes the helpers for one collection, unless another thread uses them.
    pub(crate) fn try_acquire(&'static self) -> Option<PoolGuard> {
        let guard = self.in_use.try_lock().ok()?;
        Some(PoolGuard {
            pool: self,
            _in_use: guard,
        })
    }

    /// Has the helpers give back the memory they freed, unless another heap uses them now, which does the same once it is
    /// done. What a helper allocates while it marks, such as room in its queue, is freed by the thread that collects
    /// once the collection is over, and the allocator keeps it for the helper until the helper allocates again, which an
    /// idle helper never does.
    pub(crate) fn release_unused_memory(&'static self) {
        if !self.ran_since_release.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return;
        }
        let Some(helpers) = self.try_acquire() else {
            return;
        };
        unsafe fn release(_: *const (), _: usize) {
            ak::release_unused_allocator_memory();
        }
        // SAFETY: release() takes nothing, and any thread may call it.
        unsafe { helpers.run(release, core::ptr::null(), || {}) };
        // NB: Running this task set the flag as well. No other task runs while the helpers are taken.
        self.ran_since_release.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    fn run_helper(&self, index: usize) {
        // NB: The pool starts at generation 0, so a helper that starts after the first task was handed out still sees it.
        let mut seen_generation = 0;
        loop {
            let task = {
                let mut state = lock(&self.state);
                while state.generation == seen_generation {
                    state = self.task_available.wait(state).unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
                }
                seen_generation = state.generation;
                state.task.expect("a new generation has a task")
            };
            // SAFETY: The thread that handed out the task keeps its data alive until every helper is done with it.
            unsafe { (task.run)(task.data, index) };
            let mut state = lock(&self.state);
            state.helpers_left -= 1;
            if state.helpers_left == 0 {
                self.helpers_done.notify_one();
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The helpers, taken for one collection.
pub(crate) struct PoolGuard {
    pool: &'static Pool,
    _in_use: MutexGuard<'static, ()>,
}

impl PoolGuard {
    /// Has every helper call `run` with `data` and its index while the calling thread calls `owner`, and returns once
    /// all are done.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `run` must be safe to call with `data` and each index from 1 to helper_count(), on any thread, at the same time
    /// as `owner` runs.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn run(
        &self,
        run: unsafe fn(data: *const (), index: usize),
        data: *const (),
        owner: impl FnOnce(),
    ) {
        let pool = self.pool;
        pool.ran_since_release.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        {
            let mut state = lock(&pool.state);
            state.generation += 1;
            state.task = Some(Task { run, data });
            state.helpers_left = pool.helper_count();
            pool.task_available.notify_all();
        }
        owner();
        let mut state = lock(&pool.state);
        while state.helpers_left > 0 {
            state = pool.helpers_done.wait(state).unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        }
        state.task = None;
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/Rust/src/sanitizer.rs
/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! What AddressSanitizer and LeakSanitizer need to know about the heap: free cells are poisoned, so that any access to
//! a cell that was swept or never handed out is reported, and blocks are root regions, so that malloc memory that only
//! cells refer to is not reported as leaked. Without the address-sanitizer feature, all of this does nothing.

#[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
use core::ffi::c_void;

/// cbindgen:ignore
#[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
mod ffi {
    use core::ffi::c_void;

    unsafe extern "C" {
        pub(super) fn __asan_poison_memory_region(address: *const c_void, size: usize);
        pub(super) fn __asan_unpoison_memory_region(address: *const c_void, size: usize);
        pub(super) fn __lsan_register_root_region(address: *const c_void, size: usize);
        pub(super) fn __lsan_unregister_root_region(address: *const c_void, size: usize);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
use ffi::{
    __asan_poison_memory_region, __asan_unpoison_memory_region, __lsan_register_root_region,
    __lsan_unregister_root_region,
};

#[inline]
pub fn poison(address: usize, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: Poisoning only changes what AddressSanitizer reports.
    #[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
    unsafe {
        __asan_poison_memory_region(address as *const c_void, size);
    }
    let _ = (address, size);
}

#[inline]
pub fn unpoison(address: usize, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: As above.
    #[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
    unsafe {
        __asan_unpoison_memory_region(address as *const c_void, size);
    }
    let _ = (address, size);
}

pub fn register_root_region(address: usize, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The region is committed memory that LeakSanitizer only reads.
    #[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
    unsafe {
        __lsan_register_root_region(address as *const c_void, size);
    }
    let _ = (address, size);
}

pub fn unregister_root_region(address: usize, size: usize) {
    // SAFETY: The region was registered with register_root_region().
    #[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
    unsafe {
        __lsan_unregister_root_region(address as *const c_void, size);
    }
    let _ = (address, size);
}

#pragma once

#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/Types.h>

namespace GC {

// Zeroes the 8 KiB of stack below its caller, on the real stack even under ASan.
inline NO_SANITIZE_ADDRESS NEVER_INLINE void scrub_stack_for_testing()
{
    u8 volatile filler[8 * KiB];
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(filler); ++i)
        filler[i] = 0;
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/Timer.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2024, Tim Flynn <trflynn89@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibCore/Timer.h>
#include <LibGC/Timer.h>

namespace GC {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(Timer);

Timer::Timer()
    : m_timer(Core::Timer::create())
{
}

Timer::~Timer() = default;

void Timer::finalize()
{
    Base::finalize();
    stop();
}

void Timer::visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_on_timeout);
}

void Timer::start(u64 timeout_ms, GC::Ref<GC::Function<void()>> on_timeout)
{
    m_on_timeout = on_timeout;

    m_timer->on_timeout = [this]() {
        m_timed_out = true;

        if (m_on_timeout) {
            m_on_timeout->function()();
            m_on_timeout = nullptr;
        }
    };

    m_timer->set_interval(AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(static_cast<int>(timeout_ms)));
    m_timer->set_single_shot(true);
    m_timer->start();
}

void Timer::restart()
{
    m_timer->restart();
}

void Timer::stop_and_fire_timeout_handler()
{
    auto on_timeout = m_on_timeout;
    stop();

    if (on_timeout)
        on_timeout->function()();
}

void Timer::stop()
{
    m_on_timeout = nullptr;
    m_timer->stop();
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/Weak.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2025, Andreas Kling <andreas@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Badge.h>
#include <AK/RefPtr.h>
#include <LibGC/Export.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>

namespace GC {

class WeakBlock;

class WeakImpl {
public:
    enum class State {
        Allocated,
        Freelist,
        // The state of the null impl, which all threads share, so it does not count references.
        Null,
    };

    // NOTE: Null GC::Weaks point at this WeakImpl. This allows Weak to always chase the impl pointer without null-checking it.
    static GC_API WeakImpl the_null_weak_impl;

    WeakImpl() = default;
    explicit constexpr WeakImpl(State state)
        : m_state(state)
    {
    }
    WeakImpl(void* ptr)
        : m_ptr(ptr)
    {
    }

    void* ptr() const { return m_ptr; }
    void set_ptr(Badge<WeakBlock>, void* ptr) { m_ptr = ptr; }

    bool operator==(WeakImpl const& other) const { return m_ptr == other.m_ptr; }
    bool operator!=(WeakImpl const& other) const { return m_ptr != other.m_ptr; }

    void ref() const
    {
        if (m_state != State::Null)
            ++m_ref_count;
    }
    void unref() const
    {
        if (m_state == State::Null)
            return;
        VERIFY(m_ref_count);
        --m_ref_count;
    }

    size_t ref_count() const { return m_ref_count; }
    static constexpr size_t value_offset() { return offsetof(WeakImpl, m_ptr); }

    void set_state(State state) { m_state = state; }
    State state() const { return m_state; }

private:
    mutable size_t m_ref_count { 0 };
    State m_state { State::Allocated };
    void* m_ptr { nullptr };
};

template<typename T>
class Weak {
public:
    constexpr Weak() = default;
    Weak(nullptr_t) { }

    Weak(T const* ptr);
    Weak(T const& ptr);

    Weak(Weak&& other)
        : m_impl(exchange(other.m_impl, WeakImpl::the_null_weak_impl))
    {
    }

    Weak& operator=(Weak&& other)
    {
        if (this != &other) {
            m_impl = exchange(other.m_impl, WeakImpl::the_null_weak_impl);
        }
        return *this;
    }

    Weak(Weak const&) = default;

    template<typename U>
    Weak(Weak<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    Weak(Ref<T> const& other);

    template<typename U>
    Weak(Ref<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    Weak(Ptr<T> const& other);

    template<typename U>
    Weak(Ptr<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    Weak& operator=(Weak const& other) = default;

    template<typename U>
    Weak& operator=(Weak<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>)
    {
        m_impl = other.impl();
        return *this;
    }

    Weak& operator=(Ref<T> const& other);

    Weak& operator=(Ptr<T> const& other);

    template<typename U>
    Weak& operator=(Ptr<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    template<typename U>
    Weak& operator=(Ref<U> const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    Weak& operator=(T const& other);

    template<typename U>
    Weak& operator=(U const& other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    Weak& operator=(T const* other);

    template<typename U>
    Weak& operator=(U const* other)
    requires(IsConvertible<U*, T*>);

    T* operator->() const
    {
        ASSERT(ptr());
        return ptr().ptr();
    }

    [[nodiscard]] T& operator*() const
    {
        ASSERT(ptr());
        return *ptr();
    }

    Ptr<T> ptr() const { return static_cast<T*>(impl().ptr()); }

    explicit operator bool() const { return !!ptr(); }
    bool operator!() const { return !ptr(); }

    operator T*() const { return ptr().ptr(); }

    Ref<T> as_nonnull() const
    {
        ASSERT(ptr());
        return *ptr();
    }

    WeakImpl& impl() const { return *m_impl; }

private:
    NonnullRefPtr<WeakImpl> m_impl { WeakImpl::the_null_weak_impl };
};

// NOTE: Unlike GC::Function, captures in this callback are not visited by the garbage collector.
//       Do not capture GC-managed objects without ensuring they are kept alive through other means.
template<typename T, typename Callback>
auto weak_callback(T& obj, Callback&& callback)
{
    return [weak = Weak<T> { obj }, cb = forward<Callback>(callback)](auto&&... args) mutable {
        if (weak)
            cb(*weak, forward<decltype(args)>(args)...);
    };
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(Weak<T> const& a, Ptr<U> const& b)
{
    return a.ptr() == b;
}

template<typename T, typename U>
inline bool operator==(Weak<T> const& a, Ref<U> const& b)
{
    return a.ptr() == b;
}

}

namespace AK {

template<typename T>
struct Formatter<GC::Weak<T>> : Formatter<T const*> {
    ErrorOr<void> format(FormatBuilder& builder, GC::Weak<T> const& value)
    {
        return Formatter<T const*>::format(builder, value.ptr().ptr());
    }
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/WeakBlock.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2025, Andreas Kling <andreas@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibGC/BlockDescriptor.h>
#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibGC/WeakBlock.h>

namespace GC {

constinit WeakImpl WeakImpl::the_null_weak_impl { WeakImpl::State::Null };

WeakBlock* WeakBlock::create()
{
    auto* block = MUST(Core::System::allocate_anonymous_memory(WeakBlock::BLOCK_SIZE, Core::System::MemoryTag::GarbageCollector));
    return new (block) WeakBlock;
}

void WeakBlock::destroy(WeakBlock* block)
{
    block->~WeakBlock();
    MUST(Core::System::release_address_space(block, WeakBlock::BLOCK_SIZE));
}

WeakBlock::WeakBlock()
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < IMPL_COUNT; ++i) {
        m_impls[i].set_ptr({}, i + 1 < IMPL_COUNT ? &m_impls[i + 1] : nullptr);
        m_impls[i].set_state(WeakImpl::State::Freelist);
    }
    m_freelist = &m_impls[0];
}

WeakBlock::~WeakBlock() = default;

bool WeakBlock::has_referenced_impls() const
{
    for (auto const& impl : m_impls) {
        if (impl.ref_count() != 0)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

WeakImpl* WeakBlock::allocate(Cell* cell)
{
    auto* impl = m_freelist;
    if (!impl)
        return nullptr;
    VERIFY(impl->ref_count() == 0);
    m_freelist = impl->ptr() ? static_cast<WeakImpl*>(impl->ptr()) : nullptr;
    impl->set_ptr({}, cell);
    impl->set_state(WeakImpl::State::Allocated);
    return impl;
}

void WeakBlock::deallocate(WeakImpl* impl)
{
    VERIFY(impl->ref_count() == 0);
    impl->set_ptr({}, m_freelist);
    impl->set_state(WeakImpl::State::Freelist);
    m_freelist = impl;
}

void WeakBlock::sweep()
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < IMPL_COUNT; ++i) {
        auto& impl = m_impls[i];
        if (impl.state() == WeakImpl::State::Freelist)
            continue;
        auto* cell = static_cast<Cell*>(impl.ptr());
        if (!cell || !GC::is_marked(cell))
            impl.set_ptr({}, nullptr);
        if (impl.ref_count() == 0)
            deallocate(&impl);
    }
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibGC/WeakBlock.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2025, Andreas Kling <andreas@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/IntrusiveList.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibGC/Weak.h>

namespace GC {

class GC_API WeakBlock {
public:
    static constexpr size_t BLOCK_SIZE = 16 * KiB;

    static WeakBlock* create();
    static void destroy(WeakBlock*);

    WeakImpl* allocate(Cell*);
    void deallocate(WeakImpl*);

    bool can_allocate() const { return m_freelist != nullptr; }
    bool has_referenced_impls() const;

    void sweep();

    // Points every weak pointer at the cell that its cell moved to, which forwarding_address returns, or null if the
    // cell did not move.
    template<typename Callback>
    void update_moved_cells(Callback forwarding_address)
    {
        for (auto& impl : m_impls) {
            if (impl.state() != WeakImpl::State::Allocated || !impl.ptr())
                continue;
            if (auto* moved_to = forwarding_address(impl.ptr()))
                impl.set_ptr({}, moved_to);
        }
    }

private:
    WeakBlock();
    ~WeakBlock();

    IntrusiveListNode<WeakBlock> m_list_node;

public:
    using List = IntrusiveList<&WeakBlock::m_list_node>;

    WeakImpl* m_freelist { nullptr };

    static constexpr size_t IMPL_COUNT = (BLOCK_SIZE - sizeof(m_list_node) - sizeof(WeakImpl*)) / sizeof(WeakImpl);
    WeakImpl m_impls[IMPL_COUNT];
};

static_assert(sizeof(WeakBlock) <= WeakBlock::BLOCK_SIZE);

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>

namespace GC {

WeakContainer::WeakContainer(Heap& heap)
    : m_heap(heap)
{
    m_heap.did_create_weak_container({}, *this);
}

WeakContainer::~WeakContainer()
{
    deregister();
}

void WeakContainer::deregister()
{
    if (!m_registered)
        return;
    m_heap.did_destroy_weak_container({}, *this);
    m_registered = false;
}
