//! The data of a path: its verbs, the points that they use and the weights of its conics, and the
//! rules by which the operations of `Path` add to them.

use super::arcs;
use crate::geometry::FloatPoint;
use crate::matrix::AffineTransform;
use crate::paint_enums::WindingRule;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum PathVerb {
    Move = 0,
    Line = 1,
    Quad = 2,
    Conic = 3,
    Cubic = 4,
    Close = 5,
}

impl PathVerb {
    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(match value {
            0 => Self::Move,
            1 => Self::Line,
            2 => Self::Quad,
            3 => Self::Conic,
            4 => Self::Cubic,
            5 => Self::Close,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    /// The number of points that the verb stores.
    pub fn stored_point_count(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Move | Self::Line => 1,
            Self::Quad | Self::Conic => 2,
            Self::Cubic => 3,
            Self::Close => 0,
        }
    }
}

/// A segment of a path, with the point where it starts as its first point.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Segment {
    Line([FloatPoint; 2]),
    Quad([FloatPoint; 3]),
    Conic([FloatPoint; 3], f32),
    Cubic([FloatPoint; 4]),
}

impl Segment {
    pub fn points(&self) -> &[FloatPoint] {
        match self {
            Self::Line(points) => points,
            Self::Quad(points) | Self::Conic(points, _) => points,
            Self::Cubic(points) => points,
        }
    }

    pub fn start(&self) -> FloatPoint {
        self.points()[0]
    }

    pub fn end(&self) -> FloatPoint {
        *self.points().last().expect("a segment has points")
    }

    /// Whether every point of the segment is the same, so that it goes nowhere.
    pub fn is_degenerate(&self) -> bool {
        let start = self.start();
        self.points().iter().all(|point| *point == start)
    }
}

/// What a walk over the verbs of a path meets: the start of a contour, a segment, or a close with
/// the line back to the start of its contour.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum PathElement {
    MoveTo(FloatPoint),
    Segment(Segment),
    Close([FloatPoint; 2]),
}

impl PathElement {
    /// The segment that the element draws, if any. A close draws the line back to the start.
    pub fn drawn_segment(&self) -> Option<Segment> {
        match self {
            Self::MoveTo(_) => None,
            Self::Segment(segment) => Some(*segment),
            Self::Close(points) => Some(Segment::Line(*points)),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct PathGeometry {
    verbs: Vec<PathVerb>,
    points: Vec<FloatPoint>,
    conic_weights: Vec<f32>,
    fill_rule: WindingRule,
    has_only_finite_points: bool,

    // What the operations of Path remember between calls: whether there is a point to draw from,
    // and where the last subpath started.
    has_current_point: bool,
    last_move_to: FloatPoint,
}

fn is_finite_point(point: FloatPoint) -> bool {
    point.x.is_finite() && point.y.is_finite()
}

impl Default for PathGeometry {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl PathGeometry {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            verbs: Vec::new(),
            points: Vec::new(),
            conic_weights: Vec::new(),
            fill_rule: WindingRule::Nonzero,
            has_only_finite_points: true,
            has_current_point: false,
            last_move_to: FloatPoint::default(),
        }
    }

    pub fn verbs(&self) -> &[PathVerb] {
        &self.verbs
    }

    pub fn points(&self) -> &[FloatPoint] {
        &self.points
    }

    pub fn conic_weights(&self) -> &[f32] {
        &self.conic_weights
    }

    pub fn fill_rule(&self) -> WindingRule {
        self.fill_rule
    }

    pub fn set_fill_rule(&mut self, fill_rule: WindingRule) {
        self.fill_rule = fill_rule;
    }

    /// A path with a point that is not finite has no geometry: it draws nothing, has no length and
    /// contains no point. It still remembers its operations, so that drawing can continue from it.
    pub fn has_geometry(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_only_finite_points && !self.verbs.is_empty()
    }

    /// Whether the path has no current point.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        !self.has_current_point
    }

    pub fn last_point(&self) -> FloatPoint {
        self.points.last().copied().unwrap_or_default()
    }

    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        *self = Self::new();
    }

    /// The elements of the path. A move that ends the path starts nothing, and is left out.
    pub fn elements(&self) -> PathElements<'_> {
        PathElements {
            geometry: self,
            verb_index: 0,
            point_index: 0,
            conic_weight_index: 0,
            current_point: FloatPoint::default(),
            contour_start: FloatPoint::default(),
        }
    }

    /// The bounds of the points of the path, as x, y, width and height. A move that ends the path,
    /// and that so starts nothing, does not count, unless it is the only point.
    pub fn bounding_box(&self) -> [f32; 4] {
        if self.points.is_empty() || !self.has_only_finite_points {
            return [0.0; 4];
        }
        let mut counted_points = self.points.as_slice();
        if counted_points.len() > 1 && self.verbs.last() == Some(&PathVerb::Move) {
            counted_points = &counted_points[..counted_points.len() - 1];
        }
        let first = counted_points[0];
        let (mut left, mut top, mut right, mut bottom) = (first.x, first.y, first.x, first.y);
        for point in &counted_points[1..] {
            left = left.min(point.x);
            top = top.min(point.y);
            right = right.max(point.x);
            bottom = bottom.max(point.y);
        }
        [left, top, right - left, bottom - top]
    }

    // Contour building, without the rules of Path for a path that has no current point.

    fn push_point(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.has_only_finite_points &= is_finite_point(point);
        self.points.push(point);
    }

    fn pop_point(&mut self) {
        if let Some(point) = self.points.pop()
            && !is_finite_point(point)
        {
            self.recompute_finiteness();
        }
    }

    /// Starts a contour. A move that follows a move replaces it.
    pub fn contour_move_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        if self.verbs.last() == Some(&PathVerb::Move) {
            self.pop_point();
            self.push_point(point);
            return;
        }
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Move);
        self.push_point(point);
    }

    /// A segment needs a contour to belong to. After a close, the next contour starts where the
    /// closed one did.
    fn start_contour_for_segment(&mut self) {
        match self.verbs.last() {
            None => self.contour_move_to(FloatPoint::default()),
            Some(PathVerb::Close) => self.contour_move_to(self.start_of_last_contour()),
            Some(_) => {}
        }
    }

    fn start_of_last_contour(&self) -> FloatPoint {
        let mut point_index = 0;
        let mut start = FloatPoint::default();
        for verb in &self.verbs {
            if *verb == PathVerb::Move {
                start = self.points[point_index];
            }
            point_index += verb.stored_point_count();
        }
        start
    }

    pub fn contour_line_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.start_contour_for_segment();
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Line);
        self.push_point(point);
    }

    pub fn contour_quad_to(&mut self, control: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.start_contour_for_segment();
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Quad);
        self.push_point(control);
        self.push_point(point);
    }

    /// A conic with a weight of 1 is a quadratic curve, and is stored as one.
    pub fn contour_conic_to(&mut self, control: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint, weight: f32) {
        if weight == 1.0 {
            self.contour_quad_to(control, point);
            return;
        }
        self.start_contour_for_segment();
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Conic);
        self.push_point(control);
        self.push_point(point);
        self.conic_weights.push(weight);
    }

    pub fn contour_cubic_to(&mut self, control1: FloatPoint, control2: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.start_contour_for_segment();
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Cubic);
        self.push_point(control1);
        self.push_point(control2);
        self.push_point(point);
    }

    pub fn contour_close(&mut self) {
        if matches!(self.verbs.last(), None | Some(PathVerb::Close)) {
            return;
        }
        self.verbs.push(PathVerb::Close);
    }

    // The operations of Path.

    pub fn move_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.last_move_to = point;
        self.has_current_point = true;
        self.contour_move_to(point);
    }

    pub fn line_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        if !self.has_current_point {
            self.move_to(point);
            return;
        }
        self.contour_line_to(point);
    }

    pub fn quadratic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, control: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        if !self.has_current_point {
            self.move_to(control);
        }
        self.contour_quad_to(control, point);
    }

    pub fn cubic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, control1: FloatPoint, control2: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        if !self.has_current_point {
            self.move_to(control1);
        }
        self.contour_cubic_to(control1, control2, point);
    }

    /// An arc of an ellipse, with the parameters of the SVG path command. The rotation is in radians.
    pub fn elliptical_arc_to(
        &mut self,
        point: FloatPoint,
        radii: (f32, f32),
        x_axis_rotation: f32,
        large_arc: bool,
        sweep: bool,
    ) {
        if !self.has_current_point {
            self.move_to(point);
            return;
        }
        arcs::append_elliptical_arc(self, point, radii, x_axis_rotation, large_arc, sweep);
    }

    pub fn arc_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint, radius: f32, large_arc: bool, sweep: bool) {
        self.elliptical_arc_to(point, (radius, radius), 0.0, large_arc, sweep);
    }

    /// Closes the subpath, and starts the next one where it started.
    pub fn close(&mut self) {
        if !self.has_current_point {
            return;
        }
        self.contour_close();
        self.contour_move_to(self.last_move_to);
    }

    /// Adds the subpaths of the other path. A move that ends this path starts nothing, so it does
    /// not stay in front of the other path's first move. A path without geometry adds no subpaths,
    /// but what it remembers for the operations that follow carries over.
    pub fn append_path(&mut self, other: &PathGeometry) {
        if other.has_only_finite_points {
            self.append_mapped(other, |point| point);
        }
        if other.has_current_point {
            self.has_current_point = true;
            self.last_move_to = other.last_move_to;
        }
    }

    /// Adds the contours of the other path with its points mapped, as for glyph outlines. The state of
    /// Path is left as it was; update_state_from_contours() sets it.
    pub fn append_mapped(&mut self, other: &PathGeometry, map: impl Fn(FloatPoint) -> FloatPoint) {
        self.append_mapped_contours(&other.verbs, &other.points, &other.conic_weights, map);
    }

    /// Adds contours given as the verbs, points and conic weights of a path, with their points mapped, as
    /// append_mapped() does.
    pub fn append_mapped_contours(
        &mut self,
        verbs: &[PathVerb],
        points: &[FloatPoint],
        conic_weights: &[f32],
        map: impl Fn(FloatPoint) -> FloatPoint,
    ) {
        if verbs.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if self.verbs.last() == Some(&PathVerb::Move) {
            self.verbs.pop();
            self.pop_point();
        }
        let first_appended_point = self.points.len();
        self.verbs.extend_from_slice(verbs);
        self.points.extend(points.iter().map(|point| map(*point)));
        self.conic_weights.extend_from_slice(conic_weights);
        self.has_only_finite_points &= self.points[first_appended_point..]
            .iter()
            .all(|point| is_finite_point(*point));
    }

    /// Sets the state of Path from the contours, for a path that was not built by its operations.
    pub fn update_state_from_contours(&mut self) {
        self.has_current_point = !self.verbs.is_empty();
        self.last_move_to = self.start_of_last_contour();
    }

    /// A copy with every point mapped by the transform. Conics keep their weights.
    pub fn copy_transformed(&self, transform: AffineTransform) -> PathGeometry {
        let mut copy = self.clone();
        copy.transform(transform);
        copy
    }

    pub fn transform(&mut self, transform: AffineTransform) {
        for point in &mut self.points {
            *point = transform.map_point(*point);
        }
        if self.has_current_point {
            self.last_move_to = transform.map_point(self.last_move_to);
        }
        self.recompute_finiteness();
    }

    fn recompute_finiteness(&mut self) {
        self.has_only_finite_points = self.points.iter().all(|point| is_finite_point(*point));
    }

    /// Makes a path from contours that a decoder checked: each verb has its points and weights, and
    /// every point is finite.
    pub(super) fn from_checked_contours(
        verbs: Vec<PathVerb>,
        points: Vec<FloatPoint>,
        conic_weights: Vec<f32>,
        fill_rule: WindingRule,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut geometry = Self {
            verbs,
            points,
            conic_weights,
            fill_rule,
            has_only_finite_points: true,
            has_current_point: false,
            last_move_to: FloatPoint::default(),
        };
        geometry.update_state_from_contours();
        geometry
    }

    /// Whether both paths have the same fill rule and the same contours, point for point.
    pub fn has_same_contours(&self, other: &PathGeometry) -> bool {
        let same_bits = |a: f32, b: f32| a.to_bits() == b.to_bits();
        self.fill_rule == other.fill_rule
            && self.verbs == other.verbs
            && self.points.len() == other.points.len()
            && self
                .points
                .iter()
                .zip(&other.points)
                .all(|(a, b)| same_bits(a.x, b.x) && same_bits(a.y, b.y))
            && self.conic_weights.len() == other.conic_weights.len()
            && self
                .conic_weights
                .iter()
                .zip(&other.conic_weights)
                .all(|(a, b)| same_bits(*a, *b))
    }
}

pub struct PathElements<'a> {
    geometry: &'a PathGeometry,
    verb_index: usize,
    point_index: usize,
    conic_weight_index: usize,
    current_point: FloatPoint,
    contour_start: FloatPoint,
}

impl Iterator for PathElements<'_> {
    type Item = PathElement;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<PathElement> {
        let verbs = &self.geometry.verbs;
        let verb = *verbs.get(self.verb_index)?;
        if verb == PathVerb::Move && self.verb_index + 1 == verbs.len() {
            return None;
        }
        self.verb_index += 1;
        let points = &self.geometry.points[self.point_index..self.point_index + verb.stored_point_count()];
        self.point_index += verb.stored_point_count();
        let start = self.current_point;
        let element = match verb {
            PathVerb::Move => {
                self.contour_start = points[0];
                PathElement::MoveTo(points[0])
            }
            PathVerb::Line => PathElement::Segment(Segment::Line([start, points[0]])),
            PathVerb::Quad => PathElement::Segment(Segment::Quad([start, points[0], points[1]])),
            PathVerb::Conic => {
                let weight = self.geometry.conic_weights[self.conic_weight_index];
                self.conic_weight_index += 1;
                PathElement::Segment(Segment::Conic([start, points[0], points[1]], weight))
            }
            PathVerb::Cubic => PathElement::Segment(Segment::Cubic([start, points[0], points[1], points[2]])),
            PathVerb::Close => PathElement::Close([start, self.contour_start]),
        };
        self.current_point = match element {
            PathElement::MoveTo(point) => point,
            PathElement::Segment(segment) => segment.end(),
            PathElement::Close(_) => self.contour_start,
        };
        Some(element)
    }
}

/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Whether a point is inside a path, as the fill of the path covers it.
//!
//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ispointinpath
//!
//! Every subpath counts as closed. The winding number of the path around the point decides: the edges
//! that cross the horizontal ray from the point to the right add one when they go down and subtract one
//! when they go up. An edge includes the point where it starts in y and excludes the one where it ends,
//! so that a ray through a vertex counts it once where the path passes through and not at all where it
//! turns back.
//!
//! A point on the path itself is inside. A point where one edge ends and the next starts is on the next
//! edge only. Where the edges through a point cancel out, as where the path goes back over itself and
//! so bounds nothing, the winding number decides after all.

use super::curves::{Curve, Point};
use super::geometry::{PathElement, PathGeometry, Segment};
use crate::geometry::FloatPoint;
use crate::paint_enums::WindingRule;

/// The furthest that a point may be off a curve, relative to the size of its coordinates, and still
/// lie on it. The position of a curve at a given y is solved for numerically.
const ON_CURVE_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-6;

/// The number of bisection steps that find the parameter of a monotonic curve at a given y. Each step
/// halves the interval, so the parameter ends up as precise as a double allows.
const BISECTION_STEPS: u32 = 64;

/// How close the sum of the unit tangents of the edges through a point has to come to zero for them to
/// cancel out.
const CANCELLED_TANGENTS_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-6;

pub fn contains(geometry: &PathGeometry, x: f32, y: f32, fill_rule: WindingRule) -> bool {
    if !geometry.has_geometry() || !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() {
        return false;
    }
    let point = Point::new(f64::from(x), f64::from(y));
    let mut winding = 0i32;
    let mut tangents_through_point = Vec::new();
    for_each_filled_segment(geometry, |segment| {
        if !segment.is_degenerate() {
            add_crossings_of_segment(
                &Curve::from_segment(&segment),
                point,
                &mut winding,
                &mut tangents_through_point,
            );
        }
    });

    if !tangents_through_point.is_empty() {
        if tangents_through_point.len() % 2 == 1 {
            return true;
        }
        let tangent_sum = tangents_through_point
            .iter()
            .fold(Point::default(), |sum, tangent| sum.plus(*tangent));
        if tangent_sum.length() > CANCELLED_TANGENTS_TOLERANCE {
            return true;
        }
    }
    match fill_rule {
        WindingRule::Nonzero => winding != 0,
        WindingRule::EvenOdd => winding % 2 != 0,
    }
}

/// Calls the callback with the segments that bound the fill: those of the path, and a line back
/// to the start of every subpath that does not end there.
fn for_each_filled_segment(geometry: &PathGeometry, mut callback: impl FnMut(Segment)) {
    // The start of the subpath that is being walked, and where the walk is in it.
    let mut open_subpath: Option<(FloatPoint, FloatPoint)> = None;
    let close_open_subpath = |open_subpath: Option<(FloatPoint, FloatPoint)>, callback: &mut dyn FnMut(Segment)| {
        if let Some((start, current)) = open_subpath
            && start != current
        {
            callback(Segment::Line([current, start]));
        }
    };
    for element in geometry.elements() {
        if let PathElement::MoveTo(point) = element {
            close_open_subpath(open_subpath, &mut callback);
            open_subpath = Some((point, point));
        } else if let Some(segment) = element.drawn_segment() {
            callback(segment);
            if let Some((_, current)) = &mut open_subpath {
                *current = segment.end();
            }
        }
    }
    close_open_subpath(open_subpath, &mut callback);
}

fn unit(vector: Point) -> Point {
    vector.scaled(1.0 / vector.length())
}

/// Adds the crossings of the segment with the ray from the point to the winding number, and the unit
/// tangent of the segment where it passes through the point, if it does, to the tangents.
fn add_crossings_of_segment(curve: &Curve, point: Point, winding: &mut i32, tangents_through_point: &mut Vec<Point>) {
    if let Curve::Line([start, end]) = *curve {
        add_crossing_of_line(start, end, point, winding, tangents_through_point);
        return;
    }

    // A curve stays within the bounds of its control points.
    let control_points = curve.control_points();
    if control_points.iter().all(|control| control.y < point.y)
        || control_points.iter().all(|control| control.y > point.y)
    {
        return;
    }

    let tolerance = ON_CURVE_TOLERANCE * point.x.abs().max(point.y.abs()).max(1.0);
    // The end of a piece belongs to the next one, and the end of the segment to the next segment.
    let mut parameters_through_point: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();

    // The curve in pieces that go only one way in y.
    for (from, to) in monotonic_pieces(curve, 0.0, 1.0, |point| point.y) {
        let from_point = curve_point(curve, from);
        let to_point = curve_point(curve, to);
        let (low_y, high_y) = (from_point.y.min(to_point.y), from_point.y.max(to_point.y));
        if point.y < low_y || point.y > high_y {
            continue;
        }

        if low_y == high_y {
            // A piece that stays at one y can only have the point on it, at the parameters where it
            // reaches the x of the point, and crosses no ray.
            for (from, to) in monotonic_pieces(curve, from, to, |point| point.x) {
                let (from_x, to_x) = (curve_point(curve, from).x, curve_point(curve, to).x);
                if point.x < from_x.min(to_x) || point.x > from_x.max(to_x) {
                    continue;
                }
                let t = parameter_at(curve, from, to, from_x, to_x, point.x, |point| point.x);
                if t < to {
                    parameters_through_point.push(t);
                }
            }
            continue;
        }

        let t = parameter_at(curve, from, to, from_point.y, to_point.y, point.y, |point| point.y);
        let x_at_point = curve.point_at(t).x;
        if (x_at_point - point.x).abs() <= tolerance {
            if t < to {
                parameters_through_point.push(t);
            }
            continue;
        }
        if point.y == high_y || x_at_point < point.x {
            continue;
        }
        *winding += if to_point.y > from_point.y { 1 } else { -1 };
    }

    for t in parameters_through_point {
        if let Some(direction) = curve.direction_at(t) {
            tangents_through_point.push(unit(direction));
        }
    }
}

/// The ranges of the parameter between from and to in which the curve goes only one way in the coordinate.
fn monotonic_pieces(curve: &Curve, from: f64, to: f64, coordinate: impl Fn(Point) -> f64) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    let mut parameters = vec![from];
    parameters.extend(
        curve
            .turning_parameters(coordinate)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|t| *t > from && *t < to),
    );
    parameters.push(to);
    parameters.windows(2).map(|range| (range[0], range[1])).collect()
}

fn curve_point(curve: &Curve, t: f64) -> Point {
    if t == 0.0 {
        curve.start()
    } else if t == 1.0 {
        curve.end()
    } else {
        curve.point_at(t)
    }
}

fn add_crossing_of_line(
    start: Point,
    end: Point,
    point: Point,
    winding: &mut i32,
    tangents_through_point: &mut Vec<Point>,
) {
    let (low_y, high_y) = (start.y.min(end.y), start.y.max(end.y));
    if point.y < low_y || point.y > high_y {
        return;
    }
    let (low_x, high_x) = (start.x.min(end.x), start.x.max(end.x));
    // The sign of the cross product says on which side of the line the point is.
    let cross = (end.x - start.x) * (point.y - start.y) - (end.y - start.y) * (point.x - start.x);
    if cross == 0.0 && point.x >= low_x && point.x <= high_x {
        // The end of a line belongs to the next segment.
        if point != end {
            tangents_through_point.push(unit(end.minus(start)));
        }
        return;
    }
    if start.y == end.y || point.y == high_y {
        return;
    }
    // The point is left of a line that goes down when the cross product is positive, and left of one
    // that goes up when it is negative.
    let goes_down = end.y > start.y;
    if (goes_down && cross > 0.0) || (!goes_down && cross < 0.0) {
        *winding += if goes_down { 1 } else { -1 };
    }
}

/// The parameter in the range where the curve goes one way in the coordinate at which it reaches the given
/// value.
fn parameter_at(
    curve: &Curve,
    mut from: f64,
    mut to: f64,
    from_value: f64,
    to_value: f64,
    value: f64,
    coordinate: impl Fn(Point) -> f64,
) -> f64 {
    if value == from_value {
        return from;
    }
    if value == to_value {
        return to;
    }
    let increasing = to_value > from_value;
    for _ in 0..BISECTION_STEPS {
        let middle = (from + to) / 2.0;
        if (coordinate(curve.point_at(middle)) < value) == increasing {
            from = middle;
        } else {
            to = middle;
        }
    }
    (from + to) / 2.0
}

/*

//! Lengths of paths, and positions and directions along them.
//!
//! A curve is measured in pieces between points at equal steps of its parameter. The number of steps
//! comes from Wang's formula, which keeps the line between the ends of each piece within
//! MEASURE_TOLERANCE of the curve. The length of each piece is the integral of the speed of the curve,
//! by Gauss-Legendre quadrature, which is exact to well within float precision for pieces this flat.
//! A position within a piece is at the parameter that is as far between its ends as the distance is.

use super::curves::{Curve, Point};
use super::geometry::{PathElement, PathElements, PathGeometry, Segment};
use crate::geometry::FloatPoint;

/// The furthest that the lines that measure a curve are from it.
const MEASURE_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1.0 / 32.0;

/// The most lines with which to follow a single curve, which bounds the work for a huge curve.
const MAXIMUM_LINE_COUNT_ALONG_CURVE: u32 = 4096;

/// The number of lines between points at equal parameter steps that follow the curve within the
/// tolerance, by Wang's formula: the square root of the largest second difference of its control
/// points, scaled by its degree, over the tolerance.
pub(super) fn line_count_to_follow(curve: &Curve) -> u32 {
    let second_difference = |points: &[Point], index: usize| {
        points[index]
            .minus(points[index + 1].scaled(2.0))
            .plus(points[index + 2])
            .length()
    };
    let scaled_second_difference = match curve {
        Curve::Line(_) => return 1,
        Curve::Quad(points) => second_difference(points, 0) / 4.0,
        // A conic with a weight of at most 1, like the arcs of SVG paths, bends no more than the quadratic curve
        // with the same control points.
        Curve::Conic(points, weight) => weight.max(1.0) * second_difference(points, 0) / 4.0,
        Curve::Cubic(points) => 3.0 * second_difference(points, 0).max(second_difference(points, 1)) / 4.0,
    };
    let line_count = (scaled_second_difference / MEASURE_TOLERANCE).sqrt().ceil();
    if line_count.is_nan() {
        return 1;
    }
    line_count.clamp(1.0, f64::from(MAXIMUM_LINE_COUNT_ALONG_CURVE)) as u32
}

/// The length of the curve between two parameters: the integral of its speed, by five-point
/// Gauss-Legendre quadrature.
fn length_between(curve: &Curve, from: f64, to: f64) -> f64 {
    const NODES_AND_WEIGHTS: [(f64, f64); 5] = [
        (0.0, 0.568_888_888_888_888_9),
        (-0.538_469_310_105_683_1, 0.478_628_670_499_366_5),
        (0.538_469_310_105_683_1, 0.478_628_670_499_366_5),
        (-0.906_179_845_938_664, 0.236_926_885_056_189_1),
        (0.906_179_845_938_664, 0.236_926_885_056_189_1),
    ];
    let half_width = (to - from) / 2.0;
    let middle = (from + to) / 2.0;
    let integral: f64 = NODES_AND_WEIGHTS
        .iter()
        .map(|(node, weight)| weight * curve.derivative_at(middle + half_width * node).length())
        .sum();
    integral * half_width
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
struct MeasuredPiece {
    segment_index: usize,
    from_parameter: f64,
    to_parameter: f64,
    distance_at_end: f64,
}

/// The measure of one contour of a path that has length.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ContourMeasure {
    curves: Vec<Curve>,
    pieces: Vec<MeasuredPiece>,
}

impl ContourMeasure {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            curves: Vec::new(),
            pieces: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn distance(&self) -> f64 {
        self.pieces.last().map_or(0.0, |piece| piece.distance_at_end)
    }

    fn add_segment(&mut self, segment: &Segment) {
        let curve = Curve::from_segment(segment);
        let line_count = line_count_to_follow(&curve);
        self.add_curve(curve, line_count);
    }

    fn add_curve(&mut self, curve: Curve, line_count: u32) {
        let segment_index = self.curves.len();
        let mut distance = self.distance();
        let mut previous_point = curve.start();
        let mut previous_parameter = 0.0;
        for line in 1..=line_count {
            let parameter = f64::from(line) / f64::from(line_count);
            let point = if line == line_count {
                curve.end()
            } else {
                curve.point_at(parameter)
            };
            let length = match curve {
                Curve::Line(_) => previous_point.distance_to(point),
                _ => length_between(&curve, previous_parameter, parameter),
            };
            if length > 0.0 {
                distance += length;
                self.pieces.push(MeasuredPiece {
                    segment_index,
                    from_parameter: previous_parameter,
                    to_parameter: parameter,
                    distance_at_end: distance,
                });
            }
            previous_point = point;
            previous_parameter = parameter;
        }
        self.curves.push(curve);
    }

    pub fn length(&self) -> f32 {
        self.distance() as f32
    }

    /// The point at the distance along the contour, clamped to its ends, and the unit tangent there.
    pub fn position_and_tangent(&self, distance: f32) -> (FloatPoint, FloatPoint) {
        let distance = f64::from(distance).clamp(0.0, self.distance());
        let piece_index = self
            .pieces
            .partition_point(|piece| piece.distance_at_end < distance)
            .min(self.pieces.len() - 1);
        let piece = &self.pieces[piece_index];
        let distance_at_start = if piece_index == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            self.pieces[piece_index - 1].distance_at_end
        };
        let fraction = (distance - distance_at_start) / (piece.distance_at_end - distance_at_start);
        let curve = &self.curves[piece.segment_index];
        let parameter = piece.from_parameter + (piece.to_parameter - piece.from_parameter) * fraction;
        let position = match *curve {
            Curve::Line([start, end]) => start.lerp(end, parameter),
            _ => curve.point_at(parameter),
        };
        let direction = curve.direction_at(parameter).unwrap_or_default();
        let direction_length = direction.length();
        let tangent = if direction_length > 0.0 {
            direction.scaled(1.0 / direction_length)
        } else {
            direction
        };
        (position.to_float(), tangent.to_float())
    }

    /// The measures of the contours of the path that have length, in order, each measured when it is
    /// asked for. A close adds the line back to the start of its contour; an open contour gets no such
    /// line.
    pub fn contours_of(geometry: &PathGeometry) -> ContourMeasures<'_> {
        ContourMeasures {
            elements: geometry.has_geometry().then(|| geometry.elements()),
        }
    }

    fn of_curve(curve: Curve, line_count: u32) -> ContourMeasure {
        let mut contour = ContourMeasure::new();
        contour.add_curve(curve, line_count);
        contour
    }
}

pub struct ContourMeasures<'a> {
    elements: Option<PathElements<'a>>,
}

impl Iterator for ContourMeasures<'_> {
    type Item = ContourMeasure;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<ContourMeasure> {
        let elements = self.elements.as_mut()?;
        let mut contour = ContourMeasure::new();
        for element in elements.by_ref() {
            match element.drawn_segment() {
                Some(segment) => contour.add_segment(&segment),
                None if !contour.pieces.is_empty() => return Some(contour),
                None => contour.curves.clear(),
            }
        }
        self.elements = None;
        (!contour.pieces.is_empty()).then_some(contour)
    }
}

/// The length of the path: the sum of the lengths of its contours.
pub fn length(geometry: &PathGeometry) -> f32 {
    // Summing floats starts from -0, which a path without length must not give.
    ContourMeasure::contours_of(geometry).fold(0.0, |length, contour| length + contour.length())
}

/// The point at a distance along the path, clamped to its ends, and the unit tangent of the path there.
/// The gaps between the subpaths do not add to the distance. A path without length is only its start
/// point, where it has no tangent.
pub fn point_at_length(geometry: &PathGeometry, distance: f32) -> Option<(FloatPoint, FloatPoint)> {
    let mut remaining_distance = distance.max(0.0);
    let mut end_of_path = None;
    for contour in ContourMeasure::contours_of(geometry) {
        let contour_length = contour.length();
        end_of_path = Some(contour.position_and_tangent(remaining_distance.min(contour_length)));
        if remaining_distance <= contour_length {
            return end_of_path;
        }
        remaining_distance -= contour_length;
    }
    if end_of_path.is_some() {
        return end_of_path;
    }
    if !geometry.has_geometry() {
        return None;
    }
    Some((geometry.points()[0], FloatPoint::default()))
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PathVertex {
    pub point: FloatPoint,
    pub distance: f32,
    pub direction: FloatPoint,
}

/// The vertices of polylines through the ends of the segments of the path, with their distance along
/// it. Along a curved segment, the polylines pass through points along the curve that keep them within
/// MEASURE_TOLERANCE of it. The gaps between the subpaths do not add to the distance, so a subpath
/// starts at the distance its predecessor ends at. A path without length is only its start point.
///
/// Each vertex has the unit tangent of the path there as its direction. Where the path changes
/// direction at once, the vertex appears twice: with the direction in which the path arrives, and with
/// the one in which it leaves. A subpath start that no segment with length leaves from has no
/// direction.
pub fn vertices(geometry: &PathGeometry) -> Vec<PathVertex> {
    let mut vertices: Vec<PathVertex> = Vec::new();
    if !geometry.has_geometry() {
        return vertices;
    }
    let mut distance = 0.0f32;
    for element in geometry.elements() {
        let Some(segment) = element.drawn_segment() else {
            if let PathElement::MoveTo(point) = element {
                vertices.push(PathVertex {
                    point,
                    distance,
                    direction: FloatPoint::default(),
                });
            }
            continue;
        };

        // A segment without length has no direction, and leaves the path where it was.
        let curve = Curve::from_segment(&segment);
        let line_count = line_count_to_follow(&curve);
        let measure = ContourMeasure::of_curve(curve, line_count);
        let segment_length = measure.length();
        if segment_length <= 0.0 {
            continue;
        }
        let direction_at = |distance_in_segment: f32| measure.position_and_tangent(distance_in_segment).1;

        let start_direction = direction_at(0.0);
        if let Some(last) = vertices.last_mut()
            && last.direction == FloatPoint::default()
        {
            last.direction = start_direction;
        } else if vertices.last().map(|vertex| vertex.direction) != Some(start_direction) {
            vertices.push(PathVertex {
                point: segment.start(),
                distance,
                direction: start_direction,
            });
        }

        let mut curve = CurveToFollow {
            measure: &measure,
            distance_to_curve: distance,
            vertices: &mut vertices,
            remaining_line_count: MAXIMUM_LINE_COUNT_ALONG_CURVE - line_count,
        };
        let mut previous_distance = 0.0f32;
        let mut previous_point = segment.start();
        for line in 1..=line_count {
            let distance_in_segment = segment_length * line as f32 / line_count as f32;
            let (position, tangent) = if line == line_count {
                (segment.end(), FloatPoint::default())
            } else {
                measure.position_and_tangent(distance_in_segment)
            };
            curve.follow_between(previous_distance, previous_point, distance_in_segment, position);
            if line < line_count {
                curve.vertices.push(PathVertex {
                    point: position,
                    distance: distance + distance_in_segment,
                    direction: tangent,
                });
            }
            previous_distance = distance_in_segment;
            previous_point = position;
        }
        distance += segment_length;
        vertices.push(PathVertex {
            point: segment.end(),
            distance,
            direction: direction_at(segment_length),
        });
    }

    if vertices.is_empty() {
        vertices.push(PathVertex {
            point: geometry.points()[0],
            distance: 0.0,
            direction: FloatPoint::default(),
        });
    }
    vertices
}

struct CurveToFollow<'a> {
    measure: &'a ContourMeasure,
    distance_to_curve: f32,
    vertices: &'a mut Vec<PathVertex>,
    remaining_line_count: u32,
}

impl CurveToFollow<'_> {
    /// Appends the vertices between two points along the curve, splitting the line between them in half
    /// for as long as the curve passes further than the tolerance from it halfway, or until the curve has
    /// as many lines as it may have.
    fn follow_between(
        &mut self,
        start_distance: f32,
        start_point: FloatPoint,
        end_distance: f32,
        end_point: FloatPoint,
    ) {
        if self.remaining_line_count == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let middle_distance = (start_distance + end_distance) / 2.0;
        let (middle_point, tangent) = self.measure.position_and_tangent(middle_distance);
        let chord_middle = FloatPoint {
            x: (start_point.x + end_point.x) / 2.0,
            y: (start_point.y + end_point.y) / 2.0,
        };
        if Point::from_float(middle_point).distance_to(Point::from_float(chord_middle)) <= MEASURE_TOLERANCE {
            return;
        }

        self.remaining_line_count -= 1;
        self.follow_between(start_distance, start_point, middle_distance, middle_point);
        self.vertices.push(PathVertex {
            point: middle_point,
            distance: self.distance_to_curve + middle_distance,
            direction: tangent,
        });
        self.follow_between(middle_distance, middle_point, end_distance, end_point);
    }
}

/*

//! The area that stroking a path covers, as a path to fill with the nonzero winding rule.
//!
//! Each subpath is followed as a polyline through points along its curves, each with the directions in
//! which the path arrives at it and leaves it, and is cut into dashes when the stroke has a dash pattern.
//! Every line of a polyline adds the band between the normals of the path at its ends, every corner of the
//! path the piece that its join adds, and every open end its cap. All pieces wind the same way, so the
//! nonzero fill of them all is the area that they cover together.

use super::curves::{Curve, Point};
use super::geometry::{PathElement, PathGeometry};
use super::measure::line_count_to_follow;
use crate::geometry::FloatPoint;
use crate::paint_enums::{CapStyle, JoinStyle, WindingRule};

/// The smallest cosine of half a turn that one conic covers as a round join. A turn that comes closer to a
/// reversal gets a whole circle.
const SMALLEST_HALF_TURN_COSINE_OF_A_SECTOR: f64 = 0.1;

pub struct StrokeStyle<'a> {
    pub thickness: f32,
    pub cap_style: CapStyle,
    pub join_style: JoinStyle,
    pub miter_limit: f32,
    pub dash_array: &'a [f32],
    pub dash_offset: f32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct PolylinePoint {
    point: Point,
    // The unit directions in which the path arrives at the point and leaves it. They differ only at the
    // corners of the path.
    incoming: Point,
    outgoing: Point,
}

struct Polyline {
    points: Vec<PolylinePoint>,
    closed: bool,
}

pub fn stroke_to_fill(geometry: &PathGeometry, style: &StrokeStyle) -> PathGeometry {
    let mut output = PathGeometry::new();
    let half_thickness = f64::from(style.thickness) / 2.0;
    if !geometry.has_geometry() || !half_thickness.is_finite() || half_thickness <= 0.0 {
        return output;
    }
    let mut stroker = Stroker {
        output: &mut output,
        half_thickness,
        style,
    };
    let dash_pattern = dash_pattern(style);
    for subpath in subpaths_of(geometry) {
        match &dash_pattern {
            Some(pattern) => {
                for dash in dashes_of(&subpath, pattern, f64::from(style.dash_offset)) {
                    stroker.stroke(&dash);
                }
            }
            None => stroker.stroke(&subpath),
        }
    }
    output.set_fill_rule(WindingRule::Nonzero);
    output.update_state_from_contours();
    output
}

fn unit(vector: Point) -> Point {
    vector.scaled(1.0 / vector.length())
}

fn normal(direction: Point) -> Point {
    Point::new(-direction.y, direction.x)
}

/// The subpaths of the path as polylines. Only a subpath that a segment follows its move into is stroked,
/// even if the segment goes nowhere, so that round and square caps can draw it as a dot.
fn subpaths_of(geometry: &PathGeometry) -> Vec<Polyline> {
    let mut subpaths = Vec::new();
    // The subpath that is being followed, and whether a segment has followed its move.
    let mut current: Option<(Polyline, bool)> = None;
    for element in geometry.elements() {
        if let PathElement::MoveTo(point) = element {
            if let Some((subpath, true)) = current.take() {
                subpaths.push(subpath);
            }
            // The directions at the start are those of the first segment that goes somewhere.
            let start = PolylinePoint {
                point: Point::from_float(point),
                incoming: Point::default(),
                outgoing: Point::default(),
            };
            current = Some((
                Polyline {
                    points: vec![start],
                    closed: false,
                },
                false,
            ));
            continue;
        }
        let (subpath, has_segment) = current.as_mut().expect("a segment follows a move");
        *has_segment = true;
        let Some(segment) = element.drawn_segment() else {
            continue;
        };
        if segment.is_degenerate() {
            if let PathElement::Close(_) = element {
                subpath.closed = true;
            }
            continue;
        }
        let curve = Curve::from_segment(&segment);
        let direction_at = |t: f64| {
            unit(
                curve
                    .direction_at(t)
                    .expect("a segment that goes somewhere has directions"),
            )
        };
        leave_in_direction(subpath, direction_at(0.0));
        let line_count = line_count_to_follow(&curve);
        for line in 1..=line_count {
            let t = f64::from(line) / f64::from(line_count);
            let point = if line == line_count {
                curve.end()
            } else {
                curve.point_at(t)
            };
            push_point(subpath, point, direction_at(t));
        }
        if let PathElement::Close(_) = element {
            subpath.closed = true;
        }
    }
    if let Some((subpath, true)) = current {
        subpaths.push(subpath);
    }
    subpaths
}

/// Sets the direction in which the path leaves the last point of the polyline, and the one in which it
/// arrives at the start, if nothing has arrived there.
fn leave_in_direction(polyline: &mut Polyline, direction: Point) {
    let last = polyline.points.last_mut().expect("a polyline has a start");
    last.outgoing = direction;
    if last.incoming == Point::default() {
        last.incoming = direction;
    }
}

/// Adds a point where the path goes in the direction. A point where the polyline already is only takes the
/// direction in which the path leaves it.
fn push_point(polyline: &mut Polyline, point: Point, direction: Point) {
    if let Some(last) = polyline.points.last_mut()
        && last.point == point
    {
        last.outgoing = direction;
        return;
    }
    polyline.points.push(PolylinePoint {
        point,
        incoming: direction,
        outgoing: direction,
    });
}

/// The dash pattern of the style, if it has one that dashes anything: an even number of lengths that are
/// not negative, and that do not all add up to nothing.
fn dash_pattern(style: &StrokeStyle) -> Option<Vec<f64>> {
    let pattern: Vec<f64> = style.dash_array.iter().map(|length| f64::from(*length)).collect();
    if pattern.is_empty()
        || !pattern.len().is_multiple_of(2)
        || !pattern.iter().all(|length| length.is_finite() && *length >= 0.0)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let total: f64 = pattern.iter().sum();
    (total > 0.0 && f64::from(style.dash_offset).is_finite()).then_some(pattern)
}

/// The dashes of a subpath. The pattern starts over at the start of each subpath, at the offset. A dash
/// that runs through the start of a closed subpath is one dash. A subpath that goes nowhere has no dashes.
fn dashes_of(subpath: &Polyline, pattern: &[f64], offset: f64) -> Vec<Polyline> {
    if subpath.points.len() < 2 {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let total: f64 = pattern.iter().sum();
    let mut index = 0;
    let mut remaining = pattern[0];
    let mut phase = offset.rem_euclid(total);
    // A dash with no length at the offset still starts there, and draws a dot with round and square caps.
    while phase > remaining || (phase == remaining && remaining > 0.0) {
        phase -= remaining;
        index = (index + 1) % pattern.len();
        remaining = pattern[index];
    }
    remaining -= phase;

    // The lengths at even indices are dashes, and those at odd ones are gaps.
    let starts_in_dash = index % 2 == 0;
    let mut dashes = Vec::new();
    let mut current = starts_in_dash.then(|| vec![subpath.points[0]]);
    for pair in subpath.points.windows(2) {
        let (from, to) = (pair[0], pair[1]);
        let length = from.point.distance_to(to.point);
        let mut travelled = 0.0;
        while length - travelled > remaining {
            travelled += remaining;
            let fraction = travelled / length;
            let direction = unit(from.outgoing.lerp(to.incoming, fraction));
            let point = PolylinePoint {
                point: from.point.lerp(to.point, fraction),
                incoming: direction,
                outgoing: direction,
            };
            // The pattern alternates between dashes and gaps, so a dash ends here or one starts.
            match current.take() {
                Some(mut dash) => {
                    dash.push(point);
                    dashes.push(dash);
                }
                None => current = Some(vec![point]),
            }
            index = (index + 1) % pattern.len();
            remaining = pattern[index];
        }
        remaining -= length - travelled;
        if let Some(dash) = current.as_mut() {
            dash.push(to);
        }
    }
    let ends_in_dash = current.is_some();
    dashes.extend(current);

    if subpath.closed && starts_in_dash && ends_in_dash && dashes.len() > 1 {
        let first = dashes.remove(0);
        let last = dashes.last_mut().expect("there is more than one dash");
        last.last_mut().expect("a dash has points").outgoing = first[0].outgoing;
        last.extend(first.into_iter().skip(1));
    }
    dashes
        .into_iter()
        .map(|points| Polyline { points, closed: false })
        .collect()
}

struct Stroker<'a> {
    output: &'a mut PathGeometry,
    half_thickness: f64,
    style: &'a StrokeStyle<'a>,
}

impl Stroker<'_> {
    fn stroke(&mut self, polyline: &Polyline) {
        let mut points: Vec<PolylinePoint> = Vec::with_capacity(polyline.points.len());
        for point in &polyline.points {
            match points.last_mut() {
                Some(last) if last.point == point.point => last.outgoing = point.outgoing,
                _ => points.push(*point),
            }
        }
        if points.len() < 2 {
            if let Some(point) = points.first() {
                self.add_dot(point.point);
            }
            return;
        }

        for pair in points.windows(2) {
            self.add_band(pair[0], pair[1]);
        }
        for point in &points[1..points.len() - 1] {
            self.add_join(point.point, point.incoming, point.outgoing);
        }
        let (first, last) = (points[0], points[points.len() - 1]);
        if polyline.closed {
            self.add_join(first.point, last.incoming, first.outgoing);
        } else {
            self.add_cap(first.point, first.outgoing.scaled(-1.0));
            self.add_cap(last.point, last.incoming);
        }
    }

    /// The band that a line of the polyline sweeps, between the normals of the path where the line starts
    /// and where it ends.
    fn add_band(&mut self, from: PolylinePoint, to: PolylinePoint) {
        let from_offset = normal(from.outgoing).scaled(self.half_thickness);
        let to_offset = normal(to.incoming).scaled(self.half_thickness);
        let corners = [
            from.point.plus(from_offset),
            to.point.plus(to_offset),
            to.point.minus(to_offset),
            from.point.minus(from_offset),
        ];
        if is_convex(&corners) {
            self.add_convex_polygon(&corners);
            return;
        }
        // Where the curve bends more tightly than the stroke is wide, the normals cross on the inner side.
        // Triangles fanned from the line cover the band without needing it to be convex.
        for triangle in [
            [from.point, corners[0], corners[1]],
            [from.point, corners[1], to.point],
            [from.point, to.point, corners[2]],
            [from.point, corners[2], corners[3]],
        ] {
            self.add_convex_polygon(&triangle);
        }
    }

    /// The piece that the join adds at a corner, on the outer side of the turn.
    fn add_join(&mut self, point: Point, incoming: Point, outgoing: Point) {
        let cross = incoming.x * outgoing.y - incoming.y * outgoing.x;
        let dot = incoming.x * outgoing.x + incoming.y * outgoing.y;
        if cross == 0.0 && dot > 0.0 {
            return;
        }
        let half_turn_cosine = ((1.0 + dot) / 2.0).max(0.0).sqrt();
        // The outer side of a turn is the one away from the side that the path turns to.
        let outer_side = if cross > 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
        let incoming_offset = point.plus(normal(incoming).scaled(outer_side * self.half_thickness));
        let outgoing_offset = point.plus(normal(outgoing).scaled(outer_side * self.half_thickness));
        let miter_tip = || {
            let bisector = unit(incoming_offset.plus(outgoing_offset).minus(point.scaled(2.0)));
            point.plus(bisector.scaled(self.half_thickness / half_turn_cosine))
        };
        match self.style.join_style {
            JoinStyle::Round if half_turn_cosine < SMALLEST_HALF_TURN_COSINE_OF_A_SECTOR => {
                self.add_circle(point, self.half_thickness);
            }
            JoinStyle::Round => {
                // An arc around the corner from one offset to the other is a conic with the miter tip as its
                // control point, and the cosine of half the turn as its weight.
                self.add_sector(
                    point,
                    incoming_offset,
                    miter_tip(),
                    outgoing_offset,
                    half_turn_cosine as f32,
                );
            }
            // The miter is as long as the stroke is wide times one over the cosine of half the turn. One longer
            // than the limit is a bevel.
            JoinStyle::Miter
                if half_turn_cosine > 0.0 && 1.0 / half_turn_cosine <= f64::from(self.style.miter_limit) =>
            {
                self.add_convex_polygon(&[point, incoming_offset, miter_tip(), outgoing_offset]);
            }
            JoinStyle::Miter | JoinStyle::Bevel => {
                self.add_convex_polygon(&[point, incoming_offset, outgoing_offset]);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The cap at an open end, where the path leaves in the given direction.
    fn add_cap(&mut self, end: Point, direction: Point) {
        match self.style.cap_style {
            CapStyle::Butt => {}
            CapStyle::Round => self.add_circle(end, self.half_thickness),
            CapStyle::Square => {
                let along = direction.scaled(self.half_thickness);
                let across = normal(direction).scaled(self.half_thickness);
                self.add_convex_polygon(&[
                    end.plus(across),
                    end.plus(across).plus(along),
                    end.minus(across).plus(along),
                    end.minus(across),
                ]);
            }
        }
    }

    /// A polyline that goes nowhere: round caps make it a circle, and square caps a square along the x axis.
    fn add_dot(&mut self, point: Point) {
        match self.style.cap_style {
            CapStyle::Butt => {}
            CapStyle::Round => self.add_circle(point, self.half_thickness),
            CapStyle::Square => {
                let half = self.half_thickness;
                self.add_convex_polygon(&[
                    Point::new(point.x - half, point.y - half),
                    Point::new(point.x + half, point.y - half),
                    Point::new(point.x + half, point.y + half),
                    Point::new(point.x - half, point.y + half),
                ]);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Adds a convex polygon that winds the same way as every other piece. One without area adds nothing.
    fn add_convex_polygon(&mut self, points: &[Point]) {
        let twice_area: f64 = (0..points.len())
            .map(|index| {
                let (a, b) = (points[index], points[(index + 1) % points.len()]);
                a.x * b.y - b.x * a.y
            })
            .sum();
        if !twice_area.is_normal() {
            return;
        }
        let mut ordered: Vec<Point> = points.to_vec();
        if twice_area < 0.0 {
            ordered.reverse();
        }
        self.output.contour_move_to(ordered[0].to_float());
        for point in &ordered[1..] {
            self.output.contour_line_to(point.to_float());
        }
        self.output.contour_close();
    }

    /// Adds the sector of a circle around the center from one point on it to another, along the conic with
    /// the control point and the weight, winding the same way as the polygons.
    fn add_sector(&mut self, center: Point, from: Point, control: Point, to: Point, weight: f32) {
        let twice_area = (from.x - center.x) * (to.y - center.y) - (to.x - center.x) * (from.y - center.y);
        if !twice_area.is_normal() {
            return;
        }
        let (from, to) = if twice_area > 0.0 { (from, to) } else { (to, from) };
        self.output.contour_move_to(center.to_float());
        self.output.contour_line_to(from.to_float());
        self.output.contour_conic_to(control.to_float(), to.to_float(), weight);
        self.output.contour_close();
    }

    /// Adds a circle as four quarter circles, winding the same way as the polygons.
    fn add_circle(&mut self, center: Point, radius: f64) {
        let at = |x: f64, y: f64| FloatPoint {
            x: (center.x + x * radius) as f32,
            y: (center.y + y * radius) as f32,
        };
        let weight = std::f32::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2;
        self.output.contour_move_to(at(1.0, 0.0));
        self.output.contour_conic_to(at(1.0, 1.0), at(0.0, 1.0), weight);
        self.output.contour_conic_to(at(-1.0, 1.0), at(-1.0, 0.0), weight);
        self.output.contour_conic_to(at(-1.0, -1.0), at(0.0, -1.0), weight);
        self.output.contour_conic_to(at(1.0, -1.0), at(1.0, 0.0), weight);
        self.output.contour_close();
    }
}

/// Whether the polygon turns the same way at each corner.
fn is_convex(points: &[Point]) -> bool {
    let count = points.len();
    let turns = (0..count).map(|index| {
        let (a, b, c) = (points[index], points[(index + 1) % count], points[(index + 2) % count]);
        (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - b.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - b.x)
    });
    let (mut has_left_turn, mut has_right_turn) = (false, false);
    for turn in turns {
        has_left_turn |= turn > 0.0;
        has_right_turn |= turn < 0.0;
    }
    !(has_left_turn && has_right_turn)
}

//! The path as the text of SVG path data, with absolute commands and no separator before a command.

use super::curves::Point;
use super::geometry::{PathElement, PathGeometry, Segment};
use crate::geometry::FloatPoint;
use std::fmt::Write;

/// The furthest that the quadratic curves that stand for a conic may be from it.
const CONIC_TO_QUADS_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1.0 / 1024.0;

/// A conic becomes at most 2^5 quadratic curves.
const MAXIMUM_CONIC_SPLIT_DEPTH: u32 = 5;

pub fn to_svg_string(geometry: &PathGeometry) -> String {
    let mut output = String::new();
    if !geometry.has_geometry() {
        return output;
    }
    for element in geometry.elements() {
        match element {
            PathElement::MoveTo(point) => write_command(&mut output, 'M', &[point]),
            PathElement::Segment(Segment::Line([_, end])) => write_command(&mut output, 'L', &[end]),
            PathElement::Segment(Segment::Quad([_, control, end])) => write_command(&mut output, 'Q', &[control, end]),
            PathElement::Segment(Segment::Cubic([_, control1, control2, end])) => {
                write_command(&mut output, 'C', &[control1, control2, end]);
            }
            PathElement::Segment(Segment::Conic(points, weight)) => {
                for (control, end) in quads_for_conic(points, weight) {
                    write_command(&mut output, 'Q', &[control, end]);
                }
            }
            PathElement::Close([current, start]) => {
                if current != start {
                    write_command(&mut output, 'L', &[start]);
                }
                output.push('Z');
            }
        }
    }
    output
}

fn write_command(output: &mut String, command: char, points: &[FloatPoint]) {
    output.push(command);
    for (index, point) in points.iter().enumerate() {
        if index > 0 {
            output.push(' ');
        }
        write_number(output, point.x);
        output.push(' ');
        write_number(output, point.y);
    }
}

/// Writes the number with eight significant digits and without trailing zeros, in the notation that
/// printf() gives for "%.8g": a fixed point when the decimal exponent is at least -4 and less than 8,
/// and an exponent of at least two digits otherwise.
fn write_number(output: &mut String, value: f32) {
    const SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS: i32 = 8;
    let value = f64::from(value);
    let scientific = format!("{:.*e}", (SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS - 1) as usize, value);
    let (mantissa, exponent) = scientific
        .split_once('e')
        .expect("the scientific notation has an exponent");
    let exponent: i32 = exponent.parse().expect("the exponent is a number");
    if (-4..SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS).contains(&exponent) {
        let fixed = format!("{:.*}", (SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS - 1 - exponent) as usize, value);
        output.push_str(without_trailing_zeros(&fixed));
    } else {
        output.push_str(without_trailing_zeros(mantissa));
        let sign = if exponent < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        write!(output, "e{sign}{:02}", exponent.abs()).expect("writing to a String succeeds");
    }
}

fn without_trailing_zeros(number: &str) -> &str {
    if !number.contains('.') {
        return number;
    }
    number.trim_end_matches('0').trim_end_matches('.')
}

/// The quadratic curves that stand for a conic: the conic halved n times, with n the smallest number for
/// which the pieces are within the tolerance of it. The quadratic curve with the control points of a conic
/// of weight w is furthest from it halfway, by (1 - w) / (4 (1 + w)) times the length of p0 - 2 p1 + p2,
/// and each halving cuts that distance to about a quarter.
fn quads_for_conic(points: [FloatPoint; 3], weight: f32) -> Vec<(FloatPoint, FloatPoint)> {
    let conic = (points.map(Point::from_float), f64::from(weight));
    let ([p0, p1, p2], weight) = conic;
    let mut distance = (1.0 - weight).abs() / (4.0 * (1.0 + weight)) * p0.minus(p1.scaled(2.0)).plus(p2).length();
    let mut depth = 0;
    while depth < MAXIMUM_CONIC_SPLIT_DEPTH && distance > CONIC_TO_QUADS_TOLERANCE {
        distance /= 4.0;
        depth += 1;
    }

    let mut pieces = vec![conic];
    for _ in 0..depth {
        pieces = pieces
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|piece| {
                let (first, second) = halve_conic(*piece);
                [first, second]
            })
            .collect();
    }
    let piece_count = pieces.len();
    pieces
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(index, ([_, control, end], _))| {
            // The end of the whole conic stays exactly where it is.
            let end = if index + 1 == piece_count {
                points[2]
            } else {
                end.to_float()
            };
            (control.to_float(), end)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The two halves of a conic, each with the weight that keeps the weights of its ends at 1. In
/// homogeneous coordinates, a conic is a quadratic curve, which halves as one.
fn halve_conic(([p0, p1, p2], weight): ([Point; 3], f64)) -> (([Point; 3], f64), ([Point; 3], f64)) {
    let lift = |point: Point, w: f64| (point.x * w, point.y * w, w);
    let middle_of = |a: (f64, f64, f64), b: (f64, f64, f64)| {
        (
            a.0 + (b.0 - a.0) * 0.5,
            a.1 + (b.1 - a.1) * 0.5,
            a.2 + (b.2 - a.2) * 0.5,
        )
    };
    let project = |h: (f64, f64, f64)| Point::new(h.0 / h.2, h.1 / h.2);
    let (h0, h1, h2) = (lift(p0, 1.0), lift(p1, weight), lift(p2, 1.0));
    let first_control = middle_of(h0, h1);
    let second_control = middle_of(h1, h2);
    let middle = middle_of(first_control, second_control);
    let middle_point = project(middle);
    (
        (
            [p0, project(first_control), middle_point],
            first_control.2 / (h0.2 * middle.2).sqrt(),
        ),
        (
            [middle_point, project(second_control), p2],
            second_control.2 / (middle.2 * h2.2).sqrt(),
        ),
    )
}

/*

use png::{BitDepth, ColorType, Compression, DeflateCompression, Encoder, Filter, Info, chunk};
use std::borrow::Cow;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::io::{self, Write};

#[repr(C)]
pub struct PNGEncodeOptions {
    /// The data for an iCCP chunk, or null.
    pub icc_profile: *const u8,
    pub icc_profile_len: usize,
    pub has_cicp: bool,
    pub cicp_color_primaries: u8,
    pub cicp_transfer_function: u8,
    pub cicp_matrix_coefficients: u8,
    pub cicp_video_full_range_flag: u8,
    /// Encodes much faster, at the cost of a larger file.
    pub fast: bool,
    /// The color values of the pixels are premultiplied by their alpha, which PNG does not store them as.
    pub premultiplied: bool,
}

const STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 256 * 1024;

type PNGWriteCallback = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, data: *const u8, len: usize) -> bool;

struct CallbackWriter {
    context: *mut c_void,
    write: PNGWriteCallback,
}

impl Write for CallbackWriter {
    fn write(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
        // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on `png_rust_encode`.
        if !unsafe { (self.write)(self.context, data.as_ptr(), data.len()) } {
            return Err(io::ErrorKind::OutOfMemory.into());
        }
        Ok(data.len())
    }

    fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Divides the color values of an RGBA pixel by its alpha.
fn unpremultiplied([red, green, blue, alpha]: [u8; 4]) -> [u8; 4] {
    if alpha == 0 {
        return [0, 0, 0, 0];
    }
    let alpha_value = u32::from(alpha);
    let channel = |value: u8| u8::try_from((u32::from(value) * 255 + alpha_value / 2) / alpha_value).unwrap_or(u8::MAX);
    [channel(red), channel(green), channel(blue), alpha]
}

/// Encodes 8-bit RGBA pixels, or BGRA pixels when `is_bgra` is set, as an RGBA PNG.
///
/// # Safety
/// - `pixels` must be valid for `height` rows of `stride` bytes, the last of which holds at least `width * 4` bytes.
/// - `options` must be a valid pointer, and its ICC profile must be null or valid for `icc_profile_len` bytes.
/// - `write` is called with the encoded bytes in order, and returns false when it could not take them.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn png_rust_encode(
    pixels: *const u8,
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    stride: usize,
    is_bgra: bool,
    options: *const PNGEncodeOptions,
    context: *mut c_void,
    write: PNGWriteCallback,
) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `options` is valid.
    let options = unsafe { &*options };
    let row_bytes = width as usize * 4;
    if width == 0 || height == 0 || stride < row_bytes {
        return false;
    }
    let len = stride * (height as usize - 1) + row_bytes;
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `pixels` is valid for `len` bytes.
    let pixels = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(pixels, len) };

    let mut info = Info::with_size(width, height);
    info.color_type = ColorType::Rgba;
    info.bit_depth = BitDepth::Eight;
    if !options.icc_profile.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that the ICC profile is valid.
        let profile = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(options.icc_profile, options.icc_profile_len) };
        info.icc_profile = Some(Cow::Borrowed(profile));
    }
    let Ok(mut encoder) = Encoder::with_info(CallbackWriter { context, write }, info) else {
        return false;
    };
    if options.fast {
        // NB: Trying every filter on each row and compressing with zlib dominate the encoding time.
        encoder.set_deflate_compression(DeflateCompression::FdeflateUltraFast);
        encoder.set_filter(Filter::Sub);
    } else {
        encoder.set_compression(Compression::Balanced);
    }

    let Ok(mut writer) = encoder.write_header() else {
        return false;
    };
    if options.has_cicp {
        let cicp = [
            options.cicp_color_primaries,
            options.cicp_transfer_function,
            options.cicp_matrix_coefficients,
            options.cicp_video_full_range_flag,
        ];
        if writer.write_chunk(chunk::cICP, &cicp).is_err() {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // The rows go to the encoder one at a time, so the image is never copied whole.
    let Ok(mut stream) = writer.stream_writer_with_size(STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE) else {
        return false;
    };
    let mut row = vec![0; row_bytes];
    for y in 0..height as usize {
        let source = &pixels[y * stride..y * stride + row_bytes];
        let row = if is_bgra || options.premultiplied {
            for (source, destination) in source.as_chunks::<4>().0.iter().zip(row.as_chunks_mut::<4>().0) {
                let pixel = if is_bgra {
                    [source[2], source[1], source[0], source[3]]
                } else {
                    *source
                };
                *destination = if options.premultiplied {
                    unpremultiplied(pixel)
                } else {
                    pixel
                };
            }
            &row[..]
        } else {
            source
        };
        if stream.write_all(row).is_err() {
            return false;
        }
    }
    if stream.finish().is_err() {
        return false;
    }
    writer.finish().is_ok()
}
