struct Reader<'a> {
    data: &'a [u8],
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    fn new(data: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Self { data }
    }

    fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
        self.data.len()
    }

    fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.data.is_empty()
    }

    fn read_array<const N: usize>(&mut self) -> Option<[u8; N]> {
        let (head, tail) = self.data.split_first_chunk::<N>()?;
        self.data = tail;
        Some(*head)
    }

    fn read_u8(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
        Some(self.read_array::<1>()?[0])
    }

    fn read_u16(&mut self) -> Option<u16> {
        Some(u16::from_le_bytes(self.read_array()?))
    }

    fn read_u24(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        let [b0, b1, b2] = self.read_array()?;
        Some(u32::from_le_bytes([b0, b1, b2, 0]))
    }

    fn read_u32(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
        Some(u32::from_le_bytes(self.read_array()?))
    }

    fn read_i32(&mut self) -> Option<i32> {
        Some(i32::from_le_bytes(self.read_array()?))
    }

    fn skip(&mut self, count: usize) -> Option<()> {
        self.data = self.data.get(count..)?;
        Some(())
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ColorMask {
    mask: u32,
    // The number of right shifts that align the most significant bit of the mask with bit 7. This can be negative.
    shift: i8,
    // The number of set bits in the mask, capped at 8.
    size: u8,
}

impl ColorMask {
    fn new(mask: u32) -> Self {
        if mask == 0 {
            return Self {
                mask,
                shift: 0,
                size: 0,
            };
        }
        let mut trailing_zeros = mask.trailing_zeros() as i32;
        let mut size = (!(mask >> trailing_zeros)).trailing_zeros() as i32;
        if size > 8 {
            // Drop the lowest bits if the mask is longer than 8 bits.
            trailing_zeros += size - 8;
            size = 8;
        }
        Self {
            mask,
            shift: (size + trailing_zeros - 8) as i8,
            size: size as u8,
        }
    }

    // Scales the masked bits of `data` over the entire 8-bit range, so that for example the 5-bit value 0x1f becomes
    // 0xff instead of 0xf8.
    fn scaled_value(&self, data: u32) -> u8 {
        const SCALING_FACTORS_2BIT: [u8; 4] = [0x00, 0x55, 0xaa, 0xff];
        const SCALING_FACTORS_3BIT: [u8; 8] = [0x00, 0x24, 0x48, 0x6d, 0x91, 0xb6, 0xdb, 0xff];

        let data = data & self.mask;
        let number = if self.shift < 0 {
            (data << -self.shift) as u8
        } else {
            (data >> self.shift) as u8
        };
        match self.size {
            0 => 0,
            1 => {
                if number != 0 {
                    0xff
                } else {
                    0
                }
            }
            2 => SCALING_FACTORS_2BIT[(number >> 6) as usize],
            3 => SCALING_FACTORS_3BIT[(number >> 5) as usize],
            // With 4 or more bits, copying the most significant bits into the least significant bits scales evenly.
            size => (u32::from(number) | (u32::from(number) >> size)) as u8,
        }
    }
}

struct DIBHeader {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    bpp: u16,
    compression: u32,
    number_of_palette_colors: u32,
    masks: Vec<u32>,
    color_space: u32,
    profile_data: u32,
    profile_size: u32,
}

pub struct BMPDecoder {
    included_in_ico: bool,
    dib_type: DIBType,
    dib_size: usize,
    data_offset: usize,
    width: usize,
    height: usize,
    top_down: bool,
    bpp: u16,
    compression: u32,
    number_of_palette_colors: u32,
    masks: Vec<ColorMask>,
}

fn decode_file_header(data: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    if data.get(0..2)? != b"BM" {
        return None;
    }
    // NB: The file size field is ignored, since files disagree on whether it holds the size of the file or of the
    //     header. The four bytes after it are reserved.
    let data_offset = u32::from_le_bytes(*data.get(10..14)?.first_chunk()?) as usize;
    if data_offset >= data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(data_offset)
}

fn is_supported_compression(dib_type: DIBType, compression: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(
        compression,
        compression::RGB | compression::BITFIELDS | compression::ALPHABITFIELDS | compression::RLE8 | compression::RLE4
    ) || (compression == compression::RLE24 && dib_type <= DIBType::OSV2)
}

fn decode_core_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader, dib_type: DIBType) -> Option<()> {
    // The width and height are u16 fields in BITMAPCOREHEADER.
    if dib_type == DIBType::Core {
        dib.width = i32::from(reader.read_u16()?);
        dib.height = i32::from(reader.read_u16()?);
    } else {
        dib.width = reader.read_i32()?;
        dib.height = reader.read_i32()?;
    }
    if dib.width < 0 || dib.height == i32::MIN {
        return None;
    }
    // INTEROP: The plane count should be 1, but is ignored.
    reader.skip(2)?;
    dib.bpp = reader.read_u16()?;
    match dib.bpp {
        1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 => Some(()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn decode_osv2_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader, dib_type: DIBType) -> Option<()> {
    dib.width = reader.read_i32()?;
    dib.height = reader.read_i32()?;
    if dib.width < 0 || dib.height == i32::MIN {
        return None;
    }
    // INTEROP: The plane count should be 1, but is ignored.
    reader.skip(2)?;
    dib.bpp = reader.read_u16()?;
    // OS/2 did not expect 16 or 32 bpp to be popular.
    if !matches!(dib.bpp, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 24) {
        return None;
    }
    if dib_type == DIBType::OSV2Short {
        return Some(());
    }

    dib.compression = reader.read_u32()?;
    if !is_supported_compression(dib_type, dib.compression) {
        return None;
    }
    // Image size, horizontal resolution, vertical resolution.
    reader.skip(12)?;
    dib.number_of_palette_colors = reader.read_u32()?.min(COLOR_PALETTE_LIMIT);
    // Important colors, units, reserved, recording, halftoning, size1, size2, color encoding, identifier.
    reader.skip(4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 8)
}

fn decode_info_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader, dib_type: DIBType) -> Option<()> {
    decode_core_dib(reader, dib, dib_type)?;
    dib.compression = reader.read_u32()?;
    if !is_supported_compression(dib_type, dib.compression) {
        return None;
    }
    // Image size, horizontal resolution, vertical resolution.
    reader.skip(12)?;
    dib.number_of_palette_colors = reader.read_u32()?.min(COLOR_PALETTE_LIMIT);
    // Important colors.
    reader.skip(4)
}

fn decode_v2_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader) -> Option<()> {
    if dib.compression != compression::BITFIELDS && dib.compression != compression::ALPHABITFIELDS {
        return reader.skip(12);
    }
    for _ in 0..3 {
        dib.masks.push(reader.read_u32()?);
    }
    Some(())
}

fn decode_v3_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader) -> Option<()> {
    // There is no comprehensive documentation of when alpha masks apply, so this follows the results of the BMP test
    // suite.
    if dib.compression == compression::ALPHABITFIELDS {
        dib.masks.push(reader.read_u32()?);
        return Some(());
    }
    if dib.bpp < 16 {
        return reader.skip(4);
    }
    let mask = reader.read_u32()?;
    if dib.compression == compression::RGB && dib.bpp == 32 && mask != 0 {
        dib.masks.extend([0xff0000, 0x00ff00, 0x0000ff]);
    }
    if (dib.bpp == 32 && mask != 0) || (dib.bpp == 16 && dib.compression != compression::RGB) {
        dib.masks.push(mask);
    }
    Some(())
}

fn decode_v4_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader) -> Option<()> {
    dib.color_space = reader.read_u32()?;
    // Red, green and blue endpoints, then gamma values.
    reader.skip(36 + 12)
}

fn decode_v5_dib(reader: &mut Reader, dib: &mut DIBHeader) -> Option<()> {
    // Intent.
    reader.skip(4)?;
    dib.profile_data = reader.read_u32()?;
    dib.profile_size = reader.read_u32()?;
    // Reserved.
    reader.skip(4)
}

fn is_valid_bitmask_combination(dib_type: DIBType, dib: &DIBHeader) -> bool {
    let bpp = dib.bpp;
    let compression = dib.compression;

    if compression == compression::ALPHABITFIELDS && dib_type != DIBType::Info {
        return false;
    }

    match dib_type {
        DIBType::Core => !matches!(bpp, 2 | 16 | 32),
        DIBType::Info => match compression {
            compression::BITFIELDS | compression::ALPHABITFIELDS => bpp == 16 || bpp == 32,
            compression::RGB => true,
            compression::RLE8 => bpp <= 8,
            compression::RLE4 => bpp <= 4,
            // Other compressions are not officially supported.
            _ => false,
        },
        _ => {
            !(compression == compression::BITFIELDS && bpp != 16 && bpp != 32)
                && !(compression == compression::RLE8 && bpp > 8)
                && !(compression == compression::RLE4 && bpp > 4)
                && !(compression == compression::RLE24 && bpp != 24)
        }
    }
}

fn decode_dib(data: &[u8], included_in_ico: bool) -> Option<(BMPDecoder, BMPImageInfo)> {
    let header_size = if included_in_ico { 0 } else { BMP_FILE_HEADER_SIZE };
    let mut data_offset = if included_in_ico { 0 } else { decode_file_header(data)? };

    let dib_size = u32::from_le_bytes(*data.get(header_size..header_size + 4)?.first_chunk()?) as usize;
    if data.len() < header_size.checked_add(dib_size)? {
        return None;
    }
    if !included_in_ico && data_offset < header_size + dib_size {
        return None;
    }

    // NB: A BMP included in an ICO has no file header, so its data offset is only known after the color table size.
    //     This also means that it cannot contain extra bit masks.
    let dib_offset = if included_in_ico {
        dib_size
    } else {
        data_offset.checked_sub(header_size + 4)?
    };
    let dib_start = header_size + 4;
    if dib_offset.checked_add(dib_start)? >= data.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut reader = Reader::new(&data[dib_start..dib_start + dib_offset]);

    let dib_type = DIBType::from_size(dib_size)?;
    let mut dib = DIBHeader {
        width: 0,
        height: 0,
        bpp: 0,
        compression: compression::RGB,
        number_of_palette_colors: 0,
        masks: Vec::new(),
        color_space: 0,
        profile_data: 0,
        profile_size: 0,
    };
    match dib_type {
        DIBType::Core => decode_core_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib, dib_type)?,
        DIBType::OSV2Short | DIBType::OSV2 => decode_osv2_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib, dib_type)?,
        _ => {
            decode_info_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib, dib_type)?;
            if dib_type >= DIBType::V2 {
                decode_v2_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib)?;
            }
            if dib_type >= DIBType::V3 {
                decode_v3_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib)?;
            }
            if dib_type >= DIBType::V4 {
                decode_v4_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib)?;
            }
            if dib_type >= DIBType::V5 {
                decode_v5_dib(&mut reader, &mut dib)?;
            }
        }
    }

    if !is_valid_bitmask_combination(dib_type, &dib) {
        return None;
    }
    if dib.bpp == 16 || dib.bpp == 32 {
        if dib_type > DIBType::OSV2 && dib.bpp == 16 && dib.compression == compression::RGB {
            // RGB555.
            dib.masks.extend([0x7c00, 0x03e0, 0x001f]);
        } else if dib_type == DIBType::Info
            && (dib.compression == compression::BITFIELDS || dib.compression == compression::ALPHABITFIELDS)
        {
            // The masks follow the BITMAPINFOHEADER.
            let mask_count = if dib.compression == compression::ALPHABITFIELDS {
                4
            } else {
                3
            };
            for _ in 0..mask_count {
                dib.masks.push(reader.read_u32()?);
            }
        }
    }

    if included_in_ico {
        data_offset = dib_size;
        if dib.bpp <= 8 {
            let bytes_per_color = if dib_type == DIBType::Core { 3 } else { 4 };
            data_offset += palette_color_count(&dib) as usize * bytes_per_color;
        }
    }
    if data_offset >= data.len() {
        return None;
    }

    let mut icc_profile = BMPICCProfile::Absent;
    let mut icc_profile_offset = 0;
    let mut icc_profile_size = 0;
    // FIXME: Handle linked profiles, the sRGB color spaces, and calibrated RGB endpoints.
    if dib_type == DIBType::V5
        && dib.color_space == COLOR_SPACE_PROFILE_EMBEDDED
        && dib.profile_data != 0
        && dib.profile_size != 0
    {
        let offset = header_size as u64 + u64::from(dib.profile_data);
        if offset + u64::from(dib.profile_size) > data.len() as u64 {
            icc_profile = BMPICCProfile::OutOfBounds;
        } else {
            icc_profile = BMPICCProfile::Embedded;
            icc_profile_offset = offset as usize;
            icc_profile_size = dib.profile_size as usize;
        }
    }

    // INTEROP: An empty alpha mask means that the image has no alpha channel.
    if dib.masks.get(3) == Some(&0) {
        dib.masks.truncate(3);
    }
    let masks: Vec<ColorMask> = dib.masks.iter().map(|&mask| ColorMask::new(mask)).collect();

    // NB: A BMP included in an ICO is always given an alpha channel, since its AND mask makes pixels transparent. RLE
    //     images leave the pixels that they skip transparent.
    let is_rle = matches!(
        dib.compression,
        compression::RLE4 | compression::RLE8 | compression::RLE24
    );
    let format = if included_in_ico || is_rle {
        BMPBitmapFormat::BGRA8888
    } else {
        match dib.bpp {
            16 | 32 if masks.len() == 4 => BMPBitmapFormat::BGRA8888,
            24 => BMPBitmapFormat::RGBx8888,
            _ => BMPBitmapFormat::BGRx8888,
        }
    };

    let width = dib.width as u32;
    let absolute_height = dib.height.unsigned_abs();
    // The height of a BMP included in an ICO covers both the image and its AND mask.
    let height = if included_in_ico {
        absolute_height / 2
    } else {
        absolute_height
    };

    let decoder = BMPDecoder {
        included_in_ico,
        dib_type,
        dib_size,
        data_offset,
        width: width as usize,
        height: height as usize,
        top_down: dib.height < 0,
        bpp: dib.bpp,
        compression: dib.compression,
        number_of_palette_colors: dib.number_of_palette_colors,
        masks,
    };
    let info = BMPImageInfo {
        width,
        height,
        format,
        icc_profile,
        icc_profile_offset,
        icc_profile_size,
    };
    Some((decoder, info))
}

fn palette_color_count(dib: &DIBHeader) -> u32 {
    if dib.number_of_palette_colors > 0 {
        dib.number_of_palette_colors
    } else {
        1 << dib.bpp
    }
}

impl BMPDecoder {
    fn header_size(&self) -> usize {
        if self.included_in_ico { 0 } else { BMP_FILE_HEADER_SIZE }
    }

    fn decode_color_table(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u32>> {
        if self.bpp > 8 {
            return Some(Vec::new());
        }

        let max_colors = 1usize << self.bpp;
        let header_size = self.header_size();
        let bytes_per_color = match self.dib_type {
            // OS/2 1.x uses 3 bytes per color.
            DIBType::Core => 3,
            // OS/2 2.x uses 3 or 4 bytes per color, which is only known from the size of the color table.
            DIBType::OSV2 | DIBType::OSV2Short if self.data_offset - header_size - self.dib_size == 3 * max_colors => 3,
            _ => 4,
        };

        let size_of_color_table = if self.included_in_ico {
            let count = if self.number_of_palette_colors > 0 {
                self.number_of_palette_colors as usize
            } else {
                max_colors
            };
            count * bytes_per_color
        } else {
            self.data_offset - header_size - self.dib_size
        };

        // NB: Partial color tables are against the spec, but are accepted since most viewers process them anyway.
        let start = header_size + self.dib_size;
        let mut reader = Reader::new(data.get(start..start.checked_add(size_of_color_table)?)?);
        let mut color_table = Vec::with_capacity(max_colors);
        while !reader.is_at_end() && color_table.len() < max_colors {
            let color = if bytes_per_color == 4 {
                reader.read_u32()?
            } else {
                reader.read_u24()?
            };
            color_table.push(color | 0xff00_0000);
        }
        Some(color_table)
    }

    // Returns the number of bits per pixel of the data that `decode_rle_data()` produces.
    fn rle_bits_per_pixel(&self) -> Option<u16> {
        match self.compression {
            // INTEROP: RLE8 and RLE4 data with a lower bit count has an equally small color table, but its pixel
            //          data is still RLE8 or RLE4.
            compression::RLE8 => Some(8),
            compression::RLE4 => Some(4),
            compression::RLE24 => Some(24),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    // Returns the decoded pixel data, which of its pixels are set, and the offset in `data` where the RLE data ends.
    // The pixels that are not set were skipped and are transparent.
    fn decode_rle_data(&self, data: &[u8], bits_per_pixel: u16) -> Option<(Vec<u8>, Vec<bool>, usize)> {
        let rle_data = data.get(self.data_offset..)?;
        let mut reader = Reader::new(rle_data);
        let compression = self.compression;
        let width = self.width;
        let total_rows = self.height;
        let row_size = row_size(width, bits_per_pixel)?;
        // NB: Runs and deltas wrap at the 4-pixel boundary after the end of a row. Pixels past the end of the row are
        //     dropped.
        let total_columns = width.checked_next_multiple_of(4)?;

        let buffer_size = row_size.checked_mul(total_rows)?;
        if buffer_size > MAX_RLE_BUFFER_SIZE {
            return None;
        }
        let mut buffer = Vec::new();
        buffer.try_reserve_exact(buffer_size).ok()?;
        buffer.resize(buffer_size, 0);
        let mut pixel_is_set = Vec::new();
        let pixel_count = width.checked_mul(total_rows)?;
        pixel_is_set.try_reserve_exact(pixel_count).ok()?;
        pixel_is_set.resize(pixel_count, false);

        let mut column = 0usize;
        let mut row = 0usize;

        let mut set_pixel = |column: &mut usize, row: &mut usize, value: u32| -> Option<()> {
            if *column >= total_columns {
                *column = 0;
                *row += 1;
            }
            if *row >= total_rows {
                return None;
            }
            if *column < width {
                pixel_is_set[*row * width + *column] = true;
                let row_start = *row * row_size;
                match compression {
                    compression::RLE8 => buffer[row_start + *column] = value as u8,
                    compression::RLE4 => {
                        let byte = &mut buffer[row_start + *column / 2];
                        if (*column).is_multiple_of(2) {
                            *byte = (*byte & 0x0f) | ((value as u8) << 4);
                        } else {
                            *byte = (*byte & 0xf0) | (value as u8 & 0x0f);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {
                        let index = row_start + *column * 3;
                        buffer[index..index + 3].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes()[..3]);
                    }
                }
            }
            *column += 1;
            Some(())
        };

        let read_value = |reader: &mut Reader| -> Option<u32> {
            if compression == compression::RLE24 {
                reader.read_u24()
            } else {
                reader.read_u8().map(u32::from)
            }
        };

        loop {
            let count = reader.read_u8()?;
            if count != 0 {
                // Encoded mode: repeat one value. In RLE4, the value holds two pixels that alternate.
                let value = read_value(&mut reader)?;
                for i in 0..count {
                    let pixel = if compression == compression::RLE4 {
                        if i % 2 == 0 { value >> 4 } else { value & 0x0f }
                    } else {
                        value
                    };
                    set_pixel(&mut column, &mut row, pixel)?;
                }
                continue;
            }

            match reader.read_u8()? {
                // End of line.
                0 => {
                    column = 0;
                    row += 1;
                }
                // End of bitmap.
                1 => break,
                // Delta.
                2 => {
                    let offset_x = reader.read_u8()?;
                    let offset_y = reader.read_u8()?;
                    column += usize::from(offset_x);
                    if column >= total_columns {
                        column -= total_columns;
                        row += 1;
                    }
                    row += usize::from(offset_y);
                }
                // Absolute mode: a run of literal values, padded to a 16-bit boundary.
                count => {
                    let count = usize::from(count);
                    if compression == compression::RLE4 {
                        let byte_count = count.div_ceil(2);
                        for i in 0..count {
                            if i % 2 == 0 {
                                let byte = reader.read_u8()?;
                                set_pixel(&mut column, &mut row, u32::from(byte >> 4))?;
                                if i + 1 < count {
                                    set_pixel(&mut column, &mut row, u32::from(byte & 0x0f))?;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        if byte_count % 2 != 0 {
                            reader.read_u8()?;
                        }
                    } else {
                        for _ in 0..count {
                            let value = read_value(&mut reader)?;
                            set_pixel(&mut column, &mut row, value)?;
                        }
                        if count % 2 != 0 {
                            reader.read_u8()?;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        let end_offset = self.data_offset + (rle_data.len() - reader.remaining());
        Some((buffer, pixel_is_set, end_offset))
    }

    fn masked_color(&self, data: u32) -> u32 {
        let red = u32::from(self.masks[0].scaled_value(data));
        let green = u32::from(self.masks[1].scaled_value(data));
        let blue = u32::from(self.masks[2].scaled_value(data));
        let alpha = match self.masks.get(3) {
            Some(mask) => u32::from(mask.scaled_value(data)),
            None => 0xff,
        };
        (alpha << 24) | (red << 16) | (green << 8) | blue
    }

    fn decode(&self, data: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], stride: usize) -> Option<()> {
        let color_table = self.decode_color_table(data)?;

        let rle_data;
        // NB: The AND mask of an RLE image follows its compressed data, not the decoded pixel data.
        let (pixel_data, bits_per_pixel, rle_pixel_is_set, rle_end_offset) = match self.rle_bits_per_pixel() {
            Some(bits_per_pixel) => {
                rle_data = self.decode_rle_data(data, bits_per_pixel)?;
                (
                    rle_data.0.as_slice(),
                    bits_per_pixel,
                    rle_data.1.as_slice(),
                    Some(rle_data.2),
                )
            }
            None => (data.get(self.data_offset..)?, self.bpp, &[][..], None),
        };
        let mut reader = Reader::new(pixel_data);
        let has_alpha_mask = self.masks.len() == 4;
        let mut has_alpha_values = false;

        let width = self.width;
        let height = self.height;
        let row_bytes = width * 4;
        let output_row = |row: usize| -> usize {
            if self.top_down {
                row * stride
            } else {
                (height - 1 - row) * stride
            }
        };
        // INTEROP: Indices past the end of the color table are opaque black.
        let palette_color = |index: u8| -> u32 { color_table.get(usize::from(index)).copied().unwrap_or(0xff00_0000) };

        let skip_row_padding = |reader: &mut Reader, consumed: usize| -> Option<()> {
            let remainder = consumed % 4;
            if remainder != 0 {
                reader.skip(4 - remainder)?;
            }
            Some(())
        };

        for row in 0..height {
            let row_start = output_row(row);
            let pixels = &mut output[row_start..row_start + row_bytes];
            let remaining_before_row = reader.remaining();
            let mut set_pixel = |column: usize, color: u32| {
                pixels[column * 4..column * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&color.to_ne_bytes());
            };

            let mut column = 0;
            while column < width {
                match bits_per_pixel {
                    1 | 2 | 4 => {
                        let byte = reader.read_u8()?;
                        let pixels_per_byte = 8 / usize::from(bits_per_pixel);
                        let index_mask = (1u8 << bits_per_pixel) - 1;
                        for i in 0..pixels_per_byte {
                            if column >= width {
                                break;
                            }
                            let shift = 8 - bits_per_pixel as usize * (i + 1);
                            set_pixel(column, palette_color((byte >> shift) & index_mask));
                            column += 1;
                        }
                    }
                    8 => {
                        let byte = reader.read_u8()?;
                        set_pixel(column, palette_color(byte));
                        column += 1;
                    }
                    16 => {
                        let color = self.masked_color(u32::from(reader.read_u16()?));
                        has_alpha_values |= has_alpha_mask && color >> 24 != 0;
                        set_pixel(column, color);
                        column += 1;
                    }
                    24 => {
                        let pixel = reader.read_u24()?;
                        if self.included_in_ico {
                            // 24-bit BMPs included in ICOs are already in BGRA8888 order.
                            set_pixel(column, pixel);
                        } else if self.compression == compression::RLE24 {
                            set_pixel(column, pixel | 0xff00_0000);
                        } else {
                            set_pixel(
                                column,
                                ((pixel & 0xff) << 16) | (pixel & 0xff00) | ((pixel >> 16) & 0xff),
                            );
                        }
                        column += 1;
                    }
                    32 => {
                        let value = reader.read_u32()?;
                        if self.masks.is_empty() && self.included_in_ico {
                            has_alpha_values |= value >> 24 != 0;
                            set_pixel(column, value);
                        } else if self.masks.is_empty() {
                            // INTEROP: Without an alpha mask, the fourth byte of a standalone BMP is not alpha.
                            set_pixel(column, value | 0xff00_0000);
                        } else {
                            let color = self.masked_color(value);
                            has_alpha_values |= has_alpha_mask && color >> 24 != 0;
                            set_pixel(column, color);
                        }
                        column += 1;
                    }
                    _ => return None,
                }
            }

            if !rle_pixel_is_set.is_empty() {
                for (column, &is_set) in rle_pixel_is_set[row * width..(row + 1) * width].iter().enumerate() {
                    if !is_set {
                        set_pixel(column, 0);
                    }
                }
            }

            let consumed = remaining_before_row - reader.remaining();

            skip_row_padding(&mut reader, consumed)?;
        }

        // INTEROP: The fourth byte of a 32-bit BMP in an ICO is alpha, unless it is zero for every pixel. Only an image
        //          without alpha values uses its AND mask.
        let may_have_alpha_values = self.included_in_ico && self.bpp == 32 && self.masks.is_empty();
        if may_have_alpha_values && !has_alpha_values {
            for row in 0..height {
                let row_start = row * stride;
                for pixel in output[row_start..row_start + row_bytes].as_chunks_mut::<4>().0 {
                    *pixel = (u32::from_ne_bytes(*pixel) | 0xff00_0000).to_ne_bytes();
                }
            }
        }

        // An ICO image is followed by an AND mask with one bit per pixel, which makes pixels transparent.
        // INTEROP: An image with alpha values ignores its AND mask.
        let mut mask_reader = match rle_end_offset {
            Some(offset) => Reader::new(data.get(offset..)?),
            None => reader,
        };
        if self.included_in_ico && !has_alpha_values && !mask_reader.is_at_end() {
            for row in 0..height {
                let row_start = output_row(row);
                let pixels = &mut output[row_start..row_start + row_bytes];
                let remaining_before_row = mask_reader.remaining();

                let mut column = 0;
                while column < width {
                    let byte = mask_reader.read_u8()?;
                    for bit in (0..8).rev() {
                        if column >= width {
                            break;
                        }
                        // Pixels skipped by RLE data stay transparent.
                        if !rle_pixel_is_set.is_empty() && !rle_pixel_is_set[row * width + column] {
                            column += 1;
                            continue;
                        }
                        let pixel_bytes = &mut pixels[column * 4..column * 4 + 4];
                        let mut pixel = u32::from_ne_bytes(pixel_bytes.try_into().ok()?);
                        if (byte >> bit) & 1 != 0 {
                            pixel &= 0x00ff_ffff;
                        } else if self.bpp < 32 {
                            pixel |= 0xff00_0000;
                        }
                        pixel_bytes.copy_from_slice(&pixel.to_ne_bytes());
                        column += 1;
                    }
                }

                let consumed = remaining_before_row - mask_reader.remaining();

                skip_row_padding(&mut mask_reader, consumed)?;
            }
        }

        Some(())
    }
}

fn row_size(width: usize, bits_per_pixel: u16) -> Option<usize> {
    width
        .checked_mul(usize::from(bits_per_pixel))?
        .div_ceil(8)
        .checked_next_multiple_of(4)
}

/// # Safety
/// `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn bmp_rust_sniff(data: *const u8, data_len: usize) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        decode_file_header(data).is_some()
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// - `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
/// - `out_info` must be a valid writable pointer.
/// - The returned pointer must be freed with `bmp_rust_decoder_free`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn bmp_rust_decoder_new(
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    included_in_ico: bool,
    out_info: *mut BMPImageInfo,
) -> *mut BMPDecoder {
    catch_panic_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };
        let Some(out_info) = (unsafe { out_info.as_mut() }) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };
        let Some((decoder, info)) = decode_dib(data, included_in_ico) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };
        *out_info = info;
        Box::into_raw(Box::new(decoder))
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// `decoder` must be null or a pointer returned by `bmp_rust_decoder_new` that has not already been freed.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn bmp_rust_decoder_free(decoder: *mut BMPDecoder) {
    catch_panic_or((), || {
        if !decoder.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The caller transfers ownership of a decoder allocated by `bmp_rust_decoder_new`.
            drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(decoder) });
        }
    });
}

/// # Safety
/// - `decoder` must be a valid pointer returned by `bmp_rust_decoder_new`.
/// - `data` must be the same image passed to `bmp_rust_decoder_new` and be valid for `data_len` bytes.
/// - `buffer` must be valid for writes of `stride * height` bytes, where `height` is the height returned by
///   `bmp_rust_decoder_new`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn bmp_rust_decode(
    decoder: *const BMPDecoder,
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    buffer: *mut u8,
    stride: usize,
) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(decoder) = (unsafe { decoder.as_ref() }) else {
            return false;
        };
        if stride < decoder.width.saturating_mul(4) {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(buffer_size) = stride.checked_mul(decoder.height) else {
            return false;
        };
        // NB: An empty bitmap may have no buffer at all.
        if buffer.is_null() && buffer_size != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `buffer` is valid for writes of `stride * height` bytes.
        let output = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(buffer, buffer_size) };
        decoder.decode(data, output, stride).is_some()
    })
}

use std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe;
use std::panic::catch_unwind;

pub(crate) fn catch_panic_or<F: FnOnce() -> R, R>(fallback: R, f: F) -> R {
    match catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(f)) {
        Ok(result) => result,
        Err(payload) => {
            if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<&str>() {
                eprintln!("Rust panic at image decoder FFI boundary: {message}");
            } else if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<String>() {
                eprintln!("Rust panic at image decoder FFI boundary: {message}");
            } else {
                eprintln!("Rust panic at image decoder FFI boundary");
            }
            fallback
        }
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// `bytes` must be null or valid for `len` bytes.
pub(crate) unsafe fn bytes_from_raw<'a>(bytes: *const u8, len: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
    if len == 0 {
        return Some(&[]);
    }
    if bytes.is_null() {
        eprintln!("bytes_from_raw: null pointer with non-zero length {len}");
        return None;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that `bytes` is valid for `len` bytes.
    Some(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(bytes, len) })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::catch_panic_or;

    #[test]
    fn panic_at_ffi_boundary_is_contained() {
        assert!(!catch_panic_or(false, || panic!("expected test panic")));
    }
}

/*

use crate::ffi::{bytes_from_raw, catch_panic_or};

const ICON_TYPE_ICO: u16 = 1;
const ICON_TYPE_CUR: u16 = 2;
const ICONDIR_SIZE: usize = 6;
const ICONDIRENTRY_SIZE: usize = 16;

/// The image of an ICO or CUR file that should be displayed.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ICOImageInfo {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub image_offset: usize,
    pub image_size: usize,
}

fn read_u16(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes(*data.get(offset..)?.first_chunk()?))
}

fn read_u32(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes(*data.get(offset..)?.first_chunk()?))
}

// Returns the number of images in the file.
fn decode_icondir(data: &[u8]) -> Option<u16> {
    if read_u16(data, 0)? != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let icon_type = read_u16(data, 2)?;
    if icon_type != ICON_TYPE_ICO && icon_type != ICON_TYPE_CUR {
        return None;
    }
    read_u16(data, 4)
}

fn decode_directory(data: &[u8]) -> Option<ICOImageInfo> {
    let image_count = decode_icondir(data)?;
    if image_count == 0 {
        return None;
    }

    let mut largest: Option<(ICOImageInfo, u64, u16)> = None;
    for index in 0..usize::from(image_count) {
        let entry = data.get(ICONDIR_SIZE + index * ICONDIRENTRY_SIZE..)?;
        let entry = entry.get(..ICONDIRENTRY_SIZE)?;

        // A width or height of 0 means 256.
        let width = if entry[0] == 0 { 256 } else { u32::from(entry[0]) };
        let height = if entry[1] == 0 { 256 } else { u32::from(entry[1]) };
        // NB: In CUR files, this field holds the vertical hotspot coordinate instead.
        let bits_per_pixel = read_u16(entry, 6)?;
        let image_size = read_u32(entry, 8)? as usize;
        let image_offset = read_u32(entry, 12)? as usize;
        if image_offset.checked_add(image_size)? > data.len() {
            return None;
        }

        // Pick the largest image, and among those the one with the most bits per pixel.
        let area = u64::from(width) * u64::from(height);
        let is_better = match &largest {
            None => true,
            Some((_, largest_area, largest_bits_per_pixel)) => {
                area > *largest_area || (area == *largest_area && bits_per_pixel > *largest_bits_per_pixel)
            }
        };
        if is_better {
            let info = ICOImageInfo {
                width,
                height,
                image_offset,
                image_size,
            };
            largest = Some((info, area, bits_per_pixel));
        }
    }
    largest.map(|(info, _, _)| info)
}

/// # Safety
/// `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ico_rust_sniff(data: *const u8, data_len: usize) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        decode_icondir(data).is_some()
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// - `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
/// - `out_info` must be a valid writable pointer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ico_rust_decode_directory(
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    out_info: *mut ICOImageInfo,
) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(out_info) = (unsafe { out_info.as_mut() }) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(info) = decode_directory(data) else {
            return false;
        };
        *out_info = info;
        true
    })
}

/*

use crate::ffi::{bytes_from_raw, catch_panic_or};
use jxl::api::states::{Initialized, WithImageInfo};
use jxl::api::{JxlDecoder, JxlDecoderOptions, JxlOutputBuffer, JxlPixelFormat, ProcessingResult, check_signature};
use jxl::headers::extra_channels::ExtraChannel;
use std::ffi::c_void;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct JPEGXLImageInfo {
    pub width: usize,
    pub height: usize,
    pub is_animated: bool,
    pub alpha_premultiplied: bool,
    pub loop_count: u32,
}

type JPEGXLGetFrameBuffer =
    unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, duration_ms: u32, buffer: *mut *mut u8, stride: *mut usize) -> bool;
type JPEGXLFrameDecoded = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void) -> bool;

pub struct JPEGXLDecoder {
    decoder: Option<JxlDecoder<WithImageInfo>>,
    input_offset: usize,
}

fn decode_header(input: &mut &[u8], options: JxlDecoderOptions) -> Option<JxlDecoder<WithImageInfo>> {
    let decoder = JxlDecoder::<Initialized>::new(options);
    match decoder.process(input, None).ok()? {
        ProcessingResult::Complete { result } => Some(result),
        ProcessingResult::NeedsMoreInput { .. } => None,
    }
}

fn duration_in_milliseconds(duration: Option<f64>) -> u32 {
    duration.unwrap_or(0.0).round().clamp(0.0, u32::MAX as f64) as u32
}

/// # Safety
/// `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn jpegxl_rust_sniff(data: *const u8, data_len: usize) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        matches!(check_signature(data), ProcessingResult::Complete { result: Some(_) })
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// - `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
/// - `out_info` must be a valid writable pointer.
/// - The returned pointer must be freed with `jpegxl_rust_decoder_free`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn jpegxl_rust_decoder_new(
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    out_info: *mut JPEGXLImageInfo,
) -> *mut JPEGXLDecoder {
    catch_panic_or(std::ptr::null_mut(), || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };
        let Some(out_info) = (unsafe { out_info.as_mut() }) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };

        let mut input = data;
        let mut options = JxlDecoderOptions::default();
        // All decoded frames are full-canvas, coalesced frames.
        options.coalescing = true;
        let Some(mut decoder) = decode_header(&mut input, options) else {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        };
        let basic_info = decoder.basic_info();
        let alpha_premultiplied = basic_info
            .extra_channels
            .iter()
            .find(|channel| channel.ec_type == ExtraChannel::Alpha)
            .is_some_and(|channel| channel.alpha_associated);

        *out_info = JPEGXLImageInfo {
            width: basic_info.size.0,
            height: basic_info.size.1,
            is_animated: basic_info.animation.is_some(),
            alpha_premultiplied,
            loop_count: basic_info.animation.as_ref().map_or(0, |animation| animation.num_loops),
        };
        if decoder
            .set_pixel_format(JxlPixelFormat::rgba8(basic_info.extra_channels.len()))
            .is_err()
        {
            return std::ptr::null_mut();
        }

        Box::into_raw(Box::new(JPEGXLDecoder {
            decoder: Some(decoder),
            input_offset: data.len() - input.len(),
        }))
    })
}

/// # Safety
/// `decoder` must be null or a pointer returned by `jpegxl_rust_decoder_new` that has not already
/// been freed.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn jpegxl_rust_decoder_free(decoder: *mut JPEGXLDecoder) {
    catch_panic_or((), || {
        if !decoder.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The caller transfers ownership of a decoder allocated by
            // `jpegxl_rust_decoder_new`.
            drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(decoder) });
        }
    });
}

/// # Safety
/// - `decoder` must be a valid pointer returned by `jpegxl_rust_decoder_new`.
/// - `data` must be the same image passed to `jpegxl_rust_decoder_new` and be valid for
///   `data_len` bytes.
/// - `get_frame_buffer` must initialize `buffer` and `stride` with writable storage for an RGBA8
///   image whose dimensions were returned by `jpegxl_rust_decoder_new`. The storage must remain
///   valid until `frame_decoded` is called or this function returns.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn jpegxl_rust_decode(
    decoder: *mut JPEGXLDecoder,
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    context: *mut c_void,
    get_frame_buffer: JPEGXLGetFrameBuffer,
    frame_decoded: JPEGXLFrameDecoded,
) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(decoder) = (unsafe { decoder.as_mut() }) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(mut input) = data.get(decoder.input_offset..) else {
            return false;
        };
        // The decoder is single-use. Taking it before processing also ensures that a panic cannot
        // leave partially mutated decoder state available for another call.
        let Some(mut decoder_state) = decoder.decoder.take() else {
            return false;
        };

        let (width, height) = decoder_state.basic_info().size;
        let Some(row_bytes) = width.checked_mul(4) else {
            return false;
        };

        loop {
            let Ok(ProcessingResult::Complete {
                result: decoder_with_frame_info,
            }) = decoder_state.process(&mut input, None)
            else {
                return false;
            };

            let duration_ms = duration_in_milliseconds(decoder_with_frame_info.frame_header().duration);
            let mut buffer = std::ptr::null_mut();
            let mut stride = 0;
            // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on this function.
            if !unsafe { get_frame_buffer(context, duration_ms, &raw mut buffer, &raw mut stride) }
                || buffer.is_null()
                || stride < row_bytes
            {
                return false;
            }

            // SAFETY: The callback guarantees a writable, initialized allocation with `height`
            // rows, at least `row_bytes` bytes per row, and `stride` bytes between rows.
            let output_buffer = unsafe { JxlOutputBuffer::new_from_ptr(buffer, height, row_bytes, stride) };
            let Ok(ProcessingResult::Complete { result }) =
                decoder_with_frame_info.process(&mut input, &mut [output_buffer], None)
            else {
                return false;
            };
            decoder_state = result;

            // Commit the frame only after jxl-rs has successfully populated its output buffer.
            // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on this function.
            if !unsafe { frame_decoded(context) } {
                return false;
            }

            if !decoder_state.has_more_frames() {
                return true;
            }
        }
    })
}

/*

use crate::ffi::{bytes_from_raw, catch_panic_or};
use ::png::{BlendOp, ColorType, Decoder, DecodingError, DisposeOp, InterlaceInfo, Limits, Reader, Transformations};
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::io::Cursor;

const PNG_SIGNATURE: [u8; 8] = [0x89, b'P', b'N', b'G', 0x0D, 0x0A, 0x1A, 0x0A];

#[repr(C)]
pub struct PNGImageInfo {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    pub loop_count: u32,
    pub has_cicp: bool,
    pub cicp_color_primaries: u8,
    pub cicp_transfer_function: u8,
    pub cicp_matrix_coefficients: u8,
    pub cicp_video_full_range_flag: u8,
    /// The ICC profile, valid only for the duration of the info callback.
    pub icc_profile: *const u8,
    pub icc_profile_len: usize,
    /// The eXIf chunk, valid only for the duration of the info callback.
    pub exif: *const u8,
    pub exif_len: usize,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum PNGDecodeResult {
    /// The header or the metadata before the image data could not be read.
    InvalidHeader,
    /// The header was read, but decoding the frames failed.
    DecodingFailed,
    Success,
}

type PNGImageInfoCallback = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, info: *const PNGImageInfo) -> bool;
type PNGGetFrameBuffer =
    unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, duration_ms: u32, buffer: *mut *mut u8, stride: *mut usize) -> bool;
type PNGFrameDecoded = unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void) -> bool;

struct Callbacks {
    context: *mut c_void,
    get_frame_buffer: PNGGetFrameBuffer,
    frame_decoded: PNGFrameDecoded,
}

impl Callbacks {
    /// Hands out a BGRA buffer of the image's size, as `height` rows of `stride` bytes.
    fn frame_buffer(&mut self, duration_ms: u32, width: usize, height: usize) -> Option<(&mut [u8], usize)> {
        let mut buffer = std::ptr::null_mut();
        let mut stride = 0;
        // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on `png_rust_decode`.
        if !unsafe { (self.get_frame_buffer)(self.context, duration_ms, &raw mut buffer, &raw mut stride) }
            || buffer.is_null()
            || stride < width.checked_mul(4)?
        {
            return None;
        }
        let len = if height == 0 {
            0
        } else {
            stride.checked_mul(height - 1)?.checked_add(width * 4)?
        };
        // SAFETY: The callback guarantees a writable allocation with `height` rows of `stride` bytes, the last of
        // which holds at least `width * 4` bytes.
        let buffer = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(buffer, len) };
        Some((buffer, stride))
    }

    fn frame_decoded(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on `png_rust_decode`.
        unsafe { (self.frame_decoded)(self.context) }
    }
}

fn is_truncation(error: &DecodingError) -> bool {
    matches!(error, DecodingError::IoError(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof)
}

/// Converts one row of 8-bit RGBA or gray+alpha samples into unpremultiplied BGRA.
fn convert_row(color_type: ColorType, source: &[u8], destination: &mut [u8]) {
    match color_type {
        ColorType::Rgba => {
            for (source, destination) in source.as_chunks::<4>().0.iter().zip(destination.as_chunks_mut::<4>().0) {
                *destination = [source[2], source[1], source[0], source[3]];
            }
        }
        ColorType::GrayscaleAlpha => {
            for (source, destination) in source.as_chunks::<2>().0.iter().zip(destination.as_chunks_mut::<4>().0) {
                *destination = [source[0], source[0], source[0], source[1]];
            }
        }
        _ => unreachable!("the ALPHA transformation only produces RGBA and gray+alpha output"),
    }
}

/// How many rows the seven passes of an interlaced frame of `width` by `height` pixels have between them.
fn interlaced_row_count(width: usize, height: usize) -> usize {
    // The first column and the first row of each pass, and the step from one of its rows to the next.
    const PASSES: [(usize, usize, usize); 7] = [
        (0, 0, 8),
        (4, 0, 8),
        (0, 4, 8),
        (2, 0, 4),
        (0, 2, 4),
        (1, 0, 2),
        (0, 1, 2),
    ];
    PASSES
        .iter()
        .filter(|(first_column, ..)| width > *first_column)
        .map(|(_, first_row, row_step)| height.saturating_sub(*first_row).div_ceil(*row_step))
        .sum()
}

/// Decodes the next frame, of `width` by `height` pixels, into `destination` as BGRA rows of `stride` bytes. The pixels
/// decoded before an error are kept, and the others are left as they were.
fn decode_frame(
    reader: &mut Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>,
    (width, height): (usize, usize),
    row_buffer: &mut Vec<u8>,
    destination: &mut [u8],
    stride: usize,
) -> Result<(), DecodingError> {
    let (color_type, _) = reader.output_color_type();
    let samples = color_type.samples();

    if reader.info().interlaced {
        // Each row of an interlaced pass holds some of the pixels of one row of the frame. It is turned into BGRA, and
        // then spread out over those pixels.
        for _ in 0..interlaced_row_count(width, height) {
            let Some(row) = reader.next_interlaced_row()? else {
                break;
            };
            let InterlaceInfo::Adam7(pass) = *row.interlace() else {
                unreachable!("an interlaced frame only has Adam7 rows");
            };
            row_buffer.resize(row.data().len() / samples * 4, 0);
            convert_row(color_type, row.data(), row_buffer);
            ::png::expand_interlaced_row(destination, stride, row_buffer, &pass, 32);
        }
    } else {
        for destination in destination.chunks_mut(stride).take(height) {
            let Some(row) = reader.next_row()? else {
                break;
            };
            convert_row(
                color_type,
                &row.data()[..width * samples],
                &mut destination[..width * 4],
            );
        }
    }

    // Reading on past the last row checks the rest of the frame's data. A file that ends there still has the whole
    // frame.
    match reader.next_row() {
        Err(error) if is_truncation(&error) => Ok(()),
        result => result.map(|_| ()),
    }
}

fn decode_still_image(reader: &mut Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>, callbacks: &mut Callbacks) -> PNGDecodeResult {
    let (width, height) = reader.info().size();
    let Some((buffer, stride)) = callbacks.frame_buffer(0, width as usize, height as usize) else {
        return PNGDecodeResult::DecodingFailed;
    };

    // A truncated image keeps the rows that arrived, and the rest stays transparent.
    buffer.fill(0);
    let mut row_buffer = Vec::new();
    match decode_frame(
        reader,
        (width as usize, height as usize),
        &mut row_buffer,
        buffer,
        stride,
    ) {
        Err(error) if !is_truncation(&error) => return PNGDecodeResult::DecodingFailed,
        _ => {}
    }

    if !callbacks.frame_decoded() {
        return PNGDecodeResult::DecodingFailed;
    }
    PNGDecodeResult::Success
}

struct Rect {
    x: usize,
    y: usize,
    width: usize,
    height: usize,
}

/// An unpremultiplied BGRA image, whose rows are packed.
struct Canvas {
    pixels: Vec<u8>,
    width: usize,
    height: usize,
}

impl Canvas {
    fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(Self {
            pixels: vec![0; width.checked_mul(height)?.checked_mul(4)?],
            width,
            height,
        })
    }

    fn row(&self, y: usize) -> &[u8] {
        &self.pixels[y * self.width * 4..(y + 1) * self.width * 4]
    }

    /// Calls `callback` with each pixel of `source_rect` in `source` and the canvas pixel it lands on at `location`.
    fn for_each_frame_pixel(
        &mut self,
        location: (usize, usize),
        source: &Canvas,
        source_rect: &Rect,
        mut callback: impl FnMut(&mut [u8; 4], &[u8; 4]),
    ) {
        let width = source_rect.width.min(self.width.saturating_sub(location.0));
        let height = source_rect.height.min(self.height.saturating_sub(location.1));
        for y in 0..height {
            let destination_start = ((location.1 + y) * self.width + location.0) * 4;
            let source_start = ((source_rect.y + y) * source.width + source_rect.x) * 4;
            let destination = &mut self.pixels[destination_start..destination_start + width * 4];
            let source = &source.pixels[source_start..source_start + width * 4];
            for (destination, source) in destination
                .as_chunks_mut::<4>()
                .0
                .iter_mut()
                .zip(source.as_chunks::<4>().0)
            {
                callback(destination, source);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The source pixels replace the canvas pixels. A pixel with no alpha also loses its color.
    fn copy_pixels(&mut self, location: (usize, usize), source: &Canvas, source_rect: &Rect) {
        self.for_each_frame_pixel(location, source, source_rect, |destination, source| {
            *destination = *source;
            if source[3] == 0 {
                destination[..3].fill(0);
            }
        });
    }

    /// The source pixels go over the canvas pixels with a simple OVER operation. This takes the same steps as Skia takes
    /// when it draws an unpremultiplied bitmap onto an unpremultiplied bitmap: premultiply both, blend, and
    /// unpremultiply.
    fn blend_pixels(&mut self, location: (usize, usize), source: &Canvas) {
        let source_rect = Rect {
            x: 0,
            y: 0,
            width: source.width,
            height: source.height,
        };
        self.for_each_frame_pixel(location, source, &source_rect, |destination, source| {
            let source_alpha = source[3];
            if source_alpha == 255 {
                *destination = *source;
                return;
            }
            if source_alpha == 0 {
                if destination[3] == 0 {
                    destination[..3].fill(0);
                }
                return;
            }
            const K: f32 = 1.0 / 255.0;
            let sa = source_alpha as f32 * K;
            let da = destination[3] as f32 * K;
            let result_alpha = da * (1.0 - sa) + sa;
            let scale = 1.0 / result_alpha;
            for channel in 0..3 {
                let sc = (source[channel] as f32 * K) * sa;
                let dc = (destination[channel] as f32 * K) * da;
                let result = (dc * (1.0 - sa) + sc) * scale;
                destination[channel] = (result * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0).round_ties_even() as u8;
            }
            destination[3] = (result_alpha * 255.0).clamp(0.0, 255.0).round_ties_even() as u8;
        });
    }

    fn clear(&mut self, rect: &Rect) {
        let x_end = (rect.x + rect.width).min(self.width);
        let y_end = (rect.y + rect.height).min(self.height);
        if rect.x >= x_end {
            return;
        }
        for y in rect.y..y_end {
            self.pixels[(y * self.width + rect.x) * 4..(y * self.width + x_end) * 4].fill(0);
        }
    }
}

fn duration_in_milliseconds(delay_num: u16, delay_den: u16) -> u32 {
    if delay_num == 0 {
        return 1;
    }
    let denominator = if delay_den != 0 { delay_den as u32 } else { 100 };
    delay_num as u32 * 1000 / denominator
}

/// Decodes the frames of an animation, and returns how many were handed out. Decoding stops at the first error, and the
/// frames before it are kept.
fn decode_animation(reader: &mut Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>, frame_count: u32, callbacks: &mut Callbacks) -> u32 {
    let mut decoded_frame_count = 0;
    let (width, height) = reader.info().size();
    let Some(mut canvas) = Canvas::new(width as usize, height as usize) else {
        return decoded_frame_count;
    };

    // A default image without an fcTL chunk is not part of the animation.
    if reader.info().frame_control.is_none() && reader.next_frame_info().is_err() {
        return decoded_frame_count;
    }

    let mut frame = Canvas {
        pixels: Vec::new(),
        width: 0,
        height: 0,
    };
    let mut previous_canvas = Canvas {
        pixels: Vec::new(),
        width: 0,
        height: 0,
    };
    let mut row_buffer = Vec::new();

    for frame_index in 0..frame_count {
        // The reader starts out at the first frame's image data, and has to be moved on to each later one.
        if frame_index != 0 && reader.next_frame_info().is_err() {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        }
        let Some(frame_control) = reader.info().frame_control else {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        };
        if frame_control.width == 0 || frame_control.height == 0 {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        }
        let frame_rect = Rect {
            x: frame_control.x_offset as usize,
            y: frame_control.y_offset as usize,
            width: frame_control.width as usize,
            height: frame_control.height as usize,
        };

        frame.width = frame_rect.width;
        frame.height = frame_rect.height;
        frame.pixels.clear();
        frame.pixels.resize(frame_rect.width * frame_rect.height * 4, 0);
        let frame_size = (frame_rect.width, frame_rect.height);
        if decode_frame(
            reader,
            frame_size,
            &mut row_buffer,
            &mut frame.pixels,
            frame_rect.width * 4,
        )
        .is_err()
        {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        }

        // Only keep a copy of the canvas when the frame asks for it to be restored.
        if frame_control.dispose_op == DisposeOp::Previous {
            previous_canvas.width = canvas.width;
            previous_canvas.height = canvas.height;
            previous_canvas.pixels.clone_from(&canvas.pixels);
        }

        let location = (frame_rect.x, frame_rect.y);
        match frame_control.blend_op {
            // All color components of the frame, including alpha, overwrite the current contents of the frame's output
            // buffer region.
            BlendOp::Source => {
                let source_rect = Rect {
                    x: 0,
                    y: 0,
                    width: frame.width,
                    height: frame.height,
                };
                canvas.copy_pixels(location, &frame, &source_rect);
            }
            // The frame should be composited onto the output buffer based on its alpha, using a simple OVER operation.
            BlendOp::Over => canvas.blend_pixels(location, &frame),
        }

        let duration_ms = duration_in_milliseconds(frame_control.delay_num, frame_control.delay_den);
        let Some((buffer, stride)) = callbacks.frame_buffer(duration_ms, canvas.width, canvas.height) else {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        };
        for y in 0..canvas.height {
            buffer[y * stride..y * stride + canvas.width * 4].copy_from_slice(canvas.row(y));
        }
        if !callbacks.frame_decoded() {
            return decoded_frame_count;
        }
        decoded_frame_count += 1;

        match frame_control.dispose_op {
            // No disposal is done on this frame before rendering the next; the contents of the output buffer are left
            // as is.
            DisposeOp::None => {}
            // The frame's region of the output buffer is to be cleared to fully transparent black before rendering the
            // next frame.
            DisposeOp::Background => canvas.clear(&frame_rect),
            // The frame's region of the output buffer is to be reverted to the previous contents before rendering the
            // next frame.
            DisposeOp::Previous => canvas.copy_pixels(location, &previous_canvas, &frame_rect),
        }
    }

    decoded_frame_count
}

fn read_info(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>, DecodingError> {
    read_until_image_data(Decoder::new(Cursor::new(data)))
}

/// Reads up to the image data again, for decoding the frames of an animation.
fn read_animation_info(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>, DecodingError> {
    // The decoder counts a row of output against its memory limit for every frame it starts, and never gives it back,
    // so the default limit cuts a long animation short. The limit also bounds the inflated ICC profile and text, which
    // this reader skips, so all it allocates is bounded by the input, and it can go without one.
    let mut decoder = Decoder::new_with_limits(Cursor::new(data), Limits { bytes: usize::MAX });
    decoder.set_ignore_iccp_chunk(true);
    decoder.set_ignore_text_chunk(true);
    read_until_image_data(decoder)
}

fn read_until_image_data(mut decoder: Decoder<Cursor<&[u8]>>) -> Result<Reader<Cursor<&[u8]>>, DecodingError> {
    // Palette and low bit depth images are expanded, 16-bit samples are cut to 8 bits, and every image gets an alpha
    // channel. The output is then always 8-bit RGBA or gray+alpha.
    decoder.set_transformations(Transformations::EXPAND | Transformations::STRIP_16 | Transformations::ALPHA);
    decoder.read_info()
}

/// An ICC profile only applies to an image whose kind of color it describes.
fn icc_profile_matches_image(profile: &[u8], color_type: ColorType) -> bool {
    let Some(color_space) = profile.get(16..20) else {
        return false;
    };
    match color_type {
        ColorType::Grayscale | ColorType::GrayscaleAlpha => color_space == b"GRAY",
        ColorType::Rgb | ColorType::Rgba | ColorType::Indexed => color_space == b"RGB ",
    }
}

/// # Safety
/// `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn png_rust_sniff(data: *const u8, data_len: usize) -> bool {
    catch_panic_or(false, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return false;
        };
        data.starts_with(&PNG_SIGNATURE)
    })
}

/// Decodes a PNG or APNG image. Every frame is handed out as unpremultiplied BGRA pixels at the full image size, with
/// the animation already composed.
///
/// # Safety
/// - `data` must be valid for `data_len` bytes.
/// - `image_info` is called once, before any frame. The pointers in the info are only valid during the call.
/// - `get_frame_buffer` must initialize `buffer` and `stride` with writable storage for a BGRA8 image of the size
///   passed to `image_info`. The storage must remain valid until `frame_decoded` is called or this function returns.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn png_rust_decode(
    data: *const u8,
    data_len: usize,
    context: *mut c_void,
    image_info: PNGImageInfoCallback,
    get_frame_buffer: PNGGetFrameBuffer,
    frame_decoded: PNGFrameDecoded,
) -> PNGDecodeResult {
    catch_panic_or(PNGDecodeResult::DecodingFailed, || {
        let Some(data) = (unsafe { bytes_from_raw(data, data_len) }) else {
            return PNGDecodeResult::InvalidHeader;
        };

        let Ok(mut reader) = read_info(data) else {
            return PNGDecodeResult::InvalidHeader;
        };

        let info = reader.info();
        let animation_frame_count = info.animation_control.map_or(0, |animation| animation.num_frames);
        let cicp = info.coding_independent_code_points;
        let (icc_profile, icc_profile_len) = info
            .icc_profile
            .as_deref()
            .filter(|profile| icc_profile_matches_image(profile, info.color_type))
            .map_or((std::ptr::null(), 0), |profile| (profile.as_ptr(), profile.len()));
        let (exif, exif_len) = info
            .exif_metadata
            .as_deref()
            .map_or((std::ptr::null(), 0), |exif| (exif.as_ptr(), exif.len()));
        let image_info_value = PNGImageInfo {
            width: info.width,
            height: info.height,
            loop_count: info.animation_control.map_or(0, |animation| animation.num_plays),
            has_cicp: cicp.is_some(),
            cicp_color_primaries: cicp.map_or(0, |cicp| cicp.color_primaries),
            cicp_transfer_function: cicp.map_or(0, |cicp| cicp.transfer_function),
            cicp_matrix_coefficients: cicp.map_or(0, |cicp| cicp.matrix_coefficients),
            cicp_video_full_range_flag: cicp.map_or(0, |cicp| cicp.is_video_full_range_image as u8),
            icc_profile,
            icc_profile_len,
            exif,
            exif_len,
        };
        // SAFETY: The callback contract is documented on this function.
        if !unsafe { image_info(context, &raw const image_info_value) } {
            return PNGDecodeResult::InvalidHeader;
        }

        let mut callbacks = Callbacks {
            context,
            get_frame_buffer,
            frame_decoded,
        };
        if animation_frame_count == 0 {
            return decode_still_image(&mut reader, &mut callbacks);
        }
        if let Ok(mut animation_reader) = read_animation_info(data)
            && decode_animation(&mut animation_reader, animation_frame_count, &mut callbacks) > 0
        {
            return PNGDecodeResult::Success;
        }

        // An animation that is broken before its first frame shows the default image instead.
        decode_still_image(&mut reader, &mut callbacks)
    })
}

namespace IPC {

Attachment::Attachment(Attachment&& other)
    : m_fd(exchange(other.m_fd, -1))
{
}

Attachment& Attachment::operator=(Attachment&& other)
{
    if (this != &other) {
        if (m_fd != -1)
            (void)Core::System::close(m_fd);
        m_fd = exchange(other.m_fd, -1);
    }
    return *this;
}

Attachment::~Attachment()
{
    if (m_fd != -1)
        (void)Core::System::close(m_fd);
}

Attachment Attachment::from_fd(int fd)
{
    Attachment attachment;
    attachment.m_fd = fd;
    return attachment;
}

int Attachment::to_fd()
{
    return exchange(m_fd, -1);
}

}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Aliaksandr Kalenik <kalenik.aliaksandr@gmail.com>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/Format.h>
#include <LibCore/MachPort.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibIPC/Attachment.h>
#include <errno.h>

// fileport_makeport() and fileport_makefd() are private macOS APIs that convert
// between file descriptors and Mach port rights. Since Mach messages can only
// carry port rights (not file descriptors), we convert FDs to "file ports" for
// transmission and convert them back on the receiving side. These APIs are stable
// and used by Apple's own frameworks (including XPC).
extern "C" {
int fileport_makeport(int fd, mach_port_t* port);
int fileport_makefd(mach_port_t port);
}

namespace IPC {

Attachment::Attachment(Attachment&& other)
    : m_port(move(other.m_port))
    , m_message_right(other.m_message_right)
{
}

Attachment& Attachment::operator=(Attachment&& other)
{
    if (this != &other) {
        m_port = move(other.m_port);
        m_message_right = other.m_message_right;
    }
    return *this;
}

Attachment::~Attachment() = default;

Attachment Attachment::from_fd(int fd)
{
    mach_port_t port = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    auto result = fileport_makeport(fd, &port);
    (void)Core::System::close(fd);
    VERIFY(result == 0);
    return from_mach_port(Core::MachPort::adopt_right(port, Core::MachPort::PortRight::Send), Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveSend);
}

int Attachment::to_fd()
{
    VERIFY(MACH_PORT_VALID(m_port.port()));
    int fd = fileport_makefd(m_port.port());
    if (fd < 0) {
        dbgln("IPC::Attachment: Failed to obtain a file descriptor from a file port: {}", Error::from_errno(errno));
        return -1;
    }
    mach_port_deallocate(mach_task_self(), m_port.release());
    return fd;
}

Attachment Attachment::from_mach_port(Core::MachPort port, Core::MachPort::MessageRight right)
{
    // NB: MACH_PORT_DEAD is a legitimate name for a right whose port has died; see attachment_from_descriptor().
    VERIFY(port.port() != MACH_PORT_NULL);
    Attachment attachment;
    attachment.m_port = move(port);
    attachment.m_message_right = right;
    return attachment;
}

Core::MachPort Attachment::release_mach_port()
{
    VERIFY(m_port.port() != MACH_PORT_NULL);
    return move(m_port);
}

}

#pragma once

#include <AK/DistinctNumeric.h>
#include <AK/HashMap.h>

namespace IPC {

template<typename T>
class Encoded;

}

// These concepts are used to help the compiler distinguish between specializations that would be
// ambiguous otherwise. For example, if the specializations for int and Vector<T> were declared as
// follows:
//
//     template<> ErrorOr<int> decode(Decoder& decoder);
//     template<typename T> ErrorOr<Vector<T>> decode(Decoder& decoder);
//
// Then decode<int>() would be ambiguous because either declaration could work (the compiler would
// not be able to distinguish if you wanted to decode an int or a Vector of int).
//
// They also serve to work around the inability to do partial function specialization in C++.
namespace IPC::Concepts {

namespace Detail {

// Cannot use SpecializationOf with these templates because they have non-type parameters. See:
// https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2022/p1985r3.pdf
template<typename T>
constexpr inline bool IsArray = false;
template<typename T, size_t N>
constexpr inline bool IsArray<Array<T, N>> = true;

template<typename T>
constexpr inline bool IsVector = false;
template<typename T, size_t inline_capacity>
constexpr inline bool IsVector<Vector<T, inline_capacity>> = true;

template<typename T>
constexpr inline bool IsHashMap = false;
template<typename K, typename V, typename KeyTraits, typename ValueTraits, bool IsOrdered>
constexpr inline bool IsHashMap<HashMap<K, V, KeyTraits, ValueTraits, IsOrdered>> = true;

}

template<typename T>
concept Array = Detail::IsArray<T>;

template<typename T>
concept Vector = Detail::IsVector<T>;

template<typename T>
concept Span = SpecializationOf<T, AK::Span>;

template<typename T>
concept HashMap = Detail::IsHashMap<T>;

template<typename T>
concept Optional = SpecializationOf<T, AK::Optional>;

template<typename T>
concept Variant = SpecializationOf<T, AK::Variant>;

template<typename T>
concept DistinctNumeric = SpecializationOf<T, AK::DistinctNumeric>;

template<typename T>
concept Encoded = SpecializationOf<T, IPC::Encoded>;

}
