#include <LibIPC/Limits.h>
#include <LibIPC/Message.h>

namespace IPC {

MessageBuffer::MessageBuffer()
{
}

ErrorOr<void> MessageBuffer::extend_data_capacity(size_t capacity)
{
    TRY(m_data.try_ensure_capacity(m_data.size() + capacity));
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> MessageBuffer::append_data(u8 const* values, size_t count)
{
    TRY(m_data.try_append(values, count));
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> MessageBuffer::append_attachment(Attachment attachment)
{
    TRY(m_attachments.try_append(move(attachment)));
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> MessageBuffer::extend(MessageBuffer&& buffer)
{
    TRY(m_data.try_extend(move(buffer.m_data)));
    TRY(m_attachments.try_extend(move(buffer.m_attachments)));
    return {};
}

ErrorOr<void> MessageBuffer::transfer_message(Transport& transport)
{
    VERIFY(m_data.size() <= MAX_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SIZE);
    VERIFY(m_attachments.size() <= MAX_MESSAGE_FD_COUNT);

    TRY(transport.post_message(take_data(), m_attachments));
    return {};
}

}

class MessageBuffer {
public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    MessageBuffer();

    MessageBuffer(MessageDataType data, Vector<Attachment> attachments)
        : m_data(move(data))
        , m_attachments(move(attachments))
    {
    }

    ErrorOr<void> extend_data_capacity(size_t capacity);
    ErrorOr<void> append_data(u8 const* values, size_t count);

    ErrorOr<void> append_attachment(Attachment);

    ErrorOr<void> extend(MessageBuffer&& buffer);

    ErrorOr<void> transfer_message(Transport& transport);

    MessageDataType const& data() const { return m_data; }
    MessageDataType take_data() { return move(m_data); }

    Vector<Attachment> const& attachments() const { return m_attachments; }
    Vector<Attachment> take_attachments() { return move(m_attachments); }

private:
    MessageDataType m_data;
    Vector<Attachment> m_attachments;
};

enum class ErrorCode : u32 {
    PeerDisconnected
};

using IPCErrorOr = ErrorOr<Value, ErrorCode>;

class Message {
public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    virtual ~Message() = default;

    virtual u32 endpoint_magic() const = 0;
    virtual int message_id() const = 0;
    virtual StringView message_name() const = 0;
    virtual ErrorOr<MessageBuffer> encode() const = 0;

protected:
    Message() = default;
};

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/RawAttachment.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibIPC/Message.h>
#include <LibIPC/RawAttachment.h>

namespace IPC {

Vector<Attachment> adopt_raw_attachments(ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> raw_attachments)
{
    Vector<Attachment> attachments;
    for (auto const& raw : raw_attachments) {
#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
        auto disposition = static_cast<Core::MachPort::MessageRight>(raw.disposition);
        auto right = Core::MachPort::PortRight::Send;
        if (disposition == Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveReceive || disposition == Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSend || disposition == Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSendOnce)
            right = Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive;
        else if (disposition == Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveSendOnce)
            right = Core::MachPort::PortRight::SendOnce;
        attachments.append(Attachment::from_mach_port(Core::MachPort::adopt_right(static_cast<mach_port_t>(raw.value), right), disposition));
#else
        attachments.append(Attachment::from_fd(raw.value));
#endif
    }
    return attachments;
}

Vector<RawAttachment> release_raw_attachments(Vector<Attachment> attachments)
{
    Vector<RawAttachment> raw;
    for (auto& attachment : attachments) {
#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
        auto disposition = to_underlying(attachment.message_right());
        raw.append({ static_cast<int>(attachment.release_mach_port().release()), disposition });
#else
        raw.append({ attachment.to_fd(), 0 });
#endif
    }
    return raw;
}

MessageBuffer adopt_encoded_message(ReadonlyBytes bytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> attachments)
{
    MessageDataType data;
    MUST(data.try_append(bytes.data(), bytes.size()));
    return { move(data), adopt_raw_attachments(attachments) };
}

}

    int value;
    u32 disposition;

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/RawMessage.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/ByteReader.h>
#include <LibIPC/RawMessage.h>

namespace IPC {

Optional<RawMessage::Header> RawMessage::read_header(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    if (bytes.size() < sizeof(u32) + sizeof(i32))
        return {};
    Header header;
    AK::ByteReader::load(bytes.data(), header.endpoint_magic);
    AK::ByteReader::load(bytes.data() + sizeof(u32), header.message_id);
    return header;
}

RawMessage::RawMessage(Header header, StringView message_name, ReceivedMessageBytes bytes, Vector<Attachment> attachments)
    : m_header(header)
    , m_message_name(message_name)
    , m_bytes(move(bytes))
    , m_attachments(move(attachments))
{
}

RawMessage::~RawMessage() = default;

ErrorOr<MessageBuffer> RawMessage::encode() const
{
    return Error::from_string_literal("A message that arrived undecoded cannot be encoded");
}

RawMessage::OutcomeInRust RawMessage::hand_to_rust(Function<void(FfiRawMessage)> const& hand_over)
{
    auto attachments = release_raw_attachments(move(m_attachments));
    OutcomeInRust outcome;
    hand_over({
        .bytes_including_header = m_bytes.bytes(),
        .attachments = attachments,
        .outcome = &outcome,
        .respond = [](void* outcome, ReadonlyBytes bytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> attachments) { static_cast<OutcomeInRust*>(outcome)->response = make<MessageBuffer>(adopt_encoded_message(bytes, attachments)); },
        .did_misbehave = [](void* outcome, ReadonlyBytes what_the_peer_did) { static_cast<OutcomeInRust*>(outcome)->misbehavior = ByteString { what_the_peer_did }; },
    });
    return outcome;
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/RawMessage.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/ByteString.h>
#include <AK/Function.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/OwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibIPC/Attachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/Message.h>
#include <LibIPC/RawAttachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/ReceivedMessageBytes.h>

namespace IPC {

// A message as Rust is handed it, with where what Rust makes of it goes: `libipc_rust::cpp_connection::RawMessage`.
struct FfiRawMessage {
    ReadonlyBytes bytes_including_header;
    ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> attachments;
    void* outcome;
    void (*respond)(void* outcome, ReadonlyBytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment>);
    void (*did_misbehave)(void* outcome, ReadonlyBytes what_the_peer_did);
};
static_assert(sizeof(FfiRawMessage) == 7 * sizeof(void*), "RawMessage of libipc_rust is written to match this by hand");

class RawMessage final : public Message {
public:
    struct Header {
        u32 endpoint_magic { 0 };
        i32 message_id { 0 };
    };
    static Optional<Header> read_header(ReadonlyBytes);

    RawMessage(Header, StringView message_name, ReceivedMessageBytes, Vector<Attachment>);
    virtual ~RawMessage() override;

    virtual u32 endpoint_magic() const override { return m_header.endpoint_magic; }
    virtual int message_id() const override { return m_header.message_id; }
    virtual StringView message_name() const override { return m_message_name; }
    virtual ErrorOr<MessageBuffer> encode() const override;

    struct OutcomeInRust {
        // What the sender did that it must not do, for which its connection is closed.
        Optional<ByteString> misbehavior;
        // The response of a synchronous message.
        OwnPtr<MessageBuffer> response;
    };
    // Rust decodes the message and hands it to a stub of its endpoint, which `hand_over` reaches with what it is given.
    OutcomeInRust hand_to_rust(Function<void(FfiRawMessage)> const& hand_over);

private:
    Header m_header;
    StringView m_message_name;
    ReceivedMessageBytes m_bytes;
    Vector<Attachment> m_attachments;
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/ReceivedMessageBytes.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Aliaksandr Kalenik <kalenik.aliaksandr@gmail.com>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/RefCounted.h>
#include <LibIPC/ReceivedMessageBytes.h>

namespace IPC {

class ReceivedMessageBytes::Impl final : public RefCounted<ReceivedMessageBytes::Impl> {
public:
    explicit Impl(Vector<u8> bytes)
        : m_vector(move(bytes))
        , m_bytes(m_vector)
    {
    }

    Impl(ReadonlyBytes bytes, void* foreign_owner, void (*release_foreign_owner)(void*))
        : m_bytes(bytes)
        , m_foreign_owner(foreign_owner)
        , m_release_foreign_owner(release_foreign_owner)
    {
    }

    ~Impl()
    {
        if (m_release_foreign_owner)
            m_release_foreign_owner(m_foreign_owner);
    }

    ReadonlyBytes bytes() const { return m_bytes; }

private:
    Vector<u8> m_vector;
    ReadonlyBytes m_bytes;
    void* m_foreign_owner { nullptr };
    void (*m_release_foreign_owner)(void*) { nullptr };
};

ReceivedMessageBytes::ReceivedMessageBytes() = default;
ReceivedMessageBytes::ReceivedMessageBytes(ReceivedMessageBytes const&) = default;
ReceivedMessageBytes::ReceivedMessageBytes(ReceivedMessageBytes&&) = default;
ReceivedMessageBytes::~ReceivedMessageBytes() = default;

ReceivedMessageBytes& ReceivedMessageBytes::operator=(ReceivedMessageBytes const&) = default;
ReceivedMessageBytes& ReceivedMessageBytes::operator=(ReceivedMessageBytes&&) = default;

ReceivedMessageBytes::ReceivedMessageBytes(NonnullRefPtr<Impl> impl)
    : m_impl(move(impl))
{
}

ReceivedMessageBytes ReceivedMessageBytes::from_vector(Vector<u8> bytes)
{
    if (bytes.is_empty())
        return {};
    return ReceivedMessageBytes { adopt_ref(*new Impl(move(bytes))) };
}

ReceivedMessageBytes ReceivedMessageBytes::adopt_foreign_storage(ReadonlyBytes bytes, void* owner, void (*release)(void* owner))
{
    if (bytes.is_empty()) {
        release(owner);
        return {};
    }
    return ReceivedMessageBytes { adopt_ref(*new Impl(bytes, owner, release)) };
}

ReadonlyBytes ReceivedMessageBytes::bytes() const
{
    if (!m_impl)
        return {};
    return m_impl->bytes();
}

}

use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");

    // NB: A CMake build of the shared target directory links what it builds into libraries that link AK. Unit tests
    //     link without it.
    println!("cargo::rustc-check-cfg=cfg(ladybird_links_ak)");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=LADYBIRD_LINKS_AK");
    if env::var_os("LADYBIRD_LINKS_AK").is_some() {
        println!("cargo::rustc-cfg=ladybird_links_ak");
    }

    // NB: Only LibIPC's copy of the crate, which C++ calls, has the C++ interface.
    if env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_CPP_TRANSPORT").is_none() || env::var_os("CARGO_CFG_UNIX").is_none() {
        return Ok(());
    }

    let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")?);
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR")?);
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");

    let mut config = cbindgen::Config::from_file(manifest_dir.join("cbindgen.toml"))?;
    // NB: An ak::Span is laid out as an AK ReadonlySpan, which C++ passes it as.
    for (rust_name, cpp_name) in [("Span", "AK::ReadonlySpan"), ("RawAttachment", "IPC::RawAttachment")] {
        config.export.rename.insert(rust_name.to_string(), cpp_name.to_string());
    }

    let mut sources = vec!["src/cpp_transport.rs"];
    // NB: The bootstrap of a helper's transport only exists on macOS.
    if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS")? == "macos" {
        sources.push("src/cpp_mach_bootstrap.rs");
    }
    let mut builder = cbindgen::Builder::new().with_config(config);
    for source in sources {
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={source}");
        builder = builder.with_src(manifest_dir.join(source));
    }
    builder.generate()?.write_to_file(out_dir.join("RustFFI.h"));
    Ok(())
}

/*

//! Derives of `libipc_rust::wire::Encode` and `libipc_rust::wire::Decode`.
//!
//! A struct goes as its fields in declaration order. An enum of unit variants with an integer `repr` goes as the
//! integer of its variant. Any other enum goes as the index of its variant, as a `u8`, then the variant's fields, as an
//! `AK::Variant` goes.
//!
//! Attributes:
//! - `#[ipc(skip = EXPR)]` on a field: the field is not sent, and decodes as `EXPR`.
//! - `#[ipc(max_size = N)]` on a field: the field decodes with `Decoder::decode_with_max_size(N)`.
//! - `#[ipc(validate = PATH)]` on a type: `PATH(&self) -> Result<(), &'static str>` refuses a value before it is
//!   encoded and after it is decoded.

use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use proc_macro2::{Literal, TokenStream as TokenStream2};
use quote::{format_ident, quote};
use syn::{
    Attribute, Data, DataEnum, DeriveInput, Expr, Fields, Generics, Ident, Index, Member, Path, Type, Variant,
    parse_macro_input, parse_quote,
};

#[proc_macro_derive(Encode, attributes(ipc))]
pub fn derive_encode(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    expand_encode(&input)
        .unwrap_or_else(syn::Error::into_compile_error)
        .into()
}

#[proc_macro_derive(Decode, attributes(ipc))]
pub fn derive_decode(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    expand_decode(&input)
        .unwrap_or_else(syn::Error::into_compile_error)
        .into()
}

const INTEGER_REPRS: [&str; 8] = ["u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64"];

struct TypeAttributes {
    validate: Option<Path>,
}

fn type_attributes(attributes: &[Attribute]) -> syn::Result<TypeAttributes> {
    let mut validate = None;
    for attribute in attributes.iter().filter(|attribute| attribute.path().is_ident("ipc")) {
        attribute.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
            if meta.path.is_ident("validate") {
                validate = Some(meta.value()?.parse()?);
                return Ok(());
            }
            Err(meta.error("expected `validate = PATH`"))
        })?;
    }
    Ok(TypeAttributes { validate })
}

enum FieldDecoding {
    Decoded,
    DecodedWithMaxSize(Expr),
    Skipped(Expr),
}

struct FieldInfo {
    member: Member,
    binding: Ident,
    ty: Type,
    decoding: FieldDecoding,
}

impl FieldInfo {
    fn is_sent(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self.decoding, FieldDecoding::Skipped(_))
    }

    fn decode_expression(&self) -> TokenStream2 {
        match &self.decoding {
            FieldDecoding::Decoded => quote!(decoder.decode()?),
            FieldDecoding::DecodedWithMaxSize(max_size) => quote!(decoder.decode_with_max_size(#max_size)?),
            FieldDecoding::Skipped(value) => quote!(#value),
        }
    }
}

fn field_infos(fields: &Fields) -> syn::Result<Vec<FieldInfo>> {
    fields
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(index, field)| {
            let member = match &field.ident {
                Some(ident) => Member::Named(ident.clone()),
                None => Member::Unnamed(Index::from(index)),
            };
            let mut decoding = FieldDecoding::Decoded;
            for attribute in field.attrs.iter().filter(|attribute| attribute.path().is_ident("ipc")) {
                attribute.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
                    if !matches!(decoding, FieldDecoding::Decoded) {
                        return Err(meta.error("a field takes one of `skip` and `max_size`"));
                    }
                    if meta.path.is_ident("skip") {
                        decoding = FieldDecoding::Skipped(meta.value()?.parse()?);
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    if meta.path.is_ident("max_size") {
                        decoding = FieldDecoding::DecodedWithMaxSize(meta.value()?.parse()?);
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    Err(meta.error("expected `skip = EXPR` or `max_size = N`"))
                })?;
            }
            Ok(FieldInfo {
                member,
                binding: format_ident!("field_{}", index),
                ty: field.ty.clone(),
                decoding,
            })
        })
        .collect()
}

fn integer_repr(attributes: &[Attribute]) -> syn::Result<Option<Ident>> {
    let mut repr = None;
    for attribute in attributes.iter().filter(|attribute| attribute.path().is_ident("repr")) {
        attribute.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
            if let Some(ident) = meta.path.get_ident()
                && INTEGER_REPRS.contains(&ident.to_string().as_str())
            {
                repr = Some(ident.clone());
            }
            if meta.input.peek(syn::token::Paren) {
                let _arguments;
                syn::parenthesized!(_arguments in meta.input);
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
    }
    Ok(repr)
}

enum EnumForm {
    Integer(Ident),
    Tagged,
}

fn enum_form(input: &DeriveInput, data: &DataEnum) -> syn::Result<EnumForm> {
    if data.variants.is_empty() {
        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
            &input.ident,
            "an enum without variants cannot be sent",
        ));
    }
    let is_unit_only = data.variants.iter().all(|variant| variant.fields.is_empty());
    if let Some(repr) = integer_repr(&input.attrs)?
        && is_unit_only
    {
        if input.generics.params.iter().next().is_some() {
            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
                &input.generics,
                "an enum going as an integer cannot be generic",
            ));
        }
        return Ok(EnumForm::Integer(repr));
    }
    if let Some(variant) = data.variants.iter().find(|variant| variant.discriminant.is_some()) {
        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
            variant,
            "an enum with discriminants goes as an integer, so it needs unit variants and an integer repr",
        ));
    }
    if data.variants.len() > 256 {
        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(&input.ident, "a variant index goes as a u8"));
    }
    Ok(EnumForm::Tagged)
}

fn generics_bound_by(generics: &Generics, bound: TokenStream2) -> Generics {
    let mut generics = generics.clone();
    for parameter in generics.type_params_mut() {
        parameter.bounds.push(parse_quote!(#bound));
    }
    generics
}

fn variant_tag(index: usize) -> Literal {
    Literal::u8_suffixed(u8::try_from(index).expect("the variant count is checked"))
}

fn struct_pattern(path: TokenStream2, fields: &[FieldInfo]) -> TokenStream2 {
    let sent: Vec<_> = fields.iter().filter(|field| field.is_sent()).collect();
    let members = sent.iter().map(|field| &field.member);
    let bindings = sent.iter().map(|field| &field.binding);
    quote!(#path { #(#members: #bindings,)* .. })
}

fn expand_encode(input: &DeriveInput) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    let name = &input.ident;
    let generics = generics_bound_by(&input.generics, quote!(::libipc_rust::wire::Encode));
    let (impl_generics, type_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
    let attributes = type_attributes(&input.attrs)?;
    let (validate_borrowed, validate_owned) = match &attributes.validate {
        Some(validate) => (
            quote!(#validate(self).map_err(::libipc_rust::wire::EncodeError::InvalidValue)?;),
            quote!(#validate(&self).map_err(::libipc_rust::wire::EncodeError::InvalidValue)?;),
        ),
        None => (quote!(), quote!()),
    };

    let mut encode_uses_encoder = true;
    let (encode_body, encode_owned_body) = match &input.data {
        Data::Struct(data) => {
            let fields = field_infos(&data.fields)?;
            let sent: Vec<_> = fields.iter().filter(|field| field.is_sent()).collect();
            encode_uses_encoder = !sent.is_empty();
            let members = sent.iter().map(|field| &field.member);
            let encode = quote! {
                #validate_borrowed
                #(encoder.encode(&self.#members)?;)*
                ::core::result::Result::Ok(())
            };
            let encode_owned = (!sent.is_empty()).then(|| {
                let pattern = struct_pattern(quote!(Self), &fields);
                let bindings = sent.iter().map(|field| &field.binding);
                quote! {
                    #validate_owned
                    let #pattern = self;
                    #(encoder.encode_owned(#bindings)?;)*
                    ::core::result::Result::Ok(())
                }
            });
            (encode, encode_owned)
        }
        Data::Enum(data) => match enum_form(input, data)? {
            EnumForm::Integer(repr) => {
                let variants = data.variants.iter().map(|variant| &variant.ident);
                let encode = quote! {
                    #validate_borrowed
                    let value: #repr = match self {
                        #(Self::#variants => Self::#variants as #repr,)*
                    };
                    encoder.encode(&value)
                };
                (encode, None)
            }
            EnumForm::Tagged => {
                let variants = data
                    .variants
                    .iter()
                    .map(|variant| Ok((variant, field_infos(&variant.fields)?)))
                    .collect::<syn::Result<Vec<(&Variant, Vec<FieldInfo>)>>>()?;
                let arms = |method: TokenStream2| {
                    variants.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, (variant, fields))| {
                        let ident = &variant.ident;
                        let pattern = struct_pattern(quote!(Self::#ident), fields);
                        let tag = variant_tag(index);
                        let bindings = fields
                            .iter()
                            .filter(|field| field.is_sent())
                            .map(|field| &field.binding);
                        quote! {
                            #pattern => {
                                encoder.encode(&#tag)?;
                                #(encoder.#method(#bindings)?;)*
                            }
                        }
                    })
                };
                let borrowed_arms = arms(quote!(encode));
                let encode = quote! {
                    #validate_borrowed
                    match self {
                        #(#borrowed_arms)*
                    }
                    ::core::result::Result::Ok(())
                };
                let has_sent_fields = variants.iter().any(|(_, fields)| fields.iter().any(FieldInfo::is_sent));
                let encode_owned = has_sent_fields.then(|| {
                    let owned_arms = arms(quote!(encode_owned));
                    quote! {
                        #validate_owned
                        match self {
                            #(#owned_arms)*
                        }
                        ::core::result::Result::Ok(())
                    }
                });
                (encode, encode_owned)
            }
        },
        Data::Union(_) => return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(name, "a union cannot be sent")),
    };

    let encoder_parameter = if encode_uses_encoder {
        quote!(encoder)
    } else {
        quote!(_)
    };
    let encode_owned = encode_owned_body.map(|body| {
        quote! {
            #[inline]
            fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut ::libipc_rust::wire::Encoder) -> ::core::result::Result<(), ::libipc_rust::wire::EncodeError> {
                #body
            }
        }
    });

    Ok(quote! {
        #[automatically_derived]
        impl #impl_generics ::libipc_rust::wire::Encode for #name #type_generics #where_clause {
            #[inline]
            fn encode(&self, #encoder_parameter: &mut ::libipc_rust::wire::Encoder) -> ::core::result::Result<(), ::libipc_rust::wire::EncodeError> {
                #encode_body
            }

            #encode_owned
        }
    })
}

fn expand_decode(input: &DeriveInput) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
    let name = &input.ident;
    let name_string = name.to_string();
    let generics = generics_bound_by(&input.generics, quote!(::libipc_rust::wire::Decode));
    let (impl_generics, type_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
    let attributes = type_attributes(&input.attrs)?;
    let invalid = quote!(::core::result::Result::Err(::libipc_rust::wire::DecodeError::InvalidValue(#name_string)));

    let mut decode_uses_decoder = true;
    let (min_encoded_size, value) = match &input.data {
        Data::Struct(data) => {
            let fields = field_infos(&data.fields)?;
            decode_uses_decoder = fields.iter().any(FieldInfo::is_sent);
            let sizes: Vec<_> = fields
                .iter()
                .filter(|field| field.is_sent())
                .map(|field| {
                    let ty = &field.ty;
                    quote!(<#ty as ::libipc_rust::wire::Decode>::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE)
                })
                .collect();
            let min_encoded_size = if sizes.is_empty() {
                quote!(0)
            } else {
                quote!(#(#sizes)+*)
            };
            let members = fields.iter().map(|field| &field.member);
            let values = fields.iter().map(FieldInfo::decode_expression);
            (min_encoded_size, quote!(Self { #(#members: #values,)* }))
        }
        Data::Enum(data) => match enum_form(input, data)? {
            EnumForm::Integer(repr) => {
                let variants: Vec<_> = data.variants.iter().map(|variant| &variant.ident).collect();
                let discriminants: Vec<_> = (0..variants.len())
                    .map(|index| format_ident!("DISCRIMINANT_{}", index))
                    .collect();
                let value = quote! {{
                    #(const #discriminants: #repr = #name::#variants as #repr;)*
                    match decoder.decode::<#repr>()? {
                        #(#discriminants => Self::#variants,)*
                        _ => return #invalid,
                    }
                }};
                (quote!(::core::mem::size_of::<#repr>()), value)
            }
            EnumForm::Tagged => {
                let arms = data
                    .variants
                    .iter()
                    .enumerate()
                    .map(|(index, variant)| {
                        let ident = &variant.ident;
                        let fields = field_infos(&variant.fields)?;
                        let members = fields.iter().map(|field| &field.member);
                        let values = fields.iter().map(FieldInfo::decode_expression);
                        let tag = Literal::usize_unsuffixed(index);
                        Ok(quote!(#tag => Self::#ident { #(#members: #values,)* },))
                    })
                    .collect::<syn::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                let value = quote! {
                    match decoder.decode::<u8>()? {
                        #(#arms)*
                        _ => return #invalid,
                    }
                };
                (quote!(::core::mem::size_of::<u8>()), value)
            }
        },
        Data::Union(_) => return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(name, "a union cannot be sent")),
    };

    let decoder_parameter = if decode_uses_decoder {
        quote!(decoder)
    } else {
        quote!(_)
    };
    let body = match &attributes.validate {
        Some(validate) => quote! {
            let value = #value;
            #validate(&value).map_err(::libipc_rust::wire::DecodeError::InvalidValue)?;
            ::core::result::Result::Ok(value)
        },
        None => quote!(::core::result::Result::Ok(#value)),
    };

    Ok(quote! {
        #[automatically_derived]
        impl #impl_generics ::libipc_rust::wire::Decode for #name #type_generics #where_clause {
            const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = #min_encoded_size;

            #[inline]
            fn decode(#decoder_parameter: &mut ::libipc_rust::wire::Decoder<'_>) -> ::core::result::Result<Self, ::libipc_rust::wire::DecodeError> {
                #body
            }
        }
    })
}

//! What a message carries besides its bytes: Mach port rights, Unix file descriptors or Windows handles.

#[cfg(unix)]
use std::os::fd::OwnedFd;

#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
use crate::mach::{self, MachPort};

#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Attachment {
    port: MachPort,
    disposition: u32,
}

#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
impl Attachment {
    /// An attachment moving a right in a message, with the disposition the right is moved with.
    pub fn from_mach_port(port: MachPort, disposition: u32) -> Self {
        Self { port, disposition }
    }

    pub fn from_fd(fd: OwnedFd) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self::from_mach_port(
            mach::file_port_from_fd(fd)?,
            mach::MACH_MSG_TYPE_MOVE_SEND,
        ))
    }

    pub fn into_fd(self) -> std::io::Result<OwnedFd> {
        mach::fd_from_file_port(self.port)
    }

    pub fn into_mach_port(self) -> (MachPort, u32) {
        (self.port, self.disposition)
    }
}

#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Attachment {
    fd: OwnedFd,
}

#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
impl Attachment {
    pub fn from_fd(fd: OwnedFd) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self { fd })
    }

    pub fn into_fd(self) -> std::io::Result<OwnedFd> {
        Ok(self.fd)
    }

    pub fn as_fd(&self) -> std::os::fd::BorrowedFd<'_> {
        std::os::fd::AsFd::as_fd(&self.fd)
    }
}

#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
impl From<OwnedFd> for Attachment {
    fn from(fd: OwnedFd) -> Self {
        Self { fd }
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Attachment {
    descriptor: crate::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor,
}

#[cfg(windows)]
impl Attachment {
    pub fn from_descriptor(descriptor: crate::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor) -> Self {
        Self { descriptor }
    }

    pub fn into_descriptor(self) -> crate::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor {
        self.descriptor
    }

    pub(crate) fn into_raw(self) -> i32 {
        self.descriptor.into_raw()
    }
}

//! Messages that Rust encodes and decodes on a connection whose transport C++ owns: what a C++ `IPC::Connection`
//! hands over undecoded, and what it posts for Rust.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use core::ffi::{c_int, c_void};
use core::marker::PhantomData;

use crate::attachment::Attachment;
use crate::wire::{
    Decode, DecodeError, Decoder, DispatchError, EncodeError, EncodedMessage, EndpointMessage, Misbehavior,
    SyncMessage, decode_message_header,
};

/// A Mach port name and its disposition on Apple, and a descriptor elsewhere: `IPC::RawAttachment`.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct RawAttachment {
    value: c_int,
    disposition: u32,
}

impl RawAttachment {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The raw attachment must hand over one owned descriptor or Mach right.
    unsafe fn into_attachment(self) -> Attachment {
        #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
        {
            use crate::mach::{
                MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND, MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND_ONCE, MACH_MSG_TYPE_MOVE_RECEIVE,
                MACH_MSG_TYPE_MOVE_SEND_ONCE, MachPort, PortRight,
            };
            let right = match self.disposition {
                MACH_MSG_TYPE_MOVE_RECEIVE | MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND | MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND_ONCE => {
                    PortRight::Receive
                }
                MACH_MSG_TYPE_MOVE_SEND_ONCE => PortRight::SendOnce,
                _ => PortRight::Send,
            };
            Attachment::from_mach_port(MachPort::adopt(self.value as u32, right), self.disposition)
        }
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
        {
            use std::os::fd::FromRawFd;
            // SAFETY: The caller hands over the descriptor.
            Attachment::from(unsafe { std::os::fd::OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(self.value) })
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            // SAFETY: The caller hands over the descriptor.
            Attachment::from_descriptor(unsafe { crate::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor::from_raw(self.value) })
        }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Each of the raw attachments must hand over its descriptor or Mach right.
    pub unsafe fn take_all(raw: &[Self]) -> Vec<Attachment> {
        raw.iter()
            .map(|attachment| {
                let owned = Self {
                    value: attachment.value,
                    disposition: attachment.disposition,
                };
                // SAFETY: The caller hands over what each raw attachment names.
                unsafe { owned.into_attachment() }
            })
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn from_attachment(attachment: Attachment) -> Self {
        #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
        {
            let (port, disposition) = attachment.into_mach_port();
            Self {
                value: core::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(port).name() as c_int,
                disposition,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
        {
            use std::os::fd::IntoRawFd;
            Self {
                value: attachment
                    .into_fd()
                    .expect("a Unix attachment is a descriptor")
                    .into_raw_fd(),
                disposition: 0,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            Self {
                value: attachment.into_descriptor().into_raw(),
                disposition: 0,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A message that a C++ connection received and hands over undecoded, with where what Rust makes of it goes:
/// `IPC::FfiRawMessage`.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct RawMessage<'a> {
    bytes_including_header: ak::Span<'a, u8>,
    attachments: ak::Span<'a, RawAttachment>,
    outcome: *mut c_void,
    respond: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
    did_misbehave: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>),
}

impl RawMessage<'_> {
    /// Has `dispatch`, the dispatcher of the message's endpoint over a stub, decode the message and hand it to that
    /// stub. The connection gets the response of a synchronous message, or what its peer did that it must not do.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The message must be one `IPC::RawMessage::hand_to_rust()` made, which is handed to a stub once.
    pub unsafe fn hand_to(
        self,
        dispatch: impl FnOnce(&[u8], Vec<Attachment>) -> Result<Option<EncodedMessage>, DispatchError>,
    ) {
        // SAFETY: The C++ message hands over what each of its raw attachments names.
        let attachments = unsafe { RawAttachment::take_all(self.attachments.as_slice()) };
        let did_misbehave = |what_the_peer_did: &str| {
            // SAFETY: The C++ message copies the text.
            unsafe { (self.did_misbehave)(self.outcome, ak::Span::new(what_the_peer_did.as_bytes())) };
        };
        match dispatch(self.bytes_including_header.as_slice(), attachments) {
            Ok(None) => {}
            Ok(Some((bytes, attachments))) => {
                let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> =
                    attachments.into_iter().map(RawAttachment::from_attachment).collect();
                // SAFETY: The C++ message copies the bytes and takes every attachment over.
                unsafe { (self.respond)(self.outcome, ak::Span::new(&bytes), ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments)) };
            }
            Err(DispatchError::Decode(error)) => did_misbehave(&format!("Message does not decode: {error:?}")),
            Err(DispatchError::Misbehavior(Misbehavior(what_the_peer_did))) => did_misbehave(what_the_peer_did),
            Err(DispatchError::EncodeResponse(error)) => panic!("The response to a message does not encode: {error:?}"),
        }
    }
}

/// A value as C++ encoded it for Rust to decode, lent for a call: the bytes of an `IPC::Encoded<T>`.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct EncodedValue<'a>(ak::Span<'a, u8>);

impl EncodedValue<'_> {
    pub fn decode<T: Decode>(&self) -> Result<T, DecodeError> {
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(self.0.as_slice(), []);
        let value = decoder.decode()?;
        if !decoder.is_at_end() {
            return Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("bytes after an encoded value"));
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
}

/// One reference to an `IPC::ThreadSafeMessagePoster`, and how to reach it: `IPC::FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster {
    poster_with_one_reference: *mut c_void,
    try_post: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>) -> bool,
    r#ref: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
    unref: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

/// One reference to an `IPC::ConnectionBase`, and how to make synchronous requests on it: `IPC::FfiConnection`.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FfiConnection {
    connection_with_one_reference: *mut c_void,
    send_sync_request: unsafe extern "C" fn(
        *mut c_void,
        ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>,
        u32,
        i32,
        *mut c_void,
        unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, RawMessage<'_>),
    ) -> bool,
    r#ref: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
    unref: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

const _: () = {
    assert!(size_of::<RawAttachment>() == 8);
    assert!(size_of::<RawMessage<'_>>() == 7 * size_of::<usize>());
    assert!(size_of::<FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster>() == 4 * size_of::<usize>());
    assert!(size_of::<FfiConnection>() == 4 * size_of::<usize>());
};

/// Makes synchronous requests on a C++ connection, on the thread that owns it.
pub struct CppConnection {
    ffi: FfiConnection,
    _used_on_the_thread_that_owns_the_connection: PhantomData<*const ()>,
}

impl CppConnection {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `ffi` must hold one reference to a live `IPC::ConnectionBase` of this thread, which the caller gives up.
    pub unsafe fn adopt(ffi: FfiConnection) -> Self {
        Self {
            ffi,
            _used_on_the_thread_that_owns_the_connection: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    /// Waits for the response without handling any other message meanwhile. None if the request does not encode, or if
    /// the peer could not be reached or answered with what does not decode, after which C++ has shut the connection
    /// down.
    pub fn send_sync<M: SyncMessage>(&self, request: M) -> Option<M::Response> {
        unsafe extern "C" fn take_response<R: EndpointMessage + Decode>(
            response_sink: *mut c_void,
            response: RawMessage<'_>,
        ) {
            // SAFETY: send_sync() passes its sink of the response type, and C++ hands the response over once.
            unsafe {
                let response_sink = &mut *response_sink.cast::<Option<R>>();
                response.hand_to(|bytes, attachments| {
                    let mut decoder = Decoder::new(bytes, attachments);
                    let (magic, id) = decode_message_header(&mut decoder)?;
                    if magic != R::ENDPOINT_MAGIC || id != R::MESSAGE_ID {
                        return Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("response header").into());
                    }
                    *response_sink = Some(decoder.decode()?);
                    Ok(None)
                });
            }
        }

        let Ok((bytes, attachments)) = request.encode_message() else {
            return None;
        };
        let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> = attachments.into_iter().map(RawAttachment::from_attachment).collect();
        let mut response: Option<M::Response> = None;
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the connection, which copies the bytes and takes every attachment over, and
        //         hands the response to take_response() before the call returns.
        let answered = unsafe {
            (self.ffi.send_sync_request)(
                self.ffi.connection_with_one_reference,
                ak::Span::new(&bytes),
                ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments),
                <M::Response as EndpointMessage>::ENDPOINT_MAGIC,
                <M::Response as EndpointMessage>::MESSAGE_ID,
                (&raw mut response).cast(),
                take_response::<M::Response>,
            )
        };
        if answered { response } else { None }
    }
}

impl Clone for CppConnection {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the connection.
        unsafe { (self.ffi.r#ref)(self.ffi.connection_with_one_reference) };
        Self {
            ffi: self.ffi,
            _used_on_the_thread_that_owns_the_connection: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for CppConnection {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This gives up the reference it holds.
        unsafe { (self.ffi.unref)(self.ffi.connection_with_one_reference) };
    }
}

/// Posts messages to the transport of a C++ connection from any thread.
pub struct ThreadSafeMessagePoster(FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster);

// SAFETY: The C++ poster counts its references atomically and posts under its own lock.
unsafe impl Send for ThreadSafeMessagePoster {}
unsafe impl Sync for ThreadSafeMessagePoster {}

impl ThreadSafeMessagePoster {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `ffi` must hold one reference to a live `IPC::ThreadSafeMessagePoster`, which the caller gives up.
    pub unsafe fn adopt(ffi: FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster) -> Self {
        Self(ffi)
    }

    /// Answers whether the peer could still be reached.
    pub fn try_post<M: EndpointMessage>(&self, message: M) -> Result<bool, EncodeError> {
        let (bytes, attachments) = message.encode_message()?;
        Ok(self.try_post_encoded(&bytes, attachments))
    }

    /// The `IPC::ThreadSafeMessagePoster` this holds a reference to, for C++ to post what it encodes through it.
    pub fn as_cpp_poster(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.poster_with_one_reference
    }

    pub fn try_post_encoded(&self, bytes: &[u8], attachments: Vec<Attachment>) -> bool {
        let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> = attachments.into_iter().map(RawAttachment::from_attachment).collect();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the poster, which copies the bytes and takes every attachment over.
        unsafe {
            (self.0.try_post)(
                self.0.poster_with_one_reference,
                ak::Span::new(bytes),
                ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments),
            )
        }
    }
}

impl Clone for ThreadSafeMessagePoster {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the poster.
        unsafe { (self.0.r#ref)(self.0.poster_with_one_reference) };
        Self(self.0)
    }
}

impl Drop for ThreadSafeMessagePoster {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This gives up the reference it holds.
        unsafe { (self.0.unref)(self.0.poster_with_one_reference) };
    }
}

//! The Mach bootstrap as C++ `IPC::MachBootstrapListener`, `IPC::TransportBootstrapMachServer` and
//! `IPC::bootstrap_transport_from_server_port()` reach it.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::mem::ManuallyDrop;

use crate::mach::{self, BootstrapError, BootstrapRequest, MACH_PORT_NULL, MachPort, PortRight};
use crate::mach_bootstrap::{self as bootstrap, MachBootstrapListener, TransportBootstrapServer};
use crate::transport::MachPortPair;

/// What became of a request for the ports of this process's transport.
#[repr(C)]
pub enum BootstrapOutcome {
    Received,
    KernelError,
    ServerClosedBeforeReplying,
    MalformedReply,
}

fn borrowed(name: u32, right: PortRight) -> ManuallyDrop<MachPort> {
    ManuallyDrop::new(MachPort::adopt(name, right))
}

fn release(port: MachPort) -> u32 {
    ManuallyDrop::new(port).name()
}

fn optional_send_once_right(name: u32) -> Option<MachPort> {
    (name != MACH_PORT_NULL).then(|| MachPort::adopt(name, PortRight::SendOnce))
}

/// Asks the server behind a send right that the caller keeps for the ports of this process's transport. A kernel
/// failure leaves its code in `kernel_error`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(
    server_port: u32,
    reply_timeout_in_milliseconds: u32,
    receive_right: &mut u32,
    send_right: &mut u32,
    kernel_error: &mut i32,
) -> BootstrapOutcome {
    let server_port = borrowed(server_port, PortRight::Send);
    match mach::bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(&server_port, reply_timeout_in_milliseconds) {
        Ok((receive, send)) => {
            *receive_right = release(receive);
            *send_right = release(send);
            BootstrapOutcome::Received
        }
        Err(BootstrapError::Kernel { code, .. }) => {
            *kernel_error = code;
            BootstrapOutcome::KernelError
        }
        Err(BootstrapError::ServerClosedBeforeReplying) => BootstrapOutcome::ServerClosedBeforeReplying,
        Err(BootstrapError::MalformedReply) => BootstrapOutcome::MalformedReply,
    }
}

/// Takes bootstrap requests on a port it registers under the name, for as long as the listener lives.
pub struct BootstrapListener(MachBootstrapListener);

struct CppBootstrapRequestHandler {
    context: *mut c_void,
    handle: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, i32, u32, u32),
}

// SAFETY: The C++ handler is made to run on the listener's thread.
unsafe impl Send for CppBootstrapRequestHandler {}

impl CppBootstrapRequestHandler {
    fn handle(&self, request: BootstrapRequest) {
        let reply_port = request.reply_port.map_or(MACH_PORT_NULL, release);
        // SAFETY: The handler takes over both rights, and the caller keeps the context valid while the listener lives.
        unsafe {
            (self.handle)(self.context, request.pid, release(request.task_name_port), reply_port);
        }
    }
}

/// A listener that hands each request to `handle_request` on its thread, with the requester's pid, its task name
/// port and its reply port, which may be null; or null if the port could not be registered.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `context` must stay valid for `handle_request` until the listener is stopped, and the handler must take over both
/// rights.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_listener_create(
    server_port_name: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
    context: *mut c_void,
    handle_request: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, i32, u32, u32),
) -> *mut BootstrapListener {
    let Ok(server_port_name) = core::str::from_utf8(server_port_name.as_slice()) else {
        return core::ptr::null_mut();
    };
    let handler = CppBootstrapRequestHandler {
        context,
        handle: handle_request,
    };
    match MachBootstrapListener::new(server_port_name, move |request| handler.handle(request)) {
        Ok(listener) => Box::into_raw(Box::new(BootstrapListener(listener))),
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("MachBootstrapListener: Unable to register {server_port_name}: {error}");
            core::ptr::null_mut()
        }
    }
}

/// Stops taking requests, and waits until the listener's thread is done.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_listener_stop(listener: &BootstrapListener) {
    listener.0.stop();
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The listener must be one from `ipc_mach_bootstrap_listener_create()` that nothing uses afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_listener_destroy(listener: *mut BootstrapListener) {
    // SAFETY: The caller gives the listener up.
    drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(listener) });
}

/// Holds the ports of the transports of children that have yet to ask for them.
pub struct BootstrapServer(TransportBootstrapServer);

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_create() -> *mut BootstrapServer {
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(BootstrapServer(TransportBootstrapServer::new())))
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The server must be one from `ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_create()` that nothing uses afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_destroy(server: *mut BootstrapServer) {
    // SAFETY: The caller gives the server up.
    drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(server) });
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must hand over a receive right and a send right.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_register_child_transport(
    server: &BootstrapServer,
    pid: i32,
    receive_right: u32,
    send_right: u32,
) {
    server.0.register_child_transport(
        pid,
        MachPortPair {
            receive_right: MachPort::adopt(receive_right, PortRight::Receive),
            send_right: MachPort::adopt(send_right, PortRight::Send),
        },
    );
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_unregister_child_transport(server: &BootstrapServer, pid: i32) {
    server.0.unregister_child_transport(pid);
}

/// Takes the ports held for the child, answering false if none are.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_take_child_transport(
    server: &BootstrapServer,
    pid: i32,
    receive_right: &mut u32,
    send_right: &mut u32,
) -> bool {
    let Some(ports) = server.0.take_child_transport(pid) else {
        return false;
    };
    *receive_right = release(ports.receive_right);
    *send_right = release(ports.send_right);
    true
}

/// Answers a bootstrap request through its reply port, which may be null, with the ports of the requester's
/// transport, and returns the kernel's answer.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must hand over the reply port's send-once right, a receive right and a send right.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_send_transport_ports_to_child(
    reply_port: u32,
    receive_right: u32,
    send_right: u32,
) -> i32 {
    let result = mach::send_transport_ports_to_child(
        optional_send_once_right(reply_port),
        MachPort::adopt(receive_right, PortRight::Receive),
        MachPort::adopt(send_right, PortRight::Send),
    );
    result.err().unwrap_or(mach::KERN_SUCCESS)
}

/// Answers a bootstrap request through its reply port, which may be null, with the ports of a new transport, and
/// returns the kernel's answer and, on success, this end of the transport.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must hand over the reply port's send-once right.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_mach_bootstrap_create_on_demand_local_transport(
    reply_port: u32,
    receive_right: &mut u32,
    send_right: &mut u32,
) -> i32 {
    match bootstrap::create_on_demand_local_transport(optional_send_once_right(reply_port)) {
        Ok(ports) => {
            *receive_right = release(ports.receive_right);
            *send_right = release(ports.send_right);
            mach::KERN_SUCCESS
        }
        Err(error) => error,
    }
}

/*

//! The transports as C++ `IPC::Transport` reaches them: the Mach port one on Darwin, and the socket one on other Unix.
//!
//! Only LibIPC's copy of the crate is built with this, so the other libraries that bundle the crate don't export it.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use core::ffi::{c_int, c_void};
use std::os::fd::{FromRawFd, OwnedFd};

use crate::cpp_connection::RawAttachment;
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
use crate::mach::{MachPort, PortRight};
use crate::receive_queue::PayloadBytes;
#[cfg(not(target_vendor = "apple"))]
use crate::transport::SocketHandle;
use crate::transport::{IncomingMessageObserver, MonotonicDeadline, OutgoingPayload, OwnedPayload, Transport};

/// A transport, which C++ owns from its creation to `ipc_transport_destroy()`.
pub struct RustTransport(Transport);

/// The bytes of a received message, which C++ owns until `ipc_received_payload_destroy()`.
pub struct ReceivedPayload(PayloadBytes);

fn into_cpp_transport(transport: std::io::Result<Transport>) -> *mut RustTransport {
    match transport {
        Ok(transport) => Box::into_raw(Box::new(RustTransport(transport))),
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("Transport: Unable to start: {error}");
            core::ptr::null_mut()
        }
    }
}

/// Raises the number of messages a receive right queues, before a transport takes it.
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_mach_raise_receive_queue_limit(receive_right: u32) {
    // NB: The name only borrows the caller's right.
    let receive_right = core::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(MachPort::adopt(receive_right, PortRight::Receive));
    receive_right.raise_queue_limit();
}

/// A transport that takes over both rights and the write end of the read-notification pipe, or null if it could not
/// start, having released them.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must hand over a receive right, a send right (which may be a dead name), and an open descriptor.
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_create_from_mach_ports(
    receive_right: u32,
    send_right: u32,
    read_notification_pipe: c_int,
) -> *mut RustTransport {
    let receive_right = MachPort::adopt(receive_right, PortRight::Receive);
    let send_right = MachPort::adopt(send_right, PortRight::Send);
    // SAFETY: The caller hands over the descriptor.
    let read_notification_pipe = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(read_notification_pipe) };
    into_cpp_transport(Transport::with_read_notification_pipe(
        receive_right,
        send_right,
        Some(read_notification_pipe),
    ))
}

/// A transport that takes over the socket, what its last owner read off it without seeing the end of a message, and
/// the write end of the read-notification pipe, or null if it could not start, having released them.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must hand over two descriptors, each open or negative, and what each raw attachment names.
#[cfg(not(target_vendor = "apple"))]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_create_from_socket(
    socket: c_int,
    read_notification_pipe: c_int,
    unprocessed_bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
    unprocessed_attachments: ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>,
) -> *mut RustTransport {
    // SAFETY: The caller hands over what the raw attachments name.
    let unprocessed_attachments = unsafe { RawAttachment::take_all(unprocessed_attachments.as_slice()) };
    // SAFETY: The caller hands over each descriptor that is valid.
    let adopt = |fd: c_int| (fd >= 0).then(|| unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) });
    let (Some(socket), Some(read_notification_pipe)) = (adopt(socket), adopt(read_notification_pipe)) else {
        return core::ptr::null_mut();
    };
    let handle = SocketHandle {
        socket,
        unprocessed_bytes: unprocessed_bytes.as_slice().to_vec(),
        unprocessed_attachments,
    };
    into_cpp_transport(Transport::with_read_notification_pipe(
        handle,
        Some(read_notification_pipe),
    ))
}

/// Stops the transport's IO, and waits until the IO thread no longer runs its observer.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The transport must be one that C++ owns, which nothing uses afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_destroy(transport: *mut RustTransport) {
    // SAFETY: The caller gives the transport up.
    drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(transport) });
}

/// The buffer C++ encoded a message into, once it hands it over for the message to wait in: where the bytes are, and
/// how to release them.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct HandedOverPayload {
    data: *const u8,
    size: usize,
    owner: *mut c_void,
    release: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

struct CppPayload(HandedOverPayload);

// SAFETY: The C++ buffer is plain memory, which any thread may read and release.
unsafe impl Send for CppPayload {}

impl AsRef<[u8]> for CppPayload {
    fn as_ref(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: The owner keeps size bytes at data until it is released, which only dropping this does.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.0.data, self.0.size) }
    }
}

impl Drop for CppPayload {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owns the payload, which nothing reads afterwards.
        unsafe { (self.0.release)(self.0.owner) };
    }
}

/// Sends a message, or queues it behind earlier ones that wait for the peer to make room, taking whatever the
/// attachments name. The bytes are lent; only a message that has to wait behind others asks `hand_over_payload` for
/// them. Answers false for a transport that has stopped sending.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Each raw attachment must hand over one right, and `hand_over_payload`, called at most once, must hand over the
/// lent bytes with `payload_owner`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_post(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
    attachments: ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>,
    payload_owner: *mut c_void,
    hand_over_payload: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> HandedOverPayload,
) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The caller hands over what each raw attachment names.
    let attachments = unsafe { RawAttachment::take_all(attachments.as_slice()) };
    let mut hand_over = || -> OwnedPayload {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands the bytes over, once.
        Box::new(CppPayload(unsafe { hand_over_payload(payload_owner) }))
    };
    let payload = OutgoingPayload::Lent {
        bytes: bytes.as_slice(),
        hand_over: &mut hand_over,
    };
    transport
        .0
        .post_message_with_any_number_of_attachments(payload, attachments)
        .is_ok()
}

/// Hands each message that has arrived to `on_message`, and answers whether the peer was gone as they were taken. The
/// callback owns the payload and every right the attachments name, and may call back into the transport.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `on_message` must take over the payload and each raw attachment's right.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_take_incoming(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    context: *mut c_void,
    on_message: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>, *mut ReceivedPayload, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
) -> bool {
    let (messages, peer_eof) = transport.0.take_incoming();
    for message in messages {
        let (bytes, attachments) = message.into_parts();
        let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> = attachments.into_iter().map(RawAttachment::from_attachment).collect();
        let payload = Box::into_raw(Box::new(ReceivedPayload(bytes)));
        // SAFETY: The payload lives on the heap until the callback destroys it, so the bytes stay where they are.
        let payload_bytes: &[u8] = unsafe { (*payload).0.as_ref() };
        // SAFETY: The callback takes over the payload and the rights.
        unsafe {
            on_message(
                context,
                ak::Span::new(payload_bytes),
                payload,
                ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments),
            );
        }
    }
    peer_eof
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The payload must be one that `ipc_transport_take_incoming()` handed over, which nothing uses afterwards.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_received_payload_destroy(payload: *mut ReceivedPayload) {
    // SAFETY: The caller gives the payload up.
    drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(payload) });
}

/// Waits until there is a message to take, the peer is gone, or the wait is interrupted, and no longer than the
/// deadline if there is one, in nanoseconds of the clock of AK's `MonotonicTime`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_wait_until_readable(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    has_deadline: bool,
    deadline_in_monotonic_nanoseconds: i64,
) {
    transport.0.wait_until_readable(
        has_deadline.then(|| MonotonicDeadline::from_nanoseconds(deadline_in_monotonic_nanoseconds)),
    );
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_interrupt_wait_until_readable(transport: &RustTransport) {
    transport.0.interrupt_wait_until_readable();
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_flush(transport: &RustTransport) {
    transport.0.flush();
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_wait_until_incoming_is_current(transport: &RustTransport) {
    transport.0.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_is_open(transport: &RustTransport) -> bool {
    transport.0.is_open()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_close(transport: &RustTransport) {
    transport.0.close();
}

pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_close_after_sending_all_pending_messages(transport: &RustTransport) {

}

    transport.0.acknowledge_read_notification();

    transport.0.schedule_read_notification_if_readable();

/// Hands both rights over for another transport to take this end's place, answering false if they are gone already.
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn ipc_transport_release_mach_ports_for_transfer(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    receive_right: &mut u32,
    send_right: &mut u32,
) -> bool {
    let Ok(pair) = transport.0.release_for_transfer() else {
        return false;
    };
    *receive_right = core::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(pair.receive_right).name();
    *send_right = core::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(pair.send_right).name();
    true
}

/// Hands the socket over for another transport to take this end's place, along with what was read of a message that
/// has yet to arrive whole, which `on_released` takes over. Answers false if the socket is gone already.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `on_released` must take over the socket and what each raw attachment names.
#[cfg(not(target_vendor = "apple"))]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_release_socket_for_transfer(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    context: *mut c_void,
    on_released: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, c_int, ak::Span<'_, u8>, ak::Span<'_, RawAttachment>),
) -> bool {
    use std::os::fd::IntoRawFd;

    let Ok(handle) = transport.0.release_for_transfer() else {
        return false;
    };
    let raw_attachments: Vec<RawAttachment> = handle
        .unprocessed_attachments
        .into_iter()
        .map(RawAttachment::from_attachment)
        .collect();
    // SAFETY: The callback takes over the socket and what the raw attachments name.
    unsafe {
        on_released(
            context,
            handle.socket.into_raw_fd(),
            ak::Span::new(&handle.unprocessed_bytes),
            ak::Span::new(&raw_attachments),
        );
    }
    true
}

/// A C++ observer, which the transport owns once it is set: what it calls, and how to release it.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CppIncomingMessageObserver {
    context: *mut c_void,
    observe: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>),
    release: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
}

// SAFETY: The C++ observer is made to run on the IO thread, and to be released on any thread.
unsafe impl Send for CppIncomingMessageObserver {}

impl CppIncomingMessageObserver {
    fn observe(&self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        // SAFETY: The context lives until this releases it.
        unsafe { (self.observe)(self.context, ak::Span::new(bytes)) };
    }
}

impl Drop for CppIncomingMessageObserver {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owns the context, which nothing calls afterwards.
        unsafe { (self.release)(self.context) };
    }
}

/// Sets what the IO thread shows every message that arrives, and empty bytes once the peer is gone, or clears it
/// with a null `observer`. The transport owns the observer from here on, and releases the one it replaces once that
/// is no longer running, which this call does, so that concurrent calls can't release one that is still set.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// A non-null `observer` must point to one that hands its context over to the transport.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn ipc_transport_set_incoming_message_observer(
    transport: &RustTransport,
    observer: Option<&CppIncomingMessageObserver>,
) {
    let observer = observer.map(|observer| {
        let observer = CppIncomingMessageObserver {
            context: observer.context,
            observe: observer.observe,
            release: observer.release,
        };
        Box::new(move |bytes: &[u8]| observer.observe(bytes)) as IncomingMessageObserver
    });
    drop(transport.0.set_incoming_message_observer(observer));
}

/// The most attachments a message may carry, as `IPC::MAX_MESSAGE_FD_COUNT`.
pub const MAX_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT: usize = 16000;

/// The largest payload a socket frame or Mach descriptor can represent.
pub const MAX_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SIZE: usize = u32::MAX as usize;

fn validate_message_size(payload_size: usize, attachment_count: usize) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if payload_size > MAX_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SIZE || attachment_count > MAX_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT {
        return Err(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput.into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
pub mod mach;
#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
pub mod mach_bootstrap;

pub use attachment::Attachment;
pub use wire::{
    Decode, DecodeError, Decoder, DispatchError, Encode, EncodeError, EncodedMessage, Encoder, EndpointMessage,
    Misbehavior,
};

#[cfg(all(test, unix))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use transport::Transport;

    #[test]
    fn outgoing_message_size_limits() {
        validate_message_size(MAX_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SIZE, MAX_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT).unwrap();
        for (payload_size, attachment_count) in
            [(MAX_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SIZE + 1, 0), (0, MAX_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT + 1)]
        {
            assert_eq!(
                validate_message_size(payload_size, attachment_count)
                    .unwrap_err()
                    .kind(),
                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn refusing_too_many_attachments_keeps_the_connection_open() {
        // NB: On sockets, every attachment holds a descriptor until the message is sent.
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
        socket::raise_descriptor_limit();
        let (a, handle) = Transport::create_paired().unwrap();
        let b = Transport::from_handle(handle).unwrap();
        let (mut reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let attachments = (0..=MAX_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT)
            .map(|_| Attachment::from_fd(writer.try_clone().unwrap().into()).unwrap())
            .collect();
        drop(writer);
        assert_eq!(
            a.post_message(vec![1], attachments).unwrap_err().kind(),
            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput
        );
        assert_eq!(std::io::Read::read(&mut reader, &mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
        assert!(a.is_open());
        assert!(b.is_open());
        a.post_message(vec![2], vec![]).unwrap();
        b.post_message(vec![3], vec![]).unwrap();
        a.flush();
        b.flush();
        assert_eq!(a.receive().unwrap().bytes(), [3]);
        assert_eq!(b.receive().unwrap().bytes(), [2]);
    }
}
