//! How the IO thread of the socket transports waits for any of their sockets: epoll on Linux, which hands back only
//! the sockets that are ready, and poll() over every socket elsewhere.
//!
//! A socket is registered with a token, which comes back with its events, and which the IO thread never gives to
//! another socket, so that an event left over from a transport whose IO has ended finds nothing.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use std::io;
use std::os::fd::RawFd;
use std::time::Duration;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Event {
    pub(crate) token: u64,
    // NB: Also set once the peer has hung up or the socket has an error, which a read reports.
    pub(crate) readable: bool,
    pub(crate) writable: bool,
    pub(crate) hung_up: bool,
}

fn timeout_in_milliseconds(timeout: Option<Duration>) -> libc::c_int {
    match timeout {
        None => -1,
        Some(timeout) => libc::c_int::try_from(timeout.as_micros().div_ceil(1000)).unwrap_or(libc::c_int::MAX),
    }
}

#[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]
pub(crate) use epoll::Poller;
#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android")))]
pub(crate) use poll::Poller;

#[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]
mod epoll {
    use super::*;
    use std::fs::File;
    use std::io::{Read, Write};
    use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd, OwnedFd};

    const WAKEUP_TOKEN: u64 = u64::MAX;
    const MAX_EVENTS_PER_WAIT: usize = 64;

    pub(crate) struct Poller {
        epoll: OwnedFd,
        wakeup: File,
    }

    fn owned(fd: libc::c_int) -> io::Result<OwnedFd> {
        if fd < 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        // NB: The descriptor is new, and nothing else owns it.
        Ok(unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) })
    }

    impl Poller {
        pub(crate) fn new() -> io::Result<Self> {
            // NB: Both calls only create descriptors.
            let epoll = owned(unsafe { libc::epoll_create1(libc::EPOLL_CLOEXEC) })?;
            let wakeup = owned(unsafe { libc::eventfd(0, libc::EFD_CLOEXEC | libc::EFD_NONBLOCK) })?;
            let poller = Self {
                epoll,
                wakeup: wakeup.into(),
            };
            poller.control(
                libc::EPOLL_CTL_ADD,
                poller.wakeup.as_raw_fd(),
                libc::EPOLLIN as u32,
                WAKEUP_TOKEN,
            )?;
            Ok(poller)
        }

        fn control(&self, operation: libc::c_int, fd: RawFd, events: u32, token: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
            let mut event = libc::epoll_event { events, u64: token };
            // NB: The event is a local that the call reads.
            if unsafe { libc::epoll_ctl(self.epoll.as_raw_fd(), operation, fd, &raw mut event) } < 0 {
                return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
            }
            Ok(())
        }

        fn interest(writable: bool) -> u32 {
            let mut events = libc::EPOLLIN | libc::EPOLLRDHUP;
            if writable {
                events |= libc::EPOLLOUT;
            }
            events as u32
        }

        pub(crate) fn add(&self, fd: RawFd, token: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.control(libc::EPOLL_CTL_ADD, fd, Self::interest(false), token)
        }

        pub(crate) fn set_writable_interest(&self, fd: RawFd, token: u64, writable: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.control(libc::EPOLL_CTL_MOD, fd, Self::interest(writable), token)
        }

        pub(crate) fn remove(&self, fd: RawFd) -> io::Result<()> {
            // NB: EPOLL_CTL_DEL ignores the event.
            if unsafe { libc::epoll_ctl(self.epoll.as_raw_fd(), libc::EPOLL_CTL_DEL, fd, std::ptr::null_mut()) } < 0 {
                return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
            }
            Ok(())
        }

        pub(crate) fn wake(&self) {
            // NB: A counter at its maximum already has the IO thread on its way.
            let _ = (&self.wakeup).write_all(&1u64.to_ne_bytes());
        }

        /// Waits no longer than the timeout, if there is one, for the registered sockets, and answers whether anything
        /// happened, a wakeup included.
        pub(crate) fn wait(&self, events: &mut Vec<Event>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<bool> {
            events.clear();
            let mut ready = [libc::epoll_event { events: 0, u64: 0 }; MAX_EVENTS_PER_WAIT];
            // NB: The call writes at most as many events as the buffer has room for.
            let count = unsafe {
                libc::epoll_wait(
                    self.epoll.as_raw_fd(),
                    ready.as_mut_ptr(),
                    ready.len() as libc::c_int,
                    timeout_in_milliseconds(timeout),
                )
            };
            if count < 0 {
                let error = io::Error::last_os_error();
                if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {
                    return Ok(true);
                }
                return Err(error);
            }
            for event in &ready[..count as usize] {
                // NB: The struct is packed on some targets, so its fields are copied out rather than borrowed.
                let (flags, token) = (event.events as libc::c_int, event.u64);
                if token == WAKEUP_TOKEN {
                    // NB: Reading resets the counter.
                    let _ = (&self.wakeup).read(&mut [0; size_of::<u64>()]);
                    continue;
                }
                let hung_up = flags & (libc::EPOLLHUP | libc::EPOLLERR) != 0;
                events.push(Event {
                    token,
                    readable: hung_up || flags & (libc::EPOLLIN | libc::EPOLLRDHUP) != 0,
                    writable: flags & libc::EPOLLOUT != 0,
                    hung_up,
                });
            }
            Ok(count > 0)
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android")))]
mod poll {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::{PipeReader, PipeWriter, Read, Write};
    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    use crate::transport::{is_shared_io_thread, lock};

    struct Registration {
        fd: RawFd,
        token: u64,
        writable: bool,
    }

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct WaitBuffers {
        pollfds: Vec<libc::pollfd>,
        tokens: Vec<u64>,
    }

    pub(crate) struct Poller {
        registrations: Mutex<Vec<Registration>>,
        wakeup_read: PipeReader,
        wakeup_write: PipeWriter,
        // NB: Only the IO thread waits, so this lock is never contended.
        wait_buffers: Mutex<WaitBuffers>,
    }

    fn set_nonblocking(fd: RawFd) -> io::Result<()> {
        // NB: fcntl() only changes the flags of a descriptor that the caller owns.
        unsafe {
            let flags = libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFL);
            if flags < 0 || libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETFL, flags | libc::O_NONBLOCK) < 0 {
                return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    impl Poller {
        pub(crate) fn new() -> io::Result<Self> {
            let (wakeup_read, wakeup_write) = io::pipe()?;
            set_nonblocking(wakeup_read.as_raw_fd())?;
            set_nonblocking(wakeup_write.as_raw_fd())?;
            Ok(Self {
                registrations: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
                wakeup_read,
                wakeup_write,
                wait_buffers: Mutex::new(WaitBuffers::default()),
            })
        }

        // NB: A change takes effect at the IO thread's next wait, which another thread wakes it for.
        fn wake_unless_on_io_thread(&self) {
            if !is_shared_io_thread() {
                self.wake();
            }
        }

        pub(crate) fn add(&self, fd: RawFd, token: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
            lock(&self.registrations).push(Registration {
                fd,
                token,
                writable: false,
            });
            self.wake_unless_on_io_thread();
            Ok(())
        }

        pub(crate) fn set_writable_interest(&self, fd: RawFd, token: u64, writable: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
            let mut registrations = lock(&self.registrations);
            let registration = registrations
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|registration| registration.fd == fd && registration.token == token)
                .ok_or(io::ErrorKind::NotFound)?;
            registration.writable = writable;
            drop(registrations);
            self.wake_unless_on_io_thread();
            Ok(())
        }

        pub(crate) fn remove(&self, fd: RawFd) -> io::Result<()> {
            lock(&self.registrations).retain(|registration| registration.fd != fd);
            Ok(())
        }

        pub(crate) fn wake(&self) {
            // NB: A full pipe already has the IO thread on its way.
            let _ = (&self.wakeup_write).write_all(&[0]);
        }

        /// Waits no longer than the timeout, if there is one, for the registered sockets, and answers whether anything
        /// happened, a wakeup included.
        pub(crate) fn wait(&self, events: &mut Vec<Event>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<bool> {
            events.clear();
            let mut buffers = lock(&self.wait_buffers);
            let WaitBuffers { pollfds, tokens } = &mut *buffers;
            pollfds.clear();
            tokens.clear();
            pollfds.push(libc::pollfd {
                fd: self.wakeup_read.as_raw_fd(),
                events: libc::POLLIN,
                revents: 0,
            });
            for registration in lock(&self.registrations).iter() {
                let mut interest = libc::POLLIN;
                if registration.writable {
                    interest |= libc::POLLOUT;
                }
                pollfds.push(libc::pollfd {
                    fd: registration.fd,
                    events: interest,
                    revents: 0,
                });
                tokens.push(registration.token);
            }
            // NB: The call writes the results into the array, which has as many entries as it is told.
            let count = unsafe {
                libc::poll(
                    pollfds.as_mut_ptr(),
                    pollfds.len() as libc::nfds_t,
                    timeout_in_milliseconds(timeout),
                )
            };
            if count < 0 {
                let error = io::Error::last_os_error();
                if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {
                    return Ok(true);
                }
                return Err(error);
            }
            if pollfds[0].revents != 0 {
                let _ = (&self.wakeup_read).read(&mut [0; 64]);
            }
            for (pollfd, &token) in pollfds[1..].iter().zip(tokens.iter()) {
                if pollfd.revents == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let hung_up = pollfd.revents & (libc::POLLHUP | libc::POLLERR | libc::POLLNVAL) != 0;
                events.push(Event {
                    token,
                    readable: hung_up || pollfd.revents & libc::POLLIN != 0,
                    writable: pollfd.revents & libc::POLLOUT != 0,
                    hung_up,
                });
            }
            Ok(count > 0)
        }
    }
}

use crate::attachment::Attachment;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub(crate) type PayloadBytes = Vec<u8>;

/// The bytes of a received message: copied out of what carried them, or mapped where they arrived.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub enum PayloadBytes {
    Inline(Vec<u8>),
    #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
    OutOfLine(crate::mach::VmRegion),
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    Mapped(crate::shared_memory::MappedPayload),
}

#[cfg(unix)]
impl AsRef<[u8]> for PayloadBytes {
    fn as_ref(&self) -> &[u8] {
        self.bytes()
    }
}

#[cfg(unix)]
impl PayloadBytes {
    pub fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match self {
            Self::Inline(bytes) => bytes,
            #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
            Self::OutOfLine(region) => region.bytes(),
            #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
            Self::Mapped(mapping) => mapping.as_ref(),
        }
    }
}

/// A message the peer sent: its bytes and its attachments.
pub struct ReceivedMessage {
    pub(crate) bytes: PayloadBytes,
    pub attachments: Vec<Attachment>,
}

impl ReceivedMessage {
    pub fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        self.bytes.as_ref()
    }

    pub fn into_parts(self) -> (PayloadBytes, Vec<Attachment>) {
        (self.bytes, self.attachments)
    }
}

//! The anonymous files that carry the payloads of socket messages too large for a frame.
//!
//! On Linux the sender seals the file once it has written the payload, and the receiver maps it rather than copying it:
//! a sealed file can't change, shrink or grow, so the mapping holds what the sender wrote, and reading it can't fault.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use std::io;
use std::os::fd::{FromRawFd, OwnedFd};

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub(crate) fn create_anonymous_file() -> io::Result<OwnedFd> {
    // NB: memfd_create() reads a NUL-terminated name and returns a new descriptor.
    let fd = unsafe { libc::memfd_create(c"".as_ptr(), libc::MFD_CLOEXEC | libc::MFD_ALLOW_SEALING) };
    if fd < 0 {
        return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
    }
    // NB: The descriptor is new, and nothing else owns it.
    Ok(unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) })
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
const SEALS_OF_A_PAYLOAD: libc::c_int = libc::F_SEAL_WRITE | libc::F_SEAL_SHRINK | libc::F_SEAL_GROW;

/// Keeps anything from changing the file from now on, so that a receiver may map it.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub(crate) fn seal(file: &std::fs::File) -> io::Result<()> {
    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
    // NB: F_ADD_SEALS only changes the seals of the owned file.
    if unsafe {
        libc::fcntl(
            file.as_raw_fd(),
            libc::F_ADD_SEALS,
            SEALS_OF_A_PAYLOAD | libc::F_SEAL_SEAL,
        )
    } < 0
    {
        return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// A read-only mapping of the start of a sealed file, which the mapping keeps alive.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub struct MappedPayload {
    address: std::ptr::NonNull<u8>,
    size: usize,
}

// SAFETY: The mapping is read-only, and the file under it can't change.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
unsafe impl Send for MappedPayload {}
// SAFETY: As above.
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
unsafe impl Sync for MappedPayload {}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
impl MappedPayload {
    /// Maps the first `size` bytes of a file that its sender sealed, and refuses one that is unsealed or too small.
    pub(crate) fn map(file: OwnedFd, size: usize) -> io::Result<Self> {
        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
        if size == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "empty payload file"));
        }
        // NB: F_GET_SEALS only reads the seals of the owned file.
        let seals = unsafe { libc::fcntl(file.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_GET_SEALS) };
        if seals < 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        if seals & SEALS_OF_A_PAYLOAD != SEALS_OF_A_PAYLOAD {
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "unsealed payload file"));
        }
        // NB: fstat() rather than the standard library's metadata(), which tries statx() first, and the sandboxes of
        //     the helper processes allow only the former.
        let mut status: libc::stat = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        // NB: The call writes the status of the owned file to the local.
        if unsafe { libc::fstat(file.as_raw_fd(), &raw mut status) } < 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        // NB: The mapping would keep the rest of a longer file alive for as long as the message waits.
        if status.st_size as u64 != size as u64 {
            return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData));
        }
        // NB: A file of larger pages than the system's, as one in hugetlbfs, is mapped in those pages, and the size of
        //     the payload would not unmap them.
        // NB: sysconf() only reads a system value.
        if status.st_blksize as libc::c_long != unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) } {
            return Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                "payload file of unusual pages",
            ));
        }
        // NB: Reading a hole through the mapping has to allocate a page, and fails with SIGBUS if it can't. The sender
        //     writes the whole payload, so a file with holes is refused.
        // NB: lseek() only reads where the owned file's first hole is.
        let first_hole = unsafe { libc::lseek(file.as_raw_fd(), 0, libc::SEEK_HOLE) };
        if first_hole < 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        if (first_hole as u64) < size as u64 {
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "payload file with holes"));
        }
        // NB: The call maps the owned file read-only, and the mapping keeps the file once the descriptor is closed.
        let address = unsafe {
            libc::mmap(
                std::ptr::null_mut(),
                size,
                libc::PROT_READ,
                libc::MAP_SHARED,
                file.as_raw_fd(),
                0,
            )
        };
        if address == libc::MAP_FAILED {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        Ok(Self {
            address: std::ptr::NonNull::new(address.cast()).expect("a successful mmap() is not null"),
            size,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
impl AsRef<[u8]> for MappedPayload {
    fn as_ref(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: The mapping has size readable bytes until this is dropped, and its file can't change or shrink.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.address.as_ptr(), self.size) }
    }
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
impl Drop for MappedPayload {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // NB: This owns the mapping, which nothing reads afterwards.
        unsafe { libc::munmap(self.address.as_ptr().cast(), self.size) };
    }
}

#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
pub(crate) fn create_anonymous_file() -> io::Result<OwnedFd> {
    use std::hash::{BuildHasher, RandomState};
    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;

    // NB: Create the shared memory object under an unpredictable, single-use name, and unlink it immediately, so only the
    //     returned descriptor keeps it alive. O_EXCL makes the open fail if the name already exists, so try another one.
    for attempt in 0u32..16 {
        let random = RandomState::new().hash_one((std::process::id(), std::time::Instant::now(), attempt));
        let name = std::ffi::CString::new(format!("/shm-{random:016x}"))
            .map_err(|_| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput))?;
        // NB: shm_open() reads a NUL-terminated name and returns a new descriptor.
        let fd = unsafe { libc::shm_open(name.as_ptr(), libc::O_RDWR | libc::O_CREAT | libc::O_EXCL, 0o600) };
        if fd < 0 {
            let error = io::Error::last_os_error();
            if error.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::EEXIST) {
                continue;
            }
            return Err(error);
        }
        // NB: The descriptor is new, and nothing else owns it.
        let fd = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) };
        // NB: shm_unlink() reads a NUL-terminated name. fcntl() only changes the descriptor's flags.
        if unsafe { libc::shm_unlink(name.as_ptr()) } != 0
            || unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_SETFD, libc::FD_CLOEXEC) } != 0
        {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        return Ok(fd);
    }
    Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists))
}

/// A payload file as a peer that does not seal it would send it.
#[cfg(all(test, target_os = "linux"))]
pub(crate) fn create_unsealed_file_holding(bytes: &[u8]) -> std::fs::File {
    use std::io::Write;
    let mut file = std::fs::File::from(create_anonymous_file().unwrap());
    file.write_all(bytes).unwrap();
    file
}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/Rust/src/socket.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Sending and receiving bytes with file descriptors over a Unix domain socket.
//!
//! This is the crate's other island of unsafe code: `sendmsg()` and `recvmsg()` with `SCM_RIGHTS` control messages, and
//! the socket options the transport sets. None of these calls blocks, whatever mode the socket is in, as the IO thread
//! that makes them serves every transport of the process.

#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use crate::receive_queue::PayloadBytes;
use crate::shared_memory::create_anonymous_file;

use std::io;
use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, BorrowedFd, FromRawFd, OwnedFd, RawFd};

/// The most descriptors one `sendmsg()` carries, as `Core::LocalSocket::MAX_TRANSFER_FDS`.
pub const MAX_TRANSFER_FDS: usize = 128;

fn control_buffer_size(fd_count: usize) -> usize {
    // NB: CMSG_SPACE() only computes a size.
    unsafe { libc::CMSG_SPACE((fd_count * size_of::<RawFd>()) as u32) as usize }
}

// NB: Room for the control message of MAX_TRANSFER_FDS descriptors, which a test checks.
const SEND_CONTROL_BUFFER_WORDS: usize = 80;

/// Sends some of the bytes, with all of the descriptors, which go with the first byte, without waiting for room. Returns
/// how many bytes went.
pub fn send_with_fds(socket: RawFd, bytes: &[io::IoSlice<'_>], fds: &[BorrowedFd<'_>]) -> io::Result<usize> {
    assert!(fds.len() <= MAX_TRANSFER_FDS);
    // NB: IoSlice has the same layout as iovec on Unix.
    let mut control = [0u64; SEND_CONTROL_BUFFER_WORDS];
    // NB: An all-zero msghdr is a valid empty one.
    let mut message: libc::msghdr = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    message.msg_iov = bytes.as_ptr().cast_mut().cast();
    message.msg_iovlen = bytes.len() as _;
    if !fds.is_empty() {
        message.msg_control = control.as_mut_ptr().cast();
        message.msg_controllen = control_buffer_size(fds.len()) as _;
        // NB: The control buffer has room for one control message with the descriptors, which CMSG_FIRSTHDR() and
        //     CMSG_DATA() point into.
        unsafe {
            let header = libc::CMSG_FIRSTHDR(&raw const message);
            (*header).cmsg_level = libc::SOL_SOCKET;
            (*header).cmsg_type = libc::SCM_RIGHTS;
            (*header).cmsg_len = libc::CMSG_LEN((fds.len() * size_of::<RawFd>()) as u32) as _;
            let data = libc::CMSG_DATA(header).cast::<RawFd>();
            for (index, fd) in fds.iter().enumerate() {
                data.add(index).write_unaligned(fd.as_raw_fd());
            }
        }
    }
    // NB: The message points at the bytes and the control buffer, which outlive the call.
    let sent = unsafe { libc::sendmsg(socket, &raw const message, libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL | libc::MSG_DONTWAIT) };
    if sent < 0 {
        return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
    }
    Ok(sent as usize)
}

pub(crate) struct Receiver {
    control: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Receiver {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            control: vec![0; control_buffer_size(MAX_TRANSFER_FDS).div_ceil(8)],
        }
    }

    /// Receives bytes and any descriptors that came with them, without waiting for them. Zero bytes mean the peer
    /// closed its end.
    pub(crate) fn receive_with_fds(
        &mut self,
        socket: RawFd,
        buffer: &mut [u8],
        fds: &mut Vec<OwnedFd>,
    ) -> io::Result<usize> {
        self.receive_with_fd_capacity(socket, buffer, fds, MAX_TRANSFER_FDS)
    }

    pub(crate) fn receive_with_fd_capacity(
        &mut self,
        socket: RawFd,
        buffer: &mut [u8],
        fds: &mut Vec<OwnedFd>,
        fd_capacity: usize,
    ) -> io::Result<usize> {
        let mut iov = libc::iovec {
            iov_base: buffer.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
            iov_len: buffer.len(),
        };
        assert!(fd_capacity <= MAX_TRANSFER_FDS);
        let control_size = control_buffer_size(fd_capacity);
        // NB: An all-zero msghdr is a valid empty one.
        let mut message: libc::msghdr = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        message.msg_iov = &raw mut iov;
        message.msg_iovlen = 1;
        message.msg_control = self.control.as_mut_ptr().cast();
        message.msg_controllen = control_size as _;
        #[cfg(any(
            target_os = "linux",
            target_os = "android",
            target_os = "freebsd",
            target_os = "dragonfly",
            target_os = "netbsd",
            target_os = "openbsd",
            target_os = "illumos",
            target_os = "hurd",
            target_os = "cygwin",
        ))]
        let flags = libc::MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC;
        #[cfg(not(any(
            target_os = "linux",
            target_os = "android",
            target_os = "freebsd",
            target_os = "dragonfly",
            target_os = "netbsd",
            target_os = "openbsd",
            target_os = "illumos",
            target_os = "hurd",
            target_os = "cygwin",
        )))]
        let flags = 0;
        // NB: The message points at the buffer and the control buffer, which outlive the call.
        let received = unsafe { libc::recvmsg(socket, &raw mut message, flags | libc::MSG_DONTWAIT) };
        if received < 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        message.msg_controllen = (message.msg_controllen as usize).min(control_size) as _;
        let first_fd = fds.len();
        let mut malformed_control = false;
        // NB: recvmsg() filled in the control messages it received, which CMSG_FIRSTHDR() and CMSG_NXTHDR() walk, and
        //     every descriptor in an SCM_RIGHTS message is a new one that this process owns.
        unsafe {
            let control_end = message.msg_control as usize + message.msg_controllen as usize;
            let header_size = libc::CMSG_LEN(0) as usize;
            let mut header = libc::CMSG_FIRSTHDR(&raw const message);
            while !header.is_null() {
                let remaining = control_end - header as usize;
                let length = (*header).cmsg_len as usize;
                let bounded_length = length.min(remaining);
                if bounded_length < header_size {
                    malformed_control = true;
                    break;
                }
                if (*header).cmsg_level == libc::SOL_SOCKET && (*header).cmsg_type == libc::SCM_RIGHTS {
                    let data = libc::CMSG_DATA(header).cast::<RawFd>();
                    let data_size = bounded_length - header_size;
                    for index in 0..data_size / size_of::<RawFd>() {
                        fds.push(OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(data.add(index).read_unaligned()));
                    }
                }
                if length > remaining {
                    malformed_control = true;
                    break;
                }
                header = libc::CMSG_NXTHDR(&raw const message, header);
            }
        }
        if flags == 0 {
            for fd in &fds[first_fd..] {
                // NB: The descriptor is owned and F_SETFD only changes its descriptor flags.
                if unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_SETFD, libc::FD_CLOEXEC) } < 0 {
                    return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                }
            }
        }
        if malformed_control || message.msg_flags & libc::MSG_CTRUNC != 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                "truncated socket control message",
            ));
        }
        Ok(received as usize)
    }
}

/// How many bytes the socket has for the next read, as far as the kernel can tell.
pub(crate) fn readable_byte_count(socket: RawFd) -> usize {
    let mut count: libc::c_int = 0;
    // NB: FIONREAD writes the count to the local it points to.
    if unsafe { libc::ioctl(socket, libc::FIONREAD, &raw mut count) } < 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    usize::try_from(count).unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Asks for the buffer sizes LibIPC's sockets have always used, which the kernel may round or cap. A socket that keeps
/// its defaults still works.
pub(crate) fn set_buffer_sizes(socket: RawFd, size: usize) {
    let size = libc::c_int::try_from(size).unwrap_or(libc::c_int::MAX);
    for option in [libc::SO_SNDBUF, libc::SO_RCVBUF] {
        // NB: The option's value is the local the call reads.
        unsafe {
            libc::setsockopt(
                socket,
                libc::SOL_SOCKET,
                option,
                (&raw const size).cast(),
                size_of::<libc::c_int>() as libc::socklen_t,
            );
        }
    }
}

/// Shuts down one or both directions of the socket, which the peer sees whichever process has it.
pub(crate) fn shutdown(socket: RawFd, how: std::net::Shutdown) {
    let how = match how {
        std::net::Shutdown::Read => libc::SHUT_RD,
        std::net::Shutdown::Write => libc::SHUT_WR,
        std::net::Shutdown::Both => libc::SHUT_RDWR,
    };
    // NB: shutdown() only changes the state of the socket. One that is gone already has nothing left to shut down.
    unsafe { libc::shutdown(socket, how) };
}

/// Copies a payload into an anonymous file, whose descriptor goes last in the frame, and seals the file where the
/// receiver maps it.
pub(crate) fn copy_payload_to_file(bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<std::fs::File> {
    use std::io::Write;
    let mut file = std::fs::File::from(create_anonymous_file()?);
    // NB: A shared memory object of the BSDs grows by truncation only, not by writing past its end.
    file.set_len(bytes.len() as u64)?;
    file.write_all(bytes)?;
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    crate::shared_memory::seal(&file)?;
    Ok(file)
}

/// The payload of a message in the file it came in, which on Linux the sender has sealed.
pub(crate) fn payload_from_file(fd: OwnedFd, size: usize) -> io::Result<PayloadBytes> {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    return Ok(PayloadBytes::Mapped(crate::shared_memory::MappedPayload::map(
        fd, size,
    )?));
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
    return Ok(PayloadBytes::Inline(copy_payload_from_file(fd, size)?));
}

/// Copies bytes before decoding, using pread so a size change reports a short read. The sender can still write to an
/// unsealed file, so the copy is what gets decoded.
#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
fn copy_payload_from_file(fd: OwnedFd, size: usize) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;
    let file = std::fs::File::from(fd);
    if file.metadata()?.len() < size as u64 {
        return Err(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof));
    }
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    bytes
        .try_reserve_exact(size)
        .map_err(|_| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::OutOfMemory))?;
    bytes.resize(size, 0);
    file.read_exact_at(&mut bytes, 0)?;
    Ok(bytes)
}

/// Raises this process's soft limit on open file descriptors, as LibMain does for every process, so that a test can
/// hold more descriptors than the common default of 1024.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn raise_descriptor_limit() {
    let mut limit = libc::rlimit {
        rlim_cur: 0,
        rlim_max: 0,
    };
    // NB: limit is a local that getrlimit() writes and setrlimit() reads.
    unsafe {
        assert_eq!(libc::getrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_NOFILE, &raw mut limit), 0);
        limit.rlim_cur = limit.rlim_max.min(65536);
        assert_eq!(libc::setrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_NOFILE, &raw const limit), 0);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Read;
    use std::os::unix::net::UnixStream;

    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    #[test]
    fn only_sealed_payload_files_are_mapped() {
        let file = copy_payload_to_file(b"payload").unwrap();
        // NB: F_GET_SEALS only reads the seals of the owned file.
        let seals = unsafe { libc::fcntl(file.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_GET_SEALS) };
        assert_ne!(seals & libc::F_SEAL_WRITE, 0);
        assert_eq!(payload_from_file(file.into(), 7).unwrap().bytes(), b"payload");

        // NB: memfd_create() returns a new descriptor for a NUL-terminated name.
        let fd = unsafe { libc::memfd_create(c"".as_ptr(), libc::MFD_CLOEXEC) };
        assert!(fd >= 0);
        // NB: The descriptor is new and nothing else owns it.
        let mut unsealable = std::fs::File::from(unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) });
        std::io::Write::write_all(&mut unsealable, b"payload").unwrap();
        let unsealed = crate::shared_memory::create_unsealed_file_holding(b"payload");
        for file in [unsealable, unsealed] {
            assert_eq!(
                payload_from_file(file.into(), 7).err().unwrap().kind(),
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData
            );
        }

        let sparse = std::fs::File::from(crate::shared_memory::create_anonymous_file().unwrap());
        sparse.set_len(7).unwrap();
        crate::shared_memory::seal(&sparse).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            payload_from_file(sparse.into(), 7).err().unwrap().kind(),
            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData
        );

        for bytes_of_another_size in [&b"pay"[..], b"payload!"] {
            let file = copy_payload_to_file(bytes_of_another_size).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                payload_from_file(file.into(), 7).err().unwrap().kind(),
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_send_control_buffer_has_room_for_every_descriptor() {
        assert!(control_buffer_size(MAX_TRANSFER_FDS) <= SEND_CONTROL_BUFFER_WORDS * size_of::<u64>());
    }

    #[test]
    fn transports_leave_the_mode_of_their_socket_alone() {
        use crate::transport_socket::TransportSocket;

        for nonblocking in [false, true] {
            let (a, b) = std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
            a.set_nonblocking(nonblocking).unwrap();
            b.set_nonblocking(nonblocking).unwrap();
            let descriptor = a.as_raw_fd();
            let a = TransportSocket::new(a.into()).unwrap();
            let b = TransportSocket::new(b.into()).unwrap();
            // NB: The transport owns the socket, and F_GETFL only reads its status flags.
            let flags = unsafe { libc::fcntl(descriptor, libc::F_GETFL) };
            assert!(flags >= 0);
            assert_eq!(flags & libc::O_NONBLOCK != 0, nonblocking);
            a.post_message(vec![1], Vec::new()).unwrap();
            b.post_message(vec![2], Vec::new()).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(a.receive().unwrap().bytes(), [2]);
            assert_eq!(b.receive().unwrap().bytes(), [1]);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn received_descriptors_are_close_on_exec() {
        use std::os::fd::AsFd;

        let (sender, receiver) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let file = std::fs::File::open("/dev/null").unwrap();
        send_with_fds(sender.as_raw_fd(), &[io::IoSlice::new(&[1])], &[file.as_fd()]).unwrap();
        let mut fds = Vec::new();
        Receiver::new()
            .receive_with_fds(receiver.as_raw_fd(), &mut [0], &mut fds)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fds.len(), 1);
        // NB: The descriptor is owned and F_GETFD only reads its descriptor flags.
        let flags = unsafe { libc::fcntl(fds[0].as_raw_fd(), libc::F_GETFD) };
        assert!(flags >= 0);
        assert_ne!(flags & libc::FD_CLOEXEC, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn vectored_sends_keep_the_payload_and_descriptors_together() {
        use std::os::fd::AsFd;
        let (sender, receiver) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let (mut reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            send_with_fds(
                sender.as_raw_fd(),
                &[io::IoSlice::new(b"head"), io::IoSlice::new(b"payload")],
                &[writer.as_fd()]
            )
            .unwrap(),
            11
        );
        drop(writer);
        let mut bytes = [0; 11];
        let mut fds = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            Receiver::new()
                .receive_with_fds(receiver.as_raw_fd(), &mut bytes, &mut fds)
                .unwrap(),
            11
        );
        assert_eq!(&bytes, b"headpayload");
        assert_eq!(fds.len(), 1);
        drop(fds);
        assert_eq!(reader.read(&mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sending_after_the_peer_closes_returns_an_error() {
        let (sender, receiver) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        drop(receiver);
        assert_eq!(
            send_with_fds(sender.as_raw_fd(), &[io::IoSlice::new(&[1])], &[])
                .unwrap_err()
                .kind(),
            io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn received_descriptors_do_not_carry_over_between_reads() {
        use std::os::fd::AsFd;

        let (sender, socket) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let (mut reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let mut receiver = Receiver::new();
        let mut fds = Vec::new();
        send_with_fds(sender.as_raw_fd(), &[io::IoSlice::new(&[1])], &[writer.as_fd()]).unwrap();
        receiver
            .receive_with_fds(socket.as_raw_fd(), &mut [0], &mut fds)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fds.len(), 1);
        fds.clear();
        drop(writer);
        assert_eq!(reader.read(&mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
        send_with_fds(sender.as_raw_fd(), &[io::IoSlice::new(&[2])], &[]).unwrap();
        let mut byte = [0];
        assert_eq!(
            receiver
                .receive_with_fds(socket.as_raw_fd(), &mut byte, &mut fds)
                .unwrap(),
            1
        );
        assert_eq!(byte, [2]);
        assert!(fds.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn truncated_control_messages_adopt_the_delivered_descriptors() {
        use std::os::fd::AsFd;

        let (sender, receiver) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let (mut reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        send_with_fds(sender.as_raw_fd(), &[io::IoSlice::new(&[1])], &[writer.as_fd(); 3]).unwrap();
        drop(writer);
        let mut fds = Vec::new();
        let error = Receiver::new()
            .receive_with_fd_capacity(receiver.as_raw_fd(), &mut [0; 1], &mut fds, 1)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(error.kind(), io::ErrorKind::InvalidData);
        assert!(!fds.is_empty());
        assert!(fds.len() < 3);
        drop(fds);
        assert_eq!(reader.read(&mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
    }
}
