    }

    #[test]
    fn a_backlog_longer_than_one_turn_arrives_whole() {
        let (transport, mut peer) = with_raw_peer();
        let message_count = 4 * MAX_BYTES_SENT_PER_TURN / (32 * 1024);
        for i in 0..message_count {
            transport.post_message(vec![i as u8; 32 * 1024], Vec::new()).unwrap();
        }
        assert!(transport.pending_message_count() > 0);
        let flushed = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let flushing = scope.spawn(|| transport.flush());
            let mut frame_bytes = vec![0; HEADER_SIZE + 32 * 1024];
            for i in 0..message_count {
                peer.read_exact(&mut frame_bytes).unwrap();
                assert_eq!(frame_bytes[..HEADER_SIZE], frame_header(PAYLOAD_FRAME, 32 * 1024, 0));
                assert!(frame_bytes[HEADER_SIZE..].iter().all(|byte| *byte == i as u8));
            }
            flushing.join().is_ok()
        });
        assert!(flushed);
        assert_eq!(transport.pending_message_count(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn transports_on_the_shared_thread_keep_to_themselves_through_teardown_and_transfer() {
        let churned = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            scope.spawn(|| {
                for _ in 0..200 {
                    let (a, b) = paired();
                    a.post_message(vec![1], Vec::new()).unwrap();
                    if churned.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed).is_multiple_of(2) {
                        assert_eq!(b.receive().unwrap().bytes(), [1]);
                    }
                }
            });
            for pair in 0..8u32 {
                scope.spawn(move || {
                    let (a, b) = paired();
                    let sender = std::thread::spawn(move || {
                        for i in 0..2000u32 {
                            let mut bytes = pair.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
                            bytes.extend(i.to_ne_bytes());
                            bytes.resize(8 + (i as usize * 37) % 700, 0);
                            a.post_message(bytes, Vec::new()).unwrap();
                        }
                        a.close_after_sending_all_pending_messages();
                    });
                    let mut reader = b;
                    let mut next = 0u32;
                    let mut check = |message: ReceivedMessage| {
                        let bytes = message.bytes();
                        assert_eq!(bytes[..4], pair.to_ne_bytes());
                        assert_eq!(bytes[4..8], next.to_ne_bytes());
                        next += 1;
                    };
                    loop {
                        reader.wait_until_readable(None);
                        let (messages, peer_is_gone) = reader.take_incoming();
                        messages.into_iter().for_each(&mut check);
                        if peer_is_gone {
                            break;
                        }
                        let handle = reader.release_for_transfer().unwrap();
                        let (messages, _) = reader.take_incoming();
                        messages.into_iter().for_each(&mut check);
                        reader = TransportSocket::from_handle(handle).unwrap();
                    }
                    assert_eq!(next, 2000);
                    sender.join().unwrap();
                });
            }
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_receive_barrier_does_not_wait_for_an_incomplete_frame() {
        let (transport, mut peer) = with_raw_peer();
        let bytes = frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, b"A", 0);
        peer.write_all(&bytes[..1]).unwrap();
        transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        peer.write_all(&bytes[1..]).unwrap();
        transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        let (messages, peer_is_gone) = transport.take_incoming();
        assert_eq!(messages.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(messages[0].bytes(), b"A");
        assert!(!peer_is_gone);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_receive_barrier_returns_once_a_read_has_ended_inside_a_write() {
        let (transport, peer) = with_raw_peer();
        // NB: One write, longer than one read takes.
        (&peer)
            .write_all(&frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &vec![3; MAX_INLINE_PAYLOAD_SIZE], 0))
            .unwrap();
        for _ in 0..10 {
            transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        }
        assert_eq!(transport.receive().unwrap().bytes(), vec![3; MAX_INLINE_PAYLOAD_SIZE]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_receive_barrier_returns_under_a_peer_that_keeps_writing() {
        let (transport, mut peer) = with_raw_peer();
        let writing = AtomicBool::new(true);
        let frames_written = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let barrier_outlasted_the_deadline = AtomicBool::new(false);
        // NB: Stops the writer even as a failed assertion unwinds, as the scope waits for it.
        struct StopWriting<'a>(&'a AtomicBool);
        impl Drop for StopWriting<'_> {
            fn drop(&mut self) {
                self.0.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
            }
        }
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            scope.spawn(|| {
                let bytes = frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[0; 1000], 0);
                while writing.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                    peer.write_all(&bytes).unwrap();
                    frames_written.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
                }
            });
            // NB: A barrier that waits for the socket to drain would only return once the writer stops.
            scope.spawn(|| {
                let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(20);
                while writing.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                    if Instant::now() >= deadline {
                        barrier_outlasted_the_deadline.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        writing.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
                    }
                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
                }
            });
            let stop_writing = StopWriting(&writing);
            let mut frames_received = 0;
            for _ in 0..50 {
                let written_before_barrier = until(|| {
                    let written = frames_written.load(Ordering::Acquire);
                    (written > frames_received).then_some(written)
                });
                transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
                assert!(!barrier_outlasted_the_deadline.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
                frames_received += transport.take_incoming().0.len();
                assert!(frames_received >= written_before_barrier);
            }
            // NB: The IO thread keeps taking in what the writer writes, so it finishes its last frame.
            drop(stop_writing);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_backlog_of_messages_with_descriptors_is_not_mistaken_for_a_flood() {
        let (ours, peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let batch_count = 6;
        let null = std::fs::File::open("/dev/null").unwrap();
        for _ in 0..batch_count {
            let bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..MAX_TRANSFER_FDS)
                .flat_map(|_| frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, b"A", 1))
                .collect();
            write_with_fds(&peer, &bytes, &vec![null.as_fd(); MAX_TRANSFER_FDS]);
        }
        let transport = TransportSocket::new(ours.into()).unwrap();
        let mut received = 0;
        while received < batch_count * MAX_TRANSFER_FDS {
            let message = transport
                .receive()
                .expect("every message arrives before the peer is gone");
            assert_eq!(message.attachments.len(), 1);
            received += 1;
        }
        assert!(transport.is_open());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_backlog_larger_than_one_read_turn_is_delivered_after_the_peer_hangs_up() {
        let (ours, peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        // NB: A read ends with the descriptors of one write, so each of these frames takes a read of its own.
        let message_count = 3 * MAX_READS_PER_TURN;
        for i in 0..message_count {
            let descriptor = pipe_holding(i as u8);
            write_with_fds(&peer, &frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[i as u8; 1024], 1), &[descriptor.as_fd()]);
        }
        drop(peer);
        let transport = TransportSocket::new(ours.into()).unwrap();
        for i in 0..message_count {
            let message = transport.receive().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(message.bytes(), [i as u8; 1024]);
            let mut attachments = message.attachments;
            assert_eq!(byte_in(attachments.remove(0).into_fd().unwrap()), i as u8);
        }
        assert!(transport.receive().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_frame_cut_in_two_by_a_transfer_arrives_whole() {
        let (transport, mut peer) = with_raw_peer();
        let bytes = frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, b"abcd", 0);
        peer.write_all(&bytes[..HEADER_SIZE + 2]).unwrap();
        transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        let handle = transport.release_for_transfer().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(handle.unprocessed_bytes, bytes[..HEADER_SIZE + 2]);
        let new_owner = TransportSocket::from_handle(handle).unwrap();
        peer.write_all(&bytes[HEADER_SIZE + 2..]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(new_owner.receive().unwrap().bytes(), b"abcd");
        assert!(transport.take_incoming().0.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptors_ahead_of_their_message_go_along_with_a_transfer() {
        let (transport, peer) = with_raw_peer();
        let first = pipe_holding(b'a');
        write_with_fds(&peer, &frame_header(ATTACHMENTS_FRAME, 0, 1), &[first.as_fd()]);
        drop(first);
        transport.wait_until_incoming_is_current();
        let handle = transport.release_for_transfer().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(handle.unprocessed_attachments.len(), 1);
        let new_owner = TransportSocket::from_handle(handle).unwrap();
        let second = pipe_holding(b'b');
        write_with_fds(&peer, &frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, b"X", 2), &[second.as_fd()]);
        drop(second);
        let message = new_owner.receive().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(message.bytes(), b"X");
        let tags: Vec<u8> = message
            .attachments
            .into_iter()
            .map(|attachment| byte_in(attachment.into_fd().unwrap()))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(tags, b"ab");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_read_notification_waits_for_its_acknowledgement() {
        let (ours, mut peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let (mut notifications, notification_writer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        notifications.set_nonblocking(true).unwrap();
        let transport =
            TransportSocket::with_read_notification_pipe(SocketHandle::from(ours), Some(notification_writer.into()))
                .unwrap();
        peer.write_all(&frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[1], 0)).unwrap();
        let mut byte = [0];
        until(|| notifications.read(&mut byte).ok());
        // NB: The owner takes the message before its event loop acknowledges the notification.
        assert_eq!(transport.take_incoming().0.len(), 1);
        peer.write_all(&frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[2], 0)).unwrap();
        until(|| (transport.shared.inbox.lock().messages.len() == 1).then_some(()));
        assert_eq!(
            notifications.read(&mut byte).unwrap_err().kind(),
            io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock
        );
        assert_eq!(transport.take_incoming().0.len(), 1);
        transport.acknowledge_read_notification();
        peer.write_all(&frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[3], 0)).unwrap();
        until(|| notifications.read(&mut byte).ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn incomplete_bytes_are_limited_and_queued_descriptors_are_released() {
        assert_eq!(MAX_UNPROCESSED_BUFFER_SIZE, 128 * 1024 * 1024);
        let (ours, mut peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let transport = TransportSocket::with_limits(SocketHandle::from(ours), None, 24, 4).unwrap();
        let (reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        write_with_fds(
            &peer,
            &frame_header(ATTACHMENTS_FRAME, 0, 1),
            &[OwnedFd::from(writer).as_fd()],
        );
        peer.write_all(&frame_header(PAYLOAD_FRAME, 100, 1)).unwrap();
        peer.write_all(&[0; 20]).unwrap();
        assert!(transport.receive().is_none());
        assert_peer_sees_end(&mut peer);
        assert_pipe_closed(reader);
    }

    #[test]
    fn attachments_frames_have_a_cumulative_descriptor_limit() {
        assert_eq!(MAX_UNPROCESSED_FDS, 16129);
        let (ours, mut peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let transport = TransportSocket::with_limits(SocketHandle::from(ours), None, 24, 2).unwrap();
        let (reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let writer = OwnedFd::from(writer);
        for _ in 0..3 {
            write_with_fds(&peer, &frame_header(ATTACHMENTS_FRAME, 0, 1), &[writer.as_fd()]);
        }
        drop(writer);
        assert!(transport.receive().is_none());
        assert_peer_sees_end(&mut peer);
        assert_pipe_closed(reader);
    }

    #[test]
    fn complete_frames_do_not_accumulate_towards_the_limits() {
        let (ours, peer) = UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let transport = TransportSocket::with_limits(SocketHandle::from(ours), None, HEADER_SIZE, 0).unwrap();
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..100).flat_map(|_| frame(PAYLOAD_FRAME, &[], 0)).collect();
        (&peer).write_all(&bytes).unwrap();
        drop(peer);
        for _ in 0..100 {
            assert!(transport.receive().unwrap().bytes().is_empty());
        }
        assert!(transport.receive().is_none());
    }
}

//! Uses C++ `TransportWindows` for named-pipe framing, shared payloads and handle-broker attachments.

#![allow(
    unsafe_code,
    reason = "the Windows transport and descriptor owners cross the C++ boundary"
)]

use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::io;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

use crate::Attachment;
pub use crate::receive_queue::ReceivedMessage;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn ipc_windows_transport_adopt(descriptor: i32) -> *mut c_void;
    fn ipc_windows_transport_take_over() -> *mut c_void;
    fn ipc_windows_transport_pair(local: *mut *mut c_void, remote: *mut i32) -> bool;
    fn ipc_windows_transport_destroy(transport: *mut c_void);
    fn ipc_windows_transport_close(transport: *mut c_void);
    fn ipc_windows_transport_is_open(transport: *const c_void) -> bool;
    fn ipc_windows_transport_send(
        transport: *mut c_void,
        bytes: *const u8,
        size: usize,
        descriptors: *const i32,
        descriptor_count: usize,
    ) -> bool;
    fn ipc_windows_transport_receive(transport: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn ipc_windows_message_bytes(message: *const c_void, size: *mut usize) -> *const u8;
    fn ipc_windows_message_attachment_count(message: *const c_void) -> usize;
    fn ipc_windows_message_take_attachment(message: *mut c_void) -> i32;
    fn ipc_windows_message_destroy(message: *mut c_void);
    fn ipc_windows_descriptor_clone(descriptor: i32) -> i32;
    fn ipc_windows_descriptor_close(descriptor: i32);
}

/// An owned LibCore descriptor. These are native handles or sockets, not Microsoft CRT file descriptors.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct OwnedDescriptor(i32);

impl OwnedDescriptor {
    /// # Safety
    /// The caller transfers sole ownership of a valid LibCore descriptor.
    pub unsafe fn from_raw(descriptor: i32) -> Self {
        Self(descriptor)
    }

    pub fn into_raw(self) -> i32 {
        let descriptor = self.0;
        std::mem::forget(self);
        descriptor
    }

    pub fn try_clone(&self) -> io::Result<Self> {
        // SAFETY: This owner keeps its descriptor live while C++ duplicates it.
        let descriptor = unsafe { ipc_windows_descriptor_clone(self.0) };
        if descriptor == -1 {
            return Err(io::Error::other("could not duplicate the IPC descriptor"));
        }
        Ok(Self(descriptor))
    }
}

impl Drop for OwnedDescriptor {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owner releases its descriptor exactly once, using the right close operation for sockets too.
        unsafe { ipc_windows_descriptor_close(self.0) };
    }
}

impl From<OwnedDescriptor> for std::fs::File {
    fn from(descriptor: OwnedDescriptor) -> Self {
        use std::os::windows::io::FromRawHandle;
        // SAFETY: LibCore descriptors contain the native handle value, and this conversion transfers its ownership.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw_handle(descriptor.into_raw() as isize as *mut c_void) }
    }
}

pub struct TransportWindows {
    native: NonNull<c_void>,
    reader: Mutex<()>,
    pending: AtomicUsize,
}

// SAFETY: C++ serializes sends, and `reader` serializes reads. Closing and dropping require exclusive access.
unsafe impl Send for TransportWindows {}
unsafe impl Sync for TransportWindows {}

impl TransportWindows {
    fn from_native(native: *mut c_void) -> io::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            native: NonNull::new(native).ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("could not open the Windows IPC transport"))?,
            reader: Mutex::new(()),
            pending: AtomicUsize::new(0),
        })
    }

    pub fn new(descriptor: OwnedDescriptor) -> io::Result<Self> {
        // SAFETY: The native constructor consumes this descriptor on success and failure.
        Self::from_native(unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_adopt(descriptor.into_raw()) })
    }

    pub fn take_over() -> io::Result<Self> {
        // SAFETY: C++ takes the inherited descriptors and installs the process's handle-broker client.
        Self::from_native(unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_take_over() })
    }

    pub fn create_paired() -> io::Result<(Self, OwnedDescriptor)> {
        let mut native = std::ptr::null_mut();
        let mut descriptor = -1;
        // SAFETY: Both output slots are writable. On success they each own one end of a new pipe.
        if !unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_pair(&raw mut native, &raw mut descriptor) } {
            return Err(io::Error::other("could not create a Windows IPC pipe"));
        }
        Ok((Self::from_native(native)?, OwnedDescriptor(descriptor)))
    }

    pub fn post_message(&self, bytes: Vec<u8>, attachments: Vec<Attachment>) -> io::Result<()> {
        crate::validate_message_size(bytes.len(), attachments.len())?;
        let descriptors: Vec<_> = attachments
            .into_iter()
            .map(|attachment| attachment.into_raw())
            .collect();
        self.pending.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // SAFETY: The buffers remain live for this call. C++ consumes every attachment even if sending fails.
        let sent = unsafe {
            ipc_windows_transport_send(
                self.native.as_ptr(),
                bytes.as_ptr(),
                bytes.len(),
                descriptors.as_ptr(),
                descriptors.len(),
            )
        };
        self.pending.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        if sent {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe.into())
        }
    }

    pub fn pending_message_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.pending.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    // Like the C++ Windows transport, sends complete before post_message returns.
    pub fn flush(&self) {}

    pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The native transport stays live for this borrow; its open state is atomic.
        unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_is_open(self.native.as_ptr()) }
    }

    pub fn receive(&self) -> Option<ReceivedMessage> {
        let _reader = self.reader.lock().unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner());
        // SAFETY: This is the only reader. The returned message owns its bytes and attachments until dropped.
        let message = NonNull::new(unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_receive(self.native.as_ptr()) })?;
        struct Message(NonNull<c_void>);
        impl Drop for Message {
            fn drop(&mut self) {
                // SAFETY: This guard uniquely owns the native message.
                unsafe { ipc_windows_message_destroy(self.0.as_ptr()) };
            }
        }
        let message = Message(message);
        let mut size = 0;
        // SAFETY: The message is live and `size` is writable. An empty message may have a null data pointer.
        let data = unsafe { ipc_windows_message_bytes(message.0.as_ptr(), &raw mut size) };
        let bytes = if size == 0 {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            // SAFETY: The native message owns exactly `size` readable bytes for the duration of this copy.
            #[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods, reason = "the empty message case is handled above")]
            let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(data, size) };
            bytes.to_vec()
        };
        // SAFETY: The message is live and we take each attachment exactly once.
        let count = unsafe { ipc_windows_message_attachment_count(message.0.as_ptr()) };
        let attachments = (0..count)
            .map(|_| unsafe {
                Attachment::from_descriptor(OwnedDescriptor::from_raw(ipc_windows_message_take_attachment(
                    message.0.as_ptr(),
                )))
            })
            .collect();
        Some(ReceivedMessage { bytes, attachments })
    }

    pub fn close_after_sending_all_pending_messages(&mut self) {
        self.close();
    }

    pub fn close(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: Exclusive access means no send or receive is in flight.
        unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_close(self.native.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

impl Drop for TransportWindows {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This uniquely owns the native allocation, and no borrows remain.
        unsafe { ipc_windows_transport_destroy(self.native.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

//! What the transports of every platform share: what the owner of a transport gets to see of what arrives, the
//! bookkeeping of the IO thread that every transport of a process shares, and what callers hand a transport to send.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
use std::os::fd::OwnedFd;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard, OnceLock};
use std::time::Duration;

pub use crate::receive_queue::ReceivedMessage;
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
pub use crate::transport_mach_port::{MachPortPair, TransportMachPort};
#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
pub use crate::transport_socket::{SocketHandle, TransportSocket};

/// The transport of this platform.
#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
pub type Transport = TransportMachPort;
#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
pub type Transport = TransportSocket;

/// What the IO thread shows every message that arrives, before the transport's owner gets to see it, and empty bytes
/// once the peer is gone.
pub type IncomingMessageObserver = Box<dyn Fn(&[u8]) + Send>;

/// The bytes of a message that waits to be sent, which it owns, wherever they are.
pub type OwnedPayload = Box<dyn AsRef<[u8]> + Send>;

/// The time on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, which AK's `MonotonicTime` reads, and which keeps counting while the system sleeps.
#[allow(unsafe_code)]
pub(crate) fn clock_monotonic_nanoseconds() -> i64 {
    let mut now = libc::timespec { tv_sec: 0, tv_nsec: 0 };
    // NB: now points to a local that the call writes to, and the clock always exists.
    unsafe { libc::clock_gettime(libc::CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &raw mut now) };
    now.tv_sec * 1_000_000_000 + now.tv_nsec
}

/// A point in time on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, the clock of AK's `MonotonicTime`, which keeps counting while the system
/// sleeps. A wait checks it again after every wakeup, so that it ends when its caller's deadline passes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct MonotonicDeadline {
    nanoseconds: i64,
}

impl MonotonicDeadline {
    pub fn from_nanoseconds(nanoseconds: i64) -> Self {
        Self { nanoseconds }
    }

    fn remaining(self) -> Option<Duration> {
        let now = clock_monotonic_nanoseconds();
        (now < self.nanoseconds).then(|| Duration::from_nanos(self.nanoseconds.abs_diff(now)))
    }
}

/// The bytes of a message to post: owned already, or lent by a caller that hands them over only if the message has to
/// wait, as C++ does with the buffer it encoded the message into.
pub enum OutgoingPayload<'a> {
    Owned(Vec<u8>),
    Lent {
        bytes: &'a [u8],
        hand_over: &'a mut dyn FnMut() -> OwnedPayload,
    },
}

impl OutgoingPayload<'_> {
    pub(crate) fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match self {
            Self::Owned(bytes) => bytes,
            Self::Lent { bytes, .. } => bytes,
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) const IDLE_MEMORY_RELEASE_DELAY_IN_MILLISECONDS: u32 = 1000;

pub(crate) fn release_unused_allocator_memory() {
    // NB: The messages the IO thread receives are freed by the threads that handle them, and the allocator keeps that
    //     memory until this thread allocates again or collects, which an idle process may never do. Unit tests
    //     don't link AK, and use the system allocator.
    #[cfg(ladybird_links_ak)]
    ak::release_unused_allocator_memory();
}

pub(crate) fn lock<T>(mutex: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    mutex.lock().unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner())
}

pub(crate) fn wait<'a, T>(condition: &Condvar, guard: MutexGuard<'a, T>) -> MutexGuard<'a, T> {
    condition.wait(guard).unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner())
}

pub(crate) fn wait_for<'a, T>(
    condition: &Condvar,
    guard: MutexGuard<'a, T>,
    timeout: Duration,
) -> (MutexGuard<'a, T>, bool) {
    let (guard, result) = condition
        .wait_timeout(guard, timeout)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner());
    (guard, result.timed_out())
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum IoThreadState {
    Running = 0,
    SendPendingMessagesAndStop = 1,
    Stopped = 2,
}

pub(crate) struct AtomicIoThreadState(AtomicU8);

impl AtomicIoThreadState {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self(AtomicU8::new(IoThreadState::Running as u8))
    }

    pub(crate) fn load(&self) -> IoThreadState {
        match self.0.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
            0 => IoThreadState::Running,
            1 => IoThreadState::SendPendingMessagesAndStop,
            _ => IoThreadState::Stopped,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn store(&self, state: IoThreadState) {
        self.0.store(state as u8, Ordering::Release);
    }

    // NB: The IO thread may already have stopped on its own, as when the peer hung up. Stopped is final, so it is never
    //     replaced by a new stop request.
    pub(crate) fn request_stop(&self, desired_state: IoThreadState) {
        let mut state = self.0.load(Ordering::Acquire);
        while state != IoThreadState::Stopped as u8 {
            match self
                .0
                .compare_exchange(state, desired_state as u8, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Acquire)
            {
                Ok(_) => break,
                Err(current) => state = current,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// What a transport has taken in for its owner, under the transport's incoming lock. `Barrier` is what the transport
/// keeps there to tell when everything its peer sent before a receive barrier has arrived.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Incoming<Barrier> {
    pub(crate) messages: VecDeque<ReceivedMessage>,
    // NB: Set once this end's IO is over, which ends a wait for messages that can no longer come, even when the
    //     transport's end went to a new owner and the peer is not gone.
    pub(crate) local_io_is_over: bool,
    pub(crate) barrier: Barrier,
    wait_until_readable_interrupted: bool,
    read_notification_pending: bool,
    read_notification_pipe: Option<File>,
    // NB: The owner mostly hears of messages through the pipe, so a change wakes the condition variable only when
    //     something waits on it.
    waiter_count: usize,
}

/// The messages a transport's IO thread has taken in for the owner, and how the owner waits for them, which is the
/// same for every transport.
pub(crate) struct Inbox<Barrier> {
    // NB: Written under the incoming lock, so that a reader under it sees it with the messages that came before.
    peer_eof: AtomicBool,
    incoming: Mutex<Incoming<Barrier>>,
    changed: Condvar,
    // NB: This has a lock of its own, which is taken before the incoming lock: the observer may interrupt a wait.
    incoming_message_observer: Mutex<Option<IncomingMessageObserver>>,
}

impl<Barrier: Default> Inbox<Barrier> {
    /// An inbox that writes a byte to the pipe when messages are there to read, or the peer is gone, and nothing more
    /// until `acknowledge_read_notification()`.
    pub(crate) fn new(read_notification_pipe: Option<OwnedFd>) -> Self {
        Self {
            peer_eof: AtomicBool::new(false),
            incoming: Mutex::new(Incoming {
                read_notification_pipe: read_notification_pipe.map(File::from),
                ..Incoming::default()
            }),
            changed: Condvar::new(),
            incoming_message_observer: Mutex::new(None),
        }
    }
}

impl<Barrier> Inbox<Barrier> {
    pub(crate) fn lock(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Incoming<Barrier>> {
        lock(&self.incoming)
    }

    pub(crate) fn wait<'a>(
        &self,
        mut incoming: MutexGuard<'a, Incoming<Barrier>>,
    ) -> MutexGuard<'a, Incoming<Barrier>> {
        incoming.waiter_count += 1;
        let mut incoming = wait(&self.changed, incoming);
        incoming.waiter_count -= 1;
        incoming
    }

    fn wait_for<'a>(
        &self,
        mut incoming: MutexGuard<'a, Incoming<Barrier>>,
        timeout: Duration,
    ) -> MutexGuard<'a, Incoming<Barrier>> {
        incoming.waiter_count += 1;
        let mut incoming = wait_for(&self.changed, incoming, timeout).0;
        incoming.waiter_count -= 1;
        incoming
    }

    /// Changes the incoming state, and wakes whatever waits for a change.
    pub(crate) fn update<Result>(&self, change: impl FnOnce(&mut Incoming<Barrier>) -> Result) -> Result {
        let (result, has_waiters) = {
            let mut incoming = self.lock();
            let result = change(&mut incoming);
            (result, incoming.waiter_count > 0)
        };
        if has_waiters {
            self.changed.notify_all();
        }
        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn peer_eof(&self) -> bool {
        self.peer_eof.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    }

    #[cfg(all(test, not(target_vendor = "apple")))]
    pub(crate) fn has_waiters(&self) -> bool {
        self.lock().waiter_count > 0
    }

    pub(crate) fn notify_incoming_message_observer<'a>(&self, messages: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a [u8]>) {
        // NB: The observer runs under its lock, so once a new one is set, the old one is no longer running.
        if let Some(observer) = &*lock(&self.incoming_message_observer) {
            for bytes in messages {
                observer(bytes);
            }
        }
    }

    fn schedule_read_notification(incoming: &mut Incoming<Barrier>) {
        if incoming.read_notification_pending {
            return;
        }
        incoming.read_notification_pending = true;
        if let Some(pipe) = &incoming.read_notification_pipe {
            // NB: An interrupted write wrote nothing, so it is retried. The pipe does not block, and a full one already
            //     wakes the owner.
            let _ = (&*pipe).write_all(&[0]);
        }
    }

    /// Hands the messages to the owner, which the observer has seen already, along with what `change` does to the
    /// incoming state under the same lock.
    pub(crate) fn deliver(
        &self,
        messages: impl IntoIterator<Item = ReceivedMessage>,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut Incoming<Barrier>),
    ) {
        self.update(|incoming| {
            let was_empty = incoming.messages.is_empty();
            incoming.messages.extend(messages);
            change(incoming);
            if was_empty && !incoming.messages.is_empty() {
                Self::schedule_read_notification(incoming);
            }
        });
    }

    /// Hands the last messages of the peer to the owner along with its departure, so that the owner can't take them
    /// without learning that the peer is gone.
    pub(crate) fn deliver_with_peer_eof(
        &self,
        messages: impl IntoIterator<Item = ReceivedMessage>,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut Incoming<Barrier>),
    ) {
        self.notify_incoming_message_observer([&[][..]]);
        self.update(|incoming| {
            incoming.messages.extend(messages);
            change(incoming);
            self.peer_eof.store(true, Ordering::Release);
            Self::schedule_read_notification(incoming);
        });
    }

    pub(crate) fn mark_peer_eof(&self) {
        if !self.peer_eof() {
            self.deliver_with_peer_eof([], |_| {});
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn end_local_io(&self) {
        self.update(|incoming| incoming.local_io_is_over = true);
    }

    /// Waits for the next message, or returns `None` once the peer is gone and every message it sent was taken.
    pub(crate) fn receive(&self) -> Option<ReceivedMessage> {
        let mut incoming = self.lock();
        loop {
            if let Some(message) = incoming.messages.pop_front() {
                return Some(message);
            }
            if self.peer_eof() || incoming.local_io_is_over {
                return None;
            }
            incoming = self.wait(incoming);
        }
    }

    /// Takes every message that has arrived, and whether the peer was gone as they were taken. Later arrivals can't
    /// be skipped by reporting the peer gone.
    pub(crate) fn take_incoming(&self) -> (Vec<ReceivedMessage>, bool) {
        let mut incoming = self.lock();
        let messages = std::mem::take(&mut incoming.messages).into();
        (messages, self.peer_eof())
    }

    /// Waits until there is a message to take, the peer is gone, the wait is interrupted, or the deadline passes.
    pub(crate) fn wait_until_readable(&self, deadline: Option<MonotonicDeadline>) {
        let mut incoming = self.lock();
        while incoming.messages.is_empty()
            && !self.peer_eof()
            && !incoming.local_io_is_over
            && !incoming.wait_until_readable_interrupted
        {
            match deadline {
                None => incoming = self.wait(incoming),
                Some(deadline) => {
                    let Some(remaining) = deadline.remaining() else {
                        break;
                    };
                    incoming = self.wait_for(incoming, remaining);
                }
            }
        }
        incoming.wait_until_readable_interrupted = false;
    }

    pub(crate) fn interrupt_wait_until_readable(&self) {
        self.update(|incoming| incoming.wait_until_readable_interrupted = true);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_incoming_message_observer(
        &self,
        observer: Option<IncomingMessageObserver>,
    ) -> Option<IncomingMessageObserver> {
        std::mem::replace(&mut *lock(&self.incoming_message_observer), observer)
    }

    pub(crate) fn close_read_notification_pipe(&self) {
        let pipe = self.lock().read_notification_pipe.take();
        drop(pipe);
    }

    pub(crate) fn acknowledge_read_notification(&self) {
        self.lock().read_notification_pending = false;
    }

    pub(crate) fn schedule_read_notification_if_readable(&self) {
        let mut incoming = self.lock();
        if !incoming.messages.is_empty() || self.peer_eof() {
            Self::schedule_read_notification(&mut incoming);
        }
    }
}

/// Where a transport stands with the IO thread that every transport of the process shares. Both change only under the
/// lock of that thread's attention list.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct IoThreadMembership {
    needs_attention: AtomicBool,
    io_is_finished: AtomicBool,
}

pub(crate) trait SharesIoThread {
    fn io_thread_membership(&self) -> &IoThreadMembership;
}

/// The transports that asked the shared IO thread to send their backlog, take note of a peer they found gone, or stop
/// their IO, and how a transport's owner waits for its IO to be over.
pub(crate) struct AttentionList<Transport> {
    transports: Mutex<Vec<Arc<Transport>>>,
    io_finished: Condvar,
}

impl<Transport: SharesIoThread> AttentionList<Transport> {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            transports: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            io_finished: Condvar::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Puts the transport on the list, and answers whether the IO thread should be woken for it, which it need not be
    /// once the transport's IO is over.
    pub(crate) fn request(&self, transport: &Arc<Transport>) -> bool {
        let mut transports = lock(&self.transports);
        let membership = transport.io_thread_membership();
        if membership.io_is_finished.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return false;
        }
        if !membership.needs_attention.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            membership.needs_attention.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
            transports.push(Arc::clone(transport));
        }
        true
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        lock(&self.transports).is_empty()
    }

    /// Moves the transports that asked for attention into `into`, which the IO thread serves next.
    pub(crate) fn take(&self, into: &mut Vec<Arc<Transport>>) {
        let mut transports = lock(&self.transports);
        std::mem::swap(into, &mut *transports);
        for transport in into.iter() {
            transport
                .io_thread_membership()
                .needs_attention
                .store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn wait_until_io_is_finished(&self, transport: &Transport) {
        assert!(
            !IS_SHARED_IO_THREAD.get(),
            "the shared IO thread must not wait for itself"
        );
        let mut transports = lock(&self.transports);
        while !transport.io_thread_membership().io_is_finished.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            transports = wait(&self.io_finished, transports);
        }
    }

    // NB: The owner may destroy the transport as soon as this returns.
    pub(crate) fn mark_io_finished(&self, transport: &Arc<Transport>) {
        let mut transports = lock(&self.transports);
        let membership = transport.io_thread_membership();
        if membership.needs_attention.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            transports.retain(|other| !Arc::ptr_eq(other, transport));
            membership.needs_attention.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        membership.io_is_finished.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.io_finished.notify_all();
    }
}

thread_local! {
    static IS_SHARED_IO_THREAD: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
}

pub(crate) fn is_shared_io_thread() -> bool {
    IS_SHARED_IO_THREAD.get()
}

/// Starts the IO thread that every transport of the process shares, the first time a transport is made. Nothing waits
/// for the thread, which goes with the process. If it can't start, what `create` made goes with the last reference,
/// and the next transport tries again.
pub(crate) fn start_shared_io_thread<IoThread: Send + Sync + 'static>(
    io_thread: &'static OnceLock<Arc<IoThread>>,
    name: &str,
    create: impl FnOnce() -> std::io::Result<IoThread>,
    run: fn(&IoThread),
) -> std::io::Result<&'static IoThread> {
    static STARTING: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());
    if let Some(running) = io_thread.get() {
        return Ok(running);
    }
    let _starting = lock(&STARTING);
    if let Some(running) = io_thread.get() {
        return Ok(running);
    }
    let created = Arc::new(create()?);
    std::thread::Builder::new().name(name.to_string()).spawn({
        let created = Arc::clone(&created);
        move || {
            IS_SHARED_IO_THREAD.set(true);
            run(&created);
        }
    })?;
    Ok(io_thread.get_or_init(|| created))
}
