//! LibIPC's wire format, as `IPC::Encoder` and `IPC::Decoder` write and read it.
//!
//! Numbers go as their bytes in the host's order, sizes as 32-bit numbers, booleans as one byte, an optional value as a
//! boolean followed by the value, and a sequence as its size followed by its elements. File descriptors and port rights
//! go beside the bytes, as attachments, in the order they are encoded.

#[cfg(windows)]
use crate::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
#[cfg(unix)]
use std::os::fd::OwnedFd as OwnedDescriptor;

use crate::attachment::Attachment;

pub use libipc_rust_macros::{Decode, Encode};

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum EncodeError {
    SizeTooLarge(usize),
    InvalidValue(&'static str),
    Attachment(std::io::Error),
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DecodeError {
    UnexpectedEnd,
    SizeTooLarge(usize),
    InvalidBoolean(u8),
    InvalidUtf8,
    InvalidValue(&'static str),
    MissingAttachment,
    Attachment(String),
    AllocationFailed,
}

pub trait Encode {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError>;

    /// Encodes an owned value, moving its attachments into the encoder.
    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError>
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        self.encode(encoder)
    }

    fn encode_slice(elements: &[Self], encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError>
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        for element in elements {
            element.encode(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn encode_vec(elements: Vec<Self>, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError>
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        encoder.encode_size(elements.len())?;
        for element in elements {
            element.encode_owned(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub trait Decode: Sized {
    /// A lower bound on the bytes an encoded value occupies, excluding attachments.
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 0;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError>;

    fn decode_vec(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>, size: usize) -> Result<Vec<Self>, DecodeError> {
        decode_elements(decoder, size)
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Encoder {
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    attachments: Vec<Attachment>,
}

impl Encoder {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn encode<T: Encode + ?Sized>(&mut self, value: &T) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        value.encode(self)
    }

    pub fn encode_owned<T: Encode>(&mut self, value: T) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        value.encode_owned(self)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn append_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        self.bytes.extend_from_slice(bytes);
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn encode_size(&mut self, size: usize) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        let size = u32::try_from(size).map_err(|_| EncodeError::SizeTooLarge(size))?;
        self.append_bytes(&size.to_ne_bytes());
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn append_attachment(&mut self, attachment: Attachment) {
        self.attachments.push(attachment);
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<Attachment>) {
        (self.bytes, self.attachments)
    }
}

pub struct Decoder<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    position: usize,
    attachments: VecDeque<Attachment>,
    max_size_of_next_value: usize,
}

impl<'a> Decoder<'a> {
    pub fn new(bytes: &'a [u8], attachments: impl IntoIterator<Item = Attachment>) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            position: 0,
            attachments: attachments.into_iter().collect(),
            max_size_of_next_value: usize::MAX,
        }
    }

    pub fn decode<T: Decode>(&mut self) -> Result<T, DecodeError> {
        T::decode(self)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn read_bytes(&mut self, count: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecodeError> {
        let end = self.position.checked_add(count).ok_or(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)?;
        let bytes = self.bytes.get(self.position..end).ok_or(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)?;
        self.position = end;
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn decode_size(&mut self) -> Result<usize, DecodeError> {
        let max_size = std::mem::replace(&mut self.max_size_of_next_value, usize::MAX);
        let size = self.decode::<u32>()? as usize;
        if size > max_size {
            return Err(DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(size));
        }
        if size > self.remaining_bytes().saturating_add(self.attachments.len()) {
            return Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd);
        }
        Ok(size)
    }

    /// Decodes a string, byte buffer or vector, which goes as its size and then its contents, refusing one larger than
    /// `max_size` before decoding its contents.
    pub fn decode_with_max_size<T: Decode>(&mut self, max_size: usize) -> Result<T, DecodeError> {
        // NB: Decoding a string, byte buffer or vector starts with decode_size(), which checks the size against this.
        //     The bound ends with the value, so it never applies to anything decoded after it.
        self.max_size_of_next_value = max_size;
        let value = self.decode();
        self.max_size_of_next_value = usize::MAX;
        value
    }

    pub fn take_attachment(&mut self) -> Result<Attachment, DecodeError> {
        self.attachments.pop_front().ok_or(DecodeError::MissingAttachment)
    }

    pub fn remaining_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len() - self.position
    }

    pub fn remaining_attachments(&self) -> usize {
        self.attachments.len()
    }

    pub fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.remaining_bytes() == 0
    }
}

macro_rules! impl_number {
    ($($type:ty),*) => {
        $(
            impl Encode for $type {
                #[inline]
                fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
                    encoder.append_bytes(&self.to_ne_bytes());
                    Ok(())
                }

                fn encode_slice(elements: &[Self], encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
                    let byte_count = elements.len().checked_mul(size_of::<Self>()).ok_or(EncodeError::SizeTooLarge(elements.len()))?;
                    encoder.bytes.reserve(byte_count);
                    for element in elements {
                        encoder.bytes.extend_from_slice(&element.to_ne_bytes());
                    }
                    Ok(())
                }

                fn encode_vec(elements: Vec<Self>, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
                    elements.as_slice().encode(encoder)
                }
            }

            impl Decode for $type {
                const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = size_of::<$type>();

                #[inline]
                fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
                    let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(size_of::<$type>())?;
                    Ok(<$type>::from_ne_bytes(bytes.try_into().map_err(|_| DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)?))
                }

                fn decode_vec(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>, size: usize) -> Result<Vec<Self>, DecodeError> {
                    let byte_count = size.checked_mul(size_of::<$type>()).ok_or(DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(size))?;
                    let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(byte_count)?;
                    Ok(bytes.as_chunks::<{ size_of::<$type>() }>().0.iter()
                        .map(|&chunk| <$type>::from_ne_bytes(chunk))
                        .collect())
                }
            }
        )*
    };
}

impl_number!(u16, u32, u64, i8, i16, i32, i64, f32, f64);

impl Encode for u8 {
    #[inline]
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.append_bytes(&[*self]);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn encode_slice(elements: &[Self], encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.append_bytes(elements);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn encode_vec(elements: Vec<Self>, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        elements.as_slice().encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for u8 {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 1;

    #[inline]
    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(decoder.read_bytes(1)?[0])
    }

    fn decode_vec(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>, size: usize) -> Result<Vec<Self>, DecodeError> {
        Ok(decoder.read_bytes(size)?.to_vec())
    }
}

// NB: A size_t encodes as the 64-bit number it is on every target Ladybird supports.
impl Encode for usize {
    #[inline]
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        (*self as u64).encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for usize {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 8;

    #[inline]
    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        usize::try_from(decoder.decode::<u64>()?).map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidValue("size_t"))
    }

    fn decode_vec(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>, size: usize) -> Result<Vec<Self>, DecodeError> {
        let byte_count = size.checked_mul(8).ok_or(DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(size))?;
        let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(byte_count)?;
        bytes
            .as_chunks::<8>()
            .0
            .iter()
            .map(|&chunk| usize::try_from(u64::from_ne_bytes(chunk)).map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidValue("size_t")))
            .collect()
    }
}

impl Encode for bool {
    #[inline]
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        u8::from(*self).encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for bool {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 1;

    #[inline]
    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        match decoder.decode::<u8>()? {
            0 => Ok(false),
            1 => Ok(true),
            other => Err(DecodeError::InvalidBoolean(other)),
        }
    }
}

impl Encode for () {
    fn encode(&self, _: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Decode for () {
    fn decode(_: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// `String` and `StringView`: the size of the UTF-8 bytes, then the bytes.
impl Encode for str {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.as_bytes().encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Encode for String {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.as_str().encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for String {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 4;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
        let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(size)?;
        String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec()).map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidUtf8)
    }
}

/// C++ `String`: UTF-8 bytes that may include lone surrogate encodings.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Utf8String(Vec<u8>);

impl Utf8String {
    pub fn from_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        validate_utf8(&bytes)?;
        Ok(Self(bytes))
    }

    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.0
    }

    pub fn into_bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.0
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Result<&str, std::str::Utf8Error> {
        std::str::from_utf8(&self.0)
    }

    pub fn into_string(self) -> Result<String, std::string::FromUtf8Error> {
        String::from_utf8(self.0)
    }
}

impl From<&str> for Utf8String {
    fn from(string: &str) -> Self {
        Self(string.as_bytes().to_vec())
    }
}

impl From<String> for Utf8String {
    fn from(string: String) -> Self {
        Self(string.into_bytes())
    }
}

impl Encode for Utf8String {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.as_bytes().encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for Utf8String {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 4;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
        let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(size)?;
        validate_utf8(bytes)?;
        Ok(Self(bytes.to_vec()))
    }
}

/// `ByteString`: bytes in no particular encoding, which go as `String` does.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ByteString(pub Vec<u8>);

impl Encode for ByteString {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.0.as_slice().encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl Decode for ByteString {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 4;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
        Ok(Self(decoder.read_bytes(size)?.to_vec()))
    }
}

/// Validates bytes as `Utf8View::validate()` does, including lonely surrogates.
pub fn validate_utf8(mut bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
    while let Err(error) = std::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
        bytes = &bytes[error.valid_up_to()..];
        match bytes {
            [0xed, 0xa0..=0xbf, 0x80..=0xbf, rest @ ..] => bytes = rest,
            _ => return Err(DecodeError::InvalidUtf8),
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `Utf16String`: whether its code units are stored as Latin-1 bytes, their count, then the code units.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Utf16String(pub Vec<u16>);

impl From<&str> for Utf16String {
    fn from(string: &str) -> Self {
        Self(string.encode_utf16().collect())
    }
}

impl Utf16String {
    pub fn to_string_lossy(&self) -> String {
        String::from_utf16_lossy(&self.0)
    }
}

impl Encode for Utf16String {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        let is_latin1 = self.0.iter().all(|&code_unit| code_unit <= 0xFF);
        is_latin1.encode(encoder)?;
        encoder.encode_size(self.0.len())?;
        if is_latin1 {
            encoder.bytes.reserve(self.0.len());
            encoder.bytes.extend(self.0.iter().map(|&code_unit| code_unit as u8));
        } else {
            u16::encode_slice(&self.0, encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Decode for Utf16String {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 5;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let is_latin1 = decoder.decode::<bool>()?;
        let length = decoder.decode_size()?;
        if is_latin1 {
            let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(length)?;
            return Ok(Self(bytes.iter().map(|&byte| u16::from(byte)).collect()));
        }
        let byte_count = length.checked_mul(2).ok_or(DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(length))?;
        let bytes = decoder.read_bytes(byte_count)?;
        let (code_units, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<2>();
        Ok(Self(code_units.iter().map(|&pair| u16::from_ne_bytes(pair)).collect()))
    }
}

/// `Vector` and spans: the size, then the elements.
impl<T: Encode> Encode for [T] {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.encode_size(self.len())?;
        T::encode_slice(self, encoder)
    }
}

impl<T: Encode> Encode for Vec<T> {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.as_slice().encode(encoder)
    }

    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        T::encode_vec(self, encoder)
    }
}

impl<T: Decode> Decode for Vec<T> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 4;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
        T::decode_vec(decoder, size)
    }
}

fn decode_elements<T: Decode>(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>, size: usize) -> Result<Vec<T>, DecodeError> {
    if T::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE != 0 && size > decoder.remaining_bytes() / T::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE {
        return Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd);
    }
    let mut elements = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..size {
        let element = decoder.decode()?;
        if elements.len() == elements.capacity() {
            // NB: Grow only after decoding an element, independently of the peer's count.
            elements.try_reserve(1).map_err(|_| DecodeError::AllocationFailed)?;
        }
        elements.push(element);
    }
    Ok(elements)
}

/// `Array`: the size, which must match, then the elements.
impl<T: Encode, const N: usize> Encode for [T; N] {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.as_slice().encode(encoder)
    }

    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.encode_size(N)?;
        for element in self {
            element.encode_owned(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl<T: Decode, const N: usize> Decode for [T; N] {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 4;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
        if size != N {
            return Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("Array size"));
        }
        let elements = T::decode_vec(decoder, N)?;
        elements.try_into().map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidValue("Array size"))
    }
}

/// `Optional`: whether there is a value, then the value.
impl<T: Encode> Encode for Option<T> {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.is_some().encode(encoder)?;
        if let Some(value) = self {
            value.encode(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        self.is_some().encode(encoder)?;
        if let Some(value) = self {
            value.encode_owned(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl<T: Decode> Decode for Option<T> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 1;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        if decoder.decode::<bool>()? {
            return Ok(Some(decoder.decode()?));
        }
        Ok(None)
    }
}

/// A boxed value goes as the value.
impl<T: Encode + ?Sized> Encode for Box<T> {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        (**self).encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl<T: Decode> Decode for Box<T> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = T::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(Self::new(decoder.decode()?))
    }
}

/// A shared value goes as the value, and decodes to one of its own.
impl<T: Encode + ?Sized> Encode for std::sync::Arc<T> {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        (**self).encode(encoder)
    }
}

impl<T: Decode> Decode for std::sync::Arc<T> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = T::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(Self::new(decoder.decode()?))
    }
}

/// A shared or boxed slice goes as a `Vector` and decodes to one of its own.
impl<T: Decode> Decode for std::sync::Arc<[T]> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = Vec::<T>::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(decoder.decode::<Vec<T>>()?.into())
    }
}

impl<T: Decode> Decode for Box<[T]> {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = Vec::<T>::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        Ok(decoder.decode::<Vec<T>>()?.into_boxed_slice())
    }
}

/// `IPC::File`: a file descriptor, which goes as an attachment.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct File(pub OwnedDescriptor);

impl Encode for File {
    fn encode(&self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        let fd = self.0.try_clone().map_err(EncodeError::Attachment)?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_fd(fd).map_err(EncodeError::Attachment)?);
        #[cfg(windows)]
        encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_descriptor(fd));
        Ok(())
    }

    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_fd(self.0).map_err(EncodeError::Attachment)?);
        #[cfg(windows)]
        encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_descriptor(self.0));
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Decode for File {
    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let attachment = decoder.take_attachment()?;
        #[cfg(windows)]
        return Ok(Self(attachment.into_descriptor()));
        #[cfg(unix)]
        Ok(Self(
            attachment
                .into_fd()
                .map_err(|error| DecodeError::Attachment(error.to_string()))?,
        ))
    }
}

/// A message of an endpoint, which goes as the endpoint's magic number, the message's ID and the message's fields.
pub trait EndpointMessage: Encode {
    const ENDPOINT_MAGIC: u32;
    const MESSAGE_ID: i32;

    fn encode_message(self) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<Attachment>), EncodeError>
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode(&Self::ENDPOINT_MAGIC)?;
        encoder.encode(&Self::MESSAGE_ID)?;
        encoder.encode_owned(self)?;
        Ok(encoder.finish())
    }
}

/// A synchronous message, and the message that answers it.
pub trait SyncMessage: EndpointMessage {
    type Response: EndpointMessage + Decode;
}

/// Reads the endpoint magic number and message ID that a message starts with.
pub fn decode_message_header(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<(u32, i32), DecodeError> {
    Ok((decoder.decode()?, decoder.decode()?))
}

/// A message as it goes to a transport: its bytes, which start with its header, and its attachments.
pub type EncodedMessage = (Vec<u8>, Vec<Attachment>);

/// What a peer did that it must not do, for which its connection is closed.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Misbehavior(pub &'static str);

/// Why the stub of an endpoint did not get to answer a message.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum DispatchError {
    Decode(DecodeError),
    Misbehavior(Misbehavior),
    EncodeResponse(EncodeError),
}

impl From<DecodeError> for DispatchError {
    fn from(error: DecodeError) -> Self {
        Self::Decode(error)
    }
}

impl From<Misbehavior> for DispatchError {
    fn from(misbehavior: Misbehavior) -> Self {
        Self::Misbehavior(misbehavior)
    }
}

impl From<EncodeError> for DispatchError {
    fn from(error: EncodeError) -> Self {
        Self::EncodeResponse(error)
    }
}

#[cfg(all(test, unix))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::os::fd::OwnedFd;

    fn round_trip<T: Encode + Decode>(value: &T) -> (T, Vec<u8>) {
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode(value).unwrap();
        let (bytes, attachments) = encoder.finish();
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, attachments);
        let decoded = decoder.decode().unwrap();
        assert!(decoder.is_at_end());
        (decoded, bytes)
    }

    #[test]
    fn sizes_are_bounded_before_contents_and_only_within_the_value() {
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode("123456789").unwrap();
        encoder.encode(&None::<String>).unwrap();
        encoder.encode("123456789").unwrap();
        let (bytes, _) = encoder.finish();
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, []);
        assert_eq!(
            decoder.decode_with_max_size::<String>(8),
            Err(DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(9))
        );
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, []);
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode_with_max_size::<String>(9).unwrap(), "123456789");
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode_with_max_size::<Option<String>>(4).unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode::<String>().unwrap(), "123456789");
    }

    #[test]
    fn numbers_go_as_their_bytes() {
        let (value, bytes) = round_trip(&0x0102_0304u32);
        assert_eq!(value, 0x0102_0304);
        assert_eq!(bytes, 0x0102_0304u32.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&-5i64).0, -5);
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&1.5f64).0, 1.5);
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&usize::MAX).1.len(), 8);
    }

    #[test]
    fn numeric_vectors_decode_from_one_payload() {
        macro_rules! check {
            ($($type:ty),*) => {$(
                let values: Vec<$type> = vec![0 as $type, 1 as $type, <$type>::MIN, <$type>::MAX];
                let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&values);
                assert_eq!(decoded, values);
                let mut expected = 4u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
                for value in &values {
                    expected.extend_from_slice(&value.to_ne_bytes());
                }
                assert_eq!(bytes, expected);
                let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
                encoder.encode_owned(values.clone()).unwrap();
                assert_eq!(encoder.finish().0, bytes);
                for length in 4..bytes.len() {
                    assert!(Decoder::new(&bytes[..length], []).decode::<Vec<$type>>().is_err());
                }
                assert!(Decoder::new(&0u32.to_ne_bytes(), []).decode::<Vec<$type>>().unwrap().is_empty());
                assert!(<$type>::decode_vec(&mut Decoder::new(&[], []), usize::MAX).is_err());
            )*};
        }
        check!(u8, u16, u32, u64, i8, i16, i32, i64, f32, f64, usize);
    }

    #[test]
    fn booleans_go_as_one_byte_and_must_be_zero_or_one() {
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&true).1, [1]);
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&[2], []);
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode::<bool>(), Err(DecodeError::InvalidBoolean(2)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn strings_go_as_their_size_and_bytes() {
        let (value, bytes) = round_trip(&"héllo".to_string());
        assert_eq!(value, "héllo");
        let mut expected = 6u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        expected.extend_from_slice("héllo".as_bytes());
        assert_eq!(bytes, expected);

        let mut invalid = 1u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        invalid.push(0xff);
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&invalid, []).decode::<String>(),
            Err(DecodeError::InvalidUtf8)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn cpp_strings_preserve_lone_surrogates() {
        for bytes in [b"".as_slice(), "héllo".as_bytes(), b"a\xed\xa0\x80\xed\xbf\xbfb"] {
            let value = Utf8String::from_bytes(bytes.to_vec()).unwrap();
            let (decoded, encoded) = round_trip(&value);
            assert_eq!(decoded.as_bytes(), bytes);
            assert_eq!(&encoded[4..], bytes);
            assert_eq!(decoded.as_str().is_ok(), std::str::from_utf8(bytes).is_ok());
            match decoded.into_string() {
                Ok(string) => assert_eq!(string.as_bytes(), bytes),
                Err(error) => assert_eq!(error.into_bytes(), bytes),
            }
            assert_eq!(value.into_bytes(), bytes);
        }
        assert_eq!(Utf8String::from("héllo").as_str(), Ok("héllo"));
        assert_eq!(Utf8String::from("hello".to_string()).into_string().unwrap(), "hello");
        for bytes in [
            b"\xff".as_slice(),
            b"\xc0\x80",
            b"\xed\xa0",
            b"\xed\xa0\x80\xff",
            b"\xf4\x90\x80\x80",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(Utf8String::from_bytes(bytes.to_vec()), Err(DecodeError::InvalidUtf8));
            let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
            encoder.encode(bytes).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                Decoder::new(&encoder.finish().0, []).decode::<Utf8String>(),
                Err(DecodeError::InvalidUtf8)
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf8_validation_accepts_lonely_surrogates() {
        assert_eq!(validate_utf8("héllo".as_bytes()), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(validate_utf8(b"a\xed\xa0\x80\xed\xbf\xbfb"), Ok(()));
        for bytes in [
            b"\xed\xa0".as_slice(),
            b"\xed\xa0\x80\xff",
            b"\xc0\x80",
            b"\xf4\x90\x80\x80",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(validate_utf8(bytes), Err(DecodeError::InvalidUtf8));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn utf16_strings_go_as_latin1_bytes_when_they_can() {
        let (value, bytes) = round_trip(&Utf16String::from("ab"));
        assert_eq!(value.to_string_lossy(), "ab");
        assert_eq!(bytes, [1, 2, 0, 0, 0, b'a', b'b']);

        for units in [vec![], vec![0x7f], vec![0x80, 0xe9, 0xff], vec![0x100, 0xd800, 0xffff]] {
            let value = Utf16String(units.clone());
            let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&value);
            assert_eq!(decoded, value);
            let is_latin1 = units.iter().all(|&unit| unit <= 0xff);
            let mut expected = vec![u8::from(is_latin1)];
            expected.extend_from_slice(&(units.len() as u32).to_ne_bytes());
            for unit in units {
                if is_latin1 {
                    expected.push(unit as u8);
                } else {
                    expected.extend_from_slice(&unit.to_ne_bytes());
                }
            }
            assert_eq!(bytes, expected);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn optionals_and_vectors_compose() {
        let value: Vec<Option<u16>> = vec![Some(1), None, Some(3)];
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&value).0, value);
        let array = [1u8, 2, 3];
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&array).0, array);
    }

    #[test]
    fn boxed_values_go_as_their_values() {
        let value: Option<Box<[u8; 3]>> = Some(Box::new([1, 2, 3]));
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&value);
        assert_eq!(decoded, value);
        assert_eq!(bytes, round_trip(&Some([1u8, 2, 3])).1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_values_go_as_their_values() {
        let value = std::sync::Arc::new(vec![1u16, 2, 3]);
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&value);
        assert_eq!(decoded, value);
        assert_eq!(bytes, round_trip(&*value).1);
        let shared_slice: std::sync::Arc<[u16]> = std::sync::Arc::from(vec![1u16, 2, 3]);
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode(&shared_slice).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(encoder.finish().0, bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn large_byte_buffers_go_as_their_size_and_bytes() {
        let buffer: Vec<u8> = (0..64 * 1024 * 1024 + 1).map(|index| index as u8).collect();
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&buffer);
        assert_eq!(decoded, buffer);
        assert_eq!(bytes[..4], (buffer.len() as u32).to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(bytes[4..], buffer);
        drop(buffer);
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode_owned(decoded).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(encoder.finish().0, bytes);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sizes_are_bounded_by_the_remaining_input() {
        let bytes = u32::MAX.to_ne_bytes();
        assert_eq!(Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode_size(), Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd));
        let bytes = [1, 0, 0, 0, 42];
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, []);
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode_size(), Ok(1));
        assert_eq!(decoder.decode::<u8>(), Ok(42));
    }

    #[test]
    fn truncated_input_is_refused() {
        let bytes = 4u32.to_ne_bytes();
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<u8>>(),
            Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&[1, 2], []).decode::<u32>(),
            Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn vector_counts_must_fit_the_element_encoding() {
        let mut bytes = (64 * 1024 * 1024u32).to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        bytes.resize(1024 * 1024, 0);
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<String>>(),
            Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)
        );
        let mut bytes = 2u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&1u64.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<u64>>(),
            Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn vectors_grow_as_elements_decode() {
        let value = vec!["a".to_string(); 100];
        let decoded = round_trip(&value).0;
        assert_eq!(decoded, value);
        assert!(decoded.capacity() <= value.len() * 2);

        let (reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let bytes = 1u32.to_ne_bytes();
        let attachments = [Attachment::from_fd(OwnedFd::from(writer)).unwrap()];
        let files = Decoder::new(&bytes, attachments).decode::<Vec<File>>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(files.len(), 1);
        drop(files);
        drop(reader);
        assert!(matches!(
            Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<File>>(),
            Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEnd)
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_vector_of_custom_types_decodes_before_reserving() {
        struct LargeValue([u8; 8192]);
        impl Decode for LargeValue {
            fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
                decoder.decode::<bool>()?;
                Ok(Self([0; 8192]))
            }
        }
        let mut bytes = 1024u32.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        bytes.resize(4 + 1024, 2);
        assert!(matches!(
            Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<LargeValue>>(),
            Err(DecodeError::InvalidBoolean(2))
        ));
        let bytes = [1, 0, 0, 0, 1];
        let decoded = Decoder::new(&bytes, []).decode::<Vec<LargeValue>>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.capacity(), 1);
        assert_eq!(decoded[0].0[0], 0);
    }

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    struct Point {
        x: i32,
        y: u8,
    }

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    struct Wrapper(u16, Option<Point>);

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    struct Nothing;

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    struct Pair<T> {
        first: T,
        second: T,
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_structs_go_as_their_fields_in_order() {
        let point = Point { x: -2, y: 7 };
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&point);
        assert_eq!(decoded, point);
        let mut expected = (-2i32).to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
        expected.push(7);
        assert_eq!(bytes, expected);
        assert_eq!(Point::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 5);

        let wrapper = Wrapper(3, Some(Point { x: 1, y: 2 }));
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&wrapper);
        assert_eq!(decoded, wrapper);
        assert_eq!(bytes[..3], [3u16.to_ne_bytes()[0], 3u16.to_ne_bytes()[1], 1]);
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 2 + 1 + 5);
        assert_eq!(Wrapper::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 3);

        assert!(round_trip(&Nothing).1.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(Nothing::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 0);

        let pair = Pair { first: 1u32, second: 2 };
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&pair).0, pair);
        assert_eq!(Pair::<u32>::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 8);
    }

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    #[ipc(validate = Self::validate)]
    struct Record {
        #[ipc(max_size = 4)]
        name: String,
        count: u32,
        #[ipc(skip = 42)]
        local: u64,
    }

    impl Record {
        fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
            if self.count == 0 {
                return Err("Record::count");
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_fields_can_be_skipped_bounded_and_validated() {
        let record = |count, local| Record {
            name: "abc".into(),
            count,
            local,
        };
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&record(1, 7));
        assert_eq!(decoded, record(1, 42));
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 4 + 3 + 4);
        assert_eq!(Record::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 8);

        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        assert!(matches!(
            encoder.encode(&record(0, 0)),
            Err(EncodeError::InvalidValue("Record::count"))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            encoder.encode_owned(record(0, 0)),
            Err(EncodeError::InvalidValue("Record::count"))
        ));
        assert!(encoder.finish().0.is_empty());

        for (name, count, error) in [
            ("abc", 0u32, DecodeError::InvalidValue("Record::count")),
            ("abcde", 1, DecodeError::SizeTooLarge(5)),
        ] {
            let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
            encoder.encode(name).unwrap();
            encoder.encode(&count).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(Decoder::new(&encoder.finish().0, []).decode::<Record>(), Err(error));
        }
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    #[repr(i16)]
    enum Key {
        Escape = 27,
        Space = 32,
        Minus = -1,
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_enums_of_unit_variants_go_as_their_repr() {
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&Key::Space);
        assert_eq!(decoded, Key::Space);
        assert_eq!(bytes, 32i16.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&Key::Escape).0, Key::Escape);
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&Key::Minus).0, Key::Minus);
        assert_eq!(Key::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 2);
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&28i16.to_ne_bytes(), []).decode::<Key>(),
            Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("Key"))
        );
    }

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Encode, Decode)]
    enum Shape {
        Empty,
        Circle(u8),
        Rectangle { width: u16, height: u16 },
    }

    #[test]
    fn other_derived_enums_go_as_their_variant_index_and_fields() {
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&Shape::Empty).1, [0]);
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&Shape::Circle(9));
        assert_eq!(decoded, Shape::Circle(9));
        assert_eq!(bytes, [1, 9]);
        let rectangle = Shape::Rectangle { width: 3, height: 4 };
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&rectangle);
        assert_eq!(decoded, rectangle);
        let mut expected = vec![2];
        expected.extend_from_slice(&3u16.to_ne_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&4u16.to_ne_bytes());
        assert_eq!(bytes, expected);
        assert_eq!(Shape::MIN_ENCODED_SIZE, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            Decoder::new(&[3], []).decode::<Shape>(),
            Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("Shape"))
        );
    }

    #[derive(Encode, Decode)]
    struct CarriedFile {
        before: u8,
        file: File,
    }

    #[derive(Encode, Decode)]
    enum MaybeFile {
        Absent,
        Present(CarriedFile),
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_types_move_their_files_when_owned() {
        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
        let (mut reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let descriptor = writer.as_raw_fd();
        let files = vec![
            MaybeFile::Absent,
            MaybeFile::Present(CarriedFile {
                before: 1,
                file: File(OwnedFd::from(writer)),
            }),
        ];
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode_owned(files).unwrap();
        let (bytes, attachments) = encoder.finish();
        assert_eq!(attachments.len(), 1);
        let files = Decoder::new(&bytes, attachments).decode::<Vec<MaybeFile>>().unwrap();
        let [MaybeFile::Absent, MaybeFile::Present(CarriedFile { before: 1, file })] = files.as_slice() else {
            panic!("the files decode as they were encoded");
        };
        #[cfg(not(target_vendor = "apple"))]
        assert_eq!(file.0.as_raw_fd(), descriptor);
        #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
        let _ = (file, descriptor);
        drop(files);
        assert_eq!(std::io::Read::read(&mut reader, &mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_and_boxed_slices_go_as_vectors() {
        let shared: std::sync::Arc<[u16]> = std::sync::Arc::from(vec![1u16, 2, 3]);
        let (decoded, bytes) = round_trip(&shared);
        assert_eq!(decoded, shared);
        assert_eq!(bytes, round_trip(&vec![1u16, 2, 3]).1);
        let boxed: Box<[String]> = vec!["a".to_string()].into_boxed_slice();
        assert_eq!(round_trip(&boxed).0, boxed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn files_go_as_attachments() {
        let (reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode(&File(OwnedFd::from(writer))).unwrap();
        let (bytes, attachments) = encoder.finish();
        assert!(bytes.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(attachments.len(), 1);

        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, attachments);
        let File(fd) = decoder.decode().unwrap();
        let mut writer = std::fs::File::from(fd);
        std::io::Write::write_all(&mut writer, b"x").unwrap();
        drop(writer);
        let mut buffer = Vec::new();
        std::io::Read::read_to_end(&mut std::fs::File::from(OwnedFd::from(reader)), &mut buffer).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(buffer, b"x");
    }

    #[test]
    fn owned_containers_move_their_files() {
        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
        let mut readers = Vec::new();
        let mut descriptors = Vec::new();
        let files: Vec<Option<[File; 1]>> = (0..32)
            .map(|_| {
                let (reader, writer) = std::io::pipe().unwrap();
                readers.push(reader);
                descriptors.push(writer.as_raw_fd());
                Some([File(OwnedFd::from(writer))])
            })
            .collect();
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        encoder.encode_owned(files).unwrap();
        let (bytes, attachments) = encoder.finish();
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&bytes, attachments);
        assert_eq!(decoder.remaining_attachments(), 32);
        let files = decoder.decode::<Vec<Option<[File; 1]>>>().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoder.remaining_attachments(), 0);
        for (file, descriptor) in files.into_iter().zip(descriptors) {
            let [File(fd)] = file.unwrap();
            #[cfg(not(target_vendor = "apple"))]
            assert_eq!(fd.as_raw_fd(), descriptor);
            #[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]
            let _ = descriptor;
            drop(fd);
        }
        for mut reader in readers {
            assert_eq!(std::io::Read::read(&mut reader, &mut [0]).unwrap(), 0);
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/RustTransportWindows.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/Atomic.h>
#include <AK/Queue.h>
#include <AK/kmalloc.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibIPC/RustTransportWindows.h>
#include <LibIPC/StartupTransport.h>
#include <LibIPC/Transport.h>

namespace IPC {

struct RustWindowsMessage {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    explicit RustWindowsMessage(Transport::Message&& message)
        : bytes(move(message.bytes))
    {
        while (!message.attachments.is_empty())
            attachments.enqueue(message.attachments.dequeue());
    }

    ReceivedMessageBytes bytes;
    Queue<Attachment> attachments;
};

struct RustWindowsTransport {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    NonnullOwnPtr<Transport> transport;
    Queue<NonnullOwnPtr<RustWindowsMessage>> received;
    Atomic<bool> eof { false };
};

}

IPC::RustWindowsTransport* ipc_windows_transport_adopt(int descriptor)
{
    auto transport = IPC::Transport::adopt_fd(descriptor);
    if (transport.is_error()) {
        (void)Core::System::close(descriptor);
        return nullptr;
    }
    return new IPC::RustWindowsTransport { transport.release_value(), {}, false };
}

IPC::RustWindowsTransport* ipc_windows_transport_take_over()
{
    auto transport = IPC::take_over_startup_transport({});
    if (transport.is_error()) {
        warnln("Rust IPC: {}", transport.error());
        return nullptr;
    }
    return new IPC::RustWindowsTransport { transport.release_value(), {}, false };
}

bool ipc_windows_transport_pair(IPC::RustWindowsTransport** local, int* remote)
{
    auto pair = Core::System::duplex_pipe();
    if (pair.is_error())
        return false;
    *remote = pair.value()[1];
    *local = ipc_windows_transport_adopt(pair.value()[0]);
    if (!*local) {
        (void)Core::System::close(*remote);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void ipc_windows_transport_destroy(IPC::RustWindowsTransport* transport)
{
    delete transport;
}

void ipc_windows_transport_close(IPC::RustWindowsTransport* transport)
{
    transport->transport->close();
}

bool ipc_windows_transport_is_open(IPC::RustWindowsTransport const* transport)
{
    return !transport->eof.load() && transport->transport->is_open();
}

bool ipc_windows_transport_send(IPC::RustWindowsTransport* transport, u8 const* bytes, size_t size, int const* descriptors, size_t descriptor_count)
{
    // Ownership of every descriptor passes to this call, even when sending fails.
    Vector<IPC::Attachment> attachments;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < descriptor_count; ++i)
        attachments.append(IPC::Attachment::from_fd(descriptors[i]));
    IPC::MessageDataType data;
    if (data.try_append(bytes, size).is_error())
        return false;
    auto result = transport->transport->post_message(move(data), attachments);
    if (result.is_error()) {
        warnln("Rust IPC: {}", result.error());
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

IPC::RustWindowsMessage* ipc_windows_transport_receive(IPC::RustWindowsTransport* transport)
{
    while (transport->received.is_empty()) {
        if (transport->eof.load())
            return nullptr;
        auto shutdown = transport->transport->read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking([&](auto&& message) {
            transport->received.enqueue(make<IPC::RustWindowsMessage>(move(message)));
        });
        if (shutdown == IPC::Transport::ShouldShutdown::Yes)
            transport->eof.store(true);
        if (!transport->received.is_empty())
            break;
        if (!transport->eof.load())
            transport->transport->wait_until_readable();
    }
    return transport->received.dequeue().leak_ptr();
}

u8 const* ipc_windows_message_bytes(IPC::RustWindowsMessage const* message, size_t* size)
{
    auto bytes = message->bytes.bytes();
    *size = bytes.size();
    return bytes.data();
}

size_t ipc_windows_message_attachment_count(IPC::RustWindowsMessage const* message)
{
    return message->attachments.size();
}

int ipc_windows_message_take_attachment(IPC::RustWindowsMessage* message)
{
    return message->attachments.dequeue().to_fd();
}

void ipc_windows_message_destroy(IPC::RustWindowsMessage* message)
{
    delete message;
}

int ipc_windows_descriptor_clone(int descriptor)
{
    auto clone = Core::System::dup(descriptor);
    if (clone.is_error())
        return -1;
    return clone.release_value();
}

void ipc_windows_descriptor_close(int descriptor)
{
    (void)Core::System::close(descriptor);
}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/SenderClaim.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/Error.h>
#include <AK/OwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <LibIPC/Forward.h>

namespace IPC {

// What a receiver must be able to answer about one message argument type. Most types ask nothing of the
// receiver, so this is empty. A type that is a claim by the sender about itself specializes it with the
// question the claim is checked against, and with the answer a receiver that tracks nothing gives.
template<typename T>
class SenderClaimReceiver {
};

namespace Detail {

// What a repeated type contributes instead, one per position so that no two of them are the same base.
template<size_t Position>
class RepeatedSenderClaimReceiver {
};

}

// A generated stub inherits these for the argument types its endpoint carries, so a receiver that
// answers for a claim overrides an inherited function instead of having to remember the question. Two
// spellings of one type contribute one base: a type that appears again later in the list is skipped.
template<typename... Ts>
class SenderClaimReceivers;

template<>
class SenderClaimReceivers<> {
};

template<typename T, typename... Rest>
class SenderClaimReceivers<T, Rest...> : public SenderClaimReceivers<Rest...>
    , public Conditional<(IsSame<T, Rest> || ...), Detail::RepeatedSenderClaimReceiver<sizeof...(Rest)>, SenderClaimReceiver<T>> {
};

// Most argument types say nothing about the sender, so verifying one accepts anything. A type that is a
// claim declares its own verify_sender_claim() beside the type, and argument-dependent lookup finds that
// one instead of this.
template<typename Stub, typename T>
bool verify_sender_claim(Stub&, T const&)
{
    return true;
}

// What generated receive code calls for every decoded argument, before the message is dispatched.
template<typename Stub, typename T>
bool verify_message_argument(Stub& stub, T const& argument)
{
    return verify_sender_claim(stub, argument);
}

// The value a bound synchronous send gets when its object no longer has a connection. If the reply
// cannot be empty, there is no value we can invent: like a failed mandatory synchronous send, it fails.
template<typename Value>
Value empty_value()
{
    if constexpr (requires { Value {}; })
        return Value {};
    else
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

// The reply a bound synchronous send gets when its object no longer has a connection: every output
// value-initialized. If a reply cannot be empty, there is no value we can invent, so it fails like a
// mandatory synchronous send on a closed connection.
template<typename Response, typename... Outputs>
Response empty_response()
{
    if constexpr (requires { Response { Outputs {}... }; })
        return Response { Outputs {}... };
    else
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

// The reply a refused synchronous message is answered with: every output value-initialized, so the
// sender learns nothing from the refusal. A reply that cannot be built empty is not sent at all.
template<typename Response, typename... Outputs>
ErrorOr<OwnPtr<MessageBuffer>> refused_reply()
{
    if constexpr (requires { Response { Outputs {}... }; }) {
        auto response = Response { Outputs {}... };
        return make<MessageBuffer>(TRY(response.encode()));
    } else {
        return Error::from_string_literal("Refused message has no empty reply");
    }
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/ThreadSafeMessagePoster.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <LibIPC/Message.h>
#include <LibIPC/ThreadSafeMessagePoster.h>

namespace IPC {

bool ThreadSafeMessagePoster::try_post(MessageBuffer& buffer)
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
    if (!m_transport || !m_transport->is_open())
        return false;
    return !buffer.transfer_message(*m_transport).is_error();
}

void ThreadSafeMessagePoster::detach_from_transport()
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_mutex);
    m_transport = nullptr;
}

static bool try_post_bytes_and_raw_attachments(void* poster, ReadonlyBytes bytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> attachments)
{
    auto buffer = adopt_encoded_message(bytes, attachments);
    return static_cast<ThreadSafeMessagePoster*>(poster)->try_post(buffer);
}

FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster ThreadSafeMessagePoster::to_ffi_with_one_reference()
{
    ref();
    return {
        .poster_with_one_reference = this,
        .try_post = try_post_bytes_and_raw_attachments,
        .ref = [](void* poster) { static_cast<ThreadSafeMessagePoster*>(poster)->ref(); },
        .unref = [](void* poster) { static_cast<ThreadSafeMessagePoster*>(poster)->unref(); },
    };
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/ThreadSafeMessagePoster.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/AtomicRefCounted.h>
#include <AK/Mutex.h>
#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/Span.h>
#include <LibIPC/Forward.h>
#include <LibIPC/RawAttachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/Transport.h>

namespace IPC {

struct FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster {
    void* poster_with_one_reference;
    bool (*try_post)(void* poster, ReadonlyBytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment>);
    void (*ref)(void* poster);
    void (*unref)(void* poster);
};
static_assert(sizeof(FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster) == 4 * sizeof(void*), "FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster of libipc_rust is written to match this by hand");

class ThreadSafeMessagePoster final : public AtomicRefCounted<ThreadSafeMessagePoster> {
public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    static NonnullRefPtr<ThreadSafeMessagePoster> create(Transport& transport) { return adopt_ref(*new ThreadSafeMessagePoster(transport)); }

    [[nodiscard]] bool try_post(MessageBuffer&);
    void detach_from_transport();

    FfiThreadSafeMessagePoster to_ffi_with_one_reference();

private:
    explicit ThreadSafeMessagePoster(Transport& transport)
        : m_transport(&transport)
    {
    }

    Mutex m_mutex;
    Transport* m_transport { nullptr };
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibIPC/Transport.cpp
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Aliaksandr Kalenik <kalenik.aliaksandr@gmail.com>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#include <AK/AllOf.h>
#include <AK/NonnullOwnPtr.h>
#include <LibCore/Notifier.h>
#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibIPC/File.h>
#include <LibIPC/RawAttachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/RustFFI.h>
#include <LibIPC/Transport.h>

namespace IPC {

struct ReadNotificationPipe {
    File read_end;
    int write_end { -1 };
};

// NB: The transport has the pipe from the start, so that what arrives before set_up_read_hook() still leaves a byte in
//     it.
static ErrorOr<ReadNotificationPipe> create_read_notification_pipe()
{
    auto fds = TRY(Core::System::pipe2(O_CLOEXEC | O_NONBLOCK));
    return ReadNotificationPipe { File::adopt_fd(fds[0]), fds[1] };
}

#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)

ErrorOr<Transport::Paired> Transport::create_paired()
{
    auto port_a_recv = TRY(Core::MachPort::create_with_right(Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive));
    auto port_a_send = TRY(port_a_recv.insert_right(Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSend));

    auto port_b_recv = TRY(Core::MachPort::create_with_right(Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive));
    auto port_b_send = TRY(port_b_recv.insert_right(Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSend));

    // The peer may receive messages before it has constructed its transport.
    raise_receive_queue_limit(port_b_recv);

    return Paired {
        TRY(create(move(port_a_recv), move(port_b_send))),
        TransportHandle { move(port_b_recv), move(port_a_send) },
    };
}

ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> Transport::create(Core::MachPort receive_right, Core::MachPort send_right)
{
    auto pipe = TRY(create_read_notification_pipe());
    auto* transport = FFI::ipc_transport_create_from_mach_ports(receive_right.release(), send_right.release(), pipe.write_end);
    if (!transport)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Transport: Unable to take over the ports");
    return adopt_own(*new Transport(transport, move(pipe.read_end)));
}

void Transport::raise_receive_queue_limit(Core::MachPort const& receive_right)
{
    FFI::ipc_mach_raise_receive_queue_limit(receive_right.port());
}

ErrorOr<TransportHandle> Transport::release_for_transfer()
{
    mach_port_t receive_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    mach_port_t send_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    if (!FFI::ipc_transport_release_mach_ports_for_transfer(m_transport, &receive_right, &send_right))
        return Error::from_string_literal("Transport: The transport was already handed over");
    return TransportHandle {
        Core::MachPort::adopt_right(receive_right, Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive),
        Core::MachPort::adopt_right(send_right, Core::MachPort::PortRight::Send),
    };
}

#else

ErrorOr<Transport::Paired> Transport::create_paired()
{
    int fds[2] {};
    // NB: Close-on-exec from the start. Another thread could spawn a process between creating the pair and marking it.
    TRY(Core::System::socketpair(AF_LOCAL, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0, fds));
    auto remote_handle = TransportHandle { File::adopt_fd(fds[1]) };
    return Paired {
        TRY(adopt_fd(fds[0])),
        move(remote_handle),
    };
}

ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> Transport::from_socket(NonnullOwnPtr<Core::LocalSocket> socket)
{
    // NB: The transport watches the socket itself. A notifier of the socket's own would outlive the descriptor in the Qt
    //     UI, which defers destroying a QSocketNotifier, and warns about one whose descriptor was closed.
    socket->set_notifications_enabled(false);
    return adopt_fd(TRY(socket->release_fd()));
}

static bool all_descriptors_are_valid(Vector<Attachment> const& attachments)
{
    return all_of(attachments, [](auto const& attachment) { return attachment.fd() >= 0; });
}

ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> Transport::adopt_fd(int fd, ByteBuffer unprocessed_bytes, Vector<Attachment> unprocessed_attachments)
{
    auto socket = File::adopt_fd(fd);
    if (socket.fd() < 0 || !all_descriptors_are_valid(unprocessed_attachments))
        return Error::from_errno(EBADF);
    // NB: The Rust transport takes over the socket and the unprocessed attachments even when it can't start.
    auto pipe = TRY(create_read_notification_pipe());
    auto raw_attachments = release_raw_attachments(move(unprocessed_attachments));
    auto* transport = FFI::ipc_transport_create_from_socket(socket.take_fd(), pipe.write_end, unprocessed_bytes.bytes(), raw_attachments.span());
    if (!transport)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Transport: Unable to take over the socket");
    return adopt_own(*new Transport(transport, move(pipe.read_end)));
}

ErrorOr<TransportHandle> Transport::release_for_transfer()
{
    Optional<TransportHandle> handle;
    auto take_handle = [](void* handle, int socket_fd, ReadonlyBytes unprocessed_bytes, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> unprocessed_attachments) {
        *static_cast<Optional<TransportHandle>*>(handle) = TransportHandle {
            File::adopt_fd(socket_fd),
            MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(unprocessed_bytes)),
            adopt_raw_attachments(unprocessed_attachments),
        };
    };
    if (!FFI::ipc_transport_release_socket_for_transfer(m_transport, &handle, take_handle))
        return Error::from_string_literal("Transport: The transport was already handed over");
    return handle.release_value();
}

#endif

Transport::Transport(FFI::RustTransport* transport, File notify_hook_read_fd)
    : m_transport(transport)
    , m_notify_hook_read_fd(move(notify_hook_read_fd))
{
}

Transport::~Transport()
{
    // NB: Destroying the transport releases the observer, after which nothing writes to the pipe.
    FFI::ipc_transport_destroy(m_transport);
    m_read_hook_notifier.clear();
}

void Transport::set_up_read_hook(Function<void()> hook)
{
    m_on_read_hook = move(hook);
    m_read_hook_notifier = Core::Notifier::construct(m_notify_hook_read_fd.fd(), Core::NotificationType::Read);
    m_read_hook_notifier->on_activation = [this] {
        char buf[64];
        (void)Core::System::read(m_notify_hook_read_fd.fd(), { buf, sizeof(buf) });
        FFI::ipc_transport_acknowledge_read_notification(m_transport);
        if (m_on_read_hook)
            m_on_read_hook();
    };
    FFI::ipc_transport_schedule_read_notification_if_readable(m_transport);
}

void Transport::set_incoming_message_observer(Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)> observer)
{
    if (!observer) {
        FFI::ipc_transport_set_incoming_message_observer(m_transport, nullptr);
        return;
    }
    // NB: The transport owns the observer, and releases the one it replaces once that no longer runs.
    FFI::CppIncomingMessageObserver const owned_observer {
        .context = new Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)>(move(observer)),
        .observe = [](void* observer, ReadonlyBytes bytes) { (*static_cast<Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)>*>(observer))(bytes); },
        .release = [](void* observer) { delete static_cast<Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)>*>(observer); },
    };
    FFI::ipc_transport_set_incoming_message_observer(m_transport, &owned_observer);
}

bool Transport::is_open() const
{
    return FFI::ipc_transport_is_open(m_transport);
}

void Transport::close()
{
    FFI::ipc_transport_close(m_transport);
}

void Transport::close_after_sending_all_pending_messages()
{
    FFI::ipc_transport_close_after_sending_all_pending_messages(m_transport);
}

void Transport::wait_until_readable(Optional<MonotonicTime> deadline)
{
    // NB: Rust checks the deadline on the clock MonotonicTime reads, which keeps counting while the system sleeps.
    FFI::ipc_transport_wait_until_readable(m_transport, deadline.has_value(), deadline.has_value() ? deadline->nanoseconds() : 0);
}

void Transport::interrupt_wait_until_readable()
{
    FFI::ipc_transport_interrupt_wait_until_readable(m_transport);
}

void Transport::flush()
{
    FFI::ipc_transport_flush(m_transport);
}

void Transport::wait_until_incoming_is_current()
{
    FFI::ipc_transport_wait_until_incoming_is_current(m_transport);
}

ErrorOr<void> Transport::post_message(MessageDataType bytes, Vector<Attachment>& attachments)
{
#if !defined(AK_OS_MACOS) && !defined(AK_OS_IOS)
    // NB: Every descriptor goes to the Rust transport, which can't hold an invalid one.
    if (!all_descriptors_are_valid(attachments))
        return Error::from_errno(EBADF);
#endif
    auto raw_attachments = release_raw_attachments(move(attachments));
    // NB: A message that has to wait behind others keeps the buffer it was encoded into, rather than a copy.
    auto hand_over_payload = [](void* bytes) -> FFI::HandedOverPayload {
        auto* payload = new MessageDataType(move(*static_cast<MessageDataType*>(bytes)));
        return {
            .data = payload->data(),
            .size = payload->size(),
            .owner = payload,
            .release = [](void* payload) { delete static_cast<MessageDataType*>(payload); },
        };
    };
    // NB: The transport refuses a message once it no longer counts as open, and one it can't prepare for sending, as a
    //     payload whose shared memory it can't create.
    if (!FFI::ipc_transport_post(m_transport, bytes.span(), raw_attachments.span(), &bytes, hand_over_payload))
        return Error::from_string_literal("Transport: The transport refused the message");
    return {};
}

Transport::ShouldShutdown Transport::read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking(Function<void(Message&&)>&& callback)
{
    auto take_message = [](void* callback, ReadonlyBytes bytes, FFI::ReceivedPayload* payload, ReadonlySpan<RawAttachment> raw_attachments) {
        Message message;
        message.bytes = ReceivedMessageBytes::adopt_foreign_storage(bytes, payload, [](void* payload) {
            FFI::ipc_received_payload_destroy(static_cast<FFI::ReceivedPayload*>(payload));
        });
        for (auto& attachment : adopt_raw_attachments(raw_attachments))
            message.attachments.enqueue(move(attachment));
        (*static_cast<Function<void(Message&&)>*>(callback))(move(message));
    };
    auto peer_eof = FFI::ipc_transport_take_incoming(m_transport, &callback, take_message);
    return peer_eof ? ShouldShutdown::Yes : ShouldShutdown::No;
}

}

#    include <LibIPC/ReceivedMessageBytes.h>

#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
#        include <LibCore/MachPort.h>
#    endif
#endif

namespace IPC {

#if !defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)

namespace FFI {

struct RustTransport;

}

// The transport of LibIPC's Rust crate, over Mach ports on Darwin and a Unix domain socket elsewhere. It does the IO on
// one thread that every transport in the process shares.
class Transport {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Transport);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Transport);

public:
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    struct Paired {
        NonnullOwnPtr<Transport> local;
        TransportHandle remote_handle;
    };
    static ErrorOr<Paired> create_paired();

#    if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
    static ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> create(Core::MachPort receive_right, Core::MachPort send_right);
    static void raise_receive_queue_limit(Core::MachPort const&);
#    else
    static ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> from_socket(NonnullOwnPtr<Core::LocalSocket>);

    // The bytes and attachments are what the last owner read off the socket without seeing the end of the message.
    static ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> adopt_fd(int fd, ByteBuffer unprocessed_bytes = {}, Vector<Attachment> unprocessed_attachments = {});
#    endif

    ~Transport();

    void set_up_read_hook(Function<void()>);

    // Sets what the IO thread shows every message that arrives, before the transport's owner gets to see it, and empty
    // bytes once the peer is gone. This is for a thread that does not get back to its event loop on its own, like one
    // stuck in script. It runs while the IO thread holds a lock, so it should only have a look.
    void set_incoming_message_observer(Function<void(ReadonlyBytes)>);

    // False once this end is closed or asked to stop, a send has failed, or the peer is gone.
    bool is_open() const;

    void close();
    void close_after_sending_all_pending_messages();

    // Returns at the deadline as well, if one is given.
    void wait_until_readable(Optional<MonotonicTime> deadline = {});

    // Makes wait_until_readable() return, even with nothing to read, now or if none is under way, the next time. Any
    // thread may call this.
    void interrupt_wait_until_readable();

    // Wait until everything posted so far has been handed to the kernel.
    void flush();

    // Wait until everything the peer has already sent has been taken into the incoming queue.
    void wait_until_incoming_is_current();

    ErrorOr<void> post_message(MessageDataType, Vector<Attachment>& attachments);

    enum class ShouldShutdown {
        No,
        Yes,
    };
    struct Message {
        AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

        ReceivedMessageBytes bytes;
        Queue<Attachment> attachments;
    };
    ShouldShutdown read_as_many_messages_as_possible_without_blocking(Function<void(Message&&)>&&);

    // Whole messages that have arrived stay here for the old owner to take, and anything newer reaches the new owner.
    ErrorOr<TransportHandle> release_for_transfer();

private:
    Transport(FFI::RustTransport*, File notify_hook_read_fd);

    FFI::RustTransport* m_transport { nullptr };

    File m_notify_hook_read_fd;
    RefPtr<Core::Notifier> m_read_hook_notifier;
    Function<void()> m_on_read_hook;
};

#endif

}

#include <AK/ByteString.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <LibCore/MachPort.h>
#include <LibIPC/RustFFI.h>
#include <LibIPC/TransportBootstrapMach.h>

namespace IPC {

static TransportBootstrapMachPorts adopt_transport_ports(u32 receive_right, u32 send_right)
{
    return TransportBootstrapMachPorts {
        .receive_right = Core::MachPort::adopt_right(receive_right, Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive),
        .send_right = Core::MachPort::adopt_right(send_right, Core::MachPort::PortRight::Send),
    };
}

ErrorOr<TransportBootstrapMachPorts> bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(Core::MachPort const& server_port, AK::Duration reply_timeout)
{
    u32 receive_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    u32 send_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    i32 kernel_error = KERN_SUCCESS;
    auto const reply_timeout_in_milliseconds = static_cast<u32>(clamp<i64>(reply_timeout.to_milliseconds(), 0, NumericLimits<u32>::max()));
    switch (FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(server_port.port(), reply_timeout_in_milliseconds, &receive_right, &send_right, &kernel_error)) {
    case FFI::BootstrapOutcome::Received:
        return adopt_transport_ports(receive_right, send_right);
    case FFI::BootstrapOutcome::KernelError:
        return Core::mach_error_to_error(kernel_error);
    case FFI::BootstrapOutcome::ServerClosedBeforeReplying:
        return Error::from_string_literal("Mach bootstrap server closed before replying");
    case FFI::BootstrapOutcome::MalformedReply:
        return Error::from_string_literal("Malformed Mach bootstrap reply");
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

ErrorOr<TransportBootstrapMachPorts> bootstrap_transport_from_mach_server(StringView server_name)
{
    auto server_port = TRY(Core::MachPort::look_up_from_bootstrap_server(ByteString { server_name }));
    return bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(server_port);
}

TransportBootstrapMachServer::TransportBootstrapMachServer()
    : m_server(FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_create())
{
}

TransportBootstrapMachServer::~TransportBootstrapMachServer()
{
    FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_destroy(m_server);
}

void TransportBootstrapMachServer::register_child_transport(pid_t pid, TransportBootstrapMachPorts ports)
{
    FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_register_child_transport(m_server, pid, ports.receive_right.release(), ports.send_right.release());
}

void TransportBootstrapMachServer::unregister_child_transport(pid_t pid)
{
    MutexLocker locker(m_child_registration_mutex);
    FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_unregister_child_transport(m_server, pid);
}

ErrorOr<TransportBootstrapMachServer::BootstrapRequestResult> TransportBootstrapMachServer::handle_bootstrap_request(pid_t pid, Core::MachPort reply_port)
{
    Optional<TransportBootstrapMachPorts> child_transport;
    {
        MutexLocker locker(m_child_registration_mutex);
        u32 receive_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
        u32 send_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
        if (FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_server_take_child_transport(m_server, pid, &receive_right, &send_right))
            child_transport = adopt_transport_ports(receive_right, send_right);
    }

    if (child_transport.has_value()) {
        auto ports = child_transport.release_value();
        auto const result = FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_send_transport_ports_to_child(reply_port.release(), ports.receive_right.release(), ports.send_right.release());
        if (result != KERN_SUCCESS)
            return Core::mach_error_to_error(result);
        return ChildTransportHandled {};
    }

    u32 receive_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    u32 send_right = MACH_PORT_NULL;
    auto const result = FFI::ipc_mach_bootstrap_create_on_demand_local_transport(reply_port.release(), &receive_right, &send_right);
    if (result != KERN_SUCCESS)
        return Core::mach_error_to_error(result);
    return OnDemandTransport { .ports = adopt_transport_ports(receive_right, send_right) };
}

}

/*

#pragma once

#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>
#include <AK/Time.h>
#include <AK/Variant.h>

#if !defined(AK_OS_MACH)
#    error "TransportBootstrapMach is only available on Mach platforms"
#endif

#include <AK/Mutex.h>
#include <LibCore/MachPort.h>

namespace IPC {

namespace FFI {

struct BootstrapServer;

}

struct TransportBootstrapMachPorts {
    Core::MachPort receive_right;
    Core::MachPort send_right;
};

ErrorOr<TransportBootstrapMachPorts> bootstrap_transport_from_mach_server(StringView server_name);
ErrorOr<TransportBootstrapMachPorts> bootstrap_transport_from_server_port(Core::MachPort const& server_port, AK::Duration reply_timeout = AK::Duration::from_seconds(5));

class TransportBootstrapMachServer {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(TransportBootstrapMachServer);

public:
    TransportBootstrapMachServer();
    ~TransportBootstrapMachServer();

    struct ChildTransportHandled {
    };
    struct OnDemandTransport {
        TransportBootstrapMachPorts ports;
    };
    using BootstrapRequestResult = Variant<ChildTransportHandled, OnDemandTransport>;

    // Hold this lock across process spawn and child transport registration so a
    // child bootstrap request cannot observe an unregistered pid.
    Mutex& child_registration_lock() { return m_child_registration_mutex; }

    // Must be called while holding child_registration_lock().
    // NB: Until the child asks for its ports, we hold them ourselves, so nothing would tell the other end of the
    //     transport that the child is gone. A child that exits before it asks is unregistered from a thread of our
    //     own, so that this also happens while the thread that spawned the child waits for the child to answer.
    void register_child_transport(pid_t, TransportBootstrapMachPorts);
    // For a child that was ended before it asked for its transport.
    void unregister_child_transport(pid_t);
    ErrorOr<BootstrapRequestResult> handle_bootstrap_request(pid_t, Core::MachPort reply_port);

private:
    Mutex m_child_registration_mutex;
    FFI::BootstrapServer* m_server { nullptr };
};

}

/*

#include <LibCore/System.h>
#include <LibIPC/Attachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/Decoder.h>
#include <LibIPC/Encoder.h>
#include <LibIPC/Transport.h>
#include <LibIPC/TransportHandle.h>

#if !defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
#    include <sys/socket.h>
#endif

namespace IPC {

static ErrorOr<void> encode_unprocessed(Encoder& encoder, ByteBuffer const& bytes, Vector<Attachment>& attachments)
{
    TRY(encoder.encode(bytes));
    TRY(encoder.encode_size(attachments.size()));
    for (auto& attachment : attachments)
        TRY(encoder.append_attachment(move(attachment)));
    attachments.clear();
    return {};
}

static ErrorOr<void> decode_unprocessed(Decoder& decoder, ByteBuffer& bytes, Vector<Attachment>& attachments)
{
    bytes = TRY(decoder.decode<ByteBuffer>());
    auto attachment_count = TRY(decoder.decode_size());
    if (attachment_count > decoder.attachments().size())
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::decode: Missing attachments");
    TRY(attachments.try_ensure_capacity(attachment_count));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < attachment_count; ++i)
        attachments.unchecked_append(decoder.attachments().dequeue());
    return {};
}

#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)

TransportHandle::TransportHandle(Core::MachPort receive_right, Core::MachPort send_right)
    : m_receive_right(move(receive_right))
    , m_send_right(move(send_right))
{
    VERIFY(MACH_PORT_VALID(m_receive_right.port()));
    // NB: The send right is MACH_PORT_DEAD if the peer closed its end while this handle was in flight. The transport
    // built from it has nobody to send to — but it still reads whatever the peer sent before closing, and then the
    // no-senders notification reports the peer gone. WebKit's Connection::receiveSourceEventHandler does the same for
    // a connection whose send right arrives dead.
    VERIFY(m_send_right.port() != MACH_PORT_NULL);
}

ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> TransportHandle::create_transport() const
{
    VERIFY(MACH_PORT_VALID(m_receive_right.port()));
    VERIFY(m_send_right.port() != MACH_PORT_NULL);
    return Transport::create(move(m_receive_right), move(m_send_right));
}

ErrorOr<TransportHandlePair> TransportHandle::create_pair()
{
    auto port_a_receive_right = TRY(Core::MachPort::create_with_right(Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive));
    auto port_a_send_right = TRY(port_a_receive_right.insert_right(Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSend));
    auto port_b_receive_right = TRY(Core::MachPort::create_with_right(Core::MachPort::PortRight::Receive));
    auto port_b_send_right = TRY(port_b_receive_right.insert_right(Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MakeSend));

    // Either end may be written to before the other has constructed its transport.
    Transport::raise_receive_queue_limit(port_a_receive_right);
    Transport::raise_receive_queue_limit(port_b_receive_right);

    return TransportHandlePair {
        TransportHandle { move(port_a_receive_right), move(port_b_send_right) },
        TransportHandle { move(port_b_receive_right), move(port_a_send_right) },
    };
}

template<>
ErrorOr<void> encode(Encoder& encoder, TransportHandle const& handle)
{
    mach_port_t send_port = handle.m_send_right.port();
    mach_port_t receive_port = handle.m_receive_right.port();
    // NB: A dead send right is fine to pass along; the next owner finds the peer gone, same as this one did.
    if (send_port == MACH_PORT_NULL || receive_port == MACH_PORT_NULL || receive_port == MACH_PORT_DEAD)
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::encode: Invalid Mach port(s)");

    TRY(encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_mach_port(move(handle.m_receive_right), Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveReceive)));
    TRY(encoder.append_attachment(Attachment::from_mach_port(move(handle.m_send_right), Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveSend)));
    return encode_unprocessed(encoder, handle.m_unprocessed_bytes, handle.m_unprocessed_attachments);
}

template<>
ErrorOr<TransportHandle> decode(Decoder& decoder)
{
    // The attachments come from the peer, so a message that lacks them, or carries other rights in their place, is
    // a malformed message to reject, not an invariant of ours to assert.
    auto& attachments = decoder.attachments();
    auto recv_attachment = TRY(attachments.try_dequeue());
    auto send_attachment = TRY(attachments.try_dequeue());
    if (recv_attachment.message_right() != Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveReceive)
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::decode: Expected a receive right");
    if (send_attachment.message_right() != Core::MachPort::MessageRight::MoveSend)
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::decode: Expected a send right");
    auto receive_right = recv_attachment.release_mach_port();
    auto send_right = send_attachment.release_mach_port();
    // The kernel passes a dead name along with whatever disposition the sender gave it, but a receive right can't have
    // died in flight the way a send right can.
    if (!MACH_PORT_VALID(receive_right.port()))
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::decode: Expected a live receive right");
    if (send_right.port() == MACH_PORT_NULL)
        return Error::from_string_literal("TransportHandle::decode: Expected a send right");
    TransportHandle handle { move(receive_right), move(send_right) };
    TRY(decode_unprocessed(decoder, handle.m_unprocessed_bytes, handle.m_unprocessed_attachments));
    return handle;
}

#else

TransportHandle::TransportHandle(File file)
    : m_file(move(file))
{
}

TransportHandle::TransportHandle(File file, ByteBuffer unprocessed_bytes, Vector<Attachment> unprocessed_attachments)
    : m_file(move(file))
    , m_unprocessed_bytes(move(unprocessed_bytes))
    , m_unprocessed_attachments(move(unprocessed_attachments))
{
}

ErrorOr<NonnullOwnPtr<Transport>> TransportHandle::create_transport() const
{
#    if defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
    return Transport::adopt_fd(m_file.take_fd());
#    else
    return Transport::adopt_fd(m_file.take_fd(), move(m_unprocessed_bytes), move(m_unprocessed_attachments));
#    endif
}

ErrorOr<TransportHandlePair> TransportHandle::create_pair()
{
#    if defined(AK_OS_WINDOWS)
    auto handles = TRY(Core::System::duplex_pipe());
    return TransportHandlePair { TransportHandle { File::adopt_fd(handles[0]) }, TransportHandle { File::adopt_fd(handles[1]) } };
#    else
    int fds[2] {};
    TRY(Core::System::socketpair(AF_LOCAL, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0, fds));
    return TransportHandlePair { TransportHandle { File::adopt_fd(fds[0]) }, TransportHandle { File::adopt_fd(fds[1]) } };
#    endif
}

template<>
ErrorOr<void> encode(Encoder& encoder, TransportHandle const& handle)
{
    TRY(encoder.encode(handle.m_file));
    return encode_unprocessed(encoder, handle.m_unprocessed_bytes, handle.m_unprocessed_attachments);
}

template<>
ErrorOr<TransportHandle> decode(Decoder& decoder)
{
    TransportHandle handle { TRY(decoder.decode<File>()) };
    TRY(decode_unprocessed(decoder, handle.m_unprocessed_bytes, handle.m_unprocessed_attachments));
    return handle;
}

#endif

#pragma once

#include <AK/ByteBuffer.h>
#include <AK/Error.h>
#include <AK/Noncopyable.h>
#include <AK/NonnullOwnPtr.h>
#include <AK/Platform.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibIPC/Attachment.h>
#include <LibIPC/File.h>
#include <LibIPC/Forward.h>

#if defined(AK_OS_MACOS) || defined(AK_OS_IOS)
#    include <LibCore/MachPort.h>
