        RawNativeFunction => "RawNativeFunction", Some(8), true;
        DirectGetterFunction => "DirectGetterFunction", Some(8), true;
        SharedFunctionInstanceData => "SharedFunctionInstanceData", Some(8), true;
        PropertyStorage => "PropertyStorage", Some(8), true;
    }
    source {
        F64 => "f64", Some(8), false;
        F32 => "f32", Some(4), false;
        V128 => "v128", Some(16), false;
        InlineInt32 => "Int32", Some(4), false;
        SlotIndex => "SlotIndex", Some(4), false;
        BytecodeOffset => "BytecodeOffset", Some(4), false;
        EnvironmentCoordinateCacheIndex => "EnvironmentCoordinateCacheIndex", Some(2), false;
        GlobalVariableCacheIndex => "GlobalVariableCacheIndex", Some(2), false;
        PropertyLookupCacheIndex => "PropertyLookupCacheIndex", Some(2), false;
        ProfiledPropertyLookupCacheIndex => "ProfiledPropertyLookupCacheIndex", Some(2), false;
        ArithFeedbackIndex => "ArithFeedbackIndex", Some(2), false;
        ValueFeedbackIndex => "ValueFeedbackIndex", Some(2), false;
        CallFeedbackIndex => "CallFeedbackIndex", Some(2), false;
        KeyedFeedbackIndex => "KeyedFeedbackIndex", Some(2), false;
        Operand => "Operand", Some(8), false;
        Memory => "Memory", None, false;
        IntegerCondition => "IntegerCondition", None, false;
        FloatCondition => "FloatCondition", None, false;
        EqualityOperation => "EqualityOperation", None, false;

        Pointer(Box<Type>);

        Continuation(Vec<Type>);
        BinaryOperation(Box<Type>);
        CheckedBinaryOperation(Box<Type>);
        Tuple(Vec<Type>);
    }
}

impl Type {
    pub(crate) fn label() -> Self {
        Self::Continuation(Vec::new())
    }

    pub(crate) fn width(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        match self {
            Type::Boxed(_) | Type::Sequence(_) | Type::Pointer(_) | Type::Continuation(_) => Some(8),
            Type::Field(_) | Type::BinaryOperation(_) | Type::CheckedBinaryOperation(_) | Type::Tuple(_) => None,
            _ => self.simple_width(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn register_class(&self) -> Option<RegisterClass> {
        match self {
            Type::F32 | Type::F64 => Some(RegisterClass::FloatingPoint),
            Type::V128 => Some(RegisterClass::Vector),
            _ if self.width().is_some() => Some(RegisterClass::GeneralPurpose),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_operation(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Type::BinaryOperation(_)
                | Type::CheckedBinaryOperation(_)
                | Type::IntegerCondition
                | Type::FloatCondition
                | Type::EqualityOperation
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_pointer(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Type::Pointer(_) | Type::Sequence(_)) || self.simple_is_pointer()
    }

    pub(crate) fn memory_load(&self) -> Option<MemoryOperation> {
        Some(match self {
            Type::U8 | Type::Bool => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::Byte,
                signed: false,
            },
            Type::I8 => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::Byte,
                signed: true,
            },
            Type::U16 => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::HalfWord,
                signed: false,
            },
            Type::I16 => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::HalfWord,
                signed: true,
            },
            Type::U32 | Type::I32 | Type::ValueTag => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::Word,
                signed: false,
            },
            Type::F32 => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::Float,
                signed: false,
            },
            Type::F64 | Type::V128 => return None,
            _ if self.width() == Some(8) => MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::DoubleWord,
                signed: false,
            },
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_layout_type_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        if let Some(inner) = name.strip_prefix("Value<").and_then(|name| name.strip_suffix('>')) {
            return Self::from_layout_type_name(inner).map(|inner| Self::Boxed(Box::new(inner)));
        }
        if let Some(element) = name.strip_prefix("Sequence<").and_then(|name| name.strip_suffix('>')) {
            return Self::from_layout_type_name(element).map(|element| Self::Sequence(Box::new(element)));
        }
        Some(match name {
            "BindingFlags" => Self::Sequence(Box::new(Self::U8)),
            "IndexedElements" | "BindingValues" => Self::Sequence(Box::new(Self::Value)),
            "GlobalVariableCaches" => Self::Sequence(Box::new(Self::GlobalVariableCache)),
            "PropertyLookupCaches" => Self::Sequence(Box::new(Self::PropertyLookupCache)),
            _ => Self::from_layout_name(name)?,
        })
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Type {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        if let Some(name) = self.simple_name() {
            return formatter.write_str(name);
        }
        match self {
            Type::Boxed(inner) => write!(formatter, "Value<{inner}>"),
            Type::Sequence(inner) => write!(formatter, "Sequence<{inner}>"),
            Type::Pointer(inner) => write!(formatter, "ptr<{inner}>"),
            Type::Field(inner) => write!(formatter, "Field<{inner}>"),
            Type::Operand => write!(formatter, "Operand"),
            Type::Continuation(parameters) if parameters.is_empty() => write!(formatter, "Label"),
            Type::Continuation(parameters) => {
                write!(formatter, "Continuation<(")?;
                for (index, parameter) in parameters.iter().enumerate() {
                    if index != 0 {
                        write!(formatter, ", ")?;
                    }
                    write!(formatter, "{parameter}")?;
                }
                write!(formatter, ")>")
            }
            Type::BinaryOperation(inner) => write!(formatter, "BinaryOperation<{inner}>"),
            Type::CheckedBinaryOperation(inner) => write!(formatter, "CheckedBinaryOperation<{inner}>"),
            Type::Tuple(elements) => {
                write!(formatter, "(")?;
                for (index, element) in elements.iter().enumerate() {
                    if index != 0 {
                        write!(formatter, ", ")?;
                    }
                    write!(formatter, "{element}")?;
                }
                write!(formatter, ")")
            }
            _ => unreachable!("simple types have registry names"),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn centralizes_storage_and_register_properties() {
        assert_eq!(Type::U16.width(), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(Type::F64.register_class(), Some(RegisterClass::FloatingPoint));
        assert_eq!(
            Type::I32.memory_load().unwrap(),
            MemoryOperation::Load {
                width: MemoryWidth::Word,
                signed: false
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(Type::F64.memory_load(), None);
        assert!(Type::Object.is_pointer());
    }

    #[test]
    fn centralizes_interpreter_register_types() {
        assert_eq!(
            InterpreterRegister::from_name("values").unwrap().value_type(),
            Type::Sequence(Box::new(Type::Value))
        );
        assert_eq!(InterpreterRegister::from_name("pc").unwrap().value_type(), Type::U32);
        assert_eq!(InterpreterRegister::ProgramBase.as_str(), "pb");
        assert_eq!(InterpreterRegister::HeapRegionBase.source_value_type(), None);
        assert_eq!(InterpreterRegister::from_name("temporary"), None);
        assert_eq!(
            RegisterReference::new("pb"),
            RegisterReference::Interpreter(InterpreterRegister::ProgramBase)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            RegisterReference::new("temporary"),
            RegisterReference::Named("temporary".into())
        );
    }
}

/*

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, SourceInput, Target};

fn compile(body: &str, architecture: Architecture, enabled: bool) -> String {
    let source = format!("handler Check(input: in Operand) {{ {body} dispatch_next; }}");
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target: Target {
            architecture,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: enabled,
        profiling: false,
        profile: flapc::Profile::JavaScript,
    })
    .compile(CompilationUnit {
        source: SourceInput {
            name: "assertions.flap",
            contents: &source,
        },
        constants: Some(SourceInput {
            name: "layout.conf",
            contents: include_str!("interpreter-layout.conf"),
        }),
    })
    .unwrap()
    .as_str()
    .to_owned()
}

fn traps(assembly: &str, architecture: Architecture) -> usize {
    assembly
        .matches(match architecture {
            Architecture::X86_64 => "    ud2",
            Architecture::Aarch64 => "    brk",
        })
        .count()
}

#[test]
fn removes_assertions_proven_by_constants_ranges_and_successful_guards() {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        for body in [
            "assert(true);",
            "assert(!false);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(extract_tag(box_i32(number)) == INT32_TAG);",
            "let number: u64 = 42; assert(number > 0);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); let masked = number & 255; assert(u32(masked) < 256);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); guard number < 10 else @cold { exit; }; assert(number < 10);",
        ] {
            let assembly = compile(body, architecture, true);
            assert_eq!(traps(&assembly, architecture), 0, "{body}\n{assembly}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn preserves_dynamic_and_always_false_assertions() {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        for body in [
            "assert(false);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(!(number < 10));",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(number has 1);",
            "let number = i32(0xffffffff); assert(u32(number) < 128);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); let masked = number & 0x80000000; assert(masked >= 0);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); if number < 10 { } else { assert(number < 10); }",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(number < 10);",
            "assert(extract_tag(load(input)) == STRING_TAG);",
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); if number < 10 { let ignored: u64 = 1; } assert(number < 10);",
        ] {
            let assembly = compile(body, architecture, true);
            assert_eq!(traps(&assembly, architecture), 1, "{body}\n{assembly}");
            let (normal, _) = assembly.split_once("asm_assertion_failure_traps:").unwrap();
            assert_eq!(traps(normal, architecture), 0);
            assert_eq!(traps(&compile(body, architecture, false), architecture), 0);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn lowers_comparison_assertions_directly_to_failure_branches() {
    for (architecture, branch, boolean_materialization) in [
        (Architecture::X86_64, "    jge ", "    set"),
        (Architecture::Aarch64, "    b.ge ", "    cset "),
    ] {
        let assembly = compile(
            "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(number < 10);",
            architecture,
            true,
        );
        assert!(
            assembly
                .lines()
                .any(|line| line.starts_with(branch) && line.contains("assert_predicate_failure")),
            "{assembly}"
        );
        assert!(!assembly.contains(boolean_materialization), "{assembly}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn aarch64_bit_assertions_fall_through_on_success() {
    let assembly = compile(
        "let number = unbox_i32(load(input)); assert(number has 1);",
        Architecture::Aarch64,
        true,
    );
    assert!(assembly.contains("    tst "));
    assert!(
        assembly
            .lines()
            .any(|line| line.starts_with("    b.eq ") && line.contains("assert_predicate_failure"))
    );
    let handler = assembly
        .split_once("asm_handler_Check:")
        .unwrap()
        .1
        .split_once("asm_handler_Check_hot_end:")
        .unwrap()
        .0;
    assert!(!handler.contains("    tbz ") && !handler.contains("    tbnz "));
}

#[test]
fn folds_layout_value_tags_into_immediate_comparisons() {
    let assembly = compile(
        "assert(extract_tag(load(input)) != extract_tag(Value<Empty>));",
        Architecture::X86_64,
        true,
    );
    assert!(
        assembly
            .lines()
            .any(|line| line.starts_with("    cmp ") && line.ends_with(", 32763")),
        "{assembly}"
    );
    assert!(
        !assembly
            .lines()
            .any(|line| line.starts_with("    mov ") && line.ends_with(", 32763"))
    );
}

#[test]
fn reuses_tag_extractions_across_assertions() {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        for (body, expected_traps) in [
            (
                "let value = load(input); assert(extract_tag(value) == STRING_TAG); assert(extract_tag(value) == STRING_TAG);",
                1,
            ),
            (
                "let tag = extract_tag(load(input)); assert(tag == STRING_TAG); assert(tag == STRING_TAG);",
                1,
            ),
            (
                "let value = load(input); assert(extract_tag(value) != STRING_TAG); assert(extract_tag(value) != INT32_TAG);",
                2,
            ),
        ] {
            let assembly = compile(body, architecture, true);
            assert_eq!(traps(&assembly, architecture), expected_traps, "{body}\n{assembly}");
            let shift = match architecture {
                Architecture::X86_64 => "    shr ",
                Architecture::Aarch64 => "    lsr ",
            };
            assert_eq!(
                assembly.lines().filter(|line| line.starts_with(shift)).count(),
                1,
                "{body}\n{assembly}"
            );
        }
    }
}

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, SourceInput, Target};

fn compile(source: &str, architecture: Architecture) -> Result<String, String> {
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target: Target {
            architecture,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: flapc::Profile::JavaScript,
    })
    .compile(CompilationUnit {
        source: SourceInput {
            name: "closures.flap",
            contents: source,
        },
        constants: Some(SourceInput {
            name: "layout.conf",
            contents: include_str!("interpreter-layout.conf"),
        }),
    })
    .map(|assembly| assembly.as_str().to_owned())
    .map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
}

fn assert_compiles(source: &str) {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        if let Err(error) = compile(source, architecture) {
            panic!("{error}\n{source}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn compiles_closures_that_no_path_reaches() {
    // The body of an unused closure is unreachable. Inlining the call in it
    // splits the block, which must not make the uses after the call invalid.
    assert_compiles(
        r#"
inline fn note(value: Value) {
}

handler Unused(dst: out Operand, src: in Operand) {
    let slow = || @cold {
        exit;
    };
    let unused = |raw: i32| {
        let produced: Value = box_i32(raw);
        note(produced);
        store(dst, produced);
        dispatch_next;
    };
    let unused_with_label = |raw: i32| {
        guard let Value<i32>(value) = load(src) else slow;
        store(dst, box_i32(value + raw));
        dispatch_next;
    };
    store(dst, load(src));
    dispatch_next;
}
"#,
    );
}

#[test]
fn compiles_closures_passed_as_the_failure_label_of_an_inline_function() {
    // The closure is entered from inside the inline function, and its body
    // passes a label of its own to another inline function call.
    assert_compiles(
        r#"
inline fn check(value: i32, else fail: Label) -> i32 {
    guard value != 0 else fail;
    value
}

inline fn pick(value: i32, other: Label, else fail: Label) -> i32 {
    guard value != 1 else fail;
    branch_eq(value, 2, other);
    value
}

handler Checked(dst: out Operand, src: in Operand) {
    let slow = || @cold {
        exit;
    };
    let other = || @cold {
        exit;
    };
    let fallback = |raw: i32| {
        guard let picked = pick(raw, other) else slow;
        store(dst, box_i32(picked));
        dispatch_next;
    };
    guard let Value<i32>(value) = load(src) else slow;
    guard let checked = check(value) else fallback(value);
    store(dst, box_i32(checked));
    dispatch_next;
}
"#,
    );
}

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, SourceInput, Target};
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

const INTERPRETER: &str = include_str!("../../Interpreter/interpreter.flap");
const LAYOUT: &str = include_str!("interpreter-layout.conf");

fn compile_interpreter(architecture: Architecture) -> String {
    compile_interpreter_for(Target {
        architecture,
        object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
    })
}

fn compile_interpreter_for(target: Target) -> String {
    let compiler = Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target,
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: flapc::Profile::JavaScript,
    });
    compiler
        .compile(CompilationUnit {
            source: SourceInput {
                name: "interpreter.flap",
                contents: INTERPRETER,
            },
            constants: Some(SourceInput {
                name: "interpreter-layout.conf",
                contents: LAYOUT,
            }),
        })
        .expect("interpreter compilation should succeed")
        .as_str()
        .to_owned()
}

fn snapshot_path(file_name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("tests")
        .join("interpreter-assembly")
        .join(file_name)
}

fn compare_or_rebaseline(file_name: &str, assembly: &str) {
    let path = snapshot_path(file_name);
    if std::env::var_os("FLAP_REBASELINE").is_some() {
        fs::write(&path, assembly).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to write {}: {error}", path.display()));
        return;
    }

    let expected =
        fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to read {}: {error}", path.display()));
    assert!(
        assembly == expected,
        "{} is out of date; rebaseline with FLAP_REBASELINE=1 cargo test --test interpreter_assembly",
        path.display()
    );
}

#[test]
fn interpreter_assembly_matches_snapshots() {
    compare_or_rebaseline("x86_64.S", &compile_interpreter(Architecture::X86_64));
    compare_or_rebaseline("aarch64.S", &compile_interpreter(Architecture::Aarch64));
}

/// Handlers move the stack pointer around their calls, so a stack walk can only find the frame through rbp.
#[test]
fn describes_the_windows_frame_by_its_frame_register() {
    let assembly = compile_interpreter_for(Target {
        architecture: Architecture::X86_64,
        object_format: ObjectFormat::Coff,
    });
    let prologue_start = assembly.find("    .seh_pushreg rbp\n").unwrap();
    let prologue_end = assembly.find("    .seh_endprologue\n").unwrap();
    let prologue = &assembly[prologue_start..prologue_end];
    assert_eq!(prologue.matches("    push ").count(), 7, "{prologue}");
    assert!(prologue.contains("    sub rsp, 56\n"), "{prologue}");
    // NB: Seven saved registers of 8 bytes each, and the 56 bytes below them.
    assert!(prologue.ends_with("    .seh_setframe rbp, 112\n"), "{prologue}");
}

#[test]
fn keeps_helper_setup_out_of_the_hot_handler_region() {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        let assembly = compile_interpreter(architecture);
        let cold_start = assembly.find("asm_cold_handler_paths:").unwrap();
        for handler in ["Exp", "ExpRhsInt32"] {
            assert!(assembly.find(&format!("asm_handler_{handler}:")).unwrap() > cold_start);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn keeps_assertion_traps_after_all_hot_and_cold_handlers() {
    for (architecture, trap) in [(Architecture::X86_64, "    ud2"), (Architecture::Aarch64, "    brk")] {
        let assembly = compile_interpreter(architecture);
        let (hot, cold) = assembly.split_once("asm_cold_handler_paths:").unwrap();
        assert!(!hot.contains(trap));
        let (cold, traps) = cold.split_once("asm_assertion_failure_traps:").unwrap();
        assert!(!cold.contains(trap));
        assert!(traps.contains(trap));
        assert!(!traps.contains("asm_handler_"));
        assert!(hot.contains("assert_failure"));
        assert!(!assembly.contains("assert_ok"));
    }
}

.text

.globl CSYM(js_interpreter)
.p2align 4
CSYM(js_interpreter):
    .cfi_startproc
    stp x29, x30, [sp, #-112]!
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 112
    .cfi_offset x29, -112
    .cfi_offset x30, -104
    mov x29, sp
    .cfi_def_cfa_register x29
    stp x25, x26, [sp, #16]
    .cfi_offset x25, -96
    .cfi_offset x26, -88
    stp x27, x28, [sp, #32]
    .cfi_offset x27, -80
    .cfi_offset x28, -72
    stp x19, x20, [sp, #48]
    .cfi_offset x19, -64
    .cfi_offset x20, -56
    stp x21, x22, [sp, #64]
    .cfi_offset x21, -48
    .cfi_offset x22, -40
    stp x23, x24, [sp, #80]
    .cfi_offset x23, -32
    .cfi_offset x24, -24
    str d8, [sp, #96]
    .cfi_offset d8, -16
    mov x26, x0              // pb = bytecode base
    mov x27, x2              // values = values array
    mov x20, x3              // vm = VM*
    ldr x24, [x3, #72]
    ldr x28, [x3]
    // x28 = exec_ctx
    ldr x10, [x28, #88]
    ldrb w10, [x10, #56]
    and w10, w10, #7
    add x11, x3, #144
    ldr x19, [x11, x10, lsl #3]
    // x19 = dispatch table
    movz x9, #0x7ff8, lsl #48
    fmov d8, x9              // d8 = CANON_NAN_BITS
    mov w22, #32762
    // x22 = INT32_TAG
    mov w23, #32761
    // x23 = BOOLEAN_TAG
    // x24 = heap region base
    add x21, x26, w1, uxtw   // x21 = pb + entry_point
    ldrb w9, [x21]           // w9 = opcode byte
    ldr x10, [x19, x9, lsl #3]
    br x10

.p2align 4
asm_debugger_trampoline:
    mov x0, x20
    sub w1, w21, w26
    str w1, [x28, #64]
    bl CSYM(asm_debugger_check_breakpoint)
    ldr x28, [x20]
    ldr x9, [x28, #88]
    ldr x26, [x9, #40]
    add x27, x28, #136
    ldr w9, [x28, #64]
    add x21, x26, w9, uxtw
    ldrb w9, [x21]
    adrp x10, asm_dispatch_table
    add x10, x10, :lo12:asm_dispatch_table
    ldr x10, [x10, x9, lsl #3]
    br x10

.p2align 4
asm_handler_fallback:
    mov x0, x20
    sub w1, w21, w26
    str w1, [x28, #64]

.globl CSYM(js_interpreter)
.p2align 4
CSYM(js_interpreter):
    .cfi_startproc
    push rbp
    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
    .cfi_offset rbp, -16
    mov rbp, rsp
    .cfi_def_cfa_register rbp
    push rbx
    .cfi_offset rbx, -24
    push r12
    .cfi_offset r12, -32
    push r13
    .cfi_offset r13, -40
    push r14
    .cfi_offset r14, -48
    push r15
    .cfi_offset r15, -56
    sub rsp, 8
    mov r14, rdi          # pb = bytecode base
    mov r13d, esi         # pc = entry_point
    mov rbx, rdx          # values
    mov r15, QWORD PTR [rcx + 72]  # heap region base
    mov QWORD PTR [rbp - 48], rcx  # save VM*
    mov rax, QWORD PTR [rbx + -48]
    movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax + 56]
    and eax, 7
    mov r12, QWORD PTR [rcx + 144 + rax * 8]
    # r12 = dispatch table
    movzx eax, BYTE PTR [r14 + r13]
    jmp [r12 + rax * 8]

.p2align 4
asm_debugger_trampoline:
    mov DWORD PTR [rbx + -72], r13d
    mov rdi, QWORD PTR [rbp - 48]
    mov esi, r13d
    call CSYM(asm_debugger_check_breakpoint)
    mov rcx, QWORD PTR [rbp - 48]
    mov rbx, QWORD PTR [rcx + 0]
    add rbx, 136
    mov rcx, QWORD PTR [rbx + -48]
    mov r14, QWORD PTR [rcx + 40]
    mov r13d, DWORD PTR [rbx + -72]
    movzx eax, BYTE PTR [r14 + r13]
    lea rcx, [rip + asm_dispatch_table]
    jmp [rcx + rax * 8]

.p2align 4
asm_handler_fallback:
    mov DWORD PTR [rbx + -72], r13d
    mov rdi, QWORD PTR [rbp - 48]
    mov esi, r13d
    lea rdx, [r14 + r13]
    call CSYM(asm_fallback_handler)
    test rax, rax
    js .Lexit
    mov rcx, QWORD PTR [rbp - 48]
    mov rbx, QWORD PTR [rcx + 0]
    add rbx, 136
    mov rcx, QWORD PTR [rbx + -48]
    mov r14, QWORD PTR [rcx + 40]
    mov r13d, eax
    movzx eax, BYTE PTR [r14 + r13]
    jmp [r12 + rax * 8]
asm_handler_fallback_hot_end:

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, SourceInput, Target};

fn compile(program: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target: Target {
            architecture: Architecture::X86_64,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: flapc::Profile::JavaScript,
    })
    .compile(CompilationUnit {
        source: SourceInput {
            name: "operand_arrays.flap",
            contents: program,
        },
        constants: Some(SourceInput {
            name: "layout.conf",
            contents: include_str!("interpreter-layout.conf"),
        }),
    })
    .map(|assembly| assembly.as_str().to_owned())
    .map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
}

#[test]
fn an_inline_function_takes_the_address_of_its_operand_array_parameter() {
    let assembly = compile(
        "
inline fn first_operand(operands: Operand[]) -> u32 {
    let indices = &operands;
    u32(indices[0])
}

handler Check(
    operands_count: u8,
    operands: Operand[]
) {
    let first = first_operand(operands);
    values[first] = Value<Undefined>;
    let mut count: u32;
    load8(count, [pb, pc, operands_count]);
    let length: u32 = 3 + count;
    dispatch_variable(length);
}
",
    )
    .unwrap();
    // NB: The parameter is the handler's field, so its address is in the instruction, not its offset.
    assert!(assembly.contains("[r14 + r13 + 2]"), "{assembly}");
}

const CHECK_HANDLER: &str = "
handler Check(
    operands_count: u8,
    operands: Operand[]
) {
    let first = first_operand(operands);
    values[first] = Value<Undefined>;
    let mut count: u32;
    load8(count, [pb, pc, operands_count]);
    let length: u32 = 3 + count;
    dispatch_variable(length);
}
";

#[test]
fn an_inline_function_cannot_use_an_operand_array_parameter_as_a_value() {
    let error = compile(&format!(
        "
inline fn first_operand(operands: Operand[]) -> u32 {{
    let indices = operands;
    u32(indices[0])
}}
{CHECK_HANDLER}"
    ))
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("'first_operand' uses its parameter for the operand array 'operands' as a value"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_inline_function_cannot_pass_an_operand_array_parameter_on_to_a_value_use() {
    let error = compile(&format!(
        "
inline fn copy_operands(operands: Operand[]) -> u32 {{
    let indices = operands;
    u32(indices[0])
}}

inline fn first_operand(operands: Operand[]) -> u32 {{
    copy_operands(operands)
}}
{CHECK_HANDLER}"
    ))
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("'first_operand' uses its parameter for the operand array 'operands' as a value"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_handler_cannot_use_its_operand_array_as_a_value() {
    let error = compile(
        "
handler Check(
    operands_count: u8,
    operands: Operand[]
) {
    let indices = operands;
    values[u32(indices[0])] = Value<Undefined>;
    let mut count: u32;
    load8(count, [pb, pc, operands_count]);
    let length: u32 = 3 + count;
    dispatch_variable(length);
}
",
    )
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("the operand array 'operands' as a value is the field's offset"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_handler_cannot_use_its_operand_array_in_a_condition() {
    let error = compile(
        "
handler Check(
    operands_count: u8,
    operands: Operand[]
) {
    if operands != 0 {
        values[0] = Value<Undefined>;
    }
    let mut count: u32;
    load8(count, [pb, pc, operands_count]);
    let length: u32 = 3 + count;
    dispatch_variable(length);
}
",
    )
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("the operand array 'operands' as a value is the field's offset"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_inline_function_cannot_use_an_operand_array_parameter_in_a_condition() {
    let error = compile(&format!(
        "
inline fn first_operand(operands: Operand[]) -> u32 {{
    assert(operands != null);
    let indices = &operands;
    u32(indices[0])
}}
{CHECK_HANDLER}"
    ))
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("'first_operand' uses its parameter for the operand array 'operands' as a value"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Flap/tests/profiling.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, SourceInput, Target};

const PROGRAM: &str = "
inline fn count_check() @profiling {
    let vm = load_vm();
    or8_mem([vm, VM_EXECUTION_GENERATION], 2);
    or32_mem([vm, VM_EXECUTION_GENERATION], 0x30000);
    sub32_mem([vm, VM_EXECUTION_GENERATION], 5);
}

handler Check() {
    count_check();
    dispatch_next;
}
";

fn compile(architecture: Architecture, profiling: bool) -> String {
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target: Target {
            architecture,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling,
        profile: flapc::Profile::JavaScript,
    })
    .compile(CompilationUnit {
        source: SourceInput {
            name: "profiling.flap",
            contents: PROGRAM,
        },
        constants: Some(SourceInput {
            name: "layout.conf",
            contents: include_str!("interpreter-layout.conf"),
        }),
    })
    .unwrap()
    .as_str()
    .to_owned()
}

/// The hot code of the Check handler.
fn check_handler(assembly: &str) -> &str {
    let start = assembly.find("asm_handler_Check:").expect("the handler is emitted");
    let end = assembly.find("asm_handler_Check_hot_end:").expect("the handler ends");
    &assembly[start..end]
}

#[test]
fn compiles_profiling_code_only_into_the_profiling_variant() {
    for architecture in [Architecture::X86_64, Architecture::Aarch64] {
        let plain = compile(architecture, false);
        assert!(plain.contains("CSYM(js_interpreter):"), "{plain}");
        assert!(!plain.contains("_profiling"), "{plain}");
        assert!(!check_handler(&plain).contains("56]"), "{plain}");

        let profiling = compile(architecture, true);
        assert!(profiling.contains("CSYM(js_interpreter_profiling):"), "{profiling}");
        assert!(
            profiling.contains("CSYM(js_interpreter_handler_ranges_profiling):"),
            "{profiling}"
        );
        assert!(!profiling.contains("CSYM(js_interpreter):"), "{profiling}");
        assert!(check_handler(&profiling).contains("56]"), "{profiling}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn updates_memory_with_one_instruction_on_x86_64() {
    let assembly = compile(Architecture::X86_64, true);
    let handler = check_handler(&assembly);
    for instruction in ["or BYTE PTR [", "or DWORD PTR [", "sub DWORD PTR ["] {
        assert_eq!(handler.matches(instruction).count(), 1, "{instruction}\n{handler}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn updates_memory_through_scratch_registers_on_aarch64() {
    let assembly = compile(Architecture::Aarch64, true);
    let handler = check_handler(&assembly);
    for (instruction, count) in [
        ("ldrb w9, [x0, #56]", 1),
        ("orr w9, w9, #0x2", 1),
        ("strb w9, [x0, #56]", 1),
        ("ldr w9, [x0, #56]", 2),
        ("orr w9, w9, #0x30000", 1),
        ("sub x9, x9, #5", 1),
        ("str w9, [x0, #56]", 2),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(handler.matches(instruction).count(), count, "{instruction}\n{handler}");
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Flap/tests/wasm_profile.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use flapc::{Architecture, CompilationUnit, CompileOptions, Compiler, ObjectFormat, Profile, SourceInput, Target};

fn compiler(architecture: Architecture) -> Compiler {
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target: Target {
            architecture,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: true,
        has_bmi1: true,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: Profile::WebAssembly,
    })
}

fn compile_with_constants(source: &str, constants: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    compiler(Architecture::X86_64)
        .compile(CompilationUnit {
            source: SourceInput {
                name: "wasm.flap",
                contents: source,
            },
            constants: Some(SourceInput {
                name: "layout.conf",
                contents: constants,
            }),
        })
        .map(|assembly| assembly.as_str().to_owned())
        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}

fn compile(source: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    compile_with_constants(source, "")
}

fn handler<'a>(assembly: &'a str, name: &str) -> &'a str {
    let start = assembly
        .find(&format!("asm_handler_{name}:\n"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing handler {name}"));
    let end = assembly[start..].find(&format!("asm_handler_{name}_hot_end:")).unwrap();
    &assembly[start..start + end]
}

const PROGRAM: &str = r#"
handler Nop() @opcode(0x01) {
    dispatch_next;
}

handler LocalGet() @opcode(0x20) {
    let code: Sequence<u8> = alias(ip);
    let index: u64 = alias(code[1]);
    let locals: Sequence<u64> = alias(fp);
    let stack: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    stack[0] = locals[index];
    dispatch_variable(2);
}

handler Saturating() @opcode(0xfc, 7) {
    dispatch_variable(2);
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit;
}
"#;

#[test]
fn dispatches_on_the_byte_the_instruction_pointer_points_at() {
    let assembly = compile(PROGRAM).unwrap();
    let nop = handler(&assembly, "Nop");
    assert!(nop.contains("add r13, 1\n"), "{nop}");
    assert!(
        nop.contains("movzx eax, BYTE PTR [r13]\n    jmp [r12 + rax * 8]"),
        "{nop}"
    );
    assert!(!assembly.contains("r14 + r13"));

    let local_get = handler(&assembly, "LocalGet");
    assert!(local_get.contains("BYTE PTR [r13 + 1]"), "{local_get}");
    assert!(local_get.contains("[rbp + rax * 8]"), "{local_get}");
    assert!(local_get.contains("QWORD PTR [rbx]"), "{local_get}");
}

#[test]
fn builds_dispatch_tables_from_opcode_annotations() {
    let assembly = compile(PROGRAM).unwrap();
    let table = assembly
        .split("asm_dispatch_table:\n")
        .nth(1)
        .unwrap()
        .lines()
        .take(256)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(table[0x00], "    .quad asm_handler_Fallback");
    assert_eq!(table[0x01], "    .quad asm_handler_Nop");
    assert_eq!(table[0x20], "    .quad asm_handler_LocalGet");
    assert_eq!(table[0xfc], "    .quad asm_handler_Fallback");

    let secondary = assembly
        .split("asm_dispatch_table_fc:\n")
        .nth(1)
        .unwrap()
        .lines()
        .take(512)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(secondary.len(), 512);
    assert_eq!(secondary[7], "    .quad asm_handler_Saturating");
    assert_eq!(secondary[8], "    .quad asm_handler_Fallback");

    assert!(assembly.contains(".globl CSYM(wasm_interpreter)\n"));
    assert!(assembly.contains(".globl CSYM(wasm_interpreter_dispatch_table)\n"));
    assert!(assembly.contains(".globl CSYM(wasm_interpreter_end)\n"));
    assert!(!assembly.contains("js_interpreter"));
    assert!(!assembly.contains("asm_debugger_trampoline"));
}

#[test]
fn rejects_handlers_without_an_encoding() {
    let error = compile("handler Unencoded() { dispatch_next; }").unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("needs an @opcode or @fallback annotation"), "{error}");

    let error = compile("handler A() @opcode(0x10) { dispatch_next; }\nhandler B() @opcode(0x10) { dispatch_next; }")
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("another handler already has this opcode"), "{error}");

    let error = compile("handler A(dst: out Operand) @opcode(0x10) { dispatch_next; }").unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("cannot declare parameters"), "{error}");

    let error = compile("handler A() @opcode(0xfc, 7) { dispatch_next; }").unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("variable-length handler must use variable dispatch"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn rejects_registers_of_other_profiles() {
    let error = compile("handler A() @opcode(0x10) { let base: u64 = pb; dispatch_variable(base); }").unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("the WebAssembly profile has no interpreter register 'pb'"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

fn compile_for(target: Target, source: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    Compiler::new(CompileOptions {
        target,
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt: false,
        has_bmi1: false,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: Profile::WebAssembly,
    })
    .compile(CompilationUnit {
        source: SourceInput {
            name: "wasm.flap",
            contents: source,
        },
        constants: None,
    })
    .map(|assembly| assembly.as_str().to_owned())
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}

fn compile_aarch64(source: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    compile_for(
        Target {
            architecture: Architecture::Aarch64,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        source,
    )
}

#[test]
fn dispatches_on_the_byte_the_instruction_pointer_points_at_on_aarch64() {
    let assembly = compile_aarch64(PROGRAM).unwrap();
    let nop = handler(&assembly, "Nop");
    assert!(nop.contains("ldrb w9, [x21, #1]\n"), "{nop}");
    assert!(nop.contains("add x21, x21, #1\n"), "{nop}");
    assert!(nop.contains("ldr x10, [x19, x9, lsl #3]\n    br x10"), "{nop}");
    assert!(!assembly.contains("x26, w25"), "{assembly}");

    let local_get = handler(&assembly, "LocalGet");
    assert!(local_get.contains("[x21, #1]"), "{local_get}");
    assert!(local_get.contains("[x29, "), "{local_get}");
    assert!(local_get.contains("[x27]"), "{local_get}");

    let entry = assembly.split("CSYM(wasm_interpreter):\n").nth(1).unwrap();
    assert!(entry.contains("mov x21, x0"), "{entry}");
    assert!(entry.contains("mov x27, x1"), "{entry}");
    assert!(entry.contains(":lo12:asm_dispatch_table"), "{entry}");
    assert!(assembly.contains(".Lexit:\n    mov sp, x29\n"), "{assembly}");
}

#[test]
fn dispatches_prefixed_opcodes_through_their_secondary_table_on_aarch64() {
    let assembly = compile_aarch64(
        r#"
handler Prefix() @opcode(0xfc) {
    let bytes: Sequence<u8> = alias(ip);
    let sub_opcode: u64 = alias(bytes[1]);
    dispatch_secondary(0xfc, sub_opcode);
}

handler Saturating() @opcode(0xfc, 3) {
    dispatch_variable(2);
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();

    )

}

#[test]
fn compiles_atomic_operations_on_aarch64() {
    let assembly = compile_aarch64(
        r#"
handler Atomics() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let address = slots[0];
    let value = slots[1];
    let old = atomic_cmpxchg32([address, 4], value, 7);
    let swapped = atomic_xchg8([address, 0], old);
    let added = atomic_add64([address, 8], swapped);
    let loaded = atomic_load16([address, 0]);
    atomic_fence();
    slots[2] = added + loaded;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let atomics = handler(&assembly, "Atomics");
    for expected in [
        "add x9, x",
        ", #4\n",
        "casal w",
        "swpalb w",
        "ldaddal x",
        "ldarh w",
        "dmb ish",
    ] {
        assert!(atomics.contains(expected), "missing {expected}: {atomics}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn compiles_numeric_and_vector_operations_on_aarch64() {
    let assembly = compile_aarch64(
        r#"
handler Numbers() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let a = slots[0];
    let b = slots[1];
    let narrow_a = u32(a);
    let narrow_b = u32(b);
    let quotient = div_u32(narrow_a, narrow_b);
    let remainder = rem_s64(a, b);
    let zeros = ctz64(a);
    let ones = popcnt32(narrow_b);
    let rotated = rotl32(narrow_a, narrow_b);
    let narrow = quotient + ones + rotated;
    let wide: u64 = alias(narrow);
    slots[2] = remainder + zeros + wide;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Vectors() @opcode(0x02) {
    let top: u64 = vsp;
    let mut a: v128;
    load128(a, [top, 0]);
    let mut b: v128;
    load128(b, [top, 16]);
    let sum = v128_add_i32(a, b);
    let smaller = v128_min_f32(sum, b);
    let shuffled = v128_shuffle_i8(smaller, a);
    store128([top, 32], shuffled);
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(top);
    let mask = v128_bitmask_i8(shuffled);
    let high = v128_high_u64(a);
    slots[7] = mask + high;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let numbers = handler(&assembly, "Numbers");
    for expected in [
        "udiv w",
        "sdiv x9, x",
        "msub x",
        "rbit x9, x",
        "cnt v16.8b, v16.8b",
        "neg w9, w",
        "ror w",
    ] {
        assert!(numbers.contains(expected), "missing {expected}: {numbers}");
    }
    let vectors = handler(&assembly, "Vectors");
    for expected in [
        "add v",
        ".4s\n",
        "fcmgt v16.4s, v",
        "bsl v16.16b, v",
        "movi v16.16b, #0x8f",
        "tbl v",
        "usra v16.2d, v16.2d, #28",
        ", v",
        ".d[1]\n",
    ] {
        assert!(vectors.contains(expected), "missing {expected}: {vectors}");
    }
}

/// Twelve values live at once, more than there are allocatable registers.
const HIGH_PRESSURE: &str = r#"
handler Sum() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let a = slots[0];
    let b = slots[1];
    let c = slots[2];
    let d = slots[3];
    let e = slots[4];
    let f = slots[5];
    let g = slots[6];
    let h = slots[7];
    let i = slots[8];
    let j = slots[9];
    let k = slots[10];
    let l = slots[11];
    slots[12] = a + l;
    slots[13] = b + k;
    slots[14] = c + j;
    slots[15] = d + i;
    slots[16] = e + h;
    slots[17] = f + g;
    slots[18] = a + b + c + d + e + f + g + h + i + j + k + l;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#;

#[test]
fn spills_to_the_spill_area_when_registers_run_out() {
    let error = compile(HIGH_PRESSURE).unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("could not allocate spill-free handler"), "{error}");

    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        HIGH_PRESSURE,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let sum = handler(&assembly, "Sum");
    assert!(sum.contains("QWORD PTR [rsp + 64]"), "{sum}");
    assert!(!sum.contains("QWORD PTR [rsp + 128]"), "{sum}");
}

const FLOAT_PRESSURE: &str = r#"
handler FloatSum() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let a = f64_from_bits(slots[0]);
    let b = f64_from_bits(slots[1]);
    let c = f64_from_bits(slots[2]);
    let d = f64_from_bits(slots[3]);
    let e = f64_from_bits(slots[4]);
    let f = f64_from_bits(slots[5]);
    let ab = a + b;
    let abc = ab + c;
    let abcd = abc + d;
    let abcde = abcd + e;
    let sum = abcde + f;
    let fe = f * e;
    let fed = fe * d;
    let fedc = fed * c;
    let fedcb = fedc * b;
    let product = fedcb * a;
    slots[6] = f64_to_bits(sum);
    slots[7] = f64_to_bits(product);
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#;

#[test]
fn spills_floating_point_values() {
    let error = compile(FLOAT_PRESSURE).unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("could not allocate spill-free handler"), "{error}");

    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        FLOAT_PRESSURE,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let sum = handler(&assembly, "FloatSum");
    assert!(sum.contains("movsd QWORD PTR [rsp + 64], xmm"), "{sum}");
}

const VECTOR_PRESSURE: &str = r#"
handler Reverse() @opcode(0x01) {
    let top: u64 = vsp;
    let mut a: v128;
    load128(a, [top, 0]);
    let mut b: v128;
    load128(b, [top, 16]);
    let mut c: v128;
    load128(c, [top, 32]);
    let mut d: v128;
    load128(d, [top, 48]);
    let mut e: v128;
    load128(e, [top, 64]);
    let mut f: v128;
    load128(f, [top, 80]);
    store128([top, 96], f);
    store128([top, 112], e);
    store128([top, 128], d);
    store128([top, 144], c);
    store128([top, 160], b);
    store128([top, 176], a);
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#;

#[test]
fn keeps_and_spills_vectors_whole() {
    let error = compile(VECTOR_PRESSURE).unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("could not allocate spill-free handler"), "{error}");

    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        VECTOR_PRESSURE,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 8\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let reverse = handler(&assembly, "Reverse");
    // Vector slots take 16 bytes each, starting on a 16-byte boundary.
    assert!(reverse.contains("movdqu XMMWORD PTR [rsp + 16], xmm"), "{reverse}");
    assert!(reverse.contains("movdqu XMMWORD PTR [rsp + 32], xmm"), "{reverse}");
    assert!(
        !reverse.contains("[rsp + 8]") && !reverse.contains("[rsp + 24]"),
        "{reverse}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn moves_vectors_with_full_width_moves() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Swap() @opcode(0x01) {
    let top: u64 = vsp;
    let mut a: v128;
    load128(a, [top, 0]);
    let mut b: v128;
    load128(b, [top, 16]);
    let mut first: v128 = a;
    let mut second: v128 = b;
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(top);
    let flag = slots[4];
    if flag != 0 {
        first = b;
        second = a;
    }
    store128([top, 32], first);
    store128([top, 48], second);
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let swap = handler(&assembly, "Swap");
    assert!(swap.contains("movaps xmm"), "{swap}");
    assert!(!swap.contains("movq xmm"), "{swap}");
}

const ACROSS_CALL: &str = r#"
handler Call() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let kept = slots[0];
    let current: u64 = ip;
    let result: u64 = call_helper(wasm_helper, kept);
    let sum = result + kept;
    slots[1] = sum;
    let next = current + 1;
    ip = next;
    dispatch;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#;

#[test]
fn spills_values_live_across_calls_first() {
    let error = compile(ACROSS_CALL).unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.contains("could not allocate spill-free handler"), "{error}");

    // One slot is enough: the copy of ip is reread from ip, so only the value is stored.
    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        ACROSS_CALL,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 1\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let call = handler(&assembly, "Call");
    assert!(call.contains("QWORD PTR [rsp + 64]"), "{call}");
    assert!(call.contains("call "), "{call}");
}

#[test]
fn compiles_vector_operations_to_sse_instructions() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Vectors() @opcode(0x01) {
    let top: u64 = vsp;
    let mut a: v128;
    load128(a, [top, 0]);
    let mut b: v128;
    load128(b, [top, 16]);
    let sum = v128_add_i32(a, b);
    let rounded = v128_floor_f64(sum);
    store128([top, 32], rounded);
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(top);
    let low = slots[6];
    let splat = v128_from_u64x2(low, low);
    let mask = v128_bitmask_i8(splat);
    let high = v128_high_u64(a);
    slots[7] = mask + high;

        "paddd xmm",
        "roundpd xmm",
        ", 9\n",
        "pinsrq xmm",

    }

const ACROSS_STACK_POINTER_WRITE: &str = r#"
handler NewFrame() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let a = slots[0];
    let b = slots[1];
    let c = slots[2];
    let d = slots[3];
    let e = slots[4];
    let f = slots[5];
    let g = slots[6];
    let h = slots[7];
    let i = slots[8];
    let j = slots[9];
    let old_stack_pointer: u64 = sp;
    let new_stack_pointer = old_stack_pointer - 512;
    sp = new_stack_pointer;
    slots[10] = a + j;
    slots[11] = b + i;
    slots[12] = c + h;
    slots[13] = d + g;
    slots[14] = e + f;
    slots[15] = a + b + c + d + e + f + g + h + i + j;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#;

#[test]
fn spills_values_live_across_writes_to_the_stack_pointer() {
    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        ACROSS_STACK_POINTER_WRITE,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 0\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let frame = handler(&assembly, "NewFrame");
    let write = frame.find("mov rsp, ").expect("the handler writes rsp");
    let (before, after) = frame.split_at(write);
    // A value spilled before the write moves to its slot below the new stack pointer, and is reread from there.
    let new_stack_pointer = after["mov rsp, ".len()..].lines().next().unwrap().trim();
    assert!(
        before.contains(&format!("QWORD PTR [{new_stack_pointer}"))
            || before.contains(&format!("QWORD PTR [{new_stack_pointer} +")),
        "{frame}"
    );
    assert!(after.contains("QWORD PTR [rsp"), "{frame}");
}

#[test]
fn does_not_spill_handlers_that_fit() {
    let assembly =
        compile_with_constants(PROGRAM, "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n").unwrap();
    assert!(!assembly.contains("rsp +"));
}

#[test]
fn wraps_u32_arithmetic_to_32_bits() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Arithmetic() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let lhs = u32(slots[0]);
    let rhs = u32(slots[1]);
    let sum = lhs + rhs;
    let difference = rhs - lhs;
    let product = lhs * rhs;
    let wide_sum: u64 = alias(sum);
    let wide_difference: u64 = alias(difference);
    let wide_product: u64 = alias(product);
    slots[1] = wide_sum;
    slots[2] = wide_difference;
    slots[3] = wide_product;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let arithmetic = handler(&assembly, "Arithmetic");
    assert!(arithmetic.contains("add e"), "{arithmetic}");
    assert!(arithmetic.contains("sub e"), "{arithmetic}");
    assert!(arithmetic.contains("imul e"), "{arithmetic}");
    assert!(
        !arithmetic
            .lines()
            .any(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with("add r") && !line.contains("r13")),
        "{arithmetic}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn accepts_literal_left_operands_and_nested_arguments() {

        r#"
inline fn advance(length: u64) {
    let current: u64 = ip;
    let next = current + length;
    ip = next;
    dispatch;
}

handler Skip() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let length = slots[0];
    let extra = slots[1];
    advance(1 + length + (extra >> 1));
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {

#[test]
fn materializes_wide_immediates() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Wide() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let value = slots[0];
    let flipped = value ^ 0x8000000000000000;
    slots[1] = flipped;
    let masked = value & 0x3ffffffff;
    slots[2] = masked;
    let low = value & 0xffffffff;
    slots[3] = low;
    let spread = value * 0x0101010101010101;
    slots[4] = spread;
    if value == 0x8000000000000000 {
        exit();
    }
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let wide = handler(&assembly, "Wide");
    assert!(
        wide.contains("0x8000000000000000") || wide.contains("9223372036854775808"),
        "{wide}"
    );
    assert!(wide.contains("xor r"), "{wide}");
    assert!(wide.contains("and r"), "{wide}");
    assert!(wide.contains("imul r"), "{wide}");
    assert!(
        wide.lines().any(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with("mov e")),
        "{wide}"
    );
    assert!(wide.contains("cmp r"), "{wide}");
}

#[test]
fn cold_blocks_reload_instead_of_reusing_hot_loads() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Reload() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let value = slots[1];
    let flag = slots[0];
    if flag == 0 @cold {
        let again = slots[1];
        slots[3] = again;
        exit();
    }
    slots[2] = value;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    // The cold block is laid out away from the handler, so this counts the loads in both.
    assert_eq!(assembly.matches("QWORD PTR [rbx + 8]").count(), 2, "{assembly}");
}

#[test]
fn compiles_numeric_operations_to_single_instructions() {
    let assembly = compile_with_constants(
        r#"
handler Numeric() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let lhs = u32(slots[0]);
    let rhs = u32(slots[1]);
    let quotient = div_u32(lhs, rhs);
    let remainder = rem_s32(lhs, rhs);
    let leading = clz32(lhs);
    let trailing = ctz64(slots[2]);
    let population = popcnt64(slots[3]);
    let rotated = rotl32(lhs, rhs);
    let float = f64_from_bits(slots[4]);
    let truncated = trunc_f64(float);
    let bits = f64_to_bits(truncated);
    let wide_quotient: u64 = alias(quotient);
    let wide_remainder: u64 = alias(remainder);
    let wide_leading: u64 = alias(leading);
    let wide_rotated: u64 = alias(rotated);
    slots[5] = wide_quotient;
    slots[6] = wide_remainder;
    slots[7] = wide_leading;
    slots[8] = trailing;
    slots[9] = population;
    slots[10] = wide_rotated;
    slots[11] = bits;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
        "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let numeric = handler(&assembly, "Numeric");
    for instruction in [
        "div ecx",
        "idiv ecx",
        "lzcnt e",
        "tzcnt r",
        "popcnt r",
        "rol e",
        "movq xmm",
        "roundsd xmm0, xmm0, 3",
    ] {
        assert!(numeric.contains(instruction), "missing {instruction}:\n{numeric}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn counts_zeros_with_bit_scans_without_lzcnt_and_bmi1() {
    let assembly = compile_for(
        Target {
            architecture: Architecture::X86_64,
            object_format: ObjectFormat::Elf,
        },
        r#"
handler Zeros() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let leading = clz32(u32(slots[0]));
    let trailing = ctz64(slots[1]);
    let wide_leading: u64 = alias(leading);
    slots[2] = wide_leading;
    slots[3] = trailing;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let zeros = handler(&assembly, "Zeros");
    for instruction in ["bsr e", ", 63", "xor e", ", 31", "bsf r", ", 64"] {
        assert!(zeros.contains(instruction), "missing {instruction}:\n{zeros}");
    }
    for instruction in ["lzcnt", "tzcnt"] {
        assert!(!zeros.contains(instruction), "unexpected {instruction}:\n{zeros}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn moves_continuing_cold_ifs_out_of_line() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Decode() @opcode(0x01) {
    let bytes: Sequence<u8> = alias(ip);
    let first: u64 = alias(bytes[1]);
    let mut length: u64 = 2;
    if first >= 128 @cold {
        let mut byte: u64 = first;
        while byte >= 128 {
            byte = alias(bytes[length]);
            length = length + 1;
        }
    }
    dispatch_variable(length);
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let hot = handler(&assembly, "Decode");
    assert!(!hot.contains("cmp rax, 128\n    jb"), "{hot}");
    let cold = assembly.split("asm_handler_Decode_cold:").nth(1).unwrap();
    let cold = cold.split("asm_handler_Decode_cold_end:").next().unwrap();
    assert!(cold.contains("cmp"), "{cold}");
}

#[test]
fn rereads_copies_of_interpreter_registers_instead_of_spilling_them() {
    let source = HIGH_PRESSURE
        .replace(
            "    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);",
            "    let start: u64 = ip;\n    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);",
        )
        .replace(
            "    dispatch_next;\n}\n\nhandler Fallback",
            "    let next = start + 1;\n    ip = next;\n    dispatch;\n}\n\nhandler Fallback",
        );
    let assembly =
        compile_with_constants(&source, "const SPILL_AREA_OFFSET = 64\nconst SPILL_AREA_SLOTS = 8\n").unwrap();
    let sum = handler(&assembly, "Sum");
    assert!(sum.contains(", r13\n"), "{sum}");
    assert!(
        !sum.lines()
            .any(|line| line.contains("PTR [rsp") && line.trim_start().starts_with("mov r") && line.contains("r13")),
        "{sum}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn compares_floats_with_ieee_semantics() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Compare() @opcode(0x01) {
    let slots: Sequence<u64> = alias(vsp);
    let lhs = f64_from_bits(slots[0]);
    let rhs = f64_from_bits(slots[1]);
    let mut result: u64 = 0;
    if lhs < rhs {
        result = 1;
    }
    if lhs != rhs {
        result = result + 2;
    }
    slots[2] = result;
    dispatch_next;
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let compare = handler(&assembly, "Compare");
    // An unordered comparison sets the "below" flags, so a less-than tests the swapped operands for "above".
    assert!(compare.contains("ucomisd xmm1, xmm0\n    ja "), "{compare}");
    assert!(compare.contains("jp "), "{compare}");
}

#[test]
fn dispatches_prefixed_opcodes_through_their_secondary_table() {
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Prefix() @opcode(0xfc) {
    let bytes: Sequence<u8> = alias(ip);
    let sub_opcode: u64 = alias(bytes[1]);
    dispatch_secondary(0xfc, sub_opcode);
}

handler Saturating() @opcode(0xfc, 3) {
    dispatch_variable(2);
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let prefix = handler(&assembly, "Prefix");
    assert!(prefix.contains("lea rax, [rip + asm_dispatch_table_fc]"), "{prefix}");
    assert!(prefix.contains("jmp [rax + "), "{prefix}");

    // 0xff is free for a runtime's own prefixed forms.
    let assembly = compile(
        r#"
handler Internal() @opcode(0xff) {
    let bytes: Sequence<u8> = alias(ip);
    let sub_opcode: u64 = alias(bytes[1]);
    dispatch_secondary(0xff, sub_opcode);
}

handler Quickened() @opcode(0xff, 0x28) {
    dispatch_variable(2);
}

handler Fallback() @fallback {
    exit();
}
"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(assembly.contains("asm_dispatch_table_ff:"), "{assembly}");
    assert!(handler(&assembly, "Internal").contains("[rip + asm_dispatch_table_ff]"));

    let error = compile("handler A() @opcode(0x10, 3) { dispatch_variable(2); }").unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        error.contains("secondary dispatch tables exist for the prefixes"),
        "{error}"
    );
}

#pragma once

#include <LibGC/Cell.h>
#include <LibJS/Forward.h>

namespace JS {

// The base of the types through which C++ names the cells of the Rust runtime: objects, strings, symbols, BigInts,
// realms and the rest. A pointer to such a type is the runtime's cell itself, so these types add neither fields nor
// virtual functions, and only the runtime creates and destroys their cells. Like the embedder's own cells, they offer
// vm() as well.
class EngineCell : public GC::ForeignCell {
public:
    ALWAYS_INLINE VM& vm() const;

    template<typename T>
    bool fast_is() const = delete;
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/HostClassBuilder.h
/*
