//! The code buffer shared by both assemblers: bytes, labels and fixups.

use ak::Column;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// Why assembling failed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AsmError {
    /// A label was referenced but never bound.
    UnboundLabel,
    /// A branch or PC-relative reference does not reach its label.
    BranchOutOfRange,
    /// The code does not fit in the memory it is written into.
    TooLarge,
}

/// A position in the code, bound once and referenced any number of times
/// before or after binding.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Label(u32);

/// How a reference to a label is patched once the label is bound.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FixupKind {
    /// x86-64 rel8 at the fixup offset, relative to the end of the byte.
    X86Rel8,
    /// x86-64 rel32 at the fixup offset, relative to the end of the field.
    X86Rel32,
    /// AArch64 B/BL: imm26 word offset in bits 0..26.
    A64Branch26,
    /// AArch64 B.cond/CBZ/CBNZ: imm19 word offset in bits 5..24.
    A64Branch19,
    /// AArch64 TBZ/TBNZ: imm14 word offset in bits 5..19.
    A64Branch14,
    /// AArch64 ADR: 21-bit byte offset split into immlo (29..31) and immhi (5..24).
    A64Adr21,
}

impl FixupKind {
    /// The largest forward distance in bytes this kind can encode.
    pub const fn max_forward_distance(self) -> i64 {
        match self {
            FixupKind::X86Rel8 => i8::MAX as i64,
            FixupKind::X86Rel32 => i32::MAX as i64,
            FixupKind::A64Branch26 => ((1 << 25) - 1) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Branch19 => ((1 << 18) - 1) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Branch14 => ((1 << 13) - 1) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Adr21 => (1 << 20) - 1,
        }
    }

    /// The largest backward distance in bytes this kind can encode.
    pub const fn max_backward_distance(self) -> i64 {
        match self {
            FixupKind::X86Rel8 => 128,
            FixupKind::X86Rel32 => 1 << 31,
            FixupKind::A64Branch26 => (1 << 25) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Branch19 => (1 << 18) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Branch14 => (1 << 13) * 4,
            FixupKind::A64Adr21 => 1 << 20,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a reference of this kind starting at `from` reaches `to`.
    pub const fn reaches(self, from: usize, to: usize) -> bool {
        let distance = to as i64 - self.origin(from) as i64;
        distance <= self.max_forward_distance() && -distance <= self.max_backward_distance()
    }

    /// The position the displacement is relative to, for a fixup at `at`.
    const fn origin(self, at: usize) -> usize {
        match self {
            FixupKind::X86Rel8 => at + 1,
            FixupKind::X86Rel32 => at + 4,
            _ => at,
        }
    }
}

const NO_FIXUP: u32 = u32::MAX;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum LabelState {
    /// Not bound yet; the head of the list of fixups referencing it.
    Unbound {
        first_fixup: u32,
    },
    Bound(u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Fixup {
    at: u32,
    kind: FixupKind,
    label: Label,
    /// Next fixup referencing the same label.
    next: u32,
    /// Resolved fixups stay in the list but are skipped.
    resolved: bool,
}

/// A pending fixup, as seen by an assembler that manages branch veneers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PendingFixup {
    pub id: u32,
    pub at: usize,
    pub kind: FixupKind,
    pub label: Label,
}

/// A point in the emission that `CodeBuffer::rewind()` goes back to.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Checkpoint {
    offset: usize,
    fixup_count: usize,
}

impl Checkpoint {
    pub fn offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.offset
    }
}

/// A code buffer with labels. The code goes straight into the column it writes, and the labels and fixups are in a
/// zone.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CodeBuffer<'a> {
    bytes: &'a mut Column<u8>,
    /// How many bytes were emitted past the end of the column, once it is full. The offsets go on as if they were
    /// there, but nothing is written or patched any more: `finish()` fails.
    lost: usize,
    labels: ZoneVec<'a, LabelState>,
    fixups: ZoneVec<'a, Fixup>,
    /// The first error hit while emitting; reported by `finish()`.
    error: Option<AsmError>,
}

impl<'a> CodeBuffer<'a> {
    /// A buffer that writes its code into `bytes`, in place of what it holds, and keeps its labels in `work`.
    pub fn new(bytes: &'a mut Column<u8>, work: &'a Zone) -> Self {
        bytes.clear();
        Self {
            bytes,
            lost: 0,
            labels: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            fixups: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            error: None,
        }
    }

    /// The current emission offset.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len() + self.lost
    }

    pub fn emit_u8(&mut self, value: u8) {
        self.emit_bytes(&[value]);
    }

    pub fn emit_u16(&mut self, value: u16) {
        self.emit_bytes(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    pub fn emit_u32(&mut self, value: u32) {
        self.emit_bytes(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    pub fn emit_u64(&mut self, value: u64) {
        self.emit_bytes(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    pub fn emit_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        if self.lost == 0 && self.bytes.try_extend_from_slice(bytes).is_ok() {
            return;
        }
        self.set_error(AsmError::TooLarge);
        self.lost += bytes.len();
    }

    pub fn read_u32(&self, at: usize) -> u32 {
        u32::from_le_bytes(self.bytes[at..at + 4].try_into().unwrap())
    }

    pub fn write_u32(&mut self, at: usize, value: u32) {
        self.bytes[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    /// Records an error to be reported by `finish()`. The first one wins.
    pub fn set_error(&mut self, error: AsmError) {
        self.error.get_or_insert(error);
    }

    pub fn new_label(&mut self) -> Label {
        let label = Label(u32::try_from(self.labels.len()).expect("too many labels"));
        self.labels.push(LabelState::Unbound { first_fixup: NO_FIXUP });
        label
    }

    /// The offset a label is bound to, if it is bound.
    pub fn label_offset(&self, label: Label) -> Option<usize> {
        match self.labels[label.0 as usize] {
            LabelState::Bound(offset) => Some(offset as usize),
            LabelState::Unbound { .. } => None,
        }
    }

    /// Binds `label` to the current offset and patches every reference to it.
    pub fn bind(&mut self, label: Label) {
        let offset = self.offset();
        let state = &mut self.labels[label.0 as usize];
        let LabelState::Unbound { first_fixup } = *state else {
            panic!("label bound twice");
        };
        *state = LabelState::Bound(Self::offset_u32(offset));
        let mut fixup_id = first_fixup;
        while fixup_id != NO_FIXUP {
            let fixup = self.fixups[fixup_id as usize];
            if !fixup.resolved {
                self.patch(fixup.at as usize, fixup.kind, offset);
                self.fixups[fixup_id as usize].resolved = true;
            }
            fixup_id = fixup.next;
        }
    }

    /// Records a reference of `kind` at `at` to `label`. If the label is
    /// already bound, the reference is patched immediately. Returns the
    /// fixup's id if it is still pending.
    pub fn add_fixup(&mut self, label: Label, at: usize, kind: FixupKind) -> Option<u32> {
        match self.labels[label.0 as usize] {
            LabelState::Bound(target) => {
                self.patch(at, kind, target as usize);
                None
            }
            LabelState::Unbound { first_fixup } => {
                let id = u32::try_from(self.fixups.len()).expect("too many fixups");
                self.fixups.push(Fixup {
                    at: Self::offset_u32(at),
                    kind,
                    label,
                    next: first_fixup,
                    resolved: false,
                });
                self.labels[label.0 as usize] = LabelState::Unbound { first_fixup: id };
                Some(id)
            }
        }
    }

    /// The fixup with `id`, if it is still pending.
    pub fn pending_fixup(&self, id: u32) -> Option<PendingFixup> {
        let fixup = &self.fixups[id as usize];
        (!fixup.resolved).then_some(PendingFixup {
            id,
            at: fixup.at as usize,
            kind: fixup.kind,
            label: fixup.label,
        })
    }

    /// Patches a pending fixup to point at `target` instead of its label (a
    /// veneer that will itself branch to the label).
    pub fn redirect_fixup(&mut self, id: u32, target: usize) {
        let fixup = self.fixups[id as usize];
        assert!(!fixup.resolved, "redirecting a resolved fixup");
        self.patch(fixup.at as usize, fixup.kind, target);
        self.fixups[id as usize].resolved = true;
    }

    pub fn checkpoint(&self) -> Checkpoint {
        Checkpoint {
            offset: self.offset(),
            fixup_count: self.fixups.len(),
        }
    }

    /// Drops what was emitted after `checkpoint`, and the references it made. No label may have been bound since.
    pub fn rewind(&mut self, checkpoint: Checkpoint) {
        while self.fixups.len() > checkpoint.fixup_count {
            let fixup = self.fixups.pop().expect("there are fixups past the checkpoint");
            let state = &mut self.labels[fixup.label.0 as usize];
            debug_assert!(
                matches!(*state, LabelState::Unbound { first_fixup } if first_fixup as usize == self.fixups.len()),
                "a label was bound after the checkpoint"
            );
            *state = LabelState::Unbound {
                first_fixup: fixup.next,
            };
        }
        let kept = checkpoint.offset.min(self.bytes.len());
        self.bytes.truncate(kept);
        self.lost = checkpoint.offset - kept;
    }

    /// Pads with `filler` until the offset is a multiple of `alignment`.
    pub fn align_with(&mut self, alignment: usize, filler: u8) {
        assert!(alignment.is_power_of_two());
        while !self.offset().is_multiple_of(alignment) {
            self.emit_u8(filler);
        }
    }

    /// Returns the code, or the first error. Fails if a referenced label was
    /// never bound.
    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<&'a [u8], AsmError> {
        if let Some(error) = self.error {
            return Err(error);
        }
        if self.fixups.iter().any(|fixup| !fixup.resolved) {
            return Err(AsmError::UnboundLabel);
        }
        let bytes: &'a Column<u8> = self.bytes;
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    fn offset_u32(offset: usize) -> u32 {
        u32::try_from(offset).expect("code buffer exceeds 4 GiB")
    }

    fn patch(&mut self, at: usize, kind: FixupKind, target: usize) {
        // NB: The code that the column had no room for is not there to patch, and the code is not finished.
        if self.lost != 0 {
            return;
        }
        if !kind.reaches(at, target) {
            self.set_error(AsmError::BranchOutOfRange);
            return;
        }
        let distance = target as i64 - kind.origin(at) as i64;
        match kind {
            FixupKind::X86Rel8 => self.bytes[at] = distance as i8 as u8,
            FixupKind::X86Rel32 => {
                self.bytes[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&(distance as i32).to_le_bytes());
            }
            FixupKind::A64Branch26 => {
                let word = self.read_u32(at) & !0x03ff_ffff;
                self.write_u32(at, word | ((distance >> 2) as u32 & 0x03ff_ffff));
            }
            FixupKind::A64Branch19 => {
                let word = self.read_u32(at) & !(0x7ffff << 5);
                self.write_u32(at, word | (((distance >> 2) as u32 & 0x7ffff) << 5));
            }
            FixupKind::A64Branch14 => {
                let word = self.read_u32(at) & !(0x3fff << 5);
                self.write_u32(at, word | (((distance >> 2) as u32 & 0x3fff) << 5));
            }
            FixupKind::A64Adr21 => {
                let word = self.read_u32(at) & !((0x3 << 29) | (0x7ffff << 5));
                let immlo = distance as u32 & 0x3;
                let immhi = (distance >> 2) as u32 & 0x7ffff;
                self.write_u32(at, word | (immlo << 29) | (immhi << 5));
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn forward_and_backward_references_are_patched() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        let label = buffer.new_label();
        buffer.emit_u8(0xeb);
        buffer.emit_u8(0);
        assert!(buffer.add_fixup(label, 1, FixupKind::X86Rel8).is_some());
        buffer.emit_bytes(&[0x90; 3]);
        buffer.bind(label);
        buffer.emit_u8(0xe9);
        buffer.emit_u32(0);
        assert!(buffer.add_fixup(label, 6, FixupKind::X86Rel32).is_none());
        let code = buffer.finish().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(code, [0xeb, 3, 0x90, 0x90, 0x90, 0xe9, 0xfb, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rewinding_drops_code_and_its_references() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        let label = buffer.new_label();
        buffer.emit_u8(0xeb);
        buffer.emit_u8(0);
        buffer.add_fixup(label, 1, FixupKind::X86Rel8);
        let checkpoint = buffer.checkpoint();
        buffer.emit_u8(0xeb);
        buffer.emit_u8(0);
        buffer.add_fixup(label, 3, FixupKind::X86Rel8);
        buffer.rewind(checkpoint);
        assert_eq!(buffer.offset(), 2);
        buffer.emit_u8(0x90);
        buffer.emit_u8(0xeb);
        buffer.emit_u8(0);
        buffer.add_fixup(label, 4, FixupKind::X86Rel8);
        buffer.bind(label);
        let code = buffer.finish().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(code, [0xeb, 3, 0x90, 0xeb, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unbound_label_fails() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        let label = buffer.new_label();
        buffer.emit_u32(0x1400_0000);
        buffer.add_fixup(label, 0, FixupKind::A64Branch26);
        assert_eq!(buffer.finish(), Err(AsmError::UnboundLabel));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unreferenced_unbound_label_is_fine() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        let _ = buffer.new_label();
        buffer.emit_u8(0xc3);
        assert_eq!(buffer.finish(), Ok(&[0xc3][..]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn out_of_range_reference_fails() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        let label = buffer.new_label();
        buffer.emit_bytes(&[0xeb, 0]);
        buffer.add_fixup(label, 1, FixupKind::X86Rel8);
        buffer.emit_bytes(&[0x90; 128]);
        buffer.bind(label);
        assert_eq!(buffer.finish(), Err(AsmError::BranchOutOfRange));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rel8_reaches_exactly_its_range() {
        assert!(FixupKind::X86Rel8.reaches(1, 2 + 127));
        assert!(!FixupKind::X86Rel8.reaches(1, 2 + 128));
        assert!(FixupKind::X86Rel8.reaches(200, 201 - 128));
        assert!(!FixupKind::X86Rel8.reaches(200, 201 - 129));
        assert!(FixupKind::A64Branch14.reaches(0, 32764));
        assert!(!FixupKind::A64Branch14.reaches(0, 32768));
        assert!(FixupKind::A64Branch14.reaches(32768, 0));
        assert!(!FixupKind::A64Branch14.reaches(32772, 0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn alignment_pads_with_filler() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut buffer = CodeBuffer::new(&mut code, &work);
        buffer.emit_u8(0xc3);
        buffer.align_with(8, 0xcc);
        assert_eq!(
            buffer.finish().unwrap(),
            [0xc3, 0xcc, 0xcc, 0xcc, 0xcc, 0xcc, 0xcc, 0xcc]
        );
    }
}

//! Disassemblers for `dump-asm` and for checking encodings in tests.
//!
//! Tests can decode both architectures on any host. Other builds only have
//! the decoder of the host architecture; code for the other one is listed as
//! raw bytes.

use core::fmt;
use core::fmt::Write;

use super::Architecture;

/// One instruction of a listing, at `offset` from the start of the code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DisassembledInstruction<'a> {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub length: usize,
    pub text: &'a str,
    /// The 64-bit constant the instruction materializes, if any (an
    /// immediate move, or the last `movz`/`movk` of a sequence on AArch64,
    /// or a load from the constant pool).
    pub constant: Option<u64>,
    /// The offset a PC-relative memory operand refers to, if any.
    pub pc_relative_target: Option<usize>,
}

/// Calls `visit` with each instruction of `code` (assumed to start at offset 0, so branch targets are code offsets)
/// for `architecture`, in order: those up to `data_offset`, then the 64-bit constants they load (see
/// `PortableMacroAssembler::finish`). Loads of a constant list it as their `constant`.
pub fn for_each_instruction(
    architecture: Architecture,
    code: &[u8],
    data_offset: usize,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(&DisassembledInstruction<'_>),
) {
    let constant_at = |target: usize| {
        let bytes = code.get(target..target + 8)?;
        (target >= data_offset).then(|| u64::from_le_bytes(bytes.try_into().expect("eight bytes")))
    };
    let mut visit_instruction = |mut instruction: DisassembledInstruction<'_>| {
        if let Some(target) = instruction.pc_relative_target {
            instruction.constant = instruction.constant.or_else(|| constant_at(target));
        }
        visit(&instruction);
    };
    match architecture {
        Architecture::X86_64 => x86_64_instructions(&code[..data_offset], &mut visit_instruction),
        Architecture::AArch64 => aarch64_instructions(&code[..data_offset], &mut visit_instruction),
    }
    let first_constant = data_offset.next_multiple_of(8);
    let mut text = InstructionText::new();
    for offset in (first_constant..code.len()).step_by(8) {
        let value = constant_at(offset).expect("constants fill the data");
        text.clear();
        let _ = write!(text, ".quad {value:#x}");
        visit_instruction(DisassembledInstruction {
            offset,
            length: 8,
            text: text.as_str(),
            constant: Some(value),
            pc_relative_target: None,
        });
    }
}

/// The text of one instruction. It is cut at the boundary of a character if it is longer than the room for it, which
/// is far more than the longest instruction needs.
struct InstructionText {
    bytes: [u8; Self::ROOM],
    len: usize,
    /// Whether runs of white space become one space, and white space at the start and at the end goes away.
    single_spaced: bool,
    /// Whether white space came after the last character that was not.
    space: bool,
}

impl InstructionText {
    // NB: The longest instruction text of the tests of the JIT has 41 bytes.
    const ROOM: usize = 256;

    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes: [0; Self::ROOM],
            len: 0,
            single_spaced: false,
            space: false,
        }
    }

    /// A text with one space between each two words.
    #[cfg(any(test, target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    fn single_spaced() -> Self {
        Self {
            single_spaced: true,
            ..Self::new()
        }
    }

    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.len = 0;
        self.space = false;
    }

    fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
        // NB: Text goes in at the boundaries of characters only, so this never fails.
        core::str::from_utf8(&self.bytes[..self.len]).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    fn push_str(&mut self, text: &str) {
        let mut end = text.len().min(Self::ROOM - self.len);
        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        self.bytes[self.len..self.len + end].copy_from_slice(&text.as_bytes()[..end]);
        self.len += end;
    }
}

impl fmt::Write for InstructionText {
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> fmt::Result {
        if !self.single_spaced {
            self.push_str(text);
            return Ok(());
        }
        for (index, character) in text.char_indices() {
            if character.is_whitespace() {
                self.space = self.len != 0;
                continue;
            }
            if self.space {
                self.push_str(" ");
                self.space = false;
            }
            self.push_str(&text[index..index + character.len_utf8()]);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(any(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
impl iced_x86::FormatterOutput for InstructionText {
    fn write(&mut self, text: &str, _kind: iced_x86::FormatterTextKind) {
        let _ = fmt::Write::write_str(self, text);
    }
}

/// The bytes of code that no decoder in this build understands.
#[cfg(not(test))]
fn raw_instructions(code: &[u8], visit: &mut impl FnMut(DisassembledInstruction<'_>)) {
    let mut text = InstructionText::new();
    for (index, chunk) in code.chunks(8).enumerate() {
        text.clear();
        text.push_str(".byte");
        for byte in chunk {
            let _ = write!(text, " {byte:02x}");
        }
        visit(DisassembledInstruction {
            offset: 8 * index,
            length: chunk.len(),
            text: text.as_str(),
            constant: None,
            pc_relative_target: None,
        });
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(test, target_arch = "x86_64")))]
fn x86_64_instructions(code: &[u8], visit: &mut impl FnMut(DisassembledInstruction<'_>)) {
    raw_instructions(code, visit);
}

#[cfg(not(any(test, target_arch = "aarch64")))]
fn aarch64_instructions(code: &[u8], visit: &mut impl FnMut(DisassembledInstruction<'_>)) {
    raw_instructions(code, visit);
}

#[cfg(any(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn x86_64_formatter() -> iced_x86::IntelFormatter {
    use iced_x86::Formatter;
    use iced_x86::MemorySizeOptions;

    let mut formatter = iced_x86::IntelFormatter::new();
    let options = formatter.options_mut();
    options.set_space_after_operand_separator(true);
    options.set_hex_prefix("0x");
    options.set_hex_suffix("");
    options.set_uppercase_hex(false);
    options.set_branch_leading_zeros(false);
    options.set_memory_size_options(MemorySizeOptions::Always);
    formatter
}

#[cfg(any(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
fn x86_64_instructions(code: &[u8], visit: &mut impl FnMut(DisassembledInstruction<'_>)) {
    use iced_x86::Decoder;
    use iced_x86::DecoderOptions;
    use iced_x86::Formatter;
    use iced_x86::OpKind;

    let mut decoder = Decoder::with_ip(64, code, 0, DecoderOptions::NONE);
    let mut formatter = x86_64_formatter();
    let mut text = InstructionText::new();
    while decoder.can_decode() {
        let instruction = decoder.decode();
        let offset = instruction.ip() as usize;
        text.clear();
        if instruction.is_invalid() {
            let _ = write!(text, ".byte {:02x}", code[offset]);
        } else {
            formatter.format(&instruction, &mut text);
        }
        let constant = (0..instruction.op_count())
            .find(|operand| instruction.op_kind(*operand) == OpKind::Immediate64)
            .map(|operand| instruction.immediate(operand));
        let pc_relative_target = instruction
            .is_ip_rel_memory_operand()
            .then(|| instruction.ip_rel_memory_address() as usize);
        visit(DisassembledInstruction {
            offset,
            length: instruction.len(),
            text: text.as_str(),
            constant,
            pc_relative_target,
        });
    }
}

#[cfg(any(test, target_arch = "aarch64"))]
fn aarch64_instructions(code: &[u8], visit: &mut impl FnMut(DisassembledInstruction<'_>)) {
    use farm64::format::FmtFormatter;
    use farm64::format::Formatter;

    let mut decoder = farm64::Decoder::new(code, 0, farm64::DecoderOptions::default());
    let formatter = FmtFormatter::new();
    let mut text = InstructionText::single_spaced();
    // The value each register holds after a `movz`/`movk` sequence.
    let mut register_values = [None::<u64>; 32];
    while decoder.can_decode() {
        let offset = decoder.position();
        let instruction = decoder.decode();
        let word = u32::from_le_bytes(code[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap());
        text.clear();
        if instruction.is_invalid() {
            let _ = write!(text, ".word {word:#010x}");
        } else {
            formatter.format(&instruction, &mut text);
        }
        let register = (word & 0x1f) as usize;
        let shift = 16 * ((word >> 21) & 3);
        let immediate = u64::from((word >> 5) & 0xffff) << shift;
        let constant = match word & 0xff80_0000 {
            // movz Xd, #imm16, lsl #shift
            0xd280_0000 => {
                register_values[register] = Some(immediate);
                Some(immediate)
            }
            // movk Xd, #imm16, lsl #shift
            0xf280_0000 => {
                let value = register_values[register].map(|value| (value & !(0xffff << shift)) | immediate);
                register_values[register] = value;
                value
            }
            _ => None,
        };
        // LDR (literal) of a 64-bit general or FP register.
        let pc_relative_target = (word & 0xff00_0000 == 0x5800_0000 || word & 0xff00_0000 == 0x5c00_0000).then(|| {
            let imm19 = ((((word >> 5) & 0x7ffff) << 13) as i32) >> 13;
            (offset as i64 + 4 * i64::from(imm19)) as usize
        });
        visit(DisassembledInstruction {
            offset,
            length: 4,
            text: text.as_str(),
            constant,
            pc_relative_target,
        });
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]

/// Listings as lists, for tests.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod listings {
    use super::*;

    /// A `DisassembledInstruction` that keeps its text.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct ListedInstruction {
        pub offset: usize,
        pub length: usize,
        pub text: String,
        pub constant: Option<u64>,
        pub pc_relative_target: Option<usize>,
    }

    /// The instructions of `code` (assumed to start at offset 0, so branch targets are code offsets) for
    /// `architecture`.
    pub fn listing(architecture: Architecture, code: &[u8]) -> Vec<ListedInstruction> {
        listing_with_data(architecture, code, code.len())
    }

    /// Like `listing()`, for instructions up to `data_offset` followed by the 64-bit constants they load.
    pub fn listing_with_data(architecture: Architecture, code: &[u8], data_offset: usize) -> Vec<ListedInstruction> {
        let mut instructions = Vec::new();
        for_each_instruction(architecture, code, data_offset, |instruction| {
            instructions.push(ListedInstruction {
                offset: instruction.offset,
                length: instruction.length,
                text: instruction.text.to_string(),
                constant: instruction.constant,
                pc_relative_target: instruction.pc_relative_target,
            })
        });
        instructions
    }

    /// One line per instruction, Intel syntax, code assumed to start at 0.
    pub fn x86_64(code: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        listing(Architecture::X86_64, code)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|instruction| {
                assert!(
                    !instruction.text.starts_with(".byte"),
                    "invalid x86-64 encoding in {code:02x?}"
                );
                instruction.text
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// One line per instruction, code assumed to start at 0.
    pub fn aarch64(code: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        aarch64_range(code, 0, code.len())
    }

    /// Disassembles `code[start..end]`, with addresses relative to `code`.
    pub fn aarch64_range(code: &[u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        use farm64::format::FmtFormatter;
        use farm64::format::Formatter;

        let code_start = start;
        let code = &code[start..end];
        assert!(code.len().is_multiple_of(4));
        let mut decoder = farm64::Decoder::new(code, code_start as u64, farm64::DecoderOptions::default());
        let formatter = FmtFormatter::new();
        let mut lines = Vec::new();
        while decoder.can_decode() {
            let offset = decoder.position();
            let instruction = decoder.decode();
            let word = u32::from_le_bytes(code[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap());
            assert!(!instruction.is_invalid(), "invalid AArch64 encoding {word:#010x}");
            let mut text = InstructionText::single_spaced();
            formatter.format(&instruction, &mut text);
            lines.push(text.as_str().to_string());
        }
        lines
    }

    /// Where the instructions end in the code that an assembler finished: at the end of the code of an assembler, and
    /// at the data offset that a macro assembler gives.
    pub(crate) trait InstructionsEnd {
        fn instructions_end(&self) -> usize;
    }

    impl InstructionsEnd for &[u8] {
        fn instructions_end(&self) -> usize {
            self.len()
        }
    }

    impl InstructionsEnd for usize {
        fn instructions_end(&self) -> usize {
            *self
        }
    }

    /// Checks a table of `"expected; disassembly" => |assembler| emission;`
    /// entries, reporting every mismatch at once.
    macro_rules! assert_encodings {
        ($assembler:ty, $disassemble:path, { $($expected:expr => |$a:ident| $body:expr;)* }) => {{
            let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            $(
                let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
                let mut $a = <$assembler>::new(&mut code, &work);
                $body;
                let end = crate::asm::disassembler::listings::InstructionsEnd::instructions_end(
                    &$a.finish().expect("assembling failed"),
                );
                let actual = $disassemble(&code[..end]).join("; ");
                if actual != $expected {
                    failures.push(format!("{}\n    expected: {}\n    actual:   {}", stringify!($body), $expected, actual));
                }
            )*
            assert!(failures.is_empty(), "{} mismatches:\n{}", failures.len(), failures.join("\n"));
        }};
    }

    pub(crate) use assert_encodings;
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::Gpr;
    use super::super::PortableMacroAssembler;
    use super::super::aarch64;
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn instruction_text_is_cut_at_the_boundary_of_a_character() {
        let mut text = InstructionText::new();
        let _ = write!(text, "{}", "ä".repeat(InstructionText::ROOM));
        assert_eq!(text.as_str(), "ä".repeat(InstructionText::ROOM / 2));
        let _ = write!(text, "a");
        assert_eq!(text.as_str().len(), InstructionText::ROOM);
        text.clear();
        let _ = write!(text, "x{}", "€".repeat(InstructionText::ROOM));
        assert_eq!(
            text.as_str(),
            format!("x{}", "€".repeat((InstructionText::ROOM - 1) / 3))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn single_spaced_text_has_one_space_between_words() {
        let mut text = InstructionText::single_spaced();
        let _ = write!(text, "  mov   x0,");
        let _ = write!(text, "  x1 \t");
        assert_eq!(text.as_str(), "mov x0, x1");
        text.clear();
        let _ = write!(text, " ret ");
        assert_eq!(text.as_str(), "ret");
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_x86_64_code_with_constants() {
        // mov r11, 0x123456789abcdef0; call r11; ret
        let code = [
            0x49, 0xbb, 0xf0, 0xde, 0xbc, 0x9a, 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12, 0x41, 0xff, 0xd3, 0xc3,
        ];
        let listing = listing(Architecture::X86_64, &code);
        let lines = listing
            .iter()
            .map(|instruction| (instruction.offset, instruction.text.as_str(), instruction.constant))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(
            lines,
            [
                (0, "mov r11, 0x123456789abcdef0", Some(0x1234_5678_9abc_def0)),
                (10, "call r11", None),
                (13, "ret", None),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_aarch64_code_with_constants() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut masm = aarch64::MacroAssembler::new(&mut code, &work);
        masm.move_imm64(Gpr(9), 0x1234_0000_0000_def0);
        masm.finish().unwrap();
        let listing = listing(Architecture::AArch64, &code);
        assert_eq!(listing.last().unwrap().constant, Some(0x1234_0000_0000_def0));
        assert!(listing[0].text.starts_with("mov"), "{listing:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_loads_from_the_constant_pool() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut masm = aarch64::MacroAssembler::new(&mut code, &work);
        masm.move_imm64(Gpr(9), 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0);
        let data_offset = masm.finish().unwrap();
        let listing = listing_with_data(Architecture::AArch64, &code, data_offset);
        assert!(listing[0].text.starts_with("ldr"), "{listing:?}");
        assert_eq!(listing[0].constant, Some(0x1234_5678_9abc_def0));
        assert_eq!(listing.last().unwrap().text, ".quad 0x123456789abcdef0");

        let mut masm = super::super::x86_64::MacroAssembler::new(&mut code, &work);
        masm.move_imm64(Gpr(0), 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0);
        let data_offset = masm.finish().unwrap();
        let listing = listing_with_data(Architecture::X86_64, &code, data_offset);
        assert_eq!(listing[0].constant, Some(0x1234_5678_9abc_def0), "{listing:?}");
    }
}

/*

//! Machine code in executable memory, for tests that run generated code
//! natively.

/// Machine code copied into its own executable mapping (never writable and
/// executable at the same time).
pub(crate) struct ExecutableCode {
    address: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
    #[cfg_attr(windows, allow(dead_code))]
    size: usize,
}

#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn pthread_jit_write_protect_np(enabled: libc::c_int);
    fn sys_icache_invalidate(start: *mut libc::c_void, length: libc::size_t);
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", windows)))]
unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The compiler runtime's instruction cache flush (a no-op on x86-64).
    fn __clear_cache(start: *mut libc::c_char, end: *mut libc::c_char);
}

impl ExecutableCode {
    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.address as u64
    }

    pub(crate) fn new(code: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let size = code.len().max(1).next_multiple_of(16384);
        #[cfg(windows)]
        // SAFETY: A fresh reservation, written before it is made executable.
        unsafe {
            let address = ak::windows_code_memory::reserve(size);
            assert!(!address.is_null());
            assert!(ak::windows_code_memory::make_writable(address, size));
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), address, code.len());
            assert!(ak::windows_code_memory::make_executable(address, size));
            Self {
                address: address.cast(),
                size,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        // SAFETY: A fresh private anonymous mapping for JIT code, written
        // while the thread's write protection of it is off.
        unsafe {
            let address = libc::mmap(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                size,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE | libc::PROT_EXEC,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANON | libc::MAP_JIT,
                -1,
                0,
            );
            assert_ne!(address, libc::MAP_FAILED);
            pthread_jit_write_protect_np(0);
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), address.cast::<u8>(), code.len());
            pthread_jit_write_protect_np(1);
            sys_icache_invalidate(address, code.len());
            Self { address, size }
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", windows)))]
        // SAFETY: A fresh private anonymous mapping, written before it is
        // made executable.
        unsafe {
            let address = libc::mmap(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                size,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS,
                -1,
                0,
            );
            assert_ne!(address, libc::MAP_FAILED);
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(code.as_ptr(), address.cast::<u8>(), code.len());
            assert_eq!(libc::mprotect(address, size, libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_EXEC), 0);
            __clear_cache(address.cast(), address.cast::<libc::c_char>().add(code.len()));
            Self { address, size }
        }
    }

    /// Reinterprets the code as a function pointer of type `F`.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `F` must be an `extern "sysv64" fn` type matching what the code implements.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn function<F: Copy>(&self) -> F {
        assert_eq!(size_of::<F>(), size_of::<*mut core::ffi::c_void>());
        // SAFETY: The caller guarantees `F` is a matching function pointer type.
        unsafe { core::mem::transmute_copy(&self.address) }
    }
}

impl Drop for ExecutableCode {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The mapping was created in `new` with this size.
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        unsafe {
            libc::munmap(self.address, self.size);
        }
        // SAFETY: The reservation was created in `new`.
        #[cfg(windows)]
        unsafe {
            ak::windows_code_memory::release(self.address.cast());
        }
    }
}

/*
