//! Encoders of the instructions the WebAssembly JIT uses beyond what LibJS needs: VEX three-operand
//! scalar float arithmetic for f32 and f64, rounding and conversions, bitwise operations on xmm registers, BMI1 and
//! BMI2 (`andn`, `shlx`, `sarx`, `shrx`, `rorx`), bit counting (`lzcnt`, `tzcnt`, `popcnt`) and unsigned division,
//! and `vex()`, which encodes any VEX instruction from its opcode, for the vector instructions.
//!
//! VEX instructions with a scalar operand ignore VEX.L (they are LIG); this file encodes them with L = 0, like the
//! 128-bit forms.
//! With `Assembler::for_host`, SIMD, rotations and bit counts select SSE and bit-scan fallbacks as needed.

use super::super::Address;
use super::super::Fpr;
use super::super::Gpr;
use super::super::Width;
use super::super::buffer::Label;
use super::Assembler;
use super::ByteRegisters;
use super::Prefix;
use super::Rm;

/// The implied mandatory prefix of a VEX instruction (VEX.pp).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VexPrefix {
    None = 0,
    OperandSize = 1,
    Rep = 2,
    Repne = 3,
}

/// The opcode map of a VEX instruction (VEX.m-mmmm).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VexMap {
    Map0F = 1,
    Map0F38 = 2,
    Map0F3A = 3,
}

/// A VEX instruction, as the manuals write it: `VEX.128.66.0F38.W0 00` is `VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F38,
/// 0x00)`. Instructions that ignore VEX.W are encoded with W0, and VEX.L is always 0 (128 bits, or scalar).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VexOpcode {
    pub prefix: VexPrefix,
    pub map: VexMap,
    pub opcode: u8,
    pub w: bool,
}

impl VexOpcode {
    pub const fn new(prefix: VexPrefix, map: VexMap, opcode: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            prefix,
            map,
            opcode,
            w: false,
        }
    }

    /// The same instruction with VEX.W1, like the 64-bit forms of `vpinsrq` and `vmovq`.
    pub const fn w1(self) -> Self {
        Self { w: true, ..self }
    }
}

/// The r/m operand of `Assembler::vex()`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VexOperand {
    /// A register by its encoding: an xmm register, or a general purpose one for the instructions that take one.
    Register(u8),
    Memory(Address),
    /// `[rip + label]`.
    Label(Label),
}

/// A scalar float operation of SSE's arithmetic row, by its opcode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FloatOp {
    Sqrt = 0x51,
    Add = 0x58,
    Mul = 0x59,
    Sub = 0x5c,
    Min = 0x5d,
    Div = 0x5e,
    Max = 0x5f,
}

/// A bitwise operation on whole xmm registers, by its opcode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BitwiseOp {
    And = 0x54,
    AndNot = 0x55,
    Or = 0x56,
    Xor = 0x57,
}

/// The precision of a scalar float instruction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Precision {
    Single,
    Double,
}

impl Precision {
    fn scalar_prefix(self) -> VexPrefix {
        match self {
            Precision::Single => VexPrefix::Rep,
            Precision::Double => VexPrefix::Repne,
        }
    }
}

/// The rounding of `vroundss`/`vroundsd`, with the precision exception suppressed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Rounding {
    Nearest = 0x8,
    Down = 0x9,
    Up = 0xa,
    TowardZero = 0xb,
}

/// The bit counting instructions, by their second opcode byte.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BitCount {
    Popcnt = 0xb8,
    Tzcnt = 0xbc,
    Lzcnt = 0xbd,
}

/// The BMI2 shifts, by their implied prefix.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ShiftX {
    Shl,
    Sar,
    Shr,
}

impl Assembler<'_> {
    /// Emits a VEX prefix and opcode with ModRM for `reg`, the extra source `vvvv` and `rm`, using the two-byte form
    /// where it can.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(super) fn vex_instruction(
        &mut self,
        prefix: VexPrefix,
        map: VexMap,
        w: bool,
        opcode: u8,
        reg: u8,
        vvvv: u8,
        rm: Rm,
        trailing_immediate_size: usize,
    ) {
        let (x, b) = match rm {
            Rm::Reg(register) => (false, register & 8 != 0),
            Rm::Mem(address) => (
                address.index.is_some_and(|(index, _)| index.0 & 8 != 0),
                address.base.0 & 8 != 0,
            ),
            Rm::Rip(_) => (false, false),
        };
        let r = reg & 8 != 0;
        let low = (u8::from(!r) << 7) | ((!vvvv & 0xf) << 3) | prefix as u8;
        if !x && !b && !w && map == VexMap::Map0F {
            self.buffer.emit_u8(0xc5);
            self.buffer.emit_u8(low);
        } else {
            self.buffer.emit_u8(0xc4);
            self.buffer
                .emit_u8((u8::from(!r) << 7) | (u8::from(!x) << 6) | (u8::from(!b) << 5) | map as u8);
            self.buffer.emit_u8((u8::from(w) << 7) | (low & 0x7f));
        }
        self.buffer.emit_u8(opcode);
        self.emit_modrm_rm(reg, &rm, trailing_immediate_size);
    }

    /// Emits the VEX instruction `opcode` with `reg` in ModRM.reg, `vvvv` as the extra source (0 where the
    /// instruction has none), `rm` and an immediate byte. Registers are by their encoding, whatever their class.
    /// With host instruction selection, the Wasm SIMD subset uses equivalent SSE sequences without AVX2.
    pub fn vex(&mut self, opcode: VexOpcode, reg: u8, vvvv: u8, rm: VexOperand, immediate: Option<u8>) {
        if !self.cpu_features().avx2 {
            self.legacy_vector(opcode, reg, vvvv, rm, immediate);
            return;
        }
        let rm = match rm {
            VexOperand::Register(register) => Rm::Reg(register),
            VexOperand::Memory(address) => Rm::Mem(address),
            VexOperand::Label(label) => Rm::Rip(label),
        };
        self.vex_instruction(
            opcode.prefix,
            opcode.map,
            opcode.w,
            opcode.opcode,
            reg,
            vvvv,
            rm,
            usize::from(immediate.is_some()),
        );
        if let Some(immediate) = immediate {
            self.buffer.emit_u8(immediate);
        }
    }

    /// `op dst, lhs, rhs` on xmm registers.
    pub fn vex_rrr(&mut self, opcode: VexOpcode, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.vex(opcode, dst.0, lhs.0, VexOperand::Register(rhs.0), None);
    }

    // Scalar float arithmetic.

    /// `vaddss`/`vsubss`/... `dst, lhs, rhs` (and the `sd` forms). The bits above the scalar come from `lhs`.
    pub fn vfloat_rrr(&mut self, op: FloatOp, precision: Precision, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            op as u8,
            dst.0,
            lhs.0,
            Rm::Reg(rhs.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vaddss`/`vsubss`/... `dst, lhs, [address]` (and the `sd` forms).
    pub fn vfloat_rrm(&mut self, op: FloatOp, precision: Precision, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, address: &Address) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            op as u8,
            dst.0,
            lhs.0,
            Rm::Mem(*address),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `imul dst, [address]`.
    pub fn imul_rm(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.op_rm(width, &[0x0f, 0xaf], dst.0, address);
    }

    /// `vroundss`/`vroundsd dst, src, src, mode`.
    pub fn vround(&mut self, precision: Precision, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr, rounding: Rounding) {
        let opcode = match precision {
            Precision::Single => 0x0a,
            Precision::Double => 0x0b,
        };
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::OperandSize,
            VexMap::Map0F3A,
            false,
            opcode,
            dst.0,
            src.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            1,
        );
        self.buffer.emit_u8(rounding as u8);
    }

    /// `vandps`/`vandnps`/`vorps`/`vxorps dst, lhs, rhs` on all 128 bits. `AndNot` computes `!lhs & rhs`.
    pub fn vbitwise_rrr(&mut self, op: BitwiseOp, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::None,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            op as u8,
            dst.0,
            lhs.0,
            Rm::Reg(rhs.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vandps`/... `dst, lhs, xmmword [rip + label]`.
    pub fn vbitwise_r_label(&mut self, op: BitwiseOp, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, label: Label) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::None,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            op as u8,
            dst.0,
            lhs.0,
            Rm::Rip(label),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vmovaps dst, src`.
    pub fn vmovaps_rr(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(VexPrefix::None, VexMap::Map0F, false, 0x28, dst.0, 0, Rm::Reg(src.0), 0);
    }

    /// `vucomiss`/`vucomisd lhs, rhs`: ZF/PF/CF = unordered 111, less 001, equal 100, greater 000.
    pub fn vucomis(&mut self, precision: Precision, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        let prefix = match precision {
            Precision::Single => VexPrefix::None,
            Precision::Double => VexPrefix::OperandSize,
        };
        self.simd_instruction(prefix, VexMap::Map0F, false, 0x2e, lhs.0, 0, Rm::Reg(rhs.0), 0);
    }

    // Loads and stores.

    /// `vmovss`/`vmovsd dst, [address]`, zeroing the bits above the scalar.
    pub fn vmovs_rm(&mut self, precision: Precision, dst: Fpr, address: &Address) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            0x10,
            dst.0,
            0,
            Rm::Mem(*address),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vmovss`/`vmovsd [address], src`.
    pub fn vmovs_mr(&mut self, precision: Precision, address: &Address, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            0x11,
            src.0,
            0,
            Rm::Mem(*address),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vmovss`/`vmovsd dst, [rip + label]`.
    pub fn vmovs_r_label(&mut self, precision: Precision, dst: Fpr, label: Label) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            0x10,
            dst.0,
            0,
            Rm::Rip(label),
            0,
        );
    }

    // Moves between register classes.

    /// `vmovd xmm, r32` or `vmovq xmm, r64`, zeroing the rest of the register.
    pub fn vmov_xr(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Fpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::OperandSize,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            width == Width::W64,
            0x6e,
            dst.0,
            0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vmovd r32, xmm` or `vmovq r64, xmm`.
    pub fn vmov_rx(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::OperandSize,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            width == Width::W64,
            0x7e,
            src.0,
            0,
            Rm::Reg(dst.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    // Conversions.

    /// `vcvtsi2ss`/`vcvtsi2sd dst, upper, r32/r64`: the signed integer as a float, with the bits above the scalar
    /// from `upper`.
    pub fn vcvtsi2s(&mut self, precision: Precision, width: Width, dst: Fpr, upper: Fpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            width == Width::W64,
            0x2a,
            dst.0,
            upper.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vcvttss2si`/`vcvttsd2si r32/r64, src`: truncates toward zero. Produces the "integer indefinite" value (only
    /// the sign bit set) for NaN and out of range inputs.
    pub fn vcvtts2si(&mut self, precision: Precision, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            precision.scalar_prefix(),
            VexMap::Map0F,
            width == Width::W64,
            0x2c,
            dst.0,
            0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vcvtss2sd dst, upper, src`: widens a float to a double.
    pub fn vcvtss2sd(&mut self, dst: Fpr, upper: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::Rep,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            0x5a,
            dst.0,
            upper.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `vcvtsd2ss dst, upper, src`: rounds a double to a float.
    pub fn vcvtsd2ss(&mut self, dst: Fpr, upper: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.simd_instruction(
            VexPrefix::Repne,
            VexMap::Map0F,
            false,
            0x5a,
            dst.0,
            upper.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    // Integer instructions.

    /// `lzcnt`/`tzcnt`/`popcnt dst, src`.
    pub fn bit_count(&mut self, op: BitCount, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        let features = self.cpu_features();
        if (op == BitCount::Lzcnt && !features.lzcnt) || (op == BitCount::Tzcnt && !features.bmi1) {
            self.count_zeros(op, width, dst, src);
            return;
        }
        self.emit_instruction(
            Prefix::Rep,
            width == Width::W64,
            &[0x0f, op as u8],
            dst.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            ByteRegisters::No,
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `div divisor`: unsigned divide rdx:rax.
    pub fn div(&mut self, width: Width, divisor: Gpr) {
        self.emit_instruction(
            Prefix::None,
            width == Width::W64,
            &[0xf7],
            6,
            Rm::Reg(divisor.0),
            ByteRegisters::No,
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `shlx`/`sarx`/`shrx dst, src, amount`. The amount is masked to 5 (or 6) bits; the flags are left alone.
    pub fn shiftx(&mut self, op: ShiftX, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        let prefix = match op {
            ShiftX::Shl => VexPrefix::OperandSize,
            ShiftX::Sar => VexPrefix::Rep,
            ShiftX::Shr => VexPrefix::Repne,
        };
        self.vex_instruction(
            prefix,
            VexMap::Map0F38,
            width == Width::W64,
            0xf7,
            dst.0,
            amount.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    /// `rorx dst, src, amount`: rotates right by an immediate. Without BMI2, uses MOV and ROR, clobbering flags.
    pub fn rorx(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        if !self.cpu_features().bmi2 {
            self.mov_rr(width, dst, src);
            self.shift_ri(super::ShiftOp::Ror, width, dst, amount);
            return;
        }
        self.vex_instruction(
            VexPrefix::Repne,
            VexMap::Map0F3A,
            width == Width::W64,
            0xf0,
            dst.0,
            0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            1,
        );
        self.buffer.emit_u8(amount);
    }

    /// `andn dst, inverted, src`: `!inverted & src`.
    pub fn andn(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, inverted: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.vex_instruction(
            VexPrefix::None,
            VexMap::Map0F38,
            width == Width::W64,
            0xf2,
            dst.0,
            inverted.0,
            Rm::Reg(src.0),
            0,
        );
    }

    // Atomics.

    /// An instruction with a memory operand of `size` bytes (1, 2, 4 or 8), whose byte form has `byte_opcode` and
    /// whose other forms have `opcode`.
    fn sized_mr(&mut self, size: u32, byte_opcode: &[u8], opcode: &[u8], address: &Address, reg: Gpr) {
        let (prefix, w, opcode, byte_registers) = match size {
            1 => (Prefix::None, false, byte_opcode, ByteRegisters::Reg),
            2 => (Prefix::OperandSize, false, opcode, ByteRegisters::No),
            4 => (Prefix::None, false, opcode, ByteRegisters::No),
            _ => (Prefix::None, true, opcode, ByteRegisters::No),
        };
        self.emit_instruction(prefix, w, opcode, reg.0, Rm::Mem(*address), byte_registers, 0);
    }

    /// `lock xadd [address], reg` of `size` bytes: adds reg to memory and puts the old value in reg.
    pub fn lock_xadd(&mut self, size: u32, address: &Address, reg: Gpr) {
        self.buffer.emit_u8(0xf0);
        self.sized_mr(size, &[0x0f, 0xc0], &[0x0f, 0xc1], address, reg);
    }

    /// `lock cmpxchg [address], reg` of `size` bytes: stores reg if memory holds what rax does, else loads it into rax.
    pub fn lock_cmpxchg(&mut self, size: u32, address: &Address, reg: Gpr) {
        self.buffer.emit_u8(0xf0);
        self.sized_mr(size, &[0x0f, 0xb0], &[0x0f, 0xb1], address, reg);
    }

    /// `xchg [address], reg` of `size` bytes, which is locked without a prefix.
    pub fn xchg_mr(&mut self, size: u32, address: &Address, reg: Gpr) {
        self.sized_mr(size, &[0x86], &[0x87], address, reg);
    }

    /// `mfence`.
    pub fn mfence(&mut self) {
        self.buffer.emit_bytes(&[0x0f, 0xae, 0xf0]);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::super::Scale;
    use super::super::super::Width::W32;

    use super::super::super::disassembler;

    #[test]
    fn scalar_float_arithmetic() {
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "vaddss xmm0, xmm1, xmm2" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Add, Precision::Single, XMM0, XMM1, XMM2);
            "vaddsd xmm8, xmm9, xmm10" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Add, Precision::Double, XMM8, XMM9, XMM10);
            "vsubss xmm15, xmm0, xmm14" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Sub, Precision::Single, XMM15, XMM0, XMM14);
            "vmulsd xmm1, xmm12, xmm3" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Mul, Precision::Double, XMM1, XMM12, XMM3);
            "vdivss xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Div, Precision::Single, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vminsd xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Min, Precision::Double, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vmaxss xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Max, Precision::Single, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vsqrtsd xmm1, xmm2, xmm11" => |a| a.vfloat_rrr(FloatOp::Sqrt, Precision::Double, XMM1, XMM2, XMM11);
            "vroundss xmm1, xmm1, xmm1, 8" => |a| a.vround(Precision::Single, XMM1, XMM1, Rounding::Nearest);
            "vroundsd xmm9, xmm2, xmm2, 0xb" => |a| a.vround(Precision::Double, XMM9, XMM2, Rounding::TowardZero);
            "vaddsd xmm1, xmm2, qword ptr [rbp-0x48]" => |a| a.vfloat_rrm(
                FloatOp::Add,
                Precision::Double,
                XMM1,
                XMM2,
                &Address::new(RBP, -0x48)
            );
            "vmulss xmm9, xmm10, dword ptr [r13+8]" => |a| a.vfloat_rrm(
                FloatOp::Mul,
                Precision::Single,
                XMM9,
                XMM10,
                &Address::new(R13, 8)
            );
            "imul eax, dword ptr [rbp-0x10]" => |a| a.imul_rm(W32, RAX, &Address::new(RBP, -0x10));
            "imul r9, qword ptr [rbp-0x18]" => |a| a.imul_rm(W64, R9, &Address::new(RBP, -0x18));
            "vucomiss xmm1, xmm2" => |a| a.vucomis(Precision::Single, XMM1, XMM2);
            "vucomisd xmm9, xmm12" => |a| a.vucomis(Precision::Double, XMM9, XMM12);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn bitwise_and_moves() {
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "vandps xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vbitwise_rrr(BitwiseOp::And, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vandnps xmm1, xmm2, xmm13" => |a| a.vbitwise_rrr(BitwiseOp::AndNot, XMM1, XMM2, XMM13);
            "vorps xmm10, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vbitwise_rrr(BitwiseOp::Or, XMM10, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vxorps xmm0, xmm0, xmm0" => |a| a.vbitwise_rrr(BitwiseOp::Xor, XMM0, XMM0, XMM0);
            "vmovaps xmm1, xmm9" => |a| a.vmovaps_rr(XMM1, XMM9);
            "vmovd xmm1, eax" => |a| a.vmov_xr(W32, XMM1, RAX);
            "vmovq xmm9, r10" => |a| a.vmov_xr(W64, XMM9, R10);
            "vmovd r11d, xmm1" => |a| a.vmov_rx(W32, R11, XMM1);
            "vmovq rax, xmm15" => |a| a.vmov_rx(W64, RAX, XMM15);
            "vmovss xmm1, dword ptr [rbp-0x48]" => |a| a.vmovs_rm(Precision::Single, XMM1, &Address::new(RBP, -0x48));
            "vmovsd xmm9, qword ptr [r15+rax+0x10]" => |a| a.vmovs_rm(
                Precision::Double,
                XMM9,
                &Address::indexed(R15, RAX, Scale::One, 0x10)
            );
            "vmovsd qword ptr [r15+r12], xmm2" => |a| a.vmovs_mr(
                Precision::Double,
                &Address::indexed(R15, R12, Scale::One, 0),
                XMM2
            );
            "vmovss dword ptr [rsp+8], xmm14" => |a| a.vmovs_mr(Precision::Single, &Address::new(RSP, 8), XMM14);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn rip_relative_operands() {
        let (mut code, work) = (crate::asm::test_code(), crate::asm::test_work());
        let mut assembler = Assembler::new(&mut code, &work);
        let label = assembler.new_label();
        assembler.vbitwise_r_label(BitwiseOp::And, XMM1, XMM2, label);
        assembler.vmovs_r_label(Precision::Double, XMM3, label);
        assembler.bind(label);
        let code = assembler.finish().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            disassembler::x86_64(&code),
            ["vandps xmm1, xmm2, xmmword ptr [0x10]", "vmovsd xmm3, qword ptr [0x10]"]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn conversions() {
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "vcvtsi2ss xmm1, xmm1, eax" => |a| a.vcvtsi2s(Precision::Single, W32, XMM1, XMM1, RAX);
            "vcvtsi2sd xmm9, xmm2, r12" => |a| a.vcvtsi2s(Precision::Double, W64, XMM9, XMM2, R12);
            "vcvttss2si eax, xmm1" => |a| a.vcvtts2si(Precision::Single, W32, RAX, XMM1);
            "vcvttsd2si r9, xmm10" => |a| a.vcvtts2si(Precision::Double, W64, R9, XMM10);
            "vcvtss2sd xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vcvtss2sd(XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vcvtsd2ss xmm11, xmm11, xmm12" => |a| a.vcvtsd2ss(XMM11, XMM11, XMM12);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn any_vex_instruction() {
        use VexMap::{Map0F, Map0F3A, Map0F38};
        use VexPrefix::{OperandSize, Rep};
        let vpaddd = VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F, 0xfe);
        let vpshufb = VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F38, 0x00);
        let vpinsrq = VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F3A, 0x22).w1();
        let vpextrd = VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F3A, 0x16);
        let vmovdqu_load = VexOpcode::new(Rep, Map0F, 0x6f);
        let vpbroadcastb = VexOpcode::new(OperandSize, Map0F38, 0x78);
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "vpaddd xmm1, xmm2, xmm3" => |a| a.vex_rrr(vpaddd, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3);
            "vpaddd xmm9, xmm10, xmm11" => |a| a.vex_rrr(vpaddd, XMM9, XMM10, XMM11);
            "vpshufb xmm1, xmm2, xmm13" => |a| a.vex_rrr(vpshufb, XMM1, XMM2, XMM13);
            "vpinsrq xmm1, xmm2, r9, 1" => |a| a.vex(vpinsrq, 1, 2, VexOperand::Register(R9.0), Some(1));
            "vpextrd r10d, xmm3, 2" => |a| a.vex(vpextrd, 3, 0, VexOperand::Register(R10.0), Some(2));
            "vmovdqu xmm12, xmmword ptr [r15+rax+0x10]" => |a| a.vex(
                vmovdqu_load,
                12,
                0,
                VexOperand::Memory(Address::indexed(R15, RAX, Scale::One, 0x10)),
                None
            );
            "vpbroadcastb xmm0, xmm7" => |a| a.vex(vpbroadcastb, 0, 0, VexOperand::Register(7), None);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn integer_instructions() {
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "lzcnt eax, ecx" => |a| a.bit_count(BitCount::Lzcnt, W32, RAX, RCX);
            "tzcnt r8, r9" => |a| a.bit_count(BitCount::Tzcnt, W64, R8, R9);
            "popcnt rax, r15" => |a| a.bit_count(BitCount::Popcnt, W64, RAX, R15);
            "div ecx" => |a| a.div(W32, RCX);
            "div r10" => |a| a.div(W64, R10);
            "shlx eax, ecx, edx" => |a| a.shiftx(ShiftX::Shl, W32, RAX, RCX, RDX);
            "sarx r8, r9, r10" => |a| a.shiftx(ShiftX::Sar, W64, R8, R9, R10);
            "shrx rax, r12, rcx" => |a| a.shiftx(ShiftX::Shr, W64, RAX, R12, RCX);
            "rorx eax, ecx, 7" => |a| a.rorx(W32, RAX, RCX, 7);
            "rorx r13, rbx, 0x3f" => |a| a.rorx(W64, R13, RBX, 63);
            "andn eax, ecx, edx" => |a| a.andn(W32, RAX, RCX, RDX);
            "andn r9, r10, r11" => |a| a.andn(W64, R9, R10, R11);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn atomic_instructions() {
        assert_encodings!(Assembler, disassembler::x86_64, {
            "lock xadd byte ptr [rdi], sil" => |a| a.lock_xadd(1, &Address::new(RDI, 0), RSI);
            "lock xadd word ptr [r8+0x10], ax" => |a| a.lock_xadd(2, &Address::new(R8, 0x10), RAX);
            "lock xadd dword ptr [rax], r9d" => |a| a.lock_xadd(4, &Address::new(RAX, 0), R9);
            "lock xadd qword ptr [r13], rcx" => |a| a.lock_xadd(8, &Address::new(R13, 0), RCX);
            "lock cmpxchg byte ptr [rcx], dl" => |a| a.lock_cmpxchg(1, &Address::new(RCX, 0), RDX);
            "lock cmpxchg word ptr [rcx], r10w" => |a| a.lock_cmpxchg(2, &Address::new(RCX, 0), R10);
            "lock cmpxchg dword ptr [rcx], edx" => |a| a.lock_cmpxchg(4, &Address::new(RCX, 0), RDX);
            "lock cmpxchg qword ptr [r12], rdx" => |a| a.lock_cmpxchg(8, &Address::new(R12, 0), RDX);
            "xchg byte ptr [rax], dil" => |a| a.xchg_mr(1, &Address::new(RAX, 0), RDI);
            "xchg word ptr [rax], cx" => |a| a.xchg_mr(2, &Address::new(RAX, 0), RCX);
            "xchg dword ptr [rax], ecx" => |a| a.xchg_mr(4, &Address::new(RAX, 0), RCX);
            "xchg qword ptr [rax], r15" => |a| a.xchg_mr(8, &Address::new(RAX, 0), R15);
            "mfence" => |a| a.mfence();
        });
    }
}

//! The portable macro assembler on x86-64 (System V ABI).

use super::super::Address;
use super::super::Architecture;
use super::super::AsmError;
use super::super::Condition;
use super::super::DoubleCondition;
use super::super::Fpr;
use super::super::FprSet;
use super::super::Gpr;
use super::super::GprSet;
use super::super::JumpPatch;
use super::super::Label;
use super::super::MachineFrame;
use super::super::NegativeZero;
use super::super::PortableMacroAssembler;
use super::super::Width;
use super::super::Width::W32;
use super::super::Width::W64;
use super::*;
use ak::ZoneMap;

/// General scratch register: immediates, call targets, working values.
const SCRATCH: Gpr = R11;
/// Second scratch register, only used where `SCRATCH` is already taken.
const SCRATCH2: Gpr = R10;
const FP_SCRATCH: Fpr = XMM15;

/// Which of two doubles `min_or_max_double()` takes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Extreme {
    Min,
    Max,
}

/// The macro assembler for x86-64. Wraps an `Assembler`, which stays
/// available for architecture specific code.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MacroAssembler<'a> {
    pub assembler: Assembler<'a>,
    /// 64-bit constants that do not fit an immediate, loaded RIP-relative
    /// from a pool after the code, in the order of the pool.
    constants: ZoneMap<'a, u64, Label>,
    /// 128-bit constants, in the same pool.
    constants128: ZoneMap<'a, u128, Label>,
}

fn condition_code(condition: Condition) -> Cond {
    match condition {
        Condition::Equal | Condition::Zero => Cond::Equal,
        Condition::NotEqual | Condition::NonZero => Cond::NotEqual,
        Condition::LessThan => Cond::Less,
        Condition::LessThanOrEqual => Cond::LessOrEqual,
        Condition::GreaterThan => Cond::Greater,
        Condition::GreaterThanOrEqual => Cond::GreaterOrEqual,
        Condition::Below => Cond::Below,
        Condition::BelowOrEqual => Cond::BelowOrEqual,
        Condition::Above => Cond::Above,
        Condition::AboveOrEqual => Cond::AboveOrEqual,
        Condition::Overflow => Cond::Overflow,
        Condition::NoOverflow => Cond::NoOverflow,
        Condition::Negative => Cond::Sign,
        Condition::PositiveOrZero => Cond::NotSign,
    }
}

/// How a double condition maps onto `ucomisd` flags.
enum DoubleFlags {
    /// One condition code, after `ucomisd lhs, rhs` or `ucomisd rhs, lhs`.
    Single { swap: bool, cond: Cond },
    /// Both condition codes must hold.
    Both(Cond, Cond),
    /// Either condition code holds.
    Either(Cond, Cond),
}

fn double_flags(condition: DoubleCondition) -> DoubleFlags {
    use DoubleFlags::*;
    // ucomisd sets ZF,PF,CF to 111 when unordered, 001 for less, 100 for
    // equal and 000 for greater. Ordered "less" conditions swap the operands
    // so they can use CF=0, which excludes unordered.
    match condition {
        DoubleCondition::Equal => Both(Cond::Equal, Cond::NotParity),
        DoubleCondition::NotEqual => Both(Cond::NotEqual, Cond::NotParity),
        DoubleCondition::LessThan => Single {
            swap: true,
            cond: Cond::Above,
        },
        DoubleCondition::LessThanOrEqual => Single {
            swap: true,
            cond: Cond::AboveOrEqual,
        },
        DoubleCondition::GreaterThan => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::Above,
        },
        DoubleCondition::GreaterThanOrEqual => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::AboveOrEqual,
        },
        DoubleCondition::EqualOrUnordered => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::Equal,
        },
        DoubleCondition::NotEqualOrUnordered => Either(Cond::NotEqual, Cond::Parity),
        DoubleCondition::LessThanOrUnordered => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::Below,
        },
        DoubleCondition::LessThanOrEqualOrUnordered => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::BelowOrEqual,
        },
        DoubleCondition::GreaterThanOrUnordered => Single {
            swap: true,
            cond: Cond::Below,
        },
        DoubleCondition::GreaterThanOrEqualOrUnordered => Single {
            swap: true,
            cond: Cond::BelowOrEqual,
        },
        DoubleCondition::Ordered => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::NotParity,
        },
        DoubleCondition::Unordered => Single {
            swap: false,
            cond: Cond::Parity,
        },
    }
}

impl<'a> BranchGroups<'a> for MacroAssembler<'a> {
    fn branch_assembler(&mut self) -> &mut Assembler<'a> {
        &mut self.assembler
    }
}

impl<'a> MacroAssembler<'a> {
    /// The bytes the prologue of `frame` moves the stack pointer down by after saving the general purpose registers.
    fn reserved_frame_bytes(frame: &MachineFrame) -> u32 {
        frame.locals_size + 8 * frame.saved_fprs.len() as u32
    }

    /// `dst = lhs op rhs` for a commutative operation.
    fn commutative(&mut self, op: AluOp, width: Width, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        if dst == lhs {
            self.assembler.alu_rr(op, width, dst, rhs);
        } else if dst == rhs {
            self.assembler.alu_rr(op, width, dst, lhs);
        } else {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, lhs);
            self.assembler.alu_rr(op, width, dst, rhs);
        }
    }

    /// `dst = lhs - rhs`, leaving the flags of the subtraction.
    fn subtract(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        if dst == lhs {
            self.assembler.sub_rr(width, dst, rhs);
        } else if dst == rhs {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, SCRATCH, lhs);
            self.assembler.sub_rr(width, SCRATCH, rhs);
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, SCRATCH);
        } else {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, lhs);
            self.assembler.sub_rr(width, dst, rhs);
        }
    }

    /// `dst = lhs op imm`, with `imm` already in the instruction's range.
    fn with_imm32(&mut self, op: AluOp, width: Width, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32) {
        if dst != lhs {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, lhs);
        }
        self.assembler.alu_ri(op, width, dst, imm);
    }

    /// `dst = lhs op imm` for a 64-bit operation with an arbitrary immediate.
    fn with_imm64(&mut self, op: AluOp, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64) {
        if let Ok(imm) = i32::try_from(imm) {
            self.with_imm32(op, W64, dst, lhs, imm);
        } else {
            // NB: The immediate is an operand in the constant pool.
            self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, lhs);
            let label = self.constant(imm as u64);
            self.assembler.alu_r_label(op, dst, label);
        }
    }

    fn mov_if_needed(&mut self, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        if dst != src {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, src);
        }
    }

    fn shift_imm(&mut self, op: ShiftOp, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        let amount = amount & (width.bits() as u8 - 1);
        if amount == 0 {
            // A 32-bit move still zero-extends, even onto itself.
            if dst != src || width == W32 {
                self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, src);
            }
            return;
        }
        self.mov_if_needed(width, dst, src);
        self.assembler.shift_ri(op, width, dst, amount);
    }

    /// Shifts by a register amount, which x86 needs in CL. The register allocator puts the amounts of shift nodes there
    /// (see `SHIFT_AMOUNT_GPR`), and other amounts go through the scratch registers.
    fn shift_register(&mut self, op: ShiftOp, width: Width, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        if amount == RCX && dst != RCX {
            self.mov_if_needed(width, dst, src);
            self.assembler.shift_rcl(op, width, dst);
            return;
        }
        self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, SCRATCH, src);
        if amount != RCX {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, SCRATCH2, RCX);
            self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, RCX, amount);
        }
        self.assembler.shift_rcl(op, width, SCRATCH);
        if amount != RCX {
            self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, RCX, SCRATCH2);
        }
        self.assembler.mov_rr(width, dst, SCRATCH);
    }

    /// The label of `value` in the constant pool.
    fn constant(&mut self, value: u64) -> Label {
        *self
            .constants
            .entry(value)
            .or_insert_with(|| self.assembler.new_label())
    }

    /// The label of the 128-bit `value` in the constant pool.
    fn constant128(&mut self, value: u128) -> Label {
        *self
            .constants128
            .entry(value)
            .or_insert_with(|| self.assembler.new_label())
    }

    fn compare_imm(&mut self, width: Width, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64) {
        if imm == 0 {
            self.assembler.test_rr(width, lhs, lhs);
        } else if let Ok(imm) = i32::try_from(imm) {
            self.assembler.cmp_ri(width, lhs, imm);
        } else {
            let label = self.constant(imm as u64);
            self.assembler.cmp_r_label(lhs, label);
        }
    }

    fn test_mask(&mut self, width: Width, value: Gpr, mask: u64) {
        let all_ones = match width {
            W32 => u64::from(u32::MAX),
            W64 => u64::MAX,
        };
        if mask == all_ones {
            self.assembler.test_rr(width, value, value);
        } else if width == W32 {
            self.assembler.test_ri(W32, value, mask as u32 as i32);
        } else if let Ok(imm) = i32::try_from(mask as i64) {
            self.assembler.test_ri(W64, value, imm);
        } else {
            self.move_imm64(SCRATCH, mask);
            self.assembler.test_rr(W64, value, SCRATCH);
        }
    }

    fn set_condition(&mut self, cond: Cond, dst: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.setcc(cond, dst);
        self.assembler.movzx8_rr(dst, dst);
    }

    fn compare_doubles(&mut self, swap: bool, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        if swap {
            self.assembler.ucomisd(rhs, lhs);
        } else {
            self.assembler.ucomisd(lhs, rhs);
        }
    }

    /// `Math.min` or `Math.max` of two doubles: `minsd` or `maxsd` where
    /// they are ordered and differ, the bitwise or (for the minimum) or and
    /// (for the maximum) where they are equal, which makes -0 the minimum
    /// and +0 the maximum of zeros, and NaN where either is NaN.
    fn min_or_max_double(&mut self, extreme: Extreme, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        let (unordered, differ, done) = (
            self.assembler.new_label(),
            self.assembler.new_label(),
            self.assembler.new_label(),
        );
        self.assembler.movapd_rr(FP_SCRATCH, lhs);
        self.assembler.ucomisd(lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Parity, unordered);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::NotEqual, differ);
        match extreme {
            Extreme::Min => self.assembler.orpd(FP_SCRATCH, rhs),
            Extreme::Max => self.assembler.andpd(FP_SCRATCH, rhs),
        }
        self.assembler.jmp(done);
        self.assembler.bind(unordered);
        self.assembler.addsd(FP_SCRATCH, rhs);
        self.assembler.jmp(done);
        self.assembler.bind(differ);
        match extreme {
            Extreme::Min => self.assembler.minsd(FP_SCRATCH, rhs),
            Extreme::Max => self.assembler.maxsd(FP_SCRATCH, rhs),
        }
        self.assembler.bind(done);
        self.assembler.movapd_rr(dst, FP_SCRATCH);
    }

    /// `dst = lhs op rhs` for an SSE operation where `dst` must be the left operand.
    fn double_operation(
        &mut self,
        operation: fn(&mut Assembler<'a>, Fpr, Fpr),
        commutative: bool,
        dst: Fpr,
        lhs: Fpr,
        rhs: Fpr,
    ) {
        if dst == lhs {
            operation(&mut self.assembler, dst, rhs);
        } else if dst == rhs {
            if commutative {
                operation(&mut self.assembler, dst, lhs);
            } else {
                self.assembler.movapd_rr(FP_SCRATCH, lhs);
                operation(&mut self.assembler, FP_SCRATCH, rhs);
                self.assembler.movapd_rr(dst, FP_SCRATCH);
            }
        } else {
            self.assembler.movapd_rr(dst, lhs);
            operation(&mut self.assembler, dst, rhs);
        }
    }
}

impl PortableMacroAssembler for MacroAssembler<'_> {
    type In<'a> = MacroAssembler<'a>;

    const ARCHITECTURE: Architecture = Architecture::X86_64;
    const ARGUMENT_GPRS: &'static [Gpr] = &[RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9];
    const ARGUMENT_FPRS: &'static [Fpr] = &[XMM0, XMM1, XMM2, XMM3, XMM4, XMM5, XMM6, XMM7];
    const RETURN_GPRS: [Gpr; 2] = [RAX, RDX];
    const CALLEE_SAVED_GPRS: GprSet = GprSet::of(&[RBX, RBP, R12, R13, R14, R15]);
    const CALLEE_SAVED_FPRS: FprSet = FprSet::EMPTY;
    const CALLER_SAVED_GPRS: GprSet = GprSet::of(&[RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, R8, R9, R10, R11]);
    const CALLER_SAVED_FPRS: FprSet = FprSet(0xffff);
    const SCRATCH_GPRS: GprSet = GprSet::of(&[SCRATCH, SCRATCH2]);
    const SCRATCH_FPRS: FprSet = FprSet::of(&[FP_SCRATCH]);
    const ALLOCATABLE_GPRS: GprSet = GprSet::of(&[RAX, RCX, RDX, RBX, RSI, RDI, R8, R9, R12, R13, R14, R15]);
    const ALLOCATABLE_FPRS: FprSet = FprSet(0x7fff);
    const SHIFT_AMOUNT_GPR: Option<Gpr> = Some(RCX);
    const STACK_POINTER: Gpr = RSP;
    const FRAME_POINTER: Gpr = RBP;

    fn new<'a>(code: &'a mut Column<u8>, work: &'a Zone) -> MacroAssembler<'a> {
        MacroAssembler {
            assembler: Assembler::new(code, work),
            constants: ZoneMap::new_in(work),
            constants128: ZoneMap::new_in(work),
        }
    }

    fn offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.assembler.offset()
    }

    fn new_label(&mut self) -> Label {
        self.assembler.new_label()
    }

    fn bind(&mut self, label: Label) {
        self.assembler.bind(label);
    }

    fn label_offset(&self, label: Label) -> Option<usize> {
        self.assembler.label_offset(label)
    }

    fn patchable_nop(&mut self) -> usize {
        let offset = self.assembler.offset();
        // NB: As long as `jmp rel32`.
        self.assembler.nops(5);
        offset
    }

    fn jump_patch(from: usize, to: usize) -> JumpPatch {
        let displacement = i32::try_from(to as i64 - (from as i64 + 5)).expect("code is smaller than 2 GiB");
        let [b0, b1, b2, b3] = displacement.to_le_bytes();
        JumpPatch::new(&[0xe9, b0, b1, b2, b3])
    }

    fn finish(mut self) -> Result<usize, AsmError> {
        let data_offset = self.assembler.offset();
        if !self.constants128.is_empty() {
            self.assembler.align_data(16);
            for (value, label) in self.constants128.iter() {
                self.assembler.bind(*label);
                self.assembler.data_u64(*value as u64);
                self.assembler.data_u64((*value >> 64) as u64);
            }
        }
        if !self.constants.is_empty() {
            self.assembler.align_data(8);
            for (value, label) in self.constants.iter() {
                self.assembler.bind(*label);
                self.assembler.data_u64(*value);
            }
        }
        self.assembler.finish()?;
        Ok(data_offset)
    }

    fn unreachable(&mut self) {
        self.assembler.ud2();
    }

    fn move64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, src);
    }

    fn move32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.mov_rr(W32, dst, src);
    }

    fn move_imm64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, imm: u64) {
        if u32::try_from(imm).is_ok() || i32::try_from(imm as i64).is_ok() {
            self.assembler.mov_ri(dst, imm);
        } else {
            let label = self.constant(imm);
            self.assembler.mov_r_label(dst, label);
        }
    }

    fn move_imm32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, imm: u32) {
        self.assembler.mov_ri32(dst, imm);
    }

    fn sign_extend32_to_64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.movsxd_rr(dst, src);
    }

    fn load8(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movzx8_rm(dst, address);
    }

    fn load8_sign_extend(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movsx8_rm(W64, dst, address);
    }

    fn load16(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movzx16_rm(dst, address);
    }

    fn load16_sign_extend(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movsx16_rm(W64, dst, address);
    }

    fn load32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.mov_rm(W32, dst, address);
    }

    fn load32_sign_extend(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movsxd_rm(dst, address);
    }

    fn load64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.mov_rm(W64, dst, address);
    }

    fn store8(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.mov8_mr(address, src);
    }

    fn store16(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.mov16_mr(address, src);
    }

    fn store32(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.mov_mr(W32, address, src);
    }

    fn store64(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.mov_mr(W64, address, src);
    }

    fn store_imm8(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: u8) {
        self.assembler.mov8_mi(address, imm);
    }

    // OPTIMIZATION: A 16-bit immediate after an operand-size prefix stalls the legacy decoders for a few cycles, which
    //               a store of the low half of a register avoids.
    fn store_imm16(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: u16) {
        self.assembler.mov_ri32(SCRATCH, u32::from(imm));
        self.assembler.mov16_mr(address, SCRATCH);
    }

    fn store_imm32(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: u32) {
        self.assembler.mov_mi(W32, address, imm as i32);
    }

    fn store_imm64(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: u64) {
        if let Ok(imm) = i32::try_from(imm as i64) {
            self.assembler.mov_mi(W64, address, imm);
        } else {
            self.move_imm64(SCRATCH, imm);
            self.assembler.mov_mr(W64, address, SCRATCH);
        }
    }

    fn add32_to_memory_imm(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: i32) {
        self.assembler.alu_mi(AluOp::Add, W32, address, imm);
    }

    fn add64_to_memory_imm(&mut self, address: &Address, imm: i32) {
        self.assembler.alu_mi(AluOp::Add, W64, address, imm);
    }

    fn load_effective_address(&mut self, dst: Gpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.lea(W64, dst, address);
    }

    fn load_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movsd_rm(dst, address);
    }

    fn store_double(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.movsd_mr(address, src);
    }

    fn load_imm128(&mut self, dst: Fpr, imm: u128) {
        let label = self.constant128(imm);
        self.assembler.movups_r_label(dst, label);
    }

    fn store128(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.movups_mr(address, src);
    }

    fn load_float_as_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, address: &Address) {
        self.assembler.movss_rm(dst, address);
        self.assembler.cvtss2sd(dst, dst);
    }

    fn store_double_as_float(&mut self, address: &Address, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.cvtsd2ss(FP_SCRATCH, src);
        self.assembler.movss_mr(address, FP_SCRATCH);
    }

    fn add32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Add, W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn add32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32) {
        if dst == lhs {
            self.assembler.add_ri(W32, dst, imm);
        } else {
            self.assembler.lea(W32, dst, &Address::new(lhs, imm));
        }
    }

    fn add64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Add, W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn add64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64) {
        match i32::try_from(imm) {
            Ok(imm) if dst != lhs => self.assembler.lea(W64, dst, &Address::new(lhs, imm)),
            _ => self.with_imm64(AluOp::Add, dst, lhs, imm),
        }
    }

    fn sub32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.subtract(W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn sub32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::Sub, W32, dst, lhs, imm);
    }

    fn sub64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.subtract(W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn sub64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64) {
        self.with_imm64(AluOp::Sub, dst, lhs, imm);
    }

    fn and32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::And, W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn and32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u32) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::And, W32, dst, lhs, imm as i32);
    }

    fn and64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::And, W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn and64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u64) {
        if imm == u64::from(u32::MAX) {
            // Zero-extending move.
            self.assembler.mov_rr(W32, dst, lhs);
        } else {
            self.with_imm64(AluOp::And, dst, lhs, imm as i64);
        }
    }

    fn or32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Or, W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn or32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u32) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::Or, W32, dst, lhs, imm as i32);
    }

    fn or64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Or, W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn or64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u64) {
        self.with_imm64(AluOp::Or, dst, lhs, imm as i64);
    }

    fn xor32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Xor, W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn xor32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u32) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::Xor, W32, dst, lhs, imm as i32);
    }

    fn xor64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Xor, W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn xor64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u64) {
        self.with_imm64(AluOp::Xor, dst, lhs, imm as i64);
    }

    fn mul32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        if dst == rhs {
            self.assembler.imul_rr(W32, dst, lhs);
        } else {
            self.mov_if_needed(W32, dst, lhs);
            self.assembler.imul_rr(W32, dst, rhs);
        }
    }

    fn mul32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: u32) {
        self.assembler.imul_rri(W32, dst, lhs, imm as i32);
    }

    fn mul64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        if dst == rhs {
            self.assembler.imul_rr(W64, dst, lhs);
        } else {
            self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, lhs);
            self.assembler.imul_rr(W64, dst, rhs);
        }
    }

    fn neg32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.mov_if_needed(W32, dst, src);
        self.assembler.neg(W32, dst);
    }

    fn neg64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, src);
        self.assembler.neg(W64, dst);
    }

    fn not32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.mov_if_needed(W32, dst, src);
        self.assembler.not(W32, dst);
    }

    fn not64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, src);
        self.assembler.not(W64, dst);
    }

    fn shl32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Shl, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shl32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Shl, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shl64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Shl, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shl64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Shl, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shr32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Shr, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shr32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Shr, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shr64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Shr, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn shr64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Shr, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn sar32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Sar, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn sar32_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Sar, W32, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn sar64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: Gpr) {
        self.shift_register(ShiftOp::Sar, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    fn sar64_imm(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, amount: u8) {
        self.shift_imm(ShiftOp::Sar, W64, dst, src, amount);
    }

    // NB: Overflow branches do not macro-fuse with the arithmetic before them, so they keep only themselves within
    //     a branch window (see `BranchGroups::branch_group()`).
    fn branch_add32_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Add, W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_add32_imm_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32, overflow: Label) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::Add, W32, dst, lhs, imm);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_sub32_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.subtract(W32, dst, lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_sub32_imm_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32, overflow: Label) {
        self.with_imm32(AluOp::Sub, W32, dst, lhs, imm);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_mul32_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.mul32(dst, lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_neg32_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.neg32(dst, src);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_add64_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.commutative(AluOp::Add, W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch_sub64_overflow(&mut self, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, overflow: Label) {
        self.subtract(W64, dst, lhs, rhs);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Overflow, overflow);
    }

    fn branch32(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.assembler.cmp_rr(W32, lhs, rhs);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch32_imm(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.compare_imm(W32, lhs, i64::from(imm));
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch64(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.assembler.cmp_rr(W64, lhs, rhs);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch_if_stack_pointer_below(&mut self, limit: &Address, target: Label) {
        self.branch64_memory(Condition::Above, limit, RSP, target);
    }

    fn branch64_imm(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.compare_imm(W64, lhs, imm);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch32_memory_imm(&mut self, condition: Condition, address: &Address, imm: i32, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.assembler.cmp_mi(W32, address, imm);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch16_memory_imm(&mut self, condition: Condition, address: &Address, imm: u16, target: Label) {
        // NB: 16-bit compares only see the low 16 bits, so a sign-extended
        //     imm8 matches the zero-extended value if it has the same bits.
        match i8::try_from(imm as i16) {
            Ok(imm8) if matches!(condition, Condition::Equal | Condition::NotEqual) => self.branch_group(|m| {
                m.assembler.cmp16_mi8(address, imm8);
                m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
            }),
            _ => {
                self.assembler.movzx16_rm(SCRATCH, address);
                self.branch32_imm(condition, SCRATCH, i32::from(imm), target);
            }
        }
    }

    fn branch64_memory(&mut self, condition: Condition, address: &Address, rhs: Gpr, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.assembler.cmp_mr(W64, address, rhs);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch64_memory_imm(&mut self, condition: Condition, address: &Address, imm: i64, target: Label) {
        let Ok(imm) = i32::try_from(imm) else {
            self.move_imm64(SCRATCH, imm as u64);
            self.branch64_memory(condition, address, SCRATCH, target);
            return;
        };
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.assembler.cmp_mi(W64, address, imm);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch_test32(&mut self, condition: Condition, value: Gpr, mask: u32, target: Label) {
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.test_mask(W32, value, u64::from(mask));
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn branch_test64(&mut self, condition: Condition, value: Gpr, mask: u64, target: Label) {
        if mask != u64::MAX && i32::try_from(mask as i64).is_err() {
            self.move_imm64(SCRATCH, mask);
            self.branch_group(|m| {
                m.assembler.test_rr(W64, value, SCRATCH);
                m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
            });
            return;
        }
        self.branch_group(|m| {
            m.test_mask(W64, value, mask);
            m.assembler.jcc(condition_code(condition), target);
        });
    }

    fn compare32_set(&mut self, condition: Condition, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.cmp_rr(W32, lhs, rhs);
        self.set_condition(condition_code(condition), dst);
    }

    fn compare32_imm_set(&mut self, condition: Condition, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i32) {
        self.compare_imm(W32, lhs, i64::from(imm));
        self.set_condition(condition_code(condition), dst);
    }

    fn compare64_set(&mut self, condition: Condition, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.cmp_rr(W64, lhs, rhs);
        self.set_condition(condition_code(condition), dst);
    }

    fn compare64_imm_set(&mut self, condition: Condition, dst: Gpr, lhs: Gpr, imm: i64) {
        self.compare_imm(W64, lhs, imm);
        self.set_condition(condition_code(condition), dst);
    }

    fn select64(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, dst: Gpr, if_true: Gpr, if_false: Gpr) {
        let cond = condition_code(condition);
        self.assembler.cmp_rr(W64, lhs, rhs);
        if dst == if_true {
            self.assembler.cmovcc(cond.invert(), W64, dst, if_false);
        } else {
            // A plain mov does not change the flags.
            self.mov_if_needed(W64, dst, if_false);
            self.assembler.cmovcc(cond, W64, dst, if_true);
        }
    }

    fn select32(&mut self, condition: Condition, lhs: Gpr, rhs: Gpr, dst: Gpr, if_true: Gpr, if_false: Gpr) {
        let cond = condition_code(condition);
        self.assembler.cmp_rr(W32, lhs, rhs);
        if dst == if_true {
            self.assembler.cmovcc(cond.invert(), W32, dst, if_false);
        } else {
            // A plain mov does not change the flags.
            self.mov_if_needed(W32, dst, if_false);
            self.assembler.cmovcc(cond, W32, dst, if_true);
        }
    }

    fn jump(&mut self, target: Label) {
        self.assembler.jmp(target);
    }

    fn jump_absolute(&mut self, address: u64) {
        self.move_imm64(SCRATCH, address);
        self.assembler.jmp_r(SCRATCH);
    }

    fn call(&mut self, target: Label) {
        self.assembler.call(target);
    }

    fn call_register(&mut self, target: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.call_r(target);
    }

    fn call_absolute(&mut self, address: u64) {
        let label = self.constant(address);
        self.assembler.call_label_indirect(label);
    }

    fn ret(&mut self) {
        self.assembler.ret();
    }

    fn move_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        if dst != src {
            self.assembler.movapd_rr(dst, src);
        }
    }

    fn move_double_imm(&mut self, dst: Fpr, value: f64) {
        let bits = value.to_bits();
        if bits == 0 {
            self.assembler.xorpd(dst, dst);
        } else {
            let label = self.constant(bits);
            self.assembler.movsd_r_label(dst, label);
        }
    }

    fn move_gpr_to_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.movq_xr(dst, src);
    }

    fn move_double_to_gpr(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.movq_rx(dst, src);
    }

    fn add_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.double_operation(Assembler::addsd, true, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn sub_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.double_operation(Assembler::subsd, false, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn mul_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.double_operation(Assembler::mulsd, true, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn div_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.double_operation(Assembler::divsd, false, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn min_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.min_or_max_double(Extreme::Min, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn max_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        self.min_or_max_double(Extreme::Max, dst, lhs, rhs);
    }

    fn sqrt_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.sqrtsd(dst, src);
    }

    fn floor_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.roundsd(dst, src, 0b1001);
    }

    fn ceil_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.roundsd(dst, src, 0b1010);
    }

    fn neg_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        let label = self.constant(1 << 63);
        self.assembler.movsd_r_label(FP_SCRATCH, label);
        self.move_double(dst, src);
        self.assembler.xorpd(dst, FP_SCRATCH);
    }

    fn abs_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Fpr) {
        let label = self.constant(!(1 << 63));
        self.assembler.movsd_r_label(FP_SCRATCH, label);
        self.move_double(dst, src);
        self.assembler.andpd(dst, FP_SCRATCH);
    }

    fn convert_int32_to_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Gpr) {
        // Break the dependency on the old value of dst.
        self.assembler.xorpd(dst, dst);
        self.assembler.cvtsi2sd(W32, dst, src);
    }

    fn convert_int64_to_double(&mut self, dst: Fpr, src: Gpr) {
        self.assembler.xorpd(dst, dst);
        self.assembler.cvtsi2sd(W64, dst, src);
    }

    fn branch_convert_double_to_int32(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Fpr, fail: Label, negative_zero: NegativeZero) {
        self.assembler.cvttsd2si(W32, dst, src);
        self.assembler.xorpd(FP_SCRATCH, FP_SCRATCH);
        self.assembler.cvtsi2sd(W32, FP_SCRATCH, dst);
        self.assembler.ucomisd(FP_SCRATCH, src);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::NotEqual, fail);
        self.assembler.jcc(Cond::Parity, fail);
        if negative_zero == NegativeZero::Fail {
            let done = self.assembler.new_label();
            self.branch_group(|m| {
                m.assembler.test_rr(W32, dst, dst);
                m.assembler.jcc(Cond::NotEqual, done);
            });
            self.assembler.movmskpd(SCRATCH, src);
            self.branch_group(|m| {
                m.assembler.test_ri(W32, SCRATCH, 1);
                m.assembler.jcc(Cond::NotEqual, fail);
            });
            self.assembler.bind(done);
        }
    }

    fn truncate_double_to_int64(&mut self, dst: Gpr, src: Fpr) {
        self.assembler.cvttsd2si(W64, dst, src);
    }

    fn branch_double(&mut self, condition: DoubleCondition, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr, target: Label) {
        match double_flags(condition) {
            DoubleFlags::Single { swap, cond } => {
                self.compare_doubles(swap, lhs, rhs);
                self.assembler.jcc(cond, target);
            }
            DoubleFlags::Both(first, second) => {
                let skip = self.assembler.new_label();
                self.compare_doubles(false, lhs, rhs);
                self.assembler.jcc(second.invert(), skip);
                self.assembler.jcc(first, target);
                self.assembler.bind(skip);
            }
            DoubleFlags::Either(first, second) => {
                self.compare_doubles(false, lhs, rhs);
                self.assembler.jcc(second, target);
                self.assembler.jcc(first, target);
            }
        }
    }

    fn compare_double_set(&mut self, condition: DoubleCondition, dst: Gpr, lhs: Fpr, rhs: Fpr) {
        match double_flags(condition) {
            DoubleFlags::Single { swap, cond } => {
                self.compare_doubles(swap, lhs, rhs);
                self.set_condition(cond, dst);
            }
            DoubleFlags::Both(first, second) => {
                self.compare_doubles(false, lhs, rhs);
                self.assembler.setcc(first, dst);
                self.assembler.setcc(second, SCRATCH);
                self.assembler.and_rr(W32, dst, SCRATCH);
                self.assembler.movzx8_rr(dst, dst);
            }
            DoubleFlags::Either(first, second) => {
                self.compare_doubles(false, lhs, rhs);
                self.assembler.setcc(first, dst);
                self.assembler.setcc(second, SCRATCH);
                self.assembler.or_rr(W32, dst, SCRATCH);
                self.assembler.movzx8_rr(dst, dst);
            }
        }
    }

    fn frame(saved_gprs: GprSet, saved_fprs: FprSet, locals_size: u32) -> MachineFrame {
        let saved_gprs = saved_gprs.without(RSP).without(RBP);
        let pushed = 8 * saved_gprs.len() as u32;
        let fpr_area = 8 * saved_fprs.len() as u32;
        // After `push rbp` the stack is 16-byte aligned; keep it that way.
        let mut locals_size = locals_size.next_multiple_of(8);
        if !(pushed + fpr_area + locals_size).is_multiple_of(16) {
            locals_size += 8;
        }
        MachineFrame {
            saved_gprs,
            saved_fprs,
            locals_size,
            caller_stack_offset: locals_size + fpr_area + pushed + 16,
        }
    }

    fn emit_prologue(&mut self, frame: &MachineFrame) {
        self.assembler.push(RBP);
        self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, RBP, RSP);
        for register in frame.saved_gprs.iter() {
            self.assembler.push(register);
        }
        let reserved = Self::reserved_frame_bytes(frame);
        if reserved != 0 {
            self.assembler.sub_ri(W64, RSP, reserved as i32);
        }
        // NB: The saved registers are within a page of the pushes, which touched the stack.
        for (i, register) in frame.saved_fprs.iter().enumerate() {
            let offset = frame.locals_size + 8 * i as u32;
            self.assembler.movsd_mr(&Address::new(RSP, offset as i32), register);
        }
        let reserved = reserved as i32;
        if needs_stack_probes(reserved) {
            // NB: The pushes touched the stack down to where the reserved part starts.
            self.assembler.lea(W64, SCRATCH, &Address::new(RSP, reserved));
            self.assembler.probe_stack(SCRATCH, RSP, Some(reserved));
        }
    }

    fn emit_epilogue(&mut self, frame: &MachineFrame) {
        for (i, register) in frame.saved_fprs.iter().enumerate() {
            let offset = frame.locals_size + 8 * i as u32;
            self.assembler.movsd_rm(register, &Address::new(RSP, offset as i32));
        }
        let reserved = Self::reserved_frame_bytes(frame);
        if reserved != 0 {
            self.assembler.add_ri(W64, RSP, reserved as i32);
        }
        for register in frame.saved_gprs.iter().rev() {
            self.assembler.pop(register);
        }
        self.assembler.pop(RBP);
    }

    fn allocate_stack(&mut self, bytes: i64) {
        if PROBES_STACK {
            // NB: The prologue may have moved the stack pointer without touching where it ended up.
            self.assembler.mov_rm(W32, SCRATCH, &Address::new(RSP, 0));
            let bytes = i32::try_from(bytes).expect("stack allocations are smaller than 2 GiB");
            if needs_stack_probes(bytes) {
                self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, SCRATCH2, RSP);
                self.assembler.lea(W64, SCRATCH, &Address::new(RSP, -bytes));
                self.assembler.probe_stack(SCRATCH2, SCRATCH, Some(bytes));
                self.assembler.mov_rr(W64, RSP, SCRATCH);
                return;
            }
        }
        self.sub64_imm(RSP, RSP, bytes);
    }
}
