//! Calls of builtin functions the code knows (see `Intrinsic`) that compiled
//! code runs inline.

use super::Flow;
use super::GraphBuilder;
use super::checks::SlowPaths;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::Operand;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::Float64Function;
use crate::ir::Float64UnaryOp;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::snapshot::CellId;
use crate::snapshot::HelperOperand;
use crate::snapshot::HelperResult;
use crate::snapshot::Intrinsic;
use crate::snapshot::value_feedback;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// What a call of a string builtin that reads a character returns.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StringCharacter {
    /// `String.prototype.charCodeAt`: the code unit.
    CodeUnit,
    /// `String.prototype.charAt`: the string of the code unit.
    String,
}

/// How many values `try_build_array_push()` appends inline at most.
const MAX_INLINE_PUSHED_VALUES: usize = 8;

/// Keep the receiver, start, delete count and inserted values within the
/// input limit of direct calls on every target.
const MAX_INLINE_SPLICED_VALUES: usize = crate::codegen::DIRECT_CALL_MAX_INPUTS - 3;

/// How many arguments `try_build_math_min_max()` compares inline at most.
const MAX_MIN_MAX_ARGUMENTS: usize = 8;

impl<'a> GraphBuilder<'a, '_> {
    /// Calls the packed-array splice helper without a native frame. It
    /// declines before doing anything observable for receivers or species
    /// constructors that require the ordinary call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_array_splice(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if arguments.len() < 2
            || arguments.len() > 2 + MAX_INLINE_SPLICED_VALUES
            || self.runtime.array_splice == 0
            || self.peek_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback) != Some(Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypeSplice)
            || self.holds_virtual_arguments(*this_value)
            || arguments.iter().any(|argument| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*argument))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let realm = self
            .function
            .executable
            .function
            .map_or(self.runtime.realm, |function| function.realm);
        if self
            .call_feedback(*call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.native_call)
            .map(|native| native.realm)
            != Some(realm)
            || self.checked_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback, *callee)?.is_none()
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let receiver = self.read(*this_value)?;
        let mut inputs = self.node_list();
        inputs.push(receiver);
        for (index, argument) in arguments.iter().enumerate() {
            let value = self.read(*argument)?;
            inputs.push(if index < 2 {
                self.int32_or_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, value)
            } else {
                value
            });
        }
        let result = self.emit(Op::CallArraySplice, &inputs, Some(Repr::Tagged));
        self.release_node_list(inputs);
        let result = self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, result);
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(result))
            .expect("calls have a value");
        self.write(*dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds a `Call` whose feedback saw a builtin that compiled code runs
    /// inline: a function of `Math` that computes with numbers,
    /// `String.prototype.charAt` and `charCodeAt`, or `String.fromCharCode`.
    /// Returns `None`, having built nothing, if it is no such call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_builtin_call(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some(feedback) = self.call_feedback(call_feedback) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if core::iter::once(&this_value)
            .chain(arguments)
            .any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let layout = &self.runtime.layout;
        let unary_ops = [
            (layout.builtin_math_abs, Float64UnaryOp::Abs),
            (layout.builtin_math_floor, Float64UnaryOp::Floor),
            (layout.builtin_math_ceil, Float64UnaryOp::Ceil),
            (layout.builtin_math_round, Float64UnaryOp::Round),
            (layout.builtin_math_sqrt, Float64UnaryOp::Sqrt),
        ];
        let functions = [
            (layout.builtin_math_exp, Float64Function::Exp),
            (layout.builtin_math_log, Float64Function::Log),
            (layout.builtin_math_sin, Float64Function::Sin),
            (layout.builtin_math_cos, Float64Function::Cos),
            (layout.builtin_math_tan, Float64Function::Tan),
            (layout.builtin_math_pow, Float64Function::Pow),
        ];
        let characters = [
            (layout.builtin_string_prototype_char_code_at, StringCharacter::CodeUnit),
            (layout.builtin_string_prototype_char_at, StringCharacter::String),
        ];
        // NB: Only calls with as many arguments as the builtin reads take the inline path. The code calls the
        //     builtin directly for others, which are rare, and the slow path of the inline path would not.
        let Some(&first) = arguments.first() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if feedback.target_intrinsic == Some(Intrinsic::StringFromCharCode) && arguments.len() == 1 {
            return self.try_build_string_from_char_code(call_feedback, dst, callee, first);
        }
        let Some(builtin) = feedback.target_builtin else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if let Some(&(_, op)) = unary_ops.iter().find(|(id, _)| *id == builtin)
            && arguments.len() == 1
        {
            return self
                .build_math_function(op, dst, callee, first, call_feedback)
                .map(Some);
        }
        if let Some(&(_, function)) = functions.iter().find(|(id, _)| *id == builtin) {
            let count = if function == Float64Function::Pow { 2 } else { 1 };
            if arguments.len() != count {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            return self
                .build_math_call(function, dst, callee, arguments, call_feedback)
                .map(Some);
        }
        if let Some(&(_, character)) = characters.iter().find(|(id, _)| *id == builtin)
            && arguments.len() == 1
        {
            return self
                .build_string_character(character, dst, callee, this_value, first)
                .map(Some);
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    /// Builds `Math.<op>(argument)`, a `Call` of the builtin, for
    /// numbers, if `callee` is the builtin of any realm. The instruction's
    /// slow path, which calls the callee, handles everything else, or the code
    /// exits there where that did not happen before. A site that only saw
    /// the builtin checks that `callee` is the function it saw instead.
    pub(super) fn build_math_function(
        &mut self,
        op: Float64UnaryOp,
        dst: Operand,
        callee: Operand,
        argument: Operand,
        call_feedback: u16,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let layout = &self.runtime.layout;
        let builtin = match op {
            Float64UnaryOp::Abs => layout.builtin_math_abs,
            Float64UnaryOp::Floor => layout.builtin_math_floor,
            Float64UnaryOp::Ceil => layout.builtin_math_ceil,
            Float64UnaryOp::Round => layout.builtin_math_round,
            Float64UnaryOp::Sqrt => layout.builtin_math_sqrt,
            Float64UnaryOp::Negate => unreachable!("no Math function negates"),
        };
        let target = self
            .call_feedback(call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.monomorphic_builtin(builtin))
            .filter(|_| self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget));
        if let Some(target) = target {
            self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
        }
        let callee = self.read(callee)?;
        let argument = self.read(argument)?;
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        self.exit_instead_of_slow_path(&mut slow_paths);
        if target.is_none() {
            self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Builtin(builtin), &[callee], true);
        }
        let result = if let Some(integer) = self.int32_value_of(argument) {
            self.build_int32_math_function(&mut slow_paths, op, integer)
        } else if let Some(double) = self.float64_value_of(argument) {
            let result = self.emit(Op::Float64Unary { op }, &[double], Some(Repr::Float64));
            self.emit(Op::BoxFloat64, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged))
        } else {
            // NB: Int32 arguments, then doubles.
            let (int32, other) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::Int32Value, &[argument]);
            self.block = other;
            let double = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Double, &[argument], true);
            let double = self.emit(Op::UnboxDouble, &[double], Some(Repr::Float64));
            let result = self.emit(Op::Float64Unary { op }, &[double], Some(Repr::Float64));
            let double_result = self.emit(Op::BoxFloat64, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged));
            let double = self.block;

            self.block = int32;
            let integer = self.refine(BranchCondition::Int32Value, true, &[argument]);
            let integer = self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[integer], Some(Repr::Int32));
            let int32_result = self.build_int32_math_function(&mut slow_paths, op, integer);
            let int32 = self.block;

            self.join_blocks(&[int32, double]);
            self.add_phi(&[int32_result, double_result])
        };
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(result))
            .expect("the instruction has a value");
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds `Math.<function>(arguments...)`, a `Call` of the builtin, for
    /// numbers, like `build_math_function()`: the code
    /// calls the runtime's function of doubles for it, which only computes,
    /// so nothing after the call forgets what it knew.
    pub(super) fn build_math_call(
        &mut self,
        function: Float64Function,
        dst: Operand,
        callee: Operand,
        arguments: &[Operand],
        call_feedback: u16,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let layout = &self.runtime.layout;
        let builtin = match function {
            Float64Function::Exp => layout.builtin_math_exp,
            Float64Function::Log => layout.builtin_math_log,
            Float64Function::Sin => layout.builtin_math_sin,
            Float64Function::Cos => layout.builtin_math_cos,
            Float64Function::Tan => layout.builtin_math_tan,
            Float64Function::Pow => layout.builtin_math_pow,
        };
        let target = self
            .call_feedback(call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.monomorphic_builtin(builtin))
            .filter(|_| self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget));
        if let Some(target) = target {
            self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
        }
        let callee = self.read(callee)?;
        let mut values = self.node_list();
        for argument in arguments {
            values.push(self.read(*argument)?);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        self.exit_instead_of_slow_path(&mut slow_paths);
        if target.is_none() {
            self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Builtin(builtin), &[callee], true);
        }
        let mut numbers = self.node_list();
        for &value in &values {
            numbers.push(self.float64_of_number(&mut slow_paths, value));
        }
        let result = self.emit(Op::CallFloat64Function { function }, &numbers, Some(Repr::Float64));
        self.release_node_list(numbers);
        self.release_node_list(values);
        let result = self.emit(Op::BoxFloat64, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(result))
            .expect("the instruction has a value");
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// The `Repr::Int32` value of `value`, if it is known to be an int32:
    /// itself, or what it boxes.
    pub(super) fn int32_value_of(&self, value: NodeId) -> Option<NodeId> {
        let node = self.graph.node(value);
        match (node.repr, &node.op) {
            (Some(Repr::Int32), _) => Some(value),
            (_, Op::BoxInt32) => Some(node.inputs[0]),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The `Repr::Float64` value of `value`, if it is known to be a double:
    /// itself, or what it boxes.
    pub(super) fn float64_value_of(&self, value: NodeId) -> Option<NodeId> {
        let node = self.graph.node(value);
        match (node.repr, &node.op) {
            (Some(Repr::Float64), _) => Some(value),
            (_, Op::BoxFloat64) => Some(node.inputs[0]),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The `Repr::Float64` of the `Repr::Int32` `integer`.
    pub(super) fn int32_to_float64(&mut self, integer: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        match self.graph.constant_value(integer) {
            Some(bits) => self.typed_constant(f64::from((bits as u32).cast_signed()).to_bits(), Repr::Float64),
            None => self.emit(Op::Int32ToFloat64, &[integer], Some(Repr::Float64)),
        }
    }

    /// `value` as a `Repr::Float64`, where it is a number, taking a slow
    /// path of `slow_paths` otherwise.
    pub(super) fn float64_of_number(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        self.float64_of(value, |builder, condition, inputs| {
            builder.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, condition, inputs, true)
        })
    }

    /// `value` as a `Repr::Int32`, where it is an int32, taking a slow path
    /// of `slow_paths` otherwise.
    pub(super) fn int32_or_slow_path(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        if let Some(integer) = self.int32_value_of(value) {
            return integer;
        }
        let value = self.tagged(value);
        let refined = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::Int32Value, &[value], true);
        self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[refined], Some(Repr::Int32))
    }

    /// Branches on whether the tagged `value` is an int32, and if not on
    /// whether it is a double, where `otherwise` branches on that (and
    /// returns the refinement of the value where it is one). The value of
    /// the int32 case is `int32` of its `Repr::Int32`, that of the double
    /// case `double` of its `Repr::Float64`. Returns the phi of those, of
    /// `repr`.
    pub(super) fn on_int32_or_double(
        &mut self,
        value: NodeId,
        repr: Repr,
        int32: fn(&mut Self, NodeId) -> NodeId,
        double: fn(&mut Self, NodeId) -> NodeId,
        otherwise: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, BranchCondition, &[NodeId]) -> NodeId,
    ) -> NodeId {
        self.on_integer_or_double(BranchCondition::Int32Value, value, repr, int32, double, otherwise)
    }

    /// Like `on_int32_or_double()`, with `integer` deciding the first case:
    /// `BranchCondition::Int32Value`, or `BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean`,
    /// whose booleans `UnboxInt32` makes 0 or 1 of.
    pub(super) fn on_integer_or_double(
        &mut self,
        integer: BranchCondition,
        value: NodeId,
        repr: Repr,
        int32: fn(&mut Self, NodeId) -> NodeId,
        double: fn(&mut Self, NodeId) -> NodeId,
        otherwise: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, BranchCondition, &[NodeId]) -> NodeId,
    ) -> NodeId {
        let (int32_block, other) = self.branch_both_ways(integer, &[value]);
        self.block = int32_block;
        let refined = self.refine(integer, true, &[value]);
        let integer = self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[refined], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let int32_value = int32(self, integer);
        let int32_end = self.block;

        self.block = other;
        let refined = otherwise(self, BranchCondition::Double, &[value]);
        let number = self.emit(Op::UnboxDouble, &[refined], Some(Repr::Float64));
        let double_value = double(self, number);
        let double_end = self.block;

        self.join_blocks(&[int32_end, double_end]);
        let phi = self.add_phi(&[int32_value, double_value]);
        self.graph.nodes[phi.index()].repr = Some(repr);
        phi
    }

    /// The tagged result of `Math.<op>(integer)` of a `Repr::Int32`
    /// `integer`: itself for the functions that round, and the absolute
    /// value but for the smallest int32, whose absolute value is no int32
    /// and goes to a slow path of `slow_paths`.
    fn build_int32_math_function(
        &mut self,
        slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>,
        op: Float64UnaryOp,
        integer: NodeId,
    ) -> NodeId {
        match op {
            Float64UnaryOp::Floor | Float64UnaryOp::Ceil | Float64UnaryOp::Round => self.tagged(integer),
            // NB: Negating the smallest int32 overflows, and exits.
            Float64UnaryOp::Abs if self.may_speculate(ExitKind::Overflow) => {
                let zero = self.int32_constant(0);
                let negated = self.int32_binary(BinaryOp::Sub, zero, integer);
                let result = self.emit(Op::Int32Max, &[integer, negated], Some(Repr::Int32));
                self.tagged(result)
            }
            Float64UnaryOp::Abs => {
                let smallest = self.int32_constant(i32::MIN);
                let integer = self.branch_to_slow_path(
                    slow_paths,
                    BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::StrictlyEquals),
                    &[integer, smallest],
                    false,
                );
                let result = self.emit(Op::Int32Abs, &[integer], Some(Repr::Int32));
                self.tagged(result)
            }
            Float64UnaryOp::Sqrt | Float64UnaryOp::Negate => {
                let double = self.int32_to_float64(integer);
                let result = self.emit(Op::Float64Unary { op }, &[double], Some(Repr::Float64));
                self.emit(Op::BoxFloat64, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged))
            }
        }
    }

    /// Builds `this_value.charCodeAt(argument)` or `.charAt(argument)`, a
    /// `Call` of the builtin, for
    /// strings whose characters are readable and int32 indices in bounds,
    /// if `callee` is the builtin of any realm. `charAt` makes the strings
    /// of ASCII code units, which the VM keeps. The instruction's slow path,
    /// which calls the callee, handles everything else.
    pub(super) fn build_string_character(
        &mut self,
        character: StringCharacter,
        dst: Operand,
        callee: Operand,
        this_value: Operand,
        argument: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let layout = &self.runtime.layout;
        let builtin = match character {
            StringCharacter::CodeUnit => layout.builtin_string_prototype_char_code_at,
            StringCharacter::String => layout.builtin_string_prototype_char_at,
        };
        let callee = self.read(callee)?;
        let string = self.read(this_value)?;
        let index = self.read(argument)?;
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Builtin(builtin), &[callee], true);
        let index = self.int32_or_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, index);
        let code_unit = self.string_code_unit(&mut slow_paths, string, index);
        let result = match character {
            StringCharacter::CodeUnit => self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[code_unit], Some(Repr::Tagged)),
            StringCharacter::String => self.ascii_character_string(&mut slow_paths, code_unit),
        };
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(result))
            .expect("the instruction has a value");
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// The code unit at `index`, a `Repr::Int32`, of the tagged `string`,
    /// taking a slow path of `slow_paths` unless it is a string whose
    /// characters can be read and the index is in its bounds.
    pub(super) fn string_code_unit(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, string: NodeId, index: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        let string = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::String, &[string], true);
        let address = self.emit(Op::StringAddress, &[string], Some(Repr::Pointer));
        let readable = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::ResolvedString, &[address], true);
        let length = self.emit(Op::StringLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let index = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[index, length], true);
        self.emit(Op::LoadStringCodeUnit, &[readable, index], Some(Repr::Int32))
    }

    /// The VM's string of `code_unit`, taking a slow path of `slow_paths`
    /// unless it is ASCII.
    pub(super) fn ascii_character_string(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, code_unit: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        let limit = self.int32_constant(0x80);
        let code_unit = self.branch_to_slow_path(
            slow_paths,
            BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::LessThan),
            &[code_unit, limit],
            true,
        );
        self.emit(Op::SingleCharacterString, &[code_unit], Some(Repr::Tagged))
    }

    /// Builds `array.push(...values)`, a `Call` of up to
    /// `MAX_INLINE_PUSHED_VALUES` values whose callee is known to be
    /// `Array.prototype.push`, for arrays it appends to without any
    /// observable step, and exits for anything else: the values become the
    /// next elements where the elements have room for all of them, and a
    /// cold block calls the runtime to append them one by one, growing the
    /// elements, otherwise. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if it is
    /// not such a call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_array_push(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if arguments.is_empty()
            || arguments.len() > MAX_INLINE_PUSHED_VALUES
            || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::SlowPath)
            || (arguments.len() > 1 && !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::Overflow))
            || self.holds_virtual_arguments(*this_value)
            || arguments.iter().any(|value| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*value))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if self.constant_intrinsic(*callee) != Some(Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypePush) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let receiver = self.read(*this_value)?;
        let mut values = self.node_list();
        for value in *arguments {
            values.push(self.read(*value)?);
        }
        self.embed(self.runtime.array_prototype);
        self.embed(self.runtime.object_prototype);
        let receiver = self.emit_checked(Op::CheckAppendableArray, &[receiver], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let array = self.cell_address(receiver);
        let length = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[array], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let capacity = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsCapacity, &[array], Some(Repr::Int32));
        // NB: One value fits where the length is below the capacity, compared
        //     unsigned so that lengths above i32::MAX (negative as int32
        //     values) never fit. More values need that much room between
        //     them, which only overflows for such lengths, and exits for them.
        let (room_condition, room_inputs) = if values.len() == 1 {
            (BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[length, capacity])
        } else {
            let room = self.emit_checked(
                Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Sub },
                &[capacity, length],
                Some(Repr::Int32),
            );
            let count = self.int32_constant(values.len() as i32);
            (BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThanEquals), &[room, count])
        };
        let (hot, cold) = self.branch_with_cold_side(room_condition, room_inputs, true);
        self.block = cold;
        let mut pushed = None;
        for value in &values {
            pushed = Some(self.emit(Op::CallArrayPush, &[receiver, *value], Some(Repr::Tagged)));
        }
        let pushed = pushed.expect("there are values to push");
        let cold = self.block;
        self.block = hot;
        let mut new_length = if values.len() == 1 {
            self.refine(room_condition, true, room_inputs)
        } else {
            length
        };
        for &value in &values {
            new_length = self.emit(Op::AppendElement, &[array, new_length, value], Some(Repr::Int32));
        }
        self.release_node_list(values);
        let new_length = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[new_length], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let hot = self.block;
        self.join_blocks(&[hot, cold]);
        let length = self.add_phi(&[new_length, pushed]);
        self.write(*dst, length)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds `Math.min` and `Math.max` of up to `MAX_MIN_MAX_ARGUMENTS`
    /// arguments, `Call`s whose feedback saw `Math.min` or `Math.max` as
    /// their single callee, as `Int32Min` or `Int32Max` of int32 arguments
    /// where the results were int32 values, and as `Float64Min` or
    /// `Float64Max` of numbers otherwise, the code exiting for other
    /// arguments. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if it is not such a
    /// call, or where arguments that were no numbers exited before.
    pub(super) fn try_build_math_min_max(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if arguments.is_empty()
            || arguments.len() > MAX_MIN_MAX_ARGUMENTS
            || arguments.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some(feedback) = self.call_feedback(call_feedback) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some((target, intrinsic)) = feedback.monomorphic_intrinsic() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let max = match intrinsic {
            Intrinsic::MathMin => false,
            Intrinsic::MathMax => true,
            _ => return Ok(None),
        };
        if !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut values = self.node_list();
        for operand in arguments {
            values.push(self.read_value(*operand)?);
        }
        // NB: Int32 results do not prove int32 arguments (Math.min(1, 2.5)
        //     is 1). Arguments that are no int32 values exit, and code compiled
        //     after the exit computes with doubles. The results are numbers
        //     either way.
        let int32 = feedback.value == value_feedback::INT32
            && self.may_speculate(ExitKind::NotInt32)
            && self.may_be_int32(&values);
        if !int32 && !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadType) {
            self.release_node_list(values);
            return Ok(None);
        }
        self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
        // NB: All the arguments are converted before the first of the operations on them.
        let result = if int32 {
            let op = if max { Op::Int32Max } else { Op::Int32Min };
            for value in &mut values {
                *value = self.int32(*value);
            }
            let result = values
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .reduce(|result, value| self.emit(op.clone(), &[result, value], Some(Repr::Int32)))
                .expect("there are arguments");
            self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged))
        } else {
            let op = if max { Op::Float64Max } else { Op::Float64Min };
            for value in &mut values {
                *value = self.number(*value);
            }
            let result = values
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .reduce(|result, number| self.emit(op.clone(), &[result, number], Some(Repr::Float64)))
                .expect("there are arguments");
            self.emit(Op::BoxFloat64, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged))
        };
        self.release_node_list(values);
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds `Math.imul(a, b)` calls, if the site saw only that function
    /// and int32 arguments, as the low 32 bits of the int32 product.
    /// Returns `None`, having built nothing, if the `Call` is no such call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_math_imul(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        // NB: ToInt32 of an absent argument (undefined) is 0, which the slow
        //     path handles like any other call.
        if arguments.len() < 2 || arguments.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand)) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some((target, Intrinsic::MathImul)) = self
            .call_feedback(call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.monomorphic_intrinsic())
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget) || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::NotInt32) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        // NB: Only the first two arguments matter; the others are only read.
        let values = [self.read_value(arguments[0])?, self.read_value(arguments[1])?];
        if !self.may_be_int32(&values) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
        let [lhs, rhs] = values.map(|value| self.int32(value));
        let product = self.emit(
            Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Mul },
            &[lhs, rhs],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        let result = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[product], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// The intrinsic a call site's feedback saw as its single callee, with
    /// the code checking that `callee` is still that function. Returns `None`,
    /// having built nothing, if the site saw another callee.
    fn checked_intrinsic_callee(
        &mut self,
        call_feedback: u16,
        callee: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Option<Intrinsic>, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(feedback) = self.call_feedback(call_feedback) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some((target, intrinsic)) = feedback.monomorphic_intrinsic() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::SlowPath) || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
        Ok(Some(intrinsic))
    }

    /// Makes the code exit unless the value of `operand` is the function
    /// `expected`, which needs no check where it is that constant.
    pub(super) fn check_callee(&mut self, operand: Operand, expected: CellId) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let value = self.read(operand)?;
        let expected_bits = self.boxed_object(expected);
        if self.graph.constant_value(value) == Some(expected_bits) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        self.embed(expected);
        self.emit_checked(
            Op::CheckValue {
                expected: expected_bits,
                kind: ExitKind::BadCallTarget,
            },
            &[value],
            None,
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Builds a call or construct of the `Array` constructor `callee`, which
    /// the code checked, with at most one argument: an array of length
    /// `length` (a nonnegative int32), or of none, through `ArrayCreate`.
    /// Other lengths and realms take the instruction's cold slow path.
    fn build_array_of_length(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        callee: Operand,
        length: Option<Operand>,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        // 23.1.1.1 Array ( ...values ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-array
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let length = match length {
            Some(argument) => {
                let length = self.read(argument)?;
                // NB: Other numbers are lengths that throw, and other
                //     values elements.
                let length =
                    self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32, &[length], true);
                self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[length], Some(Repr::Int32))
            }
            None => self.int32_constant(0),
        };
        let function = self.read(callee)?;
        let array = self.emit(Op::ArrayCreate, &[length, function], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let array = self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, array);
        let array = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(array))
            .expect("calls have a value");
        self.write(dst, array)?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds `new Array(...)` of the `Array` constructor, if the site saw
    /// only it. Since the constructor is its own NewTarget, it makes what
    /// its call makes: with one argument, an array of that length (see
    /// `build_array_of_length()`), and otherwise an array of the arguments,
    /// which code of the constructor's realm allocates like an array
    /// literal. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if the construct is no
    /// such construct.
    pub(super) fn try_build_array_construct(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::CallConstruct {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some((target, Intrinsic::ArrayConstructor)) = self
            .call_feedback(*call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.monomorphic_intrinsic())
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if arguments.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand)) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if let [length] = *arguments {
            if self.checked_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback, *callee)?.is_none() {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            return self.build_array_of_length(*dst, *callee, Some(*length)).map(Some);
        }
        // 23.1.1.1 Array ( ...values ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-array
        if target != self.runtime.array_constructor
            || !self.can_allocate_array(arguments.len())
            || self.checked_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback, *callee)?.is_none()
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let elements = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            arguments.iter().copied().map(super::allocation::ArrayElement::Operand),
            self.work,
        );
        // NB: Arrays with holes are left to the generic construct, which reading the operands does not affect.
        if !self.try_build_new_array(*dst, &elements)? {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds calls of the `String`, `Array`, `Object` and `Boolean`
    /// constructors with at most one argument, if the site saw only that
    /// constructor: `Boolean(x)` is the truthiness of `x`, `String(x)` is a
    /// string `x` itself or the string of another primitive, `Array(n)` an
    /// array of length `n`, and `Object(x)` an object `x` itself or the
    /// object of another primitive but undefined and null. The call runs in
    /// a cold slow path otherwise. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if
    /// the `Call` is no such call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_builtin_constructor_call(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if arguments.len() > 1 || arguments.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand)) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some(constructor) = self.peek_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback).filter(|intrinsic| {
            matches!(
                intrinsic,
                Intrinsic::StringConstructor
                    | Intrinsic::ArrayConstructor
                    | Intrinsic::ObjectConstructor
                    | Intrinsic::BooleanConstructor
            )
        }) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if self.checked_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback, *callee)?.is_none() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        // 20.3.1.1 Boolean ( value ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-boolean-constructor-boolean-value
        if constructor == Intrinsic::BooleanConstructor {
            match arguments.first() {
                Some(argument) => self.build_truthiness_value(*dst, *argument, false)?,
                None => {
                    let falsity = self.constant(crate::ir::value::FALSE);
                    self.write(*dst, falsity)?;
                }
            }
            return Ok(Some(Flow::Continue));
        }
        if constructor == Intrinsic::ArrayConstructor {
            return self
                .build_array_of_length(*dst, *callee, arguments.first().copied())
                .map(Some);
        }
        let Some(argument) = arguments.first() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let value = self.read(*argument)?;
        let result = if constructor == Intrinsic::StringConstructor {
            // 22.1.1.1 String ( value ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-string-constructor-string-value
            let (string, other) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::String, &[value]);
            self.block = string;
            let string = self.refine(BranchCondition::String, true, &[value]);
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[string]);
            // NB: The VM has the strings of small integers.
            self.block = other;
            let (int32, other) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::Int32Value, &[value]);
            self.block = int32;
            let integer = self.refine(BranchCondition::Int32Value, true, &[value]);
            let unboxed = self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[integer], Some(Repr::Int32));
            let cached = self.emit(Op::IntegerToString, &[unboxed], Some(Repr::Tagged));
            let empty = self.constant(crate::ir::value::EMPTY);
            let missing = BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: true };
            let (miss, hit) = self.branch_both_ways(missing, &[cached, empty]);
            self.block = hit;
            let cached = self.refine(missing, false, &[cached, empty]);
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[cached]);
            self.block = miss;
            let string = self.emit(Op::PrimitiveToString, &[integer], Some(Repr::Tagged));
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[string]);
            self.block = other;
            let primitive = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Object, &[value], false);
            self.emit(Op::PrimitiveToString, &[primitive], Some(Repr::Tagged))
        } else {
            // 20.1.1.1 Object ( [ value ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-value
            let (object, other) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::Object, &[value]);
            self.block = object;
            let object = self.refine(BranchCondition::Object, true, &[value]);
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[object]);
            self.block = other;
            let primitive = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Nullish, &[value], false);
            let function = self.read(*callee)?;
            let object = self.emit(Op::ToObject, &[primitive, function], Some(Repr::Tagged));
            self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, object)
        };
        self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[result]);
        let result = self.join_hot_paths(slow_paths).expect("calls have a value");
        self.write(*dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds calls of builtins that JIT code calls through their runtime
    /// helpers (see `Intrinsic::helper_call()`), if the site saw only that
    /// builtin, as a `CallIntrinsic` node for a `this` value and arguments
    /// of the kinds the helper takes. The call runs in a cold slow path
    /// otherwise. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if the `Call` is no
    /// such call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_helper_call(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some((intrinsic, call)) = self
            .peek_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback)
            .and_then(|intrinsic| Some((intrinsic, intrinsic.helper_call()?)))
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        assert_ne!(
            (self.runtime.helper_calls.0)(intrinsic),
            0,
            "{intrinsic:?} has a HelperCall but no runtime helper"
        );
        // NB: Helpers run in the realm of the calling code.
        let realm = self
            .function
            .executable
            .function
            .map_or(self.runtime.realm, |function| function.realm);
        let builtin_realm = self
            .call_feedback(*call_feedback)
            .and_then(|feedback| feedback.native_call)
            .map(|native| native.realm);
        if builtin_realm != Some(realm) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        // NB: Calls without a required argument pass undefined, which the
        //     slow path converts.
        let passes_required_arguments = call
            .arguments
            .iter()
            .skip(arguments.len())
            .all(|operand| matches!(operand, HelperOperand::Int32 { absent: Some(_) }));
        if !passes_required_arguments
            || self.holds_virtual_arguments(*this_value)
            || arguments.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand))
            || self.checked_intrinsic_callee(*call_feedback, *callee)?.is_none()
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let mut inputs = self.node_list();
        let operands = core::iter::once(Some(*this_value))
            .chain((0..call.arguments.len()).map(|index| arguments.get(index).copied()));
        for (operand, kind) in operands.zip(core::iter::once(call.receiver).chain(call.arguments.iter().copied())) {
            let input = match (operand, kind) {
                (Some(operand), HelperOperand::Value) => self.read(operand)?,
                (Some(operand), HelperOperand::String) => {
                    let value = self.read(operand)?;
                    self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::String, &[value], true)
                }
                (Some(operand), HelperOperand::Int32 { .. }) => {
                    let value = self.read(operand)?;
                    self.int32_or_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, value)
                }
                (None, HelperOperand::Int32 { absent: Some(absent) }) => self.int32_constant(absent),
                (None, _) => unreachable!("calls pass the required arguments"),
            };
            inputs.push(input);
        }
        let result = self.emit(Op::CallIntrinsic { intrinsic }, &inputs, Some(call.result.repr()));
        self.release_node_list(inputs);
        let result = match call.result {
            HelperResult::Int32 => self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged)),
            HelperResult::Bool => self.emit(Op::BoxBool, &[result], Some(Repr::Tagged)),
            HelperResult::String => result,
            HelperResult::Value => self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, result),
        };
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(result))
            .expect("calls have a value");
        self.write(*dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds `String.fromCharCode` of an int32 whose code unit (ToUint16)
    /// is ASCII as the VM's string of that character, if the site saw only
    /// the builtin, and in a cold slow path otherwise. Returns `None`,
    /// having built nothing, if the site saw something else.
    pub(super) fn try_build_string_from_char_code(
        &mut self,
        call_feedback: u16,
        dst: Operand,
        callee: Operand,
        argument: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        // NB: Checks nothing yet, so building nothing is fine.
        if self.peek_intrinsic_callee(call_feedback) != Some(Intrinsic::StringFromCharCode)
            || self.checked_intrinsic_callee(call_feedback, callee)?.is_none()
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let code = self.read(argument)?;
        let code = self.int32_or_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, code);
        let mask = self.int32_constant(0xFFFF);
        let code_unit = self.emit(
            Op::Int32Binary {
                op: BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd,
            },
            &[code, mask],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        let ascii_limit = self.int32_constant(0x80);
        let code_unit = self.branch_to_slow_path(
            &mut slow_paths,
            BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::LessThan),
            &[code_unit, ascii_limit],
            true,
        );
        let string = self.emit(Op::SingleCharacterString, &[code_unit], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let result = self
            .join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(string))
            .expect("calls have a value");
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// The intrinsic a call site's feedback saw as its single callee, if any.
    fn peek_intrinsic_callee(&self, call_feedback: u16) -> Option<Intrinsic> {
        self.call_feedback(call_feedback)?
            .monomorphic_intrinsic()
            .map(|(_, intrinsic)| intrinsic)
    }

    /// Builds `CreateDataPropertyOrThrow` of an index of an object with
    /// packed or holey elements: a store to an element it has, or that fills
    /// a hole of an extensible one, and an append of the next element of a
    /// packed array where there is room, like `Array.prototype.push` appends
    /// it (defining an element runs no code). Other keys and objects take a
    /// cold slow path.
    pub(super) fn build_create_data_property(
        &mut self,
        object: Operand,
        property: Operand,
        value: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let operands = [object, property, value];
        if !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::SlowPath)
            || operands.iter().any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        // NB: Appends check that the prototype chain is the realm's default
        //     one, like pushes.
        self.embed(self.runtime.array_prototype);
        self.embed(self.runtime.object_prototype);
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(None)?;
        let object = self.read(object)?;
        let key = self.read_value(property)?;
        let value = self.read(value)?;
        let index = self.int32_or_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, key);
        let object = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Object, &[object], true);
        let kinds = [ElementsKind::Packed, ElementsKind::Holey];
        let conditions = kinds.map(BranchCondition::ElementsKind);
        self.branch_on_cases(
            &mut slow_paths,
            object,
            &conditions,
            false,
            |builder, slow_paths, case, object| {
                let kind = kinds[case];
                let address = builder.cell_address(object);
                let index = if kind == ElementsKind::Packed {
                    builder.element_index_or_append(slow_paths, object, address, index, value)
                } else {
                    // NB: Filling a hole defines a new element, which takes an
                    //     extensible object. Filling the last one may make the
                    //     elements packed, which the slow path does.
                    builder.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::Extensible, &[address], true);
                    let (_, index) = builder.element_index_in_bounds(slow_paths, kind, address, index);
                    let length = builder.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
                    let one = builder.int32_constant(1);
                    let last = builder.int32_binary(BinaryOp::Sub, length, one);
                    builder.branch_to_slow_path(
                        slow_paths,
                        BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::LessThan),
                        &[index, last],
                        true,
                    )
                };
                builder.emit(Op::StoreElementAt { kind }, &[address, index, value], None);
                builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);
            },
        );
        self.join_hot_paths(slow_paths);
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }
}

//! Keyed accesses that speculation does not cover, built as IR for the
//! cases the interpreter's keyed feedback saw.
//!
//! A `GetByValue` with an int32 key branches on the elements kind of its
//! object, one kind its feedback saw after the other, and loads the element:
//! bounds checks against the element counts, the load, and for holey
//! elements a check for a hole, each a node of its own. Sites that saw
//! holes or indices past the end read undefined there, where the prototype
//! chain has no indexed properties. Strings give the
//! strings of their ASCII characters. Other keys probe the property lookup
//! caches. Everything else takes the instruction's slow path, and all paths
//! join after the instruction. `PutByValue` is built the same way, and
//! fills holes of arrays where that runs no code.

use super::Flow;
use super::GenericInfo;
use super::GraphBuilder;
use super::checks::SlowPaths;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::Operand;
use crate::bytecode::PUT_KIND_NORMAL;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::TypedArrayElement;
use crate::ir::value;
use crate::snapshot::Forwarding;
use crate::snapshot::Intrinsic;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::HOLEY;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::INT32_INDEX;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::KEY_KINDS_MASK;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_ELEMENTS;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_KEY;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::OUT_OF_BOUNDS;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::PACKED;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::STRING_KEY;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::SYMBOL_KEY;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits::TYPED_ARRAY_SHIFT;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// What a site is built for without keyed feedback: every key and every
/// elements kind, like the interpreter handles them inline.
const UNKNOWN_KEYED_FEEDBACK: u32 =
    INT32_INDEX | PACKED | HOLEY | STRING_KEY | SYMBOL_KEY | OTHER_KEY | (0x1ff << TYPED_ARRAY_SHIFT);

/// Where a keyed access continues for each kind of key: the block for
/// int32 keys, with the index, and the block for other keys, with the key.
#[derive(Default)]
struct KeyPaths {
    indexed: Option<(BlockId, NodeId)>,
    named: Option<(BlockId, NodeId)>,
}

impl<'a> GraphBuilder<'a, '_> {
    /// What the keyed feedback of `instruction` saw, or everything if it saw
    /// nothing.
    fn keyed_access_bits(&self, instruction: &Instruction) -> u32 {
        match self.keyed_feedback_bits(instruction) {
            Some(bits) if bits != 0 => bits,
            _ => UNKNOWN_KEYED_FEEDBACK,
        }
    }

    /// The elements kinds keyed feedback `bits` saw for int32 keys.
    fn elements_kinds_seen(&self, bits: u32) -> ZoneVec<'a, ElementsKind> {
        let mut kinds = ZoneVec::new_in(self.work);
        if bits & INT32_INDEX != 0 && bits & PACKED != 0 {
            kinds.push(ElementsKind::Packed);
        }
        if bits & INT32_INDEX != 0 && bits & HOLEY != 0 {
            kinds.push(ElementsKind::Holey);
        }
        kinds.extend(self.typed_array_elements_seen(bits).map(ElementsKind::TypedArray));
        kinds
    }

    /// Splits the paths of a keyed access by its key: int32 keys (if
    /// `indexed`) continue with their index, and other keys (if `named`)
    /// with the key, each in a block of its own if a key may be either. Keys
    /// of kinds the feedback never saw take a slow path. Returns `None`,
    /// having built nothing, if keys like `key` take no path.
    fn split_key(
        &mut self,
        slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>,
        key: NodeId,
        indexed: bool,
        named: bool,
    ) -> Option<KeyPaths> {
        if !indexed && !named {
            return None;
        }
        let mut paths = KeyPaths::default();
        if let Some(index) = self.int32_value_of(key) {
            paths.indexed = Some((self.block, index));
            return indexed.then_some(paths);
        }
        let key = self.tagged(key);
        if let Some(index) = self.graph.constant_value(key).and_then(value::as_int32) {
            paths.indexed = Some((self.block, self.int32_constant(index)));
            return indexed.then_some(paths);
        }
        if self.graph.constant_value(key).is_some() {
            paths.named = Some((self.block, key));
            return named.then_some(paths);
        }
        let integer = if !named {
            self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::Int32Value, &[key], true)
        } else if indexed {
            let (integer, other) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::Int32Value, &[key]);
            paths.named = Some((other, key));
            self.block = integer;
            self.refine(BranchCondition::Int32Value, true, &[key])
        } else {
            // NB: The cache lookup misses for int32 keys.
            paths.named = Some((self.block, key));
            return Some(paths);
        };
        let index = self.emit(Op::UnboxInt32, &[integer], Some(Repr::Int32));
        paths.indexed = Some((self.block, index));
        Some(paths)
    }

    /// The storage of the elements of `kind` of the object at `address` (see
    /// `element_storage_and_bound()`), and `index`, refined to be in their
    /// bounds, taking a slow path where it is not.
    pub(super) fn element_index_in_bounds(
        &mut self,
        slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>,
        kind: ElementsKind,
        address: NodeId,
        index: NodeId,
    ) -> (NodeId, NodeId) {
        let (storage, bound) = self.element_storage_and_bound(kind, address);
        let index = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[index, bound], true);
        (storage, index)
    }

    /// `index`, refined to be in the bounds of the packed elements of the
    /// array `object` (at `address`), taking a slow path where it is not,
    /// except for the index of the next element: there, `value` becomes the
    /// next element like `Array.prototype.push` would append it, growing
    /// the elements where they have no room for it, and the access is done.
    pub(super) fn element_index_or_append(
        &mut self,
        slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>,
        object: NodeId,
        address: NodeId,
        index: NodeId,
        value: NodeId,
    ) -> NodeId {
        let length = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let (inside, outside) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[index, length]);
        self.block = outside;
        let next = BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::StrictlyEquals);
        let next_index = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, next, &[index, length], true);
        let array = self.emit_checked(Op::CheckAppendableArray, &[object], None);
        let array_address = self.cell_address(array);
        let capacity = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsCapacity, &[array_address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        // NB: Lengths above i32::MAX are negative as int32 values, which an
        //     unsigned comparison keeps from passing as room for an element.
        //     Appends without room grow the elements through the runtime,
        //     which runs no code either, but at such lengths, whose keys are
        //     no indices, which the slow path stores.
        let room = BranchCondition::IndexInBounds;
        let (hot, cold) = self.branch_with_cold_side(room, &[next_index, capacity], true);
        self.block = cold;
        let zero = self.int32_constant(0);
        let nonnegative = BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThanEquals);
        self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, nonnegative, &[next_index, zero], true);
        self.graph.blocks[self.block.index()].is_cold = true;
        self.emit(Op::CallArrayPush, &[array, value], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);
        self.block = hot;
        let next_index = self.refine(room, true, &[next_index, capacity]);
        self.emit(
            Op::AppendElement,
            &[array_address, next_index, value],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);

        self.block = inside;
        let index = self.refine(BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, true, &[index, length]);
        let capacity = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsCapacity, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[index, capacity], true)
    }

    /// Ends the current block, where the object at `address` has no element
    /// at a non-negative index, as a path that read undefined, if its
    /// prototype chain has no indexed properties. Takes the slow path
    /// otherwise.
    fn read_missing_element(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, address: NodeId) {
        self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::PlainArrayPrototypeChain, &[address], true);
        let undefined = self.constant(value::UNDEFINED);
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[undefined]);
    }

    /// Builds `GetByValue` (`Handling::Expanded`) for the keys and elements
    /// its feedback saw.
    pub(super) fn build_get_by_value(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        info: GenericInfo,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::GetByValue {
            dst,
            base,
            property,
            cache,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            unreachable!("only GetByValue is built here");
        };
        let bits = self.keyed_access_bits(instruction);
        let kinds = self.elements_kinds_seen(bits);
        let strings = bits & OTHER_KEY != 0 && self.runtime.layout.single_ascii_character_strings != 0;
        let indexed = !kinds.is_empty() || strings;
        let named = bits & (STRING_KEY | SYMBOL_KEY) != 0;
        // NB: Holes and indices past the end read undefined where the
        //     prototype chain is the realm's default one, without indexed
        //     properties. Sites that saw any are built to read them.
        let reads_missing_elements = bits & OUT_OF_BOUNDS != 0;
        if reads_missing_elements {
            self.embed(self.runtime.array_prototype);
            self.embed(self.runtime.object_prototype);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let key = self.read(property)?;
        let Some(paths) = self.split_key(&mut slow_paths, key, indexed, named) else {
            return self.build_generic(instruction, info);
        };

        if let Some((block, index)) = paths.indexed {
            self.block = block;
            let conditions = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(kinds.iter().copied().map(BranchCondition::ElementsKind), self.work);
            self.branch_on_cases(
                &mut slow_paths,
                object,
                &conditions,
                strings,
                |builder, slow_paths, case, object| {
                    let kind = kinds[case];
                    let address = builder.cell_address(object);
                    if !reads_missing_elements || matches!(kind, ElementsKind::TypedArray(_)) {
                        let (storage, index) = builder.element_index_in_bounds(slow_paths, kind, address, index);
                        let element = builder.load_element(kind, storage, index);
                        let mut element = builder.tagged(element);
                        if kind == ElementsKind::Holey {
                            element = builder.branch_if_empty(slow_paths, element);
                        }
                        builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[element]);
                        return;
                    }
                    let (storage, bound) = builder.element_storage_and_bound(kind, address);
                    let (inside, outside) = builder.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, &[index, bound]);
                    builder.block = outside;
                    let zero = builder.int32_constant(0);
                    builder.branch_to_slow_path(
                        slow_paths,
                        BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThanEquals),
                        &[index, zero],
                        true,
                    );
                    builder.read_missing_element(slow_paths, address);
                    builder.block = inside;
                    let index = builder.refine(BranchCondition::IndexInBounds, true, &[index, bound]);
                    let element = builder.load_element(kind, storage, index);
                    let element = builder.tagged(element);
                    if kind == ElementsKind::Holey {
                        let empty = builder.constant(value::EMPTY);
                        let (hole, present) =
                            builder.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: true }, &[element, empty]);
                        builder.block = hole;
                        builder.read_missing_element(slow_paths, address);
                        builder.block = present;
                        let element =
                            builder.refine(BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: true }, false, &[element, empty]);
                        builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[element]);
                    } else {
                        builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[element]);
                    }
                },
            );
            // NB: The feedback counts the characters of strings as other keys.
            if strings {
                let code_unit = self.string_code_unit(&mut slow_paths, object, index);
                let character = self.ascii_character_string(&mut slow_paths, code_unit);
                self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[character]);
            }
        }
        if let Some((block, key)) = paths.named {
            self.block = block;
            let executable = self.function.index;
            let value = self.emit(
                Op::ProbeKeyedCache { executable, cache },
                &[object, key],
                Some(Repr::Tagged),
            );
            let value = self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, value);
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[value]);
        }
        let result = self.join_hot_paths(slow_paths);
        self.write(dst, result.expect("GetByValue has a value"))?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds `PutByValue` (`Handling::Expanded`) for the keys and elements
    /// its feedback saw. Puts other than plain assignments run generically.
    pub(super) fn build_put_by_value(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        info: GenericInfo,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::PutByValue {
            base,
            property,
            src,
            kind: PUT_KIND_NORMAL,
            cache,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            return self.build_generic(instruction, info);
        };
        let bits = self.keyed_access_bits(instruction);
        let kinds = self.elements_kinds_seen(bits);
        let named = bits & (STRING_KEY | SYMBOL_KEY) != 0;
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(None)?;
        // NB: Stores of int32 indices into packed or holey elements fill holes and append inline, so their slow path
        //     only stores out of bounds otherwise, which is rare, as are stores out of the bounds of typed arrays
        //     where the feedback saw none. Exiting there instead keeps loops that store elements free of code that
        //     may change what they read. The exits are out of bounds ones, so that taking one keeps inline appends,
        //     which go once their check of the array exits with `ExitKind::SlowPath`. Where that happened, appends
        //     take the slow path, which they would otherwise exit at too.
        let appends = self.may_speculate(ExitKind::SlowPath);
        let out_of_bounds_typed_arrays =
            self.typed_array_elements_seen(bits).next().is_some() && bits & OUT_OF_BOUNDS != 0;
        if appends
            && bits & KEY_KINDS_MASK == INT32_INDEX
            && bits & OTHER_ELEMENTS == 0
            && !kinds.is_empty()
            && !out_of_bounds_typed_arrays
        {
            self.exit_with_instead_of_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, ExitKind::OutOfBounds);
        }
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let key = self.read(property)?;
        let value = self.read(src)?;
        let Some(paths) = self.split_key(&mut slow_paths, key, !kinds.is_empty(), named) else {
            return self.build_generic(instruction, info);
        };

        // NB: Appends and hole fills check that the prototype chain is the
        //     realm's default one. Appends exit for arrays that push could
        //     not append to, and hole fills take the slow path.
        if appends || kinds.contains(&ElementsKind::Holey) {
            self.embed(self.runtime.array_prototype);
            self.embed(self.runtime.object_prototype);
        }
        if let Some((block, index)) = paths.indexed {
            self.block = block;
            let conditions = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(kinds.iter().copied().map(BranchCondition::ElementsKind), self.work);
            self.branch_on_cases(
                &mut slow_paths,
                object,
                &conditions,
                false,
                |builder, slow_paths, case, object| {
                    let kind = kinds[case];
                    let stored = builder.stored_element(slow_paths, kind, value);
                    let address = builder.cell_address(object);
                    if kind == ElementsKind::Holey {
                        builder.store_holey_element(slow_paths, address, index, stored);
                        return;
                    }
                    let (storage, index) = if kind == ElementsKind::Packed && appends {
                        let index = builder.element_index_or_append(slow_paths, object, address, index, stored);
                        (address, index)
                    } else {
                        builder.element_index_in_bounds(slow_paths, kind, address, index)
                    };
                    builder.store_element(kind, storage, index, stored);
                    builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);
                },
            );
        }
        if let Some((block, key)) = paths.named {
            self.block = block;
            let executable = self.function.index;
            let stored = self.emit(
                Op::ProbeKeyedStore { executable, cache },
                &[object, key, value],
                Some(Repr::Bool),
            );
            self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Bool, &[stored], true);
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[]);
        }
        self.join_hot_paths(slow_paths);
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Stores `value` at `index` of the holey elements of the object at
    /// `address`, taking a slow path unless the index is below their length.
    /// A hole takes a new element, and elements without room for it grow,
    /// which runs no code where the object is an array with a plain prototype
    /// chain (see `BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray`); other holes take a
    /// slow path.
    fn store_holey_element(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, address: NodeId, index: NodeId, value: NodeId) {
        let kind = ElementsKind::Holey;
        let in_bounds = BranchCondition::IndexInBounds;
        let length = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let index = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, in_bounds, &[index, length], true);
        // NB: Elements made with a length, like `new Array(length)`, have no room yet, and grow as they get filled.
        let capacity = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsCapacity, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let (room, no_room) = self.branch_with_cold_side(in_bounds, &[index, capacity], true);
        self.block = no_room;
        // NB: Lengths above i32::MAX let negative int32 keys, which are no indices, pass as below the length.
        let zero = self.int32_constant(0);
        let nonnegative = BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThanEquals);
        let element_index = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, nonnegative, &[index, zero], true);
        self.graph.blocks[self.block.index()].is_cold = true;
        let array = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray, &[address], true);
        self.graph.blocks[self.block.index()].is_cold = true;
        self.emit(Op::CallStoreHoleyElement, &[array, element_index, value], None);
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);

        self.block = room;
        let index = self.refine(in_bounds, true, &[index, capacity]);
        let old = self.emit(Op::LoadElementAt { kind }, &[address, index], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let empty = self.constant(value::EMPTY);
        let (hole, element) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: true }, &[old, empty]);

        self.block = hole;
        let array = self.branch_to_slow_path(slow_paths, BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray, &[address], true);
        // NB: A store to the last index may make the elements packed, which
        //     the runtime does. The index is below the length, so the length
        //     is not 0.
        let one = self.int32_constant(1);
        let last = self.emit(
            Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Sub },
            &[length, one],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        let (before_last, at_last) = self.branch_with_cold_side(in_bounds, &[index, last], true);
        self.block = at_last;
        self.emit(Op::CallStoreHoleyElement, &[array, index, value], None);
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);
        self.block = before_last;
        let index_before_last = self.refine(in_bounds, true, &[index, last]);
        self.store_element(kind, address, index_before_last, value);
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);

        self.block = element;
        self.store_element(kind, address, index, value);
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[]);
    }

    /// `value` as elements of `kind` store it, taking a slow path for
    /// values of typed arrays that are no numbers.
    fn stored_element(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, kind: ElementsKind, value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        let int32 = self.int32_value_of(value);
        match (kind.stored_repr(), int32) {
            (Repr::Int32, Some(int32)) => int32,
            (Repr::Float64, Some(int32)) => self.int32_to_float64(int32),
            (Repr::Int32, None) => {
                let number = self.float64_of_number(slow_paths, value);
                let conversion = if kind == ElementsKind::TypedArray(TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped) {
                    Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped
                } else {
                    Op::Float64ToInt32
                };
                self.emit(conversion, &[number], Some(Repr::Int32))
            }
            (Repr::Float64, None) => self.float64_of_number(slow_paths, value),
            _ => self.tagged(value),
        }
    }

    /// Builds `object.hasOwnProperty(key)` and `hasOwnProperty.call(object,
    /// key)` calls of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` as a probe of
    /// whether the object has the property as its own, which exits where
    /// the probe cannot tell. Returns `None`, having built nothing, if the
    /// `Call` is not such a call.
    pub(super) fn try_build_has_own_property(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            arguments,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadCallTarget)
            || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::SlowPath)
            || arguments
                .iter()
                .chain([&this_value])
                .any(|operand| self.holds_virtual_arguments(*operand))
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some(feedback) = self.call_feedback(call_feedback) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let (object, key) = match (arguments, feedback.monomorphic_intrinsic()) {
            ([key], Some((target, Intrinsic::ObjectPrototypeHasOwnProperty))) => {
                self.check_callee(callee, target)?;
                (this_value, *key)
            }
            // NB: `Function.prototype.call` forwarding to hasOwnProperty.
            ([object, key], Some((call, Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeCall)))
                if feedback.forwarded.is_some_and(|forwarded| {
                    forwarded.forwarding == Forwarding::Call
                        && forwarded.target_intrinsic == Some(Intrinsic::ObjectPrototypeHasOwnProperty)
                }) =>
            {
                let forwarded = feedback.forwarded.expect("checked above");
                self.check_callee(callee, call)?;
                self.check_callee(this_value, forwarded.target)?;
                (*object, *key)
            }
            _ => return Ok(None),
        };
        // NB: The call's slow path is a call, which cold blocks cannot make,
        //     so the code exits where the probe cannot tell.
        let has = self.probe_has_property(true, object, key)?;
        let has = self.exit_if_empty(has, ExitKind::SlowPath);
        self.write(dst, has)?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds `dst = lhs in rhs` as a probe of whether the object has the
    /// property, and the instruction's slow path where the probe cannot
    /// tell. Returns `None`, having built nothing, for virtual arguments
    /// objects.
    pub(super) fn try_build_in(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        lhs: Operand,
        rhs: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        if self.holds_virtual_arguments(lhs) || self.holds_virtual_arguments(rhs) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let has = self.probe_has_property(false, rhs, lhs)?;
        let has = self.branch_if_empty(&mut slow_paths, has);
        let result = self.join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(has));
        self.write(dst, result.expect("In has a value"))?;
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Whether `object` has the property `key` names (as its own, if
    /// `own`), or the empty value where `ProbeHasProperty` cannot tell.
    fn probe_has_property(&mut self, own: bool, object: Operand, key: Operand) -> Result<NodeId, CompileFailure> {
        let object = self.read(object)?;
        let key = self.read(key)?;
        Ok(self.emit(Op::ProbeHasProperty { own }, &[object, key], Some(Repr::Tagged)))
    }
}
