            // NB: `typeof` of a global variable its cache found is the type of the value GetGlobal reads.
            Instruction::TypeofGlobal { dst, cache, .. }
                if self.runtime.layout.typeof_strings.number != 0 && self.try_build_get_global(dst, cache)? =>
            {
                let value = self.read(dst)?;
                self.assume_no_htmldda_objects();
                let result = self.emit(Op::Typeof, &[value], Some(Repr::Tagged));
                self.write(dst, result)?;
            }
            Instruction::SetGlobal { src, cache, .. } => {
                if !self.try_build_set_global(src, cache)? {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            Instruction::ResolveGlobalBinding { dst, cache, .. } => {
                if !self.try_build_resolve_global_binding(dst, cache)? {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            Instruction::GetById { dst, base, cache, .. } => {
                if self.try_build_cached_getter(dst, base, cache)? {
                    return Ok(Some(Flow::Continue));
                }
                if let Some(flow) = self.try_inline_getter(dst, base, cache)? {
                    return Ok(Some(flow));
                }
                if self.try_build_native_getter(dst, base, cache)? {
                    return Ok(Some(Flow::Continue));
                }
                if !self.try_build_get_by_id(dst, base, cache)? {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            // NB: Only data properties, whose value does not depend on the receiver, are loaded here. Getters run in
            //     the slow path with the this value.
            Instruction::GetByIdWithThis { dst, base, cache, .. } => {
                if !self.try_build_get_by_id(dst, base, cache)? {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            Instruction::PutById { base, src, cache, .. } => {
                if let Some(flow) = self.try_inline_setter(base, src, cache)? {
                    return Ok(Some(flow));
                }
                if self.try_build_native_setter(base, src, cache)? {
                    return Ok(Some(Flow::Continue));
                }
                if !self.try_build_put_by_id(base, src, cache)? && !self.try_build_add_named(base, src, cache)? {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            Instruction::GetByValue {
                dst,
                base,
                property,
                cache,
                ..
            } => {
                if !self.try_build_arguments_index(dst, base, property)?
                    && !self.try_build_element_load(instruction, dst, base, property)?
                    && !self.try_build_get_by_value(dst, base, property, cache)?
                {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            // NB: Only plain assignments store into existing data
            //     properties like the cache says.
            Instruction::PutByValue {
                base,
                property,
                src,
                kind: PUT_KIND_NORMAL,
                cache,
                ..
            } => {
                if !self.try_build_element_store(instruction, base, property, src)?
                    && !self.try_build_put_by_value(base, property, src, cache)?
                {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
            }
            _ => return Ok(None),
        }
        Ok(Some(Flow::Continue))
    }

    /// Builds a `Yield`, `YieldIteratorResult` or `Await`, which suspends
    /// the generator or async function running the compiled function and
    /// returns `value` to the code resuming it: puts the slots live at the
    /// continuation in frame memory, where the resume entry of the
    /// continuation (see `osr`) finds them, and records the continuation in
    /// the frame like the interpreter's instruction.
    fn build_suspend(
        &mut self,
        continuation: Option<Label>,
        value: Operand,
        kind: SuspendKind,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        if self.function.is_virtual() {
            return Err(CompileFailure::InvalidBytecode {
                pc: self.function.pc,
                reason: "suspension in an inlined callee",
            });
        }
        let value = self.read(value)?;
        self.check_not_returning_virtual_arguments(value)?;
        if let Some(continuation) = continuation {
            let block = self.block_for_label(continuation)?;
            let start = self.function.cfg.blocks[block].instructions.start;
            let live = self.live_in(start);
            for slot in live.iter() {
                self.sync_slot(slot);
            }
            self.release_slot_set(live);
        }
        // NB: Like the interpreter's Yield and Await, an empty value yields
        //     `undefined`.
        let layout = self.function.layout;
        let arguments = layout.arguments_base()..layout.arguments_base() + layout.number_of_arguments;
        let value = if self.graph.is_known_non_empty(value, arguments, self.work) {
            value
        } else {
            self.emit(Op::EmptyToUndefined, &[value], Some(Repr::Tagged))
        };
        self.emit(
            Op::Suspend {
                continuation: continuation.map(|label| label.0),
                kind,
            },
            &[],
            None,
        );
        self.set_control(Op::Return, &[value]);
        Ok(Flow::Ended)
    }

    /// Builds `GetCompletionFields` (`Handling::Expanded`), which a
    /// resumed generator or async function starts with: the type and the
    /// value of the completion it resumed with, which the generator object
    /// it finds in its accumulator holds, and the slow path for other
    /// completion sources (async generators).
    pub(super) fn build_get_completion_fields(
        &mut self,
        type_dst: Operand,
        value_dst: Operand,
        completion: Operand,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let source = self.read(completion)?;
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let object = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Object, &[source], true);
        let object = self.cell_address(object);
        let generator = self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::GeneratorObject, &[object], true);
        let completion_type = self.emit(Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionType, &[generator], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let completion_type = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[completion_type], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let value = self.emit(Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionValue, &[generator], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let outputs = self.join_paths(slow_paths, &[completion_type, value], |_, _| {});
        self.write(type_dst, outputs[0])?;
        self.write(value_dst, outputs[1])?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds an instruction as its handling table entry says.
    fn build_by_handling(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let opcode = instruction.opcode();
        match handling(opcode) {
            Handling::Generic(info) => self.build_generic(instruction, info),
            Handling::Expanded(info) => self.build_expanded(instruction, info),
            Handling::Unsupported(reason) => Err(CompileFailure::UnsupportedInstruction {
                pc: self.function.pc,
                opcode,
                reason,
            }),
            Handling::Native => unreachable!("{} is native but not built natively", opcode.name()),
        }
    }

    fn fallthrough_block(&self) -> Result<BlockIndex, CompileFailure> {
        self.block_for_label(Label(
            self.function.instructions[self.function.instruction_index].next_pc(),
        ))
    }

    fn build_tag_branch(
        &mut self,
        condition: BranchCondition,
        operand: Operand,
        true_target: Label,
        false_target: Label,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let if_true = self.block_for_label(true_target)?;
        let if_false = self.block_for_label(false_target)?;
        let value = self.read(operand)?;
        self.end_with_branch(
            |if_true, if_false| Op::Branch {
                condition,
                if_true,
                if_false,
            },
            &[value],
            if_true,
            if_false,
        )
    }

    /// Branches on the truthiness of `operand`. Booleans and int32 values are
    /// tested inline; other values go through a fallback block that calls the
    /// runtime's `to_boolean` helper.
    fn build_truthiness_branch(
        &mut self,
        operand: Operand,
        if_true: BlockIndex,
        if_false: BlockIndex,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let value = self.read(operand)?;
        let source = self.block;
        let frame = self.frame.clone();
        let [true_edge, false_edge, fallback] = [(); 3].map(|()| {
            let block = self.graph.add_block(Block {
                predecessors: self.graph.list(&[source]),
                ..self.graph.new_block()
            });
            self.order.push(block);
            block
        });
        self.assume_no_htmldda_objects();
        self.set_control(
            Op::BranchTruthy {
                if_true: true_edge,
                if_false: false_edge,
                fallback,
            },
            &[value],
        );
        for (edge, target) in [(true_edge, if_true), (false_edge, if_false)] {
            self.block = edge;
            self.frame.clone_from(&frame);
            self.end_with_jump(target)?;
        }
        self.block = fallback;
        self.frame = frame;
        let boolean = self.emit(Op::ToBoolean, &[value], Some(Repr::Bool));
        self.end_with_branch(
            |if_true, if_false| Op::Branch {
                condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                if_true,
                if_false,
            },
            &[boolean],
            if_true,
            if_false,
        )
    }

    /// Stores the truthiness of `src` (negated if `negate`) as a boolean
    /// value into `dst`, with a truthiness branch and a phi of constants.
    fn build_truthiness_value(&mut self, dst: Operand, src: Operand, negate: bool) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let value = self.read(src)?;
        let source = self.block;
        let frame = self.frame.clone();
        let [true_block, false_block, fallback] = [(); 3].map(|()| self.add_block_after(source));
        self.assume_no_htmldda_objects();
        self.set_control(
            Op::BranchTruthy {
                if_true: true_block,
                if_false: false_block,
                fallback,
            },
            &[value],
        );

        self.block = fallback;
        let boolean = self.emit(Op::ToBoolean, &[value], Some(Repr::Bool));
        let (fallback_true_block, fallback_false_block) = self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::Bool, &[boolean]);
        self.join_blocks(&[true_block, false_block, fallback_true_block, fallback_false_block]);
        self.frame = frame;

        let (truthy, falsy) = if negate {
            (value::FALSE, value::TRUE)
        } else {
            (value::TRUE, value::FALSE)
        };
        let truthy = self.constant(truthy);
        let falsy = self.constant(falsy);
        let result = self.add_phi(&[truthy, falsy, truthy, falsy]);
        self.write(dst, result)
    }

    /// Builds an instruction as a generic node: write back every slot it may
    /// read, run its slow path, and load the slots it writes from the frame.
    fn build_generic(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction, info: GenericInfo) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        if let Some(flow) = self.try_build_slow_path_call(instruction, info)? {
            return Ok(flow);
        }
        let op = Op::Generic {
            opcode: instruction.opcode(),
            executable: self.function.index,
            pc: self.function.pc,
        };
        self.build_generic_node(instruction, info, op)
    }

    /// Like `build_generic()`, with `op` (a `Generic` node or one that runs
    /// the instruction like one) running the instruction.
    pub(super) fn build_generic_node(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        info: GenericInfo,
        op: Op<'z>,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        self.build_generic_node_with_inputs(instruction, info, op, &[], None)
    }

    /// Like `build_generic_node()`, with the values of the operands `inputs`
    /// as the node's inputs: the node's code reads them from its inputs, and
    /// writes them to the frame itself before its slow paths read them, so
    /// they are not written to the frame before it. The node does not read
    /// `forwarded`, the arguments object operand of a call that forwards the
    /// frame's arguments instead.
    pub(super) fn build_generic_node_with_inputs(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        info: GenericInfo,
        op: Op<'z>,
        inputs: &[Operand],
        forwarded: Option<Operand>,
    ) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let opcode = instruction.opcode();
        let mut input_nodes = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(inputs.len(), self.work);
        for operand in inputs {
            let node = self.read(*operand)?;
            input_nodes.push(node);
        }
        let layout = self.function.layout;
        let is_input_slot = |slot: &usize| {
            inputs
                .iter()
                .any(|operand| layout.tracked_index(*operand) == Some(*slot))
        };
        let live_in = self.live_in(self.function.instruction_index);
        // NB: A virtual arguments object stays virtual unless the slow path reads
        //     it; codegen creates it if the slow path leaves the compiled code.
        let mut read_slots = self.slot_list();
        let mut written_slots = self.slot_list();
        instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| {
            if role.is_read() && Some(operand) != forwarded {
                read_slots.extend(layout.tracked_index(operand).filter(|slot| !is_input_slot(slot)));
            }
            if role.is_written() {
                written_slots.extend(layout.tracked_index(operand));
            }
        });
        // NB: The slow path reads its operands from the frame, and a slot it
        //     writes keeps its old value if it throws first. The other values
        //     only reach the frames if the slow path does not continue in
        //     compiled code (see `codegen::LeaveFrame`).
        let writes_only_operands = !info.reads_whole_frame;
        // NB: Calls with inputs have their result as their value, and their
        //     frame state gives the destination its old value where the call
        //     does not continue (see `ir::FrameState::in_frame`).
        let value_is_result = !input_nodes.is_empty() && matches!(op, Op::CallDirect { .. } | Op::CallNative { .. });
        let is_operand_slot = |slot: &usize| {
            read_slots.contains(slot) || (written_slots.contains(slot) && live_in.contains(*slot) && !value_is_result)
        };
        // NB: Calls in inlined callees run in the published frames of the
        //     inlined calls (see `SiteKind::Publish`), which take all their
        //     operands as inputs. Nothing else reads the frames of inlined
        //     callees (see `inlining::can_inline()`).
        if self.function.is_virtual() && !value_is_result {
            return Err(CompileFailure::UnsupportedInstruction {
                pc: self.function.pc,
                opcode,
                reason: "reads the frame of an inlined callee",
            });
        }
        // NB: Syncing a slot changes no other slot, so each one can be synced as soon as it is found to need it.
        for slot in 0..self.frame.slots.len() {
            let SlotState { node, in_sync } = self.frame.slots[slot];
            let needed = if writes_only_operands {
                is_operand_slot(&slot)
            } else {
                info.reads_whole_frame || live_in.contains(slot)
            };
            if !in_sync
                && needed
                && (!self.is_virtual_arguments(node) || info.reads_whole_frame || read_slots.contains(&slot))
            {
                self.sync_slot(slot);
            }
        }
        self.release_slot_set(live_in);
        self.release_slot_list(read_slots);

        let mut is_conditional_jump = false;
        instruction.for_each_jump_target(|_| is_conditional_jump = true);
        let repr = if is_conditional_jump {
            Some(Repr::Int32)
        } else {
            value_is_result.then_some(Repr::Tagged)
        };
        let node = self.emit(op, &input_nodes, repr);

        let mut destination = None;
        instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| {
            if role.is_written() {
                destination.get_or_insert(operand);
            }
        });
        // NB: The node writes its outputs to the frame, but for a call's result, which is its value. Where it does not
        //     continue, they hold what it wrote, or their old values, which the frame holds too (see above), so its
        //     frame state lists them as held by the frame. Where it continues, they are loaded from there. Written
        //     constants live in frame memory, where the slow path writes them.
        if value_is_result {
            written_slots.clear();
        }
        let frame_outputs = written_slots;
        for slot in &frame_outputs {
            self.frame.slots[*slot].in_sync = true;
        }
        let frame_state = self.resume_after_frame_state(destination.map_or(Operand::INVALID, Operand::raw));
        self.graph.nodes[node.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
        for &slot in &frame_outputs {
            self.load_slot(slot);
        }
        self.release_slot_list(frame_outputs);
        if value_is_result && let Some(destination) = destination {
            self.write(destination, node)?;
        }
        self.end_generic_instruction(instruction, node)
    }

    /// Ends the instruction `node` ran through its slow path: with a branch
    /// on the control word of a conditional jump, and after instructions
    /// that never continue with the next one.
    fn end_generic_instruction(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction, node: NodeId) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let mut targets = ZoneVec::new_in(self.work);
        instruction.for_each_jump_target(|label| targets.push(label));
        let is_conditional_jump = !targets.is_empty();
        if is_conditional_jump {
            let if_true = self.block_for_label(targets[0])?;
            let if_false = match targets.get(1) {
                Some(label) => self.block_for_label(*label)?,
                None => self.fallthrough_block()?,
            };
            if if_true == if_false {
                self.end_with_jump(if_true)?;
            } else {
                let true_pc = targets[0].0;
                self.end_with_branch(
                    |if_true, if_false| Op::BranchOnPc {
                        pc: true_pc,
                        if_true,
                        if_false,
                    },
                    &[node],
                    if_true,
                    if_false,
                )?;
            }
            return Ok(Flow::Ended);
        }
        if !instruction.opcode().can_fall_through() {
            self.set_control(Op::Unreachable, &[]);
            return Ok(Flow::Ended);
        }
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }
}

//! Named property accesses that speculation does not cover, built as IR on
//! the probes of the interpreter's property lookup caches: `GetById` and
//! `PutById` probe the cache of the instruction, `GetLength` branches on
//! arrays, other objects (through the cache) and strings, and
//! `IteratorClose` probes the cache for the return method of the iterator.
//! What the probes do not handle, like accessors, takes the instruction's
//! slow path.

use super::Flow;
use super::GraphBuilder;
use super::checks::SlowPaths;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::PUT_KIND_NORMAL;
use crate::code::Dependency;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;

impl<'a> GraphBuilder<'a, '_> {
    /// Builds `GetById` (`Handling::Expanded`): the property the cache has
    /// for the value (see `Op::ProbePropertyCache`).
    pub(super) fn build_get_by_id(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::GetById {
            dst,
            base,
            property,
            cache,
            ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            unreachable!("only GetById is built here");
        };
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let value = self.read(base)?;
        let property = self.probe_property_cache(&mut slow_paths, value, cache, property.0);
        let result = self.join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(property));
        self.write(dst, result.expect("GetById has a value"))?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds `PutById` (`Handling::Expanded`): stores and additions the
    /// cache has for objects.
    pub(super) fn build_put_by_id(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::PutById {
            base,
            property,
            src,
            kind,
            cache,
        } = *instruction
        else {
            unreachable!("only PutById is built here");
        };
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(None)?;
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let value = self.read(src)?;
        let executable = self.function.index;
        let property = if kind == PUT_KIND_NORMAL { property.0 } else { u32::MAX };
        let stored = self.emit(
            Op::ProbePropertyStore {
                executable,
                cache,
                property,
            },
            &[object, value],
            Some(Repr::Bool),
        );
        self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Bool, &[stored], true);
        self.join_slow_paths(slow_paths, None);
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Builds `IteratorClose` (`Handling::Expanded`): an iterator without a
    /// return method closes without doing anything, for every completion
    /// type, since the instruction after a close for a throw completion
    /// throws it again.
    pub(super) fn build_iterator_close(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::IteratorClose {
            iterator_object, cache, ..
        } = *instruction
        else {
            unreachable!("only IteratorClose is built here");
        };
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(None)?;
        let iterator = self.read(iterator_object)?;

        // NB: In fast array mode, the iterator operand holds the index of the
        //     next element (see `try_build_get_iterator()`), and a watchpoint
        //     set of the realm tells if array iterators have a return method.
        if let Some(return_watchpoint_set) = self.runtime.array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set {
            let (fast_array_mode, iterator_object) =
                self.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32, &[iterator]);
            self.block = fast_array_mode;
            self.embed(return_watchpoint_set);
            self.assume(Dependency::WatchpointSetValid(return_watchpoint_set));
            self.end_hot_path(&mut slow_paths, &[]);
            self.block = iterator_object;
        }

        let return_method = self.probe_property_cache(&mut slow_paths, iterator, cache, u32::MAX);
        self.branch_to_slow_path(&mut slow_paths, BranchCondition::Nullish, &[return_method], true);
        self.join_slow_paths(slow_paths, None);
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// The property that cache `cache` of the instruction has for the value
    /// `object`, taking a slow path where it has none. `property` is the
    /// index of its name in the property key table, if it has one there (see
    /// `Op::ProbePropertyCache`).
    fn probe_property_cache(
        &mut self,
        slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>,
        object: NodeId,
        cache: u32,
        property: u32,
    ) -> NodeId {
        // NB: The probe looks up the properties of strings, numbers and
        //     booleans in their prototypes, whose addresses it embeds.
        let snapshot = &self.function.executable;
        let prototypes = [
            snapshot.string_prototype,
            snapshot.number_prototype,
            snapshot.boolean_prototype,
        ];
        for prototype in prototypes.into_iter().flatten() {
            self.embed(prototype);
        }
        let executable = self.function.index;
        let property = self.emit(
            Op::ProbePropertyCache {
                executable,
                cache,
                property,
            },
            &[object],
            Some(Repr::Tagged),
        );
        self.branch_if_empty(slow_paths, property)
    }

    /// Builds `GetLength` (`Handling::Expanded`): the length of objects with
    /// a magical length (like arrays), the property the cache has for other
    /// objects, and the length of strings.
    pub(super) fn build_get_length(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) -> Result<Flow, CompileFailure> {
        let Instruction::GetLength { dst, base, cache, .. } = *instruction else {
            unreachable!("only GetLength is built here");
        };
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        let value = self.read(base)?;
        let conditions = [BranchCondition::Object, BranchCondition::String];
        self.branch_on_cases(
            &mut slow_paths,
            value,
            &conditions,
            false,
            |builder, slow_paths, case, value| {
                if case == 0 {
                    let address = builder.cell_address(value);
                    let (magical, named) = builder.branch_both_ways(BranchCondition::MagicalLength, &[address]);
                    builder.block = magical;
                    let array = builder.refine(BranchCondition::MagicalLength, true, &[address]);
                    let length = builder.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[array], Some(Repr::Int32));
                    builder.end_with_length(slow_paths, length);
                    builder.block = named;
                    let length = builder.probe_property_cache(slow_paths, value, cache, u32::MAX);
                    builder.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[length]);
                } else {
                    let address = builder.emit(Op::StringAddress, &[value], Some(Repr::Pointer));
                    let length = builder.emit(Op::StringLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
                    builder.end_with_length(slow_paths, length);
                }
            },
        );
        let result = self.join_hot_paths(slow_paths);
        self.write(dst, result.expect("GetLength has a value"))?;
        Ok(Flow::Continue)
    }

    /// Ends a path of `GetLength` with the `Repr::Int32` `length`, which
    /// takes a slow path where it is no int32, an unsigned length above
    /// `i32::MAX`.
    fn end_with_length(&mut self, slow_paths: &mut SlowPaths<'a>, length: NodeId) {
        let zero = self.int32_constant(0);
        let length = self.branch_to_slow_path(
            slow_paths,
            BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThanEquals),
            &[length, zero],
            true,
        );
        let length = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[length], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        self.end_hot_path(slow_paths, &[length]);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/JIT/Rust/src/builder/osr.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! On-stack replacement entries.
//!
//! The interpreter counts loop iterations at the loop back edges the bytecode
//! generator marks with the `*Loop` jump opcodes, and once an executable runs
//! out of tier-up budget there, it can continue a frame that is running in a
//! loop in compiled code. It enters at the back edge instruction, with every
//! value in the frame.
//!
//! Each back edge gets an entry block without predecessors that loads the
//! slots live into the back edge instruction from the frame and then runs the
//! instruction itself, or jumps to its block where the instruction starts it
//! (as the tests at the bottom of loops do). Where the instruction jumps to a
//! block that leads to the loop's header and nowhere else, like the body of a
//! for loop whose test is a constant, the entry runs that block itself instead.
//! Its edges are forward edges into the loop and the loop exit, so the values
//! it loaded meet the other paths in phis.
//!
//! Generators and async functions resume the same way: a suspended frame holds
//! every value live at the continuation it resumes at (see `build_suspend()`),
//! so each continuation of a `Yield`, `YieldIteratorResult` or `Await` gets an
//! entry block that loads them and jumps to the continuation's block, which
//! compiled code reaches from nowhere else. The runtime enters there like at
//! an on-stack replacement entry.
//!
//! Exception handlers are entered the same way. The frame state of an
//! instruction that throws lists every value live into its handler. Each
//! handler that caught an exception before the compile gets an entry block
//! after its `Catch`, where compiled code continues after writing that frame
//! state to the frame and running the `Catch` itself, or the interpreter
//! after running the `Catch` (see `ARCHITECTURE.md`, section 4.2).

use super::Flow;
use super::GraphBuilder;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::Label;
use crate::bytecode::OpCode;
use crate::bytecode::cfg::BlockIndex;
use crate::bytecode::cfg::Loop;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// Whether instructions with this opcode are loop back edges, which count
/// loop iterations in the interpreter.
pub(crate) fn is_loop_back_edge(opcode: OpCode) -> bool {
    use OpCode as O;
    matches!(
        opcode,
        O::JumpLoop
            | O::JumpIfLoop
            | O::JumpTrueLoop
            | O::JumpFalseLoop
            | O::JumpLessThanLoop
            | O::JumpGreaterThanLoop
            | O::JumpLessThanEqualsLoop
            | O::JumpGreaterThanEqualsLoop
            | O::JumpLooselyEqualsLoop
            | O::JumpLooselyInequalsLoop
            | O::JumpStrictlyEqualsLoop
            | O::JumpStrictlyInequalsLoop
            | O::JumpLessThanLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpLessThanEqualsLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpGreaterThanLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpGreaterThanEqualsLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpStrictlyEqualsLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpStrictlyInequalsLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpLooselyEqualsLoopRhsInt32
            | O::JumpLooselyInequalsLoopRhsInt32
    )
}

impl<'a> GraphBuilder<'a, '_> {
    /// Whether the instruction with the given index is a back edge that an on-stack replacement entry can be built at.
    pub(super) fn can_build_osr_entry(&self, index: usize) -> bool {
        let pc = self.function.instructions[index].pc;
        // NB: Back edges in unreachable code lead to blocks that are
        //     never built.
        is_loop_back_edge(self.function.instructions[index].instruction.opcode())
            && (self.has_run)(pc)
            && self
                .function
                .cfg
                .block_for_pc(pc)
                .is_some_and(|block| self.function.cfg.blocks[block].rpo_number.is_some())
    }

    /// Builds an entry block for every reachable loop back edge of the
    /// compiled function that ran, before any of its bytecode blocks is
    /// started.
    pub(super) fn build_osr_entries(&mut self) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        debug_assert!(!self.function.is_virtual());
        let mut targets = ZoneVec::new_in(self.work);
        for index in 0..self.function.instructions.len() {
            let pc = self.function.instructions[index].pc;
            if (self.snapshot.options.osr_pc != Some(pc) && !self.snapshot.options.stress.osr_at_every_loop)
                || !self.can_build_osr_entry(index)
            {
                continue;
            }
            let block = self.start_entry_block(index);
            // NB: A back edge that starts its block is entered through
            //     that block, so that loops with their test at the bottom
            //     are entered at their header like from the function entry.
            //     Unconditional back edges jump to their loop's header
            //     directly instead, since entering a block of the loop
            //     other than its header would make the loop irreducible.
            //     Those that jump to a block leading to the header (like the
            //     body of a for loop whose test is a constant, where the test
            //     is the header) have the entry run that block itself before
            //     it continues at the header.
            let opcode = self.function.instructions[index].instruction.opcode();
            let own_block = self
                .function
                .cfg
                .block_for_pc(pc)
                .filter(|block| opcode != OpCode::JumpLoop && self.function.cfg.blocks[*block].start_pc == pc);
            targets.clear();
            if let Some(own_block) = own_block {
                self.end_with_jump(own_block)?;
                targets.push(own_block);
            } else if let Some(block_before_header) = self.block_before_header_of_back_edge(index) {
                self.build_bytecode_block(block_before_header)?;
                targets.extend(self.function.cfg.blocks[block_before_header].successors.iter().copied());
            } else {
                match self.build_instruction()? {
                    Flow::Ended => {}
                    Flow::Continue => {
                        return Err(CompileFailure::InvalidBytecode {
                            pc,
                            reason: "loop back edge that does not end its block",
                        });
                    }
                }
                self.function.instructions[index]
                    .instruction
                    .for_each_jump_target(|label| {
                        targets.extend(self.function.cfg.block_for_pc(label.0));
                    });
            }
            self.graph.osr_entries.push((pc, block));
            self.record_osr_loop_back_edges(pc);
            self.note_loops_entered_at(&targets);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Builds an entry block for every continuation of a suspension of a
    /// generator or async function in the compiled function, after the
    /// on-stack replacement entries, before any of its bytecode blocks is
    /// started.
    pub(super) fn build_resume_entries(&mut self) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        debug_assert!(!self.function.is_virtual());
        for index in 0..self.function.instructions.len() {
            let (Instruction::Yield {
                continuation_label: Some(continuation),
                ..
            }
            | Instruction::YieldIteratorResult {
                continuation_label: continuation,
                ..
            }
            | Instruction::Await {
                continuation_label: continuation,
                ..
            }) = self.function.instructions[index].instruction
            else {
                continue;
            };
            let pc = continuation.0;
            let target = self.block_for_label(continuation)?;
            let target_block = &self.function.cfg.blocks[target];
            if target_block.start_pc != pc {
                return Err(CompileFailure::InvalidBytecode {
                    pc,
                    reason: "continuation that does not start a block",
                });
            }
            if target_block.rpo_number.is_some() {
                self.build_entry_into_block(target)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Builds an entry block for every exception handler of the compiled
    /// function that caught an exception and whose handler range is
    /// reachable, after the resume entries, before any of its bytecode blocks
    /// is started. Handlers start with a `Catch`, which the interpreter runs:
    /// compiled code never builds it, and is entered after it, where the
    /// handler's block continues. Handlers that never caught anything get no
    /// entry, which would merge into the paths after them.
    pub(super) fn build_catch_entries(&mut self) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        debug_assert!(!self.function.is_virtual());
        for handler in 0..self.function.cfg.blocks.len() {
            let handler_block = &self.function.cfg.blocks[handler];
            let reachable = handler_block
                .exception_predecessors
                .iter()
                .any(|predecessor| self.function.cfg.blocks[*predecessor].rpo_number.is_some());
            let catch = &self.function.instructions[handler_block.instructions.start];
            if !reachable || catch.instruction.opcode() != OpCode::Catch {
                continue;
            }
            if !(self.has_run)(catch.pc) {
                self.graph.uncaught_handlers.push(catch.pc);
                continue;
            }
            // NB: The Catch ends its block, which falls through to the block
            //     that continues the handler.
            let Ok(target) = self.block_for_label(Label(catch.next_pc())) else {
                continue;
            };
            self.build_entry_into_block(target)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Builds an entry block for a frame whose memory holds every value live
    /// at the start of `target`: it loads them and jumps there. The runtime
    /// enters it like an on-stack replacement entry.
    fn build_entry_into_block(&mut self, target: BlockIndex) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let target_block = &self.function.cfg.blocks[target];
        let pc = target_block.start_pc;
        // NB: An on-stack replacement entry at a back edge that starts the
        //     block enters the frame there just the same.
        if self.graph.osr_entries.iter().any(|(entry_pc, _)| *entry_pc == pc) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let block = self.start_entry_block(target_block.instructions.start);
        self.end_with_jump(target)?;
        self.graph.osr_entries.push((pc, block));
        self.note_loops_entered_at(&[target]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Starts an entry block into a frame that is running at the instruction with the given index: a block without
    /// predecessors that loads every slot live there from the frame, whose memory holds them all.
    fn start_entry_block(&mut self, index: usize) -> BlockId {
        let block = self.start_new_block(&[]);
        self.frame = self.dead_frame();
        self.function.instruction_index = index;
        self.function.pc = self.function.instructions[index].pc;
        self.function.eager_frame_state = None;
        let live = self.live_in(index);
        for slot in live.iter() {
            self.load_slot(slot);
        }
        self.release_slot_set(live);
        block
    }

    /// Notes the loops that an entry leads into other than at their header,
    /// over its edges to `targets`, which may only be reached from there over
    /// their back edges.
    fn note_loops_entered_at(&mut self, targets: &[BlockIndex]) {
        for &target in targets {
            for current_loop in &self.function.cfg.loops {
                if current_loop.blocks.contains(&target) && current_loop.header != target {
                    self.function.osr_loop_headers[current_loop.header] = true;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The block that the unconditional back edge at instruction `index` jumps
    /// to, if it is no loop header and leads to one and nowhere else.
    fn block_before_header_of_back_edge(&self, index: usize) -> Option<BlockIndex> {
        let instruction = &self.function.instructions[index].instruction;
        if instruction.opcode() != OpCode::JumpLoop {
            return None;
        }
        let mut target = None;
        instruction.for_each_jump_target(|label| target = self.function.cfg.block_for_pc(label.0));
        let cfg = &self.function.cfg;
        let block = &cfg.blocks[target?];
        match block.successors.as_slice() {
            [successor] if !block.is_loop_header() && cfg.blocks[*successor].is_loop_header() => target,
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Records the loop back edges in the loop of the back edge at `pc`, which
    /// has an entry. A frame running in the interpreter at one of them reaches
    /// the entry once its inner loops finish an iteration. Also records the
    /// other back edges of the loops around that loop, from where a frame may
    /// reach the entry on a later iteration.
    fn record_osr_loop_back_edges(&mut self, pc: u32) {
        let cfg = self.function.cfg;
        let Some(back_edge_block) = cfg.block_for_pc(pc) else {
            return;
        };
        // NB: The loop of a back edge is the innermost loop it is in. Its
        //     header may be the block of the back edge itself, like the test
        //     at the bottom of a for loop.
        let Some(entered_loop) = cfg
            .loops
            .iter()
            .filter(|current_loop| current_loop.blocks.contains(&back_edge_block))
            .min_by_key(|current_loop| current_loop.blocks.len())
        else {
            return;
        };
        let instructions = self.function.instructions;
        let back_edges_in = |current_loop: &'a Loop<'a>| {
            current_loop
                .blocks
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|&block| &instructions[cfg.blocks[block].instructions.clone()])
                .filter(|instruction| is_loop_back_edge(instruction.instruction.opcode()))
                .map(|instruction| instruction.pc)
        };
        for back_edge_pc in back_edges_in(entered_loop) {
            if !self.graph.osr_loop_back_edges.contains(&back_edge_pc) {
                self.graph.osr_loop_back_edges.push(back_edge_pc);
            }
        }
        for outer_loop in cfg.loops.iter().filter(|current_loop| {
            current_loop.blocks.contains(&back_edge_block) && current_loop.blocks.len() > entered_loop.blocks.len()
        }) {
            for back_edge_pc in back_edges_in(outer_loop) {
                if !self.graph.osr_outer_loop_back_edges.contains(&back_edge_pc) {
                    self.graph.osr_outer_loop_back_edges.push(back_edge_pc);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Speculative `GetById` and `PutById`, from what the interpreter's property
//! lookup caches have seen, in their guard and action form (see `caches`).
//!
//! A monomorphic or polymorphic cache whose entries all describe a property
//! of the object or of a prototype (for gets) or an existing writable own data
//! property (for puts) becomes an object check, a shape check and a direct
//! load or store of the property's slot. When the shapes keep the property at
//! different places, a shape switch dispatches to one load or store per shape.
//! Properties that held an accessor when the snapshot was taken are left to
//! inlined accessor calls or to the instruction's handling, and loads and
//! stores still exit for properties that hold one at run time.
//!
//! Methods found on a prototype become constants: the load of the property
//! is checked against the object the prototype held at compile time (a
//! valid prototype chain does not rule out assignments to the property), and
//! uses of it, like calls, see that object as a constant.
//!
//! Every access emits all of its checks and loads; check elimination (see
//! `passes`) removes those that earlier ones make redundant.
//!
//! The caches of keyed accesses (`GetByValue`, `PutByValue`) have one entry
//! per (shape, key) pair. With a key known at compile time, or a single key
//! the cache saw (checked at run time), they are built like named accesses.

use super::Flow;
use super::GraphBuilder;
use super::caches::Action;
use super::caches::CacheEntry;
use super::caches::Holder;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::Operand;
use crate::code::Dependency;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::AccessorPart;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::ShapeCheck;
use crate::ir::value;
use crate::snapshot::CellId;
use crate::snapshot::Intrinsic;
use crate::snapshot::NativeCallTarget;
use crate::snapshot::keyed_feedback_bits;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// A check that a key is the one a keyed access speculates on: `key` must
/// be `expected`, the encoded key cell `cell`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct KeyCheck {
    key: NodeId,
    expected: u64,
    cell: CellId,
}

/// Cache entries of a keyed access for one key, and the check of the key.
type KeyedEntries<'a> = (&'a [CacheEntry], Option<KeyCheck>);

impl<'a, 'z> GraphBuilder<'a, 'z> {
    /// The speculation gate: whether the current instruction may speculate
    /// in a way that exits with `kind`. A speculation that already failed at
    /// the same place is never made again.
    pub(super) fn may_speculate(&self, kind: ExitKind) -> bool {
        let executable = self.function.executable;
        if executable.builtin {
            let site = (executable.cell, self.function.pc, kind);
            return !self.snapshot[self.snapshot.executables[0].builtin_exit_sites].contains(&site);
        }
        !self.snapshot[executable.exit_sites].contains(&(self.function.pc, kind))
    }

    pub(super) fn embed(&mut self, cell: CellId) {
        if !self.graph.embedded_cells.contains(&cell) {
            self.graph.embedded_cells.push(cell);
        }
    }

    /// Emits a node that may exit with the current instruction's eager frame
    /// state. The value of a check is the input it refines (see
    /// `Op::refined_input()`).
    pub(super) fn emit_checked(&mut self, op: Op<'z>, inputs: &[NodeId], repr: Option<Repr>) -> NodeId {
        let repr = repr.or_else(|| self.graph.node(inputs[op.refined_input()?]).repr);
        let frame_state = self.eager_frame_state();
        let node = self.emit(op, inputs, repr);
        self.graph.nodes[node.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
        node
    }

    /// `value`, refined: known to be an object, or the code exits. Objects
    /// the code allocated need no check.
    pub(super) fn check_object(&mut self, value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        if matches!(
            self.graph.node(self.graph.unrefined(value)).op,
            Op::AllocateObject { .. } | Op::AllocateArray { .. } | Op::AllocateFunction { .. }
        ) {
            return value;
        }
        self.emit_checked(Op::CheckObject, &[value], None)
    }

    /// `object`, refined: known to have one of `shapes`, or the code exits.
    pub(super) fn check_shapes(&mut self, object: NodeId, shapes: &[ShapeCheck]) -> NodeId {
        for shape in shapes {
            self.embed(shape.shape);
        }
        let address = self.cell_address(object);
        self.emit_checked(
            Op::CheckShape {
                shapes: self.graph.zone.alloc_slice_copy(shapes),
            },
            &[object, address],
            None,
        )
    }

    /// Makes sure that the `WatchpointSet` cell `validity` is still
    /// valid: the code depends on it staying valid if it was when the
    /// snapshot was taken (`valid`), and checks it otherwise.
    pub(super) fn check_prototype_chain(&mut self, validity: CellId, valid: bool) {
        self.embed(validity);
        if valid {
            self.assume(Dependency::WatchpointSetValid(validity));
            return;
        }
        self.emit_checked(Op::CheckPrototypeChainValid { validity }, &[], None);
    }

    /// Makes the code depend on no `[[IsHTMLDDA]]` object existing, if none
    /// existed when the snapshot was taken, for the current instruction,
    /// which tests the truthiness, type or loose equality with null of a
    /// value. Code depending on it treats every object as truthy, of type
    /// "object" or "function", and not loosely equal to null.
    pub(super) fn assume_no_htmldda_objects(&mut self) {
        if self.runtime.no_htmldda_objects {
            self.assume(Dependency::NoHtmlDdaObjects);
        }
    }

    /// Makes the code depend on `dependency` (see `Op::AssumeValid`) from
    /// the current instruction on.
    pub(super) fn assume(&mut self, dependency: Dependency) {
        self.graph.depend_on(dependency);
        self.emit_checked(Op::AssumeValid, &[], None);
    }

    pub(super) fn load_named(&mut self, object: NodeId, offset: u32) -> NodeId {
        self.load_named_holding(object, offset, false)
    }

    /// Loads the named property at `offset` of `object`, which checks before
    /// ensure holds data if `holds_data`.
    pub(super) fn load_named_holding(&mut self, object: NodeId, offset: u32, holds_data: bool) -> NodeId {
        let address = self.cell_address(object);
        let op = Op::LoadNamed { offset, holds_data };
        if holds_data {
            return self.emit(op, &[object, address], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        }
        self.emit_checked(op, &[object, address], Some(Repr::Tagged))
    }

    pub(super) fn store_named(&mut self, object: NodeId, offset: u32, value: NodeId) {
        self.store_named_holding(object, offset, value, false);
    }

    /// Stores into the named property at `offset` of `object`, which checks
    /// before ensure holds data if `holds_data`.
    pub(super) fn store_named_holding(&mut self, object: NodeId, offset: u32, value: NodeId, holds_data: bool) {
        let address = self.cell_address(object);
        let op = Op::StoreNamed { offset, holds_data };
        if holds_data {
            self.emit(op, &[object, value, address], None);
            return;
        }
        self.emit_checked(op, &[object, value, address], None);
    }

    /// Loads the property a `Get` entry describes, from the object itself or
    /// from the prototype holding it.
    pub(super) fn load_entry(&mut self, object: NodeId, entry: &CacheEntry) -> NodeId {
        if let Action::GetMissing { prototype_chain } = entry.action {
            self.emit_checked(Op::CheckPropertyAbsenceCacheable, &[object], None);
            if let Some((validity, valid)) = prototype_chain {
                self.check_prototype_chain(validity, valid);
            }
            return self.constant(value::UNDEFINED);
        }
        let Action::Get { holder, offset } = entry.action else {
            unreachable!("only gets load");
        };
        let Holder::Prototype {
            prototype,
            validity,
            valid,
        } = holder
        else {
            return self.load_named_holding(object, offset, entry.property_holds_data);
        };
        self.check_prototype_chain(validity, valid);
        self.embed(prototype);
        let holder = self.boxed_object(prototype);
        let holder = self.constant(holder);
        match entry.prototype_property {
            Some((expected, intrinsic)) if self.may_speculate(ExitKind::UnexpectedValue) => {
                let bits = self.boxed_object(expected);
                if let Some(intrinsic) = intrinsic {
                    self.intrinsics.insert(bits, intrinsic);
                }
                if let Some(index) = entry.prototype_property_inline_executable {
                    self.inlinable_functions.insert(bits, index);
                }
                if let Some(target) = entry.prototype_property_direct_call {
                    self.direct_call_functions.insert(bits, target);
                }
                // NB: While the watchpoint set is valid, the prototype holds
                //     the object in the property, which needs no load.
                if let Some(watchpoint) = entry.prototype_property_watchpoint {
                    self.embed(watchpoint);
                    self.embed(expected);
                    self.assume(Dependency::WatchpointSetValid(watchpoint));
                    return self.constant(bits);
                }
                self.load_constant_named(holder, offset, expected)
            }
            _ => self.load_named(holder, offset),
        }
    }

    /// Loads property `offset` of `holder`, which held the object `expected`
    /// at compile time, as a constant: the load is checked against it.
    pub(super) fn load_constant_named(&mut self, holder: NodeId, offset: u32, expected: CellId) -> NodeId {
        self.embed(expected);
        let expected = self.boxed_object(expected);
        let constant = self.constant(expected);
        let loaded = self.load_named(holder, offset);
        self.emit_checked(
            Op::CheckValue {
                expected,
                kind: ExitKind::UnexpectedValue,
            },
            &[loaded],
            None,
        );
        constant
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base.property` from the instruction's property cache.
    /// Returns false, having built nothing that matters, if it cannot speculate.
    pub(super) fn try_build_get_by_id(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(entries) = self
            .cache_entries(cache)
            .or_else(|| self.megamorphic_entries_for_known_shape(cache, base))
        else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        self.build_get(dst, base, entries, None)
    }

    /// Loads a cached getter value from the receiver, after checking the
    /// accessor's identity and the prototype chain that found it.
    pub(super) fn try_build_cached_getter(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(entries) = self.cache_entries(cache) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let first = entries[0];
        let Some(accessor) = first.accessor_function else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let Some(offset) = accessor.cached_value_offset else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let same_cached_getter = entries.iter().all(|entry| {
            entry.holds_accessor
                && matches!(
                    entry.action,
                    Action::Get {
                        holder: Holder::Prototype { .. },
                        ..
                    }
                )
                && entry.action == first.action
                && entry.accessor_function.is_some_and(|entry_accessor| {
                    entry_accessor.function == accessor.function
                        && entry_accessor.cached_value_offset == accessor.cached_value_offset
                })
        });
        let gates = [ExitKind::NotObject, ExitKind::BadShape, ExitKind::UnexpectedValue];
        if !same_cached_getter || !gates.into_iter().all(|kind| self.may_speculate(kind)) {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let (object, getter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Getter)?;
        debug_assert!(getter.is_none(), "all entries have the same checked getter");
        let value = self.load_named(object, offset);
        self.write(dst, value)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Arrays whose magical length property was the only receiver kind seen
    /// need no property lookup or fallback call. Lengths above i32::MAX exit
    /// before boxing, so the interpreter can produce their double value.
    pub(super) fn try_build_array_length(
        &mut self,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        if self.keyed_feedback_bits(instruction) != Some(keyed_feedback_bits::MAGICAL_LENGTH)
            || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadType)
            || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::Overflow)
        {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let array = self.emit_checked(Op::CheckArray, &[object], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let address = self.cell_address(array);
        let length = self.emit(Op::LoadElementsLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let length = self.emit_checked(Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32, &[length], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let boxed = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[length], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        self.write(dst, boxed)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base.length` for typed arrays, whose `length` the
    /// instruction's cache entries all found to be the getter of
    /// `%TypedArray%.prototype.length` on the same prototype: the length the
    /// typed array caches, after checking the getter and that the object is
    /// a typed array. Typed arrays without a cached length (empty, detached
    /// or viewing a resizable buffer) exit, or take the instruction's slow
    /// path where that happened before.
    pub(super) fn try_build_typed_array_length(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(entries) = self.cache_entries(cache) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let first = entries[0];
        let Some(getter) = first.accessor_function else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let location @ Some((Some(_), _)) = first.accessor_location(AccessorPart::Getter) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        // NB: Typed arrays of each kind reach the getter through the prototype
        //     of their kind, so each kind's entries have their own validity cell.
        let same_length_getter = getter.intrinsic == Some(Intrinsic::TypedArrayPrototypeLength)
            && entries.iter().all(|entry| {
                entry.holds_accessor
                    && entry.accessor_location(AccessorPart::Getter) == location
                    && entry.accessor_function.map(|accessor| accessor.function) == Some(getter.function)
            });
        let gates = [
            ExitKind::NotObject,
            ExitKind::BadShape,
            ExitKind::UnexpectedValue,
            ExitKind::BadElements,
        ];
        if !same_length_getter || !gates.into_iter().all(|kind| self.may_speculate(kind)) {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let mut slow_paths = self.start_slow_paths(Some(Repr::Tagged))?;
        // NB: Exiting instead of running the slow path keeps loops bounded by the length free of code that may
        //     change what they read.
        self.exit_instead_of_slow_path(&mut slow_paths);
        let (object, checked_getter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Getter)?;
        debug_assert!(checked_getter.is_none(), "all entries have the same checked getter");
        let typed_array = self.emit_checked(Op::CheckTypedArray, &[object], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let address = self.cell_address(typed_array);
        let length = self.emit(Op::LoadTypedArrayLength, &[address], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let zero = self.int32_constant(0);
        let length = self.branch_to_slow_path(
            &mut slow_paths,
            BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::GreaterThan),
            &[length, zero],
            true,
        );
        let length = self.emit(Op::BoxInt32, &[length], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let result = self.join_slow_paths(slow_paths, Some(length));
        self.write(dst, result.expect("GetLength has a value"))?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// The entries of the instruction's property cache if they all call the
    /// `part` of the same accessor property with functions of the same
    /// executable (see `try_inline_getter()`), with the index of that
    /// executable in the snapshot.
    fn accessor_call_entries(&self, cache: u32, part: AccessorPart) -> Option<(&'a [CacheEntry], u32)> {
        let entries = self.cache_entries(cache)?;
        let first = entries[0];
        let executable_of = |entry: &CacheEntry| {
            let index = entry.accessor_function?.inline_executable?;
            Some(self.snapshot.executables.get(index as usize)?.cell)
        };
        let index = first.accessor_function?.inline_executable?;
        let executable = executable_of(&first)?;
        let same_executable = entries.iter().all(|entry| {
            entry.calls_accessor(part) && entry.action == first.action && executable_of(entry) == Some(executable)
        });
        let gates = [ExitKind::NotObject, ExitKind::BadShape, ExitKind::BadCallTarget];
        if !same_executable || !gates.into_iter().all(|kind| self.may_speculate(kind)) {
            return None;
        }
        Some((entries, index))
    }

    /// The entries of the instruction's property cache if they all call the
    /// `part` of the same accessor property (at one offset of the receiver,
    /// or of one prototype) with the same raw native function, with the
    /// target through which JIT code calls it (see `try_build_native_getter()`).
    fn native_accessor_entries(&self, cache: u32, part: AccessorPart) -> Option<(&'a [CacheEntry], NativeCallTarget)> {
        // NB: Calls in inlined callees need their inlined frames, which these calls do not build.
        if self.function.is_virtual() {
            return None;
        }
        let entries = self.cache_entries(cache)?;
        let first = entries[0];
        let accessor = first.accessor_function?;
        let mut target = accessor.native?;
        let location = first.accessor_location(part)?;
        let same_accessor = entries.iter().all(|entry| {
            entry.holds_accessor
                && entry.accessor_location(part) == Some(location)
                && entry.accessor_function.map(|accessor| accessor.function) == Some(accessor.function)
        });
        let gates = [ExitKind::NotObject, ExitKind::BadShape, ExitKind::UnexpectedValue];
        if !same_accessor || !gates.into_iter().all(|kind| self.may_speculate(kind)) {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: Like the interpreter, read a getter's value without calling it only for shapes it ran on.
        let validated = |entry: &CacheEntry| {
            entry
                .accessor_function
                .and_then(|accessor| accessor.native)
                .is_some_and(|native| native.direct_getter.is_some())
        };
        if !entries.iter().all(validated) {
            target.direct_getter = None;
        }
        Some((entries, target))
    }

    /// A `CallNativeAccessor` node calling the `part` of an accessor, the
    /// raw native function `target`, with `inputs`, whose frame state resumes
    /// after the instruction with its result in `dst`.
    fn emit_native_accessor_call(
        &mut self,
        part: AccessorPart,
        target: NativeCallTarget,
        inputs: &[NodeId],
        dst: u32,
    ) -> NodeId {
        let argument_count = inputs.len() as u64 - 1;
        let slots_offset = u64::from(self.runtime.offsets.execution_context_slots);
        self.reserve_call_frame(slots_offset + 8 * argument_count);
        self.embed(target.function);
        self.embed(target.realm);
        // NB: A call of a function of another realm makes this code's realm current again when it returns.
        self.embed(self.runtime.realm);
        let op = Op::CallNativeAccessor {
            pc: self.function.pc,
            part,
            target,
        };
        let node = self.emit(op, inputs, Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let frame_state = self.resume_after_frame_state(dst);
        self.graph.nodes[node.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
        node
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base.property` for a property that holds an accessor
    /// whose getter is a raw native function, like the getters of platform
    /// objects, as a direct call of it: the instruction's cache entries must
    /// all find the same getter at the same place (see
    /// `native_accessor_entries()`).
    pub(super) fn try_build_native_getter(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, target)) = self.native_accessor_entries(cache, AccessorPart::Getter) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let (object, getter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Getter)?;
        debug_assert!(getter.is_none(), "all entries have the same checked getter");
        let value = self.emit_native_accessor_call(AccessorPart::Getter, target, &[object], dst.raw());
        self.write(dst, value)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Builds `base.property = src` for a property that a prototype holds as
    /// an accessor whose setter is a raw native function, as a direct call of
    /// it, like `try_build_native_getter()`.
    pub(super) fn try_build_native_setter(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        src: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, target)) = self.native_accessor_entries(cache, AccessorPart::Setter) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let value = self.read(src)?;
        let (object, setter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Setter)?;
        debug_assert!(setter.is_none(), "all entries have the same checked setter");
        self.emit_native_accessor_call(AccessorPart::Setter, target, &[object, value], Operand::INVALID);
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Checks that `base` is an object of the shapes of `entries`, which all
    /// call the `part` of the accessor at their property offset, and that
    /// the accessor has the function the entries saw: in the object, or in
    /// the entries' prototype with the prototype chain of every entry
    /// unchanged. Returns
    /// the checked receiver and, if the inlined call must check the function
    /// and run it with its own environment, the function as a value. The
    /// function is absent if it is the one the entries
    /// saw.
    ///
    /// NB: Accessors of objects of one shape can have other functions, such
    ///     as closures of one executable made for each object. Their calls
    ///     are inlined for the executable once a check of the function
    ///     itself failed at the access, or if the entries saw several.
    fn check_accessor_call(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        entries: &[CacheEntry],
        part: AccessorPart,
    ) -> Result<(NodeId, Option<NodeId>), CompileFailure> {
        let first = entries[0];
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let object = self.check_object(object);
        let work = self.work;
        let shapes = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(entries.iter().map(|entry| self.shape_guard(entry)), work);
        let object = self.check_shapes(object, &shapes);
        let (Action::Get { holder, offset } | Action::Set { holder, offset }) = first.action else {
            unreachable!("accessor calls get or set");
        };
        let holder = match holder {
            Holder::Prototype { prototype, .. } => {
                let mut checked_validities = ZoneVec::new_in(self.work);
                for entry in entries {
                    let (Action::Get {
                        holder: Holder::Prototype { validity, valid, .. },
                        ..
                    }
                    | Action::Set {
                        holder: Holder::Prototype { validity, valid, .. },
                        ..
                    }) = entry.action
                    else {
                        unreachable!("the entries call an accessor of the same prototype");
                    };
                    if !checked_validities.contains(&validity) {
                        checked_validities.push(validity);
                        self.check_prototype_chain(validity, valid);
                    }
                }
                self.embed(prototype);
                let prototype = self.boxed_object(prototype);
                self.constant(prototype)
            }
            Holder::Receiver => object,
        };
        let address = self.cell_address(holder);
        let function = first.accessor_function.expect("the entries call a function").function;
        let one_function = entries.iter().all(|entry| {
            entry
                .accessor_function
                .is_some_and(|accessor| accessor.function == function)
        });
        if one_function && self.may_speculate(ExitKind::UnexpectedValue) {
            self.embed(function);
            self.emit_checked(
                Op::CheckAccessorFunction { offset, part, function },
                &[holder, address],
                None,
            );
            return Ok((object, None));
        }
        let function = self.emit_checked(
            Op::LoadAccessorFunction { offset, part },
            &[holder, address],
            Some(Repr::Tagged),
        );
        Ok((object, Some(function)))
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base.property` for a property that holds an accessor,
    /// as an inlined call of its getter: the instruction's cache entries
    /// must all be for an own property at the same offset, or for the same
    /// property of the same prototype, whose accessor must have the getter
    /// it had when the snapshot was taken. Returns `None`, having built
    /// nothing that matters, if it cannot.
    pub(super) fn try_inline_getter(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, index)) = self.accessor_call_entries(cache, AccessorPart::Getter) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let (_, getter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Getter)?;
        self.try_inline_getter_call(index, getter, base, dst)
    }

    /// Builds `base.property = src` for a property that a prototype holds as
    /// an accessor, as an inlined call of its setter, like
    /// `try_inline_getter()`. The setter's result goes into a register
    /// nothing reads before writing it again, if there is one.
    pub(super) fn try_inline_setter(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        src: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<Option<Flow>, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, index)) = self.accessor_call_entries(cache, AccessorPart::Setter) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Some(dst) = self.dead_register(&[base, src]) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let (_, setter) = self.check_accessor_call(base, entries, AccessorPart::Setter)?;
        self.try_inline_setter_call(index, setter, base, src, dst)
    }

    /// A register other than `operands` that is dead after the current
    /// instruction: nothing reads it before writing it again.
    fn dead_register(&mut self, operands: &[Operand]) -> Option<Operand> {
        let layout = self.function.layout;
        let live = self.live_out(self.function.instruction_index);
        let register = (crate::bytecode::RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT..layout.number_of_registers)
            .map(Operand::from_raw)
            .find(|register| {
                !operands.contains(register) && layout.tracked_index(*register).is_some_and(|slot| !live.contains(slot))
            });
        self.release_slot_set(live);
        register
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base[property]` for a string or symbol key from the
    /// instruction's keyed property cache, like `try_build_get_by_id()`.
    pub(super) fn try_build_get_by_value(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        property: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, key_check)) = self.keyed_cache_entries(cache, property)? else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        self.build_get(dst, base, entries, key_check)
    }

    /// Builds `base[property] = src` for a string or symbol key from the
    /// instruction's keyed property cache, like `try_build_put_by_id()`.
    pub(super) fn try_build_put_by_value(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        property: Operand,
        src: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some((entries, key_check)) = self.keyed_cache_entries(cache, property)? else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        self.build_put(base, src, entries, key_check)
    }

    /// The entries of a keyed access's cache for the key in `key`: the key's
    /// own if it is a constant, or those of the only key the cache saw, with
    /// the key check to make (see `check_key()`). Returns nothing for other
    /// keys.
    fn keyed_cache_entries(&mut self, cache: u32, key: Operand) -> Result<Option<KeyedEntries<'a>>, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(entries) = self.cache_entries(cache) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if entries.iter().any(|entry| entry.key.is_none()) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let key_of = |entry: &CacheEntry| entry.key.map(|(value, _)| value);
        let key = self.read(key)?;
        let key_value = match self.graph.constant_value(key) {
            Some(bits) => bits,
            None => {
                let first = key_of(&entries[0]);
                if !entries.iter().all(|entry| key_of(entry) == first) || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::UnexpectedValue)
                {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                first.expect("every entry has a key")
            }
        };
        let entries = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            entries
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|entry| entry.key.is_some_and(|(value, _)| value == key_value)),
            self.work,
        )
        .into_slice();
        let Some((_, cell)) = entries.first().and_then(|entry| entry.key) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let key_check = self.graph.constant_value(key).is_none().then_some(KeyCheck {
            key,
            expected: key_value,
            cell,
        });
        Ok(Some((entries, key_check)))
    }

    /// Checks that a key that is not a constant is the one speculated on.
    fn check_key(&mut self, check: Option<KeyCheck>) {
        let Some(check) = check else {
            return;
        };
        self.embed(check.cell);
        self.emit_checked(
            Op::CheckValue {
                expected: check.expected,
                kind: ExitKind::UnexpectedValue,
            },
            &[check.key],
            None,
        );
    }

    /// Builds `dst = base.property` from cache entries for the property.
    fn build_get(
        &mut self,
        dst: Operand,
        base: Operand,
        entries: &[CacheEntry],
        key_check: Option<KeyCheck>,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        // NB: Loads of properties that hold accessors exit, so these are left to the instruction's handling, which
        //     calls their getters, unless the getter is inlined (see `try_inline_getter()`).
        let speculatable = entries.iter().all(|entry| {
            matches!(entry.action, Action::Get { .. } | Action::GetMissing { .. }) && entry.is_data_access()
        });
        if !speculatable || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::NotObject) || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadShape) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        self.check_key(key_check);
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let object = self.check_object(object);
        let result = self
            .translate_entries(object, entries, |builder, entry, object| {
                Some(builder.load_entry(object, entry))
            })
            .expect("every case loads a value");
        self.write(dst, result)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Builds `base.property = src` from the instruction's property cache,
    /// for existing writable data properties.
    pub(super) fn try_build_put_by_id(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        src: Operand,
        cache: u32,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let Some(entries) = self.cache_entries(cache) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        self.build_put(base, src, entries, None)
    }

    /// Builds `base.property = src` from cache entries for the property.
    fn build_put(
        &mut self,
        base: Operand,
        src: Operand,
        entries: &[CacheEntry],
        key_check: Option<KeyCheck>,
    ) -> Result<bool, CompileFailure> {
        let speculatable = entries
            .iter()
            .all(|entry| matches!(entry.action, Action::Set { .. }) && entry.is_data_access());
        if !speculatable || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::NotObject) || !self.may_speculate(ExitKind::BadShape) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        self.check_key(key_check);
        let object = self.read(base)?;
        let value = self.read(src)?;
        let object = self.check_object(object);
        self.translate_entries(object, entries, |builder, entry, object| {
            let Action::Set { offset, .. } = entry.action else {
                unreachable!("only sets store");
            };
            builder.store_named_holding(object, offset, value, entry.property_holds_data);
            None
        });
        Ok(true)
    }
}
