    fn build(program: &Program, configure: impl FnOnce(&mut Snapshot)) -> String {
        let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(program, test_layout());
        snapshot.runtime.heap_region_offset_mask = (1 << 48) - 1;
        configure(&mut snapshot);
        dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout())
    }

    #[test]
    fn apply_forwards_the_frame_arguments() {
        // a0.method.apply(a0, arguments), with `apply` found on a prototype.
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                create_arguments(true),
                get_by_id(r(6), a(0), 0),
                get_by_id(r(7), r(6), 1),
                call(r(5), r(7), r(6), vec![a(0), l(0)]),
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let mut apply = own(PropertyCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain, 0x200, 1);
        apply.prototype = Some(CellId(0x7000));
        apply.prototype_chain_validity = Some(CellId(0x7100));
        apply.prototype_property = Some(CellId(0x7200));
        apply.prototype_property_intrinsic = Some(Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeApply);
        let text = build(&program, |snapshot| {
            snapshot.executables[0].property_caches = add_caches(
                snapshot,
                &[
                    cache(vec![own(PropertyCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty, 0x100, 0)]),
                    cache(vec![apply]),
                ],
            );
        });
        assert!(text.contains("CallForwardingArguments"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("CreateArguments"), "{text}");

        // Without knowing the callee is apply, the object is needed.
        let mut not_apply = apply;
        not_apply.prototype_property_intrinsic = None;
        let text = build(&program, |snapshot| {
            snapshot.executables[0].property_caches = add_caches(
                snapshot,
                &[
                    cache(vec![own(PropertyCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty, 0x100, 0)]),
                    cache(vec![not_apply]),
                ],
            );
        });
        assert!(text.contains("Generic CreateArguments"), "{text}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn generic_nodes_are_followed_by_loads_of_the_slots_they_write() {
        // Where the node does not continue, the frame holds what it wrote to its outputs, or their old values.
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                create_arguments(true),
                Instruction::Return { value: l(0) },
            ]
        });
        assert_dump(
            &build(&program, |_| {}),
            "
            Generic CreateArguments @1 [[[FS0]]]
            [[ARGUMENTS]] = LoadSlot l0
            [[RESULT]] = EmptyToUndefined ([[ARGUMENTS]])
            Return ([[RESULT]])
            frame states:
              [[FS0]]: pc 1 after -> l0 {} frame [l0]
            ",
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn spreads_forward_the_frame_arguments() {
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                create_arguments(false),
                Instruction::NewArray {
                    dst: r(7),
                    element_count: 0,
                    elements: &[],
                },
                Instruction::ArrayAppend {
                    dst: r(7),
                    src: l(0),
                    is_spread: true,
                },
                Instruction::CallWithArgumentArray {
                    call_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                    callee: a(0),
                    this_value: c(0),
                    arguments: r(7),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let text = build(&program, |_| {});
        assert!(text.contains("CallForwardingArguments"), "{text}");
        assert!(
            !text.contains("CreateArguments") && !text.contains("NewArray"),
            "{text}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn other_uses_create_the_object() {
        let returns_it = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                create_arguments(false),
                Instruction::Return { value: l(0) },
            ]
        });
        let text = build(&returns_it, |_| {});
        assert!(text.contains("Generic CreateArguments"), "{text}");

        // Writes to arguments keep it from being virtual, and so do writes to
        // the parameters a mapped object aliases.
        let writes_argument = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                create_arguments(false),
                Instruction::Mov { dst: a(0), src: c(1) },
                Instruction::GetLength {
                    keyed_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                    base: l(0),
                    cache: 0,
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        assert!(build(&writes_argument, |_| {}).contains("Generic CreateArguments"));
        let reads_length = |mapped| {
            assemble(move |_| {
                vec![
                    Instruction::Enter,
                    create_arguments(mapped),
                    Instruction::GetLength {
                        keyed_feedback: 0,
                        dst: r(5),
                        base: l(0),
                        cache: 0,
                    },
                    Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
                ]
            })
        };
        assert!(build(&reads_length(false), |_| {}).contains("ArgumentCount"));
        let aliased = |snapshot: &mut Snapshot| snapshot.executables[0].mapped_arguments_alias_parameters = true;
        assert!(build(&reads_length(true), aliased).contains("ArgumentCount"));
    }
}

fn dump_bitwise_or(feedback: u8) -> String {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::BitwiseOr {
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: r(6),
                arith_feedback: 0,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[feedback]);
    dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout())
}

#[test]
fn bitwise_operands_that_were_booleans_are_read_as_int32s() {
    use crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::{BOOLEAN, INT32, OTHER, STRING};
    let text = dump_bitwise_or(INT32 | BOOLEAN);
    assert_eq!(text.matches("BranchInt32OrBoolean").count(), 2, "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("Int32BitwiseOr"), "{text}");
    // Operands of other kinds never came, so they exit rather than run the slow path.
    assert!(
        text.contains("Exit SlowPath") && !text.contains("CallSlowPath"),
        "{text}"
    );
    // Other kinds that came, like undefined or strings, take the slow path.
    for other in [OTHER, STRING] {
        let text = dump_bitwise_or(INT32 | BOOLEAN | other);
        assert_eq!(text.matches("CallSlowPath BitwiseOr").count(), 1, "{text}");
    }
    // Other operands, like undefined, are no booleans.
    let text = dump_bitwise_or(INT32 | OTHER);
    assert!(!text.contains("BranchInt32OrBoolean"), "{text}");
    // Without booleans, int32 speculation checks the operands instead.
    let text = dump_bitwise_or(INT32);
    assert!(!text.contains("BranchInt32OrBoolean"), "{text}");
    assert_eq!(text.matches("CheckInt32").count(), 2, "{text}");
}

#[test]
fn numeric_feedback_uses_number_guards_instead_of_type_dispatch() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Add {
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: r(6),
                arith_feedback: 0,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::DOUBLE]);
    let graph = optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let text = dump(&graph, &test_layout());
    assert_eq!(text.matches("CheckNumber").count(), 2, "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("Float64Add"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("BranchInt32Value"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CallSlowPath"), "{text}");
}

#[test]
fn captured_object_bindings_are_guarded_before_becoming_constants() {
    let coordinate = crate::bytecode::EnvironmentCoordinate { hops: 0, index: 2 };
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::GetInitializedBinding {
                value_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                identifier: crate::bytecode::IdentifierTableIndex(0),
                cache: coordinate,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    let object = crate::snapshot::CellId(0x1234);
    let bits = value::tagged(value::OBJECT_TAG) | object.0;
    snapshot.executables[0].captured_bindings = snapshot.add(&[(
        coordinate,
        crate::snapshot::GlobalValueSnapshot {
            bits,
            cell: Some(object),
            intrinsic: None,
            inline_executable: None,
            typed_array: None,
            has_instance: None,
        },
    )]);
    let graph = optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let text = dump(&graph, &test_layout());
    assert!(text.contains("LoadEnvironmentBinding 2"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains(&format!("CheckValue {bits:#x}")), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains(&format!("Return (#0x{bits:x})")), "{text}");
    assert!(graph.embedded_cells.contains(&object));

    snapshot.executables[0].exit_sites = snapshot.add(&[(0, ExitKind::UnexpectedValue)]);
    let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
    assert!(text.contains("LoadEnvironmentBinding 2"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CheckValue"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains(&format!("Return (#0x{bits:x})")), "{text}");
}

#[test]
fn captured_typed_arrays_use_guarded_fixed_lengths() {
    use crate::ir::TypedArrayElement;
    use crate::snapshot::{GlobalValueSnapshot, KeyedFeedbackSnapshot, TypedArraySnapshot};
    let coordinate = crate::bytecode::EnvironmentCoordinate { hops: 0, index: 2 };
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::GetInitializedBinding {
                value_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                identifier: crate::bytecode::IdentifierTableIndex(0),
                cache: coordinate,
            },
            Instruction::GetByValue {
                keyed_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(6),
                base: r(5),
                property: c(0),
                cache: 0,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    snapshot.runtime.layout.typed_array_kind_uint16 = 3;
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.keyed = snapshot.add(&[KeyedFeedbackSnapshot {
        bits: 1 | (1 << (9 + 3)),
    }]);
    let object = crate::snapshot::CellId(0x1234);
    let bits = value::tagged(value::OBJECT_TAG) | object.0;
    snapshot.executables[0].captured_bindings = snapshot.add(&[(
        coordinate,
        GlobalValueSnapshot {
            bits,
            cell: Some(object),
            intrinsic: None,
            inline_executable: None,
            has_instance: None,
            typed_array: Some(TypedArraySnapshot {
                element: TypedArrayElement::Uint16,
                fixed_length: Some(8),
            }),
        },
    )]);
    let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
    assert!(text.contains("CheckTypedArrayStorage"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("LoadTypedArrayDataOffset"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("LoadTypedArrayLength"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CheckElements"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CheckBounds"), "{text}");

    let captured_bindings = snapshot.executables[0].captured_bindings;
    snapshot[captured_bindings][0]
        .1
        .typed_array
        .as_mut()
        .unwrap()
        .fixed_length = None;
    let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
    assert!(text.contains("LoadTypedArrayLength"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CheckTypedArrayStorage"), "{text}");
    assert!(!text.contains("CheckElements"), "{text}");

    let captured_bindings = snapshot.executables[0].captured_bindings;
    snapshot[captured_bindings][0].1.typed_array.as_mut().unwrap().element = TypedArrayElement::Int8;
    let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
    assert!(text.contains("CheckElements TypedArray(Uint16)"), "{text}");
}

#[test]
fn array_length_specialization_requires_monomorphic_receivers_and_exit_gates() {
    use crate::snapshot::{KeyedFeedbackSnapshot, keyed_feedback_bits};
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::GetLength {
                keyed_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                base: a(0),
                cache: 0,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.cache_value = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::value_feedback::INT32]);
    for bits in [
        0,
        keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_ELEMENTS,
        keyed_feedback_bits::MAGICAL_LENGTH | keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_ELEMENTS,
        keyed_feedback_bits::MAGICAL_LENGTH,
    ] {
        snapshot.executables[0].feedback.keyed = snapshot.add(&[KeyedFeedbackSnapshot { bits }]);
        let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
        if bits == keyed_feedback_bits::MAGICAL_LENGTH {
            assert!(text.contains("CheckArray"), "{text}");
            assert!(text.contains("CheckNonNegativeInt32"), "{text}");
            assert!(!text.contains("CallSlowPath"), "{text}");
        } else {
            assert!(!text.contains("CheckArray"), "{text}");
            assert!(text.contains("CallSlowPath"), "{text}");
        }
    }
    for kind in [ExitKind::BadType, ExitKind::Overflow] {
        snapshot.executables[0].exit_sites = snapshot.add(&[(0, kind)]);
        let text = dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout());
        assert!(!text.contains("CheckArray"), "{text}");
        assert!(text.contains("CallSlowPath"), "{text}");
    }
}

mod globals {
    use super::*;
    use crate::snapshot::CellId;
    use crate::snapshot::GlobalCacheSnapshot;
    use crate::snapshot::GlobalValueSnapshot;
    use crate::snapshot::GlobalsSnapshot;

    #[test]
    fn global_variables_the_cache_found_resolve_without_the_interpreter() {
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Enter,
                Instruction::ResolveGlobalBinding {
                    dst: r(5),
                    identifier: crate::bytecode::IdentifierTableIndex(0),
                    cache: 0,
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let build = |cache: Option<GlobalCacheSnapshot>| {
            let mut snapshot = snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
            snapshot.runtime.heap_region_offset_mask = (1 << 48) - 1;
            snapshot.executables[0].globals = Some(GlobalsSnapshot {
                object: CellId(0x1000),
                declarative_environment: CellId(0x2000),
                environment_serial: 1,
                caches: snapshot.add(&[cache]),
            });
            dump(&optimized_graph(&snapshot), &test_layout())
        };

        // A binding of the global declarative environment stays.
        let binding = GlobalCacheSnapshot::Binding {
            index: 0,
            mutable: true,
            assigned: true,
            value: None,
        };
        let text = build(Some(binding));
        assert!(!text.contains("ResolveGlobalBinding"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("CheckShape"), "{text}");

        // A property of the global object stays while the object keeps its shape.
        let property = GlobalCacheSnapshot::Property {
            shape: CellId(0x3000),
            dictionary_generation: None,
            offset: 0,
            writes_data_property: true,
            assigned: true,
            value: GlobalValueSnapshot {
                bits: crate::ir::value::UNDEFINED,
                inline_executable: None,
                cell: None,
                intrinsic: None,
                has_instance: None,
                typed_array: None,
            },
        };
        let text = build(Some(property));
        assert!(text.contains("CheckShape"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("ResolveGlobalBinding"), "{text}");

        // A variable the cache did not find is the interpreter's to resolve.
        let text = build(None);
        assert!(text.contains("CallSlowPath ResolveGlobalBinding"), "{text}");
    }
}

/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Control flow graph of an executable's bytecode.
//!
//! Blocks start at the entry, at jump targets, after terminators, after
//! `Catch`, and at the start, end and target of every exception handler range,
//! so every block lies entirely inside or outside each handler range. Edges
//! come in two kinds: normal control flow (jumps and fallthrough) and
//! exceptional control flow from a block inside a handler range to the
//! handler.
//!
//! Generator continuations (the labels of `Await`, `Yield` and
//! `YieldIteratorResult`) are treated as ordinary successors: the frame
//! survives the suspension, so values live into the continuation stay live.

use super::DecodedInstruction;
use super::ExceptionHandler;
use super::FrameLayout;
use super::OpCode;
use super::Operand;
use super::THIS_VALUE_REGISTER;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;
use core::ops::Range;

pub type BlockIndex = usize;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BasicBlock<'w> {
    /// Byte offset of the first instruction.
    pub start_pc: u32,
    /// Byte offset one past the last instruction.
    pub end_pc: u32,
    /// Indices into the decoded instruction list.
    pub instructions: Range<usize>,
    /// Normal control flow successors, without duplicates.
    pub successors: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    /// The block that receives exceptions thrown by instructions in this block.
    pub exception_handler: Option<BlockIndex>,
    /// Normal control flow predecessors, without duplicates.
    pub predecessors: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    /// Blocks whose exceptions are handled by this block.
    pub exception_predecessors: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    /// Position in `Cfg::reverse_post_order`, or `None` if unreachable.
    pub rpo_number: Option<u32>,
    /// Index into `Cfg::loops` if this block is a loop header.
    pub loop_index: Option<usize>,
}

impl BasicBlock<'_> {
    pub fn predecessor_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.predecessors.len()
    }

    pub fn is_loop_header(&self) -> bool {
        self.loop_index.is_some()
    }
}

/// A loop: a header (the target of one or more back edges) and its body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Loop<'w> {
    pub header: BlockIndex,
    /// Sources of the back edges to the header.
    pub back_edge_sources: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    /// Blocks of the loop, including the header and nested loops, in increasing order.
    pub blocks: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    /// Tracked slots (see `FrameLayout::tracked_index()`) written by any
    /// instruction in the loop, with the this value register where a
    /// `ResolveThisBinding` writes it without naming it.
    pub assigned_slots: ZoneBitSet<'w>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CfgError {
    /// A jump at `pc` targets an offset that is not an instruction boundary.
    InvalidJumpTarget { pc: u32, target: u32 },
    /// An exception handler range does not start, end, or land on instruction boundaries.
    InvalidExceptionHandler { handler_index: usize },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Cfg<'w> {
    /// Blocks in bytecode order. Block 0 is the entry.
    pub blocks: ZoneVec<'w, BasicBlock<'w>>,
    /// Reachable blocks in reverse post order, starting with the entry.
    pub reverse_post_order: ZoneVec<'w, BlockIndex>,
    pub loops: ZoneVec<'w, Loop<'w>>,
}

impl<'w> Cfg<'w> {
    /// The control flow graph of `instructions`, with its data in `work`.
    pub fn new(
        instructions: &[DecodedInstruction],
        exception_handlers: &[ExceptionHandler],
        layout: &FrameLayout,
        work: &'w Zone,
    ) -> Result<Self, CfgError> {
        let mut cfg = Self {
            blocks: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            reverse_post_order: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            loops: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        };
        if instructions.is_empty() {
            return Ok(cfg);
        }
        cfg.find_blocks(instructions, exception_handlers)?;
        cfg.connect_blocks(instructions, exception_handlers)?;
        let back_edges = cfg.compute_reverse_post_order();
        cfg.find_loops(instructions, layout, back_edges);
        Ok(cfg)
    }

    /// The block containing the instruction at `pc`.
    pub fn block_for_pc(&self, pc: u32) -> Option<BlockIndex> {
        let index = self.blocks.partition_point(|block| block.start_pc <= pc);
        let block = index.checked_sub(1)?;
        (pc < self.blocks[block].end_pc).then_some(block)
    }

    fn find_blocks(
        &mut self,
        instructions: &[DecodedInstruction],
        exception_handlers: &[ExceptionHandler],
    ) -> Result<(), CfgError> {
        let end_pc = instructions
            .last()
            .expect("Cfg::new() handles empty bytecode")
            .next_pc();
        let instruction_index_for_pc = |pc: u32| {
            instructions
                .binary_search_by_key(&pc, |instruction| instruction.pc)
                .ok()
        };

        let zone = self.blocks.zone();
        let mut is_leader = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, instructions.len(), zone);
        is_leader[0] = true;
        for (index, instruction) in instructions.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut result = Ok(());
            instruction.instruction.for_each_jump_target(|target| {
                if let Some(target_index) = instruction_index_for_pc(target.0) {
                    is_leader[target_index] = true;
                } else {
                    result = Err(CfgError::InvalidJumpTarget {
                        pc: instruction.pc,
                        target: target.0,
                    });
                }
            });
            result?;
            // NB: Compiled code enters handlers after their Catch, which the
            //     interpreter runs (see `build_catch_entries()`).
            let ends_block =
                instruction.instruction.is_terminator() || instruction.instruction.opcode() == OpCode::Catch;
            if ends_block && index + 1 < instructions.len() {
                is_leader[index + 1] = true;
            }
        }
        for (handler_index, handler) in exception_handlers.iter().enumerate() {
            let error = CfgError::InvalidExceptionHandler { handler_index };
            if handler.start_offset > handler.end_offset {
                return Err(error);
            }
            for (offset, may_be_end) in [
                (handler.start_offset, false),
                (handler.end_offset, true),
                (handler.handler_offset, false),
            ] {
                if may_be_end && offset == end_pc {
                    continue;
                }
                let index = instruction_index_for_pc(offset).ok_or(error)?;
                is_leader[index] = true;
            }
        }

        let mut start = 0;
        for index in 1..=instructions.len() {
            if index < instructions.len() && !is_leader[index] {
                continue;
            }
            self.blocks.push(BasicBlock {
                start_pc: instructions[start].pc,
                end_pc: instructions[index - 1].next_pc(),
                instructions: start..index,
                successors: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
                exception_handler: None,
                predecessors: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
                exception_predecessors: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
                rpo_number: None,
                loop_index: None,
            });
            start = index;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn connect_blocks(
        &mut self,
        instructions: &[DecodedInstruction],
        exception_handlers: &[ExceptionHandler],
    ) -> Result<(), CfgError> {
        let zone = self.blocks.zone();
        let mut successors = ZoneVec::new_in(zone);
        for block_index in 0..self.blocks.len() {
            let block = &self.blocks[block_index];
            let last = &instructions[block.instructions.end - 1];
            successors.clear();
            last.instruction
                .for_each_jump_target(|target| successors.push(target.0));
            if last.instruction.opcode().can_fall_through() && block_index + 1 < self.blocks.len() {
                successors.push(last.next_pc());
            }
            let mut successor_blocks = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(successors.len(), zone);
            for &target in &successors {
                let successor = self
                    .block_for_pc(target)
                    .ok_or(CfgError::InvalidJumpTarget { pc: last.pc, target })?;
                if !successor_blocks.contains(&successor) {
                    successor_blocks.push(successor);
                }
            }

            let start_pc = block.start_pc;
            let exception_handler = exception_handlers
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .find(|(_, handler)| handler.start_offset <= start_pc && start_pc < handler.end_offset)
                .map(|(handler_index, handler)| {
                    self.block_for_pc(handler.handler_offset)
                        .ok_or(CfgError::InvalidExceptionHandler { handler_index })
                })
                .transpose()?;

            for successor in &successor_blocks {
                self.blocks[*successor].predecessors.push(block_index);
            }
            if let Some(handler) = exception_handler {
                self.blocks[handler].exception_predecessors.push(block_index);
            }
            let block = &mut self.blocks[block_index];
            block.successors = successor_blocks;
            block.exception_handler = exception_handler;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// All successors of a block, normal and exceptional.
    fn all_successors(&self, block: BlockIndex) -> impl Iterator<Item = BlockIndex> + '_ {
        let block = &self.blocks[block];
        block.successors.iter().copied().chain(block.exception_handler)
    }

    /// Computes the reverse post order with a depth first search from the
    /// entry and returns the back edges (edges to a block on the DFS stack).
    fn compute_reverse_post_order(&mut self) -> ZoneVec<'w, (BlockIndex, BlockIndex)> {
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
        enum State {
            Unvisited,
            OnStack,
            Done,
        }
        let zone = self.blocks.zone();
        let mut state = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(State::Unvisited, self.blocks.len(), zone);
        let mut back_edges = ZoneVec::new_in(zone);
        // Each stack entry is a block and the index of the next successor to visit.
        let mut stack = ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[(0, 0)], zone);
        state[0] = State::OnStack;
        while let Some((block, next_successor)) = stack.last_mut() {
            let block = *block;
            let successor = self.all_successors(block).nth(*next_successor);
            *next_successor += 1;
            match successor {
                Some(successor) => match state[successor] {
                    State::Unvisited => {
                        state[successor] = State::OnStack;
                        stack.push((successor, 0));
                    }
                    State::OnStack => back_edges.push((block, successor)),
                    State::Done => {}
                },
                None => {
                    state[block] = State::Done;
                    self.reverse_post_order.push(block);
                    stack.pop();
                }
            }
        }
        // NB: The list holds the post order up to here.
        self.reverse_post_order.reverse();
        for (rpo_number, block) in self.reverse_post_order.iter().enumerate() {
            self.blocks[*block].rpo_number = Some(u32::try_from(rpo_number).expect("block count fits in u32"));
        }
        back_edges
    }

    fn find_loops(
        &mut self,
        instructions: &[DecodedInstruction],
        layout: &FrameLayout,
        mut back_edges: ZoneVec<'w, (BlockIndex, BlockIndex)>,
    ) {
        let zone = self.blocks.zone();
        // NB: Edges with the same key are the same edge, so the order of equal keys does not matter.
        back_edges.sort_unstable_by_key(|(source, header)| (self.blocks[*header].rpo_number, *source));
        let mut loops: ZoneVec<'w, Loop<'w>> = ZoneVec::new_in(zone);
        for &(source, header) in &back_edges {
            if let Some(existing) = loops.last_mut().filter(|existing| existing.header == header) {
                existing.back_edge_sources.push(source);
            } else {
                loops.push(Loop {
                    header,
                    back_edge_sources: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[source], zone),
                    blocks: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
                    assigned_slots: ZoneBitSet::new_in(layout.tracked_slot_count(), zone),
                });
            }
        }

        let this_register = layout.tracked_index(Operand::from_raw(THIS_VALUE_REGISTER));
        let mut in_loop = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, self.blocks.len(), zone);
        let mut worklist = ZoneVec::new_in(zone);
        for (loop_index, current_loop) in loops.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            // The natural loop: the header plus every reachable block that
            // reaches a back edge source without passing through the header.
            in_loop.fill(false);
            in_loop[current_loop.header] = true;
            worklist.assign(&current_loop.back_edge_sources);
            while let Some(block) = worklist.pop() {
                if in_loop[block] || self.blocks[block].rpo_number.is_none() {
                    continue;
                }
                in_loop[block] = true;
                let block = &self.blocks[block];
                worklist.extend(block.predecessors.iter().chain(&block.exception_predecessors));
            }
            current_loop
                .blocks
                .extend((0..self.blocks.len()).filter(|block| in_loop[*block]));

            for block in &current_loop.blocks {
                for instruction in &instructions[self.blocks[*block].instructions.clone()] {
                    if instruction.instruction.opcode() == OpCode::ResolveThisBinding
                        && let Some(slot) = this_register
                    {
                        current_loop.assigned_slots.insert(slot);
                    }
                    instruction.instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| {
                        if role.is_written()
                            && let Some(slot) = layout.tracked_index(operand)
                        {
                            current_loop.assigned_slots.insert(slot);
                        }
                    });
                }
            }
            self.blocks[current_loop.header].loop_index = Some(loop_index);
        }
        self.loops = loops;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::test_support::*;
    use super::*;
    use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
    use crate::bytecode::Label;

    #[test]
    fn straight_line_code_is_one_block() {
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: r(5) },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
            ]
        });
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].instructions, 0..3);
        assert!(cfg.blocks[0].successors.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order, [0]);
        assert!(cfg.loops.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn if_else_splits_at_targets_and_after_terminators() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::JumpIf {
                    condition: r(5),
                    true_target: label(1),
                    false_target: label(3),
                },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::Jump { target: label(4) },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: c(1) },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
            ]
        });
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        let instruction_ranges = cfg
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .map(|block| block.instructions.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(instruction_ranges, [0..1, 1..3, 3..4, 4..5]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].successors, [1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[1].successors, [3]);
        // The else block falls through into the join block.
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[2].successors, [3]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[3].predecessor_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].predecessor_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order.first(), Some(&0));
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order.last(), Some(&3));
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order.len(), 4);
        assert!(cfg.loops.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(cfg.block_for_pc(program.offsets[2]), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(cfg.block_for_pc(program.offsets[3]), Some(2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn loop_header_is_target_of_back_edge() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::JumpLessThan {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    lhs: r(5),
                    rhs: c(1),
                    true_target: label(2),
                    false_target: label(5),
                },
                Instruction::Increment {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: r(5) },
                Instruction::Jump { target: label(1) },
                Instruction::Return { value: l(1) },
            ]
        });
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        let layout = test_layout();
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(cfg.loops.len(), 1);
        let header_loop = &cfg.loops[0];
        assert_eq!(header_loop.header, 1);
        assert!(cfg.blocks[1].is_loop_header());
        assert_eq!(header_loop.back_edge_sources, [2]);
        assert_eq!(header_loop.blocks, [1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[1].predecessor_count(), 2);
        let assigned = header_loop.assigned_slots.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let local0 = layout.tracked_index(l(0)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(assigned, [5, local0]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order, [0, 1, 3, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_loops_include_inner_assignments() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::JumpTrue {
                    condition: r(5),
                    target: label(3),
                },
                Instruction::JumpTrue {
                    condition: r(6),
                    target: label(0),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(7), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::JumpTrue {
                    condition: r(7),
                    target: label(3),
                },
                Instruction::Jump { target: label(0) },
            ]
        });
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        let layout = test_layout();
        // JumpTrue continues with the next instruction when not taken.
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].successors, [3, 1]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.loops.len(), 2);
        let outer = &cfg.loops[0];
        let inner = &cfg.loops[1];
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[outer.header].instructions, 0..1);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[inner.header].instructions, 3..5);
        assert!(outer.blocks.contains(&inner.header));
        assert!(outer.assigned_slots.contains(layout.tracked_index(r(7)).unwrap()));
        assert!(!outer.assigned_slots.contains(layout.tracked_index(r(6)).unwrap()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn exception_handler_ranges_split_blocks_and_add_exception_edges() {
        let program = assemble_with_handlers(
            |label| {
                vec![
                    Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                    Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: a(0) },
                    Instruction::Throw { src: r(6) },
                    Instruction::Catch {
                        value_feedback: 0,
                        dst: r(7),
                    },
                    Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
                    Instruction::Jump { target: label(0) },
                ]
            },
            &[(1, 3, 3)],
        );
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        let instruction_ranges = cfg
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .map(|block| block.instructions.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        // The Catch ends its block.
        assert_eq!(instruction_ranges, [0..1, 1..3, 3..4, 4..5, 5..6]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].successors, [1]);
        assert!(cfg.blocks[1].successors.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[1].exception_handler, Some(2));
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[2].exception_predecessors, [1]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[2].predecessor_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[2].successors, [3]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.reverse_post_order, [0, 1, 2, 3]);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[4].rpo_number, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn generator_continuations_are_successors() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Yield {
                    continuation_label: Some(label(1)),
                    value: r(5),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let cfg = program.cfg();
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(cfg.blocks[0].successors, [1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_jumps_into_the_middle_of_instructions() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Jump {
                    target: Label(label(1).0 + 4),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let instructions = crate::bytecode::decode_all(&program.bytes, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        let error = Cfg::new(&instructions, &[], &test_layout(), crate::test_zone()).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(error, CfgError::InvalidJumpTarget { pc: 0, .. }));
    }
}

/*

//! Decoder for assembled bytecode.
//!
//! The `OpCode` and `Instruction` enums, the per-opcode field decoder and the
//! operand / jump target visitors are generated by build.rs from
//! interpreter.flap. The input is the exact byte stream the interpreter
//! executes: operands are flat slot indices, labels are absolute byte offsets.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/decoder_generated.rs"));

/// A frame slot, as a flat index into the interpreter's
/// `[registers | locals | constants | arguments]` value array.
///
/// See `FrameLayout` for how to classify an index.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct Operand(u32);

impl Operand {
    /// The encoding of an absent `Optional<Operand>`.
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    /// The raw operand that an operand byte of the bytecode stands for, `INVALID` for an absent one.
    pub fn raw_from_byte(byte: u8) -> u32 {
        if byte == u8::MAX {
            Self::INVALID
        } else {
            u32::from(byte)
        }
    }

    pub fn from_raw(raw: u32) -> Self {
        Self(raw)
    }

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }

    /// The flat slot index, as the bytecode encodes it.
    pub fn raw(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }
}

/// Whether an instruction reads an operand, writes it, or both.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OperandRole {
    In,
    Out,
    InOut,
}

impl OperandRole {
    pub fn is_read(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, OperandRole::In | OperandRole::InOut)
    }

    pub fn is_written(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, OperandRole::Out | OperandRole::InOut)
    }
}

/// A bytecode offset (absolute, from the start of the executable's bytecode).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct Label(pub u32);

/// Index into the executable's identifier table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IdentifierTableIndex(pub u32);

impl IdentifierTableIndex {
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }
}

/// Index into the executable's property key table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PropertyKeyTableIndex(pub u32);

/// Index into the executable's string table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StringTableIndex(pub u32);

impl StringTableIndex {
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }
}

/// Environment coordinate used by the binding instructions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct EnvironmentCoordinate {
    pub hops: u32,
    pub index: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DecodeErrorKind {
    UnknownOpcode,
    TruncatedInstruction,
    InvalidLength,
}

/// Why the instruction at `pc` could not be decoded.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DecodeError {
    pub pc: u32,
    pub kind: DecodeErrorKind,
}

/// How a slow path that takes an instruction's `Op` record receives its
/// operands, following Flap's `SlowPathLayout`. The record (`Op::Values`) has
/// one value per scalar operand field, in field order, followed by the values
/// of the operand array.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SlowPathAbi {
    /// `AsmSlowPathResult f(VM*, u32 pc, Op const*, Value input...)`: the
    /// inputs are passed by value and the single output, if any, comes back as
    /// the second return word.
    Scalar,
    /// `i64 f(VM*, u32 pc, Op const*, Op::Values& outputs, Value input...)`:
    /// inputs (and input/outputs) by value, outputs written to the record.
    ScalarInputs,
    /// `i64 f(VM*, u32 pc, Op const*, Op::Values& values)`: everything in the
    /// record, including the operand array.
    Record,
}

/// One scalar operand field of an instruction, as seen by its slow path.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SlowPathField {
    /// Byte offset of the operand within the instruction.
    pub instruction_offset: u32,
    pub role: OperandRole,
    /// Whether the operand is an `Optional<Operand>`; absent ones read as the empty value.
    pub optional: bool,
}

/// The operand array of an instruction, as seen by its slow path.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SlowPathArray {
    /// Byte offset of the first operand of the array within the instruction.
    pub instruction_offset: u32,
    /// Byte offset of the one-byte element count within the instruction.
    pub count_offset: u32,
    pub optional: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SlowPathLayout {
    pub abi: SlowPathAbi,
    pub fields: &'static [SlowPathField],
    pub array: Option<SlowPathArray>,
}

/// The interpreter feedback slots one instruction records into, one index
/// space per feedback kind (see `Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/layout/feedback.rs`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FeedbackSlots {
    pub arith: Option<u16>,
    pub value: Option<u16>,
    pub call: Option<u16>,
    pub keyed: Option<u16>,
    /// The property lookup cache whose site's value feedback the instruction records.
    pub cache_value: Option<u16>,
}

/// One decoded instruction and where it lives in the bytecode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DecodedInstruction<'a> {
    /// Byte offset of the instruction.
    pub pc: u32,
    /// Encoded length in bytes; the next instruction starts at `pc + length`.
    pub length: u32,
    pub instruction: Instruction<'a>,
}

impl OpCode {
    /// Whether an instruction of this opcode costs nothing in inlined code:
    /// entering the frame, moves between slots (which SSA values rename),
    /// and jumps.
    pub fn is_free_when_inlined(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            OpCode::Enter | OpCode::EnterCoercingThis | OpCode::Mov | OpCode::Jump
        )
    }
}

/// How many of a callee's instructions cost something in inlined code,
/// which decides whether it is small enough to always inline.
pub fn inlining_size(instructions: &[DecodedInstruction]) -> usize {
    instructions
        .iter()
        .filter(|decoded| !decoded.instruction.opcode().is_free_when_inlined())
        .count()
}

impl Instruction<'_> {
    /// The property lookup cache whose entries compiled code speculates on
    /// for this instruction, as shape checks that exit with
    /// `ExitKind::BadShape`.
    pub fn speculated_property_lookup_cache(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        match *self {
            Instruction::GetById { cache, .. }
            | Instruction::PutById { cache, .. }
            | Instruction::GetLength { cache, .. }
            | Instruction::GetByValue { cache, .. }
            | Instruction::PutByValue { cache, .. } => Some(cache),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl DecodedInstruction<'_> {
    pub fn next_pc(&self) -> u32 {
        self.pc + self.length
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
fn narrow_index(index: u32) -> u16 {
    if index == u32::MAX {
        return u16::MAX;
    }
    u16::try_from(index).expect("bytecode indices fit in 16 bits")
}

/// See `WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK` of the bytecode generator.
const WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK: u16 = 0xff00;
const NO_NAME_INDEX: u16 = u16::MAX;

#[cfg(test)]
fn is_wide_name_index(index: u32) -> bool {
    index != u32::MAX && index >= u32::from(WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK)
}

#[cfg(test)]
fn name_index_field(index: u32, distance: usize) -> u16 {
    if index == u32::MAX {
        return NO_NAME_INDEX;
    }
    if !is_wide_name_index(index) {
        return index as u16;
    }
    WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK + u16::try_from(distance).unwrap()
}

fn read_optional_name_index(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    match read_u16(bytes, at) {
        NO_NAME_INDEX => None,
        raw if raw >= WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK => Some(read_u32(bytes, at - usize::from(raw - WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK))),
        raw => Some(u32::from(raw)),
    }
}

fn read_name_index(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    read_optional_name_index(bytes, at).expect("the field holds a name table index")
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 2].try_into().unwrap())
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 4].try_into().unwrap())
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 8].try_into().unwrap())
}

/// The opcode and the encoded length of the instruction starting at byte offset `pc`, after a check that the whole
/// instruction lies within `bytes`.
fn opcode_and_length(bytes: &[u8], pc: u32) -> Result<(u8, usize), DecodeError> {
    let error = |kind| DecodeError { pc, kind };
    let at = pc as usize;
    if at >= bytes.len() {
        return Err(error(DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction));
    }
    let opcode = bytes[at];
    let length = instruction_length_from_bytes(opcode, bytes, at).map_err(error)?;
    if length == 0 || at + length > bytes.len() {
        return Err(error(DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction));
    }
    if u32::try_from(length).is_err() {
        return Err(error(DecodeErrorKind::InvalidLength));
    }
    Ok((opcode, length))
}

/// Decodes the instruction starting at byte offset `pc`. Its array, if it has one, is in `zone`.
pub fn decode_instruction<'a>(bytes: &[u8], pc: u32, zone: &'a Zone) -> Result<DecodedInstruction<'a>, DecodeError> {
    let error = |kind| DecodeError { pc, kind };
    let (opcode, length) = opcode_and_length(bytes, pc)?;
    let instruction = match decode_fields(opcode, bytes, pc as usize, length, zone).map_err(error)? {
        // NB: The rest of the compiler has no reason to care how far up the frame a move reaches.
        Instruction::MovWide { dst_slot, src_slot } => Instruction::Mov {
            dst: Operand::from_raw(dst_slot),
            src: Operand::from_raw(src_slot),
        },
        instruction => instruction,
    };
    Ok(DecodedInstruction {
        pc,
        length: length as u32,
        instruction,
    })
}

/// The feedback slots of the instruction starting at byte offset `pc`, or `None` if it cannot be decoded.
pub fn feedback_slots_at(bytes: &[u8], pc: u32) -> Option<FeedbackSlots> {
    let (opcode, _) = opcode_and_length(bytes, pc).ok()?;
    Some(feedback_slots_from_bytes(opcode, bytes, pc as usize))
}

/// Decodes a whole instruction stream into `zone`.
pub fn decode_all<'a>(bytes: &[u8], zone: &'a Zone) -> Result<&'a [DecodedInstruction<'a>], DecodeError> {
    let end = u32::try_from(bytes.len()).map_err(|_| DecodeError {
        pc: 0,
        kind: DecodeErrorKind::InvalidLength,
    })?;
    // NB: The list gets its size before the first instruction is decoded, so the arrays that the zone gives out
    //     after it never make it move.
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut pc = 0;
    while pc < end {
        let (_, length) = opcode_and_length(bytes, pc)?;
        pc += length as u32;
        count += 1;
    }
    let mut instructions = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(count, zone);
    let mut pc = 0;
    while pc < end {
        let instruction = decode_instruction(bytes, pc, zone)?;
        pc = instruction.next_pc();
        instructions.push(instruction);
    }
    Ok(instructions.into_slice())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn operand(index: u32) -> Operand {
        Operand::from_raw(index)
    }

    fn operands_with_roles(instruction: &Instruction) -> Vec<(u32, OperandRole)> {
        let mut operands = Vec::new();
        instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| operands.push((operand.raw(), role)));
        operands
    }

    fn jump_targets(instruction: &Instruction) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut targets = Vec::new();
        instruction.for_each_jump_target(|label| targets.push(label.0));
        targets
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_hand_assembled_mov() {
        let mut bytes = vec![OpCode::Mov as u8];
        bytes.push(7); // dst
        bytes.push(12); // src

        let decoded = decode_instruction(&bytes, 0, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.pc, 0);
        assert_eq!(decoded.length, 3);
        assert_eq!(
            decoded.instruction,
            Instruction::Mov {
                dst: operand(7),
                src: operand(12)
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(decoded.instruction.opcode(), OpCode::Mov);
        assert_eq!(
            operands_with_roles(&decoded.instruction),
            [(7, OperandRole::Out), (12, OperandRole::In)]
        );
        assert!(!decoded.instruction.is_terminator());
        assert!(OpCode::Mov.can_fall_through());
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_hand_assembled_jump_if() {
        let mut bytes = vec![0; 16];
        let mut jump = vec![OpCode::JumpIf as u8];
        jump.push(5); // condition
        jump.extend(32u32.to_ne_bytes()); // true_target
        jump.extend(48u32.to_ne_bytes()); // false_target
        bytes.extend(jump);

        let decoded = decode_instruction(&bytes, 16, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.pc, 16);
        assert_eq!(decoded.length, 10);
        assert_eq!(decoded.next_pc(), 26);
        assert_eq!(
            decoded.instruction,
            Instruction::JumpIf {
                condition: operand(5),
                true_target: Label(32),
                false_target: Label(48)
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(jump_targets(&decoded.instruction), [32, 48]);
        assert_eq!(operands_with_roles(&decoded.instruction), [(5, OperandRole::In)]);
        assert!(decoded.instruction.is_terminator());
        assert!(OpCode::JumpIf.is_terminator());
        assert!(!OpCode::JumpIf.can_fall_through());
        assert!(OpCode::JumpTrue.is_terminator());
        assert!(OpCode::JumpTrue.can_fall_through());
        assert!(!OpCode::Return.can_fall_through());
    }

    #[test]
    fn decodes_variable_length_call() {
        let call = Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback: 0,
            dst: operand(5),
            callee: operand(6),
            this_value: operand(7),
            argument_count: 3,
            arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[operand(8), operand(20), operand(21)]),
        };
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        call.encode(&mut bytes);

        let decoded = decode_instruction(&bytes, 0, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.length as usize, bytes.len());
        assert_eq!(decoded.length as usize, call.encoded_size());
        assert_eq!(decoded.instruction, call);
        assert_eq!(
            operands_with_roles(&decoded.instruction),
            [
                (5, OperandRole::Out),
                (6, OperandRole::In),
                (7, OperandRole::In),
                (8, OperandRole::In),
                (20, OperandRole::In),
                (21, OperandRole::In),
            ]
        );
        assert!(!decoded.instruction.is_terminator());
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_trips_a_stream_of_instructions() {
        let instructions = [
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::NewPrimitiveArray {
                dst: operand(5),
                element_count: 2,
                elements: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[0x7ff8_0000_0000_0001, 42]),
            },
            Instruction::NewClass {
                element_keys_are_in_array: false,
                dst: operand(6),
                super_class: None,
                proto_parent: None,
                class_environment: operand(7),
                class_blueprint_index: 1,
                lhs_name: Some(IdentifierTableIndex(4)),
                computed_name: None,
                element_keys_count: 3,
                element_keys: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[Some(operand(8)), None, Some(operand(9))]),
            },
            Instruction::GetBinding {
                value_feedback: 0,
                dst: operand(5),
                identifier: IdentifierTableIndex(3),
                cache: EnvironmentCoordinate { hops: 1, index: 2 },
            },
            Instruction::CreateArguments {
                dst: None,
                kind: 1,
                is_immutable: true,
                creates_parameter_bindings: false,
            },
            Instruction::AddRhsInt32 {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: operand(5),
                lhs: operand(6),
                rhs: -5,
            },
            Instruction::Mov {
                dst: operand(5),
                src: operand(6),
            },
            Instruction::PostfixIncrement {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: operand(5),
                src: operand(6),
            },
            Instruction::Yield {
                continuation_label: Some(Label(0)),
                value: operand(5),
            },
            Instruction::Yield {
                continuation_label: None,
                value: operand(5),
            },
        ];
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        for instruction in &instructions {
            instruction.encode(&mut bytes);
        }

        let decoded = decode_all(&bytes, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decoded.len(), instructions.len());
        let mut pc = 0;
        for (decoded, instruction) in decoded.iter().zip(&instructions) {
            assert_eq!(&decoded.instruction, instruction);
            assert_eq!(decoded.pc, pc);
            pc += u32::try_from(instruction.encoded_size()).unwrap();
        }

        assert_eq!(
            operands_with_roles(&decoded[2].instruction),
            [
                (6, OperandRole::Out),
                (7, OperandRole::In),
                (8, OperandRole::In),
                (9, OperandRole::In)
            ]
        );
        assert!(operands_with_roles(&decoded[4].instruction).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            operands_with_roles(&decoded[6].instruction),
            [(5, OperandRole::Out), (6, OperandRole::In)]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            operands_with_roles(&decoded[7].instruction),
            [(5, OperandRole::Out), (6, OperandRole::InOut)]
        );
        assert_eq!(jump_targets(&decoded[8].instruction), [0]);
        assert!(jump_targets(&decoded[9].instruction).is_empty());
        assert!(decoded[9].instruction.is_terminator());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_malformed_instructions() {
        let error = |bytes: &[u8]| decode_instruction(bytes, 0, crate::test_zone()).unwrap_err().kind;

        assert_eq!(error(&[]), DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction);
        assert_eq!(error(&[u8::MAX, 0]), DecodeErrorKind::UnknownOpcode);

        let mut mov = Vec::new();
        Instruction::Mov {
            dst: operand(5),
            src: operand(6),
        }
        .encode(&mut mov);
        assert_eq!(error(&mov[..2]), DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction);

        let mut call = Vec::new();
        Instruction::Call {
            call_feedback: 0,
            dst: operand(5),
            callee: operand(6),
            this_value: operand(7),
            argument_count: 1,
            arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[operand(8)]),
        }
        .encode(&mut call);
        // Call's layout: header, call feedback slot, dst, callee, this_value, argument_count at 6.
        let mut too_many_arguments = call.clone();
        too_many_arguments[6] = 100;
        assert_eq!(error(&too_many_arguments), DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction);
        assert_eq!(error(&call[..call.len() - 1]), DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction);

        let mut stream = mov.clone();
        stream.extend(&mov[..2]);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_all(&stream, crate::test_zone()).unwrap_err(),
            DecodeError {
                pc: 3,
                kind: DecodeErrorKind::TruncatedInstruction
            }
        );
    }
}
