/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Per-instruction liveness of a frame's registers, locals and arguments.
//!
//! Sets are indexed by `FrameLayout::tracked_index()`. Constants are read-only
//! and never live. The reserved registers (accumulator, exception, this value,
//! return value and saved lexical environment) are always live, since some
//! instructions read or write them implicitly. So are the arguments of a
//! function with a legacy `arguments`, which the code it calls can read.
//!
//! An instruction inside an exception handler range may throw before writing
//! its outputs, so everything live into the handler is live into, and out of,
//! every such instruction.

use super::DecodedInstruction;
use super::FrameLayout;
use super::RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT;
use super::cfg::BasicBlock;
use super::cfg::Cfg;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// The live set after every this many instructions of a block, counted from its end, is kept, and the sets of the
/// instructions in between are computed again from it when asked for.
const CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL: usize = 64;

/// The block of instructions in no block.
const NO_BLOCK: u32 = u32::MAX;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Liveness<'w> {
    transfers: Transfers<'w>,
    /// The block of each instruction, or `NO_BLOCK`.
    block_of_instruction: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// For each instruction, the index into `checkpoints` of the nearest one at or after it in its block, which holds
    /// the instruction index and the slots live out of it.
    checkpoint_of_instruction: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    checkpoints: ZoneVec<'w, (usize, ZoneBitSet<'w>)>,
}

/// What turns the slots live out of an instruction into those live into it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Transfers<'w> {
    always_live: ZoneBitSet<'w>,
    block_live_in: ZoneVec<'w, ZoneBitSet<'w>>,
    /// The exception handler of each block.
    exception_handlers: ZoneVec<'w, Option<usize>>,
    /// The slots each instruction writes and then reads: those of instruction `i` are at
    /// `slots[slot_starts[i].0..slot_starts[i].1]` and `slots[slot_starts[i].1..slot_starts[i + 1].0]`.
    slots: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    slot_starts: ZoneVec<'w, (u32, u32)>,
}

impl<'w> Liveness<'w> {
    /// The liveness of the slots of `instructions`, with its data in `work`.
    pub fn compute(
        instructions: &[DecodedInstruction],
        cfg: &Cfg<'_>,
        layout: &FrameLayout,
        has_legacy_arguments: bool,
        work: &'w Zone,
    ) -> Self {
        let slot_count = layout.tracked_slot_count();
        let mut always_live = ZoneBitSet::new_in(slot_count, work);
        always_live.insert_range(0..(RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT.min(layout.registers_and_locals_count) as usize));
        if has_legacy_arguments {
            always_live.insert_range(layout.registers_and_locals_count as usize..slot_count);
        }

        let mut slots = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut slot_starts = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(instructions.len() + 1, work);
        for instruction in instructions {
            let start = slots.len() as u32;
            for_each_written_slot(instruction, layout, |slot| slots.push(slot as u32));
            let reads_start = slots.len() as u32;
            for_each_read_slot(instruction, layout, |slot| slots.push(slot as u32));
            slot_starts.push((start, reads_start));
        }
        slot_starts.push((slots.len() as u32, slots.len() as u32));

        // Upward exposed uses and definitions of each block.
        let mut block_uses = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(cfg.blocks.len(), work);
        let mut block_definitions = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(cfg.blocks.len(), work);
        for block in &cfg.blocks {
            let mut uses = ZoneBitSet::new_in(slot_count, work);
            let mut definitions = ZoneBitSet::new_in(slot_count, work);
            for index in block.instructions.clone().rev() {
                let (written, read) = instruction_slots(&slots, &slot_starts, index);
                for slot in written {
                    uses.remove(*slot as usize);
                    definitions.insert(*slot as usize);
                }
                for slot in read {
                    uses.insert(*slot as usize);
                }
            }
            block_uses.push(uses);
            block_definitions.push(definitions);
        }

        // Iterate to a fixed point, visiting blocks in post order so that most
        // successors are processed before their predecessors.
        let mut block_live_in = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(always_live.clone(), cfg.blocks.len(), work);
        let post_order = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            cfg.reverse_post_order
                .iter()
                .rev()
                .copied()
                .chain((0..cfg.blocks.len()).filter(|block| cfg.blocks[*block].rpo_number.is_none())),
            work,
        );
        let mut live_in = ZoneBitSet::new_in(slot_count, work);
        let mut changed = true;
        while changed {
            changed = false;
            for &block_index in &post_order {
                let block = &cfg.blocks[block_index];
                block_live_out(block, &block_live_in, &always_live, &mut live_in);
                live_in.subtract(&block_definitions[block_index]);
                live_in.union_with(&block_uses[block_index]);
                if let Some(handler) = block.exception_handler {
                    live_in.union_with(&block_live_in[handler]);
                }
                live_in.union_with(&always_live);
                changed |= block_live_in[block_index].union_with(&live_in);
            }
        }

        // NB: Keeping the sets of every instruction would take memory (and time) quadratic in the size of code that
        //     keeps many slots live over many instructions, like a large array literal of arrays.
        let transfers = Transfers {
            always_live,
            block_live_in,
            exception_handlers: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(cfg.blocks.iter().map(|block| block.exception_handler), work),
            slots,
            slot_starts,
        };
        let mut block_of_instruction = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(NO_BLOCK, instructions.len(), work);
        let mut checkpoint_of_instruction = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, instructions.len(), work);
        let mut checkpoints = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut live = live_in;
        for (block_index, block) in cfg.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            block_live_out(block, &transfers.block_live_in, &transfers.always_live, &mut live);
            for (offset, index) in block.instructions.clone().rev().enumerate() {
                block_of_instruction[index] = block_index as u32;
                if offset % CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL == 0 {
                    checkpoints.push((index, live.clone()));
                }
                checkpoint_of_instruction[index] = (checkpoints.len() - 1) as u32;
                transfers.transfer(index, block_index, &mut live);
            }
        }
        Self {
            transfers,
            block_of_instruction,
            checkpoint_of_instruction,
            checkpoints,
        }
    }

    /// Makes `live` the slots live before the instruction with the given index executes. `live` keeps its memory where
    /// they fit.
    pub fn live_in(&self, instruction_index: usize, live: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>) {
        self.live_out(instruction_index, live);
        let block = self.block_of_instruction[instruction_index];
        if block != NO_BLOCK {
            self.transfers.transfer(instruction_index, block as usize, live);
        }
    }

    /// Makes `live` the slots live after the instruction with the given index executes, including slots live into its
    /// exception handler. `live` keeps its memory where they fit.
    pub fn live_out(&self, instruction_index: usize, live: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>) {
        let block = self.block_of_instruction[instruction_index];
        if block == NO_BLOCK {
            // NB: The set of always live slots has the capacity of every set.
            live.clone_from(&self.transfers.always_live);
            live.clear();
            return;
        }
        let (checkpoint_index, checkpoint) =
            &self.checkpoints[self.checkpoint_of_instruction[instruction_index] as usize];
        live.clone_from(checkpoint);
        if instruction_index < *checkpoint_index {
            for index in (instruction_index + 1..=*checkpoint_index).rev() {
                self.transfers.transfer_slots(index, live);
            }
            self.transfers.add_slots_live_throughout(block as usize, live);
        }
    }
}

impl<'w> Transfers<'w> {
    /// Turns the slots live out of an instruction into those live into it.
    fn transfer(&self, index: usize, block: usize, live: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>) {
        self.transfer_slots(index, live);
        self.add_slots_live_throughout(block, live);
    }

    fn transfer_slots(&self, index: usize, live: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>) {
        let (written, read) = instruction_slots(&self.slots, &self.slot_starts, index);
        for slot in written {
            live.remove(*slot as usize);
        }
        for slot in read {
            live.insert(*slot as usize);
        }
    }

    /// Adds the slots live into and out of every instruction of the block: those always live and those live into its
    /// exception handler. Transfers of several instructions in a row need to add them only once, at the end.
    fn add_slots_live_throughout(&self, block: usize, live: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>) {
        if let Some(handler) = self.exception_handlers[block] {
            live.union_with(&self.block_live_in[handler]);
        }
        live.union_with(&self.always_live);
    }
}

fn instruction_slots<'a>(slots: &'a [u32], slot_starts: &[(u32, u32)], index: usize) -> (&'a [u32], &'a [u32]) {
    let (start, reads_start) = slot_starts[index];
    let end = slot_starts[index + 1].0;
    (
        &slots[start as usize..reads_start as usize],
        &slots[reads_start as usize..end as usize],
    )
}

/// Makes `live_out` the slots live out of `block`.
fn block_live_out<'w>(
    block: &BasicBlock<'_>,
    block_live_in: &[ZoneBitSet<'w>],
    always_live: &ZoneBitSet<'w>,
    live_out: &mut ZoneBitSet<'w>,
) {
    live_out.clone_from(always_live);
    for successor in block.successors.iter().chain(&block.exception_handler) {
        live_out.union_with(&block_live_in[*successor]);
    }
}

fn for_each_read_slot(instruction: &DecodedInstruction, layout: &FrameLayout, mut callback: impl FnMut(usize)) {
    instruction.instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| {
        if role.is_read()
            && let Some(slot) = layout.tracked_index(operand)
        {
            callback(slot);
        }
    });
}

fn for_each_written_slot(instruction: &DecodedInstruction, layout: &FrameLayout, mut callback: impl FnMut(usize)) {
    instruction.instruction.for_each_operand(|operand, role| {
        if role.is_written()
            && let Some(slot) = layout.tracked_index(operand)
        {
            callback(slot);
        }
    });
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::test_support::*;
    use super::*;
    use crate::bytecode::Instruction;
    use crate::bytecode::Operand;

    struct Analysis {
        liveness: Liveness<'static>,
        layout: FrameLayout,
    }

    impl Analysis {
        fn new(program: &Program) -> Self {
            let layout = test_layout();
            let instructions = program.instructions();
            let cfg = program.cfg();
            Self {
                liveness: Liveness::compute(&instructions, &cfg, &layout, false, crate::test_zone()),
                layout,
            }
        }

        /// The live in set of an instruction, without the always live reserved registers.
        fn live_in(&self, index: usize) -> Vec<Operand> {
            let mut live = ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, crate::test_zone());
            self.liveness.live_in(index, &mut live);
            self.operands(&live)
        }

        fn live_out(&self, index: usize) -> Vec<Operand> {
            let mut live = ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, crate::test_zone());
            self.liveness.live_out(index, &mut live);
            self.operands(&live)
        }

        fn operands(&self, set: &ZoneBitSet<'_>) -> Vec<Operand> {
            for reserved in 0..RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT as usize {
                assert!(set.contains(reserved), "reserved register {reserved} is not live");
            }
            set.iter()
                .filter(|slot| *slot >= RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT as usize)
                .map(|slot| self.layout.operand_for_tracked_index(slot))
                .collect()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn straight_line() {
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::Add {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(6),
                    lhs: r(5),
                    rhs: a(0),
                },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(1) },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
            ]
        });
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(0), [a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(0), [r(5), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(1), [r(5), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(1), [r(6)]);
        // The second write of r5 is dead.
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(2), [r(6)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(2), [r(6)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(3), [r(6)]);
        assert!(analysis.live_out(3).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_blocks_match_a_walk_over_every_instruction() {
        // NB: The sets of most instructions of a block this long are computed again from a checkpoint after them.
        let slots = [r(5), r(6), r(7), l(0), l(1)];
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            (0..3 * CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL + 5)
                .map(|index| Instruction::Add {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: slots[index % 5],
                    lhs: slots[(index * 3 + 1) % 5],
                    rhs: if index % 7 == 0 {
                        a(0)
                    } else {
                        slots[(index * 2 + 3) % 5]
                    },
                })
                .chain([Instruction::Return { value: r(5) }])
                .collect()
        });
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        let instructions = program.instructions();
        let mut live = ZoneBitSet::new_in(analysis.layout.tracked_slot_count(), crate::test_zone());
        live.insert_range(0..RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT as usize);
        for index in (0..instructions.len()).rev() {
            assert_eq!(
                analysis.live_out(index),
                analysis.operands(&live),
                "live out of {index}"
            );
            for_each_written_slot(&instructions[index], &analysis.layout, |slot| live.remove(slot));
            for_each_read_slot(&instructions[index], &analysis.layout, |slot| live.insert(slot));
            assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(index), analysis.operands(&live), "live in of {index}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn if_else() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::JumpIf {
                    condition: r(5),
                    true_target: label(1),
                    false_target: label(3),
                },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: r(6) },
                Instruction::Jump { target: label(4) },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: r(7) },
                Instruction::Add {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                    lhs: l(0),
                    rhs: l(1),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(0), [r(5), r(6), r(7), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(0), [r(6), r(7), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(1), [r(6), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(2), [l(0), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(3), [r(7), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(4), [l(0), l(1)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(4), [r(5)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn loop_carried_values_stay_live_around_the_back_edge() {
        let program = assemble(|label| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: c(0) },
                Instruction::JumpLessThan {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    lhs: r(5),
                    rhs: a(0),
                    true_target: label(3),
                    false_target: label(7),
                },
                Instruction::Add {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(6),
                    lhs: l(0),
                    rhs: r(5),
                },
                Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: r(6) },
                Instruction::Increment {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                },
                Instruction::Jump { target: label(2) },
                Instruction::Return { value: l(0) },
            ]
        });
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(0), [a(0)]);
        // At the loop header, the counter, the sum and the bound are live.
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(2), [r(5), l(0), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(2), [r(5), l(0), a(0)]);
        // The temporary r6 only lives between its definition and use.
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(3), [r(5), r(6), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(5), [r(5), l(0), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(6), [r(5), l(0), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(7), [l(0)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn values_used_by_a_catch_handler_are_live_throughout_the_try_block() {
        let program = assemble_with_handlers(
            |_| {
                vec![
                    Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(0) },
                    Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: a(0) },
                    Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(1) },
                    Instruction::Throw { src: r(6) },
                    Instruction::Catch {
                        value_feedback: 0,
                        dst: r(7),
                    },
                    Instruction::Add {
                        arith_feedback: 0,
                        dst: r(7),
                        lhs: r(7),
                        rhs: r(5),
                    },
                    Instruction::Return { value: r(7) },
                ]
            },
            &[(1, 4, 4)],
        );
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        // r5 is live into the handler, so its first value must survive until
        // the second write, and the second until the throw.
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(1), [r(5), a(0)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(1), [r(5), r(6)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(2), [r(5), r(6)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(2), [r(5), r(6)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(3), [r(5)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(4), [r(5)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(5), [r(5), r(7)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inout_operands_are_both_used_and_defined() {
        let program = assemble(|_| {
            vec![
                Instruction::Increment {
                    arith_feedback: 0,
                    dst: r(5),
                },
                Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
            ]
        });
        let analysis = Analysis::new(&program);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_in(0), [r(5)]);
        assert_eq!(analysis.live_out(0), [r(5)]);
    }
}

//! Assembled bytecode: decoding, control flow and liveness.

pub mod cfg;
mod instruction;
pub mod liveness;

pub use instruction::*;

/// Number of reserved registers at the start of every frame: accumulator,
/// exception, this value, return value and saved lexical environment.
pub const RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT: u32 = 5;

/// The reserved register holding the exception a handler receives.
pub const EXCEPTION_REGISTER: u32 = 1;

/// The reserved register holding the frame's `this` value.
pub const THIS_VALUE_REGISTER: u32 = 2;

/// The `yield_continuation` of a frame whose generator completes
/// (`ExecutionContext::NO_YIELD_CONTINUATION`).
pub const NO_YIELD_CONTINUATION: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The `kind` of a `CreateArguments` that creates a mapped arguments object
/// (`ArgumentsKind::Mapped` in `Libraries/LibJS/ABI`).
pub const MAPPED_ARGUMENTS: u8 = 0;

/// The `kind` of a `PutByValue` or `PutById` of a plain assignment
/// (`PutKind::Normal` in `Libraries/LibJS/ABI`).
pub const PUT_KIND_NORMAL: u8 = 0;

/// How an executable's flat slot indices are partitioned. Operands index the
/// frame's value array laid out as `[registers | locals | constants | arguments]`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct FrameLayout {
    pub number_of_registers: u32,
    /// Registers plus locals; also the index of the first constant.
    pub registers_and_locals_count: u32,
    pub number_of_constants: u32,
    /// One past the highest argument index the bytecode references.
    pub number_of_arguments: u32,
}

/// What kind of frame slot an operand refers to, with its index within that kind.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SlotKind {
    Register(u32),
    Local(u32),
    Constant(u32),
    Argument(u32),
}

impl FrameLayout {
    pub fn constants_base(&self) -> u32 {
        self.registers_and_locals_count
    }

    pub fn arguments_base(&self) -> u32 {
        self.registers_and_locals_count + self.number_of_constants
    }

    pub fn slot_kind(&self, operand: Operand) -> SlotKind {
        let index = operand.raw();
        if index < self.number_of_registers {
            SlotKind::Register(index)
        } else if index < self.registers_and_locals_count {
            SlotKind::Local(index - self.number_of_registers)
        } else if index < self.arguments_base() {
            SlotKind::Constant(index - self.constants_base())
        } else {
            SlotKind::Argument(index - self.arguments_base())
        }
    }

    /// Number of slots that can hold mutable state: registers, locals and
    /// arguments. Constants are read-only and are not tracked.
    pub fn tracked_slot_count(&self) -> usize {
        (self.registers_and_locals_count + self.number_of_arguments) as usize
    }

    /// Dense index of a mutable slot (registers and locals first, then
    /// arguments), or `None` for a constant.
    pub fn tracked_index(&self, operand: Operand) -> Option<usize> {
        let index = operand.raw();
        if index < self.registers_and_locals_count {
            return Some(index as usize);
        }
        if index < self.arguments_base() {
            return None;
        }
        let argument = index - self.arguments_base();
        assert!(
            argument < self.number_of_arguments,
            "operand {index} is past the frame's arguments"
        );
        Some((self.registers_and_locals_count + argument) as usize)
    }

    /// Inverse of `tracked_index()`.
    pub fn operand_for_tracked_index(&self, tracked_index: usize) -> Operand {
        let index = u32::try_from(tracked_index).expect("tracked index fits in u32");
        if index < self.registers_and_locals_count {
            return Operand::from_raw(index);
        }
        let argument = index - self.registers_and_locals_count;
        assert!(argument < self.number_of_arguments, "tracked index out of range");
        Operand::from_raw(self.arguments_base() + argument)
    }
}

/// An exception handler range of an executable: an exception thrown by an
/// instruction in `start_offset..end_offset` transfers control to `handler_offset`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ExceptionHandler {
    pub start_offset: u32,
    pub end_offset: u32,
    pub handler_offset: u32,
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod test_support {
    use super::cfg::Cfg;
    use super::*;

    /// Eight registers (five reserved), two locals, two constants and one argument.
    pub fn test_layout() -> FrameLayout {
        FrameLayout {
            number_of_registers: 8,
            registers_and_locals_count: 10,
            number_of_constants: 2,
            number_of_arguments: 1,
        }
    }

    pub fn r(index: u32) -> Operand {
        assert!(index < 8);
        Operand::from_raw(index)
    }

    pub fn l(index: u32) -> Operand {
        assert!(index < 2);
        Operand::from_raw(8 + index)
    }

    pub fn c(index: u32) -> Operand {
        assert!(index < 2);
        Operand::from_raw(10 + index)
    }

    pub fn a(index: u32) -> Operand {
        assert!(index < 1);
        Operand::from_raw(12 + index)
    }

    pub struct Program {
        pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
        /// Byte offset of each instruction.
        pub offsets: Vec<u32>,
        pub handlers: Vec<ExceptionHandler>,
    }

    impl Program {
        pub fn instructions(&self) -> &'static [DecodedInstruction<'static>] {
            decode_all(&self.bytes, crate::test_zone()).unwrap()
        }

        pub fn cfg(&self) -> Cfg<'static> {
            Cfg::new(self.instructions(), &self.handlers, &test_layout(), crate::test_zone()).unwrap()
        }
    }

    /// Encodes the instructions returned by `build`, which receives a function
    /// that turns an instruction index into a label pointing at that instruction.
    pub fn assemble(build: impl Fn(&dyn Fn(usize) -> Label) -> Vec<Instruction<'static>>) -> Program {
        assemble_with_handlers(build, &[])
    }

    /// Like `assemble()`, with exception handlers given as instruction indices
    /// `(start, end, handler)`, where `end` is exclusive.
    pub fn assemble_with_handlers(
        build: impl Fn(&dyn Fn(usize) -> Label) -> Vec<Instruction<'static>>,
        handlers: &[(usize, usize, usize)],
    ) -> Program {
        let mut offsets = Vec::new();
        let mut offset = 0;
        for instruction in build(&|_| Label(0)) {
            offsets.push(offset);
            offset += u32::try_from(instruction.encoded_size()).unwrap();
        }
        offsets.push(offset);

        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        for instruction in build(&|index| Label(offsets[index])) {
            instruction.encode(&mut bytes);
        }
        assert_eq!(bytes.len(), offset as usize);

        let handlers = handlers
            .iter()
            .map(|(start, end, handler)| ExceptionHandler {
                start_offset: offsets[*start],
                end_offset: offsets[*end],
                handler_offset: offsets[*handler],
            })
            .collect();
        offsets.pop();
        Program {
            bytes,
            offsets,
            handlers,
        }
    }
}

//! The output of a compile job: machine code and the metadata the runtime
//! needs to install it and to exit from it into the interpreter.

use core::fmt;

use ak::Column;

use crate::artifact::Artifact;
use crate::artifact::Layout;
use crate::artifact::MAX_WORDS;
use crate::snapshot::CellId;

/// Compiled machine code for one executable, not yet installed. The code and its tables are in memory that comes
/// straight from the system, and that serves the next compile into this, so they are no blocks of the heap.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CompiledCode {
    /// Position independent code, apart from absolute helper addresses,
    /// followed by the constants it loads.
    pub code: Column<u8>,
    /// Where the instructions end and the constants begin.
    pub data_offset: u32,
    /// Offset of the entry point within `code`.
    pub entry_offset: u32,
    /// The offset from the frame pointer of the 32-bit word where the code
    /// keeps the index of a site the runtime reads the values of: that of
    /// an exit or leave, while a slow path in an inlined callee runs in
    /// frames the runtime published, that of their publication, and while a
    /// call in an inlined callee runs in frames the runtime materialized for
    /// it, that of the call.
    pub site_index_frame_offset: i32,
    /// The offset from the frame pointer of the register dump (see
    /// `ValueLocation::Register`) that exits, leaves and publications fill,
    /// which holds the values of a publication while its slow path runs.
    pub register_dump_frame_offset: i32,
    /// The tables of the code (see `artifact()`), which have `layout`.
    pub words: Column<u32>,
    pub layout: Layout,
    /// The debug dumps `CompileOptions` asked for, as UTF-8 text to print (see `dump()`).
    pub(crate) dump: Option<Column<u8>>,
    /// With `CompileOptions::coverage`, what the code contains, one key on each line (see `coverage()`).
    pub(crate) coverage: Option<Column<u8>>,
}

impl Default for CompiledCode {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl CompiledCode {
    /// The most bytes the code of one compile can have. A compile that needs more fails.
    const MAX_CODE_BYTES: usize = 1 << 27;

    /// What a compile writes its code into (see `compile()`). It takes no memory before then.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            code: Column::new(Self::MAX_CODE_BYTES, c"JIT compiled code"),
            data_offset: 0,
            entry_offset: 0,
            site_index_frame_offset: 0,
            register_dump_frame_offset: 0,
            words: Column::new(MAX_WORDS, c"JIT compiled tables"),
            layout: Layout::default(),
            dump: None,
            coverage: None,
        }
    }

    /// The most bytes of text the debug dumps of one compile, or its coverage keys, can have. A dump that does not
    /// fit is cut.
    const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 1 << 30;

    /// Drops the code. This keeps its memory for the next compile.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.code.clear();
        self.words.clear();
        self.layout = Layout::default();
        for text in [&mut self.dump, &mut self.coverage].into_iter().flatten() {
            text.clear();
        }
    }

    /// Makes room for the texts that a compile with these options writes, and drops the others. A column for text
    /// takes no memory before it gets text (see `Column`).
    pub(crate) fn keep_texts(&mut self, dump: bool, coverage: bool) {
        for (text, wanted, name) in [
            (&mut self.dump, dump, c"JIT dump"),
            (&mut self.coverage, coverage, c"JIT coverage keys"),
        ] {
            if !wanted {
                *text = None;
            } else if text.is_none() {
                *text = Some(Column::new(Self::MAX_TEXT_BYTES, name));
            }
        }
    }

    /// The debug dumps `CompileOptions` asked for, as text to print, or `None` if it asked for none.
    pub fn dump(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.dump.as_deref().map(text_of)
    }

    /// With `CompileOptions::coverage`, what the code contains (see `coverage::write_coverage_keys()`).
    pub fn coverage(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        self.coverage.as_deref().map_or("", text_of).lines()
    }

    /// Gives memory back to the system: all that is past the code and its tables, and past the room for
    /// `code_bytes` bytes of code and for `words` words of tables, and all that is past the texts.
    pub fn trim(&mut self, code_bytes: usize, words: usize) {
        self.code.trim(code_bytes);
        self.words.trim(words);
        for text in [&mut self.dump, &mut self.coverage].into_iter().flatten() {
            text.trim(0);
        }
    }

    /// What the runtime reads to install the code, to enter it, and to translate its state into interpreter frames.
    pub fn artifact(&self) -> Artifact<'_> {
        Artifact::new(&self.words, &self.layout)
    }
}

/// The text in the bytes of a column of `CompiledCode`, which a `TextWriter` wrote.
fn text_of(bytes: &[u8]) -> &str {
    core::str::from_utf8(bytes).expect("a text writer writes UTF-8 and cuts it at the boundaries of characters")
}

/// Writes text into a column of `CompiledCode`: a debug dump, or coverage keys. When the column has no room for more,
/// a dump keeps what fits and ends with a line that says so, and a list of keys keeps the keys that fit. Writes fail
/// from then on.
pub(crate) struct TextWriter<'a> {
    column: &'a mut Column<u8>,
    /// Whether the text is a list of lines, of which only whole ones are kept.
    whole_lines: bool,
    full: bool,
}

impl<'a> TextWriter<'a> {
    /// The line that ends a dump that did not fit.
    const CUT: &'static str = "[the dump goes on, but there is no room for more of it]\n";

    /// A writer of a debug dump.
    pub(crate) fn dump(column: &'a mut Column<u8>) -> Self {
        Self {
            column,
            whole_lines: false,
            full: false,
        }
    }

    /// A writer of coverage keys, one on each line.
    pub(crate) fn lines(column: &'a mut Column<u8>) -> Self {
        Self {
            column,
            whole_lines: true,
            full: false,
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Write for TextWriter<'_> {
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> fmt::Result {
        if self.full {
            return Err(fmt::Error);
        }
        // NB: The room for the last line of a dump that does not fit stays free.
        let room = (self.column.limit() - self.column.len()).saturating_sub(Self::CUT.len() + 1);
        if text.len() <= room {
            return self
                .column
                .try_extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes())
                .map_err(|_| fmt::Error);
        }
        self.full = true;
        if self.whole_lines {
            let end = self
                .column
                .iter()
                .rposition(|byte| *byte == b'\n')
                .map_or(0, |index| index + 1);
            self.column.truncate(end);
            return Err(fmt::Error);
        }
        let mut end = room;
        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        let _ = self.column.try_extend_from_slice(&text.as_bytes()[..end]);
        if self.column.last().is_some_and(|byte| *byte != b'\n') {
            let _ = self.column.try_push(b'\n');
        }
        let _ = self.column.try_extend_from_slice(Self::CUT.as_bytes());
        Err(fmt::Error)
    }
}

/// The status word of `JitResult { u64 value; u64 status; }`, returned by
/// compiled code in the second return register.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u64)]
pub enum JitStatus {
    /// `value` is the return value. The frame is still on the interpreter
    /// stack; the caller pops it like the interpreter's `Return` would.
    Returned = 0,
    /// Continue interpreting the running execution context at its
    /// `program_counter`.
    Resume = 1,
    /// An exception propagates out of the executable, as when a slow path
    /// returns a negative control word.
    ExitInterpreter = 2,
}

/// Why compiled code exits to the interpreter. Exit sites are recorded per
/// executable as `(pc, ExitKind)` so the same speculation is never repeated.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum ExitKind {
    /// The bytecode never ran in the interpreter, so it was compiled as an
    /// unconditional exit.
    NoFeedback,
    /// A value speculated to be an object was not one.
    NotObject,
    /// An object did not have one of the shapes its property cache had seen,
    /// or a cached property turned out to be an accessor, or a cached
    /// prototype chain was invalidated.
    BadShape,
    /// A call inlined for the callee its call feedback had seen called
    /// another function.
    BadCallTarget,
    /// A value the compiled code had folded to the constant it held at
    /// compile time (a method on a prototype, the key of a keyed access)
    /// was another value.
    UnexpectedValue,
    /// An instruction whose slow path cannot run from compiled code, or that
    /// was compiled to exit instead of running its slow path, met a case only
    /// its slow path handles (like an append that needs to grow an array, a
    /// probe that cannot tell, or `Math.abs` of a string), so the
    /// interpreter runs it.
    SlowPath,
    /// An `arguments[i]` the compiled code read from the frame's arguments
    /// had an index that is not an int32 within the passed arguments.
    ArgumentsIndex,
    /// A value speculated to be an int32, from the arithmetic feedback of
    /// the instruction using it, was not one.
    NotInt32,
    /// Int32 arithmetic speculated not to overflow, from the instruction's
    /// arithmetic feedback, overflowed or produced -0.
    Overflow,
    /// An object accessed by index did not have the elements kind (packed or
    /// holey array, or typed array of one kind) its keyed feedback had seen.
    BadElements,
    /// An index was out of the bounds of the elements, or hit a hole, or a
    /// keyed store compiled to exit instead of running its slow path met a
    /// case only its slow path handles.
    OutOfBounds,
    /// A value had another type than the instruction's feedback had seen.
    BadType,
    /// A binding or local variable speculated to be initialized was not, so
    /// the interpreter throws its ReferenceError.
    Uninitialized,
    /// A node that may exit, which loop invariant code motion moved out of a
    /// block that not every iteration of its loop runs, exited before the
    /// loop. Exits of this kind are recorded at the loop header, and keep
    /// such nodes in that loop, but not the nodes from blocks every iteration
    /// runs.
    Hoisted,
    /// Something the code depended on stopped holding while it ran other
    /// code (see `Dependency`), so the code was invalidated.
    Invalidated,
    /// Another thread interrupted the VM, so script has to stop, which the
    /// interpreter does at once. Or the stack got so deep that calls leave
    /// compiled code, which is no reason to stop.
    Interrupted,
    /// Code that a call in an inlined function ran read the legacy
    /// `arguments` of the function's frame, among which were objects the
    /// code never allocated: the runtime created them, and the code exited
    /// after the call (see `Op::AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread`). Recorded at
    /// the call, in the executable of the function. Recompiles allocate the
    /// objects among the function's arguments at that call.
    LegacyArgumentsRead,
}

impl ExitKind {
    /// Every kind, each at the index that is its discriminant.
    pub const ALL: [Self; 17] = [
        Self::NoFeedback,
        Self::NotObject,
        Self::BadShape,
        Self::BadCallTarget,
        Self::UnexpectedValue,
        Self::SlowPath,
        Self::ArgumentsIndex,
        Self::NotInt32,
        Self::Overflow,
        Self::BadElements,
        Self::OutOfBounds,
        Self::BadType,
        Self::Uninitialized,
        Self::Hoisted,
        Self::Invalidated,
        Self::Interrupted,
        Self::LegacyArgumentsRead,
    ];
}

const _: () = {
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < ExitKind::ALL.len() {
        assert!(ExitKind::ALL[index] as usize == index);
        index += 1;
    }
};

/// Something compiled code assumes keeps holding, without checking it where
/// it relies on it. The runtime invalidates the code when it stops holding:
/// every `Op::AssumeValid` of the code then exits, and the code is
/// discarded. Each kind stops holding in the runtime event that every fast
/// path breaking it needs first, so fast paths never break it unnoticed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Dependency {
    /// The `WatchpointSet` cell stays valid.
    WatchpointSetValid(CellId),
    /// The global declarative environment `environment` keeps the serial
    /// number `serial`: it gets no bindings, which could shadow properties of
    /// the global object.
    GlobalDeclarations { environment: CellId, serial: u64 },
    /// Binding `index` of the global declarative environment `environment`
    /// is never assigned after its initialization.
    GlobalBindingUnassigned { environment: CellId, index: u32 },
    /// The own property at `offset` of the global object `object`, which
    /// holds the value it got first that is not undefined, is never
    /// assigned and never deleted. The global object shares its shape with
    /// no other object while it is a dictionary, so that nothing but the
    /// runtime writes to the property until it is assigned.
    GlobalPropertyUnassigned { object: CellId, offset: u32 },
    /// No object has the `[[IsHTMLDDA]]` internal slot (`document.all`), so
    /// no object is falsy, loosely equal to null, or of type "undefined".
    NoHtmlDdaObjects,
    /// The shape stays stable: no object leaves it, so objects that have it
    /// keep it while other code runs.
    StableShape(CellId),
}

/// What a site of compiled code is. The runtime translates the state of
/// compiled code at any of them into interpreter frames the same way.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SiteKind {
    /// Compiled code exits to the interpreter, for this reason, which the
    /// executable records so that its recompiles do not repeat what failed.
    Exit(ExitKind),
    /// A slow path did not continue in compiled code: the runtime writes the
    /// frame state into the compiled function's frame and the frames
    /// compiled code pushed for a slow path in an inlined callee, as far as
    /// they are still on the stack. No exit: nothing is recorded, and only
    /// an exception that a handler of an inlined callee caught is counted.
    Leave,
    /// A slow path or call in an inlined callee, which runs in the frames of
    /// the inlined calls with its operands as values: the runtime pushes
    /// those frames with their headers only (Header translation: the
    /// function, `this`, the arguments and the pc), uninitialized, and the
    /// slow path runs in the innermost one. Compiled code pops them again
    /// if the slow path continues in it; otherwise a leave writes them.
    Publish,
    /// A call in an inlined callee that runs without the frames of the
    /// inlined calls it is in (see `Op::CallDirect`), with its values in
    /// stack slots of the JIT frame. Stack walks show those frames from it,
    /// and the call's slow paths materialize them.
    Call,
}

/// What kind of object the runtime creates for one that compiled code never allocated (see
/// `artifact::ObjectView`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VirtualObjectDescriptorKind {
    /// A plain object of `shape`, with the values of its properties in
    /// offset order.
    Object { shape: CellId },
    /// A closure like the sample of a closure template in `sample_slot` (see
    /// `ClosureTemplateSnapshot::sample_slot`), with the lexical and private
    /// environments at the two locations, which are `Repr::Pointer`, the
    /// latter null for none.
    Closure { sample_slot: CellId },
}

/// Set in the return pc (`ExecutionContext::caller_return_pc`) of the frame of
/// a callee that a call in an inlined callee made without the frames of the
/// inlined calls it is in (see `SiteKind::Call`): the other bits are the
/// index of the call's site in the code of the caller frame, which runs the
/// compiled function. The frame's destination
/// (`ExecutionContext::caller_dst_raw`) is then the low half of the JIT
/// frame's frame pointer, from which the site's stack slots are, while the
/// call runs.
pub const INLINED_CALL_SITE_BIT: u32 = 1 << 31;

/// Where the interpreter resumes a frame after an exit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ResumeMode {
    /// Eager exit: rerun the bytecode at `pc` from its pre-state.
    ResumeAt,
    /// Lazy exit after a call: continue after the bytecode at `pc`, with the
    /// call's result stored in the slot `dst`.
    ResumeAfter { dst: u32 },
}

/// The slot among the values of a frame (see `artifact::FrameView::values()`) that holds the function object of a frame
/// of an inlined closure, whose frames run the closure that was called
/// rather than the function object of the snapshot. It is in no frame slot.
pub const CALLEE_SLOT: u32 = u32::MAX - 1;

/// Where an exit finds a value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ValueLocation {
    /// A machine register, as saved in the exit's register dump.
    Register(u8, Repr),
    /// A stack slot at the given offset from the JIT frame.
    Stack(i32, Repr),
    /// A slot of the compiled function's frame (an operand) that holds the value wherever compiled code runs, which
    /// is tagged: one of its arguments or its `this` value register that nothing writes.
    Frame(u32),
    /// A NaN-boxed constant, or for the environments of a closure the code never created (see
    /// `VirtualObjectDescriptorKind::Closure`), the address of a cell the code embeds, or null.
    Constant(u64),
    /// The frame's arguments object, which the compiled code never created:
    /// the runtime creates it from the frame's arguments like
    /// `CreateArguments` does, mapped or unmapped, once per exit.
    ArgumentsObject { mapped: bool },
    /// The object at this index among those of the site (see `artifact::SiteView::object()`).
    VirtualObject(u32),
}

/// How a value is represented in a register or stack slot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Repr {
    /// A NaN-boxed JS value.
    Tagged,
    Int32,
    Float64,
    Bool,
    /// The address of a GC cell. In frame states, only as an environment of a
    /// closure the code never allocated (see `VirtualObjectDescriptorKind`).
    Pointer,
}

impl Repr {
    /// Every representation, each at the index that is its discriminant.
    pub const ALL: [Self; 5] = [Self::Tagged, Self::Int32, Self::Float64, Self::Bool, Self::Pointer];
}

const _: () = {
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < Repr::ALL.len() {
        assert!(Repr::ALL[index] as usize == index);
        index += 1;
    }
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::fmt::Write;

    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn a_dump_that_does_not_fit_is_cut_with_a_last_line_that_says_so() {
        let mut column = Column::new(100, c"test");
        let mut writer = TextWriter::dump(&mut column);
        assert!(write!(writer, "b0:\n").is_ok());
        assert!(write!(writer, "{}", "ä".repeat(100)).is_err());
        assert!(write!(writer, "more").is_err());
        let text = text_of(&column);
        assert!(text.len() <= 100);
        assert!(text.starts_with("b0:\nää"), "{text}");
        assert!(text.ends_with(&format!("ä\n{}", TextWriter::CUT)), "{text}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn coverage_keys_that_do_not_fit_are_left_out() {
        let mut column = Column::new(100, c"test");
        let mut writer = TextWriter::lines(&mut column);
        assert!(writeln!(writer, "Phi").is_ok());
        assert!(writeln!(writer, "Return").is_ok());
        assert!(write!(writer, "Exit.").is_ok());
        assert!(writeln!(writer, "{}", "x".repeat(100)).is_err());
        assert!(writeln!(writer, "Jump").is_err());
        assert_eq!(text_of(&column), "Phi\nReturn\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn texts_are_kept_only_for_the_options_that_ask_for_them() {
        let mut compiled = CompiledCode::new();
        assert_eq!(compiled.dump(), None);
        compiled.keep_texts(true, true);
        let _ = write!(TextWriter::dump(compiled.dump.as_mut().unwrap()), "dump");
        let _ = write!(TextWriter::lines(compiled.coverage.as_mut().unwrap()), "Phi\nJump\n");
        assert_eq!(compiled.dump(), Some("dump"));
        assert_eq!(compiled.coverage().collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["Phi", "Jump"]);
        compiled.clear();
        assert_eq!(compiled.dump(), Some(""));
        assert_eq!(compiled.coverage().count(), 0);
        compiled.keep_texts(false, false);
        assert_eq!(compiled.dump(), None);
        assert!(compiled.coverage.is_none());
    }
}
