//! Lowering of element accesses: checks of the elements kind, bounds and
//! holes, and loads and stores of elements.

use super::Codegen;
use super::InputValue;
use crate::asm::Address;
use crate::asm::Condition;
use crate::asm::Gpr;
use crate::asm::Label;
use crate::asm::PortableMacroAssembler;
use crate::asm::Scale;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::TypedArrayElement;
use crate::ir::value;

pub(super) fn scale(element: TypedArrayElement) -> Scale {
    match element {
        TypedArrayElement::Uint8 | TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped | TypedArrayElement::Int8 => Scale::One,
        TypedArrayElement::Uint16 | TypedArrayElement::Int16 => Scale::Two,
        TypedArrayElement::Int32 | TypedArrayElement::Uint32 | TypedArrayElement::Float32 => Scale::Four,
        TypedArrayElement::Float64 => Scale::Eight,
    }
}

impl<M: PortableMacroAssembler> Codegen<'_, '_, M> {
    /// The `TypedArrayBase::Kind` value of `element`.
    pub(super) fn typed_array_kind_value(&self, element: TypedArrayElement) -> u8 {
        let layout = &self.runtime.layout;
        match element {
            TypedArrayElement::Uint8 => layout.typed_array_kind_uint8,
            TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped => layout.typed_array_kind_uint8_clamped,
            TypedArrayElement::Int8 => layout.typed_array_kind_int8,
            TypedArrayElement::Uint16 => layout.typed_array_kind_uint16,
            TypedArrayElement::Int16 => layout.typed_array_kind_int16,
            TypedArrayElement::Int32 => layout.typed_array_kind_int32,
            TypedArrayElement::Uint32 => layout.typed_array_kind_uint32,
            TypedArrayElement::Float32 => layout.typed_array_kind_float32,
            TypedArrayElement::Float64 => layout.typed_array_kind_float64,
        }
    }

    /// Continues where `value` is a typed array, of any kind, with its
    /// address in `object`, and branches to `fail` otherwise.
    fn branch_unless_typed_array(&mut self, value: Gpr, object: Gpr, fail: Label) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::NotEqual, value, value::OBJECT_TAG, scratch, fail);
        self.emit_unbox_cell(object, value);
        self.masm
            .load16(scratch, &Address::new(object, self.runtime.offsets.object_flags as i32));
        self.masm.branch_test32(
            Condition::Zero,
            scratch,
            u32::from(self.runtime.layout.object_flag_is_typed_array),
            fail,
        );
    }

    /// Continues where `value` is an object whose elements are of `kind`,
    /// with its address in `object`, and branches to `fail` otherwise.
    fn branch_unless_elements_kind(&mut self, value: Gpr, object: Gpr, kind: ElementsKind, fail: Label) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        if let ElementsKind::TypedArray(element) = kind {
            self.branch_unless_typed_array(value, object, fail);
            self.masm
                .load8(scratch, &Address::new(object, layout.typed_array_kind as i32));
            let kind_value = self.typed_array_kind_value(element);
            self.masm
                .branch32_imm(Condition::NotEqual, scratch, i32::from(kind_value), fail);
            return;
        }
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::NotEqual, value, value::OBJECT_TAG, scratch, fail);
        self.emit_unbox_cell(object, value);
        self.masm
            .load16(scratch, &Address::new(object, self.runtime.offsets.object_flags as i32));
        self.masm.branch_test32(
            Condition::NonZero,
            scratch,
            u32::from(layout.object_flag_is_typed_array | layout.object_flag_may_interfere),
            fail,
        );
        self.masm.load8(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(object, layout.object_indexed_storage_kind as i32),
        );
        let packed = i32::from(layout.indexed_storage_kind_packed);
        if kind == ElementsKind::Packed {
            self.masm.branch32_imm(Condition::NotEqual, scratch, packed, fail);
        } else {
            let ok = self.masm.new_label();
            self.masm.branch32_imm(Condition::Equal, scratch, packed, ok);
            self.masm.branch32_imm(
                Condition::NotEqual,
                scratch,
                i32::from(layout.indexed_storage_kind_holey),
                fail,
            );
            self.masm.bind(ok);
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn emit_check_elements(&mut self, node: NodeId, kind: ElementsKind) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        let (value, object) = (self.input(node, 0), self.temp(node, 0));
        self.branch_unless_elements_kind(value, object, kind, exit);
    }

    /// A `CheckTypedArray` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_check_typed_array(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        let (value, object) = (self.input(node, 0), self.temp(node, 0));
        self.branch_unless_typed_array(value, object, exit);
    }

    /// A `CheckArray` node. The magical length flag is set when an array is
    /// created and never changes, regardless of its elements storage kind.
    pub(super) fn emit_check_array(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        let (value, object) = (self.input(node, 0), self.temp(node, 0));
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::NotEqual, value, value::OBJECT_TAG, scratch, exit);
        self.emit_unbox_cell(object, value);
        self.masm
            .load16(scratch, &Address::new(object, self.runtime.offsets.object_flags as i32));
        self.masm.branch_test32(
            Condition::Zero,
            scratch,
            u32::from(self.runtime.layout.object_flag_has_magical_length),
            exit,
        );
    }

    /// A branch on `BranchCondition::ElementsKind`: to `target` where it
    /// holds, or where it does not, with `invert`.
    pub(super) fn emit_branch_on_elements_kind(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        kind: ElementsKind,
        target: Label,
        invert: bool,
    ) {
        let (value, object) = (self.input(node, 0), self.temp(node, 0));
        if invert {
            self.branch_unless_elements_kind(value, object, kind, target);
            return;
        }
        let other = self.masm.new_label();
        self.branch_unless_elements_kind(value, object, kind, other);
        self.masm.jump(target);
        self.masm.bind(other);
    }

    /// A `LoadTypedArrayLength` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_load_typed_array_length(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (object, output) = (self.input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let done = self.masm.new_label();
        self.masm.move_imm32(output, 0);
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(object, layout.typed_array_cached_data_offset as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch64_imm(
            Condition::Equal,
            scratch,
            layout.typed_array_cached_data_offset_invalid as i64,
            done,
        );
        self.masm
            .load64(output, &Address::new(object, layout.typed_array_array_length as i32));
        // NB: A length that does not fit in 32 bits counts as 0, which sends every access to the slow path.
        self.masm
            .branch_test64(Condition::Zero, output, !u64::from(u32::MAX), done);
        self.masm.move_imm32(output, 0);
        self.masm.bind(done);
    }

    /// A `CheckBounds` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_check_bounds(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        match (self.input_value(node, 0), self.input_value(node, 1)) {
            (InputValue::Register(index), InputValue::Register(count)) => {
                self.masm.branch32(Condition::AboveOrEqual, index, count, exit);
            }
            (InputValue::Register(index), InputValue::Constant(count)) => {
                self.masm
                    .branch32_imm(Condition::AboveOrEqual, index, count as i32, exit);
            }
            (InputValue::Constant(index), InputValue::Register(count)) => {
                self.masm
                    .branch32_imm(Condition::BelowOrEqual, count, index as i32, exit);
            }
            (InputValue::Constant(index), InputValue::Constant(count)) => {
                let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
                self.masm.move_imm32(scratch, index as u32);
                self.masm
                    .branch32_imm(Condition::AboveOrEqual, scratch, count as i32, exit);
            }
        }
    }

    /// A `CheckNotHole` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_check_not_hole(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        let value = self.input(node, 0);
        self.masm
            .branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, value, value::EMPTY as i64, exit);
    }

    /// The address of the element a load or store accesses. Uses `temp`
    /// and the scratch register, folding constant indices into offsets.
    fn element_address(&mut self, node: NodeId, temp: Gpr, kind: ElementsKind) -> Address {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let storage = self.input(node, 0);
        let index = self.input_value(node, 1);
        match kind {
            ElementsKind::Packed | ElementsKind::Holey => {
                self.masm
                    .load64(temp, &Address::new(storage, layout.object_indexed_elements as i32));
                match index {
                    InputValue::Register(index) => {
                        self.masm.move32(scratch, index);
                        Address::indexed(temp, scratch, Scale::Eight, 0)
                    }
                    InputValue::Constant(index) => {
                        let offset = u64::from(index as u32) << Scale::Eight.log2();
                        if let Ok(offset) = i32::try_from(offset) {
                            Address::new(temp, offset)
                        } else {
                            self.masm.add64_imm(temp, temp, offset as i64);
                            Address::new(temp, 0)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            // NB: The storage is a `TypedArrayDataAddress`, from which the
            //     zero-extended index stays within the cage or its guard.
            ElementsKind::TypedArray(element) => {
                match index {
                    // NB: Stores use the scratch register for their values.
                    InputValue::Register(index) => {
                        self.masm.move32(temp, index);
                        Address::indexed(storage, temp, scale(element), 0)
                    }
                    InputValue::Constant(index) => {
                        let offset = u64::from(index as u32) << scale(element).log2();
                        if let Ok(offset) = i32::try_from(offset) {
                            Address::new(storage, offset)
                        } else {
                            self.masm.add64_imm(temp, storage, offset as i64);
                            Address::new(temp, 0)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// A `LoadElementAt` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_load_element_at(&mut self, node: NodeId, kind: ElementsKind) {
        let temp = self.temp(node, 0);
        let address = self.element_address(node, temp, kind);
        let ElementsKind::TypedArray(element) = kind else {
            let output = self.output(node);
            self.masm.load64(output, &address);
            return;
        };
        if kind.loaded_repr() == Repr::Float64 {
            let output = self.float_output(node);
            match element {
                TypedArrayElement::Uint32 => {
                    self.masm.load32(temp, &address);
                    self.masm.convert_int64_to_double(output, temp);
                }
                TypedArrayElement::Float32 => self.masm.load_float_as_double(output, &address),
                _ => self.masm.load_double(output, &address),
            }
            return;
        }
        let output = self.output(node);
        match element {
            TypedArrayElement::Uint8 | TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped => self.masm.load8(output, &address),
            TypedArrayElement::Int8 => self.masm.load8_sign_extend(output, &address),
            TypedArrayElement::Uint16 => self.masm.load16(output, &address),
            TypedArrayElement::Int16 => self.masm.load16_sign_extend(output, &address),
            _ => self.masm.load32(output, &address),
        }
    }

    /// A `StoreElementAt` node.
    pub(super) fn emit_store_element_at(&mut self, node: NodeId, kind: ElementsKind) {
        let temp = self.temp(node, 0);
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let address = self.element_address(node, temp, kind);
        if kind.stored_repr() == Repr::Float64 {
            let source = self.float_input(node, 2);
            if kind == ElementsKind::TypedArray(TypedArrayElement::Float32) {
                self.masm.store_double_as_float(&address, source);
            } else {
                self.masm.store_double(&address, source);
            }
            return;
        }
        if let InputValue::Constant(bits) = self.input_value(node, 2) {
            let ElementsKind::TypedArray(element) = kind else {
                self.masm.store_imm64(&address, bits);
                return;
            };
            let integer = (bits as u32).cast_signed();
            match element {
                TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped => self.masm.store_imm8(&address, integer.clamp(0, 255) as u8),
                TypedArrayElement::Uint8 | TypedArrayElement::Int8 => self.masm.store_imm8(&address, integer as u8),
                TypedArrayElement::Uint16 | TypedArrayElement::Int16 => {
                    self.masm.store_imm16(&address, integer as u16);
                }
                _ => self.masm.store_imm32(&address, integer.cast_unsigned()),
            }
            return;
        }
        let source = self.input(node, 2);
        let ElementsKind::TypedArray(element) = kind else {
            self.masm.store64(&address, source);
            return;
        };
        match element {
            TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped => {
                let (clamp_low, clamp_high, store) =
                    (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
                self.masm.move32(scratch, source);
                self.masm.branch32_imm(Condition::LessThan, scratch, 0, clamp_low);
                self.masm.branch32_imm(Condition::GreaterThan, scratch, 255, clamp_high);
                self.masm.jump(store);
                self.masm.bind(clamp_low);
                self.masm.move_imm32(scratch, 0);
                self.masm.jump(store);
                self.masm.bind(clamp_high);
                self.masm.move_imm32(scratch, 255);
                self.masm.bind(store);
                self.masm.store8(&address, scratch);
            }
            TypedArrayElement::Uint8 | TypedArrayElement::Int8 => self.masm.store8(&address, source),
            TypedArrayElement::Uint16 | TypedArrayElement::Int16 => self.masm.store16(&address, source),
            _ => self.masm.store32(&address, source),
        }
    }
}

//! The entry trampoline: how native code enters JIT code.
//!
//! JIT code expects the VM in its pinned register when it is entered, and
//! neither keeps nor restores the pinned VM and scratch registers, which JIT
//! code that calls other JIT code needs to set up or keep for nothing. Native
//! code enters JIT code through the trampoline instead, which saves those
//! registers like the platform ABI wants, loads the VM, and calls the entry:
//! `JitResult trampoline(VM*, ExecutionContext* frame, entry)`, whose result
//! is the entry's.

use ak::Column;
use ak::Zone;

use super::STUB_CODE_LIMIT;
use super::STUB_ZONE_LIMIT;
use super::target_registers;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::asm::FprSet;
use crate::asm::GprSet;
use crate::asm::PortableMacroAssembler;

/// Generates the entry trampoline.
pub fn generate_entry_trampoline<M: PortableMacroAssembler>() -> Result<Column<u8>, CompileFailure> {
    let (_, pinned) = target_registers::<M>();
    let arguments = M::ARGUMENT_GPRS;
    let frame = M::frame(GprSet::EMPTY.with(pinned.vm).with(pinned.scratch), FprSet::EMPTY, 0);
    let work = Zone::new(STUB_ZONE_LIMIT, c"JIT entry trampoline");
    let mut code = Column::new(STUB_CODE_LIMIT, c"JIT entry trampoline code");
    let mut masm = M::new(&mut code, &work);
    masm.emit_prologue(&frame);
    masm.move64(pinned.vm, arguments[0]);
    masm.call_register(arguments[2]);
    masm.emit_epilogue(&frame);
    masm.ret();
    masm.finish().map_err(super::assembly_failure)?;
    Ok(code)
}

//! The probes of global variable caches, like the interpreter's
//! `GetGlobal` / `SetGlobal` handlers, the mutability test of bindings that
//! `BranchCondition::BindingMutable` shares with them, and the bindings
//! that environments of a shape get next, like its `CreateVariable`
//! handler.

use super::Codegen;
use super::checked_i32;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::asm::Address;
use crate::asm::Condition;
use crate::asm::Gpr;
use crate::asm::Label;
use crate::asm::PortableMacroAssembler;
use crate::asm::Scale;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::value;

impl<M: PortableMacroAssembler> Codegen<'_, '_, M> {
    /// Branches to `fail` unless binding `index` (a register) of the
    /// declarative environment `environment` is mutable, like the
    /// interpreter's `load_binding_flag`. Clobbers `temp` and the scratch
    /// register.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn branch_unless_binding_mutable(
        &mut self,
        environment: Gpr,
        index: Gpr,
        temp: Gpr,
        fail: Label,
    ) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let (rare_at_index, rare_at_offset, check) =
            (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        let rare_flags = |codegen: &mut Self| {
            codegen.emit_load_compressed_cell(
                scratch,
                &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_rare_data as i32),
            );
            codegen
                .masm
                .load64(scratch, &Address::new(scratch, layout.rare_data_binding_flags as i32));
        };

        self.emit_load_compressed_cell_or_branch(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_shape as i32),
            rare_at_index,
        );
        // Flags past the shape's are in the rare data, after the shape's.
        self.masm.load32(
            temp,
            &Address::new(scratch, layout.environment_shape_binding_flags_size as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch64(Condition::BelowOrEqual, temp, index, rare_at_offset);
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(scratch, layout.environment_shape_binding_flags as i32),
        );
        self.masm
            .load8(scratch, &Address::indexed(scratch, index, Scale::One, 0));
        self.masm.jump(check);

        self.masm.bind(rare_at_offset);
        self.masm.sub64(temp, index, temp);
        rare_flags(self);
        self.masm
            .load8(scratch, &Address::indexed(scratch, temp, Scale::One, 0));
        self.masm.jump(check);

        self.masm.bind(rare_at_index);
        rare_flags(self);
        self.masm
            .load8(scratch, &Address::indexed(scratch, index, Scale::One, 0));

        self.masm.bind(check);
        self.masm
            .branch_test32(Condition::Zero, scratch, u32::from(layout.binding_flag_mutable), fail);
    }

    /// Branches to `fail` unless the binding the shape of the environment
    /// `environment` has next is the binding `name` with `flags`, which
    /// `emit_append_environment_binding()` can append (see
    /// `BranchCondition::NextBindingOfShape`). Clobbers the temps of `node`
    /// and the scratch register.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_next_binding_of_shape_test(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        environment: Gpr,
        name: u64,
        flags: u8,
        fail: Label,
    ) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let (shape, index) = (self.temp(node, 0), self.temp(node, 1));

        // Only declarative environments have shapes, and module environments
        // find bindings their shapes do not have.
        self.masm.load8(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.environment_declarative as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch_test32(Condition::Zero, scratch, 0xFF, fail);
        self.emit_load_class(scratch, environment);
        self.masm.move_imm64(shape, layout.module_environment_class);
        self.masm.branch64(Condition::Equal, scratch, shape, fail);

        self.emit_load_compressed_cell_or_branch(
            shape,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_shape as i32),
            fail,
        );
        self.masm.load8(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(shape, layout.environment_shape_has_unique_binding_names as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch_test32(Condition::Zero, scratch, 0xFF, fail);
        self.masm.load32(
            index,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_binding_values_size as i32),
        );
        self.masm.load32(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(shape, layout.environment_shape_binding_flags_size as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch64(Condition::BelowOrEqual, scratch, index, fail);
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(shape, layout.environment_shape_binding_flags as i32),
        );
        self.masm
            .load8(scratch, &Address::indexed(scratch, index, Scale::One, 0));
        self.masm
            .branch32_imm(Condition::NotEqual, scratch, i32::from(flags), fail);
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(shape, layout.environment_shape_binding_names as i32),
        );
        self.masm
            .load64(scratch, &Address::indexed(scratch, index, Scale::Eight, 0));
        self.masm.move_imm64(shape, name);
        self.masm.branch64(Condition::NotEqual, scratch, shape, fail);

        // Values that do not fit in their storage move first. Outside of the cell, they have their capacity in front of
        // the first value, if there is any storage.
        let have_capacity = self.masm.new_label();
        self.masm.load8(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(
                environment,
                layout.declarative_environment_inline_binding_capacity as i32,
            ),
        );
        self.masm
            .branch_test32(Condition::NonZero, scratch, 0xFF, have_capacity);
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_binding_values as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, scratch, 0, fail);
        self.masm.load64(scratch, &Address::new(scratch, -8));
        self.masm.bind(have_capacity);
        self.masm.branch64(Condition::BelowOrEqual, scratch, index, fail);
    }

    /// An `AppendEnvironmentBinding` node of the declarative environment
    /// `environment`: an uninitialized binding after the others.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_append_environment_binding(&mut self, node: NodeId, environment: Gpr) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let index = self.temp(node, 0);
        self.masm.load32(
            index,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_binding_values_size as i32),
        );
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_binding_values as i32),
        );
        self.masm
            .store_imm64(&Address::indexed(scratch, index, Scale::Eight, 0), value::EMPTY);
        self.masm.add64_imm(index, index, 1);
        self.masm.store32(
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_binding_values_size as i32),
            index,
        );
    }

    /// The common start of GetGlobal and SetGlobal, with the realm and the
    /// executable in the inputs after `context`: loads the global variable
    /// cache, the realm's global declarative environment and its global
    /// object, and checks the cache's environment serial number.
    /// Continues with the global object's named property at `property`, or
    /// branches to `environment_binding` if the cache entry does not match
    /// the global object's shape.
    fn emit_global_variable_prologue(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        context: usize,
        cache_index: u32,
        environment_binding: Label,
        slow: Label,
    ) -> Result<GlobalRegisters, CompileFailure> {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let registers = GlobalRegisters {
            cache: self.temp(node, 0),
            environment: self.temp(node, 1),
            object: self.temp(node, 2),
            temp: self.temp(node, 3),
        };
        let GlobalRegisters {
            cache,
            environment,
            object,
            temp,
        } = registers;

        let (realm, executable) = (self.input(node, context), self.input(node, context + 1));
        self.masm
            .load64(object, &Address::new(realm, layout.realm_global_object as i32));
        self.masm.load64(
            environment,
            &Address::new(realm, layout.realm_global_declarative_environment as i32),
        );
        self.masm.load64(
            cache,
            &Address::new(executable, layout.executable_global_variable_caches as i32),
        );
        let cache_offset = u64::from(cache_index) * u64::from(layout.global_variable_cache_size);
        self.masm.add64_imm(cache, cache, i64::from(checked_i32(cache_offset)?));

        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(environment, layout.declarative_environment_serial as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch64_memory(
            Condition::NotEqual,
            &Address::new(cache, layout.global_variable_cache_environment_serial as i32),
            scratch,
            slow,
        );

        self.emit_load_compressed_cell(scratch, &Address::new(object, self.runtime.offsets.object_shape as i32));
        self.masm.branch64_memory(
            Condition::NotEqual,
            &Address::new(cache, layout.global_variable_cache_shape as i32),
            scratch,
            environment_binding,
        );
        let expected = Address::new(cache, layout.global_variable_cache_dictionary_generation as i32);
        self.branch_unless_dictionary_generation_is(scratch, expected, [temp, scratch], environment_binding);
        Ok(registers)
    }

    /// The address of the global object's named property the cache is for.
    /// Clobbers `temp` and the scratch register.
    fn global_property_address(&mut self, registers: &GlobalRegisters) -> Address {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        self.masm.load32(
            registers.temp,
            &Address::new(registers.cache, layout.global_variable_cache_property_offset as i32),
        );
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(registers.object, self.runtime.offsets.object_named_properties as i32),
        );
        Address::indexed(scratch, registers.temp, Scale::Eight, 0)
    }

    /// Puts the index of the global declarative environment binding the
    /// cache is for in `temp`, or branches to `slow` if it is for none.
    fn load_global_binding_index(&mut self, registers: &GlobalRegisters, slow: Label) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        self.masm.load8(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(
                registers.cache,
                layout.global_variable_cache_has_environment_binding as i32,
            ),
        );
        self.masm.branch_test32(Condition::Zero, scratch, 0xFF, slow);
        self.masm.load32(
            registers.temp,
            &Address::new(
                registers.cache,
                layout.global_variable_cache_environment_binding_index as i32,
            ),
        );
    }

    /// The address of the global declarative environment binding whose
    /// index is in `temp`. Clobbers the scratch register.
    fn global_binding_address(&mut self, registers: &GlobalRegisters) -> Address {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        self.masm.load64(
            scratch,
            &Address::new(
                registers.environment,
                layout.declarative_environment_binding_values as i32,
            ),
        );
        Address::indexed(scratch, registers.temp, Scale::Eight, 0)
    }

    /// A `ProbeGlobalCache` node.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_probe_global_cache(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        cache_index: u32,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let output = self.output(node);
        let (failure, done) = (self.probe_failure_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        let slow = failure.0;
        let environment_binding = self.masm.new_label();
        let registers = self.emit_global_variable_prologue(node, 0, cache_index, environment_binding, slow)?;
        let (object, temp) = (registers.object, registers.temp);

        let property = self.global_property_address(&registers);
        self.masm.load64(object, &property);
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::Equal, object, value::ACCESSOR_TAG, temp, slow);
        self.masm.move64(output, object);
        self.masm.jump(done);

        self.masm.bind(environment_binding);
        self.load_global_binding_index(&registers, slow);
        let binding = self.global_binding_address(&registers);
        self.masm.load64(object, &binding);
        self.masm
            .branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, object, value::EMPTY as i64, slow);
        self.masm.move64(output, object);
        self.bind_probe_failure(output, value::EMPTY, failure, done);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A `ProbeGlobalStore` node.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_probe_global_store(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        cache_index: u32,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let (source, output) = (self.input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        let layout = self.runtime.layout;
        let (failure, stored, done) = (self.probe_failure_label(), self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        let slow = failure.0;
        let environment_binding = self.masm.new_label();
        let registers = self.emit_global_variable_prologue(node, 1, cache_index, environment_binding, slow)?;
        let (cache, environment, object, temp) =
            (registers.cache, registers.environment, registers.object, registers.temp);

        let property = self.global_property_address(&registers);
        // NB: The address uses `temp` and the scratch register; `object` is free.
        self.masm.load64(object, &property);
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::Equal, object, value::ACCESSOR_TAG, object, slow);
        self.masm.load8(
            object,
            &Address::new(cache, layout.global_variable_cache_writes_data_property as i32),
        );
        self.masm.branch_test32(Condition::Zero, object, 0xFF, slow);
        self.masm.store64(&property, source);
        self.masm.jump(stored);

        self.masm.bind(environment_binding);
        self.load_global_binding_index(&registers, slow);
        self.branch_unless_binding_mutable(environment, temp, object, slow);
        let binding = self.global_binding_address(&registers);
        self.masm.load64(object, &binding);
        self.masm
            .branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, object, value::EMPTY as i64, slow);
        self.masm.store64(&binding, source);
        self.masm.bind(stored);
        self.masm.move_imm32(output, 1);
        self.bind_probe_failure(output, 0, failure, done);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The registers of the global variable fast paths.
struct GlobalRegisters {
    cache: Gpr,
    environment: Gpr,
    object: Gpr,
    temp: Gpr,
}

//! Lowering of number ops: unboxing and boxing of numbers, double
//! arithmetic and comparisons, conversions, and `Math` functions of
//! doubles. `Repr::Float64` values are in floating point registers.

use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::asm::Condition;
use crate::asm::DoubleCondition;
use crate::asm::Gpr;
use crate::asm::Label;
use crate::asm::PortableMacroAssembler;
use crate::codegen::Codegen;
use crate::codegen::InputValue;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::Float64Function;
use crate::ir::Float64UnaryOp;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::value;

const SIGN_BIT: u64 = 1 << 63;

impl<M: PortableMacroAssembler> Codegen<'_, '_, M> {
    /// `UnboxDouble`: the double of a tagged double, its bits.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_unbox_double(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (input, output) = (self.input(node, 0), self.float_output(node));
        self.masm.move_gpr_to_double(output, input);
    }

    /// `CheckNumber`: the double of a tagged number, which exits for other
    /// values.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_check_number(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let exit = self.exit_site(node);
        let (input, output, scratch) = (self.input(node, 0), self.float_output(node), self.pinned.scratch);
        let (int32, double, done) = (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        self.branch_on_tag(Condition::Equal, input, value::INT32_TAG, scratch, int32);
        // NB: The double test of emit_double_test(), on the tag branch_on_tag() left in the scratch register.
        self.masm
            .branch32_imm(Condition::Equal, scratch, i32::from(value::BASE_TAG), double);
        self.masm.and32_imm(scratch, scratch, u32::from(value::BASE_TAG));
        self.masm
            .branch32_imm(Condition::Equal, scratch, i32::from(value::BASE_TAG), exit);
        self.masm.bind(double);
        self.masm.move_gpr_to_double(output, input);
        self.masm.jump(done);
        self.masm.bind(int32);
        self.masm.convert_int32_to_double(output, input);
        self.masm.bind(done);
    }

    /// Jumps to `yes` if the tagged `value` is a double, and to `no`
    /// otherwise.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_double_test(&mut self, value: Gpr, yes: Label, no: Label) {
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        self.masm.shr64_imm(scratch, value, value::TAG_SHIFT);
        // NB: Canonical NaN has the tag bits other values have set.
        self.masm
            .branch32_imm(Condition::Equal, scratch, i32::from(value::BASE_TAG), yes);
        self.masm.and32_imm(scratch, scratch, u32::from(value::BASE_TAG));
        self.masm
            .branch32_imm(Condition::NotEqual, scratch, i32::from(value::BASE_TAG), yes);
        self.masm.jump(no);
    }

    /// `BoxFloat64`: the tagged number of a double.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_box_float64(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (input, output) = (self.float_input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        self.box_number(output, input);
    }

    /// `Float64Unary`: `op` of a double. Floor and ceil are machine
    /// instructions. Round rounds up from the floor for fractions of at
    /// least a half, and a zero result of it has the sign of the input,
    /// which makes -0 where `Math` does.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_float64_unary(&mut self, node: NodeId, op: Float64UnaryOp) {
        let (input, output) = (self.float_input(node, 0), self.float_output(node));
        match op {
            Float64UnaryOp::Abs => self.masm.abs_double(output, input),
            Float64UnaryOp::Negate => self.masm.neg_double(output, input),
            Float64UnaryOp::Sqrt => self.masm.sqrt_double(output, input),
            Float64UnaryOp::Floor => self.masm.floor_double(output, input),
            Float64UnaryOp::Ceil => self.masm.ceil_double(output, input),
            Float64UnaryOp::Round => {
                let (fraction, constant) = (Self::lowering_fpr(0), Self::lowering_fpr(1));
                let (rounded, done) = (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
                let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
                self.masm.floor_double(output, input);
                // NB: The difference of a double and its floor is exact; it
                //     is NaN for infinities and NaN, which are their own floor.
                self.masm.sub_double(fraction, input, output);
                self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 0.5);
                self.masm
                    .branch_double(DoubleCondition::LessThanOrUnordered, fraction, constant, rounded);
                self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 1.0);
                self.masm.add_double(output, output, constant);
                self.masm.bind(rounded);
                // NB: The bits of +0 are zero.
                self.masm.move_double_to_gpr(scratch, output);
                self.masm.branch_test64(Condition::NonZero, scratch, u64::MAX, done);
                self.masm.move_double_to_gpr(scratch, input);
                self.masm.and64_imm(scratch, scratch, SIGN_BIT);
                self.masm.move_gpr_to_double(output, scratch);
                self.masm.bind(done);
            }
        }
    }

    /// `CallFloat64Function`: calls the runtime's function of doubles. The
    /// registers C calls take doubles in (and return the first in) are
    /// lowering registers, which hold no values.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_call_float64_function(
        &mut self,
        node: NodeId,
        function: Float64Function,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let address = (self.runtime.float64_functions.0)(function);
        if address == 0 {
            return Err(CompileFailure::MissingRuntimeHelper { opcode: None });
        }
        for index in 0..function.argument_count() {
            let argument = M::ARGUMENT_FPRS[index];
            assert_eq!(argument, Self::lowering_fpr(index));
            let input = self.float_input(node, index);
            self.masm.move_double(argument, input);
        }
        self.masm.call_absolute(address);
        let output = self.float_output(node);
        self.masm.move_double(output, M::ARGUMENT_FPRS[0]);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `Float64Binary`: `op` of two doubles.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_float64_binary(&mut self, node: NodeId, op: BinaryOp) {
        let (lhs, rhs, output) = (
            self.float_input(node, 0),
            self.float_input(node, 1),
            self.float_output(node),
        );
        match op {
            BinaryOp::Add => self.masm.add_double(output, lhs, rhs),
            BinaryOp::Sub => self.masm.sub_double(output, lhs, rhs),
            BinaryOp::Mul => self.masm.mul_double(output, lhs, rhs),
            BinaryOp::Div => self.masm.div_double(output, lhs, rhs),
            _ => unreachable!("only Add, Sub, Mul and Div are double operations"),
        }
    }

    /// `Float64Compare`: `comparison` of two doubles, as a boolean. Only
    /// the inequalities hold for NaN.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_float64_compare(&mut self, node: NodeId, comparison: Comparison) {
        let (lhs, rhs, output) = (self.float_input(node, 0), self.float_input(node, 1), self.output(node));
        self.masm
            .compare_double_set(double_condition(comparison), output, lhs, rhs);
    }

    /// `Float64ToInt32`: ToInt32 of a double. Doubles in the int64 range
    /// truncate to an int64 whose low half it is. For the others, x - floor(x
    /// / 2^32) * 2^32 is exact (they are integers, and every step is), and in
    /// that range; it is NaN for NaN and the infinities, whose truncation has
    /// a zero low half.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_float64_to_int32(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (input, output) = (self.float_input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        let (large, done) = (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        // NB: Truncations out of range result in the smallest or (on some
        //     targets) the largest int64.
        self.masm.truncate_double_to_int64(output, input);
        self.masm.branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, output, i64::MIN, large);
        self.masm.branch64_imm(Condition::Equal, output, i64::MAX, large);
        self.masm.move32(output, output);
        self.masm.jump(done);
        self.masm.bind(large);
        let (multiple, constant) = (Self::lowering_fpr(0), Self::lowering_fpr(1));
        self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 2f64.powi(-32));
        self.masm.mul_double(multiple, input, constant);
        self.masm.floor_double(multiple, multiple);
        self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 2f64.powi(32));
        self.masm.mul_double(multiple, multiple, constant);
        self.masm.sub_double(multiple, input, multiple);
        self.masm.truncate_double_to_int64(output, multiple);
        self.masm.move32(output, output);
        self.masm.bind(done);
    }

    /// ToUint8Clamp ( argument ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-touint8clamp
    /// NB: The input has already undergone ToNumber. Bounds checks also
    ///     handle infinities, before converting the finite value to an integer.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_float64_to_uint8_clamped(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (input, output) = (self.float_input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        let (fraction, constant) = (Self::lowering_fpr(0), Self::lowering_fpr(1));
        let (increment, done) = (self.masm.new_label(), self.masm.new_label());
        // 1. Let number be ? ToNumber(argument).
        // 2. If number is NaN, return +0𝔽.
        // 3. Let mv be the extended mathematical value of number.
        // 4. Let clamped be the result of clamping mv between 0 and 255.
        self.masm.move_imm32(output, 0);
        self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 0.0);
        self.masm
            .branch_double(DoubleCondition::LessThanOrEqualOrUnordered, input, constant, done);
        self.masm.move_imm32(output, 255);
        self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 255.0);
        self.masm
            .branch_double(DoubleCondition::GreaterThanOrEqual, input, constant, done);
        // 5. Let f be floor(clamped).
        self.masm.floor_double(fraction, input);
        self.masm.truncate_double_to_int64(output, fraction);
        // 6. If clamped < f + 0.5, return 𝔽(f).
        // 7. If clamped > f + 0.5, return 𝔽(f + 1).
        // NB: Subtracting the floor is exact in this range.
        self.masm.sub_double(fraction, input, fraction);
        self.masm.move_double_imm(constant, 0.5);
        self.masm
            .branch_double(DoubleCondition::LessThan, fraction, constant, done);
        self.masm
            .branch_double(DoubleCondition::GreaterThan, fraction, constant, increment);
        // 8. If f is even, return 𝔽(f).
        self.masm.branch_test32(Condition::Zero, output, 1, done);
        // 9. Return 𝔽(f + 1).
        self.masm.bind(increment);
        self.masm.add32_imm(output, output, 1);
        self.masm.bind(done);
    }

    /// `Uint32ShiftRight`: the bits of the unsigned result of `>>>`, which
    /// shifts by the low five bits of the amount.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_uint32_shift_right(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (lhs, output) = (self.input(node, 0), self.output(node));
        match self.input_value(node, 1) {
            InputValue::Register(amount) => self.masm.shr32(output, lhs, amount),
            InputValue::Constant(bits) => self.masm.shr32_imm(output, lhs, (bits & 31) as u8),
        }
    }

    /// `Uint32ToFloat64`: the double of the bits of an int32, as an unsigned
    /// integer.
    pub(in crate::codegen) fn emit_uint32_to_float64(&mut self, node: NodeId) {
        let (input, output) = (self.input(node, 0), self.float_output(node));
        let scratch = self.pinned.scratch;
        self.masm.move32(scratch, input);
        self.masm.convert_int64_to_double(output, scratch);
    }
}

/// The condition of a comparison of doubles: false if either is NaN, but
/// for the inequalities.
pub(in crate::codegen) fn double_condition(comparison: Comparison) -> DoubleCondition {
    match comparison {
        Comparison::LessThan => DoubleCondition::LessThan,
        Comparison::LessThanEquals => DoubleCondition::LessThanOrEqual,
        Comparison::GreaterThan => DoubleCondition::GreaterThan,
        Comparison::GreaterThanEquals => DoubleCondition::GreaterThanOrEqual,
        Comparison::StrictlyEquals | Comparison::LooselyEquals => DoubleCondition::Equal,
        Comparison::StrictlyInequals | Comparison::LooselyInequals => DoubleCondition::NotEqualOrUnordered,
        Comparison::Below | Comparison::BelowOrEqual | Comparison::Above | Comparison::AboveOrEqual => {
            unreachable!("doubles compare signed")
        }
    }
}

//! What the lowering of each node needs from register allocation and the frame layout, declared next to the
//! lowerings in one exhaustive match (`lowering_info()`): where its inputs and its output are, how many temps it
//! takes, what it clobbers out of line, and which parts of the JIT frame it uses. The register allocator, its verifier
//! and the frame layout read it from here, and code generation checks that each lowering takes exactly the temps it
//! declares and uses the saves area only where it says so (see `Codegen::verify_lowerings()`).

use super::Codegen;
use super::DIRECT_CALL_TEMPS;
use super::SlowPathCall;
use super::probes::PUT_BY_ID_RECORD_BYTES;
use super::slow_path_call;
use crate::asm::Gpr;
use crate::asm::PortableMacroAssembler;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::debug_text::DebugText;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Float64UnaryOp;
use crate::ir::Node;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;

/// A register of the target's calling convention, which the register allocator resolves (see
/// `RegisterSet::fixed()`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FixedRegister {
    /// Argument register `n` of calls.
    Argument(u8),
    /// The register calls return their (first) result in.
    Return,
    /// The register shifts by a register amount take the amount in, on targets that have one (see
    /// `RegisterSet::shift_amount_gpr`).
    ShiftAmount,
}

/// Where a node finds one of its inputs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum InputConstraint {
    #[default]
    Register,
    Fixed(FixedRegister),
    /// A register, or the constant itself if the input is one, which code
    /// generation uses as an immediate.
    RegisterOrConstant,
    /// Wherever the value is: a register, its stack slot or a constant.
    Anywhere,
    /// The amount of a shift: the constant itself if the input is one, which code generation uses as an immediate,
    /// and otherwise the register the target shifts by, or any register on targets that shift by any (see
    /// `RegisterSet::resolve()`).
    ShiftAmount,
}

/// Where a node finds each of its inputs. It is a plain value, whatever the number of inputs: the first inputs each
/// have their own constraint, and one rule gives the constraints of all the inputs after them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct InputConstraints {
    /// How many inputs the node has.
    len: usize,
    first: [InputConstraint; Self::FIRST_COUNT],
    rest: RestConstraint,
}

/// Where a node finds its inputs after the first ones.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum RestConstraint {
    /// Each of them as this says.
    Each(InputConstraint),
    /// Each of them in the argument register after that of the input before it.
    NextArgument,
}

impl InputConstraints {
    /// How many of the first inputs have their own constraint.
    const FIRST_COUNT: usize = 4;

    /// The constraints of `len` inputs that the node finds each as `constraint` says.
    fn all(constraint: InputConstraint, len: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            len,
            first: [constraint; Self::FIRST_COUNT],
            rest: RestConstraint::Each(constraint),
        }
    }

    /// The constraints of `len` inputs that the node finds in the argument registers after the first one, in order.
    fn arguments_after_the_first(len: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            len,
            first: core::array::from_fn(|index| InputConstraint::Fixed(FixedRegister::Argument(index as u8 + 1))),
            rest: RestConstraint::NextArgument,
        }
    }

    /// How many inputs have a constraint.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }

    /// Where the node finds input `index`.
    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> InputConstraint {
        assert!(index < self.len, "the node has an input {index}");
        match (self.first.get(index), self.rest) {
            (Some(constraint), _) => *constraint,
            (None, RestConstraint::Each(constraint)) => constraint,
            (None, RestConstraint::NextArgument) => InputConstraint::Fixed(FixedRegister::Argument(index as u8 + 1)),
        }
    }

    /// Makes the node find input `index`, one of the first inputs, as `constraint` says.
    fn set(&mut self, index: usize, constraint: InputConstraint) {
        assert!(index < self.len, "the node has an input {index}");
        self.first[index] = constraint;
    }

    /// Makes the node find each input from `index` on as `constraint` says.
    fn set_from(&mut self, index: usize, constraint: InputConstraint) {
        self.first[index..].fill(constraint);
        self.rest = RestConstraint::Each(constraint);
    }
}

// NB: Two values are equal if they say the same about each input.
impl PartialEq for InputConstraints {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.len == other.len && (0..self.len).all(|index| self.get(index) == other.get(index))
    }
}

impl Eq for InputConstraints {}

/// Where a node puts its value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OutputConstraint {
    None,
    Register,
    /// The register calls return their result in.
    Return,
}

/// The registers a node's code clobbers, beyond its temps, its output and the scratch register.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Clobbers {
    Nothing,
    /// Every floating point register: its out of line code calls the runtime saving only the general purpose
    /// registers that may hold values (see `slow_path_saved_registers()`). Float64 values live across it get stack
    /// slots, like values live across a call.
    Floats,
    /// Every register a call clobbers: it is a call (`NodeProperties::is_call`).
    CallerSaved,
}

/// The part of the operand record (see `Locals::record`) a node's code uses.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Record {
    None,
    Bytes(u32),
    /// The operands of the slow path of its instruction, and the stack arguments of its call, which the frame layout
    /// sizes from the bytecode (see `Codegen::lay_out_frame()`).
    SlowPathOperands,
}

/// What the lowering of a node needs (see `lowering_info()`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LoweringInfo {
    pub inputs: InputConstraints,
    pub output: OutputConstraint,
    /// How many general purpose registers it computes with, besides its inputs and its output, which no input is in.
    pub temps: u8,
    pub clobbers: Clobbers,
    /// Whether it computes its output from its first input as two-address instructions do, so that the output may take
    /// the register of that input where it dies.
    pub reuses_first_input: bool,
    /// Whether its code uses the saves area (see `Locals::saves`), wherever it runs.
    pub uses_saves_area: bool,
    /// Whether, in an inlined callee, it runs in the published frames of the inlined calls it is in (see
    /// `Codegen::emit_publish_frames()`), which also uses the saves area.
    pub publishes_frames: bool,
    /// Whether it runs a slow path or a call that may leave compiled code, so that in an inlined callee, its leave
    /// writes its frame state (see `Codegen::leave_frame_of()`).
    pub may_leave_from_inlined_callee: bool,
    pub record: Record,
}

impl LoweringInfo {
    /// Takes its inputs in registers, from which it computes its value (if it has one) in a register, and nothing else.
    fn plain(node: &Node) -> Self {
        Self {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Register, node.inputs.len()),
            output: if node.repr.is_some() {
                OutputConstraint::Register
            } else {
                OutputConstraint::None
            },
            temps: 0,
            clobbers: if node.op.properties().is_call {
                Clobbers::CallerSaved
            } else {
                Clobbers::Nothing
            },
            reuses_first_input: false,
            uses_saves_area: false,
            publishes_frames: false,
            may_leave_from_inlined_callee: false,
            record: Record::None,
        }
    }

    fn with_temps(self, temps: u8) -> Self {
        Self { temps, ..self }
    }

    /// Calls the runtime out of line saving only the general purpose registers, in the saves area.
    fn saving_registers(self) -> Self {
        debug_assert_eq!(self.clobbers, Clobbers::Nothing, "calls clobber more");
        Self {
            clobbers: Clobbers::Floats,
            uses_saves_area: true,
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// Takes input `index` as an immediate if it is a constant.
    fn with_immediate(mut self, index: usize) -> Self {
        self.inputs.set(index, InputConstraint::RegisterOrConstant);
        self
    }

    /// Shifts by input `index`, which it takes as an immediate if it is a constant.
    fn with_shift_amount(mut self, index: usize) -> Self {
        self.inputs.set(index, InputConstraint::ShiftAmount);
        self
    }

    /// Calls a runtime function with the VM in the first argument register and its inputs in the next ones, returning
    /// its value.
    fn runtime_call(node: &Node) -> Self {
        Self {
            inputs: InputConstraints::arguments_after_the_first(node.inputs.len()),
            output: OutputConstraint::Return,
            ..Self::plain(node)
        }
    }
}

/// What the lowering of `node` needs. Nodes without code (constants, phis, virtual objects, refinements and legacy
/// arguments guards, which are gone before register allocation) need nothing but what every node does.
pub fn lowering_info(node: &Node) -> LoweringInfo {
    let plain = LoweringInfo::plain(node);
    match &node.op {
        Op::Constant(_) | Op::Phi | Op::VirtualObject { .. } | Op::Refine { .. } | Op::AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread => {
            plain
        }
        Op::LoadSlot { .. } | Op::StoreSlot { .. } | Op::PublishFrame | Op::Suspend { .. } => plain,
        // A value and a cursor for filling the registers and locals.
        Op::InitializeFrame | Op::EnsureFrameInitialized => plain.with_temps(2),
        Op::LoadOuterEnvironment | Op::LoadEnvironmentBinding { .. } => plain,
        // The environment's binding values.
        Op::StoreEnvironmentBinding { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The index of the appended binding.
        Op::AppendEnvironmentBinding => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::BoxCell | Op::SetLexicalEnvironment | Op::LeavePrivateEnvironment | Op::IsCallable => plain,
        // The function, besides the scratch register.
        Op::KeepOwnEnvironments => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::ToBoolean => LoweringInfo {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Fixed(FixedRegister::Argument(0)), 1),
            output: OutputConstraint::Return,
            ..plain
        },
        // NB: The VM is the first argument.
        Op::PrimitiveToString | Op::CallIntrinsic { .. } | Op::ToObject | Op::ArrayCreate => {
            LoweringInfo::runtime_call(node)
        }
        // NB: The inserted values go on the native stack.
        Op::CallArraySplice => {
            let mut info = LoweringInfo::runtime_call(node);
            info.inputs.set_from(3, InputConstraint::RegisterOrConstant);
            info
        }
        Op::Generic { opcode, .. } => LoweringInfo {
            output: if node.repr.is_some() {
                OutputConstraint::Return
            } else {
                OutputConstraint::None
            },
            may_leave_from_inlined_callee: true,
            record: slow_path_record(*opcode, false),
            ..plain
        },
        // NB: The call stores its operands to the frame first.
        Op::CallDirect {
            stores_operands: true,
            inlined_frame_bytes,
            ..
        }
        | Op::CallNative {
            stores_operands: true,
            inlined_frame_bytes,
            ..
        } => LoweringInfo {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Anywhere, node.inputs.len()),
            output: OutputConstraint::Return,
            publishes_frames: *inlined_frame_bytes == 0,
            may_leave_from_inlined_callee: true,
            ..plain
        },
        // Direct and native calls with inputs build the callee's frame in
        // temps.
        Op::CallDirect {
            inlined_frame_bytes, ..
        }
        | Op::CallNative {
            inlined_frame_bytes, ..
        } => {
            let info = LoweringInfo {
                publishes_frames: *inlined_frame_bytes == 0,
                may_leave_from_inlined_callee: true,
                ..plain
            };
            if node.inputs.is_empty() {
                info
            } else {
                // NB: Calls in inlined callees return their result.
                LoweringInfo {
                    output: if node.repr.is_some() {
                        OutputConstraint::Return
                    } else {
                        OutputConstraint::None
                    },
                    ..info.with_temps(DIRECT_CALL_TEMPS)
                }
            }
        }
        // Native accessor calls build the callee's frame in temps, and return
        // the result.
        Op::CallNativeAccessor { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            output: OutputConstraint::Return,
            ..plain.with_temps(DIRECT_CALL_TEMPS)
        },
        Op::ArgumentCount | Op::LoadFrameField { .. } | Op::LoadArgument { .. } => plain,
        Op::CallForwardingArguments { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            may_leave_from_inlined_callee: true,
            ..plain
        },
        Op::CheckInt32 | Op::CheckNumber | Op::BoxInt32 | Op::BoxBool => plain,
        // NB: Comparisons and int32 arithmetic take a constant right-hand side as an immediate.
        Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Mul } => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain
        },
        // The quotient of a remainder.
        Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Mod } => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain.with_immediate(1).with_temps(1)
        },
        Op::Int32Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::LeftShift | BinaryOp::RightShift | BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift,
        }
        | Op::Int32WrappingBinary {
            op: BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift,
        } => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain.with_shift_amount(1)
        },
        Op::Int32Binary { .. } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain.with_immediate(1)
        },
        Op::Int32Compare { .. } | Op::TaggedEquals { .. } => plain.with_immediate(1),
        // The object's address.
        Op::CheckElements { .. } | Op::CheckTypedArray | Op::CheckArray => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::CheckPropertyAbsenceCacheable => plain.with_temps(2),
        Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32 | Op::LoadTypedArrayLength | Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset => plain,
        Op::TypedArrayDataAddress => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain
        },
        Op::CheckTypedArrayStorage => plain,
        Op::CheckBounds => plain.with_immediate(0).with_immediate(1),
        // The elements or the element address.
        Op::LoadElementAt { .. } => plain.with_immediate(1).with_temps(1),
        // The elements or the element address. Stores of integer and tagged constants store immediates.
        Op::StoreElementAt { kind } => {
            let info = plain.with_immediate(1).with_temps(1);
            if kind.stored_repr() == Repr::Float64 {
                info
            } else {
                info.with_immediate(2)
            }
        }
        Op::CheckNotHole | Op::CheckInitialized | Op::CellAddress => plain,
        // The heap and a value.
        Op::AllocateObject { .. } => plain.with_temps(2).saving_registers(),
        // The object's property storage.
        Op::InitializeNamed { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The element storage and a value.
        Op::AllocateArray { .. } => plain.with_temps(2).saving_registers(),
        // The array's elements.
        Op::InitializeElement { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The function and a value.
        Op::AllocateFunction { .. } => plain.with_temps(2).saving_registers(),
        // The environment and a value.
        Op::AllocateEnvironment { .. } => plain.with_temps(2).saving_registers(),
        Op::SliceArguments => LoweringInfo {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Fixed(FixedRegister::Argument(2)), 1),
            output: OutputConstraint::Return,
            ..plain
        },
        // The tag of an operand, with a bit that tells two of the tags apart set.
        Op::CheckIdentityComparable => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::CheckObject => plain,
        // The function object.
        Op::CheckClosure { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::LoadFunctionEnvironment { .. } | Op::CheckValue { .. } => plain,
        Op::EmptyToUndefined | Op::Typeof | Op::TypeofIs { .. } => plain,
        Op::CheckShape { .. } | Op::CheckPrototypeChainValid { .. } => plain,
        // The object whose prototype comes next.
        Op::HasInPrototypeChain => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::AssumeValid | Op::CheckInterrupt | Op::LoadGlobalBinding { .. } => plain,
        // The environment's binding values.
        Op::StoreGlobalBinding { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The object's property storage, then the accessor.
        Op::CheckAccessorFunction { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::LoadAccessorFunction { .. } | Op::LoadNamed { .. } => plain,
        // The object's property storage.
        Op::AddNamed { .. } | Op::StoreNamed { .. } => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::Jump { .. } => plain,
        Op::Branch { condition, .. } => branch_lowering_info(*condition, plain),
        Op::BranchTruthy { .. } | Op::BranchOnPc { .. } | Op::ShapeSwitch { .. } => plain,
        Op::Return => LoweringInfo {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Fixed(FixedRegister::Return), 1),
            ..plain
        },
        Op::Exit { .. } | Op::Unreachable => plain,
        // NB: Slow path calls read their operands from where they are.
        Op::CallSlowPath {
            saves_registers,
            opcode,
            ..
        } => {
            let info = LoweringInfo {
                inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Anywhere, node.inputs.len()),
                // NB: A call's value is moved into the return register once its
                //     slow path continued, where a conditional jump's control
                //     word is.
                output: if !saves_registers && node.repr.is_some() {
                    OutputConstraint::Return
                } else {
                    plain.output
                },
                uses_saves_area: true,
                publishes_frames: true,
                may_leave_from_inlined_callee: true,
                record: slow_path_record(*opcode, true),
                ..plain
            };
            if *saves_registers {
                LoweringInfo {
                    clobbers: Clobbers::Floats,
                    ..info
                }
            } else {
                info
            }
        }
        Op::UnboxInt32 | Op::Int32Abs | Op::Int32Min | Op::Int32Max | Op::Uint32Min | Op::Int32ToFloat64 => plain,
        Op::BoolToInt32 => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain
        },
        // NB: Rounding reads its input after writing its output.
        Op::UnboxDouble
        | Op::BoxFloat64
        | Op::Float64Unary {
            op: Float64UnaryOp::Round,
        } => plain,
        // OPTIMIZATION: The SSE instructions of x86 write their result over their first operand, which then needs no
        //     copy where it dies.
        Op::Float64Unary { .. } | Op::Float64Binary { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            reuses_first_input: true,
            ..plain
        },
        Op::Float64Min | Op::Float64Max | Op::CallFloat64Function { .. } | Op::Float64Compare { .. } => plain,
        Op::Float64ToInt32 | Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped | Op::CheckFloat64Int32 => plain,
        Op::Uint32ShiftRight => plain.with_shift_amount(1),
        Op::Uint32ToFloat64 | Op::StringAddress | Op::StringLength | Op::LoadStringCodeUnit => plain,
        Op::SingleCharacterString => plain,
        // The first string's address, then its length or its storage word.
        Op::StringsEqual => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The new rope string, its length and a temp.
        Op::ConcatenateStrings { .. } => plain.with_temps(3).saving_registers(),
        Op::IntegerToString => plain,
        // The array, then its prototypes.
        Op::CheckAppendableArray => plain.with_temps(2),
        Op::LoadElementsLength => plain,
        // The object's elements.
        Op::LoadElementsCapacity | Op::AppendElement => plain.with_temps(1),
        Op::CallArrayPush | Op::CallStoreHoleyElement | Op::OpenArrayIteration => plain.saving_registers(),
        Op::LoadArrayIteratorArray | Op::LoadArrayIteratorIndex => plain,
        Op::StoreArrayIteratorIndex | Op::FinishArrayIterator => plain,
        Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionType | Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionValue => plain,
        Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKeyCount | Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKey => plain,
        // NB: The output comes from where the slow path call left it.
        Op::SlowPathOutput { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            inputs: InputConstraints::all(InputConstraint::Anywhere, 1),
            ..plain
        },
        // The object, its shape and the cache entry.
        Op::ProbePropertyCache { .. } => plain.with_temps(3).saving_registers(),
        // The object, its shape and the cache entry.
        Op::ProbeKeyedCache { .. } => plain.with_temps(3),
        // The object, its shape, the cache entry and the named property storage of property additions.
        // NB: It calls no runtime function: the subroutine that grows named property storage keeps every register
        //     but the scratch register, saving the ones it uses in the saves area.
        Op::ProbeKeyedStore { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            uses_saves_area: true,
            ..plain.with_temps(4)
        },
        // The object, its shape, the cache entry and the named property storage of property additions.
        Op::ProbePropertyStore { .. } => LoweringInfo {
            record: Record::Bytes(PUT_BY_ID_RECORD_BYTES),
            ..plain.with_temps(4).saving_registers()
        },
        // The cache, the global declarative environment, the global object
        // and a temp.
        Op::ProbeGlobalCache { .. } | Op::ProbeGlobalStore { .. } => plain.with_temps(4),
        // The object or its elements, and the keyed cache's registers.
        Op::ProbeHasProperty { .. } => plain.with_temps(3).saving_registers(),
    }
}

/// What a branch on `condition` needs, beyond `plain`.
fn branch_lowering_info(condition: BranchCondition, plain: LoweringInfo) -> LoweringInfo {
    match condition {
        BranchCondition::Bool
        | BranchCondition::Nullish
        | BranchCondition::Undefined
        | BranchCondition::Object
        | BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32
        | BranchCondition::IndexInBounds
        | BranchCondition::MagicalLength
        | BranchCondition::Extensible
        | BranchCondition::ArrayIterator
        | BranchCondition::GeneratorObject
        | BranchCondition::HoldsValidWatchpointSet
        | BranchCondition::Shape(_)
        | BranchCondition::Float64(_)
        | BranchCondition::Int32Value
        | BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean
        | BranchCondition::Double
        | BranchCondition::String
        | BranchCondition::ResolvedString => plain,
        // NB: Comparisons take a constant right-hand side as an immediate.
        BranchCondition::Int32(_) | BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { .. } => plain.with_immediate(1),
        // The address of the object.
        BranchCondition::ElementsKind(_) => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The array's prototypes.
        BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The object's prototypes.
        BranchCondition::PlainArrayPrototypeChain => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The object's shape.
        BranchCondition::ArrayWithRealmArrayPrototypeAndNoNamedProperties => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The function object.
        BranchCondition::Builtin(_) => plain.with_temps(1),
        // The binding's index, and a temp.
        BranchCondition::BindingMutable { .. } => plain.with_temps(2),
        // The environment's shape and the binding's index.
        BranchCondition::NextBindingOfShape { .. } => plain.with_temps(2),
        // The object, the property iterator cache, and a temp.
        BranchCondition::PropertyIteratorCacheValid => plain.with_temps(3),
    }
}

/// The part of the operand record the slow path of `opcode` uses, called by a `CallSlowPath` node (`on_values`) or a
/// `Generic` one.
fn slow_path_record(opcode: crate::bytecode::OpCode, on_values: bool) -> Record {
    match slow_path_call(opcode) {
        Some(SlowPathCall::Record) => Record::SlowPathOperands,
        // NB: Binary slow paths called on values write their result into the record.
        Some(SlowPathCall::BinaryValues) if on_values => Record::Bytes(8),
        Some(SlowPathCall::BinaryValues | SlowPathCall::JumpValues | SlowPathCall::JitCall) | None => Record::None,
    }
}

impl<'a, M: PortableMacroAssembler> Codegen<'a, '_, M> {
    /// Temp `index` of `node`, which its lowering declares (see `LoweringInfo::temps`). Lowerings take every temp
    /// they declare through this, even on paths that do not use it, so that the declarations can be checked.
    pub(super) fn temp(&self, node: NodeId, index: usize) -> Gpr {
        let requested = &self.requested_temps[node.index()];
        requested.set(requested.get().max(index as u8 + 1));
        Gpr(self.allocation.node(node).temps[index])
    }

    /// Notes that the code being emitted uses the saves area.
    pub(super) fn note_saves_area_use(&self) {
        if self.verify
            && let Some(node) = self.emitting
            && !self.uses_saves_area(node)
        {
            self.undeclared_saves_area_uses.borrow_mut().push(node);
        }
    }

    /// Checks that the lowering of every node took exactly the temps it declares, and that only nodes that declare
    /// it used the saves area, whose size depends on that.
    pub(super) fn verify_lowerings(&self) -> Result<(), DebugText<'a>> {
        let mut errors = DebugText::new_in(self.work);
        let mut report = |error: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>| {
            if !errors.is_empty() {
                errors.push('\n');
            }
            errors.write_fmt(error);
        };
        for block in 0..self.graph.blocks.len() {
            for node in self.graph.block_nodes(BlockId::from_index(block)) {
                let declared = lowering_info(self.graph.node(node)).temps;
                let requested = self.requested_temps[node.index()].get();
                if requested != declared {
                    report(format_args!(
                        "v{} ({}) takes {requested} temps, but declares {declared}",
                        node.0,
                        self.graph.node(node).op.name()
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        let mut previous = None;
        for node in self.undeclared_saves_area_uses.borrow().iter().copied() {
            if previous == Some(node) {
                continue;
            }
            previous = Some(node);
            report(format_args!(
                "v{} ({}) uses the saves area, but does not declare it",
                node.0,
                self.graph.node(node).op.name()
            ));
        }
        if errors.is_empty() { Ok(()) } else { Err(errors) }
    }
}

//! Lowers register allocated IR onto a `PortableMacroAssembler`.
//!
//! Compiled code is entered as `JitResult entry(VM*, ExecutionContext* frame)`
//! and keeps the VM and the frame in callee-saved registers. Frame slots are
//! embedded in the `ExecutionContext`, so they are addressed relative to the
//! frame register.
//!
//! The JIT frame (the locals area of the machine frame) holds, from the stack
//! pointer up: outgoing stack arguments of slow path calls, the operand record
//! slow paths take by reference, the index of the exit being taken, the
//! register dump of the exit stub, and the spill slots.
//!
//! Generic nodes call the interpreter's slow paths with the interpreter's
//! calling conventions (see `slow_path`). A slow path returns a control word:
//! a continuation with the next instruction's pc means the instruction is done
//! and compiled code continues; anything else returns to the caller with
//! `JitStatus::Resume` (the interpreter continues where the slow path left the
//! running execution context) or, for negative control words,
//! `JitStatus::ExitInterpreter`.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum InputValue {
    Register(Gpr),
    Constant(u64),
}

/// The most bytes of code a stub or the entry trampoline has, and of lists its code generator makes.
const STUB_CODE_LIMIT: usize = 1 << 20;
const STUB_ZONE_LIMIT: usize = 1 << 24;

/// Bit 32 of a slow path control word marks a continuation in the same frame.
const CONTINUATION_BIT: u64 = 1 << 32;

/// The registers codegen keeps for itself; none of them is allocatable.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PinnedRegisters {
    pub vm: Gpr,
    pub frame: Gpr,
    /// The register allocator's scratch register: moves between stack slots
    /// go through it, and node lowerings may clobber it.
    pub scratch: Gpr,
}

/// The register allocator's view of the target, and the registers codegen
/// pins: the first three callee-saved allocatable registers.
pub fn target_registers<M: PortableMacroAssembler>() -> (RegisterSet, PinnedRegisters) {
    let mut callee_saved = M::CALLEE_SAVED_GPRS.intersection(M::ALLOCATABLE_GPRS).iter();
    let mut next = || {
        callee_saved
            .next()
            .expect("the target has three callee-saved registers")
    };
    let pinned = PinnedRegisters {
        vm: next(),
        frame: next(),
        scratch: next(),
    };
    let allocatable = M::ALLOCATABLE_GPRS
        .without(pinned.vm)
        .without(pinned.frame)
        .without(pinned.scratch);
    // NB: Lowerings compute with the first floating point registers (see
    //     `Codegen::lowering_fpr()`), which hold no values.
    let allocatable_fprs = M::ALLOCATABLE_FPRS
        .iter()
        .skip(values::LOWERING_FPRS)
        .fold(0u64, |mask, register| mask | (1 << register.0));
    let registers = RegisterSet {
        allocatable_gprs: RegisterMask(u64::from(allocatable.0)),
        allocatable_fprs: RegisterMask(allocatable_fprs),
        caller_saved_gprs: RegisterMask(u64::from(M::CALLER_SAVED_GPRS.0)),
        caller_saved_fprs: RegisterMask(u64::from(M::CALLER_SAVED_FPRS.0)),
        argument_gprs: M::ARGUMENT_GPRS,
        return_gpr: M::RETURN_GPRS[0].0,
        shift_amount_gpr: M::SHIFT_AMOUNT_GPR.map(|register| register.0),
        scratch_gpr: pinned.scratch.0,
    };
    (registers, pinned)
}

/// The registers an exit stub saves in its `RegisterDump`: every GPR and
/// FPR encoding below these counts (16 + 16 on x86-64, 31 + 32 on AArch64).
pub fn register_dump_counts<M: PortableMacroAssembler>() -> (u32, u32) {
    let gprs = M::ALLOCATABLE_GPRS
        .union(M::CALLER_SAVED_GPRS)
        .union(M::CALLEE_SAVED_GPRS)
        .union(M::SCRATCH_GPRS)
        .with(M::FRAME_POINTER);
    let fprs = M::ALLOCATABLE_FPRS
        .union(M::CALLER_SAVED_FPRS)
        .union(M::CALLEE_SAVED_FPRS)
        .union(M::SCRATCH_FPRS);
    let count = |highest: Option<u8>| u32::from(highest.map_or(0, |register| register + 1));
    (
        count(gprs.iter().next_back().map(|register| register.0)),
        count(fprs.iter().next_back().map(|register| register.0)),
    )
}

/// A register of either class, from its number in `Location`s (see
/// `regalloc::FPR_BASE`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Register {
    General(Gpr),
    Float(Fpr),
}

pub(super) fn register_of(register: u8) -> Register {
    if register >= crate::regalloc::FPR_BASE {
        Register::Float(Fpr(register - crate::regalloc::FPR_BASE))
    } else {
        Register::General(Gpr(register))
    }
}

/// A list of at most 32 values (one for each register of a class), in an array of its own: the short lists that the
/// code generator makes for a node, mostly of registers, take no memory of a zone.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct RegisterList<T> {
    values: [T; 32],
    len: u8,
}

impl<T: Copy + Default> RegisterList<T> {
    pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            values: [T::default(); 32],
            len: 0,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        self.values[usize::from(self.len)] = value;
        self.len += 1;
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default> Default for RegisterList<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl<T> core::ops::Deref for RegisterList<T> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        &self.values[..usize::from(self.len)]
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default> FromIterator<T> for RegisterList<T> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(values: I) -> Self {
        let mut list = Self::new();
        for value in values {
            list.push(value);
        }
        list
    }
}

/// Machine code for one graph, before it becomes `CompiledCode`. The code is in the column it was generated into.
pub struct GeneratedCode<'a> {
    /// Where the instructions end and the constants they load begin.
    pub data_offset: u32,
    pub entry_offset: u32,
    /// What the code from each offset on was generated for, in emission
    /// order. Only `dump-asm` reads it.
    pub annotations: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, CodeAnnotation)>,
