//! A readable textual form of the IR.

use super::BlockId;
use super::BranchCondition;
use super::Graph;
use super::NodeId;
use super::Op;
use super::ShapeCheck;
use super::SuspendKind;
use super::VirtualObjectKind;
use super::value;
use crate::bytecode::FrameLayout;
use crate::bytecode::Operand;
use crate::bytecode::SlotKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::code::ResumeMode;
use core::fmt;

/// The name of a frame slot, like the bytecode disassembler prints operands.
pub fn slot_name(layout: &FrameLayout, slot: u32) -> SlotName {
    SlotName(layout.slot_kind(Operand::from_raw(slot)))
}

/// The text of `slot_name()`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct SlotName(SlotKind);

impl fmt::Display for SlotName {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self.0 {
            SlotKind::Register(index) => write!(f, "r{index}"),
            SlotKind::Local(index) => write!(f, "l{index}"),
            SlotKind::Constant(index) => write!(f, "c{index}"),
            SlotKind::Argument(index) => write!(f, "a{index}"),
        }
    }
}

/// Writes the text of each item, with ", " between them.
fn write_joined<T>(
    f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>,
    items: impl IntoIterator<Item = T>,
    mut write_item: impl FnMut(&mut fmt::Formatter<'_>, T) -> fmt::Result,
) -> fmt::Result {
    for (index, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            f.write_str(", ")?;
        }
        write_item(f, item)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The name of a value: its node, or the constant it is.
struct ValueName<'a, 'z> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'z>,
    id: NodeId,
}

fn value_name<'a, 'z>(graph: &'a Graph<'z>, id: NodeId) -> ValueName<'a, 'z> {
    ValueName { graph, id }
}

impl fmt::Display for ValueName<'_, '_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let (graph, id) = (self.graph, self.id);
        match (graph.constant_value(id), graph.node(id).repr) {
            (Some(bits), Some(Repr::Int32)) => write!(f, "#i32:{}", (bits as u32).cast_signed()),
            (Some(bits), Some(Repr::Bool)) => write!(f, "#bool:{}", bits != 0),
            (Some(bits), Some(Repr::Pointer)) => write!(f, "#pointer:{bits:#x}"),
            (Some(bits), _) => write!(f, "#{}", value::describe(bits)),
            (None, _) => write!(f, "v{}", id.0),
        }
    }
}

struct BlockName(BlockId);

impl fmt::Display for BlockName {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "b{}", self.0.0)
    }
}

fn repr_name(repr: Repr) -> &'static str {
    match repr {
        Repr::Tagged => "tagged",
        Repr::Int32 => "int32",
        Repr::Float64 => "float64",
        Repr::Bool => "bool",
        Repr::Pointer => "pointer",
    }
}

fn write_shapes(f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>, shapes: &[ShapeCheck]) -> fmt::Result {
    write_joined(f, shapes, |f, shape| match shape.dictionary_generation {
        Some(generation) => write!(f, "{:#x}@{generation}", shape.shape.0),
        None => write!(f, "{:#x}", shape.shape.0),
    })
}

struct ConditionText(BranchCondition);

impl fmt::Display for ConditionText {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let name = match self.0 {
            BranchCondition::Bool => "Bool",
            BranchCondition::Nullish => "Nullish",
            BranchCondition::Undefined => "Undefined",
            BranchCondition::Object => "Object",
            BranchCondition::ElementsKind(kind) => return write!(f, "ElementsKind {kind:?}"),
            BranchCondition::IndexInBounds => "IndexInBounds",
            BranchCondition::MagicalLength => "MagicalLength",
            BranchCondition::Extensible => "Extensible",
            BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray => "HoleFillableArray",
            BranchCondition::ArrayIterator => "ArrayIterator",
            BranchCondition::GeneratorObject => "GeneratorObject",
            BranchCondition::PlainArrayPrototypeChain => "PlainArrayPrototypeChain",
            BranchCondition::ArrayWithRealmArrayPrototypeAndNoNamedProperties => {
                "ArrayWithRealmArrayPrototypeAndNoNamedProperties"
            }
            BranchCondition::HoldsValidWatchpointSet => "HoldsValidWatchpointSet",
            BranchCondition::Shape(shape) => {
                f.write_str("Shape ")?;
                return write_shapes(f, core::slice::from_ref(&shape));
            }
            BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32 => "NonNegativeInt32",
            BranchCondition::Int32(comparison) => return write!(f, "Int32{comparison:?}"),
            BranchCondition::Float64(comparison) => return write!(f, "Float64{comparison:?}"),
            BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: true } => "TaggedEquals",
            BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: false } => "TaggedNotEquals",
            BranchCondition::Int32Value => "Int32Value",
            BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean => "Int32OrBoolean",
            BranchCondition::Double => "Double",
            BranchCondition::String => "String",
            BranchCondition::ResolvedString => "ResolvedString",
            BranchCondition::Builtin(id) => return write!(f, "Builtin {id}"),
            BranchCondition::PropertyIteratorCacheValid => "PropertyIteratorCacheValid",
            BranchCondition::BindingMutable { index } => return write!(f, "BindingMutable {index}"),
            BranchCondition::NextBindingOfShape { name, flags } => {
                return write!(f, "NextBindingOfShape {name:#x} {flags}");
            }
        };
        f.write_str(name)
    }
}

/// Where a call or a slow path call is in the bytecode: `@pc`, or `@e<executable>:pc` in an inlined executable.
struct Site {
    executable: u32,
    pc: u32,
}

impl fmt::Display for Site {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        if self.executable == 0 {
            write!(f, "@{}", self.pc)
        } else {
            write!(f, "@e{}:{}", self.executable, self.pc)
        }
    }
}

/// The text of " without inlined frames (<bytes> bytes)", or of nothing for none.
struct InlinedFrames(u32);

impl fmt::Display for InlinedFrames {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        if self.0 == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        write!(f, " without inlined frames ({} bytes)", self.0)
    }
}

/// The inputs of a node, like `(v1, #i32:2)`, or nothing if it has none.
struct Inputs<'a, 'z> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'z>,
    inputs: &'a [NodeId],
}

impl Inputs<'_, '_> {
    /// Writes `head`, and the inputs after it with a space between.
    fn after(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>, head: fmt::Arguments<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_fmt(head)?;
        if self.inputs.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        write!(f, " {self}")
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Inputs<'_, '_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        if self.inputs.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        f.write_str("(")?;
        write_joined(f, self.inputs, |f, input| {
            write!(f, "{}", value_name(self.graph, *input))
        })?;
        f.write_str(")")
    }
}

/// Writes the text of a node's op, with `inputs` in place.
fn write_op(f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>, layout: &FrameLayout, op: &Op, inputs: &Inputs<'_, '_>) -> fmt::Result {
    let name = op.name();
    match op {
        Op::Constant(bits) => write!(f, "Constant {}", value::describe(*bits)),
        Op::LoadSlot { slot } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadSlot {}", slot_name(layout, *slot))),
        Op::StoreSlot { slot } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("StoreSlot {}", slot_name(layout, *slot))),
        Op::Phi => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Phi")),
        Op::InitializeFrame => inputs.after(f, format_args!("InitializeFrame")),
        Op::EnsureFrameInitialized => inputs.after(f, format_args!("EnsureFrameInitialized")),
        Op::PublishFrame => inputs.after(f, format_args!("PublishFrame")),
        Op::Suspend { continuation, kind } => {
            let kind = match kind {
                SuspendKind::Yield => "",
                SuspendKind::YieldIteratorResult => " iterator-result",
                SuspendKind::Await => " await",
            };
            match continuation {
                Some(pc) => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Suspend pc {pc}{kind}")),
                None => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Suspend completed{kind}")),
            }
        }
        Op::BoxCell => inputs.after(f, format_args!("BoxCell")),
        Op::LoadOuterEnvironment => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadOuterEnvironment")),
        Op::LoadEnvironmentBinding { index } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadEnvironmentBinding {index}")),
        Op::StoreEnvironmentBinding { index } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("StoreEnvironmentBinding {index}")),
        Op::AppendEnvironmentBinding => inputs.after(f, format_args!("AppendEnvironmentBinding")),
        Op::SetLexicalEnvironment => inputs.after(f, format_args!("SetLexicalEnvironment")),
        Op::LeavePrivateEnvironment => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LeavePrivateEnvironment")),
        Op::KeepOwnEnvironments => inputs.after(f, format_args!("KeepOwnEnvironments")),
        Op::IsCallable => inputs.after(f, format_args!("IsCallable")),
        Op::CheckInt32 => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckInt32")),
        Op::CheckNumber => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckNumber")),
        Op::CheckIdentityComparable => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckIdentityComparable")),
        Op::BoxInt32 => inputs.after(f, format_args!("BoxInt32")),
        Op::BoxBool => inputs.after(f, format_args!("BoxBool")),
        Op::CellAddress => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CellAddress")),
        Op::Int32Binary { op } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Int32{op:?}")),
        Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Int32Wrapping{op:?}")),
        Op::Int32Compare { comparison } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Int32{comparison:?}")),
        Op::CheckElements { kind } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckElements {kind:?}")),
        Op::LoadElementAt { kind } | Op::StoreElementAt { kind } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name} {kind:?}")),
        Op::TaggedEquals { equal: true } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("TaggedEquals")),
        Op::TaggedEquals { equal: false } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("TaggedNotEquals")),
        Op::ToBoolean => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ToBoolean")),
        Op::PrimitiveToString | Op::ToObject | Op::ArrayCreate => inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name}")),
        Op::CallIntrinsic { intrinsic } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CallIntrinsic {intrinsic:?}")),
        Op::Generic { opcode, executable, pc } => {
            let site = Site {
                executable: *executable,
                pc: *pc,
            };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("Generic {} {site}", opcode.name()))
        }
        Op::ArgumentCount => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ArgumentCount")),
        Op::SliceArguments => inputs.after(f, format_args!("SliceArguments")),
        Op::LoadFrameField { field } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadFrameField {field:?}")),
        Op::LoadArgument { .. } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadArgument")),
        Op::CallForwardingArguments { executable, pc } => {
            let site = Site {
                executable: *executable,
                pc: *pc,
            };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("CallForwardingArguments {site}"))
        }
        Op::CallDirect {
            executable,
            pc,
            inlined_frame_bytes,
            stores_operands,
            target,
        } => {
            let site = Site {
                executable: *executable,
                pc: *pc,
            };
            let frames = InlinedFrames(*inlined_frame_bytes);
            let stores = if *stores_operands { " storing operands" } else { "" };
            match target {
                Some(target) => inputs.after(
                    f,
                    format_args!("CallDirect {site}{frames}{stores} of constant target {target}"),
                ),
                None => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CallDirect {site}{frames}{stores}")),
            }
        }
        Op::CallNative {
            executable,
            pc,
            inlined_frame_bytes,
            stores_operands,
        } => {
            let site = Site {
                executable: *executable,
                pc: *pc,
            };
            let frames = InlinedFrames(*inlined_frame_bytes);
            let stores = if *stores_operands { " storing operands" } else { "" };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("CallNative {site}{frames}{stores}"))
        }
        Op::CallNativeAccessor { pc, part, target } => {
            let direct = if target.direct_getter.is_some() { " direct" } else { "" };
            inputs.after(
                f,
                format_args!("CallNativeAccessor @{pc} {part:?} {:#x}{direct}", target.function.0),
            )
        }
        Op::AllocateObject {
            shape,
            property_count,
            reserve,
        } => {
            write!(
                f,
                "AllocateObject {:#x} with {property_count} properties, room for {reserve}",
                shape.0
            )
        }
        Op::InitializeNamed { offset } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("InitializeNamed +{offset}")),
        Op::AllocateArray { count } => write!(f, "AllocateArray with {count} elements"),
        Op::VirtualObject {
            kind: VirtualObjectKind::Object { shape },
            ..
        } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("VirtualObject {:#x}", shape.0)),
        Op::VirtualObject {
            kind: VirtualObjectKind::Closure { sample_slot },
            ..
        } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("VirtualObject closure {:#x}", sample_slot.0)),
        Op::AllocateEnvironment { shape_cache, capacity } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("AllocateEnvironment {shape_cache} capacity {capacity}"))
        }
        Op::AllocateFunction {
            executable,
            shared_function_data_index,
            ..
        } => inputs.after(
            f,
            format_args!("AllocateFunction e{executable}:{shared_function_data_index}"),
        ),
        Op::InitializeElement { index } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("InitializeElement [{index}]")),
        Op::CheckObject => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckObject")),
        Op::CheckValue { expected, .. } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckValue {expected:#x}")),
        Op::CheckClosure { shared_data } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CheckClosure {:#x}", shared_data.0)),
        Op::LoadFunctionEnvironment { private: true } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadFunctionEnvironment private"))
        }
        Op::LoadFunctionEnvironment { private: false } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadFunctionEnvironment")),
        Op::EmptyToUndefined => inputs.after(f, format_args!("EmptyToUndefined")),
        Op::Typeof => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Typeof")),
        Op::TypeofIs { kind, equal } => {
            let negation = if *equal { "" } else { "Not" };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("TypeofIs{negation} {kind:?}"))
        }
        Op::CheckShape { shapes } => {
            f.write_str("CheckShape [")?;
            write_shapes(f, shapes)?;
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("]"))
        }
        Op::CheckPrototypeChainValid { validity } => write!(f, "CheckPrototypeChainValid {:#x}", validity.0),
        Op::AssumeValid => f.write_str("AssumeValid"),
        Op::CheckInterrupt => f.write_str("CheckInterrupt"),
        Op::AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread => f.write_str("AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread"),
        Op::HasInPrototypeChain => inputs.after(f, format_args!("HasInPrototypeChain")),
        Op::LoadGlobalBinding { environment, index } => {
            write!(f, "LoadGlobalBinding {:#x}[{index}]", environment.0)
        }
        Op::StoreGlobalBinding { environment, index } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("StoreGlobalBinding {:#x}[{index}]", environment.0))
        }
        Op::LoadAccessorFunction { offset, part } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadAccessorFunction +{offset} {part:?}"))
        }
        Op::CheckAccessorFunction { offset, part, function } => inputs.after(
            f,
            format_args!("CheckAccessorFunction +{offset} {part:?} {:#x}", function.0),
        ),
        Op::LoadNamed { offset, holds_data } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("LoadNamed +{offset}"))?;
            f.write_str(if *holds_data { " data" } else { "" })
        }
        Op::StoreNamed { offset, holds_data } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("StoreNamed +{offset}"))?;
            f.write_str(if *holds_data { " data" } else { "" })
        }
        Op::AddNamed { offset, shape, .. } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("AddNamed +{offset} to {:#x}", shape.0)),
        Op::ShapeSwitch { shapes, targets } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("ShapeSwitch"))?;
            f.write_str(" [")?;
            write_joined(f, shapes.iter().zip(*targets), |f, (shape, block)| {
                write_shapes(f, core::slice::from_ref(shape))?;
                write!(f, " -> {}", BlockName(*block))
            })?;
            f.write_str("]")
        }
        Op::CallSlowPath {
            opcode, executable, pc, ..
        } => {
            let site = Site {
                executable: *executable,
                pc: *pc,
            };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name} {} {site}", opcode.name()))
        }
        Op::Float64Unary { op } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Float64{}", op.name())),
        Op::CallFloat64Function { function } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("CallFloat64{}", function.name())),
        Op::Float64Binary { op } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Float64{op:?}")),
        Op::Float64Compare { comparison } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Float64{comparison:?}")),
        Op::Refine { condition, holds } => {
            let negation = if *holds { "" } else { "Not" };
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("Refine{negation}{}", ConditionText(*condition)))
        }
        Op::SlowPathOutput { index } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("SlowPathOutput {index}")),
        Op::UnboxInt32
        | Op::Int32Abs
        | Op::Int32Min
        | Op::Uint32Min
        | Op::Int32Max
        | Op::Float64Min
        | Op::Float64Max
        | Op::Int32ToFloat64
        | Op::BoolToInt32
        | Op::UnboxDouble
        | Op::BoxFloat64
        | Op::StringAddress
        | Op::StringLength
        | Op::LoadStringCodeUnit
        | Op::SingleCharacterString
        | Op::Float64ToInt32
        | Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped
        | Op::CheckFloat64Int32
        | Op::Uint32ShiftRight
        | Op::Uint32ToFloat64
        | Op::StringsEqual
        | Op::IntegerToString
        | Op::CheckAppendableArray
        | Op::LoadElementsLength
        | Op::LoadElementsCapacity
        | Op::AppendElement
        | Op::CallArrayPush
        | Op::CallArraySplice
        | Op::CallStoreHoleyElement
        | Op::OpenArrayIteration
        | Op::LoadArrayIteratorArray
        | Op::LoadArrayIteratorIndex
        | Op::StoreArrayIteratorIndex
        | Op::FinishArrayIterator
        | Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionType
        | Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionValue
        | Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKeyCount
        | Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKey => inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name}")),
        Op::CheckBounds
        | Op::CheckNotHole
        | Op::CheckInitialized
        | Op::CheckTypedArray
        | Op::CheckArray
        | Op::CheckPropertyAbsenceCacheable
        | Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32
        | Op::LoadTypedArrayLength
        | Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset
        | Op::TypedArrayDataAddress
        | Op::CheckTypedArrayStorage => inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name}")),
        Op::ConcatenateStrings { key: false } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ConcatenateStrings")),
        Op::ConcatenateStrings { key: true } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ConcatenateKeyStrings")),
        Op::ProbeHasProperty { own: true } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ProbeHasOwnProperty")),
        Op::ProbeHasProperty { own: false } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("ProbeHasProperty")),
        Op::ProbeGlobalCache { cache } | Op::ProbeGlobalStore { cache } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name} cache {cache}"))
        }
        Op::ProbePropertyCache { executable, cache, .. }
        | Op::ProbeKeyedCache { executable, cache }
        | Op::ProbeKeyedStore { executable, cache }
        | Op::ProbePropertyStore { executable, cache, .. } => {
            if *executable == 0 {
                inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name} cache {cache}"))
            } else {
                inputs.after(f, format_args!("{name} cache e{executable}:{cache}"))
            }
        }
        Op::Jump { target } => write!(f, "Jump {}", BlockName(*target)),
        Op::Branch {
            condition,
            if_true,
            if_false,
        } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("Branch{}", ConditionText(*condition)))?;
            write!(f, " -> {}, {}", BlockName(*if_true), BlockName(*if_false))
        }
        Op::BranchTruthy {
            if_true,
            if_false,
            fallback,
        } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("BranchTruthy"))?;
            write!(
                f,
                " -> {}, {}, fallback {}",
                BlockName(*if_true),
                BlockName(*if_false),
                BlockName(*fallback)
            )
        }
        Op::BranchOnPc { pc, if_true, if_false } => {
            inputs.after(f, format_args!("BranchOnPc @{pc}"))?;
            write!(f, " -> {}, {}", BlockName(*if_true), BlockName(*if_false))
        }
        Op::Return => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Return")),
        Op::Exit { kind } => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Exit {kind:?}")),
        Op::Unreachable => inputs.after(f, format_args!("Unreachable")),
    }
}

/// One node as text, like `v3 = Generic GetById @12 (v1) [fs2]` (see `node_text()`).
pub struct NodeText<'a, 'z> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'z>,
    layout: &'a FrameLayout,
    node_id: NodeId,
}

/// One node as text, like `v3 = Generic GetById @12 (v1) [fs2]`.
pub fn node_text<'a, 'z>(graph: &'a Graph<'z>, layout: &'a FrameLayout, node_id: NodeId) -> NodeText<'a, 'z> {
    NodeText { graph, layout, node_id }
}

impl fmt::Display for NodeText<'_, '_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let node = self.graph.node(self.node_id);
        if let Some(repr) = node.repr {
            write!(f, "v{}", self.node_id.0)?;
            if repr != Repr::Tagged {
                write!(f, ":{}", repr_name(repr))?;
            }
            f.write_str(" = ")?;
        }
        let inputs = Inputs {
            graph: self.graph,
            inputs: &node.inputs,
        };
        write_op(f, self.layout, &node.op, &inputs)?;
        if let Some(frame_state) = node.frame_state {
            write!(f, " [fs{}]", frame_state.0)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// `graph` as text, with frame slots named according to `layout` (see `dump()`).
pub struct Dump<'a, 'z> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'z>,
    layout: &'a FrameLayout,
}

/// Prints `graph` as text, naming frame slots according to `layout`.
pub fn dump<'a, 'z>(graph: &'a Graph<'z>, layout: &'a FrameLayout) -> Dump<'a, 'z> {
    Dump { graph, layout }
}

impl fmt::Display for Dump<'_, '_> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        let (graph, layout) = (self.graph, self.layout);
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            let id = BlockId::from_index(index);
            write!(f, "{}", BlockName(id))?;
            if let Some(pc) = block.bytecode_start {
                write!(f, " (pc {pc})")?;
            }
            if !block.predecessors.is_empty() {
                f.write_str(" <- ")?;
                write_joined(f, &block.predecessors, |f, block| write!(f, "{}", BlockName(*block)))?;
            }
            if block.is_loop_header {
                f.write_str(" loop")?;
            }
            if block.is_cold {
                f.write_str(" cold")?;
            }
            f.write_str(":\n")?;
            for node_id in graph.block_nodes(id) {
                writeln!(f, "  {}", node_text(graph, layout, node_id))?;
            }
        }
        for (pc, block) in &graph.osr_entries {
            writeln!(f, "osr entry at pc {pc}: b{}", block.0)?;
        }
        if !graph.frame_states.is_empty() {
            f.write_str("frame states:\n")?;
        }
        for (index, frame_state) in graph.frame_states.iter().enumerate() {
            write!(f, "  fs{index}: ")?;
            if frame_state.executable != 0 {
                write!(f, "e{} ", frame_state.executable)?;
            }
            write!(f, "pc {}", frame_state.pc)?;
            match frame_state.mode {
                ResumeMode::ResumeAt => f.write_str(" at")?,
                ResumeMode::ResumeAfter { dst } if dst == Operand::INVALID => f.write_str(" after")?,
                ResumeMode::ResumeAfter { dst } => write!(f, " after -> {}", slot_name(layout, dst))?,
            }
            f.write_str(" {")?;
            write_joined(f, &frame_state.values, |f, (slot, value)| {
                write!(f, "{}={}", slot_name(layout, *slot), value_name(graph, *value))
            })?;
            f.write_str("}")?;
            if !frame_state.in_frame.is_empty() {
                f.write_str(" frame [")?;
                write_joined(f, &frame_state.in_frame, |f, slot| {
                    write!(f, "{}", slot_name(layout, *slot))
                })?;
                f.write_str("]")?;
            }
            if let Some(parent) = frame_state.parent {
                write!(f, " in fs{}", parent.0)?;
            }
            f.write_str("\n")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! The memory nodes read and write, as sets of abstract locations.
//!
//! Every op declares the locations it may read and write beyond its inputs
//! and outputs (see `NodeProperties`). Passes ask one question of them: may
//! a node's writes change what another node read (`Locations::intersects`)?
//! Locations are coarse kinds of memory, so subdividing one (named slots by
//! offset, say) would not change that question.

/// A set of abstract locations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Locations(u16);

impl Locations {
    pub const NONE: Self = Self(0);
    /// Interpreter frame slots and the fields of execution contexts.
    pub const FRAME: Self = Self(1 << 0);
    /// The values of named properties of objects.
    pub const NAMED_SLOTS: Self = Self(1 << 1);
    /// The shapes of objects, and with them their prototypes and which named
    /// properties they have.
    pub const SHAPES: Self = Self(1 << 2);
    /// The values of indexed elements of objects.
    pub const ELEMENTS: Self = Self(1 << 3);
    /// How objects store their elements: the kind of storage, how many
    /// elements there are and how many there is room for.
    pub const ELEMENT_COUNTS: Self = Self(1 << 4);
    /// The bindings of global declarative environments.
    pub const GLOBAL_BINDINGS: Self = Self(1 << 5);
    /// The bindings of declarative environments at static coordinates. The
    /// nodes that access them also count as accessing `GLOBAL_BINDINGS`,
    /// since a coordinate may lead to the global declarative environment.
    pub const BINDINGS: Self = Self(1 << 6);
    /// The internal state of iterators.
    pub const ITERATORS: Self = Self(1 << 7);
    /// The entries of keyed collections (Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet
    /// objects).
    pub const COLLECTIONS: Self = Self(1 << 8);
    /// Whether another thread interrupted the VM. Nothing reads it but
    /// `Op::CheckInterrupt`, which counts as writing it: a check has to stay
    /// in its loop, and no other node gets in its way.
    pub const INTERRUPT: Self = Self(1 << 9);
    /// Every location.
    pub const ALL: Self = Self(u16::MAX);

    /// Named properties: their values and which objects have them.
    pub const NAMED: Self = Self::NAMED_SLOTS.union(Self::SHAPES);
    /// Indexed elements: their values and how they are stored.
    pub const ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS: Self = Self::ELEMENTS.union(Self::ELEMENT_COUNTS);

    pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self {
        Self(self.0 | other.0)
    }

    pub const fn intersects(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        self.0 & other.0 != 0
    }

    pub const fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.0 == 0
    }
}

impl core::ops::BitOr for Locations {
    type Output = Self;

    fn bitor(self, other: Self) -> Self {
        self.union(other)
    }
}

impl core::ops::BitOrAssign for Locations {
    fn bitor_assign(&mut self, other: Self) {
        *self = self.union(other);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::Locations;

    #[test]
    fn sets_of_locations() {
        assert!(Locations::NAMED.intersects(Locations::SHAPES));
        assert!(!Locations::NAMED.intersects(Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS));
        assert!(!Locations::ELEMENTS.intersects(Locations::ELEMENT_COUNTS));
        assert!(Locations::ALL.intersects(Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS));
        assert!(Locations::NONE.is_empty() && !Locations::NONE.intersects(Locations::ALL));
        let mut locations = Locations::FRAME;
        locations |= Locations::ELEMENTS;
        assert_eq!(locations, Locations::FRAME | Locations::ELEMENTS);
    }
}

//! What the compiler knows about each op, apart from how code generation lowers it (see
//! `codegen::lowering_info`): its effects, how it exits, which input it refines, whether it ends a block and which
//! inputs it takes. `Op::info()` decides all of them for every op in one exhaustive match, so that a new op cannot
//! be added without deciding each, and the passes and the verifier read them from there.

use super::BranchCondition;
use super::ElementsKind;
use super::Locations;
use super::Op;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::snapshot::HelperResult;
use crate::snapshot::Intrinsic;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NodeProperties {
    /// May need to exit to the interpreter after it returns, resuming after
    /// the current bytecode.
    pub can_lazy_exit: bool,
    /// Calls out of JIT code; every caller-saved register is clobbered.
    pub is_call: bool,
    /// The locations it may read and write, beyond its inputs and outputs.
    pub reads: Locations,
    pub writes: Locations,
    /// May run other code (which may write any location), or invalidate
    /// the compiled code (see `Dependency`).
    pub runs_code: bool,
    pub allocates: bool,
}

impl NodeProperties {
    pub(super) const PURE: Self = Self {
        can_lazy_exit: false,
        is_call: false,
        reads: Locations::NONE,
        writes: Locations::NONE,
        runs_code: false,
        allocates: false,
    };

    /// Reads `reads` and has no other effect.
    const fn reading(reads: Locations) -> Self {
        Self { reads, ..Self::PURE }
    }

    /// Writes `writes` and has no other effect.
    const fn writing(writes: Locations) -> Self {
        Self { writes, ..Self::PURE }
    }

    /// Calls out of JIT code and has no other effect: it only computes its value.
    const CALL: Self = Self {
        is_call: true,
        ..Self::PURE
    };

    /// Calls out of JIT code, which may allocate.
    const ALLOCATING_CALL: Self = Self {
        is_call: true,
        allocates: true,
        ..Self::PURE
    };

    /// Stores or adds a named property through a cache.
    const STORE_PROBE: Self = Self {
        reads: Locations::NAMED,
        writes: Locations::NAMED,
        allocates: true,
        ..Self::PURE
    };

    /// Runs code of the program: a call that may do anything and exit after it returns.
    const RUNS_ANYTHING: Self = Self {
        can_lazy_exit: true,
        is_call: true,
        reads: Locations::ALL,
        writes: Locations::ALL,
        runs_code: true,
        allocates: true,
    };
}

/// The inputs an op takes, which the verifier checks every node against.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Inputs {
    /// Exactly these, in this order.
    Exactly(&'static [Repr]),
    /// These, then any number of `rest`.
    AtLeast(&'static [Repr], Repr),
    /// The first ones, then either none or all of the others.
    WithOptional(&'static [Repr], &'static [Repr]),
    /// The receiver and the arguments of the intrinsic's `HelperCall`.
    HelperCall(Intrinsic),
    /// Not checked by their representations: phis take one input per predecessor, of their own representation (which
    /// the verifier checks with the predecessors), constants take none, and `StoreSlot` stores any value.
    Unchecked,
}

impl Inputs {
    const NONE: Self = Self::Exactly(&[]);
    const TAGGED: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged]);
    const TAGGED_2: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged]);
    const TAGGED_3: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged]);
    const INT32: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Int32]);
    const INT32_2: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Int32, Repr::Int32]);
    const FLOAT64: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Float64]);
    const FLOAT64_2: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Float64, Repr::Float64]);
    const BOOL: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Bool]);
    const POINTER: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer]);
    const POINTER_2: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Pointer]);
    const POINTER_INT32: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32]);
    /// An object and its `CellAddress`.
    const OBJECT: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Pointer]);
    /// An object, a value and the object's `CellAddress`.
    const OBJECT_VALUE: Self = Self::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged, Repr::Pointer]);
    /// Any number of tagged values.
    const TAGGED_ANY: Self = Self::AtLeast(&[], Repr::Tagged);
    /// An object and a key, and if the key is the key of a for-in loop's property iterator cache at an index, that
    /// cache and the index.
    const OBJECT_KEY: Self = Self::WithOptional(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged], &[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Int32]);

    /// The representations of `count` inputs, if they are of this signature, or `None` if `count` is wrong. A
    /// `HelperCall` of an intrinsic without one, and `Unchecked`, accept anything.
    pub fn reprs(self, count: usize) -> Result<Option<impl Iterator<Item = Repr>>, usize> {
        let takes = match self {
            Inputs::Exactly(reprs) if reprs.len() == count => true,
            Inputs::Exactly(reprs) => return Err(reprs.len()),
            Inputs::AtLeast(first, _) if count >= first.len() => true,
            Inputs::AtLeast(first, _) => return Err(first.len()),
            Inputs::WithOptional(first, optional) => {
                if count != first.len() && count != first.len() + optional.len() {
                    return Err(first.len());
                }
                true
            }
            Inputs::HelperCall(intrinsic) => {
                let Some(call) = intrinsic.helper_call() else {
                    return Ok(None);
                };
                if call.arguments.len() + 1 != count {
                    return Err(call.arguments.len() + 1);
                }
                true
            }
            Inputs::Unchecked => false,
        };
        Ok(takes.then(|| (0..count).map(move |index| self.repr(index))))
    }

    /// The representation of input `index`, of a count of inputs that `reprs()` accepts.
    fn repr(self, index: usize) -> Repr {
        match self {
            Inputs::Exactly(reprs) => reprs[index],
            Inputs::AtLeast(first, rest) => first.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(rest),
            Inputs::WithOptional(first, optional) => first
                .get(index)
                .copied()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| optional[index - first.len()]),
            Inputs::HelperCall(intrinsic) => {
                let call = intrinsic.helper_call().expect("the intrinsic has a helper call");
                match index {
                    0 => call.receiver.repr(),
                    _ => call.arguments[index - 1].repr(),
                }
            }
            Inputs::Unchecked => unreachable!("unchecked inputs have no representations"),
        }
    }
}

/// What the compiler knows about an op (see `Op::info()`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OpInfo {
    pub properties: NodeProperties,
    /// Why the node exits to the interpreter, if it can exit eagerly: before its side effects, resuming at the
    /// current bytecode.
    pub exit_kind: Option<ExitKind>,
    /// For checks and refinements, whose value is an input known to pass them: which input that is (see
    /// "Refinements" in `Op`).
    pub refined_input: Option<usize>,
    /// Whether it ends its block (see `Op::successors()`).
    pub is_control: bool,
    /// Whether its value is never the empty value (see `Graph::is_known_non_empty()`, which decides constants, slots
    /// and phis itself). False is always safe.
    pub never_empty: bool,
    pub inputs: Inputs,
}

impl OpInfo {
    /// An op without effects or exits, taking `inputs`.
    const fn pure(inputs: Inputs) -> Self {
        Self {
            properties: NodeProperties::PURE,
            exit_kind: None,
            refined_input: None,
            is_control: false,
            never_empty: false,
            inputs,
        }
    }

    /// A check of input 0 that exits with `kind` where it fails, and has that input, refined, as its value.
    const fn check(kind: ExitKind, inputs: Inputs) -> Self {
        Self {
            exit_kind: Some(kind),
            refined_input: Some(0),
            ..Self::pure(inputs)
        }
    }

    /// A control node taking `inputs`.
    const fn control(inputs: Inputs) -> Self {
        Self {
            is_control: true,
            ..Self::pure(inputs)
        }
    }

    const fn with_properties(self, properties: NodeProperties) -> Self {
        Self { properties, ..self }
    }

    const fn exiting(self, kind: ExitKind) -> Self {
        Self {
            exit_kind: Some(kind),
            ..self
        }
    }

    const fn never_empty(self) -> Self {
        Self {
            never_empty: true,
            ..self
        }
    }
}

impl Op<'_> {
    /// What the compiler knows about the op.
    pub fn info(&self) -> OpInfo {
        use Inputs as I;
        use NodeProperties as P;
        match self {
            Op::Constant(_) | Op::Phi => OpInfo::pure(I::Unchecked),
            Op::LoadSlot { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::FRAME)),
            Op::StoreSlot { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::Unchecked).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::FRAME)),
            Op::InitializeFrame | Op::EnsureFrameInitialized | Op::PublishFrame => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::FRAME))
            }
            // NB: It hands the frame's slots to the code that resumes it.
            Op::Suspend { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::FRAME,
                writes: Locations::FRAME,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::LoadOuterEnvironment | Op::BoxCell => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER),
            Op::LoadEnvironmentBinding { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::BINDINGS.union(Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS))),
            Op::StoreEnvironmentBinding { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Tagged]))
                .with_properties(P::writing(Locations::BINDINGS.union(Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS))),
            Op::AppendEnvironmentBinding => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER)
                .with_properties(P::writing(Locations::BINDINGS.union(Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS))),
            Op::SetLexicalEnvironment => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::FRAME,
                writes: Locations::FRAME,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::LeavePrivateEnvironment | Op::KeepOwnEnvironments => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::FRAME,
                writes: Locations::FRAME,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::IsCallable => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).never_empty(),
            Op::ToBoolean => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).with_properties(P::CALL),
            Op::PrimitiveToString => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).with_properties(P::ALLOCATING_CALL),
            Op::CallIntrinsic { intrinsic } => {
                let call = intrinsic
                    .helper_call()
                    .expect("intrinsics called through a helper have one");
                // NB: Helpers that answer with a number or a boolean make no
                //     cells.
                OpInfo::pure(I::HelperCall(*intrinsic)).with_properties(P {
                    is_call: true,
                    allocates: matches!(call.result, HelperResult::String | HelperResult::Value),
                    reads: call.reads,
                    writes: call.writes,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
            }
            Op::CallArraySplice => OpInfo::pure(I::AtLeast(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Int32, Repr::Int32], Repr::Tagged))
                .with_properties(P {
                    is_call: true,
                    allocates: true,
                    reads: Locations::NAMED.union(Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS),
                    writes: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                    ..P::PURE
                }),
            Op::ToObject => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P::ALLOCATING_CALL),
            Op::ArrayCreate => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Int32, Repr::Tagged])).with_properties(P::ALLOCATING_CALL)
            }
            Op::Generic { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P::RUNS_ANYTHING),
            // NB: Calls return values, never the empty value.
            Op::CallDirect { .. } | Op::CallNative { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_ANY)
                .with_properties(P::RUNS_ANYTHING)
                .never_empty(),
            Op::CallNativeAccessor { part, .. } => {
                let inputs = match part {
                    super::AccessorPart::Getter => I::TAGGED,
                    super::AccessorPart::Setter => I::TAGGED_2,
                };
                OpInfo::pure(inputs).with_properties(P::RUNS_ANYTHING)
            }
            Op::ArgumentCount => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::FRAME))
                .never_empty(),
            Op::LoadFrameField { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::FRAME)),
            Op::LoadArgument { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::FRAME))
                .exiting(ExitKind::ArgumentsIndex)
                .never_empty(),
            Op::CallForwardingArguments { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE).with_properties(P::RUNS_ANYTHING),
            Op::CheckInt32 => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).exiting(ExitKind::NotInt32),
            Op::CheckNumber => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).exiting(ExitKind::BadType),
            Op::BoxInt32 => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32).never_empty(),
            Op::BoxBool => OpInfo::pure(I::BOOL).never_empty(),
            Op::Int32Binary { op } => {
                let info = OpInfo::pure(I::INT32_2);
                if op.int32_can_overflow() {
                    info.exiting(ExitKind::Overflow)
                } else {
                    info
                }
            }
            Op::Int32WrappingBinary { .. } | Op::Int32Compare { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32_2),
            Op::TaggedEquals { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2),
            // NB: The elements kind of a typed array never changes.
            Op::CheckElements {
                kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(_),
            } => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadElements, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckElements { .. } => {
                OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadElements, I::TAGGED).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ELEMENT_COUNTS))
            }
            Op::CheckTypedArray => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadElements, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckArray => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadType, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckPropertyAbsenceCacheable => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadShape, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32 => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::Overflow, I::INT32),
            Op::LoadTypedArrayLength | Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ELEMENT_COUNTS))
            }
            Op::TypedArrayDataAddress => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER),
            Op::CheckTypedArrayStorage => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::OutOfBounds, I::POINTER),
            Op::CheckBounds => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::OutOfBounds, I::INT32_2),
            Op::LoadElementAt { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER_INT32).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ELEMENTS)),
            // NB: Stores within the bounds change no element count.
            Op::StoreElementAt { kind } => {
                let inputs = match kind.stored_repr() {
                    Repr::Float64 => I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32, Repr::Float64]),
                    Repr::Int32 => I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32, Repr::Int32]),
                    _ => I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32, Repr::Tagged]),
                };
                OpInfo::pure(inputs).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::ELEMENTS))
            }
            Op::CheckNotHole => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::OutOfBounds, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckInitialized => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::Uninitialized, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CellAddress => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            Op::AllocateObject { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P {
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .never_empty(),
            Op::InitializeNamed { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::NAMED_SLOTS)),
            // NB: Virtual objects are in no block, so the verifier sees no inputs of theirs.
            Op::VirtualObject { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::Unchecked),
            Op::AllocateArray { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P {
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .never_empty(),
            Op::InitializeElement { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::ELEMENTS)),
            Op::AllocateFunction { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER_2)
                .with_properties(P {
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .never_empty(),
            Op::AllocateEnvironment { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED)
                .with_properties(P {
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .never_empty(),
            Op::SliceArguments => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED)
                .with_properties(P {
                    is_call: true,
                    reads: Locations::FRAME,
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .exiting(ExitKind::ArgumentsIndex)
                .never_empty(),
            Op::CheckIdentityComparable => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadType, I::TAGGED_2),
            Op::CheckObject => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::NotObject, I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckClosure { .. } => OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadCallTarget, I::TAGGED),
            Op::LoadFunctionEnvironment { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER),
            Op::CheckValue { kind, .. } => OpInfo::check(*kind, I::TAGGED),
            Op::EmptyToUndefined | Op::Typeof => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).never_empty(),
            Op::TypeofIs { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            Op::CheckShape { .. } => {
                OpInfo::check(ExitKind::BadShape, I::OBJECT).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::SHAPES))
            }
            Op::CheckPrototypeChainValid { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::SHAPES))
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadShape),
            Op::HasInPrototypeChain => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::SHAPES))
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadType),
            // NB: Reading everything keeps loops whose code may invalidate
            //     the code from hoisting it.
            Op::AssumeValid | Op::AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ALL))
                .exiting(ExitKind::Invalidated),
            Op::CheckInterrupt => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P::writing(Locations::INTERRUPT))
                .exiting(ExitKind::Interrupted),
            Op::LoadGlobalBinding { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::NONE)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS))
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadShape),
            Op::StoreGlobalBinding { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED)
                .with_properties(P {
                    reads: Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS,
                    writes: Locations::GLOBAL_BINDINGS,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadShape),
            Op::CheckAccessorFunction { .. } => {
                OpInfo::check(ExitKind::UnexpectedValue, I::OBJECT).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::NAMED_SLOTS))
            }
            Op::LoadAccessorFunction { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::NAMED_SLOTS))
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadCallTarget),
            Op::LoadNamed { holds_data, .. } => {
                let info = OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::NAMED_SLOTS));
                if *holds_data {
                    info
                } else {
                    info.exiting(ExitKind::BadShape)
                }
            }
            Op::AddNamed { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT_VALUE).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::NAMED,
                writes: Locations::NAMED,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            // NB: Stores to a property an object has change no shape.
            Op::StoreNamed { holds_data, .. } => {
                let info = OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT_VALUE).with_properties(P {
                    reads: Locations::NAMED_SLOTS,
                    writes: Locations::NAMED_SLOTS,
                    ..P::PURE
                });
                if *holds_data {
                    info
                } else {
                    info.exiting(ExitKind::BadShape)
                }
            }
            Op::Jump { .. } | Op::Unreachable => OpInfo::control(I::NONE),
            Op::Branch { condition, .. } => OpInfo::control(I::Exactly(condition.input_reprs())),
            Op::BranchTruthy { .. } | Op::Return => OpInfo::control(I::TAGGED),
            Op::BranchOnPc { .. } => OpInfo::control(I::INT32),
            Op::ShapeSwitch { .. } => OpInfo::control(I::OBJECT)
                .with_properties(P::reading(Locations::SHAPES))
                .exiting(ExitKind::BadShape),
            Op::Exit { kind } => OpInfo::control(I::NONE).exiting(*kind),
            Op::Refine { condition, .. } => OpInfo {
                refined_input: Some(0),
                ..OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(condition.input_reprs()))
            },
            Op::CallSlowPath {
                saves_registers: false,
                opcode,
                ..
            } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_ANY).with_properties(
                Op::Generic {
                    opcode: *opcode,
                    executable: 0,
                    pc: 0,
                }
                .properties(),
            ),
            // NB: The slow path saves the registers it clobbers, so the node
            //     is not a call for the register allocator.
            Op::CallSlowPath { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_ANY).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::ALL,
                writes: Locations::ALL,
                runs_code: true,
                allocates: true,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::UnboxInt32 | Op::UnboxDouble => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            Op::Int32Abs | Op::Int32ToFloat64 => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32),
            Op::Int32Min | Op::Int32Max | Op::Uint32Min | Op::Uint32ShiftRight => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32_2),
            Op::BoolToInt32 => OpInfo::pure(I::BOOL),
            Op::BoxFloat64 => OpInfo::pure(I::FLOAT64).never_empty(),
            Op::Float64Unary { .. } | Op::Float64ToInt32 | Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped => OpInfo::pure(I::FLOAT64),
            Op::Float64Binary { .. } | Op::Float64Min | Op::Float64Max | Op::Float64Compare { .. } => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::FLOAT64_2)
            }
            Op::CallFloat64Function { function } => {
                let inputs = match function.argument_count() {
                    1 => I::FLOAT64,
                    _ => I::FLOAT64_2,
                };
                OpInfo::pure(inputs).with_properties(P::CALL)
            }
            Op::CheckFloat64Int32 => OpInfo::pure(I::FLOAT64).exiting(ExitKind::NotInt32),
            Op::Uint32ToFloat64 => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32),
            Op::StringAddress => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            // NB: Strings never change. These take the refinements of the
            //     checks they rely on as inputs.
            Op::StringLength => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER),
            Op::LoadStringCodeUnit => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER_INT32),
            Op::SingleCharacterString => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32),
            // NB: A cache miss and strings whose characters only the slow
            //     path reads stay that way until the slow path ran.
            Op::StringsEqual => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2),
            Op::ConcatenateStrings { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P {
                allocates: true,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::IntegerToString => OpInfo::pure(I::INT32),
            // NB: It reads the shapes and the indexed properties of the
            //     prototypes too.
            Op::CheckAppendableArray => {
                OpInfo::check(ExitKind::SlowPath, I::TAGGED).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ALL))
            }
            Op::LoadElementsLength | Op::LoadElementsCapacity => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ELEMENT_COUNTS))
            }
            Op::AppendElement => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32, Repr::Tagged])).with_properties(P {
                    reads: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                    writes: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                    ..P::PURE
                })
            }
            Op::CallArrayPush => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                writes: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                allocates: true,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::CallStoreHoleyElement => OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Pointer, Repr::Int32, Repr::Tagged]))
                .with_properties(P {
                    reads: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                    writes: Locations::ELEMENTS_AND_COUNTS,
                    allocates: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                }),
            // NB: The runtime watches the intrinsics anew with new watchpoint sets once the old ones fired.
            Op::OpenArrayIteration => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).with_properties(P {
                reads: Locations::ALL,
                allocates: true,
                ..P::PURE
            }),
            Op::LoadArrayIteratorArray
            | Op::LoadArrayIteratorIndex
            | Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionType
            | Op::LoadGeneratorCompletionValue => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ITERATORS))
            }
            Op::StoreArrayIteratorIndex => {
                OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER_INT32).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::ITERATORS))
            }
            Op::FinishArrayIterator => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER).with_properties(P::writing(Locations::ITERATORS)),
            // NB: The keys of a cache never change.
            Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKeyCount => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            Op::LoadPropertyIteratorKey => OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Int32])),
            // NB: The slow path call leaves its outputs where the node reads
            //     them, so it stays right after the call (which the verifier
            //     checks). Its input, the call, ties it there.
            Op::SlowPathOutput { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED),
            Op::ProbePropertyCache { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::NAMED)),
            Op::ProbeKeyedCache { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT_KEY).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::NAMED)),
            // NB: Additions may grow the object's storage.
            Op::ProbePropertyStore { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_2).with_properties(P::STORE_PROBE),
            Op::ProbeKeyedStore { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::TAGGED_3).with_properties(P::STORE_PROBE),
            // NB: Global variables are properties of the global object and
            //     bindings of the global declarative environment.
            Op::ProbeGlobalCache { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::POINTER_2).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ALL)),
            Op::ProbeGlobalStore { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::Exactly(&[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Pointer, Repr::Pointer]))
                .with_properties(P {
                    reads: Locations::ALL,
                    writes: Locations::ALL,
                    runs_code: true,
                    ..P::PURE
                }),
            Op::ProbeHasProperty { .. } => OpInfo::pure(I::OBJECT_KEY).with_properties(P::reading(Locations::ALL)),
        }
    }

    pub fn properties(&self) -> NodeProperties {
        self.info().properties
    }

    /// Why this node exits to the interpreter, if it can exit eagerly.
    pub fn exit_kind(&self) -> Option<ExitKind> {
        self.info().exit_kind
    }

    /// Whether the node may exit to the interpreter before its side effects,
    /// resuming at the current bytecode: whether it has an exit kind.
    pub fn can_eager_exit(&self) -> bool {
        self.exit_kind().is_some()
    }

    /// For checks and refinements, whose value is an input known to pass
    /// them: which input that is (see "Refinements" in `Op`).
    pub fn refined_input(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.info().refined_input
    }

    pub fn is_control(&self) -> bool {
        self.info().is_control
    }
}

impl BranchCondition {
    /// The representations of the inputs a branch on the condition (and a `Refine` of it) takes.
    pub fn input_reprs(self) -> &'static [Repr] {
        match self {
            BranchCondition::Bool => &[Repr::Bool],
            BranchCondition::Nullish
            | BranchCondition::Undefined
            | BranchCondition::Object
            | BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32
            | BranchCondition::ElementsKind(_)
            | BranchCondition::Int32Value
            | BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean
            | BranchCondition::Double
            | BranchCondition::String
            | BranchCondition::Builtin(_) => &[Repr::Tagged],
            BranchCondition::IndexInBounds | BranchCondition::Int32(_) => &[Repr::Int32, Repr::Int32],
            BranchCondition::MagicalLength
            | BranchCondition::Extensible
            | BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray
            | BranchCondition::ArrayIterator
            | BranchCondition::GeneratorObject
            | BranchCondition::PlainArrayPrototypeChain
            | BranchCondition::ArrayWithRealmArrayPrototypeAndNoNamedProperties
            | BranchCondition::HoldsValidWatchpointSet
            | BranchCondition::ResolvedString
            | BranchCondition::BindingMutable { .. }
            | BranchCondition::NextBindingOfShape { .. } => &[Repr::Pointer],
            BranchCondition::Shape(_) => &[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Pointer],
            BranchCondition::Float64(_) => &[Repr::Float64, Repr::Float64],
            BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { .. } | BranchCondition::PropertyIteratorCacheValid => {
                &[Repr::Tagged, Repr::Tagged]
            }
        }
    }
}
