        /// did. Other values than objects are not stored to. `property` is the
        /// index of the property's name in the executable's property key table,
        /// or `u32::MAX` for puts of another kind than a normal one:
        /// megamorphic caches with one also look in the VM's keyed store cache,
        /// which the runtime fills for them.
        ProbePropertyStore {
            executable: u32,
            cache: u32,
            property: u32,
        },
        /// Stores input 2 into the writable own data property that the string or
        /// symbol input 1 names on the object in input 0 (or adds it), where
        /// keyed property lookup cache `cache` of executable `executable` or the
        /// VM's keyed store cache has it, as a `Repr::Bool` telling whether it
        /// did.
        ProbeKeyedStore {
            executable: u32,
            cache: u32,
        },
        /// The global variable that global variable cache `cache` of the
        /// executable in input 1 is for, like the interpreter's `GetGlobal`
        /// handler finds it with the realm in input 0 (both `Repr::Pointer`
        /// frame fields): a data property of the
        /// global object of the cached shape, or an initialized binding of the
        /// global declarative environment, while the environment has the cached
        /// serial number. The empty value where the cache does not apply.
        ProbeGlobalCache {
            cache: u32,
        },
        /// Stores input 0 into the global variable that global variable cache
        /// `cache` of the executable in input 2 is for, with the realm in input
        /// 1 (both `Repr::Pointer` frame fields), like the interpreter's
        /// `SetGlobal` handler: a writable data
        /// property or an initialized mutable binding. A `Repr::Bool` telling
        /// whether it did.
        ProbeGlobalStore {
            cache: u32,
        },
        /// Whether the object in input 0 has the property that the key in input
        /// 1 names, as its own (`own`, like `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty`)
        /// or in its prototype chain too (like `in`), as a tagged boolean, where
        /// the VM can tell without running code (from its keyed lookup cache,
        /// the elements, or the runtime's lookup of objects whose lookups run no
        /// code). The empty value otherwise, and for other values than objects.
        /// Like `ProbeKeyedCache`, it may have a for-in loop's property
        /// iterator cache and index as inputs 2 and 3, which tell for own
        /// properties of objects of the cache's shape.
        ProbeHasProperty {
            own: bool,
        },
    }
}

/// What `Op::Float64Unary` computes. Floor, Ceil and Round are those of
/// `Math`: Round rounds halves up, and zeros keep the sign of the input.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Float64UnaryOp {
    Abs,
    Negate,
    Floor,
    Ceil,
    Round,
    Sqrt,
}

impl Float64UnaryOp {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Float64UnaryOp::Abs => "Abs",
            Float64UnaryOp::Negate => "Negate",
            Float64UnaryOp::Floor => "Floor",
            Float64UnaryOp::Ceil => "Ceil",
            Float64UnaryOp::Round => "Round",
            Float64UnaryOp::Sqrt => "Sqrt",
        }
    }
}

/// What `Op::CallFloat64Function` computes: the `Math` function of that
/// name, of numbers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Float64Function {
    Exp,
    Log,
    Sin,
    Cos,
    Tan,
    Pow,
}

impl Float64Function {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Float64Function::Exp => "Exp",
            Float64Function::Log => "Log",
            Float64Function::Sin => "Sin",
            Float64Function::Cos => "Cos",
            Float64Function::Tan => "Tan",
            Float64Function::Pow => "Pow",
        }
    }

    /// How many numbers the function takes.
    pub fn argument_count(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Float64Function::Pow => 2,
            _ => 1,
        }
    }
}

impl<'z> Op<'z> {
    /// The blocks a control node can continue at.
    pub fn successors(&self) -> Successors<'z> {
        let inline = |blocks: &[BlockId]| {
            let mut inline = [BlockId(0); 3];
            inline[..blocks.len()].copy_from_slice(blocks);
            Successors::Inline {
                blocks: inline,
                count: blocks.len() as u8,
            }
        };
        match self {
            Op::Jump { target } => inline(&[*target]),
            Op::Branch { if_true, if_false, .. } | Op::BranchOnPc { if_true, if_false, .. } => {
                inline(&[*if_true, *if_false])
            }
            Op::BranchTruthy {
                if_true,
                if_false,
                fallback,
            } => inline(&[*if_true, *if_false, *fallback]),
            Op::ShapeSwitch { targets, .. } => Successors::Cases(targets),
            _ => inline(&[]),
        }
    }

    /// Calls `visit` with each block a control node can continue at, in the order of `successors()`.
    pub fn for_each_successor(&self, mut visit: impl FnMut(BlockId)) {
        match self {
            Op::Jump { target } => visit(*target),
            Op::Branch { if_true, if_false, .. } | Op::BranchOnPc { if_true, if_false, .. } => {
                visit(*if_true);
                visit(*if_false);
            }
            Op::BranchTruthy {
                if_true,
                if_false,
                fallback,
            } => {
                visit(*if_true);
                visit(*if_false);
                visit(*fallback);
            }
            Op::ShapeSwitch { targets, .. } => {
                for block in *targets {
                    visit(*block);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Makes a control node continue at `map(block)` where it continued at `block`. A shape switch that changes
    /// gets its new list of blocks from `zone`.
    fn map_successors(&mut self, zone: &'z Zone, map: impl Fn(BlockId) -> BlockId) {
        match self {
            Op::Jump { target } => *target = map(*target),
            Op::Branch { if_true, if_false, .. } | Op::BranchOnPc { if_true, if_false, .. } => {
                *if_true = map(*if_true);
                *if_false = map(*if_false);
            }
            Op::BranchTruthy {
                if_true,
                if_false,
                fallback,
            } => {
                *if_true = map(*if_true);
                *if_false = map(*if_false);
                *fallback = map(*fallback);
            }
            Op::ShapeSwitch { targets, .. } if targets.iter().any(|block| map(*block) != *block) => {
                *targets = zone.alloc_slice_from_iter(targets.iter().map(|block| map(*block)));
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

/// The blocks a control node can continue at (see `Op::successors()`):
/// those of jumps and branches inline, and the cases of shape switches.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Successors<'z> {
    Inline { blocks: [BlockId; 3], count: u8 },
    Cases(&'z [BlockId]),
}

impl core::ops::Deref for Successors<'_> {
    type Target = [BlockId];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[BlockId] {
        match self {
            Successors::Inline { blocks, count } => &blocks[..usize::from(*count)],
            Successors::Cases(blocks) => blocks,
        }
    }
}

impl<'z> IntoIterator for Successors<'z> {
    type Item = BlockId;
    type IntoIter = SuccessorsIntoIter<'z>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> SuccessorsIntoIter<'z> {
        SuccessorsIntoIter {
            successors: self,
            next: 0,
        }
    }
}

pub struct SuccessorsIntoIter<'z> {
    successors: Successors<'z>,
    next: usize,
}

impl Iterator for SuccessorsIntoIter<'_> {
    type Item = BlockId;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<BlockId> {
        let block = self.successors.get(self.next).copied()?;
        self.next += 1;
        Some(block)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Node<'z> {
    pub op: Op<'z>,
    pub inputs: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>,
    /// The representation of the value this node produces, if it produces one.
    pub repr: Option<Repr>,
    /// The interpreter state to rebuild if this node exits.
    pub frame_state: Option<FrameStateId>,
    /// The bytecode offset of the instruction this node was built for.
    pub pc: u32,
}

impl<'z> Node<'z> {
    /// A node without a frame state.
    pub fn new(op: Op<'z>, inputs: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>, repr: Option<Repr>, pc: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            op,
            inputs,
            repr,
            frame_state: None,
            pc,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Block<'z> {
    pub predecessors: ZoneVec<'z, BlockId>,
    pub phis: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>,
    pub body: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>,
    /// The control node ending this block. Every finished block has one.
    pub control: Option<NodeId>,
    /// The bytecode offset of the first instruction, for blocks that start a
    /// bytecode basic block. Blocks the builder adds on control flow edges
    /// have none.
    pub bytecode_start: Option<u32>,
    pub is_loop_header: bool,
    /// Code that rarely runs, like the slow path of an instruction: code
    /// generation puts cold blocks after all other blocks, and the register
    /// allocator keeps the other blocks' values where they are on the
    /// edges into and out of them.
    pub is_cold: bool,
    /// For merges and loop headers of the compiled function that start a
    /// bytecode block, the frame state at their start, which checks of the
    /// values entering them exit with (see `edit::frame_state_entering()`).
    /// Passes forget it once frame states are final.
    pub start_frame_state: Option<FrameStateId>,
}

impl<'z> Block<'z> {
    /// A block with no nodes and no predecessors, whose lists are in `zone`.
    pub fn new_in(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            predecessors: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            phis: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            body: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            control: None,
            bytecode_start: None,
            is_loop_header: false,
            is_cold: false,
            start_frame_state: None,
        }
    }

    /// The block's nodes, in order: its phis, its body and its control node.
    pub fn nodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> + '_ {
        self.phis.iter().chain(&self.body).chain(&self.control).copied()
    }
}

/// The interpreter state of a frame at a point where compiled code may exit.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FrameState<'z> {
    /// Index into `Snapshot::executables`.
    pub executable: u32,
    pub pc: u32,
    pub mode: ResumeMode,
    /// The SSA value of every live frame slot (a flat operand index) whose
    /// frame memory does not already hold it, in slot order. Frames of
    /// inlined calls have no memory, so they list every live slot.
    pub values: ZoneVec<'z, (u32, NodeId)>,
    /// The live frame slots whose value frame memory holds: the compiled
    /// function's slots that are in sync, and the slots a slow path in an
    /// inlined callee wrote into the frames pushed for it. With `values`,
    /// every live slot is listed once. The destination of a `ResumeAfter`
    /// frame state is listed with the value it had before the instruction:
    /// where the instruction did not continue (it threw, or its callee runs
    /// in the interpreter and writes it when it returns), that is what the
    /// frame needs. Exits after the instruction keep what it wrote.
    pub in_frame: ZoneVec<'z, u32>,
    /// For frames of inlined calls, the frame state of the caller: resuming
    /// after its `Call` instruction, with the call's result in `dst`.
    pub parent: Option<FrameStateId>,
    /// For a caller at an inlined call that passes the callee other
    /// arguments than its `Call` instruction's (a call forwarded through
    /// `Function.prototype.apply` or `call`, or a bound function): how many.
    pub passed_argument_count: Option<u32>,
    /// The argument slots whose values code that calls in the frame run can
    /// read through the legacy `arguments` of the frame's function. Only
    /// frames of inlined calls of functions that are not strict have them.
    pub legacy_arguments: core::ops::Range<u32>,
}

/// The memory of all the lists of a graph is in one zone (see `ak::Zone`): a graph makes no block of the heap, and
/// all of it goes away when its zone is reset.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Graph<'z> {
    /// Where the lists of the graph are, and where its nodes, blocks and frame states get their lists.
    pub zone: &'z Zone,
    /// Every node the graph ever had: passes remove nodes from blocks, never from here.
    pub nodes: ZoneVec<'z, Node<'z>>,
    /// Blocks in linear order. Block 0 is the entry, and every block comes
    /// after all its predecessors except those reaching it over a loop back
    /// edge, and cold ones once the passes moved cold blocks last.
    pub blocks: ZoneVec<'z, Block<'z>>,
    pub frame_states: ZoneVec<'z, FrameState<'z>>,
    /// Cells the graph compares against or reads from (shapes, prototype
    /// holders, validity cells, inlined functions). The code is only valid
    /// while they live.
    pub embedded_cells: ZoneVec<'z, CellId>,
    /// What the code assumes keeps holding where it has `Op::AssumeValid`
    /// nodes (see `Dependency`).
    pub dependencies: ZoneVec<'z, crate::code::Dependency>,
    /// The shapes from the snapshot that were stable, which check
    /// elimination may make the code depend on.
    pub stable_shapes: ZoneVec<'z, CellId>,
    /// Immutable properties of embedded typed arrays. Their fixed lengths
    /// require a valid cached storage offset before each access.
    pub typed_array_constants: ZoneVec<'z, (u64, crate::snapshot::TypedArraySnapshot)>,
    /// The targets of `Op::CallDirect` nodes that call function constants.
    pub direct_call_targets: ZoneVec<'z, crate::snapshot::DirectCallTarget>,
    /// The most bytes of interpreter stack that materializing the frames of
    /// inlined calls, and the frames of direct and native calls on top of
    /// them, take at once. Compiled code checks at entry that they fit.
    pub materialized_frame_bytes: u64,
    /// On-stack replacement entries: blocks without predecessors where code
    /// already running in the interpreter enters compiled code, with the pc
    /// each one starts at: a loop back edge, the continuation of a generator,
    /// or the instruction after the `Catch` of an exception handler. The frame
    /// holds every value.
    pub osr_entries: ZoneVec<'z, (u32, BlockId)>,
    /// The pcs of the loop back edges in the loops of the on-stack
    /// replacement entries (including those of the entries), from where a
    /// frame running in the interpreter reaches an entry.
    pub osr_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec<'z, u32>,
    /// The pcs of the loop back edges in the loops around the loops of the
    /// on-stack replacement entries, from where a frame running in the
    /// interpreter may reach an entry on a later iteration.
    pub osr_outer_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec<'z, u32>,
    /// The pcs of the `Catch` of the exception handlers that got no catch
    /// entry because they never caught an exception before the compile (see
    /// `builder::osr`). A compile after they caught gives them one.
    pub uncaught_handlers: ZoneVec<'z, u32>,
    /// The register-saving `CallSlowPath` nodes that may run before the
    /// frame is initialized, and so initialize it first if it is not.
    pub slow_paths_initializing_frame: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>,
    /// Where exits of each executable were taken before, as (executable,
    /// pc, kind), for passes that must not repeat a failed speculation.
    pub exit_sites: ZoneVec<'z, (u32, u32, ExitKind)>,
    /// The nodes that loop invariant code motion moved out of blocks that not
    /// every iteration of their loop runs, which exit with
    /// `ExitKind::Hoisted` instead of their own kind of exit.
    pub speculatively_hoisted: ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>,
    /// The argument slots of the compiled function that its legacy
    /// `arguments` shows. Empty for functions without legacy `arguments`.
    pub legacy_arguments: core::ops::Range<u32>,
    /// The `AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread` nodes, each with the nodes of its
    /// instruction that run code.
    pub legacy_arguments_guards: ZoneVec<'z, (NodeId, ZoneVec<'z, NodeId>)>,
    /// The slots of the compiled function (as operands) whose frame memory holds the value the function started with
    /// wherever its code runs: the arguments and the `this` value register, unless an instruction writes them. Nothing
    /// stores to them (the verifier enforces this), so the register allocator reloads what was loaded from them from
    /// there (see `regalloc::frame_home()`).
    pub unwritten_slots: ak::ZoneBitSet<'z>,
}

impl<'z> Graph<'z> {
    /// A graph with nothing in it, whose lists are in `zone`.
    pub fn new_in(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            zone,
            nodes: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            blocks: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            frame_states: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            embedded_cells: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            dependencies: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            stable_shapes: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            typed_array_constants: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            direct_call_targets: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            materialized_frame_bytes: 0,
            osr_entries: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            osr_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            osr_outer_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            uncaught_handlers: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            slow_paths_initializing_frame: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            exit_sites: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            speculatively_hoisted: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
            legacy_arguments_guards: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            unwritten_slots: ak::ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, zone),
        }
    }

    /// A copy of the graph, whose lists are in `zone`.
    pub fn clone_in<'c>(&self, zone: &'c Zone) -> Graph<'c>
    where
        'z: 'c,
    {
        let Graph {
            zone: _,
            nodes,
            blocks,
            frame_states,
            embedded_cells,
            dependencies,
            stable_shapes,
            typed_array_constants,
            direct_call_targets,
            materialized_frame_bytes,
            osr_entries,
            osr_loop_back_edges,
            osr_outer_loop_back_edges,
            uncaught_handlers,
            slow_paths_initializing_frame,
            exit_sites,
            speculatively_hoisted,
            legacy_arguments,
            legacy_arguments_guards,
            unwritten_slots,
        } = self;
        let list = |values: &[NodeId]| ZoneVec::from_slice_in(values, zone);
        let mut unwritten = ak::ZoneBitSet::new_in(unwritten_slots.capacity(), zone);
        unwritten.union_with(unwritten_slots);
        Graph {
            zone,
            nodes: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
                nodes.iter().map(|node| Node {
                    op: node.op.clone(),
                    inputs: list(&node.inputs),
                    repr: node.repr,
                    frame_state: node.frame_state,
                    pc: node.pc,
                }),
                zone,
            ),
            blocks: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
                blocks.iter().map(|block| Block {
                    predecessors: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&block.predecessors, zone),
                    phis: list(&block.phis),
                    body: list(&block.body),
                    control: block.control,
                    bytecode_start: block.bytecode_start,
                    is_loop_header: block.is_loop_header,
                    is_cold: block.is_cold,
                    start_frame_state: block.start_frame_state,
                }),
                zone,
            ),
            frame_states: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
                frame_states.iter().map(|frame_state| FrameState {
                    executable: frame_state.executable,
                    pc: frame_state.pc,
                    mode: frame_state.mode,
                    values: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&frame_state.values, zone),
                    in_frame: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&frame_state.in_frame, zone),
                    parent: frame_state.parent,
                    passed_argument_count: frame_state.passed_argument_count,
                    legacy_arguments: frame_state.legacy_arguments.clone(),
                }),
                zone,
            ),
            embedded_cells: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(embedded_cells, zone),
            dependencies: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(dependencies, zone),
            stable_shapes: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(stable_shapes, zone),
            typed_array_constants: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(typed_array_constants, zone),
            direct_call_targets: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(direct_call_targets, zone),
            materialized_frame_bytes: *materialized_frame_bytes,
            osr_entries: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(osr_entries, zone),
            osr_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(osr_loop_back_edges, zone),
            osr_outer_loop_back_edges: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(osr_outer_loop_back_edges, zone),
            uncaught_handlers: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(uncaught_handlers, zone),
            slow_paths_initializing_frame: list(slow_paths_initializing_frame),
            exit_sites: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(exit_sites, zone),
            speculatively_hoisted: list(speculatively_hoisted),
            legacy_arguments: legacy_arguments.clone(),
            legacy_arguments_guards: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
                legacy_arguments_guards
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(guard, nodes)| (*guard, list(nodes))),
                zone,
            ),
            unwritten_slots: unwritten,
        }
    }

    /// A list of `values` in the memory of the graph.
    pub fn list<T: Clone>(&self, values: &[T]) -> ZoneVec<'z, T> {
        ZoneVec::from_slice_in(values, self.zone)
    }

    /// A block with no nodes and no predecessors, whose lists are in the memory of the graph.
    pub fn new_block(&self) -> Block<'z> {
        Block::new_in(self.zone)
    }

    /// Adds a node with `inputs` and no frame state.
    pub fn add(&mut self, op: Op<'z>, inputs: &[NodeId], repr: Option<Repr>, pc: u32) -> NodeId {
        let inputs = self.list(inputs);
        self.add_node(Node::new(op, inputs, repr, pc))
    }

    /// Records that the code relies on `dependency`, which makes the
    /// runtime discard the code once it no longer holds.
    pub fn depend_on(&mut self, dependency: crate::code::Dependency) {
        if !self.dependencies.contains(&dependency) {
            self.dependencies.push(dependency);
        }
    }

    pub fn node(&self, id: NodeId) -> &Node<'z> {
        &self.nodes[id.index()]
    }

    /// Whether `node` never is the empty value. `arguments` are the slots
    /// of the compiled function's arguments, which always hold values.
    pub fn is_known_non_empty(&self, node: NodeId, arguments: core::ops::Range<u32>, work: &Zone) -> bool {
        // NB: Only phis lead to other nodes, so only they are kept in `seen`.
        let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut seen = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut next = Some(node);
        while let Some(node) = next.take().or_else(|| pending.pop()) {
            if seen.contains(&node) {
                continue;
            }
            let data = self.node(node);
            if data.repr.is_some_and(|repr| repr != Repr::Tagged) {
                continue;
            }
            match &data.op {
                Op::Constant(bits) if *bits != value::EMPTY => {}
                Op::LoadSlot { slot } if arguments.contains(&crate::bytecode::Operand::from_raw(*slot).raw()) => {}
                Op::Phi => {
                    seen.push(node);
                    pending.extend(data.inputs.iter().copied());
                }
                op if op.info().never_empty => {}
                _ => return false,
            }
        }
        true
    }

    pub fn block(&self, id: BlockId) -> &Block<'z> {
        &self.blocks[id.index()]
    }

    pub fn frame_state(&self, id: FrameStateId) -> &FrameState<'z> {
        &self.frame_states[id.index()]
    }

    /// A frame state and its callers' frame states, innermost first.
    pub fn frame_state_chain(&self, id: FrameStateId) -> impl Iterator<Item = FrameStateId> + Clone + '_ {
        core::iter::successors(Some(id), |id| self.frame_state(*id).parent)
    }

    /// The values `node` uses: its inputs, then the values of its frame
    /// state.
    pub fn used_values<'a>(&'a self, node: NodeId, work: &'a Zone) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> + 'a {
        let data = self.node(node);
        data.inputs.iter().copied().chain(
            data.frame_state
                .into_iter()
                .flat_map(move |id| self.frame_state_values(id, work).map(|(_, value)| value)),
        )
    }

    /// The values that code `node` runs may read through the legacy
    /// `arguments` of the frames of its frame state chain for which
    /// `frames` holds.
    pub fn legacy_argument_values_read_by(
        &self,
        node: NodeId,
        frames: impl Fn(&FrameState<'z>) -> bool,
    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> {
        let data = self.node(node);
        let frame_state = data.frame_state.filter(|_| data.op.properties().runs_code);
        frame_state
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|frame_state| self.frame_state_chain(frame_state))
            .map(|id| self.frame_state(id))
            .filter(move |frame_state| frames(frame_state))
            .flat_map(|frame_state| {
                frame_state
                    .values
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|(slot, _)| frame_state.legacy_arguments.contains(slot))
                    .map(|(_, value)| *value)
            })
    }

    /// Whether code that `node` runs may read objects the code never
    /// allocated through the legacy `arguments` of the frames of its frame
    /// state chain, which the runtime then creates from the values of the
    /// node's site (see `Op::AssumeLegacyArgumentsUnread`).
    pub fn defers_legacy_argument_objects(&self, node: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.legacy_argument_values_read_by(node, |_| true)
            .any(|value| matches!(self.node(value).op, Op::VirtualObject { .. }))
    }

    /// The values of every frame of a frame state chain, innermost frame first.
    ///
    /// They are followed by the properties of the virtual objects among them
    /// (see `virtual_objects()`), in order, with the slot
    /// `VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY`: exits need those values too.
    ///
    /// The list of the virtual objects goes in `work`, if the chain has any.
    pub fn frame_state_values<'a>(
        &'a self,
        id: FrameStateId,
        work: &'a Zone,
    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u32, NodeId)> + 'a {
        self.chain_values(id).chain(
            core::iter::once_with(move || self.virtual_objects(id, work))
                .flatten()
                .flat_map(|object| {
                    self.node(object)
                        .inputs
                        .iter()
                        .map(|property| (VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY, *property))
                }),
        )
    }

    /// The virtual objects the values of a frame state chain refer to,
    /// directly or through other virtual objects, each once, in the order
    /// they are first referred to.
    pub fn virtual_objects<'w>(&self, id: FrameStateId, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneVec<'w, NodeId> {
        let is_virtual_object = |value: NodeId| matches!(self.node(value).op, Op::VirtualObject { .. });
        let mut objects = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        // NB: Most frame states refer to no virtual object.
        if !self.chain_values(id).any(|(_, value)| is_virtual_object(value)) {
            return objects;
        }
        let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        for (_, value) in self.chain_values(id) {
            pending.push(value);
            while let Some(value) = pending.pop() {
                if !is_virtual_object(value) || objects.contains(&value) {
                    continue;
                }
                objects.push(value);
                pending.extend(self.node(value).inputs.iter().rev().copied());
            }
        }
        objects
    }

    fn chain_values(&self, id: FrameStateId) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u32, NodeId)> + '_ {
        self.frame_state_chain(id)
            .flat_map(|id| self.frame_state(id).values.iter().copied())
    }

    /// The blocks code starts at: block 0, and the on-stack replacement
    /// entries.
    pub fn entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = BlockId> + '_ {
        core::iter::once(BlockId(0)).chain(self.osr_entries.iter().map(|(_, entry)| *entry))
    }

    /// The control node ending `block`, which every block has once built.
    pub fn control_id(&self, block: BlockId) -> NodeId {
        self.block(block).control.expect("finished blocks have a control node")
    }

    pub fn control(&self, block: BlockId) -> &Node<'z> {
        self.node(self.control_id(block))
    }

    pub fn successors(&self, block: BlockId) -> Successors<'z> {
        self.control(block).op.successors()
    }

    pub fn add_node(&mut self, node: Node<'z>) -> NodeId {
        let id = NodeId::from_index(self.nodes.len());
        self.nodes.push(node);
        id
    }

    pub fn add_block(&mut self, block: Block<'z>) -> BlockId {
        let id = BlockId::from_index(self.blocks.len());
        self.blocks.push(block);
        id
    }

    pub fn add_frame_state(&mut self, frame_state: FrameState<'z>) -> FrameStateId {
        let id = FrameStateId(u32::try_from(self.frame_states.len()).expect("frame state count fits in u32"));
        self.frame_states.push(frame_state);
        id
    }

    /// The nodes of a block in execution order: phis, body, control.
    pub fn block_nodes(&self, block: BlockId) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> + '_ {
        self.block(block).nodes()
    }

    /// Makes the edges from `block` to `from` lead to `to` instead.
    pub fn replace_successor(&mut self, block: BlockId, from: BlockId, to: BlockId) {
        let control = self.blocks[block.index()]
            .control
            .expect("finished blocks have a control node");
        let zone = self.zone;
        self.nodes[control.index()]
            .op
            .map_successors(zone, |successor| if successor == from { to } else { successor });
    }

    /// Reorders the blocks so that `order[i]` becomes block `i`. Blocks not
    /// in `order` are dropped; nothing may refer to them.
    pub fn reorder_blocks(&mut self, order: &[BlockId], work: &Zone) {
        if order.len() == self.blocks.len() && order.iter().enumerate().all(|(index, block)| block.index() == index) {
            return;
        }
        let mut new_index = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, self.blocks.len(), work);
        for (index, block) in order.iter().enumerate() {
            assert!(new_index[block.index()].is_none(), "blocks appear once in the order");
            new_index[block.index()] = Some(BlockId::from_index(index));
        }
        let new_id = |block: BlockId| new_index[block.index()].expect("reordering keeps every referenced block");
        let zone = self.zone;
        for block in order {
            let block = &mut self.blocks[block.index()];
            for predecessor in &mut block.predecessors {
                *predecessor = new_id(*predecessor);
            }
            if let Some(control) = block.control {
                self.nodes[control.index()].op.map_successors(zone, new_id);
            }
        }
        for (_, block) in &mut self.osr_entries {
            *block = new_id(*block);
        }
        // Move each retained block to its destination, carrying the displaced
        // block's destination with it. Dropped blocks end up past the new end.
        for index in 0..self.blocks.len() {
            while let Some(target) = new_index[index] {
                if target.index() == index {
                    break;
                }
                self.blocks.swap(index, target.index());
                new_index.swap(index, target.index());
            }
        }
        self.blocks.truncate(order.len());
    }

    /// Whether `slot` (an operand of the compiled function) is one of `unwritten_slots`.
    pub fn is_unwritten_slot(&self, slot: u32) -> bool {
        (slot as usize) < self.unwritten_slots.capacity() && self.unwritten_slots.contains(slot as usize)
    }

    /// The bits of `id` if it is a constant, or a refinement of one.
    pub fn constant_value(&self, id: NodeId) -> Option<u64> {
        match self.node(self.unrefined(id)).op {
            Op::Constant(bits) => Some(bits),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The value of `id`, if it is a `Repr::Int32` constant.
    pub fn int32_constant(&self, id: NodeId) -> Option<i32> {
        let node = self.node(self.unrefined(id));
        match (&node.op, node.repr) {
            (Op::Constant(bits), Some(Repr::Int32)) => Some((*bits as u32).cast_signed()),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The value `id` refines, through any number of refinements (see
    /// `Op::refined_input()`), or `id` itself.
    pub fn unrefined(&self, mut id: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        while let Some(index) = self.node(id).op.refined_input() {
            id = self.node(id).inputs[index];
        }
        id
    }

    /// Whether `id` is `value`, or refines it through any number of
    /// refinements.
    pub fn refines(&self, mut id: NodeId, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        while id != value {
            let Some(index) = self.node(id).op.refined_input() else {
                return false;
            };
            id = self.node(id).inputs[index];
        }
        true
    }

    /// Whether `id` always has the value of `value`, because it refines
    /// `value` or a phi whose inputs all have that value.
    pub fn has_value_of(&self, id: NodeId, value: NodeId, work: &Zone) -> bool {
        let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut seen = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
        let mut next = Some(id);
        while let Some(mut node) = next.take().or_else(|| pending.pop()) {
            while node != value
                && let Some(index) = self.node(node).op.refined_input()
            {
                node = self.node(node).inputs[index];
            }
            if node == value || seen.contains(&node) {
                continue;
            }
            if !matches!(self.node(node).op, Op::Phi) {
                return false;
            }
            seen.push(node);
            pending.extend(self.node(node).inputs.iter().copied());
        }
        true
    }
}

// NB: Tests make graphs and blocks with no zone at hand. They get the zone of their thread, which lives as long as
//     the thread.
#[cfg(test)]
impl Default for Graph<'static> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new_in(crate::test_zone())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl Default for Block<'static> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new_in(crate::test_zone())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn state(graph: &mut Graph, values: Vec<(u32, NodeId)>, parent: Option<FrameStateId>) -> FrameStateId {
        graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: graph.list(&values),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn reordering_moves_blocks_and_remaps_edges_and_entries() {
        for order in [[2, 0, 3], [3, 2, 0], [0, 3, 2]] {
            let mut graph = Graph::default();
            for index in 0..4 {
                graph.add_block(Block {
                    bytecode_start: Some(index),
                    ..Block::default()
                });
            }
            let control = graph.add(Op::Jump { target: BlockId(2) }, &[], None, 0);
            graph.blocks[0].control = Some(control);
            graph.blocks[2].predecessors.push(BlockId(0));
            graph.osr_entries.push((10, BlockId(3)));
            let storage = graph.blocks.as_ptr();
            let order = order.map(BlockId);
            graph.reorder_blocks(&order, crate::test_zone());
            assert_eq!(graph.blocks.as_ptr(), storage);
            assert_eq!(graph.blocks.len(), 3);
            for (index, old) in order.iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(graph.blocks[index].bytecode_start, Some(old.0));
            }
            let new_id = |old| BlockId::from_index(order.iter().position(|block| *block == BlockId(old)).unwrap());
            assert_eq!(graph.blocks[new_id(2).index()].predecessors, [new_id(0)]);
            assert!(matches!(graph.node(control).op, Op::Jump { target } if target == new_id(2)));
            assert_eq!(graph.osr_entries, [(10, new_id(3))]);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn frame_state_values_keep_caller_and_nested_object_order() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        let value = graph.add(Op::Constant(value::UNDEFINED), &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        let inner = graph.add(
            Op::VirtualObject {
                kind: VirtualObjectKind::Object { shape: CellId(1) },
                allocation: NodeId(0),
            },
            &[value],
            Some(Repr::Tagged),
            0,
        );
        let outer = graph.add(
            Op::VirtualObject {
                kind: VirtualObjectKind::Object { shape: CellId(2) },
                allocation: NodeId(1),
            },
            &[inner, value],
            Some(Repr::Tagged),
            0,
        );
        let parent = state(&mut graph, vec![(0, value), (1, inner)], None);
        let current = state(&mut graph, vec![(0, outer), (1, inner)], Some(parent));
        assert_eq!(graph.virtual_objects(current, crate::test_zone()), [outer, inner]);
        assert_eq!(
            graph
                .frame_state_values(current, crate::test_zone())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [
                (0, outer),
                (1, inner),
                (0, value),
                (1, inner),
                (VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY, inner),
                (VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY, value),
                (VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY, value),
            ]
        );
        graph.nodes[inner.index()].inputs.push(outer);
        assert_eq!(graph.virtual_objects(current, crate::test_zone()), [outer, inner]);
        assert_eq!(
            graph.frame_state_values(current, crate::test_zone()).last(),
            Some((VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY, outer))
        );
        let empty = state(&mut graph, vec![], None);
        assert_eq!(graph.frame_state_values(empty, crate::test_zone()).count(), 0);
    }
}

//! NaN-boxed encodings of the JS values the compiler creates itself.
//!
//! These match `GC::NanBoxedValue` and `JS::Value`.

/// How far the tag of a value is shifted up.
pub const TAG_SHIFT: u8 = 48;
/// The top 16 bits of values that are no doubles have these bits set.
pub const BASE_TAG: u16 = 0x7FF8;
const IS_CELL_BIT: u16 = 0x8000 | BASE_TAG;

/// The top 16 bits of each kind of value.
pub const BOOLEAN_TAG: u16 = 0b001 | BASE_TAG;
pub const INT32_TAG: u16 = 0b010 | BASE_TAG;
pub const EMPTY_TAG: u16 = 0b011 | BASE_TAG;
pub const UNDEFINED_TAG: u16 = 0b110 | BASE_TAG;
pub const NULL_TAG: u16 = 0b111 | BASE_TAG;
pub const OBJECT_TAG: u16 = 0b001 | IS_CELL_BIT;
pub const ACCESSOR_TAG: u16 = 0b100 | IS_CELL_BIT;
pub const STRING_TAG: u16 = 0b010 | IS_CELL_BIT;
pub const SYMBOL_TAG: u16 = 0b011 | IS_CELL_BIT;
pub const BIGINT_TAG: u16 = 0b101 | IS_CELL_BIT;

/// The one NaN that is a value; other NaNs are canonicalized to it.
pub const CANONICAL_NAN: u64 = tagged(BASE_TAG);

/// The bits of a value with tag `tag` and no payload.
pub const fn tagged(tag: u16) -> u64 {
    (tag as u64) << TAG_SHIFT
}

pub const EMPTY: u64 = tagged(EMPTY_TAG);
pub const UNDEFINED: u64 = tagged(UNDEFINED_TAG);
pub const NULL: u64 = tagged(NULL_TAG);
pub const FALSE: u64 = tagged(BOOLEAN_TAG);
pub const TRUE: u64 = tagged(BOOLEAN_TAG) | 1;

/// Stand-ins for the frame's arguments object while compiled code has not
/// created it, of the unmapped and mapped kind. Only frame states refer to
/// them: no value has these bits, and no node takes them as input.
pub const VIRTUAL_UNMAPPED_ARGUMENTS: u64 = tagged(EMPTY_TAG) | 0xa0;
pub const VIRTUAL_MAPPED_ARGUMENTS: u64 = tagged(EMPTY_TAG) | 0xa1;

/// Whether `bits` stand for an arguments object that was never created, and
/// if so whether it is a mapped one.
pub fn virtual_arguments_kind(bits: u64) -> Option<bool> {
    match bits {
        VIRTUAL_UNMAPPED_ARGUMENTS => Some(false),
        VIRTUAL_MAPPED_ARGUMENTS => Some(true),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The tag of a value: its top 16 bits.
pub fn tag(bits: u64) -> u16 {
    (bits >> TAG_SHIFT) as u16
}

/// The int32 a value is, if it is one.
pub fn as_int32(bits: u64) -> Option<i32> {
    (tag(bits) == INT32_TAG).then_some((bits as u32).cast_signed())
}

/// Whether a value is a double, canonical NaN included.
pub fn is_double(bits: u64) -> bool {
    bits == CANONICAL_NAN || tag(bits) & BASE_TAG != BASE_TAG
}

pub fn int32(value: i32) -> u64 {
    tagged(INT32_TAG) | u64::from(value.cast_unsigned())
}

/// The NaN-boxed value of the bits of a constant node of representation
/// `repr`: int32 constants hold their value in the low 32 bits, boolean
/// constants are 0 or 1.
pub fn boxed_constant(bits: u64, repr: crate::code::Repr) -> u64 {
    match repr {
        crate::code::Repr::Tagged => bits,
        crate::code::Repr::Int32 => int32((bits as u32).cast_signed()),
        crate::code::Repr::Bool => {
            if bits != 0 {
                TRUE
            } else {
                FALSE
            }
        }
        crate::code::Repr::Float64 => number(f64::from_bits(bits)),
        crate::code::Repr::Pointer => bits,
    }
}

/// A number boxed like `JS::Value(double)` boxes it: as an int32 if it is
/// one (but not -0), and NaN canonicalized.
pub fn number(number: f64) -> u64 {
    let integer = number as i32;
    if f64::from(integer) == number && !(integer == 0 && number.is_sign_negative()) {
        int32(integer)
    } else if number.is_nan() {
        CANONICAL_NAN
    } else {
        number.to_bits()
    }
}

/// A short human readable description of a NaN-boxed value, for IR dumps.
pub fn describe(bits: u64) -> Description {
    Description(bits)
}

/// The text of `describe()`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Description(u64);

impl Description {
    /// The name of the value, if it has one rather than its bits in hex.
    fn name(self) -> Option<&'static str> {
        match self.0 {
            EMPTY => Some("empty"),
            VIRTUAL_UNMAPPED_ARGUMENTS => Some("arguments"),
            VIRTUAL_MAPPED_ARGUMENTS => Some("mapped arguments"),
            UNDEFINED => Some("undefined"),
            NULL => Some("null"),
            FALSE => Some("false"),
            TRUE => Some("true"),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn is_int32(self) -> bool {
        self.0 >> TAG_SHIFT == u64::from(INT32_TAG)
    }

    /// Whether the text tells what the value is, rather than only giving its bits in hex.
    pub fn is_known_value(self) -> bool {
        self.name().is_some() || self.is_int32()
    }
}

impl core::fmt::Display for Description {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        let bits = self.0;
        match self.name() {
            Some(name) => f.write_str(name),
            None if self.is_int32() => write!(f, "{}", (bits as u32).cast_signed()),
            None => write!(f, "{bits:#018x}"),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn describes_known_values() {
        assert_eq!(describe(EMPTY).to_string(), "empty");
        assert_eq!(describe(TRUE).to_string(), "true");
        assert_eq!(describe(int32(-5)).to_string(), "-5");
        assert_eq!(describe(int32(7)).to_string(), "7");
        assert_eq!(describe(0x4000_0000_0000_0000).to_string(), "0x4000000000000000");
        assert!(describe(int32(-5)).is_known_value());
        assert!(!describe(0x4000_0000_0000_0000).is_known_value());
    }
}

//! The LibJS optimizing JIT compiler.
//!
//! This crate is a pure compiler: it turns a `Snapshot` (plain data captured on
//! the main thread) into `CompiledCode` (plain data installed by the main
//! thread). It calls nothing in the runtime and has no access to the GC heap, so
//! it can run on a worker thread.

// NB: A compile makes no block in the heap: all its data is in zones (see `ak::Zone`). Without `std` (and without
//     `alloc`), rustc rejects code of the compiler that would make one. The tests keep `std`.
#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]

pub mod artifact;
pub mod asm;
pub mod builder;
pub mod bytecode;
pub mod code;
pub mod codegen;
pub mod coverage;
pub mod debug_text;
pub mod ir;
pub mod passes;
pub mod regalloc;
pub mod scratch;
pub mod snapshot;
pub mod tables;

// NB: The tests get their memory on Windows from `ak::windows_code_memory`, which is for x86-64.
#[cfg(all(test, windows, not(target_arch = "x86_64")))]
compile_error!("the tests of the JIT run on Windows on x86-64 only");

use ak::Zone;
use artifact::Artifact;
use artifact::ArtifactWriter;
use artifact::Tail;
use bytecode::OpCode;
use code::CompiledCode;
use code::TextWriter;
use core::fmt::Write;
use scratch::Scratch;
use snapshot::Snapshot;

/// Why a compile job did not produce code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CompileFailure {
    /// The bytecode could not be decoded or refers to things that do not exist.
    InvalidBytecode { pc: u32, reason: &'static str },
    /// The JIT does not handle the instruction at `pc`.
    UnsupportedInstruction {
        pc: u32,
        opcode: OpCode,
        reason: &'static str,
    },
    /// `RuntimeInfo` lacks the address of a helper the code needs: the slow
    /// path of `opcode`, or another runtime helper if `opcode` is `None`.
    MissingRuntimeHelper { opcode: Option<OpCode> },
    /// The assembler could not finish the code (a branch out of range).
    CodeGeneration,
    /// The compile needs more of something than the compiler has room for.
    TooLarge,
}

impl From<ak::ColumnFull> for CompileFailure {
    fn from(_: ak::ColumnFull) -> Self {
        Self::TooLarge
    }
}

/// The zone of the thread of a test, for the graphs that the test makes. It lives as long as the thread.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn test_zone() -> &'static ak::Zone {
    thread_local! {
        static ZONE: &'static ak::Zone = Box::leak(Box::new(ak::Zone::new(1 << 30, c"test")));
    }
    ZONE.with(|zone| *zone)
}

/// A zone for the work data of the passes that a test runs.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn test_work() -> ak::Zone {
    ak::Zone::new(1 << 30, c"test")
}

/// The zones for the steps of the passes that a test runs (see `Scratch::steps`).
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn test_steps() -> [ak::Zone; 2] {
    [test_work(), test_work()]
}

/// The allocator of the tests, which counts the blocks that `count_heap_blocks()` makes on its thread.
#[cfg(test)]
mod heap_counter {
    use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
    use std::cell::Cell;

    struct CountingAllocator;

    std::thread_local! {
        static COUNTING: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
        static BLOCKS: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };
    }

    fn count_block() {
        if COUNTING.with(Cell::get) {
            BLOCKS.with(|blocks| blocks.set(blocks.get() + 1));
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: Each method passes its call on to `System` as it is.
    unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for CountingAllocator {
        unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
            count_block();
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract of `GlobalAlloc::alloc`.
            unsafe { System.alloc(layout) }
        }

        unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
            count_block();
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract of `GlobalAlloc::alloc_zeroed`.
            unsafe { System.alloc_zeroed(layout) }
        }

        unsafe fn realloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout, new_size: usize) -> *mut u8 {
            count_block();
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract of `GlobalAlloc::realloc`.
            unsafe { System.realloc(ptr, layout, new_size) }
        }

        unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the contract of `GlobalAlloc::dealloc`.
            unsafe { System.dealloc(ptr, layout) }
        }
    }

    #[global_allocator]
    static ALLOCATOR: CountingAllocator = CountingAllocator;

    /// Runs `f`, and gives the number of blocks of the heap that it made or grew on this thread.
    pub(crate) fn count_heap_blocks(f: impl FnOnce()) -> usize {
        BLOCKS.with(|blocks| blocks.set(0));
        COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(true));
        f();
        COUNTING.with(|counting| counting.set(false));
        BLOCKS.with(Cell::get)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) use heap_counter::count_heap_blocks;

/// Compiles `snapshot.executables[0]` for the host architecture with the memory of `scratch`, into `compiled` in
/// place of what it holds. After a failure, `compiled` holds no complete code.
pub fn compile(snapshot: &Snapshot, scratch: &mut Scratch, compiled: &mut CompiledCode) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    compile_into::<asm::MacroAssembler>(
        snapshot,
        &|pc| {
            snapshot
                .executables
                .first()
                .is_none_or(|executable| builder::has_run(snapshot, executable, pc))
        },
        scratch,
        compiled,
    )
}

/// The cells the code embeds, which keep their addresses for as long as it lives: those the graph lists, those of its
/// constants and of the values its checks compare against, and those of the constants of the compiled executable, which
/// the code writes into the frames it initializes. Values that hold cells end up in the code and in its tables as they
/// are, so the cells of all of them stay where they are.
fn embedded_cells<'w>(graph: &ir::Graph<'_>, snapshot: &Snapshot, work: &'w Zone) -> ak::ZoneVec<'w, snapshot::CellId> {
    let runtime = &snapshot.runtime;
    let pattern = runtime.shifted_is_cell_pattern;
    let values = graph.nodes.iter().filter_map(|node| match node.op {
        ir::Op::Constant(bits) if node.repr == Some(code::Repr::Tagged) => Some(bits),
        ir::Op::CheckValue { expected, .. } => Some(expected),
        _ => None,
    });
    let frame_constants = snapshot
        .executables
        .first()
        .map_or(&[][..], |executable| &snapshot[executable.constants]);
    let mut value_cells = ak::ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        values
            .chain(frame_constants.iter().copied())
            .filter(|bits| bits & pattern == pattern)
            .map(|bits| runtime.heap_region_base + (bits & runtime.heap_region_offset_mask)),
        work,
    );
    value_cells.sort_unstable();
    value_cells.dedup();
    let mut listed = ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&graph.embedded_cells, work);
    listed.sort_unstable();
    let mut cells = ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&graph.embedded_cells, work);
    for cell in value_cells.into_iter().map(snapshot::CellId) {
        if listed.binary_search(&cell).is_err() {
            cells.push(cell);
        }
    }
    cells
}

/// With `StressOptions::few_registers`, how many registers values get
/// besides the ones calls use.
const STRESS_EXTRA_REGISTERS: u32 = 2;

/// Compiles `snapshot.executables[0]` with the macro assembler `M`, into memory of the code's own. The
/// instructions for which `has_run(pc)` is false become unconditional exits.
pub fn compile_for<M: asm::PortableMacroAssembler>(
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    has_run: &dyn Fn(u32) -> bool,
    scratch: &mut Scratch,
) -> Result<CompiledCode, CompileFailure> {
    let mut compiled = CompiledCode::new();
    compile_into::<M>(snapshot, has_run, scratch, &mut compiled)?;
    Ok(compiled)
}

/// Compiles `snapshot.executables[0]` with the macro assembler `M`, like `compile()`. The instructions for which
/// `has_run(pc)` is false become unconditional exits.
fn compile_into<M: asm::PortableMacroAssembler>(
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    has_run: &dyn Fn(u32) -> bool,
    scratch: &mut Scratch,
    compiled: &mut CompiledCode,
) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    let result = run_stages::<M>(snapshot, has_run, scratch, compiled);
    scratch.end_compile();
    result
}

/// The stages of `compile_into()`, which leave their data in `scratch`.
fn run_stages<M: asm::PortableMacroAssembler>(
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    has_run: &dyn Fn(u32) -> bool,
    scratch: &mut Scratch,
    compiled: &mut CompiledCode,
) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    compiled.clear();
    let options = &snapshot.options;
    compiled.keep_texts(
        options.dump_ir || options.dump_asm || options.dump_passes,
        options.coverage,
    );
    if !snapshot.is_complete() {
        return Err(CompileFailure::TooLarge);
    }
    let Scratch { zone, work, steps } = scratch;
    // NB: Nothing of the compile before this one is in use (see `Scratch`).
    work.reset();
    let mut graph = {
        let mut attempts = builder::Attempts::new(snapshot, has_run, work);
        loop {
            // NB: This drops the graph of the compile before this one, and a graph that the builder gave up.
            zone.reset();
            if let Some(graph) = attempts.build(zone)? {
                break graph;
            }
        }
    };
    // NB: The builder is done, and nothing of the graph is in its work data.
    work.reset();
    let executable = &snapshot.executables[0];
    // NB: The text of a dump that does not fit is cut (see `TextWriter`), so a failed write needs nothing more.
    let mut dump = compiled.dump.as_mut().map(TextWriter::dump);
    match &mut dump {
        Some(dump) if options.dump_passes => {
            passes::optimize_with_dumps(&mut graph, &executable.layout, options.verify_ir, work, steps, dump)?;
        }
        _ => passes::optimize(&mut graph, &executable.layout, options.verify_ir, work, steps)?,
    }
    let (mut registers, _) = codegen::target_registers::<M>();
    if snapshot.options.stress.few_registers {
        registers.allocatable_gprs = registers.few_registers(STRESS_EXTRA_REGISTERS);
    }
    // NB: The allocation is in the work zone, and the code generator reads it, so the work data of the register
    //     allocator, and of the stages after it, stays until the compile ends.
    let work: &Zone = work;
    let allocation = regalloc::allocate(&graph, &registers, work)?;
    if snapshot.options.verify_ir
        && let Err(errors) = regalloc::verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, work)
    {
        panic!(
            "invalid register allocation:\n{errors}\n{}",
            regalloc::dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
        );
    }
    let mut artifact = ArtifactWriter::new_in(work);
    let mut generated = codegen::generate::<M>(
        &graph,
        snapshot,
        snapshot.options.verify_ir,
        &mut artifact,
        &allocation,
        &mut compiled.code,
        work,
    )?;
    generated.osr_entries.sort_unstable();
    let embedded_cells = embedded_cells(&graph, snapshot, work);
    let layout = artifact.finish(
        &Tail {
            osr_entries: &generated.osr_entries,
            osr_loop_back_edges: &graph.osr_loop_back_edges,
            osr_outer_loop_back_edges: &graph.osr_outer_loop_back_edges,
            uncaught_handlers: &graph.uncaught_handlers,
            invalidation_patches: &generated.invalidation_patches,
            embedded_cells: &embedded_cells,
            dependencies: &graph.dependencies,
        },
        &mut compiled.words,
    )?;

    if let Some(dump) = &mut dump {
        if options.dump_ir {
            let _ = write!(
                dump,
                "{}{}",
                ir::dump(&graph, &executable.layout),
                regalloc::dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
            );
        }
        if options.dump_asm {
            let _ = write!(
                dump,
                "{}",
                codegen::dump_code(
                    &graph,
                    executable,
                    &snapshot.runtime,
                    M::ARCHITECTURE,
                    &compiled.code,
                    &generated,
                    Artifact::new(&compiled.words, &layout),
                )
            );
        }
    }
    if let Some(coverage) = &mut compiled.coverage {
        // NB: The keys that do not fit are left out (see `TextWriter`).
        let _ = coverage::write_coverage_keys(&graph, &mut TextWriter::lines(coverage));
    }
    compiled.data_offset = generated.data_offset;
    compiled.entry_offset = generated.entry_offset;
    compiled.site_index_frame_offset = generated.site_index_frame_offset;
    compiled.register_dump_frame_offset = generated.register_dump_frame_offset;
    compiled.layout = layout;
    Ok(())
}

// Compile jobs move between threads.
const _: () = {
    const fn assert_send<T: Send>() {}
    assert_send::<Snapshot>();
    assert_send::<CompiledCode>();
    assert_send::<Scratch>();
};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn compile_jobs_can_move_between_threads() {
        let snapshot = Snapshot::default();
        let mut scratch = Scratch::new();
        let mut compiled = CompiledCode::new();
        let (result, compiled) = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let result = compile(&snapshot, &mut scratch, &mut compiled);
            (result, compiled)
        })
        .join()
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            result.unwrap_err(),
            CompileFailure::InvalidBytecode { pc: 0, .. }
        ));
        assert!(compiled.code.is_empty());
    }
}

/*
