 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Bounds check elimination: bounds checks of indices whose ranges are
//! known to be within the count go away.
//!
//! The ranges come from loop induction variables and from int32 arithmetic
//! on them. An induction variable is a loop header phi that starts at a
//! value of known range and grows by a constant step on every iteration,
//! where the back edge is only taken while the grown value compares below a
//! constant bound, like the counters of loops that test at their bottom
//! (`do { ... } while (++i != 1024)`). Its values then lie between its
//! start and the bound. Arithmetic on values of known ranges has a known
//! range where it cannot overflow: additions, subtractions, shifts by
//! constants and masks with constants.
//!
//! The pass runs after loop invariant code motion, which gives every loop
//! one entry: a header phi's first input comes from outside the loop, and
//! its others over back edges. Merges of values from outside the loop, like
//! the starts of a counter that the function entry and an on-stack
//! replacement entry bring, are in the range of all their inputs.
//!
//! The counter an on-stack replacement entry finds in the frame could be
//! anything. Where the entry checks it to be an int32, it is checked to be
//! below the loop's bound there too, once, unless such a check exited there
//! before: the loop keeps it below the bound anyway. Those checks are only
//! added where a bounds check, a rewritten shift or an operation that stops
//! checking for overflow relies on them, including through the counts of
//! the bounds checks that bound its operands.
//!
//! With the same ranges, `((x << k) + c) >> k` becomes `x + (c >> k)` where
//! nothing overflows and `c` is a multiple of 2^k, like the index arithmetic
//! of asm.js heap accesses.
//!
//! Additions, subtractions and multiplications whose operands' ranges keep
//! the result an int32 (and, for multiplications, from being -0) stop
//! checking for that, like `(a & 0x3fff) * (b >> 14)` and the `i + 1` after
//! an access at `i`. Besides the ranges above, the ranges of operands come
//! from masks and shifts of any int32, and from the bounds checks of
//! accesses (and the branches on an index being in bounds) that dominate
//! the operation: an index is below the elements' count there.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use super::edit::Constants;
use super::edit::Replacements;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Node;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneMap;

/// The inclusive range of an int32 value.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Range {
    min: i64,
    max: i64,
}

impl Range {
    /// Every int32.
    const INT32: Self = Self {
        min: i32::MIN as i64,
        max: i32::MAX as i64,
    };

    fn new(min: i64, max: i64) -> Option<Self> {
        (i64::from(i32::MIN) <= min && min <= max && max <= i64::from(i32::MAX)).then_some(Self { min, max })
    }

    fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::new(self.min.max(other.min), self.max.min(other.max))
    }

    fn contains(self, value: i64) -> bool {
        self.min <= value && value <= self.max
    }

    /// The range of the sum of values of `self` and `other`, if it is
    /// within the int32 range.
    fn sum(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::new(self.min + other.min, self.max + other.max)
    }

    /// The range of the difference of values of `self` and `other`, if it
    /// is within the int32 range.
    fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::new(self.min - other.max, self.max - other.min)
    }

    /// The range of the product of values of `self` and `other`, if it is
    /// within the int32 range.
    fn product(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
        let products = [
            self.min * other.min,
            self.min * other.max,
            self.max * other.min,
            self.max * other.max,
        ];
        Self::new(*products.iter().min()?, *products.iter().max()?)
    }
}

struct Ranges<'a> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'a>,
    dominators: &'a Dominators<'a>,
    /// The block of each phi.
    phi_blocks: &'a ZoneMap<'a, NodeId, BlockId>,
    /// The ranges of entering counters that checks added where they enter
    /// would give them.
    assumed: &'a ZoneMap<'a, NodeId, Range>,
    known: ZoneMap<'a, NodeId, Option<Range>>,
}

impl Ranges<'_> {
    fn of(&mut self, value: NodeId) -> Option<Range> {
        if let Some(range) = self.assumed.get(&value) {
            return Some(*range);
        }
        if let Some(range) = self.known.get(&value) {
            return *range;
        }
        // NB: Cycles through phis that are no induction variables have no
        //     range; a phi in progress has none until it is done.
        self.known.insert(value, None);
        let range = self.compute(value);
        self.known.insert(value, range);
        range
    }

    fn constant(&self, value: NodeId) -> Option<i64> {
        self.graph.int32_constant(value).map(i64::from)
    }

    fn compute(&mut self, value: NodeId) -> Option<Range> {
        let node = self.graph.node(value);
        if node.repr != Some(Repr::Int32) {
            return None;
        }
        if let Some(constant) = self.constant(value) {
            return Range::new(constant, constant);
        }
        // NB: A value past its bounds check is below the count, and other
        //     refinements keep the range of what they refine.
        if bounds_index(&node.op) {
            let index = self.of(node.inputs[0]);
            return self.below_count(index, node.inputs[1]);
        }
        if let Some(refined) = node.op.refined_input() {
            return self.of(node.inputs[refined]);
        }
        match node.op {
            Op::Phi if self.is_merge(value) => {
                let mut range: Option<Range> = None;
                for input in node.inputs.iter().copied() {
                    let input = self.of(input)?;
                    range = Some(match range {
                        None => input,
                        Some(range) => Range::new(range.min.min(input.min), range.max.max(input.max))?,
                    });
                }
                range
            }
            Op::Phi => self.induction_variable(value),
            Op::Int32Binary { op } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op } => {
                let (lhs, rhs) = (node.inputs[0], node.inputs[1]);
                match op {
                    BinaryOp::Add => self.of(lhs)?.sum(self.of(rhs)?),
                    BinaryOp::Sub => self.of(lhs)?.difference(self.of(rhs)?),
                    BinaryOp::LeftShift => {
                        let (lhs, shift) = (self.of(lhs)?, self.constant(rhs)? & 31);
                        Range::new(lhs.min << shift, lhs.max << shift)
                    }
                    BinaryOp::RightShift => {
                        let shift = self.constant(rhs)? & 31;
                        let lhs = self.of(lhs).unwrap_or(Range::INT32);
                        Range::new(lhs.min >> shift, lhs.max >> shift)
                    }
                    BinaryOp::Mul => self.of(lhs)?.product(self.of(rhs)?),
                    // NB: Shifting any int32 right as an unsigned number by
                    //     at least one leaves a non-negative int32.
                    BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => {
                        let shift = self.constant(rhs)? & 31;
                        match self.of(lhs) {
                            Some(lhs) if lhs.min >= 0 => Range::new(lhs.min >> shift, lhs.max >> shift),
                            _ if shift > 0 => Range::new(0, i64::from(u32::MAX) >> shift),
                            _ => None,
                        }
                    }
                    BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => {
                        let mask = self.constant(rhs).filter(|mask| *mask >= 0)?;
                        match self.of(lhs) {
                            Some(lhs) if lhs.min >= 0 => Range::new(0, lhs.max.min(mask)),
                            _ => Range::new(0, mask),
                        }
                    }
                    _ => None,
                }
            }
            // NB: Storage capacities are int32 values (see
            //     `Op::LoadElementsCapacity`), which are never negative.
            Op::LoadElementsCapacity => Range::new(0, Range::INT32.max),
            // NB: The smaller of two values as unsigned numbers is at most
            //     the one that is not negative.
            Op::Uint32Min => {
                let (lhs, rhs) = (self.of(node.inputs[0]), self.of(node.inputs[1]));
                [lhs, rhs]
                    .into_iter()
                    .flatten()
                    .filter(|range| range.min >= 0)
                    .map(|range| range.max)
                    .min()
                    .and_then(|max| Range::new(0, max))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The range of `index` (of range `range`, if it has one) where it is
    /// below `count` as unsigned numbers, which a bounds check made it. A
    /// count of unknown range leaves the range of the index.
    fn below_count(&mut self, range: Option<Range>, count: NodeId) -> Option<Range> {
        let count = match self.constant(count) {
            Some(count) => Range::new(count, count)?,
            None => match self.of(count).filter(|count| count.min >= 0) {
                Some(count) => count,
                None => return range,
            },
        };
        let below = Range::new(0, count.max - 1)?;
        match range {
            Some(range) => range.intersection(below),
            None => Some(below),
        }
    }

    /// For `((x << k) + c) >> k` and `(x << k) >> k` where nothing can
    /// overflow and `c` is a multiple of 2^k: `x` and `c >> k`, which it is.
    fn unscaled(&mut self, shift: NodeId) -> Option<(NodeId, i64)> {
        let node = self.graph.node(shift);
        let amount = self.constant(node.inputs[1])? & 31;
        let shifted = self.graph.node(node.inputs[0]);
        let (scaled, offset) = match shifted.op {
            Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Add } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Add } => {
                (shifted.inputs[0], self.constant(shifted.inputs[1])?)
            }
            _ => (node.inputs[0], 0),
        };
        if offset % (1 << amount) != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let scaled_node = self.graph.node(scaled);
        let is_left_shift = matches!(
            scaled_node.op,
            Op::Int32Binary {
                op: BinaryOp::LeftShift
            } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary {
                op: BinaryOp::LeftShift
            }
        );
        if !is_left_shift || self.constant(scaled_node.inputs[1])? & 31 != amount {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: Known ranges of the shifted value and the sum mean neither
        //     overflowed.
        self.of(scaled)?;
        self.of(node.inputs[0])?;
        Some((scaled_node.inputs[0], offset >> amount))
    }

    /// Whether `predecessor` reaches `block` over a back edge.
    fn is_back_edge(&self, predecessor: BlockId, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        self.dominators.dominates(block, predecessor)
    }

    /// Whether `phi` merges values that no back edge brings.
    fn is_merge(&self, phi: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.phi_blocks.get(&phi).is_some_and(|block| {
            self.graph
                .block(*block)
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .all(|predecessor| !self.is_back_edge(*predecessor, *block))
        })
    }

    /// The step, the comparison and the bound of the loop header phi `phi`,
    /// if it is shaped like an induction variable, whatever its start.
    fn induction_step(&self, phi: NodeId) -> Option<(i64, Comparison, i64)> {
        let block = *self.phi_blocks.get(&phi)?;
        let inputs = &self.graph.node(phi).inputs;
        let predecessors = &self.graph.block(block).predecessors;
        if inputs.len() != 2 || self.is_back_edge(predecessors[0], block) || !self.is_back_edge(predecessors[1], block)
        {
            return None;
        }
        let next = self.graph.unrefined(inputs[1]);
        let next_node = self.graph.node(next);
        let step = match next_node.op {
            Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Add } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Add }
                if self.graph.unrefined(next_node.inputs[0]) == phi =>
            {
                self.constant(next_node.inputs[1]).filter(|step| *step > 0)?
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let (comparison, bound) = self.back_edge_condition(predecessors[1], next)?;
        Some((step, comparison, bound))
    }

    /// The range of the loop header phi `phi`, if it is an induction
    /// variable that grows by a constant step while the grown value stays
    /// below a constant bound.
    fn induction_variable(&mut self, phi: NodeId) -> Option<Range> {
        let (step, comparison, bound) = self.induction_step(phi)?;
        let start = self.of(self.graph.node(phi).inputs[0])?;
        // NB: The phi's values are its start, and grown values for which the
        //     back edge was taken.
        let last = match comparison {
            Comparison::LessThan => bound - 1,
            Comparison::LessThanEquals => bound,
            // NB: A loop until the grown value equals the bound only stops
            //     there if it steps on it.
            Comparison::StrictlyInequals | Comparison::LooselyInequals
                if start.max < bound && (step == 1 || (start.min == start.max && (bound - start.min) % step == 0)) =>
            {
                bound - step
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        let max = start.max.max(last);
        // NB: Growing the last value must not overflow either.
        Range::new(max, max + step)?;
        Range::new(start.min, max)
    }

    /// The comparison and constant bound of the grown value `next` under
    /// which the back edge from `source` is taken: `source` only jumps to
    /// the header, after a branch on comparing `next` with a constant.
    fn back_edge_condition(&self, source: BlockId, next: NodeId) -> Option<(Comparison, i64)> {
        if !matches!(self.graph.control(source).op, Op::Jump { .. }) {
            return None;
        }
        let [branch_block] = self.graph.block(source).predecessors[..] else {
            return None;
        };
        let branch = self.graph.control(branch_block);
        let Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
            if_true,
            if_false,
        } = branch.op
        else {
            return None;
        };
        let compare = self.graph.node(self.graph.unrefined(branch.inputs[0]));
        let Op::Int32Compare { comparison } = compare.op else {
            return None;
        };
        if self.graph.unrefined(compare.inputs[0]) != next {
            return None;
        }
        let bound = self.constant(compare.inputs[1])?;
        let comparison = if if_true == source {
            comparison
        } else if if_false == source {
            match comparison {
                Comparison::GreaterThanEquals => Comparison::LessThan,
                Comparison::GreaterThan => Comparison::LessThanEquals,
                Comparison::StrictlyEquals => Comparison::StrictlyInequals,
                Comparison::LooselyEquals => Comparison::LooselyInequals,
                _ => return None,
            }
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        Some((comparison, bound))
    }

    /// The entering counters of `assumed` that the range of `value` relies
    /// on, added to `used`. `pending` is for its own use.
    fn assumptions_of(
        &self,
        value: NodeId,
        used: &mut ZoneBitSet,
        visited: &mut ZoneBitSet,
        pending: &mut ZoneVec<NodeId>,
    ) {
        pending.clear();
        pending.push(value);
        while let Some(value) = pending.pop() {
            if visited.contains(value.index()) {
                continue;
            }
            visited.insert(value.index());
            if self.assumed.contains_key(&value) {
                used.insert(value.index());
                continue;
            }
            pending.extend(self.graph.node(value).inputs.iter().copied());
        }
    }
}

/// Whether `op` makes its input 0 below its input 1 as unsigned numbers:
/// a bounds check, or the refinement of a branch on that where it holds.
fn bounds_index(op: &Op) -> bool {
    matches!(
        op,
        Op::CheckBounds
            | Op::Refine {
                condition: BranchCondition::IndexInBounds,
                holds: true,
            }
    )
}

/// The blocks that only on-stack replacement entries reach.
fn osr_only_blocks<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneBitSet<'w> {
    let reach = |starts: &mut dyn Iterator<Item = BlockId>| {
        let mut reached = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.blocks.len(), work);
        let mut pending = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(starts, work);
        while let Some(block) = pending.pop() {
            if reached.contains(block.index()) {
                continue;
            }
            reached.insert(block.index());
            pending.extend(graph.successors(block).iter().copied());
        }
        reached
    };
    let mut osr = reach(&mut graph.osr_entries.iter().map(|(_, block)| *block));
    osr.subtract(&reach(&mut core::iter::once(BlockId::from_index(0))));
    osr
}

/// The counters that on-stack replacement entries bring to induction
/// variables and check to be int32 values, with the bound each could be
/// checked against: the tightest of the loops it starts.
fn entering_counters<'w>(
    graph: &Graph,
    dominators: &Dominators,
    phi_blocks: &ZoneMap<NodeId, BlockId>,
    work: &'w Zone,
) -> ZoneMap<'w, NodeId, Range> {
    let mut entering = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    if graph.osr_entries.is_empty() {
        return entering;
    }
    let osr_only = osr_only_blocks(graph, work);
    let mut block_of = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        for node in &block.body {
            block_of.insert(*node, index);
        }
    }
    let none = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let ranges = Ranges {
        graph,
        dominators,
        phi_blocks,
        assumed: &none,
        known: ZoneMap::new_in(work),
    };
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut seen = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for phi in phi_blocks.keys() {
        let Some((_, comparison, bound)) = ranges.induction_step(*phi) else {
            continue;
        };
        if bound <= 0
            || !matches!(
                comparison,
                Comparison::LessThan | Comparison::StrictlyInequals | Comparison::LooselyInequals
            )
        {
            continue;
        }
        // NB: Look through merges of the values the entries bring.
        pending.clear();
        pending.push(graph.node(*phi).inputs[0]);
        seen.clear();
        while let Some(value) = pending.pop() {
            let value = graph.unrefined(value);
            if seen.contains(value.index()) {
                continue;
            }
            seen.insert(value.index());
            let node = graph.node(value);
            if node.op == Op::Phi && ranges.is_merge(value) {
                pending.extend(node.inputs.iter().copied());
                continue;
            }
            let Some(frame_state) = node.frame_state else {
                continue;
            };
            let state = graph.frame_state(frame_state);
            let failed_before = graph
                .exit_sites
                .contains(&(state.executable, state.pc, ExitKind::OutOfBounds));
            if node.op == Op::CheckInt32
                && !failed_before
                && block_of.get(&value).is_some_and(|block| osr_only.contains(*block))
            {
                let range = Range::new(0, bound - 1).expect("the bound is a positive int32");
                match entering.get_mut(&value) {
                    Some(assumed) => assumed.max = assumed.max.min(range.max),
                    None => {
                        entering.insert(value, range);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    entering
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let mut phi_blocks = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let mut checks = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut shifts = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut arithmetic = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    // NB: For every index that bounds checks and branches check, where
    //     those checks are and the counts.
    let mut bounded: ZoneMap<NodeId, ZoneVec<(BlockId, usize, NodeId)>> = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        for phi in &block.phis {
            phi_blocks.insert(*phi, BlockId::from_index(index));
        }
        for (position, node) in block.body.iter().enumerate() {
            let check = graph.node(*node);
            if bounds_index(&check.op) {
                bounded
                    .entry(graph.unrefined(check.inputs[0]))
                    .or_insert_with(|| ZoneVec::new_in(work))
                    .push((BlockId::from_index(index), position, check.inputs[1]));
            }
            match check.op {
                Op::CheckBounds => checks.push(*node),
                Op::Int32Binary {
                    op: BinaryOp::RightShift,
                } => shifts.push((*node, BlockId::from_index(index))),
                Op::Int32Binary {
                    op: BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::Mul,
                } => arithmetic.push((*node, BlockId::from_index(index), position)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    // NB: Only bounds checks against constant counts can go away, and only
    //     operations whose operands may have ranges (see `Ranges::compute()`)
    //     can stop checking for overflow. The others need no analysis.
    let may_have_range = |value: NodeId| {
        let value = graph.unrefined(value);
        graph.int32_constant(value).is_some()
            || bounded.contains_key(&value)
            || match graph.node(value).op {
                Op::Phi
                | Op::Int32Binary { .. }
                | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { .. }
                | Op::LoadElementsCapacity
                | Op::Uint32Min => true,
                // NB: The counters that on-stack replacement entries check.
                Op::CheckInt32 => !graph.osr_entries.is_empty(),
                _ => false,
            }
    };
    checks.retain(|check| graph.int32_constant(graph.node(*check).inputs[1]).is_some());
    arithmetic.retain(|(node, ..)| graph.node(*node).inputs.iter().all(|input| may_have_range(*input)));
    if checks.is_empty() && shifts.is_empty() && arithmetic.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let dominators = &Dominators::of(graph, work);
    let entering = entering_counters(graph, dominators, &phi_blocks, work);
    let mut ranges = Ranges {
        graph,
        dominators,
        phi_blocks: &phi_blocks,
        assumed: &entering,
        known: ZoneMap::new_in(work),
    };
    let passing = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        checks.iter().copied().filter(|check| {
            let node = graph.node(*check);
            match (ranges.constant(node.inputs[1]), ranges.of(node.inputs[0])) {
                (Some(count), Some(index)) => index.min >= 0 && index.max < count,
                _ => false,
            }
        }),
        work,
    );
    let scaled = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        shifts.iter().copied().filter_map(|(shift, block)| {
            ranges
                .unscaled(shift)
                .map(|(value, offset)| (shift, block, value, offset))
        }),
        work,
    );

    // NB: With the counts of the bounds checks that their operands' ranges
    //     rely on: those of `exact[i]` are `exact_counts[exact[i].1..exact[i].2]`.
    let mut exact = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut exact_counts = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (node, block, position) in arithmetic.iter().copied() {
        let node_data = graph.node(node);
        let Op::Int32Binary { op } = node_data.op else {
            unreachable!("only int32 arithmetic is collected");
        };
        let start = exact_counts.len();
        // NB: Every dominating bounds check narrows the range of an
        //     operand further.
        let mut operand = |input: NodeId| {
            let mut range = ranges.of(input);
            let dominating = bounded.get(&graph.unrefined(input)).into_iter().flatten().filter(
                |(check_block, check_position, _)| {
                    if *check_block == block {
                        *check_position < position
                    } else {
                        dominators.dominates(*check_block, block)
                    }
                },
            );
            for (_, _, count) in dominating {
                let narrowed = ranges.below_count(range, *count);
                if narrowed.is_some() && narrowed != range {
                    exact_counts.push(*count);
                    range = narrowed;
                }
            }
            range
        };
        let operands = operand(node_data.inputs[0]).and_then(|lhs| Some((lhs, operand(node_data.inputs[1])?)));
        let is_exact = operands.is_some_and(|(lhs, rhs)| match op {
            BinaryOp::Add => lhs.sum(rhs).is_some(),
            BinaryOp::Sub => lhs.difference(rhs).is_some(),
            // NB: A zero product is -0 where an operand is negative.
            BinaryOp::Mul => {
                lhs.product(rhs).is_some() && ((lhs.min >= 0 && rhs.min >= 0) || (!lhs.contains(0) && !rhs.contains(0)))
            }
            _ => unreachable!("only additions, subtractions and multiplications are collected"),
        });
        if is_exact {
            exact.push((node, start, exact_counts.len()));
        } else {
            exact_counts.truncate(start);
        }
    }
    if passing.is_empty() && scaled.is_empty() && exact.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    // NB: Only the entering counters that the removed checks, the
    //     rewritten shifts and the operations that stop checking for overflow
    //     relied on get checked where they enter.
    let mut used = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut visited = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for check in &passing {
        ranges.assumptions_of(graph.node(*check).inputs[0], &mut used, &mut visited, &mut pending);
    }
    for (shift, ..) in &scaled {
        ranges.assumptions_of(*shift, &mut used, &mut visited, &mut pending);
    }
    for (node, start, end) in &exact {
        ranges.assumptions_of(*node, &mut used, &mut visited, &mut pending);
        for count in &exact_counts[*start..*end] {
            ranges.assumptions_of(*count, &mut used, &mut visited, &mut pending);
        }
    }
    let guards = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        entering
            .iter()
            .filter(|(value, _)| used.contains(value.index()))
            .map(|(value, range)| (*value, range.max + 1)),
        work,
    );

    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for check in passing.iter().copied() {
        replacements.replace(check, graph.node(check).inputs[0]);
        removed.insert(check.index());
    }
    let mut constants = Constants::new(graph, work);
    let mut guard_nodes = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (value, bound) in guards.iter().copied() {
        let count = constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from((bound as i32).cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32);
        let (frame_state, pc) = (graph.node(value).frame_state, graph.node(value).pc);
        let guard = graph.add_node(Node {
            op: Op::CheckBounds,
            inputs: graph.list(&[value, count]),
            repr: Some(Repr::Int32),
            frame_state,
            pc,
        });
        let block = graph
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .position(|block| block.body.contains(&value))
            .expect("values are in their blocks");
        let body = &mut graph.blocks[block].body;
        let position = body
            .iter()
            .position(|node| *node == value)
            .expect("the block has the value");
        body.insert(position + 1, guard);
        replacements.replace(value, guard);
        guard_nodes.push((guard, value));
    }
    for (shift, block, value, offset) in scaled.iter().copied() {
        let replacement = if offset == 0 {
            value
        } else {
            let offset = constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from((offset as i32).cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32);
            let sum = graph.add(
                Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Add },
                &[value, offset],
                Some(Repr::Int32),
                graph.node(shift).pc,
            );
            let body = &mut graph.blocks[block.index()].body;
            let position = body
                .iter()
                .position(|node| *node == shift)
                .expect("nodes are in their blocks");
            body.insert(position, sum);
            sum
        };
        replacements.replace(shift, replacement);
        removed.insert(shift.index());
    }
    for (node, ..) in exact.iter().copied() {
        super::edit::make_wrapping(graph, node);
    }
    replacements.apply(graph);
    // NB: The guards check the values they replace.
    for (guard, value) in guard_nodes.iter().copied() {
        graph.nodes[guard.index()].inputs[0] = value;
    }
    super::edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Branch fusion: a branch on a comparison that nothing else uses compares
//! the comparison's inputs itself, so code generation emits a compare and a
//! conditional jump instead of materializing a boolean and testing it.
//! A constant operand goes on the right, where it is an immediate.
//!
//! A block that only branches on a phi of booleans (where an instruction's
//! paths join, like those of a comparison) hands the branch to its
//! predecessors first: each branches on its own boolean, or jumps where it
//! is a constant, so that its comparison fuses with the branch there.

use super::edit;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::Block;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// The comparison of swapped operands that has the same result.
fn mirrored(comparison: Comparison) -> Comparison {
    match comparison {
        Comparison::LessThan => Comparison::GreaterThan,
        Comparison::LessThanEquals => Comparison::GreaterThanEquals,
        Comparison::GreaterThan => Comparison::LessThan,
        Comparison::GreaterThanEquals => Comparison::LessThanEquals,
        Comparison::Below => Comparison::Above,
        Comparison::BelowOrEqual => Comparison::AboveOrEqual,
        Comparison::Above => Comparison::Below,
        Comparison::AboveOrEqual => Comparison::BelowOrEqual,
        Comparison::StrictlyEquals
        | Comparison::StrictlyInequals
        | Comparison::LooselyEquals
        | Comparison::LooselyInequals => comparison,
    }
}

/// How many nodes and frame states use each node.
fn count_uses<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneVec<'w, u32> {
    let mut uses = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0u32, graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            for value in graph.used_values(node, work) {
                uses[value.index()] += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    uses
}

/// Makes the predecessors of each block that only branches on a phi of
/// booleans, which nothing else uses, branch on their input of the phi
/// themselves (through a new block on each edge, which jumps on), or jump
/// to the target of a constant one.
fn thread_boolean_phis(graph: &mut Graph, uses: &[u32], work: &Zone) {
    let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
    // NB: A block whose jump becomes a branch gets the two blocks of its edges. It then jumps nowhere, so it gets
    //     no more.
    let mut new_blocks: ZoneVec<Option<[BlockId; 2]>> = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, block_count, work);
    let mut threaded = ZoneBitSet::new_in(block_count, work);
    let mut predecessors = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in 0..block_count {
        let data = &graph.blocks[block];
        let (Some(control), [phi]) = (data.control, data.phis.as_slice()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let phi = *phi;
        let Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
            if_true,
            if_false,
        } = graph.node(control).op
        else {
            continue;
        };
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block);
        let jumps_here = |predecessor: &BlockId| {
            graph.control(*predecessor).op == Op::Jump { target: block_id } && predecessor.index() < block
        };
        if !data.body.is_empty()
            || data.is_loop_header
            || graph.node(control).inputs[0] != phi
            || uses[phi.index()] != 1
            || if_true.index() <= block
            || if_false.index() <= block
            || !data.predecessors.iter().all(jumps_here)
        {
            continue;
        }
        let pc = graph.node(control).pc;
        predecessors.assign(&data.predecessors);
        inputs.assign(&graph.node(phi).inputs);
        for (predecessor, input) in predecessors.iter().copied().zip(inputs.iter().copied()) {
            let truth = (graph.node(input).repr == Some(Repr::Bool))
                .then(|| graph.constant_value(input))
                .flatten();
            let predecessor_control = graph.control_id(predecessor);
            if let Some(bits) = truth {
                let target = if bits != 0 { if_true } else { if_false };
                edit::make_jump(graph, predecessor_control, target);
                add_predecessor(graph, target, predecessor, block_id);
                continue;
            }
            let is_cold = graph.block(predecessor).is_cold;
            let edges = [if_true, if_false].map(|target| {
                let edge = graph.add_block(Block {
                    predecessors: graph.list(&[predecessor]),
                    is_cold,
                    ..graph.new_block()
                });
                let jump = graph.add(Op::Jump { target }, &[], None, pc);
                graph.blocks[edge.index()].control = Some(jump);
                add_predecessor(graph, target, edge, block_id);
                edge
            });
            let data = &mut graph.nodes[predecessor_control.index()];
            data.op = Op::Branch {
                condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                if_true: edges[0],
                if_false: edges[1],
            };
            data.inputs.assign(&[input]);
            assert!(
                new_blocks[predecessor.index()].is_none(),
                "a block gets the blocks of one branch"
            );
            new_blocks[predecessor.index()] = Some(edges);
        }
        // NB: Nothing reaches the block anymore.
        for target in [if_true, if_false] {
            remove_predecessor(graph, target, block_id);
        }
        threaded.insert(block);
    }
    if threaded.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    // NB: The new blocks follow their predecessor, before their targets.
    let order = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        (0..block_count)
            .filter(|block| !threaded.contains(*block))
            .flat_map(|block| {
                core::iter::once(BlockId::from_index(block)).chain(new_blocks[block].into_iter().flatten())
            }),
        work,
    );
    graph.reorder_blocks(&order, work);
}

/// Removes `predecessor` from the predecessors of `target`, and its inputs
/// from the phis of `target`.
fn remove_predecessor(graph: &mut Graph, target: BlockId, predecessor: BlockId) {
    let index = graph
        .block(target)
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .position(|block| *block == predecessor)
        .expect("the threaded block is a predecessor of its targets");
    graph.blocks[target.index()].predecessors.remove(index);
    for phi in &graph.blocks[target.index()].phis {
        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.remove(index);
    }
}

/// Makes `predecessor` a predecessor of `target`, with the inputs to its
/// phis that `like` (a predecessor of it already) gives them.
fn add_predecessor(graph: &mut Graph, target: BlockId, predecessor: BlockId, like: BlockId) {
    let index = graph
        .block(target)
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .position(|block| *block == like)
        .expect("the target is a successor of the threaded block");
    graph.blocks[target.index()].predecessors.push(predecessor);
    for phi in &graph.blocks[target.index()].phis {
        let input: NodeId = graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs[index];
        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.push(input);
    }
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    // NB: Threading moves the uses of each phi's inputs to the branches.
    let uses = count_uses(graph, work);
    thread_boolean_phis(graph, &uses, work);
    let count = graph.nodes.len();
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    let mut inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let control = graph.control_id(BlockId::from_index(block));
        let Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
            if_true,
            if_false,
        } = graph.node(control).op
        else {
            continue;
        };
        let comparison = graph.node(control).inputs[0];
        // NB: The comparison must be in the branch's block, so that fusing
        //     it does not keep its inputs alive any longer than to its end.
        if uses[comparison.index()] != 1 || !graph.blocks[block].body.contains(&comparison) {
            continue;
        }
        let condition = match graph.node(comparison).op {
            Op::Int32Compare { comparison } => BranchCondition::Int32(comparison),
            Op::Float64Compare { comparison } => BranchCondition::Float64(comparison),
            Op::TaggedEquals { equal } => BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal },
            _ => continue,
        };
        inputs.assign(&graph.node(comparison).inputs);
        // NB: Code generation takes a constant on the right as an immediate.
        let constant = |input| graph.constant_value(input).is_some();
        let condition = if constant(inputs[0]) && !constant(inputs[1]) {
            inputs.swap(0, 1);
            match condition {
                BranchCondition::Int32(comparison) => BranchCondition::Int32(mirrored(comparison)),
                BranchCondition::Float64(comparison) => BranchCondition::Float64(mirrored(comparison)),
                condition => condition,
            }
        } else {
            condition
        };
        let data = &mut graph.nodes[control.index()];
        data.op = Op::Branch {
            condition,
            if_true,
            if_false,
        };
        data.inputs.assign(&inputs);
        removed.insert(comparison.index());
    }
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Branch splitting: a block that joins two paths only to branch on which of
//! them it came from goes away. Where an instruction's paths join with a
//! boolean phi of constants (like the "done" result of a for-in loop's next
//! key), and the next instruction branches on it, each path jumps straight
//! to its side of the branch instead, and the code there sees the values of
//! its own path rather than phis of both. A for-in loop's body then reads
//! the key the cache holds, not a phi that also holds `undefined`.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;

/// A block to split: its phis, the block that branches (itself, or the one
/// it jumps to), and for each side of the branch, the predecessor that takes
/// it and its target. The nodes before that branch, which each side gets a
/// copy of, are in `Lists::moved`.
struct Split {
    block: BlockId,
    branch_block: BlockId,
    sides: [(BlockId, BlockId); 2],
}

/// The lists that the splits use, which each split clears.
struct Lists<'w> {
    zone: &'w Zone,
    /// The nodes that each side gets a copy of.
    moved: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// The phis of the block, and the nodes in `moved`.
    phis: ZoneBitSet<'w>,
    frame_state_sides: ZoneVec<'w, (FrameStateId, usize)>,
    block_phis: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    predecessors: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
    renames: [ZoneVec<'w, (NodeId, NodeId)>; 2],
    copies: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
}

/// Whether a copy of `node` can run at the start of each side instead: an
/// `AssumeValid`, or a node without effects that cannot exit.
fn is_movable(graph: &Graph, node: NodeId) -> bool {
    let data = graph.node(node);
    if data.op == Op::AssumeValid {
        return true;
    }
    let properties = data.op.properties();
    data.frame_state.is_none()
        && data.op.exit_kind().is_none()
        && !data.op.is_control()
        && !properties.can_lazy_exit
        && !properties.is_call
        && !properties.runs_code
        && !properties.allocates
        && properties.reads.is_empty()
        && properties.writes.is_empty()
}

/// Which side's target dominates `block`, if one does.
fn side_of(dominators: &Dominators, split: &Split, block: BlockId) -> Option<usize> {
    (0..2).find(|side| dominators.dominates(split.sides[*side].1, block))
}

/// Whether `block` has the shape of `Split`, and its split if so.
/// It puts the nodes that each side gets a copy of in `moved`.
fn find_split(graph: &Graph, dominators: &Dominators, block: BlockId, moved: &mut ZoneVec<NodeId>) -> Option<Split> {
    let data = graph.block(block);
    if data.phis.is_empty() || data.is_loop_header || data.predecessors.len() != 2 || !dominators.is_reachable(block) {
        return None;
    }
    let movable = |body: &[NodeId]| body.iter().all(|node| is_movable(graph, *node));
    let branch_block = match graph.control(block).op {
        Op::Jump { target } if target.index() > block.index() => {
            let target_data = graph.block(target);
            if target_data.predecessors != [block] || !target_data.phis.is_empty() || target_data.is_loop_header {
                return None;
            }
            target
        }
        Op::Branch { .. } => block,
        _ => return None,
    };
    let branch_data = graph.block(branch_block);
    if !movable(&data.body) || (branch_block != block && !movable(&branch_data.body)) {
        return None;
    }
    let control = graph.control(branch_block);
    let Op::Branch {
        condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
        if_true,
        if_false,
    } = control.op
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let condition = control.inputs[0];
    if !data.phis.contains(&condition) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut sides = [None, None];
    for (predecessor, input) in data.predecessors.iter().zip(&graph.node(condition).inputs) {
        let side = match graph.constant_value(*input)? {
            0 => 1,
            _ => 0,
        };
        if sides[side].is_some() {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: An edge is redirected by replacing its target, which must not also be the other edge of a branch.
        let control = graph.control(*predecessor);
        if !matches!(control.op, Op::Jump { .. } | Op::Branch { .. })
            || control
                .op
                .successors()
                .iter()
                .filter(|successor| **successor == block)
                .count()
                != 1
        {
            return None;
        }
        sides[side] = Some(*predecessor);
    }
    let targets = [if_true, if_false];
    if if_true == if_false {
        return None;
    }
    for target in targets {
        let target_data = graph.block(target);
        if target_data.predecessors != [branch_block]
            || !target_data.phis.is_empty()
            || target_data.is_loop_header
            || target.index() <= branch_block.index()
        {
            return None;
        }
    }
    moved.assign(&data.body);
    if branch_block != block {
        moved.extend_from_slice(&branch_data.body);
    }
    // NB: Refines must stay at the head of their block, so the copies of the moved nodes cannot go before one.
    let starts_with_refine = |target: BlockId| {
        graph
            .block(target)
            .body
            .first()
            .is_some_and(|node| matches!(graph.node(*node).op, Op::Refine { .. }))
    };
    if !moved.is_empty() && targets.into_iter().any(starts_with_refine) {
        return None;
    }
    Some(Split {
        block,
        branch_block,
        sides: [(sides[0]?, targets[0]), (sides[1]?, targets[1])],
    })
}

/// The side of each frame state that a node or block of one side uses and
/// that holds one of the phis, or `None` if one of them cannot be renamed: a
/// node or block of another place uses it, or the phi is in a frame of its
/// chain other than its own, or in a virtual object. The sides go in `sides`.
fn frame_state_sides(
    graph: &Graph,
    dominators: &Dominators,
    split: &Split,
    phis: &ZoneBitSet,
    sides: &mut ZoneVec<(FrameStateId, usize)>,
    work: &Zone,
) -> Option<()> {
    sides.clear();
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
        if !dominators.is_reachable(block_id) || block_id == split.block || block_id == split.branch_block {
            continue;
        }
        // NB: Start frame states are renamed too: passes after this one still exit with them (see
        //     `edit::frame_state_entering()`).
        let frame_states = block
            .nodes()
            .filter_map(|node| graph.node(node).frame_state)
            .chain(block.start_frame_state);
        for frame_state in frame_states {
            let holds_phi = |id| {
                graph
                    .frame_state_values(id, work)
                    .any(|(_, value)| phis.contains(value.index()))
            };
            if !holds_phi(frame_state) {
                continue;
            }
            let own_holds = graph
                .frame_state(frame_state)
                .values
                .iter()
                .any(|(_, value)| phis.contains(value.index()));
            let chain_holds = graph.frame_state_chain(frame_state).skip(1).any(|id| {
                graph
                    .frame_state(id)
                    .values
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(_, value)| phis.contains(value.index()))
            });
            let all_count = graph.frame_state_values(frame_state, work).count();
            let chain_count: usize = graph
                .frame_state_chain(frame_state)
                .map(|id| graph.frame_state(id).values.len())
                .sum();
            // NB: Virtual objects add values past those of the chain's frames.
            let virtual_holds = all_count != chain_count
                && graph
                    .frame_state_values(frame_state, work)
                    .skip(chain_count)
                    .any(|(_, value)| phis.contains(value.index()));
            if !own_holds || chain_holds || virtual_holds {
                return None;
            }
            let side = side_of(dominators, split, block_id)?;
            match sides.iter().find(|(id, _)| *id == frame_state) {
                Some((_, existing)) if *existing != side => return None,
                Some(_) => {}
                None => sides.push((frame_state, side)),
            }
        }
    }
    Some(())
}

/// `value`, or what `renames` renames it to.
fn renamed(renames: &[(NodeId, NodeId)], value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
    renames
        .iter()
        .find(|(from, _)| *from == value)
        .map_or(value, |(_, to)| *to)
}

/// Splits one block, if any has the shape of `Split` and all uses of its
/// phis are on one side of its branch. Returns whether it split one. The
/// data of the split that `lists` does not keep goes in `step`.
fn split_one(graph: &mut Graph, dominators: &mut Dominators, lists: &mut Lists, step: &Zone) -> bool {
    dominators.compute(graph);
    let dominators = &*dominators;
    // NB: Splits add nodes, so the set grows ahead of them.
    if lists.phis.capacity() < graph.nodes.len() {
        lists.phis = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len().max(lists.phis.capacity() * 2), lists.zone);
    }
    for index in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let Some(split) = find_split(graph, dominators, BlockId::from_index(index), &mut lists.moved) else {
            continue;
        };
        let phis = &mut lists.phis;
        phis.clear();
        for phi in &graph.block(split.block).phis {
            phis.insert(phi.index());
        }
        for node in &lists.moved {
            phis.insert(node.index());
        }
        let phis = &lists.phis;
        // Every use of a phi must be on one side. A phi's input is used at the end of its predecessor.
        let mut uses_ok = true;
        'blocks: for (block_index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block_index);
            if !dominators.is_reachable(block_id) || block_id == split.block || block_id == split.branch_block {
                continue;
            }
            for phi in &block.phis {
                for (predecessor, input) in block.predecessors.iter().zip(&graph.node(*phi).inputs) {
                    if phis.contains(input.index()) && side_of(dominators, &split, *predecessor).is_none() {
                        uses_ok = false;
                        break 'blocks;
                    }
                }
            }
            let side = side_of(dominators, &split, block_id);
            for node in block.body.iter().chain(block.control.iter()) {
                if graph
                    .node(*node)
                    .inputs
                    .iter()
                    .any(|input| phis.contains(input.index()))
                    && side.is_none()
                {
                    uses_ok = false;
                    break 'blocks;
                }
            }
        }
        if !uses_ok {
            continue;
        }
        if frame_state_sides(graph, dominators, &split, phis, &mut lists.frame_state_sides, step).is_none() {
            continue;
        }

        let Lists {
            moved: moved_nodes,
            frame_state_sides,
            block_phis,
            predecessors,
            renames,
            copies,
            ..
        } = lists;
        block_phis.assign(&graph.block(split.block).phis);
        predecessors.assign(&graph.block(split.block).predecessors);
        for (side, side_renames) in renames.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let predecessor = split.sides[side].0;
            let index = predecessors
                .iter()
                .position(|block| *block == predecessor)
                .expect("the side's predecessor enters the block");
            side_renames.clear();
            side_renames.extend(block_phis.iter().map(|phi| (*phi, graph.node(*phi).inputs[index])));
        }
        // Each side starts with copies of the moved nodes, with its values.
        for (side, side_renames) in renames.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let target = split.sides[side].1;
            copies.clear();
            for moved in moved_nodes.iter() {
                let mut node = graph.node(*moved).clone();
                for input in &mut node.inputs {
                    *input = renamed(side_renames, *input);
                }
                node.frame_state = node.frame_state.map(|id| {
                    let mut frame_state = graph.frame_state(id).clone();
                    for (_, value) in &mut frame_state.values {
                        *value = renamed(side_renames, *value);
                    }
                    graph.add_frame_state(frame_state)
                });
                let copy = graph.add_node(node);
                side_renames.push((*moved, copy));
                copies.push(copy);
            }
            let body = &mut graph.blocks[target.index()].body;
            copies.extend_from_slice(body);
            body.assign(copies);
        }
        let rename = |side: usize, value: NodeId| renamed(&renames[side], value);

        // Rename the uses of each side.
        for block_index in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block_index);
            if !dominators.is_reachable(block_id) || block_id == split.block || block_id == split.branch_block {
                continue;
            }
            // NB: The blocks stay as they are while the inputs of their nodes change.
            let block = &graph.blocks[block_index];
            for phi in &block.phis {
                for (input_index, predecessor) in block.predecessors.iter().enumerate() {
                    if let Some(side) = side_of(dominators, &split, *predecessor) {
                        let input = graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs[input_index];
                        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs[input_index] = rename(side, input);
                    }
                }
            }
            if let Some(side) = side_of(dominators, &split, block_id) {
                for node in block.body.iter().chain(block.control.iter()) {
                    for input in &mut graph.nodes[node.index()].inputs {
                        *input = rename(side, *input);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for (frame_state, side) in frame_state_sides.iter().copied() {
            for (_, value) in &mut graph.frame_states[frame_state.0 as usize].values {
                *value = rename(side, *value);
            }
        }

        // Each side's predecessor jumps straight to its target.
        for side in 0..2 {
            let (predecessor, target) = split.sides[side];
            graph.replace_successor(predecessor, split.block, target);
            graph.blocks[target.index()].predecessors.assign(&[predecessor]);
        }
        graph.blocks[split.block.index()].predecessors.clear();
        for phi in block_phis.iter() {
            graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.clear();
        }
        super::edit::clean_up_control_flow(graph, step);
        return true;
    }
    false
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone, steps: &mut [Zone; 2]) {
    let [step, _] = steps;
    let mut lists = Lists {
        zone: work,
        moved: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        phis: ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, work),
        frame_state_sides: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        block_phis: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        predecessors: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        renames: [ZoneVec::new_in(work), ZoneVec::new_in(work)],
        copies: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
    };
    let mut dominators = Dominators::new_in(work);
    for _ in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        // NB: Each split cleans up the control flow, with data as large as the graph, which goes when the split ends.
        if !step.scope(|step| split_one(graph, &mut dominators, &mut lists, step)) {
            break;
        }
    }
}
