//! Redundant check and load elimination.
//!
//! A forward dataflow analysis over the control flow graph computes, before
//! every node, what is known about values (see `Facts`): what kinds of value
//! they may be, which shapes and elements kinds objects may have, which
//! prototype chains are valid, which values passed which value checks, and
//! what named properties, bindings, element counts and elements hold. Loop
//! headers start optimistically with what holds on entry and are revisited
//! until what the back edges bring agrees with it.
//!
//! Branches on the kind of a value tell their targets what it is, and
//! become jumps where what is known decides them. So do branches on values
//! alone (comparisons, builtin tests), which go the way a branch on the same
//! values went before.
//!
//! With those facts, checks that already passed are removed, loads of a
//! property whose value is known are replaced by that value (including
//! values stored before, and the constants a value check established), and
//! shape switches on objects whose shapes are known only keep the cases
//! that can match, or become jumps.
//!
//! A removed check's value is the latest refinement of its input on every
//! path to it, which a check or branch that passed made, so that what uses
//! it stays behind that check. Checks with no such refinement stay.
//!
//! Objects keep stable shapes (see `Dependency::StableShape`) while other
//! code runs, as long as the compiled code stays valid. The first shape
//! check that relies on that after other code ran becomes an `AssumeValid`,
//! and the code depends on the stable shapes known from then on.

use super::edit;
use super::edit::Constants;
use super::edit::Replacements;
use super::facts::BranchKey;
use super::facts::ElementCount;
use super::facts::Facts;
use super::facts::Location;
use super::facts::Moved;
use super::facts::ValueKind;
use super::facts::elements_kind_implies;
use crate::bytecode::OpCode;
use crate::code::Dependency;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::ShapeCheck;
use crate::ir::value;
use crate::snapshot::CellId;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// What the analysis decided for the nodes of one visit of the graph.
struct Decisions<'w> {
    replacements: Replacements<'w>,
    removed: ZoneBitSet<'w>,
    /// Control nodes to replace, with what.
    controls: ZoneVec<'w, (NodeId, NewControl<'w>)>,
    /// Shape checks that become `AssumeValid` nodes.
    assumptions: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// The stable shapes the code relies on staying stable.
    stable_shapes: ZoneVec<'w, CellId>,
    /// The inputs of the node being visited, as the analysis knows them.
    inputs: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// The cases of the shape switch being visited that can match.
    possible: ZoneVec<'w, (ShapeCheck, BlockId)>,
}

/// Facts flowing along edges, each with the block the edge leads to.
type Edges<'w> = ZoneVec<'w, (BlockId, Facts<'w>)>;

/// What a control node is replaced with.
enum NewControl<'w> {
    Jump {
        target: BlockId,
    },
    /// A shape switch with fewer cases, each a shape and its target.
    ShapeSwitch {
        cases: &'w [(ShapeCheck, BlockId)],
    },
}

impl Decisions<'_> {
    /// Forgets the decisions of the last visit.
    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.replacements.clear();
        self.removed.clear();
        self.controls.clear();
        self.assumptions.clear();
        self.stable_shapes.clear();
    }

    /// The value the analysis knows `value` as: what it is replaced by, and
    /// the value it refines (facts are about values, whatever refines them).
    fn value(&self, graph: &Graph, value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        let mut value = self.replacements.resolve(value);
        loop {
            let unrefined = graph.unrefined(value);
            let replaced = self.replacements.resolve(unrefined);
            if replaced == value {
                return value;
            }
            value = replaced;
        }
    }
}

/// The edges out of a block, each with the slot of the facts along it in the `Store`.
type EdgeSlots<'w> = ZoneVec<'w, (BlockId, u32)>;

/// The facts that the visits of blocks hand on to later ones, in a step zone. Each is in a slot, which the tables of
/// `Round` name, so that a move of the facts in use copies those and nothing else.
struct Store<'f> {
    zone: &'f Zone,
    /// The facts of each slot, or none for a slot that is free.
    facts: ZoneVec<'f, Option<Facts<'f>>>,
    /// The facts along the edges into the block being visited, which is empty between visits.
    incoming: Edges<'f>,
    /// The facts along the edges out of the block being visited, which is empty between visits.
    outgoing: Edges<'f>,
}

impl<'f> Store<'f> {
    fn new_in(zone: &'f Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            zone,
            facts: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            incoming: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            outgoing: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
        }
    }

    /// Puts `facts` in a slot that `free` lists, or in a new one, and returns the slot.
    fn put(&mut self, facts: Facts<'f>, free: &mut ZoneVec<u32>) -> u32 {
        if let Some(slot) = free.pop() {
            self.facts[slot as usize] = Some(facts);
            return slot;
        }
        self.facts.push(Some(facts));
        u32::try_from(self.facts.len() - 1).expect("the facts in use fit in 2^32 slots")
    }

    /// Takes the facts of `slot`, which becomes free.
    fn take(&mut self, slot: u32, free: &mut ZoneVec<u32>) -> Facts<'f> {
        free.push(slot);
        self.facts[slot as usize].take().expect("a slot in use holds facts")
    }

    fn get(&self, slot: u32) -> &Facts<'f> {
        self.facts[slot as usize].as_ref().expect("a slot in use holds facts")
    }

    fn get_mut(&mut self, slot: u32) -> &mut Facts<'f> {
        self.facts[slot as usize].as_mut().expect("a slot in use holds facts")
    }

    /// The same facts in the same slots, in `zone`, with lists that are shared where they are here.
    fn move_to(self, zone: &Zone) -> Store<'_> {
        debug_assert!(self.incoming.is_empty() && self.outgoing.is_empty());
        let mut moved = Moved::new_in(zone);
        let facts = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            self.facts
                .iter()
                .map(|facts| facts.as_ref().map(|facts| facts.move_to(&mut moved))),
            zone,
        );
        Store {
            zone,
            facts,
            incoming: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            outgoing: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
        }
    }
}

/// How many bytes a step zone of the pass may hold before the facts still in use move to the other one: twice what
/// they took right after the last move, and at least 1 MiB, so that the zone holds at most about three times the facts
/// in use, and the facts of small functions never move.
fn move_limit(kept: usize) -> usize {
    (2 * kept).max(1 << 20)
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone, steps: &mut [Zone; 2]) {
    let mut constants = Constants::new(graph, work);
    // NB: The visits add no nodes to blocks, only constants.
    let mut decisions = Decisions {
        replacements: Replacements::new(graph, work),
        removed: ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work),
        controls: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        assumptions: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        stable_shapes: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        inputs: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        possible: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
    };
    let mut round = Round::new(graph, &mut constants, &mut decisions, work);
    // NB: The facts of each block copy lists of the facts before it, which a zone takes back only all at once. So
    //     the visits stop when the store of the facts holds much more than after the last move, the facts in use
    //     move to the other step zone, and the zone they leave is reset.
    let [zone, other] = steps;
    let mut store = Store::new_in(zone);
    let mut kept = 0;
    loop {
        if round.run(&mut store, move_limit(kept)) {
            break;
        }
        let mut moved = store.move_to(other);
        kept = other.used();
        zone.reset();
        if round.run(&mut moved, move_limit(kept)) {
            break;
        }
        store = moved.move_to(zone);
        kept = zone.used();
        other.reset();
    }

    decisions.replacements.apply(graph);
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &decisions.removed);
    for node in decisions.assumptions.drain_all() {
        graph.nodes[node.index()].op = Op::AssumeValid;
        graph.nodes[node.index()].inputs.clear();
        graph.nodes[node.index()].repr = None;
    }
    for shape in decisions.stable_shapes.drain_all() {
        graph.depend_on(Dependency::StableShape(shape));
    }
    let changed_control_flow = !decisions.controls.is_empty();
    for (node, control) in decisions.controls.drain_all() {
        match control {
            NewControl::Jump { target } => edit::make_jump(graph, node, target),
            NewControl::ShapeSwitch { cases } => {
                let zone = graph.zone;
                graph.nodes[node.index()].op = Op::ShapeSwitch {
                    shapes: zone.alloc_slice_from_iter(cases.iter().map(|(shape, _)| *shape)),
                    targets: zone.alloc_slice_from_iter(cases.iter().map(|(_, target)| *target)),
                };
            }
        }
    }
    if changed_control_flow {
        edit::clean_up_control_flow(graph, work);
    }
}

/// The rounds of visits of the blocks, until the facts stop changing, with what lasts from one visit to the next
/// apart from the facts themselves: the slots of the facts in the `Store`, which can move to another zone between
/// two visits.
struct Round<'a, 'g, 'w> {
    graph: &'a mut Graph<'g>,
    constants: &'a mut Constants<'w>,
    decisions: &'a mut Decisions<'w>,
    /// Whether each block has predecessors later in the order. Only those can see other facts in another round:
    /// they decide when the rounds are done.
    revisited: ZoneVec<'w, bool>,
    visited: ZoneVec<'w, bool>,
    skipped: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
    /// For each block, the edges out of it from its latest visit that no block took the facts of yet.
    edges: ZoneVec<'w, EdgeSlots<'w>>,
    /// For each block that `revisited` holds for, the slot of its facts at entry from its latest visit, if any.
    entry_facts: ZoneVec<'w, Option<u32>>,
    /// The slots of the store that are free.
    free: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// Whether the facts changed in this round.
    changed: bool,
    /// The block to visit next in this round.
    next: usize,
}

impl<'a, 'g, 'w> Round<'a, 'g, 'w> {
    fn new(
        graph: &'a mut Graph<'g>,
        constants: &'a mut Constants<'w>,
        decisions: &'a mut Decisions<'w>,
        work: &'w Zone,
    ) -> Self {
        let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
        let revisited = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            (0..block_count).map(|block| {
                graph.blocks[block]
                    .predecessors
                    .iter()
                    .any(|predecessor| predecessor.index() >= block)
            }),
            work,
        );
        let mut round = Self {
            graph,
            constants,
            decisions,
            revisited,
            visited: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, block_count, work),
            skipped: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            edges: ZoneVec::from_iter_in((0..block_count).map(|_| ZoneVec::new_in(work)), work),
            entry_facts: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, block_count, work),
            free: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            changed: false,
            next: 0,
        };
        round.start();
        round
    }

    /// Starts a round.
    fn start(&mut self) {
        self.decisions.clear();
        self.changed = false;
        self.visited.fill(false);
        self.skipped.clear();
        self.next = 0;
    }

    /// Visits blocks until the facts stop changing, and returns true, or until `store` holds more than `limit` bytes
    /// before a visit, and returns false. It goes on where it stopped when it is called again.
    fn run(&mut self, store: &mut Store, limit: usize) -> bool {
        loop {
            if self.next == self.graph.blocks.len() {
                // NB: A block that only back edges lead to (code after an entry that comes later in the order,
                //     such as an on-stack replacement entry) is skipped until they bring facts, which they did if
                //     a predecessor visited later has facts along its edge. What can be reached from it then saw
                //     other facts along the other paths in this round.
                let edges = &self.edges;
                let graph = &*self.graph;
                self.changed |= self.skipped.iter().any(|block| {
                    graph
                        .block(*block)
                        .predecessors
                        .iter()
                        .any(|predecessor| edges[predecessor.index()].iter().any(|(target, _)| target == block))
                });
                if !self.changed {
                    return true;
                }
                self.start();
                continue;
            }
            if store.zone.used() > limit {
                return false;
            }
            self.visit(store, self.next);
            self.next += 1;
        }
    }

    /// Frees the slots of the edges out of `block`.
    fn clear_edges(&mut self, store: &mut Store, block: usize) {
        for (_, slot) in self.edges[block].drain_all() {
            store.take(slot, &mut self.free);
        }
    }

    /// Visits `block`, with the facts along the edges into it, and hands on the facts along the edges out of it.
    fn visit(&mut self, store: &mut Store, block: usize) {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block);
        let mut incoming = store.incoming.take();
        let facts = facts_at_entry(
            self.graph,
            block_id,
            (&mut self.edges, store, &mut self.free, &mut incoming),
            &self.visited,
            &self.revisited,
            self.decisions,
        );
        store.incoming = incoming;
        let Some(mut facts) = facts else {
            // No visited predecessor reaches this block.
            self.clear_edges(store, block);
            self.skipped.push(block_id);
            return;
        };
        self.visited[block] = true;
        if self.revisited[block] {
            match self.entry_facts[block] {
                Some(slot) if *store.get(slot) == facts => {}
                Some(slot) => {
                    self.changed = true;
                    *store.get_mut(slot) = facts.share();
                }
                None => {
                    self.changed = true;
                    self.entry_facts[block] = Some(store.put(facts.share(), &mut self.free));
                }
            }
        }
        self.clear_edges(store, block);
        let mut outgoing = store.outgoing.take();
        visit_block(
            self.graph,
            self.constants,
            block_id,
            facts,
            self.decisions,
            &mut outgoing,
        );
        for (target, facts) in outgoing.drain_all() {
            let slot = store.put(facts, &mut self.free);
            self.edges[block].push((target, slot));
        }
        store.outgoing = outgoing;
    }
}

/// The facts at the start of `block`, which takes them from the edges into
/// it: what holds on every edge into it from a visited predecessor. Edges
/// from predecessors not visited yet in this round (loop back edges) are
/// assumed to agree, and checked when the next round sees what they bring.
/// Roots start knowing nothing, except that the code is valid: invalidated
/// code is discarded, so nothing enters it.
///
/// A phi of a block that no back edge leads to is of a kind one of its
/// inputs is, where it comes from.
///
/// It takes the facts of the edges into the block out of `store`, whose
/// slots `edges` names, and frees their slots in `free`. `incoming` is a list
/// for the facts along the edges into the block, which is empty and stays
/// empty.
fn facts_at_entry<'f>(
    graph: &Graph,
    block: BlockId,
    (edges, store, free, incoming): (&mut [EdgeSlots], &mut Store<'f>, &mut ZoneVec<u32>, &mut Edges<'f>),
    visited: &[bool],
    revisited: &[bool],
    decisions: &Decisions,
) -> Option<Facts<'f>> {
    let zone = store.zone;
    let predecessors = &graph.block(block).predecessors;
    if predecessors.is_empty() {
        let mut facts = Facts::new_in(zone);
        facts.assume_code_valid();
        return Some(facts);
    }
    for predecessor in predecessors {
        let is_back_edge = predecessor.index() >= block.index();
        if !is_back_edge && !visited[predecessor.index()] {
            continue;
        }
        let edges = &mut edges[predecessor.index()];
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < edges.len() {
            if edges[index].0 == block {
                let (_, slot) = edges.remove(index);
                incoming.push((*predecessor, store.take(slot, free)));
            } else {
                index += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let phis = &graph.block(block).phis;
    // NB: Each predecessor brings the facts along its one edge here.
    let knows_phi_inputs = !revisited[block.index()]
        && !phis.is_empty()
        && incoming.len() == predecessors.len()
        && predecessors
            .iter()
            .all(|predecessor| incoming.iter().filter(|(source, _)| source == predecessor).count() == 1);
    if !knows_phi_inputs {
        return match incoming.len() {
            0 => None,
            1 => incoming.pop().map(|(_, facts)| facts),
            _ => Some(Facts::merge(zone, incoming.drain_all().map(|(_, facts)| facts))),
        };
    }
    let mut facts = Facts::merge(zone, incoming.iter_mut().map(|(_, facts)| facts.share()));
    for phi in phis {
        let inputs = graph
            .node(*phi)
            .inputs
            .iter()
            .zip(predecessors)
            .map(|(input, predecessor)| {
                let (_, facts) = incoming
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(source, _)| source == predecessor)
                    .expect("each predecessor brings facts");
                (facts, decisions.value(graph, *input))
            });
        facts.set_phi_kinds(graph, *phi, inputs);
    }
    incoming.clear();
    Some(facts)
}

/// Applies the nodes of `block` to `facts`, recording decisions, and adds
/// the facts flowing along each of its outgoing edges to `edges`.
fn visit_block<'f>(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    constants: &mut Constants,
    block: BlockId,
    mut facts: Facts<'f>,
    decisions: &mut Decisions,
    edges: &mut Edges<'f>,
) {
    // NB: A phi makes another value of the objects it merges, which anything
    //     may see.
    for phi in &graph.block(block).phis {
        for input in &graph.node(*phi).inputs {
            facts.expose(decisions.value(graph, *input));
        }
    }
    for index in 0..graph.block(block).body.len() {
        let node = graph.block(block).body[index];
        visit_node(graph, constants, node, &mut facts, decisions);
    }
    let control = graph.control_id(block);
    // A branch on the kind of a value (or of the elements of an object)
    // knows it where it holds, and only keeps the edge that what is known
    // already decides.
    if let Op::Branch {
        condition,
        if_true,
        if_false,
    } = graph.node(control).op
        && Facts::is_about_kinds(condition)
    {
        let value = decisions.value(graph, graph.node(control).inputs[0]);
        if let Some(holds) = facts.decides(graph, value, condition) {
            let target = if holds { if_true } else { if_false };
            decisions.controls.push((control, NewControl::Jump { target }));
            edges.push((target, facts));
            return;
        }
        let mut passed = facts.share();
        passed.forget_refinement(value);
        passed.set_passed(value, condition);
        facts.set_failed(value, condition);
        edges.push((if_true, passed));
        edges.push((if_false, facts));
        return;
    }
    // A branch on values alone goes the way a branch on the same values
    // went before.
    if let Op::Branch { .. } = graph.node(control).op {
        let mut inputs = decisions.inputs.take();
        inputs.clear();
        inputs.extend(
            graph
                .node(control)
                .inputs
                .iter()
                .map(|input| decisions.value(graph, *input)),
        );
        let undecided = visit_value_branch(graph, control, &inputs, facts, decisions, edges);
        decisions.inputs = inputs;
        let Some(undecided) = undecided else {
            return;
        };
        facts = undecided;
    }
    let Op::ShapeSwitch { shapes, targets } = graph.node(control).op else {
        let successors = graph.successors(block);
        let Some((last, others)) = successors.split_last() else {
            return;
        };
        for successor in others {
            edges.push((*successor, facts.share()));
        }
        edges.push((*last, facts));
        return;
    };
    let object = decisions.value(graph, graph.node(control).inputs[0]);
    // NB: Shapes known only while the code is valid would need a check.
    let known = facts.shapes(object).filter(|_| !facts.is_unvalidated(object));
    let mut possible = decisions.possible.take();
    possible.clear();
    possible.extend(
        shapes
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .zip(targets.iter().copied())
            .filter(|(shape, _)| known.is_none_or(|known| known.contains(shape))),
    );
    let covers_known =
        known.is_some_and(|known| known.iter().all(|shape| possible.iter().any(|(case, _)| case == shape)));
    match possible.as_slice() {
        [(_, target)] if covers_known => decisions.controls.push((control, NewControl::Jump { target: *target })),
        _ if possible.len() < shapes.len() && !possible.is_empty() => {
            let cases = possible.zone().alloc_slice_copy(&possible);
            decisions.controls.push((control, NewControl::ShapeSwitch { cases }));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    for (shape, target) in &possible {
        let mut case_facts = facts.share();
        case_facts.set_shapes(object, &[*shape]);
        edges.push((*target, case_facts));
    }
    decisions.possible = possible;
}

/// The edges of the branch `control` on values alone, its `inputs` as the
/// analysis knows them: it goes the way a branch on the same values went
/// before. Gives `facts` back where it is no such branch.
fn visit_value_branch<'f>(
    graph: &Graph,
    control: NodeId,
    inputs: &[NodeId],
    mut facts: Facts<'f>,
    decisions: &mut Decisions,
    edges: &mut Edges<'f>,
) -> Option<Facts<'f>> {
    let Op::Branch {
        condition,
        if_true,
        if_false,
    } = graph.node(control).op
    else {
        return Some(facts);
    };
    // NB: A value of a known kind is no empty value (like a binding that
    //     is initialized, which a store of it checks).
    if let BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal } = condition
        && graph.constant_value(inputs[1]) == Some(value::EMPTY)
        && facts.value_kind(inputs[0]).is_some()
    {
        let target = if equal { if_false } else { if_true };
        decisions.controls.push((control, NewControl::Jump { target }));
        edges.push((target, facts));
        return None;
    }
    let Some(key) = BranchKey::of(graph, condition, inputs) else {
        return Some(facts);
    };
    if let Some(holds) = facts.branch_outcome(&key) {
        let target = if holds { if_true } else { if_false };
        decisions.controls.push((control, NewControl::Jump { target }));
        edges.push((target, facts));
        return None;
    }
    let mut passed = facts.share();
    passed.set_branch_outcome(key, true);
    facts.set_branch_outcome(key, false);
    // Strings that are the empty value where only the slow path makes
    // them are strings where they are not.
    if let BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal } = condition
        && graph.constant_value(inputs[1]) == Some(value::EMPTY)
        && matches!(
            graph.node(inputs[0]).op,
            Op::ConcatenateStrings { .. } | Op::IntegerToString
        )
    {
        let not_empty = if equal { &mut facts } else { &mut passed };
        not_empty.set_value_kind(inputs[0], ValueKind::String);
    }
    edges.push((if_true, passed));
    edges.push((if_false, facts));
    None
}

/// Whether input `index` of a node with `op` is an object whose properties
/// (or shape) the node accesses, and nothing else.
fn accesses_properties(op: &Op, index: usize) -> bool {
    match op {
        Op::CheckObject | Op::CellAddress | Op::InitializeNamed { .. } => index == 0,
        Op::CheckShape { .. }
        | Op::ShapeSwitch { .. }
        | Op::LoadNamed { .. }
        | Op::CheckAccessorFunction { .. }
        | Op::LoadAccessorFunction { .. } => true,
        Op::StoreNamed { .. } | Op::AddNamed { .. } => index != 1,
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn visit_node(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    constants: &mut Constants,
    node_id: NodeId,
    facts: &mut Facts,
    decisions: &mut Decisions,
) {
    let mut inputs = decisions.inputs.take();
    inputs.clear();
    inputs.extend(
        graph
            .node(node_id)
            .inputs
            .iter()
            .map(|input| decisions.value(graph, *input)),
    );
    visit_node_with_inputs(graph, constants, node_id, &inputs, facts, decisions);
    decisions.inputs = inputs;
}

/// `visit_node()`, with the inputs of the node as the analysis knows them.
fn visit_node_with_inputs(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    constants: &mut Constants,
    node_id: NodeId,
    inputs: &[NodeId],
    facts: &mut Facts,
    decisions: &mut Decisions,
) {
    let node = graph.node(node_id);
    let input = |index: usize| inputs[index];
    for (index, input) in inputs.iter().enumerate() {
        if facts.is_unexposed(*input) && !accesses_properties(&node.op, index) {
            facts.expose(*input);
        }
    }
    for value in graph.legacy_argument_values_read_by(node_id, |_| true) {
        facts.expose(decisions.value(graph, value));
    }
    // NB: A check known to pass is replaced by what refined its input
    //     before (see `Facts::refinement()`), and stays where nothing did.
    let refines = node.op.refined_input().is_some() && node.repr.is_some();
    let anchor = if refines {
        facts
            .refinement(input(0))
            .or_else(|| graph.constant_value(input(0)).map(|_| input(0)))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let removable = !refines || anchor.is_some();
    let mut remove = false;
    let mut becomes_assumption = false;
    match node.op {
        Op::CheckObject => {
            let value = input(0);
            let is_object_constant = graph
                .constant_value(value)
                .is_some_and(|bits| crate::ir::value::tag(bits) == crate::ir::value::OBJECT_TAG);
            remove = removable && (is_object_constant || facts.is_object(value));
            facts.set_object(value);
        }
        Op::CheckShape { shapes } => {
            let object = input(0);
            remove = removable
                && facts
                    .shapes(object)
                    .is_some_and(|known| known.iter().all(|shape| shapes.contains(shape)));
            if remove && facts.is_unvalidated(object) {
                // The object still has its stable shape if the code is still
                // valid, and so do all objects with known shapes after this.
                if !facts.is_code_valid() {
                    remove = false;
                    becomes_assumption = true;
                    decisions.assumptions.push(node_id);
                    if let Some(anchor) = anchor {
                        decisions.replacements.replace(node_id, anchor);
                    }
                    facts.assume_code_valid();
                }
                validate(facts, &graph.stable_shapes, decisions);
            } else if !remove {
                facts.set_shapes(object, shapes);
            }
        }
        // NB: Values that pass are int32 values.
        Op::CheckInt32 => facts.set_value_kind(input(0), ValueKind::Int32),
        // NB: ConcatString makes a string, also in its slow path, which may
        //     run other code.
        ref op @ Op::CallSlowPath {
            opcode: OpCode::ConcatString,
            ..
        } => {
            facts.apply(&op.properties(), &graph.stable_shapes);
            facts.set_value_kind(node_id, ValueKind::String);
        }
        Op::CheckPrototypeChainValid { validity } => {
            remove = facts.is_prototype_chain_valid(validity);
            facts.set_prototype_chain_valid(validity);
        }
        Op::CheckValue { expected, .. } => {
            let value = input(0);
            remove =
                removable && (graph.constant_value(value) == Some(expected) || facts.is_checked_value(value, expected));
            if !remove {
                facts.set_checked_value(value, expected);
                // A checked load of a property or a global binding makes it
                // known to hold the constant.
                if let Some(location @ (Location::Named { .. } | Location::GlobalBinding { .. })) =
                    loaded_location(graph, decisions, value)
                    && facts.contents(location) == Some(value)
                {
                    let constant = constants.get(graph, expected);
                    facts.set_contents(location, constant);
                }
            }
        }
        Op::LoadNamed { .. }
        | Op::LoadGlobalBinding { .. }
        | Op::LoadEnvironmentBinding { .. }
        | Op::LoadElementsLength
        | Op::LoadElementsCapacity
        | Op::LoadTypedArrayLength
        | Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset
        | Op::LoadElementAt { .. } => {
            let location = loaded_location(graph, decisions, node_id).expect("loads load a location");
            remove = reuse_contents(facts, location, node_id, decisions);
        }
        Op::AssumeValid => {
            remove = facts.is_code_valid();
            facts.assume_code_valid();
            validate(facts, &graph.stable_shapes, decisions);
        }
        Op::StoreGlobalBinding { environment, index } => {
            facts.forget_bindings_at(index);
            facts.set_contents(Location::GlobalBinding { environment, index }, input(0));
        }
        Op::StoreEnvironmentBinding { index } => {
            facts.forget_bindings_at(index);
            let location = Location::Binding {
                environment: input(0),
                index,
            };
            facts.set_contents(location, input(1));
        }
        Op::StoreNamed { offset, .. } => {
            let (object, value) = (input(0), input(1));
            facts.forget_named_properties_at(offset);
            facts.set_contents(Location::Named { object, offset }, value);
        }
        Op::AddNamed { offset, shape, .. } => {
            // NB: Values known to have the old shape may be the object, which
            //     has the new one now. No object had the new property before.
            let object = input(0);
            facts.forget_shapes_of(object);
            facts.set_object(object);
            facts.set_shapes(
                object,
                &[ShapeCheck {
                    shape,
                    dictionary_generation: None,
                }],
            );
            facts.set_contents(Location::Named { object, offset }, input(1));
        }
        Op::CheckElements { kind } => {
            let object = input(0);
            // NB: A holey access takes packed elements too.
            remove = removable
                && graph
                    .constant_value(object)
                    .and_then(|bits| graph.typed_array_constants.iter().find(|(value, _)| *value == bits))
                    .map(|(_, array)| ElementsKind::TypedArray(array.element))
                    .or_else(|| facts.elements_kind(object))
                    .is_some_and(|known| elements_kind_implies(known, kind) == Some(true));
            facts.set_object(object);
            if !remove {
                facts.set_elements_kind(object, kind);
            }
        }
        Op::AllocateObject {
            shape, property_count, ..
        } => {
            // A new object of the shape, with every property undefined.
            new_object(facts, node_id);
            facts.set_unexposed(node_id);
            facts.set_shapes(
                node_id,
                &[ShapeCheck {
                    shape,
                    dictionary_generation: None,
                }],
            );
            let undefined = constants.get(graph, crate::ir::value::UNDEFINED);
            for offset in 0..property_count {
                facts.set_contents(
                    Location::Named {
                        object: node_id,
                        offset,
                    },
                    undefined,
                );
            }
        }
        Op::InitializeNamed { offset } => {
            // NB: Nothing else can see the object yet, so no other object's
            //     property is the same one.
            facts.set_contents(
                Location::Named {
                    object: input(0),
                    offset,
                },
                input(1),
            );
        }
        // NB: SliceArguments is a runtime call that makes a new array and
        //     runs nothing else.
        Op::AllocateFunction { .. } | Op::SliceArguments => new_object(facts, node_id),
        Op::AllocateArray { count } => {
            // A new array, with packed elements if it has any.
            new_object(facts, node_id);
            if count != 0 {
                facts.set_elements_kind(node_id, ElementsKind::Packed);
            }
        }
        Op::CheckAppendableArray | Op::CheckArray => {
            // It exits for anything but arrays.
            facts.set_object(input(0));
        }
        ref op => {
            facts.apply(&op.properties(), &graph.stable_shapes);
        }
    }
    if remove {
        if let Some(anchor) = anchor {
            decisions.replacements.replace(node_id, anchor);
        }
        decisions.removed.insert(node_id.index());
    } else if refines && !becomes_assumption {
        facts.set_refinement(input(0), node_id);
    }
}

/// The location the load `load` reads, which facts may know the contents
/// of.
fn loaded_location(graph: &Graph, decisions: &Decisions, load: NodeId) -> Option<Location> {
    let node = graph.node(load);
    let input = |index: usize| decisions.value(graph, node.inputs[index]);
    Some(match node.op {
        Op::LoadNamed { offset, .. } => Location::Named {
            object: input(0),
            offset,
        },
        Op::LoadGlobalBinding { environment, index } => Location::GlobalBinding { environment, index },
        Op::LoadEnvironmentBinding { index } => Location::Binding {
            environment: input(0),
            index,
        },
        Op::LoadElementAt { kind } => Location::Element {
            storage: storage_object(graph, decisions, input(0)),
            index: index_value(graph, decisions, input(1)),
            kind,
        },
        ref op => {
            let count = ElementCount::loaded_by(op);
            if count.is_none() && !matches!(op, Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset) {
                return None;
            }
            let object = storage_object(graph, decisions, input(0));
            match count {
                Some(count) => Location::ElementCount { count, object },
                None => Location::TypedArrayDataOffset { object },
            }
        }
    })
}

/// The value that the index `index` of an element access is, as the
/// analysis knows it: refinements of a value (like the bounds checks of each
/// access) and int32 checks and unboxings of a value are the same index.
fn index_value(graph: &Graph, decisions: &Decisions, index: NodeId) -> NodeId {
    let mut index = decisions.value(graph, index);
    while matches!(graph.node(index).op, Op::CheckInt32 | Op::UnboxInt32) {
        index = decisions.value(graph, graph.node(index).inputs[0]);
    }
    index
}

/// The object whose address or whose typed array data address is
/// `address`, or `address` itself if it is none's.
fn storage_object(graph: &Graph, decisions: &Decisions, address: NodeId) -> NodeId {
    // NB: Before value numbering, an object may have several addresses,
    //     and every access of a typed array computes its data address.
    //     Writes of element counts, which change the storage offset, forget
    //     the elements of every storage.
    let node = graph.node(address);
    match node.op {
        Op::CellAddress => decisions.value(graph, node.inputs[0]),
        Op::TypedArrayDataAddress => {
            let offset = graph.node(graph.unrefined(decisions.value(graph, node.inputs[0])));
            match offset.op {
                Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset => storage_object(graph, decisions, offset.inputs[0]),
                _ => address,
            }
        }
        _ => address,
    }
}

/// `object` is a new object, which is what it is by its definition.
fn new_object(facts: &mut Facts, object: NodeId) {
    facts.set_object(object);
    facts.set_refinement(object, object);
}

/// The code is known to be valid from here on, which what is known about
/// shapes relies on.
fn validate(facts: &mut Facts, stable_shapes: &[CellId], decisions: &mut Decisions) {
    facts.validate(stable_shapes, &mut decisions.stable_shapes);
}

/// A load of `location` by `node`: replaced by what the location is known
/// to hold (returning true), or what it holds from now on.
fn reuse_contents(facts: &mut Facts, location: Location, node: NodeId, decisions: &mut Decisions) -> bool {
    match facts.contents(location) {
        Some(value) => {
            decisions.replacements.replace(node, value);
            true
        }
        None => {
            facts.set_contents(location, node);
            false
        }
    }
}

//! Dead code elimination: removes nodes whose values nobody uses, as long
//! as running them has no effect beyond producing their value. Frame states
//! count as uses, since exits need their values. Int32 arithmetic only
//! exits to produce a value that is no int32, so it goes too. Branches both
//! of whose edges lead to the same place, doing nothing, become jumps.

use super::edit;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// Whether a node can be dropped when its value is unused.
fn is_removable(op: &Op) -> bool {
    if matches!(op, Op::Phi | Op::Int32Binary { .. }) {
        return true;
    }
    let properties = op.properties();
    !op.is_control()
        && !op.can_eager_exit()
        && !properties.can_lazy_exit
        && !properties.allocates
        && properties.writes.is_empty()
        && !properties.runs_code
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    remove_dead_nodes(graph, work);
    // NB: Branches whose edges did the same are left jumping where they go,
    //     which leaves what only they used dead.
    if edit::fold_branches_to_one_target(graph, work) {
        remove_dead_nodes(graph, work);
    }
}

fn remove_dead_nodes(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let count = graph.nodes.len();
    let mut live = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    let mut live_frames = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.frame_states.len(), work);
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        pending.extend(block.nodes().filter(|node| {
            let data = graph.node(*node);
            data.repr.is_none() || !is_removable(&data.op)
        }));
    }
    while let Some(node) = pending.pop() {
        if live.contains(node.index()) {
            continue;
        }
        live.insert(node.index());
        let data = graph.node(node);
        pending.extend(data.inputs.iter().copied());
        let mut frame = data.frame_state;
        while let Some(id) = frame {
            if live_frames.contains(id.index()) {
                break;
            }
            live_frames.insert(id.index());
            let state = graph.frame_state(id);
            pending.extend(state.values.iter().map(|(_, value)| *value));
            frame = state.parent;
        }
    }
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            if !live.contains(node.index()) {
                removed.insert(node.index());
            }
        }
    }
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::code::{Repr, ResumeMode};
    use crate::ir::{BinaryOp, Block, FrameState, NodeId};
    use crate::snapshot::CellId;

    #[test]
    fn unused_cycles_of_pure_values_are_removed() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let constant = graph.add(Op::Constant(1), &[], Some(Repr::Int32), 0);
        let phi = graph.add(Op::Phi, &[], Some(Repr::Int32), 0);
        let add = graph.add(
            Op::Int32Binary {
                op: BinaryOp::BitwiseOr,
            },
            &[phi, constant],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
            0,
        );
        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.assign(&[phi, add]);
        graph.blocks[0].phis.push(phi);
        graph.blocks[0].body.push(add);
        let returned = graph.add(Op::Return, &[constant], None, 0);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(returned);
        remove_dead_nodes(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        assert!(graph.blocks[0].phis.is_empty());
        assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(graph.blocks[0].control, Some(returned));
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_frame_states_keep_nested_virtual_object_properties_alive() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let constant = graph.add(Op::Constant(1), &[], Some(Repr::Int32), 0);
        let boxed = graph.add(Op::BoxInt32, &[constant], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        let object = graph.add(
            Op::VirtualObject {
                kind: crate::ir::VirtualObjectKind::Object { shape: CellId(1) },
                allocation: NodeId(0),
            },
            &[boxed],
            Some(Repr::Tagged),
            0,
        );
        let frame = graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[(0, object)], crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        });
        graph.blocks[0].body.push(boxed);
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let check = graph.add(Op::CheckObject, &[boxed], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
            graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(frame);
            graph.blocks[0].body.push(check);
        }
        let returned = graph.add(Op::Return, &[constant], None, 0);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(returned);
        remove_dead_nodes(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&boxed));
        assert_eq!(graph.blocks[0].body.len(), 3);
    }
}

//! The dominator tree of a graph's blocks.
//!
//! The entries (block 0 and the on-stack replacement entries) have no
//! immediate dominator, and neither has a block reached from several
//! entries.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::tables::Lists;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;

/// The dominator tree of a graph, in lists of a work zone. `compute()` makes them anew for the graph as it is then,
/// in the memory they have where it is enough.
pub struct Dominators<'w> {
    /// The immediate dominator of each block, if it has one.
    idom: ZoneVec<'w, Option<BlockId>>,
    /// Whether each block is reachable from an entry.
    reachable: ZoneVec<'w, bool>,
    /// When a depth first walk of the dominator tree enters and leaves each reachable block. A block dominates those
    /// it enters and leaves while it is entered.
    tree_intervals: ZoneVec<'w, (u32, u32)>,
    /// The children of each block in the dominator tree, in linear order.
    children: Lists<'w, BlockId>,
    /// The reachable blocks in reverse postorder.
    order: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
    /// The place of each reachable block in `order`, plus one.
    ranks: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// Whether each block has an immediate dominator or the virtual root above every entry as its dominator so far.
    processed: ZoneVec<'w, bool>,
    /// The blocks that a walk still has to enter or leave, and whether it is to leave them.
    pending: ZoneVec<'w, (BlockId, bool)>,
}

impl<'w> Dominators<'w> {
    /// The most blocks a graph has whose dominators a compile computes. A compile whose graph has more fails (see
    /// `passes::optimize()`).
    pub const MAX_BLOCKS: usize = 1 << 24;

    /// Lists for the dominators of a graph, which take no memory before `compute()` uses them.
    pub fn new_in(work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            idom: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            reachable: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            tree_intervals: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            children: Lists::new_in(work),
            order: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            ranks: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            processed: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            pending: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        }
    }

    /// The dominators of `graph` as it is now, in `work`.
    pub fn of(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        let mut dominators = Self::new_in(work);
        dominators.compute(graph);
        dominators
    }

    /// Computes the dominators of `graph` with the iterative algorithm of Cooper,
    /// Harvey and Kennedy, visiting blocks in reverse postorder. The lists then hold the dominators of `graph` as
    /// it is now, and nothing of an earlier graph.
    pub fn compute(&mut self, graph: &Graph) {
        let count = graph.blocks.len();
        self.reachable.clear();
        self.reachable.resize(count, false);
        self.order.clear();
        self.order.reserve(count);
        self.pending.clear();
        // NB: A block waits to be left one time, and to be entered one time for each edge into it and for each entry
        //     it is.
        let edges = graph.blocks.iter().map(|block| block.predecessors.len()).sum::<usize>();
        self.pending.reserve(count + edges + graph.entries().count());
        for entry in graph.entries() {
            self.pending.push((entry, false));
        }
        while let Some((block, leaving)) = self.pending.pop() {
            if leaving {
                self.order.push(block);
                continue;
            }
            if self.reachable[block.index()] {
                continue;
            }
            self.reachable[block.index()] = true;
            self.pending.push((block, true));
            graph.control(block).op.for_each_successor(|successor| {
                self.pending.push((successor, false));
            });
        }
        self.order.reverse();
        // NB: Rank zero is the virtual root. Walking to an immediate
        //     dominator decreases the rank, avoiding ancestor-depth scans.
        self.ranks.clear();
        self.ranks.resize(count, 0);
        for (index, block) in self.order.iter().enumerate() {
            self.ranks[block.index()] = index as u32 + 1;
        }

        // NB: `None` with `processed` set means "dominated by the virtual root".
        self.idom.clear();
        self.idom.resize(count, None);
        self.processed.clear();
        self.processed.resize(count, false);
        let mut changed = true;
        while changed {
            changed = false;
            for block in self.order.iter().map(|block| block.index()) {
                let predecessors = &graph.blocks[block].predecessors;
                let new_idom = if predecessors.is_empty() {
                    None
                } else {
                    let mut candidates = predecessors
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|predecessor| self.processed[predecessor.index()]);
                    let Some(first) = candidates.next() else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let mut new_idom = Some(*first);
                    for predecessor in candidates {
                        new_idom = intersect(&self.idom, &self.ranks, new_idom, Some(*predecessor));
                    }
                    new_idom
                };
                if !self.processed[block] || self.idom[block] != new_idom {
                    self.processed[block] = true;
                    self.idom[block] = new_idom;
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        self.compute_children();
        self.compute_tree_intervals();
    }

    fn compute_children(&mut self) {
        let count = self.idom.len();
        self.children.begin_counts(count);
        for block in 0..count {
            if let Some(idom) = self.idom[block]
                && self.reachable[block]
            {
                self.children.count(idom.index());
            }
        }
        self.children.end_counts(BlockId(0));
        for block in 0..count {
            if let Some(idom) = self.idom[block]
                && self.reachable[block]
            {
                self.children.fill(idom.index(), BlockId::from_index(block));
            }
        }
        self.children.end_fill();
    }

    fn compute_tree_intervals(&mut self) {
        let count = self.idom.len();
        self.tree_intervals.clear();
        self.tree_intervals.resize(count, (0, 0));
        let mut time = 0;
        self.pending.clear();
        for block in 0..count {
            if self.reachable[block] && self.idom[block].is_none() {
                self.pending.push((BlockId::from_index(block), false));
            }
        }
        while let Some((block, leaving)) = self.pending.pop() {
            time += 1;
            if leaving {
                self.tree_intervals[block.index()].1 = time;
                continue;
            }
            self.tree_intervals[block.index()].0 = time;
            self.pending.push((block, true));
            for child in self.children.get(block.index()) {
                self.pending.push((*child, false));
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn idom(&self, block: BlockId) -> Option<BlockId> {
        self.idom[block.index()]
    }

    pub fn is_reachable(&self, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        self.reachable[block.index()]
    }

    /// The predecessors of `header` that it dominates: the sources of the
    /// back edges of the loop it heads, if it heads one.
    pub fn back_edge_sources<'v>(&self, graph: &Graph, header: BlockId, work: &'v Zone) -> ZoneVec<'v, BlockId> {
        ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
            graph
                .block(header)
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|predecessor| self.dominates(header, *predecessor)),
            work,
        )
    }

    /// The blocks of the loop that `header` heads, with back edges from
    /// `back_edge_sources`: the header and every reachable block that reaches
    /// one of them without going through it.
    pub fn loop_blocks<'v>(
        &self,
        graph: &Graph,
        header: BlockId,
        back_edge_sources: &[BlockId],
        work: &'v Zone,
    ) -> ZoneBitSet<'v> {
        let mut blocks = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.blocks.len(), work);
        blocks.insert(header.index());
        let mut pending = ZoneVec::from_slice_in(back_edge_sources, work);
        while let Some(block) = pending.pop() {
            if blocks.contains(block.index()) || !self.is_reachable(block) {
                continue;
            }
            blocks.insert(block.index());
            pending.extend(graph.block(block).predecessors.iter().copied());
        }
        blocks
    }

    /// Whether every iteration of a loop with back edges from
    /// `back_edge_sources` that goes around runs `block`.
    pub fn runs_every_iteration(&self, block: BlockId, back_edge_sources: &[BlockId]) -> bool {
        back_edge_sources.iter().all(|source| self.dominates(block, *source))
    }

    /// Whether every path from an entry to `block` goes through `dominator`.
    /// A block dominates itself.
    pub fn dominates(&self, dominator: BlockId, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        // OPTIMIZATION: Walking up from the block would take time proportional to the depth of the dominator tree,
        //               which is large in long straight-line code with many branches, like inlined assertions.
        if self.reachable[dominator.index()] && self.reachable[block.index()] {
            let (enter, leave) = self.tree_intervals[dominator.index()];
            let (block_enter, block_leave) = self.tree_intervals[block.index()];
            return enter <= block_enter && block_leave <= leave;
        }
        let mut current = Some(block);
        while let Some(candidate) = current {
            if candidate == dominator {
                return true;
            }
            current = self.idom[candidate.index()];
        }
        false
    }

    /// The children of `block` in the dominator tree, in linear order.
    pub fn children(&self, block: BlockId) -> &[BlockId] {
        self.children.get(block.index())
    }
}

/// The nearest common dominator of two blocks, `None` standing for the
/// virtual root above every entry.
fn intersect(
    idom: &[Option<BlockId>],
    ranks: &[u32],
    mut a: Option<BlockId>,
    mut b: Option<BlockId>,
) -> Option<BlockId> {
    let rank = |block: Option<BlockId>| block.map_or(0, |block| ranks[block.index()]);
    while a != b {
        if rank(a) > rank(b) {
            a = a.and_then(|block| idom[block.index()]);
        } else {
            b = b.and_then(|block| idom[block.index()]);
        }
    }
    a
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::ir::{Block, BranchCondition, Op};

    #[test]
    fn cyclic_graphs_with_multiple_entries_match_dominator_sets() {
        let work = crate::test_work();
        let mut dominators = Dominators::new_in(&work);
        for seed in 1..33u64 {
            let mut random = seed;
            let mut graph = Graph::default();
            let count = 24;
            for _ in 0..count {
                graph.add_block(Block::default());
            }
            graph.osr_entries.push((0, BlockId(1)));
            for block in 0..count {
                let mut target = || {
                    random = random.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1);
                    BlockId::from_index(2 + (random >> 32) as usize % (count - 2))
                };
                let (a, b) = (target(), target());
                let control = graph.add(
                    Op::Branch {
                        condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                        if_true: a,
                        if_false: b,
                    },
                    &[],
                    None,
                    0,
                );
                graph.blocks[block].control = Some(control);
                for successor in [a, b] {
                    graph.blocks[successor.index()]
                        .predecessors
                        .push(BlockId::from_index(block));
                }
            }
            // NB: The tables of one graph serve the next one.
            dominators.compute(&graph);
            // NB: Independently solve the defining set equations: each
            //     block dominates itself and inherits the intersection of
            //     its predecessors' dominators.
            let mut sets = vec![vec![true; count]; count];
            for entry in graph.entries() {
                sets[entry.index()].fill(false);
                sets[entry.index()][entry.index()] = true;
            }
            loop {
                let mut changed = false;
                for block in 2..count {
                    if !dominators.is_reachable(BlockId::from_index(block)) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mut next = vec![true; count];
                    for predecessor in &graph.blocks[block].predecessors {
                        if dominators.is_reachable(*predecessor) {
                            for (value, inherited) in next.iter_mut().zip(&sets[predecessor.index()]) {
                                *value &= inherited;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    next[block] = true;
                    if sets[block] != next {
                        sets[block] = next;
                        changed = true;
                    }
                }
                if !changed {
                    break;
                }
            }
            for (block, expected) in sets.iter().enumerate() {
                let block = BlockId::from_index(block);
                if !dominators.is_reachable(block) {
                    continue;
                }
                for (candidate, expected) in expected.iter().enumerate() {
                    assert_eq!(
                        dominators.dominates(BlockId::from_index(candidate), block),
                        *expected,
                        "seed {seed}, block {block:?}, candidate {candidate}"
                    );
                }
                if let Some(parent) = dominators.idom(block) {
                    assert!(dominators.children(parent).contains(&block));
                }
            }
            for block in 0..count {
                let children = dominators.children(BlockId::from_index(block));
                assert!(children.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0].index() < pair[1].index()));
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Graph edits shared by the passes: replacing values, removing nodes, and
//! cleaning up the control flow graph after control nodes lost successors.

use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::FrameState;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneMap;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// Values to replace by other values, as a pass decides them.
pub struct Replacements<'w> {
    map: ZoneVec<'w, Option<NodeId>>,
    initial_node_count: usize,
}

impl<'w> Replacements<'w> {
    /// No replacements, which keep their table in `work`.
    pub fn new(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            map: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            initial_node_count: graph.nodes.len(),
        }
    }

    /// Forgets all replacements. The table keeps its memory.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.map.clear();
    }

    /// Makes every use of `value` a use of `replacement` instead.
    pub fn replace(&mut self, value: NodeId, replacement: NodeId) {
        debug_assert_ne!(value, replacement);
        if value.index() >= self.map.len() {
            self.map.resize((value.index() + 1).max(self.initial_node_count), None);
        }
        self.map[value.index()] = Some(replacement);
    }

    /// What a use of `value` uses after the replacements.
    pub fn resolve(&self, mut value: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        while let Some(Some(replacement)) = self.map.get(value.index()) {
            value = *replacement;
        }
        value
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.map.is_empty()
    }

    /// Rewrites every input and frame state value of the graph.
    pub fn apply(&self, graph: &mut Graph) {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        for node in &mut graph.nodes {
            for input in &mut node.inputs {
                *input = self.resolve(*input);
            }
        }
        for frame_state in &mut graph.frame_states {
            for (_, value) in &mut frame_state.values {
                *value = self.resolve(*value);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Makes every use of a refined value (see `Op::refined_input()`) a use of
/// the value it refines, once the passes no longer move or share nodes:
/// `Refine` nodes go away, and checks no longer have a value, so that
/// refining costs no register.
pub fn remove_refinements(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut checks = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in &block.body {
            let data = graph.node(*node);
            let Some(index) = data.op.refined_input() else {
                continue;
            };
            if data.repr.is_some() {
                replacements.replace(*node, data.inputs[index]);
            }
            match data.op {
                Op::Refine { .. } => removed.insert(node.index()),
                _ => checks.push(*node),
            }
        }
    }
    replacements.apply(graph);
    remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
    for check in checks {
        graph.nodes[check.index()].repr = None;
    }
}

/// Removes the nodes in `removed` from the blocks they are in. Nodes added
/// after `removed` was made are kept.
pub fn remove_nodes(graph: &mut Graph, removed: &ZoneBitSet) {
    let is_removed = |node: &NodeId| node.index() < removed.capacity() && removed.contains(node.index());
    for block in &mut graph.blocks {
        block.body.retain(|node| !is_removed(node));
        block.phis.retain(|node| !is_removed(node));
    }
}

/// Makes the int32 operation `node` wrap around instead of checking its
/// result, which it then never exits for.
pub fn make_wrapping(graph: &mut Graph, node: NodeId) {
    let data = &mut graph.nodes[node.index()];
    let Op::Int32Binary { op } = data.op else {
        unreachable!("only int32 operations wrap");
    };
    data.op = Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op };
    data.frame_state = None;
}

/// The constant nodes of a graph by their bits and representation, for
/// passes that need constants: `get()` and `get_typed()` add those the
/// graph does not have yet.
pub struct Constants<'w> {
    nodes: ZoneMap<'w, (u64, Repr), NodeId>,
}

impl<'w> Constants<'w> {
    /// The constants of `graph`, with their table in `work`.
    pub fn new(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        let nodes = ZoneMap::from_iter_in(
            graph
                .nodes
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter_map(|(index, node)| match (&node.op, node.repr) {
                    (Op::Constant(bits), Some(repr)) => Some(((*bits, repr), NodeId::from_index(index))),
                    _ => None,
                }),
            work,
        );
        Self { nodes }
    }

    /// The tagged constant node with `bits`.
    pub fn get(&mut self, graph: &mut Graph, bits: u64) -> NodeId {
        self.get_typed(graph, bits, Repr::Tagged)
    }

    /// The constant node with `bits` in representation `repr`.
    pub fn get_typed(&mut self, graph: &mut Graph, bits: u64, repr: Repr) -> NodeId {
        *self
            .nodes
            .entry((bits, repr))
            .or_insert_with(|| graph.add(Op::Constant(bits), &[], Some(repr), 0))
    }
}

/// Whether an entry reaches each block over the edges the control nodes
/// have.
fn reachable_blocks<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneVec<'w, bool> {
    let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
    let mut reachable = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, block_count, work);
    // NB: A loop header that only its back edges would reach has no
    //     predecessors if none of them was built, but is no entry.
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(graph.entries().map(BlockId::index), work);
    while let Some(block) = pending.pop() {
        if core::mem::replace(&mut reachable[block], true) {
            continue;
        }
        pending.extend(
            graph
                .successors(BlockId::from_index(block))
                .iter()
                .map(|successor| successor.index()),
        );
    }
    reachable
}

/// Drops the blocks no entry reaches, if there are any.
pub fn remove_unreachable_blocks(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    if reachable_blocks(graph, work).iter().any(|reachable| !reachable) {
        clean_up_control_flow(graph, work);
    }
}

/// Brings predecessor lists and phis in line with the control nodes after
/// passes changed them to branch to fewer blocks, then drops the blocks no
/// entry reaches anymore and the phis left with a single distinct input.
pub fn clean_up_control_flow(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
    let reachable = reachable_blocks(graph, work);

    // Keep the predecessor entries (and their phi inputs) of reachable
    // blocks that still branch here, as many times as they do.
    let mut remaining_edges = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        (0..block_count).map(|block| ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&graph.successors(BlockId::from_index(block)), work)),
        work,
    );
    let mut keep = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in 0..block_count {
        if !reachable[block] {
            continue;
        }
        let predecessors = &graph.blocks[block].predecessors;
        keep.clear();
        keep.extend(predecessors.iter().map(|predecessor| {
            if !reachable[predecessor.index()] {
                return false;
            }
            let successors = &mut remaining_edges[predecessor.index()];
            let Some(index) = successors.iter().position(|successor| successor.index() == block) else {
                return false;
            };
            successors.swap_remove(index);
            true
        }));
        if keep.iter().all(|keep| *keep) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut index = 0;
        graph.blocks[block].predecessors.retain(|_| {
            let retained = keep[index];
            index += 1;
            retained
        });
        for phi in &graph.blocks[block].phis {
            let mut index = 0;
            graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.retain(|_| {
                let retained = keep[index];
                index += 1;
                retained
            });
        }
    }

    let order = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        (0..block_count)
            .filter(|block| reachable[*block])
            .map(BlockId::from_index),
        work,
    );
    if order.len() != block_count {
        graph.reorder_blocks(&order, work);
    }
    remove_trivial_phis(graph, work);
}

/// Makes the control node `control` jump to `target`, without inputs and
/// a frame state, which jumps never have.
pub fn make_jump(graph: &mut Graph, control: NodeId, target: BlockId) {
    let node = &mut graph.nodes[control.index()];
    node.op = Op::Jump { target };
    node.inputs.clear();
    node.frame_state = None;
}

/// Makes branches whose edges both lead to the same place, through blocks
/// that only jump on, jumps: where the target's phis get the same values
/// from both. Returns whether it changed any.
pub fn fold_branches_to_one_target(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) -> bool {
    // NB: Where an edge leads, and the block it enters that from.
    // NB: Blocks that only jump on can make a loop, which leads nowhere.
    let end_of = |graph: &Graph, mut block: BlockId, mut from: BlockId| {
        for _ in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
            let data = graph.block(block);
            let Op::Jump { target } = graph.control(block).op else {
                return (block, from);
            };
            if !data.phis.is_empty() || !data.body.is_empty() || target == block {
                return (block, from);
            }
            from = block;
            block = target;
        }
        (block, from)
    };
    let mut changed = false;
    for block in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block);
        let control = graph.control_id(block_id);
        let Op::Branch { if_true, if_false, .. } = graph.node(control).op else {
            continue;
        };
        let (true_end, true_from) = end_of(graph, if_true, block_id);
        let (false_end, false_from) = end_of(graph, if_false, block_id);
        if true_end != false_end {
            continue;
        }
        let target = graph.block(true_end);
        let input_from = |from: BlockId| target.predecessors.iter().position(|block| *block == from);
        let (Some(true_index), Some(false_index)) = (input_from(true_from), input_from(false_from)) else {
            continue;
        };
        if target
            .phis
            .iter()
            .any(|phi| graph.node(*phi).inputs[true_index] != graph.node(*phi).inputs[false_index])
        {
            continue;
        }
        make_jump(graph, control, if_true);
        changed = true;
    }
    if changed {
        clean_up_control_flow(graph, work);
    }
    changed
}

/// A frame state for exits at the end of `predecessor`, resuming at the
/// start of the bytecode block `block` with the values flowing into it from
/// there, if `block` has a start frame state (see
/// `Block::start_frame_state`).
pub fn frame_state_entering<'z>(
    graph: &Graph<'z>,
    block: BlockId,
    predecessor: BlockId,
    work: &Zone,
) -> Option<FrameState<'z>> {
    let (template, values) = values_entering(graph, block, predecessor, work)?;
    Some(frame_state_with_values(graph, template, values))
}

/// The values of a frame state, with the frame state it is made from (see `values_entering()`).
pub type EnteringValues<'w> = (FrameStateId, &'w [(u32, NodeId)]);

/// The values of the frame state of `frame_state_entering()`, in `work`, with the start frame state of `block` that it
/// is made from.
pub fn values_entering<'w>(
    graph: &Graph,
    block: BlockId,
    predecessor: BlockId,
    work: &'w Zone,
) -> Option<EnteringValues<'w>> {
    let data = graph.block(block);
    let template = data.start_frame_state?;
    let entry_index = data
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .position(|block| *block == predecessor)
        .expect("the predecessor enters the block");
    let phis = &data.phis;
    let values = &graph.frame_state(template).values;
    // NB: Values made in the block do not exist before it.
    if values
        .iter()
        .any(|(_, value)| !phis.contains(value) && data.body.contains(value))
    {
        return None;
    }
    let values = work.alloc_slice_from_iter(values.iter().map(|(slot, value)| {
        if phis.contains(value) {
            (*slot, graph.node(*value).inputs[entry_index])
        } else {
            (*slot, *value)
        }
    }));
    Some((template, values))
}

/// The frame state `template` with `values` in place of its values.
pub fn frame_state_with_values<'z>(
    graph: &Graph<'z>,
    template: FrameStateId,
    values: &[(u32, NodeId)],
) -> FrameState<'z> {
    let template = graph.frame_state(template);
    FrameState {
        executable: template.executable,
        pc: template.pc,
        mode: template.mode,
        values: graph.list(values),
        in_frame: template.in_frame.clone(),
        parent: template.parent,
        passed_argument_count: template.passed_argument_count,
        legacy_arguments: template.legacy_arguments.clone(),
    }
}

/// Moves the cold blocks after all other blocks, keeping the order of
/// each, so that the code of every other block comes first and the cold
/// code is out of the way.
pub fn move_cold_blocks_last(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    if !graph.blocks.iter().any(|block| block.is_cold) {
        return;
    }
    let blocks = || (0..graph.blocks.len()).map(BlockId::from_index);
    let hot = blocks().filter(|block| !graph.block(*block).is_cold);
    let cold = blocks().filter(|block| graph.block(*block).is_cold);
    let order = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(hot.chain(cold), work);
    graph.reorder_blocks(&order, work);
}

/// Replaces phis whose inputs are all one value (or the phi itself) by
/// that value, until none is left.
pub fn remove_trivial_phis(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    // NB: Nothing adds nodes here.
    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    loop {
        replacements.clear();
        removed.clear();
        for block in &graph.blocks {
            for phi in &block.phis {
                let mut distinct = graph.nodes[phi.index()]
                    .inputs
                    .iter()
                    .map(|input| replacements.resolve(*input))
                    .filter(|input| input != phi);
                let Some(first) = distinct.next() else {
                    continue;
                };
                if distinct.all(|input| input == first) {
                    replacements.replace(*phi, first);
                    removed.insert(phi.index());
                }
            }
        }
        if replacements.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        replacements.apply(graph);
        remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
    }
}

/// Drops the frame states no node uses anymore (directly or as the parent
/// of one it uses) and renumbers the others in their order.
pub fn remove_unused_frame_states(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    // NB: No pass exits to the start of blocks anymore.
    for block in &mut graph.blocks {
        block.start_frame_state = None;
    }
    let count = graph.frame_states.len();
    let mut used = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, count, work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            let mut frame_state = graph.nodes[node.index()].frame_state;
            while let Some(id) = frame_state {
                if core::mem::replace(&mut used[id.index()], true) {
                    break;
                }
                frame_state = graph.frame_states[id.index()].parent;
            }
        }
    }
    if used.iter().all(|used| *used) {
        return;
    }
    let mut new_index = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, count, work);
    let mut next = 0;
    for (index, used) in used.iter().enumerate() {
        if *used {
            new_index[index] = Some(FrameStateId(next));
            next += 1;
        }
    }
    let remap = |id: FrameStateId| new_index[id.index()].expect("used frame states only refer to used ones");
    let mut index = 0;
    graph.frame_states.retain_mut(|frame_state| {
        let used = used[index];
        index += 1;
        if used {
            frame_state.parent = frame_state.parent.map(remap);
        }
        used
    });
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            let node = &mut graph.nodes[node.index()];
            node.frame_state = node.frame_state.map(remap);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn replacements_allocate_lazily_and_follow_updated_chains() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        for _ in 0..4 {
            graph.add(Op::Constant(0), &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        }
        let mut replacements = Replacements::new(&graph, crate::test_zone());
        assert_eq!(replacements.map.capacity(), 0);
        assert!(replacements.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(replacements.resolve(NodeId(0)), NodeId(0));
        replacements.replace(NodeId(0), NodeId(1));
        replacements.replace(NodeId(1), NodeId(2));
        assert_eq!(replacements.resolve(NodeId(0)), NodeId(2));
        replacements.replace(NodeId(1), NodeId(3));
        assert_eq!(replacements.resolve(NodeId(0)), NodeId(3));
        let added = graph.add(Op::Constant(0), &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        replacements.replace(added, NodeId(0));
        assert_eq!(replacements.resolve(added), NodeId(3));
        assert!(!replacements.is_empty());
    }
}
