//! Key strings: concatenations that are the keys of property accesses look
//! for the strings that they made before.
//!
//! `object["on" + type]` concatenates two strings into a rope string, which
//! the access resolves right away to find the property key. The rope string
//! is a new string every time, so the caches of the access, which know keys
//! by their strings, never have it, and the access takes its slow path every
//! time. The VM remembers the two strings of a rope that became a key, and
//! the string that it became. A concatenation whose value is the key of a
//! keyed access is marked (`Op::ConcatenateStrings::key`), and then takes
//! the string that the VM remembers for its two strings, if any, which the
//! caches of the access know by now.
//!
//! The key of an access is a phi of the concatenation and of what the slow
//! path of its instruction made, and may be one of several concatenations,
//! so the pass looks through phis and refinements. A string that a loop puts
//! together piece by piece is a key once, and its pieces never are, so the
//! pass does not look through the phis of loop headers, and leaves alone a
//! concatenation that adds to one. The strings of a marked concatenation
//! are looked at as well: the key `a + b + c` only finds its string if
//! `a + b` is the same string every time, which the VM remembers too. A
//! concatenation with other uses than keys is marked all the same: its
//! string has the same characters either way.

use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            let node = graph.node(node);
            if matches!(
                node.op,
                Op::ProbeKeyedCache { .. } | Op::ProbeKeyedStore { .. } | Op::ProbeHasProperty { .. }
            ) {
                pending.push(node.inputs[1]);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut loop_phis = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for block in graph.blocks.iter().filter(|block| block.is_loop_header) {
        for phi in &block.phis {
            loop_phis.insert(phi.index());
        }
    }
    let mut seen = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut concatenations: ZoneVec<NodeId> = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    while let Some(value) = pending.pop() {
        let value = graph.unrefined(value);
        if seen.contains(value.index()) {
            continue;
        }
        seen.insert(value.index());
        let node = graph.node(value);
        match node.op {
            Op::Phi if !loop_phis.contains(value.index()) => pending.extend(&node.inputs),
            Op::ConcatenateStrings { key: false } => {
                let adds_to_loop_phi = node
                    .inputs
                    .iter()
                    .any(|&input| loop_phis.contains(graph.unrefined(input).index()));
                if adds_to_loop_phi {
                    continue;
                }
                concatenations.push(value);
                pending.extend(&node.inputs);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    for concatenation in concatenations {
        graph.nodes[concatenation.index()].op = Op::ConcatenateStrings { key: true };
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/JIT/Rust/src/passes/licm.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Loop invariant code motion.
//!
//! Nodes in a loop whose inputs are all defined outside of it, which have
//! no effects and read no memory the loop may write, move to the loop's
//! preheader: the one block outside the loop that enters it. Loads of the
//! slots that nothing writes (`Graph::unwritten_slots`) read memory no loop
//! writes, even one that calls. Loops entered
//! from several blocks (like the function entry and an on-stack replacement
//! entry) first get a preheader that merges what those bring.
//!
//! Checks and other nodes that may exit move too, only in loops whose header
//! has a frame state to exit with: the interpreter then resumes at the loop
//! header, with the values the preheader brings into the loop. Those from
//! blocks that not every iteration runs (like the code after a `continue`),
//! but for cold ones, move speculatively: they may exit where the loop would
//! never have run them, and exit with `ExitKind::Hoisted` instead of their
//! own kind. Hoisting a check whose kind of exit was taken at the loop header
//! before is never repeated, nor are speculative hoists where one of them
//! exited there, so a speculation that fails costs one exit, and keeps the
//! other checks moving.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use super::edit;
use crate::code::ExitKind;
use crate::ir::Block;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Locations;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;

struct Loop<'w> {
    header: BlockId,
    preheader: BlockId,
    blocks: ZoneBitSet<'w>,
    /// The blocks in the loop that jump back to its header.
    back_edge_sources: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
}

/// Gives each loop header that several earlier blocks outside the loop
/// enter, or one that also leads elsewhere, a preheader: a new block right
/// before the header that they jump to instead, with phis of what they
/// bring.
/// Returns whether it added any.
fn add_preheaders(graph: &mut Graph, dominators: &Dominators, work: &Zone) -> bool {
    let count = graph.blocks.len();
    let mut order = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut predecessors = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut back_edge_sources = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut entries = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut phis = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut back_inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut entry_inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for header in (0..count).map(BlockId::from_index) {
        predecessors.assign(&graph.block(header).predecessors);
        back_edge_sources.clear();
        entries.clear();
        for predecessor in predecessors.iter().copied() {
            if dominators.dominates(header, predecessor) {
                back_edge_sources.push(predecessor);
            } else {
                entries.push(predecessor);
            }
        }
        // NB: Edges from later blocks the header does not dominate are
        //     back edges of cycles around the header, which an on-stack
        //     replacement entry inside them reaches without the header.
        if back_edge_sources.is_empty()
            || entries.is_empty()
            || entries.iter().any(|entry| entry.index() > header.index())
            || (entries.len() == 1 && *graph.successors(entries[0]) == [header])
        {
            order.push(header);
            continue;
        }
        let preheader = graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&entries),
            ..graph.new_block()
        });
        for entry in &entries {
            graph.replace_successor(*entry, header, preheader);
        }
        phis.assign(&graph.block(header).phis);
        for phi in phis.iter().copied() {
            back_inputs.clear();
            entry_inputs.clear();
            for (predecessor, input) in predecessors.iter().zip(graph.node(phi).inputs.iter().copied()) {
                if back_edge_sources.contains(predecessor) {
                    back_inputs.push(input);
                } else {
                    entry_inputs.push(input);
                }
            }
            let entering = if entry_inputs.iter().all(|input| *input == entry_inputs[0]) {
                entry_inputs[0]
            } else {
                let merged = graph.add(Op::Phi, &entry_inputs, graph.node(phi).repr, graph.node(phi).pc);
                graph.blocks[preheader.index()].phis.push(merged);
                merged
            };
            let inputs = &mut graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs;
            inputs.clear();
            inputs.push(entering);
            inputs.extend_from_slice(&back_inputs);
        }
        let jump = graph.add(Op::Jump { target: header }, &[], None, graph.control(header).pc);
        graph.blocks[preheader.index()].control = Some(jump);
        let header_predecessors = &mut graph.blocks[header.index()].predecessors;
        header_predecessors.clear();
        header_predecessors.push(preheader);
        header_predecessors.extend_from_slice(&back_edge_sources);
        order.push(preheader);
        order.push(header);
    }
    if graph.blocks.len() == count {
        return false;
    }
    graph.reorder_blocks(&order, work);
    true
}

fn find_loops<'w>(graph: &Graph, dominators: &Dominators, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneVec<'w, Loop<'w>> {
    let mut loops = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let header = BlockId::from_index(index);
        let back_edge_sources = dominators.back_edge_sources(graph, header, work);
        if back_edge_sources.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let blocks = dominators.loop_blocks(graph, header, &back_edge_sources, work);
        let mut entries = block
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .filter(|predecessor| !blocks.contains(predecessor.index()));
        let (Some(preheader), None) = (entries.next(), entries.next()) else {
            continue;
        };
        if *graph.successors(*preheader) != [header] {
            continue;
        }
        loops.push(Loop {
            header,
            preheader: *preheader,
            blocks,
            back_edge_sources,
        });
    }
    loops
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    // NB: Loops have a back edge from a later block or the block itself.
    let has_loops = graph.blocks.iter().enumerate().any(|(index, block)| {
        block
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .any(|predecessor| predecessor.index() >= index)
    });
    if !has_loops {
        return;
    }
    let mut dominators = Dominators::of(graph, work);
    if add_preheaders(graph, &dominators, work) {
        // NB: The phis of headers that merged their entries in a preheader
        //     only take the value the preheader brings where the loop leaves
        //     it as it is, which is then invariant in the loop.
        edit::remove_trivial_phis(graph, work);
        dominators.compute(graph);
    }
    let dominators = &dominators;
    let loops = find_loops(graph, dominators, work);
    if loops.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut block_of = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut hoisted = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut body = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            block_of[node.index()] = Some(index);
        }
    }

    // Inner loops come later in this order; hoisting out of them first lets
    // their invariants move on out of the outer loops.
    for loop_ in loops.iter().rev() {
        // NB: Code that runs may write anything. Calls of runtime helpers
        //     that run no code write what they say they do.
        let mut writes = Locations::NONE;
        for block in loop_.blocks.iter() {
            for node in graph.block_nodes(BlockId::from_index(block)) {
                let properties = graph.node(node).op.properties();
                writes |= if properties.runs_code {
                    Locations::ALL
                } else {
                    properties.writes
                };
            }
        }
        let header_state = graph.block(loop_.header).start_frame_state;
        let mut exit_state: Option<Option<FrameStateId>> = None;
        hoisted.clear();
        for block in loop_.blocks.iter() {
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block);
            let runs_every_iteration = dominators.runs_every_iteration(block_id, &loop_.back_edge_sources);
            let is_cold = graph.block(block_id).is_cold;
            body.assign(&graph.block(block_id).body);
            for node in body.iter().copied() {
                let data = graph.node(node);
                let mut properties = data.op.properties();
                // OPTIMIZATION: Nothing writes these slots, so their loads leave even loops that call, like the
                //               reloads the builder puts at loop headers (see `GraphBuilder::merge()`).
                if let Op::LoadSlot { slot } = data.op
                    && graph.is_unwritten_slot(slot)
                {
                    properties.reads = Locations::NONE;
                }
                let invariant_inputs = data
                    .inputs
                    .iter()
                    .all(|input| block_of[input.index()].is_none_or(|block| !loop_.blocks.contains(block)));
                // NB: Refinements belong to the edge into their block. Calls in
                //     cold blocks stay there, where they rarely run, rather
                //     than run whenever the loop is entered.
                let movable = !matches!(data.op, Op::Refine { .. })
                    && !(properties.is_call && is_cold)
                    && !properties.can_lazy_exit
                    && !properties.allocates
                    && properties.writes.is_empty()
                    && !properties.runs_code
                    && !properties.reads.intersects(writes);
                if !invariant_inputs || !movable {
                    continue;
                }
                if let Some(kind) = data.op.exit_kind() {
                    let speculative = !runs_every_iteration || graph.speculatively_hoisted.contains(&node);
                    let exited = |kind| {
                        header_state.is_some_and(|state| {
                            let state = graph.frame_state(state);
                            graph.exit_sites.contains(&(state.executable, state.pc, kind))
                        })
                    };
                    if (speculative && is_cold) || exited(kind) || (speculative && exited(ExitKind::Hoisted)) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let state = *exit_state.get_or_insert_with(|| {
                        let state = edit::frame_state_entering(graph, loop_.header, loop_.preheader, work)?;
                        Some(graph.add_frame_state(state))
                    });
                    let Some(state) = state else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    graph.nodes[node.index()].frame_state = Some(state);
                    if speculative && !graph.speculatively_hoisted.contains(&node) {
                        graph.speculatively_hoisted.push(node);
                    }
                }
                graph.blocks[block].body.retain(|other| *other != node);
                block_of[node.index()] = Some(loop_.preheader.index());
                hoisted.push(node);
            }
        }
        graph.blocks[loop_.preheader.index()].body.extend_from_slice(&hoisted);
    }
}

/*

//! Loop rotation.
//!
//! Loops with their test at the bottom start at the test: the code before the loop jumps there, and the test jumps
//! back to the body. An on-stack replacement entry at a test that does more than branch (like `i < this.length`, whose
//! property load starts the test's block) runs the branch itself and enters the body, so the loop has two entries:
//! the test, from before the loop, and the body. Such a loop is irreducible: none of its blocks dominates the others,
//! and loop invariant code motion leaves it alone.
//!
//! This pass rotates such loops: the blocks that the test dominates are copied for the paths that enter the test from
//! before the loop, which then run the copy and enter the body (or leave the loop) from there, like the on-stack
//! replacement entry does. The body becomes the loop's only entry, its header, and the test its latch. Values the
//! test makes only reach the blocks it leads to through their phis, since it dominates none of them, so the copy's
//! edges bring its values to those phis.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use super::edit;
use crate::ir::Block;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;

/// How many nodes the blocks of a test that gets copied may have at most.
const MAX_COPIED_NODES: usize = 64;

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone, steps: &mut [Zone; 2]) {
    let [step, _] = steps;
    if graph.osr_entries.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut rotated = false;
    let mut dominators = Dominators::new_in(work);
    // NB: Each rotation makes one irreducible loop reducible; a graph has fewer such loops than blocks.
    for _ in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        // NB: Each rotation makes tables as large as the graph, which go when it ends.
        let rotated_one = step.scope(|step| {
            dominators.compute(graph);
            let Some((test, region, sources)) = find_rotatable_test(graph, &dominators, step) else {
                return false;
            };
            rotate(graph, test, &region, &sources, step);
            true
        });
        if !rotated_one {
            break;
        }
        rotated = true;
    }
    if rotated {
        lay_out_in_reverse_post_order(graph, work);
        edit::remove_trivial_phis(graph, work);
    }
}

/// The blocks a depth-first walk from the entries reaches each block from over a retreating edge: an edge to a block
/// the walk is still in.
fn retreating_edges<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneVec<'w, ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>> {
    let mut sources = ZoneVec::from_iter_in((0..graph.blocks.len()).map(|_| ZoneVec::new_in(work)), work);
    let mut state = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0u8, graph.blocks.len(), work);
    const ON_STACK: u8 = 1;
    const DONE: u8 = 2;
    let mut stack = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for entry in graph.entries() {
        if state[entry.index()] != 0 {
            continue;
        }
        stack.clear();
        stack.push((entry, 0usize));
        state[entry.index()] = ON_STACK;
        while let Some((block, next)) = stack.last_mut() {
            let block = *block;
            let successors = graph.successors(block);
            let Some(successor) = successors.get(*next).copied() else {
                state[block.index()] = DONE;
                stack.pop();
                continue;
            };
            *next += 1;
            match state[successor.index()] {
                0 => {
                    state[successor.index()] = ON_STACK;
                    stack.push((successor, 0));
                }
                ON_STACK => sources[successor.index()].push(block),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    sources
}

/// A block that a retreating edge it does not dominate leads to, with the blocks it dominates, if they can be copied
/// for the paths that enter it from elsewhere, and the sources of the retreating edges to it.
fn find_rotatable_test<'w>(
    graph: &Graph,
    dominators: &Dominators,
    work: &'w Zone,
) -> Option<(BlockId, ZoneBitSet<'w>, ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>)> {
    let mut retreating = retreating_edges(graph, work);
    let entries = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(graph.entries(), work);
    let mut region = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.blocks.len(), work);
    'blocks: for (index, sources) in retreating.iter().enumerate() {
        let test = BlockId::from_index(index);
        if sources.is_empty()
            || entries.contains(&test)
            || sources.iter().all(|source| dominators.dominates(test, *source))
        {
            continue;
        }
        region.clear();
        let mut node_count = 0;
        for (block, block_sources) in retreating.iter().enumerate() {
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(block);
            if !dominators.is_reachable(block_id) || !dominators.dominates(test, block_id) {
                continue;
            }
            region.insert(block);
            node_count += graph.block_nodes(block_id).count();
            // NB: Copying a loop inside the region would take more than copying its blocks.
            if node_count > MAX_COPIED_NODES || (block != index && !block_sources.is_empty()) {
                continue 'blocks;
            }
        }
        let enters_from_before = graph
            .block(test)
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .any(|predecessor| !sources.contains(predecessor));
        // NB: Where the other entry enters an inner loop at its header, the test leads to that header, and rotating
        //     would make it the header of both loops: the inner loop would be no loop of its own anymore.
        let leads_to_loop_header = region.iter().any(|block| {
            graph
                .successors(BlockId::from_index(block))
                .iter()
                .any(|successor| !region.contains(successor.index()) && graph.block(*successor).is_loop_header)
        });
        if sources.iter().any(|source| region.contains(source.index())) || !enters_from_before || leads_to_loop_header {
            continue;
        }
        return Some((test, region, retreating[index].take()));
    }
    None
}

/// Copies the blocks of `region`, which `test` dominates, for the predecessors of `test` that enter it from before
/// the loop (all but the `sources` of retreating edges), and makes those predecessors branch to the copy of `test`.
fn rotate(graph: &mut Graph, test: BlockId, region: &ZoneBitSet, sources: &[BlockId], work: &Zone) {
    let entering = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        graph
            .block(test)
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .map(|predecessor| !sources.contains(predecessor)),
        work,
    );
    let mut inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut phis = ZoneVec::new_in(work);

    // The copies of the blocks, and of their nodes, with the inputs and frame states of the originals for now. The
    // copy of the test takes the phi inputs from the predecessors that enter it.
    let mut block_copy = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, graph.blocks.len(), work);
    let mut node_copy: ZoneVec<Option<NodeId>> = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let blocks = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(region.iter().map(BlockId::from_index), work);
    for &block in &blocks {
        let data = graph.block(block);
        let copy = graph.add_block(Block {
            bytecode_start: data.bytecode_start,
            is_cold: data.is_cold,
            start_frame_state: data.start_frame_state,
            ..graph.new_block()
        });
        block_copy[block.index()] = Some(copy);
    }
    let copied = |block: BlockId, block_copy: &[Option<BlockId>]| block_copy[block.index()].expect("in the region");
    let test_copy = copied(test, &block_copy);
    phis.assign(&graph.block(test).phis);
    for phi in phis.iter().copied() {
        inputs.clear();
        inputs.extend(
            graph
                .node(phi)
                .inputs
                .iter()
                .zip(&entering)
                .filter(|(_, entering)| **entering)
                .map(|(input, _)| *input),
        );
        node_copy[phi.index()] = Some(if inputs.iter().all(|input| *input == inputs[0]) {
            inputs[0]
        } else {
            let data = graph.node(phi);
            let copy = graph.add(Op::Phi, &inputs, data.repr, data.pc);
            graph.blocks[test_copy.index()].phis.push(copy);
            copy
        });
    }
    let mut copies = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut body = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut predecessors = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for &block in &blocks {
        let copy = copied(block, &block_copy);
        let data = graph.block(block);
        phis.clear();
        if block != test {
            phis.extend_from_slice(&data.phis);
        }
        body.assign(&data.body);
        let control = data.control;
        predecessors.assign(&data.predecessors);
        for (node, is_phi) in phis
            .iter()
            .map(|node| (*node, true))
            .chain(body.iter().chain(&control).map(|node| (*node, false)))
        {
            let new = graph.add_node(graph.node(node).clone());
            node_copy.resize(graph.nodes.len(), None);
            node_copy[node.index()] = Some(new);
            copies.push(new);
            let copy_data = &mut graph.blocks[copy.index()];
            if is_phi {
                copy_data.phis.push(new);
            } else if Some(node) == control {
                copy_data.control = Some(new);
            } else {
                copy_data.body.push(new);
            }
        }
        if block != test {
            let copy_predecessors = &mut graph.blocks[copy.index()].predecessors;
            copy_predecessors.clear();
            copy_predecessors.extend(predecessors.iter().map(|predecessor| copied(*predecessor, &block_copy)));
        }
    }
    let map =
        |node: NodeId, node_copy: &[Option<NodeId>]| node_copy.get(node.index()).copied().flatten().unwrap_or(node);

    // The copies use the copies of the region's values, and exit with copies of the frame states that refer to them.
    // Frame states that refer to none (like those of the callers of inlined calls) stay shared.
    let mut frame_state_copy: ZoneVec<Option<FrameStateId>> =
        ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, graph.frame_states.len(), work);
    let mut chain = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut values = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut copy_frame_state = |graph: &mut Graph, id: FrameStateId| -> FrameStateId {
        chain.clear();
        chain.extend(graph.frame_state_chain(id));
        let mut copied_parent = None;
        for id in chain.iter().rev() {
            if let Some(copy) = frame_state_copy[id.index()] {
                copied_parent = Some(copy);
                continue;
            }
            let original = graph.frame_state(*id);
            values.clear();
            values.extend(
                original
                    .values
                    .iter()
                    .map(|(slot, value)| (*slot, map(*value, &node_copy))),
            );
            let parent = if copied_parent.is_some() {
                copied_parent
            } else {
                original.parent
            };
            let copy = if *original.values == *values && original.parent == parent {
                *id
            } else {
                let mut state = edit::frame_state_with_values(graph, *id, &values);
                state.parent = parent;
                graph.add_frame_state(state)
            };
            frame_state_copy[id.index()] = Some(copy);
            copied_parent = Some(copy);
        }
        copied_parent.expect("the chain is not empty")
    };
    for &copy in &copies {
        for input in &mut graph.nodes[copy.index()].inputs {
            *input = map(*input, &node_copy);
        }
        if let Some(frame_state) = graph.node(copy).frame_state {
            graph.nodes[copy.index()].frame_state = Some(copy_frame_state(graph, frame_state));
        }
    }
    for &block in &blocks {
        let copy = copied(block, &block_copy);
        for successor in graph.successors(copy) {
            if let Some(successor_copy) = block_copy[successor.index()] {
                graph.replace_successor(copy, successor, successor_copy);
            }
        }
        if let Some(frame_state) = graph.block(copy).start_frame_state {
            graph.blocks[copy.index()].start_frame_state = Some(copy_frame_state(graph, frame_state));
        }
    }

    // The edges of the copies out of the region bring the copies of the values the originals bring.
    for &block in &blocks {
        let copy = copied(block, &block_copy);
        for successor in graph.successors(block) {
            if region.contains(successor.index()) {
                continue;
            }
            // NB: A block that branches to the same block twice is its predecessor twice.
            let already = graph
                .block(successor)
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .filter(|predecessor| **predecessor == copy)
                .count();
            let position = graph
                .block(successor)
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter(|(_, predecessor)| **predecessor == block)
                .map(|(position, _)| position)
                .nth(already)
                .expect("each edge from the block has a place among the predecessors");
            graph.blocks[successor.index()].predecessors.push(copy);
            phis.assign(&graph.block(successor).phis);
            for phi in phis.iter().copied() {
                let input = map(graph.node(phi).inputs[position], &node_copy);
                graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.push(input);
            }
        }
    }

    // The blocks of the loop that the test leads to are its header now, which a rotation of a loop around it must not
    // make the header of that loop too.
    let mut visited = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.blocks.len(), work);
    let mut pending = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for &block in &blocks {
        for successor in graph.successors(block) {
            if !region.contains(successor.index())
                && reaches_without(graph, successor, sources, test, (&mut visited, &mut pending))
            {
                graph.blocks[successor.index()].is_loop_header = true;
            }
        }
    }
    graph.blocks[test.index()].is_loop_header = false;

    // The predecessors that entered the test enter its copy instead, and the test keeps the others.
    predecessors.assign(&graph.block(test).predecessors);
    for (predecessor, entering) in predecessors.iter().zip(&entering) {
        if *entering {
            graph.replace_successor(*predecessor, test, test_copy);
        }
    }
    let selected = |keep: bool| {
        predecessors
            .iter()
            .zip(&entering)
            .filter(move |(_, entering)| **entering == keep)
            .map(|(predecessor, _)| *predecessor)
    };
    let test_copy_predecessors = &mut graph.blocks[test_copy.index()].predecessors;
    test_copy_predecessors.clear();
    test_copy_predecessors.extend(selected(true));
    let test_predecessors = &mut graph.blocks[test.index()].predecessors;
    test_predecessors.clear();
    test_predecessors.extend(selected(false));
    phis.assign(&graph.block(test).phis);
    for phi in phis.iter().copied() {
        inputs.clear();
        inputs.extend(
            graph
                .node(phi)
                .inputs
                .iter()
                .zip(&entering)
                .filter(|(_, entering)| !**entering)
                .map(|(input, _)| *input),
        );
        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.assign(&inputs);
    }
    let zone = graph.zone;
    for index in 0..graph.legacy_arguments_guards.len() {
        let (guard, nodes) = &graph.legacy_arguments_guards[index];
        if let Some(copy) = node_copy.get(guard.index()).copied().flatten() {
            let nodes = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(nodes.iter().map(|node| map(*node, &node_copy)), zone);
            graph.legacy_arguments_guards.push((copy, nodes));
        }
    }
    for index in 0..graph.slow_paths_initializing_frame.len() {
        let node = graph.slow_paths_initializing_frame[index];
        if let Some(copy) = node_copy.get(node.index()).copied().flatten() {
            graph.slow_paths_initializing_frame.push(copy);
        }
    }
}

/// Whether a path that does not go through `avoided` leads from `start` to one of `targets`. `visited` and `pending`
/// are lists for the walk, which it empties first.
fn reaches_without(
    graph: &Graph,
    start: BlockId,
    targets: &[BlockId],
    avoided: BlockId,
    (visited, pending): (&mut ZoneBitSet, &mut ZoneVec<BlockId>),
) -> bool {
    visited.clear();
    pending.clear();
    pending.push(start);
    while let Some(block) = pending.pop() {
        if targets.contains(&block) {
            return true;
        }
        if block == avoided || visited.contains(block.index()) {
            continue;
        }
        visited.insert(block.index());
        pending.extend(graph.successors(block).iter().copied());
    }
    false
}

/// Orders the blocks so that each comes after its predecessors but those that reach it over a retreating edge, and
/// marks the blocks such edges lead to as loop headers too.
fn lay_out_in_reverse_post_order(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let mut post_order = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(graph.blocks.len(), work);
    let mut visited = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(false, graph.blocks.len(), work);
    // NB: The walk starts at the on-stack replacement entries, so that block 0 comes first.
    let entries = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(graph.entries(), work);
    let mut stack = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for &entry in entries.iter().rev() {
        if visited[entry.index()] {
            continue;
        }
        visited[entry.index()] = true;
        stack.clear();
        stack.push((entry, graph.successors(entry).len()));
        while let Some((block, remaining)) = stack.last_mut() {
            let block = *block;
            if *remaining == 0 {
                post_order.push(block);
                stack.pop();
                continue;
            }
            *remaining -= 1;
            // NB: Successors are visited last to first, so that the first comes right after its block.
            let successor = graph.successors(block)[*remaining];
            if !visited[successor.index()] {
                visited[successor.index()] = true;
                stack.push((successor, graph.successors(successor).len()));
            }
        }
    }
    post_order.reverse();
    graph.reorder_blocks(&post_order, work);
    for index in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let is_cold = graph.blocks[index].is_cold;
        let reached_from_later = graph.blocks[index]
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .any(|predecessor| predecessor.index() >= index && !(graph.block(*predecessor).is_cold && !is_cold));
        graph.blocks[index].is_loop_header |= reached_from_later;
    }
}

//! Optimization passes over the IR, run between graph building and register
//! allocation.
//!
//! The builder translates bytecode to SSA form and records its speculation
//! decisions as explicit checks and typed nodes; it folds nothing. The passes
//! then simplify the graph, one transformation per pass. Debug builds and
//! tests check the graph's invariants (see `verify`) after building and after
//! every pass.

mod bounds_check_elimination;
mod branch_fusion;
mod branch_splitting;
mod check_elimination;
mod dce;
pub mod dominators;
pub mod edit;
mod enumerated_keys;
mod escape_analysis;
mod exit_unboxing;
mod facts;
mod frame_initialization;
mod gvn;
mod interrupt_check_elimination;
mod key_strings;
mod licm;
mod loop_rotation;
mod representation;
mod simplify;
mod truncation;
pub mod verify;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use ak::Zone;
use core::fmt;

use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::bytecode::FrameLayout;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use dominators::Dominators;

/// One transformation of the graph.
struct Pass {
    name: &'static str,
    run: Run,
}

/// How a pass runs. A pass that repeats a step whose work data grows with the graph keeps the data of each step in
/// the step zone, which drops it when the step ends: the work zone takes nothing back before the pass ends, so it
/// would hold the data of every step. A pass whose steps hand data on to later steps moves what is still in use from
/// one step zone to the other (see `check_elimination`).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Run {
    /// A pass that keeps its data in the work zone.
    Once(fn(&mut Graph, &Zone)),
    /// A pass that keeps what lasts for the whole pass in the work zone, and the data of its steps in the step zones
    /// (see `Scratch::steps`).
    Steps(fn(&mut Graph, &Zone, &mut [Zone; 2])),
}

/// How many bytes of memory each step zone keeps after a pass, so that the steps of most functions take no memory from
/// the system again.
const STEP_MEMORY_KEPT: usize = 4 << 20;

/// Runs the pass `run`. It keeps its own data in `work` and `steps`, which hold none of it when this returns.
fn run_pass(run: Run, graph: &mut Graph, work: &mut Zone, steps: &mut [Zone; 2]) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    fits(graph)?;
    match run {
        Run::Once(run) => work.scope(|work| run(graph, work)),
        Run::Steps(run) => {
            work.scope(|work| run(graph, work, steps));
            // NB: A pass that moves its data between the step zones leaves data in both. The memory of large steps
            //     goes back to the system, so that it does not stay on top of what the stages after this one take
            //     in the work zone.
            for zone in steps {
                zone.reset();
                zone.trim(STEP_MEMORY_KEPT);
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Fails the compile if the passes cannot compute the dominators of `graph`, which has too many blocks.
// NB: The passes add blocks, so the count is checked again before each of them.
fn fits(graph: &Graph) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    if graph.blocks.len() > Dominators::MAX_BLOCKS {
        return Err(CompileFailure::TooLarge);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The passes, in the order they run.
const PASSES: &[Pass] = &[
    Pass {
        name: "loop rotation",
        run: Run::Steps(loop_rotation::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "trivial phi removal",
        run: Run::Once(edit::remove_trivial_phis),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "truncation",
        run: Run::Once(truncation::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "simplification",
        run: Run::Once(simplify::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "representation selection",
        run: Run::Once(representation::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "simplification",
        run: Run::Once(simplify::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "branch splitting",
        run: Run::Steps(branch_splitting::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "global value numbering",
        run: Run::Once(gvn::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "check elimination",
        run: Run::Steps(check_elimination::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "simplification",
        run: Run::Once(simplify::run_after_check_elimination),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "global value numbering",
        run: Run::Once(gvn::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "loop invariant code motion",
        run: Run::Once(licm::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "bounds check elimination",
        run: Run::Once(bounds_check_elimination::run),
    },
    Pass {
        name: "interrupt check elimination",
        run: Run::Once(interrupt_check_elimination::run),
    },
    Pass {

    },
    Pass {

    },

    },
    Pass {
        name: "dead code elimination",
        run: Run::Once(dce::run),
    },
    Pass {

    },

    Pass {

        run: Run::Once(key_strings::run),
    },
];

/// Runs every pass over `graph`, whose compiled function has frame layout
/// `layout` (for dumps of invalid graphs). Checks the graph's invariants
/// before and after every pass in debug builds and tests, or if `verify`.
pub fn optimize(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    layout: &FrameLayout,
    verify: bool,
    work: &mut Zone,
    steps: &mut [Zone; 2],
) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    run_passes(graph, layout, verify, work, steps, &mut |_, _| {})
}

/// `optimize()`, writing the graph as text to `dumps` after building it and
/// after every pass, each headed by "=== after <pass>" (for tests of passes).
/// Text that `dumps` has no room for is left out.
pub fn optimize_with_dumps(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    layout: &FrameLayout,
    verify: bool,
    work: &mut Zone,
    steps: &mut [Zone; 2],
    dumps: &mut dyn fmt::Write,
) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    run_passes(graph, layout, verify, work, steps, &mut |graph, after| {
        // NB: A write fails only when `dumps` has no room for more text.
        let _ = write!(dumps, "=== after {after}\n{}", crate::ir::dump(graph, layout));
    })
}

fn run_passes(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    layout: &FrameLayout,
    verify: bool,
    work: &mut Zone,
    steps: &mut [Zone; 2],
    observe: &mut dyn FnMut(&Graph, &str),
) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
    let verify = verify || cfg!(debug_assertions) || cfg!(test);
    // NB: Graph building builds the loops around OSR entries even without
    //     a forward entry, which no entry reaches when every path out of the
    //     inner loop ends in an exit.
    work.scope(|work| edit::remove_unreachable_blocks(graph, work));
    check(graph, layout, verify, work, "graph building");
    observe(graph, "graph building");
    for pass in PASSES {
        run_pass(pass.run, graph, work, steps)?;
        check(graph, layout, verify, work, pass.name);
        observe(graph, pass.name);
    }
    // NB: Nodes that took different refinements of one value compute the
    //     same once the refinements are gone, and nothing moves anymore.
    work.scope(|work| edit::remove_refinements(graph, work));
    run_pass(Run::Once(gvn::run), graph, work, steps)?;
    // NB: Checks that merged took their frame states along, which may have been the last uses of what those refer to.
    run_pass(Run::Once(dce::run), graph, work, steps)?;
    check(graph, layout, verify, work, "refinement removal");
    observe(graph, "refinement removal");
    work.scope(|work| frame_initialization::run(graph, layout, work));
    check(graph, layout, verify, work, "frame initialization");
    work.scope(|work| edit::remove_unused_frame_states(graph, work));
    // NB: Only the final block order puts the cold code last; passes see
    //     every block after its predecessors (except over back edges).
    //     On-stack replacement entries run once per entry, so they are cold
    //     code too, which keeps the blocks they lead to from starting with
    //     their register state.
    for index in 0..graph.osr_entries.len() {
        let (_, block) = graph.osr_entries[index];
        graph.blocks[block.index()].is_cold = true;
    }
    work.scope(|work| edit::move_cold_blocks_last(graph, work));
    check(graph, layout, verify, work, "cold block layout");
    observe(graph, "frame initialization");
    Ok(())
}

fn check(graph: &Graph, layout: &FrameLayout, verify: bool, work: &mut Zone, after: &str) {
    if !verify {
        return;
    }
    // NB: The errors are in the work zone, so the panic happens while it holds them.
    work.scope(|work| {
        if let Err(errors) = verify::verify_with(graph, work).and(verify::verify_frame_writes(graph, layout, work)) {
            panic!(
                "invalid graph after {after}:\n{errors}\n{}",
                crate::ir::dump(graph, layout)
            );
        }
    });
}

//! Representation selection: unboxes phis.
//!
//! The builder makes every phi tagged, boxing unboxed values that flow into
//! one. A phi whose inputs are all boxed int32 values, int32 constants or
//! other such phis becomes an int32 phi of the unboxed values instead, like
//! loop counters; likewise for booleans, like the results of comparisons
//! merging before a branch, and for numbers, whose int32 inputs become
//! doubles, like the results of arithmetic that saw doubles. Unboxing only
//! pays off for phis connected (through other phis) to unboxed inputs,
//! unboxing checks or branches.
//!
//! An unboxed phi's int32 checks become the phi itself, and its other users
//! get one boxing of it at the start of its block. Exits take it unboxed.
//! The boxings feeding it are left for dead code elimination.

use super::edit;
use super::edit::Constants;
use super::edit::Replacements;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Node;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::value;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneMap;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// An unboxed representation phis can take.
struct Unboxed {
    repr: Repr,
    /// Boxes a value of the representation.
    box_op: Op<'static>,
    /// The unboxed bits of a tagged constant of the representation.
    constant: fn(u64) -> Option<u64>,
    /// Unboxes a tagged value, if it is of the representation.
    check_op: Option<Op<'static>>,
    /// Whether a user of a phi benefits from it being unboxed.
    wants_unboxed: fn(&Op) -> bool,
    /// Whether int32 values become values of the representation through
    /// `Op::Int32ToFloat64`.
    converts_int32: bool,
}

const UNBOXED: [Unboxed; 3] = [
    Unboxed {
        repr: Repr::Int32,
        box_op: Op::BoxInt32,
        constant: |bits| value::as_int32(bits).map(|integer| u64::from(integer.cast_unsigned())),
        check_op: Some(Op::CheckInt32),
        wants_unboxed: |op| *op == Op::CheckInt32,
        converts_int32: false,
    },
    Unboxed {
        repr: Repr::Bool,
        box_op: Op::BoxBool,
        constant: |bits| match bits {
            value::TRUE => Some(1),
            value::FALSE => Some(0),
            _ => None,
        },
        check_op: None,
        wants_unboxed: |op| matches!(op, Op::BranchTruthy { .. }),
        converts_int32: false,
    },
    Unboxed {
        repr: Repr::Float64,
        box_op: Op::BoxFloat64,
        constant: |bits| {
            if let Some(integer) = value::as_int32(bits) {
                return Some(f64::from(integer).to_bits());
            }
            value::is_double(bits).then_some(bits)
        },
        check_op: Some(Op::CheckNumber),
        wants_unboxed: |op| matches!(op, Op::UnboxDouble | Op::CheckNumber),
        converts_int32: true,
    },
];

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    for unboxed in &UNBOXED {
        unbox_phis(graph, unboxed, work);
    }
}

/// Whether `node` is among the phis being unboxed. Nodes added by the pass
/// are not.
fn is_candidate(candidates: &ZoneBitSet, node: NodeId) -> bool {
    node.index() < candidates.capacity() && candidates.contains(node.index())
}

/// What a phi input is unboxed, if it can be one without a check.
enum UnboxedInput {
    Value(NodeId),
    Constant(u64),
    /// The `Repr::Int32` value, which a conversion makes one of the
    /// representation.
    Converted(NodeId),
}

fn unboxed_input(graph: &Graph, unboxed: &Unboxed, input: NodeId, candidates: &ZoneBitSet) -> Option<UnboxedInput> {
    let node = graph.node(input);
    match node.op {
        ref op if *op == unboxed.box_op => Some(UnboxedInput::Value(node.inputs[0])),
        Op::Constant(bits) if node.repr == Some(Repr::Tagged) => (unboxed.constant)(bits).map(UnboxedInput::Constant),
        Op::Phi if is_candidate(candidates, input) => Some(UnboxedInput::Value(input)),
        Op::BoxInt32 if unboxed.converts_int32 => Some(UnboxedInput::Converted(node.inputs[0])),
        _ if unboxed.converts_int32 && node.repr == Some(Repr::Int32) => Some(UnboxedInput::Converted(input)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Marks the phis of `phis` connected to marked ones through their inputs.
fn spread_over_phis(graph: &Graph, phis: &ZoneBitSet, marked: &mut ZoneBitSet) {
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for phi in phis.iter() {
            for input in &graph.nodes[phi].inputs {
                if is_candidate(phis, *input) && marked.contains(phi) != marked.contains(input.index()) {
                    marked.insert(phi);
                    marked.insert(input.index());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The phis of `phis` whose values the code checks with `Unboxed::check_op`
/// somewhere, and the phis connected to them, through which the same values
/// flow. Their tagged inputs are worth checking where they enter (see
/// `checkable_inputs()`): the values already have to pass the check, so
/// checking them once where they enter, rather than wherever they are used
/// (like loop invariant values carried around loops entered at their header
/// and at an on-stack replacement entry), at worst exits before the check
/// would, once.
fn checked_phis<'w>(graph: &Graph, unboxed: &Unboxed, phis: &ZoneBitSet, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneBitSet<'w> {
    let mut checked = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let Some(check) = &unboxed.check_op else {
        return checked;
    };
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in &block.body {
            let data = graph.node(*node);
            if data.op == *check && is_candidate(phis, data.inputs[0]) {
                checked.insert(data.inputs[0].index());
            }
        }
    }
    spread_over_phis(graph, phis, &mut checked);
    checked
}

/// For each phi of `graph`, its block, and the frame states that checks at
/// the end of the predecessors its inputs come from can exit with, where
/// they can unbox the inputs (see `Unboxed::check_op`): tagged values from
/// predecessors that only jump to the phi's block, which starts a bytecode
/// block that the check never exited at before. Exits start that block over.
/// Only the values of `checked` phis, which the code checks elsewhere, are
/// checked where they enter.
fn checkable_inputs<'w>(
    graph: &Graph,
    unboxed: &Unboxed,
    checked: &ZoneBitSet,
    work: &'w Zone,
) -> ZoneMap<'w, NodeId, (BlockId, &'w [Option<edit::EnteringValues<'w>>])> {
    let mut checkable = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let mut entering = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
        let gated = match (unboxed.check_op.as_ref(), block.start_frame_state) {
            (Some(check), Some(state)) => {
                let state = graph.frame_state(state);
                check
                    .exit_kind()
                    .is_none_or(|kind| graph.exit_sites.contains(&(state.executable, state.pc, kind)))
            }
            _ => true,
        };
        // OPTIMIZATION: The frame state entering the block from a predecessor is the same for every phi, and blocks of
        //               large functions can have hundreds of phis with as many values in that frame state.
        entering.clear();
        entering.resize(block.predecessors.len(), None);
        for phi in &block.phis {
            let inputs =
                work.alloc_slice_from_iter(block.predecessors.iter().zip(&graph.node(*phi).inputs).enumerate().map(
                    |(entry, (predecessor, input))| {
                        let checkable = !gated
                            && checked.contains(phi.index())
                            && graph.node(*input).repr == Some(Repr::Tagged)
                            && graph.control(*predecessor).op == (Op::Jump { target: block_id });
                        checkable
                            .then(|| {
                                *entering[entry]
                                    .get_or_insert_with(|| edit::values_entering(graph, block_id, *predecessor, work))
                            })
                            .flatten()
                    },
                ));
            checkable.insert(*phi, (block_id, &*inputs));
        }
    }
    checkable
}

fn unbox_phis(graph: &mut Graph, unboxed: &Unboxed, work: &Zone) {
    let phis = ZoneVec::from_iter_in(
        graph
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|block| block.phis.iter().copied())
            .filter(|phi| graph.node(*phi).repr == Some(Repr::Tagged)),
        work,
    );
    if phis.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let count = graph.nodes.len();
    let mut candidates = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    for phi in &phis {
        candidates.insert(phi.index());
    }
    // NB: Phis that benefit from being unboxed: those of boxed values, and
    //     those that users unbox.
    let mut benefiting = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    for phi in candidates.iter() {
        if graph.nodes[phi]
            .inputs
            .iter()
            .any(|input| graph.node(*input).op == unboxed.box_op)
        {
            benefiting.insert(phi);
        }
    }
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.body.iter().chain(&block.control) {
            let data = graph.node(*node);
            if (unboxed.wants_unboxed)(&data.op)
                && let Some(input) = data.inputs.first()
                && is_candidate(&candidates, *input)
            {
                benefiting.insert(input.index());
            }
        }
    }
    if benefiting.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let checked = checked_phis(graph, unboxed, &candidates, work);
    let checkable = checkable_inputs(graph, unboxed, &checked, work);
    // Drop phis with an input that cannot be unboxed until none is left.
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for phi in &phis {
            if candidates.contains(phi.index())
                && graph.node(*phi).inputs.iter().enumerate().any(|(index, input)| {
                    unboxed_input(graph, unboxed, *input, &candidates).is_none()
                        && checkable.get(phi).expect("phis are checkable").1[index].is_none()
                })
            {
                candidates.remove(phi.index());
                changed = true;
            }
        }
    }

    // Keep the phis connected to something that benefits.
    let mut useful = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    for phi in benefiting.iter().filter(|phi| candidates.contains(*phi)) {
        useful.insert(phi);
    }
    spread_over_phis(graph, &candidates, &mut useful);
    let candidates = useful;
    if candidates.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

    // Unbox the phis in place.
    let mut constants = Constants::new(graph, work);
    let mut conversions = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let mut checks = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let mut phi_inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for phi in candidates.iter() {
        let phi_id = NodeId::from_index(phi);
        let (block, states) = *checkable.get(&phi_id).expect("phis are checkable");
        phi_inputs.assign(&graph.nodes[phi].inputs);
        inputs.clear();
        for (index, input) in phi_inputs.iter().copied().enumerate() {
            let value = match unboxed_input(graph, unboxed, input, &candidates) {
                Some(UnboxedInput::Value(value)) => value,
                Some(UnboxedInput::Constant(bits)) => constants.get_typed(graph, bits, unboxed.repr),
                Some(UnboxedInput::Converted(integer)) => match graph.constant_value(integer) {
                    Some(bits) => {
                        let number = f64::from((bits as u32).cast_signed());
                        constants.get_typed(graph, number.to_bits(), unboxed.repr)
                    }
                    None => *conversions
                        .entry(integer)
                        .or_insert_with(|| convert_int32(graph, integer)),
                },
                None => {
                    let predecessor = graph.block(block).predecessors[index];
                    let (template, values) = states[index].expect("candidate phis only have unboxable inputs");
                    *checks
                        .entry((predecessor, input))
                        .or_insert_with(|| check_at_end(graph, unboxed, predecessor, input, template, values))
                }
            };
            inputs.push(value);
        }
        let node = &mut graph.nodes[phi];
        node.inputs.assign(&inputs);
        node.repr = Some(unboxed.repr);
    }

    // Unboxing checks of the phis are the phis themselves; other users that
    // need a tagged value get one boxing per phi.
    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut boxes = ZoneMap::new_in(work);
    let mut nodes = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for block in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let block_data = &graph.blocks[block];
        nodes.clear();
        nodes.extend(
            block_data
                .phis
                .iter()
                .chain(&block_data.body)
                .chain(&block_data.control)
                .copied(),
        );
        for user in nodes.iter().copied() {
            let user_node = graph.node(user);
            if unboxed.check_op.as_ref() == Some(&user_node.op) && is_candidate(&candidates, user_node.inputs[0]) {
                replacements.replace(user, user_node.inputs[0]);
                removed.insert(user.index());
                continue;
            }
            if (user_node.op == Op::Phi && is_candidate(&candidates, user))
                || user_node.op == unboxed.box_op
                || matches!(user_node.op, Op::StoreSlot { .. })
            {
                continue;
            }
            for index in 0..graph.node(user).inputs.len() {
                let input = graph.node(user).inputs[index];
                if !is_candidate(&candidates, input) {
                    continue;
                }
                let boxed = *boxes.entry(input).or_insert_with(|| box_phi(graph, unboxed, input));
                graph.nodes[user.index()].inputs[index] = boxed;
            }
        }
    }
    replacements.apply(graph);
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
}

/// Adds a check that unboxes `value` at the end of `predecessor`, exiting
/// with the frame state `template` with `values` where it fails.
fn check_at_end(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    unboxed: &Unboxed,
    predecessor: BlockId,
    value: NodeId,
    template: FrameStateId,
    values: &[(u32, NodeId)],
) -> NodeId {
    let state = edit::frame_state_with_values(graph, template, values);
    let pc = state.pc;
    let frame_state = Some(graph.add_frame_state(state));
    let check = graph.add_node(Node {
        op: unboxed
            .check_op
            .clone()
            .expect("only checked representations check inputs"),
        inputs: graph.list(&[value]),
        repr: Some(unboxed.repr),
        frame_state,
        pc,
    });
    graph.blocks[predecessor.index()].body.push(check);
    check
}

/// Adds the `Repr::Float64` conversion of the `Repr::Int32` `integer` right
/// after it.
fn convert_int32(graph: &mut Graph, integer: NodeId) -> NodeId {
    let (block, position) = graph
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .find_map(|(index, block)| {
            if block.phis.contains(&integer) {
                return Some((index, 0));
            }
            block
                .body
                .iter()
                .position(|node| *node == integer)
                .map(|position| (index, position + 1))
        })
        .expect("values are in blocks");
    let converted = graph.add(
        Op::Int32ToFloat64,
        &[integer],
        Some(Repr::Float64),
        graph.node(integer).pc,
    );
    graph.blocks[block].body.insert(position, converted);
    converted
}

/// Adds a boxing of `phi` at the start of its block.
fn box_phi(graph: &mut Graph, unboxed: &Unboxed, phi: NodeId) -> NodeId {
    let block = graph
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .position(|block| block.phis.contains(&phi))
        .expect("phis are in blocks");
    let boxed = graph.add(unboxed.box_op.clone(), &[phi], Some(Repr::Tagged), graph.node(phi).pc);
    graph.blocks[block].body.insert(0, boxed);
    boxed
}
