//! Constant folding and strength reduction.
//!
//! - Conversions and int32 operations of constants become constants, and
//!   conversions of conversions the values they started from.
//! - Int32 operations that leave their left-hand side as it is, like
//!   `x | 0`, become that value, and commutative ones take constants as
//!   their right-hand sides.
//! - Branches on constants become jumps; truthiness branches on boxed
//!   booleans test the unboxed boolean, and on boxed int32 values compare
//!   the unboxed value with 0.

use super::edit;
use super::edit::Constants;
use super::edit::Replacements;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Comparison;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::value;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// The truthiness of a constant, where it does not depend on the heap.
fn constant_truthiness(bits: u64, repr: Repr) -> Option<bool> {
    match repr {
        Repr::Bool => Some(bits != 0),
        Repr::Int32 => Some(bits as u32 != 0),
        Repr::Float64 | Repr::Pointer => None,
        Repr::Tagged => match value::tag(bits) {
            value::BOOLEAN_TAG | value::INT32_TAG => Some(bits as u32 != 0),
            value::UNDEFINED_TAG | value::NULL_TAG => Some(false),
            _ => None,
        },
    }
}

fn int32_of(graph: &Graph, node: NodeId) -> Option<i32> {
    graph.int32_constant(node)
}

/// The value of `node`, if it is a `Repr::Float64` constant.
fn float64_of(graph: &Graph, node: NodeId) -> Option<f64> {
    let bits = graph.constant_value(node)?;
    (graph.node(graph.unrefined(node)).repr == Some(Repr::Float64)).then(|| f64::from_bits(bits))
}

/// ToInt32 of a number.
fn to_int32(number: f64) -> i32 {
    if !number.is_finite() {
        return 0;
    }
    (number.trunc().rem_euclid(4_294_967_296.0) as u32).cast_signed()
}

/// ToUint8Clamp of a number.
fn to_uint8_clamp(number: f64) -> i32 {
    if number.is_nan() {
        return 0;
    }
    number.clamp(0.0, 255.0).round_ties_even() as i32
}

fn fold_int32_binary(op: BinaryOp, lhs: i32, rhs: i32) -> Option<i32> {
    let shift = (rhs & 31) as u32;
    match op {
        BinaryOp::Add => lhs.checked_add(rhs),
        BinaryOp::Sub => lhs.checked_sub(rhs),
        BinaryOp::Mul => lhs
            .checked_mul(rhs)
            .filter(|product| *product != 0 || (lhs >= 0 && rhs >= 0)),
        BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => Some(lhs & rhs),
        BinaryOp::BitwiseOr => Some(lhs | rhs),
        BinaryOp::BitwiseXor => Some(lhs ^ rhs),
        BinaryOp::LeftShift => Some(lhs.wrapping_shl(shift)),
        BinaryOp::RightShift => Some(lhs.wrapping_shr(shift)),
        BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => i32::try_from(lhs.cast_unsigned().wrapping_shr(shift)).ok(),
        // NB: A zero remainder of a negative dividend is -0.
        BinaryOp::Mod => lhs.checked_rem(rhs).filter(|remainder| *remainder != 0 || lhs >= 0),
        BinaryOp::Div => None,
    }
}

fn fold_int32_wrapping_binary(op: BinaryOp, lhs: i32, rhs: i32) -> i32 {
    match op {
        BinaryOp::Add => lhs.wrapping_add(rhs),
        BinaryOp::Sub => lhs.wrapping_sub(rhs),
        BinaryOp::Mul => lhs.wrapping_mul(rhs),
        BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => lhs.cast_unsigned().wrapping_shr((rhs & 31) as u32).cast_signed(),
        _ => unreachable!("only additions, subtractions, multiplications and unsigned right shifts wrap"),
    }
}

/// Whether `x op rhs` is `x` for every int32 `x`. An unsigned right shift
/// by 0 is not, unless it wraps: it makes negative values large numbers.
fn is_int32_identity(op: BinaryOp, rhs: i32, wrapping: bool) -> bool {
    match op {
        BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::BitwiseOr | BinaryOp::BitwiseXor => rhs == 0,
        BinaryOp::LeftShift | BinaryOp::RightShift => rhs & 31 == 0,
        BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => wrapping && rhs & 31 == 0,
        BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => rhs == -1,
        BinaryOp::Mul => rhs == 1,
        BinaryOp::Mod | BinaryOp::Div => false,
    }
}

/// Double arithmetic of int32 values, which ToInt32 of its result can do
/// as wrapping int32 arithmetic instead.
enum Int32Term<'w> {
    Value(NodeId),
    Constant(i32),
    Binary(BinaryOp, &'w Int32Term<'w>, &'w Int32Term<'w>),
}

/// How many levels of additions and subtractions `int32_term()` looks
/// through: the exact results of at most 2^8 int32 values are below 2^53,
/// so doubles hold them exactly, and ToInt32 of them is what wrapping int32
/// arithmetic computes.
const MAX_INT32_TERM_DEPTH: u32 = 8;

/// `value`, a `Repr::Float64`, as double arithmetic of int32 values, if it
/// is that: conversions of int32 values, int32 constants, and additions and
/// subtractions of such. The terms it is made of are in `work`.
fn int32_term<'w>(graph: &Graph, value: NodeId, depth: u32, work: &'w Zone) -> Option<Int32Term<'w>> {
    let node = graph.node(graph.unrefined(value));
    match node.op {
        Op::Int32ToFloat64 => Some(Int32Term::Value(node.inputs[0])),
        Op::Constant(bits) if node.repr == Some(Repr::Float64) => {
            let number = f64::from_bits(bits);
            let integer = number as i32;
            (f64::from(integer) == number && !(number == 0.0 && number.is_sign_negative()))
                .then_some(Int32Term::Constant(integer))
        }
        Op::Float64Binary {
            op: op @ (BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub),
        } if depth < MAX_INT32_TERM_DEPTH => Some(Int32Term::Binary(
            op,
            work.alloc(int32_term(graph, node.inputs[0], depth + 1, work)?),
            work.alloc(int32_term(graph, node.inputs[1], depth + 1, work)?),
        )),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Adds the wrapping int32 arithmetic of `term` to `block` before
/// `position`, returning its value and the position after it.
fn build_int32_term(
    graph: &mut Graph,
    constants: &mut Constants,
    term: &Int32Term,
    block: BlockId,
    position: usize,
    pc: u32,
) -> (NodeId, usize) {
    match term {
        Int32Term::Value(value) => (*value, position),
        Int32Term::Constant(integer) => (
            constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(integer.cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32),
            position,
        ),
        Int32Term::Binary(op, lhs, rhs) => {
            let (lhs, position) = build_int32_term(graph, constants, lhs, block, position, pc);
            let (rhs, position) = build_int32_term(graph, constants, rhs, block, position, pc);
            let node = graph.add(Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: *op }, &[lhs, rhs], Some(Repr::Int32), pc);
            graph.blocks[block.index()].body.insert(position, node);
            (node, position + 1)
        }
    }
}

/// The double `value` checks to be an int32, if it is a `CheckInt32` of a
/// boxed double.
fn checked_double(graph: &Graph, value: NodeId) -> Option<NodeId> {
    let check = graph.node(value);
    if check.op != Op::CheckInt32 {
        return None;
    }
    let boxed = graph.node(graph.unrefined(check.inputs[0]));
    (boxed.op == Op::BoxFloat64).then(|| boxed.inputs[0])
}

/// Whether a fold may replace an operation with `value`, which leaves
/// `value` standing for the operation's result. An int32 check of a boxed
/// double may not, nor one of what may become a boxed double (a phi that
/// representation selection unboxes, or a boxing of a check that goes): only
/// the check's exit makes the double the result (like ToInt32 of a double
/// for `x | 0`, and +0 for `-0 + 0`), while the check goes where its users
/// all take the double (see `dissolvable_checks()`).
fn may_stand_for_result(graph: &Graph, value: NodeId) -> bool {
    let check = graph.node(graph.unrefined(value));
    check.op != Op::CheckInt32
        || !matches!(
            graph.node(graph.unrefined(check.inputs[0])).op,
            Op::BoxFloat64 | Op::Phi | Op::BoxInt32
        )
}

/// The checks of doubles to be int32 values whose users all take the
/// double instead (see `checked_double()`): comparisons, conversions to
/// doubles, boxings and frame states. The values of doubles are numbers,
/// so the checks guard no conversion with effects, and they go before check
/// elimination could rely on what they established.
fn dissolvable_checks<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> ZoneBitSet<'w> {
    let mut checks = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut blocked = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            let data = graph.node(node);
            if checked_double(graph, node).is_some() {
                checks.insert(node.index());
            }
            let takes_double = match data.op {
                Op::Int32Compare { comparison } => !matches!(
                    comparison,
                    Comparison::Below | Comparison::BelowOrEqual | Comparison::Above | Comparison::AboveOrEqual
                ),
                Op::Int32ToFloat64 | Op::BoxInt32 => true,
                _ => false,
            };
            if !takes_double {
                for input in &data.inputs {
                    blocked.insert(input.index());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    checks.subtract(&blocked);
    checks
}

fn fold_int32_compare(comparison: Comparison, lhs: i32, rhs: i32) -> bool {
    match comparison {
        Comparison::LessThan => lhs < rhs,
        Comparison::LessThanEquals => lhs <= rhs,
        Comparison::GreaterThan => lhs > rhs,
        Comparison::GreaterThanEquals => lhs >= rhs,
        Comparison::StrictlyEquals | Comparison::LooselyEquals => lhs == rhs,
        Comparison::StrictlyInequals | Comparison::LooselyInequals => lhs != rhs,
        Comparison::Below => lhs.cast_unsigned() < rhs.cast_unsigned(),
        Comparison::BelowOrEqual => lhs.cast_unsigned() <= rhs.cast_unsigned(),
        Comparison::Above => lhs.cast_unsigned() > rhs.cast_unsigned(),
        Comparison::AboveOrEqual => lhs.cast_unsigned() >= rhs.cast_unsigned(),
    }
}

/// Whether `condition` holds of the tagged constants `input` (and `other`,
/// for comparisons), if they are constants.
fn constant_condition(graph: &Graph, condition: BranchCondition, input: NodeId, other: Option<NodeId>) -> Option<bool> {
    if graph.node(input).repr != Some(Repr::Tagged) {
        return None;
    }
    if condition == BranchCondition::Int32Value && graph.node(input).op == Op::BoxInt32 {
        return Some(true);
    }
    if condition == BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean && matches!(graph.node(input).op, Op::BoxInt32 | Op::BoxBool) {
        return Some(true);
    }
    let bits = graph.constant_value(input)?;
    let tag = value::tag(bits);
    match condition {
        BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal } => {
            let other = other?;
            if graph.node(other).repr != Some(Repr::Tagged) {
                return None;
            }
            Some((bits == graph.constant_value(other)?) == equal)
        }
        BranchCondition::Nullish => Some(bits == value::UNDEFINED || bits == value::NULL),
        BranchCondition::Undefined => Some(bits == value::UNDEFINED),
        BranchCondition::Object => Some(tag == value::OBJECT_TAG),
        BranchCondition::NonNegativeInt32 => Some(value::as_int32(bits).is_some_and(|integer| integer >= 0)),
        BranchCondition::Int32Value => Some(tag == value::INT32_TAG),
        BranchCondition::Int32OrBoolean => Some(tag == value::INT32_TAG || tag == value::BOOLEAN_TAG),
        BranchCondition::Double => Some(value::is_double(bits)),
        BranchCondition::String => Some(tag == value::STRING_TAG),
        // NB: Constant strings are made as such, but strings may become
        //     resolved when the code runs.
        BranchCondition::Bool
        | BranchCondition::Int32(_)
        | BranchCondition::Float64(_)
        | BranchCondition::ResolvedString
        | BranchCondition::Builtin(_)
        | BranchCondition::PropertyIteratorCacheValid
        | BranchCondition::BindingMutable { .. }
        | BranchCondition::NextBindingOfShape { .. }
        | BranchCondition::ElementsKind(_)
        | BranchCondition::IndexInBounds
        | BranchCondition::MagicalLength
        | BranchCondition::Extensible
        | BranchCondition::HoleFillableArray
        | BranchCondition::ArrayIterator
        | BranchCondition::GeneratorObject
        | BranchCondition::PlainArrayPrototypeChain
        | BranchCondition::ArrayWithRealmArrayPrototypeAndNoNamedProperties
        | BranchCondition::HoldsValidWatchpointSet
        | BranchCondition::Shape(_) => None,
    }
}

/// The number a tagged constant is, if it is one.
fn constant_number(graph: &Graph, node: NodeId) -> Option<f64> {
    if graph.node(node).repr != Some(Repr::Tagged) {
        return None;
    }
    let bits = graph.constant_value(node)?;
    match value::as_int32(bits) {
        Some(integer) => Some(f64::from(integer)),
        None => value::is_double(bits).then(|| f64::from_bits(bits)),
    }
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    simplify(graph, true, work);
}

/// Simplification after check elimination, which keeps every int32 check of
/// a double: check elimination may have relied on what one established, like
/// the int32 that an unboxing in a branch it decided takes.
pub fn run_after_check_elimination(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    simplify(graph, false, work);
}

fn simplify(graph: &mut Graph, dissolve_checks: bool, work: &Zone) {
    let dissolvable = if dissolve_checks {
        dissolvable_checks(graph, work)
    } else {
        ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, work)
    };
    let dissolved_double = |graph: &Graph, value: NodeId| {
        // NB: Nodes the pass adds are no checks.
        (value.index() < dissolvable.capacity() && dissolvable.contains(value.index()))
            .then(|| checked_double(graph, value))
            .flatten()
    };
    let mut constants = Constants::new(graph, work);
    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    let mut inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut control_inputs = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut changed_control_flow = false;
    for block in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        let block = BlockId::from_index(block);
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < graph.block(block).body.len() {
            let node = graph.block(block).body[index];
            index += 1;
            if !matches!(
                graph.node(node).op,
                Op::CheckNumber
                    | Op::UnboxDouble
                    | Op::UnboxInt32
                    | Op::EmptyToUndefined
                    | Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32
                    | Op::CheckBounds
                    | Op::Int32ToFloat64
                    | Op::Float64ToInt32
                    | Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped
                    | Op::BoxInt32
                    | Op::BoxBool
                    | Op::CheckInt32
                    | Op::Int32Binary { .. }
                    | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { .. }
                    | Op::Int32Min
                    | Op::Int32Max
                    | Op::Uint32Min
                    | Op::Int32Compare { .. }
            ) {
                continue;
            }
            inputs.clear();
            inputs.extend(graph.node(node).inputs.iter().map(|input| replacements.resolve(*input)));
            // NB: A number check of a boxed int32 value converts the value.
            let converted = (graph.node(node).op == Op::CheckNumber)
                .then(|| graph.node(graph.unrefined(inputs[0])))
                .filter(|unrefined| unrefined.op == Op::BoxInt32)
                .map(|unrefined| replacements.resolve(unrefined.inputs[0]));
            // NB: ToInt32 of double arithmetic of int32 values is wrapping
            //     int32 arithmetic.
            let wrapping = (graph.node(node).op == Op::Float64ToInt32)
                .then(|| int32_term(graph, inputs[0], 0, work))
                .flatten()
                .filter(|term| matches!(term, Int32Term::Binary(..)));
            // NB: An int32 comparison of a double checked to be an int32
            //     compares the doubles, which needs no check.
            let double_compare = match graph.node(node).op {
                Op::Int32Compare { comparison }
                    if !matches!(
                        comparison,
                        Comparison::Below | Comparison::BelowOrEqual | Comparison::Above | Comparison::AboveOrEqual
                    ) =>
                {
                    let doubles = [dissolved_double(graph, inputs[0]), dissolved_double(graph, inputs[1])];
                    doubles.iter().any(Option::is_some).then_some((comparison, doubles))
                }
                _ => None,
            };
            let constant_bits = |graph: &Graph, input: usize| graph.constant_value(inputs[input]);
            let boxed = |op: Op, input: NodeId| {
                let unrefined = graph.node(graph.unrefined(input));
                (unrefined.op == op).then(|| unrefined.inputs[0])
            };
            let folded = match graph.node(node).op {
                // NB: Numeric constants are numbers.
                Op::CheckNumber if let Some(number) = constant_number(graph, inputs[0]) => {
                    Some(constants.get_typed(graph, number.to_bits(), Repr::Float64))
                }
                // NB: Unboxing a boxed value is the value (where a branch
                //     established the box holds the kind it unboxes).
                Op::UnboxDouble | Op::CheckNumber => boxed(Op::BoxFloat64, inputs[0]),
                Op::UnboxInt32 => boxed(Op::BoxInt32, inputs[0]),
                // NB: Inlined callees return values that representation
                //     selection may have found to be boxes, never empty.
                Op::EmptyToUndefined => graph.is_known_non_empty(inputs[0], 0..0, work).then_some(inputs[0]),
                Op::CheckNonNegativeInt32 => int32_of(graph, inputs[0])
                    .filter(|value| *value >= 0)
                    .map(|_| inputs[0]),
                Op::CheckBounds => match (int32_of(graph, inputs[0]), int32_of(graph, inputs[1])) {
                    (Some(index), Some(count)) if (index as u32) < count as u32 => Some(inputs[0]),
                    _ => None,
                },
                // NB: The double of a double checked to be an int32 is the
                //     double, which needs no check. A CheckFloat64Int32 stays
                //     where it is, since it may exit.
                Op::Int32ToFloat64 => match graph.node(inputs[0]).op {
                    Op::UnboxInt32 => boxed(Op::BoxFloat64, graph.node(inputs[0]).inputs[0]),
                    Op::CheckFloat64Int32 => Some(graph.node(inputs[0]).inputs[0]),
                    _ => dissolved_double(graph, inputs[0]),
                },
                Op::Float64ToInt32 if let Some(number) = float64_of(graph, inputs[0]) => {
                    Some(constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(to_int32(number).cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32))
                }
                Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped => float64_of(graph, inputs[0]).map(|number| {
                    constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(to_uint8_clamp(number).cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32)
                }),
                // NB: Both signed and unsigned int32 values are exactly
                //     representable as doubles. ToInt32 recovers their bits.
                Op::Float64ToInt32 => match graph.node(inputs[0]).op {
                    Op::Int32ToFloat64 | Op::Uint32ToFloat64 => {
                        Some(graph.node(inputs[0]).inputs[0]).filter(|integer| may_stand_for_result(graph, *integer))
                    }
                    _ => None,
                },
                // NB: A boxed double checked to be an int32 is the boxing of the
                //     int32, which needs no check.
                Op::BoxInt32 => int32_of(graph, inputs[0])
                    .map(|integer| constants.get(graph, value::int32(integer)))
                    .or_else(|| dissolved_double(graph, inputs[0]).map(|_| graph.node(inputs[0]).inputs[0])),
                Op::BoxBool => constant_bits(graph, 0).map(|bits| {
                    let boolean = if bits != 0 { value::TRUE } else { value::FALSE };
                    constants.get(graph, boolean)
                }),
                // NB: Boxing the double of an int32 boxes the int32.
                Op::CheckInt32
                    if let Some(double) = boxed(Op::BoxFloat64, inputs[0])
                        && graph.node(double).op == Op::Int32ToFloat64 =>
                {
                    Some(graph.node(double).inputs[0])
                }
                Op::CheckInt32 if let Some(integer) = boxed(Op::BoxInt32, inputs[0]) => Some(integer),
                Op::CheckInt32 => constant_bits(graph, 0)
                    .filter(|bits| graph.node(inputs[0]).repr == Some(Repr::Tagged) && value::as_int32(*bits).is_some())
                    .map(|bits| constants.get_typed(graph, bits & u64::from(u32::MAX), Repr::Int32)),
                Op::Int32Binary { op } => match (int32_of(graph, inputs[0]), int32_of(graph, inputs[1])) {
                    (Some(lhs), Some(rhs)) => fold_int32_binary(op, lhs, rhs)
                        .map(|result| constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(result.cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32)),
                    (None, Some(rhs))
                        if is_int32_identity(op, rhs, false) && may_stand_for_result(graph, inputs[0]) =>
                    {
                        Some(inputs[0])
                    }
                    _ => None,
                },
                Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op } => match (int32_of(graph, inputs[0]), int32_of(graph, inputs[1])) {
                    (Some(lhs), Some(rhs)) => {
                        let result = fold_int32_wrapping_binary(op, lhs, rhs);
                        Some(constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(result.cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32))
                    }
                    (None, Some(rhs)) if is_int32_identity(op, rhs, true) && may_stand_for_result(graph, inputs[0]) => {
                        Some(inputs[0])
                    }
                    _ => None,
                },
                Op::Int32Min | Op::Int32Max | Op::Uint32Min if inputs[0] == inputs[1] => Some(inputs[0]),
                Op::Int32Min | Op::Int32Max | Op::Uint32Min => {
                    match (int32_of(graph, inputs[0]), int32_of(graph, inputs[1])) {
                        (Some(lhs), Some(rhs)) => {
                            let result = match graph.node(node).op {
                                Op::Int32Min => lhs.min(rhs),
                                Op::Int32Max => lhs.max(rhs),
                                _ => lhs.cast_unsigned().min(rhs.cast_unsigned()).cast_signed(),
                            };
                            Some(constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(result.cast_unsigned()), Repr::Int32))
                        }
                        _ => None,
                    }
                }
                Op::Int32Compare { comparison } => match (int32_of(graph, inputs[0]), int32_of(graph, inputs[1])) {
                    (Some(lhs), Some(rhs)) => Some(constants.get_typed(
                        graph,
                        u64::from(fold_int32_compare(comparison, lhs, rhs)),
                        Repr::Bool,
                    )),
                    _ => None,
                },
                _ => None,
            };
            let folded = folded.or_else(|| {
                let (comparison, doubles) = double_compare?;
                let pc = graph.node(node).pc;
                let mut operands = [inputs[0], inputs[1]];
                for (operand, double) in operands.iter_mut().zip(doubles) {
                    let input = *operand;
                    *operand = double.unwrap_or_else(|| {
                        let conversion = graph.add(Op::Int32ToFloat64, &[input], Some(Repr::Float64), pc);
                        graph.blocks[block.index()].body.insert(index - 1, conversion);
                        index += 1;
                        conversion
                    });
                }
                let compare = graph.add(Op::Float64Compare { comparison }, &operands, Some(Repr::Bool), pc);
                graph.blocks[block.index()].body.insert(index - 1, compare);
                index += 1;
                Some(compare)
            });
            let folded = folded.or_else(|| {
                let term = wrapping?;
                let pc = graph.node(node).pc;
                let (result, position) = build_int32_term(graph, &mut constants, &term, block, index - 1, pc);
                index = position + 1;
                Some(result)
            });
            let folded = folded.or_else(|| {
                let integer = converted?;
                if let Some(double) = dissolved_double(graph, integer) {
                    return Some(double);
                }
                let pc = graph.node(node).pc;
                let conversion = graph.add(Op::Int32ToFloat64, &[integer], Some(Repr::Float64), pc);
                graph.blocks[block.index()].body.insert(index - 1, conversion);
                index += 1;
                Some(conversion)
            });
            if let Some(constant) = folded {
                replacements.replace(node, constant);
                removed.insert(node.index());
                continue;
            }
            // NB: Once no check of a double goes anymore, an int32 check of a
            //     boxed double checks the double itself, so that only users
            //     that need the boxing keep it.
            if !dissolve_checks
                && graph.node(node).op == Op::CheckInt32
                && let boxing = graph.node(graph.unrefined(inputs[0]))
                && boxing.op == Op::BoxFloat64
            {
                let double = boxing.inputs[0];
                let data = &mut graph.nodes[node.index()];
                data.op = Op::CheckFloat64Int32;
                data.inputs.assign(&[double]);
                continue;
            }
            // NB: Int32 operations take constant right-hand sides as
            //     immediates, so commutative ones get their constants there.
            if let Op::Int32Binary { op } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op } = graph.node(node).op
                && op.is_commutative_on_int32()
                && int32_of(graph, inputs[0]).is_some()
                && int32_of(graph, inputs[1]).is_none()
            {
                graph.nodes[node.index()].inputs.assign(&[inputs[1], inputs[0]]);
            }
        }

        // Branches.
        let control = graph.control_id(block);
        let input = graph
            .node(control)
            .inputs
            .first()
            .map(|input| replacements.resolve(*input));
        control_inputs.clear();
        let new_op = match (graph.node(control).op.clone(), input) {
            (
                Op::BranchTruthy { if_true, if_false, .. }
                | Op::Branch {
                    condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                    if_true,
                    if_false,
                },
                Some(input),
            ) if graph.constant_value(input).is_some() => {
                let repr = graph.node(input).repr.unwrap_or(Repr::Tagged);
                constant_truthiness(graph.constant_value(input).expect("a constant"), repr).map(|truthy| Op::Jump {
                    target: if truthy { if_true } else { if_false },
                })
            }
            (
                Op::Branch {
                    condition,
                    if_true,
                    if_false,
                },
                Some(input),
            ) => constant_condition(
                graph,
                condition,
                input,
                graph
                    .node(control)
                    .inputs
                    .get(1)
                    .map(|input| replacements.resolve(*input)),
            )
            .map(|holds| Op::Jump {
                target: if holds { if_true } else { if_false },
            }),
            (Op::BranchTruthy { if_true, if_false, .. }, Some(input)) if graph.node(input).op == Op::BoxBool => {
                control_inputs.push(graph.node(input).inputs[0]);
                Some(Op::Branch {
                    condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                    if_true,
                    if_false,
                })
            }
            (Op::BranchTruthy { if_true, if_false, .. }, Some(input)) if graph.node(input).op == Op::BoxInt32 => {
                control_inputs.push(graph.node(input).inputs[0]);
                control_inputs.push(constants.get_typed(graph, 0, Repr::Int32));
                Some(Op::Branch {
                    condition: BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::StrictlyInequals),
                    if_true,
                    if_false,
                })
            }
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(op) = new_op {
            let data = &mut graph.nodes[control.index()];
            data.op = op;
            data.inputs.assign(&control_inputs);
            changed_control_flow = true;
        }
    }
    replacements.apply(graph);
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
    // NB: Folds can give a check users that need the int32, like the
    //     unboxing of a boxing of it, and the loop never visits the nodes
    //     that folds add before the node they replace. A check that any node
    //     still uses stays, and frame states take the doubles of the others.
    if dissolvable.is_empty() {
        if changed_control_flow {
            edit::clean_up_control_flow(graph, work);
        }
        return;
    }
    let mut dissolvable = dissolvable;
    dissolvable.subtract(&removed);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            for input in &graph.node(node).inputs {
                if input.index() < dissolvable.capacity() {
                    dissolvable.remove(input.index());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let mut replacements = Replacements::new(graph, work);
    let mut removed = ZoneBitSet::new_in(graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for check in dissolvable.iter() {
        let check = NodeId::from_index(check);
        let double = checked_double(graph, check).expect("dissolvable checks check doubles");
        replacements.replace(check, double);
        removed.insert(check.index());
    }
    replacements.apply(graph);
    edit::remove_nodes(graph, &removed);
    if changed_control_flow {
        edit::clean_up_control_flow(graph, work);
    }
}

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use super::verify::verify_with;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::Block;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::BranchCondition;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Node;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;

/// The violated invariants of `graph`, one on each line (see `verify_with()`).
fn verify(graph: &Graph) -> Result<(), String> {
    verify_with(graph, &crate::test_work()).map_err(|errors| errors.to_string())
}

fn node<'z>(graph: &mut Graph<'z>, op: Op<'z>, inputs: Vec<NodeId>, repr: Option<Repr>) -> NodeId {
    graph.add_node(Node {
        op,
        inputs: graph.list(&inputs),
        repr,
        frame_state: None,
        pc: 0,
    })
}

/// A diamond: b0 branches to b1 and b2, which join in b3 with a phi of the
/// values they load.
fn diamond() -> (Graph<'static>, NodeId) {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0)], vec![BlockId(0)], vec![BlockId(1), BlockId(2)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let condition = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let branch = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Undefined,
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![condition],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[0].body.push(condition);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(branch);
    let mut loads = Vec::new();
    for block in 1..3 {
        let load = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: block }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let jump = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(3) }, vec![], None);
        graph.blocks[block as usize].body.push(load);
        graph.blocks[block as usize].control = Some(jump);
        loads.push(load);
    }
    let phi = node(&mut graph, Op::Phi, loads, Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![phi], None);
    graph.blocks[3].phis.push(phi);
    graph.blocks[3].control = Some(ret);
    (graph, condition)
}

#[test]
fn dominators_of_a_diamond() {
    let (graph, _) = diamond();
    let dominators = Dominators::of(&graph, crate::test_zone());
    assert_eq!(dominators.idom(BlockId(0)), None);
    assert_eq!(dominators.idom(BlockId(1)), Some(BlockId(0)));
    assert_eq!(dominators.idom(BlockId(3)), Some(BlockId(0)));
    assert!(dominators.dominates(BlockId(0), BlockId(3)));
    assert!(!dominators.dominates(BlockId(1), BlockId(3)));
    assert!(dominators.dominates(BlockId(3), BlockId(3)));
}

#[test]
fn verifier_accepts_a_valid_graph() {
    let (graph, _) = diamond();
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_uses_of_values_from_blocks_that_do_not_dominate() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    // The return uses b1's load, which b2 does not see.
    let load = graph.blocks[1].body[0];
    let ret = graph.blocks[3].control.unwrap();
    graph.nodes[ret.index()].inputs.assign(&[load]);
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("not defined before it"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_refinements_away_from_the_edge_they_refine() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    // The join has two predecessors, so no one edge refines anything there.
    let load = graph.blocks[0].body[0];
    let repr = graph.nodes[load.index()].repr;
    let refinement = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Refine {
            condition: BranchCondition::Object,
            holds: true,
        },
        vec![load],
        repr,
    );
    graph.blocks[3].body.insert(0, refinement);
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("is not at the head of"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_inconsistent_edges_and_phis() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    graph.blocks[3].predecessors.pop();
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("phi"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_edges_missing_from_predecessor_lists() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    let jump = graph.blocks[2].control.unwrap();
    graph.nodes[jump.index()].op = Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) };
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("edges to b1"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_inputs_of_the_wrong_representation() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    let branch = graph.blocks[0].control.unwrap();
    if let Op::Branch { condition, .. } = &mut graph.nodes[branch.index()].op {
        *condition = BranchCondition::Bool;
    }
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("takes"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_blocks_no_entry_reaches() {
    let (mut graph, _) = diamond();
    // b4 is a loop of its own that nothing enters.
    let block = graph.add_block(Block {
        predecessors: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[BlockId(4)], crate::test_zone()),
        is_loop_header: true,
        ..Block::default()
    });
    let jump = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: block }, vec![], None);
    graph.blocks[block.index()].control = Some(jump);
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("b4 is reachable from no entry"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn verifier_rejects_slow_path_outputs_away_from_their_call() {
    let (mut graph, condition) = diamond();
    let call = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::CallSlowPath {
            opcode: crate::bytecode::OpCode::GetIterator,
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            saves_registers: false,
        },
        vec![condition],
        Some(Repr::Tagged),
    );
    let frame_state = graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    });
    graph.nodes[call.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    let output = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::SlowPathOutput { index: 1 },
        vec![call],
        Some(Repr::Tagged),
    );
    graph.blocks[0].body.extend([call, output]);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    // Anything between the call and the output may reuse the record.
    let load = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 5 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    graph.blocks[0].body.insert(2, load);
    let errors = verify(&graph).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("does not follow its slow path call"), "{errors}");
}

#[test]
fn simplification_removes_number_checks_of_numeric_constants() {
    use crate::ir::value;
    for (bits, expected) in [
        (0.5_f64.to_bits(), Some(0.5_f64)),
        (value::int32(-3), Some(-3.0)),
        (value::UNDEFINED, None),
    ] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let constant = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(bits), vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let check = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckNumber, vec![constant], Some(Repr::Float64));
        graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        }));
        let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxFloat64, vec![check], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
        graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[check, boxed]);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();

        super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(!graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&check), expected.is_some());
        let input = graph.node(boxed).inputs[0];
        assert_eq!(
            graph.constant_value(input).map(f64::from_bits),
            expected,
            "{}",
            value::describe(bits)
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn simplification_removes_int32_checks_that_number_checks_convert() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0)], vec![BlockId(0)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let frame_state = graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    });
    let double = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(2.0_f64.to_bits()), vec![], Some(Repr::Float64));
    let boxed_double = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxFloat64, vec![double], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let check = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckInt32, vec![boxed_double], Some(Repr::Int32));
    graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![check], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let branch = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Int32Value,
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![boxed],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[boxed_double, check, boxed]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(branch);
    // The number check sees the boxing through a refinement, which
    // simplification does not replace.
    let refined = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Refine {
            condition: BranchCondition::Int32Value,
            holds: true,
        },
        vec![boxed],
        Some(Repr::Tagged),
    );
    let number = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckNumber, vec![refined], Some(Repr::Float64));
    graph.nodes[number.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    let result = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxFloat64, vec![number], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![result], None);
    graph.blocks[1].body.assign(&[refined, number, result]);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(ret);
    let other_ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
    graph.blocks[2].control = Some(other_ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    assert!(!graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&check));
    assert_eq!(graph.node(result).inputs, vec![double]);
}

/// A loop that stores elements in their bounds, and loads how many elements
/// an object it does not change has: the stores change no element count, so
/// the load moves out of the loop.
#[test]
fn element_counts_move_out_of_loops_that_only_store_elements() {
    use crate::ir::Comparison;
    use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(1)], vec![BlockId(1)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let object = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let address = node(&mut graph, Op::CellAddress, vec![object], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let zero = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(0), vec![], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let enter = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) }, vec![], None);
    graph.blocks[0].body.extend([object, address]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(enter);
    let length = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadElementsLength, vec![address], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let store = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::StoreElementAt {
            kind: ElementsKind::Packed,
        },
        vec![address, zero, object],
        None,
    );
    let more = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::LessThan),
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![zero, length],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[1].is_loop_header = true;
    graph.blocks[1].body.extend([length, store]);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(more);
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![object], None);
    graph.blocks[2].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::licm::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&length), "{:?}", graph.blocks);
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[1].body, vec![store]);
}

/// A loop that calls, and loads a slot that nothing writes and one that something may: only the first load moves out
/// of the loop, since code the call runs may write any frame memory but that of slots nothing writes.
#[test]
fn loads_of_slots_that_nothing_writes_move_out_of_loops_that_call() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(1)], vec![BlockId(1)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    graph.unwritten_slots = ak::ZoneBitSet::new_in(8, graph.zone);
    graph.unwritten_slots.insert(7);
    let enter = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) }, vec![], None);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(enter);
    let unwritten = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 7 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let written = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 6 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let call = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Generic {
            opcode: crate::bytecode::OpCode::Call,
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
        },
        vec![],
        None,
    );
    graph.nodes[call.index()].frame_state = Some(graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    }));
    let more = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Nullish,
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![written],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[1].is_loop_header = true;
    graph.blocks[1].body.extend([unwritten, written, call]);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(more);
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![unwritten], None);
    graph.blocks[2].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::licm::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[0].body, vec![unwritten], "{:?}", graph.blocks);
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[1].body, vec![written, call]);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn typed_array_storage_offsets_are_reused_across_stores_but_not_calls() {
    use crate::ir::{ElementsKind, TypedArrayElement};
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    graph.add_block(Block::default());
    let object = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let address = node(&mut graph, Op::CellAddress, vec![object], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let first = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset,
        vec![address],
        Some(Repr::Pointer),
    );
    let first_data = node(&mut graph, Op::TypedArrayDataAddress, vec![first], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let zero = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(0), vec![], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let store = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::StoreElementAt {
            kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(TypedArrayElement::Int32),
        },
        vec![first_data, zero, zero],
        None,
    );
    let second = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset,
        vec![address],
        Some(Repr::Pointer),
    );
    let second_data = node(&mut graph, Op::TypedArrayDataAddress, vec![second], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let load = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::LoadElementAt {
            kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(TypedArrayElement::Int32),
        },
        vec![second_data, zero],
        Some(Repr::Int32),
    );
    let call = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Generic {
            opcode: crate::bytecode::OpCode::Call,
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
        },
        vec![],
        None,
    );
    let third = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset,
        vec![address],
        Some(Repr::Pointer),
    );
    graph.nodes[call.index()].frame_state = Some(graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    }));
    graph.blocks[0].body.extend([
        object,
        address,
        first,
        first_data,
        store,
        second,
        second_data,
        load,
        call,
        third,
    ]);
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![object], None);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    super::check_elimination::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone(), &mut crate::test_steps());
    assert!(!graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&second));
    assert_eq!(graph.node(second_data).inputs[0], first);
    assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&third));
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn typed_array_storage_metadata_moves_out_of_loops_that_only_store_elements() {
    use crate::ir::{Comparison, ElementsKind, TypedArrayElement};
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(1)], vec![BlockId(1)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let object = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let address = node(&mut graph, Op::CellAddress, vec![object], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let zero = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(0), vec![], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let enter = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) }, vec![], None);
    graph.blocks[0].body.extend([object, address]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(enter);
    let length = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadTypedArrayLength, vec![address], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let offset = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset,
        vec![address],
        Some(Repr::Pointer),
    );
    let data = node(&mut graph, Op::TypedArrayDataAddress, vec![offset], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let store = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::StoreElementAt {
            kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(TypedArrayElement::Int32),
        },
        vec![data, zero, zero],
        None,
    );
    let more = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Int32(Comparison::LessThan),
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![zero, length],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[1].is_loop_header = true;
    graph.blocks[1].body.extend([length, offset, data, store]);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(more);
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![object], None);
    graph.blocks[2].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    super::licm::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    for metadata in [length, offset, data] {
        assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&metadata));
    }
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[1].body, vec![store]);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
}

/// A branch on the kind of a value tells its edges which kind the value is,
/// so a later branch on the same value there takes the edge it decides.
#[test]
fn branches_on_known_kinds_fold() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [
        vec![],
        vec![BlockId(0)],
        vec![BlockId(0)],
        vec![BlockId(1)],
        vec![BlockId(1)],
    ] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let value = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let branch = |graph: &mut Graph, if_true: u32, if_false: u32| {
        node(
            graph,
            Op::Branch {
                condition: BranchCondition::String,
                if_true: BlockId(if_true),
                if_false: BlockId(if_false),
            },
            vec![value],
            None,
        )
    };
    let first = branch(&mut graph, 1, 2);
    graph.blocks[0].body.push(value);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(first);
    let second = branch(&mut graph, 3, 4);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(second);
    for block in [2, 3, 4] {
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![value], None);
        graph.blocks[block].control = Some(ret);
    }
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::check_elimination::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone(), &mut crate::test_steps());
    let branches = graph
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|block| block.control)
        .filter(|control| matches!(graph.node(*control).op, Op::Branch { .. }))
        .count();
    assert_eq!(branches, 1, "{:?}", graph.blocks);
}

/// The zones of check elimination hold about as much as the facts in use, not every copy of a list that the visits
/// of blocks made.
#[test]
fn check_elimination_keeps_the_facts_in_use() {
    // NB: Each block of the chain knows the kind of one more value, so the lists of its facts copy all those before.
    let bytes = |count: u32| {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        for index in 0..count {
            let predecessors = if index == 0 {
                vec![]
            } else {
                vec![BlockId(2 * index - 2)]
            };
            graph.add_block(Block {
                predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
                ..Block::default()
            });
            graph.add_block(Block {
                predecessors: graph.list(&[BlockId(2 * index)]),
                ..Block::default()
            });
        }
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&[BlockId(2 * count - 2)]),
            ..Block::default()
        });
        let mut value = NodeId(0);
        for index in 0..count {
            value = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: index }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
            let branch = node(
                &mut graph,
                Op::Branch {
                    condition: BranchCondition::String,
                    if_true: BlockId(2 * index + 2),
                    if_false: BlockId(2 * index + 1),
                },
                vec![value],
                None,
            );
            graph.blocks[2 * index as usize].body.push(value);
            graph.blocks[2 * index as usize].control = Some(branch);
            let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![value], None);
            graph.blocks[2 * index as usize + 1].control = Some(ret);
        }
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![value], None);
        graph.blocks[2 * count as usize].control = Some(ret);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        let work = crate::test_work();
        let mut steps = crate::test_steps();
        super::check_elimination::run(&mut graph, &work, &mut steps);
        work.used() + steps[0].used() + steps[1].used()
    };
    let (small, large) = (bytes(1000), bytes(4000));
    assert!(
        large < 8 * small,
        "{small} bytes for 1000 blocks, {large} bytes for 4000 blocks"
    );
}

/// A value that passed an int32 check is no empty value, so a branch on
/// whether it is one (like the initialization check of a binding store)
/// takes the edge where it is not.
#[test]
fn branches_on_whether_values_of_known_kinds_are_empty_fold() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0)], vec![BlockId(0)]] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let frame_state = graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    });
    let value = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let check = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckInt32, vec![value], Some(Repr::Int32));
    graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    let empty = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Constant(crate::ir::value::EMPTY),
        vec![],
        Some(Repr::Tagged),
    );
    let branch = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::TaggedEquals { equal: false },
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        },
        vec![value, empty],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[value, check]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(branch);
    for block in [1, 2] {
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![value], None);
        graph.blocks[block].control = Some(ret);
    }
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::check_elimination::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone(), &mut crate::test_steps());
    let control = graph.blocks[0].control.unwrap();
    assert!(
        matches!(graph.node(control).op, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) }),
        "{:?}",
        graph.node(control)
    );
}

/// b4 is reached from the entry b0, which checks a constant, and from b2,
/// which only the on-stack replacement entry b1 reaches through b3 (a block
/// later in the order than b2). b2 is skipped until b3 has been visited, so
/// what b4 knows must not stay what b0 checked.
#[test]
fn check_elimination_keeps_checks_that_a_later_entry_reaches_blocks_before_it() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    for predecessors in [
        vec![],
        vec![],
        vec![BlockId(3)],
        vec![BlockId(1)],
        vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(2)],
    ] {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    graph.blocks[2].is_loop_header = true;
    graph.osr_entries.push((0, BlockId(1)));
    let constant = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(0x1234), vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let frame_state = graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
        executable: 0,
        pc: 0,
        mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
        values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
        parent: None,
        passed_argument_count: None,
        legacy_arguments: 0..0,
    });
    let first = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckObject, vec![constant], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    graph.nodes[first.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    graph.blocks[0].body.push(first);
    for (block, target) in [(0, 4), (1, 3), (2, 4), (3, 2)] {
        let jump = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Jump {
                target: BlockId(target),
            },
            vec![],
            None,
        );
        graph.blocks[block].control = Some(jump);
    }
    let second = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckObject, vec![constant], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    graph.nodes[second.index()].frame_state = Some(frame_state);
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![second], None);
    graph.blocks[4].body.push(second);
    graph.blocks[4].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::check_elimination::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone(), &mut crate::test_steps());
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[4].body, vec![second]);
}

#[test]
fn simplification_removes_integer_double_round_trips() {
    for conversion in [Op::Int32ToFloat64, Op::Uint32ToFloat64] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let bits = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(0xffff_ffff), vec![], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let double = node(&mut graph, conversion, vec![bits], Some(Repr::Float64));
        let integer = node(&mut graph, Op::Float64ToInt32, vec![double], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![integer], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
        graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[double, integer, boxed]);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();

        super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        assert!(!graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&integer));
        assert_eq!(
            graph.constant_value(graph.node(ret).inputs[0]),
            Some(crate::ir::value::int32(-1))
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn simplification_tests_the_truthiness_of_boxed_int32_values_unboxed() {
    // b0 branches on the truthiness of a boxed int32 to b1 and b2, with b3
    // as the fallback for other values.
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    graph.add_block(Block::default());
    for _ in 1..4 {
        graph.add_block(Block {
            predecessors: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[BlockId(0)], crate::test_zone()),
            ..Block::default()
        });
    }
    let array = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let address = node(&mut graph, Op::CellAddress, vec![array], Some(Repr::Pointer));
    let unboxed = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadElementsLength, vec![address], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![unboxed], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let branch = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::BranchTruthy {
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
            fallback: BlockId(3),
        },
        vec![boxed],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[array, address, unboxed, boxed]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(branch);
    for block in 1..4 {
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![array], None);
        graph.blocks[block].control = Some(ret);
    }
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    let branch = graph.blocks[0].control.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        graph.node(branch).op,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Int32(crate::ir::Comparison::StrictlyInequals),
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(2),
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(graph.node(branch).inputs[0], unboxed);
    assert_eq!(graph.constant_value(graph.node(branch).inputs[1]), Some(0));
}

#[test]
fn simplification_keeps_double_integer_round_trips() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    graph.add_block(Block::default());
    let load = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 5 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let double = node(&mut graph, Op::UnboxDouble, vec![load], Some(Repr::Float64));
    let integer = node(&mut graph, Op::Float64ToInt32, vec![double], Some(Repr::Int32));
    let converted = node(&mut graph, Op::Int32ToFloat64, vec![integer], Some(Repr::Float64));
    let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxFloat64, vec![converted], Some(Repr::Tagged));
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
    graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[load, double, integer, converted, boxed]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
    verify(&graph).unwrap();

    super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    verify(&graph).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(graph.node(converted).inputs, vec![integer]);
    assert!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&integer));
}

#[test]
fn simplification_converts_constant_doubles_to_integers() {
    for (op, number, expected) in [
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, 1.5, 1),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, -1.5, -1),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, -0.0, 0),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, f64::NAN, 0),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, f64::INFINITY, 0),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, 4_294_967_301.0, 5),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, 2_147_483_648.0, i32::MIN),
        (Op::Float64ToInt32, -2_147_483_649.0, i32::MAX),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, 2.5, 2),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, 3.5, 4),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, 254.9, 255),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, 300.0, 255),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, -1.0, 0),
        (Op::Float64ToUint8Clamped, f64::NAN, 0),
    ] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let double = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(number.to_bits()), vec![], Some(Repr::Float64));
        let integer = node(&mut graph, op.clone(), vec![double], Some(Repr::Int32));
        let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![integer], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
        graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[integer, boxed]);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();

        super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            graph.constant_value(graph.node(ret).inputs[0]),
            Some(crate::ir::value::int32(expected)),
            "{op:?} of {number}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn constant_bounds_checks_only_fold_when_the_unsigned_index_is_in_bounds() {
    for (index, count, folds) in [
        (0, 1, true),
        (7, 8, true),
        (8, 8, false),
        (-1, 8, false),
        (0, 0, false),
        (i32::MAX, i32::MIN, true),
    ] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let index = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Constant(u64::from(index as u32)),
            vec![],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        let count = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Constant(u64::from(count as u32)),
            vec![],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        let check = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckBounds, vec![index, count], Some(Repr::Int32));
        graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(graph.add_frame_state(crate::ir::FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            mode: crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        }));
        let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![check], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
        graph.blocks[0].body.extend([check, boxed]);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        super::simplify::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        assert_eq!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&check), !folds);
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
    }
}

/// A register-saving slow path initializes the frame if it runs, so a frame
/// write after it initializes the frame only if it still is not, instead of
/// emptying the frame the slow path may have initialized and written.
#[test]
fn frame_writes_after_slow_paths_that_may_initialize_the_frame_check_first() {
    use crate::bytecode::FrameLayout;
    use crate::bytecode::RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT;
    let layout = FrameLayout {
        number_of_registers: RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT + 1,
        registers_and_locals_count: RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT + 1,
        number_of_constants: 0,
        number_of_arguments: 0,
    };
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    graph.add_block(Block::default());
    let initialize = node(&mut graph, Op::InitializeFrame, vec![], None);
    let call = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::CallSlowPath {
            opcode: crate::bytecode::OpCode::GetIterator,
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            saves_registers: true,
        },
        vec![],
        Some(Repr::Tagged),
    );
    let store = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::StoreSlot {
            slot: RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT,
        },
        vec![call],
        None,
    );
    let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![call], None);
    graph.blocks[0].body.assign(&[initialize, call, store]);
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(ret);

    super::frame_initialization::run(&mut graph, &layout, crate::test_zone());
    assert_eq!(graph.slow_paths_initializing_frame, vec![call]);
    let ops: Vec<&Op> = graph.blocks[0].body.iter().map(|node| &graph.node(*node).op).collect();
    assert!(matches!(
        ops.as_slice(),
        [
            Op::CallSlowPath { .. },
            Op::EnsureFrameInitialized,
            Op::StoreSlot { .. }
        ]
    ));
}

#[test]
fn hoisted_checks_gate_exits_by_the_loop_headers_executable() {
    use crate::code::{ExitKind, ResumeMode};
    use crate::ir::FrameState;
    for failed_executable in [0, 1] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        for predecessors in [vec![], vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(1)], vec![BlockId(1)]] {
            graph.add_block(Block {
                predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
                ..Block::default()
            });
        }
        let object = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let condition = node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(1), vec![], Some(Repr::Bool));
        let enter = node(&mut graph, Op::Jump { target: BlockId(1) }, vec![], None);
        graph.blocks[0].body.push(object);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(enter);
        let parent = graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 10,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAfter { dst: 5 },
            values: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[(0, object)], crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        });
        let state = graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 1,
            pc: 77,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[(0, object)], crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: Some(parent),
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        });
        let check = node(&mut graph, Op::CheckObject, vec![object], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(state);
        graph.blocks[1].bytecode_start = Some(77);
        graph.blocks[1].start_frame_state = Some(state);
        graph.blocks[1].is_loop_header = true;
        graph.blocks[1].body.push(check);
        let more = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Branch {
                condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                if_true: BlockId(1),
                if_false: BlockId(2),
            },
            vec![condition],
            None,
        );
        graph.blocks[1].control = Some(more);
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![object], None);
        graph.blocks[2].control = Some(ret);
        graph.exit_sites.push((failed_executable, 77, ExitKind::NotObject));
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        super::licm::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(graph.blocks[0].body.contains(&check), failed_executable == 0);
        let recovery = graph.frame_state(graph.node(check).frame_state.unwrap());
        assert_eq!(recovery.executable, 1);
        assert_eq!(recovery.parent, Some(parent));
    }
}

#[test]
fn control_flow_cleanup_preserves_duplicate_edges_and_phi_input_order() {
    let mut graph = Graph::default();
    graph.add_block(Block::default());
    graph.add_block(Block {
        predecessors: ak::ZoneVec::from_elem_in(BlockId(0), 3, crate::test_zone()),
        ..Block::default()
    });
    let values = (0..3)
        .map(|bits| node(&mut graph, Op::Constant(bits), vec![], Some(Repr::Bool)))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let branch = node(
        &mut graph,
        Op::Branch {
            condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
            if_true: BlockId(1),
            if_false: BlockId(1),
        },
        vec![values[0]],
        None,
    );
    graph.blocks[0].control = Some(branch);
    let phi = node(&mut graph, Op::Phi, values.clone(), Some(Repr::Bool));
    graph.blocks[1].phis.push(phi);
    let returned = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![phi], None);
    graph.blocks[1].control = Some(returned);
    super::edit::clean_up_control_flow(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
    assert_eq!(graph.blocks[1].predecessors, [BlockId(0), BlockId(0)]);
    assert_eq!(graph.node(phi).inputs, values[..2]);
}

/// An addition whose operand a bounds check keeps below a count, where the
/// count is a loop counter that an on-stack replacement entry brings, relies
/// on the counter being below the loop's bound where it enters: it stops
/// checking for overflow only together with the check of the counter there.
#[test]
fn overflow_checks_removed_by_bounds_checks_check_the_counters_of_their_counts() {
    use crate::code::ExitKind;
    use crate::code::ResumeMode;
    use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
    use crate::ir::Comparison;
    use crate::ir::FrameState;
    // b0 and the on-stack replacement entry b1 start the counter in b2, the
    // loop's preheader. The loop b3 (with the back edge from b4) adds one to
    // an index that a bounds check against the counter checks (not to the
    // value the check refines), and to the counter until it is 100.
    for failed_before in [false, true] {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        for predecessors in [
            vec![],
            vec![],
            vec![BlockId(0), BlockId(1)],
            vec![BlockId(2), BlockId(4)],
            vec![BlockId(3)],
            vec![BlockId(3)],
        ] {
            graph.add_block(Block {
                predecessors: graph.list(&predecessors),
                ..Block::default()
            });
        }
        graph.blocks[3].is_loop_header = true;
        graph.osr_entries.push((7, BlockId(1)));
        let state = graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 7,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        });
        if failed_before {
            graph.exit_sites.push((0, 7, ExitKind::OutOfBounds));
        }
        let int32 = |graph: &mut Graph, value: i32| {
            node(graph, Op::Constant(u64::from(value as u32)), vec![], Some(Repr::Int32))
        };
        let checked = |graph: &mut Graph<'static>, op: Op<'static>, inputs: Vec<NodeId>| {
            let id = node(graph, op, inputs, Some(Repr::Int32));
            graph.nodes[id.index()].frame_state = Some(state);
            id
        };
        let jump = |graph: &mut Graph, block: usize, target: u32| {
            let jump = node(
                graph,
                Op::Jump {
                    target: BlockId(target),
                },
                vec![],
                None,
            );
            graph.blocks[block].control = Some(jump);
        };

        let zero = int32(&mut graph, 0);
        jump(&mut graph, 0, 2);

        let slot = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let counter = checked(&mut graph, Op::CheckInt32, vec![slot]);
        graph.blocks[1].body.extend([slot, counter]);
        jump(&mut graph, 1, 2);

        let start = node(&mut graph, Op::Phi, vec![zero, counter], Some(Repr::Int32));
        graph.blocks[2].phis.push(start);
        let index_slot = node(&mut graph, Op::LoadSlot { slot: 1 }, vec![], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let index = checked(&mut graph, Op::CheckInt32, vec![index_slot]);
        graph.blocks[2].body.extend([index_slot, index]);
        jump(&mut graph, 2, 3);

        let one = int32(&mut graph, 1);
        let bound = int32(&mut graph, 100);
        let phi = node(&mut graph, Op::Phi, vec![start], Some(Repr::Int32));
        graph.blocks[3].phis.push(phi);
        let check = checked(&mut graph, Op::CheckBounds, vec![index, phi]);
        let sum = checked(&mut graph, Op::Int32Binary { op: BinaryOp::Add }, vec![index, one]);
        let next = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op: BinaryOp::Add },
            vec![phi, one],
            Some(Repr::Int32),
        );
        graph.nodes[phi.index()].inputs.push(next);
        let compare = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Int32Compare {
                comparison: Comparison::LessThan,
            },
            vec![next, bound],
            Some(Repr::Bool),
        );
        let branch = node(
            &mut graph,
            Op::Branch {
                condition: BranchCondition::Bool,
                if_true: BlockId(4),
                if_false: BlockId(5),
            },
            vec![compare],
            None,
        );
        graph.blocks[3].body.extend([check, sum, next, compare]);
        graph.blocks[3].control = Some(branch);
        jump(&mut graph, 4, 3);

        let boxed = node(&mut graph, Op::BoxInt32, vec![sum], Some(Repr::Tagged));
        let ret = node(&mut graph, Op::Return, vec![boxed], None);
        graph.blocks[5].body.push(boxed);
        graph.blocks[5].control = Some(ret);

        verify(&graph).unwrap();
        super::bounds_check_elimination::run(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        verify(&graph).unwrap();

        let guarded = graph.blocks[1].body.iter().any(|node| {
            let node = graph.node(*node);
            node.op == Op::CheckBounds && node.inputs[0] == counter && graph.int32_constant(node.inputs[1]) == Some(100)
        });
        let wrapping = matches!(graph.node(sum).op, Op::Int32WrappingBinary { .. });
        assert_eq!(guarded, !failed_before);
        assert_eq!(wrapping, !failed_before);
    }
}

/*
