//! Truncation: int32 operations whose results only reach users that read
//! their low 32 bits stop checking for overflow.
//!
//! Additions, subtractions and unsigned right shifts of int32 values exit
//! where the result is no int32, so that the interpreter can produce the
//! number. But where every user converts the result with ToInt32 or
//! ToUint32 (`(a + b) | 0`, shifts, other bitwise operations, stores to
//! integer typed arrays), the low 32 bits of the result are all that
//! matters, and the operation wraps instead (`Op::Int32WrappingBinary`).
//!
//! Wrapping additions and subtractions read only the low 32 bits of their
//! operands too: the sum of int32 values that wrapped is congruent modulo
//! 2^32 to the exact sum, which doubles hold exactly as long as it stays
//! below 2^53, so chains like `(a + b + c) | 0` wrap as a whole. So do the
//! wrapping multiplications of `Math.imul`.
//!
//! Frame states need the exact value, so values they hold do not wrap.
//! The pass runs before simplification removes the `x | 0` that ToInt32 of
//! an int32 builds.
//!
//! Comparisons of uint32 values (`(a >>> 0) < (b >>> 0)`, whose results
//! may also be doubles) only read the bits of the shifted values as well:
//! they first become unsigned comparisons of those bits, which leaves the
//! shifts unused.

use super::edit::Constants;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::ir::BinaryOp;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::ir::TypedArrayElement;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneBitSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// The operations that wrap where their users only read the low 32 bits.
fn can_wrap(op: &Op) -> bool {
    matches!(
        op,
        Op::Int32Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift
        }
    )
}

/// Whether input `index` of `user` only reads its low 32 bits, given the
/// nodes that are to wrap.
fn reads_low_bits(graph: &Graph, user: NodeId, index: usize, wrapping: &ZoneBitSet) -> bool {
    match graph.node(user).op {
        Op::Int32Binary { op } | Op::Int32WrappingBinary { op } if op.is_bitwise() => true,
        Op::Int32Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub,
        } => wrapping.contains(user.index()),
        // NB: The low 32 bits of a product only depend on the low 32 bits of
        //     its factors.
        Op::Int32WrappingBinary {
            op: BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::Mul,
        } => true,
        // NB: Clamped elements clamp the value instead.
        Op::StoreElementAt {
            kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(element),
        } => {
            index == 2
                && !matches!(
                    element,
                    TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped | TypedArrayElement::Float32 | TypedArrayElement::Float64
                )
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// An operand of a comparison of uint32 values.
enum Uint32Operand {
    /// The `Repr::Int32` value whose bits are the uint32 value.
    Bits(NodeId),
    Constant(u32),
}

/// What `value`, an operand of an int32 comparison (or a float64 one, if
/// `float64`), is as a uint32 value, if it is one.
fn uint32_operand(graph: &Graph, value: NodeId, float64: bool) -> Option<Uint32Operand> {
    let node = graph.node(graph.unrefined(value));
    let shifted_by_zero = |node: &crate::ir::Node| {
        graph
            .constant_value(node.inputs[1])
            .is_some_and(|amount| amount & 31 == 0)
            .then_some(Uint32Operand::Bits(node.inputs[0]))
    };
    match (&node.op, float64) {
        (Op::Constant(bits), false) => {
            let integer = (*bits as u32).cast_signed();
            (integer >= 0).then_some(Uint32Operand::Constant(integer.cast_unsigned()))
        }
        (Op::Constant(bits), true) => {
            let number = f64::from_bits(*bits);
            (number.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..4294967296.0).contains(&number))
                .then_some(Uint32Operand::Constant(number as u32))
        }
        (
            Op::Int32Binary {
                op: BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift,
            }
            | Op::Int32WrappingBinary {
                op: BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift,
            },
            false,
        ) => shifted_by_zero(node),
        // NB: Simplification has not removed the boxing of operands yet.
        (Op::CheckNumber | Op::UnboxDouble, true) => {
            let boxed = graph.node(graph.unrefined(node.inputs[0]));
            (boxed.op == Op::BoxFloat64)
                .then(|| uint32_operand(graph, boxed.inputs[0], true))
                .flatten()
        }
        (Op::Int32ToFloat64, true) => uint32_operand(graph, node.inputs[0], false),
        (Op::Uint32ToFloat64, true) => {
            let bits = graph.node(node.inputs[0]);
            let shifted = (bits.op == Op::Uint32ShiftRight)
                .then(|| shifted_by_zero(bits))
                .flatten();
            shifted.or(Some(Uint32Operand::Bits(node.inputs[0])))
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Makes comparisons of uint32 values unsigned int32 comparisons of their
/// bits.
fn compare_uint32_bits(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    let mut constants = Constants::new(graph, work);
    for block in 0..graph.blocks.len() {
        for index in 0..graph.blocks[block].body.len() {
            let node = graph.blocks[block].body[index];
            let (comparison, float64) = match graph.node(node).op {
                Op::Int32Compare { comparison } => (comparison, false),
                Op::Float64Compare { comparison } => (comparison, true),
                _ => continue,
            };
            let inputs = &graph.node(node).inputs;
            let (Some(lhs), Some(rhs)) = (
                uint32_operand(graph, inputs[0], float64),
                uint32_operand(graph, inputs[1], float64),
            ) else {
                continue;
            };
            if matches!((&lhs, &rhs), (Uint32Operand::Constant(_), Uint32Operand::Constant(_))) {
                continue;
            }
            let inputs = [lhs, rhs].map(|operand| match operand {
                Uint32Operand::Bits(value) => value,
                Uint32Operand::Constant(integer) => constants.get_typed(graph, u64::from(integer), Repr::Int32),
            });
            let data = &mut graph.nodes[node.index()];
            data.op = Op::Int32Compare {
                comparison: comparison.unsigned(),
            };
            data.inputs.assign(&inputs);
        }
    }
}

pub fn run(graph: &mut Graph, work: &Zone) {
    compare_uint32_bits(graph, work);
    let count = graph.nodes.len();
    let mut wrapping = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    // The users of each node, with the index of the input that it is: those of node `n` are
    // `user_list[user_starts[n]..user_starts[n + 1]]`.
    let mut user_starts = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, count + 1, work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        for node in block.nodes() {
            for input in &graph.node(node).inputs {
                user_starts[input.index() + 1] += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    for index in 1..user_starts.len() {
        user_starts[index] += user_starts[index - 1];
    }
    let mut user_list = ZoneVec::from_elem_in((NodeId(0), 0), user_starts[count], work);
    let mut user_ends = ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&user_starts[..count], work);
    // The node each frame state belongs to alone, if any: those of nodes
    // that wrap go away with their exits.
    let mut owners = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(Owner::None, graph.frame_states.len(), work);
    for block in &graph.blocks {
        if let Some(frame_state) = block.start_frame_state {
            share(&mut owners, frame_state, Owner::Shared);
        }
        for node in block.nodes() {
            let data = graph.node(node);
            if can_wrap(&data.op) {
                wrapping.insert(node.index());
            }
            if let Some(frame_state) = data.frame_state {
                share(&mut owners, frame_state, Owner::Node(node));
            }
            for (index, input) in data.inputs.iter().enumerate() {
                user_list[user_ends[input.index()]] = (node, index);
                user_ends[input.index()] += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    if wrapping.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let users = |node: usize| &user_list[user_starts[node]..user_starts[node + 1]];
    for frame_state in &graph.frame_states {
        if let Some(parent) = frame_state.parent {
            share(&mut owners, parent, Owner::Shared);
        }
    }

    // Start from every candidate wrapping, and drop those with users that
    // need more than the low 32 bits until none is left. Values of frame
    // states that stay need all their bits too.
    let mut in_frame_state = ZoneBitSet::new_in(count, work);
    let mut candidates = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    loop {
        in_frame_state.clear();
        for (frame_state, owner) in graph.frame_states.iter().zip(&owners) {
            if matches!(owner, Owner::Node(node) if wrapping.contains(node.index())) {
                continue;
            }
            for (_, value) in &frame_state.values {
                in_frame_state.insert(value.index());
            }
        }
        // NB: Boxings nothing uses are left for dead code elimination; the
        //     builder boxes every result it writes to a slot.
        let is_unused_boxing = |node: NodeId| {
            graph.node(node).op == Op::BoxInt32
                && users(node.index()).is_empty()
                && !in_frame_state.contains(node.index())
        };
        let mut changed = false;
        candidates.clear();
        candidates.extend(wrapping.iter());
        for node in candidates.iter().copied() {
            let keeps_checking = in_frame_state.contains(node)
                || users(node)
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(user, index)| !is_unused_boxing(*user) && !reads_low_bits(graph, *user, *index, &wrapping));
            if keeps_checking {
                wrapping.remove(node);
                changed = true;
            }
        }
        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }

    for node in wrapping.iter() {
        super::edit::make_wrapping(graph, NodeId::from_index(node));
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Owner {
    None,
    Node(NodeId),
    Shared,
}

fn share(owners: &mut [Owner], frame_state: FrameStateId, owner: Owner) {
    let current = &mut owners[frame_state.index()];
    *current = match *current {
        Owner::None => owner,
        _ => Owner::Shared,
    };
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/JIT/Rust/src/passes/verify.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Checks the structural invariants of a graph that every pass relies on
//! and must preserve:
//!
//! - every block ends in one control node, has only phis among its phis and
//!   no phis or control nodes in its body, and no node is in two places;
//! - predecessor lists match the successors of the predecessors' control
//!   nodes, phis have one input per predecessor, and the predecessors of
//!   blocks with phis lead nowhere else (so moves into the phis have a place
//!   at the end of each predecessor);
//! - blocks come after their predecessors in linear order, except loop
//!   headers reached over back edges and blocks that cold blocks rejoin,
//!   and an entry (block 0 or an on-stack replacement entry, exactly the
//!   blocks without predecessors) reaches every block;
//! - every input and every frame state value is defined before it is used:
//!   earlier in the same block, or in a block dominating the use (for phi
//!   inputs, dominating the end of the predecessor the input flows in from);
//! - nodes have as many inputs as their op takes, with the representations
//!   it expects of them, and jumps have none;
//! - no branch tests shapes (only `ShapeSwitch` does);
//! - every node that can exit, eagerly or lazily, has a frame state, and frame states list
//!   each slot once (with a value or as held by the frame), with values
//!   that have a representation (or virtual objects);
//! - slow path calls have a frame state, and those that save registers
//!   are in cold blocks;
//! - `StoreSlot` writes only written constants, the arguments the compiled
//!   function's legacy `arguments` shows, and slots that the next call
//!   reading the frame (a `Generic` node, or a call that reads its operands
//!   from the frame) or `Suspend` reads (see `verify_frame_writes()`), and
//!   never one of `Graph::unwritten_slots`.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;
use core::fmt;

use super::dominators::Dominators;
use crate::bytecode::FrameLayout;
use crate::bytecode::Operand;
use crate::bytecode::RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT;
use crate::code::Repr;
use crate::debug_text::DebugText;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::ElementsKind;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::Locations;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;

/// The descriptions of the violated invariants, one on each line.
struct Errors<'w>(DebugText<'w>);

impl<'w> Errors<'w> {
    fn new_in(work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self(DebugText::new_in(work))
    }

    /// Adds the description of a violated invariant. This is what `write!` calls.
    fn write_fmt(&mut self, message: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
        if !self.0.is_empty() {
            self.0.push('\n');
        }
        self.0.write_fmt(message);
    }

    fn finish(self) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
        if self.0.is_empty() { Ok(()) } else { Err(self.0) }
    }
}

/// Where a node is: its block and its position there (phis come first, then
/// the body, then the control node).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Place {
    block: BlockId,
    index: usize,
}

/// Checks that `StoreSlot` writes frame memory only where something reads it: written constants, which live there,
/// the arguments the compiled function's legacy `arguments` shows, and the slots a node that reads the frame reads,
/// right before it. Merges and back edges never write frame memory: slots that differ get phis.
pub fn verify_frame_writes<'w>(graph: &Graph, layout: &FrameLayout, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut errors = Errors::new_in(work);
    let mut nodes = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        nodes.assign(&block.body);
        nodes.extend(block.control);
        for (position, node) in nodes.iter().enumerate() {
            let Op::StoreSlot { slot } = graph.node(*node).op else {
                continue;
            };
            let operand = Operand::from_raw(slot).raw();
            if graph.is_unwritten_slot(operand) {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "StoreSlot v{} in b{index} writes slot {operand}, which nothing writes (see `Graph::unwritten_slots`)",
                    node.0
                );
            }
            let is_constant = operand >= layout.registers_and_locals_count && operand < layout.arguments_base();
            if is_constant || graph.legacy_arguments.contains(&operand) {
                continue;
            }
            // NB: Conversions of the reader's inputs may come in between, and
            //     so may the frame's initialization for stores of arguments
            //     and reserved registers, which it leaves as they are (see
            //     `frame_initialization`).
            let survives_initialization = operand >= layout.arguments_base() || operand < RESERVED_REGISTER_COUNT;
            let reader = nodes[position + 1..].iter().find(|next| {
                let op = &graph.node(**next).op;
                let properties = op.properties();
                let initializes_frame =
                    matches!(op, Op::InitializeFrame | Op::EnsureFrameInitialized | Op::PublishFrame);
                !matches!(op, Op::StoreSlot { .. })
                    && !(survives_initialization && initializes_frame)
                    && (properties.reads != Locations::NONE || properties.writes != Locations::NONE)
            });
            let reads_frame = reader.is_some_and(|reader| {
                let op = &graph.node(*reader).op;
                let properties = op.properties();
                (properties.is_call && properties.reads.intersects(Locations::FRAME))
                    || matches!(op, Op::Suspend { .. })
            });
            if !reads_frame {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "StoreSlot v{} in b{index} writes a slot that no node reading the frame reads next",
                    node.0
                );
            }
        }
    }
    errors.finish()
}

/// Returns a description of every violated invariant, one on each line, or `Ok` if there is none. The description and
/// the lists of the checks are in `work`.
pub fn verify_with<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let places = verify_blocks(graph, work)?;
    verify_edges(graph, work)?;
    verify_nodes(graph, &places, work)?;
    verify_frame_states(graph, work)
}

/// Checks what each block holds, and returns where each node is.
fn verify_blocks<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<ZoneVec<'w, Option<Place>>, DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut errors = Errors::new_in(work);
    let mut places: ZoneVec<Option<Place>> = ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, graph.nodes.len(), work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
        let Some(control) = block.control else {
            write!(errors, "b{index} has no control node");
            continue;
        };
        if !graph.node(control).op.is_control() {
            write!(errors, "b{index} ends in v{}, which is not a control node", control.0);
        }
        for phi in &block.phis {
            if graph.node(*phi).op != Op::Phi {
                write!(errors, "b{index} has v{} among its phis", phi.0);
            }
            if graph.node(*phi).inputs.len() != block.predecessors.len() {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "phi v{} of b{index} has {} inputs for {} predecessors",
                    phi.0,
                    graph.node(*phi).inputs.len(),
                    block.predecessors.len()
                );
            }
        }
        for node in &block.body {
            let op = &graph.node(*node).op;
            if *op == Op::Phi || op.is_control() || matches!(op, Op::Constant(_)) {
                write!(errors, "b{index} has {} v{} in its body", op.name(), node.0);
            }
        }
        for (position, node) in graph.block_nodes(block_id).enumerate() {
            match places[node.index()] {
                Some(other) => write!(errors, "v{} is in b{} and in b{index}", node.0, other.block.0),
                None => {
                    places[node.index()] = Some(Place {
                        block: block_id,
                        index: position,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    errors.finish().map(|()| places)
}

/// Checks the edges between blocks and their order.
fn verify_edges<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut errors = Errors::new_in(work);
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
        for successor in graph.successors(block_id) {
            let edges_out = graph.successors(block_id).iter().filter(|s| **s == successor).count();
            let edges_in = graph
                .block(successor)
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .filter(|predecessor| **predecessor == block_id)
                .count();
            if edges_out != edges_in {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "b{index} has {edges_out} edges to b{}, which lists it {edges_in} times",
                    successor.0
                );
            }
        }
        if !block.phis.is_empty() {
            for predecessor in &block.predecessors {
                if graph.successors(*predecessor).len() != 1 {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "b{index} has phis, but its predecessor b{} also leads elsewhere",
                        predecessor.0
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        for predecessor in &block.predecessors {
            if !graph.successors(*predecessor).contains(&block_id) {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "b{index} lists b{} as a predecessor, which does not branch to it",
                    predecessor.0
                );
            }
            // NB: Cold code comes after the code it rejoins.
            if predecessor.index() >= index
                && !block.is_loop_header
                && !(graph.block(*predecessor).is_cold && !block.is_cold)
            {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "b{index} is reached from the later b{} but is no loop header",
                    predecessor.0
                );
            }
        }
    }
    errors.finish()
}

/// Checks that values are defined before their uses, and the rules of each
/// kind of node.
fn verify_nodes<'w>(graph: &Graph, places: &[Option<Place>], work: &'w Zone) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut errors = Errors::new_in(work);
    if graph.blocks.len() > Dominators::MAX_BLOCKS {
        write!(
            errors,
            "the graph has more blocks than the tables of the dominators hold"
        );
        return errors.finish();
    }
    let dominators = &Dominators::of(graph, work);
    let is_defined_before = |value: NodeId, block: BlockId, index: usize| -> bool {
        // NB: Virtual objects are in no block; their properties are listed
        //     with the frame state values that need them.
        if matches!(graph.node(value).op, Op::Constant(_) | Op::VirtualObject { .. }) {
            return true;
        }
        let Some(place) = places[value.index()] else {
            return false;
        };
        if place.block == block {
            return place.index < index;
        }
        dominators.dominates(place.block, block)
    };
    for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
        let is_entry = graph.entries().any(|entry| entry == block_id);
        if block.predecessors.is_empty() != is_entry {
            write!(
                errors,
                "b{index} has {} predecessors, but is {}",
                block.predecessors.len(),
                if is_entry { "an entry" } else { "no entry" }
            );
        }
        if !dominators.is_reachable(block_id) {
            write!(errors, "b{index} is reachable from no entry");
            continue;
        }
        for phi in &block.phis {
            for (input, predecessor) in graph.node(*phi).inputs.iter().zip(&block.predecessors) {
                if graph.node(*input).repr != graph.node(*phi).repr {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "phi v{} of b{index} is {:?}, but its input v{} is {:?}",
                        phi.0,
                        graph.node(*phi).repr,
                        input.0,
                        graph.node(*input).repr
                    );
                }
                let end = graph.block_nodes(*predecessor).count();
                if !is_defined_before(*input, *predecessor, end) {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "phi v{} of b{index} uses v{} from b{}, where it is not defined",
                        phi.0, input.0, predecessor.0
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        for (position, node_id) in graph.block_nodes(block_id).enumerate() {
            let node = graph.node(node_id);
            if node.op == Op::Phi {
                continue;
            }
            for input in &node.inputs {
                if !is_defined_before(*input, block_id, position) {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "v{} ({}) in b{index} uses v{}, which is not defined before it",
                        node_id.0,
                        node.op.name(),
                        input.0
                    );
                } else if graph.node(*input).repr.is_none() {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "v{} ({}) uses v{}, which has no value",
                        node_id.0,
                        node.op.name(),
                        input.0
                    );
                }
            }
            // NB: Lazy exits of calls find their values after the call, but
            //     those are defined before it all the same.
            if let Some(frame_state) = node.frame_state {
                for (slot, value) in graph.frame_state_values(frame_state, work) {
                    if graph.node(value).repr.is_none() && !matches!(graph.node(value).op, Op::VirtualObject { .. }) {
                        write!(
                            errors,
                            "the frame state of v{} has v{} for slot {slot}, which has no value",
                            node_id.0, value.0
                        );
                    }
                    // NB: Only the environments of virtual closures are cell addresses (see `VirtualObjectKind`).
                    if graph.node(value).repr == Some(Repr::Pointer) && slot != crate::ir::VIRTUAL_OBJECT_PROPERTY {
                        write!(
                            errors,
                            "the frame state of v{} has the cell address v{} for slot {slot}",
                            node_id.0, value.0
                        );
                    }
                    if !is_defined_before(value, block_id, position) {
                        write!(
                            errors,
                            "the frame state of v{} ({}) in b{index} has v{} for slot {slot}, which is not defined before it",
                            node_id.0,
                            node.op.name(),
                            value.0
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
            check_input_reprs(graph, node_id, &mut errors);
            if (node.op.can_eager_exit() || node.op.properties().can_lazy_exit) && node.frame_state.is_none() {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "v{} ({}) can exit, but has no frame state",
                    node_id.0,
                    node.op.name()
                );
            }
            match node.op {
                Op::Jump { .. } if !node.inputs.is_empty() => {
                    write!(errors, "v{} (Jump) has inputs", node_id.0);
                }
                Op::Branch {
                    condition: crate::ir::BranchCondition::Shape(_),
                    ..
                } => write!(errors, "v{} branches on a shape", node_id.0),
                _ => {}
            }
            if let Op::CallSlowPath { .. } = node.op {
                if node.frame_state.is_none() {
                    write!(errors, "v{} (CallSlowPath) has no frame state", node_id.0);
                }
                if matches!(
                    node.op,
                    Op::CallSlowPath {
                        saves_registers: true,
                        ..
                    }
                ) && !block.is_cold
                {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "v{} (CallSlowPath) is in b{index}, which is not cold",
                        node_id.0
                    );
                }
            }
            if let Op::Refine { .. } = node.op {
                let at_head = block.body[..position - block.phis.len()]
                    .iter()
                    .all(|other| matches!(graph.node(*other).op, Op::Refine { .. }));
                if !at_head || block.predecessors.len() != 1 {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "v{} (Refine) is not at the head of b{index}, a block with one predecessor",
                        node_id.0
                    );
                }
            }
            if let Some(index) = node.op.refined_input()
                && node.repr.is_some()
                && node.repr != graph.node(node.inputs[index]).repr
            {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "v{} ({}) changes the representation of the value it refines",
                    node_id.0,
                    node.op.name()
                );
            }
            // NB: Typed-array element accesses take the storage offset from
            //     its load or the check that it is valid, which they rely on.
            if let Op::LoadElementAt {
                kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(_),
            }
            | Op::StoreElementAt {
                kind: ElementsKind::TypedArray(_),
            } = node.op
                && graph.node(node.inputs[0]).op != Op::TypedArrayDataAddress
            {
                write!(
                    errors,
                    "v{} ({}) takes no typed array data address",
                    node_id.0,
                    node.op.name()
                );
            }
            if node.op == Op::TypedArrayDataAddress
                && !matches!(
                    graph.node(node.inputs[0]).op,
                    Op::LoadTypedArrayDataOffset | Op::CheckTypedArrayStorage
                )
            {
                write!(errors, "v{} (TypedArrayDataAddress) takes no storage offset", node_id.0);
            }
            // A slow path's further outputs are where its call left them only
            // until anything else runs.
            if let Op::SlowPathOutput { .. } = node.op {
                let call = node.inputs[0];
                let before = || graph.block_nodes(block_id).take(position);
                let follows_call = matches!(graph.node(call).op, Op::CallSlowPath { .. })
                    && before().position(|other| other == call).is_some_and(|start| {
                        before()
                            .skip(start + 1)
                            .all(|other| matches!(graph.node(other).op, Op::SlowPathOutput { .. }))
                    });
                if !follows_call {
                    write!(
                        errors,
                        "v{} (SlowPathOutput) does not follow its slow path call v{} directly",
                        node_id.0, call.0
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    errors.finish()
}

/// Checks that frame states list each slot once.
fn verify_frame_states<'w>(graph: &Graph, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut errors = Errors::new_in(work);
    let mut slots = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    for (index, frame_state) in graph.frame_states.iter().enumerate() {
        slots.clear();
        slots.extend(frame_state.values.iter().map(|(slot, _)| *slot));
        slots.extend_from_slice(&frame_state.in_frame);
        slots.sort_unstable();
        if slots.windows(2).any(|pair| pair[0] == pair[1]) {
            write!(errors, "fs{index} lists a slot more than once");
        }
    }
    errors.finish()
}

/// Reports the first input of `node_id` that does not have the representation its op takes, or a wrong count of inputs.
fn check_input_reprs(graph: &Graph, node_id: NodeId, errors: &mut Errors<'_>) {
    let node = graph.node(node_id);
    let expected = match node.op.info().inputs.reprs(node.inputs.len()) {
        Ok(Some(expected)) => expected,
        Ok(None) => return,
        Err(count) => {
            write!(
                errors,
                "v{} ({}) has {} inputs, but takes {count}",
                node_id.0,
                node.op.name(),
                node.inputs.len(),
            );
            return;
        }
    };
    for (input, repr) in node.inputs.iter().zip(expected) {
        let Some(actual) = graph.node(*input).repr else {
            return;
        };
        if actual != repr {
            write!(
                errors,
                "v{} ({}) takes v{} as {repr:?}, but it is {actual:?}",
                node_id.0,
                node.op.name(),
                input.0
            );
            return;
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Spill slot coalescing: phis share their stack slots with their inputs.
//!
//! Where a phi and the value flowing into it both live in stack slots, the
//! predecessor copies the value from one slot to the other at its end. Loops
//! carrying many values around, and merges of many values, then copy them
//! all on every iteration. Phis and inputs whose live ranges do not overlap
//! can use the same slot instead, which leaves nothing to copy.
//!
//! Two SSA values overlap exactly where one is live right after the other
//! is defined. Values join a class of values sharing one slot only if they
//! overlap with no value already in it.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::liveness::ValueLiveness;
use super::liveness::is_allocated_value;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::tables::Lists;

/// The most values one class holds, which keeps the pairwise checks cheap.
const MAX_CLASS_SIZE: u32 = 32;

/// Where a value is defined: its block, and its position in linear order
/// (`None` for phis, which are defined where their block starts).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Definition {
    block: usize,
    position: Option<u32>,
}

/// The spill slot classes of the values of a graph, in tables in the work zone of a compile.
pub(super) struct Coalescing<'w> {
    /// The class of each value: values of one class share their spill slot.
    /// Classes are named by one of their values.
    pub classes: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// For each value, the next value of its class. The values of a class are a ring, so that two classes join with
    /// no list to copy.
    next: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// For each value that names a class, how many values the class has.
    sizes: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    definitions: ZoneVec<'w, Definition>,
    /// For each value, the blocks where it dies and the positions there.
    deaths: Lists<'w, (usize, u32)>,
}

struct Interference<'a> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'a>,
    liveness: &'a ValueLiveness<'a>,
    definitions: &'a [Definition],
    deaths: &'a Lists<'a, (usize, u32)>,
    work: &'a Zone,
}

impl Interference<'_> {
    /// Whether `value` is live right after `defined` is defined.
    fn is_live_after_definition_of(&self, value: NodeId, defined: NodeId) -> bool {
        let at = self.definitions[defined.index()];
        let of_value = self.definitions[value.index()];
        let at_block = BlockId::from_index(at.block);
        let available = self.liveness.is_live_in(at_block, value)
            || (of_value.block == at.block
                && match (of_value.position, at.position) {
                    (None, _) => true,
                    (Some(_), None) => false,
                    (Some(value_position), Some(position)) => value_position < position,
                });
        let Some(position) = at.position else {
            return available;
        };
        if !available {
            return false;
        }
        // NB: Lazy exits of calls read their frame state values after the
        //     call defined its value.
        let read_after_definition = || {
            let node = self.graph.node(defined);
            node.op.properties().is_call
                && node.frame_state.is_some_and(|frame_state| {
                    self.graph
                        .frame_state_values(frame_state, self.work)
                        .any(|(_, frame_value)| frame_value == value)
                })
        };
        self.liveness.is_live_out(at_block, value)
            || self.deaths.get(value.index()).iter().any(|(block, death)| {
                *block == at.block && (*death > position || (*death == position && read_after_definition()))
            })
    }

    fn overlap(&self, a: NodeId, b: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.is_live_after_definition_of(a, b) || self.is_live_after_definition_of(b, a)
    }
}

/// The values of the class of `value`, which starts with `value`.
fn members(next: &[u32], value: u32) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> + '_ {
    let mut member = Some(value);
    core::iter::from_fn(move || {
        let current = member?;
        let following = next[current as usize];
        member = (following != value).then_some(following);
        Some(NodeId(current))
    })
}

impl<'w> Coalescing<'w> {
    /// Finds the class of each value of `graph`.
    pub fn compute(graph: &Graph, liveness: &ValueLiveness, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        let count = graph.nodes.len();
        let mut coalescing = Self {
            classes: ZoneVec::from_iter_in(0..count as u32, work),
            next: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            sizes: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            definitions: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            deaths: Lists::new_in(work),
        };
        // NB: Without phis, each value is a class of its own.
        if graph.blocks.iter().all(|block| block.phis.is_empty()) {
            return coalescing;
        }
        coalescing.join_classes(graph, liveness, work);
        coalescing
    }

    /// Puts phis and their inputs in one class where they do not overlap.
    fn join_classes(&mut self, graph: &Graph, liveness: &ValueLiveness, work: &Zone) {
        let count = graph.nodes.len();
        self.definitions.resize(
            count,
            Definition {
                block: 0,
                position: None,
            },
        );
        self.deaths.begin_counts(count);
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            for phi in &block.phis {
                self.definitions[phi.index()] = Definition {
                    block: index,
                    position: None,
                };
            }
            for node in block.body.iter().chain(&block.control) {
                self.definitions[node.index()] = Definition {
                    block: index,
                    position: Some(liveness.positions[node.index()]),
                };
                for value in liveness.dies_at(*node) {
                    self.deaths.count(value.index());
                }
            }
        }
        self.deaths.end_counts((0, 0));
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            for node in block.body.iter().chain(&block.control) {
                let position = liveness.positions[node.index()];
                for value in liveness.dies_at(*node) {
                    self.deaths.fill(value.index(), (index, position));
                }
            }
        }
        self.deaths.end_fill();
        self.next.extend_from_slice(&self.classes);
        self.sizes.resize(count, 1);

        let Self {
            classes,
            next,
            sizes,
            definitions,
            deaths,
        } = self;
        let interference = Interference {
            graph,
            liveness,
            definitions,
            deaths,
            work,
        };
        for block in &graph.blocks {
            for phi in &block.phis {
                for input in &graph.node(*phi).inputs {
                    // NB: Values with a frame slot as their home have no spill slot to share.
                    if input == phi || !is_allocated_value(graph, *input) || super::frame_home(graph, *input).is_some()
                    {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let (a, b) = (classes[phi.index()], classes[input.index()]);
                    if a == b || sizes[a as usize] + sizes[b as usize] > MAX_CLASS_SIZE {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let overlapping = members(next, a).any(|x| members(next, b).any(|y| interference.overlap(x, y)));
                    if overlapping {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mut member = b;
                    loop {
                        classes[member as usize] = a;
                        member = next[member as usize];
                        if member == b {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    // NB: This makes one ring of the two.
                    next.swap(a as usize, b as usize);
                    sizes[a as usize] += sizes[b as usize];
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Liveness of SSA values, the pre-pass of the register allocator.
//!
//! Constants are never live: they are rematerialized at every use. A value
//! used by a frame state is live at the node carrying it; for calls, frame
//! state uses happen after the call returns.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::Size;
use super::check_items;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::codegen::lowering_info::Clobbers as LoweringClobbers;
use crate::codegen::lowering_info::lowering_info;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::FrameStateId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::tables::Lists;
use crate::tables::Run;

/// A value that nobody uses.
const DEAD_OUTPUT: u8 = 1 << 0;
/// A value that must have a stack slot that holds it from its definition on.
const NEEDS_SPILL: u8 = 1 << 1;

/// In place of the frame state uses of a frame state: they are not listed yet.
const NOT_LISTED: Run = Run::NOT_WRITTEN;

/// The liveness of the values of a graph, in tables in the work zone of a compile.
///
/// No table here is a set that grows. A graph in SSA form makes that possible: a value is live into exactly the blocks
/// that a walk up from its uses passes before it reaches the block of its definition, so one walk for each value
/// gives all the blocks at one time. The values are walked in the order of their indices, so the list of the values
/// that are live into a block is sorted as it is written.
pub(super) struct ValueLiveness<'w> {
    /// The values live into each block and out of each block, sorted.
    pub live_in: Lists<'w, NodeId>,
    live_out: Lists<'w, NodeId>,
    /// For each node, the values whose last use (on this path) it is, as a part of `dying`.
    deaths: ZoneVec<'w, Run>,
    dying: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// For each value, `DEAD_OUTPUT` and `NEEDS_SPILL`.
    flags: ZoneVec<'w, u8>,
    /// The position of each node in linear order.
    pub positions: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// For each value, the positions of the nodes that use it as an input, in order, as a part of `uses`. A phi input
    /// is used at the control node of its predecessor, where the moves into the phis are.
    use_runs: ZoneVec<'w, Run>,
    uses: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// The blocks each block continues at.
    pub successors: Lists<'w, BlockId>,

    // NB: Only fill() reads what is below.
    /// The block of each node.
    blocks: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// The uses of values as inputs, as the value in the high half and the position in the low half.
    use_pairs: ZoneVec<'w, u64>,
    /// Where the walks up start: the value in the high half, then the block, then whether the value is only known to
    /// flow out of the block (to a phi) in the lowest bit.
    seeds: ZoneVec<'w, u64>,
    /// For each block, the value (plus one) that was last found live into it and out of it.
    in_marks: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    out_marks: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// The blocks a walk up has still to pass.
    pending: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// What the walks found: the block in the high half and the value in the low half, in the order of the values.
    in_pairs: ZoneVec<'w, u64>,
    out_pairs: ZoneVec<'w, u64>,
    /// For each frame state, the allocated values that a node uses through it, as a part of `frame_uses`.
    frame_runs: ZoneVec<'w, Run>,
    frame_uses: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// For each value, the block (plus one) whose backwards walk has it live at the place it is at.
    live: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// The values that were live at some place of the block that is walked.
    touched: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// The values the node that is walked uses.
    used: ZoneVec<'w, NodeId>,
    /// For each value, the node (plus one) that was last noted as its death.
    last_death: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    live_since: ZoneVec<'w, Option<(BlockId, Clobbers)>>,
}

/// Whether a node is a value the register allocator tracks.
pub(super) fn is_allocated_value(graph: &Graph, node: NodeId) -> bool {
    let node = graph.node(node);
    node.repr.is_some() && !matches!(node.op, Op::Constant(_) | Op::VirtualObject { .. })
}

/// For a merge or a loop header: the predecessor whose register state the
/// block starts with, the first one in linear order, which comes before it.
/// Every other predecessor (another one before it, a cold one or a back
/// edge after it) jumps to it, and moves its values to match that state at
/// its end. `None` for blocks with one predecessor, and for merges that
/// start with every value in its stack slot.
pub(super) fn state_predecessor(graph: &Graph, block: BlockId) -> Option<BlockId> {
    let data = graph.block(block);
    if data.predecessors.len() < 2 {
        return None;
    }
    let first = *data.predecessors.iter().min()?;
    if first >= block {
        return None;
    }
    let others_conform = data
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .filter(|predecessor| **predecessor != first)
        .all(|predecessor| matches!(graph.control(*predecessor).op, Op::Jump { .. }));
    others_conform.then_some(first)
}

/// The input of each phi of `successor` that flows in from `block`.
pub(super) fn phi_inputs_from<'g>(
    graph: &'g Graph<'g>,
    block: BlockId,
    successor: BlockId,
) -> impl Iterator<Item = (NodeId, NodeId)> + 'g {
    let successor_block = graph.block(successor);
    let index = if successor_block.phis.is_empty() {
        0
    } else {
        successor_block
            .predecessors
            .iter()
            .position(|predecessor| *predecessor == block)
            .expect("successors list their predecessors")
    };
    successor_block
        .phis
        .iter()
        .map(move |phi| (*phi, graph.node(*phi).inputs[index]))
}

/// How many calls, and how many nodes that clobber the floating point registers (calls among them), the backwards walk
/// of the liveness computation passed.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct Clobbers {
    calls: u32,
    float_clobbers: u32,
}

fn pair(high: u32, low: u32) -> u64 {
    u64::from(high) << 32 | u64::from(low)
}

fn high(pair: u64) -> u32 {
    (pair >> 32) as u32
}

fn low(pair: u64) -> u32 {
    pair as u32
}

impl<'w> ValueLiveness<'w> {
    /// The liveness of the values of `graph`, which has `size`. A compile fails if the lists of the liveness grow
    /// past their limit (see `check_items()`).
    pub fn compute(graph: &Graph, size: &Size, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<Self, CompileFailure> {
        let mut liveness = Self {
            live_in: Lists::new_in(work),
            live_out: Lists::new_in(work),
            deaths: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(Run::default(), size.nodes, work),
            // NB: Most values die once for each use.
            dying: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(size.inputs, work),
            flags: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.nodes, work),
            positions: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.nodes, work),
            use_runs: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(Run::default(), size.nodes, work),
            uses: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(size.inputs, work),
            successors: Lists::with_capacity_in(size.blocks, size.edges, work),
            blocks: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.nodes, work),
            use_pairs: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(size.inputs, work),
            seeds: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(size.inputs, work),
            in_marks: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.blocks, work),
            out_marks: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.blocks, work),
            // NB: A walk up passes each block one time.
            pending: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(size.blocks, work),
            in_pairs: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            out_pairs: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            frame_runs: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(NOT_LISTED, size.frame_states, work),
            frame_uses: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            live: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.nodes, work),
            touched: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            used: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            last_death: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, size.nodes, work),
            live_since: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, size.nodes, work),
        };
        liveness.fill(graph, work)?;
        Ok(liveness)
    }

    pub fn is_live_in(&self, block: BlockId, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.live_in.get(block.index()).binary_search(&value).is_ok()
    }

    pub fn is_live_out(&self, block: BlockId, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.live_out.get(block.index()).binary_search(&value).is_ok()
    }

    /// The values whose last use (on this path) `node` is.
    pub fn dies_at(&self, node: NodeId) -> &[NodeId] {
        &self.dying[self.deaths[node.index()].range()]
    }

    /// Whether nobody uses `value`.
    pub fn is_dead_output(&self, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.flags[value.index()] & DEAD_OUTPUT != 0
    }

    /// Whether `value` must have a stack slot that holds it from its definition on: a value that is live across a
    /// call, or live into a loop header (or a merge without a state predecessor).
    pub fn needs_spill(&self, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.flags[value.index()] & NEEDS_SPILL != 0
    }

    /// The positions of the nodes that use `value` as an input, in order.
    pub fn use_positions(&self, value: NodeId) -> &[u32] {
        &self.uses[self.use_runs[value.index()].range()]
    }

    /// Lists the allocated values of the frame state `frame`, if they are not listed yet.
    fn list_frame_uses(&mut self, graph: &Graph, frame: FrameStateId, work: &Zone) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        if self.frame_runs[frame.index()] != NOT_LISTED {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let start = self.frame_uses.len();
        for (_, value) in graph.frame_state_values(frame, work) {
            if is_allocated_value(graph, value) {
                self.frame_uses.push(value);
            }
        }
        self.frame_runs[frame.index()] = Run::new(start, self.frame_uses.len());
        // NB: How many values the frame states of a graph have in all is known only when they are listed.
        check_items(self.frame_uses.len())
    }

    /// Notes that `value` is used in `block`, at a node or (`flows_out`) by a phi of a block that `block` continues
    /// at. Fails the compile if the seeds would be past their limit (see `check_items()`).
    fn add_seed(&mut self, value: NodeId, block: usize, flows_out: bool) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        // NB: A use in the block of the definition makes the value live into no block.
        if !flows_out && self.blocks[value.index()] as usize == block {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // NB: The frame states of the nodes give a block seeds that its inputs do not tell, so the seeds of one
        //     block alone can be past the limit.
        check_items(self.seeds.len() + 1)?;
        self.seeds
            .push(pair(value.0, (block as u32) << 1 | u32::from(flows_out)));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Fills the tables, which `compute()` made for `graph`.
    fn fill(&mut self, graph: &Graph, work: &Zone) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let block_count = graph.blocks.len();

        self.successors.begin();
        let mut position = 0;
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            for node in block.nodes() {
                self.positions[node.index()] = position;
                self.blocks[node.index()] = index as u32;
                position += 1;
            }
            graph
                .control(BlockId::from_index(index))
                .op
                .for_each_successor(|successor| self.successors.push(successor));
            self.successors.end_list();
        }

        // The uses of each value: where it is an input, and the blocks it is used in that are not its own.
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            for node_id in block.body.iter().chain(&block.control) {
                let node = graph.node(*node_id);
                let position = self.positions[node_id.index()];
                for input in &node.inputs {
                    if is_allocated_value(graph, *input) {
                        self.use_pairs.push(pair(input.0, position));
                        self.add_seed(*input, index, false)?;
                    }
                }
                if let Some(frame) = node.frame_state {
                    self.list_frame_uses(graph, frame, work)?;
                    for use_index in self.frame_runs[frame.index()].range() {
                        self.add_seed(self.frame_uses[use_index], index, false)?;
                    }
                }
            }
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
            let end = self.positions[graph.control_id(block_id).index()];
            for successor_index in 0..self.successors.get(index).len() {
                let successor = self.successors.get(index)[successor_index];
                for (_, input) in phi_inputs_from(graph, block_id, successor) {
                    if is_allocated_value(graph, input) {
                        self.use_pairs.push(pair(input.0, end));
                        self.add_seed(input, index, true)?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        self.use_pairs.sort_unstable();
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < self.use_pairs.len() {
            let value = high(self.use_pairs[index]);
            let start = index;
            while index < self.use_pairs.len() && high(self.use_pairs[index]) == value {
                self.uses.push(low(self.use_pairs[index]));
                index += 1;
            }
            self.use_runs[value as usize] = Run::new(start, index);
        }

        // Walk up from the uses of each value, as far as the block of its definition.
        self.seeds.sort_unstable();
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < self.seeds.len() {
            let value = high(self.seeds[index]);
            let mark = value + 1;
            let definition = self.blocks[value as usize];
            self.pending.clear();
            while index < self.seeds.len() && high(self.seeds[index]) == value {
                let seed = low(self.seeds[index]);
                let (block, flows_out) = (seed >> 1, seed & 1 != 0);
                index += 1;
                if flows_out {
                    if self.out_marks[block as usize] != mark {
                        self.out_marks[block as usize] = mark;
                        self.out_pairs.push(pair(block, value));
                    }
                    if block == definition {
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                if self.in_marks[block as usize] != mark {
                    self.in_marks[block as usize] = mark;
                    self.in_pairs.push(pair(block, value));
                    self.pending.push(block);
                }
            }
            while let Some(block) = self.pending.pop() {
                for predecessor in &graph.blocks[block as usize].predecessors {
                    let predecessor = predecessor.0;
                    if self.out_marks[predecessor as usize] != mark {
                        self.out_marks[predecessor as usize] = mark;
                        self.out_pairs.push(pair(predecessor, value));
                    }
                    if predecessor != definition && self.in_marks[predecessor as usize] != mark {
                        self.in_marks[predecessor as usize] = mark;
                        self.in_pairs.push(pair(predecessor, value));
                        self.pending.push(predecessor);
                    }
                }
            }
            // NB: How many blocks a value is live into is known only when its walk is done.
            check_items(self.in_pairs.len())?;
            check_items(self.out_pairs.len())?;
        }
        // NB: The pairs are in the order of the values, so the list of each block comes out sorted.
        fn lists_of_blocks(lists: &mut Lists<NodeId>, pairs: &[u64], block_count: usize) {
            lists.begin_counts(block_count);
            for pair in pairs {
                lists.count(high(*pair) as usize);
            }
            lists.end_counts(NodeId(0));
            for pair in pairs {
                lists.fill(high(*pair) as usize, NodeId(low(*pair)));
            }
            lists.end_fill();
        }
        lists_of_blocks(&mut self.live_in, &self.in_pairs, block_count);
        lists_of_blocks(&mut self.live_out, &self.out_pairs, block_count);

        // OPTIMIZATION: Rather than marking every value live across each call or float clobbering slow path there,
        //               which takes time quadratic in the size of code that keeps many values live past many of them
        //               (like a large array literal of arrays), the walk counts those nodes, notes the counts where
        //               each value becomes live, and compares them where the value is defined or the block starts.
        let mut clobbers = Clobbers::default();
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            let block_id = BlockId::from_index(index);
            let block_start = clobbers;
            let since = |live_since: &[Option<(BlockId, Clobbers)>], value: usize| match live_since[value] {
                Some((since_block, since)) if since_block == block_id => since,
                _ => block_start,
            };
            let check_spill = |flags: &mut [u8], since: Clobbers, clobbers: Clobbers, value: usize| {
                let is_float = graph.nodes[value].repr == Some(crate::code::Repr::Float64);
                if clobbers.calls != since.calls || (is_float && clobbers.float_clobbers != since.float_clobbers) {
                    flags[value] |= NEEDS_SPILL;
                }
            };
            // Walk the block backwards from the values live at its end. A value is live where the walk is if `live`
            // has the mark of the block for it.
            let mark = index as u32 + 1;
            self.touched.clear();
            for value in self.live_out.get(index) {
                self.live[value.index()] = mark;
                self.touched.push(*value);
            }
            for node_id in block.body.iter().chain(&block.control).rev() {
                let node = graph.node(*node_id);
                self.used.clear();
                for input in &node.inputs {
                    if is_allocated_value(graph, *input) {
                        self.used.push(*input);
                    }
                }
                let frame_uses = match node.frame_state {
                    Some(frame) => self.frame_runs[frame.index()].range(),
                    None => 0..0,
                };
                self.used.extend_from_slice(&self.frame_uses[frame_uses.clone()]);

                if self.live[node_id.index()] == mark {
                    check_spill(
                        &mut self.flags,
                        since(&self.live_since, node_id.index()),
                        clobbers,
                        node_id.index(),
                    );
                } else if is_allocated_value(graph, *node_id) {
                    self.flags[node_id.index()] |= DEAD_OUTPUT;
                }
                let (is_call, clobbers_floats) = match lowering_info(node).clobbers {
                    LoweringClobbers::CallerSaved => (true, false),
                    // NB: Their slow paths clobber the floating point registers.
                    LoweringClobbers::Floats => (false, true),
                    LoweringClobbers::Nothing => (false, false),
                };
                if is_call || clobbers_floats {
                    clobbers.float_clobbers += 1;
                    clobbers.calls += u32::from(is_call);
                    for value in &self.frame_uses[frame_uses] {
                        let is_float = graph.nodes[value.index()].repr == Some(crate::code::Repr::Float64);
                        if value != node_id && (is_call || is_float) {
                            self.flags[value.index()] |= NEEDS_SPILL;
                        }
                    }
                }
                let deaths = self.dying.len();
                for value in &self.used {
                    if self.live[value.index()] != mark && self.last_death[value.index()] != node_id.0 + 1 {
                        self.last_death[value.index()] = node_id.0 + 1;
                        self.dying.push(*value);
                        self.live_since[value.index()] = Some((block_id, clobbers));
                    }
                }
                self.deaths[node_id.index()] = Run::new(deaths, self.dying.len());

                self.live[node_id.index()] = 0;
                for value in &self.used {
                    if self.live[value.index()] != mark {
                        self.live[value.index()] = mark;
                        self.touched.push(*value);
                    }
                }
            }
            for phi in &block.phis {
                self.live[phi.index()] = 0;
            }
            // NB: `touched` may have a value more than one time, which does no harm here.
            for value in &self.touched {
                if self.live[value.index()] == mark {
                    check_spill(
                        &mut self.flags,
                        since(&self.live_since, value.index()),
                        clobbers,
                        value.index(),
                    );
                }
            }
            // NB: The phis of the block are live from its start if anything uses them.
            for phi in &block.phis {
                let is_live = self.live_since[phi.index()].is_some_and(|(since_block, _)| since_block == block_id)
                    || self.live_out.get(index).binary_search(phi).is_ok();
                if is_live {
                    check_spill(
                        &mut self.flags,
                        since(&self.live_since, phi.index()),
                        clobbers,
                        phi.index(),
                    );
                }
            }
            // NB: Most merges start with the register state of one of their
            //     predecessors (see `state_predecessor()`).
            let predecessors = &block.predecessors;
            if (predecessors.len() > 1 || predecessors.first().is_some_and(|predecessor| *predecessor >= block_id))
                && state_predecessor(graph, block_id).is_none()
            {
                for value in self.live_in.get(index) {
                    self.flags[value.index()] |= NEEDS_SPILL;
                }
            }
            // NB: The frame states of the nodes give a block deaths that its inputs do not tell.
            check_items(self.dying.len())?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::code::{Repr, ResumeMode};
    use crate::ir::{Block, FrameState};

    #[test]
    fn shared_frames_and_duplicate_uses_have_one_last_use_per_value() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        graph.add_block(Block::default());
        let value = graph.add(Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        graph.blocks[0].body.push(value);
        let frame = graph.add_frame_state(FrameState {
            executable: 0,
            pc: 0,
            mode: ResumeMode::ResumeAt,
            values: ak::ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[(0, value), (1, value)], crate::test_zone()),
            in_frame: ak::ZoneVec::new_in(crate::test_zone()),
            parent: None,
            passed_argument_count: None,
            legacy_arguments: 0..0,
        });
        let mut checks = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let check = graph.add(Op::CheckObject, &[value], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
            graph.nodes[check.index()].frame_state = Some(frame);
            graph.blocks[0].body.push(check);
            checks.push(check);
        }
        let constant = graph.add(Op::Constant(0), &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
        let returned = graph.add(Op::Return, &[constant], None, 0);
        graph.blocks[0].control = Some(returned);
        let size = Size::of(&graph).unwrap();
        let liveness = ValueLiveness::compute(&graph, &size, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
        assert!(liveness.dies_at(checks[0]).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(liveness.dies_at(checks[1]), [value]);
        assert!(!liveness.is_dead_output(value));
        assert!(liveness.live_in.get(0).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn many_blocks_with_short_live_ranges() {
        let mut graph = Graph::default();
        let block_count = 8192;
        let mut values = Vec::new();
        for index in 0..block_count {
            let mut block = Block::default();
            let value = if index == 0 {
                graph.add(Op::LoadSlot { slot: 0 }, &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0)
            } else {
                block.predecessors.push(BlockId::from_index(index - 1));
                graph.add(Op::CheckObject, &[values[index - 1]], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0)
            };
            values.push(value);
            block.body.push(value);
            block.control = Some(if index + 1 == block_count {
                graph.add(Op::Return, &[value], None, 0)
            } else {
                graph.add(
                    Op::Jump {
                        target: BlockId::from_index(index + 1),
                    },
                    &[],
                    None,
                    0,
                )
            });
            graph.add_block(block);
        }
        let size = Size::of(&graph).unwrap();
        // NB: The second time, the zone holds what the first time left in it.
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let liveness = ValueLiveness::compute(&graph, &size, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
            assert!(liveness.live_in.get(0).is_empty());
            assert!(liveness.live_out.get(block_count - 1).is_empty());
            for index in 1..block_count {
                assert_eq!(liveness.live_in.get(index), [values[index - 1]]);
                assert_eq!(liveness.live_out.get(index - 1), [values[index - 1]]);
                assert!(liveness.is_live_in(BlockId::from_index(index), values[index - 1]));
                assert!(!liveness.is_live_out(BlockId::from_index(index), values[index - 1]));
                assert_eq!(liveness.dies_at(values[index]), [values[index - 1]]);
                assert!(!liveness.is_dead_output(values[index - 1]));
            }
            assert_eq!(
                liveness.dies_at(graph.blocks[block_count - 1].control.unwrap()),
                [values[block_count - 1]]
            );
        }
    }
}

//! The loops of a graph as the register allocator sees them: which blocks
//! each one runs, and which values it only carries through.
//!
//! Linear order does not keep a loop together (its exits may come before its
//! back edges), so loops are sets of blocks. Their cold blocks are left out:
//! those take values from where they are, and cost the loop nothing.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

use super::check_items;
use super::liveness::ValueLiveness;
use crate::CompileFailure;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::passes::dominators::Dominators;
use crate::tables::Lists;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct Loop {
    pub header: BlockId,
    /// The first and last positions of its blocks.
    pub start: u32,
    end: u32,
    /// Which loop of the graph it is, in the order of the headers.
    index: u32,
    /// How many blocks it has, without the cold ones.
    block_count: u32,
}

/// In place of the loop around a block that is in no loop.
const NO_LOOP: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The loops of a graph, in tables in the work zone of a compile.
pub(super) struct Loops<'w> {
    loops: ZoneVec<'w, Loop>,
    /// The blocks of each loop but the cold ones: for each loop, `words_for_each_loop` words with one bit for each
    /// block of the graph.
    blocks: ZoneVec<'w, u64>,
    words_for_each_loop: usize,
    /// The innermost loop around each block, as an index into `loops`, or `NO_LOOP`.
    innermost: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// The block of each position.
    position_blocks: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    /// For each loop, the values live into the header that no node of the loop uses, sorted.
    carried_through: Lists<'w, NodeId>,
    /// The blocks that the back edges of a loop come from.
    back_edge_sources: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
    /// The blocks that the walk over a loop still has to visit.
    pending: ZoneVec<'w, BlockId>,
    /// The loops, from the one with the most blocks to the one with the fewest.
    by_size: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
}

impl<'w> Loops<'w> {
    /// Finds the loops of `graph`.
    pub fn compute(graph: &Graph, liveness: &ValueLiveness, work: &'w Zone) -> Result<Self, CompileFailure> {
        let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
        let mut loops = Self {
            loops: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            blocks: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            words_for_each_loop: block_count.div_ceil(64),
            innermost: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(NO_LOOP, block_count, work),
            position_blocks: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(graph.nodes.len(), work),
            carried_through: Lists::new_in(work),
            back_edge_sources: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            pending: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
            by_size: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        };
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            let end = loops.position_blocks.len() + block.nodes().count();
            loops.position_blocks.resize(end, index as u32);
        }
        // NB: Cold blocks are left out of loops, so only the edges from hot blocks make loops. Cold blocks come after
        //     the hot ones, so their edges back into hot code would otherwise look like loops wherever they rejoin it.
        let is_hot = |block: BlockId| !graph.blocks[block.index()].is_cold;
        let has_back_edges = graph.blocks.iter().enumerate().any(|(index, block)| {
            block
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .any(|predecessor| predecessor.index() >= index && is_hot(*predecessor))
        });
        if !has_back_edges {
            return Ok(loops);
        }
        let dominators = Dominators::of(graph, work);
        loops.find(graph, liveness, &dominators, work)?;
        Ok(loops)
    }

    /// Finds the loops of `graph`, which has back edges.
    fn find(
        &mut self,
        graph: &Graph,
        liveness: &ValueLiveness,
        dominators: &Dominators,
        work: &'w Zone,
    ) -> Result<(), CompileFailure> {
        let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
        let is_hot = |block: BlockId| !graph.blocks[block.index()].is_cold;
        // The sources of the back edges of the loop that a block heads, if it heads one: its predecessors that it
        // dominates.
        let is_back_edge =
            |header: BlockId, predecessor: BlockId| dominators.dominates(header, predecessor) && is_hot(predecessor);
        let mut loop_count = 0;
        let mut header_live_values = 0;
        let mut edges = 0;
        for (index, block) in graph.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            let header = BlockId::from_index(index);
            edges += block.predecessors.len();
            if block
                .predecessors
                .iter()
                .any(|predecessor| is_back_edge(header, *predecessor))
            {
                loop_count += 1;
                header_live_values += liveness.live_in.get(index).len();
            }
        }
        check_items(loop_count * self.words_for_each_loop)?;
        self.loops = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(loop_count, work);
        self.blocks = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(loop_count * self.words_for_each_loop, work);
        self.carried_through = Lists::with_capacity_in(loop_count, header_live_values, work);
        self.carried_through.begin();
        self.pending = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(edges, work);
        self.by_size = ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(loop_count, work);
        for index in 0..block_count {
            let header = BlockId::from_index(index);
            self.back_edge_sources.clear();
            for predecessor in &graph.block(header).predecessors {
                if is_back_edge(header, *predecessor) {
                    self.back_edge_sources.push(*predecessor);
                }
            }
            if self.back_edge_sources.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            // The blocks of the loop: the header and every reachable block that reaches a source of a back edge
            // without going through the header.
            let row = self.blocks.len();
            self.blocks.resize(row + self.words_for_each_loop, 0);
            let blocks = &mut self.blocks[row..];
            let contains = |blocks: &[u64], block: usize| blocks[block / 64] & (1 << (block % 64)) != 0;
            blocks[index / 64] |= 1 << (index % 64);
            self.pending.clear();
            self.pending.extend_from_slice(&self.back_edge_sources);
            while let Some(block) = self.pending.pop() {
                if contains(blocks, block.index()) || !dominators.is_reachable(block) {
                    continue;
                }
                blocks[block.index() / 64] |= 1 << (block.index() % 64);
                self.pending.extend_from_slice(&graph.block(block).predecessors);
            }
            let position_of = |node: NodeId| liveness.positions[node.index()];
            let start = position_of(graph.block_nodes(header).next().expect("blocks have a control node"));
            let mut end = None;
            let mut count = 0;
            for (word_index, word) in blocks.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                let mut bits = *word;
                while bits != 0 {
                    let bit = bits.trailing_zeros();
                    bits &= bits - 1;
                    let block = word_index * 64 + bit as usize;
                    if graph.blocks[block].is_cold {
                        *word &= !(1 << bit);
                        continue;
                    }
                    count += 1;
                    end = end.max(Some(position_of(graph.control_id(BlockId::from_index(block)))));
                }
            }
            let loop_ = Loop {
                header,
                start,
                end: end.unwrap_or(start),
                index: self.loops.len() as u32,
                block_count: count,
            };
            // NB: The values live into a block are in the order of their numbers, so this list is in that order too.
            for value in liveness.live_in.get(index) {
                let uses = liveness.use_positions(*value);
                if loop_
                    .first_use_in(blocks, uses, &self.position_blocks, 0..uses.len())
                    .is_none()
                {
                    self.carried_through.push(*value);
                }
            }
            self.carried_through.end_list();
            self.loops.push(loop_);
        }

        // NB: A loop inside another one has fewer blocks, so the smallest loop around a block is the innermost one.
        //     Of two loops with as many blocks, the later one is taken.
        for index in 0..self.loops.len() as u32 {
            self.by_size.push(index);
        }
        let loops = &self.loops;
        self.by_size
            .sort_unstable_by_key(|index| (core::cmp::Reverse(loops[*index as usize].block_count), *index));
        for index in &self.by_size {
            let row = *index as usize * self.words_for_each_loop;
            let blocks = &self.blocks[row..row + self.words_for_each_loop];
            for (word_index, word) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {
                let mut word = *word;
                while word != 0 {
                    let block = word_index * 64 + word.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                    self.innermost[block] = *index;
                    word &= word - 1;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The bits for the blocks of `loop_`.
    fn blocks_of(&self, loop_: &Loop) -> &[u64] {
        let start = loop_.index as usize * self.words_for_each_loop;
        &self.blocks[start..start + self.words_for_each_loop]
    }

    fn loop_around(&self, block: usize) -> Option<&Loop> {
        let index = self.innermost[block];
        (index != NO_LOOP).then(|| &self.loops[index as usize])
    }

    /// The innermost loop around the node at `position`.
    pub fn innermost_at(&self, position: u32) -> Option<&Loop> {
        let block = *self.position_blocks.get(position as usize)?;
        self.loop_around(block as usize)
    }

    /// The loop that `header` heads, if it heads one.
    pub fn headed_by(&self, header: BlockId) -> Option<&Loop> {
        self.loop_around(header.index()).filter(|loop_| loop_.header == header)
    }

    /// The first of the use positions `uses[range]` (in order) that is in `loop_`.
    pub fn first_use_in(&self, loop_: &Loop, uses: &[u32], range: core::ops::Range<usize>) -> Option<u32> {
        loop_.first_use_in(self.blocks_of(loop_), uses, &self.position_blocks, range)
    }

    /// Whether no node of `loop_` uses `value`, which is live into its header.
    pub fn carries_through(&self, loop_: &Loop, value: NodeId) -> bool {
        self.carried_through
            .get(loop_.index as usize)
            .binary_search(&value)
            .is_ok()
    }
}

impl Loop {
    /// The first of the use positions `uses[range]` (in order) that is in the loop, which has the blocks with a bit
    /// in `blocks`.
    fn first_use_in(
        &self,
        blocks: &[u64],
        uses: &[u32],
        position_blocks: &[u32],
        range: core::ops::Range<usize>,
    ) -> Option<u32> {
        let uses = &uses[range];
        let from = uses.partition_point(|position| *position < self.start);
        let to = uses.partition_point(|position| *position <= self.end);
        uses[from..to.max(from)].iter().copied().find(|position| {
            let block = position_blocks[*position as usize] as usize;
            blocks[block / 64] & (1 << (block % 64)) != 0
        })
    }
}
