#[test]
fn swapping_loop_phis_go_through_a_temp_slot() {
    let program = assemble(|label| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: c(0) },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(1), src: c(1) },
            Instruction::JumpIf {
                condition: l(0),
                true_target: label(4),
                false_target: label(8),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: l(0) },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: l(1) },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(1), src: r(5) },
            Instruction::Jump { target: label(3) },
            Instruction::Return { value: l(1) },
        ]
    });
    let graph = build(&program);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let header = graph.blocks.iter().position(|block| block.is_loop_header).unwrap();
    let back_edge = graph.blocks[header].predecessors[1];
    // NB: The back edge's block starts with the phis in their registers,
    //     like the merge it is, so the swap goes through a temp slot.
    let moves = allocation.block_end_moves(back_edge);
    assert_eq!(moves.len(), 3, "{moves:?}");
    assert!(moves.iter().any(|m| matches!(m.to, Location::Stack(_))), "{moves:?}");
    // The loop header starts with the registers of the block entering the
    // loop: the condition, a phi, stays in r0, with no reload in the loop.
    assert_text(
        &dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation).to_string(),
        "
        b0:
          v6 Jump
        b1:
          moves #0 -> r0, #10 -> r1
          v11 Jump
        b2:
          v12 Phi -> r0
          v13 Phi -> r1
          v14 BranchTruthy (r0)
        b3:
          v15 Jump
        b4:
          v16 Jump
        b5:
          moves r0 -> r1
          v17 ToBoolean (r1) -> r0
          v18 Branch (r0)
        b6:
          moves s0 -> r0, s1 -> r1
          v19 Jump
        b7:
          moves s1 -> r1
          v20 Jump
        b8:
          moves r1 -> r0
          v21 Return (r0)
        b9:
          moves r0 -> s2, r1 -> r0, s2 -> r1
          v22 Jump
        spill slots: 3
        ",
    );
}

#[test]
fn loop_phis_share_spill_slots_with_their_inputs() {
    // Values carried around a loop with calls in it need stack slots. Each
    // phi shares its slot with the value flowing into it over the back edge,
    // so that nothing moves between slots where both are in theirs.
    let program = assemble(|label| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: a(0) },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: l(0),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(1), src: l(0) },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: l(1),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: l(1) },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(6),
            },
            Instruction::JumpIf {
                condition: l(0),
                true_target: label(8),
                false_target: label(12),
            },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: l(0),
            },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: l(1),
            },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(6),
            },
            Instruction::Jump { target: label(7) },
            Instruction::Add {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: l(0),
                rhs: l(1),
            },
            Instruction::Add {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: r(5),
                rhs: r(6),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let graph = build(&program);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let header = graph.blocks.iter().position(|block| block.is_loop_header).unwrap();
    let back_edge = graph.blocks[header]
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .position(|predecessor| predecessor.index() > header)
        .unwrap();
    let (mut shared, mut filled) = (0, 0);
    for phi in &graph.blocks[header].phis {
        let input = graph.node(*phi).inputs[back_edge];
        let (phi_slot, input_slot) = (allocation.node(*phi).spill_slot, allocation.node(input).spill_slot);
        if let (Some(phi_slot), Some(input_slot)) = (phi_slot, input_slot) {
            assert_eq!(phi_slot, input_slot, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
            shared += 1;
        }
        // NB: Where all inputs fill the slot, the phi needs no store to it.
        if graph
            .node(*phi)
            .inputs
            .iter()
            .all(|input| allocation.node(*input).spill_slot == phi_slot)
        {
            assert_eq!(phi_spill_store(&graph, &allocation, *phi), None);
            filled += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(shared, 2, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
    assert!(filled > 0, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
}

#[test]
fn loops_leave_the_values_they_only_carry_through_in_their_stack_slots() {
    // r(5) to r(9) are live across the call, back in registers before the loop and used only after it. With them in
    // registers, the six registers would not hold the counter, the bound and `last` as well. The loop leaves them in
    // their stack slots, so that its back edge neither reloads them nor stores the counter. r(11) is live across the
    // call too, and the loop only uses it as the input of `last`'s phi: it keeps its register.
    let layout = FrameLayout {
        number_of_registers: 16,
        registers_and_locals_count: 18,
        number_of_constants: 0,
        number_of_arguments: 1,
    };
    let r = Operand::from_raw;
    let (counter, last, argument) = (Operand::from_raw(16), Operand::from_raw(17), Operand::from_raw(18));
    let xor = |arith_feedback, dst, lhs, rhs| Instruction::BitwiseXor {
        arith_feedback,
        dst,
        lhs,
        rhs,
    };
    let program = assemble(|label| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            xor(0, r(5), argument, argument),
            xor(1, r(6), r(5), argument),
            xor(2, r(7), r(6), argument),
            xor(3, r(8), r(7), argument),
            xor(4, r(9), r(8), argument),
            xor(14, r(11), r(9), argument),
            Instruction::Call {
                call_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(14),
                callee: r(15),
                this_value: r(15),
                argument_count: 0,
                arguments: &[],
            },
            xor(5, r(10), r(5), r(6)),
            xor(6, r(12), r(7), r(11)),
            Instruction::Mov {
                dst: counter,
                src: r(10),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: last, src: r(5) },
            Instruction::JumpLessThan {
                arith_feedback: 8,
                lhs: counter,
                rhs: r(12),
                true_target: label(13),
                false_target: label(16),
            },
            Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 9,
                dst: counter,
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: last, src: r(11) },
            Instruction::Jump { target: label(12) },
            xor(10, r(13), r(5), r(6)),
            xor(11, r(13), r(13), r(7)),
            xor(12, r(13), r(13), r(8)),
            xor(13, r(13), r(13), r(9)),
            xor(15, r(13), r(13), last),
            Instruction::Return { value: r(13) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = crate::builder::tests::snapshot_for(&program, layout);
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::INT32; 16]);
    let graph = crate::builder::tests::optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let header = graph.blocks.iter().position(|block| block.is_loop_header).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        graph.blocks[header].phis.len(),
        2,
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
    let back_edge = *graph.blocks[header]
        .predecessors
        .iter()
        .find(|predecessor| predecessor.index() > header)
        .unwrap();
    assert!(
        allocation
            .block_end_moves(back_edge)
            .iter()
            .all(|m| !matches!(m.from, Location::Stack(_)) && !matches!(m.to, Location::Stack(_))),
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
    for phi in &graph.blocks[header].phis {
        assert!(
            matches!(allocation.node(*phi).output, Some(Location::Register(_))),
            "{}",
            dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn int32_operations_write_over_their_first_input_where_it_dies() {
    // The first XOR's value dies at the second, whose output then takes its
    // register: two-address instructions need no copy of it.
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::BitwiseXor {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: a(0),
            },
            Instruction::BitwiseXor {
                arith_feedback: 1,
                dst: r(6),
                lhs: r(5),
                rhs: a(0),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = crate::builder::tests::snapshot_for(&program, crate::bytecode::test_support::test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::INT32; 2]);
    let graph = crate::builder::tests::optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let xors = graph
        .nodes
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, node)| {
            node.op
                == Op::Int32Binary {
                    op: crate::ir::BinaryOp::BitwiseXor,
                }
        })
        .map(|(index, _)| index)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(xors.len(), 2, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
    let second = allocation.node(NodeId::from_index(xors[1]));
    assert_eq!(
        second.output,
        Some(second.inputs[0]),
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
}

#[test]
fn shift_amounts_are_in_the_targets_shift_register_or_immediates() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::BitwiseXorRhsInt32 {
                arith_feedback: 2,
                dst: r(4),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: 5,
            },
            Instruction::LeftShift {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: r(4),
            },
            Instruction::RightShiftRhsInt32 {
                arith_feedback: 1,
                dst: r(6),
                lhs: r(5),
                rhs: 3,
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = crate::builder::tests::snapshot_for(&program, crate::bytecode::test_support::test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::INT32; 3]);
    let graph = crate::builder::tests::optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let shift = |op| find_node(&graph, |node| node.op == Op::Int32Binary { op });
    let (variable, constant) = (
        shift(crate::ir::BinaryOp::LeftShift),
        shift(crate::ir::BinaryOp::RightShift),
    );
    for shift_amount_gpr in [None, Some(3), Some(4)] {
        let registers = RegisterSet {
            shift_amount_gpr,
            ..RegisterSet::test_configuration()
        };
        let allocation = allocate_with(&graph, &registers);
        if let Err(errors) = verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, crate::test_zone()) {
            panic!("{errors}\n{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
        }
        let dump = dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation);
        let amount = allocation.node(variable).inputs[1];
        match shift_amount_gpr {
            Some(register) => assert_eq!(amount, Location::Register(register), "{dump}"),
            None => assert!(matches!(amount, Location::Register(_)), "{dump}"),
        }
        assert!(
            matches!(allocation.node(constant).inputs[1], Location::Constant(bits) if bits as u32 == 3),
            "{dump}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn float64_operations_write_over_their_first_input_where_it_dies() {
    // The first product dies at the second, whose output then takes its register, also for non-commutative
    // operations; the argument stays live, so the first product does not take its register.
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::Mul {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                lhs: a(0),
                rhs: a(0),
            },
            Instruction::Sub {
                arith_feedback: 1,
                dst: r(6),
                lhs: r(5),
                rhs: a(0),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = crate::builder::tests::snapshot_for(&program, crate::bytecode::test_support::test_layout());
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.arith = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::arith_feedback::DOUBLE; 2]);
    let graph = crate::builder::tests::optimized_graph(&snapshot);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let binaries = graph
        .nodes
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, node)| matches!(node.op, Op::Float64Binary { .. }))
        .map(|(index, _)| index)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(binaries.len(), 2, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
    let (first, second) = (
        allocation.node(NodeId::from_index(binaries[0])),
        allocation.node(NodeId::from_index(binaries[1])),
    );
    assert_ne!(
        first.output,
        Some(first.inputs[0]),
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        second.output,
        Some(second.inputs[0]),
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(second.output, Some(Location::Register(register)) if register >= FPR_BASE),
        "{}",
        dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
    );
}

#[test]
fn exits_find_constants_registers_and_spilled_values() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(5), src: c(1) },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: a(0) },
            Instruction::Add {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(7),
                lhs: r(5),
                rhs: r(6),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(7) },
        ]
    });
    let graph = build_with_layout(&program, test_layout(), &[2]);
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let exit = find_node(&graph, |node| matches!(node.op, Op::Exit { .. }));
    let work = crate::test_work();
    let mut sites = crate::codegen::sites::SiteScratch::new_in(&graph, &work).unwrap();
    let mut artifact = crate::artifact::ArtifactWriter::new_in(&work);
    SiteSource {
        graph: &graph,
        allocation: &allocation,
        node: exit,
        kind: SiteKind::Exit(ExitKind::NoFeedback),
        stack_slot_offset: &|slot| -8 * (i32::try_from(slot).unwrap() + 1),
        saves: &[],
        work: crate::test_zone(),
    }
    .write(&mut sites, &mut artifact)
    .unwrap();
    let mut words = ak::Column::new(crate::artifact::MAX_WORDS, c"test");
    let layout = artifact.finish(&Tail::default(), &mut words).unwrap();
    let artifact = Artifact::new(&words, &layout);
    let argument = find_node(&graph, |node| node.op == Op::LoadSlot { slot: a(0).raw() });
    let Some(Location::Register(argument_register)) = allocation.node(argument).output else {
        panic!("the argument is in a register");
    };
    assert_eq!(artifact.site_count(), 1);
    let site = artifact.site(0);
    assert_eq!(site.kind(), SiteKind::Exit(ExitKind::NoFeedback));
    assert_eq!(site.frame_count(), 1);
    assert_eq!(site.object_count(), 0);
    assert_eq!(site.inlined_frame_bytes(), 0);
    let frame = site.frame(0);
    assert_eq!(frame.executable(), 0);
    assert_eq!(frame.pc(), program.offsets[2]);
    assert_eq!(frame.mode(), crate::code::ResumeMode::ResumeAt);
    assert_eq!(
        frame.values().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [
            (r(5).raw(), ValueLocation::Constant(value::int32(10))),
            (r(6).raw(), ValueLocation::Register(argument_register, Repr::Tagged)),
        ]
    );
    assert!(frame.in_frame().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(frame.passed_argument_count(), None);
    assert_eq!(frame.legacy_arguments(), 0..0);
}

#[test]
fn the_verifier_finds_values_in_the_wrong_place() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: a(0) },
            Instruction::Call {
                call_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(7),
                callee: r(5),
                this_value: r(5),
                argument_count: 1,
                arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[r(6)]),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: a(0), src: r(7) },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let graph = build(&program);
    let registers = RegisterSet::test_configuration();
    let allocation = allocate_with(&graph, &registers);
    verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();

    // Forgetting to spill a value that is live across a call loses it.
    let argument = find_node(&graph, |node| node.op == Op::LoadSlot { slot: a(0).raw() });
    let mut broken = allocate_with(&graph, &registers);
    broken.set_spill_slot(argument, None);
    assert!(verify(&graph, &registers, &broken, crate::test_zone()).is_err());

    // Reading an input from a register that holds something else.
    let call = find_node(&graph, |node| matches!(node.op, Op::CallSlowPath { .. }));
    let mut broken = allocation;
    let Location::Register(register) = broken.node(call).inputs[2] else {
        panic!("the argument is in a register");
    };
    broken.set_input(call, 2, Location::Register((register + 1) % 6));
    assert!(verify(&graph, &registers, &broken, crate::test_zone()).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn the_verifier_finds_values_reloaded_from_frame_slots_that_do_not_hold_them() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Mov { dst: r(6), src: a(0) },
            Instruction::Call {
                call_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(7),
                callee: r(5),
                this_value: r(5),
                argument_count: 1,
                arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[r(6)]),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let graph = build(&program);
    let registers = RegisterSet::test_configuration();
    let allocation = allocate_with(&graph, &registers);
    verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
    let returned = find_node(&graph, |node| matches!(node.op, Op::Return));
    assert_eq!(
        allocation.node(returned).moves_before,
        [Move {
            from: Location::Frame(a(0).raw()),
            to: Location::Register(0),
        }]
    );

    // A frame slot that the code may write is no home.
    let mut written = graph.clone_in(crate::test_zone());
    written.unwritten_slots = ak::ZoneBitSet::new_in(0, written.zone);
    assert!(verify(&written, &registers, &allocation, crate::test_zone()).is_err());

    // Another frame slot holds another value.
    let mut broken = allocate_with(&graph, &registers);
    let wrong_move = Move {
        from: Location::Frame(r(5).raw()),
        ..broken.node(returned).moves_before[0]
    };
    broken.set_move_before(returned, 0, wrong_move);
    assert!(verify(&graph, &registers, &broken, crate::test_zone()).is_err());

    // A store to the slot, which nothing may do, makes it hold another value.
    let mut stored = graph.clone_in(crate::test_zone());
    let undefined = stored.add(Op::Constant(value::UNDEFINED), &[], Some(Repr::Tagged), 0);
    let store = stored.add(Op::StoreSlot { slot: a(0).raw() }, &[undefined], None, 0);
    let block = stored
        .blocks
        .iter()
        .position(|block| block.control == Some(returned))
        .unwrap();
    stored.blocks[block].body.push(store);
    let mut allocation = allocation;
    allocation.push_node(&[], None);
    allocation.push_node(&[Location::Constant(value::UNDEFINED)], None);
    let errors = verify(&stored, &registers, &allocation, crate::test_zone()).unwrap_err();
    assert!(errors.contains("nothing writes"), "{errors}");
}

/// A tiny deterministic random number generator (xorshift64).
pub(crate) struct Random(pub(crate) u64);

impl Random {
    pub(crate) fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 13;
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 7;
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 17;
        self.0
    }

    pub(crate) fn below(&mut self, bound: usize) -> usize {
        (self.next() % bound as u64) as usize
    }

    pub(crate) fn chance(&mut self, percent: usize) -> bool {
        self.below(100) < percent
    }
}

/// An instruction whose jump targets are instruction indices.
#[derive(Clone)]
enum Item {
    Plain(Instruction<'static>),
    Jump(usize),
    JumpIf(Operand, usize, usize),
    JumpTrue(Operand, usize),
    JumpFalse(Operand, usize),
    JumpNullish(Operand, usize, usize),
    JumpLessThan(Operand, Operand, usize, usize),
}

/// Generates structured random programs: nested ifs and loops around moves,
/// native and generic instructions, calls and returns.
pub(crate) struct ProgramGenerator {
    random: Random,
    layout: FrameLayout,
    items: Vec<Item>,
    /// Whether to emit GetById (with property caches 0 and 1) and PutById
    /// (with property caches 2 and 3).
    property_access: bool,
}

impl ProgramGenerator {
    fn writable(&mut self) -> Operand {
        let layout = self.layout;
        let count = layout.registers_and_locals_count - 5 + layout.number_of_arguments;
        let index = 5 + u32::try_from(self.random.below(count as usize)).unwrap();
        if index < layout.registers_and_locals_count {
            Operand::from_raw(index)
        } else {
            Operand::from_raw(layout.arguments_base() + index - layout.registers_and_locals_count)
        }
    }

    fn readable(&mut self) -> Operand {
        match self.random.below(10) {
            0 => Operand::from_raw(u32::try_from(self.random.below(5)).unwrap()),
            1 | 2 => Operand::from_raw(
                self.layout.constants_base()
                    + u32::try_from(self.random.below(self.layout.number_of_constants as usize)).unwrap(),
            ),
            _ => self.writable(),
        }
    }

    /// Usually an argument, where the property access tests pass objects.
    fn object_operand(&mut self) -> Operand {
        if self.random.chance(80) {
            let argument = u32::try_from(self.random.below(self.layout.number_of_arguments as usize)).unwrap();
            Operand::from_raw(self.layout.arguments_base() + argument)
        } else {
            self.readable()
        }
    }

    fn plain(&mut self) -> Instruction<'static> {
        if self.property_access && self.random.chance(30) {
            let cache = u32::try_from(self.random.below(2)).unwrap();
            return if self.random.chance(60) {
                Instruction::GetById {
                    dst: self.writable(),
                    base: self.object_operand(),
                    property: crate::bytecode::PropertyKeyTableIndex(0),
                    cache,
                }
            } else {
                Instruction::PutById {
                    base: self.object_operand(),
                    property: crate::bytecode::PropertyKeyTableIndex(0),
                    src: self.readable(),
                    kind: 0,
                    cache: 2 + cache,
                }
            };
        }
        match self.random.below(13) {
            0..=2 => Instruction::Mov {
                dst: self.writable(),
                src: self.readable(),
            },
            3 | 4 => Instruction::MovSrcUndefined { dst: self.writable() },
            5 => Instruction::Add {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: self.writable(),
                lhs: self.readable(),
                rhs: self.readable(),
            },
            6 => Instruction::Increment {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: self.writable(),
            },
            7 => Instruction::Not {
                dst: self.writable(),
                src: self.readable(),
            },
            8 => Instruction::GetLexicalEnvironment { dst: self.writable() },
            9 => Instruction::IsCallable {
                dst: self.writable(),
                value: self.readable(),
            },
            10 => Instruction::SetLexicalEnvironment {
                environment: self.readable(),
            },
            11 => {
                let argument_count = self.random.below(3);
                Instruction::Call {
                    call_feedback: 0,
                    dst: self.writable(),
                    callee: self.readable(),
                    this_value: self.readable(),
                    argument_count: u32::try_from(argument_count).unwrap(),
                    arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_from_iter((0..argument_count).map(|_| self.readable())),
                }
            }
            _ => Instruction::ToBoolean {
                dst: self.writable(),
                value: self.readable(),
            },
        }
    }

    fn statements(&mut self, depth: usize) {
        for _ in 0..1 + self.random.below(5) {
            match self.random.below(10) {
                0 | 1 if depth < 4 => self.if_else(depth + 1),
                2 if depth < 4 => self.while_loop(depth + 1),
                3 if self.random.chance(15) => {
                    let value = self.readable();
                    self.items.push(Item::Plain(Instruction::Return { value }));
                }
                _ => {
                    let instruction = self.plain();
                    self.items.push(Item::Plain(instruction));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn if_else(&mut self, depth: usize) {
        let condition = self.readable();
        let branch = self.items.len();
        self.items.push(Item::Jump(0));
        let then_start = self.items.len();
        self.statements(depth);
        let jump_to_end = self.items.len();
        self.items.push(Item::Jump(0));
        let else_start = self.items.len();
        self.statements(depth);
        let end = self.items.len();
        self.items[jump_to_end] = Item::Jump(end);
        self.items[branch] = match self.random.below(5) {
            0 => Item::JumpIf(condition, then_start, else_start),
            1 => Item::JumpFalse(condition, else_start),
            2 => Item::JumpTrue(condition, else_start),
            3 => Item::JumpNullish(condition, then_start, else_start),
            _ => Item::JumpLessThan(condition, self.readable(), then_start, else_start),
        };
    }

    fn while_loop(&mut self, depth: usize) {
        let header = self.items.len();
        let condition = self.readable();
        self.items.push(Item::Jump(0));
        let body = self.items.len();
        self.statements(depth);
        self.items.push(Item::Jump(header));
        let end = self.items.len();
        self.items[header] = match self.random.below(3) {
            0 => Item::JumpFalse(condition, end),
            1 => Item::JumpIf(condition, body, end),
            _ => Item::JumpLessThan(condition, self.readable(), body, end),
        };
    }

    pub(crate) fn generate(seed: u64, layout: FrameLayout) -> Program {
        Self::generate_with(seed, layout, false)
    }

    pub(crate) fn generate_with(seed: u64, layout: FrameLayout, property_access: bool) -> Program {
        let mut generator = Self {
            random: Random(seed),
            layout,
            items: vec![Item::Plain(Instruction::Enter)],
            property_access,
        };
        generator.statements(0);
        let value = generator.readable();
        generator.items.push(Item::Plain(Instruction::Return { value }));
        let items = generator.items;
        assemble(|label| {
            items
                .iter()
                .map(|item| match item.clone() {
                    Item::Plain(instruction) => instruction,
                    Item::Jump(target) => Instruction::Jump { target: label(target) },
                    Item::JumpIf(condition, if_true, if_false) => Instruction::JumpIf {
                        condition,
                        true_target: label(if_true),
                        false_target: label(if_false),
                    },
                    Item::JumpTrue(condition, target) => Instruction::JumpTrue {
                        condition,
                        target: label(target),
                    },
                    Item::JumpFalse(condition, target) => Instruction::JumpFalse {
                        condition,
                        target: label(target),
                    },
                    Item::JumpNullish(condition, if_true, if_false) => Instruction::JumpNullish {
                        condition,
                        true_target: label(if_true),
                        false_target: label(if_false),
                    },
                    Item::JumpLessThan(lhs, rhs, if_true, if_false) => Instruction::JumpLessThan {
                        arith_feedback: 0,
                        lhs,
                        rhs,
                        true_target: label(if_true),
                        false_target: label(if_false),
                    },
                })
                .collect()
        })
    }
}

/// Marks `blocks` cold and lays the graph out like the passes do.
fn make_cold(graph: &mut Graph, blocks: &[BlockId]) {
    for block in blocks {
        graph.blocks[block.index()].is_cold = true;
    }
    crate::passes::edit::move_cold_blocks_last(graph, crate::test_zone());
    if let Err(errors) = crate::passes::verify::verify_with(graph, &crate::test_work()) {
        panic!("{errors}\n{}", crate::ir::dump(graph, &test_layout()));
    }
}

#[test]
fn cold_blocks_cost_the_code_around_them_no_spills() {
    // The then branch is cold: the value in l(1), live across it, and the
    // phi of l(0) at the join stay in registers.
    let program = assemble(|label| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(1), src: a(0) },
            Instruction::JumpNullish {
                condition: r(5),
                true_target: label(2),
                false_target: label(4),
            },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: c(0) },
            Instruction::Jump { target: label(5) },
            Instruction::Mov { dst: l(0), src: r(5) },
            Instruction::Add {
                arith_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(6),
                lhs: l(0),
                rhs: l(1),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(6) },
        ]
    });
    let mut graph = build(&program);
    let then_block = (0..graph.blocks.len())
        .map(|index| BlockId(u32::try_from(index).unwrap()))
        .find(|block| graph.block(*block).bytecode_start == Some(program.offsets[2]))
        .expect("the then branch has a block");
    make_cold(&mut graph, &[then_block]);
    let join = (0..graph.blocks.len())
        .map(|index| BlockId(u32::try_from(index).unwrap()))
        .find(|block| liveness::state_predecessor(&graph, *block).is_some())
        .expect("the join has a state predecessor");
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let kept = find_node(&graph, |node| node.op == Op::LoadSlot { slot: a(0).raw() });
    assert_eq!(allocation.node(kept).spill_slot, None);
    let phi = graph.block(join).phis[0];
    assert!(matches!(allocation.node(phi).output, Some(Location::Register(_))));
    assert_eq!(allocation.node(phi).spill_slot, None);
    assert_eq!(
        allocation.spill_slot_count, 1,
        "only the cycle temp of the cold block's moves"
    );
}

#[test]
fn random_structured_programs_with_cold_blocks_allocate_correctly() {
    let layout = FrameLayout {
        number_of_registers: 12,
        registers_and_locals_count: 16,
        number_of_constants: 2,
        number_of_arguments: 2,
    };
    for seed in 1..=1000u64 {
        let program = ProgramGenerator::generate(seed.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15), layout);
        let mut graph = build_with_layout(&program, layout, &[]);
        let mut random = Random(seed);
        let osr_blocks = graph.osr_entries.iter().map(|(_, block)| *block).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let cold = (1..graph.blocks.len())
            .map(|index| BlockId(u32::try_from(index).unwrap()))
            .filter(|block| !graph.block(*block).is_loop_header && !osr_blocks.contains(block) && random.chance(25))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        for block in &cold {
            graph.blocks[block.index()].is_cold = true;
        }
        crate::passes::edit::move_cold_blocks_last(&mut graph, crate::test_zone());
        if let Err(errors) = crate::passes::verify::verify_with(&graph, &crate::test_work()) {
            panic!("seed {seed}: {errors}\n{}", crate::ir::dump(&graph, &layout));
        }
        let registers = RegisterSet::test_configuration();
        let work = crate::test_work();
        let allocation = allocate(&graph, &registers, &work).unwrap();
        if let Err(errors) = verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, &work) {
            panic!(
                "seed {seed}: {errors}\n{}\n{}",
                crate::ir::dump(&graph, &layout),
                dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn random_structured_programs_allocate_correctly() {
    let layout = FrameLayout {
        number_of_registers: 12,
        registers_and_locals_count: 16,
        number_of_constants: 2,
        number_of_arguments: 2,
    };
    for seed in 1..=2000u64 {
        let program = ProgramGenerator::generate(seed.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15), layout);
        let mut random = Random(seed);
        let never_ran = (0..program.offsets.len())
            .filter(|_| random.chance(3))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let graph = build_with_layout(&program, layout, &never_ran);
        let registers = RegisterSet::test_configuration();
        let work = crate::test_work();
        let allocation = allocate(&graph, &registers, &work).unwrap();
        if let Err(errors) = verify(&graph, &registers, &allocation, &work) {
            panic!(
                "seed {seed}: {errors}\n{}\n{}",
                crate::ir::dump(&graph, &layout),
                dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn float64_values_get_floating_point_registers() {
    let program = assemble(|_| {
        vec![
            Instruction::Enter,
            Instruction::Call {
                call_feedback: 0,
                dst: r(5),
                callee: r(6),
                this_value: r(7),
                argument_count: 1,
                arguments: crate::test_zone().alloc_slice_copy(&[a(0)]),
            },
            Instruction::Return { value: r(5) },
        ]
    });
    let mut snapshot = crate::builder::tests::snapshot_for(&program, test_layout());
    snapshot.runtime.layout.builtin_math_sqrt = 13;
    snapshot.executables[0].feedback.call = snapshot.add(&[crate::snapshot::CallFeedbackSnapshot {
        target_builtin: Some(13),
        ..Default::default()
    }]);
    let mut graph = crate::builder::build_graph_with_feedback(&snapshot, &|_| true, crate::test_zone()).unwrap();
    crate::passes::optimize(
        &mut graph,
        &snapshot.executables[0].layout,
        true,
        &mut crate::test_work(),
        &mut crate::test_steps(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let allocation = allocate_and_verify(&graph);
    let mut floats = 0;
    for (index, node) in graph.nodes.iter().enumerate() {
        let output = allocation.node(NodeId::from_index(index)).output;
        match (node.repr, output) {
            (Some(Repr::Float64), Some(Location::Register(register))) => {
                assert!(register >= FPR_BASE, "v{index} is a float64 in r{register}");
                floats += 1;
            }
            (_, Some(Location::Register(register))) => {
                assert!(
                    register < FPR_BASE,
                    "v{index} is in the floating point register r{register}"
                );
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    assert!(floats >= 2, "{}", dump_allocation(&graph, &allocation));
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Checks a register allocation by simulating what every location holds.
//!
//! The verifier walks the allocated program and tracks, for every register
//! and stack slot, which value it holds on every path reaching each point.
//! Every input, phi input and exit value must be found in the location the
//! allocation claims, no matter which path led there.
//!
//! A slot of the compiled function's frame that nothing writes (see
//! `frame_home()`) holds the value the function started with everywhere, and
//! nothing on any path may store to it. Every load of such a slot loads that
//! value, so the state names it by the slot rather than by a load.

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;
use core::fmt;

use super::Allocation;
use super::Location;
use super::Move;
use super::RegisterSet;
use super::liveness::phi_inputs_from;
use crate::codegen::lowering_info::Clobbers;
use crate::codegen::lowering_info::InputConstraint;
use crate::codegen::lowering_info::lowering_info;
use crate::debug_text::DebugText;
use crate::ir::BlockId;
use crate::ir::Graph;
use crate::ir::NodeId;
use crate::ir::Op;
use crate::tables::Run;

/// What a location holds.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Content {
    Value(NodeId),
    Constant(u64),
    /// The value a slot that nothing writes holds, which every load of it loads.
    UnwrittenSlot(u32),
}

/// How many places a state has for registers, which come before the places for stack slots: one for each number a
/// register can have.
const REGISTER_PLACES: usize = 256;

/// The place of `location` in a state, if a state has one for it: registers and stack slots, in the order of
/// `Location`. Moves never write the other locations.
fn place(location: Location) -> Option<usize> {
    match location {
        Location::Register(register) => Some(usize::from(register)),
        Location::Stack(slot) => Some(REGISTER_PLACES + slot as usize),
        Location::Constant(_) | Location::Frame(_) => None,
    }
}

/// The location that has the place `place` in a state.
fn location_at(place: usize) -> Location {
    match u8::try_from(place) {
        Ok(register) => Location::Register(register),
        Err(_) => Location::Stack((place - REGISTER_PLACES) as u32),
    }
}

/// What the locations hold at one point of the program.
trait Holds {
    fn holds(&self, location: Location) -> Option<Content>;
}

/// What each location holds at the point that the walk is at, with a place for each register and stack slot.
struct State<'w> {
    contents: ZoneVec<'w, Option<Content>>,
    /// The places that were given contents since the state was last cleared, maybe more than one time.
    filled: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
}

impl<'w> State<'w> {
    /// A state in which nothing holds anything, with places for `stack_slots` stack slots.
    fn new_in(stack_slots: usize, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            contents: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, REGISTER_PLACES + stack_slots, work),
            filled: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        }
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, location: Location, content: Content) {
        let Some(place) = place(location) else {
            return;
        };
        if self.contents[place].is_none() {
            self.filled.push(place as u32);
        }
        self.contents[place] = Some(content);
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, location: Location) -> Option<Content> {
        self.contents[place(location)?].take()
    }

    /// Makes the state what `stored` (see `store()`) says.
    fn load(&mut self, stored: &[(Location, Content)]) {
        for place in self.filled.drain_all() {
            self.contents[place as usize] = None;
        }
        for (location, content) in stored {
            self.insert(*location, *content);
        }
    }

    /// Writes what each location holds to `out`, in the order of the locations.
    fn store(&mut self, out: &mut ZoneVec<'_, (Location, Content)>) {
        self.filled.sort_unstable();
        self.filled.dedup();
        out.clear();
        for place in &self.filled {
            if let Some(content) = self.contents[*place as usize] {
                out.push((location_at(*place as usize), content));
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Holds for State<'_> {
    fn holds(&self, location: Location) -> Option<Content> {
        self.contents[place(location)?]
    }
}

/// What each location holds, in the order of the locations (see `State::store()`).
impl Holds for [(Location, Content)] {
    fn holds(&self, location: Location) -> Option<Content> {
        let index = self.binary_search_by_key(&location, |(location, _)| *location).ok()?;
        Some(self[index].1)
    }
}

/// A state for each block, if it has one yet, as what `State::store()` writes. The states of all the blocks are in
/// one list.
struct States<'w> {
    runs: ZoneVec<'w, Option<Run>>,
    /// How many elements the part of `items` of each block has room for.
    rooms: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    items: ZoneVec<'w, (Location, Content)>,
}

impl<'w> States<'w> {
    fn new_in(block_count: usize, work: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            runs: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(None, block_count, work),
            rooms: ZoneVec::from_elem_in(0, block_count, work),
            items: ZoneVec::new_in(work),
        }
    }

    fn get(&self, block: BlockId) -> Option<&[(Location, Content)]> {
        Some(&self.items[self.runs[block.index()]?.range()])
    }

    fn set(&mut self, block: BlockId, state: &[(Location, Content)]) {
        let index = block.index();
        match self.runs[index] {
            // NB: A new state of a block takes the place of the one it had where it fits, which it mostly does: the
            //     states of a block mostly hold less each time they are computed again.
            Some(run) if state.len() <= self.rooms[index] as usize => {
                let start = run.range().start;
                self.items[start..start + state.len()].copy_from_slice(state);
                self.runs[index] = Some(Run::new(start, start + state.len()));
            }
            _ => {
                let start = self.items.len();
                self.items.extend_from_slice(state);
                self.rooms[index] = state.len() as u32;
                self.runs[index] = Some(Run::new(start, self.items.len()));
            }
        }
    }
}

/// How many stack slots the locations of `allocation` name.
fn stack_slot_count(allocation: &Allocation) -> usize {
    let mut count = allocation.spill_slot_count as usize;
    let mut note = |location: Location| {
        if let Location::Stack(slot) = location {
            count = count.max(slot as usize + 1);
        }
    };
    for row in &allocation.nodes {
        row.output.into_iter().for_each(&mut note);
        row.spill_slot.map(Location::Stack).into_iter().for_each(&mut note);
    }
    for move_ in &allocation.moves {
        note(move_.from);
        note(move_.to);
    }
    allocation.locations.iter().copied().for_each(&mut note);
    allocation.exit_values.iter().for_each(|(_, location)| note(*location));
    count
}

/// What an error is about.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Context {
    Node(NodeId),
    Input(NodeId, usize),
    /// The exit value of a node for a slot.
    ExitValue(NodeId, u32),
    /// The moves at the end of a block.
    EndOfBlock(BlockId),
}

impl fmt::Display for Context {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match *self {
            Self::Node(node) => write!(f, "v{}", node.0),
            Self::Input(node, index) => write!(f, "v{}, input {index}", node.0),
            Self::ExitValue(node, slot) => write!(f, "v{}, exit value for slot {slot}", node.0),
            Self::EndOfBlock(block) => write!(f, "end of b{}", block.0),
        }
    }
}

struct Verifier<'a, 'w> {
    graph: &'a Graph<'a>,
    registers: &'a RegisterSet,
    allocation: &'a Allocation<'a>,
    /// Whether to report errors; off while the block states are still
    /// being computed.
    checking: bool,
    /// The errors, one on each line.
    errors: DebugText<'w>,
    work: &'w Zone,
}

/// Checks `allocation` against `graph`, returning a description of every
/// problem found.
pub fn verify<'w>(
    graph: &Graph,
    registers: &RegisterSet,
    allocation: &Allocation,
    work: &'w Zone,
) -> Result<(), DebugText<'w>> {
    let mut verifier = Verifier {
        graph,
        registers,
        allocation,
        checking: false,
        errors: DebugText::new_in(work),
        work,
    };
    let block_count = graph.blocks.len();
    let block_ids = (0..block_count).map(BlockId::from_index);
    let mut state = State::new_in(stack_slot_count(allocation), work);
    let mut entry = ZoneVec::new_in(work);
    let mut exit = ZoneVec::new_in(work);

    // Compute the state at the start of every block: what holds on all
    // paths, starting optimistically from the predecessors seen so far.
    let mut entry_states = States::new_in(block_count, work);
    let mut exit_states = States::new_in(block_count, work);
    let mut changed = true;
    while changed {
        changed = false;
        for block in block_ids.clone() {
            if !verifier.entry_state(block, &exit_states, &mut state, &mut entry) {
                continue;
            }
            if entry_states.get(block) == Some(&entry[..]) && exit_states.get(block).is_some() {
                continue;
            }
            verifier.simulate_block(block, &entry, &mut state, &mut exit);
            entry_states.set(block, &entry);
            exit_states.set(block, &exit);
            changed = true;
        }
    }

    verifier.checking = true;
    for block in block_ids {
        match entry_states.get(block) {
            Some(entry) => {
                verifier.check_phi_inputs(block, &exit_states);
                verifier.simulate_block(block, entry, &mut state, &mut exit);
            }
            None => verifier.error(format_args!("b{} is unreachable", block.0)),
        }
    }

    if verifier.errors.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(verifier.errors)
    }
}

impl Verifier<'_, '_> {
    fn error(&mut self, message: fmt::Arguments<'_>) {
        if self.checking {
            if !self.errors.is_empty() {
                self.errors.push('\n');
            }
            self.errors.write_fmt(message);
        }
    }

    fn content_of_value(&self, value: NodeId) -> Content {
        if matches!(self.graph.node(value).op, Op::VirtualObject { .. }) {
            return Content::Constant(crate::ir::value::EMPTY);
        }
        if let Op::LoadSlot { slot } = self.graph.node(value).op
            && self.graph.is_unwritten_slot(slot)
        {
            return Content::UnwrittenSlot(slot);
        }
        match self.graph.constant_value(value) {
            Some(bits) => Content::Constant(bits),
            None => Content::Value(value),
        }
    }

    fn read(&self, state: &(impl Holds + ?Sized), location: Location) -> Option<Content> {
        match location {
            Location::Constant(bits) => Some(Content::Constant(bits)),
            Location::Frame(slot) if self.graph.is_unwritten_slot(slot) => Some(Content::UnwrittenSlot(slot)),
            _ => state.holds(location),
        }
    }

    /// Writes to `out` the state at the start of `block`: what holds at the end of all its predecessors seen so far,
    /// with the phis in place. Returns false if no predecessor was seen yet. `state` is for the work.
    fn entry_state(
        &self,
        block: BlockId,
        exit_states: &States,
        state: &mut State,
        out: &mut ZoneVec<'_, (Location, Content)>,
    ) -> bool {
        out.clear();
        // NB: The entry and the on-stack replacement entries start with
        //     every value in the frame.
        let block_data = self.graph.block(block);
        if block.0 == 0 || block_data.predecessors.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let mut seen = false;
        for predecessor in &block_data.predecessors {
            let Some(exit) = exit_states.get(*predecessor) else {
                continue;
            };
            state.load(exit);
            for (phi, input) in phi_inputs_from(self.graph, *predecessor, block) {
                let output = self.allocation.node(phi).output.expect("phis have a location");
                for location in core::iter::once(output).chain(self.filled_slot(phi)) {
                    if self.read(&*state, location) == Some(self.content_of_value(input)) {
                        state.insert(location, Content::Value(phi));
                    } else {
                        state.remove(location);
                    }
                }
            }
            if seen {
                out.retain(|(location, content)| state.holds(*location) == Some(*content));
            } else {
                state.store(out);
                seen = true;
            }
        }
        seen
    }

    fn check_phi_inputs(&mut self, block: BlockId, exit_states: &States) {
        let graph = self.graph;
        for predecessor in graph.block(block).predecessors.iter().copied() {
            let Some(exit) = exit_states.get(predecessor) else {
                continue;
            };
            for (phi, input) in phi_inputs_from(self.graph, predecessor, block) {
                let output = self.allocation.node(phi).output.expect("phis have a location");
                for location in core::iter::once(output).chain(self.filled_slot(phi)) {
                    let found = self.read(exit, location);
                    if found != Some(self.content_of_value(input)) {
                        self.error(format_args!(
                            "phi v{} in b{}: input from b{} should be {:?} in {location:?}, found {found:?}",
                            phi.0,
                            block.0,
                            predecessor.0,
                            self.content_of_value(input)
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The spill slot of a phi in a register that its inputs fill, rather
    /// than a store at the start of its block.
    fn filled_slot(&self, phi: NodeId) -> Option<Location> {
        let allocation = self.allocation.node(phi);
        match (allocation.output, allocation.spill_slot) {
            (Some(Location::Register(_)), Some(slot))
                if super::phi_spill_store(self.graph, self.allocation, phi).is_none() =>
            {
                Some(Location::Stack(slot))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn apply_moves(&mut self, state: &mut State, moves: &[Move], context: Context) {
        for m in moves {
            if matches!(m.to, Location::Constant(_) | Location::Frame(_)) {
                self.error(format_args!("{context}: move into {:?}", m.to));
                continue;
            }
            self.check_location(m.to, context);
            match self.read(state, m.from) {
                Some(content) => {
                    state.insert(m.to, content);
                }
                None => {
                    self.error(format_args!("{context}: move reads {:?}, which holds nothing", m.from));
                    state.remove(m.to);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn check_location(&mut self, location: Location, context: Context) {
        if let Location::Register(register) = location
            && !self
                .registers
                .allocatable(super::RegisterClass::General)
                .contains(register)
            && !self
                .registers
                .allocatable(super::RegisterClass::Float)
                .contains(register)
        {
            self.error(format_args!("{context}: r{register} is not allocatable"));
        }
    }

    fn expect(&mut self, state: &State, location: Location, value: NodeId, context: Context) {
        let expected = self.content_of_value(value);
        let found = self.read(state, location);
        if found != Some(expected) {
            self.error(format_args!(
                "{context}: expected {expected:?} in {location:?}, found {found:?}"
            ));
        }
    }

    fn check_exit_values(&mut self, state: &State, node: NodeId, context: Context) {
        let Some(frame_state) = self.graph.node(node).frame_state else {
            return;
        };
        let expected_count = self.graph.frame_state_values(frame_state, self.work).count();
        let exit_values = self.allocation.node(node).exit_values;
        if expected_count != exit_values.len() {
            self.error(format_args!(
                "{context}: exit has {} values, frame state {}",
                exit_values.len(),
                expected_count
            ));
            return;
        }
        for ((slot, value), (exit_slot, location)) in
            self.graph.frame_state_values(frame_state, self.work).zip(exit_values)
        {
            if slot != *exit_slot {
                self.error(format_args!(
                    "{context}: exit value for slot {exit_slot}, frame state slot {slot}"
                ));
            }
            self.expect(state, *location, value, Context::ExitValue(node, slot));
        }
    }

    /// Writes to `out` what holds at the end of `block`, which starts with `entry`. `state` is for the work.
    fn simulate_block(
        &mut self,
        block: BlockId,
        entry: &[(Location, Content)],
        state: &mut State,
        out: &mut ZoneVec<'_, (Location, Content)>,
    ) {
        state.load(entry);
        let block_data = self.graph.block(block);
        // Phis in registers are stored to their spill slots first, unless
        // their inputs filled them already (see `filled_slot()`).
        for phi in &block_data.phis {
            if let Some(slot) = super::phi_spill_store(self.graph, self.allocation, *phi) {
                state.insert(Location::Stack(slot), Content::Value(*phi));
            }
        }
        for node in &block_data.body {
            self.simulate_node(state, *node);
        }
        let end_moves = self.allocation.block_end_moves(block);
        self.apply_moves(state, end_moves, Context::EndOfBlock(block));
        self.simulate_node(state, self.graph.control_id(block));
        state.store(out);
    }

    fn simulate_node(&mut self, state: &mut State, node_id: NodeId) {
        let node = self.graph.node(node_id);
        let allocation = self.allocation.node(node_id);
        let context = Context::Node(node_id);
        debug_assert!(node.op != Op::Phi);

        self.apply_moves(state, allocation.moves_before, context);
        if let Op::StoreSlot { slot } = node.op
            && self.graph.is_unwritten_slot(slot)
        {
            self.error(format_args!("{context}: stores to slot {slot}, which nothing writes"));
        }
        if allocation.inputs.len() != node.inputs.len() {
            self.error(format_args!("{context}: wrong number of input locations"));
            return;
        }
        let lowering = lowering_info(node);
        if allocation.temps.len() != usize::from(lowering.temps) {
            self.error(format_args!(
                "{context}: {} temps, but its lowering takes {}",
                allocation.temps.len(),
                lowering.temps
            ));
        }
        for (index, (input, location)) in node.inputs.iter().zip(allocation.inputs).enumerate() {
            if let Location::Constant(bits) = location {
                if self.graph.constant_value(*input) != Some(*bits) {
                    self.error(format_args!("{context}: input {index} is not the constant {bits:#x}"));
                }
                continue;
            }
            // NB: Slow path calls, and calls that store their operands, read
            //     them from where they are.
            let reads_input_anywhere = lowering.inputs.get(index) == InputConstraint::Anywhere;
            if !matches!(location, Location::Register(_)) && !reads_input_anywhere {
                self.error(format_args!("{context}: input {index} is not in a register"));
            }
            if let InputConstraint::Fixed(register) = self.registers.resolve(lowering.inputs.get(index), false)
                && *location != Location::Register(self.registers.fixed(register))
            {
                self.error(format_args!("{context}: input {index} is not in its fixed register"));
            }
            self.check_location(*location, context);
            self.expect(state, *location, *input, Context::Input(node_id, index));
        }

        // A node may exit at any point after reading its inputs, including
        // after it wrote its temps and its output: exit values must survive both.
        for temp in allocation.temps {
            self.check_location(Location::Register(*temp), context);
            if allocation.inputs.contains(&Location::Register(*temp)) {
                self.error(format_args!("{context}: temp r{temp} is also an input"));
            }
            state.remove(Location::Register(*temp));
        }
        let clobbered = match lowering.clobbers {
            Clobbers::CallerSaved => self.registers.caller_saved(),
            Clobbers::Floats => self.registers.allocatable(super::RegisterClass::Float),
            Clobbers::Nothing => super::RegisterMask::default(),
        };
        for register in clobbered.iter() {
            state.remove(Location::Register(register));
        }
        if let Some(output @ Location::Register(_)) = allocation.output {
            // NB: Cloning the state instead would take time quadratic in the size of code that keeps many values in
            //     their stack slots past many nodes.
            let previous = state.remove(output);
            self.check_exit_values(state, node_id, context);
            if let Some(previous) = previous {
                state.insert(output, previous);
            }
        } else {
            self.check_exit_values(state, node_id, context);
        }

        match (node.repr.is_some(), allocation.output) {
            (true, Some(Location::Register(register))) => {
                self.check_location(Location::Register(register), context);
                if super::RegisterClass::of_register(register) != super::RegisterClass::of(node.repr) {
                    self.error(format_args!(
                        "{context}: the output is in a register of the other class"
                    ));
                }
                state.insert(Location::Register(register), self.content_of_value(node_id));
                if let Some(slot) = allocation.spill_slot {
                    state.insert(Location::Stack(slot), self.content_of_value(node_id));
                }
            }
            (false, None) => {}
            (_, output) => self.error(format_args!("{context}: unexpected output location {output:?}")),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn states_keep_the_order_of_the_locations_and_their_places() {
        let work = crate::test_work();
        let mut state = State::new_in(4, &work);
        let mut stored = ZoneVec::new_in(&work);
        state.insert(Location::Stack(3), Content::Constant(1));
        state.insert(Location::Register(200), Content::Value(NodeId(2)));
        state.insert(Location::Register(1), Content::Value(NodeId(3)));
        state.insert(Location::Stack(0), Content::UnwrittenSlot(4));
        assert_eq!(state.remove(Location::Stack(3)), Some(Content::Constant(1)));
        state.insert(Location::Stack(3), Content::Constant(5));
        state.insert(Location::Frame(7), Content::Constant(6));
        state.store(&mut stored);
        let expected = [
            (Location::Register(1), Content::Value(NodeId(3))),
            (Location::Register(200), Content::Value(NodeId(2))),
            (Location::Stack(0), Content::UnwrittenSlot(4)),
            (Location::Stack(3), Content::Constant(5)),
        ];
        assert_eq!(stored, expected);
        assert_eq!(stored.holds(Location::Stack(0)), Some(Content::UnwrittenSlot(4)));
        assert_eq!(stored.holds(Location::Stack(1)), None);
        assert_eq!(state.holds(Location::Frame(7)), None);

        state.load(&expected[1..]);
        assert_eq!(state.holds(Location::Register(1)), None);
        assert_eq!(state.holds(Location::Register(200)), Some(Content::Value(NodeId(2))));

        let mut states = States::new_in(2, &work);
        assert_eq!(states.get(BlockId(1)), None);
        states.set(BlockId(1), &expected);
        states.set(BlockId(0), &expected[..1]);
        assert_eq!(states.get(BlockId(1)), Some(&expected[..]));
        // NB: A smaller state takes the place of the one before it, and a larger one goes to new room.
        states.set(BlockId(1), &expected[2..]);
        assert_eq!(states.items.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(states.get(BlockId(1)), Some(&expected[2..]));
        states.set(BlockId(0), &expected[..2]);
        assert_eq!(states.items.len(), 7);
        assert_eq!(states.get(BlockId(0)), Some(&expected[..2]));
        assert_eq!(states.get(BlockId(1)), Some(&expected[2..]));
    }
}

//! The memory a thread compiles with.

use ak::Zone;

/// What a compile keeps its data in, apart from what the heap still holds of it. A thread that compiles has one, and
/// every compile of the thread uses it: a compile leaves nothing in it that the next one reads, only the memory.
/// The memory is in four ranges of address space that are the scratch's own, so all of it can go back to the system
/// at any time between two compiles (see `release_memory()`), whatever else the process allocated since.
pub struct Scratch {
    /// Where the graph of a compile is, with all the lists of its nodes, blocks and frame states. A compile starts
    /// with a zone that holds nothing.
    pub(crate) zone: Zone,
    /// Where the stages of a compile keep the data that only they use. The driver drops the data of the builder,
    /// and of each pass, when it ends. The register allocator keeps the allocation here, with its own work data,
    /// for the code generator, so those stay until the compile ends, with the data of the code generator and of the
    /// tables of the code.
    pub(crate) work: Zone,
    /// Where a stage that repeats a step keeps the data of one step, which the step drops when it ends. A stage
    /// keeps what lasts from one step to the next in `work`. So a stage whose steps each make data as large as the
    /// graph takes the memory of one step, not of all of them. A stage whose steps hand data on to later steps
    /// keeps that data in one of the two zones; when that zone holds much more than the data still in use, the
    /// stage moves the data in use to the other zone and resets the first (see `check_elimination`). The driver
    /// empties both after each stage.
    pub(crate) steps: [Zone; 2],
}

impl Default for Scratch {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// The most bytes that a zone of a compile gives out. It is address space, which costs nothing before it is used, and
/// it is far above what the largest function that the builder accepts takes.
const ZONE_LIMIT: usize = 1 << 34;

impl Scratch {
    /// A scratch, which takes no memory before a compile uses it.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            zone: Zone::new(ZONE_LIMIT, c"JIT graph"),
            work: Zone::new(ZONE_LIMIT, c"JIT work"),
            steps: [Zone::new(ZONE_LIMIT, c"JIT step"), Zone::new(ZONE_LIMIT, c"JIT step 2")],
        }
    }

    /// Drops the data of the compile that ended. The zones keep their memory, so that the next compile of the thread
    /// does not take it from the system again: a thread that has no compile for a while gives it back (see
    /// `release_memory()`).
    pub(crate) fn end_compile(&mut self) {
        let [step, other_step] = &mut self.steps;
        for zone in [&mut self.zone, &mut self.work, step, other_step] {
            zone.reset();
        }
    }

    /// Gives the memory of the scratch back to the system. The next compile takes memory again.
    pub fn release_memory(&mut self) {
        let [step, other_step] = &mut self.steps;
        for zone in [&mut self.zone, &mut self.work, step, other_step] {
            zone.reset();
            zone.trim(0);
        }
    }
}
