    pub execution_context_yield_is_await: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::yield_value_is_iterator_result` (bool).
    pub execution_context_yield_value_is_iterator_result: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::caller_is_construct` (bool).
    pub execution_context_caller_is_construct: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::this_value` (a value, empty if absent).
    pub execution_context_this_value: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::caller_frame` (pointer).
    pub execution_context_caller_frame: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::passed_argument_count` (u32).
    pub execution_context_passed_argument_count: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::caller_return_pc` (u32).
    pub execution_context_caller_return_pc: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::caller_dst_raw` (u32).
    pub execution_context_caller_dst_raw: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::registers_and_constants_and_locals_and_arguments_count` (u32).
    pub execution_context_slot_count: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::argument_count` (u32).
    pub execution_context_argument_count: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::returns_to_native_caller` (bool).
    pub execution_context_returns_to_native_caller: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::runs_jit_code` (bool).
    pub execution_context_runs_jit_code: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::caller_is_derived_construct` (bool).
    pub execution_context_caller_is_derived_construct: u32,
    /// `ExecutionContext::new_target` (a value).
    pub execution_context_new_target: u32,
    /// `EcmascriptFunctionObject::environment` (cell pointer).
    pub ecmascript_function_environment: u32,
    /// `EcmascriptFunctionObjectWithRareData::private_environment` (cell
    /// pointer), of functions with the flag for it.
    pub ecmascript_function_private_environment: u32,
    /// `Object::class_bits` (u8).
    pub object_class_bits: u32,
    /// The bit of `Object::class_bits` of an ECMAScript function that has
    /// a private environment field.
    pub ecmascript_function_flag_has_rare_data: u32,
    /// `VmHead::execution_generation` (u32).
    pub vm_execution_generation: u32,
}

/// How much one compile job inlines, in bytecode instructions of the callees.
/// The default inlines nothing.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct InliningLimits {
    /// Callees of at most this many instructions are always inlined.
    pub always_inlined_instructions: u32,
    /// Otherwise, callees of at most this many instructions are inlined...
    pub max_instructions: u32,
    /// ...as long as all inlined callees together have at most this many.
    pub budget_instructions: u32,
    /// Constructors of at most this many instructions are inlined into
    /// their constructs whatever the budget says: constructs that are not
    /// inlined go through the generic construct path, which costs more than
    /// most constructors that only initialize the properties of `this`.
    pub max_construct_instructions: u32,
    /// Inlined calls nest at most this deep.
    pub max_depth: u32,
}

/// Options of one compile job.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct CompileOptions {
    /// Return the IR and the register allocation as text in `CompiledCode::dump`.
    pub dump_ir: bool,
    /// Return the IR after building it and after every pass as text in
    /// `CompiledCode::dump`, each headed by "=== after <pass>".
    pub dump_passes: bool,
    /// Return the machine code, annotated with the IR, as text in `CompiledCode::dump`.
    pub dump_asm: bool,
    /// Check the invariants of the IR between passes, also in release builds.
    pub verify_ir: bool,
    /// The loop back edge whose tier-up budget ran out, if a loop (rather
    /// than calls) triggered the compile. Only it gets an on-stack
    /// replacement entry: such an entry merges into the loop, which costs
    /// every iteration.
    pub osr_pc: Option<u32>,
    /// Whether the compiled executable is top-level code, which runs once: no frame of it enters the code at its
    /// start once a loop triggered the compile.
    pub runs_once: bool,
    pub inlining: InliningLimits,
    pub stress: StressOptions,
    /// Return what the code contains in `CompiledCode::coverage`.
    pub coverage: bool,
}

/// Options that make compiled code take its rare paths often, for testing
/// the compiler. All of them are off by default.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct StressOptions {
    /// The address of a u32 that compiled code counts down before every
    /// node that can exit, taking the node's exit when it reaches 0 (the
    /// runtime then sets it again), or 0 for none. Every node may exit at
    /// its start, before it has any effect, so these exits are always
    /// correct; they show whether the frame states are.
    pub exit_countdown: u64,
    /// Every loop back edge that ran gets an on-stack replacement entry,
    /// not only `CompileOptions::osr_pc`.
    pub osr_at_every_loop: bool,
    /// The register allocator assigns values only to the registers calls
    /// take their arguments and return their results in and two more, so
    /// that values get spilled and reloaded far more often.
    pub few_registers: bool,
}

/// A list of rows of type `T` of a snapshot. The snapshot gives its rows: `&snapshot[list]`. A list is only good for
/// the snapshot it was added to.
pub type List<T> = ak::RowList<T>;

/// A list of a snapshot that is being written row by row (see `SnapshotWriter::begin()`).
#[must_use]
pub struct ListStart<T> {
    rows: PhantomData<fn() -> T>,
}

/// A type that snapshots have lists of.
pub trait Row: Copy + Send + Sync + 'static {
    #[doc(hidden)]
    const INDEX: usize;
    #[doc(hidden)]
    fn open(lists: &OpenLists) -> &Column<Self>;
    #[doc(hidden)]
    fn open_mut(lists: &mut OpenLists) -> &mut Column<Self>;
}

/// How many bytes of rows a list that is written row by row holds at most.
const MAX_OPEN_LIST_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

/// The most bytes that the scratch zone of a capture gives out. It is address space, which costs nothing before it
/// is used.
const MAX_CAPTURE_SCRATCH_BYTES: usize = 1 << 30;

macro_rules! rows {
    ($($name:ident: $row:ty,)*) => {
        #[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
        enum RowIndex {
            $($name,)*
        }

        const ROW_TYPE_COUNT: usize = [$(RowIndex::$name,)*].len();

        /// For each type of row, the rows of the list that is being written row by row, if one is. A snapshot is
        /// one block of lists, so the rows of a list have to be next to each other, and lists of other types get
        /// written while the list gets its rows. So the rows wait here until the list ends.
        ///
        /// This is memory that comes straight from the system, and it keeps that memory: one of these serves
        /// capture after capture, and its memory goes back to the system as a whole when it is dropped.
        #[derive(Debug)]
        pub struct OpenLists {
            $($name: Column<$row>,)*
            /// Whether a list of each type is being written.
            open: [bool; ROW_TYPE_COUNT],
            /// Where a step of a capture keeps data that only it reads, like the array of the instruction that a
            /// walk over bytecode is at. It holds nothing from one step to the next.
            scratch: Zone,
        }

        impl OpenLists {
            pub fn new() -> Self {
                Self {
                    $($name: Column::new(MAX_OPEN_LIST_BYTES / size_of::<$row>(), c"JIT snapshot open lists"),)*
                    open: [false; ROW_TYPE_COUNT],
                    scratch: Zone::new(MAX_CAPTURE_SCRATCH_BYTES, c"JIT snapshot scratch"),
                }
            }

            /// Drops the lists that are being written.
            fn reset(&mut self) {
                $(self.$name.clear();)*
                self.open = [false; ROW_TYPE_COUNT];
                self.scratch.reset();
            }
        }

        impl Default for OpenLists {
            fn default() -> Self {
                Self::new()
            }
        }

        $(
            impl Row for $row {
                const INDEX: usize = RowIndex::$name as usize;

                fn open(lists: &OpenLists) -> &Column<Self> {
                    &lists.$name
                }

                fn open_mut(lists: &mut OpenLists) -> &mut Column<Self> {
                    &mut lists.$name
                }
            }
        )*
    };
}

rows! {
    bytes: u8,
    halves: u16,
    offsets: u32,
    words: u64,
    cells: CellId,
    exception_handlers: ExceptionHandler,
    exit_sites: (u32, ExitKind),
    builtin_exit_sites: (CellId, u32, ExitKind),
    property_caches: PropertyCacheSnapshot,
    property_cache_entries: PropertyCacheEntrySnapshot,
    call_feedback: CallFeedbackSnapshot,
    keyed_feedback: KeyedFeedbackSnapshot,
    captured_bindings: (EnvironmentCoordinate, GlobalValueSnapshot),
    mutable_bindings: EnvironmentCoordinate,
    object_shape_caches: Option<ObjectShapeCacheSnapshot>,
    closure_templates: Option<ClosureTemplateSnapshot>,
    lexical_environment_templates: Option<LexicalEnvironmentTemplateSnapshot>,
    environment_templates: EnvironmentTemplateSnapshot,
    global_caches: Option<GlobalCacheSnapshot>,
    literal_fields: (u32, u64),
    derived_fields: (u32, u64, Option<CellId>),
    object_size_classes: ObjectSizeClass,
    storage_size_classes: StorageSizeClass,
}

/// The input of one compile job.
///
/// The thread of the VM writes it and a compile thread reads it. All its lists are in one block of memory, list
/// after list, and its executables are in a second one. Both come straight from the system and go back there as a
/// whole. A snapshot that was cleared keeps its memory for what is written next, so a snapshot that is used again
/// and again takes nothing from the system and nothing from the heap.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Snapshot {
    /// Index 0 is the function being compiled; the rest are inlining candidates.
    pub executables: Column<ExecutableSnapshot>,
    rows: RowBlock,
    pub runtime: RuntimeInfo,
    pub options: CompileOptions,
    /// Whether a row had no room (see `is_complete()`).
    overflowed: bool,
}

impl Snapshot {
    const MAX_EXECUTABLES: usize = 1 << 16;
    /// How many bytes of rows the lists of a snapshot hold at most. A capture that needs more gives a snapshot that
    /// is not complete (see `is_complete()`).
    const MAX_ROW_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
    /// How many bytes of rows and how many executables a snapshot keeps the memory for when it serves the next
    /// capture: the first step its memory grows by.
    const SPARE_ROW_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;
    const SPARE_EXECUTABLES: usize = 64 * 1024 / size_of::<ExecutableSnapshot>();

    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            executables: Column::new(Self::MAX_EXECUTABLES, c"JIT snapshot executables"),
            rows: RowBlock::new(Self::MAX_ROW_BYTES, c"JIT snapshot rows"),
            runtime: RuntimeInfo::default(),
            options: CompileOptions::default(),
            overflowed: false,
        }
    }

    /// Makes this a snapshot of nothing, which keeps its memory. The lists of the snapshot are lists of no snapshot
    /// after this.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.executables.clear();
        self.rows.clear();
        self.runtime = RuntimeInfo::default();
        self.options = CompileOptions::default();
        self.overflowed = false;
    }

    /// Gives memory back to the system: what is above the needs of a usual snapshot.
    pub fn trim(&mut self) {
        self.executables.trim(Self::SPARE_EXECUTABLES);
        self.rows.trim(Self::SPARE_ROW_BYTES);
    }

    /// Whether the snapshot holds all that was written into it. One that does not is too large to compile, and has
    /// lists that miss rows.
    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
        !self.overflowed
    }

    /// Adds an executable, and returns its index.
    pub fn add_executable(&mut self, executable: ExecutableSnapshot) -> u32 {
        let index = self.executables.len() as u32;
        if self.executables.try_push(executable).is_err() {
            self.overflowed = true;
        }
        index
    }

    /// Adds `rows` as a list.
    pub fn add<T: Row>(&mut self, rows: &[T]) -> List<T> {
        self.rows.try_add(rows).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            self.overflowed = true;
            List::empty()
        })
    }
}

impl Default for Snapshot {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl<T: Row> Index<List<T>> for Snapshot {
    type Output = [T];

    fn index(&self, list: List<T>) -> &[T] {
        self.rows.rows(list)
    }
}

impl<T: Row> IndexMut<List<T>> for Snapshot {
    fn index_mut(&mut self, list: List<T>) -> &mut [T] {
        self.rows.rows_mut(list)
    }
}

/// A snapshot that is being captured, with what writes its lists row by row: `begin()`, `push()` and `end()`. A list
/// that is ready is added in one go, with `Snapshot::add()`.
pub struct SnapshotWriter<'a> {
    snapshot: &'a mut Snapshot,
    lists: OpenLists,
}

impl<'a> SnapshotWriter<'a> {
    /// Writes into `snapshot`, with the memory of `lists` for the lists that are written row by row.
    pub fn new(snapshot: &'a mut Snapshot, mut lists: OpenLists) -> Self {
        lists.reset();
        Self { snapshot, lists }
    }

    /// The memory for lists that are written row by row, for the next capture. The snapshot keeps what was written.
    pub fn finish(self) -> OpenLists {
        self.lists
    }

    /// A zone for data that one step of the capture reads and then drops (see `Zone::scope()`). Its memory serves
    /// capture after capture, like that of the lists that are written row by row.
    pub fn scratch(&mut self) -> &mut Zone {
        &mut self.lists.scratch
    }

    /// Starts a list, which gets the rows that `push()` adds until `end()`. Only one list of a type of row can be
    /// written at a time.
    pub fn begin<T: Row>(&mut self) -> ListStart<T> {
        // NB: Rows of two lists that mix would be wrong input for the compiler, so this is checked in every build.
        assert!(!self.lists.open[T::INDEX], "another list of this type is being written");
        self.lists.open[T::INDEX] = true;
        ListStart { rows: PhantomData }
    }

    /// Adds a row to the list of its type that is being written.
    pub fn push<T: Row>(&mut self, row: T) {
        assert!(self.lists.open[T::INDEX], "no list of this type is being written");
        if T::open_mut(&mut self.lists).try_push(row).is_err() {
            self.snapshot.overflowed = true;
        }
    }

    /// The rows that the list that is being written has so far.
    pub fn rows_of<T: Row>(&self, _list: &ListStart<T>) -> &[T] {
        T::open(&self.lists)
    }

    /// Drops the rows of the list that is being written.
    pub fn drop_rows<T: Row>(&mut self, _list: &ListStart<T>) {
        T::open_mut(&mut self.lists).clear();
    }

    /// Ends the list that is being written, and adds it to the snapshot.
    pub fn end<T: Row>(&mut self, _list: ListStart<T>) -> List<T> {
        assert!(self.lists.open[T::INDEX], "no list of this type is being written");
        self.lists.open[T::INDEX] = false;
        let rows = T::open_mut(&mut self.lists);
        let list = self.snapshot.add(rows);
        rows.clear();
        list
    }
}

impl Deref for SnapshotWriter<'_> {
    type Target = Snapshot;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Snapshot {
        self.snapshot
    }
}

impl DerefMut for SnapshotWriter<'_> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Snapshot {
        self.snapshot
    }
}

/// The VM's strings of the results of `typeof`, as values.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TypeofStrings {
    pub number: u64,
    pub undefined: u64,
    pub object: u64,
    pub string: u64,
    pub symbol: u64,

/// What the inline code of compiled nodes needs to know about the runtime's
/// data structures beyond `RuntimeOffsets`: offsets of their fields (byte
/// offsets into the named objects), the values of their flags and kinds,
/// and the addresses of the VM's caches, as `jit/runtime_info.rs` fills

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RuntimeLayout {
    /// `Object::indexed_elements`: a pointer to the first `Value` of the
    /// indexed elements buffer, or null.

    /// `Object::indexed_array_like_size` (u32).

    pub indexed_elements_capacity: i32,

    /// `IndexedStorageKind::Holey`.
    pub indexed_storage_kind_none: u8,
    pub indexed_storage_kind_packed: u8,
    pub indexed_storage_kind_holey: u8,
    /// `Object::Flag::IsExtensible`.
    pub object_flag_is_extensible: u16,
    /// `Object::Flag::HasMagicalLengthProperty`, which only arrays have.
    pub object_flag_has_magical_length: u16,
    /// The classes (pointers) of plain objects, of `StringObject`s and of
    /// `%String.prototype%`.
    pub object_class: u64,
    pub string_object_class: u64,
    pub string_prototype_class: u64,
    /// `Object::Flag::MayInterfereWithIndexedPropertyAccess`.
    pub object_flag_may_interfere: u16,
    /// Where an array keeps its flags (u8), and the bits of them that say that its length is not writable and that it
    /// is the target of a proxy.
    pub array_flags: u32,
    pub array_flag_length_not_writable: u8,
    pub array_flag_is_proxy_target: u8,
    /// `Shape::prototype`.
    pub shape_prototype: u32,
    /// `Object::Flag::IsTypedArray`.
    pub object_flag_is_typed_array: u16,
    /// `Object::Flag::IsHTMLDDA`.
    pub object_flag_is_htmldda: u16,
    /// `Object::Flag::IsPlatformObject` and `Object::Flag::IsGlobalObject`.
    pub object_flag_is_platform_object: u16,
    pub object_flag_is_global_object: u16,
    /// `Object::Flag::RequiresSlowAddOwnProperty`.
    pub object_flag_requires_slow_add_own_property: u16,
    /// The capacity (u32) of heap named property storage, relative to the
    /// pointer to its first property.
    pub named_properties_capacity: i32,
    /// `Shape::property_count` (u32).
    pub shape_property_count: u32,
    /// `TypedArrayBase::cached_data_offset` (u64): the offset of the
    /// element data in the primitive storage cage, or
    /// `typed_array_cached_data_offset_invalid`.
    pub typed_array_cached_data_offset: u32,
    pub typed_array_cached_data_offset_invalid: u64,
    /// `TypedArrayBase::array_length.length` (u64).
    pub typed_array_array_length: u32,
    /// `TypedArrayBase::kind` (u8).
    pub typed_array_kind: u32,
    /// `TypedArrayBase::Kind` values.
    pub typed_array_kind_uint8: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_uint8_clamped: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_uint16: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_uint32: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_int8: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_int16: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_int32: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_float32: u8,
    pub typed_array_kind_float64: u8,
    /// `GC::PrimitiveStorage::cage_offset_mask`. Compiled code finds typed
    /// array elements at `primitive_storage_cage_base + (cached_data_offset &
    /// cage_offset_mask) + byte_index`, for 32-bit indices, which
    /// `GC::PrimitiveStorage::cage_guard_size` keeps within reach.
    pub primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask: u64,
    /// `PrimitiveString::length_in_utf16_code_units` (u32).
    pub primitive_string_length: u32,
    /// `PrimitiveString::utf16_string`: the word of the string's storage,
    /// once it has one, which is the identity of a fly string.
    pub primitive_string_storage: u32,
    /// The byte of `PrimitiveString` that holds its interned flag, and the flag's bit
    /// in it: a string is interned if `byte & primitive_string_interned_mask` is not 0.
    pub primitive_string_is_interned: u32,
    pub primitive_string_interned_mask: u8,
    /// The bits of the same byte that hold the kind of a deferred string
    /// (a rope, a substring or an inline string), which has no storage yet:
    /// 0 once resolved.
    pub primitive_string_deferred_kind_mask: u8,
    /// The deferred kind of inline strings, which keep their ASCII bytes in
    /// the cell, at `primitive_string_inline_storage`.
    pub primitive_string_deferred_kind_inline: u8,
    pub primitive_string_inline_storage: u32,
    /// Short `Utf16String`s keep their ASCII bytes in the storage word: its
    /// lowest byte holds `utf16_short_string_flag` and the byte count,
    /// shifted left by `utf16_short_string_byte_count_shift`, and the bytes
    /// follow. Other storage words point at a `Utf16StringData`.
    pub utf16_short_string_flag: u8,
    pub utf16_short_string_byte_count_shift: u8,
    /// `Utf16StringDataHeader::flags` (u32), and its flag for storage of UTF-16
    /// code units rather than ASCII bytes.
    pub utf16_string_data_flags: u32,
    pub utf16_string_data_has_utf16_storage: u32,
    /// Where the code units of a `Utf16StringData` start.
    pub utf16_string_data_storage: u32,
    /// The address of the VM's array of the strings of the 128 ASCII
    /// characters (cell pointers), or 0 for code without one.
    pub single_ascii_character_strings: u64,
    /// `Object::class_bits` (u8): the builtin a function is plus one, if
    /// it is one.
    pub function_object_builtin: u32,
    /// `Builtin` values.
    pub builtin_string_prototype_char_code_at: u8,
    pub builtin_string_prototype_char_at: u8,

//! Lists in the tables of a compile.
//!
//! The data of a compile is rows in columns: lists in a zone, with one element for each row. Where a row has a list
//! of something, the elements of the list are next to each other in a column that holds the lists of all the rows,
//! and the row says which part of that column is its own. So a compile makes one list in its zone for all the lists
//! of a kind, however many lists it has.

use core::ops::Range;

use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneVec;

/// The elements of one list: a part of a column that holds many lists.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Run {
    start: u32,
    len: u32,
}

impl Run {
    /// In place of the elements of a list that is not written yet. It is a part of no column.
    pub const NOT_WRITTEN: Run = Run {
        start: u32::MAX,
        len: 0,
    };

    /// The elements from index `start` to index `end` of a column, without the one at `end`.
    pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
        // NB: A list of a zone holds fewer than 2^32 elements.
        let start = u32::try_from(start).expect("the columns of a compile have 32-bit indices");
        let end = u32::try_from(end).expect("the columns of a compile have 32-bit indices");
        Self {
            start,
            len: end - start,
        }
    }

    /// Where the elements are in their column.
    pub fn range(self) -> Range<usize> {
        self.start as usize..self.start as usize + self.len as usize
    }

    pub fn len(self) -> usize {
        self.len as usize
    }

    pub fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0
    }
}

/// A list of `T` for each index from 0 on, all in one column, in the order of the indices.
///
/// The lists are written in one of two ways. In the order of their indices: `begin()`, then for each index `push()`
/// for its elements and `end_list()`. Or in any order, when it is known first how long each list is:
/// `begin_counts()`, `count()` for each element, `end_counts()`, `fill()` for each element, `end_fill()`.
pub struct Lists<'w, T: Copy> {
    /// Where the list of each index starts in `items`, and one more: where the last list ends.
    starts: ZoneVec<'w, u32>,
    items: ZoneVec<'w, T>,
}

impl<'w, T: Copy> Lists<'w, T> {
    /// Lists for no index, which take no memory before they have some.
    pub fn new_in(zone: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            starts: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            items: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
        }
    }

    /// Lists for no index, with room for the lists of `lists` indices with `items` elements in all.
    pub fn with_capacity_in(lists: usize, items: usize, zone: &'w Zone) -> Self {
        Self {
            starts: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(lists + 2, zone),
            items: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(items, zone),
        }
    }

    /// How many indices have a list.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.starts.len().saturating_sub(1)
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// The list of `index`.
    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> &[T] {
        &self.items[self.starts[index] as usize..self.starts[index + 1] as usize]
    }

    /// Drops the lists, to write new ones in the order of their indices.
    pub fn begin(&mut self) {
        self.starts.clear();
        self.items.clear();
        self.starts.push(0);
    }

    /// Adds an element to the list that is being written: the list of the first index that has none.
    pub fn push(&mut self, item: T) {
        self.items.push(item);
    }

    /// Ends the list that is being written.
    pub fn end_list(&mut self) {
        // NB: A list of a zone holds fewer than 2^32 elements.
        self.starts.push(self.items.len() as u32);
    }

    /// Drops the lists, to write the lists of the indices below `count` in any order.
    pub fn begin_counts(&mut self, count: usize) {
        self.starts.clear();
        self.items.clear();
        // NB: While the lists are counted and filled, the entry of an index is one place further on, so that the
        //     entries are where get() reads them when all the lists are full (see fill()).
        self.starts.resize(count + 2, 0);
    }

    /// Notes that the list of `index` gets one more element.
    pub fn count(&mut self, index: usize) {
        self.starts[index + 2] += 1;
    }

    /// Makes room for the elements that were counted, as copies of `filler`.
    pub fn end_counts(&mut self, filler: T) {
        let mut total = 0_u32;
        for start in self.starts.iter_mut().skip(2) {
            total = total
                .checked_add(*start)
                .expect("a list of a zone holds fewer than 2^32 elements");
            *start = total;
        }
        self.items.resize(total as usize, filler);
    }

    /// Puts `item` in the next place of the list of `index`, which has a place left.
    pub fn fill(&mut self, index: usize, item: T) {
        let place = self.starts[index + 1];
        self.items[place as usize] = item;
        self.starts[index + 1] = place + 1;
    }

    /// Ends the writing of lists that were counted, when all of them are full.
    pub fn end_fill(&mut self) {
        let count = self.starts.len() - 1;
        debug_assert!(self.starts[count - 1] == self.starts[count]);
        self.starts.truncate(count);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn lists_written_in_the_order_of_their_indices() {
        let mut lists = Lists::new_in(crate::test_zone());
        assert!(lists.is_empty());
        lists.begin();
        lists.push(5_u32);
        lists.push(6);
        lists.end_list();
        lists.end_list();
        lists.push(7);
        lists.end_list();
        assert_eq!(lists.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(lists.get(0), [5, 6]);
        assert_eq!(lists.get(1), []);
        assert_eq!(lists.get(2), [7]);
        lists.begin();
        assert!(lists.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_written_in_any_order() {
        let mut lists = Lists::new_in(crate::test_zone());
        let items = [(2, 'a'), (0, 'b'), (2, 'c'), (3, 'd'), (0, 'e'), (2, 'f')];
        for _ in 0..2 {
            lists.begin_counts(5);
            for (index, _) in items {
                lists.count(index);
            }
            lists.end_counts(' ');
            for (index, item) in items {
                lists.fill(index, item);
            }
            lists.end_fill();
            assert_eq!(lists.len(), 5);
            assert_eq!(lists.get(0), ['b', 'e']);
            assert_eq!(lists.get(1), []);
            assert_eq!(lists.get(2), ['a', 'c', 'f']);
            assert_eq!(lists.get(3), ['d']);
            assert_eq!(lists.get(4), []);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn lists_grow_past_the_room_they_were_made_with() {
        let mut lists = Lists::with_capacity_in(2, 3, crate::test_zone());
        lists.begin_counts(2);
        for _ in 0..4 {
            lists.count(1);
        }
        lists.end_counts(0_u8);
        for item in 0..4 {
            lists.fill(1, item);
        }
        lists.end_fill();
        assert_eq!(lists.get(1), [0, 1, 2, 3]);
        lists.begin();
        for item in 0..4 {
            lists.push(item);
        }
        lists.end_list();
        lists.end_list();
        lists.end_list();
        assert_eq!(lists.len(), 3);
        assert_eq!(lists.get(0), [0, 1, 2, 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_run_is_a_part_of_a_column() {
        let run = Run::new(3, 7);
        assert_eq!(run.range(), 3..7);
        assert_eq!(run.len(), 4);
        assert!(!run.is_empty());
        assert!(Run::default().is_empty());
        assert!(Run::new(9, 9).is_empty());
    }
}

static void set_utf16_fly_string(void* context, u16 const* code_units, size_t length_in_code_units)
{
    auto& string = *static_cast<Utf16FlyString*>(context);
    string = Utf16FlyString::from_utf16(Utf16View { reinterpret_cast<char16_t const*>(code_units), length_in_code_units });
}

Realm& Module::realm()
{
    return cell_ref_from_abi<Realm>(js_module_realm(module_to_abi(*this)));
}

Realm const& Module::realm() const
{
    return cell_ref_from_abi<Realm>(js_module_realm(module_to_abi(*this)));
}

GC::Ptr<ModuleEnvironment> Module::environment()
{
    return reinterpret_cast<ModuleEnvironment*>(js_module_environment(module_to_abi(*this)));
}

GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> Module::host_defined() const
{
    return static_cast<GC::Cell*>(js_module_host_defined(module_to_abi(*this)));
}

ThrowCompletionOr<void> Module::link(VM& vm)
{
    return completion_from_abi<void>(js_module_link(vm_to_abi(vm), module_to_abi(*this)));
}

ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<PromiseCapability>> Module::evaluate(VM& vm)
{
    return completion_from_abi<GC::Ref<PromiseCapability>>(js_module_evaluate(vm_to_abi(vm), module_to_abi(*this)));
}

ResolvedBinding Module::resolve_export(VM& vm, Utf16FlyString const& export_name)
{
    Utf16FlyString binding_name;
    JSResolvedBinding abi_binding {
        .module = nullptr,
        .binding_name = { .context = &binding_name, .append = set_utf16_fly_string },
        .type = JS_RESOLVED_BINDING_NULL,
    };
    js_module_resolve_export(vm_to_abi(vm), module_to_abi(*this), utf16_view_to_abi(export_name.view()), &abi_binding);

    ResolvedBinding binding;
    binding.type = static_cast<ResolvedBinding::Type>(abi_binding.type);
    binding.module = cell_from_abi<Module>(abi_binding.module);
    binding.export_name = move(binding_name);
    return binding;
}

PromiseCapability& Module::load_requested_modules(GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> host_defined)
{
    auto* capability = js_module_load_requested_modules(vm_to_abi(vm()), module_to_abi(*this), host_defined.ptr());
    VERIFY(capability);
    return *reinterpret_cast<PromiseCapability*>(capability);
}

void Module::set_environment(GC::Ref<ModuleEnvironment> environment)
{
    js_host_module_set_environment(module_to_abi(*this), reinterpret_cast<JSEnvironment*>(environment.ptr()));
}

// 16.2.1.10 FinishLoadingImportedModule ( referrer, moduleRequest, payload, result ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule
void finish_loading_imported_module(ImportedModuleReferrer referrer, ModuleRequest const& module_request, ImportedModulePayload payload, ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<Module>> const& result)
{
    ModuleRequestForABI abi_module_request { module_request };
    js_module_finish_loading_imported_module(
        vm_to_abi(VM::the()),
        imported_module_referrer_to_abi(referrer),
        abi_module_request.ptr(),
        imported_module_payload_to_abi(payload),
        module_completion_to_abi(result));
}

}

namespace JS {

struct ResolvedBinding {
    enum Type {
        BindingName,
        Namespace,
        Ambiguous,
        Null,
    };

    static ResolvedBinding null()
    {
        return {};
    }

    static ResolvedBinding ambiguous()
    {
        ResolvedBinding binding;
        binding.type = Ambiguous;
        return binding;
    }

    Type type { Null };
    GC::Ptr<Module> module;
    Utf16FlyString export_name;

    bool is_valid() const
    {
        return type == BindingName || type == Namespace;
    }

    bool is_namespace() const
    {
        return type == Namespace;
    }

    bool is_ambiguous() const
    {
        return type == Ambiguous;
    }
};

// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#graphloadingstate-record
// The state of loading a module graph, which the runtime keeps to itself; a host only passes it back to
// finish_loading_imported_module() in the payload it received.
struct GraphLoadingState final : public EngineCell {
};

// 16.2.1.4 Abstract Module Records, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-abstract-module-records
// A Module Record of the Rust runtime. The facade types of its kinds derive from Module. The abstract methods dispatch
// to the record's kind inside the runtime.
class JS_API Module : public EngineCell {
public:
    Realm& realm();
    Realm const& realm() const;

    GC::Ptr<ModuleEnvironment> environment();

    GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> host_defined() const;

    ThrowCompletionOr<void> link(VM& vm);
    ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<PromiseCapability>> evaluate(VM& vm);

    // The runtime resolves an export with a resolve set of its own, so a host passes none.
    ResolvedBinding resolve_export(VM& vm, Utf16FlyString const& export_name);

    PromiseCapability& load_requested_modules(GC::Ptr<GC::Cell> host_defined);

protected:
    // Only for host modules, whose initialize_environment hook creates their environment.
    void set_environment(GC::Ref<ModuleEnvironment> environment);
};

JS_API void finish_loading_imported_module(ImportedModuleReferrer, ModuleRequest const&, ImportedModulePayload, ThrowCompletionOr<GC::Ref<Module>> const&);

#pragma once

#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/StringView.h>
#include <LibGC/RootVector.h>
#include <LibJS/EmbeddingABIConversions.h>

// Conversions of the object model between the facade and the Rust runtime's embedding ABI: property descriptors, lists
// of keys, lookup phases, inline cache metadata and native functions. Like EmbeddingABIConversions.h, which it builds
// on, only the facade's own .cpp files may include it.

namespace JS::EmbeddingABI {

static_assert(to_underlying(Object::PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty) == JS_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_PHASE_OWN_PROPERTY);
static_assert(to_underlying(Object::PropertyLookupPhase::PrototypeChain) == JS_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_PHASE_PROTOTYPE_CHAIN);

inline JSObject* optional_object_to_abi(Object const* object)
{
    return object ? object_to_abi(*object) : nullptr;
}

inline u8 lookup_phase_to_abi(Object::PropertyLookupPhase phase)
{
    return to_underlying(phase);
}

// The runtime's own inline cache metadata, which passes through the facade unread.
inline JSGetCacheMetadata* get_cache_metadata_to_abi(CacheableGetPropertyMetadata* metadata)
{
    return reinterpret_cast<JSGetCacheMetadata*>(metadata);
}

inline JSSetCacheMetadata* set_cache_metadata_to_abi(CacheableSetPropertyMetadata* metadata)
{
    return reinterpret_cast<JSSetCacheMetadata*>(metadata);
}

inline JSPropertyDescriptor property_descriptor_to_abi(PropertyDescriptor const& descriptor)
{
    JSPropertyDescriptor abi_descriptor {};
    u16 flags = JS_PD_PRESENT;
    if (descriptor.value.has_value()) {
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_VALUE;
        abi_descriptor.value = value_to_abi(*descriptor.value);
    }
    if (descriptor.get.has_value()) {
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_GET;
        abi_descriptor.get = optional_object_to_abi(descriptor.get->ptr());
    }
    if (descriptor.set.has_value()) {
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_SET;
        abi_descriptor.set = optional_object_to_abi(descriptor.set->ptr());
    }
    if (descriptor.writable.has_value())
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_WRITABLE | (*descriptor.writable ? JS_PD_WRITABLE : 0);
    if (descriptor.enumerable.has_value())
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_ENUMERABLE | (*descriptor.enumerable ? JS_PD_ENUMERABLE : 0);
    if (descriptor.configurable.has_value())
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_CONFIGURABLE | (*descriptor.configurable ? JS_PD_CONFIGURABLE : 0);
    if (descriptor.property_offset.has_value()) {
        flags |= JS_PD_HAS_PROPERTY_OFFSET;
        abi_descriptor.property_offset = *descriptor.property_offset;
    }
    abi_descriptor.flags = flags;
    return abi_descriptor;
}

// An absent descriptor is a zeroed one, without JS_PD_PRESENT.
inline JSPropertyDescriptor optional_property_descriptor_to_abi(Optional<PropertyDescriptor> const& descriptor)
{
    if (!descriptor.has_value())
        return {};
    return property_descriptor_to_abi(*descriptor);
}

inline Optional<PropertyDescriptor> property_descriptor_from_abi(JSPropertyDescriptor const& abi_descriptor)
{
    auto flags = abi_descriptor.flags;
    if (!(flags & JS_PD_PRESENT))
        return {};
    // The runtime only ever puts functions in a descriptor's getter and setter.
    auto function_from_abi = [](JSObject* function) -> GC::Ptr<FunctionObject> {
        return reinterpret_cast<FunctionObject*>(function);
    };
    PropertyDescriptor descriptor;
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_VALUE)
        descriptor.value = value_from_abi(abi_descriptor.value);
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_GET)
        descriptor.get = function_from_abi(abi_descriptor.get);
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_SET)
        descriptor.set = function_from_abi(abi_descriptor.set);
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_WRITABLE)
        descriptor.writable = (flags & JS_PD_WRITABLE) != 0;
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_ENUMERABLE)
        descriptor.enumerable = (flags & JS_PD_ENUMERABLE) != 0;
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_CONFIGURABLE)
        descriptor.configurable = (flags & JS_PD_CONFIGURABLE) != 0;
    if (flags & JS_PD_HAS_PROPERTY_OFFSET)
        descriptor.property_offset = abi_descriptor.property_offset;
    return descriptor;
}

// A descriptor that the runtime writes back after defining a property with it, as it does to report the storage offset
// of a new property.
inline void update_property_descriptor_from_abi(PropertyDescriptor& descriptor, JSPropertyDescriptor const& abi_descriptor)
{
    if (auto written_back_descriptor = property_descriptor_from_abi(abi_descriptor); written_back_descriptor.has_value())
        descriptor = written_back_descriptor.release_value();
}

// A [[GetOwnProperty]] result that a caller already has: null for none, and a zeroed descriptor for an absent property.
struct PrecomputedOwnPropertyForABI {
    explicit PrecomputedOwnPropertyForABI(Optional<PropertyDescriptor> const* precomputed_get_own_property)
    {
        if (precomputed_get_own_property)
            abi_descriptor = optional_property_descriptor_to_abi(*precomputed_get_own_property);
        is_present = precomputed_get_own_property != nullptr;
    }

    JSPropertyDescriptor const* pointer() const { return is_present ? &abi_descriptor : nullptr; }

    JSPropertyDescriptor abi_descriptor {};
    bool is_present { false };
};

// A sink that appends what the runtime hands it to a list that roots it.
struct RootedValueSink {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(RootedValueSink);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(RootedValueSink);

public:
    RootedValueSink()
        : sink { this, [](void* context, JSValue value) { static_cast<RootedValueSink*>(context)->values.append(value_from_abi(value)); } }
    {
    }

    GC::RootVector<Value> values;
    JSValueSink sink;
};

template<typename Collect>
ThrowCompletionOr<GC::RootVector<Value>> collect_values_from_abi(Collect collect)
{
    RootedValueSink rooted_values;
    TRY(completion_from_abi<void>(collect(&rooted_values.sink)));
    return move(rooted_values.values);
}

// The pointer of a completion whose payload is an object or null.
inline ThrowCompletionOr<Object*> optional_object_completion_from_abi(JSCompletion completion)
{
    return TRY(completion_from_abi<GC::Ptr<Object>>(completion)).ptr();
}

struct PrefixForABI {
    explicit PrefixForABI(Optional<StringView> const& prefix)
    {
        if (prefix.has_value()) {
            // A present but empty prefix still has to be told apart from no prefix, which is null.
            characters = prefix->is_empty() ? "" : prefix->characters_without_null_termination();
            length = prefix->length();
        }
    }

    char const* characters { nullptr };
    size_t length { 0 };
};

// A raw native function returns a ThrowCompletionOr<Value> in the registers where the runtime expects its
// JSCompletion, so the runtime calls a NativeFunctionPointer as a JSNativeFunction.
inline JSNativeFunction native_function_to_abi(NativeFunctionPointer native_function)
{
    return bit_cast<JSNativeFunction>(native_function);
}

// A null realm stands for the current realm, as an absent one does for CreateBuiltinFunction.
inline JSRealm* builtin_function_realm_to_abi(Optional<GC::Ptr<Realm>> const& realm)
{
    if (!realm.has_value())
        return nullptr;
    VERIFY(*realm);
    return cell_to_abi<JSRealm>(**realm);
}

}

//! Parser state, scope analysis and the function boundary.
//!
//! Scope analysis keeps no map per scope. Each name has one row of state, and scopes are numbered in opening order, so
//! a scope's subtree is every scope id at or above its own once it closes:
//!
//! - A use pushes a row on the `uses` stack, linked to the name's previous use. Repeated uses in one scope are free.
//! - When a scope closes, each of its bindings pops the name's uses from that subtree. A popped use from another
//!   function means the binding is captured. The work is proportional to bindings, not to references.
//! - When a function closes, what is left of its uses are its free names. They collapse to one row each, which is what
//!   the function index keeps, and which is all an enclosing scope ever needs to know about the function.
//!
//! Errors do not unwind. The first one is recorded and the token stream ends, so every loop in the parser finishes on
//! its own, and no parse function has to return a Result.

use super::columns::*;
use super::intern::Interner;
use super::intern::NameTables;
use super::token::*;
use super::unit::Unit;
use ak::Zone;
use ak::ZoneMap;
use ak::ZoneSet;
use ak::ZoneVec;
use core::fmt;
use core::fmt::Write as _;

/// On the function of a use: the use is inside a `with`.
pub const USE_IN_WITH: u32 = 1 << 31;

/// How many zero code units the lexer needs after the source.
pub const SOURCE_PADDING: usize = 64;

    pub has_ended: bool,
    /// Where the first directive with a legacy escape is, or `NONE`.
    pub legacy_escape: u32,
}

impl Default for Prologue {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            has_ended: false,
            legacy_escape: NONE,
        }
    }
}

    Full,
}

/// How the parser checks a regular expression literal with the regex engine of the runtime that embeds it, so that an
/// invalid one becomes an early error.
pub type ValidateRegex = for<'z> fn(zone: &'z Zone, pattern: &[u16], flags: &[u16]) -> Result<(), RegexCheckError<'z>>;

/// Why a regular expression literal did not pass [`ValidateRegex`].
pub enum RegexCheckError<'z> {
    /// The literal is invalid, with the message of the error written into the zone.
    Invalid(&'z str),
    /// The stack that is left does not hold the check.
    OutOfStack,
}

/// The first syntax error, at a source offset, with its message in the work zone or in the program.
pub struct PendingError<'z> {
    pub pos: u32,
    pub message: &'z str,
}

/// Text that is written into a zone, for the message of an error.
pub(crate) struct ZoneText<'z>(ZoneVec<'z, u8>);

impl<'z> ZoneText<'z> {
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn new(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self(ZoneVec::new_in(zone))
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn push_str(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.0.extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn finish(self) -> &'z str {
        core::str::from_utf8(self.0.into_slice()).expect("the text is made of strings")
    }
}

impl fmt::Write for ZoneText<'_> {
    #[inline]
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> fmt::Result {
        self.push_str(text);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// UTF-8 that may have bytes in it that are not, which show as U+FFFD, like `String::from_utf8_lossy()` does it.
pub(crate) struct LossyText<'t>(pub(crate) &'t [u8]);

impl fmt::Display for LossyText<'_> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        for chunk in self.0.utf8_chunks() {
            formatter.write_str(chunk.valid())?;
            if !chunk.invalid().is_empty() {
                formatter.write_char(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// What the first parse of a top level went by, which parsing it again has to go by too.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ProgramContext {
    pub context: u32,
    pub starts_in_strict_mode: bool,
    pub initiated_by_eval: bool,
    /// Whether no name means a global binding.
    pub has_no_globals: bool,
}

/// The state of a name that no scope declares or uses.
pub const UNUSED_NAME: NameState = NameState {
    use_head: NONE,
    use_scope: NONE,
    decl_head: NONE,
    stamp: 0,
};

/// A parser, whose work data is in a zone for `'a`. It lives as long as one parse job: the first parse of a source, or
/// the parse of one function again, which borrows the names of the source and their states from its reparse context for
/// `'k`.
pub struct Parser<'a, 'k, U: Unit> {
    pub(crate) zone: &'a Zone,
    /// Where in `rows_by_params_start` the last lookup ended up.
    row_cursor: core::cell::Cell<usize>,
    /// Whether the tree is one for a sweep: rows get marks, and change their tag where a mark is about them.
    pub marks: bool,
    /// The row in the index of the code of a class that was parsed last, and what it knows of that code by now.
    pub(crate) pseudo_function_row: u32,
    pub(crate) pseudo_function_flags: u32,
    /// The mark of the block being parsed, for the functions it declares, and the function that it declared last.
    pub(crate) block_mark: u32,
    pub(crate) last_function_of_block: u32,
    /// Whether the list of arguments that was parsed last is evaluated into an array for a sweep.
    pub(crate) arguments_in_array: bool,
    /// How many arguments a sweep can keep as separate operands before putting them into an array.
    pub inline_argument_limit: usize,
    /// Whether anything uses what scopes declare and what code refers to, which a sweep with a summary does not.
    pub tracks_scopes: bool,
    pub(crate) validate_regex: ValidateRegex,
    /// How many bindings of the function being parsed have a place in its summary.
    pub(crate) summary_ordinal: u32,
    /// Where the unit at offset 0 of the source is. A parse of a function again may have only a tail of the source,
    /// which puts this outside of what it can read.
    pub(crate) src: *const U,
    pub len: u32,
    pub(crate) pos: u32,
    pub(crate) tok: T,
    pub(crate) tok_start: u32,
    pub(crate) tok_end: u32,
    pub(crate) tok_name: u32,
    pub(crate) nl_before: bool,
    pub(crate) tok_escaped: bool,
    /// A legacy octal number or a string with a legacy octal escape, both of which strict mode rejects.
    pub(crate) tok_legacy: bool,
    pub(crate) prev_end: u32,
    pub(crate) prev_start: u32,
    pub(crate) regex_body_end: u32,
    pub(crate) name_buffer: ZoneVec<'a, u8>,
    pub interner: Interner<'k>,

    pub ast: Ast<'a>,
    pub index: FunctionIndexBuilder<'a>,
    pub(crate) scratch: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    pub(crate) mode: Mode,
    pub(crate) retain: bool,

    pub module: bool,
    pub strict: bool,
    pub(crate) ctx: u32,
    pub(crate) labels: ZoneVec<'a, Label>,
    pub(crate) labels_base: u32,
    pub stack_limit: usize,
    recursion_depth: u32,
    pub(crate) potential_arrow_at: u32,
    pub(crate) cover_error: u32,
    pub(crate) yield_pos: u32,
    pub(crate) await_pos: u32,
    pub(crate) await_ident_pos: u32,
    pub(crate) duplicate_parameter: u32,
    /// The node of the last arrow function, which no operator may follow.
    pub(crate) last_arrow: u32,
    /// Whether the function expression about to be parsed follows `(` or `!`.
    /// Where the expression in the parentheses opened last starts. A function there is likely to be called, but not one
    /// that starts after the `(` of a list of arguments, which an arrow function usually is.
    pub(crate) parenthesized_expression_start: u32,

    /// The state of each name, by its id. A parse of a function again has the states of its reparse context, which
    /// are all clean when it starts and ends.
    pub(crate) names: &'k mut [NameState],
    pub(crate) uses: ZoneVec<'a, UseRow>,
    pub(crate) decls: ZoneVec<'a, DeclRow>,
    pub(crate) scopes: ZoneVec<'a, Scope>,
    pub(crate) cur_scope: u32,
    pub(crate) cur_func: u32,
    pub(crate) next_scope: u32,
    pub(crate) next_func: u32,
    /// The index row of each function id, or NONE for what only counts as a function.
    pub(crate) function_rows: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    /// The row whose summary tells of the scopes of each function id, which is that of the function around a `with`.
    pub(crate) summary_rows: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    pub(crate) stamp: u32,

    pub has_top_level_await: bool,
    pub first_token_start: u32,
    pub(crate) last_pseudo_function_row: u32,
    pub(crate) class_start: u32,
    pub(crate) if_start: u32,
    pub(crate) retain_next_function: bool,
    /// While reparsing: what the first parse found out about the functions of the source.
    first_pass_index: Option<FunctionIndexView<'k>>,
    /// While reparsing: where the function being reparsed starts over.
    pub(crate) reparse_target: u32,
    pub(crate) with_depth: u32,
    pub(crate) names_used_in_with: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    pub(crate) free_names_scratch: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    /// The innermost label of each name, as its index in `labels`.
    pub(crate) label_indices: ZoneMap<'a, u32, u32>,
    /// The undeclared names that something in a `with` uses, which are not simply globals.
    pub global_names_used_in_with: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    pub(crate) hoists: ZoneVec<'a, Hoist>,
    /// The captures in the order they got resolved, as (index row, name).
    pub(crate) pending_captures: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32)>,
    /// (index row, entry) for a binding that comes up early, and with bit 31 of the row set, (index row, ordinal) for
    /// one that is captured.
    pub(crate) pending_summaries: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32)>,
    /// (index row, where the scope starts, entry) for a binding of a scope inside a function that has to exist when the
    /// scope starts.
    pub(crate) pending_scope_bindings: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32, u32)>,
    pub(crate) uses_this: bool,
    pub(crate) uses_this_from_environment: bool,
    pub(crate) might_need_arguments: bool,
    /// How many mentions of `arguments` in the function so far are something other than reading `arguments.length` or
    /// `arguments[key]`, which the function can answer from its frame.
    pub(crate) arguments_other_uses: u32,
    /// Whether the function reads `arguments[key]`.
    pub(crate) reads_arguments_index: bool,
    /// Whether something in the function may write a binding of the name of one of its parameters.
    pub(crate) may_write_parameters: bool,
    /// Whether the code being parsed is strict, but `arguments` in it may be that of a function around it that is not.
    /// That is so in the heritage and computed keys of a class, and in an arrow function with its own "use strict".
    pub(crate) arguments_of_sloppy_function: bool,
    /// Whether the closest function, counting static blocks, is an arrow function.
    pub(crate) in_arrow: bool,

    /// The private names of each open class, created when a class first declares one.
    pub(crate) private_declared: ZoneVec<'a, ZoneMap<'a, u32, u8>>,
    pub(crate) private_used: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32)>,
    pub(crate) class_marks: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32)>,
    pub(crate) export_names: ZoneSet<'a, u32>,
    pub(crate) export_locals: ZoneVec<'a, (u32, u32)>,

    pub err: Option<PendingError<'a>>,
    /// Whether this is the code of an eval, whose private names the code around it may declare.
    pub initiated_by_eval: bool,
    /// The private names that no class in this code declares, for an eval.
    pub eval_referenced_private_names: ZoneVec<'a, u32>,
    _marker: core::marker::PhantomData<&'a [U]>,
}

/// How much native stack parsing may use by default. Nesting past this is a syntax error rather than a crash.
pub const DEFAULT_STACK_BUDGET: usize = 4 << 20;

/// How deeply statements and expressions may nest.
const MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH: u32 = 2000;

/// How many member accesses, calls and tagged templates one chain like `a.b[c](d)` may have. The parser goes through a
/// chain in a loop, so the recursion limit does not apply to it.
pub(crate) const MAX_SUBSCRIPT_CHAIN_LENGTH: u32 = 10000;

pub const RECURSION_LIMIT_MESSAGE: &str = "Maximum parser recursion depth exceeded";

/// A function could not be parsed or compiled, because the stack that is left does not hold it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct OutOfStack;

/// The address that the stack can only go `bytes` below where it is now.
pub fn stack_limit_for_budget(bytes: usize) -> usize {
    ak::stack::limit_for_budget(bytes)
}

impl<'a: 'k, 'k, U: Unit> Parser<'a, 'k, U> {
    /// A parser for the first parse of `source`, with its work data in `zone`. `initial_names` are the tables of an
    /// interner with the names that every interner starts with. `vm_stack_limit` is how low a VM lets the stack of this
    /// thread go, if that can be told.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `source` must be followed by at least 64 units of zeros within the same allocation.
    pub unsafe fn new(
        zone: &'a Zone,
        source: &'a [U],
        module: bool,
        mode: Mode,
        initial_names: &NameTables<'_>,
        validate_regex: ValidateRegex,
        vm_stack_limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Self {
        let interner = Interner::new(zone, source.len(), initial_names);
        // NB: A lazy parse skips the code of functions, which is most of the code of most sources, so a tree of the
        //     whole source is only the most it is likely to have.
        let whole_source_nodes = source.len() / 3 + 16;
        let estimated_nodes = match mode {
            Mode::Lazy => whole_source_nodes.min(1 << 16),
            Mode::Full => whole_source_nodes,
        };
        let estimated_functions = source.len() / 128;
        let estimated_uses = (source.len() / 8 + 16).min(1 << 16);
        let estimated_names = if estimated_uses < 1 << 16 {
            interner.len().next_power_of_two()
        } else {
            1 << 12
        };
        let index = FunctionIndexBuilder::with_capacity(zone, estimated_functions);
        let mut parser = Self::with_capacities(
            zone,
            source.as_ptr(),
            source.len(),
            module,
            mode,
            interner,
            zone.alloc_slice_fill(estimated_names, UNUSED_NAME),
            index,
            estimated_nodes,
            estimated_uses,
            validate_regex,
        );
        parser.ast.likely_most_nodes = whole_source_nodes;
        // NB: Code can start parsing with less stack left than the budget, as eval near the end of the stack does.
        parser.stack_limit = stack_limit_for_budget(DEFAULT_STACK_BUDGET).max(vm_stack_limit.unwrap_or(0));
        parser.pending_captures.reserve(estimated_functions * 2);
        if source.len() >= u32::MAX as usize - 64 {
            parser.len = 0;
            parser.fail(0, "Source too long");
        }
        parser.skip_hashbang();
        parser
    }

    fn skip_hashbang(&mut self) {
        if self.at(0) == 0x23 && self.at(1) == 0x21 {
            // Hashbang comment.
            let mut p = 2;
            while p < self.len as usize && !matches!(self.at(p), 0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029) {
                p += 1;
            }
            self.pos = p as u32;
        }
    }

    /// A parser that parses one function again, knowing what the first parse of its source found, with its work data in
    /// `zone`. The names of the source with their states come from the reparse context of the source, and the parser
    /// works with them in place. Its source comes with the function.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn for_reparsing(
        zone: &'a Zone,
        module: bool,
        interner: Interner<'k>,
        names: &'k mut [NameState],
        stamp: u32,
        first_pass_index: FunctionIndexView<'k>,
        source_length: u32,
        estimated_nodes: usize,
        validate_regex: ValidateRegex,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut parser = Self::with_capacities(
            zone,
            core::ptr::null(),
            source_length as usize,
            module,
            Mode::Lazy,
            interner,
            names,
            FunctionIndexBuilder::with_capacity(zone, 0),
            estimated_nodes,
            256,
            validate_regex,
        );
        parser.stamp = stamp;
        parser.first_pass_index = Some(first_pass_index);
        parser
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn with_capacities(
        zone: &'a Zone,
        source: *const U,
        length: usize,
        module: bool,
        mode: Mode,
        interner: Interner<'k>,
        names: &'k mut [NameState],
        index: FunctionIndexBuilder<'a>,
        estimated_nodes: usize,
        estimated_uses: usize,
        validate_regex: ValidateRegex,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            zone,
            row_cursor: core::cell::Cell::new(0),
            marks: false,
            pseudo_function_row: NONE,
            pseudo_function_flags: 0,
            block_mark: NONE,
            last_function_of_block: 0,
            arguments_in_array: false,
            inline_argument_limit: 0,
            tracks_scopes: true,
            validate_regex,
            summary_ordinal: 0,
            src: source,
            len: length as u32,
            pos: 0,
            tok: T::Eof,
            tok_start: 0,
            tok_end: 0,
            tok_name: 0,
            nl_before: false,
            tok_escaped: false,
            tok_legacy: false,
            prev_end: 0,
            prev_start: 0,
            regex_body_end: 0,
            name_buffer: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            interner,
            ast: Ast::with_capacity(zone, estimated_nodes),
            index,
            scratch: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(estimated_uses.min(4096), zone),
            mode,
            retain: true,
            module,
            strict: module,
            ctx: if module { ctx::CAN_AWAIT } else { 0 },
            labels: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            labels_base: 0,
            stack_limit: 0,
            recursion_depth: 0,
            potential_arrow_at: NONE,
            cover_error: NONE,
            yield_pos: 0,
            await_pos: 0,
            await_ident_pos: 0,
            duplicate_parameter: NONE,
            last_arrow: 0,
            parenthesized_expression_start: NONE,
            names,
            uses: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(estimated_uses, zone),
            decls: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in(estimated_uses / 16, zone),
            scopes: ZoneVec::with_capacity_in((length / 64 + 1).min(256), zone),
            cur_scope: 0,
            cur_func: 0,
            next_scope: 1,
            next_func: 1,
            function_rows: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[NONE], zone),
            summary_rows: ZoneVec::from_slice_in(&[PROGRAM_SUMMARY_ROW], zone),
            stamp: 0,
            has_top_level_await: false,
            first_token_start: 0,
            last_pseudo_function_row: NONE,
            class_start: 0,
            if_start: 0,
            retain_next_function: false,
            first_pass_index: None,
            reparse_target: NONE,
            with_depth: 0,
            names_used_in_with: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            free_names_scratch: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            label_indices: ZoneMap::new_in(zone),
            global_names_used_in_with: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            hoists: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            pending_captures: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            pending_summaries: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            pending_scope_bindings: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            uses_this: false,
            uses_this_from_environment: false,
            might_need_arguments: false,
            arguments_other_uses: 0,
            reads_arguments_index: false,
            may_write_parameters: false,
            arguments_of_sloppy_function: false,
            in_arrow: false,

            private_declared: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            private_used: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            class_marks: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            export_names: ZoneSet::new_in(zone),
            export_locals: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            err: None,
            initiated_by_eval: false,
            eval_referenced_private_names: ZoneVec::new_in(zone),
            _marker: core::marker::PhantomData,
        }
    }

    /// Allows what `context` allows from the start of the program.
    pub fn add_context(&mut self, context: u32) {
        self.ctx |= context;
    }

    pub fn parse_program(&mut self) -> u32 {
        self.open_scope_with(scope_flag::TOP, 0);
        self.lex();
        self.first_token_start = self.tok_start;
        let mark = self.scratch.len();
        let mut prologue = Prologue::default();
        while self.tok != T::Eof {
            let (statement, _) = self.parse_statement_of_prologue(&mut prologue, true);
            self.scratch.push(statement);
        }
        let list = self.finish_list(mark);
        if self.is_reparsing() {
            let scope_row = self.close_scope();
            return self.ast.push(tag::PROGRAM, 0, list, scope_row);
        }
        if self.module {
            self.check_exported_locals();
        }
        self.check_unresolved_private_names();
        self.index.program_has_direct_eval = self.scopes.last().unwrap().eval_in_function;
        let scope_row = self.close_scope();
        for row in &self.uses {
            if row.name != USE_DEAD && row.func & USE_IN_WITH != 0 {
                self.global_names_used_in_with.push(row.name);
            }
        }
        self.group_captures();
        self.group_summaries();
        self.ast.push(tag::PROGRAM, 0, list, scope_row)
    }

    /// Goes through the top level once more with marks for a sweep, past all functions, after a parse that went well.
    pub fn parse_top_level_rows(
        &mut self,
        context: ProgramContext,
        index: FunctionIndexView<'a>,
        inline_argument_limit: usize,
    ) -> Result<(Ast<'a>, u32), OutOfStack> {
        // NB: The rows are those of the tree, and marks, which some code has many of.
        let nodes = self.ast.tag.len();
        let rows = Ast::with_capacities(self.zone, nodes + nodes / 2, self.ast.extra.len());
        let tree = core::mem::replace(&mut self.ast, rows);
        let private_names = self.eval_referenced_private_names.take();
        let (first_token_start, strict, has_top_level_await) =
            (self.first_token_start, self.strict, self.has_top_level_await);
        self.finish_reparse();
        self.export_names.clear();
        self.first_pass_index = Some(index);
        self.tracks_scopes = false;
        self.marks = true;
        self.inline_argument_limit = inline_argument_limit;
        let node = self.reparse_program(context);
        self.first_pass_index = None;
        let error = self.err.take();
        let rows = core::mem::replace(&mut self.ast, tree);
        self.eval_referenced_private_names = private_names;
        self.first_token_start = first_token_start;
        self.strict = strict;
        self.has_top_level_await = has_top_level_await;
        match error {
            None => Ok((rows, node)),
            Some(error) => {
                assert_eq!(
                    error.message, RECURSION_LIMIT_MESSAGE,
                    "the first parse found no errors"
                );
                Err(OutOfStack)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Gets ready to go through the top level again, past all functions, like the first parse did.
    pub(crate) fn reparse_program(&mut self, context: ProgramContext) -> u32 {
        self.reparse_target = NONE;
        self.strict = context.starts_in_strict_mode;
        self.initiated_by_eval = context.initiated_by_eval;
        self.ctx = if self.module { ctx::CAN_AWAIT } else { 0 } | context.context;
        self.retain = true;
        self.retain_next_function = false;
        self.uses_this = false;
        self.uses_this_from_environment = false;
        self.might_need_arguments = false;
        self.arguments_other_uses = 0;
        self.reads_arguments_index = false;
        self.may_write_parameters = false;
        self.in_arrow = false;
        self.cover_error = NONE;
        self.potential_arrow_at = NONE;
        self.last_arrow = 0;
        self.pos = 0;
        self.tok_end = 0;
        self.prev_end = 0;
        self.prev_start = 0;
        self.skip_hashbang();
        let node = self.parse_program();
        self.initiated_by_eval = false;
        node
    }

    /// Groups the captures by function, now that all of them are known.
    fn group_captures(&mut self) {
        let pending = self.pending_captures.take();
        let index = &mut self.index;
        for &(row, _) in &pending {
            index.capture_count[row as usize] += 1;
        }
        let mut next = 0;
        for row in 0..index.capture_start.len() {
            index.capture_start[row] = next;
            next += index.capture_count[row];
        }
        index.capture_names.resize(next as usize, 0);
        let filled = self.zone.alloc_slice_fill(index.capture_start.len(), 0u32);
        for (row, name) in pending {
            let slot = index.capture_start[row as usize] + filled[row as usize];
            filled[row as usize] += 1;
            index.capture_names[slot as usize] = name;
        }
    }

    /// Writes out the summaries of all functions, now that all of their scopes closed.
    fn group_summaries(&mut self) {
        #[inline]
        fn write_varint(bytes: &mut ZoneVec<'_, u8>, mut value: u32) {
            while value >= 0x80 {
                bytes.push(value as u8 | 0x80);
                value >>= 7;
            }
            bytes.push(value as u8);
        }
        fn write_scope_bindings(bytes: &mut ZoneVec<'_, u8>, bindings: &[(u32, u32, u32)]) {
            let scope_count = bindings.chunk_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1).count();
            write_varint(bytes, scope_count as u32);
            let mut last_position = 0;
            for scope in bindings.chunk_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1) {
                write_varint(bytes, scope[0].1 - last_position);
                last_position = scope[0].1;
                write_varint(bytes, scope.len() as u32);
                for binding in scope {
                    write_varint(bytes, binding.2);
                }
            }
        }
        let mut pending = self.pending_summaries.take();
        let index = &mut self.index;
        pending.sort_unstable();
        // NB: Rows with bit 31 set sort after all the others, so that each kind is a run of its own.
        let captured_start = pending.partition_point(|&(row, _)| row & SUMMARY_SLOT_EARLY == 0);
        let (mut early, mut captured) = (0, captured_start);
        let mut scope_bindings = self.pending_scope_bindings.take();
        scope_bindings.sort_unstable();
        let mut scope_binding = 0;
        let mut bitmap = ZoneVec::new_in(self.zone);
        // NB: The top level has no row of its own, so its summary comes first, and it has only scopes in it.
        let of_program = scope_bindings.partition_point(|binding| binding.0 != PROGRAM_SUMMARY_ROW);
        write_varint(&mut index.summaries, 0);
        write_scope_bindings(&mut index.summaries, &scope_bindings[of_program..]);
        index.program_summary_end = index.summaries.len() as u32;
        scope_bindings.truncate(of_program);
        for row in 0..index.summary_start.len() as u32 {
            index.summary_start[row as usize] = index.summaries.len() as u32;
            let early_start = early;
            while early < captured_start && pending[early].0 == row {
                early += 1;
            }
            bitmap.clear();
            while captured < pending.len() && pending[captured].0 & !SUMMARY_SLOT_EARLY == row {
                let ordinal = pending[captured].1 as usize;
                if ordinal / 8 >= bitmap.len() {
                    bitmap.resize(ordinal / 8 + 1, 0u8);
                }
                bitmap[ordinal / 8] |= 1 << (ordinal % 8);
                captured += 1;
            }
            let scope_bindings_start = scope_binding;
            while scope_binding < scope_bindings.len() && scope_bindings[scope_binding].0 == row {
                scope_binding += 1;
            }
            let bindings_of_scopes = &scope_bindings[scope_bindings_start..scope_binding];
            if early == early_start && bitmap.is_empty() && bindings_of_scopes.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            write_varint(&mut index.summaries, (early - early_start) as u32);
            for entry in &pending[early_start..early] {
                write_varint(&mut index.summaries, entry.1);
            }
            write_scope_bindings(&mut index.summaries, bindings_of_scopes);
            index.summaries.extend_from_slice(&bitmap);
        }
    }

    /// A declaration of something that was only the name of a function expression makes that a binding like any other.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn note_redeclared_function_name(&mut self, declaration: u32, name: u32, scope_index: usize, bind: Bind) {
        if self.decls[declaration as usize].flags & !decl::FUNCTION_NAME == 0 {
            self.note_new_binding_of(declaration as usize, name, scope_index, bind);
        }
    }

    /// A new binding of the function being parsed came up.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn note_new_binding(&mut self, name: u32, scope_index: usize, bind: Bind) {
        self.note_new_binding_of(self.decls.len() - 1, name, scope_index, bind);
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn note_new_binding_of(&mut self, d: usize, name: u32, scope_index: usize, bind: Bind) {
        let scope = &self.scopes[scope_index];
        let head = self.names[name as usize].use_head;
        let is_function_level = scope.flags & scope_flag::VAR_SCOPE != 0;
        let kind = match bind {
            Bind::Let | Bind::Lexical | Bind::CatchPattern => 1,
            Bind::Const => 2,
            _ => 0,
        };
        // NB: A declaration of the name `arguments` has a say in the arguments object, which comes before all else.
        let is_of_arguments = name == N_ARGUMENTS && is_function_level;
        let is_early = bind != Bind::Parameter
            && (is_of_arguments || (head != NONE && self.uses[head as usize].scope >= scope.id));
        self.decls[d].summary_slot = if is_early {
            SUMMARY_SLOT_EARLY | kind
        } else if is_function_level {
            self.summary_ordinal += 1;
            self.summary_ordinal - 1
        } else {
            SUMMARY_SLOT_INNER | kind
        };
    }

    /// What the summary of its function says of a binding whose scope closes.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn note_closed_binding(&mut self, summary_slot: u32, name: u32, is_captured: bool, scope: Scope) {
        if summary_slot == NONE {
            return;
        }
        let index_row = self.summary_rows[scope.func as usize];
        if index_row == NONE {
            return;
        }
        // NB: What the top level itself declares is no business of a summary, that is declaration instantiation.
        if index_row == PROGRAM_SUMMARY_ROW && scope.flags & scope_flag::VAR_SCOPE != 0 {
            return;
        }
        let is_early = summary_slot & SUMMARY_SLOT_EARLY != 0;
        let entry = name << 3 | (summary_slot & 3) << 1 | u32::from(is_captured);
        if scope.flags & scope_flag::VAR_SCOPE == 0 {
            // NB: A `case` can be skipped, so that a declaration in a switch is no sign of having been initialized.
            if is_early || is_captured || scope.flags & scope_flag::SWITCH != 0 {
                self.pending_scope_bindings.push((index_row, scope.start, entry));
            }
        } else if is_early {
            self.pending_summaries.push((index_row, entry));
        } else if is_captured {
            self.pending_summaries
                .push((index_row | SUMMARY_SLOT_EARLY, summary_slot));
        }
    }

    /// The text of `message` in the work zone, for an error.
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn message(&self, message: fmt::Arguments<'_>) -> &'a str {
        if let Some(text) = message.as_str() {
            return text;
        }
        let mut text = ZoneText::new(self.zone);
        text.write_fmt(message).expect("writing to a zone does not fail");
        text.finish()
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn fail(&mut self, pos: u32, message: &'a str) {
        if self.err.is_none() {
            self.err = Some(PendingError { pos, message });
        }
        self.tok = T::Eof;
        self.tok_start = self.len;
        self.tok_end = self.len;
        self.pos = self.len;
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn unexpected(&mut self) {
        let message = self.unexpected_token_message();
        self.fail(self.tok_start, message);
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(crate) fn expected(&mut self, what: &str) {
        let message = self.message(format_args!("{}. Expected {what}", self.unexpected_token_message()));
        self.fail(self.tok_start, message);
    }

    /// Fails for a token where a list goes on with a comma or ends.
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn expected_comma_or(&mut self, close: T) {
        let what = self.message(format_args!("',' or {}", close.spelling()));
        self.expected(what);
    }

    /// What a list expects after an item: a comma, or the token that ends the list, which the caller looks for.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn expect_comma_or(&mut self, close: T) {
        if self.tok == T::Comma {
            self.next();
        } else {
            self.expected_comma_or(close);
        }
    }

    /// Calls the current token what the source calls it.
    fn unexpected_token_message(&self) -> &'a str {
        const LONGEST_TOKEN_SHOWN: u32 = 40;
        if self.tok == T::Eof {
            return "Unexpected end of input";
        }
        let end = self.tok_end.min(self.tok_start + LONGEST_TOKEN_SHOWN);
        let mut text = ZoneText::new(self.zone);
        text.push_str("Unexpected token '");
        for unit in char::decode_utf16((self.tok_start..end).map(|index| self.at(index as usize) as u16)) {
            text.push_str(unit.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER).encode_utf8(&mut [0; 4]));
        }
        if end < self.tok_end {
            text.push_str("...");
        }
        text.push_str("'");
        text.finish()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn eat(&mut self, kind: T) -> bool {
        if self.tok == kind {
            self.next();
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn expect(&mut self, kind: T) {
        if self.tok == kind {
            self.next();
        } else {
            self.expected(kind.spelling());
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn is_contextual(&self, name: u32) -> bool {
        self.tok == T::Name && self.tok_name == name && !self.tok_escaped
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn eat_contextual(&mut self, name: u32) -> bool {
        if self.is_contextual(name) {
            self.next();
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn can_insert_semicolon(&self) -> bool {
        self.tok == T::Eof || self.tok == T::RBrace || self.nl_before
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn semicolon(&mut self) {
        if !self.eat(T::Semi) && !self.can_insert_semicolon() {
            self.expected("';'");
        }
    }

    /// Runs `look` on the token stream and puts it back. An error it runs into comes up again if the parser gets there.
    pub(crate) fn look_ahead<R>(&mut self, look: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R {
        let saved = (
            self.pos,
            self.tok,
            self.tok_start,
            self.tok_end,
            self.tok_name,
            self.nl_before,
            self.tok_escaped,
            self.tok_legacy,
            self.prev_end,
            self.prev_start,
        );
        let had_error = self.err.is_some();
        let result = look(self);
        if !had_error {
            self.err = None;
        }
        (
            self.pos,
            self.tok,
            self.tok_start,
            self.tok_end,
            self.tok_name,
            self.nl_before,
            self.tok_escaped,
            self.tok_legacy,
            self.prev_end,
            self.prev_start,
        ) = saved;
        result
    }

    /// The kind and name of the token after the current one, and whether a newline comes before it.
    pub(crate) fn peek(&mut self) -> (T, u32, bool) {
        self.look_ahead(|parser| {
            parser.lex();
            (parser.tok, parser.tok_name, parser.nl_before)
        })
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn finish_list(&mut self, mark: usize) -> u32 {
        let start = self.ast.extra.len() as u32;
        let count = self.scratch.len() - mark;
        self.ast.extra.push(count as u32);
        self.ast.extra.extend_from_slice(&self.scratch[mark..]);
        self.scratch.truncate(mark);
        start
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn list(&self, start: u32) -> &[u32] {
        let count = self.ast.extra[start as usize] as usize;
        &self.ast.extra[start as usize + 1..start as usize + 1 + count]
    }

    /// Leaves a mark in the rows, for a sweep over them.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn mark(&mut self, mark: u8, a: u32) {
        self.mark_at(mark, a, self.tok_start);
    }

    /// Leaves a mark in the rows. What it makes of a reference goes by `position` from then on, which is where whatever the
    /// reference is for is in the source.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn mark_at(&mut self, mark: u8, a: u32, position: u32) {
        if !self.marks {
            return;
        }
        if (tag::MARK_CALLEE..=tag::MARK_KEY).contains(&mark) {
            let mut node = self.ast.tag.len() - 1;
            while self.ast.tag[node] == tag::PAREN {
                node = self.ast.a[node] as usize;
            }
            if self.mark_node(node, mark, a, position) {
                return;
            }
        }
        self.ast.push(mark, self.prev_start, a, 0);
    }

    /// Marks the reference at the row `node` in place with `mark`, one of those from `MARK_CALLEE` to `MARK_KEY`, if it
    /// is a reference that the mark is for. Returns whether it was.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn mark_node(&mut self, mut node: usize, mark: u8, a: u32, position: u32) -> bool {
        // NB: What `delete` of an optional chain is about is the end of the chain.
