//! Name interning. An identifier's bytes up to 16 long are its own key, so a lookup is one multiply and a compare of
//! two words, with no text compare. Names of one or two bytes, which is most of minified code, skip even that.
//!
//! The tables of an interner are slices. Those of a first parse are in its work zone, and the ones that it outgrows
//! stay there until the parse ends. The reparse context of a source keeps the names of the source in tables of its own
//! (see `KeptNames` in LibJS), and each parse of a function again interns its names with those tables in place.

use super::token::{KEYWORDS, SPECIAL_NAMES};
use ak::Zone;
use core::mem::MaybeUninit;

pub const NONE: u32 = u32::MAX;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C, align(32))]
pub struct Row {
    k0: u64,
    k1: u64,
    id: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct LongRow {
    hash: u64,
    id: u32,
}

const EMPTY_ROW: Row = Row { k0: 0, k1: 0, id: NONE };
const EMPTY_LONG_ROW: LongRow = LongRow { hash: 0, id: NONE };

pub struct Interner<'z> {
    /// Where the tables move when they grow.
    zone: &'z Zone,
    short: &'z mut [u32],
    rows: &'z mut [Row],
    shift: u32,
    count: u32,
    long_rows: &'z mut [LongRow],
    long_count: u32,
    /// Each name's text, in UTF-8, in the first `text_len` bytes, which are written. The rest is room for more.
    text: &'z mut [MaybeUninit<u8>],
    text_len: u32,
    /// The start and the length of the text of each name, in the first `len` entries, which are written.
    spans: &'z mut [MaybeUninit<(u32, u32)>],
    len: u32,
}

/// The tables of an interner, all of which are written, for a copy of them that stays around.
pub struct NameTables<'t> {
    pub rows: &'t [Row],
    pub shift: u32,
    pub count: u32,
    pub long_rows: &'t [LongRow],
    pub long_count: u32,
    pub text: &'t [u8],
    pub spans: &'t [(u32, u32)],
}

/// Tables that an interner can work with in place (see `Interner::of_tables()`).
pub struct NameTablesMut<'t> {
    pub rows: &'t mut [Row],
    pub shift: u32,
    pub count: u32,
    pub long_rows: &'t mut [LongRow],
    pub long_count: u32,
    pub text: &'t mut [u8],
    pub spans: &'t mut [(u32, u32)],
}

/// Makes room for `more` values after the first `len` of `list`. A list that is too short for them moves to new memory
/// of `zone`, with at least twice the room.
fn reserve<'z, T: Copy>(zone: &'z Zone, list: &mut &'z mut [MaybeUninit<T>], len: usize, more: usize) {
    if len + more <= list.len() {
        return;
    }
    let grown = zone.alloc_uninit_slice((len + more).max(list.len() * 2));
    grown[..len].copy_from_slice(&list[..len]);
    *list = grown;
}

/// `values` as room for values, all of which is written.
fn as_room<T: Copy>(values: &mut [T]) -> &mut [MaybeUninit<T>] {
    // SAFETY: A `MaybeUninit<T>` has the layout of a `T`. An interner only writes values into its room, so the values
    //         that the caller sees again stay written.
    unsafe { &mut *(core::ptr::from_mut(values) as *mut [MaybeUninit<T>]) }
}

#[inline(always)]
fn hash_key(k0: u64, k1: u64) -> u64 {
    (k0 ^ k1.rotate_left(29)).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15) ^ k1.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2_AE3D_27D4_EB4F)
}

fn hash_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut h = bytes.len() as u64;
    let (chunks, remainder) = bytes.as_chunks::<8>();
    for chunk in chunks {
        h = (h ^ u64::from_le_bytes(*chunk)).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
        h ^= h >> 29;
    }
    for &b in remainder {
        h = (h ^ b as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
    }
    h ^ (h >> 32)
}

/// The key of a name of at most 16 bytes: its bytes in order, as two little-endian words.
/// Names ending in NUL use the full-text table, since zero padding would erase their length.
#[inline(always)]
fn key_from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> (u64, u64) {
    let word_at = |at: usize| u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[at..at + 8].try_into().unwrap());
    let half_word_at = |at: usize| u64::from(u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[at..at + 4].try_into().unwrap()));
    let length = bytes.len();
    match length {
        0 => (0, 0),
        1..=3 => {
            let (middle, last) = (length / 2, length - 1);
            let word = u64::from(bytes[0]) | u64::from(bytes[middle]) << (middle * 8);
            (word | u64::from(bytes[last]) << (last * 8), 0)
        }
        4..=7 => (half_word_at(0) | half_word_at(length - 4) << ((length - 4) * 8), 0),
        8 => (word_at(0), 0),
        _ => (word_at(0), word_at(length - 8) >> ((16 - length) * 8)),
    }
}

impl<'z> Interner<'z> {
    /// An interner for a source of `source_len` units. `initial` are the tables of an interner with the names that every
    /// interner starts with (see `Interner::initial()`), which a small source starts from.
    pub(super) fn new(zone: &'z Zone, source_len: usize, initial: &NameTables<'_>) -> Self {
        let wanted = (source_len / 16).clamp(1 << 8, 1 << 22).next_power_of_two();
        // OPTIMIZATION: Tiny scripts, such as repeated evals, do not amortize the setup of a direct table for two-byte
        // names.
        let short: &'z mut [u32] = if source_len >= 1 << 16 {
            zone.alloc_slice_fill(1 << 16, NONE)
        } else {
            &mut []
        };
        let long_rows = (source_len / 128).clamp(1 << 4, 1 << 10).next_power_of_two();
        if wanted == 1 << 8 && long_rows == 1 << 4 {
            // OPTIMIZATION: Every parser starts with the same reserved names. Copy their tables for small sources
            // instead of interning all of them again, which is more work than parsing many eval strings.
            let text = zone.alloc_uninit_slice(initial.text.len().max(512));
            text[..initial.text.len()].write_copy_of_slice(initial.text);
            let spans = zone.alloc_uninit_slice(initial.spans.len().max(1 << 7));
            spans[..initial.spans.len()].write_copy_of_slice(initial.spans);
            return Self {
                zone,
                short,
                rows: zone.alloc_slice_copy(initial.rows),
                shift: initial.shift,
                count: initial.count,
                long_rows: zone.alloc_slice_copy(initial.long_rows),
                long_count: initial.long_count,
                text,
                text_len: initial.text.len() as u32,
                spans,
                len: initial.spans.len() as u32,
            };
        }
        Self::with_tables(zone, short, wanted, long_rows, (source_len / 8).max(512))
    }

    /// An interner with only the names that every interner starts with, at the size that `new()` gives a small source.
    pub fn initial(zone: &'z Zone) -> Self {
        Self::with_tables(zone, &mut [], 1 << 8, 1 << 4, 512)
    }

    fn with_tables(zone: &'z Zone, short: &'z mut [u32], rows: usize, long_rows: usize, text_capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let mut interner = Self::empty(zone, short, rows, long_rows, text_capacity);
        for (word, _) in KEYWORDS {
            interner.intern_bytes(word.as_bytes());
        }
        for word in SPECIAL_NAMES {
            interner.intern_bytes(word.as_bytes());
        }
        for pseudo in [".this", ".new.target", ".super", ".unbound"] {
            interner.intern_bytes(pseudo.as_bytes());
        }
        interner
    }

    fn empty(zone: &'z Zone, short: &'z mut [u32], rows: usize, long_rows: usize, text_capacity: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            zone,
            short,
            rows: zone.alloc_slice_fill(rows, EMPTY_ROW),
            shift: 64 - rows.trailing_zeros(),
            count: 0,
            long_rows: zone.alloc_slice_fill(long_rows, EMPTY_LONG_ROW),
            long_count: 0,
            text: zone.alloc_uninit_slice(text_capacity),
            text_len: 0,
            spans: zone.alloc_uninit_slice(rows / 2),
            len: 0,
        }
    }

    /// An interner that gives the names of an earlier parse the ids they had, sized to stay around with a source of any
    /// size (see `tables()`). `names` yields them in id order, none of them twice, and starts with the names that every
    /// interner starts with.
    pub fn with_names<'a>(zone: &'z Zone, names: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a [u8]>) -> Self {
        let rows = (names.len() * 2).next_power_of_two();
        let mut interner = Self::empty(zone, &mut [], rows, 1 << 4, names.len() * 8);
        let mask = rows - 1;
        for name in names {
            if name.len() > 16 || name.last() == Some(&0) {
                interner.intern_bytes(name);
                continue;
            }
            let id = interner.add_name(name);
            let (k0, k1) = key_from_bytes(name);
            let mut index = (hash_key(k0, k1) >> interner.shift) as usize;
            // NB: The names are all different, so the first free row is the one.
            while interner.rows[index].id != NONE {
                index = (index + 1) & mask;
            }
            interner.rows[index] = Row { k0, k1, id };
            interner.count += 1;
        }
        interner
    }

    /// The tables, at the size they have, to copy. The table of short names is left out.
    #[inline]
    pub fn tables(&self) -> NameTables<'_> {
        NameTables {
            rows: self.rows,
            shift: self.shift,
            count: self.count,
            long_rows: self.long_rows,
            long_count: self.long_count,
            text: self.all_text(),
            spans: self.spans(),
        }
    }

    /// An interner with `tables` in place. The text and the span of a name that they do not have go to `zone`, and so
    /// do the rows when they grow, so that the tables never refer to the zone. But the row of such a name is written
    /// into `tables` first, so that they stay as they were only if no name is new.
    pub fn of_tables(zone: &'z Zone, tables: NameTablesMut<'z>) -> Self {
        Self {
            zone,
            short: &mut [],
            shift: tables.shift,
            count: tables.count,
            long_count: tables.long_count,
            text_len: tables.text.len() as u32,
            len: tables.spans.len() as u32,
            rows: tables.rows,
            long_rows: tables.long_rows,
            text: as_room(tables.text),
            spans: as_room(tables.spans),
        }
    }

    // NB: An interner is never empty: it starts with the names that every interner has.
    #[allow(clippy::len_without_is_empty)]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len as usize
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn text(&self, id: u32) -> &[u8] {
        let (start, len) = self.spans()[id as usize];
        // SAFETY: The text of a name is written.
        unsafe { self.text[start as usize..(start + len) as usize].assume_init_ref() }
    }

    fn all_text(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: The first `text_len` bytes are written.
        unsafe { self.text[..self.text_len as usize].assume_init_ref() }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn spans(&self) -> &[(u32, u32)] {
        // SAFETY: The first `len` spans are written.
        unsafe { self.spans[..self.len()].assume_init_ref() }
    }

    fn add_name(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {
        let id = self.len;
        let start = self.text_len as usize;
        reserve(self.zone, &mut self.spans, id as usize, 1);
        reserve(self.zone, &mut self.text, start, bytes.len());
        self.spans[id as usize].write((start as u32, bytes.len() as u32));
        self.text[start..start + bytes.len()].write_copy_of_slice(bytes);
        self.len += 1;
        self.text_len += bytes.len() as u32;
        id
    }

    /// Interns a name of at most 16 bytes, given as its key.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn intern_key(&mut self, k0: u64, k1: u64, len: usize) -> u32 {
        if len <= 2 && !self.short.is_empty() {
            let id = self.short[k0 as usize];
            if id != NONE {
                return id;
            }
            return self.add_short(k0, len);
        }
        let mask = self.rows.len() - 1;
        let mut index = (hash_key(k0, k1) >> self.shift) as usize;
        loop {
            // SAFETY: The index is masked to the table.
            let row = unsafe { self.rows.get_unchecked(index) };
            // NB: The empty name has the key of an empty row.
            if row.id == NONE {
                return self.insert_key(k0, k1, len, index);
            }
            if row.k0 == k0 && row.k1 == k1 {
                return row.id;
            }
            index = (index + 1) & mask;
        }
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn add_short(&mut self, k0: u64, len: usize) -> u32 {
        let bytes = k0.to_le_bytes();
        let id = self.add_name(&bytes[..len]);
        self.short[k0 as usize] = id;
        id
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    fn insert_key(&mut self, k0: u64, k1: u64, len: usize, index: usize) -> u32 {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 16];
        bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(&k0.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[8..].copy_from_slice(&k1.to_le_bytes());
        let id = self.add_name(&bytes[..len]);
        self.rows[index] = Row { k0, k1, id };
        self.count += 1;
        if self.count as usize * 2 > self.rows.len() {
            self.grow();
        }
        id
    }

    #[cold]
    fn grow(&mut self) {
        let new_len = self.rows.len() * 2;
        // NB: The old table stays in the zone until the parse ends.
        let old = core::mem::replace(&mut self.rows, self.zone.alloc_slice_fill(new_len, EMPTY_ROW));
        self.shift -= 1;
        let mask = new_len - 1;
        for &row in old.iter() {
            if row.id == NONE {
                continue;
            }
            let mut index = (hash_key(row.k0, row.k1) >> self.shift) as usize;
            while self.rows[index].id != NONE {
                index = (index + 1) & mask;
            }
            self.rows[index] = row;
        }
    }

    /// Interns any name, given as UTF-8.
    pub fn intern_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {
        if bytes.len() <= 16 && bytes.last() != Some(&0) {
            let (k0, k1) = key_from_bytes(bytes);
            return self.intern_key(k0, k1, bytes.len());
        }
        let hash = hash_bytes(bytes);
        let mut mask = self.long_rows.len() - 1;
        let mut index = hash as usize & mask;
        loop {
            let row = self.long_rows[index];
            if row.id == NONE {
                break;
            }
            if row.hash == hash && self.text(row.id) == bytes {
                return row.id;
            }
            index = (index + 1) & mask;
        }
        let id = self.add_name(bytes);
        self.long_rows[index] = LongRow { hash, id };
        self.long_count += 1;
        if self.long_count as usize * 2 > self.long_rows.len() {
            let new_len = self.long_rows.len() * 2;
            let old = core::mem::replace(&mut self.long_rows, self.zone.alloc_slice_fill(new_len, EMPTY_LONG_ROW));
            mask = new_len - 1;
            for &row in old.iter() {
                if row.id == NONE {
                    continue;
                }
                let mut index = row.hash as usize & mask;
                while self.long_rows[index].id != NONE {
                    index = (index + 1) & mask;
                }
                self.long_rows[index] = row;
            }
        }
        id
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::Interner;
    use super::NameTablesMut;
    use ak::Zone;

    #[test]
    fn trailing_nuls_preserve_name_identity() {
        // Exercise the prepared small interner, the general fallback, and the direct short-name table.
        for source_len in [0, 20_000, 65_536] {
            for reverse in [false, true] {
                let zone = Zone::new(1 << 30, c"test");
                let initial = Interner::initial(&zone);
                let mut interner = Interner::new(&zone, source_len, &initial.tables());
                let mut expected = Vec::new();
                for prefix in [
                    b"".as_slice(),
                    b"a",
                    b"ab",
                    b"in",
                    b"\0a",
                    b"a\0b",
                    b"abcdefgh",
                    b"abcdefghijklmnop",
                ] {
                    for index in 0..=17 - prefix.len() {
                        let padding = if reverse { 17 - prefix.len() - index } else { index };
                        let mut name = prefix.to_vec();
                        name.resize(prefix.len() + padding, 0);
                        let id = interner.intern_bytes(&name);
                        assert_eq!(interner.text(id), name);
                        expected.push((name, id));
                    }
                }

                // Grow the tables before looking up the names again.
                for index in 0..512 {
                    interner.intern_bytes(format!("extra_name_{index}").as_bytes());
                }
                for (name, id) in &expected {
                    assert_eq!(interner.intern_bytes(name), *id);
                }

                // NB: The tables of a reparse context are a copy of those that an interner makes with the names.
                let made = Interner::with_names(&zone, (0..interner.len()).map(|id| interner.text(id as u32)));
                let tables = made.tables();
                let kept = NameTablesMut {
                    rows: zone.alloc_slice_copy(tables.rows),
                    shift: tables.shift,
                    count: tables.count,
                    long_rows: zone.alloc_slice_copy(tables.long_rows),
                    long_count: tables.long_count,
                    text: zone.alloc_slice_copy(tables.text),
                    spans: zone.alloc_slice_copy(tables.spans),
                };
                let mut reparsed = Interner::of_tables(&zone, kept);
                for (name, id) in &expected {
                    assert_eq!(reparsed.intern_bytes(name), *id);
                    assert_eq!(reparsed.text(*id), name);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! The tokenizer. It runs on demand, one token ahead of the parser, because `/` and `}` mean different things depending
//! on where the parser is. No value is computed for numbers or strings here: a literal is validated and left in the
//! source, and only code that gets compiled reads it again.

use super::base::Parser;
use super::base::RECURSION_LIMIT_MESSAGE;
use super::base::RegexCheckError;
use super::token::*;
use super::unit::*;

const fn keyword_kinds() -> [T; 36] {
    let mut kinds = [T::Eof; 36];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 36 {
        kinds[i] = KEYWORDS[i].1;
        i += 1;
    }
    kinds
}
static KEYWORD_KINDS: [T; 36] = keyword_kinds();

// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-IdentifierStartChar
// IdentifierStartChar :: UnicodeIDStart | $ | _
#[inline]
pub fn is_id_start(c: u32) -> bool {
    if c < 128 {
        return (c as u8).is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == 0x24 || c == 0x5F;
    }
    libunicode_rust::character_types::code_point_has_identifier_start_property(c)
}

// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-IdentifierPartChar
// IdentifierPartChar :: UnicodeIDContinue | $
#[inline]
pub fn is_id_continue(c: u32) -> bool {
    if c < 128 {
        return (c as u8).is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == 0x24 || c == 0x5F;
    }
    matches!(c, 0x200C | 0x200D) || libunicode_rust::character_types::code_point_has_identifier_continue_property(c)
}

#[inline]
fn is_unicode_whitespace(c: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0xA0 | 0xFEFF | 0x1680 | 0x2000..=0x200A | 0x202F | 0x205F | 0x3000)
}

#[inline]
fn hex_value(c: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    char::from_u32(c)?.to_digit(16)
}

impl<'a: 'k, 'k, U: Unit> Parser<'a, 'k, U> {
    /// The unit at `index`, which may be in the padding after the source.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn at(&self, index: usize) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: The lexer never goes further than one block into the padding.
        unsafe { (*self.src.wrapping_add(index)).code() }
    }

    /// The source text from `start` up to `end`.
    pub(crate) fn source_view(&self, start: usize, end: usize) -> &[U] {
        debug_assert!(start <= end && end <= self.len as usize);
        // SAFETY: The range is within the source.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.src.wrapping_add(start), end - start) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn block(&self, index: usize) -> Block {
        // SAFETY: As for at().
        unsafe { U::load(self.src.wrapping_add(index)) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn next(&mut self) {
        self.prev_end = self.tok_end;
        self.prev_start = self.tok_start;
        self.lex();
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn token(&mut self, kind: T, end: usize) {
        self.tok = kind;
        self.tok_end = end as u32;
        self.pos = end as u32;
    }

    pub(crate) fn lex(&mut self) {
        // NB: A parse that has failed lexes no further into the source, whose end may have no padding.
        if self.err.is_some() {
            self.tok = T::Eof;
            return;
        }
        let mut p = self.pos as usize;
        let mut newline = false;
        let c = loop {
            let c = self.at(p);
            match c {
                0x20 | 0x09 | 0x0B | 0x0C => p += 1,
                0x0A | 0x0D => {
                    newline = true;
                    p += 1;
                }
                0x2F => {
                    let d = self.at(p + 1);
                    if d == 0x2F {
                        p = self.skip_line_comment(p + 2);
                    } else if d == 0x2A {
                        match self.skip_block_comment(p + 2) {
                            Some((end, had_newline)) => {
                                p = end;
                                newline |= had_newline;
                            }
                            None => {
                                self.fail(self.len, "Unterminated multi-line comment");
                                return;
                            }
                        }
                    } else {
                        break c;
                    }
                }
                0x3C if !self.module && self.at(p + 1) == 0x21 && self.at(p + 2) == 0x2D && self.at(p + 3) == 0x2D => {
                    p = self.skip_line_comment(p + 4);
                }
                0x2D if !self.module
                    && (newline || self.tok_end == 0)
                    && self.at(p + 1) == 0x2D
                    && self.at(p + 2) == 0x3E =>
                {
                    p = self.skip_line_comment(p + 3);
                }
                _ if c >= 0x80 => {
                    if c == 0x2028 || c == 0x2029 {
                        newline = true;
                        p += 1;
                    } else if is_unicode_whitespace(c) {
                        p += 1;
                    } else {
                        break c;
                    }
                }
                _ => break c,
            }
        };
        self.nl_before = newline;
        self.tok_start = p as u32;

        if c >= 0x80 {
            self.lex_identifier_slow(p, false);
            return;
        }
        match c as u8 {
            b'a'..=b'z' | b'A'..=b'Z' | b'_' | b'$' => self.lex_identifier(p),
            b'0'..=b'9' => self.lex_number(p),
            b'"' | b'\'' => self.lex_string(p, c as u8),
            b'`' => self.token(T::Backtick, p + 1),
            b'(' => self.token(T::LParen, p + 1),
            b')' => self.token(T::RParen, p + 1),
            b'{' => self.token(T::LBrace, p + 1),
            b'}' => self.token(T::RBrace, p + 1),
            b'[' => self.token(T::LBracket, p + 1),
            b']' => self.token(T::RBracket, p + 1),
            b';' => self.token(T::Semi, p + 1),
            b',' => self.token(T::Comma, p + 1),
            b':' => self.token(T::Colon, p + 1),
            b'~' => self.token(T::Tilde, p + 1),
            b'.' => {
                let d = self.at(p + 1);
                if (0x30..=0x39).contains(&d) {
                    self.lex_number(p);
                } else if d == 0x2E && self.at(p + 2) == 0x2E {
                    self.token(T::Ellipsis, p + 3);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Dot, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'=' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::EqEqEq, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::EqEq, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3E {
                    self.token(T::Arrow, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Assign, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'!' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::NotEqEq, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::NotEq, p + 2);
                    }
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Not, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'+' => match self.at(p + 1) {
                0x2B => self.token(T::Inc, p + 2),
                0x3D => self.token(T::AddAssign, p + 2),
                _ => self.token(T::Plus, p + 1),
            },
            b'-' => match self.at(p + 1) {
                0x2D => self.token(T::Dec, p + 2),
                0x3D => self.token(T::SubAssign, p + 2),
                _ => self.token(T::Minus, p + 1),
            },
            b'*' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x2A {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::ExpAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::StarStar, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::MulAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Star, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'/' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::DivAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Slash, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'%' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::ModAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Percent, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'<' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3C {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::ShlAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::Shl, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::Le, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Lt, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'>' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3E {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3E {
                        if self.at(p + 3) == 0x3D {
                            self.token(T::UShrAssign, p + 4);
                        } else {
                            self.token(T::UShr, p + 3);
                        }
                    } else if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::ShrAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::Shr, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::Ge, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Gt, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'&' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x26 {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::LogAndAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::LogAnd, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::AndAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::BitAnd, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'|' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x7C {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::LogOrAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::LogOr, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::OrAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::BitOr, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'^' => {
                if self.at(p + 1) == 0x3D {
                    self.token(T::XorAssign, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::BitXor, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'?' => {
                let d = self.at(p + 1);
                if d == 0x3F {
                    if self.at(p + 2) == 0x3D {
                        self.token(T::NullishAssign, p + 3);
                    } else {
                        self.token(T::Nullish, p + 2);
                    }
                } else if d == 0x2E && !(0x30..=0x39).contains(&self.at(p + 2)) {
                    self.token(T::QDot, p + 2);
                } else {
                    self.token(T::Question, p + 1);
                }
            }
            b'#' => self.lex_identifier_slow(p + 1, true),
            b'\\' => self.lex_identifier_slow(p, false),
            0 if p >= self.len as usize => {
                self.tok = T::Eof;
                self.tok_end = p as u32;
                self.pos = p as u32;
            }
            _ => {
                self.tok_start = p as u32;
                self.token(T::Invalid, p + 1);
            }
        }
    }

    fn skip_line_comment(&mut self, start: usize) -> usize {
        let mut p = start;
        let len = self.len as usize;
        loop {
            let x = self.block(p);
            // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
            let mut mask = unsafe { eq_mask(x, b'\n') | eq_mask(x, b'\r') };
            if U::WIDE {
                // SAFETY: As above.
                mask |= unsafe { high_mask(x) };
            }
            while mask != 0 {
                let q = p + mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                let c = self.at(q);
                if c == 0x0A || c == 0x0D || c == 0x2028 || c == 0x2029 {
                    return q.min(len);
                }
                mask &= mask - 1;
            }
            p += BLOCK;
            if p >= len {
                return len;
            }
        }
    }

    fn skip_block_comment(&mut self, start: usize) -> Option<(usize, bool)> {
        let mut p = start;
        let len = self.len as usize;
        let mut newline = false;
        loop {
            let x = self.block(p);
            // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
            let mut mask = unsafe {
                let mut mask = eq_mask(x, b'*') | eq_mask(x, b'\n') | eq_mask(x, b'\r');
                if U::WIDE {
                    mask |= high_mask(x);
                }
                mask
            };
            while mask != 0 {
                let q = p + mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
                match self.at(q) {
                    0x2A => {
                        if self.at(q + 1) == 0x2F && q + 1 < len {
                            return Some((q + 2, newline));
                        }
                    }
                    0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029 => newline = true,
                    _ => {}
                }
                mask &= mask - 1;
            }
            p += BLOCK;
            if p >= len {
                return None;
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn lex_identifier(&mut self, p: usize) {
        let x = self.block(p);
        // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
        let n = unsafe { (!ident_mask(x)).trailing_zeros() } as usize;
        let stop = self.at(p + n);
        if n > 16 || n == BLOCK || stop >= 0x80 || stop == 0x5C {
            self.lex_identifier_long(p);
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: As above.
        let (k0, k1) = unsafe { key_of(x, n) };
        let id = self.interner.intern_key(k0, k1, n);
        self.tok_name = id;
        self.tok_escaped = false;
        self.tok = if id < KEYWORD_COUNT {
            KEYWORD_KINDS[id as usize]
        } else {
            T::Name
        };
        self.tok_end = (p + n) as u32;
        self.pos = (p + n) as u32;
    }

    /// An ASCII name of more than 16 units, or the start of something the slow path has to look at.
    #[inline(never)]
    fn lex_identifier_long(&mut self, p: usize) {
        let mut q = p;
        loop {
            // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
            let n = unsafe { (!ident_mask(self.block(q))).trailing_zeros() } as usize;
            q += n;
            if n < BLOCK {
                break;
            }
        }
        let stop = self.at(q);
        if stop >= 0x80 || stop == 0x5C {
            self.lex_identifier_slow(p, false);
            return;
        }
        self.name_buffer.clear();
        for i in p..q {
            let c = self.at(i) as u8;
            self.name_buffer.push(c);
        }
        let id = self.interner.intern_bytes(&self.name_buffer);
        self.tok_name = id;
        self.tok_escaped = false;
        self.tok = if id < KEYWORD_COUNT {
            KEYWORD_KINDS[id as usize]
        } else {
            T::Name
        };
        self.tok_end = q as u32;
        self.pos = q as u32;
    }

    fn code_point_at(&self, p: usize) -> (u32, usize) {
        let c = self.at(p);
        if U::WIDE && (0xD800..0xDC00).contains(&c) {
            let d = self.at(p + 1);
            if (0xDC00..0xE000).contains(&d) {
                return (0x10000 + ((c - 0xD800) << 10) + (d - 0xDC00), 2);
            }
        }
        (c, 1)
    }

    /// `\uXXXX` or `\u{X...}` from the `u`. Returns the code point and the position after it.
    fn read_unicode_escape(&self, p: usize) -> Option<(u32, usize)> {
        if self.at(p) != 0x75 {
            return None;
        }
        if self.at(p + 1) == 0x7B {
            let mut q = p + 2;
            let mut value = 0u32;
            let mut digits = 0;
            while let Some(digit) = hex_value(self.at(q)) {
                value = value * 16 + digit;
                if value > 0x10FFFF {
                    return None;
                }
                digits += 1;
                q += 1;
            }
            if digits == 0 || self.at(q) != 0x7D {
                return None;
            }
            Some((value, q + 1))
        } else {
            let mut value = 0;
            for i in 1..=4 {
                value = value * 16 + hex_value(self.at(p + i))?;
            }
            Some((value, p + 5))
        }
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    fn lex_identifier_slow(&mut self, start: usize, private: bool) {
        let mut p = start;
        let mut escaped = false;
        let mut first = true;
        let mut buffer = self.name_buffer.take();
        buffer.clear();
        loop {
            let (mut c, width) = self.code_point_at(p);
            let mut next = p + width;
            if c == 0x5C {
                let Some((value, after)) = self.read_unicode_escape(p + 1) else {
                    self.fail(p as u32, "Malformed unicode escape sequence");
                    break;
                };
                c = value;
                next = after;
                escaped = true;
                let valid = if first { is_id_start(c) } else { is_id_continue(c) };
                if !valid {
                    self.fail(p as u32, "Invalid escaped identifier character");
                    break;
                }
            } else if !(if first { is_id_start(c) } else { is_id_continue(c) }) {
                break;
            }
            let mut encoded = [0u8; 4];
            let ch = char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}');
            buffer.extend_from_slice(ch.encode_utf8(&mut encoded).as_bytes());
            first = false;
            p = next;
        }
        if self.err.is_some() {
            self.name_buffer = buffer;
            return;
        }
        if first {
            self.name_buffer = buffer;
            self.fail(p as u32, "Illegal character");
            return;
        }
        let id = self.interner.intern_bytes(&buffer);
        self.name_buffer = buffer;
        self.tok_name = id;
        self.tok_escaped = escaped;
        self.tok = if private {
            T::PrivateName
        } else if id < KEYWORD_COUNT {
            if escaped {
                T::EscapedKeyword
            } else {
                KEYWORD_KINDS[id as usize]
            }
        } else {
            T::Name
        };
        self.tok_end = p as u32;
        self.pos = p as u32;
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    fn lex_number(&mut self, start: usize) {
        let mut p = start;
        let first = self.at(p);
        let mut kind = T::Num;
        self.tok_legacy = false;
        let radix = if first == 0x30 {
            match self.at(p + 1) | 0x20 {
                0x78 => 16,
                0x6F => 8,
                0x62 => 2,
                _ => 10,
            }
        } else {
            10
        };
        if radix != 10 {
            p += 2;
            if !self.scan_digits(&mut p, radix, true) {
                return;
            }
            if self.at(p) == 0x6E {
                kind = T::BigInt;
                p += 1;
            }
        } else if first == 0x30 && (0x30..=0x39).contains(&self.at(p + 1)) {
            // Legacy octal, or a decimal with a leading zero.
            self.tok_legacy = true;
            let mut octal = true;
            while (0x30..=0x39).contains(&self.at(p)) {
                if self.at(p) >= 0x38 {
                    octal = false;
                }
                p += 1;
            }
            if self.at(p) == 0x5F {
                self.fail(
                    p as u32,
                    "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
                );
                return;
            }
            if !octal && !self.scan_fraction_and_exponent(&mut p) {
                return;
            }
        } else {
            if first != 0x2E {
                if !self.scan_digits(&mut p, 10, true) {
                    return;
                }
                if first == 0x30 && p != start + 1 {
                    self.fail(
                        start as u32,
                        "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
                    );
                    return;
                }
                if self.at(p) == 0x6E {
                    kind = T::BigInt;
                    p += 1;
                }
            }
            if kind == T::Num && !self.scan_fraction_and_exponent(&mut p) {
                return;
            }
        }
        let (c, _) = self.code_point_at(p);
        if is_id_start(c) || (0x30..=0x39).contains(&c) || c == 0x5C {
            self.fail(
                p as u32,
                "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
            );
            return;
        }
        self.token(kind, p);
    }

    fn scan_fraction_and_exponent(&mut self, p: &mut usize) -> bool {
        if self.at(*p) == 0x2E {
            *p += 1;
            if (0x30..=0x39).contains(&self.at(*p)) && !self.scan_digits(p, 10, true) {
                return false;
            }
            if self.at(*p) == 0x5F {
                self.fail(
                    *p as u32,
                    "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
                );
                return false;
            }
        }
        if self.at(*p) | 0x20 == 0x65 {
            *p += 1;
            if matches!(self.at(*p), 0x2B | 0x2D) {
                *p += 1;
            }
            if !self.scan_digits(p, 10, true) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        true
    }

    fn scan_digits(&mut self, p: &mut usize, radix: u32, separators: bool) -> bool {
        let start = *p;
        let mut last_separator = false;
        loop {
            let c = self.at(*p);
            if c == 0x5F && separators {
                if last_separator || *p == start {
                    self.fail(
                        *p as u32,
                        "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
                    );
                    return false;
                }
                last_separator = true;
                *p += 1;
                continue;
            }
            match char::from_u32(c).and_then(|ch| ch.to_digit(radix)) {
                Some(_) => {
                    last_separator = false;
                    *p += 1;
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }
        if last_separator {
            self.fail(
                *p as u32,
                "Numeric literal must not be immediately followed by identifier",
            );
            return false;
        }
        if *p == start {
            self.fail(start as u32, "Invalid numeric literal");
            return false;
        }
        true
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn lex_string(&mut self, start: usize, quote: u8) {
        self.tok_legacy = false;
        self.tok_escaped = false;
        let len = self.len as usize;
        let mut p = start + 1;
        loop {
            let x = self.block(p);
            // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
            let mask = unsafe { eq_mask(x, quote) | eq_mask(x, b'\\') | eq_mask(x, b'\n') | eq_mask(x, b'\r') };
            if mask == 0 {
                p += BLOCK;
                if p >= len {
                    self.fail(start as u32, "Unterminated string literal");
                    return;
                }
                continue;
            }
            p += mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
            let c = self.at(p);
            if c == quote as u32 {
                self.token(T::Str, p + 1);
                return;
            }
            if c == 0x5C {
                self.tok_escaped = true;
                match self.skip_escape(p + 1) {
                    Some(after) => p = after,
                    None => return,
                }
            } else {
                self.fail(start as u32, "Unterminated string literal");
                return;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Validates a string escape from the unit after the backslash, and returns the position after it.
    #[inline(never)]
    fn skip_escape(&mut self, p: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let c = self.at(p);
        match c {
            0x0D => Some(if self.at(p + 1) == 0x0A { p + 2 } else { p + 1 }),
            0x78 => {
                if hex_value(self.at(p + 1)).is_some() && hex_value(self.at(p + 2)).is_some() {
                    Some(p + 3)
                } else {
                    self.fail(p as u32, "Malformed hexadecimal escape sequence");
                    None
                }
            }
            0x75 => match self.read_unicode_escape(p) {
                Some((_, after)) => Some(after),
                None => {
                    self.fail(p as u32, "Malformed unicode escape sequence");
                    None
                }
            },
            0x30..=0x37 => {
                let next = self.at(p + 1);
                if c == 0x30 && !(0x30..=0x39).contains(&next) {
                    return Some(p + 1);
                }
                self.tok_legacy = true;
                let mut q = p + 1;
                if (0x30..=0x37).contains(&self.at(q)) {
                    q += 1;
                    if c <= 0x33 && (0x30..=0x37).contains(&self.at(q)) {
                        q += 1;
                    }
                }
                Some(q)
            }
            0x38 | 0x39 => {
                self.tok_legacy = true;
                Some(p + 1)
            }
            0 if p >= self.len as usize => {
                self.fail(p as u32, "Unterminated string literal");
                None
            }
            _ => Some(p + self.code_point_at(p).1),
        }
    }

    /// Reads template characters from `self.pos`. Returns whether the chunk ended the template, and whether it has an
    /// escape that only a tagged template may contain, and leaves `self.pos` after the closing `` ` `` or `${`.
    pub(crate) fn read_template_chunk(&mut self) -> (bool, bool) {
        let len = self.len as usize;
        let mut p = self.pos as usize;
        let mut invalid = false;
        loop {
            let x = self.block(p);
            // SAFETY: The block came from a load.
            let mask = unsafe { eq_mask(x, b'`') | eq_mask(x, b'$') | eq_mask(x, b'\\') };
            if mask == 0 {
                p += BLOCK;
                if p >= len {
                    break;
                }
                continue;
            }
            p += mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
            if p >= len {
                break;
            }
            match self.at(p) {
                0x60 => {
                    self.pos = (p + 1) as u32;
                    return (true, invalid);
                }
                0x24 => {
                    if self.at(p + 1) == 0x7B {
                        self.pos = (p + 2) as u32;
                        return (false, invalid);
                    }
                    p += 1;
                }
                _ => {
                    let c = self.at(p + 1);
                    match c {
                        0x30 if !(0x30..=0x39).contains(&self.at(p + 2)) => p += 2,
                        0x30..=0x39 => {
                            invalid = true;
                            p += 2;
                        }
                        0x78 => {
                            if hex_value(self.at(p + 2)).is_some() && hex_value(self.at(p + 3)).is_some() {
                                p += 4;
                            } else {
                                invalid = true;
                                p += 2;
                            }
                        }
                        0x75 => match self.read_unicode_escape(p + 1) {
                            Some((_, after)) => p = after,
                            None => {
                                invalid = true;
                                p += 2;
                            }
                        },
                        0x0D if self.at(p + 2) == 0x0A => p += 3,
                        _ => p += 1 + self.code_point_at(p + 1).1,
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        self.fail(self.tok_start, "Unterminated template literal");
        (true, false)
    }

    /// Reads a regular expression literal in place of the `/` or `/=` token.
    pub(crate) fn rescan_regex(&mut self) {
        let start = self.tok_start as usize;
        let len = self.len as usize;
        let mut p = start + 1;
        let mut in_class = false;
        loop {
            if p >= len {
                self.fail(start as u32, "Unterminated regular expression literal");
                return;
            }
            let c = self.at(p);
            match c {
                0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029 => {
                    self.fail(start as u32, "Unterminated regular expression literal");
                    return;
                }
                0x5C => {
                    let d = self.at(p + 1);
                    if matches!(d, 0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029) {
                        self.fail(start as u32, "Unterminated regular expression literal");
                        return;
                    }
                    p += 2;
                    continue;
                }
                0x5B => in_class = true,
                0x5D => in_class = false,
                0x2F if !in_class => break,
                _ => {}
            }
            p += 1;
        }
        self.regex_body_end = p as u32;
        p += 1;
        let flags_start = p;
        loop {
            let (c, width) = self.code_point_at(p);
            if c == 0x5C {
                self.fail(p as u32, "Invalid regular expression flags");
                return;
            }
            if !is_id_continue(c) {
                break;
            }
            p += width;
        }
        let zone = self.zone;
        let flags: &[u16] = zone.alloc_slice_from_iter((flags_start..p).map(|i| self.at(i) as u16));
        let mut seen = [false; 128];
        for &flag in flags {
            if flag >= 128 || !b"dgimsuvy".contains(&(flag as u8)) {
                let flag = char::from_u32(flag as u32).unwrap_or('?');
                let message = self.message(format_args!("Invalid RegExp flag '{flag}'"));
                self.fail(self.tok_start, message);
                return;
            }
            if seen[flag as usize] {
                let flag = flag as u8 as char;
                let message = self.message(format_args!("Repeated RegExp flag '{flag}'"));
                self.fail(self.tok_start, message);
                return;
            }
            seen[flag as usize] = true;
        }
        // 13.2.7.1 Static Semantics: Early Errors, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-primary-expression-regular-expression-literals-static-semantics-early-errors
        // PrimaryExpression : RegularExpressionLiteral
        // It is a Syntax Error if IsValidRegularExpressionLiteral(RegularExpressionLiteral) is false.
        // NB: A reparse only follows a first parse that checked every pattern.
        if !self.is_reparsing() {
            let pattern: &[u16] =
                zone.alloc_slice_from_iter((start + 1..self.regex_body_end as usize).map(|i| self.at(i) as u16));
            if let Err(error) = (self.validate_regex)(zone, pattern, flags) {
                let message = match error {
                    RegexCheckError::Invalid(message) => message,
                    RegexCheckError::OutOfStack => RECURSION_LIMIT_MESSAGE,
                };
                self.fail(start as u32, message);
                return;
            }
        }
        self.token(T::Regex, p);
    }
}

//! The core of the LibJS parser: the lexer, the parser, the interner of names, the columns of the syntax tree and the
//! resolver.
//!
//! A parse job has all of its work data in one zone (see `ak::Zone`), which the code that starts the job hands it. What
//! the job keeps of its results is copied out of the zone by that code, which is also what reaches the runtime for the
//! parser (see `base::ValidateRegex`).

// NB: A parse job makes no block in the heap: all its work data is in its zone. Without `std` (and without `alloc`),
//     rustc rejects code of the parser that would make one. The tests keep `std`.
#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]

pub mod base;
pub mod columns;
pub mod escapes;
mod expr;
pub mod intern;
mod lexer;
pub mod resolve;
mod stmt;
pub mod token;
pub mod tree;
pub mod unit;

/// Convert a `usize` to `u32`, panicking if the value exceeds `u32::MAX`.
/// Prefer this over `as u32` which silently truncates on 64-bit platforms.
#[inline]
pub fn u32_from_usize(value: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(value).expect("value exceeds u32::MAX")
}
