//! Generates Rust bytecode instruction types from Flap.
//!
//! The generated code lives in $OUT_DIR/instruction_generated.rs and is
//! included! from src/bytecode/instruction.rs.

use flapc::metadata::Field;
use flapc::metadata::InstructionDefinition;
use flapc::metadata::Specialization;
use flapc::metadata::SpecializationConstraint;
use flapc::metadata::SpecializedInstruction;
use flapc::metadata::SpecializedParameterBinding;
use flapc::metadata::compute_layouts;
use flapc::metadata::field_type_info;
use flapc::metadata::user_fields;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::ArrayFields;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::InstructionSet;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::count_field_name;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_encode_method;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_field_reads;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_instruction_enum;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_instruction_is_terminator_from_opcode;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_instruction_length_from_bytes;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_instruction_name_from_opcode;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_num_opcodes_const;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_opcode_enum;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::generate_typed_instructions;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::rust_field_name;
use flapc::rust_bytecode::scaled;
use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;

/// Path prefix of the `read_u32` / `read_u64` helpers used by generated field reads.
const READER: &str = "super::operand::";

fn generate_rust_code(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
    specializations: &[Specialization],
    specialized_ops: &[SpecializedInstruction],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    writeln!(w, "// @generated from Libraries/LibJS/Interpreter/interpreter.flap")?;
    writeln!(w, "// Do not edit manually.")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    writeln!(w, "use super::operand::*;")?;
    writeln!(w)?;

    generate_opcode_enum(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_num_opcodes_const(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_instruction_enum(&mut w, ops, "Debug, Clone", ArrayFields::Owned)?;
    generate_instruction_impl(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_instruction_length_from_bytes(&mut w, ops, "super::operand::InstructionLengthError")?;
    generate_instruction_name_from_opcode(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_instruction_dump_from_bytes(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_visit_labels_from_bytes(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_visit_operands_from_bytes(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_instruction_is_terminator_from_opcode(&mut w, ops)?;
    generate_specialization_selector(&mut w, ops, specializations, specialized_ops)?;
    generate_typed_instructions(
        &mut w,
        ops,
        "typed",
        "crate::bytecode::codegen::emitter::BlockEncoder<'_>",
        &|name| specializable_operands(name, specializations),
    )?;

    Ok(())
}

/// The operands of the instruction called `name` that a specialization looks at.
fn specializable_operands(name: &str, specializations: &[Specialization]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut operands = Vec::new();
    for specialization in specializations {
        if name != "Mov" && specialization.bytecode == name {
            for parameter in &specialization.parameters {
                let operand = rust_field_name(&parameter.name);
                if !operands.contains(&operand) {
                    operands.push(operand);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    operands
}

/// Emits `instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes()`, which reads the feedback slot indices of the instruction at
/// `bytes[at..]`, one per feedback kind it records.
fn generate_instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    const KINDS: [&str; 5] = [
        "ArithFeedbackIndex",
        "ValueFeedbackIndex",
        "CallFeedbackIndex",
        "KeyedFeedbackIndex",
        "ProfiledPropertyLookupCacheIndex",
    ];
    writeln!(
        w,
        "/// The feedback slot indices of the instruction at `bytes[at..]`: arith, value, call, keyed and the property"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "/// lookup cache whose site's value feedback it records.")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "pub fn instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes(opcode: u8, bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> [Option<u16>; 5] {{"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "    match opcode {{")?;
    for (i, op) in ops.iter().enumerate() {
        let slots = KINDS
            .iter()
            .map(|kind| {
                user_fields(op).into_iter().find(|field| field.ty == *kind).map_or_else(
                    || "None".to_string(),
                    |field| {
                        let offset = op.layout.field_offsets[&field.name];
                        format!("Some({READER}read_u16(bytes, at + {offset}))")
                    },
                )
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if slots.iter().all(|slot| slot == "None") {
            continue;
        }
        writeln!(w, "        {i} => [{}], // {}", slots.join(", "), op.name)?;
    }
    writeln!(w, "        _ => [None; 5],")?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    writeln!(w, "}}")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_specialization_selector(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
    specializations: &[Specialization],
    specialized_ops: &[SpecializedInstruction],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut order = (0..specializations.len()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    order.sort_by_key(|index| std::cmp::Reverse(specializations[*index].parameters.len()));

    writeln!(w, "#[allow(unused_variables)]")?;
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(clippy::clone_on_copy)]")?;
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(clippy::collapsible_if)]")?;
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(clippy::redundant_clone)]")?;
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_unwrap)]")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "pub fn specialize_instruction(instruction: &Instruction, constants: &[super::executable_data::ConstantValue]) -> Option<Instruction> {{"
    )?;
    for index in order {
        let specialization = &specializations[index];
        let specialized_op = &specialized_ops[index];
        let op = &specialization.bytecode;
        let base_op = ops
            .iter()
            .find(|definition| definition.name == *op)
            .expect("specialization bytecodes are validated");
        let bindings = user_fields(base_op)
            .iter()
            .map(|field| rust_field_name(&field.name))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        writeln!(
            w,
            "    if let Instruction::{op} {{ {} }} = instruction {{",
            bindings.join(", ")
        )?;

        let mut conditions = Vec::new();
        let mut extracted_values = Vec::new();
        for parameter in &specialization.parameters {
            let operand = &parameter.name;
            match &parameter.constraint {
                SpecializationConstraint::Int32 => {
                    let value = format!("specialized_{operand}");
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "            let {value} = constants.get({operand}.index() as usize).and_then(|constant| match constant {{"
                    )?;
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "                super::executable_data::ConstantValue::Number(number) if number.fract() == 0.0 && *number >= i32::MIN as f64 && *number <= i32::MAX as f64 && number.to_bits() != (-0.0_f64).to_bits() => Some(*number as i32),"
                    )?;
                    writeln!(w, "                _ => None,")?;
                    writeln!(w, "            }});")?;
                    conditions.push(format!("{operand}.is_constant() && {value}.is_some()"));
                    extracted_values.push(value);
                }
                SpecializationConstraint::Undefined => {
                    conditions.push(format!(
                        "{operand}.is_constant() && matches!(constants.get({operand}.index() as usize), Some(super::executable_data::ConstantValue::Undefined))"
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        if !conditions.is_empty() {
            writeln!(w, "            if {} {{", conditions.join(" && "))?;
        }
        for value in &extracted_values {
            writeln!(w, "                let {value} = {value}.unwrap();")?;
        }
        writeln!(
            w,
            "                return Some(Instruction::{} {{",
            specialized_op.definition.name
        )?;
        for field in &specialized_op.definition.fields {
            let field_name = rust_field_name(&field.name);
            let parameter = specialized_op
                .parameters
                .iter()
                .find_map(|(parameter, binding)| {
                    (binding == &SpecializedParameterBinding::Field(field_name.clone())).then_some(parameter)
                })
                .expect("every specialized field has a source");
            let is_int32 = specialization.parameters.iter().any(|specialized| {
                &specialized.name == parameter && matches!(specialized.constraint, SpecializationConstraint::Int32)
            });
            let source = if is_int32 {
                format!("specialized_{parameter}")
            } else {
                format!("(*{parameter}).clone()")
            };
            writeln!(w, "                    {field_name}: {source},")?;
        }
        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
        if !conditions.is_empty() {
            writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
        }
        writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    }
    writeln!(w, "    None")?;
    writeln!(w, "}}")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_array_bounds(
    w: &mut impl Write,
    op: &InstructionDefinition,
    layouts: &std::collections::HashMap<String, flapc::metadata::OpLayout>,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let layout = layouts.get(&op.name).expect("layout missing for op");
    for f in user_fields(op) {
        if !f.is_array {
            continue;
        }
        let rname = rust_field_name(&f.name);
        let count_name = rust_field_name(count_field_name(op, f));
        let offset = layout.field_offsets.get(&f.name).expect("array offset missing");
        let elem_size = field_type_info(&f.ty).size;
        writeln!(w, "            let {rname}_offset = at + {offset};")?;
        writeln!(w, "            let {rname}_count = {count_name} as usize;")?;
        let length = scaled(&format!("{rname}_count"), elem_size);
        writeln!(w, "            let {rname}_end = {rname}_offset + {length};")?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_instruction_dump_from_bytes(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let layouts = compute_layouts(ops);

    writeln!(w, "#[cfg(not(test))]")?;
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(unused_variables)]")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "pub fn dump_instruction_from_bytes(opcode: u8, bytes: &[u8], at: usize, dumper: &mut super::dump::BytecodeDumper<'_>) {{"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "    match opcode {{")?;

    for (i, op) in ops.iter().enumerate() {
        if op.name == "Instruction" {
            continue;
        }
        writeln!(w, "        {i} => {{")?;
        generate_field_reads(&mut w, op, READER)?;
        generate_array_bounds(&mut w, op, &layouts)?;
        writeln!(w, "            dumper.begin_instruction(\"{}\");", op.name)?;

        let arrays: Vec<&Field> = op.fields.iter().filter(|f| f.is_array).collect();
        let mut array_to_count = std::collections::HashMap::new();
        let mut count_fields = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for af in arrays {
            let count_field_name = count_field_name(op, af);
            count_fields.insert(count_field_name);
            array_to_count.insert(af.name.clone(), rust_field_name(count_field_name));
        }

        for f in &op.fields {
            if f.name == "m_length" || f.name == "m_cache" {
                continue;
            }

            let ty = f.ty.trim();
            let label = rust_field_name(&f.name);
            let rname = rust_field_name(&f.name);

            if f.is_array {
                let count_name = array_to_count.get(&f.name).expect("array count missing");
                match ty {
                    "Operand" => {
                        writeln!(w, "            if {count_name} != 0 {{")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| {{")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                    dumper.append_operand_list(\"{label}\", bytes, {rname}_offset, {rname}_count);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
                        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                    }
                    "Optional<Operand>" => {
                        writeln!(w, "            if {count_name} != 0 {{")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| {{")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                    dumper.append_optional_operand_list(\"{label}\", bytes, {rname}_offset, {rname}_count);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
                        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                    }
                    "Value" => {
                        writeln!(w, "            if {count_name} != 0 {{")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| {{")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                    dumper.append_value_list(\"{label}\", bytes, {rname}_offset, {rname}_count);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
                        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                    }
                    "Label" => {
                        writeln!(w, "            if {count_name} != 0 {{")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| {{")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                    dumper.append_label_list(\"{label}\", bytes, {rname}_offset, {rname}_count);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
                        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                    }
                    "Optional<Label>" => {
                        writeln!(w, "            if {count_name} != 0 {{")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| {{")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                    dumper.append_optional_label_list(\"{label}\", bytes, {rname}_offset, {rname}_count);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                }});")?;
                        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
                continue;
            }

            match ty {
                "Operand" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_operand(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                )?,
                "Optional<Operand>" => {
                    writeln!(w, "            if let Some({rname}) = {rname} {{")?;
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_operand(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                    )?;
                    writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                }
                "Label" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_label(\"{label}\", {rname}.0));"
                )?,
                "Optional<Label>" => {
                    writeln!(w, "            if let Some({rname}) = {rname} {{")?;
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_label(\"{label}\", {rname}.0));"
                    )?;
                    writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                }
                "PropertyKeyTableIndex" => {
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_property_key_quoted({rname}.0));"
                    )?;
                }
                "IdentifierTableIndex" => {
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_identifier_quoted({rname}.0));"
                    )?;
                }
                "Optional<IdentifierTableIndex>" => {
                    let mut property_key_field = None;
                    let mut property_operand_field = None;
                    for other in &op.fields {
                        if other.ty.trim() == "PropertyKeyTableIndex" {
                            property_key_field = Some(rust_field_name(&other.name));
                            break;
                        }
                        if other.ty.trim() == "Operand" && other.name == "m_property" {
                            property_operand_field = Some(rust_field_name(&other.name));
                            break;
                        }
                    }

                    writeln!(w, "            if let Some({rname}) = {rname} {{")?;
                    if let Some(property_key_field) = property_key_field {
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\" \\u{{1b}}[37;1m(\");")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_identifier_plain({rname}.0);")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\".\");")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                dumper.append_property_key_plain({property_key_field}.0);"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\")\\u{{1b}}[0m\");")?;
                    } else if let Some(property_operand_field) = property_operand_field {
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\" \\u{{1b}}[37;1m(\");")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_identifier_plain({rname}.0);")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\"[\\u{{1b}}[0m\");")?;
                        writeln!(
                            w,
                            "                dumper.append_operand(\"\", {property_operand_field});"
                        )?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\"\\u{{1b}}[37;1m])\\u{{1b}}[0m\");")?;
                    } else if op.name == "GetLength" {
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\" \\u{{1b}}[37;1m(\");")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_identifier_plain({rname}.0);")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\".length)\\u{{1b}}[0m\");")?;
                    } else {
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\" \\u{{1b}}[37;1m(\");")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append_identifier_plain({rname}.0);")?;
                        writeln!(w, "                dumper.append(\")\\u{{1b}}[0m\");")?;
                    }
                    writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                }
                "StringTableIndex" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_string({rname}.0));"
                )?,
                "Optional<StringTableIndex>" => {
                    writeln!(w, "            if let Some({rname}) = {rname} {{")?;
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "                dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_string({rname}.0));"
                    )?;
                    writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
                }
                "bool" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_bool(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                )?,
                "PutKind" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_put_kind(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                )?,
                "ArithFeedbackIndex"
                | "ValueFeedbackIndex"
                | "CallFeedbackIndex"
                | "KeyedFeedbackIndex"
                | "PropertyLookupCacheIndex"
                | "ProfiledPropertyLookupCacheIndex"
                | "GlobalVariableCacheIndex"
                | "EnvironmentCoordinateCacheIndex"
                | "ObjectShapeCacheIndex" => writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_number(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                )?,
                _ if (ty == "i32" || ty == "u32" || ty == "u64" || ty == "u8" || ty == "u16")
                    && !count_fields.contains(f.name.as_str()) =>
                {
                    writeln!(
                        w,
                        "            dumper.append_piece(|dumper| dumper.append_number(\"{label}\", {rname}));"
                    )?;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        writeln!(w, "        }}")?;
    }

    writeln!(w, "        _ => unreachable!(\"unknown bytecode opcode\"),")?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    writeln!(w, "}}")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Emit the function that finds every operand of the instruction at an offset, for the code that rewrites what
/// has been assembled. It calls the visitor with the offset of the operand and whether the instruction reads it,
/// writes it, and may leave it out.
fn generate_visit_operands_from_bytes(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(unused_variables)]")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "pub fn visit_operands_from_bytes(opcode: u8, bytes: &[u8], at: usize, visitor: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, bool, bool, bool)) {{"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "    match opcode {{")?;
    for (i, op) in ops.iter().enumerate() {
        let operand_fields: Vec<&Field> = user_fields(op)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|f| f.ty == "Operand" || f.ty == "Optional<Operand>")
            .collect();
        if operand_fields.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        writeln!(w, "        {i} => {{")?;
        generate_field_reads(&mut w, op, READER)?;
        for f in operand_fields {
            let offset = op.layout.field_offsets[&f.name];
            let reads = f.mode != flapc::metadata::ParameterMode::Out;
            let writes = f.mode != flapc::metadata::ParameterMode::In;
            let optional = f.ty != "Operand";
            if f.is_array {
                let count = rust_field_name(count_field_name(op, f));
                let element_size = op.array.as_ref().expect("array metadata").element_size;
                writeln!(w, "            for index in 0..{count} as usize {{")?;
                let element_offset = scaled("index", element_size);
                writeln!(
                    w,
                    "                visitor(at + {offset} + {element_offset}, {reads}, {writes}, {optional});"
                )?;
                writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
            } else {
                writeln!(w, "            visitor(at + {offset}, {reads}, {writes}, {optional});")?;
            }
        }
        writeln!(w, "        }}")?;
    }
    writeln!(w, "        _ => {{}}")?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    writeln!(w, "}}")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_visit_labels_from_bytes(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    writeln!(w, "#[allow(unused_variables)]")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "pub fn visit_labels_from_bytes(opcode: u8, bytes: &[u8], at: usize, visitor: &mut dyn FnMut(u32)) {{"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "    match opcode {{")?;

    for (i, op) in ops.iter().enumerate() {
        let label_fields: Vec<&Field> = user_fields(op)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|f| f.ty == "Label" || f.ty == "Optional<Label>")
            .collect();
        if label_fields.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        writeln!(w, "        {i} => {{")?;
        generate_field_reads(&mut w, op, READER)?;
        for f in label_fields {
            let rname = rust_field_name(&f.name);
            if f.ty == "Label" {
                writeln!(w, "            visitor({rname}.0);")?;
            } else {
                writeln!(
                    w,
                    "            if let Some({rname}) = {rname} {{ visitor({rname}.0); }}"
                )?;
            }
        }
        writeln!(w, "        }}")?;
    }

    writeln!(w, "        _ => {{}}")?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    writeln!(w, "}}")?;
    writeln!(w)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_instruction_impl(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    writeln!(w, "impl Instruction {{").unwrap();
    generate_encode_method(
        &mut w,
        ops,
        "encode_into_block",
        "crate::bytecode::codegen::emitter::BlockEncoder<'_>",
        ArrayFields::Owned,
    )?;
    generate_visit_labels_method(&mut w, ops)?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    Ok(())
}

fn generate_visit_labels_method(
    mut w: impl Write,
    ops: &[InstructionDefinition],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    writeln!(w, "    /// Visit all `Label` fields (for label linking).")?;
    writeln!(
        w,
        "    pub fn visit_labels(&mut self, visitor: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Label)) {{"
    )?;
    writeln!(w, "        match self {{")?;

    for op in ops {
        let fields = user_fields(op);
        let label_fields: Vec<&&Field> = fields
            .iter()
            .filter(|f| f.ty == "Label" || f.ty == "Optional<Label>")
            .collect();

        if label_fields.is_empty() {
            let pat = if fields.is_empty() {
                format!("Instruction::{}", op.name)
            } else {
                format!("Instruction::{} {{ .. }}", op.name)
            };
            writeln!(w, "            {pat} => {{}}")?;
            continue;
        }

        let bindings: Vec<String> = fields
            .iter()
            .map(|f| {
                let rname = rust_field_name(&f.name);
                if f.ty == "Label" || f.ty == "Optional<Label>" {
                    rname
                } else {
                    format!("{rname}: _")
                }
            })
            .collect();
        writeln!(
            w,
            "            Instruction::{} {{ {} }} => {{",
            op.name,
            bindings.join(", ")
        )?;

        for f in &label_fields {
            let rname = rust_field_name(&f.name);
            if f.is_array {
                if f.ty == "Optional<Label>" {
                    writeln!(w, "                for item in {rname}.iter_mut() {{")?;
                    writeln!(w, "                    if let Some(lbl) = item {{ visitor(lbl); }}")?;
                    writeln!(w, "                }}")?;
                } else {
                    writeln!(w, "                for item in {rname}.iter_mut() {{ visitor(item); }}")?;
                }
            } else if f.ty == "Optional<Label>" {
                writeln!(w, "                if let Some(lbl) = {rname} {{ visitor(lbl); }}")?;
            } else {
                writeln!(w, "                visitor({rname});")?;
            }
        }

        writeln!(w, "            }}")?;
    }

    writeln!(w, "        }}")?;
    writeln!(w, "    }}")?;
    Ok(())
}

pub fn generate(flap_path: &Path, out_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
        .write(true)
        .create(true)
        .truncate(true) // empties contents of the file
        .open(out_dir.join("instruction_generated.rs"))?;
    let instruction_set = InstructionSet::load(flap_path)?;
    generate_rust_code(
        file,
        &instruction_set.ops,
        &instruction_set.specializations,
        &instruction_set.specialized_ops,
    )
}

/// The crate's tests never dereference cells, so they hash the compressed address, as cells that never moved do.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// None, unlike the real one.
pub unsafe fn cell_identity_hash(cell: *const core::ffi::c_void) -> u32 {
    (cell.addr() >> 3) as u32
}

/// The build script never decodes compressed pointers. The crate's tests decode them against this base, which is
/// aligned like LibGC aligns the real one, and where nothing is mapped.
pub fn heap_region_base() -> usize {
    0x7a00_0000_0000
}

//! Writes LibJS/Embedding/Layout.h: the offsets, sizes and constants of the runtime's structures that an embedder
//! reads or writes directly, computed from the crate's layout module the same way as the interpreter's layout. Every
//! offset and size is also written out as a static assertion that the crate compiles. The header's C++ section checks
//! the size, alignment, field count and the offset and type of every field of the layout module's mirror of
//! LibJS/HostObjectABI.h, and the value of every constant the mirror defines, against that header. A constant that
//! only the header defines goes unnoticed.

use core::mem::offset_of;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fmt::{Display, Write};

use crate::c_type_spelling::{CTypeSpelling, c_type_spelling_of_field};
use crate::class_id::{ALL_CLASS_IDS, CLASS_COUNT};
use crate::layout::cell::*;
use crate::layout::class::*;
use crate::layout::execution_context::*;
use crate::layout::function_object::*;
use crate::layout::host_class::*;
use crate::layout::host_object::*;
use crate::layout::object::*;
use crate::layout::primitive_string::*;
use crate::layout::realm::*;
use crate::layout::shape::*;
use crate::layout::vm::*;

/// The imports the static assertions need to name the same types as the header.
const STATIC_ASSERTIONS_PREAMBLE: &str = "\
use crate::layout::cell::*;
use crate::layout::class::*;
use crate::layout::execution_context::*;
use crate::layout::function_object::*;
use crate::layout::host_object::*;
use crate::layout::object::*;
use crate::layout::primitive_string::*;
use crate::layout::realm::*;
use crate::layout::shape::*;
use crate::layout::vm::*;

const fn size_of_field<Struct, Field>(_: fn(&Struct) -> *const Field) -> usize {
    size_of::<Field>()
}
";

const PREAMBLE: &str = "\
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

// Generated by the build script of libjs_embedding_headers from the runtime's layout module -- DO NOT EDIT
//
// The offsets, sizes and constants of the runtime's structures that an embedder reads or writes directly.

#ifndef LIBJS_EMBEDDING_LAYOUT_H
#define LIBJS_EMBEDDING_LAYOUT_H

#include <LibJS/HostObjectABI.h>
";

/// The start of the header's C++ section, which checks the layout module's mirror of LibJS/HostObjectABI.h against
/// that header.
const HOST_OBJECT_ABI_CHECKS_PREAMBLE: &str = "\
#ifdef __cplusplus
#    include <type_traits>
#    include <utility>

// The runtime mirrors LibJS/HostObjectABI.h in src/layout/host_class.rs and src/layout/host_object.rs. These check the
// size, alignment, field count and the offset and type of every field of that mirror, and the value of every constant
// it defines, against the header.
namespace JSEmbeddingLayoutChecks {

struct InitializerOfAnyField {
    template<typename Field>
    operator Field() const;
};

template<size_t>
using InitializerOfAnyFieldAt = InitializerOfAnyField;

template<typename Aggregate, size_t... field_indices>
consteval bool initializes_from_initializers(std::index_sequence<field_indices...>)
{
    return requires { Aggregate { InitializerOfAnyFieldAt<field_indices> {}... }; };
}

// Aggregate initialization takes one initializer per field and no more, which also counts fields that fit in padding.
template<typename Aggregate, size_t field_count>
constexpr bool has_exactly_fields = initializes_from_initializers<Aggregate>(std::make_index_sequence<field_count> {})
    && !initializes_from_initializers<Aggregate>(std::make_index_sequence<field_count + 1> {});

}

";

pub struct LayoutHeader {
    pub text: String,
    pub static_assertions: String,
}

struct HeaderWriter {
    definitions: String,
    defined_names: HashSet<String>,
    host_object_abi_checks: String,
    static_assertions: String,
}

impl HeaderWriter {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            definitions: String::new(),
            defined_names: HashSet::new(),
            host_object_abi_checks: String::new(),
            static_assertions: STATIC_ASSERTIONS_PREAMBLE.to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn section(&mut self, title: &str) {
        let _ = write!(self.definitions, "\n// {title}\n");
    }

    fn define(&mut self, name: &str, value: impl Display) {
        assert!(
            self.defined_names.insert(name.to_string()),
            "JS_LAYOUT_{name} is defined twice"
        );
        let _ = writeln!(self.definitions, "#define JS_LAYOUT_{name} {value}");
    }

    fn define_hex(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) {
        self.define(name, format!("0x{value:X}"));
    }

    fn assert_offset(&mut self, type_path: &str, field_path: &str, offset: usize) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.static_assertions,
            "const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({type_path}, {field_path}) == {offset});"
        );
    }

    fn assert_size(&mut self, type_path: &str, size: usize) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.static_assertions,
            "const _: () = assert!(size_of::<{type_path}>() == {size});"
        );
    }

    fn assert_field_size(&mut self, type_path: &str, field_path: &str, size: usize) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.static_assertions,
            "const _: () = assert!(size_of_field(|value: &{type_path}| &raw const value.{field_path}) == {size});"
        );
    }

    fn check_host_object_abi(&mut self, condition: &str) {
        let _ = writeln!(self.host_object_abi_checks, "static_assert({condition});");
    }

    fn finish(self) -> LayoutHeader {
        let mut text = String::from(PREAMBLE);
        text.push_str(&self.definitions);
        text.push('\n');
        text.push_str(HOST_OBJECT_ABI_CHECKS_PREAMBLE);
        text.push_str(&self.host_object_abi_checks);
        text.push_str("#endif\n\n#endif // LIBJS_EMBEDDING_LAYOUT_H\n");
        LayoutHeader {
            text,
            static_assertions: self.static_assertions,
        }
    }
}

/// Takes a raw pointer to the field, since a field of a packed struct such as CellHeader cannot have a reference.
fn size_of_field<Struct, Field>(_: fn(&Struct) -> *const Field) -> usize {
    size_of::<Field>()
}

/// Defines the offset of a field and its size, which tells an embedder the width to read it at.
macro_rules! offset {
    ($writer:expr, $name:expr, $type:ident, $($field:tt)+) => {{
        let name = $name;
        let offset = offset_of!($type, $($field)+);
        $writer.define(&format!("{name}_OFFSET"), offset);
        $writer.assert_offset(stringify!($type), stringify!($($field)+), offset);
        let size = size_of_field(|value: &$type| &raw const value.$($field)+);
        $writer.define(&format!("{name}_SIZE"), size);
        $writer.assert_field_size(stringify!($type), stringify!($($field)+), size);
    }};
}

macro_rules! size {
    ($writer:expr, $name:expr, $type:ident) => {{
        let size = size_of::<$type>();
        $writer.define(&format!("{}_SIZE", $name), size);
        $writer.assert_size(stringify!($type), size);
    }};
}

/// Defines the offset of each listed field. The list has to name every field of the struct, so that one added to it
/// fails to compile here until the header has it too.
macro_rules! every_field_offset {
    ($writer:expr, $prefix:literal, $type:ident { $($field:ident),* $(,)? }) => {{
        const _: fn(&$type) = |value| {
            let $type { $($field: _),* } = value;
        };
        $(offset!($writer, format!("{}_{}", $prefix, stringify!($field).to_uppercase()), $type, $field);)*
    }};
}

/// Checks the size, alignment, field count and the offset and type of every field of a struct that mirrors one of
/// LibJS/HostObjectABI.h.
macro_rules! check_host_object_abi_struct {
    ($writer:expr, $type:ident { $($field:ident),* $(,)? }) => {{
        const _: fn(&$type) = |value| {
            let $type { $($field: _),* } = value;
        };
        let type_name = stringify!($type);
        $writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!("sizeof({type_name}) == {}", size_of::<$type>()));
        $writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!("alignof({type_name}) == {}", align_of::<$type>()));
        let field_count = [$(stringify!($field)),*].len();
        $writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!(
            "JSEmbeddingLayoutChecks::has_exactly_fields<{type_name}, {field_count}>"
        ));
        $(
            let field_name = stringify!($field).trim_start_matches("r#");
            $writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!(
                "offsetof({type_name}, {field_name}) == {}",
                offset_of!($type, $field)
            ));
            $writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!(
                "std::is_same_v<decltype({type_name}::{field_name}), {}>",
                c_type_spelling_of_field(|value: &$type| &value.$field)
            ));
        )*
    }};
}

macro_rules! check_host_object_abi_constants {
    ($writer:expr, $($name:ident),* $(,)?) => {
        $($writer.check_host_object_abi(&format!("{} == {}", stringify!($name), $name));)*
    };
}

/// Spells a class name such as RawJSONObject the way C spells constants, RAW_JSON_OBJECT.
fn screaming_snake_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let characters: Vec<char> = name.chars().collect();
    let mut result = String::new();
    for (index, &character) in characters.iter().enumerate() {
        if index > 0 && character.is_ascii_uppercase() {
            let previous = characters[index - 1];
            let next_is_lowercase = characters.get(index + 1).is_some_and(char::is_ascii_lowercase);
            if previous.is_ascii_lowercase()
                || previous.is_ascii_digit()
                || (previous.is_ascii_uppercase() && next_is_lowercase)
            {
                result.push('_');
            }
        }
        result.push(character.to_ascii_uppercase());
    }
    result
}

fn cell_kind_name(kind: CellKind) -> &'static str {
    match kind {
        CellKind::Other => "OTHER",
        CellKind::Object => "OBJECT",
        CellKind::PrimitiveString => "PRIMITIVE_STRING",
        CellKind::Symbol => "SYMBOL",
        CellKind::BigInt => "BIG_INT",
        CellKind::Accessor => "ACCESSOR",
    }
}

#[rustfmt::skip]
pub fn generate() -> LayoutHeader {
    let mut w = HeaderWriter::new();

    w.section("Cell header, at the start of every cell");
    offset!(w, "CELL_STATE", CellHeader, state);
    offset!(w, "CELL_KIND", CellHeader, kind);
    for kind in [CellKind::Other, CellKind::Object, CellKind::PrimitiveString, CellKind::Symbol, CellKind::BigInt, CellKind::Accessor] {

    let mut class_id_names = HashSet::new();
    for (value, class_id) in ALL_CLASS_IDS.iter().enumerate() {

        let name = screaming_snake_case(&format!("{class_id:?}"));

        prevent_extensions,
        get_own_property,
        define_own_property,
        has_property,

        own_property_keys,

        error_data,

    check_host_object_abi_struct!(w, JSHostFunctionHooks { call, construct, finalize });
    check_host_object_abi_struct!(w, JSHostArrayHooks { define_own_property, set, delete_property });
    check_host_object_abi_struct!(w, JSResolvedBinding { module, binding_name, r#type });
    check_host_object_abi_struct!(w, JSHostModuleHooks { get_exported_names, resolve_export, initialize_environment, execute_module });
    check_host_object_abi_struct!(w, JSHostClass { kind, flags, name, name_length, parent, hooks, user_data });
    check_host_object_abi_constants!(
        w,
        JS_COMPLETION_NORMAL,
        JS_COMPLETION_THROW,
        JS_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_PHASE_OWN_PROPERTY,
        JS_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_PHASE_PROTOTYPE_CHAIN,
        JS_PD_HAS_VALUE,
        JS_PD_HAS_GET,
        JS_PD_HAS_SET,
        JS_PD_HAS_WRITABLE,
        JS_PD_WRITABLE,
        JS_PD_HAS_ENUMERABLE,
        JS_PD_ENUMERABLE,
        JS_PD_HAS_CONFIGURABLE,
        JS_PD_CONFIGURABLE,
        JS_PD_HAS_PROPERTY_OFFSET,
        JS_PD_PRESENT,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_OBJECT,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_ARRAY,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_MODULE,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_IS_PLATFORM_OBJECT,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_REQUIRES_SLOW_ADD_OWN_PROPERTY,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_MAY_INTERFERE_WITH_INDEXED_PROPERTY_ACCESS,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_IS_HTMLDDA,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_IS_GLOBAL_OBJECT,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_IMMUTABLE_PROTOTYPE,
        JS_HOST_CLASS_NOT_CACHEABLE_FOR_PROPERTY_ABSENCE,

        JS_RESOLVED_BINDING_BINDING_NAME,

        JS_RESOLVED_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS,

//! Writes the layout file that flapc compiles the interpreter against. Every offset and size it prints is also written
//! out as a static assertion that the crate compiles, since the offsets are computed here with stand-ins for the types
//! outside the layout module.

use std::fmt::Write;

use crate::layout::accessor::*;
use crate::layout::buffer::*;
use crate::layout::environment::*;
use crate::layout::executable::*;
use crate::layout::execution_context::*;
use crate::layout::feedback::*;
use crate::layout::function_object::*;
use crate::layout::object::*;
use crate::layout::primitive_string::*;
use crate::layout::property_lookup_cache::*;
use crate::layout::realm::*;
use crate::layout::shape::*;
use crate::layout::value::*;
use crate::layout::vm::*;
use crate::layout_forward::Utf16StringDataHeader;
use libjs_abi::{PutKind, register, value as nan_box};

/// The imports the static assertions need to name the same types as the table.
const STATIC_ASSERTIONS_PREAMBLE: &str = "\
use crate::layout::accessor::*;
use crate::layout::buffer::*;
use crate::layout::environment::*;
use crate::layout::executable::*;
use crate::layout::execution_context::*;
use crate::layout::feedback::*;
use crate::layout::function_object::*;
use crate::layout::object::*;
use crate::layout::primitive_string::*;
use crate::layout::property_lookup_cache::*;
use crate::layout::realm::*;
use crate::layout::shape::*;
use crate::layout::value::*;
use crate::layout::vm::*;
use crate::layout_forward::Utf16StringDataHeader;
";

/// Build configuration that the layout depends on but Rust's own cfg cannot see.
pub struct LayoutConfiguration {
    pub heap_region_offset_mask: u64,
    pub primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask: u64,
    pub vm_stack_space_limit: u64,
}

pub struct LayoutWriter {
    pub text: String,
    pub static_assertions: String,
}

impl LayoutWriter {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            text: String::new(),
            static_assertions: STATIC_ASSERTIONS_PREAMBLE.to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn line(&mut self, line: &str) {
        self.text.push_str(line);
        self.text.push('\n');
    }

    fn section(&mut self, name: &str) {
        let _ = write!(self.text, "\n# {name}\n");
    }

    fn constant(&mut self, name: &str, value: impl std::fmt::Display) {
        let _ = writeln!(self.text, "const {name} = {value}");
    }

    fn hex_constant(&mut self, name: &str, value: u64) {
        let _ = writeln!(self.text, "const {name} = 0x{value:X}");
    }

    fn field(&mut self, field: &str, flap_type: &str, offset: &str, storage: &str, representation: &str) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.text,
            "field {field} {flap_type} {offset} {storage} {representation}"
        );
    }

    fn paired_field(
        &mut self,
        field: &str,
        flap_type: &str,
        offset: &str,
        storage: &str,
        representation: &str,
        pair: &str,
    ) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.text,
            "field {field} {flap_type} {offset} {storage} {representation} {pair}"
        );
    }

    fn assert_offset(&mut self, type_path: &str, field_path: &str, offset: usize) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.static_assertions,
            "const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({type_path}, {field_path}) == {offset});"
        );
    }

    fn assert_size(&mut self, type_path: &str, size: usize) {
        let _ = writeln!(
            self.static_assertions,
            "const _: () = assert!(size_of::<{type_path}>() == {size});"
        );
    }
}

fn size_of_field<T, F>(_: fn(&T) -> &F) -> usize {
    size_of::<F>()
}

macro_rules! offset {
    ($writer:expr, $name:literal, $type:path, $($field:tt)+) => {{
        let offset = core::mem::offset_of!($type, $($field)+);
        $writer.constant($name, offset);
        $writer.assert_offset(stringify!($type), stringify!($($field)+), offset);
        offset
    }};
}

macro_rules! size {
    ($writer:expr, $name:literal, $type:path) => {{
        let size = size_of::<$type>();
        $writer.constant($name, size);
        $writer.assert_size(stringify!($type), size);
        size
    }};
}

/// Emits a field the interpreter accesses, checking that its Rust type has the size the interpreter accesses it with.
macro_rules! field {
    ($writer:expr, $name:literal, $field:literal, $flap_type:literal, $type:path, $member:ident, $size:expr, $storage:literal, $representation:literal) => {{
        assert_eq!(
            size_of_field(|object: &$type| &object.$member),
            $size,
            "size of {}",
            $field
        );
        offset!($writer, $name, $type, $member);
        $writer.field($field, $flap_type, $name, $storage, $representation);
    }};
    ($writer:expr, $name:literal, $field:literal, $flap_type:literal, $type:path, $member:ident, $size:expr, $storage:literal, $representation:literal, $pair:literal) => {{
        assert_eq!(
            size_of_field(|object: &$type| &object.$member),
            $size,
            "size of {}",
            $field
        );
        offset!($writer, $name, $type, $member);
        $writer.paired_field($field, $flap_type, $name, $storage, $representation, $pair);
    }};
}

    field!(w, "OBJECT_INDEXED_ELEMENTS", "Object.indexed_elements", "IndexedElements", Object, indexed_elements, 8, "nullable", "scalar");
    field!(w, "OBJECT_INDEXED_STORAGE_KIND", "Object.indexed_storage_kind", "u8", Object, indexed_storage_kind, 1, "nullable", "scalar");
    field!(w, "OBJECT_INDEXED_ARRAY_LIKE_SIZE", "Object.indexed_array_like_size", "u32", Object, indexed_array_like_size, 4, "nullable", "scalar");

    w.line("field GlobalVariableCache.environment_binding_index u32 GLOBAL_VARIABLE_CACHE_ENVIRONMENT_BINDING_INDEX nullable scalar");
    w.line("field GlobalVariableCache.has_environment_binding_index u8 GLOBAL_VARIABLE_CACHE_HAS_ENVIRONMENT_BINDING nullable scalar");

    w.section("RawNativeFunction layout");
    field!(w, "RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTION_NATIVE_FUNCTION_INDEX", "RawNativeFunction.native_function_index", "u32", NativeFunction, raw_native_function_index, 4, "nullable", "scalar");
    assert_eq!(size_of_field(|entry: &NativeFunctionTableEntry| &entry.function), 8);

/*

//! Writes a #[repr(C)] view of every bytecode instruction, laid out as flapc lays it out, and the Values record of
//! every instruction whose slow path receives one. Each offset flapc computed is asserted on the generated type.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::fmt::Write;

use flapc::metadata::{InstructionDefinition, SlowPathLayout, field_type_info};
use flapc::rust_bytecode::scaled;

const RUST_KEYWORDS: &[&str] = &[
    "abstract", "as", "async", "await", "become", "box", "break", "const", "continue", "do", "dyn", "else", "enum",
    "extern", "false", "final", "fn", "for", "gen", "if", "impl", "in", "let", "loop", "macro", "match", "mod", "move",
    "mut", "override", "priv", "pub", "ref", "return", "static", "struct", "trait", "true", "try", "type", "typeof",
    "unsafe", "unsized", "use", "virtual", "where", "while", "yield",
];

pub fn rust_identifier(name: &str) -> String {
    if RUST_KEYWORDS.contains(&name) {
        format!("r#{name}")
    } else {
        name.to_string()
    }
}

/// The Rust name of a bytecode field, without the m_ prefix of its name in the instruction definitions.
pub fn field_name(name: &str) -> String {
    rust_identifier(name.strip_prefix("m_").unwrap_or(name))
}

fn rust_type(ty: &str) -> String {
    match ty {
        "Operand" => "Operand".to_string(),
        "Optional<Operand>" => "OptionalOperand".to_string(),
        "Label" => "Label".to_string(),
        "Optional<Label>" => "OptionalLabel".to_string(),
        "IdentifierTableIndex" | "PropertyKeyTableIndex" | "StringTableIndex" => ty.to_string(),
        "Optional<IdentifierTableIndex>" => "OptionalIndex<IdentifierTableIndex>".to_string(),
        "Optional<StringTableIndex>" => "OptionalIndex<StringTableIndex>".to_string(),
        "EnvironmentCoordinate" => "BytecodeEnvironmentCoordinate".to_string(),
        "Value" => "Value".to_string(),
        "Builtin" => "u8".to_string(),
        _ => {
            let info = field_type_info(ty);
            match info.kind {
                "bool" | "u8" | "u16" | "i32" | "u32" | "u64" => info.kind.to_string(),
                "byte_count" => "u8".to_string(),
                "cache_index" => "u16".to_string(),
                other => panic!("no Rust view for bytecode field type {ty} ({other})"),
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn generate(ops: &[InstructionDefinition], ops_with_values: &BTreeSet<String>) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str("// Generated by the libjs_rust build script -- DO NOT EDIT\n\n");

    for op in ops {
        if op.name == "Instruction" {
            continue;
        }
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "#[repr(C, packed)]\npub struct {} {{\n    pub header: InstructionHeader,",
            op.name
        );
        let mut assertions = String::new();
        for field in &op.fields {
            if field.name == "m_type" || field.name == "m_strict" {
                continue;
            }
            let name = field_name(&field.name);
            let ty = rust_type(&field.ty);
            if field.is_array {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "    pub {name}: [{ty}; 0],");
            } else {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "    pub {name}: {ty},");
            }
            let offset = op.layout.field_offsets[&field.name];
            let _ = writeln!(
                assertions,
                "const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({}, {name}) == {offset});",
                op.name
            );
        }
        // NB: Only bytecode holds instructions, so nothing outside this module can make one.
        out.push_str("    _view_of_bytecode: (),\n}\n");
        out.push_str(&assertions);
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "// SAFETY: The struct lays out the instruction of this opcode, and is only ever a view of bytecode.\nunsafe impl super::BytecodeOp for {name} {{\n    const OPCODE: u8 = crate::bytecode::instruction::OpCode::{name} as u8;\n\n    fn length(&self) -> u32 {{\n        {name}::length(self)\n    }}\n}}",
            name = op.name
        );
        if let Some(array) = &op.array {
            let array_field = &op.fields[array.field_index];
            let count_field = field_name(&op.fields[array.count_field_index].name);
            let name = field_name(&array_field.name);
            let ty = rust_type(&array_field.ty);
            let accessor = if ty == "Value" {
                format!(
                    "impl {op_name} {{\n    /// The elements the instruction holds after its fixed fields, within the length it records.\n    pub fn {name}(&self) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = Value> + '_ {{\n        let count = self.{count_field} as usize;\n        assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({op_name}, {name}) + count * size_of::<Value>() <= self.length() as usize);\n        let elements = core::ptr::addr_of!(self.{name}).cast::<Value>();\n        // SAFETY: The instruction is a view of bytecode that holds the length it records, which the elements are\n        //         within. They can be unaligned, so they are read as such.\n        (0..count).map(move |index| unsafe {{ elements.add(index).read_unaligned() }})\n    }}\n}}",
                    op_name = op.name
                )
            } else {
                format!(
                    "impl {op_name} {{\n    /// The elements the instruction holds after its fixed fields, within the length it records.\n    pub fn {name}(&self) -> &[{ty}] {{\n        let count = self.{count_field} as usize;\n        assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({op_name}, {name}) + count * size_of::<{ty}>() <= self.length() as usize);\n        // SAFETY: The instruction is a view of bytecode that holds the length it records, which the elements are\n        //         within. {ty} has an alignment of 1.\n        unsafe {{ ak::slice_from_raw_parts(core::ptr::addr_of!(self.{name}).cast::<{ty}>(), count) }}\n    }}\n}}",
                    op_name = op.name
                )
            };
            out.push_str(&accessor);
            out.push('\n');
        }
        match (op.layout.size, &op.array) {
            (Some(size), _) => {
                let _ = writeln!(
                    out,
                    "impl {} {{\n    /// The size of every {} instruction in the bytecode.\n    pub const LENGTH: u32 = {size};\n\n    pub fn length(&self) -> u32 {{\n        Self::LENGTH\n    }}\n}}",
                    op.name, op.name
                );
            }
            (None, Some(array)) => {
                let count_field = &op.fields[array.count_field_index];
                let count_name = field_name(&count_field.name);
                let count = if rust_type(&count_field.ty) == "u32" {
                    format!("self.{count_name}")
                } else {
                    format!("u32::from(self.{count_name})")
                };
                let _ = writeln!(
                    out,
                    "impl {} {{\n    /// The instruction's size in the bytecode.\n    pub fn length(&self) -> u32 {{\n        let count = {count};\n        {} + {}\n    }}\n}}",
                    op.name,
                    op.layout.minimum_size,
                    scaled("count", array.element_size)
                );
            }
            (None, None) => panic!("{} has neither a fixed size nor a count field", op.name),
        }

        if ops_with_values.contains(&op.name) {
            let layout = SlowPathLayout::new(op);
            let _ = writeln!(out, "#[repr(C)]\npub struct {}Values {{", op.name);
            let mut assertions = String::new();
            for field in &layout.fields {
                let name = field_name(&field.name);
                let _ = writeln!(out, "    pub {name}: Value,");
                let _ = writeln!(
                    assertions,
                    "const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!({}Values, {name}) == {});",
                    op.name, field.value_offset
                );
            }
            if let Some(array) = &layout.array {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "    pub {}: [Value; 0],", field_name(&array.name));
            }
            out.push_str("}\n");
            out.push_str(&assertions);
        }
        out.push('\n');
    }
    out
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/generate/runtime_functions.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Writes the RuntimeFunctions trait, with one method per function the generated interpreter calls, and an
//! extern "C" entry point for each with exactly the signature the interpreter's call sites assume. The entry points
//! translate every calling convention into one Rust signature per kind of call. The methods have no default bodies, so
//! the runtime does not build unless it defines every function that the interpreter, in either of its variants, calls.
//!
//! JIT code calls the same functions, with the System V calling convention on every x86-64 target. Only on Windows is
//! that not the one the interpreter uses, so there every entry point has a forwarder for JIT code to call.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt::Write;

use flapc::metadata::{InstructionDefinition, ParameterMode, SlowPathAbi, SlowPathLayout};
use flapc::runtime_interface::{RuntimeFunction, RuntimeFunctionKind};

use crate::ops::{field_name, rust_identifier};

fn method_name(symbol: &str) -> String {
    rust_identifier(
        symbol
            .strip_prefix("asm_slow_path_")
            .or_else(|| symbol.strip_prefix("asm_"))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("unexpected runtime function symbol {symbol}")),
    )
}

struct Record<'a> {
    op: &'a str,
    layout: &'a SlowPathLayout,
    /// The array name and the name of the instruction field that counts its elements.
    array: Option<(String, String)>,
}

impl<'a> Record<'a> {
    fn new(op: &'a str, layout: &'a SlowPathLayout, ops: &HashMap<&str, &InstructionDefinition>) -> Self {
        let array = layout.array.as_ref().map(|array| {
            let definition = ops[op];
            let array_layout = definition.array.as_ref().expect("an operand array has a layout");
            (
                field_name(&array.name),
                field_name(&definition.fields[array_layout.count_field_index].name),
            )
        });
        Self { op, layout, array }
    }

    fn method_parameters(&self) -> String {
        let mut parameters = format!("_instruction: &op::{0}, _values: &mut op::{0}Values", self.op);
        if let Some((array, _)) = &self.array {
            let _ = write!(parameters, ", _{array}: &mut [Value]");
        }
        parameters
    }

    /// Statements that turn the raw record pointer `values` into the method's arguments.
    fn bind_record(&self, out: &mut String) {
        if let Some((array, count)) = &self.array {
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "    // SAFETY: The interpreter stores the instruction's {count} operands after the record."
            );
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "    let {array} = unsafe {{ ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut((&raw mut (*values).{array}).cast::<Value>(), instruction.{count} as usize) }};"
            );
        }
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes a record for the instruction it is executing."
        );
        let _ = writeln!(out, "    let values = unsafe {{ &mut *values }};");
    }

    fn call_arguments(&self) -> String {
        match &self.array {
            Some((array, _)) => format!("instruction, values, {array}"),
            None => "instruction, values".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// Where the interpreter's calling convention is not the one JIT code calls with.
const WINDOWS_X86_64: &str = "all(target_arch = \"x86_64\", windows)";

/// The Rust signature of the entry point of a runtime function.
struct EntryPointSignature {
    is_unsafe: bool,
    /// The name and the type of each parameter.
    parameters: Vec<(String, String)>,
    result: Option<&'static str>,
}

/// Parameters of these names and types.
fn parameters(parameters: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    parameters
        .iter()
        .map(|(name, ty)| (name.to_string(), ty.to_string()))
        .collect()
}

impl EntryPointSignature {
    fn of(kind: &RuntimeFunctionKind) -> Self {
        let instruction_parameters = |op: &str| {
            parameters(&[
                ("vm", "*const Vm"),
                ("pc", "u32"),
                ("instruction", format!("*const op::{op}").as_str()),
            ])
        };
        let (is_unsafe, parameters, result) = match kind {
            RuntimeFunctionKind::SlowPath { op, abi, layout } => {
                let inputs = layout
                    .fields
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|field| field.mode != ParameterMode::Out)
                    .map(|field| (field_name(&field.name), "Value".to_string()));
                let mut parameters = instruction_parameters(op);
                match abi {
                    SlowPathAbi::Scalar => {
                        parameters.extend(inputs);
                        (true, parameters, Some("AsmSlowPathResult"))
                    }
                    SlowPathAbi::Mixed => {
                        parameters.push(("outputs".to_string(), format!("*mut op::{op}Values")));
                        parameters.extend(inputs);
                        (true, parameters, Some("i64"))
                    }
                    SlowPathAbi::Record => {
                        parameters.push(("values".to_string(), format!("*mut op::{op}Values")));
                        (true, parameters, Some("i64"))
                    }
                }
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::Try { op, .. } => {
                let mut parameters = instruction_parameters(op);
                parameters.push(("values".to_string(), format!("*mut op::{op}Values")));
                (true, parameters, Some("i64"))
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::BinarySlowPath => (
                true,
                parameters(&[
                    ("vm", "*const Vm"),
                    ("pc", "u32"),
                    ("dst", "*mut Value"),
                    ("lhs", "Value"),
                    ("rhs", "Value"),
                    ("length", "u32"),
                ]),
                Some("i64"),
            ),
            RuntimeFunctionKind::JumpSlowPath => (
                true,
                parameters(&[
                    ("vm", "*const Vm"),
                    ("pc", "u32"),
                    ("lhs", "Value"),
                    ("rhs", "Value"),
                    ("true_target", "u32"),
                    ("false_target", "u32"),
                ]),
                Some("i64"),
            ),
            RuntimeFunctionKind::Helper => (false, parameters(&[("argument", "u64")]), Some("u64")),
            RuntimeFunctionKind::HelperWithTwoArguments => {
                (false, parameters(&[("first", "u64"), ("second", "u64")]), Some("u64"))
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::FallbackHandler => (
                true,
                parameters(&[("vm", "*const Vm"), ("pc", "u32"), ("instruction", "*const u8")]),
                Some("i64"),
            ),
            RuntimeFunctionKind::BreakpointCheck => (true, parameters(&[("vm", "*const Vm"), ("pc", "u32")]), None),
            RuntimeFunctionKind::StackOverflowSlowPath => {
                (true, parameters(&[("vm", "*const Vm"), ("pc", "u32")]), Some("i64"))
            }
        };
        Self {
            is_unsafe,
            parameters,
            result,
        }
    }

    /// The function up to and including its opening brace.
    fn write_header(&self, out: &mut String, abi: &str, name: &str) {
        let safety = if self.is_unsafe { "unsafe " } else { "" };
        let result = self.result.map_or(String::new(), |result| format!(" -> {result}"));
        let parameters = self
            .parameters
            .iter()
            .map(|(name, ty)| format!("{name}: {ty}"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(", ");
        let _ = writeln!(out, "pub {safety}extern \"{abi}\" fn {name}({parameters}){result} {{");
    }

    fn write_system_v_forwarder(&self, out: &mut String, symbol: &str) {
        let arguments = self
            .parameters
            .iter()
            .map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(", ");
        let _ = writeln!(out, "#[cfg({WINDOWS_X86_64})]");
        self.write_header(out, "sysv64", &format!("{symbol}_sysv64"));
        if self.is_unsafe {
            out.push_str("    // SAFETY: JIT code calls this like the interpreter calls the entry point.\n");
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    unsafe {{ {symbol}({arguments}) }}\n}}");
        } else {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    {symbol}({arguments})\n}}");
        }
    }
}

pub fn generate(functions: &[RuntimeFunction], ops: &[InstructionDefinition]) -> String {
    let ops: HashMap<&str, &InstructionDefinition> = ops.iter().map(|op| (op.name.as_str(), op)).collect();
    let mut methods = String::new();
    let mut entry_points = String::new();

    for function in functions {
        let symbol = &function.symbol;
        let name = method_name(symbol);
        let _ = writeln!(methods, "    /// Called as `{symbol}`.");
        let signature = EntryPointSignature::of(&function.kind);
        let _ = writeln!(entry_points, "#[unsafe(no_mangle)]");
        signature.write_header(&mut entry_points, "C", symbol);
        match &function.kind {
            RuntimeFunctionKind::SlowPath { op, abi, layout } => {
                let record = Record::new(op, layout, &ops);
                let _ = writeln!(
                    methods,
                    "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32, {}) -> SlowPathControl;",
                    record.method_parameters()
                );
                generate_slow_path_entry_point(&mut entry_points, &name, *abi, &record);
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::Try { op, layout } => {
                let record = Record::new(op, layout, &ops);
                let _ = writeln!(
                    methods,
                    "    /// Returns whether it handled the instruction; if not, the interpreter takes the instruction's slow path.\n    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, _pc: u32, {}) -> bool;",
                    record.method_parameters()
                );
                entry_points
                    .push_str("    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM and the instruction it is executing.\n");
                entry_points.push_str("    let (vm, instruction) = unsafe { (&*vm, &*instruction) };\n");
                record.bind_record(&mut entry_points);
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    i64::from(!<Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc, {}))\n}}",
                    record.call_arguments()
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::BinarySlowPath => {
                let _ = writeln!(
                    methods,
                    "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32, _dst: &Cell<Value>, _lhs: Value, _rhs: Value, _length: u32) -> SlowPathControl;"
                );
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM and a live value slot.\n    let (vm, dst) = unsafe {{ (&*vm, &*dst.cast::<Cell<Value>>()) }};\n    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc, dst, lhs, rhs, length).0\n}}"
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::JumpSlowPath => {
                let _ = writeln!(
                    methods,
                    "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32, _lhs: Value, _rhs: Value, _true_target: u32, _false_target: u32) -> SlowPathControl;"
                );
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM.\n    let vm = unsafe {{ &*vm }};\n    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc, lhs, rhs, true_target, false_target).0\n}}"
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::Helper => {
                let _ = writeln!(methods, "    fn {name}(_argument: u64) -> u64;");
                let _ = writeln!(entry_points, "    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(argument)\n}}");
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::HelperWithTwoArguments => {
                let _ = writeln!(methods, "    fn {name}(_first: u64, _second: u64) -> u64;");
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(first, second)\n}}"
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::FallbackHandler => {
                let _ = writeln!(
                    methods,
                    "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32, _instruction: *const u8) -> SlowPathControl;"
                );
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM.\n    let vm = unsafe {{ &*vm }};\n    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc, instruction).0\n}}"
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::BreakpointCheck => {
                let _ = writeln!(methods, "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32);");
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM.\n    let vm = unsafe {{ &*vm }};\n    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc);\n}}"
                );
            }
            RuntimeFunctionKind::StackOverflowSlowPath => {
                let _ = writeln!(methods, "    fn {name}(_vm: &Vm, pc: u32) -> SlowPathControl;");
                let _ = writeln!(
                    entry_points,
                    "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM.\n    let vm = unsafe {{ &*vm }};\n    <Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc).0\n}}"
                );
            }
        }
        signature.write_system_v_forwarder(&mut entry_points, symbol);
        entry_points.push('\n');
    }

    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str("// Generated by the libjs_rust build script -- DO NOT EDIT\n\n");
    out.push_str("pub trait RuntimeFunctions {\n");
    out.push_str(&methods);
    out.push_str("}\n\n");
    out.push_str(&entry_points);
    let _ = writeln!(
        out,
        "pub const RUNTIME_FUNCTION_SYMBOLS: [&str; {}] = [",
        functions.len()
    );
    for function in functions {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "    \"{}\",", function.symbol);
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");
    for (condition, suffix) in [
        (format!("not({WINDOWS_X86_64})"), ""),
        (WINDOWS_X86_64.to_string(), "_sysv64"),
    ] {
        out.push_str(
            "/// The address JIT code calls every runtime function at, by symbol, in the order of RUNTIME_FUNCTION_SYMBOLS.\n",
        );
        let _ = writeln!(out, "#[cfg({condition})]");
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "pub fn runtime_function_addresses() -> [(&'static str, usize); {}] {{\n    [",
            functions.len()
        );
        for function in functions {
            let _ = writeln!(
                out,
                "        (\"{0}\", {0}{suffix} as *const () as usize),",
                function.symbol
            );
        }
        out.push_str("    ]\n}\n");
    }
    out
}

fn generate_slow_path_entry_point(out: &mut String, name: &str, abi: SlowPathAbi, record: &Record) {
    let op = record.op;
    let fields = &record.layout.fields;
    let initialize_values = || {
        let initializers: Vec<String> = fields
            .iter()
            .map(|field| {
                let name = field_name(&field.name);
                if field.mode == ParameterMode::Out {
                    format!("{name}: Value::EMPTY")
                } else {
                    name
                }
            })
            .collect();
        format!(
            "    let mut values = op::{op}Values {{ {} }};\n",
            initializers.join(", ")
        )
    };
    let call = format!(
        "<Runtime as RuntimeFunctions>::{name}(vm, pc, {})",
        record.call_arguments()
    );
    let bind_vm = "    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes its VM and the instruction it is executing.\n    let (vm, instruction) = unsafe { (&*vm, &*instruction) };\n";

    match abi {
        SlowPathAbi::Scalar => {
            let primary_output = fields
                .iter()
                .find(|field| field.mode == ParameterMode::Out && !field.optional)
                .map(|field| field_name(&field.name));
            out.push_str(bind_vm);
            out.push_str(&initialize_values());
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    let values = &mut values;\n    let control = {call};");
            match primary_output {
                Some(output) => {
                    let _ = writeln!(
                        out,
                        "    AsmSlowPathResult {{ control: control.0, value: values.{output}.0 }}\n}}"
                    );
                }
                None => {
                    out.push_str("    AsmSlowPathResult { control: control.0, value: 0 }\n}\n");
                }
            }
        }
        SlowPathAbi::Mixed => {
            out.push_str(bind_vm);
            out.push_str(&initialize_values());
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    let values = &mut values;\n    let control = {call};");
            out.push_str("    // SAFETY: The interpreter passes a record to receive the outputs.\n    let outputs = unsafe { &mut *outputs };\n");
            for field in fields.iter().filter(|field| field.mode != ParameterMode::In) {
                let name = field_name(&field.name);
                let _ = writeln!(out, "    outputs.{name} = values.{name};");
            }
            out.push_str("    control.0\n}\n");
        }
        SlowPathAbi::Record => {
            out.push_str(bind_vm);
            record.bind_record(out);
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    {call}.0\n}}");
        }
    }
}

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

/// Writes `contents` to `path` unless the file already holds them, so that what depends on the file is not rebuilt
/// for a write that changed nothing.
pub fn write_if_changed(path: &Path, contents: &str) {
    if fs::read_to_string(path).is_ok_and(|existing| existing == contents) {
        return;
    }
    fs::write(path, contents).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("write {}: {error}", path.display()));
}
