impl SwitchCase<'_> {
    pub fn range(&self) -> SourceRange {
        self.tree.range(self.offset)
    }
}

impl<'a> ListItem<'a> for SwitchCase<'a> {
    type Context = ();

    fn read(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, case: u32, _: ()) -> Self {
        let test = tree.a(case);
        SwitchCase {
            tree,
            offset: tree.pos(case),
            scope: Scope::of_list(tree, tree.b(case)),
            test: (test != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, test)),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ImportStatementData<'a> {
    tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    node: u32,
}

impl ImportStatementData<'_> {
    pub fn module_request(&self) -> ModuleRequest {
        self.tree.module_request(self.tree.b(self.node))
    }

    pub fn entries(&self) -> Vec<ImportEntry> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        tree.list(tree.a(self.node))
            .iter()
            .map(|&specifier| {
                let imported = tree.a(specifier);
                ImportEntry {
                    import_name: match imported {
                        0 => Some(Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("default"))),
                        NONE => None,
                        _ => Some(tree.specifier_name(imported)),
                    },
                    local_name: tree.name_text(Name(tree.b(specifier))).into(),
                }
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ExportStatementData<'a> {
    tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    node: u32,
    pub statement: Option<Statement<'a>>,
    pub is_default_export: bool,
}

impl ExportStatementData<'_> {
    pub fn module_request(&self) -> Option<ModuleRequest> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(self.node), tree.b(self.node));
        match tree.tag(self.node) {
            tag::EXPORT_ALL => Some(tree.module_request(b)),
            tag::EXPORT_NAMED if a != 0 && b != 0 => Some(tree.module_request(b)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn entries(&self) -> Vec<ExportEntry> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(self.node), tree.b(self.node));
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        match tree.tag(self.node) {
            tag::EXPORT_ALL => {
                if a == 0 {
                    entries.push(ExportEntry {
                        kind: ExportEntryKind::ModuleRequestAllButDefault,
                        export_name: None,
                        local_or_import_name: None,
                    });
                } else {
                    entries.push(ExportEntry {
                        kind: ExportEntryKind::ModuleRequestAll,
                        export_name: Some(tree.specifier_name(a)),
                        local_or_import_name: None,
                    });
                }
            }
            tag::EXPORT_DEFAULT => {
                let inner_tag = tree.tag(a);
                let mut local_name = Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("*default*"));
                if inner_tag == tag::FUNCTION && b != 0 {
                    let name = tree.script.index.name[tree.b(a) as usize];
                    if name != NONE {
                        local_name = tree.name_text(Name(name)).into();
                    }
                } else if inner_tag == tag::CLASS_DECL {
                    local_name = tree.name_text(Name(tree.a(tree.a(a)))).into();
                }
                entries.push(ExportEntry {
                    kind: ExportEntryKind::NamedExport,
                    export_name: Some(Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("default"))),
                    local_or_import_name: Some(local_name),
                });
            }
            _ if a != 0 => {
                for &specifier in tree.list(a) {
                    entries.push(ExportEntry {
                        kind: ExportEntryKind::NamedExport,
                        export_name: Some(tree.specifier_name(tree.b(specifier))),
                        local_or_import_name: Some(tree.specifier_name(tree.a(specifier))),
                    });
                }
                if entries.is_empty() {
                    entries.push(ExportEntry {
                        kind: ExportEntryKind::EmptyNamedExport,
                        export_name: None,
                        local_or_import_name: None,
                    });
                }
            }
            _ => {
                let mut names = Vec::new();
                match tree.tag(b) {
                    tag::FUNCTION_DECL => names.push(tree.name_text(Name(tree.b(b))).into()),
                    tag::CLASS_DECL => names.push(tree.name_text(Name(tree.a(tree.a(b)))).into()),
                    _ => {
                        for &declarator in tree.list(tree.a(b)) {
                            tree.pattern_names(tree.a(declarator), &mut names);
                        }
                    }
                }
                for name in names {
                    entries.push(ExportEntry {
                        kind: ExportEntryKind::NamedExport,
                        export_name: Some(name.clone()),
                        local_or_import_name: Some(name),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        entries
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ProgramData<'a> {
    pub scope: Scope<'a>,
    pub program_type: ProgramType,
    pub is_strict_mode: bool,
    pub has_top_level_await: bool,
}

// =============================================================================
// Scopes
// =============================================================================

/// What statements a scope has, which the tree does not always hold as a list.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ScopeChildren<'a> {
    List(List<'a, Statement<'a>>),
    One(Statement<'a>),
    None,
}

impl<'a> Sequence for ScopeChildren<'a> {
    type Item = Statement<'a>;

    fn len(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            ScopeChildren::List(list) => list.len(),
            ScopeChildren::One(_) => 1,
            ScopeChildren::None => 0,
        }
    }

    fn at(&self, index: usize) -> Statement<'a> {
        match self {
            ScopeChildren::List(list) => list.at(index),
            ScopeChildren::One(statement) => *statement,
            ScopeChildren::None => unreachable!("a scope without children has no child {index}"),
        }
    }
}

/// A scope with statements of its own: a program, a function body, a block or a case of a switch.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Scope<'a> {
    tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    pub children: ScopeChildren<'a>,
    /// What scope analysis found out if this is the scope of a function, a static block or a program.
    row: Option<&'a ScopeRow>,
}

impl<'a> Scope<'a> {
    fn new(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, children: ScopeChildren<'a>) -> Self {
        Self {
            tree,
            children,
            row: None,
        }
    }

    fn of_list(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, list: u32) -> Self {
        Self::new(tree, ScopeChildren::List(List::new(tree, list, ())))
    }

    fn of_function(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, children: ScopeChildren<'a>, row: &'a ScopeRow) -> Self {
        Self {
            tree,
            children,
            row: Some(row),
        }
    }

    pub fn local_variables(&self) -> &'a [LocalVariable] {
        self.row
            .map_or(&[], |row| row.local_variables.of(self.tree.scopes.local_variables))
    }

    /// Function names hoisted from inner blocks via Annex B.3.3. The FDI should create `var` bindings initialized to
    /// `undefined` for each name.
    pub fn annexb_function_names(&self) -> &'a [Name] {
        self.row.map_or(&[], |row| {
            row.annexb_function_names.of(self.tree.scopes.annexb_function_names)
        })
    }

    pub fn uses_this(&self) -> bool {
        self.row.is_some_and(|row| row.uses_this)
    }

    pub fn uses_this_from_environment(&self) -> bool {
        self.row.is_some_and(|row| row.uses_this_from_environment)
    }

    pub fn contains_direct_call_to_eval(&self) -> bool {
        self.row.is_some_and(|row| row.contains_direct_call_to_eval)
    }

    pub fn contains_access_to_arguments_object(&self) -> bool {
        self.row.is_some_and(|row| row.contains_access_to_arguments_object)
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Expressions
// =============================================================================

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ExpressionForm {
    /// The expression that the node's tag says.
    Node,
    /// The name of an identifier node as a string.
    PropertyKeyName,
    /// The property name after a member node's dot, which has no node of its own.
    MemberName,
    /// The key of a shorthand property node.
    ShorthandKey,
    /// The value of a shorthand property node.
    ShorthandValue { object_start: u32 },
    /// The string of a template chunk node.
    TemplateChunk { is_tagged: bool, template_start: u32 },
    /// The template node of a tagged template.
    TaggedTemplate,
    /// The default constructor of a class node.
    DefaultConstructor,
    /// The `super(...args)` of the default constructor of a class node.
    DefaultConstructorSuperCall,
    /// The `args` of the default constructor of a class node.
    DefaultConstructorArgument,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Expression<'a> {
    tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    node: u32,
    form: ExpressionForm,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct BinaryExpressionData<'a> {
    pub op: BinaryOp,
    pub lhs: Expression<'a>,
    pub rhs: Expression<'a>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct LogicalExpressionData<'a> {
    pub op: LogicalOp,
    pub lhs: Expression<'a>,
    pub rhs: Expression<'a>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct UpdateExpressionData<'a> {
    pub op: UpdateOp,
    pub argument: Expression<'a>,
    pub prefixed: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum AssignmentLhs<'a> {
    Expression(Expression<'a>),
    Pattern(BindingPattern<'a>),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct AssignmentExpressionData<'a> {
    pub op: AssignmentOp,
    pub lhs: AssignmentLhs<'a>,
    pub rhs: Expression<'a>,
    pub lhs_is_parenthesized: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ConditionalExpressionData<'a> {
    pub test: Expression<'a>,
    pub consequent: Expression<'a>,
    pub alternate: Expression<'a>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct MemberExpressionData<'a> {
    pub object: Expression<'a>,
    pub property: Expression<'a>,
    pub computed: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct TaggedTemplateData<'a> {
    pub tag: Expression<'a>,
    pub template_literal: Expression<'a>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ImportCallData<'a> {
    pub specifier: Expression<'a>,
    pub options: Option<Expression<'a>>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct YieldExpressionData<'a> {
    pub argument: Option<Expression<'a>>,
    pub is_yield_from: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ExpressionKind<'a> {
    // Literals
    NumericLiteral(NumericLiteral<'a>),
    StringLiteral(StringLiteral<'a>),
    BooleanLiteral(bool),
    NullLiteral,
    BigIntLiteral(Utf16View<'a>),
    RegExpLiteral(RegExpLiteralData<'a>),

    // Identifiers
    Identifier(Identifier<'a>),
    PrivateIdentifier(PrivateIdentifier<'a>),

    // Operators
    Binary(BinaryExpressionData<'a>),
    Logical(LogicalExpressionData<'a>),
    Unary { op: UnaryOp, operand: Expression<'a> },
    Update(UpdateExpressionData<'a>),
    Assignment(AssignmentExpressionData<'a>),
    Conditional(ConditionalExpressionData<'a>),
    Sequence(List<'a, Expression<'a>>),

    // Member access
    Member(MemberExpressionData<'a>),
    OptionalChain(OptionalChainData<'a>),

    // Calls
    Call(CallExpressionData<'a>),
    New(CallExpressionData<'a>),
    SuperCall(SuperCallData<'a>),

    // Spread
    Spread(Expression<'a>),

    // This / Super
    This,
    Super,

    // Functions
    Function(FunctionId),

    // Classes
    Class(ClassData<'a>),

    // Collections
    Array(List<'a, Option<Expression<'a>>>),
    Object(List<'a, ObjectProperty<'a>>),

    // Templates
    TemplateLiteral(TemplateLiteralData<'a>),
    TaggedTemplateLiteral(TaggedTemplateData<'a>),

    // Meta
    MetaProperty(MetaPropertyType),
    ImportCall(ImportCallData<'a>),

    // Async / Generator
    Yield(YieldExpressionData<'a>),
    Await(Expression<'a>),
}

pub(crate) const BINARY_OPERATORS: [Option<BinaryOp>; 25] = [
    None,
    None,
    None,
    Some(BinaryOp::BitwiseOr),
    Some(BinaryOp::BitwiseXor),
    Some(BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd),
    Some(BinaryOp::LooselyEquals),
    Some(BinaryOp::LooselyInequals),
    Some(BinaryOp::StrictlyEquals),
    Some(BinaryOp::StrictlyInequals),
    Some(BinaryOp::LessThan),
    Some(BinaryOp::GreaterThan),
    Some(BinaryOp::LessThanEquals),
    Some(BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals),
    Some(BinaryOp::LeftShift),
    Some(BinaryOp::RightShift),
    Some(BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift),
    Some(BinaryOp::Addition),
    Some(BinaryOp::Subtraction),
    Some(BinaryOp::Multiplication),
    Some(BinaryOp::Division),
    Some(BinaryOp::Modulo),
    Some(BinaryOp::Exponentiation),
    Some(BinaryOp::In),
    Some(BinaryOp::InstanceOf),
];

pub(crate) const ASSIGNMENT_OPERATORS: [AssignmentOp; 16] = [
    AssignmentOp::Assignment,
    AssignmentOp::AdditionAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::SubtractionAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::MultiplicationAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::DivisionAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::ModuloAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::ExponentiationAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::LeftShiftAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::RightShiftAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::UnsignedRightShiftAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::BitwiseAndAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::BitwiseOrAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::BitwiseXorAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::AndAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::OrAssignment,
    AssignmentOp::NullishAssignment,
];

impl<'a> Expression<'a> {
    /// The expression at `node`, which a pair of parentheses leaves as it is.
    pub(crate) fn new(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, mut node: u32) -> Self {
        while tree.tag(node) == tag::PAREN {
            node = tree.a(node);
        }
        Self::with_form(tree, node, ExpressionForm::Node)
    }

    fn with_form(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, node: u32, form: ExpressionForm) -> Self {
        Self { tree, node, form }
    }

    /// Where the expression starts in the source.
    pub fn source_offset(&self) -> u32 {
        let tree = self.tree;
        match self.form {
            ExpressionForm::Node if tree.tag(self.node) == tag::STR => tree.b(self.node),
            ExpressionForm::MemberName => tree.name_after(tree.pos(self.node)),
            ExpressionForm::ShorthandKey => tree.pos(tree.b(self.node)),
            ExpressionForm::ShorthandValue { object_start } => object_start,
            ExpressionForm::TemplateChunk { template_start, .. } if self.is_failed_template_chunk() => template_start,
            _ => tree.pos(self.node),
        }
    }

    pub fn range(&self) -> SourceRange {
        self.tree.range(self.source_offset())
    }

    fn is_failed_template_chunk(&self) -> bool {
        let ExpressionForm::TemplateChunk { is_tagged: true, .. } = self.form else {
            return false;
        };
        literals::process_escape_sequences_impl(template_chunk_units(self.tree, self.node), EscapeMode::TaggedTemplate)
            .failed
    }

    fn template(&self, is_tagged: bool) -> TemplateLiteralData<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let items = tree.list(tree.a(self.node));
        TemplateLiteralData {
            tree,
            items,
            expressions: List::of_items(
                tree,
                items,
                TemplateElementContext {
                    is_tagged,
                    template_start: tree.pos(self.node),
                },
            ),
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self) -> ExpressionKind<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(node), tree.b(node));
        match self.form {
            ExpressionForm::Node => {}
            ExpressionForm::PropertyKeyName => {
                return ExpressionKind::StringLiteral(StringLiteral::Name(tree.name_text(Name(a))));
            }
            ExpressionForm::MemberName => {
                let offset = tree.name_after(tree.pos(node));
                return if tree.tag(node) == tag::MEMBER {
                    ExpressionKind::Identifier(tree.plain_identifier(Name(b), offset))
                } else {
                    ExpressionKind::PrivateIdentifier(tree.private_identifier(b, offset))
                };
            }
            ExpressionForm::ShorthandKey => {
                return ExpressionKind::StringLiteral(StringLiteral::Name(tree.name_text(Name(a))));
            }
            ExpressionForm::ShorthandValue { object_start } => {
                return ExpressionKind::Identifier(tree.identifier(Name(a), object_start, node));
            }
            ExpressionForm::TemplateChunk { is_tagged, .. } => {
                return if self.is_failed_template_chunk() {
                    ExpressionKind::NullLiteral
                } else {
                    let mode = if is_tagged {
                        EscapeMode::TaggedTemplate
                    } else {
                        EscapeMode::StringLiteral
                    };
                    ExpressionKind::StringLiteral(StringLiteral::Source(template_chunk_units(tree, node), mode))
                };
            }
            ExpressionForm::TaggedTemplate => return ExpressionKind::TemplateLiteral(self.template(true)),
            ExpressionForm::DefaultConstructor => {
                return ExpressionKind::Function(FunctionId {
                    node,
                    source: FunctionSource::DefaultConstructor,
                });
            }
            ExpressionForm::DefaultConstructorSuperCall => {
                return ExpressionKind::SuperCall(SuperCallData {
                    arguments: CallArguments::DefaultConstructorSpread(CallArgument {
                        value: Expression::with_form(tree, node, ExpressionForm::DefaultConstructorArgument),
                        is_spread: true,
                    }),
                    is_synthetic: true,
                });
            }
            ExpressionForm::DefaultConstructorArgument => {
                return ExpressionKind::Identifier(
                    tree.plain_identifier(tree.script.default_constructor_parameter_name, tree.pos(node)),
                );
            }
        }
        let node_tag = tree.tag(node);
        let start = tree.pos(node);
        match node_tag {
            tag::IDENT => ExpressionKind::Identifier(tree.identifier(Name(a), start, node)),
            tag::NUM => ExpressionKind::NumericLiteral(NumericLiteral {
                text: tree.source_units(start, a),
            }),
            tag::BIGINT => ExpressionKind::BigIntLiteral(tree.source_units(start, a)),
            tag::STR => ExpressionKind::StringLiteral(StringLiteral::Source(
                tree.string_units(node),
                EscapeMode::StringLiteral,
            )),
            tag::REGEX => ExpressionKind::RegExpLiteral(RegExpLiteralData {
                pattern: tree.source_units(start + 1, a),
                flags: tree.source_units(a + 1, b),
            }),
            tag::TRUE => ExpressionKind::BooleanLiteral(true),
            tag::FALSE => ExpressionKind::BooleanLiteral(false),
            tag::NULL => ExpressionKind::NullLiteral,
            tag::THIS => ExpressionKind::This,
            tag::SUPER => ExpressionKind::Super,
            tag::NEW_TARGET => ExpressionKind::MetaProperty(MetaPropertyType::NewTarget),
            tag::IMPORT_META => ExpressionKind::MetaProperty(MetaPropertyType::ImportMeta),
            tag::PRIVATE_NAME => ExpressionKind::PrivateIdentifier(tree.private_identifier(a, start)),
            tag::FUNCTION => ExpressionKind::Function(FunctionId::function(node)),
            tag::MEMBER | tag::PRIVATE_MEMBER => ExpressionKind::Member(MemberExpressionData {
                object: Expression::new(tree, a),
                property: Expression::with_form(tree, node, ExpressionForm::MemberName),
                computed: false,
            }),
            tag::INDEX => ExpressionKind::Member(MemberExpressionData {
                object: Expression::new(tree, a),
                property: Expression::new(tree, b),
                computed: true,
            }),
            tag::CHAIN => ExpressionKind::OptionalChain(OptionalChainData { tree, node: a }),
            tag::SPREAD => ExpressionKind::Spread(Expression::new(tree, a)),
            tag::YIELD | tag::YIELD_STAR => ExpressionKind::Yield(YieldExpressionData {
                argument: (a != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, a)),
                is_yield_from: node_tag == tag::YIELD_STAR,
            }),
            tag::AWAIT => ExpressionKind::Await(Expression::new(tree, a)),
            tag::CONDITIONAL => ExpressionKind::Conditional(ConditionalExpressionData {
                test: Expression::new(tree, a),
                consequent: Expression::new(tree, tree.extra(b)),
                alternate: Expression::new(tree, tree.extra(b + 1)),
            }),
            tag::UNARY => {
                let op = match b {
                    token if token == T::Not as u32 => UnaryOp::Not,
                    token if token == T::Tilde as u32 => UnaryOp::BitwiseNot,
                    token if token == T::Plus as u32 => UnaryOp::Plus,
                    token if token == T::Minus as u32 => UnaryOp::Minus,
                    token if token == T::KTypeof as u32 => UnaryOp::Typeof,
                    token if token == T::KVoid as u32 => UnaryOp::Void,
                    _ => UnaryOp::Delete,
                };
                ExpressionKind::Unary {
                    op,
                    operand: Expression::new(tree, a),
                }
            }
            tag::PREFIX_UPDATE | tag::POSTFIX_UPDATE => ExpressionKind::Update(UpdateExpressionData {
                op: if b == T::Inc as u32 {
                    UpdateOp::Increment
                } else {
                    UpdateOp::Decrement
                },
                argument: Expression::new(tree, a),
                prefixed: node_tag == tag::PREFIX_UPDATE,
            }),
            tag::TAGGED_TEMPLATE => ExpressionKind::TaggedTemplateLiteral(TaggedTemplateData {
                tag: Expression::new(tree, a),
                template_literal: Expression::with_form(tree, b, ExpressionForm::TaggedTemplate),
            }),
            tag::IMPORT_CALL => ExpressionKind::ImportCall(ImportCallData {
                specifier: Expression::new(tree, a),
                options: (b != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, b)),
            }),
            tag::CALL if tree.tag(a) == tag::SUPER => ExpressionKind::SuperCall(SuperCallData {
                arguments: CallArguments::List(List::new(tree, b, ())),
                is_synthetic: false,
            }),
            tag::CALL | tag::NEW => {
                let data = CallExpressionData {
                    callee: Expression::new(tree, a),
                    arguments: CallArguments::List(List::new(tree, b, ())),
                };
                if node_tag == tag::CALL {
                    ExpressionKind::Call(data)
                } else {
                    ExpressionKind::New(data)
                }
            }
            tag::ARRAY => ExpressionKind::Array(List::new(tree, a, ())),
            tag::OBJECT => ExpressionKind::Object(List::new(tree, a, start)),
            tag::SEQUENCE => ExpressionKind::Sequence(List::new(tree, a, ())),
            tag::TEMPLATE => ExpressionKind::TemplateLiteral(self.template(false)),
            tag::CLASS => ExpressionKind::Class(tree.class(node)),
            tag::ASSIGN_PATTERN => self.assignment(0, a, b),
            _ if node_tag >= tag::BINARY_BASE => self.binary(node_tag - tag::BINARY_BASE, a, b),
            _ if node_tag >= tag::ASSIGN_BASE => self.assignment(node_tag - tag::ASSIGN_BASE, a, b),
            other => unreachable!("tag {other} is no expression"),
        }
    }

    fn binary(&self, operator: u8, a: u32, b: u32) -> ExpressionKind<'a> {
        let lhs = Expression::new(self.tree, a);
        let rhs = Expression::new(self.tree, b);
        match BINARY_OPERATORS[operator as usize] {
            Some(op) => ExpressionKind::Binary(BinaryExpressionData { op, lhs, rhs }),
            None => {
                let op = match operator {
                    0 => LogicalOp::NullishCoalescing,
                    1 => LogicalOp::Or,
                    _ => LogicalOp::And,
                };
                ExpressionKind::Logical(LogicalExpressionData { op, lhs, rhs })
            }
        }
    }

    fn assignment(&self, operator: u8, a: u32, b: u32) -> ExpressionKind<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let lhs = if matches!(tree.tag(a), tag::ARRAY_PATTERN | tag::OBJECT_PATTERN) {
            AssignmentLhs::Pattern(BindingPattern::new(tree, a, PatternMode::Assignment))
        } else {
            AssignmentLhs::Expression(Expression::new(tree, a))
        };
        ExpressionKind::Assignment(AssignmentExpressionData {
            op: ASSIGNMENT_OPERATORS[operator as usize],
            lhs,
            rhs: Expression::new(tree, b),
            lhs_is_parenthesized: tree.tag(a) == tag::PAREN,
        })
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Statements
// =============================================================================

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum StatementForm {
    /// The statement that the node's tag says.
    Node,
    /// The body of a function node.
    FunctionBody,
    /// The `return` that the expression of an arrow function node means.
    ExpressionBodyReturn,
    /// The body of a static block node.
    StaticBlockBody { class_start: u32 },
    /// The expression of `export default` at the node.
    ExportedExpression,
    /// The declaration of `export default` of a function node.
    ExportedFunction,
    /// The evaluation of the initializer of a class field node.
    ClassFieldInitializer,
    /// The body of the default constructor of a class node.
    DefaultConstructorBody,
    /// The `return super(...args)` of the default constructor of a class node.
    DefaultConstructorReturn,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Statement<'a> {
    tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    node: u32,
    form: StatementForm,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum StatementKind<'a> {
    // Basic
    Empty,
    Expression(Expression<'a>),
    Debugger,

    // Blocks (carry ScopeData for scope analysis)
    Block(Scope<'a>),
    FunctionBody { scope: Scope<'a>, in_strict_mode: bool },
    Program(ProgramData<'a>),

    // Control flow
    If(IfStatementData<'a>),
    While(WhileStatementData<'a>),
    DoWhile(WhileStatementData<'a>),
    For(ForStatementData<'a>),
    ForInOf(ForInOfStatementData<'a>),
    Switch(SwitchStatementData<'a>),
    With(WithStatementData<'a>),
    Labelled(LabelledStatementData<'a>),

    // Jumps
    Break { target_label: Option<Utf16View<'a>> },
    Continue { target_label: Option<Utf16View<'a>> },
    Return(Option<Expression<'a>>),
    Throw(Expression<'a>),
    Try(TryStatementData<'a>),

    // Declarations
    VariableDeclaration(VariableDeclarationData<'a>),
    UsingDeclaration(UsingDeclarationData<'a>),
    FunctionDeclaration(FunctionDeclarationData<'a>),
    ClassDeclaration(ClassData<'a>),

    // Module
    Import(ImportStatementData<'a>),
    Export(ExportStatementData<'a>),

    // Special
    ClassFieldInitializer(ClassFieldInitializerData<'a>),
}

impl<'a> Statement<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, node: u32) -> Self {
        Self::with_form(tree, node, StatementForm::Node)
    }

    fn with_form(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, node: u32, form: StatementForm) -> Self {
        Self { tree, node, form }
    }

    /// Where the statement starts in the source.
    pub fn source_offset(&self) -> u32 {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        match self.form {
            StatementForm::Node => match tree.tag(node) {
                tag::PROGRAM => tree.first_token_start,
                tag::FUNCTION_DECL => tree.pos(tree.a(node)),
                _ => tree.pos(node),
            },
            StatementForm::FunctionBody => {
                let function_tree = tree.a(node);
                if tree.extra(function_tree + 6) != 0 {
                    tree.pos(node)
                } else {
                    tree.extra(function_tree + 5)
                }
            }
            StatementForm::StaticBlockBody { class_start } => class_start,
            StatementForm::ExportedExpression => Expression::new(tree, node).source_offset(),
            StatementForm::ClassFieldInitializer => Expression::new(tree, tree.a(tree.b(node))).source_offset(),
            StatementForm::ExpressionBodyReturn
            | StatementForm::ExportedFunction
            | StatementForm::DefaultConstructorBody
            | StatementForm::DefaultConstructorReturn => tree.pos(node),
        }
    }

    pub fn range(&self) -> SourceRange {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        match self.form {
            StatementForm::Node if tree.tag(node) == tag::BLOCK => {
                tree.range_between(tree.pos(node), tree.block_end(tree.a(node)))
            }
            StatementForm::StaticBlockBody { class_start } => {
                tree.range_between(class_start, tree.block_end(tree.a(node)))
            }
            StatementForm::ClassFieldInitializer => {
                let initializer = tree.b(node);
                let mut range = Expression::new(tree, tree.a(initializer)).range();
                range.end = tree.script.positions.lines.position(tree.pos(initializer));
                range
            }
            _ => tree.range(self.source_offset()),
        }
    }

    fn function_scope(&self, children: ScopeChildren<'a>) -> Scope<'a> {
        Scope::of_function(self.tree, children, self.tree.function_scope(self.node))
    }

    fn static_block_scope(&self) -> Scope<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let row = tree.scope_row(tree.resolution(self.node).0);
        Scope::of_function(tree, ScopeChildren::List(List::new(tree, tree.a(self.node), ())), row)
    }

    fn loop_kind(&self) -> StatementKind<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(node), tree.b(node));
        let is_declaration = |node: u32| {
            matches!(
                tree.tag(node),
                tag::VAR | tag::LET | tag::CONST | tag::USING | tag::AWAIT_USING
            )
        };
        match tree.tag(node) {
            tag::FOR => {
                let (test, update, body) = (tree.extra(b), tree.extra(b + 1), tree.extra(b + 2));
                StatementKind::For(ForStatementData {
                    init: (a != 0).then(|| {
                        if is_declaration(a) {
                            ForInit::Declaration(Statement::new(tree, a))
                        } else {
                            ForInit::Expression(Expression::new(tree, a))
                        }
                    }),
                    test: (test != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, test)),
                    update: (update != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, update)),
                    body: Statement::new(tree, body),
                })
            }
            other => {
                let kind = match other {
                    tag::FOR_IN => ForInOfKind::ForIn,
                    tag::FOR_OF => ForInOfKind::ForOf,
                    _ => ForInOfKind::ForAwaitOf,
                };
                let (right, body) = (tree.extra(b), tree.extra(b + 1));
                let lhs = if matches!(tree.tag(a), tag::ARRAY_PATTERN | tag::OBJECT_PATTERN) {
                    ForInOfLhs::Pattern(BindingPattern::new(tree, a, PatternMode::Assignment))
                } else if is_declaration(a) {
                    ForInOfLhs::Declaration(Statement::new(tree, a))
                } else {
                    ForInOfLhs::Expression(Expression::new(tree, a))
                };
                StatementKind::ForInOf(ForInOfStatementData {
                    kind,
                    lhs,
                    rhs: Expression::new(tree, right),
                    body: Statement::new(tree, body),
                })
            }
        }
    }

    fn export_kind(&self) -> StatementKind<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(node), tree.b(node));
        let (statement, is_default_export) = match tree.tag(node) {
            tag::EXPORT_ALL => (None, false),
            tag::EXPORT_DEFAULT => {
                let inner_tag = tree.tag(a);
                let statement = if inner_tag == tag::FUNCTION && b != 0 {
                    Statement::with_form(tree, a, StatementForm::ExportedFunction)
                } else if inner_tag == tag::CLASS_DECL {
                    Statement::new(tree, a)
                } else {
                    Statement::with_form(tree, a, StatementForm::ExportedExpression)
                };
                (Some(statement), true)
            }
            _ if a != 0 => (None, false),
            _ => (Some(Statement::new(tree, b)), false),
        };
        StatementKind::Export(ExportStatementData {
            tree,
            node,
            statement,
            is_default_export,
        })
    }

    pub fn kind(&self) -> StatementKind<'a> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let node = self.node;
        match self.form {
            StatementForm::Node => {}
            StatementForm::FunctionBody => {
                let function_tree = tree.a(node);
                let body = tree.extra(function_tree + 1);
                let is_expression = tree.extra(function_tree + 6) != 0;
                let children = if is_expression {
                    ScopeChildren::One(Statement::with_form(tree, node, StatementForm::ExpressionBodyReturn))
                } else {
                    ScopeChildren::List(List::new(tree, body, ()))
                };
                return StatementKind::FunctionBody {
                    scope: self.function_scope(children),
                    in_strict_mode: tree.script.index.flags[tree.b(node) as usize] & function_flag::STRICT != 0,
                };
            }
            StatementForm::ExpressionBodyReturn => {
                return StatementKind::Return(Some(Expression::new(tree, tree.extra(tree.a(node) + 1))));
            }
            StatementForm::StaticBlockBody { .. } => {
                return StatementKind::FunctionBody {
                    scope: self.static_block_scope(),
                    in_strict_mode: true,
                };
            }
            StatementForm::ExportedExpression => return StatementKind::Expression(Expression::new(tree, node)),
            StatementForm::ExportedFunction => {
                let name = tree.script.index.name[tree.b(node) as usize];
                return StatementKind::FunctionDeclaration(tree.function_declaration(node, name));
            }
            StatementForm::ClassFieldInitializer => {
                return StatementKind::ClassFieldInitializer(ClassFieldInitializerData {
                    expression: Expression::new(tree, tree.a(tree.b(node))),
                    key: ClassElementNode {
                        tree,
                        node,
                        class_start: 0,
                    }
                    .property_key(tree.a(node), tree.tag(node) == tag::COMPUTED_CLASS_FIELD),
                });
            }
            StatementForm::DefaultConstructorBody => {
                let has_super_class = tree.extra(tree.b(node)) != 0;
                return StatementKind::Block(Scope::new(
                    tree,
                    if has_super_class {
                        ScopeChildren::One(Statement::with_form(
                            tree,
                            node,
                            StatementForm::DefaultConstructorReturn,
                        ))
                    } else {
                        ScopeChildren::None
                    },
                ));
            }
            StatementForm::DefaultConstructorReturn => {
                return StatementKind::Return(Some(Expression::with_form(
                    tree,
                    node,
                    ExpressionForm::DefaultConstructorSuperCall,
                )));
            }
        }
        let (a, b) = (tree.a(node), tree.b(node));
        match tree.tag(node) {
            tag::PROGRAM => StatementKind::Program(ProgramData {
                scope: Scope::of_function(
                    tree,
                    ScopeChildren::List(List::new(tree, a, ())),
                    tree.scope_row(tree.program_scope_row),
                ),
                program_type: tree.program_type(),
                is_strict_mode: tree.is_strict_mode,
                has_top_level_await: tree.has_top_level_await,
            }),
            tag::EMPTY => StatementKind::Empty,
            tag::DEBUGGER => StatementKind::Debugger,
            tag::EXPR_STMT => StatementKind::Expression(Expression::new(tree, a)),
            tag::SCOPED => StatementKind::Block(Scope::new(tree, ScopeChildren::One(Statement::new(tree, a)))),
            tag::FOR | tag::FOR_IN | tag::FOR_OF | tag::FOR_AWAIT_OF => self.loop_kind(),
            tag::IF_FUNCTION_BLOCK => {
                StatementKind::Block(Scope::new(tree, ScopeChildren::One(Statement::new(tree, a))))
            }
            tag::BLOCK => StatementKind::Block(Scope::of_list(tree, a)),
            tag::IF => {
                let (consequent, alternate) = (tree.extra(b), tree.extra(b + 1));
                StatementKind::If(IfStatementData {
                    test: Expression::new(tree, a),
                    consequent: Statement::new(tree, consequent),
                    alternate: (alternate != 0).then(|| Statement::new(tree, alternate)),
                })
            }
            tag::WHILE => StatementKind::While(WhileStatementData {
                test: Expression::new(tree, a),
                body: Statement::new(tree, b),
            }),
            tag::DO_WHILE => StatementKind::DoWhile(WhileStatementData {
                test: Expression::new(tree, b),
                body: Statement::new(tree, a),
            }),
            tag::SWITCH => StatementKind::Switch(SwitchStatementData {
                discriminant: Expression::new(tree, a),
                cases: List::new(tree, tree.extra(b), ()),
            }),
            tag::WITH => StatementKind::With(WithStatementData {
                object: Expression::new(tree, a),
                body: Statement::new(tree, tree.extra(b)),
            }),
            tag::LABELED => StatementKind::Labelled(LabelledStatementData {
                label: tree.name_text(Name(a)),
                item: Statement::new(tree, b),
            }),
            tag::BREAK => StatementKind::Break {
                target_label: (a != NONE).then(|| tree.name_text(Name(a))),
            },
            tag::CONTINUE => StatementKind::Continue {
                target_label: (a != NONE).then(|| tree.name_text(Name(a))),
            },
            tag::RETURN => StatementKind::Return((a != 0).then(|| Expression::new(tree, a))),
            tag::THROW => StatementKind::Throw(Expression::new(tree, a)),
            tag::TRY => {
                let (parameter, handler, finalizer) = (tree.extra(b), tree.extra(b + 1), tree.extra(b + 2));
                StatementKind::Try(TryStatementData {
                    block: Statement::new(tree, a),
                    handler: (handler != 0).then(|| CatchClause {
                        tree,
                        offset: tree.extra(b + 3),
                        parameter: (parameter != 0).then(|| {
                            if tree.tag(parameter) == tag::IDENT {
                                CatchBinding::Identifier(tree.identifier(
                                    Name(tree.a(parameter)),
                                    tree.pos(parameter),
                                    parameter,
                                ))
                            } else {
                                CatchBinding::BindingPattern(BindingPattern::new(tree, parameter, PatternMode::Binding))
                            }
                        }),
                        body: Statement::new(tree, handler),
                    }),
                    finalizer: (finalizer != 0).then(|| Statement::new(tree, finalizer)),
                })
            }
            node_tag @ (tag::VAR | tag::LET | tag::CONST | tag::USING | tag::AWAIT_USING) => {
                let declarations = List::new(tree, a, tree.pos(node));
                match node_tag {
                    tag::USING | tag::AWAIT_USING => StatementKind::UsingDeclaration(UsingDeclarationData {
                        is_await: node_tag == tag::AWAIT_USING,
                        declarations,
                    }),
                    _ => StatementKind::VariableDeclaration(VariableDeclarationData {
                        kind: match node_tag {
                            tag::VAR => DeclarationKind::Var,
                            tag::LET => DeclarationKind::Let,
                            _ => DeclarationKind::Const,
                        },
                        declarations,
                    }),
                }
            }
            tag::FUNCTION_DECL => StatementKind::FunctionDeclaration(tree.function_declaration(a, b)),
            tag::CLASS_DECL => StatementKind::ClassDeclaration(tree.class(a)),
            tag::IMPORT => StatementKind::Import(ImportStatementData { tree, node }),
            tag::EXPORT_ALL | tag::EXPORT_DEFAULT | tag::EXPORT_NAMED => self.export_kind(),
            other => unreachable!("tag {other} is no statement"),
        }
    }

    pub fn function_declaration_for_labelled_item(&self) -> Option<FunctionDeclarationData<'a>> {
        // https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-static-semantics-lexicallyscopeddeclarations
        // LabelledItem : FunctionDeclaration
        // 1. Return « |FunctionDeclaration| ».
        let mut statement = *self;
        loop {
            match statement.kind() {
                StatementKind::FunctionDeclaration(function) => return Some(function),
                StatementKind::Labelled(data) => statement = data.item,
                _ => return None,
            }
        }
    }
}

impl_sequence_into_iterator!(FunctionParameters, ClassElements, ScopeChildren, CallArguments);

//! The positions in a source that a debugger can stop at: those that the bytecode of the source maps back to.

use crate::ast::ProgramType;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ExecutableData;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::PendingSharedFunctionData;
use crate::compile::FunctionPayload;
use crate::compile::compile_function;
use crate::compile::compile_parsed_program_off_thread;
use crate::compile::parse;
use libjs_parser::base::DEFAULT_STACK_BUDGET;
use libjs_parser::base::stack_limit_for_budget;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct BreakpointPosition {
    pub line: u32,
    pub column: u32,
}

/// The breakpoint positions of `source`, sorted and without repeats, with lines counted as [`parse()`] counts them
/// from `initial_line_number`. A source with syntax errors has none. Every function gets compiled to find them, on its
/// own, the way that it would on its first call. The positions of what does not fit the stack left out.
pub fn breakpoint_positions_for_source(
    source: &ak::Utf16String,
    program_type: ProgramType,
    initial_line_number: usize,
) -> Vec<BreakpointPosition> {
    let parsed = parse(source, program_type, initial_line_number);
    if parsed.has_errors() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let compiled = compile_parsed_program_off_thread(parsed);
    let mut positions = Vec::new();
    match program_type {
        ProgramType::Script => {
            let script = compiled.into_script();
            add_positions_of_executable(&script.executable, &mut positions);
            for function in &script.declarations.functions_to_initialize {
                add_positions_of_function(&function.shared_function_data, &mut positions);
            }
        }
        ProgramType::Module => {
            let module = compiled.into_module();
            add_positions_of_executable(&module.executable, &mut positions);
            for function in &module.declarations.functions_to_initialize {
                add_positions_of_payload(&function.description.payload, &mut positions);
            }
        }
    }
    positions.sort_unstable();
    positions.dedup();
    positions
}

fn add_positions_of_executable(executable: &ExecutableData, positions: &mut Vec<BreakpointPosition>) {
    for entry in executable.source_positions() {
        if entry.line != 0 {
            positions.push(BreakpointPosition {
                line: entry.line,
                column: entry.column,
            });
        }
    }
    for function in &executable.shared_function_data {
        add_positions_of_function(function, positions);
    }
}

fn add_positions_of_function(function: &PendingSharedFunctionData, positions: &mut Vec<BreakpointPosition>) {
    if let Some(precompiled) = &function.precompiled_function {
        add_positions_of_executable(&precompiled.executable, positions);
    } else {
        add_positions_of_payload(&function.description.payload, positions);
    }
}

fn add_positions_of_payload(payload: &FunctionPayload, positions: &mut Vec<BreakpointPosition>) {
    if let Ok(compiled) = compile_function(payload, false, stack_limit_for_budget(DEFAULT_STACK_BUDGET)) {
        add_positions_of_executable(&compiled.executable, positions);
    }
}

//! Values that depend on how LibGC and the interpreter were built, as the build script determined them.

const fn parse_decimal(text: &str) -> u64 {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let mut value = 0u64;
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < bytes.len() {
        assert!(bytes[index].is_ascii_digit());
        value = value * 10 + (bytes[index] - b'0') as u64;
        index += 1;
    }
    value
}

pub const HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK: u64 = parse_decimal(env!("LIBJS_RUNTIME_HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK"));
pub const PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_CAGE_OFFSET_MASK: u64 =
    parse_decimal(env!("LIBJS_RUNTIME_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_CAGE_OFFSET_MASK"));
/// How much native stack must stay free for the interpreter to keep running JavaScript.
pub const VM_STACK_SPACE_LIMIT: u64 = parse_decimal(env!("LIBJS_RUNTIME_VM_STACK_SPACE_LIMIT"));

//! The classes an executable declares.

use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;

use crate::utf16::Utf16View;
use libjs_abi::ClassElementKind;
use libjs_runtime_macros::Trace;

use crate::bytecode::executable_data::{PendingClassBlueprint, PendingClassElement, PendingLiteralValueKind};
use crate::gc::defer_gc::DeferGc;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::primitive_string::PrimitiveString;
use crate::source_code::SourceCode;

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
pub struct ClassElementDescriptor {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub kind: ClassElementKind,
    pub is_static: bool,
    pub is_private: bool,
    pub private_identifier: Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    pub shared_function_data_index: Option<u32>,
    pub has_initializer: bool,
    pub literal_value: Option<Value>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
pub struct ClassBlueprint {
    pub constructor_shared_function_data_index: u32,
    pub has_super_class: bool,
    pub has_name: bool,
    pub name: Utf16FlyString,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub source_code: Option<Rc<SourceCode>>,
    pub source_text_offset: usize,
    pub source_text_length: usize,
    pub elements: Vec<ClassElementDescriptor>,
}

fn class_element_kind(kind: u8) -> ClassElementKind {
    match kind {
        0 => ClassElementKind::Method,
        1 => ClassElementKind::Getter,
        2 => ClassElementKind::Setter,
        3 => ClassElementKind::Field,
        4 => ClassElementKind::StaticInitializer,
        _ => unreachable!("{kind} is not a class element kind"),
    }
}

impl ClassBlueprint {
    /// Creates the blueprint of a class the frontend compiled, as rust_create_class_blueprint does.
    pub fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        blueprint: &PendingClassBlueprint,
        source_code: Option<&Rc<SourceCode>>,
        _defer_gc: &DeferGc<'_>,
    ) -> ClassBlueprint {
        let name = match &blueprint.name {
            Some(name) if !name.is_empty() => Utf16View::of_string(name).to_utf16_fly_string(),
            _ => Utf16FlyString::default(),
        };
        let elements = blueprint
            .elements
            .iter()
            .map(|element| Self::create_element(vm, element))
            .collect();
        ClassBlueprint {
            constructor_shared_function_data_index: blueprint.constructor_sfd_index,
            has_super_class: blueprint.has_super_class,
            has_name: blueprint.has_name,
            name,
            source_code: source_code.cloned(),
            source_text_offset: blueprint.source_text_offset,
            source_text_length: blueprint.source_text_length,
            elements,
        }
    }

    fn create_element(vm: &Vm, element: &PendingClassElement) -> ClassElementDescriptor {
        let private_identifier = element
            .private_identifier
            .as_ref()
            .filter(|identifier| !identifier.is_empty())
            .map(|identifier| Utf16View::of_string(identifier).to_utf16_fly_string());
        let literal_value = match element.literal_value_kind {
            PendingLiteralValueKind::None => None,
            PendingLiteralValueKind::Number => Some(Value::from_f64(element.literal_value_number)),
            PendingLiteralValueKind::BooleanTrue => Some(Value::TRUE),
            PendingLiteralValueKind::BooleanFalse => Some(Value::FALSE),
            PendingLiteralValueKind::Null => Some(Value::NULL),
            PendingLiteralValueKind::String => {
                let string = element.literal_value_string.clone().unwrap_or_default();
                Some(Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, string)))
            }
        };
        ClassElementDescriptor {
            kind: class_element_kind(element.kind),
            is_static: element.is_static,
            is_private: element.is_private,
            private_identifier,
            shared_function_data_index: element.shared_function_data_index,
            has_initializer: element.has_initializer,
            literal_value,
        }
    }
}

//! Reading and writing bindings.

use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::*;

use super::context::Generator;
use super::environment::BindingLocation;
use super::environment::location_for_instructions;

pub(super) fn emit_get_binding(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    dst: Operand,
    identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    known_initialized: bool,
) {
    let location = generator.binding_location_for_identifier(identifier);
    emit_get_binding_at(generator, dst, identifier, location, known_initialized);
}

/// Reads the binding at `location`, as seen from the running lexical environment.
pub(super) fn emit_get_binding_at(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    dst: Operand,
    identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    location: Option<BindingLocation>,
    known_initialized: bool,
) {
    // Prefer an eagerly-computed coordinate when the generator can prove that
    // the binding lives in a known declarative environment. The dynamic forms
    // remain necessary for script and eval code, eval-poisoned scopes, and
    // `with`.
    match (location_for_instructions(location), known_initialized) {
        (Some(BindingLocation::Import(import_index)), _) => generator.put(op::GetImport {
            dst,
            identifier,
            import_index,
        }),
        (Some(BindingLocation::Environment(cache)), true) => {
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::GetInitializedBinding {
                value_feedback,
                dst,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
        (Some(BindingLocation::Environment(cache)), false) => {
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::GetBinding {
                value_feedback,
                dst,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
        (None, true) => {
            let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::DynamicGetInitializedBinding {
                value_feedback,
                dst,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
        (None, false) => {
            let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::DynamicGetBinding {
                value_feedback,
                dst,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_get_callee_and_this_from_environment(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    callee: Operand,
    this_value: Operand,
    identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
) {
    match location_for_instructions(generator.binding_location_for_identifier(identifier)) {
        Some(BindingLocation::Environment(cache)) => {
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::GetCalleeAndThisFromEnvironment {
                value_feedback,
                callee,
                this_value,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
        Some(BindingLocation::Import(import_index)) => {
            generator.put(op::GetImport {
                dst: callee,
                identifier,
                import_index,
            });
            let undefined = generator.add_constant_undefined();
            generator.emit_mov(this_value, undefined);
        }
        None => {
            let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
            let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
            generator.put(op::DynamicGetCalleeAndThisFromEnvironment {
                value_feedback,
                callee,
                this_value,
                identifier,
                cache,
            });
        }
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_initialize_lexical_binding(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    src: Operand,
) {
    if let Some(cache) = generator.environment_coordinate_for_identifier(identifier) {
        generator.put(op::InitializeLexicalBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
        generator.put(op::DynamicInitializeLexicalBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_initialize_variable_binding(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    src: Operand,
) {
    // Var bindings are resolved from vm.variable_environment(), not from the
    // current lexical environment. Use the generator's variable-environment
    // anchor so nested lexical scopes do not affect the coordinate hops.
    if let Some(cache) = generator.variable_environment_coordinate_for_identifier(identifier) {
        generator.put(op::InitializeVariableBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
        generator.put(op::DynamicInitializeVariableBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_set_lexical_binding(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, identifier: IdentifierTableIndex, src: Operand) {
    if let Some(cache) = generator.environment_coordinate_for_identifier(identifier) {
        generator.put(op::SetLexicalBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
        generator.put(op::DynamicSetLexicalBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_set_variable_binding(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, identifier: IdentifierTableIndex, src: Operand) {
    // See emit_initialize_variable_binding for why var coordinates use a
    // different lookup anchor than ordinary lexical operations.
    if let Some(cache) = generator.variable_environment_coordinate_for_identifier(identifier) {
        generator.put(op::SetVariableBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
        generator.put(op::DynamicSetVariableBinding { identifier, src, cache });
    }
}

pub(super) fn emit_typeof_binding(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, dst: Operand, identifier: IdentifierTableIndex) {
    match location_for_instructions(generator.binding_location_for_identifier(identifier)) {
        Some(BindingLocation::Environment(cache)) => {
            generator.put(op::TypeofBinding { dst, identifier, cache });
        }
        Some(BindingLocation::Import(import_index)) => {
            generator.put(op::GetImport {
                dst,
                identifier,
                import_index,
            });
            generator.put(op::Typeof { dst, src: dst });
        }
        None => {
            let cache = generator.next_environment_coordinate_cache();
            generator.put(op::DynamicTypeofBinding { dst, identifier, cache });
        }
    }
}

pub(super) enum ResolvedBinding {
    /// The environment ResolveBinding found the binding in, or null if the reference is unresolvable.
    Environment {
        environment: Operand,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    },
    /// Whether ResolveGlobalBinding found the binding of an identifier the compiler found no binding of before the
    /// global environment, in which case it is stored with SetGlobal.
    Global {
        is_resolvable: Operand,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
        cache: u32,
    },
}

pub(super) fn emit_set_resolved_binding(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    resolved_binding: &ResolvedBinding,
    value: Operand,
) {
    match resolved_binding {
        ResolvedBinding::Environment {
            environment,
            identifier,
        } => {
            generator.put(op::SetResolvedBinding {
                environment: *environment,
                identifier: *identifier,
                src: value,
            });
        }
        ResolvedBinding::Global {
            is_resolvable,
            identifier,
            cache,
        } => {
            let set_block = generator.new_label();
            let unresolvable_block = generator.new_label();
            let end_block = generator.new_label();
            generator.emit_jump_if(*is_resolvable, set_block, unresolvable_block);

            generator.bind_reachable_label(set_block);
            generator.put(op::SetGlobal {
                identifier: *identifier,
                src: value,
                cache: *cache,
            });
            generator.put(op::Jump { target: end_block });

            // NB: PutValue of an unresolvable reference throws a ReferenceError in strict mode code.
            generator.bind_reachable_label(unresolvable_block);
            let null = generator.add_constant_null();
            generator.put(op::SetResolvedBinding {
                environment: null,
                identifier: *identifier,
                src: value,
            });
            generator.put(op::Jump { target: end_block });

            generator.bind_reachable_label(end_block);
        }
    }
}

/*

//! What the JavaScript of the engine itself can say that other code cannot: abstract operations that it calls by name,
//! and constants.

use crate::ast::Name;
use crate::bytecode::constant::AbstractOperationKind;
use crate::bytecode::constant::WellKnownSymbolKind;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ConstantValue;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::*;
use crate::u32_from_usize;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

use super::context::Generator;

/// The abstract operations that are calls of an intrinsic function.
const INTRINSIC_OPERATIONS: &[(&[u16], AbstractOperationKind)] = &[
    (utf16!("ArraySpeciesCreate"), AbstractOperationKind::ArraySpeciesCreate),
    (utf16!("AsyncIteratorClose"), AbstractOperationKind::AsyncIteratorClose),
    (utf16!("GetMethod"), AbstractOperationKind::GetMethod),
    (utf16!("GetIteratorDirect"), AbstractOperationKind::GetIteratorDirect),
    (
        utf16!("GetIteratorFromMethod"),
        AbstractOperationKind::GetIteratorFromMethod,
    ),
    (utf16!("IteratorComplete"), AbstractOperationKind::IteratorComplete),
];

/// The abstract operations that have an instruction of their own.
const INSTRUCTION_OPERATIONS: &[&[u16]] = &[
    utf16!("IsCallable"),
    utf16!("IsConstructor"),
    utf16!("ToBoolean"),
    utf16!("ToObject"),
    utf16!("ToLength"),
    utf16!("ThrowIfNotObject"),
    utf16!("ThrowNotAFunction"),
    utf16!("ArgumentCount"),
    utf16!("ThrowTypeError"),
    utf16!("NewTypeError"),
    utf16!("NewObjectWithNoPrototype"),
    utf16!("NewArrayWithLength"),
    utf16!("CreateAsyncFromSyncIterator"),
    utf16!("CreateDataPropertyOrThrow"),
    utf16!("Call"),
];

impl Generator<'_> {
    /// Whether a call of the global `name` is an abstract operation.
    pub(super) fn is_builtin_operation(&self, name: Name) -> bool {
        let text = self.tree.name_text(name);
        INSTRUCTION_OPERATIONS.iter().any(|&operation| text == operation)
            || INTRINSIC_OPERATIONS.iter().any(|&(operation, _)| text == operation)
    }

    /// The text of the string constant `operand`, which an error of the engine gets as its message.
    fn intern_message(&mut self, operand: Operand) -> StringTableIndex {
        let Some(ConstantValue::String(text)) = self.context.constants.get(operand) else {
            panic!("the message of a builtin error is a string literal");
        };
        let text = text.clone();
        self.intern_string_text(Utf16View::of_string(&text))
    }

    /// The abstract operation `name` with `arguments`, which writes its value to `dst` if it has one.
    pub(super) fn builtin_operation(&mut self, name: Name, arguments: &[Operand], dst: Operand) {
        let text = self.tree.name_text(name);
        let is = |operation: &[u16]| text == operation;
        match arguments {
            [value] if is(utf16!("IsCallable")) => self.put(op::IsCallable { dst, value: *value }),
            [value] if is(utf16!("IsConstructor")) => self.put(op::IsConstructor { dst, value: *value }),
            [value] if is(utf16!("ToBoolean")) => self.put(op::ToBoolean { dst, value: *value }),
            [value] if is(utf16!("ToObject")) => self.put(op::ToObject { dst, value: *value }),
            [value] if is(utf16!("ToLength")) => self.put(op::ToLength { dst, value: *value }),
            [src] if is(utf16!("ThrowIfNotObject")) => self.put(op::ThrowIfNotObject { src: *src }),
            [src] if is(utf16!("ThrowNotAFunction")) => self.put(op::ThrowNotAFunction { src: *src }),
            [] if is(utf16!("ArgumentCount")) => self.put(op::GetArgumentCount { dst }),
            [message] if is(utf16!("ThrowTypeError")) => {
                let error_string = self.intern_message(*message);
                self.put(op::NewTypeError { dst, error_string });
                self.put(op::Throw { src: dst });
            }
            [message] if is(utf16!("NewTypeError")) => {
                let error_string = self.intern_message(*message);
                self.put(op::NewTypeError { dst, error_string });
            }
            [] if is(utf16!("NewObjectWithNoPrototype")) => self.put(op::NewObjectWithNoPrototype { dst }),
            [array_length] if is(utf16!("NewArrayWithLength")) => self.put(op::NewArrayWithLength {
                dst,
                array_length: *array_length,
            }),
            [iterator, next_method, done] if is(utf16!("CreateAsyncFromSyncIterator")) => {
                self.put(op::CreateAsyncFromSyncIterator {
                    dst,
                    iterator: *iterator,
                    next_method: *next_method,
                    done: *done,
                });
            }
            [object, property, value] if is(utf16!("CreateDataPropertyOrThrow")) => {
                self.put(op::CreateDataPropertyOrThrow {
                    object: *object,
                    property: *property,
                    value: *value,
                });
            }
            [callee, this_value, rest @ ..] if is(utf16!("Call")) => {
                self.put_builtin_call(dst, *callee, *this_value, rest);
            }
            _ => {
                let &(_, operation) = INTRINSIC_OPERATIONS
                    .iter()
                    .find(|&&(operation, _)| text == operation)
                    .expect("a builtin operation takes the arguments it is declared with");
                let callee = self.add_constant_abstract_operation(operation);
                let undefined = self.context.constants.add_undefined();
                self.put_builtin_call(dst, callee, undefined, arguments);
            }
        }
    }

    fn put_builtin_call(&mut self, dst: Operand, callee: Operand, this_value: Operand, arguments: &[Operand]) {
        let call_feedback = self.next_call_feedback();
        self.put(op::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst,
            callee,
            this_value,
            argument_count: u32_from_usize(arguments.len()),
            arguments,
        });
    }

    /// The constant that the global `name` stands for in the JavaScript of the engine, if it is one.
    pub(super) fn builtin_constant(&mut self, name: Name) -> Option<Operand> {
        if !self.builtin_abstract_operations_enabled {
            return None;
        }
        let text = self.tree.name_text(name);
        if text == utf16!("SYMBOL_ITERATOR") {
            return Some(self.add_constant_well_known_symbol(WellKnownSymbolKind::SymbolIterator));
        }
        if text == utf16!("SYMBOL_ASYNC_ITERATOR") {
            return Some(self.add_constant_well_known_symbol(WellKnownSymbolKind::SymbolAsyncIterator));
        }
        if text == utf16!("MAX_ARRAY_LIKE_INDEX") {
            return Some(self.add_constant_number(9007199254740991.0));
        }
        None
    }
}

//! The constant pool of an executable. The numbering is part of the output: every value that is not a duplicate takes
//! the next index, and only the kinds that deduplicate here do so.

use crate::bytecode::constant::AbstractOperationKind;
use crate::bytecode::constant::WellKnownSymbolKind;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ConstantValue;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::MAXIMUM_INTERNED_CONSTANT_LENGTH;
use crate::bytecode::operand::Operand;
use crate::u32_from_usize;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;
use ak::Utf16String;

use super::context::MAXIMUM_SPARE_CAPACITY;
use super::names::NameTables;

/// An open-addressed table from a key to a constant index that forgets everything by moving on to a new generation.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct IndexTable {
    slots: Vec<IndexSlot>,
    used_slots: usize,
    generation: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct IndexSlot {
    key: u64,
    index: u32,
    generation: u32,
}

impl IndexTable {
    const INITIAL_SLOT_COUNT: usize = 32;

    pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
        if self.slots.len() > MAXIMUM_SPARE_CAPACITY {
            self.slots = Vec::new();
            self.generation = 0;
        }
        self.used_slots = 0;
        self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);
        if self.generation == 0 {
            self.slots.fill(IndexSlot::default());
            self.generation = 1;
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn first_slot_of(key: u64, slot_count: usize) -> usize {
        (key.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15) >> 40) as usize & (slot_count - 1)
    }

    /// The slots with the key, in the order a lookup visits them, until an empty one: `matches` decides on each index,
    /// and the result is the index it accepted or the slot to insert at.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn find(&mut self, key: u64, matches: impl Fn(u32) -> bool) -> Result<u32, usize> {
        if (self.used_slots + 1) * 4 > self.slots.len() * 3 {
            self.grow();
        }
        let mask = self.slots.len() - 1;
        let mut slot = Self::first_slot_of(key, self.slots.len());
        loop {
            let entry = &self.slots[slot];
            if entry.generation != self.generation {
                return Err(slot);
            }
            if entry.key == key && matches(entry.index) {
                return Ok(entry.index);
            }
            slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn insert_at(&mut self, slot: usize, key: u64, index: u32) {
        self.used_slots += 1;
        self.slots[slot] = IndexSlot {
            key,
            index,
            generation: self.generation,
        };
    }

    #[cold]
    fn grow(&mut self) {
        // NB: Slots that were never used are of generation zero, which no table is.
        self.generation = self.generation.max(1);
        let slot_count = (self.slots.len() * 2).max(Self::INITIAL_SLOT_COUNT);
        let old_slots = std::mem::replace(&mut self.slots, vec![IndexSlot::default(); slot_count]);
        for old_slot in old_slots {
            if old_slot.generation == self.generation {
                let mut slot = Self::first_slot_of(old_slot.key, slot_count);
                while self.slots[slot].generation == self.generation {
                    slot = (slot + 1) & (slot_count - 1);
                }
                self.slots[slot] = old_slot;
            }
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct ConstantTable {
    pub(super) values: Vec<ConstantValue>,
    true_constant: Option<u32>,
    false_constant: Option<u32>,
    null_constant: Option<u32>,
    undefined_constant: Option<u32>,
    empty_constant: Option<u32>,
    numbers: IndexTable,
    strings: IndexTable,
}

/// A hash of the code units of a string, which does not depend on how the string stores them.
#[inline(always)]
pub(super) fn hash_of_units(text: Utf16View<'_>) -> u64 {
    const MULTIPLIER: u64 = 0x517C_C1B7_2722_0A95;
    let mut hash = text.length_in_code_units() as u64;
    match text {
        Utf16View::Ascii(units) | Utf16View::Latin1(units) => {
            for &unit in units {
                hash = (hash.rotate_left(5) ^ u64::from(unit)).wrapping_mul(MULTIPLIER);
            }
        }
        Utf16View::Utf16(units) => {
            for &unit in units {
                hash = (hash.rotate_left(5) ^ u64::from(unit)).wrapping_mul(MULTIPLIER);
            }
        }
    }
    // NB: Zero means that a name has no hash yet.
    hash | 1
}

impl ConstantTable {
    pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.values.clear();
        self.true_constant = None;
        self.false_constant = None;
        self.null_constant = None;
        self.undefined_constant = None;
        self.empty_constant = None;
        self.numbers.clear();
        self.strings.clear();
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn append(&mut self, value: ConstantValue) -> u32 {
        let index = u32_from_usize(self.values.len());
        self.values.push(value);
        index
    }

    /// Deduplicates by bit pattern, which tells -0 from 0, and takes every other number for itself.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_number(&mut self, value: f64) -> Operand {
        let key = value.to_bits();
        match self.numbers.find(key, |_| true) {
            Ok(index) => Operand::constant(index),
            Err(slot) => {
                let index = self.append(ConstantValue::Number(value));
                self.numbers.insert_at(slot, key, index);
                Operand::constant(index)
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_boolean(&mut self, value: bool) -> Operand {
        let slot = if value {
            &mut self.true_constant
        } else {
            &mut self.false_constant
        };
        if let Some(index) = *slot {
            return Operand::constant(index);
        }
        let index = u32_from_usize(self.values.len());
        *slot = Some(index);
        self.values.push(ConstantValue::Boolean(value));
        Operand::constant(index)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_null(&mut self) -> Operand {
        if let Some(index) = self.null_constant {
            return Operand::constant(index);
        }
        let index = self.append(ConstantValue::Null);
        self.null_constant = Some(index);
        Operand::constant(index)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_undefined(&mut self) -> Operand {
        if let Some(index) = self.undefined_constant {
            return Operand::constant(index);
        }
        let index = self.append(ConstantValue::Undefined);
        self.undefined_constant = Some(index);
        Operand::constant(index)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_empty(&mut self) -> Operand {
        if let Some(index) = self.empty_constant {
            return Operand::constant(index);
        }
        let index = self.append(ConstantValue::Empty);
        self.empty_constant = Some(index);
        Operand::constant(index)
    }

    /// A string whose value is `text`, which is only looked at if the table does not have it yet: a text that gets
    /// interned when the code is linked comes from what `names` knows of the script, and any other gets copied.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_string_view(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>, names: &mut NameTables) -> Operand {
        let key = hash_of_units(text);
        let values = &self.values;
        let found = self.strings.find(key, |index| {
            matches!(&values[index as usize], ConstantValue::String(string) if Utf16View::of_string(string) == text)
        });
        match found {
            Ok(index) => Operand::constant(index),
            Err(slot) => {
                let string = if text.length_in_code_units() <= MAXIMUM_INTERNED_CONSTANT_LENGTH {
                    Utf16String::from(names.fly_string_of_text(text, key))
                } else {
                    text.into()
                };
                let index = self.append(ConstantValue::String(string));
                self.strings.insert_at(slot, key, index);
                Operand::constant(index)
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn add_string(&mut self, value: Utf16String) -> Operand {
        let text = Utf16View::of_string(&value);
        let key = hash_of_units(text);
        let values = &self.values;
        let found = self.strings.find(key, |index| {
            matches!(&values[index as usize], ConstantValue::String(string) if Utf16View::of_string(string) == text)
        });
        match found {
            Ok(index) => Operand::constant(index),
            Err(slot) => {
                let index = self.append(ConstantValue::String(value));
                self.strings.insert_at(slot, key, index);
                Operand::constant(index)
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn add_bigint(&mut self, value: String) -> Operand {
        Operand::constant(self.append(ConstantValue::BigInt(Box::new(value.into_boxed_str()))))
    }

    pub(super) fn add_well_known_symbol(&mut self, symbol: WellKnownSymbolKind) -> Operand {
        Operand::constant(self.append(ConstantValue::WellKnownSymbol(symbol)))
    }

    pub(super) fn add_abstract_operation(&mut self, operation: AbstractOperationKind) -> Operand {
        Operand::constant(self.append(ConstantValue::AbstractOperation(operation)))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn get(&self, operand: Operand) -> Option<&ConstantValue> {
        if operand.is_constant() {
            self.values.get(operand.index() as usize)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }
}

//! Constructs whose code does not come in the order of their rows: statements that have to look at their parts before
//! running them, and patterns, which a value goes through after everything in the rows that follow them. These walk their
//! rows by what they are, and let `sweep` go through the pieces of code in them. All of it goes to the same emission core.

use libjs_abi::ClassElementKind;

use crate::ast::BinaryOp;

/// Where the parameters of the function that a tree is of start.
const FIRST_ROW_OF_REPARSED_FUNCTION: usize = 1;

/// The name of a field whose key is not computed, which a computed key gets only when the class is defined.
fn class_field_name(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, field: NodeId) -> Option<ak::Utf16String> {
    if tree.node_tag(field) == tag::COMPUTED_CLASS_FIELD {
        return None;
    }
    let key = NodeId(tree.node_a(field));
    match tree.node_tag(key) {
        tag::PRIVATE_NAME => {
            let mut text = Utf16StringBuilder::new();
            text.append_ascii("#");
            text.append(tree.name_text(Name(tree.node_a(key))));
            Some(text.to_utf16_string())
        }
        tag::IDENT | tag::IDENT_KEY | tag::STR_KEY | tag::NUM_KEY => Some(tree.pattern_key_text(key).view().into()),
        _ => {
            let literal = tree.source_range_units(tree.node_pos(key), tree.node_a(key));
            let digits = ascii_code_units_to_string(crate::ast::bigint_literal_digits(literal))?;
            let value = parse_bigint(&digits).expect("the lexer only produces valid BigInt literals");
            Some(ak::Utf16String::from_utf8(&value.to_string()))
        }
    }
}

/// What the targets of a pattern are.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum PatternMode {
    /// Names that a declaration of this kind declares.
    Declares(DeclarationKind),
    /// References, that get evaluated right before the value they get is.
    Assigns,
}

/// What the head of a `for-in` or `for-of` loop gives each value to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum LoopTarget {
    Declared {
        target: NodeId,
        first_row: usize,
        kind: DeclarationKind,
        /// Whether the value is a resource that gets disposed of, and if so whether that is asynchronous.
        resource: Option<bool>,
    },
    Expression {
        target: NodeId,
        first_row: usize,
    },
    Pattern {
        target: NodeId,
        first_row: usize,
    },
}

impl Generator<'_> {
    /// The rows from `first_row` up to and including `root`, which are of something that a mark at `position` left here.
    pub(super) fn sweep_subtree(
        &mut self,
        root: NodeId,
        first_row: usize,
        position: u32,
        detail: u32,
    ) -> Result<(), OutOfStack> {
        if self.should_stop_generating() {
            return Err(OutOfStack);
        }
        self.current_source_offset = SourceOffset(position);
        let tree = self.tree;
        let mark_row = first_row;
        let first_row = first_row + 1;
        match tree.node_tag(root) {
