            self.bind_pattern_element(item, row, element_value, mode)?;
            self.release_temporaries_from(first_temporary);
            row = item.index() + 1;
        }

        self.pop_control();
        self.set_handler(outer_handler);
        let end_label = self.new_label();
        self.jump_if(done, end_label);
        let undefined = self.context.constants.add_undefined();
        let cache = self.next_property_lookup_cache();
        self.put(op::IteratorClose {
            iterator_object: object,
            iterator_next: next,
            iterator_done: done,
            completion_type: libjs_abi::CompletionType::Normal as u8,
            completion_value: undefined,
            cache,
        });
        self.jump(end_label);
        self.bind_reachable_label(close_handler.label);
        self.close_iterator_after_exception(iterator, entry_environment);
        self.bind_label(end_label);
        self.release_held_registers(held);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The literal that an initializer of a field consists of, if it does.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct LiteralInitializer {
    pub(super) kind: Option<PendingLiteralValueKind>,
    pub(super) number: f64,
    pub(super) string: Option<ak::Utf16String>,
}

pub(super) fn literal_initializer(generator: &Generator<'_>, initializer: NodeId) -> LiteralInitializer {
    let tree = generator.tree;
    let of_kind = |kind| LiteralInitializer {
        kind: Some(kind),
        ..LiteralInitializer::default()
    };
    match tree.node_tag(initializer) {
        tag::NUM => LiteralInitializer {
            kind: Some(PendingLiteralValueKind::Number),
            number: tree.number_value(initializer),
            string: None,
        },
        tag::TRUE => of_kind(PendingLiteralValueKind::BooleanTrue),
        tag::FALSE => of_kind(PendingLiteralValueKind::BooleanFalse),
        tag::NULL => of_kind(PendingLiteralValueKind::Null),
        tag::STR => LiteralInitializer {
            kind: Some(PendingLiteralValueKind::String),
            number: 0.0,
            string: Some(tree.string_literal_value(initializer)),
        },
        tag::UNARY if tree.unary_operator(initializer) == UnaryOp::Minus => {
            let operand = tree.expression_a(initializer);
            if tree.node_tag(operand) == tag::NUM {
                LiteralInitializer {
                    kind: Some(PendingLiteralValueKind::Number),
                    number: -tree.number_value(operand),
                    string: None,
                }
            } else {
                LiteralInitializer::default()
            }
        }
        _ => LiteralInitializer::default(),
    }
}

/// Whether a parameter has anything that gets evaluated in it.
fn parameter_has_expression(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, parameter: NodeId) -> bool {
    let target = match tree.node_tag(parameter) {
        tag::ASSIGN_PATTERN => return true,
        tag::REST => NodeId(tree.node_a(parameter)),
        _ => parameter,
    };
    matches!(tree.node_tag(target), tag::ARRAY_PATTERN | tag::OBJECT_PATTERN)
        && tree.pattern_contains_expression(target.0)
}

/// Calls `callback` with each of the BoundNames of `target`, an identifier or a binding pattern, in the order of the
/// source.
fn for_each_bound_name(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, target: NodeId, callback: &mut impl FnMut(Name)) {
    match tree.node_tag(target) {
        tag::ARRAY_PATTERN | tag::OBJECT_PATTERN => {
            for item in tree.node_list(tree.node_a(target)).iter() {
                match tree.node_tag(item) {
                    tag::HOLE => {}
                    tag::PROPERTY | tag::COMPUTED_PROPERTY => {
                        for_each_bound_name(tree, NodeId(tree.node_b(item)), callback);
                    }
                    tag::SHORTHAND => callback(Name(tree.node_a(item))),
                    _ => for_each_bound_name(tree, item, callback),
                }
            }
        }
        tag::REST | tag::ASSIGN_PATTERN => for_each_bound_name(tree, NodeId(tree.node_a(target)), callback),
        _ => callback(Name(tree.node_a(target))),
    }
}

/// What a function has for parameters.
#[inline(always)]
fn parameters_of<'a>(tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>, function: NodeId) -> NodeList<'a> {
    tree.node_list(tree.extra_at(tree.node_a(function)))
}

//! The state of a compile. [`CodegenContext`] holds everything with memory of its own, which every compile of a thread
//! reuses, and [`Generator`] the rest of what one compile needs.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;
use ak::Utf16String;

use crate::ast::FunctionKind;
use crate::ast::Name;
use crate::ast::SyntaxTree;
use crate::bytecode::constant::AbstractOperationKind;
use crate::bytecode::constant::WellKnownSymbolKind;
use crate::bytecode::constant_fold::ConstantPool;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ConstantValue;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ExecutableCacheCounts;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::PendingClassBlueprint;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::Instruction;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::OpCode;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::*;
use crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceOffset;
use crate::parser::EnclosingCode;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

use super::constants::ConstantTable;
use super::environment::BindingLocation;
use super::environment::EnclosingEnvironmentScope;
use super::environment::EnvironmentCoordinateScope;
use super::names::NameClass;
use super::names::NameTables;

/// The most entries that a table keeps its memory for when the next compile takes over.
pub(super) const MAXIMUM_SPARE_CAPACITY: usize = 1024;

const MAXIMUM_SPARE_BYTECODE_SIZE: usize = 64 * 1024;

/// Feedback slot indices are encoded as u16. Sites beyond the last index share
/// it, which only merges their feedback.
const MAX_FEEDBACK_SLOT_COUNT: u32 = u16::MAX as u32 + 1;

const ENVIRONMENT_MODE_LEXICAL: u8 = libjs_abi::EnvironmentMode::Lexical as u8;

/// Everything of a compile that has memory of its own, which stays around for the next compile on the thread. It resets
/// by clearing and by moving on to a new generation, never by allocating anew.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CodegenContext {
    pub(super) stream: super::stream::Stream,
    pub(super) scope: super::scope::CodeScope,
    pub(super) constants: ConstantTable,
    pub(super) names: NameTables,

    pub(super) lexical_environment_register_stack: Vec<Operand>,
    pub(super) environment_coordinate_scope_stack: Vec<EnvironmentCoordinateScope>,
    pub(super) initialized_locals: Vec<bool>,
    pub(super) initialized_arguments: Vec<bool>,
    pub(super) annexb_function_names: Vec<Name>,

    /// The memo of what `binding_location_for_identifier()` found, by identifier, while `environment_generation` stays.
    pub(super) binding_locations: Vec<(u32, Option<BindingLocation>)>,
    /// What moves on whenever an environment or a binding of one comes or goes.
    pub(super) environment_generation: u32,
    /// The values of the NewPrimitiveArray being put together.
    pub(super) primitive_values: Vec<u64>,
}

impl CodegenContext {
    /// Drops what the last compile left, so that the next one starts from nothing.
    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.lexical_environment_register_stack.clear();
        self.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.clear();
        self.initialized_locals.clear();
        self.initialized_arguments.clear();
        self.annexb_function_names.clear();
        self.environment_generation = self.environment_generation.wrapping_add(1);
        self.stream.clear();
        self.scope.clear();
        self.constants.clear();
        self.names.clear();
    }
}

thread_local! {
    /// The context of this thread. A compile nested in another one finds nothing here and starts from nothing.
    static SPARE_CONTEXT: Cell<Option<Box<CodegenContext>>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

/// The state of generating code for one function.
pub struct Generator<'t> {
    pub(super) tree: &'t SyntaxTree<'t>,
    pub(super) context: ManuallyDrop<Box<CodegenContext>>,

    pub(super) current_source_offset: SourceOffset,
    pub(super) strict: bool,
    /// Whether the code can change the running lexical environment. Without that, nothing saves or restores it.
    pub(super) creates_environment: bool,
    pub(super) stack_limit: usize,

    pub(super) this_value_needs_resolution: bool,
    pub(super) enclosing_function_kind: FunctionKind,
    pub(super) builtin_abstract_operations_enabled: bool,
    pub(super) eager_compile_direct_iifes: bool,
    pub(super) contains_direct_call_to_eval_in_non_strict_mode: bool,
    /// Whether the code makes private or variable environments, so that it starts with `EnterWithOwnEnvironments`.
    pub(super) keeps_own_environments: bool,
    /// Whether the code is a sloppy function that uses its this value, which its callers pass as it is, so that it
    /// starts with `EnterCoercingThis`.
    pub(super) coerces_this: bool,
    pub(super) enclosing_environment_scope: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
    pub(super) variable_environment_coordinate_scope_index: Option<usize>,
    pub(super) enclosing_code: Arc<EnclosingCode>,

    pub(super) class_blueprints: Vec<PendingClassBlueprint>,
    pub(super) length_identifier: Option<PropertyKeyTableIndex>,

    pub(super) next_property_lookup_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_global_variable_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_environment_coordinate_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_template_object_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_object_shape_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_object_property_iterator_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_environment_shape_cache: u32,
    pub(super) next_arith_feedback: u32,
    pub(super) next_value_feedback: u32,
    pub(super) next_call_feedback: u32,
    pub(super) next_keyed_feedback: u32,
}

macro_rules! next_cache_method {
    ($method:ident, $field:ident) => {
        #[inline(always)]
        pub(super) fn $method(&mut self) -> u32 {
            let index = self.$field;
            self.$field += 1;
            index
        }
    };
}

macro_rules! next_shared_cache_method {
    ($method:ident, $field:ident) => {
        #[inline(always)]
        pub(super) fn $method(&mut self) -> u32 {
            let index = self.$field.min(UNCACHED_SITE);
            self.$field = index + 1;
            index
        }
    };
}

macro_rules! next_feedback_slot_method {
    ($method:ident, $field:ident) => {
        #[inline(always)]
        pub(super) fn $method(&mut self) -> u16 {
            let index = u16::try_from(self.$field).unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
            self.$field = (self.$field + 1).min(MAX_FEEDBACK_SLOT_COUNT);
            index
        }
    };
}

impl Drop for Generator<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This is the last that anything sees of the context.
        let mut context = unsafe { ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.context) };
        // NB: Free an outsized context rather than keep its memory for good.
        if context.stream.bytecode_capacity() > MAXIMUM_SPARE_BYTECODE_SIZE {
            return;
        }
        context.clear();
        SPARE_CONTEXT.set(Some(context));
    }
}

impl<'t> Generator<'t> {
    pub(super) fn new(tree: &'t SyntaxTree<'t>, enclosing_code: Arc<EnclosingCode>, stack_limit: usize) -> Self {
        let mut context = SPARE_CONTEXT.take().unwrap_or_default();
        context.names.begin_compile(&tree.script);
        Self {
            tree,
            context: ManuallyDrop::new(context),
            current_source_offset: SourceOffset::NONE,
            strict: false,
            creates_environment: true,
            stack_limit,
            this_value_needs_resolution: true,
            enclosing_function_kind: FunctionKind::Normal,
            builtin_abstract_operations_enabled: false,
            eager_compile_direct_iifes: false,
            contains_direct_call_to_eval_in_non_strict_mode: false,
            keeps_own_environments: false,
            coerces_this: false,
            enclosing_environment_scope: None,
            variable_environment_coordinate_scope_index: None,
            enclosing_code,
            class_blueprints: Vec::new(),
            length_identifier: None,
            next_property_lookup_cache: 0,
            next_global_variable_cache: 0,
            next_environment_coordinate_cache: 0,
            next_template_object_cache: 0,
            next_object_shape_cache: 0,
            next_object_property_iterator_cache: 0,
            next_environment_shape_cache: 0,
            next_arith_feedback: 0,
            next_value_feedback: 0,
            next_call_feedback: 0,
            next_keyed_feedback: 0,
        }
    }

    // --- Function kind queries ---

    pub(super) fn is_in_generator_function(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.enclosing_function_kind,
            FunctionKind::Generator | FunctionKind::AsyncGenerator
        )
    }

    pub(super) fn is_in_async_generator_function(&self) -> bool {
        self.enclosing_function_kind == FunctionKind::AsyncGenerator
    }

    pub(super) fn is_in_generator_or_async_function(&self) -> bool {
        self.enclosing_function_kind != FunctionKind::Normal
    }

    // --- Constant pool ---

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_number(&mut self, value: f64) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_number(value)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_i32(&mut self, value: i32) -> Operand {
        self.add_constant_number(f64::from(value))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_boolean(&mut self, value: bool) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_boolean(value)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_null(&mut self) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_null()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_undefined(&mut self) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_undefined()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_string(&mut self, value: Utf16String) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_string(value)
    }

    /// A constant of the string `text`.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn add_constant_string_view(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> Operand {
        let context = &mut *self.context;
        context.constants.add_string_view(text, &mut context.names)
    }

    pub(super) fn add_constant_bigint(&mut self, value: String) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_bigint(value)
    }

    pub(super) fn add_constant_well_known_symbol(&mut self, symbol: WellKnownSymbolKind) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_well_known_symbol(symbol)
    }

    pub(super) fn add_constant_abstract_operation(&mut self, operation: AbstractOperationKind) -> Operand {
        self.context.constants.add_abstract_operation(operation)
    }

    /// Get the constant value for a constant operand.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn get_constant(&self, operand: Operand) -> Option<&ConstantValue> {
        self.context.constants.get(operand)
    }

    // --- Table interning ---

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn intern_identifier(&mut self, name: Name) -> IdentifierTableIndex {
        self.context.names.intern_identifier(self.tree, name)
    }

    pub(super) fn intern_identifier_text(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> IdentifierTableIndex {
        self.context.names.intern_identifier_text(self.tree, text)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn intern_property_key(&mut self, name: Name) -> PropertyKeyTableIndex {
        self.context.names.intern_property_key(self.tree, name)
    }

    pub(super) fn intern_property_key_text(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> PropertyKeyTableIndex {
        self.context.names.intern_property_key_text(self.tree, text)
    }

    pub(super) fn intern_string_text(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> StringTableIndex {
        self.context.names.intern_string_text(self.tree, text)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn name_class(&mut self, name: Name) -> NameClass {
        self.context.names.class_of(self.tree, name)
    }

    /// Whether generating code for something any deeper in the tree makes no sense: the code may overflow the stack, or
    /// is a lost cause already.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn should_stop_generating(&mut self) -> bool {
        let marker = 0u8;
        (&raw const marker as usize) < self.stack_limit
    }

    /// If `operand` is a constant string that is not an array index, intern it as a property key and return the index.
    pub(super) fn try_constant_string_to_property_key(&mut self, operand: Operand) -> Option<PropertyKeyTableIndex> {
        let context = &mut *self.context;
        let ConstantValue::String(string) = context.constants.get(operand)? else {
            return None;
        };
        if crate::bytecode::constant_fold::is_array_index(&string.to_utf16()) {
            return None;
        }
        Some(
            context
                .names
                .intern_property_key_text(self.tree, Utf16View::of_string(string)),
        )
    }

    // --- Instruction emission ---

    /// Keep coordinate scopes in lockstep with the actual declarative environment shape. Most bindings are created
    /// explicitly, while CreateArguments can implicitly create an `arguments` binding.
    #[cold]
    pub(super) fn note_environment_change(&mut self, instruction: &Instruction) {
        match instruction {
            Instruction::CreateVariable {
                identifier,
                mode,
                is_global,
                ..
            } => {
                if !is_global {
                    let name = self.context.names.identifier_fly_string(self.tree, *identifier);
                    if *mode == ENVIRONMENT_MODE_LEXICAL {
                        self.record_environment_binding(name);
                    } else {
                        self.record_variable_environment_binding(name);
                    }
                }
            }
            Instruction::CreateMutableBinding { identifier, .. }
            | Instruction::CreateImmutableBinding { identifier, .. } => {
                let name = self.context.names.identifier_fly_string(self.tree, *identifier);
                self.record_environment_binding(name);
            }
            Instruction::CreateArguments { dst: None, .. } => {
                self.record_environment_binding(Utf16FlyString::from_utf8("arguments"));
            }
            Instruction::CreateArguments { .. } | Instruction::GetLexicalEnvironment { .. } => {}
            _ => assert!(
                self.creates_environment,
                "scope analysis missed an environment of this code"
            ),
        }
    }

    /// Emit a Mov instruction (optimized away if src == dst).
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn emit_mov(&mut self, dst: Operand, src: Operand) {
        if dst != src {
            self.put(op::Mov { dst, src });
        }
    }

    /// Emit a conditional jump, with comparison fusion and constant folding.
    pub(super) fn emit_jump_if(&mut self, condition: Operand, true_target: Label, false_target: Label) {
        self.put(op::JumpIf {
            condition,
            true_target,
            false_target,
        });
    }

    // --- Cache index allocation ---

    next_shared_cache_method!(next_property_lookup_cache, next_property_lookup_cache);
    next_shared_cache_method!(next_global_variable_cache, next_global_variable_cache);
    next_shared_cache_method!(next_environment_coordinate_cache, next_environment_coordinate_cache);
    next_cache_method!(next_template_object_cache, next_template_object_cache);
    next_shared_cache_method!(next_object_shape_cache, next_object_shape_cache);
    next_cache_method!(next_object_property_iterator_cache, next_object_property_iterator_cache);
    next_cache_method!(next_environment_shape_cache, next_environment_shape_cache);
    next_feedback_slot_method!(next_arith_feedback, next_arith_feedback);
    next_feedback_slot_method!(next_value_feedback, next_value_feedback);
    next_feedback_slot_method!(next_call_feedback, next_call_feedback);
    next_feedback_slot_method!(next_keyed_feedback, next_keyed_feedback);

    // --- Local variable initialization tracking ---

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_local_initialized(&self, index: u32) -> bool {
        self.context
            .initialized_locals
            .get(index as usize)
            .copied()
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Whether a local starts out uninitialized. Besides what a declaration binds lexically, that goes for the names of a
    /// binding pattern of a parameter or a catch clause: initializers in the pattern can read them before they are bound.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn local_has_temporal_dead_zone(&self, index: u32) -> bool {
        self.context.scope.is_local_lexical(index)
    }

    pub(super) fn mark_local_initialized(&mut self, index: u32) {
        let index = index as usize;
        if index >= self.context.initialized_locals.len() {
            self.context.initialized_locals.resize(index + 1, false);
        }
        self.context.initialized_locals[index] = true;
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_argument_initialized(&self, index: u32) -> bool {
        self.context
            .initialized_arguments
            .get(index as usize)
            .copied()
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    pub(super) fn mark_argument_initialized(&mut self, index: u32) {
        let index = index as usize;
        if index >= self.context.initialized_arguments.len() {
            self.context.initialized_arguments.resize(index + 1, false);
        }
        self.context.initialized_arguments[index] = true;
    }

    pub(super) fn cache_counts(&self) -> ExecutableCacheCounts {
        ExecutableCacheCounts {
            property_lookup: self.next_property_lookup_cache,
            global_variable: self.next_global_variable_cache,
            environment_coordinate: self.next_environment_coordinate_cache,
            template_object: self.next_template_object_cache,
            object_shape: self.next_object_shape_cache,
            object_property_iterator: self.next_object_property_iterator_cache,
            environment_shape: self.next_environment_shape_cache,
            arith_feedback: self.next_arith_feedback,
            value_feedback: self.next_value_feedback,
            call_feedback: self.next_call_feedback,
            keyed_feedback: self.next_keyed_feedback,
        }
    }
}

impl ConstantPool for Generator<'_> {
    fn get_constant(&self, operand: Operand) -> Option<&ConstantValue> {
        Generator::get_constant(self, operand)
    }

    fn add_constant_number(&mut self, value: f64) -> Operand {
        Generator::add_constant_number(self, value)
    }

    fn add_constant_boolean(&mut self, value: bool) -> Operand {
        Generator::add_constant_boolean(self, value)
    }

    fn add_constant_string(&mut self, value: Utf16String) -> Operand {
        Generator::add_constant_string(self, value)
    }

    fn add_constant_bigint(&mut self, value: String) -> Operand {
        Generator::add_constant_bigint(self, value)
    }
}

/// Whether an instruction changes which environments there are, or which bindings they have.
#[inline(always)]
pub(super) const fn changes_environment_state(opcode: OpCode) -> bool {
    matches!(
        opcode,
        OpCode::CreateVariable
            | OpCode::CreateMutableBinding
            | OpCode::CreateImmutableBinding
            | OpCode::CreateArguments
            | OpCode::CreateLexicalEnvironment
            | OpCode::CreateVariableEnvironment
            | OpCode::EnterObjectEnvironment
            | OpCode::SetLexicalEnvironment
            | OpCode::GetLexicalEnvironment
    )
}

//! What the emission core writes instructions with, and what it leaves when it is done.

use crate::bytecode::executable_data::{ExceptionHandler, StrictRange};
use crate::bytecode::operand::Operand;
use crate::bytecode::operand::OperandType;
use crate::layout::buffer::BlockSlice;
use crate::u32_from_usize;

/// The result of assembling bytecode.
pub struct AssembledBytecode {
    pub bytecode: BlockSlice<u8>,
    pub strict_ranges: Box<[StrictRange]>,
    pub source_map: BlockSlice<u8>,
    pub exception_handlers: Box<[ExceptionHandler]>,
    pub number_of_registers: u32,
    /// One past the highest `Operand::argument` index referenced by any
    /// instruction, or 0 if the bytecode never reads an argument.
    pub number_of_arguments: u32,
}

/// A place in the bytes of a block.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub(super) struct BlockPosition {
    pub(super) block: u32,
    pub(super) offset: u32,
}

/// The first frame slot that an operand cannot name, which is what an operand that is left out holds.
pub(crate) const FIRST_WIDE_SLOT: u32 = 255;

/// Where an operand that is not a low register sits in a block, and what kind of operand it is.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct OperandPosition {
    pub(super) offset: u32,
    pub(super) operand_type: OperandType,
    /// The index among the operands of that type, which only a full operand can hold before the frame is laid out.
    pub(super) index: u32,
}

/// What the generated encoder writes an instruction with: the bytes of its block, and the notes for `finish()`.
pub struct BlockEncoder<'a> {
    pub bytes: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
    block: u32,
    operand_positions: &'a mut Vec<OperandPosition>,
    label_positions: &'a mut Vec<BlockPosition>,
    /// One past the highest argument that an instruction refers to so far.
    number_of_arguments: &'a mut u32,
    /// The register to note the position of the first time it comes up.
    watched: Operand,
    pub(super) watched_position: u32,
}

impl<'a> BlockEncoder<'a> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn for_stream(
        bytes: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
        operand_positions: &'a mut Vec<OperandPosition>,
        label_positions: &'a mut Vec<BlockPosition>,
        number_of_arguments: &'a mut u32,
        watched: Operand,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            block: 0,
            operand_positions,
            label_positions,
            number_of_arguments,
            watched,
            watched_position: u32::MAX,
        }
    }
}

impl BlockEncoder<'_> {
    /// An operand of the instruction about to be written, `offset` bytes into it. Only registers have their place in
    /// the frame at this point: the others come after the registers, whose number is not known yet.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn operand(&mut self, operand: Operand, offset: usize) -> u32 {
        match operand.operand_type() {
            OperandType::Register => {
                if operand == self.watched {
                    self.watched = Operand::invalid();
                    self.watched_position = u32_from_usize(self.bytes.len() + offset);
                }
                if operand.index() >= FIRST_WIDE_SLOT {
                    self.note_operand(offset, operand);
                }
            }
            OperandType::Argument => {
                *self.number_of_arguments = (*self.number_of_arguments).max(operand.index() + 1);
                self.note_operand(offset, operand);
            }
            OperandType::Local | OperandType::Constant => self.note_operand(offset, operand),
        }
        operand.raw()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn note_operand(&mut self, offset: usize, operand: Operand) {
        self.operand_positions.push(OperandPosition {
            offset: u32_from_usize(self.bytes.len() + offset),
            operand_type: operand.operand_type(),
            index: operand.index(),
        });
    }

    /// Notes that the instruction about to be written has a label `offset` bytes in.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn note_label(&mut self, offset: usize) {
        self.label_positions.push(BlockPosition {
            block: self.block,
            offset: u32_from_usize(self.bytes.len() + offset),
        });
    }
}

/// Where the parts of a frame start: `[registers | locals | constants | arguments]`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct FrameLayout {
    pub(super) register_count: u32,
    pub(super) local_count: u32,
    pub(super) constant_count: u32,
}

impl FrameLayout {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn start_of(self, operand_type: OperandType) -> u32 {
        match operand_type {
            OperandType::Register => 0,
            OperandType::Local => self.register_count,
            OperandType::Constant => self.register_count + self.local_count,
            OperandType::Argument => self.register_count + self.local_count + self.constant_count,
        }
    }
}

//! Which environments the running code has, and what is known of the bindings in them.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::OnceLock;
use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;

use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::*;
use crate::fast_hash::HashMap;
use crate::u32_from_usize;

use super::context::Generator;

/// What a function closes over of an environment, as of the moment that the function came up.
pub struct EnclosingEnvironmentScope {
    /// All bindings that the environment ends up with, for all that close over it, whenever that is.
    bindings: Arc<OnceLock<HashMap<ak::Utf16FlyString, u32>>>,
    /// The bindings of lower indices are the ones that existed at that moment.
    binding_count: u32,
    imports: HashMap<ak::Utf16FlyString, u32>,
    kind: EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind,
    stops_unresolved_lookups: AtomicBool,
    parent: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
}

impl EnclosingEnvironmentScope {
    pub fn for_module_environment(
        binding_names: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
        import_names: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
    ) -> Arc<Self> {
        fn index_names(names: Vec<ak::Utf16FlyString>) -> HashMap<ak::Utf16FlyString, u32> {
            let mut indices = HashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(names.len(), Default::default());
            for name in names {
                let index = u32_from_usize(indices.len());
                let previous_index = indices.insert(name, index);
                debug_assert!(previous_index.is_none());
            }
            indices
        }
        let bindings = index_names(binding_names);
        Arc::new(Self {
            binding_count: u32_from_usize(bindings.len()),
            bindings: Arc::new(OnceLock::from(bindings)),
            imports: index_names(import_names),
            kind: EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind::Static,
            stops_unresolved_lookups: AtomicBool::new(false),
            parent: None,
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum BindingLocation {
    Environment(EnvironmentCoordinate),
    Import(u32),
}

/// Where instructions find a binding at `location`: by name, unless they can hold its coordinate.
pub(super) fn location_for_instructions(location: Option<BindingLocation>) -> Option<BindingLocation> {
    match location {
        Some(BindingLocation::Environment(coordinate)) if !coordinate.fits_in_instruction() => None,
        location => location,
    }
}

pub(super) enum ScopeLookup {
    Found(u32),
    NotFound,
    Unresolvable,
}

pub(super) fn look_up_in_scope(
    name: &ak::Utf16FlyString,
    bindings: &HashMap<ak::Utf16FlyString, u32>,
    binding_count: u32,
    kind: EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind,
    stops_unresolved_lookups: bool,
) -> ScopeLookup {
    // Coordinates are only safe through fully-known declarative scopes. If
    // any dynamic scope is crossed, preserve the runtime lookup semantics.
    if kind == EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind::Dynamic {
        return ScopeLookup::Unresolvable;
    }
    if let Some(&index) = bindings.get(name)
        && index < binding_count
    {
        return ScopeLookup::Found(index);
    }
    if stops_unresolved_lookups {
        return ScopeLookup::Unresolvable;
    }
    ScopeLookup::NotFound
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub(super) enum EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind {
    // A declarative environment whose bindings are created by bytecode we emit,
    // or by module linking in an order we mirror. The binding indexes are
    // therefore known while generating the instruction stream and can be
    // embedded in EnvironmentCoordinate operands.
    Static,
    // An object environment, such as `with`, can intercept any name. Once one
    // is between the current point and a binding, resolution must stay dynamic.
    Dynamic,
}

pub(super) struct EnvironmentCoordinateScope {
    bindings: HashMap<Utf16FlyString, u32>,
    next_binding_index: u32,
    kind: EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind,
    stops_unresolved_lookups: bool,
    captured_scope: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
    /// Where the bindings go once they are all known, if anything closes over the scope.
    final_bindings: Option<Arc<OnceLock<HashMap<Utf16FlyString, u32>>>>,
}

impl Drop for EnvironmentCoordinateScope {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(final_bindings) = &self.final_bindings {
            final_bindings
                .set(std::mem::take(&mut self.bindings))
                .expect("a scope ends once");
        }
    }
}

impl Generator<'_> {
    pub(super) fn current_lexical_environment(&mut self) -> Operand {
        self.context
            .lexical_environment_register_stack
            .last()
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Operand::register(Register::SAVED_LEXICAL_ENVIRONMENT))
    }

    pub(super) fn capture_saved_lexical_environment_with_coordinates(&mut self, has_function_environment: bool) {
        let env_reg = Operand::register(Register::SAVED_LEXICAL_ENVIRONMENT);
        if self.creates_environment {
            self.put(op::GetLexicalEnvironment { dst: env_reg });
        }
        if !has_function_environment {
            self.push_untracked_lexical_environment(env_reg);
            return;
        }
        self.push_static_variable_environment(env_reg);
    }

    /// Makes `environment` the running one again, on the way out of an environment or at the start of a handler, where
    /// exception unwinding left the running environment as it was. Code that never changes it has nothing to restore.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn restore_lexical_environment(&mut self, environment: Operand) {
        if self.creates_environment {
            self.put(op::SetLexicalEnvironment { environment });
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn push_new_lexical_environment(&mut self, capacity: u32) -> Operand {
        self.push_new_lexical_environment_impl(capacity, false)
    }

    fn push_new_lexical_environment_impl(&mut self, capacity: u32, is_catch_environment: bool) -> Operand {
        let parent = self.current_lexical_environment();
        let new_env = self.held_register();
        let shape_cache = self.next_environment_shape_cache();
        self.put(op::CreateLexicalEnvironment {
            dst: new_env,
            parent,
            capacity,
            shape_cache,
            is_catch_environment,
        });
        self.push_static_lexical_environment(new_env);
        new_env
    }

    pub(super) fn push_untracked_lexical_environment(&mut self, environment: Operand) {
        self.context.lexical_environment_register_stack.push(environment);
    }

    pub(super) fn push_static_lexical_environment(&mut self, environment: Operand) {
        self.push_untracked_lexical_environment(environment);
        self.push_environment_coordinate_scope(EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind::Static);
    }

    pub(super) fn push_dynamic_lexical_environment(&mut self, environment: Operand) {
        self.push_untracked_lexical_environment(environment);
        self.push_environment_coordinate_scope(EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind::Dynamic);
    }

    pub(super) fn push_static_variable_environment(&mut self, environment: Operand) {
        self.push_static_lexical_environment(environment);
        let scope_index = self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.len() - 1;
        self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack[scope_index].stops_unresolved_lookups =
            self.contains_direct_call_to_eval_in_non_strict_mode;
        self.variable_environment_coordinate_scope_index = Some(scope_index);
    }

    pub(super) fn pop_untracked_lexical_environment(&mut self) -> Option<Operand> {
        self.context.lexical_environment_register_stack.pop()
    }

    pub(super) fn pop_tracked_lexical_environment(&mut self) -> Option<Operand> {
        self.pop_environment_coordinate_scope();
        self.pop_untracked_lexical_environment()
    }

    fn push_environment_coordinate_scope(&mut self, kind: EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind) {
        self.context.environment_generation = self.context.environment_generation.wrapping_add(1);
        self.context
            .environment_coordinate_scope_stack
            .push(EnvironmentCoordinateScope {
                bindings: HashMap::default(),
                next_binding_index: 0,
                kind,
                stops_unresolved_lookups: false,
                captured_scope: None,
                final_bindings: None,
            });
    }

    pub(super) fn capture_environment_coordinate_scopes(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>> {
        let mut parent = self.enclosing_environment_scope.clone();
        let mut parent_was_captured_again = false;
        for scope in &mut self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack {
            if parent_was_captured_again || scope.captured_scope.is_none() {
                scope.captured_scope = Some(Arc::new(EnclosingEnvironmentScope {
                    bindings: scope.final_bindings.get_or_insert_default().clone(),
                    binding_count: scope.next_binding_index,
                    imports: HashMap::default(),
                    kind: scope.kind,
                    stops_unresolved_lookups: AtomicBool::new(scope.stops_unresolved_lookups),
                    parent,
                }));
                parent_was_captured_again = true;
            }
            parent = scope.captured_scope.clone();
        }
        parent
    }

    /// Nothing gets declared in the scopes around the end of the code, and what closes over them can have their bindings.
    pub(super) fn end_environment_coordinate_scopes(&mut self) {
        self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.clear();
    }

    fn pop_environment_coordinate_scope(&mut self) {
        self.context.environment_generation = self.context.environment_generation.wrapping_add(1);
        self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.pop();
    }

    /// Records a binding of the innermost environment that an instruction other than CreateVariable creates.
    pub(super) fn record_environment_binding_created_elsewhere(&mut self, identifier: IdentifierTableIndex) {
        let name = self.context.names.identifier_fly_string(self.tree, identifier);
        self.record_environment_binding(name);
    }

    pub(super) fn record_environment_binding(&mut self, name: Utf16FlyString) {
        let Some(scope_index) = self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.len().checked_sub(1) else {
            return;
        };
        self.record_environment_binding_at_scope_index(name, scope_index);
    }

    pub(super) fn record_variable_environment_binding(&mut self, name: Utf16FlyString) {
        let Some(scope_index) = self.variable_environment_coordinate_scope_index else {
            return;
        };
        self.record_environment_binding_at_scope_index(name, scope_index);
    }

    fn record_environment_binding_at_scope_index(&mut self, name: Utf16FlyString, scope_index: usize) {
        self.context.environment_generation = self.context.environment_generation.wrapping_add(1);
        let Some(scope) = self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.get_mut(scope_index) else {
            return;
        };
        if scope.kind == EnvironmentCoordinateScopeKind::Dynamic {
            return;
        }
        debug_assert!(!scope.bindings.contains_key(&name));
        scope.bindings.insert(name, scope.next_binding_index);
        scope.next_binding_index += 1;
        if let Some(captured_scope) = scope.captured_scope.take() {
            captured_scope.stops_unresolved_lookups.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }

    fn environment_coordinate_for_from_scope_index(
        &self,
        name: &Utf16FlyString,
        scope_index: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Option<EnvironmentCoordinate> {
        match location_for_instructions(self.binding_location_for_from_scope_index(name, scope_index))? {
            BindingLocation::Environment(coordinate) => Some(coordinate),
            BindingLocation::Import(_) => None,
        }
    }

    fn binding_location_for_from_scope_index(
        &self,
        name: &Utf16FlyString,
        scope_index: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Option<BindingLocation> {
        let local_scopes = match scope_index {
            Some(scope_index) => &self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack[..=scope_index],
            None => &[],
        };
        let mut hops = 0;
        for scope in local_scopes.iter().rev() {
            match look_up_in_scope(
                name,
                &scope.bindings,
                scope.next_binding_index,
                scope.kind,
                scope.stops_unresolved_lookups,
            ) {
                ScopeLookup::Found(index) => {
                    return Some(BindingLocation::Environment(EnvironmentCoordinate { hops, index }));
                }
                ScopeLookup::NotFound => hops += 1,
                ScopeLookup::Unresolvable => return None,
            }
        }
        let mut enclosing_scope = self.enclosing_environment_scope.as_deref();
        while let Some(scope) = enclosing_scope {
            let stops_unresolved_lookups = scope.stops_unresolved_lookups.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
            let bindings = scope
                .bindings
                .get()
                .expect("the code around a function ended before it");
            match look_up_in_scope(
                name,
                bindings,
                scope.binding_count,
                scope.kind,
                stops_unresolved_lookups,
            ) {
                ScopeLookup::Found(index) => {
                    return Some(BindingLocation::Environment(EnvironmentCoordinate { hops, index }));
                }
                ScopeLookup::NotFound => hops += 1,
                ScopeLookup::Unresolvable => return None,
            }
            if let Some(import_index) = scope.imports.get(name) {
                return Some(BindingLocation::Import(*import_index));
            }
            enclosing_scope = scope.parent.as_deref();
        }
        None
    }

    pub(super) fn environment_coordinate_for_identifier(
        &mut self,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    ) -> Option<EnvironmentCoordinate> {
        match location_for_instructions(self.binding_location_for_identifier(identifier))? {
            BindingLocation::Environment(coordinate) => Some(coordinate),
            BindingLocation::Import(_) => None,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn binding_location_for_identifier(
        &mut self,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    ) -> Option<BindingLocation> {
        let generation = self.context.environment_generation;
        if let Some((memo_generation, location)) = self.context.binding_locations.get(identifier.0 as usize)
            && *memo_generation == generation
        {
            return *location;
        }
        self.look_up_binding_location(identifier)
    }

    fn look_up_binding_location(&mut self, identifier: IdentifierTableIndex) -> Option<BindingLocation> {
        let name = &self.context.names.identifier_fly_string(self.tree, identifier);
        let location = self.binding_location_for_from_scope_index(
            name,
            self.context.environment_coordinate_scope_stack.len().checked_sub(1),
        );
        let index = identifier.0 as usize;
        let generation = self.context.environment_generation;
        let memo = &mut self.context.binding_locations;
        if index >= memo.len() {
            memo.resize(index + 1, (generation.wrapping_sub(1), None));
        }
        memo[index] = (generation, location);
        location
    }

    pub(super) fn variable_environment_coordinate_for_identifier(
        &mut self,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    ) -> Option<EnvironmentCoordinate> {
        let name = &self.context.names.identifier_fly_string(self.tree, identifier);
        self.environment_coordinate_for_from_scope_index(name, Some(self.variable_environment_coordinate_scope_index?))
    }
}

//! Yield, await and yield*, and disposing of resources, which can take awaiting.

use libjs_abi::CompletionType;
use libjs_abi::IteratorHint;

use crate::ast::BinaryOp;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::*;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

use super::context::Generator;
use super::stream::Exit;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum YieldBehavior {
    Normal,
    AwaitValue,
    IteratorResult,
}

/// Where code goes on after a yield: `resumed` with the completion still in the accumulator, and `received` once
/// the completion registers hold it and its fields.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct YieldContinuation {
    resumed: Label,
    received: Label,
}

impl YieldContinuation {
    fn new(generator: &mut Generator<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            resumed: generator.new_label(),
            received: generator.new_label(),
        }
    }

    fn bind(self, generator: &mut Generator<'_>, received: CompletionRegisters) {
        // NB: Only a sync generator resumes at `resumed`. An async one reads the completion while unwrapping it.
        if !generator.is_in_async_generator_function() {
            generator.bind_reachable_label(self.resumed);
            received.receive(generator);
        }
        generator.bind_reachable_label(self.received);
    }
}

/// The registers that hold a completion that a suspended function was resumed with, and its fields.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct CompletionRegisters {
    pub(super) completion: Operand,
    pub(super) completion_type: Operand,
    pub(super) value: Operand,
}

impl CompletionRegisters {
    /// The caller's held-register region owns these registers across suspension and resumption.
    pub(super) fn allocate(generator: &mut Generator<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            completion: generator.held_register(),
            completion_type: generator.held_register(),
            value: generator.held_register(),
        }
    }

    /// Jumps to `true_target` if the completion is of `completion_type`, and to `false_target` otherwise.
    fn jump_if_type(
        self,
        generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
        completion_type: CompletionType,
        true_target: Label,
        false_target: Label,
    ) {
        let completion_type = generator.add_constant_number(f64::from(completion_type as u8));
        generator.emit_comparison_jump(
            BinaryOp::StrictlyEquals,
            self.completion_type,
            completion_type,
            true_target,
            false_target,
        );
    }

    /// Takes the completion that the function was resumed with from the accumulator.
    fn receive(self, generator: &mut Generator<'_>) {
        generator.emit_mov(self.completion, Operand::register(Register::ACCUMULATOR));
        self.read_fields(generator);
    }

    fn read_fields(self, generator: &mut Generator<'_>) {
        generator.put(op::GetCompletionFields {
            type_dst: self.completion_type,
            value_dst: self.value,
            completion: self.completion,
        });
    }
}

/// Emit a property access by a name of the iteration protocol, which is not "length".
fn emit_get_by_known_name(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, dst: Operand, base: Operand, name: Utf16View<'_>) {
    let key = generator.intern_property_key_text(name);
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::GetById {
        dst,
        base,
        property: key,
        cache,
    });
}

/// Generate bytecode that awaits `value`.
pub(super) fn generate_await_of_value(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, value: Operand) -> Operand {
    let received = CompletionRegisters::allocate(generator);
    generate_await_with_completions(generator, value, received)
}

/// Generate bytecode that yields `value`, and goes on with what the generator gets resumed with.
pub(super) fn generate_yield_of_value(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    value: Operand,
    is_yield_from: bool,
    received: CompletionRegisters,
) -> Operand {
    if is_yield_from {
        return generate_yield_from(generator, value, received);
    }

    let continuation = YieldContinuation::new(generator);
    generate_yield(
        generator,
        continuation,
        value,
        received,
        if generator.is_in_async_generator_function() {
            YieldBehavior::AwaitValue
        } else {
            YieldBehavior::Normal
        },
    );

    continuation.bind(generator, received);

    let normal_block = generator.new_label();
    let throw_cont = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(generator, CompletionType::Normal, normal_block, throw_cont);

    let throw_value_block = generator.new_label();
    let return_value_block = generator.new_label();

    generator.bind_reachable_label(throw_cont);
    received.jump_if_type(generator, CompletionType::Throw, throw_value_block, return_value_block);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(throw_value_block);
    generator.put(op::Throw { src: received.value });

    generator.bind_reachable_label(return_value_block);
    generator.emit_exit(Exit::Return, received.value);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(normal_block);
    received.value
}

/// Await `argument` and capture its completion without propagating a rejection.
fn generate_await_completion(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, argument: Operand, received: CompletionRegisters) {
    let continuation = generator.new_label();
    generator.put(op::Await {
        continuation_label: continuation,
        argument,
    });
    generator.bind_reachable_label(continuation);

    received.receive(generator);
}

/// Await `argument` using caller-provided completion registers, throwing on rejection.
pub(super) fn generate_await_with_completions(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    argument: Operand,
    received: CompletionRegisters,
) -> Operand {
    generate_await_completion(generator, argument, received);

    let normal_block = generator.new_label();
    let throw_block = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(generator, CompletionType::Normal, normal_block, throw_block);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(throw_block);
    generator.put(op::Throw { src: received.value });

    generator.bind_reachable_label(normal_block);
    received.value
}

/// Yield* (yield from) delegation.
///
/// Implements the iterator delegation protocol from
/// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-generator-function-definitions-runtime-semantics-evaluation
///
/// The delegating generator forwards next/throw/return to the inner iterator.
fn generate_yield_from(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, value: Operand, received: CompletionRegisters) -> Operand {
    let is_async = generator.is_in_async_generator_function();

    // 4. Let iteratorRecord be ? GetIterator(value, generatorKind).
    let iterator = generator.held_register();
    let next_method = generator.held_register();
    let inner_result = generator.held_register();
    let done = generator.held_register();
    let return_value = generator.held_register();
    let hint = if is_async {
        IteratorHint::Async
    } else {
        IteratorHint::Sync
    } as u8;
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::GetIterator {
        dst_iterator_object: iterator,
        dst_iterator_next: next_method,
        // NB: The iterator of yield* is never done before its first step, and `done` gets written before it is read.
        dst_iterator_done: done,
        iterable: value,
        hint,
        // NB: yield* passes the iterator to calls of its methods.
        fast_array_mode_allowed: false,
        cache,
    });

    // 6. Let received be NormalCompletion(undefined).
    let normal_const = generator.add_constant_number(f64::from(CompletionType::Normal as u8));
    generator.emit_mov(received.completion_type, normal_const);
    let undef = generator.add_constant_undefined();
    generator.emit_mov(received.value, undef);

    // 7. Repeat,
    let loop_block = generator.new_label();
    let continuation = YieldContinuation::new(generator);
    let loop_end_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.put(op::Jump { target: loop_block });
    generator.bind_reachable_label(loop_block);

    // Branch on received.[[Type]].
    let type_is_normal_block = generator.new_label();
    let is_type_throw_block = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(
        generator,
        CompletionType::Normal,
        type_is_normal_block,
        is_type_throw_block,
    );

    // =========================================================================
    // a. If received.[[Type]] is normal, then
    // =========================================================================
    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_normal_block);
    // NB: Each branch ends by yielding, throwing or leaving the loop, so the registers that it holds do not outlive it.
    let branch_registers = generator.hold_registers();

    // i. Let _innerResult_ be ? Call(_next_, _iterator_, « _received_.[[Value]] »).
    let call_feedback = generator.next_call_feedback();
    generator.put(op::Call {
        call_feedback,
        dst: inner_result,
        callee: next_method,
        this_value: iterator,
        argument_count: 1,
        arguments: &[received.value],
    });

    // ii. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _innerResult_ to ? Await(_innerResult_).
    if is_async {
        let awaited = generate_await_with_completions(generator, inner_result, received);
        generator.emit_mov(inner_result, awaited);
    }

    // iii. If _innerResult_ is not an Object, throw a *TypeError* exception.
    generator.put(op::ThrowIfNotObject { src: inner_result });

    // iv. Let _done_ be ? IteratorComplete(_innerResult_).
    emit_get_by_known_name(generator, done, inner_result, utf16!("done").into());

    // v. If _done_ is *true*, then return ? IteratorValue(_innerResult_).
    let type_is_normal_done_block = generator.new_label();
    let type_is_normal_not_done_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.emit_jump_if(done, type_is_normal_done_block, type_is_normal_not_done_block);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_normal_done_block);
    emit_get_by_known_name(generator, return_value, inner_result, utf16!("value").into());
    generator.put(op::Jump { target: loop_end_block });

    // vi. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _received_ to Completion(AsyncGeneratorYield(? IteratorValue(_innerResult_))).
    // vii. Else, set _received_ to Completion(GeneratorYield(_innerResult_)).
    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_normal_not_done_block);
    {
        let (yield_value, yield_behavior) = if is_async {
            let current_value = generator.held_register();
            emit_get_by_known_name(generator, current_value, inner_result, utf16!("value").into());
            (current_value, YieldBehavior::Normal)
        } else {
            (inner_result, YieldBehavior::IteratorResult)
        };

        generate_yield(generator, continuation, yield_value, received, yield_behavior);
    }
    generator.release_held_registers(branch_registers);

    // =========================================================================
    // b. Else if received.[[Type]] is throw, then
    // =========================================================================
    generator.bind_reachable_label(is_type_throw_block);
    let type_is_throw_block = generator.new_label();
    let type_is_return_block = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(
        generator,
        CompletionType::Throw,
        type_is_throw_block,
        type_is_return_block,
    );

    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_throw_block);
    let branch_registers = generator.hold_registers();

    // i. Let _throw_ be ? GetMethod(_iterator_, *"throw"*).
    let throw_method = generator.held_register();
    let throw_key = generator.intern_property_key_text(utf16!("throw").into());
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::GetMethod {
        dst: throw_method,
        object: iterator,
        property: throw_key,
        cache,
    });

    // ii. If _throw_ is not *undefined*, then
    let throw_method_defined_block = generator.new_label();
    let throw_method_undefined_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.put(op::JumpUndefined {
        condition: throw_method,
        true_target: throw_method_undefined_block,
        false_target: throw_method_defined_block,
    });

    generator.bind_reachable_label(throw_method_defined_block);

    // 1. Let _innerResult_ be ? Call(_throw_, _iterator_, « _received_.[[Value]] »).
    let call_feedback = generator.next_call_feedback();
    generator.put(op::Call {
        call_feedback,
        dst: inner_result,
        callee: throw_method,
        this_value: iterator,
        argument_count: 1,
        arguments: &[received.value],
    });

    // 2. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _innerResult_ to ? Await(_innerResult_).
    if is_async {
        let awaited = generate_await_with_completions(generator, inner_result, received);
        generator.emit_mov(inner_result, awaited);
    }

    // 4. If _innerResult_ is not an Object, throw a *TypeError* exception.
    generator.put(op::ThrowIfNotObject { src: inner_result });

    // 5. Let _done_ be ? IteratorComplete(_innerResult_).
    emit_get_by_known_name(generator, done, inner_result, utf16!("done").into());

    // 6. If _done_ is *true*, return ? IteratorValue(_innerResult_).
    let type_is_throw_done_block = generator.new_label();
    let type_is_throw_not_done_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.emit_jump_if(done, type_is_throw_done_block, type_is_throw_not_done_block);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_throw_done_block);
    emit_get_by_known_name(generator, return_value, inner_result, utf16!("value").into());
    generator.put(op::Jump { target: loop_end_block });

    // 7. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _received_ to Completion(AsyncGeneratorYield(? IteratorValue(_innerResult_))).
    // 8. Else, set _received_ to Completion(GeneratorYield(_innerResult_)).
    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_throw_not_done_block);
    {
        let (yield_value, yield_behavior) = if is_async {
            let current_value = generator.held_register();
            emit_get_by_known_name(generator, current_value, inner_result, utf16!("value").into());
            (current_value, YieldBehavior::Normal)
        } else {
            (inner_result, YieldBehavior::IteratorResult)
        };
        generate_yield(generator, continuation, yield_value, received, yield_behavior);
    }

    // throw is undefined: close iterator, throw TypeError.
    generator.bind_reachable_label(throw_method_undefined_block);

    if is_async {
        // AsyncIteratorClose: get return method, call it, await, check object.
        let return_method = generator.held_register();
        let return_key = generator.intern_property_key_text(utf16!("return").into());
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::GetMethod {
            dst: return_method,
            object: iterator,
            property: return_key,
            cache,
        });

        let call_return_block = generator.new_label();
        let after_close = generator.new_label();
        generator.put(op::JumpUndefined {
            condition: return_method,
            true_target: after_close,
            false_target: call_return_block,
        });
        generator.bind_reachable_label(call_return_block);

        let close_result = generator.held_register();
        let call_feedback = generator.next_call_feedback();
        generator.put(op::Call {
            call_feedback,
            dst: close_result,
            callee: return_method,
            this_value: iterator,
            argument_count: 0,
            arguments: &[],
        });

        let awaited = generate_await_with_completions(generator, close_result, received);
        generator.put(op::ThrowIfNotObject { src: awaited });

        generator.put(op::Jump { target: after_close });
        generator.bind_reachable_label(after_close);
    } else {
        // Sync: IteratorClose with Normal completion.
        let undef = generator.add_constant_undefined();
        let not_done = generator.add_constant_boolean(false);
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::IteratorClose {
            iterator_object: iterator,
            iterator_next: next_method,
            iterator_done: not_done,
            completion_type: CompletionType::Normal as u8,
            completion_value: undef,
            cache,
        });
    }

    // Throw a TypeError: iterator does not have a throw method.
    let exception = generator.held_register();
    let error_string =
        generator.intern_string_text(utf16!("yield* protocol violation: iterator must have a throw method").into());
    generator.put(op::NewTypeError {
        dst: exception,
        error_string,
    });
    generator.put(op::Throw { src: exception });
    generator.release_held_registers(branch_registers);

    // =========================================================================
    // c. Else (received.[[Type]] is return)
    // =========================================================================
    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_return_block);
    let branch_registers = generator.hold_registers();

    // ii. Let _return_ be ? GetMethod(_iterator_, *"return"*).
    let return_method = generator.held_register();
    let return_key = generator.intern_property_key_text(utf16!("return").into());
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::GetMethod {
        dst: return_method,
        object: iterator,
        property: return_key,
        cache,
    });

    // iii. If _return_ is *undefined*, then
    let return_is_undefined_block = generator.new_label();
    let return_is_defined_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.put(op::JumpUndefined {
        condition: return_method,
        true_target: return_is_undefined_block,
        false_target: return_is_defined_block,
    });

    generator.bind_reachable_label(return_is_undefined_block);
    // 1. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _received_.[[Value]] to ? Await(_received_.[[Value]]).
    if is_async {
        generate_await_with_completions(generator, received.value, received);
    }
    // 2. Return _received_.
    generator.emit_exit(Exit::Return, received.value);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(return_is_defined_block);

    // iv. Let _innerReturnResult_ be ? Call(_return_, _iterator_, « _received_.[[Value]] »).
    let inner_return_result = generator.held_register();
    let call_feedback = generator.next_call_feedback();
    generator.put(op::Call {
        call_feedback,
        dst: inner_return_result,
        callee: return_method,
        this_value: iterator,
        argument_count: 1,
        arguments: &[received.value],
    });

    // v. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _innerReturnResult_ to ? Await(_innerReturnResult_).
    if is_async {
        let awaited = generate_await_with_completions(generator, inner_return_result, received);
        generator.emit_mov(inner_return_result, awaited);
    }

    // vi. If _innerReturnResult_ is not an Object, throw a *TypeError* exception.
    generator.put(op::ThrowIfNotObject {
        src: inner_return_result,
    });

    // vii. Let _done_ be ? IteratorComplete(_innerReturnResult_).
    emit_get_by_known_name(generator, done, inner_return_result, utf16!("done").into());

    // viii. If _done_ is *true*, then
    let type_is_return_done_block = generator.new_label();
    let type_is_return_not_done_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.emit_jump_if(done, type_is_return_done_block, type_is_return_not_done_block);

    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_return_done_block);
    let inner_return_result_value = generator.held_register();
    emit_get_by_known_name(
        generator,
        inner_return_result_value,
        inner_return_result,
        utf16!("value").into(),
    );
    generator.emit_exit(Exit::Return, inner_return_result_value);

    // ix. If _generatorKind_ is ~async~, set _received_ to Completion(AsyncGeneratorYield(? IteratorValue(_innerReturnResult_))).
    // x. Else, set _received_ to Completion(GeneratorYield(_innerReturnResult_)).
    generator.bind_reachable_label(type_is_return_not_done_block);
    let (yielded, yield_behavior) = if is_async {
        let current_value = generator.held_register();
        emit_get_by_known_name(generator, current_value, inner_return_result, utf16!("value").into());
        (current_value, YieldBehavior::Normal)
    } else {
        (inner_return_result, YieldBehavior::IteratorResult)
    };
    generate_yield(generator, continuation, yielded, received, yield_behavior);
    generator.release_held_registers(branch_registers);

    // =========================================================================
    // Continuation block: resume after any yield, extract completion, loop back.
    // =========================================================================
    continuation.bind(generator, received);
    generator.put(op::Jump { target: loop_block });

    // =========================================================================
    // Loop end: return the accumulated return_value.
    // =========================================================================
    generator.bind_reachable_label(loop_end_block);
    return_value
}

/// Unified yield function.
///
/// For non-async generators: just emits a Yield instruction.
/// For async generators: optionally awaits the argument first, then yields,
/// then handles AsyncGeneratorUnwrapYieldResumption (check return type,
/// await return value, re-classify).
/// Goes on at `continuation`, and for an async generator with the completion fields read.
fn generate_yield(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    continuation: YieldContinuation,
    argument: Operand,
    received: CompletionRegisters,
    yield_behavior: YieldBehavior,
) {
    if !generator.is_in_async_generator_function() {
        if yield_behavior == YieldBehavior::IteratorResult {
            generator.put(op::YieldIteratorResult {
                continuation_label: continuation.resumed,
                value: argument,
            });
        } else {
            generator.put(op::Yield {
                continuation_label: Some(continuation.resumed),
                value: argument,
            });
        }
        return;
    }

    let argument = if yield_behavior == YieldBehavior::AwaitValue {
        generate_await_with_completions(generator, argument, received)
    } else {
        argument
    };

    // Yield, then UnwrapYieldResumption.
    let unwrap_block = generator.new_label();
    generator.put(op::Yield {
        continuation_label: Some(unwrap_block),
        value: argument,
    });
    generator.bind_reachable_label(unwrap_block);

    received.receive(generator);

    // If resumptionValue.[[Type]] is not return, jump to continuation.
    let return_block = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(generator, CompletionType::Return, return_block, continuation.received);

    // Return path: Await(resumptionValue.[[Value]]).
    generator.bind_reachable_label(return_block);
    // NB: A rejection must reach the yield continuation so yield* can forward it to the delegated iterator.
    generate_await_completion(generator, received.value, received);

    // If awaited.[[Type]] is throw, jump to continuation.
    let awaited_normal_block = generator.new_label();
    received.jump_if_type(
        generator,
        CompletionType::Throw,
        continuation.received,
        awaited_normal_block,
    );

    // awaited.[[Type]] is normal: set type to Return and jump to continuation.
    generator.bind_reachable_label(awaited_normal_block);
    generator.put(op::SetCompletionType {
        completion: received.completion,
        completion_type: CompletionType::Return as u8,
    });
    // NB: SetCompletionType changes the completion itself, so its fields have to be read again.
    received.read_fields(generator);
    generator.jump(continuation.received);
}

/// How the resources of a scope are disposed of, if the scope has `using` or `await using` declarations.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum DisposalKind {
    Sync,
    Async,
}

/// Disposes of the resources in `stack`, which replaces the completion with a throw completion if a dispose method throws.
// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-disposeresources
pub(super) fn emit_dispose_resources(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    kind: DisposalKind,
    stack: Operand,
    completion_type: Operand,
    completion_value: Operand,
) {
    match kind {
        DisposalKind::Sync => {
            generator.put(op::DisposeResources {
                stack,
                completion_type,
                completion_value,
            });
        }
        DisposalKind::Async => {
            // NB: DisposeResources awaits between some of its steps here, so the bytecode performs it one step at a
            //     time, with an Await after each step that asks for one.
            let awaited = CompletionRegisters::allocate(generator);
            let done = generator.held_register();
            let awaited_value = generator.held_register();
            let normal_type = generator.add_constant_number(f64::from(CompletionType::Normal as u8));
            let undefined = generator.add_constant_undefined();
            generator.emit_mov(awaited.completion_type, normal_type);
            generator.emit_mov(awaited.value, undefined);

            let step_block = generator.new_label();
            let await_block = generator.new_label();
            let continuation_block = generator.new_label();
            let done_block = generator.new_label();
            generator.put(op::Jump { target: step_block });

            generator.bind_reachable_label(step_block);
            generator.put(op::AsyncDisposeResourcesStep {
                done,
                awaited_value,
                stack,
                completion_type,
                completion_value,
                await_completion_type: awaited.completion_type,
                await_completion_value: awaited.value,
            });
            generator.emit_jump_if(done, done_block, await_block);

            generator.bind_reachable_label(await_block);
            generator.put(op::Await {
                continuation_label: continuation_block,
                argument: awaited_value,
            });

            generator.bind_reachable_label(continuation_block);
            awaited.receive(generator);
            generator.put(op::Jump { target: step_block });

            generator.bind_reachable_label(done_block);
        }
    }
}

//! Member access, super properties and delete.

use libjs_abi::PutKind;

/// Emit a property access by key, using GetLength for the "length" property.
pub(super) fn emit_get_by_key(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, dst: Operand, base: Operand, key: PropertyKeyTableIndex) {
    if generator.context.names.is_length_property_key(key) {
        generator.length_identifier = Some(key);
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        let keyed_feedback = generator.next_keyed_feedback();
        generator.put(op::GetLength {
            keyed_feedback,
            dst,
            base,
            cache,
        });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::GetById {
            dst,
            base,
            property: key,
            cache,
        });
    }
}

/// Emit a property access by name with a this value.
pub(super) fn emit_get_by_id_with_this(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    dst: Operand,
    base: Operand,
    property_name: Name,
    this_value: Operand,
) {
    let key = generator.intern_property_key(property_name);
    emit_get_by_key_with_this(generator, dst, base, key, this_value);
}

/// Emit a property access by key with a this value, using GetLengthWithThis for the "length" property.
fn emit_get_by_key_with_this(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    dst: Operand,
    base: Operand,
    key: PropertyKeyTableIndex,
    this_value: Operand,
) {
    if generator.context.names.is_length_property_key(key) {
        generator.length_identifier = Some(key);
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::GetLengthWithThis {
            dst,
            base,
            this_value,
            cache,
        });
    } else {
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::GetByIdWithThis {
            dst,
            base,
            property: key,
            this_value,
            cache,
        });
    }
}

/// Emit a property read by value, optimizing constant string properties to GetById.
pub(super) fn emit_get_by_value(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, dst: Operand, base: Operand, property: Operand) {
    if let Some(key) = generator.try_constant_string_to_property_key(property) {
        emit_get_by_key(generator, dst, base, key);
        return;
    }
    let keyed_feedback = generator.next_keyed_feedback();
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::GetByValue {
        keyed_feedback,
        dst,
        base,
        property,
        cache,
    });
}

/// Emit a property read by value with explicit this, optimizing constant string properties.
pub(super) fn emit_get_by_value_with_this(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    dst: Operand,
    base: Operand,
    property: Operand,
    this_value: Operand,
) {
    if let Some(key) = generator.try_constant_string_to_property_key(property) {
        emit_get_by_key_with_this(generator, dst, base, key, this_value);
        return;
    }
    let value_feedback = generator.next_value_feedback();
    generator.put(op::GetByValueWithThis {
        value_feedback,
        dst,
        base,
        property,
        this_value,
    });
}

/// Emit a normal property write by value with explicit this, optimizing constant string properties.
pub(super) fn emit_put_normal_by_value_with_this(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    base: Operand,
    property: Operand,
    this_value: Operand,
    src: Operand,
) {
    if let Some(key) = generator.try_constant_string_to_property_key(property) {
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::PutByIdWithThis {
            base,
            this_value,
            property: key,
            src,
            cache,
            kind: PutKind::Normal as u8,
        });
        return;
    }
    generator.put(op::PutByValueWithThis {
        base,
        property,
        this_value,
        src,
        kind: PutKind::Normal as u8,
    });
}

/// Emit a property write by value, optimizing constant string properties to the ById variant.
pub(super) fn emit_put_by_value(
    generator: &mut Generator<'_>,
    base: Operand,
    property: Operand,
    src: Operand,
    kind: PutKind,
) {
    if let Some(key) = generator.try_constant_string_to_property_key(property) {
        let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
        generator.put(op::PutById {
            base,
            property: key,
            src,
            cache,
            kind: kind as u8,
        });
        return;
    }
    let keyed_feedback = generator.next_keyed_feedback();
    let cache = generator.next_property_lookup_cache();
    generator.put(op::PutByValue {
        keyed_feedback,
        base,
        property,
        src,
        kind: kind as u8,
        cache,
    });
}

/// A private name as the tables hold it, with its `#`.
pub(super) fn intern_private_name(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, name: Name) -> IdentifierTableIndex {
    let mut text = Utf16StringBuilder::new();
    text.append_ascii("#");
    text.append(generator.tree.name_text(name));
    let text = text.to_utf16_string();
    generator.intern_identifier_text(Utf16View::of_string(&text))
}
