//! Bytecode generation from the columns of the syntax tree, straight into bytes.
//!
//! A top level has marks in its rows from its first parse, and a function gets parsed again with them. `sweep` goes
//! through the rows in one loop, leaving what does not come in the order of its rows to `constructs`. Both call the emission core in `stream`, which
//! knows nothing of rows, and writes each instruction into bytes. What names mean comes from `scope`, which goes by a
//! summary of the first parse. Everything with memory of its own is in `context`, and comes back for the next compile
//! on the thread.

mod bindings;
mod builtins;
mod constants;
mod constructs;
mod context;
pub mod emitter;
mod environment;
mod generators;
mod members;
mod names;
mod nodes;
mod operators;
pub mod scope;
pub mod stream;
mod sweep;

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::ast::FunctionKind;
use crate::ast::SyntaxTree;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ExecutableData;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::PrecompiledFunction;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::parser::EnclosingCode;
use crate::parser::TopLevelRows;
use ak::Zone;
use context::Generator;
pub use environment::EnclosingEnvironmentScope;
use libjs_parser::base::OutOfStack;
use nodes::NodeId;
pub use stream::DisposableResourceKind;

/// How many arguments a call keeps as separate operands before the rest go into an array.
pub(crate) fn inline_argument_limit(builtin_abstract_operations_enabled: bool) -> usize {
    // NB: Intrinsic calls consume their operands directly rather than an argument array.
    if builtin_abstract_operations_enabled {
        usize::MAX
    } else {
        crate::bytecode::operand::MAX_OPERAND_LIST_LENGTH
    }
}

/// Compiles the function at `row`, which gets parsed again for that, into a tree in `zone`.
pub fn compile_function(
    zone: &Zone,
    script: &Arc<crate::parser::ScriptData>,
    row: crate::parser::FunctionRow,
    enclosing_environment_scope: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
    enclosing_code: &Arc<EnclosingCode>,
    builtin_abstract_operations_enabled: bool,
    stack_limit: usize,
) -> Result<PrecompiledFunction, OutOfStack> {
    let (tree, node) = script.reparse_for_sweep(
        zone,
        row,
        stack_limit,
        inline_argument_limit(builtin_abstract_operations_enabled),
    )?;
    let mut generator = Generator::new(&tree, enclosing_code.clone(), stack_limit);
    generator.enclosing_environment_scope = enclosing_environment_scope;
    generator.builtin_abstract_operations_enabled = builtin_abstract_operations_enabled;
    generator.begin_function_scope(row);
    let function = NodeId(node);
    let flags = script.index.flags[row.0 as usize];
    use libjs_parser::columns::function_flag::*;
    let swept = if flags & FIELD_INITIALIZER != 0 {
        generator.sweep_field_initializer(function)
    } else if flags & STATIC_BLOCK != 0 {
        generator.sweep_static_block(function)
    } else if flags & DEFAULT_CONSTRUCTOR != 0 {
        generator.current_source_offset = crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceOffset(script.index.start[row.0 as usize]);
        generator.generate_default_constructor(flags & DERIVED_CONSTRUCTOR != 0);
        Ok(())
    } else {
        generator.sweep_parameter_names(function);
        generator
            .sweep_parameters(function)
            .and_then(|()| sweep::sweep_function_body(&mut generator, function))
    };
    swept.map(|()| generator.finish_function())
}

/// What a compile needs to know of a program, which `compile.rs` works out.
pub struct ProgramInput<'a> {
    pub tree: &'a SyntaxTree<'a>,
    /// The rows of the top level of the tree for a sweep, which its parse made.
    pub top_level_rows: TopLevelRows<'a>,
    pub strict: bool,
    /// Whether the program is a module with top-level await, which runs like an async function.
    pub is_async_module: bool,
    pub enclosing_environment_scope: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
    pub stack_limit: usize,
}

/// Compiles the script, module or eval that is the program of the tree in `input`, from the rows that its parse left.
/// The functions that the program calls right away are marked for an eager compile, which is up to the caller, as it
/// is a job of its own for each of them (see `crate::compile::compile_function()`).
pub fn compile_program(input: &ProgramInput<'_>) -> Result<ExecutableData, OutOfStack> {
    let parsed = input.tree;
    let script = &parsed.script;
    let (rows, node) = input.top_level_rows?;
    let tree = script.tree_of_rows(rows, node);
    let kind = if script.program_type == crate::ast::ProgramType::Module {
        scope::ProgramKind::Module
    } else if script.program_context.has_no_globals {
        scope::ProgramKind::WithoutGlobals
    } else {
        scope::ProgramKind::Script
    };
    let mut generator = Generator::new(&tree, EnclosingCode::of_program(parsed), input.stack_limit);
    generator.strict = input.strict;
    generator.eager_compile_direct_iifes = true;
    generator.enclosing_environment_scope = input.enclosing_environment_scope.clone();
    if input.is_async_module {
        generator.enclosing_function_kind = FunctionKind::Async;
    }
    generator.context.annexb_function_names.extend_from_slice(
        parsed
            .program_scope()
            .annexb_function_names
            .of(parsed.scopes.annexb_function_names),
    );
    generator.begin_program_scope(kind, input.is_async_module);
    sweep::sweep_program(&mut generator, NodeId(node))?;
    let compiled = generator.finish_function();
    Ok(Arc::into_inner(compiled.executable).expect("nothing else holds on to new code"))
}

/// The code of a program that nests too deeply to generate code for it with the stack there is. Running it throws, like
/// a function does that is too deep to compile.
pub fn compile_program_too_deep_to_generate(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>) -> ExecutableData {
    let mut generator = Generator::new(tree, EnclosingCode::of_program(tree), 0);
    generator.begin_program_scope(scope::ProgramKind::Script, true);
    let exception = generator.temporary();
    let error_string = generator.intern_string_text(crate::utf16::Utf16View::Utf16(utf16!(
        "Maximum call stack size exceeded"
    )));
    generator.put(op::NewTypeError {
        dst: exception,
        error_string,
    });
    generator.put(op::Throw { src: exception });
    let compiled = generator.finish_function();
    Arc::into_inner(compiled.executable).expect("nothing else holds on to new code")
}

//! The string, identifier and property key tables of an executable. Their order is part of the output: a text takes the
//! next index of a table the first time it comes up, whether it comes up as a name of the tree or as any other text, and
//! both ways have to land on the same entry.
//!
//! Generating code takes no global lock and touches no fly string: an entry is the `Name` it came from, and entries are
//! found by a hash of their text that is known once per name of a script. Fly strings only come into it when the tables
//! leave the compile, and then only once per name of a script on this thread. Everything here is per thread, so
//! compiling the functions of a script on several threads needs no lock on the script either.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::Weak;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;

use crate::ast::Name;
use crate::ast::SyntaxTree;
use crate::bytecode::operand::IdentifierTableIndex;
use crate::bytecode::operand::PropertyKeyTableIndex;
use crate::bytecode::operand::StringTableIndex;
use crate::layout::buffer::BlockSlice;
use crate::parser::ScriptData;
use crate::slice_block::SliceBlock;
use crate::slice_block::SliceBlockBuilder;
use crate::u32_from_usize;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

use super::constants::IndexTable;
use super::constants::hash_of_units;
use super::context::MAXIMUM_SPARE_CAPACITY;

const NO_INDEX: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// How many texts that are no names a thread remembers of a script.
const MAXIMUM_SCRIPT_TEXTS: usize = 1 << 16;

/// What code generation treats specially about a name.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum NameClass {
    Plain,
    Undefined,
    NaN,
    Infinity,
    Eval,
    Length,
}

impl NameClass {
    fn of(text: Utf16View<'_>) -> Self {
        if text == utf16!("undefined") {
            Self::Undefined
        } else if text == utf16!("NaN") {
            Self::NaN
        } else if text == utf16!("Infinity") {
            Self::Infinity
        } else if text == utf16!("eval") {
            Self::Eval
        } else if text == utf16!("length") {
            Self::Length
        } else {
            Self::Plain
        }
    }
}

/// What is known about a name once it came up.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct NameFacts {
    /// The hash of the name's text, or zero if the name did not come up yet.
    hash: u64,
    class: NameClass,
}

/// What a script's names turn into, kept from one function of the script to the next on this thread.
#[derive(Default)]
struct ScriptNames {
    /// Compared by address only. The weak reference keeps the address from going to another script.
    script: Weak<ScriptData>,
    facts: Vec<NameFacts>,
    fly_strings: Vec<Option<Utf16FlyString>>,
    /// Texts that are no names, which code that was minified repeats a lot: `a.b` for the error of a call, for example.
    texts: Vec<Utf16FlyString>,
    text_hashes: Vec<u64>,
    text_index: IndexTable,
}

impl ScriptNames {
    fn adopt(&mut self, script: &Arc<ScriptData>) {
        if self.script.as_ptr() != Arc::as_ptr(script) {
            self.script = Arc::downgrade(script);
            self.facts.clear();
            self.fly_strings.clear();
            self.forget_texts();
        }
    }

    fn forget_texts(&mut self) {
        self.texts.clear();
        self.text_hashes.clear();
        self.text_index.clear();
    }

    /// The id of a text, which only takes the global table once per text of a script on this thread.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn text_id(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>, hash: u64) -> u32 {
        if self.texts.len() >= MAXIMUM_SCRIPT_TEXTS {
            self.forget_texts();
        }
        let texts = &self.texts;
        let found = self
            .text_index
            .find(hash, |index| Utf16View::of_fly_string(&texts[index as usize]) == text);
        match found {
            Ok(index) => index,
            Err(slot) => {
                let index = u32_from_usize(self.texts.len());
                self.texts.push(text.to_utf16_fly_string());
                self.text_hashes.push(hash);
                self.text_index.insert_at(slot, hash, index);
                index
            }
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn facts_of(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> NameFacts {
        let index = name.0 as usize;
        if index >= self.facts.len() || self.facts[index].hash == 0 {
            return self.learn(tree, name);
        }
        self.facts[index]
    }

    #[cold]
    fn learn(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> NameFacts {
        let index = name.0 as usize;
        if index >= self.facts.len() {
            let unknown = NameFacts {
                hash: 0,
                class: NameClass::Plain,
            };
            self.facts.resize((index + 1).next_power_of_two(), unknown);
        }
        let text = tree.name_text(name);
        self.facts[index] = NameFacts {
            hash: hash_of_units(text),
            class: NameClass::of(text),
        };
        self.facts[index]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn fly_string(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> &Utf16FlyString {
        let index = name.0 as usize;
        if index >= self.fly_strings.len() {
            self.fly_strings.resize((index + 1).next_power_of_two(), None);
        }
        self.fly_strings[index].get_or_insert_with(|| tree.name_text(name).to_utf16_fly_string())
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct NameSlot {
    name: u32,
    generation: u32,
    identifier: u32,
    property_key: u32,
}

/// Where the names of the tree went in the tables, in an open-addressed table that forgets everything by moving on to a
/// new generation: the names of a function are few, and looking them up takes no strings.
#[derive(Default)]
struct NameIndices {
    slots: Vec<NameSlot>,
    used_slots: usize,
    generation: u32,
}

impl NameIndices {
    const INITIAL_SLOT_COUNT: usize = 64;

    fn clear(&mut self) {
        if self.slots.len() > MAXIMUM_SPARE_CAPACITY {
            self.slots = Vec::new();
            self.generation = 0;
        }
        self.used_slots = 0;
        self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);
        if self.generation == 0 {
            self.slots.fill(NameSlot::default());
            self.generation = 1;
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn first_slot_of(name: u32, slot_count: usize) -> usize {
        // NB: Names count up from zero in order of appearance, which an odd multiplier spreads over the slots.
        (name.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B1) >> 7) as usize & (slot_count - 1)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn slot_of(&mut self, name: Name) -> &mut NameSlot {
        if (self.used_slots + 1) * 4 > self.slots.len() * 3 {
            self.grow();
        }
        let mask = self.slots.len() - 1;
        let mut slot = Self::first_slot_of(name.0, self.slots.len());
        loop {
            let entry = self.slots[slot];
            if entry.generation != self.generation {
                self.used_slots += 1;
                self.slots[slot] = NameSlot {
                    name: name.0,
                    generation: self.generation,
                    identifier: NO_INDEX,
                    property_key: NO_INDEX,
                };
                return &mut self.slots[slot];
            }
            if entry.name == name.0 {
                return &mut self.slots[slot];
            }
            slot = (slot + 1) & mask;
        }
    }

    #[cold]
    fn grow(&mut self) {
        // NB: Slots that were never used are of generation zero, which no table is.
        self.generation = self.generation.max(1);
        let slot_count = (self.slots.len() * 2).max(Self::INITIAL_SLOT_COUNT);
        let old_slots = std::mem::replace(&mut self.slots, vec![NameSlot::default(); slot_count]);
        for old_slot in old_slots {
            if old_slot.generation == self.generation {
                let mut slot = Self::first_slot_of(old_slot.name, slot_count);
                while self.slots[slot].generation == self.generation {
                    slot = (slot + 1) & (slot_count - 1);
                }
                self.slots[slot] = old_slot;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// An entry of a table, in the form it came up in.
enum TableEntry {
    Name(Name),
    Text(Utf16FlyString),
}

/// One table of the executable. Entries are found by the hash of their text, which also finds a name by its text.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Table {
    entries: Vec<TableEntry>,
    index_of: IndexTable,
}

impl Table {
    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.entries.clear();
        self.index_of.clear();
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn intern_name(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name, hash: u64) -> u32 {
        let entries = &self.entries;
        let text = tree.name_text(name);
        let found = self.index_of.find(hash, |index| match &entries[index as usize] {
            TableEntry::Name(other) => *other == name,
            TableEntry::Text(other) => Utf16View::of_fly_string(other) == text,
        });
        match found {
            Ok(index) => index,
            Err(slot) => {
                let index = u32_from_usize(self.entries.len());
                self.entries.push(TableEntry::Name(name));
                self.index_of.insert_at(slot, hash, index);
                index
            }
        }
    }

    fn intern_text(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, script_names: &mut ScriptNames, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> u32 {
        let hash = hash_of_units(text);
        let entries = &self.entries;
        let found = self.index_of.find(hash, |index| match &entries[index as usize] {
            TableEntry::Name(other) => tree.name_text(*other) == text,
            TableEntry::Text(other) => Utf16View::of_fly_string(other) == text,
        });
        match found {
            Ok(index) => index,
            Err(slot) => {
                let index = u32_from_usize(self.entries.len());
                let id = script_names.text_id(text, hash);
                self.entries
                    .push(TableEntry::Text(script_names.texts[id as usize].clone()));
                self.index_of.insert_at(slot, hash, index);
                index
            }
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct NameTables {
    script_names: ScriptNames,
    name_indices: NameIndices,
    identifiers: Table,
    property_keys: Table,
    strings: Table,
    length_property_key: Option<u32>,
}

macro_rules! define_intern_methods {
    ($name_method:ident, $text_method:ident, $index_type:ident, $table:ident, $slot_field:ident) => {
        #[inline(always)]
        pub(super) fn $name_method(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> $index_type {
            let index = self.name_indices.slot_of(name).$slot_field;
            if index != NO_INDEX {
                return $index_type(index);
            }
            let hash = self.script_names.facts_of(tree, name).hash;
            let index = self.$table.intern_name(tree, name, hash);
            self.name_indices.slot_of(name).$slot_field = index;
            $index_type(index)
        }

        pub(super) fn $text_method(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> $index_type {
            $index_type(self.$table.intern_text(tree, &mut self.script_names, text))
        }
    };
}

impl NameTables {
    pub(super) fn begin_compile(&mut self, script: &Arc<ScriptData>) {
        self.script_names.adopt(script);
    }

    pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.name_indices.clear();
        self.identifiers.clear();
        self.property_keys.clear();
        self.strings.clear();
        self.length_property_key = None;
    }

    define_intern_methods!(
        intern_identifier,
        intern_identifier_text,
        IdentifierTableIndex,
        identifiers,
        identifier
    );
    pub(super) fn intern_string_text(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, text: Utf16View<'_>) -> StringTableIndex {
        StringTableIndex(self.strings.intern_text(tree, &mut self.script_names, text))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn intern_property_key(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> PropertyKeyTableIndex {
        let index = self.name_indices.slot_of(name).property_key;
        if index != NO_INDEX {
            return PropertyKeyTableIndex(index);
        }
        let facts = self.script_names.facts_of(tree, name);
        let index = self.property_keys.intern_name(tree, name, facts.hash);
        self.name_indices.slot_of(name).property_key = index;
        if facts.class == NameClass::Length {
            self.length_property_key = Some(index);
        }
        PropertyKeyTableIndex(index)
    }

    pub(super) fn intern_property_key_text(
        &mut self,
        tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>,
        text: Utf16View<'_>,
    ) -> PropertyKeyTableIndex {
        let index = self.property_keys.intern_text(tree, &mut self.script_names, text);
        if text == utf16!("length") {
            self.length_property_key = Some(index);
        }
        PropertyKeyTableIndex(index)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn class_of(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> NameClass {
        self.script_names.facts_of(tree, name).class
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_length_property_key(&self, key: PropertyKeyTableIndex) -> bool {
        self.length_property_key == Some(key.0)
    }

    /// The text of an entry of the identifier table as a fly string, which is what environment scopes know names by.
    pub(super) fn identifier_fly_string(
        &mut self,
        tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>,
        identifier: IdentifierTableIndex,
    ) -> Utf16FlyString {
        match &self.identifiers.entries[identifier.0 as usize] {
            TableEntry::Name(name) => self.script_names.fly_string(tree, *name).clone(),
            TableEntry::Text(text) => text.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// The fly string of a text with `hash`, which only takes the global table once per text of a script on this thread.
    pub(super) fn fly_string_of_text(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>, hash: u64) -> &Utf16FlyString {
        let id = self.script_names.text_id(text, hash);
        &self.script_names.texts[id as usize]
    }

    /// The fly string of a name, which only takes the global table once per name of a script on this thread.
    pub(super) fn fly_string_of(&mut self, tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, name: Name) -> Utf16FlyString {
        self.script_names.fly_string(tree, name).clone()
    }

    /// How much of a block the tables that stay with the code take.
    pub(super) fn room_for_tables(&self) -> usize {
        SliceBlock::room_for::<Utf16FlyString>(self.identifiers.entries.len())
    }

    /// How much of a block the table that only linking reads takes.
    pub(super) fn room_for_link_tables(&self) -> usize {
        SliceBlock::room_for::<Utf16FlyString>(self.property_keys.entries.len())
    }

    /// Hands out the tables, as an executable keeps them: identifiers from `block`, property keys from `link_block`, and
    /// strings, which few executables have, on their own.
    pub(super) fn take_tables(
        &mut self,
        tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>,
        block: &mut SliceBlockBuilder,
        link_block: &mut SliceBlockBuilder,
    ) -> (
        BlockSlice<Utf16FlyString>,
        BlockSlice<Utf16FlyString>,
        Box<[Utf16FlyString]>,
    ) {
        let script_names = &mut self.script_names;
        let mut fly_string_of = |entry: &TableEntry| match entry {
            TableEntry::Name(name) => script_names.fly_string(tree, *name).clone(),
            TableEntry::Text(text) => text.clone(),
        };
        (
            block.slice(self.identifiers.entries.iter().map(&mut fly_string_of)),
            link_block.slice(self.property_keys.entries.iter().map(&mut fly_string_of)),
            self.strings.entries.iter().map(&mut fly_string_of).collect(),
        )
    }
}

//! Inline accessors over the columns of the syntax tree, for code generation. A node is only ever looked at through
//! what a generating function needs of it right then: nothing here builds a view of a whole node, and the small structs
//! are the fields of one tag, which are gone again once inlined.

use crate::ast::AssignmentOp;
use crate::ast::BinaryOp;
use crate::ast::ClassMethodKind;
use crate::ast::DeclarationKind;
use crate::ast::LocalType;
use crate::ast::LogicalOp;
use crate::ast::Name;
use crate::ast::SyntaxTree;
use crate::ast::UnaryOp;
use crate::ast::UpdateOp;
use crate::parser::literals;
pub(super) use crate::parser::literals::EscapeMode;
pub(super) use crate::parser::literals::StringLiteralText;
use crate::parser::literals::has_escape_sequence;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;
use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_parser::columns::NONE;
use libjs_parser::columns::tag;
use libjs_parser::token::T;

/// A node of the tree. Zero stands for no node.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct NodeId(pub(super) u32);

impl NodeId {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn index(self) -> usize {
        self.0 as usize
    }
}

/// The nodes of a list of the tree.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct NodeList<'t>(&'t [u32]);

impl<'t> NodeList<'t> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn len(self) -> usize {
        self.0.len()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn at(self, index: usize) -> NodeId {
        NodeId(self.0[index])
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn iter(self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = NodeId> + ExactSizeIterator + 't {
        self.0.iter().map(|&node| NodeId(node))
    }
}

/// An identifier with what scope analysis found out about it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct Identifier {
    pub(super) name: Name,
    pub(super) local_type: Option<LocalType>,
    pub(super) local_index: u32,
    pub(super) is_global: bool,
    pub(super) declaration_kind: Option<DeclarationKind>,
}

impl Identifier {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_local(&self) -> bool {
        self.local_type.is_some()
    }
}

/// The parts of a class node.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct ClassData<'t> {
    pub(super) name: Option<Name>,
    pub(super) super_class: Option<NodeId>,
    /// The constructor that the class spells out, as a function node.
    pub(super) constructor: Option<NodeId>,
    /// Every element of the class, including the constructor that `constructor_index` tells apart.
    pub(super) elements: NodeList<'t>,
    pub(super) constructor_index: Option<usize>,
    pub(super) source_text_start: u32,
    pub(super) source_text_end: u32,
}

impl ClassData<'_> {
    /// The elements of the class, without its constructor.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn elements_without_constructor(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeId> + '_ {
        self.elements
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(index, _)| Some(*index) != self.constructor_index)
            .map(|(_, element)| element)
    }
}

/// The key of a class element.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum ClassElementKey {
    /// A name that stands for itself as a string.
    Name(Name),
    /// Anything else: a literal, a private name or a computed key.
    Expression(NodeId),
}

/// A class element, with `static` taken off.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum ClassElementData {
    Method {
        key: ClassElementKey,
        function: NodeId,
        kind: ClassMethodKind,
        is_static: bool,
    },
    Field {
        key: ClassElementKey,
        initializer: Option<NodeId>,
        /// The field itself, which the function that evaluates `initializer` goes by.
        field: NodeId,
        is_static: bool,
    },
    StaticInitializer {
        block: NodeId,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct SwitchData<'t> {
    pub(super) cases: NodeList<'t>,
}

/// The parts of a try statement.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct TryData {
    pub(super) block: NodeId,
    pub(super) parameter: Option<NodeId>,
    /// The body of the catch clause, if there is one.
    pub(super) handler: Option<NodeId>,
    pub(super) finalizer: Option<NodeId>,
}

impl SyntaxTree<'_> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn node_tag(&self, node: NodeId) -> u8 {
        self.ast.tag[node.index()]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn node_pos(&self, node: NodeId) -> u32 {
        self.ast.pos[node.index()]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn node_a(&self, node: NodeId) -> u32 {
        self.ast.a[node.index()]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn node_b(&self, node: NodeId) -> u32 {
        self.ast.b[node.index()]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn extra_at(&self, index: u32) -> u32 {
        self.ast.extra[index as usize]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn node_list(&self, start: u32) -> NodeList<'_> {
        let start = start as usize;
        let count = self.ast.extra[start] as usize;
        NodeList(&self.ast.extra[start + 1..start + 1 + count])
    }

    /// The expression at `node`, which a pair of parentheses leaves as it is.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn skip_parens(&self, mut node: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        while self.node_tag(node) == tag::PAREN {
            node = NodeId(self.node_a(node));
        }
        node
    }

    /// The child in the `a` operand of `node`, as an expression.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn expression_a(&self, node: NodeId) -> NodeId {
        self.skip_parens(NodeId(self.node_a(node)))
    }

    /// The value of a numeric literal node.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn number_value(&self, node: NodeId) -> f64 {
        self.number_at(self.node_pos(node), self.node_a(node))
    }

    /// The value of the numeric literal between two offsets of the source.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn number_at(&self, start: u32, end: u32) -> f64 {
        let text = self.source_range_units(start, end);
        // OPTIMIZATION: Nearly all numbers in code are short decimal integers, which an f64 holds exactly.
        if let Utf16View::Ascii(digits) | Utf16View::Latin1(digits) = text
            && digits.len() <= 15
            && (digits.len() == 1 || digits[0] != b'0')
            && digits.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit)
        {
            let value = digits
                .iter()
                .fold(0u64, |value, digit| value * 10 + u64::from(digit - b'0'));
            return value as f64;
        }
        literals::parse_numeric_value(text)
    }

    /// The text between two offsets of the source.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn source_range_units(&self, start: u32, end: u32) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        Utf16View::of_string(&self.source).substring_view(start as usize, (end - start) as usize)
    }

    /// The text between the quotes of a string literal node.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn string_literal_units(&self, node: NodeId) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        self.source_range_units(self.node_pos(node) + 1, self.node_a(node) - 1)
    }

    /// The value of a string literal node, without a copy if that is possible.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn string_literal_text(&self, node: NodeId) -> StringLiteralText<'_> {
        literals::string_literal_text(self.string_literal_units(node))
    }

    /// The value of a string literal node.
    pub(super) fn string_literal_value(&self, node: NodeId) -> Utf16String {
        literals::process_escape_sequences_impl(self.string_literal_units(node), EscapeMode::StringLiteral).value
    }

    /// The text of a template chunk node, as the source has it.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn template_chunk_units(&self, chunk: NodeId) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        let start = self.node_a(chunk);
        self.source_range_units(start, start + (self.node_b(chunk) >> 1))
    }

    /// The value of a template chunk node, or `None` if an escape sequence in it makes it have none.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn template_chunk_text(&self, chunk: NodeId, mode: EscapeMode) -> Option<StringLiteralText<'_>> {
        let units = self.template_chunk_units(chunk);
        // NB: A template normalizes the line terminators in it as well.
        if !has_escape_sequence(units) && !units.code_units().any(|unit| unit == u16::from(b'\r')) {
            return Some(StringLiteralText::Source(units));
        }
        let result = literals::process_escape_sequences_impl(units, mode);
        (!result.failed || mode != EscapeMode::TaggedTemplate).then_some(StringLiteralText::Processed(result.value))
    }

    /// Whether the element of a template is a string with nothing in it, which leaves no trace in the result.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_empty_template_element(&self, element: NodeId) -> bool {
        if self.node_tag(element) == tag::TEMPLATE_CHUNK {
            return match self.template_chunk_text(element, EscapeMode::StringLiteral) {
                Some(text) => text.view().length_in_code_units() == 0,
                None => false,
            };
        }
        let element = self.skip_parens(element);
        self.node_tag(element) == tag::STR && self.string_literal_text(element).view().length_in_code_units() == 0
    }

    /// The operator of a binary or logical expression tag.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn binary_operator(node_tag: u8) -> BinaryOrLogical {
        let operator = node_tag - tag::BINARY_BASE;
        match crate::ast::BINARY_OPERATORS[operator as usize] {
            Some(op) => BinaryOrLogical::Binary(op),
            None => BinaryOrLogical::Logical(match operator {
                0 => LogicalOp::NullishCoalescing,
                1 => LogicalOp::Or,
                _ => LogicalOp::And,
            }),
        }
    }

    /// The operator of an assignment tag. A default of a pattern in expression position is a plain assignment.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn assignment_operator(node_tag: u8) -> AssignmentOp {
        if node_tag == tag::ASSIGN_PATTERN {
            return AssignmentOp::Assignment;
        }
        crate::ast::ASSIGNMENT_OPERATORS[(node_tag - tag::ASSIGN_BASE) as usize]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn unary_operator(&self, node: NodeId) -> UnaryOp {
        match self.node_b(node) {
            token if token == T::Not as u32 => UnaryOp::Not,
            token if token == T::Tilde as u32 => UnaryOp::BitwiseNot,
            token if token == T::Plus as u32 => UnaryOp::Plus,
            token if token == T::Minus as u32 => UnaryOp::Minus,
            token if token == T::KTypeof as u32 => UnaryOp::Typeof,
            token if token == T::KVoid as u32 => UnaryOp::Void,
            _ => UnaryOp::Delete,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn update_operator(&self, node: NodeId) -> UpdateOp {
        if self.node_b(node) == T::Inc as u32 {
            UpdateOp::Increment
        } else {
            UpdateOp::Decrement
        }
    }

    /// The cases of a switch statement.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn switch_data(&self, node: NodeId) -> SwitchData<'_> {
        SwitchData {
            cases: self.node_list(self.extra_at(self.node_b(node))),
        }
    }

    /// The text of the key of a property of a pattern, which refers to no binding.
    pub(super) fn pattern_key_text(&self, key: NodeId) -> StringLiteralText<'_> {
        match self.node_tag(key) {
            tag::IDENT | tag::IDENT_KEY => StringLiteralText::Source(self.name_text(Name(self.node_a(key)))),
            tag::STR | tag::STR_KEY => self.string_literal_text(key),
            tag::NUM | tag::NUM_KEY => StringLiteralText::Processed(crate::host::js_number_to_utf16(
                literals::parse_numeric_value(self.source_range_units(self.node_pos(key), self.node_a(key))),
            )),
            _ => {
                let literal = self.source_range_units(self.node_pos(key), self.node_a(key)).to_utf8();
                let value = crate::bytecode::constant_fold::parse_bigint(literal.trim_end_matches('n'))
                    .expect("the lexer only accepts valid BigInts");
                StringLiteralText::Processed(Utf16String::from_utf8(&value.to_string()))
            }
        }
    }

    /// The parts of a class node.
    pub(super) fn class_data(&self, class: NodeId) -> ClassData<'_> {
        let name = self.node_a(class);
        let extra = self.node_b(class);
        let super_class = self.extra_at(extra);
        let constructor = self.extra_at(extra + 3);
        let elements = self.node_list(self.extra_at(extra + 1));
        let constructor_index = elements.iter().position(|element| {
            constructor != 0 && self.node_tag(element) == tag::METHOD && self.node_b(element) == constructor
        });
        ClassData {
            name: (name != NONE).then_some(Name(name)),
            super_class: (super_class != 0).then(|| self.skip_parens(NodeId(super_class))),
            constructor: constructor_index.map(|_| NodeId(constructor)),
            elements,
            constructor_index,
            source_text_start: self.node_pos(class),
            source_text_end: self.extra_at(extra + 4),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn class_element_key(&self, key: NodeId, computed: bool) -> ClassElementKey {
        if !computed && matches!(self.node_tag(key), tag::IDENT | tag::IDENT_KEY) {
            ClassElementKey::Name(Name(self.node_a(key)))
        } else {
            ClassElementKey::Expression(self.skip_parens(key))
        }
    }

    /// What the class element at `element` is.
    pub(super) fn class_element(&self, element: NodeId) -> ClassElementData {
        let is_static = self.node_tag(element) == tag::STATIC_ELEMENT;
        let inner = if is_static {
            NodeId(self.node_a(element))
        } else {
            element
        };
        let (a, b) = (NodeId(self.node_a(inner)), self.node_b(inner));
        let inner_tag = self.node_tag(inner);
        match inner_tag {
            tag::CLASS_FIELD | tag::COMPUTED_CLASS_FIELD => ClassElementData::Field {
                key: self.class_element_key(a, inner_tag == tag::COMPUTED_CLASS_FIELD),
                initializer: (b != 0).then(|| self.expression_a(NodeId(b))),
                field: inner,
                is_static,
            },
            tag::CLASS_STATIC_BLOCK => ClassElementData::StaticInitializer { block: inner },
            other => ClassElementData::Method {
                key: self.class_element_key(
                    a,
                    matches!(
                        other,
                        tag::COMPUTED_METHOD | tag::COMPUTED_GETTER | tag::COMPUTED_SETTER
                    ),
                ),
                function: self.skip_parens(NodeId(b)),
                kind: match other {
                    tag::GETTER | tag::COMPUTED_GETTER => ClassMethodKind::Getter,
                    tag::SETTER | tag::COMPUTED_SETTER => ClassMethodKind::Setter,
                    _ => ClassMethodKind::Method,
                },
                is_static,
            },
        }
    }

    /// The one child of a node that holds a statement as its `a` operand, as a list.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn try_data(&self, node: NodeId) -> TryData {
        let extra = self.node_b(node);
        let optional = |index: u32| {
            let node = self.extra_at(index);
            (node != 0).then_some(NodeId(node))
        };
        TryData {
            block: NodeId(self.node_a(node)),
            parameter: optional(extra),
            handler: optional(extra + 1),
            finalizer: optional(extra + 2),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) enum BinaryOrLogical {
    Binary(BinaryOp),
    Logical(LogicalOp),
}

//! Unary, binary, logical, conditional and update expressions.

use crate::ast::BinaryOp;
use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ConstantValue;
use crate::bytecode::operand::Operand;

use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;

use super::context::Generator;

pub(super) fn emit_binary_op(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, op: BinaryOp, dst: Operand, lhs: Operand, rhs: Operand) {
    match op {
        BinaryOp::Addition => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Add {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::Subtraction => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Sub {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::Multiplication => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Mul {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::Division => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Div {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::Modulo => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Mod {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::Exponentiation => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::Exp {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::StrictlyEquals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::StrictlyEquals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::StrictlyInequals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::StrictlyInequals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::LooselyEquals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::LooselyEquals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::LooselyInequals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::LooselyInequals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::GreaterThan => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::GreaterThan {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::GreaterThanEquals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::LessThan => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::LessThan {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::LessThanEquals {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::BitwiseAnd {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseOr => {
            // OPTIMIZATION: x | 0 == ToInt32(x)
            if let Some(ConstantValue::Number(n)) = generator.get_constant(rhs) {
                if *n == 0.0 && n.is_sign_positive() {
                    let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                    generator.put(op::ToInt32 {
                        arith_feedback,
                        dst,
                        value: lhs,
                    });
                } else {
                    let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                    generator.put(op::BitwiseOr {
                        arith_feedback,
                        dst,
                        lhs,
                        rhs,
                    });
                }
            } else {
                let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                generator.put(op::BitwiseOr {
                    arith_feedback,
                    dst,
                    lhs,
                    rhs,
                });
            }
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseXor => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::BitwiseXor {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::LeftShift => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::LeftShift {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::RightShift => {
            // OPTIMIZATION: x >> 0 == ToInt32(x) (matches C++)
            if let Some(ConstantValue::Number(n)) = generator.get_constant(rhs) {
                if *n == 0.0 && n.is_sign_positive() {
                    let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                    generator.put(op::ToInt32 {
                        arith_feedback,
                        dst,
                        value: lhs,
                    });
                } else {
                    let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                    generator.put(op::RightShift {
                        arith_feedback,
                        dst,
                        lhs,
                        rhs,
                    });
                }
            } else {
                let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
                generator.put(op::RightShift {
                    arith_feedback,
                    dst,
                    lhs,
                    rhs,
                });
            }
        }
        BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => {
            let arith_feedback = generator.next_arith_feedback();
            generator.put(op::UnsignedRightShift {
                arith_feedback,
                dst,
                lhs,
                rhs,
            });
        }
        BinaryOp::In => generator.put(op::In { dst, lhs, rhs }),
        BinaryOp::InstanceOf => generator.put(op::InstanceOf { dst, lhs, rhs }),
    }
}

/// Convert a property name to the primitive that ToPropertyKey turns into a property key without observable effects,
/// in a register of its own unless it is a constant, which is a primitive already.
pub(super) fn emit_to_primitive_property_key(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, property_name: Operand) -> Operand {
    if property_name.is_constant() {
        return property_name;
    }
    // NB: The name can be the operand of a variable or of `this`, which converting it in place would change.
    let property_key = generator.held_register();
    generator.put(op::ToPrimitiveWithStringHint {
        dst: property_key,
        value: property_name,
    });
    property_key
}

//! What a name means in the code being generated. The first parse left a summary of the bindings of the function: which
//! ones functions nested in it capture, and which ones come up before their declaration. Going through the code in
//! source order, that is all it takes: a name that is not declared by the time it comes up is free.
//!
//! A binding gets its place when its declaration comes up. What has to happen for it at the start of the function goes
//! into a head segment that ends up in front of everything else.

use std::sync::Arc;

use crate::bytecode::executable_data::PendingSharedFunctionData;

use crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceOffset;

use crate::parser::FunctionRow;

use libjs_parser::token::N_DOT_NEW_TARGET;
use libjs_parser::token::N_DOT_SUPER;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Location {
    Local(u32),
    Argument(u32),
    Environment,
    Outer,
    /// The arguments object of a function that reads only `arguments.length` and `arguments[key]` of it, which its frame
    /// answers without the object.
    Frame,
}

/// A binding of the function being generated, or what a free name means.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Binding {
    name: Name,
    location: Location,
    kind: Option<DeclarationKind>,
    is_global: bool,
    /// The block that declares it.
    block: BlockId,
    /// The binding of the same name that this one hides.
    shadowed: Option<BindingId>,
    /// Whether this is what a `catch` clause calls its value.
    is_catch_parameter: bool,
    /// Whether this is of the parameters, which have a scope apart from the body, and has no `var` of the same name yet.
    in_parameters: bool,
    /// Whether this has the name of a parameter of a function with a scope for its parameters.
    is_parameter: bool,
}

/// What is known of a name in the function being generated.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
struct NameEntry {
    generation: u32,
    binding: Option<BindingId>,
}

/// A binding in the table of the function being generated.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct BindingId(u32);

/// A block of the function being generated, where zero is the function itself.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
struct BlockId(u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct LocalSlot {
    name: Name,
    is_mutable: bool,
    is_lexical: bool,
    /// Where in the source the block that declares it starts and ends, if a block does.
    block_range: Option<(u32, u32)>,
}

/// The name that a function nested in the one being generated gets from around it.
enum NestedFunctionName {
    None,
    Identifier(IdentifierTableIndex),
    /// The initializer of a field, with what the field is called if that is known and whether that is a private name.
    Field(Option<ak::Utf16String>, bool),
}

/// A function nested in the one being generated.
struct NestedFunction {
    row: u32,
    name: NestedFunctionName,
    /// What the function sees of environments if it is in the environment of a scope, which only it sees.
    environment: Option<Arc<EnclosingEnvironmentScope>>,
    /// Whether the function gets compiled along with the code around it.
    is_eager: bool,
}

/// The bindings of a scope inside a function that exist from the start of the scope, as a range of the summary.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct ScopeBindings {
    position: u32,
    /// Where in the pool of summaries the bindings start.
    start: u32,
    count: u32,
    captured_count: u32,
}

/// What the summary says of a binding that exists from the start of its scope.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ScopeBinding {
    name: Name,
    kind: BindingKind,
    is_captured: bool,
}

/// How the summary tells kinds of bindings apart.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum BindingKind {
    Plain,
    Let,
    Const,
}

impl ScopeBinding {
    #[inline(always)]
    fn from_entry(entry: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: Name(entry >> 3),
            kind: match (entry >> 1) & 3 {
                1 => BindingKind::Let,
                2 => BindingKind::Const,
                _ => BindingKind::Plain,
            },
            is_captured: entry & 1 != 0,
        }
    }
}

/// A simple parameter, including repeated occurrences of the same binding.
struct SimpleParameter {
    name: Name,
    is_captured: bool,
    is_first: bool,
}

/// What `declare_parameters()` has to know of a parameter that is more than a name.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct ParameterShape {
    /// How many names it binds.
    pub(super) name_count: u32,
    /// Whether it binds one name in the place of its argument, which a default or being a rest parameter leaves it at.
    pub(super) is_name: bool,
    /// Whether anything gets evaluated in it.
    pub(super) has_expression: bool,
}

/// What the top level of a program does with names, which is what declaration instantiation sees to.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum ProgramKind {
    /// A name that nothing binds is global.
    Script,
    /// A name that nothing binds is up to the environments around the code.
    WithoutGlobals,
    /// A name is in the environment of the module, or else global.
    Module,
}

/// The names of the function being generated, which keep their memory for the next function on the thread.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CodeScope {
    pub(super) is_active: bool,
    row: u32,
    /// The flags of the function, or what stands for them at the top level.
    flags: u32,
    /// What the code is, if it is the top level of a program.
    program: Option<ProgramKind>,
    /// Whether the next nested function is one to compile right away.
    next_function_is_eager: bool,
    generation: u32,
    entries: Vec<NameEntry>,
    bindings: Vec<Binding>,
    /// Where the bindings of the open blocks start, as indices of `bindings`, and the block around each.
    block_starts: Vec<(u32, BlockId)>,
    next_block: BlockId,
    current_block: BlockId,
    locals: Vec<LocalSlot>,
    parameters: Vec<(Name, bool)>,
    /// What is left of the bitmap of the summary, as a range of its bytes in the index, and the next bit.
    bitmap_start: usize,
    bitmap_end: usize,
    next_bit: usize,
    environment_binding_count: u32,
    /// Simple parameters in source order, including duplicates for mapped arguments.
    simple_parameters: Vec<SimpleParameter>,
    /// Whether the body has a scope of its own, apart from the parameters.
    has_parameter_scope: bool,
    /// hasParamExprs of FunctionDeclarationInstantiation: whether a parameter has a default or a computed key.
    has_parameter_expressions: bool,
    /// Whether a name can still be in the dead zone of a parameter.
    checks_parameters: bool,
    is_in_parameters: bool,
    has_function_in_parameters: bool,
    parameter_function_count: u32,
    has_mapped_parameters: bool,
    /// What the summary has on bindings that come up early, as a range of it, which waits for the end of the parameters.
    deferred_early_bindings: Option<(usize, usize)>,
    /// Whether nested functions capture a `var` of the name `arguments`, which is the binding of the arguments object.
    var_of_arguments_is_captured: bool,
    /// Whether a lexical declaration of the name `arguments` takes the place of the arguments object.
    has_lexical_arguments: bool,
    /// Whether the frame may answer for the arguments object, which nothing else needs, unless the parameters say
    /// otherwise.
    may_read_arguments_from_frame: bool,
    /// What the arguments object would be, if the frame answers for it.
    arguments_from_frame: Option<ArgumentsKind>,
    /// Whether a call of the function creates an environment of its own, which the environment coordinates count.
    has_function_environment: bool,
    /// Whether the lexical declarations of the function have an environment of their own.
    has_lexical_environment: bool,
    /// Whether the parameters have an environment of their own, for what an `eval` in them declares.
    has_parameter_expressions_with_eval: bool,
    /// How many of the bindings are in the function environment, if the body has a variable environment of its own.
    function_environment_binding_count: Option<u32>,
    /// The scopes with bindings that exist from their start, by position.
    scope_bindings: Vec<ScopeBindings>,
    /// How many environments of scopes are open.
    scope_environment_depth: u32,
    /// How many `with` statements are around the code.
    with_depth: u32,
    /// What functions nested in scopes see of the bindings of those scopes, which are gone by the end of the function.
    scope_resolutions: Vec<(u64, Resolution)>,
    nested_functions: Vec<NestedFunction>,
    /// The memory of what `sweep_parameter_names()` puts together.
    pub(super) spare_parameter_names: Vec<Name>,
    pub(super) spare_parameter_shapes: Vec<ParameterShape>,
    /// What a name means that no scope around the function binds, once something asked.
    unbound: Option<Resolution>,
}

impl CodeScope {
    pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
        if !self.is_active {
            return;
        }
        self.is_active = false;
        self.bindings.clear();
        self.block_starts.clear();
        self.locals.clear();
        self.parameters.clear();
        self.nested_functions.clear();
        self.scope_bindings.clear();
        self.scope_resolutions.clear();
        self.scope_environment_depth = 0;
        self.with_depth = 0;
        self.unbound = None;
        self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);
        if self.generation == 0 {
            self.entries.fill(NameEntry::default());
            self.generation = 1;
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn entry(&mut self, name: Name) -> &mut NameEntry {
        let index = name.0 as usize;
        if index >= self.entries.len() {
            self.entries
                .resize((index + 1).next_power_of_two(), NameEntry::default());
        }
        &mut self.entries[index]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn binding_of(&mut self, name: Name) -> Option<BindingId> {
        let generation = self.generation;
        let entry = self.entry(name);
        if entry.generation == generation {
            entry.binding
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn binding(&self, id: BindingId) -> Binding {
        self.bindings[id.0 as usize]
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn add_binding(&mut self, binding: Binding) -> BindingId {
        let id = BindingId(u32_from_usize(self.bindings.len()));
        self.bindings.push(binding);
        let generation = self.generation;
        *self.entry(binding.name) = NameEntry {
            generation,
            binding: Some(id),
        };
        id
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_local_lexical(&self, index: u32) -> bool {
        self.locals.get(index as usize).is_some_and(|local| local.is_lexical)
    }

    pub(super) fn local_count(&self) -> u32 {
        u32_from_usize(self.locals.len())
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn has_simple_parameters(&self) -> bool {
        self.flags & function_flag::SIMPLE_PARAMETERS != 0
    }

    /// Whether the function, of simple parameters, has none.
    pub(super) fn has_no_simple_parameters(&self) -> bool {
        self.simple_parameters.is_empty()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_program(&self) -> bool {
        self.program.is_some()
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_program_without_globals(&self) -> bool {
        self.program == Some(ProgramKind::WithoutGlobals)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_in_with(&self) -> bool {
        self.with_depth != 0
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(super) fn is_in_block(&self) -> bool {
        self.current_block != BlockId::default()
    }

    pub(super) fn block_begin(&mut self) {
        self.block_starts
            .push((u32_from_usize(self.bindings.len()), self.current_block));
        self.next_block = BlockId(self.next_block.0 + 1);
        self.current_block = self.next_block;
    }

    /// The block that ends here goes from `start` to `end` in the source, which is what a debugger goes by for its locals.
    pub(super) fn note_block_range(&mut self, start: u32, end: u32) {
        let first_binding = self.block_starts.last().expect("a block is open").0 as usize;
        for binding in &self.bindings[first_binding..] {
            if binding.block == self.current_block
                && let Location::Local(index) = binding.location
            {
                self.locals[index as usize].block_range = Some((start, end));
            }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn block_end(&mut self) {
        let (start, outer_block) = self.block_starts.pop().expect("a block is open");
        // NB: Everything that a block declares goes away with it, and what is left in here are free names and `var`s.
        for index in (start as usize..self.bindings.len()).rev() {
            let binding = self.bindings[index];
            if binding.block == self.current_block {
                let generation = self.generation;
                *self.entry(binding.name) = NameEntry {
                    generation,
                    binding: binding.shadowed,
                };
            }
        }
        self.current_block = outer_block;
    }
}

/// Whether the function at a row with `flags` gets `this` from its environment, which the initializers of a class
/// always do.
fn this_comes_from_environment(flags: u32) -> bool {
    use function_flag::*;
    flags & (SCOPE_THIS_FROM_ENVIRONMENT | INSIGHT_THIS_FROM_ENVIRONMENT | FIELD_INITIALIZER | STATIC_BLOCK) != 0
}

/// Reads a variable length integer of a summary.
#[inline(always)]
fn read_varint(bytes: &[u8], at: &mut usize) -> u32 {
    let mut value = 0u32;
    let mut shift = 0;
    loop {
        let byte = bytes[*at];
        *at += 1;
        value |= u32::from(byte & 0x7F) << shift;
        if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
            return value;
        }
        shift += 7;
    }
}

impl Generator<'_> {
    /// Gets ready for the function at `row`, which the summary says the bindings of.
    pub(super) fn begin_function_scope(&mut self, row: FunctionRow) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let index = &tree.script.index;
        let flags = index.flags[row.0 as usize];
        let (summary_start, summary_end) = index.summary_range(row.0);
        let summary = &index.summaries[summary_start..summary_end];
        self.strict = flags & function_flag::STRICT != 0;
        let this_from_environment = this_comes_from_environment(flags);
        // NB: The this value of a derived constructor is not initialized until it calls super(), which its frame keeps
        //     track of if it has no environment for it.
        self.this_value_needs_resolution = this_from_environment || flags & function_flag::DERIVED_CONSTRUCTOR != 0;
        self.coerces_this = flags & (function_flag::STRICT | function_flag::ARROW) == 0
            && flags & function_flag::INSIGHT_USES_THIS != 0
            && !self.this_value_needs_resolution;
        self.enclosing_function_kind = FunctionKind::from_async_generator(
            flags & function_flag::ASYNC != 0,
            flags & function_flag::GENERATOR != 0,
        );
        self.creates_environment = false;
        self.contains_direct_call_to_eval_in_non_strict_mode =
            flags & function_flag::DIRECT_EVAL != 0 && flags & function_flag::STRICT == 0;
        let is_arrow = flags & function_flag::ARROW != 0;

        self.reset_scope(row.0, flags, None);
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;

        let mut at = 0;
        let early_count = if summary.is_empty() {
            0
        } else {
            read_varint(summary, &mut at)
        };
        let early_start = at;
        let mut has_captures = false;
        let mut has_var_of_arguments = false;
        let mut declares_arguments = false;
        for _ in 0..early_count {
            let early = ScopeBinding::from_entry(read_varint(summary, &mut at));
            has_captures |= early.is_captured;
            declares_arguments |= early.name.0 == N_ARGUMENTS;
            if early.name.0 == N_ARGUMENTS && flags & function_flag::SIMPLE_PARAMETERS != 0 {
                if early.kind == BindingKind::Plain {
                    has_var_of_arguments = true;
                    scope.var_of_arguments_is_captured = early.is_captured;
                } else {
                    scope.has_lexical_arguments = true;
                }
            }
        }
        let early_end = at;
        if !summary.is_empty() {
            read_scope_bindings(&mut scope.scope_bindings, summary, summary_start, &mut at);
        }
        has_captures |= at < summary.len();
        scope.bitmap_start = summary_start + at;
        scope.bitmap_end = summary_end;

        use function_flag::*;
        let is_simple = flags & SIMPLE_PARAMETERS != 0;
        let is_mapped = is_simple && flags & STRICT == 0;
        // NB: The frame keeps the values that were passed, which the parameters of an unmapped arguments object must not
        //     overwrite. Generators and async functions keep the object, as their frames get suspended.
        let may_read_arguments_from_frame = !is_arrow
            && !declares_arguments
            && flags & ARGUMENTS_FROM_FRAME != 0
            && flags & (USES_ARGUMENTS | MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS) != 0
            && flags
                & (CAPTURES_ARGUMENTS
                    | CONTAINS_EVAL
                    | GENERATOR
                    | ASYNC
                    | FIELD_INITIALIZER
                    | STATIC_BLOCK
                    | DEFAULT_CONSTRUCTOR)
                == 0
            && (is_mapped || flags & READS_ARGUMENTS_INDEX == 0 || (is_simple && flags & MAY_WRITE_PARAMETERS == 0));
        self.context.scope.may_read_arguments_from_frame = may_read_arguments_from_frame;

        self.begin_stream();
        self.begin_head();
        self.put(op::Enter {});
        let needs_function_environment = has_captures
            || flags & function_flag::CONTAINS_EVAL != 0
            || (!is_arrow && this_from_environment)
            || (!is_arrow
                && flags & function_flag::CAPTURES_ARGUMENTS != 0
                && flags & (function_flag::MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS | function_flag::USES_ARGUMENTS) != 0)
            || (!is_arrow
                && !may_read_arguments_from_frame
                && flags & function_flag::ARGUMENTS_ACCESS != 0
                && flags & function_flag::SIMPLE_PARAMETERS != 0
                && index.parameter_count[row.0 as usize] != 0);
        self.context.scope.has_function_environment = needs_function_environment;
        self.capture_saved_lexical_environment_with_coordinates(needs_function_environment);
        self.end_head();
        self.begin_stream_temporaries();

        if flags & (FIELD_INITIALIZER | STATIC_BLOCK | DEFAULT_CONSTRUCTOR) == 0
            && (flags & SIMPLE_PARAMETERS == 0
                || self.contains_direct_call_to_eval_in_non_strict_mode
                || (has_var_of_arguments && !is_arrow))
        {
            // NB: The parameters do not see what is in the body, and what an `eval` declares has to clash with `let`.
            //     A `var` of the name `arguments` has to find the arguments object.
            let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
            scope.is_in_parameters = true;
            scope.deferred_early_bindings = Some((summary_start + early_start, summary_start + early_end));
        } else {
            self.declare_early_bindings(summary_start + early_start, summary_start + early_end);
        }
    }

    fn reset_scope(&mut self, row: u32, flags: u32, program: Option<ProgramKind>) {
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
        scope.is_active = true;
        scope.row = row;
        scope.flags = flags;
        scope.program = program;
        scope.next_function_is_eager = false;
        scope.next_block = BlockId::default();
        scope.current_block = BlockId::default();
        scope.environment_binding_count = 0;
        scope.has_parameter_scope = false;
        scope.has_parameter_expressions = false;
        scope.checks_parameters = false;
        scope.is_in_parameters = false;
        scope.has_function_in_parameters = false;
        scope.parameter_function_count = 0;
        scope.var_of_arguments_is_captured = false;
        scope.has_lexical_arguments = false;
        scope.may_read_arguments_from_frame = false;
        scope.arguments_from_frame = None;
        scope.has_function_environment = false;
        scope.has_mapped_parameters = false;
        scope.deferred_early_bindings = None;
        scope.has_parameter_expressions_with_eval = false;
        scope.has_lexical_environment = false;
        scope.function_environment_binding_count = None;
        scope.next_bit = 0;
        if scope.generation == 0 {
            scope.generation = 1;
        }
    }

    /// Gets ready for the top level of a program, whose own declarations are up to declaration instantiation.
    pub(super) fn begin_program_scope(&mut self, kind: ProgramKind, is_async_module: bool) {
        let script = self.tree.script.clone();
        let index = &script.index;
        let summary = &index.summaries[..index.program_summary_end as usize];
        self.creates_environment = false;
        let flags = if index.program_has_direct_eval {
            function_flag::DIRECT_EVAL
        } else {
            0
        };
        self.reset_scope(u32::MAX, flags, Some(kind));
        if !summary.is_empty() {
            let mut at = 0;
            read_varint(summary, &mut at);
            read_scope_bindings(&mut self.context.scope.scope_bindings, summary, 0, &mut at);
        }
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
        scope.bitmap_start = 0;
        scope.bitmap_end = 0;

        self.begin_stream();
        self.begin_head();
        self.put(op::Enter {});
        self.capture_saved_lexical_environment_with_coordinates(is_async_module);
        self.end_head();
        self.begin_stream_temporaries();
        if !is_async_module {
            self.begin_completion();
        }
    }

    /// The function about to come up gets compiled along with the code around it.
    pub(super) fn note_next_function_is_eager(&mut self) {
        self.context.scope.next_function_is_eager = true;
    }

    /// What the summary says comes up before its declaration, which then finds it here.
    fn declare_early_bindings(&mut self, mut at: usize, end: usize) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let summaries = &tree.script.index.summaries;
        while at < end {
            let early = ScopeBinding::from_entry(read_varint(summaries, &mut at));
            if early.kind != BindingKind::Plain {
                self.add_early_lexical_binding(early);
                continue;
            }
            let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
            let existing = scope
                .binding_of(early.name)
                .filter(|&binding| scope.binding(binding).location != Location::Outer);
            match existing {
                Some(parameter) if scope.binding(parameter).in_parameters => {
                    self.add_var_of_parameter(parameter, early.is_captured);
                }
                Some(_) => {}
                None => {
                    self.add_var_binding(early.name, early.is_captured, None);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// A scope inside the function starts at `position`, and its environment if it needs one.
    pub(super) fn begin_scope(&mut self, position: u32, is_catch: bool) -> Option<ScopeEnvironment> {
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
        scope.block_begin();
        if scope.scope_bindings.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let bindings = self.scope_bindings_at(position)?;
        self.declare_scope_bindings(bindings);
        (bindings.captured_count != 0).then(|| self.enter_scope_environment(bindings, is_catch, None))
    }

    pub(super) fn end_scope(&mut self, environment: Option<ScopeEnvironment>) {
        if let Some(environment) = environment {
            self.leave_scope_environment(environment);
        }
        self.context.scope.block_end();
    }

    pub(super) fn scope_bindings_at(&self, position: u32) -> Option<ScopeBindings> {
        let scopes = &self.context.scope.scope_bindings;
        let index = scopes
            .binary_search_by_key(&position, |bindings| bindings.position)
            .ok()?;
        Some(scopes[index])
    }

    /// Calls `callback` with what the summary says of each binding of a scope.
    fn for_each_scope_binding(&mut self, bindings: ScopeBindings, mut callback: impl FnMut(&mut Self, ScopeBinding)) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let summaries = &tree.script.index.summaries;
        let mut at = bindings.start as usize;
        for _ in 0..bindings.count {
            callback(self, ScopeBinding::from_entry(read_varint(summaries, &mut at)));
        }
    }

    /// The bindings of a scope that exist from its start get their place. Those in locals are in their dead zone, whatever
    /// a run through the scope before left in them.
    fn declare_scope_bindings(&mut self, bindings: ScopeBindings) {
        self.for_each_scope_binding(bindings, |generator, binding| {
            let scope = &mut generator.context.scope;
            let location = if binding.is_captured {
                Location::Environment
            } else {
                let index = scope.local_count();
                scope.locals.push(LocalSlot {
                    name: binding.name,
                    is_mutable: binding.kind != BindingKind::Const,
                    is_lexical: binding.kind != BindingKind::Plain,
                    block_range: None,
                });
                Location::Local(index)
            };
            let shadowed = scope.binding_of(binding.name);
            let block = scope.current_block;
            scope.add_binding(Binding {
                name: binding.name,
                location,
                kind: Some(match binding.kind {
                    BindingKind::Const => DeclarationKind::Const,
                    _ => DeclarationKind::Let,
                }),
                is_global: false,
                block,
                shadowed,
                is_catch_parameter: false,
                in_parameters: false,
                is_parameter: false,
            });
            if let Location::Local(index) = location {
                let empty = generator.context.constants.add_empty();
                generator.emit_mov(Operand::local(index), empty);
            }
        });
    }

    /// The code changes the running environment somewhere, so that it has to know the one that it started with.
    fn note_creates_environment(&mut self) {
        if !self.creates_environment {
            self.creates_environment = true;
            self.in_function_head(|generator| {
                generator.put(op::GetLexicalEnvironment {
                    dst: Operand::register(Register::SAVED_LEXICAL_ENVIRONMENT),
                });
            });
        }
    }

    /// Creates the environment of a scope, in `register` if the scope had one before.
    pub(super) fn enter_scope_environment(
        &mut self,
        bindings: ScopeBindings,
        is_catch: bool,
        register: Option<Operand>,
    ) -> ScopeEnvironment {
        self.note_creates_environment();
        let parent = self.current_lexical_environment();
        let held = self.hold_registers();
        let register = register.unwrap_or_else(|| self.held_register());
        let shape_cache = self.next_environment_shape_cache();
        self.put(op::CreateLexicalEnvironment {
            dst: register,
            parent,
            capacity: bindings.captured_count,
            shape_cache,
            is_catch_environment: is_catch,
        });
        self.push_static_lexical_environment(register);
        self.context.scope.scope_environment_depth += 1;
        self.for_each_scope_binding(bindings, |generator, binding| {
            if !binding.is_captured {
                return;
            }
            let identifier = generator.intern_identifier(binding.name);
            let is_const = binding.kind == BindingKind::Const;
            generator.put(op::CreateVariable {
                identifier,
                mode: libjs_abi::EnvironmentMode::Lexical as u8,
                is_immutable: is_const,
                is_global: false,
                is_strict: is_const,
            });
        });
        ScopeEnvironment { register, parent, held }
    }

    pub(super) fn leave_scope_environment(&mut self, environment: ScopeEnvironment) {
        self.pop_tracked_lexical_environment();
        self.context.scope.scope_environment_depth -= 1;
        if !self.is_stream_dead() {
            let parent = environment.parent;
            self.restore_lexical_environment(parent);
        }
        self.release_held_registers(environment.held);
    }

    /// The body of a `with` starts, whose environment is `object`.
    pub(super) fn enter_object_environment(&mut self, object: Operand, held: HeldRegisters) -> ScopeEnvironment {
        self.note_creates_environment();
        let parent = self.current_lexical_environment();
        let register = self.held_register();
        self.put(op::EnterObjectEnvironment { dst: register, object });
        self.push_dynamic_lexical_environment(register);
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
        scope.scope_environment_depth += 1;
        scope.with_depth += 1;
        ScopeEnvironment { register, parent, held }
    }

    pub(super) fn leave_object_environment(&mut self, environment: ScopeEnvironment) {
        self.context.scope.with_depth -= 1;
        self.leave_scope_environment(environment);
    }

    /// Gives a loop a new copy of the environment of its head for the next iteration.
    pub(super) fn copy_scope_environment(&mut self, bindings: ScopeBindings, environment: ScopeEnvironment) {
        let mut names = Vec::with_capacity(bindings.captured_count as usize);
        self.for_each_scope_binding(bindings, |generator, binding| {
            if binding.is_captured {
                let identifier = generator.intern_identifier(binding.name);
                let value = generator.temporary();
                emit_get_binding(generator, value, identifier, false);
                names.push((identifier, value));
            }
        });
        self.pop_tracked_lexical_environment();
        self.context.scope.scope_environment_depth -= 1;
        let parent = environment.parent;
        self.restore_lexical_environment(parent);
        self.enter_scope_environment(bindings, false, Some(environment.register));
        for (identifier, value) in names {
            emit_initialize_lexical_binding(self, identifier, value);
        }
        self.end_of_statement();
    }

    /// A `var` of the body with the name of what `parameter` is, which starts out with the value of that. Without anything
    /// that sees them apart they stay one binding.
    fn add_var_of_parameter(&mut self, parameter: BindingId, is_captured: bool) -> BindingId {
        // 10.2.11 FunctionDeclarationInstantiation ( func, argList ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-functiondeclarationinstantiation
        let scope = &mut self.context.scope;
        let binding = scope.binding(parameter);

        // 29. If hasParamExprs is false, then
        //     a. NOTE: Only a single Environment Record is needed for the parameters and top-level vars.
        //     b. Let instantiatedVariableNames be a copy of the List paramBindings.
        let shares_environment = binding.location == Location::Environment && !scope.has_parameter_expressions;

        // NB: A var with the name of a parameter starts out with its value, so a parameter in a register that nothing
        //     captures is one binding with its var.
        let stays_local = !is_captured && binding.location != Location::Environment;
        if stays_local || shares_environment {
            let binding = &mut scope.bindings[parameter.0 as usize];
            binding.in_parameters = false;
            binding.kind = Some(DeclarationKind::Var);
            return parameter;
        }
        self.add_var_binding(binding.name, is_captured, Some(binding))
    }

    /// A `var` of the function, which starts out as `undefined` or with the value of `parameter`.
    fn add_var_binding(&mut self, name: Name, is_captured: bool, parameter: Option<Binding>) -> BindingId {
        let initial_value = |generator: &mut Self| match parameter.map(|parameter| parameter.location) {
            None => generator.context.constants.add_undefined(),
            Some(Location::Local(index)) => Operand::local(index),
            Some(Location::Argument(index)) => Operand::argument(index),
            Some(_) => {
                let value = generator.temporary();
                let identifier = generator.intern_identifier(name);
                // NB: This runs where the body starts, before any scope around the `var` has an environment.
