//! A sweep over the rows of a tree: one loop over the rows of the body of a function in evaluation order, without
//! recursion. Children come before their parents, and the parser left mark rows where something has to happen before a
//! parent is reached: after the test of a conditional, say. Every row is one call to the emission core in `stream`.
//!
//! What does not happen in the order of its rows has a mark at its start that says where it ends. That goes to `constructs`,
//! which walks it by what it is and comes back here for the pieces of code in it.

use libjs_abi::FunctionNamePrefix;

use crate::ast::AssignmentOp;
use crate::ast::BinaryOp;
use crate::ast::DeclarationKind;
use crate::ast::Name;
use crate::ast::SyntaxTree;
use crate::ast::UnaryOp;
use crate::bytecode::instruction::typed as op;
use crate::bytecode::operand::IdentifierTableIndex;
use crate::bytecode::operand::Operand;
use crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceOffset;
use libjs_parser::base::OutOfStack;
use libjs_parser::columns::NONE;
use libjs_parser::columns::function_flag;
use libjs_parser::columns::tag;
use libjs_parser::token::N_ARGUMENTS;
use libjs_parser::token::N_PROTO;

use super::context::Generator;
use super::nodes::*;
use super::stream::TargetBinding;
use super::stream::ValKind;
use crate::bytecode::constant_fold::ascii_code_units_to_string;

/// The operator of an assignment that also computes something.
pub(super) fn binary_operator_of_assignment(operator: AssignmentOp) -> Option<BinaryOp> {
    Some(match operator {
        AssignmentOp::AdditionAssignment => BinaryOp::Addition,
        AssignmentOp::SubtractionAssignment => BinaryOp::Subtraction,
        AssignmentOp::MultiplicationAssignment => BinaryOp::Multiplication,
        AssignmentOp::DivisionAssignment => BinaryOp::Division,
        AssignmentOp::ModuloAssignment => BinaryOp::Modulo,
        AssignmentOp::ExponentiationAssignment => BinaryOp::Exponentiation,
        AssignmentOp::BitwiseAndAssignment => BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd,
        AssignmentOp::BitwiseOrAssignment => BinaryOp::BitwiseOr,
        AssignmentOp::BitwiseXorAssignment => BinaryOp::BitwiseXor,
        AssignmentOp::LeftShiftAssignment => BinaryOp::LeftShift,
        AssignmentOp::RightShiftAssignment => BinaryOp::RightShift,
        AssignmentOp::UnsignedRightShiftAssignment => BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// The tag after `row`, parentheses aside, which is what decides what `row` is for.
#[inline(always)]
pub(super) fn next_tag(tags: &[u8], row: usize) -> u8 {
    let mut next = row + 1;
    while tags[next] == tag::PAREN {
        next += 1;
    }
    tags[next]
}

/// Generates the body of `function`.
pub(super) fn sweep_function_body(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, function: NodeId) -> Result<(), OutOfStack> {
    let tree = generator.tree;
    let function_tree = tree.node_a(function);
    let first_row = tree.extra_at(function_tree + 7) as usize;
    let is_expression_body = tree.extra_at(function_tree + 6) != 0;
    let last_row = function.0 as usize;
    if generator.is_in_generator_function() {
        // NB: The code of a generator starts when something asks for its first value.
        let start = generator.new_label();
        generator.reference_label(start);
        let undefined = generator.context.constants.add_undefined();
        generator.put(op::Yield {
            continuation_label: Some(start),
            value: undefined,
        });
        generator.bind_label(start);
    }
    generator.sweep_rows(first_row, last_row)?;
    generator.end_disposal();
    if is_expression_body {
        generator.current_source_offset = SourceOffset(tree.ast.pos[last_row]);
        generator.return_statement(true);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Generates the top level of a program.
pub(super) fn sweep_program(generator: &mut Generator<'_>, program: NodeId) -> Result<(), OutOfStack> {
    generator.sweep_rows(1, program.index())?;
    generator.end_disposal();
    Ok(())
}

impl Generator<'_> {
    /// Goes through the rows from `first_row` up to `end_row`, which are all of some piece of code.
    pub(super) fn sweep_rows(&mut self, first_row: usize, end_row: usize) -> Result<(), OutOfStack> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let tags = tree.ast.tag;
        let positions = tree.ast.pos;
        let a_column = tree.ast.a;
        let b_column = tree.ast.b;
        let mut declaration_kind = DeclarationKind::Var;
        let mut declared_ident = None;
        let mut declared_resource = None;

        let mut row = first_row;
        while row < end_row {
            // SAFETY: All columns have a row for every node of the tree, and `end_row` is at most one past the last.
            let (row_tag, a, b, position) = unsafe {
                (
                    *tags.get_unchecked(row),
                    *a_column.get_unchecked(row),
                    *b_column.get_unchecked(row),
                    *positions.get_unchecked(row),
                )
            };
            let node = NodeId(row as u32);
            self.current_source_offset = SourceOffset(position);
            match row_tag {
                tag::IDENT => {
                    if let Some(kind) = (a == N_ARGUMENTS).then(|| self.arguments_from_frame()).flatten() {
                        self.value_of_arguments_from_frame(kind);
                    } else {
                        let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                        self.value_of_identifier(ident);
                    }
                }
                tag::IDENT_CALLEE => {
                    let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                    if self.builtin_abstract_operations_enabled
                        && ident.is_global
                        && ident.declaration_kind.is_none()
                        && self.is_builtin_operation(ident.name)
                    {
                        self.callee_of_builtin_operation(ident.name);
                    } else {
                        self.callee_of_identifier(ident, SourceOffset(b));
                    }
                }
                tag::IDENT_TARGET => {
                    let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                    self.target_of_identifier(ident, TargetBinding::MightAppear);
                }
                tag::IDENT_READ_TARGET => {
                    let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                    self.target_of_identifier(ident, TargetBinding::Known);
                    self.read_target(Some(ident));
                }
                tag::IDENT_DECLARATION => {
                    declaration_kind = declaration_kind_of_mark(b);
                    declared_resource = resource_of_mark(b);
                    if let Some(is_async) = declared_resource {
                        self.begin_disposal(is_async);
                    }
                    let ident = self.declare_binding(Name(a), declaration_kind);
                    // NB: A `var` without an initializer does nothing, not even resolve its name.
                    if declaration_kind != DeclarationKind::Var || tags[row + 1] != tag::DECLARATOR {
                        self.target_of_declaration(ident);
                    }
                    declared_ident = Some(ident);
                }
                tag::IDENT_TYPEOF => {
                    let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                    self.value_of_typeof_identifier(ident, SourceOffset(b));
                }
                tag::IDENT_DELETE => {
                    let ident = self.identifier_of(Name(a));
                    self.value_of_delete_identifier(ident);
                }
                tag::IDENT_KEY | tag::STR_KEY | tag::NUM_KEY => {}
                tag::MEMBER => self.value_of_member(Name(b)),
                tag::MEMBER_CALLEE => self.callee_of_member(Name(b)),
                tag::MEMBER_TARGET | tag::MEMBER_DELETE => self.target_of_member(Name(b)),
                tag::MEMBER_READ_TARGET => {
                    self.target_of_member(Name(b));
                    self.read_target(None);
                }
                tag::INDEX => self.value_of_index(),
                tag::INDEX_CALLEE => self.callee_of_index(),
                tag::INDEX_TARGET | tag::INDEX_DELETE => self.target_of_index(),
                tag::INDEX_READ_TARGET => {
                    self.target_of_index();
                    self.read_target(None);
                }
                tag::NUM => self.value_of_number(tree.number_value(node)),
                tag::STR => {
                    let operand = match tree.string_literal_text(node) {
                        StringLiteralText::Source(text) => self.add_constant_string_view(text),
                        StringLiteralText::Processed(value) => self.context.constants.add_string(value),
                    };
                    self.value_of_constant(operand);
                }
                tag::TRUE => {
                    let operand = self.context.constants.add_boolean(true);
                    self.value_of_constant(operand);
                }
                tag::FALSE => {
                    let operand = self.context.constants.add_boolean(false);
                    self.value_of_constant(operand);
                }
                tag::NULL => {
                    let operand = self.context.constants.add_null();
                    self.value_of_constant(operand);
                }
                tag::HOLE => {
                    let operand = self.context.constants.add_empty();
                    self.value_of_constant(operand);
                }
                tag::REGEX => {
                    let pattern = tree.source_range_units(positions[row] + 1, a);
                    let flags = tree.source_range_units(a + 1, b);
                    let source_index = self.intern_string_text(pattern);
                    let flags_index = self.intern_string_text(flags);
                    self.value_of_regular_expression(source_index, flags_index);
                }
                tag::THIS => self.value_of_this(),
                tag::PAREN => {}
                tag::CALL | tag::OPT_CALL => self.call(tree.node_list(b).len()),
                tag::NEW => self.construct(tree.node_list(b).len()),
                tag::CALL_ARRAY => self.call_with_array(),
                tag::CALL_DIRECT_EVAL => self.direct_eval(tree.node_list(b).len()),
                tag::CALL_DIRECT_EVAL_ARRAY => self.direct_eval_with_array(),
                tag::NEW_ARRAY => self.construct_with_array(),
                tag::ARRAY_SPREAD => {}
                tag::MARK_ARRAY_START => self.array_begin(a as usize),
                tag::SPREAD => self.append_element(true),
                tag::MARK_APPEND => self.append_element(false),
                tag::OBJECT_SPREAD => self.object_spread(),
                tag::MARK_OPTIONAL => self.optional_link(a != 0),
                tag::CHAIN => {
                    if self.top_value_kind() == ValKind::Callee {
                        self.chain_end_of_callee();
                    } else {
                        let is_delete = self.is_top_value_target();
                        if is_delete {
                            self.delete_target();
                        }
                        self.chain_end(is_delete);
                    }
                }
                tag::PRIVATE_NAME => self.value_of_constant(Operand::invalid()),
                tag::SUPER => self.value_of_super_this(),
                tag::SUPER_CALLEE => self.value_of_super_constructor(),
                tag::SUPER_CALL => {
                    let arguments = tree.node_list(b);
                    if arguments.len() <= super::inline_argument_limit(self.builtin_abstract_operations_enabled)
                        && !arguments.iter().any(|argument| tree.node_tag(argument) == tag::SPREAD)
                    {
                        self.super_call_with_operands(arguments.len());
                    } else {
                        self.super_call();
                    }
                }
                tag::SUPER_MEMBER => self.value_of_super_property(Some(Name(b)), false),
                tag::SUPER_MEMBER_CALLEE => self.value_of_super_property(Some(Name(b)), true),
                tag::SUPER_MEMBER_TARGET | tag::SUPER_MEMBER_DELETE => self.target_of_super_property(Some(Name(b))),
                tag::SUPER_MEMBER_READ_TARGET => {
                    self.target_of_super_property(Some(Name(b)));
                    self.read_target(None);
                }
                tag::SUPER_INDEX => self.value_of_super_property(None, false),
                tag::SUPER_INDEX_CALLEE => self.value_of_super_property(None, true),
                tag::SUPER_INDEX_TARGET | tag::SUPER_INDEX_DELETE => self.target_of_super_property(None),
                tag::SUPER_INDEX_READ_TARGET => {
                    self.target_of_super_property(None);
                    self.read_target(None);
                }
                tag::PRIVATE_MEMBER | tag::OPT_PRIVATE_MEMBER => self.value_of_private_member(Name(b)),
                tag::PRIVATE_MEMBER_CALLEE => self.callee_of_private_member(Name(b)),
                tag::PRIVATE_MEMBER_TARGET => self.target_of_private_member(Name(b)),
                tag::PRIVATE_MEMBER_READ_TARGET => {
                    self.target_of_private_member(Name(b));
                    self.read_target(None);
                }
                tag::NEW_TARGET => self.value_of_new_target(),
                tag::IMPORT_META => self.value_of_import_meta(),
                tag::IMPORT_CALL => self.import_call(b != 0),
                tag::DEBUGGER => self.put(op::Debugger {}),
                tag::BIGINT => {
                    let literal = tree.source_range_units(positions[row], a);
                    let digits = crate::ast::bigint_literal_digits(literal);
                    self.value_of_bigint(ascii_code_units_to_string(digits).expect("the digits of a BigInt are ASCII"));
                }
                tag::TAGGED_TEMPLATE => {
                    let elements = tree.node_list(tree.node_a(NodeId(b))).len();
                    self.call(elements / 2 + 1);
                }
                tag::MARK_LOGICAL_ASSIGNMENT => {
                    self.logical_assignment_after_read(logical_operator_of_assignment(a as u8));
                }
                tag::OPT_MEMBER => self.value_of_member(Name(b)),
                tag::OPT_MEMBER_CALLEE => self.callee_of_member(Name(b)),
                tag::OPT_INDEX => self.value_of_index(),
                tag::OPT_INDEX_CALLEE => self.callee_of_index(),
                tag::UNARY => {
                    let operator = tree.unary_operator(node);
                    match operator {
                        UnaryOp::Typeof if tree.node_tag(tree.skip_parens(NodeId(a))) == tag::IDENT_TYPEOF => {}
                        UnaryOp::Delete => match tree.node_tag(tree.skip_parens(NodeId(a))) {
                            tag::IDENT_DELETE => {}
                            tag::CHAIN
                                if matches!(
                                    tree.node_tag(NodeId(tree.node_a(tree.skip_parens(NodeId(a))))),
                                    tag::MEMBER_DELETE | tag::INDEX_DELETE
                                ) => {}
                            _ if self.top_value_kind() == ValKind::Value => self.delete_value(),
                            _ => self.delete_target(),
                        },
                        _ => self.unary(operator),
                    }
                }
                tag::PREFIX_UPDATE | tag::POSTFIX_UPDATE => {
                    if self.top_value_kind() == ValKind::InvalidTarget {
                        self.result_of_invalid_target();
                        row += 1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    let value_is_used = (next_tag(tags, row) != tag::EXPR_STMT || self.tracks_completion())
                        && !self.is_unused_value_row(row);
                    self.update(tree.update_operator(node), row_tag == tag::PREFIX_UPDATE, value_is_used);
                }
                tag::CONDITIONAL => self.conditional_end(),
                tag::MARK_CONDITIONAL_TEST => self.conditional_after_test(),
                tag::MARK_CONDITIONAL_ELSE => self.conditional_after_consequent(),
                tag::MARK_LOGICAL => self.logical_after_left(logical_operator_of_mark(a)),
                tag::SEQUENCE => self.sequence(tree.node_list(a).len()),
                tag::ARRAY => self.array(tree.node_list(a).len()),
                tag::MARK_OBJECT => self.object_begin(a != 0),
                tag::OBJECT => self.object_end(),
                tag::PROPERTY | tag::SHORTHAND => {
                    let key = if row_tag == tag::SHORTHAND {
                        self.intern_property_key(Name(a))
                    } else {
                        let key = NodeId(a);
                        if is_proto_key(tree, key) {
                            self.object_prototype_property();
                            row += 1;
                            continue;
                        }
                        match tree.node_tag(key) {
                            tag::IDENT_KEY => self.intern_property_key(Name(tree.node_a(key))),
                            tag::STR_KEY => {
                                let text = tree.string_literal_text(key);
                                self.intern_property_key_text(text.view())
                            }
                            tag::NUM_KEY => {
                                self.object_number_property(tree.number_value(key), libjs_abi::PutKind::Own);
                                row += 1;
                                continue;
                            }
                            _ => {
                                self.sweep_computed_property(b);
                                row += 1;
                                continue;
                            }
                        }
                    };
                    self.object_property(key);
                }
                tag::COMPUTED_PROPERTY => self.sweep_computed_property(b),
                tag::METHOD | tag::GETTER | tag::SETTER => {
                    let key = NodeId(a);
                    let kind = put_kind_of_method(row_tag);
                    let property_key = match tree.node_tag(key) {
                        tag::IDENT_KEY => self.intern_property_key(Name(tree.node_a(key))),
                        tag::STR_KEY => {
                            let text = tree.string_literal_text(key);
                            self.intern_property_key_text(text.view())
                        }
                        tag::NUM_KEY => {
                            self.object_number_property(tree.number_value(key), kind);
                            row += 1;
                            continue;
                        }
                        _ => {
                            self.object_computed_method(kind, function_name_prefix_of_method(row_tag));
                            row += 1;
                            continue;
                        }
                    };
                    self.object_put_by_id(property_key, kind);
                }
                tag::COMPUTED_METHOD | tag::COMPUTED_GETTER | tag::COMPUTED_SETTER => {
                    let (kind, prefix) = match row_tag {
                        tag::COMPUTED_GETTER => (libjs_abi::PutKind::Getter, FunctionNamePrefix::Get),
                        tag::COMPUTED_SETTER => (libjs_abi::PutKind::Setter, FunctionNamePrefix::Set),
                        _ => (libjs_abi::PutKind::Own, FunctionNamePrefix::None),
                    };
                    self.object_computed_method(kind, prefix);
                }
                tag::MARK_COMPUTED_KEY => self.object_computed_key(),
                tag::FUNCTION => {
                    if tags[row + 1] == tag::FUNCTION_DECL {
                        if self.context.scope.is_in_block() {
                            self.function_declaration_in_block(Name(b_column[row + 1]));
                        } else {
                            self.function_declaration(Name(b_column[row + 1]), b);
                        }
                    } else if (tag::METHOD..=tag::COMPUTED_SETTER).contains(&tags[row + 1]) {
                        self.sweep_object_method(b, row);
                    } else {
                        self.sweep_function_expression(node, row);
                    }
                }
                tag::FUNCTION_DECL => {}
                tag::EXPR_STMT => self.end_of_expression_statement(),
                tag::DECLARATOR => {
                    let ident = declared_ident.take().expect("a declarator comes after its name");
                    self.declare(ident, b != 0, declaration_kind, declared_resource);
                }
                tag::VAR | tag::LET | tag::CONST | tag::USING | tag::AWAIT_USING | tag::EMPTY => {}
                tag::MARK_IF_TEST => {
                    self.reset_completion();
                    self.if_after_test();
                }
                tag::MARK_ELSE => self.if_else(),
                tag::IF => self.if_end(),
                tag::MARK_LOOP_HEAD => {
                    self.reset_completion();
                    self.while_head();
                }
                tag::MARK_WHILE_TEST => self.while_after_test(),
                tag::WHILE => self.while_end(),
                tag::MARK_DO_HEAD => {
                    self.reset_completion();
                    self.do_head();
                }
                tag::MARK_DO_TEST => self.do_before_test(),
                tag::DO_WHILE => self.do_end(),
                tag::MARK_BLOCK => {
                    self.block_begin(a);
                    if b != 0 {
                        self.instantiate_functions_of_block(NodeId(b));
                    }
                }
                tag::BLOCK => {
                    self.context.scope.note_block_range(position, tree.end_of_block(node.0));
                    self.block_end();
                }
                tag::IF_FUNCTION_BLOCK => self.block_end(),
                tag::RETURN => self.return_statement(a != 0),
                tag::THROW => self.throw_statement(),
                tag::AWAIT => self.await_value(),
                tag::YIELD => self.yield_value(a != 0, false),
                tag::YIELD_STAR => self.yield_value(true, true),
                tag::BREAK => self.break_statement((a != NONE).then_some(Name(a))),
                tag::CONTINUE => self.continue_statement((a != NONE).then_some(Name(a))),
                // NB: Anything but a pattern that a mark for a target still stands alone for is nothing that can be written.
                tag::MARK_TARGET | tag::MARK_READ_TARGET
                    if !matches!(tags[row - 1], tag::ARRAY_PATTERN | tag::OBJECT_PATTERN) =>
                {
                    self.invalid_target();
                }
                tag::MARK_KEY if tags[row - 1] == tag::BIGINT => self.object_computed_key(),
                tag::MARK_TARGET
                | tag::MARK_READ_TARGET
                | tag::MARK_CALLEE
                | tag::MARK_DECLARATION
                | tag::MARK_TYPEOF
                | tag::MARK_DELETE
                | tag::MARK_KEY => {}
                tag::MARK_SUBTREE => {
                    // NB: An assignment that turned into an element of a pattern goes by the rows of the pattern.
                    if a != 0 && tags[a as usize] != tag::ASSIGN_PATTERN {
                        self.sweep_subtree(NodeId(a), row, position, b)?;
                        row = a as usize + 1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    // NB: The elements of an array literal come next, each as a value, which can be very many.
                    if a == 0 {
                        self.reserve_values(b as usize);
                    }
                }
                other if (tag::BINARY_BASE..tag::MARK_CALLEE).contains(&other) => {
                    match crate::ast::SyntaxTree::binary_operator(other) {
                        BinaryOrLogical::Binary(BinaryOp::In) if tree.node_tag(NodeId(a)) == tag::PRIVATE_NAME => {
                            self.private_name_in(Name(tree.node_a(NodeId(a))));
                        }
                        BinaryOrLogical::Binary(operator) => self.binary(operator),
                        BinaryOrLogical::Logical(_) => self.logical_end(),
                    }
                }
                other if (tag::ASSIGN_BASE..tag::BINARY_BASE).contains(&other) => self.sweep_assignment(other),
                other => unreachable!("no sweep comes across a row with the tag {other}"),
            }
            row += 1;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn sweep_assignment(&mut self, row_tag: u8) {
        let operator = crate::ast::SyntaxTree::assignment_operator(row_tag);
        if matches!(
            operator,
            AssignmentOp::AndAssignment | AssignmentOp::OrAssignment | AssignmentOp::NullishAssignment
        ) {
            self.logical_assignment_end();
            return;
        }
        if self.is_invalid_target_below_top() {
            self.drop_value();
            self.result_of_invalid_target();
            return;
        }
        if operator == AssignmentOp::Assignment {
            self.assign_to_binding();
            return;
        }
        let operator = binary_operator_of_assignment(operator).expect("the logical ones are handled above");
        self.compound_assign(operator);
    }

    /// The function of a method, a getter or a setter of an object, whose row is `row`.
    fn sweep_object_method(&mut self, function_row: u32, row: usize) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let method_tag = tree.ast.tag[row + 1];
        let key = NodeId(tree.ast.a[row + 1]);
        if matches!(
            method_tag,
            tag::COMPUTED_METHOD | tag::COMPUTED_GETTER | tag::COMPUTED_SETTER
        ) {
            let object = self.object_below(1);
            self.value_of_function_with_text_name(function_row, None, Some(object));
            return;
        }
        if tree.node_tag(key) == tag::BIGINT {
            let object = self.object_below(1);
            self.value_of_function_with_text_name(function_row, None, Some(object));
            return;
        }
        let text = tree.pattern_key_text(key);
        let name = match method_tag {
            tag::GETTER | tag::SETTER => {
                let mut prefixed = crate::utf16::Utf16StringBuilder::new();
                prefixed.append_ascii(if method_tag == tag::GETTER { "get " } else { "set " });
                prefixed.append(text.view());
                let prefixed = prefixed.to_utf16_string();
                self.intern_identifier_text(crate::utf16::Utf16View::of_string(&prefixed))
            }
            _ => self.intern_identifier_text(text.view()),
        };
        let object = self.object_below(0);
        self.value_of_function_with_text_name(function_row, Some(name), Some(object));
    }

    /// `key: value` with a key that only has a value once it gets evaluated, and with both on top of the stack.
    fn sweep_computed_property(&mut self, value: u32) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let value = tree.skip_parens(NodeId(value));
        let is_anonymous_definition = match tree.node_tag(value) {
            tag::FUNCTION => is_anonymous(tree, value),
            // NB: A class has its name before its static elements run, which `NewClass` sees to.
            _ => false,
        };
        self.object_computed_property(is_anonymous_definition);
    }

    fn sweep_function_expression(&mut self, node: NodeId, row: usize) {
        let tree = self.tree;
        if self.eager_compile_direct_iifes && is_called_right_away(tree, row) {
            self.note_next_function_is_eager();
        }
        let function_row = tree.node_b(node);
        let flags = tree.script.index.flags[function_row as usize];
        let has_name = tree.script.index.name[function_row as usize] != NONE && flags & function_flag::METHOD == 0;
        if has_name && flags & function_flag::NAME_UNUSED == 0 {
            self.value_of_named_function_at_row(function_row, Name(tree.script.index.name[function_row as usize]));
            return;
        }
        let name = if has_name {
            None
        } else {
            self.name_of_anonymous_definition(row, row + 1)
        };
        self.value_of_function_with_text_name(function_row, name, None);
    }

    /// The name that an anonymous function or class gets from what it is the value of, if it is all there is of that
    /// value. Its rows go from `row` up to `next_row`.
    pub(super) fn name_of_anonymous_definition(&mut self, row: usize, next_row: usize) -> Option<IdentifierTableIndex> {
        let tree = self.tree;
        let tags = tree.ast.tag;
        if let Some(name) = self.context.stream.pending_function_name.take() {
            return Some(name);
        }
        if row < 2 {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: `async` in front of an arrow function was a reference until the arrow came up.
        let mark_row = if tags[row - 1] == tag::EMPTY { row - 2 } else { row - 1 };
        let next = next_tag(tags, next_row - 1);
        let mark_node = NodeId(mark_row as u32);
        match tags[mark_row] {
            tag::MARK_LOGICAL_ASSIGNMENT
                if tags[mark_row - 1] == tag::IDENT_READ_TARGET
                    && (tag::ASSIGN_BASE..tag::BINARY_BASE).contains(&next) =>
            {
                Some(self.intern_identifier(Name(tree.node_a(NodeId(mark_row as u32 - 1)))))
            }
            tag::IDENT_KEY if next == tag::PROPERTY && is_proto_key(tree, mark_node) => None,
            tag::IDENT_TARGET | tag::IDENT_DECLARATION | tag::IDENT_KEY
                if next == tag::DECLARATOR || next == tag::ASSIGN_BASE || next == tag::PROPERTY =>
            {
                Some(self.intern_identifier(Name(tree.node_a(mark_node))))
            }
            tag::STR_KEY if next == tag::PROPERTY && is_proto_key(tree, mark_node) => None,
            tag::STR_KEY | tag::NUM_KEY if next == tag::PROPERTY => {
                let text = tree.pattern_key_text(mark_node);
                Some(self.intern_identifier_text(text.view()))
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Whether the function expression at `row` is what the code around it calls, directly or through `call` or `apply`.
fn is_called_right_away(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, row: usize) -> bool {
    let mut next = row + 1;
    while tree.ast.tag[next] == tag::PAREN {
        next += 1;
    }
    match tree.ast.tag[next] {
        tag::MARK_CALLEE => true,
        tag::MEMBER_CALLEE => {
            let name = tree.name_text(Name(tree.ast.b[next]));
            name == utf16!("call") || name == utf16!("apply")
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Whether `key` of a property is what makes a property set the prototype.
fn is_proto_key(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, key: NodeId) -> bool {
    match tree.node_tag(key) {
        tag::IDENT_KEY => tree.node_a(key) == N_PROTO,
        tag::STR_KEY => tree.string_literal_text(key).view() == crate::utf16::Utf16View::Ascii(b"__proto__"),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Whether the function at `function` has no name of its own.
pub(super) fn is_anonymous(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, function: NodeId) -> bool {
    tree.script.index.name[tree.node_b(function) as usize] == NONE
}

/// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-static-semantics-isfunctiondefinition
#[inline(always)]
fn is_function_definition(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, expression: NodeId) -> bool {
    matches!(tree.node_tag(expression), tag::FUNCTION | tag::CLASS)
}

/// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-static-semantics-hasname
#[inline(always)]
fn has_name(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, expression: NodeId) -> bool {
    match tree.node_tag(expression) {
        tag::FUNCTION => !is_anonymous(tree, expression),
        tag::CLASS => tree.node_a(expression) != NONE,
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isanonymousfunctiondefinition
pub(super) fn is_anonymous_function_definition(tree: &SyntaxTree<'_>, expression: NodeId) -> bool {
    // NB: IsFunctionDefinition and HasName of a ParenthesizedExpression are those of the expression in it.
    let expression = tree.skip_parens(expression);

    // 1. If IsFunctionDefinition of expr is false, return false.
    if !is_function_definition(tree, expression) {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. Let hasName be HasName of expr.
    // 3. If hasName is true, return false.
    if has_name(tree, expression) {
        return false;
    }

    // 4. Return true.
    true
}

/// The operator of a logical assignment, by the token that it is.
fn logical_operator_of_assignment(token: u8) -> crate::ast::LogicalOp {
    use libjs_parser::token::T;
    if token == T::LogAndAssign as u8 {
        crate::ast::LogicalOp::And
    } else if token == T::LogOrAssign as u8 {
        crate::ast::LogicalOp::Or
    } else {
        crate::ast::LogicalOp::NullishCoalescing
    }
}

fn function_name_prefix_of_method(method_tag: u8) -> FunctionNamePrefix {
    match method_tag {
        tag::GETTER => FunctionNamePrefix::Get,
        tag::SETTER => FunctionNamePrefix::Set,
        _ => FunctionNamePrefix::None,
    }
}

fn put_kind_of_method(method_tag: u8) -> libjs_abi::PutKind {
    match method_tag {
        tag::GETTER => libjs_abi::PutKind::Getter,
        tag::SETTER => libjs_abi::PutKind::Setter,
        _ => libjs_abi::PutKind::Own,
    }
}

pub(super) fn declaration_kind_of_mark(kind: u32) -> DeclarationKind {
    match kind as u8 {
        tag::LET => DeclarationKind::Let,
        tag::CONST | tag::USING | tag::AWAIT_USING => DeclarationKind::Const,
        _ => DeclarationKind::Var,
    }
}

/// Whether what a declaration of the kind of a mark declares is a resource, and if so whether it goes asynchronously.
pub(super) fn resource_of_mark(kind: u32) -> Option<bool> {
    match kind as u8 {
        tag::USING => Some(false),
        tag::AWAIT_USING => Some(true),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn logical_operator_of_mark(operator_tag: u32) -> crate::ast::LogicalOp {
    match crate::ast::SyntaxTree::binary_operator(operator_tag as u8) {
        BinaryOrLogical::Logical(operator) => operator,
        BinaryOrLogical::Binary(_) => unreachable!("the parser marks logical operators"),
    }
}

//! What generating code can work out about constants.

use num_bigint::BigInt;
use num_traits::FromPrimitive;
use num_traits::One;
use num_traits::Zero;

use libjs_abi::value as nan_box;

use crate::ast::BinaryOp;
use crate::ast::UnaryOp;
use crate::lexer::ch;
use crate::utf16::Utf16StringBuilder;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;
use ak::Utf16String;

use super::executable_data::ConstantValue;
use super::operand::Operand;

/// The constants of a generator, as folding sees them.
pub(super) trait ConstantPool {
    fn get_constant(&self, operand: Operand) -> Option<&ConstantValue>;
    fn add_constant_number(&mut self, value: f64) -> Operand;
    fn add_constant_boolean(&mut self, value: bool) -> Operand;
    fn add_constant_string(&mut self, value: Utf16String) -> Operand;
    fn add_constant_bigint(&mut self, value: String) -> Operand;
}

/// Convert a constant value to a boolean, matching JS `ToBoolean`.
/// Returns `None` for VM-specific constants whose truthiness cannot be
/// determined until the Executable is materialized.
pub fn constant_to_boolean(value: &ConstantValue) -> Option<bool> {
    match value {
        ConstantValue::Boolean(b) => Some(*b),
        ConstantValue::Null | ConstantValue::Undefined | ConstantValue::Empty => Some(false),
        ConstantValue::Number(n) => Some(*n != 0.0 && !n.is_nan()),
        ConstantValue::String(s) => Some(!s.is_empty()),
        ConstantValue::BigInt(s) => parse_bigint(s).map(|bi| bi != num_bigint::BigInt::ZERO),
        ConstantValue::WellKnownSymbol(_) | ConstantValue::AbstractOperation(_) => None,
    }
}

/// Parse a BigInt string to an arbitrary-precision BigInt.
/// Handles decimal, 0b binary, 0o octal, and 0x hex prefixes.
pub fn parse_bigint(s: &str) -> Option<num_bigint::BigInt> {
    use num_bigint::BigInt;
    if s.len() > 2 {
        let (prefix, rest) = s.split_at(2);
        match prefix {
            "0b" | "0B" => return BigInt::parse_bytes(rest.as_bytes(), 2),
            "0o" | "0O" => return BigInt::parse_bytes(rest.as_bytes(), 8),
            "0x" | "0X" => return BigInt::parse_bytes(rest.as_bytes(), 16),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    s.parse::<BigInt>().ok()
}

/// Check if a UTF-16 string is a canonical array index (non-negative integer < 2^32 - 1).
/// These strings become integer PropertyKeys,
/// not string PropertyKeys, so they must NOT be optimized to GetById/PutById.
pub(crate) fn is_array_index(s: &[u16]) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() || s.len() > 10 {
        return false;
    }
    // Must not have leading zeros (except "0" itself)
    if s.len() > 1 && s[0] == ch(b'0') {
        return false;
    }
    let mut value: u64 = 0;
    for &c in s {
        if c < ch(b'0') || c > ch(b'9') {
            return false;
        }
        value = value * 10 + (c - ch(b'0')) as u64;
    }
    value <= 0xFFFF_FFFE
}

/// JS ToInt32 conversion (ECMA-262 7.1.6).
pub(super) fn to_int32(n: f64) -> i32 {
    if n.is_nan() || n.is_infinite() || n == 0.0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let int_val = n.signum() * n.abs().floor();
    let int32bit = int_val % 4294967296.0; // 2^32
    let int32bit = if int32bit < 0.0 {
        int32bit + 4294967296.0
    } else {
        int32bit
    };
    if int32bit >= 2147483648.0 {
        (int32bit - 4294967296.0) as i32
    } else {
        int32bit as i32
    }
}

/// JS ToUint32 conversion (ECMA-262 7.1.7).
pub(super) fn to_u32(n: f64) -> u32 {
    if n.is_nan() || n.is_infinite() || n == 0.0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let int_val = n.signum() * n.abs().floor();
    let int32bit = int_val % 4294967296.0; // 2^32
    if int32bit < 0.0 {
        (int32bit + 4294967296.0) as u32
    } else {
        int32bit as u32
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Constant folding
// =============================================================================

/// Try to constant-fold a unary operation when the operand is a constant.
pub(super) fn try_constant_fold_unary<G: ConstantPool>(
    generator: &mut G,
    op: UnaryOp,
    operand: Operand,
) -> Option<Operand> {
    let constant = generator.get_constant(operand)?;
    match op {
        UnaryOp::Minus => {
            let n = constant_to_number(constant)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(-n))
        }
        UnaryOp::Plus => {
            let n = constant_to_number(constant)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(n))
        }
        UnaryOp::BitwiseNot => {
            if let ConstantValue::BigInt(s) = constant {
                let n = parse_bigint(&s.clone())?;
                return Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((-(n + BigInt::one())).to_string()));
            }
            let n = constant_to_number(constant)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((!to_int32(n)) as f64))
        }
        UnaryOp::Not => {
            let as_bool = constant_to_boolean(constant)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(!as_bool))
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Implement IsLooselyEqual for constant values.
/// https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-islooselyequal
fn try_constant_loosely_equals(lhs: &ConstantValue, rhs: &ConstantValue) -> Option<bool> {
    // Same type: use strict equality rules.
    match (lhs, rhs) {
        (ConstantValue::Null | ConstantValue::Undefined, ConstantValue::Null | ConstantValue::Undefined) => {
            return Some(true);
        }
        (ConstantValue::Null | ConstantValue::Undefined, _) | (_, ConstantValue::Null | ConstantValue::Undefined) => {
            return Some(false);
        }
        (ConstantValue::Number(a), ConstantValue::Number(b)) => return Some(a == b),
        (ConstantValue::String(a), ConstantValue::String(b)) => return Some(a == b),
        (ConstantValue::Boolean(a), ConstantValue::Boolean(b)) => return Some(a == b),
        (ConstantValue::BigInt(a), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) => return Some(a == b),
        _ => {}
    }
    // Cross-type comparisons: Boolean → Number first, then retry.
    match (lhs, rhs) {
        (ConstantValue::Boolean(b), _) => {
            let coerced = ConstantValue::Number(if *b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 });
            return try_constant_loosely_equals(&coerced, rhs);
        }
        (_, ConstantValue::Boolean(b)) => {
            let coerced = ConstantValue::Number(if *b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 });
            return try_constant_loosely_equals(lhs, &coerced);
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    // Number == String → compare ToNumber(string) to number.
    // String == Number → compare number to ToNumber(string).
    match (lhs, rhs) {
        (ConstantValue::Number(n), ConstantValue::String(s)) | (ConstantValue::String(s), ConstantValue::Number(n)) => {
            Some(*n == crate::host::string_to_number(&s.to_utf16()))
        }
        // BigInt == Number or Number == BigInt: compare mathematical values.
        (ConstantValue::BigInt(b), ConstantValue::Number(n)) | (ConstantValue::Number(n), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) => {
            if n.is_nan() || n.is_infinite() {
                return Some(false);
            }
            if n.fract() != 0.0 {
                return Some(false);
            }
            let bi = parse_bigint(b)?;
            Some(BigInt::from_f64(*n)? == bi)
        }
        // BigInt == String or String == BigInt: parse string as BigInt per StringToBigInt.
        // If the string cannot be parsed, the result is false (not equal).
        (ConstantValue::BigInt(b), ConstantValue::String(s)) | (ConstantValue::String(s), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) => {
            match crate::host::string_to_bigint(&s.to_utf16()) {
                Some(s_bi) => {
                    let bi = parse_bigint(b)?;
                    Some(bi == s_bi)
                }
                None => Some(false),
            }
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

pub(crate) fn ascii_code_units_to_string(text: Utf16View<'_>) -> Option<String> {
    text.code_units()
        .map(|code_unit| {
            u8::try_from(code_unit)
                .ok()
                .and_then(|byte| byte.is_ascii().then_some(char::from(byte)))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Constant-fold a binary operation on two BigInt operands.
fn try_constant_fold_bigint_binary<G: ConstantPool>(
    generator: &mut G,
    op: BinaryOp,
    a_str: &str,
    b_str: &str,
) -> Option<Operand> {
    let a = parse_bigint(a_str)?;
    let b = parse_bigint(b_str)?;
    match op {
        // Arithmetic operations: produce a BigInt result.
        BinaryOp::Addition => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a + &b).to_string())),
        BinaryOp::Subtraction => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a - &b).to_string())),
        BinaryOp::Multiplication => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a * &b).to_string())),
        BinaryOp::Division => {
            if b.is_zero() {
                return None; // Division by zero throws at runtime.
            }
            use num_integer::Integer;
            let (quotient, _) = a.div_rem(&b);
            Some(generator.add_constant_bigint(quotient.to_string()))
        }
        BinaryOp::Modulo => {
            if b.is_zero() {
                return None; // Modulo by zero throws at runtime.
            }
            // JS BigInt remainder has the sign of the dividend (truncated division).
            Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a % &b).to_string()))
        }
        BinaryOp::Exponentiation => {
            // Only fold small exponents to avoid huge results.
            if b > BigInt::from(1000) {
                return None;
            }
            let result = crate::host::bigint_exponentiate(&a, &b)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_bigint(result.to_string()))
        }
        // Comparison operations: produce a Boolean result.
        BinaryOp::StrictlyEquals | BinaryOp::LooselyEquals => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a == b)),
        BinaryOp::StrictlyInequals | BinaryOp::LooselyInequals => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a != b)),
        BinaryOp::LessThan => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a < b)),
        BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a <= b)),
        BinaryOp::GreaterThan => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a > b)),
        BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals => Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(a >= b)),
        // Bitwise operations on BigInt.
        BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a & &b).to_string())),
        BinaryOp::BitwiseOr => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a | &b).to_string())),
        BinaryOp::BitwiseXor => Some(generator.add_constant_bigint((&a ^ &b).to_string())),
        // Only fold shifts that grow the value a little, to avoid huge results.
        BinaryOp::LeftShift => {
            if b > BigInt::from(512) {
                return None;
            }
            let result = crate::host::bigint_left_shift(&a, &b)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_bigint(result.to_string()))
        }
        BinaryOp::RightShift => {
            if b < BigInt::from(-512) {
                return None;
            }
            let result = crate::host::bigint_signed_right_shift(&a, &b)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_bigint(result.to_string()))
        }
        // UnsignedRightShift throws TypeError for BigInt.
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Convert a constant value to a JS number for constant folding purposes.
fn constant_to_number(val: &ConstantValue) -> Option<f64> {
    match val {
        ConstantValue::Number(n) => Some(*n),
        ConstantValue::Boolean(b) => Some(if *b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }),
        ConstantValue::Null => Some(0.0),
        ConstantValue::Undefined => Some(f64::NAN),
        ConstantValue::String(s) => Some(crate::host::string_to_number(&s.to_utf16())),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Convert a constant value to a JS string (ToString) for string concatenation.
/// Returns None for types where ToString requires runtime (e.g. objects).
pub fn constant_to_string(val: &ConstantValue) -> Option<Utf16String> {
    match val {
        ConstantValue::String(s) => Some(s.clone()),
        ConstantValue::Number(n) => Some(crate::host::js_number_to_utf16(*n)),
        ConstantValue::Boolean(b) => Some(if *b {
            Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("true"))
        } else {
            Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("false"))
        }),
        ConstantValue::Null => Some(Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("null"))),
        ConstantValue::Undefined => Some(Utf16String::from_utf16(utf16!("undefined"))),
        ConstantValue::BigInt(s) => {
            // BigInt.prototype.toString() returns the decimal string representation.
            Some(Utf16String::from_utf8(&parse_bigint(s)?.to_string()))
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Compare a BigInt and a Number using Abstract Relational Comparison semantics.
/// Returns None if comparison cannot be folded (non-safe integer, etc).
/// Returns Some(None) for NaN (undefined result - all comparisons return false).
/// Returns Some(Some(Ordering)) for the BigInt relative to the Number.
fn compare_bigint_and_number(bigint_str: &str, number: f64) -> Option<Option<std::cmp::Ordering>> {
    use std::cmp::Ordering;
    if number.is_nan() {
        return Some(None); // Comparisons with NaN return undefined → false.
    }
    if number == f64::INFINITY {
        return Some(Some(Ordering::Less)); // Any BigInt < +Infinity
    }
    if number == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
        return Some(Some(Ordering::Greater)); // Any BigInt > -Infinity
    }
    let bigint = parse_bigint(bigint_str)?;
    if number.fract() != 0.0 {
        // The number has a fractional part, so we can still compare:
        // floor(number) < bigint means bigint > number, etc.
        let floored = number.floor();
        let floored_bigint = BigInt::from_f64(floored)?;
        if bigint <= floored_bigint {
            // bigint <= floor(number) means bigint < number
            return Some(Some(Ordering::Less));
        } else {
            // bigint > floor(number) means bigint > number (since number = floor + fract where fract > 0)
            return Some(Some(Ordering::Greater));
        }
    }
    let number_bigint = BigInt::from_f64(number)?;
    Some(Some(bigint.cmp(&number_bigint)))
}

/// Try to constant-fold a binary operation when both operands are constants.
pub(super) fn try_constant_fold_binary<G: ConstantPool>(
    generator: &mut G,
    op: BinaryOp,
    lhs: Operand,
    rhs: Operand,
) -> Option<Operand> {
    let lhs_const = generator.get_constant(lhs)?;
    let rhs_const = generator.get_constant(rhs)?;

    // BigInt constant folding: if both operands are BigInt, handle separately.
    // Clone strings to release the immutable borrow on gen before the mutable call.
    if let (ConstantValue::BigInt(a), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) = (lhs_const, rhs_const) {
        let a = a.clone();
        let b = b.clone();
        return try_constant_fold_bigint_binary(generator, op, &a, &b);
    }

    match op {
        BinaryOp::Addition => {
            // If either operand is a string, do string concatenation using ToString.
            if matches!(lhs_const, ConstantValue::String(_)) || matches!(rhs_const, ConstantValue::String(_)) {
                let a = constant_to_string(lhs_const)?;
                let b = constant_to_string(rhs_const)?;
                let mut result = Utf16StringBuilder::new();
                result.append(Utf16View::of_string(&a));
                result.append(Utf16View::of_string(&b));
                return Some(generator.add_constant_string(result.to_utf16_string()));
            }
            // Numeric addition: both operands coerced to number
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(a + b))
        }
        BinaryOp::Subtraction => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(a - b))
        }
        BinaryOp::Multiplication => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(a * b))
        }
        BinaryOp::Division => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(a / b))
        }
        BinaryOp::Modulo => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(a % b))
        }
        BinaryOp::Exponentiation => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number(crate::host::exponentiate(a, b)))
        }
        BinaryOp::StrictlyEquals | BinaryOp::StrictlyInequals => {
            let equal = match (lhs_const, rhs_const) {
                (ConstantValue::Number(a), ConstantValue::Number(b)) => a == b,
                (ConstantValue::String(a), ConstantValue::String(b)) => a == b,
                (ConstantValue::Boolean(a), ConstantValue::Boolean(b)) => a == b,
                (ConstantValue::Null, ConstantValue::Null) => true,
                (ConstantValue::Undefined, ConstantValue::Undefined) => true,
                (ConstantValue::WellKnownSymbol(a), ConstantValue::WellKnownSymbol(b)) => a == b,
                // Different types are never strictly equal.
                _ => false,
            };
            let result = if op == BinaryOp::StrictlyInequals {
                !equal
            } else {
                equal
            };
            Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(result))
        }
        BinaryOp::GreaterThan | BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals | BinaryOp::LessThan | BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => {
            // String-string comparison is lexicographic (by UTF-16 code units).
            if let (ConstantValue::String(a), ConstantValue::String(b)) = (lhs_const, rhs_const) {
                let result = match op {
                    BinaryOp::GreaterThan => a.to_utf16() > b.to_utf16(),
                    BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals => a.to_utf16() >= b.to_utf16(),
                    BinaryOp::LessThan => a.to_utf16() < b.to_utf16(),
                    BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => a.to_utf16() <= b.to_utf16(),
                    _ => unreachable!("outer match arm only matches comparison operators"),
                };
                return Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(result));
            }
            // BigInt-Number/Boolean cross-type comparison.
            // Per spec, Booleans are converted to Number first.
            let lhs_for_cmp = match lhs_const {
                ConstantValue::Boolean(b) => &ConstantValue::Number(if *b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }),
                other => other,
            };
            let rhs_for_cmp = match rhs_const {
                ConstantValue::Boolean(b) => &ConstantValue::Number(if *b { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }),
                other => other,
            };
            // BigInt vs Number comparison using Abstract Relational Comparison.
            let bigint_ord = match (lhs_for_cmp, rhs_for_cmp) {
                (ConstantValue::BigInt(b), ConstantValue::Number(n)) => compare_bigint_and_number(b, *n),
                (ConstantValue::Number(n), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) => {
                    compare_bigint_and_number(b, *n).map(|o| o.map(|o| o.reverse()))
                }
                // BigInt vs String: per spec, parse the string as a BigInt
                // using StringToBigInt, then compare the two BigInts.
                // If the string is not a valid StringIntegerLiteral,
                // the result is undefined (= false for all comparisons).
                (ConstantValue::BigInt(b), ConstantValue::String(s)) => {
                    match crate::host::string_to_bigint(&s.to_utf16()) {
                        Some(rhs_bi) => {
                            let lhs_bi = parse_bigint(b)?;
                            Some(Some(lhs_bi.cmp(&rhs_bi)))
                        }
                        None => Some(None),
                    }
                }
                (ConstantValue::String(s), ConstantValue::BigInt(b)) => {
                    match crate::host::string_to_bigint(&s.to_utf16()) {
                        Some(lhs_bi) => {
                            let rhs_bi = parse_bigint(b)?;
                            Some(Some(lhs_bi.cmp(&rhs_bi)))
                        }
                        None => Some(None),
                    }
                }
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Some(ord) = bigint_ord {
                let result = match op {
                    BinaryOp::GreaterThan => matches!(ord, Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Greater)),
                    BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals => {
                        matches!(ord, Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Greater | std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
                    }
                    BinaryOp::LessThan => matches!(ord, Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Less)),
                    BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => {
                        matches!(ord, Some(std::cmp::Ordering::Less | std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
                    }
                    _ => unreachable!("outer match arm only matches comparison operators"),
                };
                return Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(result));
            }
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_for_cmp)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_for_cmp)?;
            let result = match op {
                BinaryOp::GreaterThan => a > b,
                BinaryOp::GreaterThanEquals => a >= b,
                BinaryOp::LessThan => a < b,
                BinaryOp::LessThanEquals => a <= b,
                _ => unreachable!("outer match arm only matches comparison operators"),
            };
            Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(result))
        }
        BinaryOp::LooselyEquals => {
            let result = try_constant_loosely_equals(lhs_const, rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(result))
        }
        BinaryOp::LooselyInequals => {
            let result = try_constant_loosely_equals(lhs_const, rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_boolean(!result))
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseAnd => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_int32(a) & to_int32(b)) as f64))
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseOr => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_int32(a) | to_int32(b)) as f64))
        }
        BinaryOp::BitwiseXor => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_int32(a) ^ to_int32(b)) as f64))
        }
        BinaryOp::LeftShift => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_int32(a) << (to_u32(b) & 0x1f)) as f64))
        }
        BinaryOp::RightShift => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_int32(a) >> (to_u32(b) & 0x1f)) as f64))
        }
        BinaryOp::UnsignedRightShift => {
            let a = constant_to_number(lhs_const)?;
            let b = constant_to_number(rhs_const)?;
            Some(generator.add_constant_number((to_u32(a) >> (to_u32(b) & 0x1f)) as f64))
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// NaN-boxing helpers
// =============================================================================

// NanBoxed Value encoding helpers (ABI-compatible with GC::NanBoxedValue).
// Used by NewPrimitiveArray to encode constant primitive values inline.

pub(super) fn nanboxed_number(value: f64) -> u64 {
    let is_negative_zero = value.to_bits() == nan_box::NEGATIVE_ZERO_BITS;
    if value >= i32::MIN as f64 && value <= i32::MAX as f64 && value.trunc() == value && !is_negative_zero {
        nan_box::SHIFTED_INT32_TAG | ((value as i32 as u32) as u64)
    } else if value.is_nan() {
        nan_box::CANON_NAN_BITS
    } else {
        value.to_bits()
    }
}

pub(super) fn nanboxed_boolean(value: bool) -> u64 {
    nan_box::SHIFTED_BOOLEAN_TAG | u64::from(value)
}

pub(super) fn nanboxed_null() -> u64 {
    nan_box::NULL_VALUE
}

pub(super) fn nanboxed_empty() -> u64 {
    nan_box::EMPTY_VALUE
}

use super::executable::{Executable, append_double_formatted_like_ak, append_value_formatted_like_ak};
use super::executable_data::ExceptionHandler;
use super::instruction::dump_instruction_from_bytes;
use super::instruction::instruction_is_terminator_from_opcode;
use super::instruction::instruction_length_from_bytes;
use super::instruction::instruction_name_from_opcode;
use super::instruction::visit_labels_from_bytes;
use super::native_disassembler::disassemble;
use super::operand::Operand;
use super::operand::read_u32;
use crate::bytecode::encoded_value::EncodedValue;
use crate::bytecode::encoded_value::EncodedValueKind;
use crate::interpreter::run::should_dump_interpreter_assembly;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

/// Where the native code of an opcode's handler lives, which flapc emits with the interpreter.
#[repr(C)]
struct InterpreterHandlerRange {
    hot_start: *const u8,
    hot_end: *const u8,
    cold_start: *const u8,
    cold_end: *const u8,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    safe static js_interpreter_handler_ranges: [InterpreterHandlerRange; 256];
}

impl InterpreterHandlerRange {
    fn hot_code(&'static self) -> &'static [u8] {
        // SAFETY: flapc delimits the handler's hot code with these, and the interpreter is mapped for as long as the
        // process runs.
        unsafe { native_code_between(self.hot_start, self.hot_end) }
    }

    fn cold_code(&'static self) -> &'static [u8] {
        // SAFETY: flapc delimits the handler's cold code with these, and the interpreter is mapped for as long as the
        // process runs.
        unsafe { native_code_between(self.cold_start, self.cold_end) }
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// start and end must delimit native code that stays mapped for as long as the process runs.
unsafe fn native_code_between(start: *const u8, end: *const u8) -> &'static [u8] {
    let start_address = start as usize;
    let end_address = end as usize;
    assert!(end_address >= start_address, "native code range must be ordered");
    if start_address == end_address {
        return &[];
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees the range.
    unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(start, end_address - start_address) }
}

struct ColdCodeRange {
    code: &'static [u8],
    owners: Vec<&'static str>,
}

pub struct BytecodeDumper<'a> {
    output: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
    executable: &'a Executable,
    basic_block_start_offsets: &'a [u32],
    first_piece: bool,
}

fn append_native_code(dumper: &mut BytecodeDumper<'_>, code: &[u8]) {
    if code.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

    let instructions = disassemble(code, code.as_ptr() as u64);
    if instructions.is_empty() {
        dumper.append("          <native disassembly unavailable>\n");
        return;
    }
    for instruction in instructions {
        let instruction_bytes = &code[instruction.offset..instruction.offset + instruction.length];
        dumper.append("          ");
        dumper.append(&format!("{:016x}  ", instruction.address));
        for byte in instruction_bytes {
            dumper.append(&format!("{byte:02x} "));
        }
        for _ in instruction_bytes.len()..15 {
            dumper.append("   ");
        }
        dumper.append(" ");
        dumper.append(&instruction.text);
        dumper.append("\n");
    }
}

fn record_cold_code_range(ranges: &mut Vec<ColdCodeRange>, code: &'static [u8], owner: &'static str) {
    if code.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(range) = ranges.iter_mut().find(|range| std::ptr::eq(range.code, code)) {
        if !range.owners.contains(&owner) {
            range.owners.push(owner);
        }
        return;
    }
    ranges.push(ColdCodeRange {
        code,
        owners: vec![owner],
    });
}

fn append_cold_code_ranges(dumper: &mut BytecodeDumper<'_>, ranges: &[ColdCodeRange]) {
    if ranges.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

    dumper.append("\n\x1b[36;1mCold native paths\x1b[0m:\n");
    for range in ranges {
        dumper.append("\n  \x1b[36m");
        dumper.append(&range.owners.join(", "));
        dumper.append("\x1b[0m:\n");
        append_native_code(dumper, range.code);
    }
}

impl BytecodeDumper<'_> {
    pub fn append(&mut self, text: &str) {
        self.output.extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
    }

    pub fn begin_instruction(&mut self, name: &str) {
        self.first_piece = true;
        self.append(name);
    }

    pub fn append_piece(&mut self, append_piece: impl FnOnce(&mut Self)) {
        if self.first_piece {
            self.append(" ");
            self.first_piece = false;
        } else {
            self.append(", ");
        }
        append_piece(self);
    }

    pub fn append_operand(&mut self, name: &str, operand: Operand) {
        if !name.is_empty() {
            self.append("\x1b[32m");
            self.append(name);
            self.append("\x1b[0m:");
        }

        let raw = operand.raw();
        if raw < self.executable.number_of_registers() {
            if raw == 2 {
                self.append("\x1b[33mthis\x1b[0m");
            } else {
                self.append("\x1b[33mreg");
                self.append(&raw.to_string());
                self.append("\x1b[0m");
            }
        } else if raw < self.executable.registers_and_locals_count() {
            let index = raw - self.executable.local_index_base();
            self.append("\x1b[34m");
            Utf16View::of_fly_string(&self.executable.local_variable_names()[index as usize])
                .append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
            self.append("~");
            self.append(&index.to_string());
            self.append("\x1b[0m");
        } else if raw < self.executable.argument_index_base() {
            let index = raw - self.executable.registers_and_locals_count();
            self.append_value(self.executable.constants()[index as usize].0);
        } else {
            let index = raw - self.executable.argument_index_base();
            self.append("\x1b[34marg");
            self.append(&index.to_string());
            self.append("\x1b[0m");
        }
    }

    fn append_value(&mut self, encoded: u64) {
        match EncodedValue::from_encoded(encoded).kind() {
            EncodedValueKind::Empty => self.append("<Empty>"),
            EncodedValueKind::Boolean(value) => {
                self.append("Bool(");
                self.append(if value { "true" } else { "false" });
                self.append(")");
            }
            EncodedValueKind::Int32(value) => {
                self.append("Int32(");
                self.append(&value.to_string());
                self.append(")");
            }
            EncodedValueKind::Double(value) => {
                self.append("Double(");
                self.append_double(value);
                self.append(")");
            }
            EncodedValueKind::BigInt => {
                self.append("BigInt(");
                self.append_bigint(encoded);
                self.append(")");
            }
            EncodedValueKind::String => {
                self.append("String(\"");
                self.append_string_value(encoded);
                self.append("\")");
            }
            EncodedValueKind::Undefined => self.append("Undefined"),
            EncodedValueKind::Null => self.append("Null"),
            EncodedValueKind::Other => {
                self.append("Value(");
                self.append_value_fallback(encoded);
                self.append(")");
            }
        }
    }

    fn append_value_without_side_effects(&mut self, encoded: u64) {
        match EncodedValue::from_encoded(encoded).kind() {
            EncodedValueKind::Empty => self.append("<empty>"),
            EncodedValueKind::Boolean(value) => self.append(if value { "true" } else { "false" }),
            EncodedValueKind::Int32(value) => self.append(&value.to_string()),
            EncodedValueKind::Double(value) => self.append_double(value),
            EncodedValueKind::BigInt => self.append_bigint(encoded),
            EncodedValueKind::String => self.append_string_value(encoded),
            EncodedValueKind::Undefined => self.append("undefined"),
            EncodedValueKind::Null => self.append("null"),
            EncodedValueKind::Other => self.append_value_fallback(encoded),
        }
    }

    pub fn append_label(&mut self, name: &str, address: u32) {
        if !name.is_empty() {
            self.append("\x1b[32m");
            self.append(name);
            self.append("\x1b[0m:");
        }

        if let Ok(index) = self.basic_block_start_offsets.binary_search(&address) {
            self.append("\x1b[35mblock");
            self.append(&index.to_string());
            self.append("\x1b[0m");
        } else {
            self.append("@");
            self.append(&format!("{address:x}"));
        }
    }

    fn append_double(&mut self, value: f64) {
        append_double_formatted_like_ak(self.output, value);
    }

    fn append_bigint(&mut self, encoded: u64) {
        Utf16View::of_string(&Value::from_bits(encoded).as_bigint().to_utf16_string()).append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
    }

    fn append_string_value(&mut self, encoded: u64) {
        Utf16View::of_string(&Value::from_bits(encoded).as_string().utf16_string()).append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
    }

    fn append_value_fallback(&mut self, encoded: u64) {
        append_value_formatted_like_ak(self.output, Value::from_bits(encoded));
    }

    fn append_quoted(&mut self, text: Utf16View<'_>) {
        self.append("\x1b[36m`");
        text.append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
        self.append("`\x1b[0m");
    }

    pub fn append_identifier_quoted(&mut self, index: u32) {
        self.append_quoted(Utf16View::of_fly_string(
            &self.executable.identifier_table()[index as usize],
        ));
    }

    pub fn append_identifier_plain(&mut self, index: u32) {
        Utf16View::of_fly_string(&self.executable.identifier_table()[index as usize]).append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
    }

    /// A PropertyKey is the text it was made from, since only canonical index strings become numbers.
    pub fn append_property_key_quoted(&mut self, index: u32) {
        let key = self.executable.property_key(index as usize).to_utf16_string();
        self.append_quoted(Utf16View::of_string(&key));
    }

    pub fn append_property_key_plain(&mut self, index: u32) {
        let key = self.executable.property_key(index as usize).to_utf16_string();
        Utf16View::of_string(&key).append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
    }

    pub fn append_string(&mut self, index: u32) {
        Utf16View::of_fly_string(&self.executable.string_table()[index as usize]).append_as_wtf8_to(self.output);
    }

    pub fn append_bool(&mut self, name: &str, value: bool) {
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":");
        self.append(if value { "true" } else { "false" });
    }

    pub fn append_number(&mut self, name: &str, value: impl std::fmt::Display) {
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":");
        self.append(&value.to_string());
    }

    pub fn append_put_kind(&mut self, name: &str, value: u8) {
        let kind = match value {
            0 => "Normal",
            1 => "Getter",
            2 => "Setter",
            3 => "Prototype",
            4 => "Own",
            _ => unreachable!("invalid PutKind"),
        };
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":");
        self.append(kind);
    }

    pub fn append_operand_list(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize, count: usize) {
        self.append("\x1b[32m");
        self.append(name);
        self.append("\x1b[0m:[");
        for i in 0..count {
            if i != 0 {
                self.append(", ");
            }
            self.append_operand("", Operand::from_raw(u32::from(bytes[offset + i])));
        }
        self.append("]");
    }

    pub fn append_optional_operand_list(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize, count: usize) {
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":[");
        let mut first_elem = true;
        for i in 0..count {
            let raw = bytes[offset + i];
            if raw == u8::MAX {
                continue;
            }
            let operand = Operand::from_raw(u32::from(raw));
            if !first_elem {
                self.append(", ");
            }
            first_elem = false;
            self.append_operand(name, operand);
        }
        self.append("]");
    }

    pub fn append_label_list(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize, count: usize) {
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":[");
        for i in 0..count {
            if i != 0 {
                self.append(", ");
            }
            self.append_label("", read_u32(bytes, offset + i * 4));
        }
        self.append("]");
    }

    pub fn append_optional_label_list(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize, count: usize) {
        self.append(name);
        self.append(":[");
        let mut first_elem = true;
        for i in 0..count {
            let element_offset = offset + i * 5;
            if bytes[element_offset + 4] == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            if !first_elem {
                self.append(", ");
            }
            first_elem = false;
            self.append_label("", read_u32(bytes, element_offset));
        }
        self.append("]");
    }

    pub fn append_value_list(&mut self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize, count: usize) {
        if !name.is_empty() {
            self.append("\x1b[32m");
            self.append(name);
            self.append("\x1b[0m:[");
        }
        for i in 0..count {
            if i != 0 {
                self.append(", ");
            }
            let value = u64::from_ne_bytes(bytes[offset + i * 8..offset + (i + 1) * 8].try_into().unwrap());
            self.append_value_without_side_effects(value);
        }
        self.append("]");
    }

    pub fn append_exception_handlers(&mut self, exception_handlers: &[ExceptionHandler]) {
        if exception_handlers.is_empty() {
            return;
        }

        self.append("\nException handlers:\n");
        for handler in exception_handlers {
            self.append("  [");
            self.append(&format!("{:4x}", handler.start_offset));
            self.append(" .. ");
            self.append(&format!("{:4x}", handler.end_offset));
            self.append("] => handler ");
            self.append_label("", handler.handler_offset);
            self.append("\n");
        }
    }
}

fn collect_basic_block_start_offsets(bytecode: &[u8], exception_handlers: &[ExceptionHandler]) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut offsets = vec![0];
    let append_offset = |offsets: &mut Vec<u32>, offset: usize| {
        let offset = u32::try_from(offset).expect("bytecode offset exceeds u32::MAX");
        if !offsets.contains(&offset) {
            offsets.push(offset);
        }
    };
    let append_instruction_offset = |offsets: &mut Vec<u32>, offset: u32| {
        if (offset as usize) < bytecode.len() {
            append_offset(offsets, offset as usize);
        }
    };

    let mut at = 0;
    while at < bytecode.len() {
        let opcode = bytecode[at];
        let length = instruction_length_from_bytes(opcode, bytecode, at)
            .expect("generated bytecode has valid instruction lengths");
        let next_offset = at + length;

        visit_labels_from_bytes(opcode, bytecode, at, &mut |address| {
            append_offset(&mut offsets, address as usize);
        });

        if instruction_is_terminator_from_opcode(opcode) && next_offset < bytecode.len() {
            append_offset(&mut offsets, next_offset);
        }

        at = next_offset;
    }

    for handler in exception_handlers {
        append_instruction_offset(&mut offsets, handler.start_offset);
        append_instruction_offset(&mut offsets, handler.end_offset);
        append_instruction_offset(&mut offsets, handler.handler_offset);
    }

    offsets.sort_unstable();
    offsets
}

/// Count basic blocks in a bytecode instruction stream.
pub fn count_basic_blocks(executable: &Executable) -> usize {
    collect_basic_block_start_offsets(executable.bytecode(), executable.exception_handlers()).len()
}

/// Dump the bytecode of an executable, and with LADYBIRD_JS_INTERPRETER_DUMP set, the native code of the
/// interpreter handler of each instruction.
pub fn dump_bytecode(output: &mut Vec<u8>, executable: &Executable) {
    let bytecode = executable.bytecode();
    let exception_handlers = executable.exception_handlers();
    let dump_interpreter = should_dump_interpreter_assembly();
    let basic_block_start_offsets = collect_basic_block_start_offsets(bytecode, exception_handlers);
    let mut dumper = BytecodeDumper {
        output,
        executable,
        basic_block_start_offsets: &basic_block_start_offsets,
        first_piece: true,
    };
    let mut basic_block_offset_index = 0;
    let mut cold_code_ranges = Vec::new();

    let mut at = 0;
    while at < bytecode.len() {
        if basic_block_offset_index < basic_block_start_offsets.len()
            && at == basic_block_start_offsets[basic_block_offset_index] as usize
        {
            if basic_block_offset_index > 0 {
                dumper.append("\n");
            }
            dumper.append("\x1b[35;1mblock");
            dumper.append(&basic_block_offset_index.to_string());
            dumper.append("\x1b[0m:\n");
            basic_block_offset_index += 1;
        }

        dumper.append("  [");
        dumper.append(&format!("{at:4x}"));
        dumper.append("] ");
        dump_instruction_from_bytes(bytecode[at], bytecode, at, &mut dumper);
        dumper.append("\n");

        if dump_interpreter {
            let handler_range = &js_interpreter_handler_ranges[bytecode[at] as usize];
            append_native_code(&mut dumper, handler_range.hot_code());
            record_cold_code_range(
                &mut cold_code_ranges,
                handler_range.cold_code(),
                instruction_name_from_opcode(bytecode[at]),
            );
        }

        at += instruction_length_from_bytes(bytecode[at], bytecode, at)
            .expect("generated bytecode has valid instruction lengths");
    }

    dumper.append_exception_handlers(exception_handlers);
    append_cold_code_ranges(&mut dumper, &cold_code_ranges);
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
