use libjs_abi::value as nan_box;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum EncodedValueKind {
    Empty,
    Boolean(bool),
    Int32(i32),
    Double(f64),
    String,
    BigInt,
    Undefined,
    Null,
    Other,
}

/// The encoded representation of a LibJS `Value`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct EncodedValue(u64);

impl EncodedValue {
    const CANON_NAN_BITS: u64 = nan_box::CANON_NAN_BITS;
    const TAG_SHIFT: u64 = nan_box::TAG_SHIFT;
    const STRING_TAG: u64 = nan_box::STRING_TAG;
    const BIGINT_TAG: u64 = nan_box::BIGINT_TAG;
    const UNDEFINED_TAG: u64 = nan_box::UNDEFINED_TAG;
    const NULL_TAG: u64 = nan_box::NULL_TAG;
    const BOOLEAN_TAG: u64 = nan_box::BOOLEAN_TAG;
    const INT32_TAG: u64 = nan_box::INT32_TAG;
    const EMPTY_TAG: u64 = nan_box::EMPTY_TAG;

    pub const fn from_encoded(encoded: u64) -> Self {
        Self(encoded)
    }

    pub const fn encoded(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    pub fn kind(self) -> EncodedValueKind {
        let tag = self.0 >> Self::TAG_SHIFT;
        if self.0 == (Self::EMPTY_TAG << Self::TAG_SHIFT) {
            EncodedValueKind::Empty
        } else if tag == Self::BOOLEAN_TAG {
            EncodedValueKind::Boolean(self.0 & 1 != 0)
        } else if tag == Self::INT32_TAG {
            EncodedValueKind::Int32((self.0 & 0xffff_ffff) as u32 as i32)
        } else if (self.0 & Self::CANON_NAN_BITS) != Self::CANON_NAN_BITS || self.0 == Self::CANON_NAN_BITS {
            EncodedValueKind::Double(f64::from_bits(self.0))
        } else if tag == Self::BIGINT_TAG {
            EncodedValueKind::BigInt
        } else if tag == Self::STRING_TAG {
            EncodedValueKind::String
        } else if self.0 == (Self::UNDEFINED_TAG << Self::TAG_SHIFT) {
            EncodedValueKind::Undefined
        } else if self.0 == (Self::NULL_TAG << Self::TAG_SHIFT) {
            EncodedValueKind::Null
        } else {
            EncodedValueKind::Other
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn decodes_immediate_values() {
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded(EncodedValue::EMPTY_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Empty
        );
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded((EncodedValue::BOOLEAN_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT) | 1).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Boolean(true)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded(EncodedValue::BOOLEAN_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Boolean(false)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded((EncodedValue::INT32_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT) | 0xffff_ffff).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Int32(-1)
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded(EncodedValue::CANON_NAN_BITS).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Double(value) if value.to_bits() == EncodedValue::CANON_NAN_BITS
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded(EncodedValue::UNDEFINED_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Undefined
        );
        assert_eq!(
            EncodedValue::from_encoded(EncodedValue::NULL_TAG << EncodedValue::TAG_SHIFT).kind(),
            EncodedValueKind::Null
        );
    }
}

use core::marker::PhantomData;

use crate::layout::property_lookup_cache::EnvironmentCoordinate;

/// The bytes every instruction starts with.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct InstructionHeader {
    pub opcode: u8,
}

/// An operand: the index of its slot in the frame.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct Operand(pub u8);

impl Operand {
    pub fn index(self) -> usize {
        self.0 as usize
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct OptionalOperand(pub u8);

impl OptionalOperand {
    const NONE: u8 = u8::MAX;

    pub fn get(self) -> Option<Operand> {
        (self.0 != Self::NONE).then_some(Operand(self.0))
    }
}

/// The bytecode offset of a basic block.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct Label(pub u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct OptionalLabel {
    pub label: Label,
    pub has_value: bool,
}

impl OptionalLabel {
    pub fn get(self) -> Option<Label> {
        self.has_value.then_some(self.label)
    }
}

/// The coordinate of a binding as an instruction holds it: a byte of hops and two bytes of binding index. The generator
/// looks bindings up by name where a coordinate does not fit.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct BytecodeEnvironmentCoordinate {
    hops: u8,
    index: [u8; 2],
}

impl BytecodeEnvironmentCoordinate {
    pub fn get(self) -> EnvironmentCoordinate {
        EnvironmentCoordinate {
            hops: u32::from(self.hops),
            index: u32::from(u16::from_ne_bytes(self.index)),
        }
    }
}

/// The name table index that the field `field` of an instruction in `bytecode` holds, if it holds one. An index too
/// large for the field is in the WideNameIndices before the instruction, which only the bytecode can reach.
fn name_index_in(field: &[u8; 2], bytecode: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let at = field.as_ptr().addr().wrapping_sub(bytecode.as_ptr().addr());
    assert!(at < bytecode.len(), "the name table index is a field of the bytecode");
    super::operand::read_optional_name_index(bytecode, at).map(|index| index as usize)
}

macro_rules! define_table_index {
    ($($name:ident),*) => {
        $(
            /// The field of an instruction that holds an index into a name table of its executable.
            #[derive(Debug)]
            #[repr(C, packed)]
            pub struct $name([u8; 2]);

            impl $name {
                /// The index the field holds, which is a field of an instruction in `bytecode`.
                pub fn index_in(&self, bytecode: &[u8]) -> usize {
                    name_index_in(&self.0, bytecode).expect("the field holds a name table index")
                }
            }
        )*
    };
}

define_table_index!(IdentifierTableIndex, PropertyKeyTableIndex, StringTableIndex);

/// The field of an instruction that holds an index into a name table of its executable, if it holds one.
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct OptionalIndex<T>([u8; 2], PhantomData<T>);

impl<T> OptionalIndex<T> {
    /// The index the field holds, which is a field of an instruction in `bytecode`.
    pub fn index_in(&self, bytecode: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
        name_index_in(&self.0, bytecode)
    }
}

//! Compiled bytecode together with everything needed to run it, as owned Rust values.

use core::num::NonZeroU32;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16String;

/// Exception handler range (with byte offsets, post-linking).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ExceptionHandler {
    pub start_offset: u32,
    pub end_offset: u32,
    pub handler_offset: u32,
    pub catches_exception: bool,
}

/// The longest string constant that gets interned. Long ones are rarely compared, and not worth hashing.
pub(crate) const MAXIMUM_INTERNED_CONSTANT_LENGTH: usize = 256;

/// A typed constant value stored in the constant pool.
///
/// The actual NaN-boxed encoding happens at the FFI boundary when
/// creating the `Bytecode::Executable`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ConstantValue {
    Number(f64),
    Boolean(bool),
    Null,
    Undefined,
    Empty,
    String(Utf16String),
    /// The text of the literal, boxed once more so that a constant takes 16 bytes: a BigInt literal is rare.
    BigInt(Box<Box<str>>),
    /// A VM-specific well-known symbol resolved when the Executable is materialized.
    WellKnownSymbol(WellKnownSymbolKind),
    /// A NativeJavaScriptBackedFunction intrinsic resolved when the Executable is materialized.
    AbstractOperation(AbstractOperationKind),
}

// NB: Every constant of code has these bytes, until the code is linked for the last time.
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ConstantValue>() == 16);

pub struct PendingSharedFunctionData {
    pub description: SharedFunctionDescription,
    /// The name of the class field whose initializer the function is, and whether the name is private.
    pub class_field_initializer_name: Option<Box<(Utf16String, bool)>>,
    pub should_eager_compile: bool,
    pub precompiled_function: Option<Arc<PrecompiledFunction>>,
}

// NB: Code has these bytes for every function it creates, until the code is linked for the last time.

/// Metadata computed from scope analysis for a SharedFunctionInstanceData.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct FunctionSfdMetadata {
    /// The parameter names if a mapped arguments object goes by them, and empty otherwise.
    pub parameter_names: Box<[ak::Utf16FlyString]>,
    pub uses_this: bool,
    pub this_value_needs_environment_resolution: bool,
    pub function_environment_needed: bool,
    /// Whether the code of the function can change the running lexical environment.
    pub creates_environment: bool,
    pub function_environment_bindings_count: usize,
    pub var_environment_bindings_count: usize,
    pub might_need_arguments: bool,
    pub contains_eval: bool,
}

/// GC-free compiled bytecode for a function that top-level code will immediately invoke.
pub struct PrecompiledFunction {
    pub executable: Arc<ExecutableData>,
    pub metadata: FunctionSfdMetadata,
}

impl PrecompiledFunction {
    /// The bytes of this function's code, without the functions kept for its payloads.
    pub fn memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of::<Self>() + size_of_val(&*self.metadata.parameter_names) + self.executable.memory_size()
    }

    /// This function again, sharing its code.
    pub fn shared_copy(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            executable: self.executable.clone(),
            metadata: self.metadata.clone(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum PendingLiteralValueKind {
    None,
    Number,
    BooleanTrue,
    BooleanFalse,
    Null,
    String,
}

pub struct PendingClassElement {
    pub kind: u8,
    pub is_static: bool,
    pub is_private: bool,
    pub private_identifier: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub shared_function_data_index: Option<u32>,
    pub has_initializer: bool,
    pub literal_value_kind: PendingLiteralValueKind,
    pub literal_value_number: f64,
    pub literal_value_string: Option<Utf16String>,
}

pub struct PendingClassBlueprint {
    pub name: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub source_text_offset: usize,
    pub source_text_length: usize,
    pub constructor_sfd_index: u32,
    pub has_super_class: bool,
    pub has_name: bool,
    pub elements: Vec<PendingClassElement>,
}

impl PendingClassBlueprint {
    pub fn memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        let string_size = |string: &Option<Utf16String>| string.as_ref().map_or(0, utf16_string_memory_size);
        size_of::<Self>()
            + string_size(&self.name)
            + self.elements.capacity() * size_of::<PendingClassElement>()
            + self
                .elements
                .iter()
                .map(|element| string_size(&element.private_identifier) + string_size(&element.literal_value_string))
                .sum::<usize>()
    }
}

/// How many inline cache and feedback slots of each kind the bytecode indexes into.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ExecutableCacheCounts {
    pub property_lookup: u32,
    pub global_variable: u32,
    pub environment_coordinate: u32,
    pub template_object: u32,
    pub object_shape: u32,
    pub object_property_iterator: u32,
    pub environment_shape: u32,
    pub arith_feedback: u32,
    pub value_feedback: u32,
    pub call_feedback: u32,
    pub keyed_feedback: u32,
}

/// Executable::LocalVariableMetadata
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct LocalVariableMetadata {
    pub is_mutable: bool,
    /// The part of the source code in which the local variable is in scope.
    pub scope_start: SourceOffset,
    pub scope_end: SourceOffset,
}

/// A range of bytecode offsets, from `start_offset` up to but not including `end_offset`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct StrictRange {
    pub start_offset: u32,
    pub end_offset: u32,
}

impl StrictRange {
    /// The same range, `distance` bytes later.
    pub fn shifted(self, distance: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            start_offset: self.start_offset + distance,
            end_offset: self.end_offset + distance,
        }
    }
}

/// One compiled script, module or function body: everything about it that does not depend on where it runs. Nothing
/// here changes once it is compiled, so any number of [`Executable`]s can link it, each with caches, constants and
/// functions of its own, and they all run the same bytecode.
///
/// Nested functions are compiled lazily: unless an entry of
/// `shared_function_data` was precompiled, it describes the function that gets
/// parsed and compiled when it is first called.
///
/// [`Executable`]: super::executable::Executable
pub struct ExecutableData {
    pub bytecode: BlockSlice<u8>,
    /// Sorted by bytecode offset: where in the source code the instructions from each offset on came from.
    pub source_map: BlockSlice<u8>,
    pub number_of_registers: u32,
    pub number_of_arguments: u32,
    pub is_strict: bool,
    cache_slot_counts: CacheSlotCounts,
    /// The index of the length in the property key table, plus one.
    length_identifier: Option<NonZeroU32>,
    pub identifier_table: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
    /// The names of the local variables, then the names of the arguments.
    pub variable_names: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
    /// One for each of the local variables.
    pub local_variable_metadata: BlockSlice<LocalVariableMetadata>,
    rare_data: Option<Box<RareExecutableData>>,
    /// What linking reads, and nothing after it (see [`ExecutableData::release_link_inputs()`]).
    pub property_key_table: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
    pub constants: BlockSlice<ConstantValue>,
    pub shared_function_data: BlockSlice<PendingSharedFunctionData>,
    pub class_blueprints: BlockSlice<PendingClassBlueprint>,
    /// What turns the source offsets of a source map that has them into lines and columns.
    pub position_source: Arc<crate::parser::SourcePositions>,
    /// The memory of everything above that running the code reads, which gets dropped before it.
    pub tables: SliceBlock,
    /// The memory of what only linking reads.
    pub link_tables: SliceBlock,
}

// NB: Every compiled function has these bytes.
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ExecutableData>() == 136);

/// The parts of code that few codes have.
#[derive(Default)]
struct RareExecutableData {
    /// Sorted by start offset, and not overlapping.
    exception_handlers: Box<[ExceptionHandler]>,
    /// Sorted by start offset. Where a class body makes the code strict, if the function is not.
    strict_ranges: Box<[StrictRange]>,
    string_table: Box<[ak::Utf16FlyString]>,
    template_object_caches: u32,
    object_property_iterator_caches: u32,
    environment_shape_caches: u32,
}

/// The counts of the kinds of cache and feedback slots whose sites past the last slot index share it, so that each is
/// at most 65536, kept in two bytes as `u16::MAX`. Code with exactly 65535 slots of a kind gets one more, which no
/// site uses.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct CacheSlotCounts {
    property_lookup: u16,
    global_variable: u16,
    environment_coordinate: u16,
    object_shape: u16,
    arith_feedback: u16,
    value_feedback: u16,
    call_feedback: u16,
    keyed_feedback: u16,
}

impl CacheSlotCounts {
    fn compact(count: u32) -> u16 {
        assert!(
            count <= u32::from(u16::MAX) + 1,
            "sites past the last slot index share it"
        );
        u16::try_from(count).unwrap_or(u16::MAX)
    }

    fn expand(count: u16) -> u32 {
        if count == u16::MAX {
            u32::from(u16::MAX) + 1
        } else {
            u32::from(count)
        }
    }
}

fn constant_memory_size(constant: &ConstantValue) -> usize {
    match constant {
        ConstantValue::String(string) => utf16_string_memory_size(string),
        ConstantValue::BigInt(literal) => size_of::<Box<str>>() + literal.len(),
        _ => 0,
    }
}

// SAFETY: Code compiles away from the heap, so it cannot hold a cell. What it describes turns into cells only when an
//         Executable links it, and those stay with that Executable.
#[cfg(not(test))]
unsafe impl crate::gc::lint_markers::HoldsNoCells for ExecutableData {}

impl ExecutableData {
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        bytecode: BlockSlice<u8>,
        source_map: BlockSlice<u8>,
        exception_handlers: Box<[ExceptionHandler]>,
        strict_ranges: Box<[StrictRange]>,
        number_of_registers: u32,
        number_of_arguments: u32,
        is_strict: bool,
        cache_counts: ExecutableCacheCounts,
        identifier_table: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
        string_table: Box<[ak::Utf16FlyString]>,
        variable_names: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
        local_variable_metadata: BlockSlice<LocalVariableMetadata>,
        length_identifier: Option<PropertyKeyTableIndex>,
        property_key_table: BlockSlice<ak::Utf16FlyString>,
        constants: BlockSlice<ConstantValue>,
        shared_function_data: BlockSlice<PendingSharedFunctionData>,
        class_blueprints: BlockSlice<PendingClassBlueprint>,
        position_source: Arc<crate::parser::SourcePositions>,
        tables: SliceBlock,
        link_tables: SliceBlock,
    ) -> Self {
        let rare_data = RareExecutableData {
            exception_handlers,
            strict_ranges,
            string_table,
            template_object_caches: cache_counts.template_object,
            object_property_iterator_caches: cache_counts.object_property_iterator,
            environment_shape_caches: cache_counts.environment_shape,
        };
        let has_rare_data = !rare_data.exception_handlers.is_empty()
            || !rare_data.strict_ranges.is_empty()
            || !rare_data.string_table.is_empty()
            || rare_data.template_object_caches != 0
            || rare_data.object_property_iterator_caches != 0
            || rare_data.environment_shape_caches != 0;
        Self {
            bytecode,
            source_map,
            number_of_registers,
            number_of_arguments,
            is_strict,
            cache_slot_counts: CacheSlotCounts {
                property_lookup: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.property_lookup),
                global_variable: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.global_variable),
                environment_coordinate: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.environment_coordinate),
                object_shape: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.object_shape),
                arith_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.arith_feedback),
                value_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.value_feedback),
                call_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.call_feedback),
                keyed_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::compact(cache_counts.keyed_feedback),
            },
            length_identifier: length_identifier
                .map(|index| NonZeroU32::new(index.0 + 1).expect("the index plus one is not zero")),
            identifier_table,
            variable_names,
            local_variable_metadata,
            rare_data: has_rare_data.then(|| Box::new(rare_data)),
            property_key_table,
            constants,
            shared_function_data,
            class_blueprints,
            position_source,
            tables,
            link_tables,
        }
    }

    /// How many inline cache and feedback slots of each kind the bytecode indexes into.
    pub fn cache_counts(&self) -> ExecutableCacheCounts {
        let counts = &self.cache_slot_counts;
        let rare_data = self.rare_data.as_deref();
        ExecutableCacheCounts {
            property_lookup: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.property_lookup),
            global_variable: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.global_variable),
            environment_coordinate: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.environment_coordinate),
            template_object: rare_data.map_or(0, |rare_data| rare_data.template_object_caches),
            object_shape: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.object_shape),
            object_property_iterator: rare_data.map_or(0, |rare_data| rare_data.object_property_iterator_caches),
            environment_shape: rare_data.map_or(0, |rare_data| rare_data.environment_shape_caches),
            arith_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.arith_feedback),
            value_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.value_feedback),
            call_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.call_feedback),
            keyed_feedback: CacheSlotCounts::expand(counts.keyed_feedback),
        }
    }

    pub fn length_identifier(&self) -> Option<PropertyKeyTableIndex> {
        self.length_identifier
            .map(|index| PropertyKeyTableIndex(index.get() - 1))
    }

    /// Sorted by start offset, and not overlapping.
    pub fn exception_handlers(&self) -> &[ExceptionHandler] {
        self.rare_data
            .as_deref()
            .map_or(&[], |rare_data| &rare_data.exception_handlers)
    }

    /// Sorted by start offset. Where a class body makes the code strict, if the function is not.
    pub fn strict_ranges(&self) -> &[StrictRange] {
        self.rare_data
            .as_deref()
            .map_or(&[], |rare_data| &rare_data.strict_ranges)
    }

    pub fn string_table(&self) -> &[ak::Utf16FlyString] {
        self.rare_data
            .as_deref()
            .map_or(&[], |rare_data| &rare_data.string_table)
    }

    /// The entries of the source map, with the lines and columns that they stand for, which get worked out when something
    /// asks.
    pub fn source_positions(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceMapEntry> + '_ {
        use crate::bytecode::source_map::SourceMapEntry;
        SourceMapEntries::new(&self.source_map).map(|entry| {
            if entry.source_offset == SourceOffset::NONE {
                return SourceMapEntry {
                    bytecode_offset: entry.bytecode_offset,
                    line: 0,
                    column: 0,
                };
            }
            let position = self.position_source.lines.position(entry.source_offset.0);
            SourceMapEntry {
                bytecode_offset: entry.bytecode_offset,
                line: position.line,
                column: position.column,
            }
        })
    }

    /// The bytes of this code and of what it holds for the functions and classes it declares. A name in one of the tables
    /// counts as its slot in the table, since the text of a name is shared by everything that uses it.
    pub fn memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of::<Self>()
            + size_of_val(&*self.bytecode)
            + self.rare_data.as_ref().map_or(0, |rare_data| {
                size_of::<RareExecutableData>()
                    + size_of_val(&*rare_data.exception_handlers)
                    + size_of_val(&*rare_data.strict_ranges)
                    + size_of_val(&*rare_data.string_table)
            })
            + size_of_val(&*self.source_map)
            + size_of_val(&*self.identifier_table)
            + size_of_val(&*self.variable_names)
            + size_of_val(&*self.local_variable_metadata)
            + size_of_val(&*self.property_key_table)
            + size_of_val(&*self.constants)
            + self.constants.iter().map(constant_memory_size).sum::<usize>()
            + self
                .shared_function_data
                .iter()
                .map(PendingSharedFunctionData::memory_size)
                .sum::<usize>()
            + self
                .class_blueprints
                .iter()
                .map(PendingClassBlueprint::memory_size)
                .sum::<usize>()
    }

    /// Frees what only linking reads, for an executable that is the last to hold this code, so that code nothing can
    /// link again costs no more than what running it reads.
    pub fn release_link_inputs(&mut self) {
        self.property_key_table = BlockSlice::empty();
        self.constants = BlockSlice::empty();
        self.shared_function_data = BlockSlice::empty();
        self.class_blueprints = BlockSlice::empty();
        self.link_tables = SliceBlock::empty();
    }
}

/// The contents of a cache entry, copied out of the cache so that no reference into its storage outlives a call that
/// may update the cache and free that storage.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
    pub entry_type: PropertyLookupCacheEntryType,
    pub property_offset: u32,
    pub writes_data_property: bool,
    pub new_shape: Option<Gc<Shape>>,
    pub shape: Option<ShapeKey>,
    pub prototype: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    pub prototype_chain_validity: Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>>,
    /// See PropertyLookupCacheEntry::key.
    pub key: u64,
    pub getter: Option<Gc<FunctionObject>>,
}

impl Default for PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            entry_type: PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty,
            property_offset: 0,
            writes_data_property: false,
            new_shape: None,
            shape: None,
            prototype: None,
            prototype_chain_validity: None,
            key: 0,
            getter: None,
        }
    }
}

impl PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
    fn has_same_cache_key_as(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        if self.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty
            || other.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty
        {
            return false;
        }
        if self.entry_type != other.entry_type || self.key != other.key {
            return false;
        }

        // NB: An entry for an earlier dictionary generation of the shape is replaced too.
        let same_shape = self.shape.map(|key| key.shape) == other.shape.map(|key| key.shape);
        match self.entry_type {
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty => same_shape && self.new_shape == other.new_shape,
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::MissingOwnProperty => same_shape,
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                same_shape && self.prototype == other.prototype
            }
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty => unreachable!("empty entries have no cache key"),
        }
    }

    fn has_dead_cell(&self, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) -> bool {
        (self.key != 0 && sweep.is_dead_or_moving(Value::from_bits(self.key).as_cell()))
            || self.new_shape.is_some_and(|shape| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(shape))
            || self.shape.is_some_and(|key| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(key.shape))
            || self
                .prototype
                .is_some_and(|prototype| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(prototype))
            || self
                .prototype_chain_validity
                .is_some_and(|validity| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(validity))
    }
}

// SAFETY: Entries live in the inline caches of executables and of the VM, which the VM sweeps after each collection (see
// Vm::remove_dead_cells_from_property_lookup_caches()).
unsafe impl SweptAfterCollection for PropertyLookupCacheEntry {}

impl PropertyLookupCacheEntry {
    /// An empty entry, like the default PropertyLookupCacheEntryData.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            entry_type: Cell::new(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty),
            property_offset: Cell::new(0),
            shape_dictionary_generation: Cell::new(0),
            writes_data_property: Cell::new(false),
            new_shape: Cell::new(None),
            shape: Cell::new(None),
            prototype: Cell::new(None),
            prototype_chain_validity: Cell::new(None),
            key: Cell::new(0),
            getter: Cell::new(None),
        }
    }

    fn from_data(data: PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> Self {
        Self {
            entry_type: Cell::new(data.entry_type),
            property_offset: Cell::new(data.property_offset),
            shape_dictionary_generation: Cell::new(data.shape.map_or(0, |key| key.dictionary_generation)),
            writes_data_property: Cell::new(data.writes_data_property),
            new_shape: Cell::new(data.new_shape),
            shape: Cell::new(data.shape.map(|key| key.shape)),
            prototype: Cell::new(data.prototype),
            prototype_chain_validity: Cell::new(data.prototype_chain_validity),
            key: Cell::new(data.key),
            getter: Cell::new(data.getter),
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
            entry_type: self.entry_type.get(),
            property_offset: self.property_offset.get(),
            writes_data_property: self.writes_data_property.get(),
            new_shape: self.new_shape.get(),
            shape: self.shape_key(),
            prototype: self.prototype.get(),
            prototype_chain_validity: self.prototype_chain_validity.get(),
            key: self.key.get(),
            getter: self.getter.get(),
        }
    }

    pub fn set(&self, data: PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) {
        self.entry_type.set(data.entry_type);
        self.property_offset.set(data.property_offset);
        self.shape_dictionary_generation
            .set(data.shape.map_or(0, |key| key.dictionary_generation));
        self.writes_data_property.set(data.writes_data_property);
        self.new_shape.set(data.new_shape);
        self.shape.set(data.shape.map(|key| key.shape));
        self.prototype.set(data.prototype);
        self.prototype_chain_validity.set(data.prototype_chain_validity);
        self.key.set(data.key);
        self.getter.set(data.getter);
    }

    pub fn shape_key(&self) -> Option<ShapeKey> {
        self.shape.get().map(|shape| ShapeKey {
            shape,
            dictionary_generation: self.shape_dictionary_generation.get(),
        })
    }

    /// Forgets the whole entry if one of its cells died in this collection, as clear_cache_entry_if_dead does.
    fn clear_if_it_has_a_dead_cell(&self, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) {
        if self.get().has_dead_cell(sweep) {
            self.set(PropertyLookupCacheEntryData::default());
        }
        if self.getter.get().is_some_and(|getter| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(getter)) {
            self.getter.set(None);
        }
    }
}

impl Default for PropertyLookupCacheEntry {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

pub const MAX_NUMBER_OF_SHAPES_TO_REMEMBER: usize = 4;
// NB: GetById probes the entries of polymorphic caches unrolled.
const _: () = assert!(MAX_NUMBER_OF_SHAPES_TO_REMEMBER == 4);
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_INDEX_BITS: u32 = 4;
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_PRIMARY_CACHE_SIZE: usize = 1 << MEGAMORPHIC_INDEX_BITS;
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_SECONDARY_CACHE_SIZE: usize = 1 << MEGAMORPHIC_INDEX_BITS;
/// Fibonacci hashing (see megamorphic_hash()).
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_HASH_MULTIPLIER: u32 = 0x9e37_79b9;
const POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG: usize = PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG;
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_DATA_TAG: usize = 2;
/// How many (shape, key) pairs a megamorphic cache of a keyed access may miss and learn before it gives up (see
/// PropertyLookupCache::is_keyed_generic()).
const MAX_KEYED_MEGAMORPHIC_MISSES: u32 = 1024;
/// How many entries JIT code may copy into the tables of a megamorphic cache of a named access from the VM's keyed
/// property lookup cache, where it found them after missing the tables (see
/// PropertyLookupCache::take_vm_cache_lesson()). An access whose tables keep missing sees more shapes than they hold,
/// and then only uses the VM's cache.
pub const MAX_MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS: u32 = 16;

/// Which tier a property lookup cache is in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PropertyLookupCacheTier {
    Empty,
    Monomorphic,
    Polymorphic,
    Megamorphic,
}

const _: () = assert!(MEGAMORPHIC_PRIMARY_CACHE_SIZE.is_power_of_two());
const _: () = assert!(MEGAMORPHIC_SECONDARY_CACHE_SIZE.is_power_of_two());

// The interpreter reads the first entry at the start of each tier's data.
#[repr(C)]
struct MonomorphicData {
    entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry,
}

/// The data of the caches of the slot that the sites past the last one share, in every thread. Its entry stays empty,
/// so that their accesses go straight to their slow paths.
#[repr(transparent)]
struct UncacheableData(MonomorphicData);

// SAFETY: Nothing writes the entry, so threads only ever read it: monomorphic_data() does not hand it out, so neither
//         do first_entry_slot(), entries() and entry_slots_for_shape(), update(), forget_entries() and
//         remove_dead_entries() skip the caches that share it, and clear() does not free it.
unsafe impl Sync for UncacheableData {}

static UNCACHEABLE_DATA: UncacheableData = UncacheableData(MonomorphicData {
    entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new(),
});

/// The data pointer of the caches that share UNCACHEABLE_DATA.
fn uncacheable_data() -> usize {
    core::ptr::addr_of!(UNCACHEABLE_DATA.0).expose_provenance()
}

#[repr(C)]
struct PolymorphicData {
    entries: [PropertyLookupCacheEntry; MAX_NUMBER_OF_SHAPES_TO_REMEMBER],
}

// Keep the most recently used entry first so generated interpreter code can use the
// same fast path for every cache tier. Other shapes use the bounded two-level cache.
#[repr(C)]
struct MegamorphicData {
    entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry,
    primary_entries: [PropertyLookupCacheEntry; MEGAMORPHIC_PRIMARY_CACHE_SIZE],
    secondary_entries: [PropertyLookupCacheEntry; MEGAMORPHIC_SECONDARY_CACHE_SIZE],
    /// Misses of a keyed access (see MAX_KEYED_MEGAMORPHIC_MISSES).
    keyed_misses: Cell<u32>,
    /// Entries JIT code copied from the VM's keyed property lookup cache (see MAX_MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS).
    vm_cache_lessons: Cell<u32>,
}

const _: () = assert!(align_of::<MonomorphicData>() > PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK);
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<PolymorphicData>() > PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK);
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<MegamorphicData>() > PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(MonomorphicData, entry) == 0);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(PolymorphicData, entries) == 0);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(MegamorphicData, entry) == 0);

/// Where the hash tables of a megamorphic cache's data are, for JIT code that probes them.
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_PRIMARY_ENTRIES_OFFSET: usize = core::mem::offset_of!(MegamorphicData, primary_entries);
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_SECONDARY_ENTRIES_OFFSET: usize = core::mem::offset_of!(MegamorphicData, secondary_entries);
pub const MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS_OFFSET: usize = core::mem::offset_of!(MegamorphicData, vm_cache_lessons);

/// Fibonacci hashing of the low 32 bits of the shape pointer, mixed with the key of keyed caches: the indices are the
/// top bits of the product, which takes a multiply and a shift.
fn megamorphic_hash(shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> u32 {
    ((shape.as_ptr().addr() as u64 ^ key) as u32).wrapping_mul(MEGAMORPHIC_HASH_MULTIPLIER)
}

fn megamorphic_primary_index(shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> usize {
    (megamorphic_hash(shape, key) >> (32 - MEGAMORPHIC_INDEX_BITS)) as usize
}

fn megamorphic_secondary_index(shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> usize {
    (megamorphic_hash(shape, key) >> (32 - 2 * MEGAMORPHIC_INDEX_BITS)) as usize
        & (MEGAMORPHIC_SECONDARY_CACHE_SIZE - 1)
}

/// The slot of a megamorphic cache's hash tables that holds the entry for `shape` and `key`, if one does.
fn megamorphic_slot_for_shape(data: &MegamorphicData, shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> Option<&PropertyLookupCacheEntry> {
    let is_for_shape = |slot: &&PropertyLookupCacheEntry| {
        let entry = slot.get();
        entry.shape.is_some_and(|entry_shape| entry_shape.shape == shape) && entry.key == key
    };
    Some(&data.primary_entries[megamorphic_primary_index(shape, key)])
        .filter(is_for_shape)
        .or_else(|| Some(&data.secondary_entries[megamorphic_secondary_index(shape, key)]).filter(is_for_shape))
}

fn insert_megamorphic_entry(data: &MegamorphicData, entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) {
    let lookup_shape = entry.shape.expect("a megamorphic entry has a shape").shape;

    let primary_entry = &data.primary_entries[megamorphic_primary_index(lookup_shape, entry.key)];
    let primary = primary_entry.get();
    if let Some(displaced_shape) = primary.shape.map(|key| key.shape)
        && (displaced_shape != lookup_shape || primary.key != entry.key)
    {
        data.secondary_entries[megamorphic_secondary_index(displaced_shape, primary.key)].set(primary);
    }
    primary_entry.set(*entry);
}

/// The entries of a cache that may hold a shape, copied out by PropertyLookupCache::entries_for_shape().
pub struct PropertyLookupCacheEntries {
    entries: [PropertyLookupCacheEntryData; MAX_NUMBER_OF_SHAPES_TO_REMEMBER],
    count: usize,
}

impl PropertyLookupCacheEntries {
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[PropertyLookupCacheEntryData] {
        &self.entries[..self.count]
    }
}

// Represents one tiered inline cache used for property lookups. The tier is in the low bits of the data pointer.
impl PropertyLookupCache {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { data: Cell::new(0) }
    }

    /// The cache of the slot that the sites past the last one share.
    fn new_uncacheable() -> Self {
        Self {
            data: Cell::new(uncacheable_data()),
        }
    }

    fn is_uncacheable(&self) -> bool {
        self.data.get() == uncacheable_data()
    }

    fn data_pointer<T>(&self, tag: usize) -> Option<&T> {
        let data = self.data.get();
        if data == 0 || data & PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK != tag {
            return None;
        }
        let pointer = core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance::<T>(data & !PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK);
        // SAFETY: The tagged pointer came from Box::into_raw of a T with this tag, and the cache owns it until clear(), or
        //         it is UNCACHEABLE_DATA, which is static.
        Some(unsafe { &*pointer })
    }

    /// The data of a monomorphic cache, never UNCACHEABLE_DATA, whose entry must not be lent out.
    fn monomorphic_data(&self) -> Option<&MonomorphicData> {
        if self.is_uncacheable() {
            return None;
        }
        self.data_pointer(0)
    }

    fn polymorphic_data(&self) -> Option<&PolymorphicData> {
        self.data_pointer(POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG)
    }

    fn megamorphic_data(&self) -> Option<&MegamorphicData> {
        self.data_pointer(MEGAMORPHIC_DATA_TAG)
    }

    /// Whether this megamorphic cache may learn one more entry from the VM's keyed property lookup cache (see
    /// MAX_MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS), counting it if so.
    pub fn take_vm_cache_lesson(&self) -> bool {
        let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() else {
            return false;
        };
        let lessons = data.vm_cache_lessons.get();
        if lessons >= MAX_MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS {
            return false;
        }
        data.vm_cache_lessons.set(lessons + 1);
        true
    }

    fn set_data<T>(&self, data: Box<T>, tag: usize) {
        let address = Box::into_raw(data).expose_provenance();
        assert!(address & PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK == 0);
        self.data.set(address | tag);
    }

    /// Whether this cache keeps the entries of more shapes than a polymorphic cache can hold in hash tables.
    pub fn is_megamorphic(&self) -> bool {
        self.megamorphic_data().is_some()
    }

    /// Whether this is the cache of a keyed access that saw too many (shape, key) pairs to keep track of. Such a cache
    /// stays empty, so its accesses go straight to their slow paths.
    pub fn is_keyed_generic(&self) -> bool {
        self.data.get() == PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_KEYED_GENERIC_DATA
    }

    pub fn first_entry(&self) -> Option<PropertyLookupCacheEntryData> {
        self.first_entry_slot().map(PropertyLookupCacheEntry::get)
    }

    /// The entry the interpreter consults, for updating it in place. The reference must not be held across anything
    /// that may update the cache.
    pub fn first_entry_slot(&self) -> Option<&PropertyLookupCacheEntry> {
        if let Some(data) = self.monomorphic_data() {
            return Some(&data.entry);
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.polymorphic_data() {
            return Some(&data.entries[0]);
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() {
            return Some(&data.entry);
        }
        None
    }

    pub fn tier(&self) -> PropertyLookupCacheTier {
        let data = self.data.get();
        if data == 0 {
            return PropertyLookupCacheTier::Empty;
        }
        if self.is_keyed_generic() {
            return PropertyLookupCacheTier::Megamorphic;
        }
        match data & PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK {
            POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG => PropertyLookupCacheTier::Polymorphic,
            MEGAMORPHIC_DATA_TAG => PropertyLookupCacheTier::Megamorphic,
            _ => PropertyLookupCacheTier::Monomorphic,
        }
    }

    /// The entries the interpreter looks through: every entry of a polymorphic cache, and the most recently used one
    /// of the others.
    pub fn entries(&self) -> &[PropertyLookupCacheEntry] {
        if let Some(data) = self.monomorphic_data() {
            return core::slice::from_ref(&data.entry);
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.polymorphic_data() {
            return &data.entries;
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() {
            return core::slice::from_ref(&data.entry);
        }
        &[]
    }

    fn copy_entries(entries: &[PropertyLookupCacheEntry]) -> PropertyLookupCacheEntries {
        let mut copied = PropertyLookupCacheEntries {
            entries: [PropertyLookupCacheEntryData::default(); MAX_NUMBER_OF_SHAPES_TO_REMEMBER],
            count: entries.len(),
        };
        for (copy, entry) in copied.entries.iter_mut().zip(entries) {
            *copy = entry.get();
        }
        copied
    }

    /// The entries that may be for `shape` and `key` (see PropertyLookupCacheEntry::key; 0 for named accesses).
    /// Callers check each entry's shape and key. A megamorphic cache finds the one for the shape and key and moves it
    /// first, where the interpreter looks.
    pub fn entries_for_shape(&self, shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> PropertyLookupCacheEntries {
        Self::copy_entries(self.entry_slots_for_shape(shape, key))
    }

    /// entries_for_shape() in place, for the cache-only fast paths. The entries must not be held across anything that
    /// may update the cache.
    #[inline]
    pub fn entry_slots_for_shape(&self, shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> &[PropertyLookupCacheEntry] {
        let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() else {
            return self.entries();
        };
        let Some(slot) = megamorphic_slot_for_shape(data, shape, key) else {
            return &[];
        };

        data.entry.set(slot.get());
        core::slice::from_ref(&data.entry)
    }

    /// The entry a megamorphic cache has for `shape` and `key`, if it has one, without moving it to the front like
    /// `entry_slots_for_shape()` does.
    pub fn megamorphic_entry_for_shape(&self, shape: Gc<Shape>, key: u64) -> Option<&PropertyLookupCacheEntry> {
        megamorphic_slot_for_shape(self.megamorphic_data()?, shape, key)
    }

    /// Records an entry of `entry_type`, filled in by `callback`, moving the cache to the next tier when it has no
    /// room for it. Keyed sites also refresh entries after hits in the VM cache. Keep this out of line instead of
    /// growing the frames of the property access paths that every access runs through.
    #[inline(never)]
    pub fn update(
        &self,
        entry_type: PropertyLookupCacheEntryType,
        callback: impl FnOnce(&mut PropertyLookupCacheEntryData),
    ) {
        if self.is_keyed_generic() || self.is_uncacheable() {
            return;
        }

        let mut new_entry = PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
            entry_type,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        callback(&mut new_entry);

        if let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() {
            // NB: A keyed access that keeps missing cycles through more keys than the cache can hold, and filling it
            //     would cost more than it saves.
            if new_entry.key != 0 {
                let lookup_shape = new_entry.shape.expect("a megamorphic entry has a shape").shape;
                let is_known = |entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntry| {
                    let entry = entry.get();
                    entry.shape.is_some_and(|key| key.shape == lookup_shape) && entry.key == new_entry.key
                };
                let known = is_known(&data.primary_entries[megamorphic_primary_index(lookup_shape, new_entry.key)])
                    || is_known(&data.secondary_entries[megamorphic_secondary_index(lookup_shape, new_entry.key)]);
                if !known {
                    data.keyed_misses.set(data.keyed_misses.get() + 1);
                }
                if data.keyed_misses.get() > MAX_KEYED_MEGAMORPHIC_MISSES {
                    self.clear();
                    self.data.set(PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_KEYED_GENERIC_DATA);
                    return;
                }
            }
            insert_megamorphic_entry(data, &new_entry);
            data.entry.set(new_entry);
            return;
        }

        if self.data.get() == 0 {
            self.set_data(
                Box::new(MonomorphicData {
                    entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry::from_data(new_entry),
                }),
                0,
            );
            return;
        }

        if let Some(data) = self.monomorphic_data() {
            let old_entry = data.entry.get();
            if old_entry.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty
                || old_entry.has_same_cache_key_as(&new_entry)
            {
                data.entry.set(new_entry);
                return;
            }

            let new_data = Box::new(PolymorphicData {
                entries: core::array::from_fn(|_| PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new()),
            });
            new_data.entries[0].set(new_entry);
            new_data.entries[1].set(old_entry);
            self.clear();
            self.set_data(new_data, POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG);
            return;
        }

        let entries = &self
            .polymorphic_data()
            .expect("a cache with data is in one of the tiers")
            .entries;
        let mut insertion_index = entries
            .iter()
            .position(|entry| entry.get().has_same_cache_key_as(&new_entry))
            .unwrap_or(entries.len());

        if insertion_index == entries.len()
            && entries[entries.len() - 1].entry_type.get() != PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty
        {
            self.move_full_polymorphic_entries_to_megamorphic_tier(&new_entry);
            return;
        }

        if insertion_index == entries.len() {
            insertion_index = entries.len() - 1;
        }

        for index in (1..=insertion_index).rev() {
            entries[index].set(entries[index - 1].get());
        }
        entries[0].set(new_entry);
    }

    /// Boxing a MegamorphicData builds it on the stack first, in a frame of a few KB, so this stays out of line from
    /// update(), which runs on every miss.
    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn move_full_polymorphic_entries_to_megamorphic_tier(&self, new_entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) {
        let entries = &self
            .polymorphic_data()
            .expect("only a polymorphic cache becomes megamorphic")
            .entries;
        let new_data = Box::new(MegamorphicData {
            entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new(),
            primary_entries: core::array::from_fn(|_| PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new()),
            secondary_entries: core::array::from_fn(|_| PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new()),
            keyed_misses: Cell::new(0),
            vm_cache_lessons: Cell::new(0),
        });
        for entry in entries.iter().rev() {
            let entry = entry.get();
            if entry.shape.is_some() {
                insert_megamorphic_entry(&new_data, &entry);
            }
        }
        insert_megamorphic_entry(&new_data, new_entry);
        new_data.entry.set(*new_entry);
        self.clear();
        self.set_data(new_data, MEGAMORPHIC_DATA_TAG);
    }

    /// Forgets the entries, but keeps the storage of a monomorphic cache, whose next entry then takes the place of the
    /// empty one.
    pub fn forget_entries(&self) {
        if self.is_uncacheable() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.monomorphic_data() {
            data.entry.set(PropertyLookupCacheEntryData::default());
            return;
        }
        self.clear();
    }

    pub fn clear(&self) {
        if !self.is_uncacheable() {
            self.free_data();
        }
    }

    fn free_data(&self) {
        let data = self.data.get();
        if data == 0 || data == PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_KEYED_GENERIC_DATA {
            self.data.set(0);
            return;
        }
        let address = data & !PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK;
        // SAFETY: The tagged pointer came from Box::into_raw of the tier its tag names.
        unsafe {
            match data & PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK {
                0 => drop(Box::from_raw(
                    core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<MonomorphicData>(address),
                )),
                POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG => {
                    drop(Box::from_raw(
                        core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<PolymorphicData>(address),
                    ));
                }
                MEGAMORPHIC_DATA_TAG => {
                    drop(Box::from_raw(
                        core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<MegamorphicData>(address),
                    ));
                }
                _ => unreachable!("a cache tier tag"),
            }
        }
        self.data.set(0);
    }

    /// Forgets the entries with a cell that died in this collection.
    pub fn remove_dead_entries(&self, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) {
        if self.is_uncacheable() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(data) = self.megamorphic_data() {
            for entry in data
                .primary_entries
                .iter()
                .chain(&data.secondary_entries)
                .chain(core::iter::once(&data.entry))
            {
                entry.clear_if_it_has_a_dead_cell(sweep);
            }
            return;
        }

        for entry in self.entries() {
            entry.clear_if_it_has_a_dead_cell(sweep);
        }
    }
}

impl Default for PropertyLookupCache {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Drop for PropertyLookupCache {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.clear();
    }
}

impl Default for GlobalVariableCache {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            entry: PropertyLookupCacheEntry::new(),
            environment_serial_number: Cell::new(0),
            environment_binding_index: Cell::new(0),
            has_environment_binding_index: Cell::new(false),
        }
    }
}

impl GlobalVariableCache {
    /// Assigns a default GlobalVariableCache.
    pub fn reset(&self) {
        self.entry.set(PropertyLookupCacheEntryData::default());
        self.environment_serial_number.set(0);
        self.environment_binding_index.set(0);
        self.has_environment_binding_index.set(false);
    }

    pub fn first_entry(&self) -> Option<PropertyLookupCacheEntryData> {
        let entry = self.entry.get();
        (entry.entry_type != PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty).then_some(entry)
    }

    pub fn update(
        &self,
        entry_type: PropertyLookupCacheEntryType,
        callback: impl FnOnce(&mut PropertyLookupCacheEntryData),
    ) {
        let mut entry = PropertyLookupCacheEntryData {
            entry_type,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        callback(&mut entry);
        self.entry.set(entry);
    }
}
