//! Interpreter feedback consumed by the optimizing JIT.
//!
//! Every instruction that collects feedback carries one slot index per feedback kind it records, and each kind has
//! its own index space in `ExecutableFeedback`. Instructions with a property lookup cache record their value feedback
//! in the slot of their cache instead, which spares them an index.
//!
//! Slot indices are encoded as u16. An executable with more sites of one kind than fit in a u16 shares the last slot
//! between the remaining sites, which only merges their feedback (see `generator::MAX_FEEDBACK_SLOT_COUNT`).

use core::cell::{Cell, OnceCell};
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use crate::build_configuration::HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK;
use crate::gc::primitive_storage::{OwnedPrimitiveStorage, ZeroFillNewBytes};
use crate::gc::sweep::Sweep;
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, Gc};
use crate::layout::executable::CallCache;
pub use crate::layout::feedback::*;
use crate::layout::object::Object;
use crate::runtime::ecmascript_function_object::as_ecmascript_function_object;

/// How many feedback slots of each kind an executable's bytecode indexes into.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FeedbackSlotCounts {
    pub arith: u32,
    pub value: u32,
    pub call: u32,
    pub keyed: u32,
}

/// The `count` elements of type T at `offset` in `storage`.
fn array_in<T>(storage: Option<&OwnedPrimitiveStorage>, offset: usize, count: usize) -> &[T] {
    let Some(storage) = storage else {
        return &[];
    };
    // SAFETY: The feedback laid out `count` initialized elements of type T, aligned for T, at `offset` in the storage,
    //         which lives as long as the feedback. Its elements are cells, which allow shared mutation.
    unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(storage.data().add(offset).cast::<T>(), count) }
}

/// Where in the cage the interpreter finds the array at `offset` in `storage`, or 0 if there is none.
fn cage_offset_in(storage: Option<&OwnedPrimitiveStorage>, offset: usize) -> u64 {
    storage.map_or(0, |storage| (storage.offset() + offset) as u64)
}

fn allocate_feedback_storage(size: usize) -> Option<OwnedPrimitiveStorage> {
    // NB: No arith feedback, no call targets, no keyed feedback and no value feedback are all zero bytes.
    (size != 0).then(|| {
        OwnedPrimitiveStorage::allocate(size, ZeroFillNewBytes::Yes)
            .expect("there is memory for the feedback of an executable")
    })
}

/// The feedback of one executable, one array per kind, indexed by the slot indices of its instructions. The arrays
/// live in primitive storage, outside the GC heap.
///
/// Executables that warm up or that the JIT never compiles only run the profiling handlers of calls, returns and loop
/// back edges, which write arith and call feedback, and slow paths record keyed and value feedback for them. The value
/// buckets, which only the profiling tier writes, are made when the executable moves to it (see
/// `ensure_value_buckets()`), as most executables never get that warm. Until then, slow paths record values right into
/// the value feedback.
pub struct ExecutableFeedback {
    /// The arith feedback, the call feedback, the keyed feedback, the value feedback, then the value feedback of the
    /// sites of the property lookup caches.
    storage: Option<OwnedPrimitiveStorage>,
    counts: FeedbackSlotCounts,
    property_lookup_cache_count: u32,
    /// The value buckets of the sites of the property lookup caches, the last one first, then the other value buckets,
    /// once the profiling tier needs them. The interpreter finds both kinds from the start of the others.
    value_bucket_storage: OnceCell<OwnedPrimitiveStorage>,
    /// The call cache of each call site, which `ExecutableHead::call_caches` points at. They hold pointers that the
    /// interpreter trusts, so they are not in the primitive storage.
    call_caches: Box<[CallCache]>,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ExecutableFeedback>() == 120);

impl ExecutableFeedback {
    /// Where the call feedback starts in the storage.
    fn call_offset(&self) -> usize {
        const _: () = assert!(align_of::<CallFeedback>() <= 8);
        (self.counts.arith as usize).next_multiple_of(8)
    }

    /// Where the value buckets of the sites without a property lookup cache start in their storage.
    fn value_buckets_offset(&self) -> usize {
        size_of::<Cell<u64>>() * self.property_lookup_cache_count as usize
    }

    /// Where the keyed feedback starts in the storage.
    fn keyed_offset(&self) -> usize {
        const _: () = assert!(align_of::<KeyedFeedback>() <= 8);
        self.call_offset() + size_of::<CallFeedback>() * self.counts.call as usize
    }

    /// Where the value feedback starts in the storage.
    fn value_offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.keyed_offset() + size_of::<KeyedFeedback>() * self.counts.keyed as usize
    }

    /// Where the value feedback of the sites of the property lookup caches starts in the storage.
    fn cache_value_offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.value_offset() + size_of::<Cell<u16>>() * self.counts.value as usize
    }

    fn value_buckets_storage(&self) -> Option<&OwnedPrimitiveStorage> {
        self.value_bucket_storage.get()
    }

    fn value_bucket_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.counts.value as usize + self.property_lookup_cache_count as usize
    }

    pub fn arith(&self) -> &[Cell<u8>] {
        array_in(self.storage.as_ref(), 0, self.counts.arith as usize)
    }

    pub fn call(&self) -> &[CallFeedback] {
        array_in(self.storage.as_ref(), self.call_offset(), self.counts.call as usize)
    }

    /// Whether the value buckets exist, which the profiling tier writes. Executables without value feedback slots and
    /// property lookup caches need none, so they count as having them.
    pub fn has_value_buckets(&self) -> bool {
        self.value_bucket_count() == 0 || self.value_bucket_storage.get().is_some()
    }

    /// One bucket per value feedback slot, see `value_feedback`. Empty while there are none.
    pub fn value_buckets(&self) -> &[Cell<u64>] {
        if !self.has_value_buckets() {
            return &[];
        }
        array_in(
            self.value_buckets_storage(),
            self.value_buckets_offset(),
            self.counts.value as usize,
        )
    }

    /// The value bucket of the site of property lookup cache `cache`. There have to be value buckets.
    pub fn cache_value_bucket(&self, cache: u32) -> &Cell<u64> {
        let buckets = self.cache_value_buckets();
        &buckets[buckets.len() - 1 - cache as usize]
    }

    /// One value bucket per property lookup cache, the last one first. Empty while there are none.
    fn cache_value_buckets(&self) -> &[Cell<u64>] {
        if !self.has_value_buckets() {
            return &[];
        }
        array_in(
            self.value_buckets_storage(),
            0,
            self.property_lookup_cache_count as usize,
        )
    }

    pub fn keyed(&self) -> &[KeyedFeedback] {
        array_in(self.storage.as_ref(), self.keyed_offset(), self.counts.keyed as usize)
    }

    /// The value feedback, one per value feedback slot.
    pub fn value(&self) -> &[Cell<u16>] {
        array_in(self.storage.as_ref(), self.value_offset(), self.counts.value as usize)
    }

    /// The value feedback of the sites of the property lookup caches, indexed like the caches.
    pub fn cache_value(&self) -> &[Cell<u16>] {
        array_in(
            self.storage.as_ref(),
            self.cache_value_offset(),
            self.property_lookup_cache_count as usize,
        )
    }

    /// Records `value` for value feedback slot `slot`: in its bucket once there are buckets, and right into its value
    /// feedback before.
    pub fn record_value(&self, slot: usize, value: u64) {
        if self.has_value_buckets() {
            self.value_buckets()[slot].set(value);
        } else {
            let bits = &self.value()[slot];
            bits.set(bits.get() | value_feedback::for_bits(value));
        }
    }

    /// record_value() for the site of property lookup cache `cache`.
    pub fn record_cache_value(&self, cache: u32, value: u64) {
        if self.has_value_buckets() {
            self.cache_value_bucket(cache).set(value);
        } else {
            let bits = &self.cache_value()[cache as usize];
            bits.set(bits.get() | value_feedback::for_bits(value));
        }
    }

    /// Forgets the call targets and keys that died in this collection, which the feedback holds weakly. The value
    /// buckets are not references, but they are folded into the value feedback here as well.
    pub fn remove_dead_cells(&self, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) {
        self.update_value_feedback();
        let clear_if_dead = |cell: &Cell<Option<Gc<CellHeader>>>| {
            if decode_weak_reference(cell).is_some_and(|cell| sweep.is_dead_or_moving(cell)) {
                cell.set(None);
            }
        };
        for call in self.call() {
            clear_if_dead(&call.target);
            clear_if_dead(&call.forwarded_target);
        }
        for keyed in self.keyed() {
            clear_if_dead(&keyed.last_key);
        }
    }

    /// Folds the value buckets, the call sites' too, into the value feedback bits. The buckets are not references, so
    /// this runs when the feedback is about to be used and at every garbage collection.
    pub fn update_value_feedback(&self) {
        let buckets = self.value_buckets().iter().zip(self.value());
        let cache_buckets = self.cache_value_buckets().iter().rev().zip(self.cache_value());
        for (bucket, value) in buckets.chain(cache_buckets) {
            let bits = bucket.get();
            if bits != value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET {
                value.set(value.get() | value_feedback::for_bits(bits));
            }
        }
        for call in self.call() {
            let tag = call.value_bucket.get();
            if tag != value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG {
                call.value
                    .set(call.value.get() | value_feedback::for_bits(u64::from(tag) << 48));
            }
        }
    }

    /// The feedback of an executable, without the value buckets.
    pub fn new(counts: FeedbackSlotCounts, property_lookup_cache_count: u32) -> Self {
        let mut feedback = Self {
            storage: None,
            counts,
            property_lookup_cache_count,
            value_bucket_storage: OnceCell::new(),
            call_caches: (0..counts.call).map(|_| CallCache::default()).collect(),
        };
        feedback.storage = allocate_feedback_storage(
            feedback.cache_value_offset() + size_of::<Cell<u16>>() * property_lookup_cache_count as usize,
        );
        const _: () = assert!(arith_feedback::NONE == 0 && value_feedback::NONE == 0);
        for call in feedback.call() {
            call.value_bucket.set(value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG);
        }
        feedback
    }

    pub fn call_caches(&self) -> &[CallCache] {
        &self.call_caches
    }

    /// Makes the value buckets, if they are not there yet. The interpreter has to be pointed at them.
    pub fn ensure_value_buckets(&self) {
        if self.has_value_buckets() {
            return;
        }
        let Some(storage) = allocate_feedback_storage(size_of::<Cell<u64>>() * self.value_bucket_count()) else {
            unreachable!("has_value_buckets() is true for executables without value buckets");
        };
        if self.value_bucket_storage.set(storage).is_err() {
            unreachable!("the value buckets are made once");
        }
        for bucket in self.value_buckets().iter().chain(self.cache_value_buckets()) {
            bucket.set(value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET);
        }
    }

    /// Where the arith feedback, the value buckets, the call feedback and the keyed feedback start, as offsets into
    /// the primitive storage cage, for the interpreter, or 0 if there are none.
    pub fn array_offsets(&self) -> [u64; 4] {
        let value_buckets_storage = self.value_buckets_storage();
        [
            cage_offset_in(self.storage.as_ref(), 0),
            cage_offset_in(value_buckets_storage, self.value_buckets_offset()),
            cage_offset_in(self.storage.as_ref(), self.call_offset()),
            cage_offset_in(self.storage.as_ref(), self.keyed_offset()),
        ]
    }
}

/// A weak reference the feedback holds, decoded into the heap region like a cell value. The feedback lives in primitive
/// storage, where anything may have overwritten it, so the runtime only ever dereferences its references as cells of
/// the heap region.
fn decode_weak_reference(reference: &Cell<Option<Gc<CellHeader>>>) -> Option<Gc<CellHeader>> {
    let cell = reference.get()?;
    // NB: The heap region base was fixed before any cell existed.
    let base = crate::layout_forward::heap_region_base() as u64;
    let address = base + (cell.as_ptr() as u64 & HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK);
    let address = NonNull::new(core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut::<CellHeader>(address as usize))
        .expect("the heap region does not start at null");
    // SAFETY: The address is in the heap region, where the feedback's references to cells that are alive point.
    Some(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(address) })
}

impl CallFeedback {
    /// The first callee seen at this site, if it is still alive.
    pub fn target(&self) -> Option<Gc<CellHeader>> {
        decode_weak_reference(&self.target)
    }

    /// The function the first callee forwarded the first call through it to, if it is still alive.
    pub fn forwarded_target(&self) -> Option<Gc<CellHeader>> {
        decode_weak_reference(&self.forwarded_target)
    }

    /// Records that the first callee forwarded a call to `target`.
    pub fn record_forwarded_call(
        &self,
        target: Gc<CellHeader>,
        forwarding: CallFeedbackForwarding,
        argument_count: usize,
    ) {
        let argument_count = u16::try_from(argument_count).unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
        let Some(forwarded_target) = self.forwarded_target() else {
            self.forwarded_target.set(Some(target));
            self.forwarding.set(forwarding as u8);
            self.forwarded_argument_count.set(argument_count);
            return;
        };
        if self.forwarding.get() != forwarding as u8 || self.forwarded_argument_count.get() != argument_count {
            self.flags
                .set(self.flags.get() | call_feedback_flags::FORWARDED_POLYMORPHIC);
        } else if forwarded_target != target {
            let flag = if are_closures_of_one_function(forwarded_target, target) {
                call_feedback_flags::FORWARDED_CLOSURES
            } else {
                call_feedback_flags::FORWARDED_POLYMORPHIC
            };
            self.flags.set(self.flags.get() | flag);
        }
    }
}

/// Whether two cells are closures of one ECMAScript function.
pub fn are_closures_of_one_function(first: Gc<CellHeader>, second: Gc<CellHeader>) -> bool {
    let function_of = |cell: Gc<CellHeader>| as_ecmascript_function_object(cell.downcast::<Object>()?);
    match (function_of(first), function_of(second)) {
        (Some(first), Some(second)) => first.shared_data() == second.shared_data(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

impl KeyedFeedback {
    /// The last string or symbol key seen at this site, if it is still alive.
    pub fn last_key(&self) -> Option<Gc<CellHeader>> {
        decode_weak_reference(&self.last_key)
    }
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Code flushing: the code of functions that nothing ran for a while goes away, and comes back through the lazy compile
//! path when the function is called again.
//!
//! Each executable counts the collections since a frame last entered it (`ExecutableHead::idle_collection_count`): the
//! interpreter's Enter, the resume of a generator and the prologue of JIT code set it to 0, and the VM's sweep callback
//! counts it up (and sets it to 0 for the executables that frames still run). The VM keeps the times of the last
//! collections, which tell how long an executable was not entered for.
//!
//! There are two layers, each with an idle time of its own:
//! - The JIT code of an executable that idled for the first one is dropped, like a discard that does not count against
//!   the executable (see `Executable::flush_idle_jit_code()`).
//! - The executable of a function that idled for the second one is dropped as a whole. While a collection marks, the
//!   shared data of the function does not visit such an executable, so it dies unless something else holds it: a frame
//!   on a stack or in a suspended generator, JIT code that inlined it or calls it directly, a compile job, a local of
//!   native code. If it dies, the shared data goes back to its lazy state. It keeps the shared data of the functions
//!   the executable creates and the executable's template objects, which the next executable of its code takes over,
//!   so that a recompile changes nothing that code can observe.
//!
//! A layer's idle time is its base shifted left by how often the function was compiled again after a flush in that
//! layer, up to a limit, and a function that was compiled again that often is not flushed in that layer anymore.
//! Nothing is flushed while a debugger is attached.
//!
//! LIBJS_CODE_FLUSH holds comma-separated options: `on`, `off`, `stress` (flush everything that nothing else holds at
//! every collection), `jit=SECONDS`, `bytecode=SECONDS`, `collections=N` (the fewest collections an executable idles
//! for), `backoff=N` (the largest shift of the idle times) and `max-recompiles=N`.

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use std::collections::{HashSet, VecDeque};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::bytecode::executable::Executable;
use crate::gc::sweep::Sweep;
use crate::gc::weak::SweptAfterCollection;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::jit::code::CompileState;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::runtime::shared_function_instance_data::SharedFunctionInstanceData;

/// The flush layers, each with a count of recompiles on the shared data of a function.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FlushLayer {
    /// The JIT code of an executable.
    Jit = 0,
    /// The whole executable of a function.
    Bytecode = 1,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct CodeFlushingOptions {
    pub enabled: bool,
    /// Flush everything that nothing else holds at every collection, whatever its age.
    pub stress: bool,
    pub jit_idle_time: Duration,
    pub bytecode_idle_time: Duration,
    /// The fewest collections that an executable has to idle for to be flushed.
    pub min_idle_collections: u8,
    /// The largest left shift of the idle times by recompiles.
    pub max_backoff_shift: u8,
    /// After this many recompiles in a layer, a function is no longer flushed in that layer.
    pub max_recompiles: u8,
}

impl Default for CodeFlushingOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            enabled: true,
            stress: false,
            jit_idle_time: Duration::from_secs(10),
            bytecode_idle_time: Duration::from_secs(20),
            min_idle_collections: 2,
            max_backoff_shift: 3,
            max_recompiles: 6,
        }
    }
}

impl CodeFlushingOptions {
    /// The options that LIBJS_CODE_FLUSH asks for. Options it does not know are reported and ignored.
    pub fn from_environment() -> Self {
        let mut options = Self::default();
        let Ok(value) = std::env::var("LIBJS_CODE_FLUSH") else {
            return options;
        };
        for option in value.split(',').filter(|option| !option.is_empty()) {
            let (name, argument) = option.split_once('=').unwrap_or((option, ""));
            let seconds = || {
                argument
                    .parse::<f64>()
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|seconds| Duration::try_from_secs_f64(seconds).ok())
            };
            let number = || argument.parse::<u8>().ok();
            let known = match name {
                "off" => {
                    options.enabled = false;
                    true
                }
                "on" => {
                    options.enabled = true;
                    true
                }
                "stress" => {
                    options.stress = true;
                    true
                }
                "jit" => seconds().map(|time| options.jit_idle_time = time).is_some(),
                "bytecode" => seconds().map(|time| options.bytecode_idle_time = time).is_some(),
                "collections" => number().map(|count| options.min_idle_collections = count).is_some(),
                "backoff" => number()
                    .map(|shift| options.max_backoff_shift = shift.min(16))
                    .is_some(),
                "max-recompiles" => number().map(|count| options.max_recompiles = count).is_some(),
                _ => false,
            };
            if !known {
                eprintln!("LIBJS_CODE_FLUSH: Ignoring the option '{option}'");
            }
        }
        options
    }
}

/// What code flushing did in a VM, for measurements.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CodeFlushingStats {
    pub passes: Cell<u64>,
    pub flushes: [Cell<u64>; 2],
    pub recompiles: [Cell<u64>; 2],
    /// Recompiles that made a function reach the most recompiles of a layer, which stops its flushes there.
    pub backoff_stops: [Cell<u64>; 2],
    /// Recompiles of functions whose idle time was longer than the base time because of earlier recompiles.
    pub backed_off_recompiles: [Cell<u64>; 2],
    /// Executables of the bytecode layer that something else still held.
    pub held_bytecode_candidates: Cell<u64>,
    pub flushed_bytecode_bytes: Cell<u64>,
    pub recompile_nanoseconds: Cell<u64>,
}

impl CodeFlushingStats {
    fn count(counter: &Cell<u64>, amount: u64) {
        counter.set(counter.get().saturating_add(amount));
    }
}

/// A flush pass, from the start of the marking of a collection to its sweep.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Pass {
    now: Instant,
    /// The layers in which to flush whatever nothing else holds, whatever its age, by bit (see `FlushLayer`).
    forced_layers: u8,
    /// Whether the pass is there to give memory back to the system, for a process that is short of it.
    releases_memory: bool,
}

impl Pass {
    fn forces(self, layer: FlushLayer) -> bool {
        self.forced_layers & (1 << layer as u8) != 0
    }
}

/// Every flush layer, as bits.
pub const ALL_FLUSH_LAYERS: u8 = 1 << FlushLayer::Jit as u8 | 1 << FlushLayer::Bytecode as u8;

/// The most collections whose times the VM keeps, one more than an idle collection count can be.
const KEPT_COLLECTION_TIMES: usize = u8::MAX as usize + 1;

/// The shared data of a function that a flush pass found, which does not keep it alive.
struct FlushCandidate(Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData>);

// SAFETY: A pass finds its candidates while its collection marks, each in the trace of its own shared data, which is
//         live then. The sweep callback of that collection takes the bytecode candidates, and its post-GC task the JIT
//         candidates, neither of which allocates while it holds them. begin_pass() drops whatever is left before the
//         next collection marks, so no candidate ever outlives a collection.
unsafe impl SweptAfterCollection for FlushCandidate {}

/// The code flushing state of a VM.
pub struct CodeFlushing {
    pub options: CodeFlushingOptions,
    /// When the last collections swept, the latest last.
    collection_times: RefCell<VecDeque<Instant>>,
    flush_at_next_collection: Cell<u8>,
    pass: Cell<Option<Pass>>,
    /// The shared data whose executable it did not visit in the marking of this collection.
    bytecode_candidates: RefCell<Vec<FlushCandidate>>,
    /// The shared data whose executable's JIT code idled long enough in this collection.
    jit_candidates: RefCell<Vec<FlushCandidate>>,
    pub stats: CodeFlushingStats,
}

thread_local! {
    /// The code flushing state of the VM whose collection marks on this thread, while it runs a flush pass.
    static ACTIVE_PASS: Cell<Option<NonNull<CodeFlushing>>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

impl CodeFlushing {
    pub fn new(options: CodeFlushingOptions) -> Self {
        Self {
            options,
            collection_times: RefCell::new(VecDeque::with_capacity(KEPT_COLLECTION_TIMES)),
            flush_at_next_collection: Cell::new(0),
            pass: Cell::new(None),
            bytecode_candidates: RefCell::default(),
            jit_candidates: RefCell::default(),
            stats: CodeFlushingStats::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Makes the next collection flush whatever nothing else holds in `layers` (bits of `FlushLayer`), whatever its
    /// age. Only for tests.
    pub fn flush_at_next_collection(&self, layers: u8) {
        self.flush_at_next_collection.set(layers);
    }

    /// Starts a flush pass for the collection that is about to mark the live cells, if the VM flushes code now.
    pub fn begin_pass(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // NB: Only a collection uses up a forced flush; other markings (such as graph dumps) leave it for the next one.
        if !vm.heap().is_marking_for_collection() {
            return;
        }
        // NB: The candidates are not traced, so none may outlive the collection that found them, flush pass or not.
        self.bytecode_candidates.borrow_mut().clear();
        self.jit_candidates.borrow_mut().clear();
        let mut forced_layers = self.flush_at_next_collection.replace(0);
        // NB: A process that is short of memory is better off compiling its code again than keeping it.
        let releases_memory = vm.heap().is_returning_memory_to_system();
        if releases_memory {
            forced_layers = ALL_FLUSH_LAYERS;
        }
        if !(self.options.enabled || forced_layers != 0) || vm.debugging_enabled() {
            return;
        }
        self.pass.set(Some(Pass {
            now: Instant::now(),
            forced_layers: if self.options.stress {
                ALL_FLUSH_LAYERS
            } else {
                forced_layers
            },
            releases_memory,
        }));
        CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.passes, 1);
        ACTIVE_PASS.set(Some(NonNull::from(self)));
    }

    /// Whether the idle time of an executable that idled for `idle_collections` collections is long enough to flush
    /// it in `layer` in this pass, for a function that was compiled again `recompiles` times after flushes there.
    fn idled_long_enough(&self, pass: Pass, layer: FlushLayer, idle_collections: u8, recompiles: u8) -> bool {
        // NB: The most recompiles are there to stop a function from being flushed and compiled over and over, which
        //     is no reason to keep its code in a process that is short of memory.
        if recompiles >= self.options.max_recompiles && !pass.releases_memory {
            return false;
        }
        if pass.forces(layer) {
            return true;
        }
        if pass.forced_layers != 0 || !self.options.enabled {
            return false;
        }
        if idle_collections == 0 || idle_collections < self.options.min_idle_collections {
            return false;
        }
        let times = self.collection_times.borrow();
        let Some(&idle_since) = times
            .len()
            .checked_sub(usize::from(idle_collections))
            .and_then(|index| times.get(index))
        else {
            return false;
        };
        let base = match layer {
            FlushLayer::Jit => self.options.jit_idle_time,
            FlushLayer::Bytecode => self.options.bytecode_idle_time,
        };
        let shift = recompiles.min(self.options.max_backoff_shift);
        pass.now.saturating_duration_since(idle_since) >= base.saturating_mul(1u32 << shift)
    }

    /// For the marking of a collection: whether the shared data `shared_data` should leave its executable unvisited,
    /// as it idled long enough to be flushed. Notes the shared data for the end of the pass.
    fn consider(&self, pass: Pass, shared_data: &SharedFunctionInstanceData, executable: Gc<Executable>) -> bool {
        if !shared_data.can_flush_code() {
            return false;
        }
        let idle_collections = executable.head.idle_collection_count.get();
        if executable.jit_compile_state() == CompileState::Installed
            && self.idled_long_enough(
                pass,
                FlushLayer::Jit,
                idle_collections,
                shared_data.recompile_count(FlushLayer::Jit),
            )
        {
            self.jit_candidates
                .borrow_mut()
                .push(FlushCandidate(Gc::from_ref(shared_data)));
        }
        if !self.idled_long_enough(
            pass,
            FlushLayer::Bytecode,
            idle_collections,
            shared_data.recompile_count(FlushLayer::Bytecode),
        ) {
            return false;
        }
        self.bytecode_candidates
            .borrow_mut()
            .push(FlushCandidate(Gc::from_ref(shared_data)));
        true
    }

    /// Ends the flush pass of the collection whose marks are final: flushes the executables of the candidates that
    /// died, and has the VM flush the JIT code of the others once the collection is over.
    pub fn finish_pass(&self, vm: &Vm, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) {
        ACTIVE_PASS.set(None);
        self.note_collection();
        if self.pass.take().is_none() {
            return;
        }
        let candidates = core::mem::take(&mut *self.bytecode_candidates.borrow_mut());
        for FlushCandidate(shared_data) in candidates {
            let Some(executable) = shared_data.executable() else {
                continue;
            };
            if !sweep.is_dead(executable) {
                CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.held_bytecode_candidates, 1);
                continue;
            }
            CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.flushes[FlushLayer::Bytecode as usize], 1);
            CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.flushed_bytecode_bytes, executable.bytecode().len() as u64);
            shared_data.flush_executable(executable, sweep);
        }
        if !self.jit_candidates.borrow().is_empty() {
            vm.enqueue_code_flushing_task();
        }
    }

    /// Notes that a collection ran now.
    fn note_collection(&self) {
        let mut times = self.collection_times.borrow_mut();
        if times.len() == KEPT_COLLECTION_TIMES {
            times.pop_front();
        }
        times.push_back(Instant::now());
    }

    /// Drops the JIT code of the executables that idled long enough in the last collection, once it is over. Frames
    /// that still run an executable on a stack keep its code.
    pub fn flush_idle_jit_code(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        let candidates = core::mem::take(&mut *self.jit_candidates.borrow_mut());
        if candidates.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let mut running = HashSet::new();
        vm.for_each_live_execution_context(|frame| {
            if let Some(executable) = frame.executable.get() {
                running.insert(executable.as_ptr());
            }
            core::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(())
        });
        for FlushCandidate(shared_data) in candidates {
            let Some(executable) = shared_data.executable() else {
                continue;
            };
            if executable.jit_compile_state() != CompileState::Installed
                || running.contains(&Executable::head(executable).as_ptr())
            {
                continue;
            }
            CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.flushes[FlushLayer::Jit as usize], 1);
            shared_data.note_flushed_jit_code();
            executable.flush_idle_jit_code(vm);
        }
    }

    /// Notes that a function whose code was flushed in `layer` was compiled again, `recompiles` times now.
    pub fn note_recompile(&self, layer: FlushLayer, recompiles: u8) {
        CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.recompiles[layer as usize], 1);
        if recompiles > 1 && self.options.max_backoff_shift != 0 {
            CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.backed_off_recompiles[layer as usize], 1);
        }
        if recompiles == self.options.max_recompiles {
            CodeFlushingStats::count(&self.stats.backoff_stops[layer as usize], 1);
        }
    }
}

/// For the marking of a collection: whether `shared_data` should leave its executable unvisited, as it idled long
/// enough to be flushed. Outside of a flush pass, it never should.
pub fn bytecode_flush_candidate(shared_data: &SharedFunctionInstanceData, executable: Gc<Executable>) -> bool {
    let Some(flushing) = ACTIVE_PASS.get() else {
        return false;
    };
    // SAFETY: The VM sets the pass when its collection starts marking and clears it in the sweep callback of that
    //         collection, and the VM outlives its collections.
    let flushing = unsafe { flushing.as_ref() };
    let Some(pass) = flushing.pass.get() else {
        return false;
    };
    flushing.consider(pass, shared_data, executable)
}

//! Bytecode instruction types generated from interpreter.flap.
//!
//! The `OpCode` enum, `Instruction` enum, and all encoding/visiting methods
//! are generated by build.rs from interpreter.flap. This is the single source
//! of truth for instruction definitions.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::bytecode::executable_data::ConstantValue;

    #[test]
    fn selects_declarative_int32_specializations() {
        let instruction = Instruction::Add {
            arith_feedback: 3,
            dst: Operand::register(Register(0)),
            lhs: Operand::register(Register(1)),
            rhs: Operand::constant(0),
        };
        let constants = [ConstantValue::Number(42.0)];

        let specialized = specialize_instruction(&instruction, &constants).expect("Add should specialize");

        assert!(matches!(
            specialized,
            Instruction::AddRhsInt32 {
                arith_feedback: 3,
                rhs: 42,
                ..
            }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn selects_declarative_undefined_move_specializations() {
        let instruction = Instruction::Mov {
            dst: Operand::register(Register(0)),
            src: Operand::constant(0),
        };
        let constants = [ConstantValue::Undefined];

        let specialized = specialize_instruction(&instruction, &constants).expect("Mov should specialize");
        assert!(matches!(specialized, Instruction::MovSrcUndefined { .. }));
    }
}

//! - `executable_data` -- ExecutableData: a compiled body and everything needed to run it
//!

//! - `executable` -- Executable: the cell that holds bytecode and its caches
//! - `feedback` -- What the profiling interpreter observes for the optimizing JIT, per executable
//! - `flushing` -- Dropping the code of functions that did not run for a while

/// The view of an instruction in `op`, which lays out the instruction of its opcode in the bytecode.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The type must lay out the instruction of `OPCODE`, and only ever be a view of bytecode that holds the instruction.
#[cfg(not(test))]
pub unsafe trait BytecodeOp: Sized {
    const OPCODE: u8;

    /// The instruction's size in the bytecode.
    fn length(&self) -> u32;
}

/// The instruction at `pc` of the executable's bytecode, which has to be an `Op`.
#[cfg(not(test))]
pub fn instruction_at<Op: BytecodeOp>(executable: &executable::Executable, pc: u32) -> &Op {
    let bytes = &executable.bytecode()[pc as usize..];
    assert_eq!(bytes[0], Op::OPCODE);
    assert!(size_of::<Op>() <= bytes.len() && bytes.as_ptr().addr().is_multiple_of(align_of::<Op>()));
    // SAFETY: Executables only hold bytecode the generator encoded, so an instruction of this opcode, with the layout
    //         of Op and valid fields, starts at pc.
    let instruction = unsafe { &*bytes.as_ptr().cast::<Op>() };
    assert!(instruction.length() as usize <= bytes.len());
    instruction
}

/// One decoded native instruction. Offsets and lengths are relative to the
/// supplied code span, while `address` is its executable address.
pub struct DisassembledInstruction {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub address: u64,
    pub length: usize,
    pub text: String,
}

pub fn disassemble(code: &[u8], address: u64) -> Vec<DisassembledInstruction> {
    architecture::disassemble(code, address)
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
mod architecture {
    use super::DisassembledInstruction;
    use iced_x86::{Decoder, DecoderOptions, Formatter, IntelFormatter};

    pub fn disassemble(code: &[u8], address: u64) -> Vec<DisassembledInstruction> {
        let mut decoder = Decoder::with_ip(64, code, address, DecoderOptions::NONE);
        let mut formatter = IntelFormatter::new();
        let mut instructions = Vec::new();

        while decoder.can_decode() {
            let instruction = decoder.decode();
            let mut text = String::new();
            formatter.format(&instruction, &mut text);
            instructions.push(DisassembledInstruction {
                offset: usize::try_from(instruction.ip() - address).expect("native instruction offset fits usize"),
                address: instruction.ip(),
                length: instruction.len(),
                text,
            });
        }

        instructions
    }
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
mod architecture {
    use super::DisassembledInstruction;
    use farm64::format::{FmtFormatter, format_to_string};
    use farm64::{Decoder, DecoderOptions};

    pub fn disassemble(code: &[u8], address: u64) -> Vec<DisassembledInstruction> {
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(code, address, DecoderOptions::default());
        let formatter = FmtFormatter::new();
        let mut instructions = Vec::new();

        while decoder.can_decode() {
            let offset = decoder.position();
            let instruction = decoder.decode();
            let instruction_address = address + offset as u64;
            let text = if instruction.is_invalid() {
                let opcode = u32::from_le_bytes(code[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap());
                format!(".word 0x{opcode:08x}")
            } else {
                format_to_string(&formatter, &instruction)
            };
            instructions.push(DisassembledInstruction {
                offset,
                address: instruction_address,
                length: 4,
                text,
            });
        }

        instructions
    }
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
mod architecture {
    use super::DisassembledInstruction;

    pub fn disassemble(_code: &[u8], _address: u64) -> Vec<DisassembledInstruction> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(all(test, target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn decodes_x86_64_code() {
        let instructions = disassemble(&[0x48, 0x89, 0xd8, 0xc3], 0x1000);

        assert_eq!(instructions.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(instructions[0].offset, 0);
        assert_eq!(instructions[0].address, 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(instructions[0].length, 3);
        assert_eq!(instructions[0].text, "mov rax,rbx");
        assert_eq!(instructions[1].offset, 3);
        assert_eq!(instructions[1].address, 0x1003);
        assert_eq!(instructions[1].length, 1);
        assert_eq!(instructions[1].text, "ret");
    }
}

    use super::*;

/// Why the length of the encoded instruction at some offset cannot be told.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InstructionLengthError {
    UnknownOpcode,
    TruncatedInstruction,
}

/// The last slot of a cache table, which all the sites past it share. It never remembers anything.
pub const UNCACHED_SITE: u32 = u16::MAX as u32;

/// Every operand of a list can need a low temporary when spilling wide slots. Leave room for those and the other
/// operands of the instruction.
pub(crate) const MAX_OPERAND_LIST_LENGTH: usize = 200;

/// A cache index as an instruction holds it. `u32::MAX` means none, which stays all bits set.
#[inline]
pub fn narrow_index(index: u32) -> u16 {
    if index == u32::MAX {
        return u16::MAX;
    }
    u16::try_from(index).expect("cache indices fit in 16 bits")
}

/// The first value of a name table index field that is not an index itself. From there up to `NO_NAME_INDEX`, the field
/// holds how many bytes back from it the index is, in the WideNameIndices right before the instruction.
pub const WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK: u16 = 0xff00;

/// What an optional name table index field holds if it holds none.
pub const NO_NAME_INDEX: u16 = u16::MAX;

/// Whether a name table index is too large for its field, so that the instruction needs a WideNameIndices. `u32::MAX`
/// means none.
#[inline]
pub fn is_wide_name_index(index: u32) -> bool {
    index != u32::MAX && index >= u32::from(WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK)
}

/// The field of a name table index, whose slot of the WideNameIndices is `distance` bytes back from the field if the
/// index is too large for it. `u32::MAX` means none.
#[inline]
pub fn name_index_field(index: u32, distance: usize) -> u16 {
    if index == u32::MAX {
        return NO_NAME_INDEX;
    }
    if !is_wide_name_index(index) {
        return index as u16;
    }
    let distance = u16::try_from(distance)
        .ok()
        .filter(|&distance| distance < NO_NAME_INDEX - WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK)
        .expect("a WideNameIndices is right before its instruction");
    WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK + distance
}

/// The name table index of the field at `at`, if it holds one.
#[inline]
pub fn read_optional_name_index(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    match read_u16(bytes, at) {
        NO_NAME_INDEX => None,
        raw if raw >= WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK => Some(read_u32(bytes, at - usize::from(raw - WIDE_NAME_INDEX_MARK))),
        raw => Some(u32::from(raw)),
    }
}

#[inline]
pub fn read_name_index(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    read_optional_name_index(bytes, at).expect("the field holds a name table index")
}

#[inline]
pub fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 2].try_into().unwrap())
}

#[inline]
pub fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 4].try_into().unwrap())
}

#[inline]
pub fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_ne_bytes(bytes[at..at + 8].try_into().unwrap())
}

/// A bytecode register index.
///
/// Reserved registers:
/// - 0: accumulator
/// - 1: exception
/// - 2: this_value
/// - 3: return_value
/// - 4: saved_lexical_environment
/// - 5+: user registers
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Register(pub u32);

impl Register {
    pub const ACCUMULATOR: Register = Register(0);
    pub const EXCEPTION: Register = Register(1);
    pub const THIS_VALUE: Register = Register(2);
    pub const RETURN_VALUE: Register = Register(3);
    pub const SAVED_LEXICAL_ENVIRONMENT: Register = Register(4);
    pub const RESERVED_COUNT: u32 = 5;
}

/// A bytecode operand.
///
/// Encoded as a single `u32` with a 3-bit type tag in the top 3 bits
/// and a 29-bit index in the lower 29 bits:
///
///   `raw = (type << 29) | index`
///
/// The bytecode does not hold this encoding, but the frame slot that the operand ends up in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Operand(u32);

impl Operand {
    const TYPE_SHIFT: u32 = 29;
    const INDEX_MASK: u32 = 0x1FFF_FFFF;
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    pub fn register(reg: Register) -> Self {
        Self((0 << Self::TYPE_SHIFT) | reg.0)
    }

    pub fn local(index: u32) -> Self {
        Self((1 << Self::TYPE_SHIFT) | index)
    }

    pub fn constant(index: u32) -> Self {
        Self((2 << Self::TYPE_SHIFT) | index)
    }

    pub fn argument(index: u32) -> Self {
        Self((3 << Self::TYPE_SHIFT) | index)
    }

    pub fn invalid() -> Self {
        Self(Self::INVALID)
    }

    pub fn is_invalid(self) -> bool {
        self.0 == Self::INVALID
    }

    pub fn is_register(self) -> bool {
        !self.is_invalid() && self.operand_type() == OperandType::Register
    }

    pub fn is_local(self) -> bool {
        !self.is_invalid() && self.operand_type() == OperandType::Local
    }

    pub fn is_argument(self) -> bool {
        !self.is_invalid() && self.operand_type() == OperandType::Argument
    }

    pub fn is_constant(self) -> bool {
        !self.is_invalid() && self.operand_type() == OperandType::Constant
    }

    pub fn operand_type(self) -> OperandType {
        assert!(!self.is_invalid(), "operand_type() called on INVALID operand");
        match (self.0 >> Self::TYPE_SHIFT) & 0x7 {
            0 => OperandType::Register,
            1 => OperandType::Local,
            2 => OperandType::Constant,
            3 => OperandType::Argument,
            _ => unreachable!("operand type bits can only be 0-3"),
        }
    }

    pub fn index(self) -> u32 {
        self.0 & Self::INDEX_MASK
    }

    pub fn raw(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }

    pub fn from_raw(raw: u32) -> Self {
        Self(raw)
    }

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OperandType {
    Register,
    Local,
    Constant,
    Argument,
}

/// A bytecode label.
///
/// During compilation, holds a basic block index. After linking,
/// holds the final byte offset in the flat bytecode stream.
/// Stored as a single `u32`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct Label(pub u32);

impl Label {}

/// Index into the string table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct StringTableIndex(pub u32);

impl StringTableIndex {
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }
}

/// Index into the identifier table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct IdentifierTableIndex(pub u32);

impl IdentifierTableIndex {
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;

    pub fn optional_from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        if raw == Self::INVALID { None } else { Some(Self(raw)) }
    }
}

/// Index into the property key table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct PropertyKeyTableIndex(pub u32);

/// Environment coordinate used by environment lookup instructions, which hold the hops in a byte and the index in two.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct EnvironmentCoordinate {
    pub hops: u32,
    pub index: u32,
}

impl EnvironmentCoordinate {
    pub const INVALID: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFE;

    /// Whether an instruction can hold the coordinate. Bindings past it are looked up by name.
    pub fn fits_in_instruction(&self) -> bool {
        self.hops <= u32::from(u8::MAX) && self.index <= u32::from(u16::MAX)
    }

    pub fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            hops: Self::INVALID,
            index: Self::INVALID,
        }
    }
}

//! The property gets and puts that consult and fill the inline caches the interpreter's fast paths read.

use ak::Utf16FlyString;
use libjs_abi::PutKind;

use crate::bytecode::executable::{
    KeyedPropertyLookup, KeyedPropertyLookupCache, PropertyLookupCache, PropertyLookupCacheEntryType,

use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
