    Normal,
    Length,
}

/// Whether the code doing a property access is strict mode code.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Strict {
    No,
    Yes,
}

pub fn get_cached_property_value(vm: &Vm, value: Value, this_value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    if !value.is_accessor() {
        return Ok(value);
    }

    // https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinaryget
    // If _getter_ is *undefined*, return *undefined*.
    let Some(getter) = value.as_accessor().getter() else {
        return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
    };
    call_function_object(vm, getter, this_value, &[])
}

pub fn object_can_cache_property_additions(object: &Object) -> bool {
    !object.may_interfere_with_indexed_property_access() && !object.requires_slow_add_own_property()
}

pub fn property_addition_is_cacheable(vm: &Vm, object: &Object, property_key: &PropertyKey) -> bool {
    if !property_key.is_string() {
        return object_can_cache_property_additions(object);
    }
    object_can_cache_property_additions(object)
        && !(object.has_magical_length_property() && property_key.as_string() == vm.names.length.as_string())
}

/// Remembers a keyed lookup that the VM's keyed property lookup cache describes in the per-site cache of the
/// instruction that made it, keyed by the identity of the key Value (see PropertyLookupCacheEntry::key).
fn remember_keyed_lookup(site_cache: &PropertyLookupCache, site_cache_key: u64, entry: &KeyedPropertyLookup) {
    site_cache.update(entry.entry_type, |site_entry| {
        site_entry.key = site_cache_key;
        site_entry.property_offset = entry.property_offset;
        site_entry.shape = entry.shape_key();
        site_entry.prototype = entry.prototype;
        site_entry.prototype_chain_validity = entry.prototype_chain_validity;
    });
}

/// Copies the entry of the VM's keyed property lookup cache for the shape of `object` and the name whose identity is
/// `name_identity` into `site_cache`, the megamorphic cache of a named get whose compiled code missed its tables and
/// then found that entry. The tables then have it inline the next time, unless the get sees more shapes than they
/// hold (see MAX_MEGAMORPHIC_VM_CACHE_LESSONS).
pub fn remember_vm_cache_get(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, site_cache: &PropertyLookupCache, name_identity: usize) {
    let shape = object.shape();
    let Some(entry) = vm
        .keyed_property_lookup_cache()
        .lookup_by_name_identity(shape, name_identity)
    else {
        return;
    };
    if entry.shape_key() == Some(ShapeKey::of(shape)) && site_cache.take_vm_cache_lesson() {
        remember_keyed_lookup(site_cache, 0, &entry);
    }
}

/// Gets a property by a key that is not known statically. Lookups of string keys are cached in the VM's keyed property
/// lookup cache, and also in `site_cache` under its key if one is given, so that the instruction can find them again
/// by the identity of its key Value.
pub fn get_by_value_with_keyed_cache(
    vm: &Vm,
    base_object: Gc<Object>,
    this_value: Value,
    property_key: &PropertyKey,
    site_cache: Option<(&PropertyLookupCache, u64)>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    if !property_key.is_string() || !base_object.is_cacheable_across_realms() {
        return base_object.internal_get(vm, property_key, this_value, None, PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty);
    }

    let property_name = property_key.as_string();
    let shape = base_object.shape();
    let keyed_property_lookup_cache = vm.keyed_property_lookup_cache();
    let entry_index = KeyedPropertyLookupCache::entry_index_for(shape, property_name);
    let remember = |entry: &KeyedPropertyLookup| {
        if let Some((site_cache, site_cache_key)) = site_cache {
            remember_keyed_lookup(site_cache, site_cache_key, entry);
        }
    };
    if let Some(entry) = keyed_property_lookup_cache.lookup(entry_index, shape, property_name)
        && entry.shape_key() == Some(ShapeKey::of(shape))
    {
        let prototype_chain_validity_is_valid = entry
            .prototype_chain_validity
            .is_some_and(|validity| validity.is_valid());
        match entry.entry_type {
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty => {
                remember(&entry);
                return get_cached_property_value(vm, base_object.get_direct(entry.property_offset), this_value);
            }
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                if prototype_chain_validity_is_valid {
                    remember(&entry);
                    let prototype = entry.prototype.expect("an inherited property has a holder");
                    return get_cached_property_value(vm, prototype.get_direct(entry.property_offset), this_value);
                }
            }
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
                if base_object.is_cacheable_for_property_absence()
                    && (shape.prototype().is_none() || prototype_chain_validity_is_valid) =>
            {
                remember(&entry);
                return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    let prototype_chain_validity = shape
        .prototype()
        .and_then(|prototype| prototype.shape().prototype_chain_validity());

    let shape_key = ShapeKey::of(shape);
    let mut cacheable_metadata = CacheableGetPropertyMetadata {
        // NB: Indexed properties live outside the shape, so a shape can't vouch for the absence of one.
        property_absence_is_cacheable: !property_key.is_number()
            && base_object.is_cacheable_for_absence_of(vm, property_key),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let value = base_object.internal_get(
        vm,
        property_key,
        this_value,
        Some(&mut cacheable_metadata),
        PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
    )?;

    // A getter may have changed the object's shape or the property storage of a dictionary shape, which
    // leaves the metadata describing a lookup that no longer applies.
    if ShapeKey::of(base_object.shape()) != shape_key
        || cacheable_metadata.r#type == CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::NotCacheable
    {
        return Ok(value);
    }

    let mut entry = KeyedPropertyLookup::for_shape(shape_key);
    match cacheable_metadata.r#type {
        CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetOwnProperty => {
            entry.entry_type = PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty;
            entry.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                .property_offset
                .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
        }
        CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
            entry.entry_type = PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain;
            entry.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                .property_offset
                .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
            entry.prototype = cacheable_metadata.prototype;
            entry.prototype_chain_validity = prototype_chain_validity;
        }
        CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetMissingProperty => {
            entry.entry_type = PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty;
            entry.prototype_chain_validity = prototype_chain_validity;
        }
        CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::NotCacheable => unreachable!("an uncacheable lookup returned above"),
    }
    remember(&entry);
    keyed_property_lookup_cache.set_entry(entry_index, entry, property_name);
    Ok(value)
}

// Non-standard
pub fn get_own_property_without_side_effects(
    object: &Object,
    property_key: &PropertyKey,
    cache: &PropertyLookupCache,
) -> Value {
    let shape = object.shape();

    if let Some(cache_entry) = cache.first_entry()
        && (cache_entry.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
            || cache_entry.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty)
        && cache_entry.shape == Some(ShapeKey::of(shape))
    {
        if cache_entry.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty {
            return Value::EMPTY;
        }
        return object.get_direct(cache_entry.property_offset);
    }

    let metadata = shape.lookup(property_key);
    let cache_type = if metadata.is_some() {
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
    } else {
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
    };
    cache.update(cache_type, |entry| {
        entry.shape = Some(ShapeKey::of(shape));
        if let Some(metadata) = metadata {
            entry.property_offset = metadata.offset;
        }
    });

    let Some(metadata) = metadata else {
        return Value::EMPTY;
    };
    object.get_direct(metadata.offset)
}

pub fn base_object_for_get_impl(vm: &Vm, base_value: Value) -> Option<Gc<Object>> {
    if base_value.is_object() {
        return Some(base_value.as_object());
    }

    // OPTIMIZATION: For various primitives we can avoid actually creating a new object for them.
    if base_value.is_nullish() {
        return None;
    }
    let realm = vm
        .current_realm()
        .expect("there is a current realm to find the prototype of a primitive in");
    if base_value.is_string() {
        return Some(realm.string_prototype(vm));
    }
    if base_value.is_number() {
        return Some(realm.number_prototype(vm));
    }
    if base_value.is_boolean() {
        return Some(realm.boolean_prototype(vm));
    }
    if base_value.is_bigint() {
        return Some(realm.bigint_prototype(vm));
    }
    if base_value.is_symbol() {
        return Some(realm.symbol_prototype(vm));
    }

    None
}

#[cold]
fn throw_null_or_undefined_property_get<T>(
    vm: &Vm,
    base_value: Value,
    get_base_identifier: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    property_name: &dyn Utf16Display,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    assert!(base_value.is_nullish());

    if let Some(base_identifier) = get_base_identifier() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::ToObjectNullOrUndefinedWithPropertyAndName,
            &[property_name, &base_value, &base_identifier],
        );
    }
    vm.throw_completion(
        ErrorKind::TypeError,
        ErrorType::ToObjectNullOrUndefinedWithProperty,
        &[property_name, &base_value],
    )
}

/// The object a property get on `base_value` looks the property up in. `property_name` is the property as the error
/// for a null or undefined base names it: a key, or the value a key has yet to be computed from.
pub fn base_object_for_get(
    vm: &Vm,
    base_value: Value,
    get_base_identifier: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    property_name: &dyn Utf16Display,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Object>> {
    if let Some(base_object) = base_object_for_get_impl(vm, base_value) {
        return Ok(base_object);
    }

    // NOTE: At this point this is guaranteed to throw (null or undefined).
    throw_null_or_undefined_property_get(vm, base_value, get_base_identifier, property_name)
}

pub fn get_by_id(
    vm: &Vm,
    mode: GetByIdMode,
    get_base_identifier: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    property_name: &PropertyKey,
    base_value: Value,
    this_value: Value,
    cache: &PropertyLookupCache,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    if mode == GetByIdMode::Length && base_value.is_string() {
        return Ok(Value::from_f64(
            base_value.as_string().length_in_utf16_code_units() as f64
        ));
    }

    if base_value.is_string() {
        // https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-stringgetownproperty
        // String exotic objects expose virtual own properties for canonical string indexes.
        let string_value = base_value.as_string().get(vm, property_name)?;
        if let Some(string_value) = string_value {
            return Ok(string_value);
        }
    }

    let base_obj = base_object_for_get(vm, base_value, get_base_identifier, property_name)?;

    // OPTIMIZATION: Fast path for the magical "length" property on Array objects.
    if mode == GetByIdMode::Length && base_obj.has_magical_length_property() {
        return Ok(Value::from_f64(f64::from(base_obj.indexed_array_like_size())));
    }

    get_with_property_lookup_cache(vm, base_obj, property_name, this_value, cache, 0)
}

/// The slot an entry of `cache` for the shape of `object` points to, which may hold an accessor, or undefined for a
/// missing property.
#[inline(always)]
pub fn cached_property_slot(object: Gc<Object>, cache: &PropertyLookupCache, cache_key: u64) -> Option<Value> {
    let shape = object.shape();
    for entry in cache.entry_slots_for_shape(shape, cache_key) {
        // NB: Only the caches of keyed accesses have keys, and named accesses pass a constant 0.
        if cache_key != 0 && entry.key.get() != cache_key {
            continue;
        }
        if entry.shape_key() != Some(ShapeKey::of(shape)) {
            continue;
        }
        let prototype_chain_is_valid = || {
            entry
                .prototype_chain_validity
                .get()
                .is_some_and(|validity| validity.is_valid())
        };
        match entry.entry_type.get() {
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty => {
                if !object.is_cacheable_for_property_absence()
                    || (shape.prototype().is_some() && !prototype_chain_is_valid())
                {
                    continue;
                }
                return Some(Value::UNDEFINED);
            }
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                let Some(prototype) = entry.prototype.get() else {
                    return Some(object.get_direct(entry.property_offset.get()));
                };
                if !prototype_chain_is_valid() {
                    continue;
                }
                return Some(prototype.get_direct(entry.property_offset.get()));
            }
            _ => continue,
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Gets the property from `base_obj` through `cache`, filling the cache on a miss. `cache_key` is the key the cache's
/// entries are for (see PropertyLookupCacheEntry::key).
#[inline(always)]
pub fn get_with_property_lookup_cache(
    vm: &Vm,
    base_obj: Gc<Object>,
    property_name: &PropertyKey,
    this_value: Value,
    cache: &PropertyLookupCache,
    cache_key: u64,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    if let Some(value) = cached_property_slot(base_obj, cache, cache_key) {
        return get_cached_property_value(vm, value, this_value);
    }
    if vm.is_static_property_lookup_cache(cache) && !base_obj.is_cacheable_across_realms() {
        return base_obj.internal_get(vm, property_name, this_value, None, PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty);
    }
    // NB: A megamorphic named access sees more shapes than its hash tables hold, so it also looks in the VM's keyed
    //     property lookup cache, which has room for many more.
    //     Objects the keyed cache does not take keep using the access's own cache.
    if cache_key == 0 && cache.is_megamorphic() && property_name.is_string() && base_obj.is_cacheable_across_realms() {
        return get_by_value_with_keyed_cache(vm, base_obj, this_value, property_name, Some((cache, 0)));
    }
    let shape = base_obj.shape();
    let prototype_chain_validity = shape
        .prototype()
        .and_then(|prototype| prototype.shape().prototype_chain_validity());

    let shape_key = ShapeKey::of(shape);
    let mut cacheable_metadata = CacheableGetPropertyMetadata {
        // NB: Indexed properties live outside the shape, so a shape can't vouch for the absence of one.
        property_absence_is_cacheable: !property_name.is_number()
            && base_obj.is_cacheable_for_absence_of(vm, property_name),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let value = base_obj.internal_get(
        vm,
        property_name,
        this_value,
        Some(&mut cacheable_metadata),
        PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
    )?;

    // If internal_get() caused object's shape change, we can no longer be sure
    // that collected metadata is valid, e.g. if getter in prototype chain added
    // property with the same name into the object itself. The same applies when
    // a getter changed the property storage of a dictionary shape.
    if ShapeKey::of(base_obj.shape()) == shape_key {
        match cacheable_metadata.r#type {
            CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetOwnProperty => {
                cache.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty, |entry| {
                    entry.key = cache_key;
                    entry.shape = Some(shape_key);
                    entry.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                        .property_offset
                        .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
                });
            }
            CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                cache.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain, |entry| {
                    entry.key = cache_key;
                    entry.shape = Some(shape_key);
                    entry.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                        .property_offset
                        .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
                    entry.prototype = cacheable_metadata.prototype;
                    entry.prototype_chain_validity = prototype_chain_validity;
                });
            }
            CacheableGetPropertyMetadataType::GetMissingProperty => {
                cache.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty, |entry| {
                    entry.key = cache_key;
                    entry.shape = Some(shape_key);
                    entry.prototype_chain_validity = prototype_chain_validity;
                });
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    Ok(value)
}

#[cold]
fn throw_null_or_undefined_property_access<T>(
    vm: &Vm,
    base_value: Value,
    base_identifier: Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    property_identifier: &dyn Utf16Display,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    assert!(base_value.is_nullish());

    if let Some(base_identifier) = base_identifier {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::ToObjectNullOrUndefinedWithPropertyAndName,
            &[property_identifier, &base_value, &base_identifier],
        );
    }
    vm.throw_completion(
        ErrorKind::TypeError,
        ErrorType::ToObjectNullOrUndefinedWithProperty,
        &[property_identifier, &base_value],
    )
}

/// Throw the TypeError of a put to `base` if it is null or undefined. ToObject converts the base before the key is
/// converted to a property key, so `property_name` is the property as the error names it: a key, or the value a key
/// has yet to be computed from.
pub fn throw_if_nullish_put_base(
    vm: &Vm,
    base: Value,
    get_base_identifier: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    property_name: &dyn Utf16Display,
    strict: Strict,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    if !base.is_nullish() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    // Better error message than to_object would give
    if strict == Strict::Yes {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::ReferenceNullishSetProperty,
            &[property_name, &base],
        );
    }
    throw_null_or_undefined_property_access(vm, base, get_base_identifier(), property_name)
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
#[inline]
pub fn put_by_property_key(
    vm: &Vm,
    base: Value,
    this_value: Value,
    value: Value,
    get_base_identifier: impl FnOnce() -> Option<Utf16FlyString>,
    name: &PropertyKey,
    kind: PutKind,
    strict: Strict,
    caches: Option<&PropertyLookupCache>,
    cache_key: u64,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    // a. Let baseObj be ? ToObject(V.[[Base]]).
    throw_if_nullish_put_base(vm, base, get_base_identifier, name, strict)?;
    let object = base.to_object(vm)?;

    if kind == PutKind::Getter || kind == PutKind::Setter {
        // The generator should only pass us functions for getters and setters.
        assert!(value.is_function());
    }
    match kind {
        PutKind::Getter | PutKind::Setter => {
            let function = value.as_function();
            if let Some(ecmascript_function) = as_ecmascript_function_object(function)
                && ecmascript_function.name().is_empty()
            {
                let prefix = if kind == PutKind::Getter { "get" } else { "set" };
                ecmascript_function.set_inferred_name(vm, &ClassElementName::PropertyKey(name.clone()), Some(prefix));
            }
            let attributes = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::ENUMERABLE);
            if kind == PutKind::Getter {
                object.define_direct_accessor(vm, name, Some(function), None, attributes);
            } else {
                object.define_direct_accessor(vm, name, None, Some(function), attributes);
            }
        }
        PutKind::Normal => {
            // NB: The this value of a super property reference need not be an object, e.g. for `super.x = v` in a method
            //     called with a null this. [[Set]] handles a non-object receiver by failing to create or change a data
            //     property (https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarysetwithowndescriptor, step 2.b), but the caches below
            //     assume an object one, so don't use them for such a receiver.
            let (caches, from_shape) = if this_value.is_object() {
                (caches, this_value.as_object().shape())
            } else {
                (None, object.shape())
            };
            let from_shape = ShapeKey::of(from_shape);
            if let Some(caches) = caches {
                for cache in caches.entries_for_shape(object.shape(), cache_key).as_slice() {
                    // NB: Only the caches of keyed accesses have keys, and named accesses pass a constant 0.
                    if cache_key != 0 && cache.key != cache_key {
                        continue;
                    }
                    match cache.entry_type {
                        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty => {}
                        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                            let Some(cached_prototype) = cache.prototype else {
                                continue;
                            };
                            // OPTIMIZATION: If the prototype chain hasn't been mutated in a way that would invalidate the cache, we can use it.
                            let can_use_cache = cache.shape == Some(ShapeKey::of(object.shape()))
                                && cache
                                    .prototype_chain_validity
                                    .is_some_and(|validity| validity.is_valid());
                            if can_use_cache {
                                let value_in_prototype = cached_prototype.get_direct(cache.property_offset);
                                if value_in_prototype.is_accessor() {
                                    let Some(setter) = value_in_prototype.as_accessor().setter() else {
                                        continue;
                                    };
                                    call_function_object(vm, setter, this_value, &[value])?;
                                    return Ok(());
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty => {
                            if cache.shape != Some(ShapeKey::of(object.shape())) {
                                continue;
                            }

                            let value_in_object = object.get_direct(cache.property_offset);
                            if value_in_object.is_accessor() {
                                let Some(setter) = value_in_object.as_accessor().setter() else {
                                    continue;
                                };
                                call_function_object(vm, setter, this_value, &[value])?;
                                return Ok(());
                            }
                            if !cache.writes_data_property {
                                continue;
                            }
                            object.put_direct_from_cache(cache.property_offset, value);
                            return Ok(());
                        }
                        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty => {
                            // OPTIMIZATION: If the object's shape is the same as the one cached before adding the new property, we can
                            //               reuse the resulting shape from the cache.
                            if cache.shape != Some(ShapeKey::of(object.shape())) {
                                continue;
                            }
                            if !property_addition_is_cacheable(vm, &object, name) {
                                continue;
                            }
                            let Some(new_shape) = cache.new_shape else {
                                continue;
                            };

                            // The cache is invalid if the prototype chain has been mutated, since such a mutation could have added a setter for the property.
                            if cache
                                .prototype_chain_validity
                                .is_some_and(|validity| !validity.is_valid())
                            {
                                continue;
                            }
                            object.unsafe_set_shape(new_shape);
                            object.initialize_direct(cache.property_offset, value);
                            return Ok(());
                        }
                        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
                        | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain
                        | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
                        | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::MissingOwnProperty => {}
                    }
                }
            }

            let caches = caches
                .filter(|cache| !vm.is_static_property_lookup_cache(cache) || object.is_cacheable_across_realms());
            let prototype_chain_validity = object
                .shape()
                .prototype()
                .and_then(|prototype| prototype.shape().prototype_chain_validity());

            let mut cacheable_metadata = CacheableSetPropertyMetadata::default();
            let succeeded = object.internal_set(
                vm,
                name,
                value,
                this_value,
                Some(&mut cacheable_metadata),
                PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
            )?;

            if let Some(caches) = caches
                && succeeded
                && cacheable_metadata.r#type == CacheableSetPropertyMetadataType::AddOwnProperty
            {
                caches.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty, |cache| {
                    cache.key = cache_key;
                    cache.shape = Some(from_shape);
                    cache.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                        .property_offset
                        .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
                    cache.new_shape = Some(object.shape());
                    if let Some(prototype) = cacheable_metadata.prototype {
                        cache.prototype_chain_validity = prototype.shape().prototype_chain_validity();
                    }
                });
            }

            // If internal_set() caused object's shape change, we can no longer be sure
            // that collected metadata is valid, e.g. if setter in prototype chain added
            // property with the same name into the object itself. The same applies when
            // a setter changed the property storage of a dictionary shape.
            if let Some(caches) = caches
                && succeeded
                && ShapeKey::of(object.shape()) == from_shape
            {
                match cacheable_metadata.r#type {
                    CacheableSetPropertyMetadataType::AddOwnProperty => {
                        // Something went wrong if we ended up here, because cacheable addition of a new property should've changed the shape.
                        unreachable!("a cacheable addition of a property changes the shape");
                    }
                    CacheableSetPropertyMetadataType::ChangeOwnProperty => {
                        caches.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty, |cache| {
                            cache.key = cache_key;
                            cache.shape = Some(from_shape);
                            cache.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                                .property_offset
                                .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
                            cache.writes_data_property = cacheable_metadata.writes_data_property;
                        });
                    }
                    CacheableSetPropertyMetadataType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                        caches.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain, |cache| {
                            cache.key = cache_key;
                            cache.shape = Some(from_shape);
                            cache.property_offset = cacheable_metadata
                                .property_offset
                                .expect("cacheable metadata has an offset");
                            let prototype = cacheable_metadata
                                .prototype
                                .expect("a property in the prototype chain has a holder");
                            cache.prototype = Some(prototype);
                            cache.prototype_chain_validity = prototype_chain_validity;
                        });
                    }
                    CacheableSetPropertyMetadataType::NotCacheable => {}
                }
            }

            if !succeeded && strict == Strict::Yes {
                if base.is_object() {
                    return vm.throw_completion(
                        ErrorKind::TypeError,
                        ErrorType::ReferenceNullishSetProperty,
                        &[name, &base],
                    );
                }
                return vm.throw_completion(
                    ErrorKind::TypeError,
                    ErrorType::ReferencePrimitiveSetProperty,
                    &[name, &base.typeof_(vm), &base],
                );
            }
        }
        PutKind::Own => {
            if let Some(caches) = caches {
                for cache in caches.entries_for_shape(object.shape(), cache_key).as_slice() {
                    // NB: Only the caches of keyed accesses have keys, and named accesses pass a constant 0.
                    if cache_key != 0 && cache.key != cache_key {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if cache.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty {
                        // PutKind::Own is not currently emitted for platform
                        // objects, but keep this aligned with the normal PutById
                        // AddOwnProperty cache hit so a future bytecode path cannot
                        // bypass subclass hooks for objects that require them.
                        if cache.shape != Some(ShapeKey::of(object.shape())) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        if !property_addition_is_cacheable(vm, &object, name) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let Some(new_shape) = cache.new_shape else {
                            continue;
                        };
                        object.unsafe_set_shape(new_shape);
                        object.initialize_direct(cache.property_offset, value);
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                }
            }

            let from_shape = object.shape();
            object.define_direct_property(
                vm,
                name,
                value,
                PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
            );

            if let Some(caches) = caches
                && from_shape != object.shape()
                && !object.shape().is_dictionary()
            {
                caches.update(PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty, |cache| {
                    cache.key = cache_key;
                    cache.shape = Some(ShapeKey::of(from_shape));
                    cache.new_shape = Some(object.shape());
                    cache.property_offset = object.shape().lookup(name).expect("the property was just added").offset;
                });
            }
        }
        PutKind::Prototype => {
            if value.is_object() || value.is_null() {
                object
                    .internal_set_prototype_of(vm, value.is_object().then(|| value.as_object()))
                    .must();
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/bytecode/reference_text.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The text of a reference for the message of an error, from the source around the instruction that threw.
//!
//! Code keeps no text for this: error messages are rare, and the source says it all. Where an instruction is in the source
//! tells what it is about. A `.` or a `[` comes right after the base of a member access, a `(` right after what gets
//! called, an assignment operator right after its target, and `new` and a prefix update right in front of theirs. Anything
//! else has no text. The source gets read backward from there, as far as a chain of members goes.

use std::cell::Cell;

use crate::host::js_number_to_utf16;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

/// What a reference starts with.
enum Base {
    Name(Vec<u16>),
    /// `this`, a string or a number.
    Literal(Vec<u16>),
    /// Something with no text of its own.
    Unnamed,
}

/// What comes after the base of a reference.
enum Link {
    Name(Vec<u16>),
    PrivateName(Vec<u16>),
    Computed(Reference),
}

struct Reference {
    base: Base,
    links: Vec<Link>,
}

/// Where a reference that `reference_after_call_ending_at()` found starts.
enum Start {
    At(usize),
    /// The reference is the result of a call, whose callee ends here.
    AfterCallee(usize),
}

impl Reference {
    fn unnamed() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: Base::Unnamed,
            links: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The text of something that got called or constructed, in which everything has a place.
    fn append_callee_text(&self, text: &mut Vec<u16>) {
        match &self.base {
            Base::Name(name) | Base::Literal(name) => text.extend_from_slice(name),
            Base::Unnamed => text.extend("<object>".encode_utf16()),
        }
        for link in &self.links {
            match link {
                Link::Name(name) | Link::PrivateName(name) => {
                    text.push(u16::from(b'.'));
                    text.extend_from_slice(name);
                }
                Link::Computed(key) => {
                    text.push(u16::from(b'['));
                    key.append_callee_text(text);
                    text.push(u16::from(b']'));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The text of the base of a member access, which leaves out what it has no text for. Returns whether it has one.
    fn append_base_text(&self, text: &mut Vec<u16>) -> bool {
        let has_base = match &self.base {
            Base::Name(name) | Base::Literal(name) => {
                text.extend_from_slice(name);
                true
            }
            Base::Unnamed => false,
        };
        for link in &self.links {
            match link {
                Link::Name(name) => {
                    text.push(u16::from(b'.'));
                    text.extend_from_slice(name);
                }
                Link::PrivateName(_) => {}
                Link::Computed(key) => {
                    let start = text.len();
                    text.push(u16::from(b'['));
                    if key.append_base_text(text) {
                        text.push(u16::from(b']'));
                    } else {
                        text.truncate(start);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        has_base || !self.links.is_empty()
    }
}

fn is_word_unit(unit: u16) -> bool {
    char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)).is_some_and(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '$')
}

fn is_whitespace_unit(unit: u16) -> bool {
    char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)).is_some_and(char::is_whitespace) || unit == 0xFEFF
}

fn is_quote(unit: u16) -> bool {
    unit == u16::from(b'"') || unit == u16::from(b'\'')
}

fn is_digit(unit: u16) -> bool {
    (0x30..=0x39).contains(&unit)
}

fn equals(units: &[u16], text: &str) -> bool {
    units.iter().copied().eq(text.encode_utf16())
}

/// Whether the word `units` is a keyword that a value comes after, so that a `(` or a `[` behind it starts something new.
fn is_keyword_in_front_of_value(units: &[u16]) -> bool {
    const KEYWORDS: [&str; 15] = [
        "await",
        "case",
        "delete",
        "do",
        "else",
        "extends",
        "in",
        "instanceof",
        "new",
        "of",
        "return",
        "throw",
        "typeof",
        "void",
        "yield",
    ];
    KEYWORDS.iter().any(|keyword| equals(units, keyword))
}

/// What the name of a number is in the message: the number, and not how the source writes it.
fn text_of_number(units: &[u16]) -> Option<Vec<u16>> {
    let text = String::from_utf16(units).ok()?;
    let text = text.replace('_', "");
    let value = match text.get(..2).map(str::to_ascii_lowercase).as_deref() {
        Some("0x") => u64::from_str_radix(&text[2..], 16).ok()? as f64,
        Some("0o") => u64::from_str_radix(&text[2..], 8).ok()? as f64,
        Some("0b") => u64::from_str_radix(&text[2..], 2).ok()? as f64,
        _ => text.parse::<f64>().ok()?,
    };
    Some(Utf16View::of_string(&js_number_to_utf16(value)).code_units().collect())
}

/// How many references in brackets a reference can be in and still have a text.
const MAXIMUM_NESTING: u32 = 8;

struct Scanner<'a> {
    units: &'a [u16],
    nesting: Cell<u32>,
}

impl<'a> Scanner<'a> {
    fn new(units: &'a [u16]) -> Self {
        Self {
            units,
            nesting: Cell::new(0),
        }
    }

    fn unit_at(&self, index: usize) -> u16 {
        self.units.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0)
    }

    fn starts_with_at(&self, index: usize, text: &str) -> bool {
        (index..)
            .zip(text.encode_utf16())
            .all(|(position, unit)| self.unit_at(position) == unit)
    }

    /// Where a word starts that ends at `end`, which is `end` itself if there is none.
    fn start_of_word(&self, first: usize, end: usize) -> usize {
        let mut start = end;
        while start > first && is_word_unit(self.units[start - 1]) {
            start -= 1;
        }
        start
    }

    fn end_of_word(&self, start: usize) -> usize {
        let mut end = start;
        while end < self.units.len() && is_word_unit(self.units[end]) {
            end += 1;
        }
        end
    }

    /// Goes back over whitespace and comments from `end`.
    fn skip_trivia_before(&self, first: usize, mut end: usize) -> usize {
        loop {
            while end > first && is_whitespace_unit(self.units[end - 1]) {
                let is_line_end = matches!(self.units[end - 1], 0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029);
                end -= 1;
                if is_line_end && let Some(comment) = self.line_comment_ending_at(first, end) {
                    end = comment;
                }
            }
            if end >= first + 2 && self.starts_with_at(end - 2, "*/") {
                let mut start = end - 2;
                while start > first && !self.starts_with_at(start, "/*") {
                    start -= 1;
                }
                if !self.starts_with_at(start, "/*") {
                    return end;
                }
                end = start;
                continue;
            }
            return end;
        }
    }

    /// Where a `//` comment starts on the line that ends at `line_end`.
    fn line_comment_ending_at(&self, first: usize, line_end: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let mut start = line_end;
        while start > first && !matches!(self.units[start - 1], 0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029) {
            start -= 1;
        }
        (start..line_end.saturating_sub(1)).find(|&index| self.starts_with_at(index, "//"))
    }

    fn skip_trivia_after(&self, mut start: usize) -> usize {
        loop {
            while start < self.units.len() && is_whitespace_unit(self.units[start]) {
                start += 1;
            }
            if self.starts_with_at(start, "//") {
                while start < self.units.len() && !matches!(self.units[start], 0x0A | 0x0D | 0x2028 | 0x2029) {
                    start += 1;
                }
                continue;
            }
            if self.starts_with_at(start, "/*") {
                start += 2;
                while start < self.units.len() && !self.starts_with_at(start, "*/") {
                    start += 1;
                }
                start += 2;
                continue;
            }
            return start;
        }
    }

    /// Where the string starts that has its closing quote at `close`.
    fn start_of_string(&self, first: usize, close: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let quote = self.units[close];
        (first..close)
            .rev()
            .find(|&index| self.units[index] == quote && (index == first || self.units[index - 1] != u16::from(b'\\')))
    }

    /// Where the `(` or `[` is that goes with the one at `close`.
    fn opening_bracket(&self, first: usize, close: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let mut depth = 0usize;
        let mut index = close + 1;
        while index > first {
            index -= 1;
            let unit = self.units[index];
            match char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)) {
                Some(')' | ']' | '}') => depth += 1,
                Some('(' | '[' | '{') => {
                    depth -= 1;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        return Some(index);
                    }
                }
                Some('"' | '\'' | '`') => index = self.start_of_string(first, index)?,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        None
    }

    /// Where the bracket that opens at `open` ends, just behind it.
    fn end_of_brackets(&self, open: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let mut depth = 0usize;
        let mut index = open;
        while index < self.units.len() {
            let unit = self.units[index];
            match char::from_u32(u32::from(unit)) {
                Some('(' | '[' | '{') => depth += 1,
                Some(')' | ']' | '}') => {
                    depth -= 1;
                    if depth == 0 {
                        return Some(index + 1);
                    }
                }
                Some('"' | '\'' | '`') => {
                    index += 1;
                    while index < self.units.len() && self.units[index] != unit {
                        index += usize::from(self.units[index] == u16::from(b'\\')) + 1;
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            index += 1;
        }
        None
    }

    /// Whether a value ends at `end`, which makes a bracket right there part of the same expression.
    fn value_ends_at(&self, first: usize, end: usize) -> bool {
        if end == first {
            return false;
        }
        let unit = self.units[end - 1];
        if is_word_unit(unit) {
            return !is_keyword_in_front_of_value(&self.units[self.start_of_word(first, end)..end]);
        }
        unit == u16::from(b')') || unit == u16::from(b']') || unit == u16::from(b'`') || is_quote(unit)
    }

    /// The reference that all of what is between `start` and `end` is, or something without a name if it is more than that.
    fn reference_of_range(&self, start: usize, end: usize) -> Reference {
        // NB: The text is for an error, which may be on its way with little of the stack left.
        let nesting = self.nesting.get();
        if nesting == MAXIMUM_NESTING {
            return Reference::unnamed();
        }
        self.nesting.set(nesting + 1);
        let (reference, first) = self.reference_ending_at(start, end);
        self.nesting.set(nesting);
        if first == self.skip_trivia_after(start) {
            reference
        } else {
            Reference::unnamed()
        }
    }

    /// The reference that ends at `end`, and where it starts, going no further back than `first`.
    fn reference_ending_at(&self, first: usize, end: usize) -> (Reference, usize) {
        let (reference, mut start) = self.reference_after_call_ending_at(first, end);
        // NB: The result of a call has no text, however far the expression goes back.
        loop {
            match start {
                Start::At(start) => return (reference, start),
                Start::AfterCallee(callee_end) => (_, start) = self.reference_after_call_ending_at(first, callee_end),
            }
        }
    }

    /// Like `reference_ending_at()`, but stopping at a call.
    fn reference_after_call_ending_at(&self, first: usize, mut end: usize) -> (Reference, Start) {
        let mut links = Vec::new();
        let base;
        let start;
        loop {
            end = self.skip_trivia_before(first, end);
            if end == first {
                return (Reference::unnamed(), Start::At(end));
            }
            let last = self.units[end - 1];
            if is_word_unit(last) {
                let mut word_start = self.start_of_word(first, end);
                let is_private = word_start > first && self.units[word_start - 1] == u16::from(b'#');
                word_start -= usize::from(is_private);
                let word = self.units[word_start..end].to_vec();
                let before = self.skip_trivia_before(first, word_start);
                let is_link = before > first
                    && self.units[before - 1] == u16::from(b'.')
                    && !(before >= first + 2 && self.units[before - 2] == u16::from(b'.'));
                if !is_link {
                    start = word_start;
                    base = Self::base_of_word(word);
                    break;
                }
                if before >= first + 2 && self.units[before - 2] == u16::from(b'?') {
                    return (Reference::unnamed(), Start::At(self.start_of_word(first, before - 2)));
                }
                let object_end = self.skip_trivia_before(first, before - 1);
                let object_start = self.start_of_word(first, object_end);
                let object = &self.units[object_start..object_end];
                // NB: These have no text. What comes after them does.
                if equals(object, "new") || equals(object, "import") {
                    start = object_start;
                    base = Base::Unnamed;
                    break;
                }
                links.push(if is_private {
                    Link::PrivateName(word)
                } else {
                    Link::Name(word)
                });
                end = before - 1;
                continue;
            }
            if last == u16::from(b']') {
                let Some(open) = self.opening_bracket(first, end - 1) else {
                    return (Self::with_links(Base::Unnamed, links), Start::At(end));
                };
                let before = self.skip_trivia_before(first, open);
                if !self.value_ends_at(first, before) {
                    start = open;
                    base = Base::Unnamed;
                    break;
                }
                links.push(Link::Computed(self.reference_of_range(open + 1, end - 1)));
                end = before;
                continue;
            }
            if last == u16::from(b')') {
                let Some(open) = self.opening_bracket(first, end - 1) else {
                    return (Self::with_links(Base::Unnamed, links), Start::At(end));
                };
                let before = self.skip_trivia_before(first, open);
                if self.value_ends_at(first, before) {
                    return (Self::with_links(Base::Unnamed, links), Start::AfterCallee(before));
                }
                let mut inner = self.reference_of_range(open + 1, end - 1);
                links.reverse();
                inner.links.extend(links);
                return (inner, Start::At(open));
            }
            if is_quote(last) {
                let Some(open) = self.start_of_string(first, end - 1) else {
                    return (Self::with_links(Base::Unnamed, links), Start::At(end));
                };
                let mut text = vec![u16::from(b'\'')];
                text.extend_from_slice(&self.units[open + 1..end - 1]);
                text.push(u16::from(b'\''));
                start = open;
                base = Base::Literal(text);
                break;
            }
            return (Self::with_links(Base::Unnamed, links), Start::At(end));
        }
        (Self::with_links(base, links), Start::At(start))
    }

    fn with_links(base: Base, mut links: Vec<Link>) -> Reference {
        links.reverse();
        Reference { base, links }
    }

    fn base_of_word(word: Vec<u16>) -> Base {
        if word.first().copied().is_some_and(is_digit) {
            return text_of_number(&word).map_or(Base::Unnamed, Base::Literal);
        }
        if equals(&word, "this") {
            return Base::Literal(word);
        }
        const NO_NAMES: [&str; 5] = ["false", "null", "super", "true", "function"];
        if NO_NAMES.iter().any(|keyword| equals(&word, keyword)) {
            return Base::Unnamed;
        }
        Base::Name(word)
    }

    /// Where the reference ends that starts at `start`, and that is no more than a chain of members.
    fn end_of_reference_at(&self, start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        let start = self.skip_trivia_after(start);
        let first = self.unit_at(start);
        let mut end = if first == u16::from(b'(') {
            self.end_of_brackets(start)?
        } else if is_quote(first) {
            let mut end = start + 1;
            while end < self.units.len() && self.units[end] != first {
                end += usize::from(self.units[end] == u16::from(b'\\')) + 1;
            }
            // NB: What is available of the source can end in the middle of a string.
            (end + 1).min(self.units.len())
        } else {
            let end = self.end_of_word(start);
            if end == start || equals(&self.units[start..end], "new") {
                return None;
            }
            end
        };
        loop {
            let next = self.skip_trivia_after(end);
            if self.unit_at(next) == u16::from(b'.') {
                let word = self.skip_trivia_after(next + 1);
                let word = word + usize::from(self.unit_at(word) == u16::from(b'#'));
                let word_end = self.end_of_word(word);
                if word_end == word {
                    return Some(end);
                }
                end = word_end;
            } else if self.unit_at(next) == u16::from(b'[') {
                end = self.end_of_brackets(next)?;
            } else {
                return Some(end);
            }
        }
    }

    /// The reference that starts at `start`.
    fn reference_at(&self, start: usize) -> Option<Reference> {
        let end = self.end_of_reference_at(start)?;
        Some(self.reference_of_range(start, end))
    }

    fn is_update_at(&self, at: usize) -> bool {
        self.starts_with_at(at, "++") || self.starts_with_at(at, "--")
    }

    fn is_new_at(&self, at: usize) -> bool {
        self.starts_with_at(at, "new") && !is_word_unit(self.unit_at(at + 3))
    }
}

/// The text of what a call or a `new` at `at` is about, if it has one.
pub fn callee_text(units: &[u16], at: usize) -> Option<Vec<u16>> {
    let scanner = Scanner::new(units);
    let reference = if scanner.is_new_at(at) {
        scanner.reference_at(at + 3)?
    } else if scanner.unit_at(at) == u16::from(b'(') {
        scanner.reference_ending_at(0, at).0
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    if reference.links.is_empty() && !matches!(reference.base, Base::Name(_)) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut text = Vec::new();
    reference.append_callee_text(&mut text);
    Some(text)
}

/// The text of the base of a member access at `at`, if it has one.
pub fn base_text(units: &[u16], at: usize) -> Option<Vec<u16>> {
    let scanner = Scanner::new(units);
    let unit = char::from_u32(u32::from(scanner.unit_at(at)))?;
    // NB: All of an optional chain is where it starts, and it has no text.
    if scanner.starts_with_at(at, "?.") {
        return None;
    }
    let reference = match unit {
        '.' | '[' => scanner.reference_ending_at(0, at).0,
        '+' | '-' if scanner.is_update_at(at) && !scanner.value_ends_at(0, scanner.skip_trivia_before(0, at)) => {
            let mut reference = scanner.reference_at(at + 2)?;
            reference.links.pop()?;
            reference
        }
        '(' | '`' | '=' | '+' | '-' | '*' | '/' | '%' | '&' | '|' | '^' | '<' | '>' | '?' => {
            let mut reference = scanner.reference_ending_at(0, at).0;
            // NB: Something computed that gets called has its base left out.
            if matches!(reference.links.pop()?, Link::Computed(_)) && unit == '(' {
                return None;
            }
            reference
        }
        // NB: A tagged template is where its tag starts.
        _ => {
            let end = scanner.end_of_reference_at(at)?;
            if scanner.unit_at(scanner.skip_trivia_after(end)) != u16::from(b'`') {
                return None;
            }
            let mut reference = scanner.reference_of_range(at, end);
            reference.links.pop()?;
            reference
        }
    };
    let mut text = Vec::new();
    reference.append_base_text(&mut text).then_some(text)
}

/// A bytecode offset with the line and column that the source map says it came from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct SourceMapEntry {
    pub bytecode_offset: u32,
    pub line: u32,
    pub column: u32,
}

/// An entry of the source map of an executable: where in the source the instructions from a bytecode offset on came from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct SourceOffsetEntry {
    pub bytecode_offset: u32,
    pub source_offset: SourceOffset,
}

/// Where an instruction came from: an offset into the source, which only turns into a line and a column for what ends
/// up in the source map.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SourceOffset(pub u32);

impl SourceOffset {
    /// An instruction that no code in the source stands for.
    pub const NONE: Self = Self(u32::MAX);
}

/// How many entries of a source map there are from one checkpoint to the next.
const ENTRIES_PER_CHECKPOINT: usize = 64;

/// The size of a checkpoint: the bytecode offset of its entry, the last source offset before that entry, and where the
/// entry starts after the first number, each as four bytes.
const CHECKPOINT_SIZE: usize = 12;

/// Packs the `entry_count` entries of a source map, in the order of their bytecode offsets, into `out`. An entry is how
/// far its bytecode offset is from the entry before it, and then how far its source offset is from the last source
/// offset there was, both as variable-length integers. A zero in place of the second stands for `SourceOffset::NONE`.
///
/// A source map with more than `ENTRIES_PER_CHECKPOINT` entries ends with a table of checkpoints, one for every
/// `ENTRIES_PER_CHECKPOINT` entries after the first, so that a lookup decodes only the entries after the closest
/// checkpoint. The lowest bit of the first number says if there is a table, and then the number of checkpoints comes
/// right after it.
pub fn encode_source_map(entry_count: usize, entries: impl Iterator<Item = SourceOffsetEntry>, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    let checkpoint_count = entry_count.saturating_sub(1) / ENTRIES_PER_CHECKPOINT;
    let mut entries = entries.peekable();
    let Some(first) = entries.peek() else {
        return;
    };
    put_variable_length(
        out,
        u64::from(first.bytecode_offset) << 1 | u64::from(checkpoint_count != 0),
    );
    if checkpoint_count != 0 {
        put_variable_length(out, checkpoint_count as u64);
    }
    let start = out.len();
    let mut checkpoints = Vec::with_capacity(checkpoint_count);
    let mut previous_bytecode_offset = 0;
    let mut previous_source_offset = 0;
    for (index, entry) in entries.enumerate() {
        if index != 0 {
            if index % ENTRIES_PER_CHECKPOINT == 0 {
                checkpoints.push([
                    entry.bytecode_offset,
                    previous_source_offset,
                    (out.len() - start) as u32,
                ]);
            }
            put_variable_length(out, u64::from(entry.bytecode_offset - previous_bytecode_offset));
        }
        previous_bytecode_offset = entry.bytecode_offset;
        if entry.source_offset == SourceOffset::NONE {
            put_variable_length(out, 0);
            continue;
        }
        let distance = entry.source_offset.0.wrapping_sub(previous_source_offset) as i32;
        previous_source_offset = entry.source_offset.0;
        put_variable_length(out, u64::from(((distance << 1) ^ (distance >> 31)) as u32) + 1);
    }
    assert_eq!(checkpoints.len(), checkpoint_count, "the entry count is right");
    for checkpoint in checkpoints {
        for field in checkpoint {
            out.extend_from_slice(&field.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }
}

fn put_variable_length(out: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {
    while value >= 0x80 {
        out.push(value as u8 | 0x80);
        value >>= 7;
    }
    out.push(value as u8);
}

fn take_variable_length(bytes: &mut &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut value = 0;
    let mut shift = 0;
    loop {
        let (&byte, rest) = bytes.split_first().expect("a source map ends after a whole entry");
        *bytes = rest;
        value |= u64::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
        if byte < 0x80 {
            return value;
        }
        shift += 7;
    }
}

/// The entries of a source map that `encode_source_map` packed.
pub struct SourceMapEntries<'a> {
    checkpoints: &'a [u8],
    entries: &'a [u8],
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    bytecode_offset: u32,
    source_offset: u32,
    /// How far the next entry is from the one before it, if that is not in `bytes`.
    next_distance: Option<u32>,
}

impl<'a> SourceMapEntries<'a> {
    pub fn new(mut bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        let mut next_distance = None;
        let mut checkpoints: &[u8] = &[];
        if !bytes.is_empty() {
            let first = take_variable_length(&mut bytes);
            next_distance = Some((first >> 1) as u32);
            if first & 1 != 0 {
                let checkpoint_count = take_variable_length(&mut bytes) as usize;
                let (entries, table) = bytes.split_at(bytes.len() - checkpoint_count * CHECKPOINT_SIZE);
                bytes = entries;
                checkpoints = table;
            }
        }
        Self {
            checkpoints,
            entries: bytes,
            bytes,
            bytecode_offset: 0,
            source_offset: 0,
            next_distance,
        }
    }

    fn checkpoint_field(&self, index: usize, field: usize) -> u32 {
        let at = index * CHECKPOINT_SIZE + field * 4;
        u32::from_le_bytes(self.checkpoints[at..at + 4].try_into().expect("four bytes"))
    }

    /// The last entry at or before the bytecode offset `offset`.
    pub fn entry_at(mut self, offset: u32) -> Option<SourceOffsetEntry> {
        let checkpoint_count = self.checkpoints.len() / CHECKPOINT_SIZE;
        let mut low = 0;
        let mut high = checkpoint_count;
        while low < high {
            let middle = (low + high) / 2;
            if self.checkpoint_field(middle, 0) <= offset {
                low = middle + 1;
            } else {
                high = middle;
            }
        }
        if low != 0 {
            let checkpoint = low - 1;
            self.bytes = &self.entries[self.checkpoint_field(checkpoint, 2) as usize..];
            take_variable_length(&mut self.bytes);
            self.bytecode_offset = 0;
            self.next_distance = Some(self.checkpoint_field(checkpoint, 0));
            self.source_offset = self.checkpoint_field(checkpoint, 1);
        }
        self.take_while(|entry| entry.bytecode_offset <= offset).last()
    }
}

impl Iterator for SourceMapEntries<'_> {
    type Item = SourceOffsetEntry;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<SourceOffsetEntry> {
        if self.bytes.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let distance = match self.next_distance.take() {
            Some(distance) => distance,
            None => take_variable_length(&mut self.bytes) as u32,
        };
        self.bytecode_offset += distance;
        let packed = take_variable_length(&mut self.bytes);
        if packed == 0 {
            return Some(SourceOffsetEntry {
                bytecode_offset: self.bytecode_offset,
                source_offset: SourceOffset::NONE,
            });
        }
        let zigzag = (packed - 1) as u32;
        let distance = (zigzag >> 1) as i32 ^ -((zigzag & 1) as i32);
        self.source_offset = self.source_offset.wrapping_add(distance as u32);
        Some(SourceOffsetEntry {
            bytecode_offset: self.bytecode_offset,
            source_offset: SourceOffset(self.source_offset),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn packed_entries_come_back_the_same() {
        let entries = [
            (0, 500),
            (3, u32::MAX),
            (3, 12),
            (9, 3_000_000_000),
            (70_000, 0),
            (70_001, u32::MAX),
            (70_100, 1),
        ];
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        encode_source_map(
            entries.len(),
            entries
                .iter()
                .map(|&(bytecode_offset, source_offset)| SourceOffsetEntry {
                    bytecode_offset,
                    source_offset: SourceOffset(source_offset),
                }),
            &mut bytes,
        );
        let decoded: Vec<_> = SourceMapEntries::new(&bytes)
            .map(|entry| (entry.bytecode_offset, entry.source_offset.0))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(decoded, entries);
        assert_eq!(SourceMapEntries::new(&bytes).entry_at(8).unwrap().source_offset.0, 12);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lookups_from_checkpoints_match_a_scan_from_the_start() {
        let entries: Vec<_> = (0..1000u32)
            .map(|index| SourceOffsetEntry {
                bytecode_offset: 5 + index * 3 - index % 2,
                source_offset: if index % 7 == 0 {
                    SourceOffset::NONE
                } else {
                    SourceOffset(index.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761) % 100_000)
                },
            })
            .collect();
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        encode_source_map(entries.len(), entries.iter().copied(), &mut bytes);
        let decoded: Vec<_> = SourceMapEntries::new(&bytes)
            .map(|entry| (entry.bytecode_offset, entry.source_offset))
            .collect();
        let expected: Vec<_> = entries
            .iter()
            .map(|entry| (entry.bytecode_offset, entry.source_offset))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(decoded, expected);
        for offset in 0..3000 {
            let scanned = entries
                .iter()
                .take_while(|entry| entry.bytecode_offset <= offset)
                .last();
            let looked_up = SourceMapEntries::new(&bytes).entry_at(offset);
            assert_eq!(
                looked_up.map(|entry| (entry.bytecode_offset, entry.source_offset)),
                scanned.map(|entry| (entry.bytecode_offset, entry.source_offset))
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_source_map_has_no_entries() {
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        encode_source_map(0, std::iter::empty(), &mut bytes);
        assert!(bytes.is_empty());
        assert!(SourceMapEntries::new(&bytes).entry_at(0).is_none());
    }
}
