use core::ffi::{c_char, c_void};

use super::capi::GCVisitor;
use super::class_id::ClassId;
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, CellHeaderTail, CellKind, CellState};
use crate::runtime::object::ObjectMethods;

#[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn __lsan_ignore_object(pointer: *const c_void);
}

/// Mirrors GCCellTypeInfo from Libraries/LibGC/CAPI.h, which LibGC dispatches every per-cell operation through.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CellTypeInfo {
    pub cell_size: u32,
    pub alignment: u32,
    pub kind: u8,
    pub visit_edges: unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut GCVisitor),
    pub finalize: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)>,
    pub destroy: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)>,
    pub external_memory_size: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void) -> usize>,
    pub class_name: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void, length: *mut usize) -> *const c_char>,
}

/// The class of a cell, which the block the cell lives in holds (see `class_of`). It starts with the type info LibGC
/// dispatches through.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Class {
    pub type_info: CellTypeInfo,
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub id: ClassId,
    /// The class of the cell type this one extends.
    pub parent: Option<&'static Class>,
    /// The internal methods of the objects of this class. Cells that are not objects have none.
    pub object_methods: Option<&'static ObjectMethods>,
    /// The kind of the cells of this class, which type_info also holds for LibGC.
    kind: CellKind,
    /// Whether LibGC may only trace the cells of this class on the thread that owns their heap, see
    /// traced_on_owner_thread_only().
    owner_thread_only: bool,
}

// The layout module's mirror of the class, through which Layout.h tells an embedder where a class keeps its id and
// the class it extends.
const _: () = {
    use crate::layout::class::{CellTypeInfoLayout, ClassLayout};
    assert!(size_of::<CellTypeInfo>() == size_of::<CellTypeInfoLayout>());
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Class, type_info) == core::mem::offset_of!(ClassLayout, type_info));
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Class, name) == core::mem::offset_of!(ClassLayout, name));
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Class, id) == core::mem::offset_of!(ClassLayout, id));
    assert!(size_of::<ClassId>() == size_of::<u16>());
    assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Class, parent) == core::mem::offset_of!(ClassLayout, parent));
    assert!(size_of::<Option<&'static Class>>() == size_of::<*const ClassLayout>());
};

/// LibGC hands out cells in the slots of fixed-size blocks, whose free list needs room for its own entry in each.
pub(crate) const MIN_CELL_SIZE: usize = 24;
const MAX_CELL_ALIGNMENT: usize = 16;

impl Class {
    pub const fn new<T: Trace>(
        name: &'static str,
        id: ClassId,
        kind: CellKind,
        parent: Option<&'static Class>,
        object_methods: Option<&'static ObjectMethods>,
        finalize: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)>,
    ) -> Self {
        // NB: Heap::allocate() checks MIN_CELL_SIZE, as a class that is only a base of others may be smaller.
        assert!(size_of::<T>().is_multiple_of(8));
        assert!(align_of::<T>() <= MAX_CELL_ALIGNMENT);
        assert!(
            matches!(kind, CellKind::Object) == object_methods.is_some(),
            "exactly the object classes have internal methods"
        );
        Self {
            type_info: CellTypeInfo {
                cell_size: size_of::<T>() as u32,
                alignment: align_of::<T>() as u32,
                kind: kind as u8,
                visit_edges: visit_edges::<T>,
                finalize,
                destroy: if core::mem::needs_drop::<T>() {
                    Some(destroy::<T>)
                } else {
                    None
                },
                external_memory_size: None,
                class_name: Some(class_name),
            },
            name,
            id,
            parent,
            object_methods,
            kind,
            owner_thread_only: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn kind(&self) -> CellKind {
        self.kind
    }

    /// LibGC traces cells on several threads at once while the thread that owns their heap is stopped. This has it
    /// trace the cells of this class on the owner only, for classes whose trace() or external_memory_size() read
    /// state of the owner thread, or state that other cells share without synchronization.
    pub const fn traced_on_owner_thread_only(mut self) -> Self {
        self.owner_thread_only = true;
        self
    }

    pub fn is_traced_on_owner_thread_only(&self) -> bool {
        self.owner_thread_only
    }

    /// Whether collections that do not scan the stack may move the cells of this class, see gc_allocator_set_movable().
    /// A class may only be movable if everything that keeps the address of its cells visits it through a slot, pins
    /// the cell, or forgets the address when the cell moves. Classes derived at run time, such as an embedder's host
    /// objects, never are, as the embedder keeps their addresses.
    pub fn is_movable(&self) -> bool {
        if self.is_derived_at_run_time() {
            return false;
        }
        matches!(
            self.id,
            ClassId::ValueStorage
                | ClassId::Object
                | ClassId::Array
                | ClassId::EcmascriptFunctionObject
                | ClassId::EcmascriptFunctionObjectWithRareData
                | ClassId::DeclarativeEnvironment
                | ClassId::FunctionEnvironment
                | ClassId::PrimitiveString
                | ClassId::RopeString
                | ClassId::Substring
                | ClassId::InlineString
                | ClassId::Shape
                | ClassId::DescriptorArray
                | ClassId::DictionaryPropertyTable
                | ClassId::BigInt
                | ClassId::Accessor
                | ClassId::BoundFunction
                | ClassId::ArgumentsObject
                | ClassId::RegExpObject
                | ClassId::Date
                | ClassId::ArrayIterator
                | ClassId::StringIterator
                | ClassId::Map
                | ClassId::MapIterator
                | ClassId::Set
                | ClassId::SetIterator
                | ClassId::Promise
        )
    }

    /// What Cell::class_name() returns for the cells of this class, which printing and messages show. It is the name
    /// of the class unless the Rust type is spelled differently.
    pub fn class_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        if self.is_derived_at_run_time() {
            return self.name;
        }
        match self.id {
            ClassId::EcmascriptFunctionObject => "ECMAScriptFunctionObject",
            ClassId::Test262GlobalObject => "GlobalObject",
            ClassId::Dollar262Object => "$262Object",
            _ => self.name,
        }
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" fn visit_edges<T: Trace>(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut GCVisitor) {
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes a live cell of this class and a visitor that outlives the call.
    let (cell, mut visitor) = unsafe { (&*cell.cast::<T>(), Visitor::from_raw(visitor)) };
    cell.trace(&mut visitor);
}

/// Cells that need to act before they are destroyed. Finalizers run during a collection, while every cell that dies
/// in it is still intact, and must not allocate.
pub trait Finalize {
    fn finalize(&self);
}

/// The finalize entry of a class whose cells implement Finalize.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls it, with a dead cell of that class.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn finalize<T: Finalize>(cell: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: LibGC finalizes each dead cell of this class once, before destroying it.
    unsafe { &*cell.cast::<T>() }.finalize();
}

/// Cells that own memory outside the heap, which LibGC counts towards the bytes that make it collect, as C++ cells
/// override Cell::external_memory_size().
pub trait ExternalMemorySize {
    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize;
}

/// The external_memory_size entry of a class whose cells implement ExternalMemorySize.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls it, with a cell of that class.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn external_memory_size<T: ExternalMemorySize>(cell: *const c_void) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes a cell of this class, which stays intact for the call.
    unsafe { &*cell.cast::<T>() }.external_memory_size()
}

impl Class {
    /// Has LibGC ask the cells of this class how much memory they own outside the heap.
    pub const fn with_external_memory_size(
        mut self,
        external_memory_size: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void) -> usize>,
    ) -> Self {
        self.type_info.external_memory_size = external_memory_size;
        self
    }

    /// Creates a class that extends `parent` while the runtime runs, as an embedder needs one for each class of host
    /// object it defines. Its cells have the parent's layout, so it shares the parent's type info and id, and code that
    /// tells classes apart by id sees the parent. It has a name and internal methods of its own, and its cells come from
    /// an allocator of their own once allocated with Heap::allocate_in(). The class lives as long as the process.
    pub fn derive_runtime(
        parent: &'static Class,
        name: &'static str,
        object_methods: &'static ObjectMethods,
    ) -> &'static Class {
        assert!(
            parent.object_methods.is_some(),
            "only object classes are derived at run time"
        );
        Self::leak_class_derived_at_run_time(parent, name, Some(object_methods))
    }

    /// Creates a class of cells that are not objects, such as the module records of a host class, that extends
    /// `parent` while the runtime runs, as derive_runtime() does for objects.
    pub fn derive_runtime_without_object_methods(parent: &'static Class, name: &'static str) -> &'static Class {
        assert!(
            parent.object_methods.is_none(),
            "the classes of objects have internal methods"
        );
        Self::leak_class_derived_at_run_time(parent, name, None)
    }

    fn leak_class_derived_at_run_time(
        parent: &'static Class,
        name: &'static str,
        object_methods: Option<&'static ObjectMethods>,
    ) -> &'static Class {
        let class = Box::leak(Box::new(Class {
            type_info: parent.type_info,
            name,
            id: parent.id,
            parent: Some(parent),
            object_methods,
            kind: parent.kind,
            owner_thread_only: parent.owner_thread_only,
        }));
        #[cfg(feature = "address-sanitizer")]
        // SAFETY: The class is a live allocation, which the process keeps for as long as it runs.
        unsafe {
            __lsan_ignore_object(core::ptr::from_ref(class).cast());
        }
        class
    }

    /// Whether Class::derive_runtime() created the class. Every class define_cell! defines has an id of its own.
    pub fn is_derived_at_run_time(&self) -> bool {
        self.parent.is_some_and(|parent| parent.id == self.id)
    }

    /// Whether the class is that of the cell type `T` or a subclass of it. Classes derived at run time have the id of
    /// the class they extend, and every cell type has an id of its own, so a class with the id of `T` is the class of
    /// `T` or one derived from it at run time. That covers the long chains of host classes without walking them.
    pub fn is_class_of<T: GcCell>(&self) -> bool {
        self.id == T::CLASS.id || self.is_subclass_of(T::CLASS)
    }

    pub fn is_subclass_of(&self, ancestor: &Class) -> bool {
        let mut class = Some(self);
        while let Some(current) = class {
            if core::ptr::eq(current, ancestor) {
                return true;
            }
            class = current.parent;
        }
        false
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" fn destroy<T>(cell: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: LibGC destroys each dead cell of this class exactly once.
    unsafe { core::ptr::drop_in_place(cell.cast::<T>()) };
}

unsafe extern "C" fn class_name(cell: *const c_void, length: *mut usize) -> *const c_char {
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes a cell of a Rust allocator.
    let class = unsafe { class_at(cell.cast()) };
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes somewhere to store the length.
    unsafe { length.write(class.name.len()) };
    class.name.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// A type whose values live in the garbage-collected heap.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The type must be #[repr(C)] and start with its cell header, either directly or through the cell it extends.
pub unsafe trait GcCell: Trace {
    const CLASS: &'static Class;
}

/// Marks that a cell type extends `Base`, starting with a `Base` at offset zero.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The type must start with a `Base`, directly or through other cells that do.
pub unsafe trait Extends<Base> {}

// SAFETY: Every type starts with itself.
unsafe impl<T: GcCell> Extends<T> for T {}

// SAFETY: Every cell starts with its header.
unsafe impl<T: GcCell> Extends<CellHeader> for T {}

// SAFETY: A header starts with itself.
unsafe impl Extends<CellHeader> for CellHeader {}

/// A cell's block starts at the cell's address rounded down to a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE, and holds the class of its
/// cells at BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET: the foreign type of the allocator that created the block (see Heap::create_allocator).
/// The block of an allocator that classes share holds the class they extend with BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG added, and each of
/// its cells keeps its own class in the word after the cell_size bytes of that class.
pub const BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
pub const BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET: usize = 2 * size_of::<usize>();
pub use crate::layout::cell::BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG;

/// The class that the block `address` is in holds, without its tag, or null for a block of C++ cells.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `address` must be in a live cell.
pub unsafe fn block_class_pointer_at(address: *const u8) -> *const Class {
    debug_assert!(is_in_heap_region(address.addr()), "only cells in the heap have a class");
    let block = address.wrapping_sub(address.addr() & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1));
    // SAFETY: The caller passes an address in a live cell, whose block is live as well.
    let class = unsafe { block.add(BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET).cast::<*const u8>().read() };
    class.wrapping_sub(class.addr() & BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG).cast()
}

/// The class of the cell at `cell`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be the address of a live cell of a Rust allocator.
pub unsafe fn class_at(cell: *const u8) -> &'static Class {
    debug_assert!(is_in_heap_region(cell.addr()), "only cells in the heap have a class");
    let block = cell.wrapping_sub(cell.addr() & (BLOCK_SIZE - 1));
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell of a Rust allocator, whose block holds a class.
    let class = unsafe { block.add(BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET).cast::<*const u8>().read() };
    if class.addr() & BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG == 0 {
        // SAFETY: The allocator created the block with the class of its cells, which lives forever.
        return unsafe { &*class.cast::<Class>() };
    }
    // SAFETY: The class that classes share an allocator of lives forever, and each cell of the allocator keeps its own
    //         class right after the bytes of that class.
    unsafe {
        let shared = &*class.wrapping_sub(BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG).cast::<Class>();
        cell.add(shared.type_info.cell_size as usize)
            .cast::<&'static Class>()
            .read()
    }
}

/// The class a cell was allocated with, which may be a subclass of its static type.
pub fn class_of<T>(cell: crate::layout::cell::Gc<T>) -> &'static Class {
    // SAFETY: The cell is live.
    unsafe { class_at(cell.as_ptr().cast()) }
}

/// The cell as a `Derived`, if it was allocated as one or as a subclass of it.
///
/// NB: A cell is only ever allocated by the allocator of its class, so the class its block holds tells what the memory
///     around it is.
pub fn downcast_ref<Base: GcCell, Derived: GcCell + Extends<Base>>(cell: &Base) -> Option<&Derived> {
    // SAFETY: The cell is live.
    let class = unsafe { class_at(core::ptr::from_ref(cell).cast()) };
    class
        .is_class_of::<Derived>()
        // SAFETY: The cell is a Derived or a subclass of it, which starts with a Derived.
        .then(|| unsafe { &*core::ptr::from_ref(cell).cast::<Derived>() })
}

/// The cell as a `Derived`, which it has to have been allocated as, or as a subclass of.
pub fn cast_ref<Base: GcCell, Derived: GcCell + Extends<Base>>(cell: &Base) -> &Derived {
    downcast_ref(cell).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("cell is not a {}", Derived::CLASS.name))
}

/// Cells are only ever mutated through interior mutability, so a shared reference is all a Gc hands out.
impl<T: GcCell> core::ops::Deref for crate::layout::cell::Gc<T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        // SAFETY: A Gc points to a live cell. Cells only move in collections that do not scan the stack, while no
        //         reference to a cell is on it.
        unsafe { self.as_non_null().as_ref() }
    }
}

impl<T: GcCell> crate::layout::cell::Gc<T> {
    /// The Gc of a cell the caller only has a reference to, like the receiver of a method. Panics if the reference is
    /// to a value that has yet to be allocated.
    pub fn from_ref(cell: &T) -> Self {
        assert!(
            is_in_heap_region(core::ptr::from_ref(cell).addr()),
            "a {} that has yet to be allocated is not a cell",
            T::CLASS.name
        );
        // SAFETY: The reference is into the heap region, where every value of a cell type is a cell that was allocated
        //         as one, since cells only ever embed the cell they extend, at their start.
        let gc = unsafe { Self::from_non_null(core::ptr::NonNull::from(cell)) };
        debug_assert!(class_of(gc).is_subclass_of(T::CLASS));
        gc
    }
}

/// Whether `address` is in the region LibGC allocates every cell in, which has no cells before it is set up.
pub(crate) fn is_in_heap_region(address: usize) -> bool {
    let base = crate::layout_forward::heap_region_base();
    base != 0 && address.wrapping_sub(base) as u64 <= crate::build_configuration::HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK
}

impl<T> crate::layout::cell::Gc<T> {
    pub fn upcast<Base>(self) -> crate::layout::cell::Gc<Base>
    where
        T: Extends<Base>,
    {
        // SAFETY: The cell starts with a Base.
        unsafe { crate::layout::cell::Gc::from_non_null(self.as_non_null().cast()) }
    }

    pub fn downcast<Derived: GcCell + Extends<T>>(self) -> Option<crate::layout::cell::Gc<Derived>> {
        class_of(self)
            .is_class_of::<Derived>()
            // SAFETY: The cell was allocated as a Derived or a subclass of it.
            .then(|| unsafe { crate::layout::cell::Gc::from_non_null(self.as_non_null().cast()) })
    }
}

impl CellHeaderTail {
    /// The header of a cell of `class` that keeps fields of its own in the first word, like `CellHeader::for_class()`.
    pub fn for_class(class: &'static Class) -> Self {
        Self {
            identity_hash_state: core::cell::Cell::new(0),
            state: CellState::Live.into(),
            kind: class.kind(),
        }
    }
}

impl CellHeader {
    /// The header of a cell of `class`, which must also be the class of the allocator the cell comes from.
    pub fn for_class(class: &'static Class) -> Self {
        Self {
            unused: [0; 8],
            identity_hash_state: core::cell::Cell::new(0),
            state: CellState::Live.into(),
            kind: class.kind(),
        }
    }

    /// The class of the cell, which its block holds.
    pub fn class(&self) -> &'static Class {
        // SAFETY: A header starts a live cell.
        unsafe { class_at(core::ptr::from_ref(self).cast()) }
    }
}

/// Defines the class of a cell type, named after the type and its ClassId. `extends` names the cell types it
/// extends, nearest first. `methods` gives an object class its internal methods, `finalize` opts into running its
/// Finalize implementation, and `external_memory_size` into reporting its ExternalMemorySize. A class that names none
/// of them inherits them from the class it extends, as C++ subclasses inherit virtual methods, so the Finalize
/// implementation of a subclass has to finalize its base as well.
macro_rules! define_cell {
    ($type:ident, $kind:ident $(, extends: [$parent:ident $(, $ancestor:ident)*])? $(, methods: $methods:path)? $(, finalize: $finalize:ident)? $(, external_memory_size: $external_memory_size:ident)? $(, traced_on: $traced_on:ident)?) => {
        const _: () = {
            static CLASS: $crate::gc::class::Class = {
                let class = $crate::gc::class::Class::new::<$type>(
                    stringify!($type),
                    $crate::gc::class_id::ClassId::$type,
                    $crate::layout::cell::CellKind::$kind,
                    define_cell!(@parent $($parent)?),
                    define_cell!(@methods [$($parent)?] [$($methods)?]),
                    define_cell!(@finalize $type [$($parent)?] [$($finalize)?]),
                )
                .with_external_memory_size(define_cell!(@external_memory_size $type [$($parent)?] [$($external_memory_size)?]));
                $(let class = define_cell!(@traced_on $traced_on class);)?
                class
            };

            // SAFETY: Checked by the asserts in Class::new and the cell's #[repr(C)] layout.
            unsafe impl $crate::gc::class::GcCell for $type {
                const CLASS: &'static $crate::gc::class::Class = &CLASS;
            }

            $(
                // SAFETY: The cell's first field is the cell it extends, which starts with each of its ancestors.
                unsafe impl $crate::gc::class::Extends<$parent> for $type {}
                $(unsafe impl $crate::gc::class::Extends<$ancestor> for $type {})*
            )?
        };
    };
    (@traced_on owner_thread_only $class:ident) => { $class.traced_on_owner_thread_only() };
    (@parent) => { None };
    (@parent $parent:ident) => { Some(<$parent as $crate::gc::class::GcCell>::CLASS) };
    (@methods [] []) => { None };
    (@methods [$parent:ident] []) => { <$parent as $crate::gc::class::GcCell>::CLASS.object_methods };
    (@methods [$($parent:ident)?] [$methods:path]) => { Some(&$methods) };
    (@finalize $type:ident [] []) => { None };
    (@finalize $type:ident [$parent:ident] []) => { <$parent as $crate::gc::class::GcCell>::CLASS.type_info.finalize };
    (@finalize $type:ident [$($parent:ident)?] [finalize]) => { Some($crate::gc::class::finalize::<$type>) };
    (@external_memory_size $type:ident [] []) => { None };
    (@external_memory_size $type:ident [$parent:ident] []) => {
        <$parent as $crate::gc::class::GcCell>::CLASS.type_info.external_memory_size
    };
    (@external_memory_size $type:ident [$($parent:ident)?] [external_memory_size]) => {
        Some($crate::gc::class::external_memory_size::<$type>)
    };
}

pub(crate) use define_cell;

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};

use super::heap::Heap;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;

/// Keeps the heap from collecting garbage while it lives.
pub struct DeferGc<'heap>(&'heap Heap);

impl<'heap> DeferGc<'heap> {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &'heap Vm) -> Self {
        Self::of_heap(vm.heap())
    }

    /// Runs `body` while nothing collects garbage, so that what it holds by value needs no root.
    pub fn scope<R>(vm: &Vm, body: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> R) -> R {
        body(&DeferGc::new(vm))
    }

    pub(super) fn of_heap(heap: &'heap Heap) -> Self {
        heap.defer_gc();
        Self(heap)
    }

    /// Ties `value`, whose cells only this deferral keeps alive, to the deferral.
    pub fn cover<T>(&self, value: T) -> Deferred<'_, T> {
        Deferred {
            value,
            _defer_gc: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for DeferGc<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.undefer_gc();
    }
}

/// A value whose cells nothing keeps alive but a deferral, such as cells in a Vec that nothing traces yet. It cannot
/// outlive the deferral.
pub struct Deferred<'d, T> {
    value: T,
    _defer_gc: PhantomData<&'d ()>,
}

impl<T> Deferred<'_, T> {
    /// Gives up the value, for moving it where the collector finds its cells.
    pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
        self.value
    }
}

impl<T> Deref for Deferred<'_, T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        &self.value
    }
}

impl<T> DerefMut for Deferred<'_, T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
        &mut self.value
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Cells that hold values of an embedder's own types, which the embedder allocates from the heap of the VM and keeps
//! alive through the host data slots of its host objects, or through any other traced place.
//!
//! The runtime does not know the embedder's types, so their cells have no class id of their own: every one has the
//! id ClassId::EmbedderCell, and the class of a type, which the embedder defines once as a static, is told apart from
//! every other class by its address. The heap keeps the allocator of such a class by that address.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::mem::{ManuallyDrop, MaybeUninit};
use core::ops::Deref;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::class::{Class, ExternalMemorySize, GcCell, MIN_CELL_SIZE, class_of};
use super::class_id::ClassId;
use super::defer_gc::DeferGc;
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, CellKind, Gc};

/// A value of an embedder's type in a cell of its own, which derefs to the value.
#[repr(C, align(8))]
pub struct EmbedderCell<T> {
    header: CellHeader,
    value: ValueWithRoomForFreeListLink<T>,
}

/// LibGC keeps the link to the next free cell in the bytes after the header of a free cell, so a cell has at least
/// MIN_CELL_SIZE bytes however small its value is.
#[repr(C)]
union ValueWithRoomForFreeListLink<T> {
    value: ManuallyDrop<T>,
    _room_for_free_list_link: [MaybeUninit<u8>; MIN_CELL_SIZE - size_of::<CellHeader>()],
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<EmbedderCell<()>>() == MIN_CELL_SIZE);
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<EmbedderCell<u64>>() == 32);

impl<T> Drop for EmbedderCell<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The union holds a value, which nothing has dropped: the cell is dropped once, by LibGC's destroy.
        unsafe { ManuallyDrop::drop(&mut self.value.value) };
    }
}

impl<T> Deref for EmbedderCell<T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        // SAFETY: The union holds a value for as long as the cell lives.
        unsafe { &self.value.value }
    }
}

// SAFETY: The value is all the cell holds.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for EmbedderCell<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        (**self).trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// The class of the cells that hold values of one of the embedder's types, which the embedder defines once per type
/// as a static and names in the type's EmbedderValue implementation:
///
/// ```ignore
/// static THING_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Thing> = EmbedderClass::new("Thing");
///
/// impl EmbedderValue for Thing {
///     const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &THING_CLASS;
/// }
/// ```
///
/// LibGC traces the cells of the class, and destroys those whose value has a destructor. It finalizes them only for a
/// class that with_finalize() gives a finalize entry, and counts memory they own outside the heap only for a class that
/// new_with_external_memory_size() creates.
pub struct EmbedderClass<T: 'static> {
    class: Class,
    _value: PhantomData<fn() -> T>,
}

impl<T: Trace + 'static> EmbedderClass<T> {
    pub const fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        let mut class = Class::new::<EmbedderCell<T>>(name, ClassId::EmbedderCell, CellKind::Other, None, None, None);
        // The cell drops its value, so Class::new sees a type that needs dropping whatever the value is. A value that
        // has no destructor leaves the collector nothing to run when the cell dies.
        if !core::mem::needs_drop::<T>() {
            class.type_info.destroy = None;
        }
        Self {
            class,
            _value: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub const fn class(&'static self) -> &'static Class {
        &self.class
    }

    /// The class with a finalize entry, which LibGC calls with each dead cell of the class while every cell that dies
    /// in the collection is still intact, before it destroys any. The entry must not allocate.
    pub const fn with_finalize(mut self, finalize: unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)) -> Self {
        self.class.type_info.finalize = Some(finalize);
        self
    }

    /// The class with its cells traced on the thread that owns their heap only, see Class::traced_on_owner_thread_only().
    pub const fn traced_on_owner_thread_only(mut self) -> Self {
        self.class = self.class.traced_on_owner_thread_only();
        self
    }
}

impl<T: Trace + ExternalMemorySize + 'static> EmbedderClass<T> {
    /// A class whose cells LibGC asks how much memory their values own outside the heap, which it counts towards the
    /// bytes that make it collect, as it asks a C++ cell that overrides Cell::external_memory_size().
    pub const fn new_with_external_memory_size(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        let mut class = Self::new(name);
        class.class.type_info.external_memory_size = Some(external_memory_size_of_value::<T>);
        class
    }
}

/// The external_memory_size entry of a class that new_with_external_memory_size() creates.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls it, with a cell of that class.
unsafe extern "C" fn external_memory_size_of_value<T: ExternalMemorySize>(cell: *const c_void) -> usize {
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes a cell of the class, whose value stays intact for the call.
    let cell = unsafe { &*cell.cast::<EmbedderCell<T>>() };
    (**cell).external_memory_size()
}

/// A type of the embedder whose values live in cells of their own.
pub trait EmbedderValue: Trace + Sized + 'static {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self>;
}

// SAFETY: The cell is #[repr(C)] and starts with its header.
unsafe impl<T: EmbedderValue> GcCell for EmbedderCell<T> {
    const CLASS: &'static Class = T::CLASS.class();
}

impl<T: EmbedderValue> EmbedderClass<T> {
    /// Moves the value that `build` returns into a new cell of the class, as Heap::allocate() does.
    pub fn allocate(&'static self, vm: &Vm, build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<T>> {
        let allocator = vm.heap().embedder_class_allocator(&self.class);
        vm.heap().allocate_in(allocator, |defer_gc| EmbedderCell {
            header: CellHeader::for_class(&self.class),
            value: ValueWithRoomForFreeListLink {
                value: ManuallyDrop::new(build(defer_gc)),
            },
        })
    }

    /// The cell behind the pointer, if it is a cell of this class.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `cell` must be a live cell that an embedder class allocated, such as the host data of a host object the
    /// embedder created with such a cell, whose block therefore holds its class.
    pub unsafe fn downcast(&'static self, cell: NonNull<c_void>) -> Option<Gc<EmbedderCell<T>>> {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell of an embedder class.
        let cell = unsafe { Gc::<EmbedderCell<T>>::from_non_null(cell.cast()) };
        core::ptr::eq(class_of(cell), &raw const self.class).then_some(cell)
    }
}

//! References from the runtime's cells to the cells of an embedder's C++ types, which LibGC allocates in the same heap.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::capi::gc_visitor_visit_cell;
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};

/// A reference to a C++ GC cell, such as the implementation object a host object wraps, which keeps that cell alive
/// for as long as the cell or root holding the slot is.
#[derive(Default)]
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct ForeignCellSlot(Cell<Option<NonNull<c_void>>>);

impl ForeignCellSlot {
    pub const fn empty() -> Self {
        Self(Cell::new(None))
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.0.get()
    }

    /// The cell, or null, as the C ABI passes it.
    pub fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.get().map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), NonNull::as_ptr)
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `cell` must be a live cell of the heap the runtime allocates from, C++ or Rust, which the slot then keeps alive.
    pub unsafe fn set(&self, cell: Option<NonNull<c_void>>) {
        self.0.set(cell);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Visits the one cell the slot holds.
unsafe impl Trace for ForeignCellSlot {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(cell) = self.get() {
            // SAFETY: The visitor is live, and set() only stores cells of its heap, which the slot has kept alive.
            unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_cell(visitor.as_raw(), cell.as_ptr()) };
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/gc/gc_ref_cell.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use core::cell::{Ref, RefCell, RefMut};
use core::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};

use super::defer_gc::DeferGc;
use super::sweep::Sweep;
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;

/// Interior mutability for the compound state of a cell, which a collection reads. A mutable borrow defers collections
/// for as long as it lives, so a collection never finds the state borrowed: allocating meanwhile only grows the heap.
pub struct GcRefCell<T>(RefCell<T>);

impl<T> GcRefCell<T> {
    pub const fn new(value: T) -> Self {
        Self(RefCell::new(value))
    }

    pub fn borrow(&self) -> Ref<'_, T> {
        self.0.borrow()
    }

    pub fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut T {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    pub fn borrow_mut<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a Vm) -> GcRefMut<'a, T> {
        let defer_gc = DeferGc::new(vm);
        GcRefMut {
            borrow: self.0.borrow_mut(),
            _defer_gc: defer_gc,
        }
    }

    /// Borrows the state mutably from the sweep callback of a collection, which nothing collects during.
    pub(crate) fn borrow_mut_in_sweep(&self, _: &Sweep<'_>) -> RefMut<'_, T> {
        self.0.borrow_mut()
    }

    pub fn replace(&self, value: T) -> T {
        self.0.replace(value)
    }

    pub fn swap(&self, other: &Self) {
        self.0.swap(&other.0);
    }
}

impl<T: Default> Default for GcRefCell<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(T::default())
    }
}

// SAFETY: Traces the current value.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for GcRefCell<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // NB: Marking may trace the cell on a thread other than the one that owns the heap, so this only reads the
        //     borrow state, rather than borrow the value.
        // SAFETY: The thread that owns the heap is stopped while its collection marks, and it holds no mutable borrow,
        //         which this checks, so nothing changes the value while it is traced.
        let Ok(value) = (unsafe { self.0.try_borrow_unguarded() }) else {
            eprintln!("libjs_rust: garbage collection while a GcRefCell is mutably borrowed");
            std::process::abort();
        };
        value.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// A mutable borrow of the state in a GcRefCell, with the deferral of collections that it holds until it ends.
pub struct GcRefMut<'a, T: ?Sized> {
    // NB: Fields drop in order, so the borrow ends before the collection it may have deferred runs.
    borrow: RefMut<'a, T>,
    _defer_gc: DeferGc<'a>,
}

impl<'a, T: ?Sized> GcRefMut<'a, T> {
    /// Borrows a part of the state, as RefMut::map() does.
    pub fn map<U: ?Sized>(borrow: Self, part: impl FnOnce(&mut T) -> &mut U) -> GcRefMut<'a, U> {
        GcRefMut {
            borrow: RefMut::map(borrow.borrow, part),
            _defer_gc: borrow._defer_gc,
        }
    }
}

impl<T: ?Sized> Deref for GcRefMut<'_, T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        &self.borrow
    }
}

impl<T: ?Sized> DerefMut for GcRefMut<'_, T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
        &mut self.borrow
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/gc/heap_function.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! GC::Function<ThrowCompletionOr<Value>()> of Libraries/LibGC/Function.h: a closure that lives in the heap, which
//! the job queues hold.

use core::mem::MaybeUninit;

use super::class::{GcCell, define_cell};
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, Gc};
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::completion::ThrowCompletionOr;

struct CapturingBehaviour<C, F> {
    captures: C,
    behaviour: F,
}

/// Room for the captures of every heap function the runtime creates, the most being Promise.all's resolve element
/// job with five, so that a heap function keeps them in its own cell rather than in an allocation of their own.
#[repr(C, align(8))]
struct CaptureStorage([MaybeUninit<u8>; 48]);

#[repr(C)]
pub struct HeapFunction {
    header: CellHeader,
    /// call_with_captures() and trace_captures() for the types of the captures and the behaviour in `storage`.
    call: unsafe fn(*const CaptureStorage, &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>,
    trace: unsafe fn(*const CaptureStorage, &mut Visitor),
    storage: CaptureStorage,
}

define_cell!(HeapFunction, Other);

// SAFETY: The captures are all the cells the function reaches, and `trace` visits them.
unsafe impl Trace for HeapFunction {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // SAFETY: create_heap_function() stored the captures that `trace` was instantiated for.
        unsafe { (self.trace)(&raw const self.storage, visitor) };
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `storage` must hold a CapturingBehaviour<C, F>.
unsafe fn call_with_captures<C, F>(storage: *const CaptureStorage, vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>
where
    C: Copy,
    F: Fn(&Vm, &C) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> + Copy,
{
    // SAFETY: The caller passes storage that holds a CapturingBehaviour<C, F>, which fits and is aligned for it.
    let behaviour = unsafe { storage.cast::<CapturingBehaviour<C, F>>().read() };
    // NB: The captures are copied out of the cell, so nothing in the call points into it.
    (behaviour.behaviour)(vm, &behaviour.captures)
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `storage` must hold a CapturingBehaviour<C, F>.
unsafe fn trace_captures<C: Trace, F>(storage: *const CaptureStorage, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes storage that holds a CapturingBehaviour<C, F>, which fits and is aligned for it.
    let behaviour = unsafe { &*storage.cast::<CapturingBehaviour<C, F>>() };
    behaviour.captures.trace(visitor);
}

/// GC::create_function(heap, function). The behaviour must not capture anything: the state it needs is `captures`,
/// which the heap function keeps alive.
pub fn create_heap_function<C, F>(vm: &Vm, captures: C, behaviour: F) -> Gc<HeapFunction>
where
    C: Trace + Copy + 'static,
    F: Fn(&Vm, &C) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> + Copy + 'static,
{
    const {
        assert!(
            size_of::<F>() == 0,
            "a heap function captures its state through its captures, not its behaviour"
        );
        assert!(size_of::<CapturingBehaviour<C, F>>() <= size_of::<CaptureStorage>());
        assert!(align_of::<CapturingBehaviour<C, F>>() <= align_of::<CaptureStorage>());
    };
    let mut storage = CaptureStorage([MaybeUninit::uninit(); 48]);
    // SAFETY: The storage is large and aligned enough for the behaviour, as checked above.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::from_mut(&mut storage)
            .cast::<CapturingBehaviour<C, F>>()
            .write(CapturingBehaviour { captures, behaviour });
    }
    // The captures stay in `storage` on the stack, where the collector finds them, until the function that keeps
    // them alive exists.
    vm.heap().allocate(|_| HeapFunction {
        header: CellHeader::for_class(HeapFunction::CLASS),
        call: call_with_captures::<C, F>,
        trace: trace_captures::<C, F>,
        storage,
    })
}

impl HeapFunction {
    /// Calls the function. The caller's Gc keeps the function and the state it captures alive for the whole call.
    pub fn call(function: Gc<HeapFunction>, vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // SAFETY: create_heap_function() stored the captures that `call` was instantiated for.
        let result = unsafe { (function.call)(&raw const function.storage, vm) };
        // NB: Using the Gc after the call keeps it where the conservative scan finds it until the call has returned.
        core::hint::black_box(function);
        result
    }
}

/*

use core::cell::{Cell, OnceCell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::mem::offset_of;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use super::capi::{self, GCAllocator, GCGatherRootsCallback, GCHeap, GCLayout};
use super::class::{BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET, BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG, BLOCK_SIZE, CellTypeInfo, Class, GcCell, MIN_CELL_SIZE};
use super::class_id::{CLASS_COUNT, ClassId};
use super::defer_gc::DeferGc;
use super::weak::WEAK_IMPL_POINTER_OFFSET;
use crate::build_configuration::{HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK, PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_CAGE_OFFSET_MASK};
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, Gc};

/// A LibGC heap, with one allocator per class of cell.
///
/// Cells are taken from the local free lists of the allocators in the heap without a call into LibGC whenever the heap
/// does not have to collect garbage (see gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list()).
pub struct Heap {
    raw: NonNull<GCHeap>,
    allocators: [Cell<Option<HeapAllocator>>; CLASS_COUNT],
    /// The allocators of the classes that have no id of their own, the classes derived at run time and the classes
    /// of an embedder's cells, by the address of their class.
    runtime_class_allocators: RefCell<HashMap<usize, HeapAllocator, foldhash::fast::RandomState>>,
    /// The allocators that the classes extending a class share, by the address of that class.
    shared_class_allocators: RefCell<HashMap<usize, SharedClassAllocator, foldhash::fast::RandomState>>,
    /// The size classes of each class, by class id, out of line, as few classes have any.
    size_class_tables: Box<[OnceCell<SizeClassTable>; CLASS_COUNT]>,
    inline_allocation_info: InlineAllocationInfo,
    /// LibGC's count of deferrals, and whether a collection waits for it to reach zero.
    deferrals: NonNull<usize>,
    collect_when_deferrals_end: NonNull<bool>,
}

/// An allocator that classes extending a class share, whose cells each keep their class in the word after them (see
/// `class_at`), with the type info of those larger cells, which has to outlive the allocator.
struct SharedClassAllocator {
    allocator: HeapAllocator,
    _type_info: Box<CellTypeInfo>,
}

/// The size classes of a class, with the type infos their blocks dispatch through, which have to outlive the
/// allocators.
struct SizeClassTable {
    allocators: Box<[SizeClassAllocator]>,
    _type_infos: Box<[CellTypeInfo]>,
}

/// What code that allocates cells from the local free lists of a heap itself, like JIT code, needs to know besides the
/// address of the list: where the heap's allocation counters are, and where a free cell keeps the link to the next free
/// cell and which bits of it count. See gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list() for how to allocate with them.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct InlineAllocationInfo {
    pub allocated_bytes_since_last_gc: NonNull<usize>,
    pub gc_bytes_threshold: NonNull<usize>,
    pub total_allocated_bytes: NonNull<usize>,
    pub free_cell_next_offset: usize,
    pub free_cell_link_mask: usize,
    /// Where an allocator keeps the cursor, the end and the cell size of the never-allocated cells it bumps through
    /// once its local free list is empty, relative to the head of the list.
    pub local_cursor_offset: usize,
    pub local_end_offset: usize,
    pub local_cell_size_offset: usize,
}

/// An allocator of a heap, with the address of its local free list in the heap, which is null if every cell has to be
/// allocated through LibGC.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct HeapAllocator {
    raw: NonNull<GCAllocator>,
    local_free_list: *mut *mut c_void,
}

impl HeapAllocator {
    fn local_free_list(self) -> Option<NonNull<*mut c_void>> {
        NonNull::new(self.local_free_list)
    }
}

/// The allocator of a class derived at run time, which only the cells of that class come from, as each C++ class that
/// declares GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR has one of its own. It belongs to the heap that created it and lives as long as it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct RuntimeClassAllocator {
    class: &'static Class,
    allocator: HeapAllocator,
    /// Whether the allocator is shared with other classes, so that each cell keeps its class in the word after it.
    class_in_tail: bool,
}

impl RuntimeClassAllocator {
    pub fn class(&self) -> &'static Class {
        self.class
    }

    /// Where the head of the allocator's local free list is, for code that allocates its cells itself.
    pub fn local_free_list(&self) -> Option<NonNull<*mut c_void>> {
        self.allocator.local_free_list()
    }
}

impl PartialEq for RuntimeClassAllocator {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.allocator.raw == other.allocator.raw
    }
}

impl Eq for RuntimeClassAllocator {}

/// One size class of a class whose cells end in a variable-size part, like an array of trailing values: an allocator of
/// its own, whose cells are larger than the type of the class. It belongs to the heap that created it and lives as long
/// as it. LibGC dispatches through the class's type info with the size class's cell size, so gc_cell_type_info() of
/// such a cell is not the type info of its class.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct SizeClassAllocator {
    class: &'static Class,
    cell_size: u32,
    allocator: HeapAllocator,
}

impl SizeClassAllocator {
    pub fn class(&self) -> &'static Class {
        self.class
    }

    /// The size of each cell, including the part beyond the type of the class.
    pub fn cell_size(&self) -> u32 {
        self.cell_size
    }

    /// Where the head of the allocator's local free list is, for code that allocates its cells itself.
    pub fn local_free_list(&self) -> Option<NonNull<*mut c_void>> {
        self.allocator.local_free_list()
    }
}

impl PartialEq for SizeClassAllocator {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.allocator.raw == other.allocator.raw
    }
}

impl Eq for SizeClassAllocator {}

/// Whether an allocation may collect garbage and counts towards the next collection, as cells do, or does neither, as
/// the cells other cells keep their storage in.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum AllocationKind {
    Cell,
    Storage,
}

impl Heap {
    /// Creates a heap that calls `gather_roots` with `context` whenever it gathers its roots. A heap that becomes the
    /// default of its thread is the one GC::Heap::the() returns to C++ code on that thread.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `context` must stay valid for as long as the heap exists, including while it is being destroyed.
    pub unsafe fn new(gather_roots: GCGatherRootsCallback, context: *mut c_void, become_thread_default: bool) -> Self {
        let layout = check_layout();
        crate::layout_forward::initialize_heap_region_base();
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the context alive for the heap's lifetime.
        let raw = unsafe { capi::gc_heap_create(gather_roots, context, become_thread_default) };
        let raw = NonNull::new(raw).expect("LibGC creates the heap");
        // NB: LibGC reports offsets of fields of its heap.
        let counter = |offset: u32| {
            NonNull::new(raw.as_ptr().wrapping_byte_add(offset as usize).cast::<usize>())
                .expect("the fields of LibGC's heap are not at null")
        };
        let (mut deferrals, mut collect_when_deferrals_end) = (core::ptr::null_mut(), core::ptr::null_mut());
        // SAFETY: LibGC just created the heap.
        capi::gc_heap_deferral_state(unsafe { raw.as_ref() }, &mut deferrals, &mut collect_when_deferrals_end);
        Self {
            raw,
            allocators: [const { Cell::new(None) }; CLASS_COUNT],
            runtime_class_allocators: RefCell::default(),
            shared_class_allocators: RefCell::default(),
            size_class_tables: Box::new([const { OnceCell::new() }; CLASS_COUNT]),
            inline_allocation_info: InlineAllocationInfo {
                allocated_bytes_since_last_gc: counter(layout.heap_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc_offset),
                gc_bytes_threshold: counter(layout.heap_gc_bytes_threshold_offset),
                total_allocated_bytes: counter(layout.heap_total_allocated_bytes_offset),
                free_cell_next_offset: layout.free_cell_next_offset as usize,
                free_cell_link_mask: layout.free_cell_link_mask as usize,
                local_cursor_offset: layout.local_cursor_offset as usize,
                local_end_offset: layout.local_end_offset as usize,
                local_cell_size_offset: layout.local_cell_size_offset as usize,
            },
            deferrals: NonNull::new(deferrals).expect("LibGC counts deferrals"),
            collect_when_deferrals_end: NonNull::new(collect_when_deferrals_end)
                .expect("LibGC tracks waiting collections"),
        }
    }

    pub fn inline_allocation_info(&self) -> InlineAllocationInfo {
        self.inline_allocation_info
    }

    /// Where the head of the local free list of the allocator of `class` is, for code that allocates its cells itself.
    pub fn local_free_list_of(&self, class: &'static Class) -> Option<NonNull<*mut c_void>> {
        self.allocator_for(class).local_free_list()
    }

    pub fn raw(&self) -> *mut GCHeap {
        self.raw.as_ptr()
    }

    /// LibGC's heap, for the functions of its C API that only need it to be live.
    pub fn handle(&self) -> &GCHeap {
        // SAFETY: This owns the heap, which stays live for as long as this does.
        unsafe { self.raw.as_ref() }
    }

    /// GC::Heap::defer_gc(), without a call into LibGC.
    pub(super) fn defer_gc(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The count is a field of the live heap, which only this thread uses.
        unsafe { *self.deferrals.as_ptr() += 1 };
    }

    /// GC::Heap::undefer_gc(), without a call into LibGC unless a collection waits for the last deferral to end.
    pub(super) fn undefer_gc(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The count and the flag are fields of the live heap, which only this thread uses.
        unsafe {
            let deferrals = self.deferrals.as_ptr();
            debug_assert!(*deferrals > 0);
            if *deferrals == 1 && *self.collect_when_deferrals_end.as_ptr() {
                capi::gc_heap_undefer_gc(self.handle());
            } else {
                *deferrals -= 1;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Moves the cell that `build` returns into the heap, with collections deferred from before `build` runs until
    /// the cell is in the heap.
    pub fn allocate<T: GcCell>(&self, build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T) -> Gc<T> {
        const { assert!(size_of::<T>() >= MIN_CELL_SIZE) };
        let allocator = self.allocator_for(T::CLASS);
        // SAFETY: The allocator is the one of the cell's static class, whose cells have the size and alignment of a T.
        unsafe { self.allocate_with(allocator, size_of::<T>(), AllocationKind::Cell, build, |_| {}) }
    }

    /// allocate() into the storage of `allocator`, which was created for the class of the cell or a class it derives
    /// from.
    pub fn allocate_in<T: GcCell>(
        &self,
        allocator: RuntimeClassAllocator,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T,
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        assert!(
            allocator.class.type_info.cell_size as usize == size_of::<T>() && allocator.class.is_subclass_of(T::CLASS),
            "{} cells are not {}s",
            allocator.class.name,
            T::CLASS.name
        );
        let build = |defer_gc: &DeferGc<'_>| {
            let cell = build(defer_gc);
            // SAFETY: Every cell starts with its header.
            debug_assert!(unsafe { (*core::ptr::from_ref(&cell).cast::<CellHeader>()).kind } == allocator.class.kind());
            cell
        };
        if !allocator.class_in_tail {
            // SAFETY: The allocator's cells have the size of a T, checked above, and T's alignment, as its class extends
            //         T's.
            return unsafe {
                self.allocate_with(allocator.allocator, size_of::<T>(), AllocationKind::Cell, build, |_| {})
            };
        }
        let class = allocator.class;
        let initialize_tail = |tail: *mut u8| {
            // SAFETY: A cell of a shared allocator has room for its class right after the T, 8-byte aligned.
            unsafe { tail.cast::<&'static Class>().write(class) };
        };
        // SAFETY: The cells of a shared allocator have the size of a T and a word, and T's alignment, as its class
        //         extends T's.
        unsafe {
            self.allocate_with(
                allocator.allocator,
                size_of::<T>() + size_of::<&'static Class>(),
                AllocationKind::Cell,
                build,
                initialize_tail,
            )
        }
    }

    /// allocate() into a cell of `size_class`, whose class is the class of the cell or one that it extends, filling the
    /// rest of the larger cell with copies of `tail`. Finding and tracing the part beyond the T is up to the T.
    pub fn allocate_with_size_class<T: GcCell, E: Copy>(
        &self,
        size_class: SizeClassAllocator,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T,
        tail: E,
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        self.allocate_in_size_class(size_class, AllocationKind::Cell, build, tail)
    }

    /// allocate_with_size_class() for a cell that another cell keeps its storage in, instead of malloc memory: it never
    /// collects garbage, so storage can grow while its owner is between states nothing may observe, and callers can hold
    /// on to anything across the growth. It still counts towards the next collection, which the next allocation that
    /// may collect starts.
    pub fn allocate_storage_with_size_class<T: GcCell, E: Copy>(
        &self,
        size_class: SizeClassAllocator,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T,
        tail: E,
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        self.allocate_in_size_class(size_class, AllocationKind::Storage, build, tail)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn allocate_in_size_class<T: GcCell, E: Copy>(
        &self,
        size_class: SizeClassAllocator,
        kind: AllocationKind,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T,
        tail: E,
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        const {
            assert!(
                size_of::<E>() > 0 && align_of::<E>() <= 8,
                "the tail starts 8-byte aligned"
            );
        }
        assert!(
            size_class.class.type_info.cell_size as usize == size_of::<T>()
                && size_class.class.is_subclass_of(T::CLASS),
            "{} cells are not {}s",
            size_class.class.name,
            T::CLASS.name
        );
        let build = |defer_gc: &DeferGc<'_>| {
            let cell = build(defer_gc);
            // SAFETY: Every cell starts with its header.
            debug_assert!(
                unsafe { (*core::ptr::from_ref(&cell).cast::<CellHeader>()).kind } == size_class.class.kind()
            );
            cell
        };
        let tail_size = size_class.cell_size as usize - size_of::<T>();
        assert!(
            tail_size.is_multiple_of(size_of::<E>()),
            "the tail of a size class is a whole number of values"
        );
        let initialize_tail = |tail_start: *mut u8| {
            let tail_start = tail_start.cast::<E>();
            for index in 0..tail_size / size_of::<E>() {
                // SAFETY: The cell has tail_size bytes beyond the T, which starts 8-byte aligned, as each class's size
                // is a multiple of 8.
                unsafe { tail_start.add(index).write(tail) };
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: The size class's cells are larger than a T, checked above, and have T's alignment, as its class
        // extends T's.
        unsafe {
            self.allocate_with(
                size_class.allocator,
                size_class.cell_size as usize,
                kind,
                build,
                initialize_tail,
            )
        }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The allocator must belong to this heap and hand out storage of `cell_size` bytes, at least the size of a T, with
    /// the alignment of a T, and `initialize_tail` must write every byte beyond the T, which it gets the address of.
    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn allocate_with<T: GcCell>(
        &self,
        allocator: HeapAllocator,
        cell_size: usize,
        kind: AllocationKind,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T,
        initialize_tail: impl FnOnce(*mut u8),
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        let defer_gc = DeferGc::of_heap(self);
        let cell = build(&defer_gc);
        // SAFETY: The allocator belongs to this heap and hands out cells of cell_size bytes.
        let cell = match unsafe { self.take_from_local_free_list(allocator, cell_size, kind) } {
            // SAFETY: The storage is a cell of the allocator, so it has the size and the alignment the caller guarantees.
            Some(storage) => unsafe { Self::write_cell(storage.cast(), cell, initialize_tail) },
            // SAFETY: The caller's guarantees about the allocator and the tail pass on.
            None => unsafe { self.allocate_from_heap(&defer_gc, allocator, kind, cell, initialize_tail) },
        };
        // NB: A collection that became due runs now, with the cell in the heap and its Gc on the stack.
        drop(defer_gc);
        cell
    }

    /// Takes the storage from LibGC, which defers the collection that is due until the deferral ends.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// As for allocate_with().
    unsafe fn allocate_from_heap<T: GcCell>(
        &self,
        _: &DeferGc<'_>,
        allocator: HeapAllocator,
        kind: AllocationKind,
        cell: T,
        initialize_tail: impl FnOnce(*mut u8),
    ) -> Gc<T> {
        let raw = allocator.raw.as_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The heap and the allocator are live.
        let storage = unsafe {
            match kind {
                AllocationKind::Cell => capi::gc_heap_allocate_cell(self.raw.as_ptr(), raw),
                AllocationKind::Storage => capi::gc_heap_allocate_storage_cell(self.raw.as_ptr(), raw),
            }
        };
        let storage = NonNull::new(storage).expect("LibGC allocates the cell").cast::<T>();
        // SAFETY: LibGC returned uninitialized storage of at least the size and the alignment of a T, as the caller
        // guarantees.
        unsafe { Self::write_cell(storage, cell, initialize_tail) }
    }

    /// Writes `cell` to `storage` and has `initialize_tail` write the rest of the cell.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `storage` must be uninitialized storage of at least the size and the alignment of a T, which nothing can collect
    /// garbage before it is written, and `initialize_tail` must write every byte beyond the T.
    unsafe fn write_cell<T: GcCell>(storage: NonNull<T>, cell: T, initialize_tail: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) -> Gc<T> {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes storage for a T with room for the tail.
        unsafe {
            storage.write(cell);
            initialize_tail(storage.as_ptr().cast::<u8>().add(size_of::<T>()));
        }
        let header = storage.cast::<CellHeader>();
        // SAFETY: Every cell starts with its header.
        unsafe {
            debug_assert!((*header.as_ptr()).class().is_subclass_of(T::CLASS));
            Gc::from_non_null(storage)
        }
    }

    /// Takes a cell from the allocator's local free list, or else from its never-allocated cells, unless LibGC has to
    /// collect garbage first or there is no local free cell, with the bookkeeping gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list()
    /// describes. These cells are in blocks that are swept already, so they never need marking.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The allocator must belong to this heap and hand out cells of `cell_size` bytes.
    #[inline(always)]
    unsafe fn take_from_local_free_list(
        &self,
        allocator: HeapAllocator,
        cell_size: usize,
        kind: AllocationKind,
    ) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        let local_free_list = allocator.local_free_list()?;
        let info = &self.inline_allocation_info;
        let link_mask = info.free_cell_link_mask;
        // SAFETY: The list, the cursor, the end and the counters are fields of the live heap, and every cell on the list
        //         is a free cell that keeps the link to the next one at free_cell_next_offset.
        unsafe {
            let cursor = local_free_list.byte_add(info.local_cursor_offset).cast::<*mut c_void>();
            let head = local_free_list.read();
            let from_list = head.addr() & link_mask != 0;
            let cell = if from_list {
                head
            } else {
                let cursor_cell = cursor.read();
                let end = local_free_list.byte_add(info.local_end_offset).cast::<usize>().read();
                if cursor_cell.addr() >= end {
                    return None;
                }
                cursor_cell
            };
            let cell = NonNull::new_unchecked(cell);
            let allocated_bytes = info.allocated_bytes_since_last_gc.read() + cell_size;
            if matches!(kind, AllocationKind::Cell) && allocated_bytes > info.gc_bytes_threshold.read() {
                return None;
            }
            info.allocated_bytes_since_last_gc.write(allocated_bytes);
            info.total_allocated_bytes
                .write(info.total_allocated_bytes.read() + cell_size);
            if from_list {
                // NB: Only the bits of the link under the mask count, so that the next cell is in the block of this one
                //     whatever the link was overwritten with.
                let link = cell.byte_add(info.free_cell_next_offset).cast::<usize>().read();
                local_free_list.write(
                    cell.as_ptr()
                        .map_addr(|address| (address & !link_mask) | (link & link_mask)),
                );
            } else {
                cursor.write(cell.as_ptr().byte_add(cell_size));
            }
            Some(cell)
        }
    }

    /// Creates an allocator of cells of `class` with `type_info`, whose blocks hold the class (see `class_of`), tagged
    /// if each cell keeps a class of its own in the word after it.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The type info must outlive the allocator.
    unsafe fn create_allocator(
        &self,
        type_info: *const CellTypeInfo,
        class: &'static Class,
        class_in_tail: bool,
    ) -> HeapAllocator {
        let name = class.name;
        let mut foreign_type = core::ptr::from_ref(class).cast::<u8>();
        if class_in_tail {
            foreign_type = foreign_type.wrapping_add(BLOCK_CLASS_TAIL_TAG);
        }
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the type info alive for as long as the allocator, and the class lives forever.
        let raw =
            unsafe { capi::gc_allocator_create(type_info, name.as_ptr().cast(), name.len(), foreign_type.cast()) };
        let raw = NonNull::new(raw).expect("LibGC creates the allocator");
        if class.is_traced_on_owner_thread_only() {
            // SAFETY: The allocator is live and has not allocated yet.
            unsafe { capi::gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only(raw.as_ptr()) };
        }
        // NB: The classes derived at run time that share an allocator are never movable.
        if class.is_movable() && !class_in_tail {
            // SAFETY: The allocator is live and has not allocated yet.
            unsafe { capi::gc_allocator_set_movable(raw.as_ptr()) };
        }
        // SAFETY: The heap and the allocator are live.
        let local_free_list = unsafe { capi::gc_heap_allocator_local_free_list(self.raw.as_ptr(), raw.as_ptr()) };
        HeapAllocator { raw, local_free_list }
    }

    /// The allocator of `class`, a class derived at run time, which the first call for the class creates.
    pub fn runtime_class_allocator(&self, class: &'static Class) -> RuntimeClassAllocator {
        assert!(
            class.is_derived_at_run_time(),
            "the cells of {} come from the allocator of its id",
            class.name
        );
        RuntimeClassAllocator {
            class,
            allocator: self.allocator_kept_by_class_address(class),
            class_in_tail: false,
        }
    }

    /// The allocator of `class`, a class derived at run time that shares the allocator of `allocating_class`, a class it
    /// extends, with the other classes that do: each cell keeps its class in the word after it (see `class_at`).
    pub fn shared_runtime_class_allocator(
        &self,
        allocating_class: &'static Class,
        class: &'static Class,
    ) -> RuntimeClassAllocator {
        assert!(
            class.is_derived_at_run_time()
                && class.is_subclass_of(allocating_class)
                && class.type_info.cell_size == allocating_class.type_info.cell_size
                && allocating_class.type_info.alignment as usize <= size_of::<&'static Class>(),
            "{} cannot share the allocator of {}",
            class.name,
            allocating_class.name
        );
        assert!(
            !class.is_traced_on_owner_thread_only() || allocating_class.is_traced_on_owner_thread_only(),
            "{} is traced on the owner thread only, unlike the allocator of {} it shares",
            class.name,
            allocating_class.name
        );
        let allocator = self
            .shared_class_allocators
            .borrow_mut()
            .entry(core::ptr::from_ref(allocating_class) as usize)
            .or_insert_with(|| {
                let type_info = Box::new(CellTypeInfo {
                    cell_size: allocating_class.type_info.cell_size + size_of::<&'static Class>() as u32,
                    ..allocating_class.type_info
                });
                // SAFETY: The box keeps the type info alive for as long as the allocator.
                let allocator = unsafe { self.create_allocator(&raw const *type_info, allocating_class, true) };
                SharedClassAllocator {
                    allocator,
                    _type_info: type_info,
                }
            })
            .allocator;
        RuntimeClassAllocator {
            class,
            allocator,
            class_in_tail: true,
        }
    }

    /// The allocator of `class`, the class of an embedder's cells, which the first call for the class creates. Such
    /// classes all have ClassId::EmbedderCell, so each has an allocator of its own, kept by its address.
    pub fn embedder_class_allocator(&self, class: &'static Class) -> RuntimeClassAllocator {
        assert!(
            class.id == ClassId::EmbedderCell && class.parent.is_none(),
            "{} is not the class of an embedder's cells",
            class.name
        );
        RuntimeClassAllocator {
            class,
            allocator: self.allocator_kept_by_class_address(class),
            class_in_tail: false,
        }
    }

    fn allocator_kept_by_class_address(&self, class: &'static Class) -> HeapAllocator {
        *self
            .runtime_class_allocators
            .borrow_mut()
            .entry(core::ptr::from_ref(class) as usize)
            // SAFETY: The class and its name live as long as the process, so they outlive the allocator.
            .or_insert_with(|| unsafe { self.create_allocator(&raw const class.type_info, class, false) })
    }

    /// The size classes of `class`, whose cells have `cell_sizes` bytes, in that order, which the first call for the
    /// class creates. A class has one set of size classes, so every call for it passes the same sizes.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn size_classes(&self, class: &'static Class, cell_sizes: &[u32]) -> &[SizeClassAllocator] {
        let table =
            self.size_class_tables[class.id as usize].get_or_init(|| self.create_size_classes(class, cell_sizes));
        debug_assert!(
            table
                .allocators
                .iter()
                .map(SizeClassAllocator::cell_size)
                .eq(cell_sizes.iter().copied())
        );
        &table.allocators
    }

    #[cold]
    fn create_size_classes(&self, class: &'static Class, cell_sizes: &[u32]) -> SizeClassTable {
        assert!(
            !class.is_derived_at_run_time(),
            "a class derived at run time shares the id of {}",
            class.name
        );
        assert!(
            class.id != ClassId::EmbedderCell,
            "the class of an embedder's cells, {}, shares its id",
            class.name
        );
        let type_infos: Box<[CellTypeInfo]> = cell_sizes
            .iter()
            .map(|&cell_size| {
                assert!(
                    cell_size >= class.type_info.cell_size && cell_size.is_multiple_of(8),
                    "a size class of {} has cells of {cell_size} bytes",
                    class.name
                );
                CellTypeInfo {
                    cell_size,
                    ..class.type_info
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let allocators = type_infos
            .iter()
            .map(|type_info| SizeClassAllocator {
                class,
                cell_size: type_info.cell_size,
                // SAFETY: The heap destroys the allocator before the type info, and the class name is static.
                allocator: unsafe { self.create_allocator(type_info, class, false) },
            })
            .collect();
        SizeClassTable {
            allocators,
            _type_infos: type_infos,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn allocator_for(&self, class: &'static Class) -> HeapAllocator {
        let slot = &self.allocators[class.id as usize];
        if let Some(allocator) = slot.get() {
            return allocator;
        }
        assert!(
            class.id != ClassId::EmbedderCell,
            "the cells of an embedder class, {}, come from the allocator kept by its address",
            class.name
        );
        // SAFETY: The class and its name are static, so they outlive the allocator.
        let allocator = unsafe { self.create_allocator(&raw const class.type_info, class, false) };
        slot.set(Some(allocator));
        allocator
    }

    pub fn collect_garbage(&self) {
        capi::gc_heap_collect_garbage(self.handle(), capi::GC_COLLECTION_TYPE_COLLECT_GARBAGE, false);
    }

    /// Collects garbage without scanning the stack, so that only roots keep cells alive, and cells may move.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller, and every frame above it, must hold no cell that is not rooted, since such a cell may be collected
    /// or moved.
    pub unsafe fn collect_garbage_without_scanning_the_stack(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The caller vouches that the stack holds no cell that is not rooted.
        unsafe { capi::gc_heap_collect_garbage_without_scanning_the_stack(self.handle()) };
    }

    /// Whether LIBGC_MOVE_EVERYTHING has collections that do not scan the stack move every cell they can, which test
    /// runners use to collect that way where they safely can.
    pub fn moves_everything() -> bool {
        capi::gc_heap_moves_everything()
    }

    /// Has the collections of this heap that do not scan the stack move every cell they can, or not, for tests.
    pub fn set_moves_everything_for_testing(&self, moves_everything: bool) {
        capi::gc_heap_set_moves_everything_for_testing(self.handle(), moves_everything);
    }

    /// Calls `callback` with `context` during every collection, after marking and finalization and before dead cells
    /// are swept, so that weak holders can drop the cells whose mark is clear.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `context` must stay valid for as long as the heap exists, including while it is being destroyed.
    pub unsafe fn register_sweep_callback(&self, callback: capi::GCCallback, context: *mut c_void) {
        // SAFETY: The heap is live, and the caller keeps the context alive for its lifetime.
        unsafe { capi::gc_heap_register_sweep_callback(self.raw.as_ptr(), callback, context) };
    }

    /// Calls `callback` with `context` once the collection in progress is over, when it is safe to allocate again.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `context` must stay valid until the callback has run.
    pub unsafe fn enqueue_post_gc_task(&self, callback: capi::GCCallback, context: *mut c_void) {
        // SAFETY: The heap is live, and the caller keeps the context alive until the task runs.
        unsafe { capi::gc_heap_enqueue_post_gc_task(self.raw.as_ptr(), callback, context) };
    }

    /// Counts memory a cell allocated outside the heap towards the next collection, which this may start.
    pub fn did_allocate_external_memory(&self, size: usize) {
        capi::gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory(self.handle(), size);
    }

    pub fn did_free_external_memory(&self, size: usize) {
        capi::gc_heap_did_free_external_memory(self.handle(), size);
    }

    pub fn account_external_memory_change(&self, old_size: usize, new_size: usize) {
        if new_size > old_size {
            self.did_allocate_external_memory(new_size - old_size);
        } else if old_size > new_size {
            self.did_free_external_memory(old_size - new_size);
        }
    }

    /// Whether the heap gathers its roots and marks the live cells for a collection now, rather than for a graph dump.
    pub fn is_marking_for_collection(&self) -> bool {
        capi::gc_heap_is_marking_for_collection(self.handle())
    }

    /// Whether the collection that runs is there to give memory back to the system, for a process that is short of it.
    pub fn is_returning_memory_to_system(&self) -> bool {
        capi::gc_heap_is_returning_memory_to_system(self.handle())
    }

    pub fn should_collect_on_every_allocation(&self) -> bool {
        capi::gc_heap_should_collect_on_every_allocation(self.handle())
    }

    pub fn set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(&self, should_collect: bool) {
        capi::gc_heap_set_should_collect_on_every_allocation(self.handle(), should_collect);
    }

    /// Heap::uproot_cell(): has the next collection leave `cell` out of its roots, so that copies of it on the stack or
    /// in the registers of a running frame no longer keep it alive. A cell that something on the heap still points at
    /// stays alive.
    pub fn uproot_cell<T>(&self, cell: Gc<T>) {
        // SAFETY: The heap is live, and LibGC only keeps the cell's address until the next collection.
        unsafe { capi::gc_heap_uproot_cell(self.raw.as_ptr(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
    }

    /// The lowest and highest addresses of the stack of the thread that created the heap.
    pub fn stack_bounds(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
        let (mut base, mut top) = (0, 0);
        capi::gc_heap_stack_bounds(self.handle(), &mut base, &mut top);
        (base, top)
    }
}

impl Drop for Heap {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This owns the heap. The allocators outlive it, as LibGC requires.
        unsafe {
            capi::gc_heap_destroy(self.raw.as_ptr());
            for allocator in self.allocators.iter().filter_map(Cell::get) {
                capi::gc_allocator_destroy(allocator.raw.as_ptr());
            }
            for allocator in self.runtime_class_allocators.get_mut().values() {
                capi::gc_allocator_destroy(allocator.raw.as_ptr());
            }
            for shared in self.shared_class_allocators.get_mut().values() {
                capi::gc_allocator_destroy(shared.allocator.raw.as_ptr());
            }
            for table in self.size_class_tables.iter().filter_map(OnceCell::get) {
                for size_class in &table.allocators {
                    capi::gc_allocator_destroy(size_class.allocator.raw.as_ptr());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Checks the layouts this crate mirrors against the LibGC it is linked with, and returns LibGC's layout.
fn check_layout() -> GCLayout {
    let mut layout = GCLayout::default();
    capi::gc_get_layout(&mut layout, size_of::<GCLayout>());
    let expect = |what: &str, actual: u64, expected: u64| {
        assert!(
            actual == expected,
            "LibGC's {what} is {actual}, the Rust runtime expects {expected}"
        );
    };
    expect(
        "visitor marker offset",
        layout.visitor_marker_offset.into(),
        super::visitor::VISITOR_MARKER_OFFSET as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "cell state offset",
        layout.cell_state_offset.into(),
        offset_of!(CellHeader, state) as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "cell kind offset",
        layout.cell_kind_offset.into(),
        offset_of!(CellHeader, kind) as u64,
    );
    expect("block size", layout.block_size.into(), BLOCK_SIZE as u64);
    expect(
        "identity hash state offset",
        layout.identity_hash_state_offset.into(),
        crate::layout_forward::IDENTITY_HASH_STATE_OFFSET as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "identity hash state offset in the cell header",
        layout.identity_hash_state_offset.into(),
        offset_of!(CellHeader, identity_hash_state) as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "identity hash bits",
        u64::from(layout.identity_hash_hashed) | (u64::from(layout.identity_hash_moved) << 8),
        u64::from(crate::layout_forward::IDENTITY_HASH_HASHED)
            | (u64::from(crate::layout_forward::IDENTITY_HASH_MOVED) << 8),
    );
    expect(
        "block foreign type offset",
        layout.block_foreign_type_offset.into(),
        BLOCK_CLASS_OFFSET as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "cell type info size",
        layout.cell_type_info_size.into(),
        size_of::<CellTypeInfo>() as u64,
    );
    expect(
        "heap region offset mask",
        layout.heap_region_offset_mask,
        HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK,
    );
    expect(
        "primitive storage cage offset mask",
        layout.primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask,
        PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_CAGE_OFFSET_MASK,
    );
    expect(
        "weak impl pointer offset",
        layout.weak_impl_pointer_offset.into(),
        WEAK_IMPL_POINTER_OFFSET as u64,
    );
    layout
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
