//! Growable storage for the buffers a cell owns and the interpreter reads through their data pointer. A buffer
//! allocated through these methods belongs to the cell that holds it, which frees it with clear() in its finalizer. The
//! interpreter may read and write elements at any time, so elements are only ever copied in and out, never borrowed.
//! A buffer can also use storage it does not own, like room in its cell: its owner then makes sure it never grows,
//! shrinks or clears it in place, but moves the elements to storage of its own or forgets the storage instead.

use core::cell::Cell;
use std::alloc::{Layout, alloc, dealloc, handle_alloc_error};

use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::layout::buffer::{BlockSlice, InterpreterBuffer, ThinSlice};
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::slice_block::THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE;

/// Mirrors AK::Vector's growth policy.
fn padded_capacity(capacity: usize) -> usize {
    4 + capacity + capacity / 4
}

impl<T: Copy> InterpreterBuffer<T> {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            data: Cell::new(core::ptr::null_mut()),
            size: Cell::new(0),
            capacity: Cell::new(0),
        }
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size.get() as usize
    }

    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity.get() as usize
    }

    fn set_size(&self, size: usize) {
        self.size
            .set(u32::try_from(size).expect("the size of a buffer fits in u32"));
    }

    fn set_capacity(&self, capacity: usize) {
        self.capacity
            .set(u32::try_from(capacity).expect("the capacity of a buffer fits in u32"));
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.size() == 0
    }

    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> T {
        assert!(
            index < self.size(),
            "index {index} is out of bounds of a buffer of {}",
            self.size()
        );
        // SAFETY: The first `size` elements are initialized.
        unsafe { self.data.get().add(index).read() }
    }

    pub fn set(&self, index: usize, value: T) {
        assert!(
            index < self.size(),
            "index {index} is out of bounds of a buffer of {}",
            self.size()
        );
        // SAFETY: The element is in bounds, and nothing borrows the buffer's elements.
        unsafe { self.data.get().add(index).write(value) };
    }

    pub fn append(&self, value: T) {
        let size = self.size();
        if size == self.capacity() {
            self.reallocate(padded_capacity(size + 1));
        }
        // SAFETY: The buffer has room for one more element.
        unsafe { self.data.get().add(size).write(value) };
        self.set_size(size + 1);
    }

    /// Makes room for `needed_capacity` elements in total, exactly like AK::Vector::ensure_capacity.
    pub fn ensure_capacity(&self, needed_capacity: usize) {
        if needed_capacity > self.capacity() {
            self.reallocate(needed_capacity);
        }
    }

    pub fn shrink_to_fit(&self) {
        if self.size() != self.capacity() {
            self.reallocate(self.size());
        }
    }

    /// Removes every element and frees the storage, like AK::Vector::clear.
    pub fn clear(&self) {
        self.size.set(0);
        self.reallocate(0);
    }

    fn reallocate(&self, new_capacity: usize) {
        const { assert!(size_of::<T>() != 0) };
        let size = self.size();
        assert!(new_capacity >= size);
        let old_data = self.data.get();
        let new_data = if new_capacity == 0 {
            core::ptr::null_mut()
        } else {
            let layout = Layout::array::<T>(new_capacity).expect("the buffer fits in memory");
            // SAFETY: The layout has a non-zero size.
            let new_data = unsafe { alloc(layout) }.cast::<T>();
            if new_data.is_null() {
                handle_alloc_error(layout);
            }
            if size != 0 {
                // SAFETY: Both allocations hold at least `size` elements and are distinct.
                unsafe { core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(old_data, new_data, size) };
            }
            new_data
        };
        if !old_data.is_null() {
            let old_layout = Layout::array::<T>(self.capacity()).expect("the buffer was allocated with this layout");
            // SAFETY: The old storage was allocated by this method with this layout.
            unsafe { dealloc(old_data.cast(), old_layout) };
        }
        self.data.set(new_data);
        self.set_capacity(new_capacity);
    }
}

impl InterpreterBuffer<u8> {
    pub fn to_vec(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        (0..self.size()).map(|index| self.get(index)).collect()
    }
}

impl<T: Copy> Default for InterpreterBuffer<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl InterpreterBuffer<Value> {
    /// Visits the values as owned values (see Visitor::visit_owned_values()).
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// As for Visitor::visit_owned_values(): nothing may change or free the buffer until the collection is over.
    pub unsafe fn trace_owned(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The first `size` elements are initialized, and the caller vouches for the memory.
        unsafe { visitor.visit_owned_values(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.data.get(), self.size())) };
    }
}

// SAFETY: Visits every element.
unsafe impl<T: Copy + Trace> Trace for InterpreterBuffer<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The first `size` elements are initialized, and nothing writes them while they are visited.
        let elements = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.data.get(), self.size()) };
        T::trace_slice(elements, visitor);
    }
}

impl<T> ThinSlice<T> {
    const fn layout_for(length: usize) -> Layout {
        const { assert!(size_of::<T>() != 0 && align_of::<T>() <= THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE) };
        // SAFETY: The size fits in memory, since the caller holds that many elements, and the alignment is a power of
        //         two.
        unsafe {
            Layout::from_size_align_unchecked(THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE + length * size_of::<T>(), THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE)
        }
    }

    /// Room for `length` elements, which is not empty, with their length in front of them. The elements are up to the
    /// caller.
    fn allocate(length: usize) -> *mut T {
        let layout = Self::layout_for(length);
        // SAFETY: The layout has a non-zero size. The allocation has room for the length, aligned for it and for the
        //         elements behind it.
        unsafe {
            let allocation = alloc(layout);
            if allocation.is_null() {
                handle_alloc_error(layout);
            }
            allocation.cast::<usize>().write(length);
            allocation.add(THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE).cast::<T>()
        }
    }

    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[T] {
        if self.data.is_null() {
            return &[];
        }
        // SAFETY: A non-null slice has its length in front of its initialized elements, which it owns.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.data, self.data.cast::<usize>().sub(1).read()) }
    }

    pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
        if self.data.is_null() {
            return &mut [];
        }
        // SAFETY: A non-null slice has its length in front of its initialized elements, which it owns.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(self.data, self.data.cast::<usize>().sub(1).read()) }
    }
}

impl<T> From<Vec<T>> for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn from(mut elements: Vec<T>) -> Self {
        let length = elements.len();
        if length == 0 {
            return Self::empty();
        }
        let data = Self::allocate(length);
        // SAFETY: The allocation has room for `length` elements, which move out of the vector.
        unsafe {
            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(elements.as_ptr(), data, length);
            elements.set_len(0);
        }
        Self::from_data(data)
    }
}

impl<T> FromIterator<T> for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(iterator: I) -> Self {
        let mut iterator = iterator.into_iter();
        let (length, upper_bound) = iterator.size_hint();
        if upper_bound != Some(length) {
            return iterator.collect::<Vec<T>>().into();
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Self::empty();
        }
        let data = Self::allocate(length);
        for index in 0..length {
            let element = iterator.next().expect("an iterator yields what its size hint says");
            // SAFETY: The allocation has room for `length` elements.
            unsafe { data.add(index).write(element) };
        }
        Self::from_data(data)
    }
}

impl<T: Clone> Clone for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        self.as_slice().to_vec().into()
    }
}

impl<T> core::ops::Deref for ThinSlice<T> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        self.as_slice()
    }
}

impl<T> core::ops::DerefMut for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
        self.as_mut_slice()
    }
}

impl<'a, T> IntoIterator for &'a ThinSlice<T> {
    type Item = &'a T;
    type IntoIter = core::slice::Iter<'a, T>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.as_slice().iter()
    }
}

impl<T> Drop for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.data.is_null() {
            return;
        }
        let elements = core::ptr::from_mut(self.as_mut_slice());
        let layout = Self::layout_for(elements.len());
        // SAFETY: The elements are initialized and nothing uses them after this. The allocation starts at the length,
        //         and From<Vec<T>> made it with this layout.
        unsafe {
            core::ptr::drop_in_place(elements);
            dealloc(self.data.cast::<u8>().sub(THIN_SLICE_HEADER_SIZE), layout);
        }
    }
}

// SAFETY: Visits every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for ThinSlice<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        T::trace_slice(self.as_slice(), visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Visits every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for BlockSlice<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        T::trace_slice(self.as_slice(), visitor);
    }
}

//! The traits Ladybird's Rust GC lints (Meta/RustLints) find the types of the GC by, so that moving or renaming one
//! does not hide it from them. The lints stop with an error if one of these traits is missing. A GC pointer needs no
//! marker: the lints count every type that implements Trace by hand as one, as Gc, Value and PropertyKey do.

use super::defer_gc::{DeferGc, Deferred};
use super::gc_ref_cell::GcRefCell;
use super::root::{CellRoot, MarkedVec, Root};
use super::sweep::Sweep;
use super::visitor::Trace;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;

/// A type whose values keep everything they hold alive, wherever they are.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Nothing that a value of the type holds may be collected while the value lives.
pub unsafe trait KeepsAlive {}

// SAFETY: The value is registered as a root while the Root lives.
unsafe impl<T: Trace + 'static> KeepsAlive for Root<'_, T> {}
// SAFETY: The values are held by a Root.
unsafe impl<T: Trace + Clone + 'static> KeepsAlive for MarkedVec<'_, T> {}
// SAFETY: The cell is a root of LibGC while the CellRoot lives.
unsafe impl<T> KeepsAlive for CellRoot<T> {}
// SAFETY: The value cannot outlive the deferral it is tied to, while which nothing is collected.
unsafe impl<T> KeepsAlive for Deferred<'_, T> {}
// SAFETY: The VM is the root set: the heap traces it through gather_roots() wherever it is held.
unsafe impl KeepsAlive for Vm {}

/// A guard that keeps the heap from collecting garbage while it lives.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Nothing may be collected while a value of the type lives.
pub unsafe trait DefersCollections {}

// SAFETY: The heap defers collections from new() until drop().
unsafe impl DefersCollections for DeferGc<'_> {}
// SAFETY: The value cannot outlive the deferral it is tied to.
unsafe impl<T> DefersCollections for Deferred<'_, T> {}
// SAFETY: The sweep callback runs inside a collection, which no other collection interrupts.
unsafe impl DefersCollections for Sweep<'_> {}

/// A type whose values hold no cell, whatever the types of their fields can hold.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// No value of the type may hold a pointer to a cell.
pub unsafe trait HoldsNoCells {}

/// Interior mutability for state that the collector traces, which state without GC pointers has no use for.
pub trait TracedState {}

impl<T> TracedState for GcRefCell<T> {}

//! GC::PrimitiveStorage through LibGC's C interface: byte buffers inside the one cage of the process, which the
//! interpreter addresses as offsets from the cage base. Like the heap, it belongs to the thread that runs the VM, so
//! its storage never leaves that thread.

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::num::NonZeroU64;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

use super::capi::{
    self, GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_INVALID_OFFSET, GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE, GCPrimitiveStorageHandle,
    GCPrimitiveStorageLayout,
};

/// GC::PrimitiveStorage::invalid_offset, the offset of storage that does not exist.
pub const INVALID_OFFSET: usize = GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_INVALID_OFFSET;

/// What PrimitiveStorage reports when the cage or the system cannot provide the memory.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OutOfMemory;

/// GC::PrimitiveStorage::ZeroFillNewBytes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ZeroFillNewBytes {
    No,
    Yes,
}

impl ZeroFillNewBytes {
    fn as_bool(self) -> bool {
        self == Self::Yes
    }
}

/// gc_primitive_storage_cage_base(), the address the interpreter adds the cached offsets of typed arrays to. LibGC
/// reserves the cage on the first call, which the VM makes when it is created.
pub fn cage_base() -> usize {
    static CAGE_BASE: OnceLock<usize> = OnceLock::new();
    // NB: The function reserves the cage once and then returns its address.
    *CAGE_BASE.get_or_init(|| capi::gc_primitive_storage_cage_base())
}

fn address_in_cage(offset: usize) -> *mut u8 {
    core::ptr::with_exposed_provenance_mut(cage_base() + offset)
}

/// Storage that the runtime allocated and frees when this is dropped. LibGC only ever changes the offset, the size
/// and the capacity of storage when its owner asks it to, and then reports them, so they are kept here with the
/// address of the first byte, where data blocks read them without calling into LibGC. Like the heap, the storage
/// belongs to the thread that runs the VM.
pub struct OwnedPrimitiveStorage {
    handle: NonZeroU64,
    layout: GCPrimitiveStorageLayout,
    data: *mut u8,
}

const LAYOUT_OF_NO_STORAGE: GCPrimitiveStorageLayout = GCPrimitiveStorageLayout {
    offset: INVALID_OFFSET,
    size: 0,
    capacity: 0,
};

impl OwnedPrimitiveStorage {
    fn from_creation(
        created: bool,
        handle: GCPrimitiveStorageHandle,
        layout: GCPrimitiveStorageLayout,
    ) -> Result<Self, OutOfMemory> {
        if !created {
            assert!(handle == GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE);
            return Err(OutOfMemory);
        }
        let mut storage = Self {
            handle: NonZeroU64::new(handle).expect("created storage has a handle"),
            layout: LAYOUT_OF_NO_STORAGE,
            data: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        };
        storage.set_layout(layout);
        Ok(storage)
    }

    fn set_layout(&mut self, layout: GCPrimitiveStorageLayout) {
        assert!(
            layout.offset != INVALID_OFFSET,
            "LibGC reports the layout of storage it created"
        );
        self.layout = layout;
        self.data = address_in_cage(layout.offset);
    }

    /// PrimitiveStorage::try_allocate(): `size` bytes, which small sizes share pages with other storage for.
    pub fn allocate(size: usize, zero_fill_new_bytes: ZeroFillNewBytes) -> Result<Self, OutOfMemory> {
        let mut handle = GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE;
        let mut layout = LAYOUT_OF_NO_STORAGE;
        // SAFETY: The handle and the layout are valid places for the results.
        let created = unsafe {
            capi::gc_primitive_storage_allocate(size, zero_fill_new_bytes.as_bool(), &raw mut handle, &raw mut layout)
        };
        Self::from_creation(created, handle, layout)
    }

    /// PrimitiveStorage::try_reserve(): `size` bytes in a reservation of `capacity` bytes of its own, which the
    /// storage can grow into without moving.
    pub fn reserve(size: usize, capacity: usize, zero_fill_new_bytes: ZeroFillNewBytes) -> Result<Self, OutOfMemory> {
        let mut handle = GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE;
        let mut layout = LAYOUT_OF_NO_STORAGE;
        // SAFETY: The handle and the layout are valid places for the results.
        let created = unsafe {
            capi::gc_primitive_storage_reserve(
                size,
                capacity,
                zero_fill_new_bytes.as_bool(),
                0,
                &raw mut handle,
                &raw mut layout,
            )
        };
        Self::from_creation(created, handle, layout)
    }

    pub fn handle(&self) -> GCPrimitiveStorageHandle {
        self.handle.get()
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.layout.offset
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.layout.size
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.layout.capacity
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn data(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.data
    }

    /// PrimitiveStorage::try_resize(): changes the size, which moves the bytes to new storage only when it exceeds
    /// the capacity. Fails without changing anything.
    pub fn resize(&mut self, new_size: usize, zero_fill_new_bytes: ZeroFillNewBytes) -> Result<(), OutOfMemory> {
        let mut layout = self.layout;
        // SAFETY: The handle names storage that self owns, and the layout is a valid place for the result.
        let resized = unsafe {
            capi::gc_primitive_storage_resize(
                self.handle.get(),
                new_size,
                zero_fill_new_bytes.as_bool(),
                &raw mut layout,
            )
        };
        if !resized {
            return Err(OutOfMemory);
        }
        self.set_layout(layout);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// PrimitiveStorage::try_reserve(handle, capacity): grows the capacity to at least `new_capacity`, in a
    /// reservation of its own. Fails without changing anything.
    pub fn reserve_capacity(&mut self, new_capacity: usize) -> Result<(), OutOfMemory> {
        let mut layout = self.layout;
        // SAFETY: The handle names storage that self owns, and the layout is a valid place for the result.
        let reserved =
            unsafe { capi::gc_primitive_storage_reserve_capacity(self.handle.get(), new_capacity, &raw mut layout) };
        if !reserved {
            return Err(OutOfMemory);
        }
        self.set_layout(layout);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Takes over storage that an embedder allocated or took from a data block, and now gives up.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `handle` must name live storage that nothing else resizes or frees from now on.
    pub unsafe fn adopt(handle: NonZeroU64) -> Self {
        let storage = ForeignPrimitiveStorage::new(handle.get());
        let mut adopted = Self {
            handle,
            layout: LAYOUT_OF_NO_STORAGE,
            data: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        };
        adopted.set_layout(GCPrimitiveStorageLayout {
            offset: storage.offset(),
            size: storage.size(),
            capacity: storage.capacity(),
        });
        adopted
    }

    /// Gives up the storage without freeing it, for an embedder that takes it over.
    pub fn into_handle(self) -> NonZeroU64 {
        let handle = self.handle;
        core::mem::forget(self);
        handle
    }
}

impl Drop for OwnedPrimitiveStorage {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The handle names storage that self owns and that nothing refers to any more.
        unsafe { capi::gc_primitive_storage_free(self.handle.get()) };
    }
}

/// Storage that an embedder owns and may resize or free at any time, so every query goes to LibGC, which reports a
/// handle that names no storage as having no bytes at the invalid offset.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ForeignPrimitiveStorage {
    handle: GCPrimitiveStorageHandle,
    _owned_by_the_thread_of_the_vm: PhantomData<*mut u8>,
}

impl ForeignPrimitiveStorage {
    pub fn new(handle: GCPrimitiveStorageHandle) -> Self {
        Self {
            handle,
            _owned_by_the_thread_of_the_vm: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn handle(self) -> GCPrimitiveStorageHandle {
        self.handle
    }

    pub fn is_valid(self) -> bool {
        capi::gc_primitive_storage_is_valid(self.handle)
    }

    pub fn offset(self) -> usize {
        capi::gc_primitive_storage_offset(self.handle)
    }

    pub fn size(self) -> usize {
        capi::gc_primitive_storage_size(self.handle)
    }

    pub fn capacity(self) -> usize {
        capi::gc_primitive_storage_capacity(self.handle)
    }

    /// The first byte, or null if the handle names no storage.
    pub fn data(self) -> *mut u8 {
        match self.offset() {
            INVALID_OFFSET => core::ptr::null_mut(),
            offset => address_in_cage(offset),
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Precise roots for values that live outside cells and outside the stack, where the collector would not find them.

use core::cell::{OnceCell, Ref, RefCell};
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::ops::{Deref, DerefMut};
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::capi::{self, GCRoot};
use super::gc_ref_cell::{GcRefCell, GcRefMut};
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;

/// The roots a VM keeps alive. Entries are boxed values registered by address, so slots never move.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct RootSet {
    entries: RefCell<Vec<Option<*const dyn Trace>>>,
    free_slots: RefCell<Vec<usize>>,
}

impl RootSet {
    fn register(&self, value: *const dyn Trace) -> usize {
        let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(slot) = self.free_slots.borrow_mut().pop() {
            entries[slot] = Some(value);
            return slot;
        }
        entries.push(Some(value));
        entries.len() - 1
    }

    fn unregister(&self, slot: usize) {
        self.entries.borrow_mut()[slot] = None;
        self.free_slots.borrow_mut().push(slot);
    }

    pub fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        for value in self.entries.borrow().iter().flatten() {
            // SAFETY: A registered value stays alive until its root unregisters it.
            unsafe { &**value }.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

/// Keeps a value and every cell it reaches alive for as long as it exists.
pub struct Root<'vm, T: Trace + 'static> {
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    value: Box<T>,
    slot: usize,
}

impl<'vm, T: Trace + 'static> Root<'vm, T> {
    pub fn new(vm: &'vm Vm, value: T) -> Self {
        let value = Box::new(value);
        let slot = vm
            .roots()
            .register(core::ptr::from_ref::<T>(&value) as *const dyn Trace);
        Self { vm, value, slot }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> &T {
        &self.value
    }
}

impl<T: Trace + Copy + 'static> Root<'_, T> {
    pub fn value(&self) -> T {
        *self.value
    }
}

impl<T: Trace + 'static> Drop for Root<'_, T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.vm.roots().unregister(self.slot);
    }
}

/// Keeps a cell alive for as long as it exists, through a root of LibGC, without borrowing the VM: for a cell to hold
/// while it must stay alive without being referenced, and to drop once it may be collected.
pub struct CellRoot<T> {
    root: NonNull<GCRoot>,
    // NB: A CellRoot holds its cell through LibGC, not through a pointer of its own.
    _cell: PhantomData<fn() -> Gc<T>>,
}

impl<T> CellRoot<T> {
    pub fn new(cell: Gc<T>) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The cell is live. The root comes with a reference this value owns.
        let root = unsafe { capi::gc_root_create(cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
        Self {
            root: NonNull::new(root).expect("LibGC creates the root"),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn cell(&self) -> Gc<T> {
        // SAFETY: The root holds the live cell it was created with, of type T.
        unsafe {
            let cell = capi::gc_root_cell(self.root.as_ptr());
            Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(cell.cast()).expect("a root holds a cell"))
        }
    }
}

impl<T> Drop for CellRoot<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This value owns the root.
        unsafe { capi::gc_root_destroy(self.root.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// A growable list of values that are kept alive, for the temporaries a Vec would hide from the collector. Elements
/// are copied in and out, or lent by values() and values_mut(), while which the list cannot change. The list registers
/// its root with the first element, so an empty one costs nothing.
pub struct MarkedVec<'vm, T: Trace + Clone + 'static> {
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    values: OnceCell<Root<'vm, GcRefCell<Vec<T>>>>,
}

impl<'vm, T: Trace + Clone + 'static> MarkedVec<'vm, T> {
    pub fn new(vm: &'vm Vm) -> Self {
        Self {
            vm,
            values: OnceCell::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_capacity(vm: &'vm Vm, capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let list = Self::new(vm);
        if capacity > 0 {
            list.rooted_values().borrow_mut(vm).reserve(capacity);
        }
        list
    }

    fn rooted_values(&self) -> &GcRefCell<Vec<T>> {
        self.values
            .get_or_init(|| Root::new(self.vm, GcRefCell::new(Vec::new())))
            .get()
    }

    pub fn push(&self, value: T) {
        self.rooted_values().borrow_mut(self.vm).push(value);
    }

    pub fn extend_from_slice(&self, values: &[T]) {
        self.rooted_values().borrow_mut(self.vm).extend_from_slice(values);
    }

    pub fn insert(&self, index: usize, value: T) {
        self.rooted_values().borrow_mut(self.vm).insert(index, value);
    }

    pub fn clear(&self) {
        if let Some(values) = self.values.get() {
            values.get().borrow_mut(self.vm).clear();
        }
    }

    pub fn pop(&self) -> Option<T> {
        self.values.get()?.get().borrow_mut(self.vm).pop()
    }

    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<T> {
        self.values.get()?.get().borrow().get(index).cloned()
    }

    pub fn resize(&self, length: usize, value: T) {
        self.rooted_values().borrow_mut(self.vm).resize(length, value);
    }

    pub fn set(&self, index: usize, value: T) {
        self.rooted_values().borrow_mut(self.vm)[index] = value;
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.values.get().map_or(0, |values| values.get().borrow().len())
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// Lends the values until the result drops, which may outlive collections. Changing the list meanwhile panics.
    pub fn values(&self) -> MarkedValues<'_, T> {
        MarkedValues(self.values.get().map(|values| values.get().borrow()))
    }

    /// Lends the values to change in place until the result drops, which collections wait for. Using the list meanwhile
    /// panics.
    pub fn values_mut(&self) -> MarkedValuesMut<'_, T> {
        MarkedValuesMut(self.values.get().map(|values| values.get().borrow_mut(self.vm)))
    }

    /// Copies the values out, for handing them to code that does not collect.
    pub fn to_vec(&self) -> Vec<T> {
        self.values
            .get()
            .map_or_else(Vec::new, |values| values.get().borrow().clone())
    }
}

/// The values of a MarkedVec, which stay alive and unchanged while this lends them.
pub struct MarkedValues<'a, T>(Option<Ref<'a, Vec<T>>>);

impl<T> Deref for MarkedValues<'_, T> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        self.0.as_deref().map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice)
    }
}

/// The values of a MarkedVec, which stay alive while this lends them to change in place.
pub struct MarkedValuesMut<'a, T>(Option<GcRefMut<'a, Vec<T>>>);

impl<T> Deref for MarkedValuesMut<'_, T> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        self.0.as_deref().map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice)
    }
}

impl<T> DerefMut for MarkedValuesMut<'_, T> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
        self.0.as_deref_mut().map_or(&mut [], Vec::as_mut_slice)
    }
}

//! The descriptor of a shared memory object, as Core::AnonymousBuffer passes it as an int: a file descriptor, or on
//! Windows a HANDLE that AK's to_fd() narrowed.

use core::ffi::c_int;

#[cfg(unix)]
pub type OwnedSharedMemory = std::os::fd::OwnedFd;
#[cfg(unix)]
pub type BorrowedSharedMemory<'descriptor> = std::os::fd::BorrowedFd<'descriptor>;

#[cfg(windows)]
pub type OwnedSharedMemory = std::os::windows::io::OwnedHandle;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub type BorrowedSharedMemory<'descriptor> = std::os::windows::io::BorrowedHandle<'descriptor>;

/// AsFd, or AsHandle on Windows.
pub trait AsSharedMemory {
    fn as_shared_memory(&self) -> BorrowedSharedMemory<'_>;
}

#[cfg(unix)]
impl<T: std::os::fd::AsFd> AsSharedMemory for T {
    fn as_shared_memory(&self) -> BorrowedSharedMemory<'_> {
        self.as_fd()
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
impl<T: std::os::windows::io::AsHandle> AsSharedMemory for T {
    fn as_shared_memory(&self) -> BorrowedSharedMemory<'_> {
        self.as_handle()
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn handle_from_descriptor(descriptor: c_int) -> std::os::windows::io::RawHandle {
    // AK's to_handle() sign-extends the int.
    descriptor as isize as std::os::windows::io::RawHandle
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn descriptor_from_handle(handle: std::os::windows::io::RawHandle) -> c_int {
    // AK's to_fd() keeps the low 32 bits, which hold every value a kernel handle can have.
    handle as isize as c_int
}

pub fn raw_descriptor(shared_memory: BorrowedSharedMemory<'_>) -> c_int {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        std::os::fd::AsRawFd::as_raw_fd(&shared_memory)
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        descriptor_from_handle(std::os::windows::io::AsRawHandle::as_raw_handle(&shared_memory))
    }
}

pub fn into_raw_descriptor(shared_memory: OwnedSharedMemory) -> c_int {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        std::os::fd::IntoRawFd::into_raw_fd(shared_memory)
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        descriptor_from_handle(std::os::windows::io::IntoRawHandle::into_raw_handle(shared_memory))
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `descriptor` must be open, and owned by nothing else.
pub unsafe fn owned_from_raw_descriptor(descriptor: c_int) -> OwnedSharedMemory {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
        unsafe { std::os::fd::FromRawFd::from_raw_fd(descriptor) }
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
        unsafe { std::os::windows::io::FromRawHandle::from_raw_handle(handle_from_descriptor(descriptor)) }
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `descriptor` must stay open for `'descriptor`.
pub unsafe fn borrowed_from_raw_descriptor<'descriptor>(descriptor: c_int) -> BorrowedSharedMemory<'descriptor> {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
        unsafe { BorrowedSharedMemory::borrow_raw(descriptor) }
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
        unsafe { BorrowedSharedMemory::borrow_raw(handle_from_descriptor(descriptor)) }
    }
}

/*

//! The sweep callback of a collection, which runs once the marks are final and before the cells that died are swept,
//! and has what holds cells without keeping them alive forget the ones that died.

use crate::gc::capi;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, CellState, Gc};
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::finalization_registry::FinalizationRegistry;

/// What code can do while the sweep callback of a collection runs: tell which cells died, which only means anything
/// then, and hand finalization registries over for cleanup. It gives no VM, as nothing may allocate meanwhile.
pub struct Sweep<'vm>(&'vm Vm);

impl<'vm> Sweep<'vm> {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Only the VM's sweep callback makes one, while the marks of its collection are final and the cells that died are
    /// not swept yet.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn new(vm: &'vm Vm) -> Self {
        Self(vm)
    }

    /// Whether `cell`, which something held without keeping it alive, did not survive the collection.
    pub fn is_dead<T>(&self, cell: Gc<T>) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: Every cell starts with its header, and a cell that died is intact until the sweep that follows.
        let header = unsafe { &*cell.as_ptr().cast::<CellHeader>() };
        // SAFETY: The cell is a cell.
        header.state.get() != CellState::Live || !unsafe { capi::gc_cell_is_marked(cell.as_ptr().cast()) }
    }

    /// Whether `cell`, which a cache held without keeping it alive, did not survive the collection, or moves in it. A
    /// cache that keeps the address of a cell without visiting it forgets the cell either way, while what holds cells
    /// weakly by identity pins them as it is traced (see Visitor::pin()).
    pub fn is_dead_or_moving<T>(&self, cell: Gc<T>) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The cell is a cell, intact until the sweep that follows.
        self.is_dead(cell) || unsafe { capi::gc_cell_will_move(cell.as_ptr().cast()) }
    }

    /// Whether the collection may move cells, which is when what holds cells without visiting their slots hands over
    /// the slots of those that survived (see record_slot()).
    pub fn moves_cells(&self) -> bool {
        // NB: The VM lets go of its heap before the collection that destroys the heap, which moves nothing.
        self.0
            .heap_if_held()
            .is_some_and(|heap| capi::gc_heap_is_moving_cells(heap.handle()))
    }

    /// Has the collection rewrite `slot`, which holds a cell that survived it, if the cell moves, as it rewrites the slots
    /// marking visited. For what holds cells without keeping them alive or in place, like the keys of a weak map, once
    /// it forgot the cells that died.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Nothing may free, move or write the slot until the collection is over.
    pub unsafe fn record_slot<T>(&self, slot: &Gc<T>) {
        // SAFETY: The slot holds a pointer to a cell that survived, and the caller vouches for its memory.
        unsafe {
            capi::gc_heap_record_slot(
                self.0.heap().raw(),
                core::ptr::from_ref(slot).cast(),
                capi::GC_RECORDED_SLOT_CELL_POINTER,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Like record_slot(), for a slot that holds a value, which may be a cell that survived the collection.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// As for record_slot().
    pub unsafe fn record_value_slot(&self, slot: &Value) {
        // SAFETY: The slot holds a value, and the caller vouches for its memory.
        unsafe {
            capi::gc_heap_record_slot(
                self.0.heap().raw(),
                core::ptr::from_ref(slot).cast(),
                capi::GC_RECORDED_SLOT_VALUE,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Hands `finalization_registry` to HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob once the collection is over.
    pub fn enqueue_finalization_registry_cleanup_job(&self, finalization_registry: Gc<FinalizationRegistry>) {
        self.0
            .enqueue_finalization_registry_cleanup_job_after_collection(self, finalization_registry);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/gc/visitor.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::capi::{
    GCMarker, GCVisitor, gc_marker_pin_cell, gc_marker_visit_cell, gc_marker_visit_ephemeron_without_pinning,
    gc_marker_visit_interior_pointer, gc_marker_visit_member, gc_marker_visit_owned_values,
    gc_marker_visit_self_pointer, gc_marker_visit_values, gc_visitor_visit_cell, gc_visitor_visit_ephemeron,
    gc_visitor_visit_values,
};
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::member::{Member, NullableMember};
use crate::layout::value::Value;

/// A LibGC visitor, which marks what it visits during a collection and roots it while roots are gathered.
pub struct Visitor(NonNull<GCVisitor>);

/// Where a visitor keeps the marker it marks for, right after the vtable pointer of the C++ Cell::Visitor, which
/// check_layout() checks against GCLayout::visitor_marker_offset.
pub(crate) const VISITOR_MARKER_OFFSET: usize = size_of::<usize>();

impl Visitor {
    /// The marker of a visitor that marks for a collection, which takes the cells it visits directly.
    #[inline(always)]
    fn marker(&self) -> Option<NonNull<GCMarker>> {
        // SAFETY: The visitor is a live Cell::Visitor, which keeps a marker pointer at this offset.
        NonNull::new(unsafe {
            self.0
                .as_ptr()
                .cast::<u8>()
                .add(VISITOR_MARKER_OFFSET)
                .cast::<*mut GCMarker>()
                .read()
        })
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `visitor` must be a visitor LibGC passed in, and outlive the returned value.
    pub unsafe fn from_raw(visitor: *mut GCVisitor) -> Self {
        Self(NonNull::new(visitor).expect("LibGC passes a visitor"))
    }

    /// The LibGC visitor, for visiting what the visitor's methods cannot name, such as an embedder's C++ cells.
    pub fn as_raw(&self) -> *mut GCVisitor {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// Visits a cell by value, which keeps it where it is in a collection that moves cells, since the collector cannot
    /// update the copy of the pointer that the caller keeps. Edges that live in a cell should be visited through their
    /// slot instead, with visit_member(), visit_nullable_member() or visit_values().
    pub fn visit<T>(&mut self, cell: Gc<T>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and a Gc points to a live cell.
            unsafe { gc_marker_visit_cell(marker.as_ptr(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live, and a Gc points to a live cell.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_cell(self.0.as_ptr(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
    }

    /// Visits the cell a member names. It takes the slot, which a collection that moves the cell rewrites if the slot
    /// is in a cell. A slot elsewhere keeps the cell where it is.
    pub fn visit_member<T>(&mut self, slot: &Member<T>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and the slot holds a compressed pointer to a live cell.
            unsafe { gc_marker_visit_member(marker.as_ptr(), core::ptr::from_ref(slot).cast()) };
            return;
        }
        self.visit(slot.get());
    }

    /// Visits the cell a member names, if it is not null, like visit_member().
    pub fn visit_nullable_member<T>(&mut self, slot: &NullableMember<T>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and the slot holds 0 or a compressed pointer to a live cell.
            unsafe { gc_marker_visit_member(marker.as_ptr(), core::ptr::from_ref(slot).cast()) };
            return;
        }
        if let Some(cell) = slot.get() {
            self.visit(cell);
        }
    }

    /// Visits `cell`, which the raw pointer in `slot` points into, past its start, as an object points into the cell
    /// that holds its property storage. A collection that moves the cell rewrites the slot if it is in a cell.
    pub fn visit_interior_pointer<T, U>(&mut self, slot: &Cell<*mut T>, cell: Gc<U>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, the slot holds a pointer, and the cell is live.
            unsafe { gc_marker_visit_interior_pointer(marker.as_ptr(), slot.as_ptr().cast(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
            return;
        }
        self.visit(cell);
    }

    /// Notes that the raw pointer in `slot` points into the cell that holds the slot, up to one past its end, as an
    /// object points to its inline property storage. A collection that moves the cell points the slot into the copy.
    pub fn visit_self_pointer<T>(&mut self, slot: &Cell<*mut T>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and the slot is in the cell being visited.
            unsafe { gc_marker_visit_self_pointer(marker.as_ptr(), slot.as_ptr().cast()) };
        }
    }

    /// Keeps `cell` where it is in a collection that moves cells, without keeping it alive, for a weak reference that
    /// the collector cannot update.
    pub fn pin<T: ?Sized>(&mut self, cell: Gc<T>) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and the cell is live.
            unsafe { gc_marker_pin_cell(marker.as_ptr(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
        }
    }

    pub fn visit_values(&mut self, values: &[Value]) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            if !values.is_empty() {
                // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and Value is a NaN-boxed u64.
                unsafe { gc_marker_visit_values(marker.as_ptr(), values.as_ptr().cast(), values.len()) };
            }
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live, and Value is a NaN-boxed u64.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_values(self.0.as_ptr(), values.as_ptr().cast(), values.len()) };
    }

    /// Visits values in memory that the cell being visited owns outside the heap, such as malloc storage, which a
    /// collection that moves cells rewrites where they are rather than keeping their cells where they are.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Nothing may free, move or write the values until the collection is over: no finalizer, destructor or sweep
    /// callback may touch them.
    pub unsafe fn visit_owned_values(&mut self, values: &[Value]) {
        if let Some(marker) = self.marker() {
            if !values.is_empty() {
                // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, Value is a NaN-boxed u64, and the caller vouches for the memory.
                unsafe { gc_marker_visit_owned_values(marker.as_ptr(), values.as_ptr().cast(), values.len()) };
            }
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live, and Value is a NaN-boxed u64.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_values(self.0.as_ptr(), values.as_ptr().cast(), values.len()) };
    }

    /// Visits a value that is reachable only while `key` is. A collection that moves cells keeps both where they are.
    pub fn visit_ephemeron<T>(&mut self, key: Gc<T>, value: &Value) {
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live, a Gc points to a live cell, and Value is a NaN-boxed u64.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_ephemeron(self.0.as_ptr(), key.as_ptr().cast(), core::ptr::from_ref(value).cast()) };
    }

    /// Visits `value`, a cell that is reachable only while `key` is, by value: it stays where it is in a collection
    /// that moves cells, even if it dies. Visitors that do not mark see the value as reachable.
    pub fn visit_ephemeron_cell<K, V>(&mut self, key: Gc<K>, value: Gc<V>) {
        let Some(marker) = self.marker() else {
            self.visit(value);
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and both are live cells. The value is pinned, so no slot needs to be
        //         handed to the collection. The key is only looked at, and moves of it change nothing the caller
        //         holds.
        unsafe {
            gc_marker_pin_cell(marker.as_ptr(), value.as_ptr().cast());
            gc_marker_visit_ephemeron_without_pinning(marker.as_ptr(), key.as_ptr().cast(), value.as_ptr().cast());
        }
    }

    /// Visits a value that is reachable only while `key` is, such as a WeakMap entry's, without keeping either from
    /// moving.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// If the entry survives a collection that moves cells, its holder must hand the slots of the key and the value to
    /// Sweep::record_slot() and Sweep::record_value_slot().
    pub unsafe fn visit_ephemeron_without_pinning<T>(&mut self, key: Gc<T>, value: &Value) {
        let Some(marker) = self.marker() else {
            self.visit_ephemeron(key, value);
            return;
        };
        if value.is_cell() {
            // SAFETY: The marker is the visitor's, and both are live cells.
            unsafe {
                gc_marker_visit_ephemeron_without_pinning(
                    marker.as_ptr(),
                    key.as_ptr().cast(),
                    value.as_cell().as_ptr().cast(),
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A value that can reach cells, which it reports to the visitor.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `trace` must visit every cell the value can reach directly; a cell it misses can be collected while still in use.
pub unsafe trait Trace {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor);

    /// Traces a slice of values, which some types can report in a single call.
    fn trace_slice(values: &[Self], visitor: &mut Visitor)
    where
        Self: Sized,
    {
        for value in values {
            value.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

/// Implements Trace for types that cannot reach any cell.
macro_rules! impl_trace_for_cell_free_types {
    ($($type:ty),* $(,)?) => {
        $(
            // SAFETY: The type holds no cells.
            unsafe impl Trace for $type {
                fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}

                fn trace_slice(_: &[Self], _: &mut Visitor) {}
            }
        )*
    };
}

impl_trace_for_cell_free_types!(
    (),
    bool,
    char,
    u8,
    u16,
    u32,
    u64,
    usize,
    i8,
    i16,
    i32,
    i64,
    isize,
    f32,
    f64,
    &'static str,
    String,
    ak::Utf16String,
    ak::Utf16FlyString,
    num_bigint::BigInt,
    crate::layout::cell::CellHeader,
);

// SAFETY: Holds nothing.
unsafe impl<T: ?Sized> Trace for core::marker::PhantomData<T> {
    fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to the boxed value.
unsafe impl<T: Trace + ?Sized> Trace for Box<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        (**self).trace(visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for [T] {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        T::trace_slice(self, visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace, const N: usize> Trace for [T; N] {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        T::trace_slice(self, visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for Vec<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        T::trace_slice(self, visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to every element.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for std::collections::VecDeque<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        let (front, back) = self.as_slices();
        T::trace_slice(front, visitor);
        T::trace_slice(back, visitor);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to every key and value. The default RandomState hasher holds no cells.
unsafe impl<K: Trace, V: Trace> Trace for std::collections::HashMap<K, V> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        for (key, value) in self {
            key.trace(visitor);
            value.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to the value once it exists.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for core::cell::OnceCell<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(value) = self.get() {
            value.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

macro_rules! impl_trace_for_tuples {
    ($(($($name:ident),+)),* $(,)?) => {
        $(
            // SAFETY: Forwards to every element.
            #[allow(non_snake_case)]
            unsafe impl<$($name: Trace),+> Trace for ($($name,)+) {
                fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
                    let ($($name,)+) = self;
                    $($name.trace(visitor);)+
                }
            }
        )*
    };
}

impl_trace_for_tuples!(
    (A, B),
    (A, B, C),
    (A, B, C, D),
    (A, B, C, D, E),
    (A, B, C, D, E, F),
    (A, B, C, D, E, F, G),
    (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H),
);

// SAFETY: A Gc reaches exactly its cell.
unsafe impl<T> Trace for Gc<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        visitor.visit(*self);
    }
}

// SAFETY: A member reaches exactly its cell.
unsafe impl<T> Trace for Member<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        visitor.visit_member(self);
    }
}

// SAFETY: A nullable member reaches exactly its cell, if it has one.
unsafe impl<T> Trace for NullableMember<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        visitor.visit_nullable_member(self);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to the contained value.
unsafe impl<T: Trace> Trace for Option<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(value) = self {
            value.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to the contained value or error.
unsafe impl<T: Trace, E: Trace> Trace for Result<T, E> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        match self {
            Ok(value) => value.trace(visitor),
            Err(error) => error.trace(visitor),
        }
    }
}

// SAFETY: LibGC decodes the value and visits its cell, if it has one.
unsafe impl Trace for Value {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        visitor.visit_values(core::slice::from_ref(self));
    }

    fn trace_slice(values: &[Self], visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        visitor.visit_values(values);
    }
}

// SAFETY: Forwards to the current value, in place, so that a collection that moves cells can update a slot in it.
unsafe impl<T: Copy + Trace> Trace for Cell<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // SAFETY: Nothing writes the value while it is traced, since the mutator waits for tracing to end.
        unsafe { &*self.as_ptr() }.trace(visitor);
    }
}

//! GC::WeakContainer: a cell that holds other cells without keeping them alive, and forgets them once they die. The
//! VM keeps a list of them, which its sweep callback prunes the way LibGC prunes its weak containers.

use super::sweep::Sweep;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::object::Object;

/// WeakContainer::remove_dead_cells(), called during every collection on each container that survived it, while the
/// cells that died are intact and before they are swept.
pub type RemoveDeadCells = fn(&Object, &Sweep<'_>);

pub struct WeakContainer {
    owner: Gc<Object>,
    remove_dead_cells: RemoveDeadCells,
}

impl WeakContainer {
    pub fn new(owner: Gc<Object>, remove_dead_cells: RemoveDeadCells) -> Self {
        Self {
            owner,
            remove_dead_cells,
        }
    }

    pub fn owner(&self) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.owner
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_dead_cells(&self, sweep: &Sweep<'_>) {
        (self.remove_dead_cells)(&self.owner, sweep);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/gc/weak.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::mem::ManuallyDrop;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::capi::{self, GCWeakImpl};
use super::heap::Heap;
use super::lint_markers::HoldsNoCells;
use super::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;

/// Mirrors the part of GC::WeakImpl the runtime reads: the pointer at this offset, which LibGC clears once the cell is
/// collected. The startup layout check compares the offset with the one gc_get_layout() reports.
pub(super) const WEAK_IMPL_POINTER_OFFSET: usize = 16;

/// A type whose GC pointers do not keep their cells alive: wherever a value of it is, the pointers to cells that a
/// collection frees are cleared before anything reads them. Ladybird's Rust GC lints accept such values in a Box or a
/// Vec.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Every value of the type must have its pointers to dead cells cleared after each collection.
pub unsafe trait SweptAfterCollection {}

/// A reference to a cell that does not keep it alive.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct GcWeak<T> {
    weak_impl: NonNull<GCWeakImpl>,
    // NB: A GcWeak gives a Gc<T> out, but holds none.
    _cell: PhantomData<fn() -> Gc<T>>,
}

impl<T> GcWeak<T> {
    pub fn new(heap: &Heap, cell: Gc<T>) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The heap and the cell are live. The impl comes with a reference this value owns.
        let weak_impl = unsafe { capi::gc_heap_create_weak_impl(heap.raw(), cell.as_ptr().cast()) };
        Self {
            weak_impl: NonNull::new(weak_impl).expect("LibGC creates the weak impl"),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn null() -> Self {
        // NB: Returns the shared null impl with a reference this value owns.
        let weak_impl = capi::gc_weak_impl_null();
        Self {
            weak_impl: NonNull::new(weak_impl).expect("LibGC has a null weak impl"),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    /// Gives up the reference for a pointer that from_raw() can take back, which is at least 2-aligned.
    pub fn into_raw(self) -> *mut () {
        ManuallyDrop::new(self).weak_impl.as_ptr().cast()
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The pointer must have come from into_raw() on a weak reference of the same type, and that reference must not be
    /// taken back any other time.
    pub unsafe fn from_raw(raw: *mut ()) -> Self {
        Self {
            // SAFETY: into_raw() gives out the non-null pointer of the impl.
            weak_impl: unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(raw.cast()) },
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&self) -> Option<Gc<T>> {
        // SAFETY: The impl stays allocated while this value holds a reference to it.
        let pointer = unsafe {
            self.weak_impl
                .as_ptr()
                .cast::<u8>()
                .add(WEAK_IMPL_POINTER_OFFSET)
                .cast::<*mut T>()
                .read()
        };
        // SAFETY: A non-null pointer is a cell that has not been collected.
        NonNull::new(pointer).map(|pointer| unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(pointer) })
    }
}

impl<T> Clone for GcWeak<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The impl is live; the clone owns the new reference.
        unsafe { capi::gc_weak_impl_ref(self.weak_impl.as_ptr()) };
        Self {
            weak_impl: self.weak_impl,
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<T> Drop for GcWeak<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This value owns one reference.
        unsafe { capi::gc_weak_impl_unref(self.weak_impl.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

// SAFETY: A weak reference keeps nothing alive.
unsafe impl<T> Trace for GcWeak<T> {
    fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}
}

// SAFETY: A weak reference holds LibGC's weak impl of its cell, not the cell.
unsafe impl<T> HoldsNoCells for GcWeak<T> {}

/*

//! AK::HashTable, for the places where the runtime walks one where the spec walks a List: the order it visits its
//! values in is the order of its buckets, which is observable, so this keeps the buckets of AK::HashTable.

use ak::Utf16FlyString;

use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

/// AK::string_hash over a sequence of characters.
fn string_hash(characters: impl Iterator<Item = u32>) -> u32 {
    let mut hash: u32 = 0;
    for character in characters {
        hash = hash.wrapping_add(character);
        hash = hash.wrapping_add(hash << 10);
        hash ^= hash >> 6;
    }
    hash = hash.wrapping_add(hash << 3);
    hash ^= hash >> 11;
    hash = hash.wrapping_add(hash << 15);
    hash
}

/// AK::string_hash over the code units of a string, which is what Utf16FlyString::hash() computes for ASCII and
/// UTF-16 storage alike.
pub fn utf16_fly_string_hash(string: &Utf16FlyString) -> u32 {
    string_hash(Utf16View::of_fly_string(string).code_units().map(u32::from))
}

/// AK::Traits<T>::hash() of the values a HashTable holds.
pub trait HashTableTraits: Eq {
    fn hash(&self) -> u32;
}

impl HashTableTraits for Utf16FlyString {
    fn hash(&self) -> u32 {
        utf16_fly_string_hash(self)
    }
}

/// The bytes of a ByteString, which AK hashes with string_hash.
impl HashTableTraits for Vec<u8> {
    fn hash(&self) -> u32 {
        string_hash(self.iter().map(|&byte| u32::from(byte)))
    }
}

struct Bucket<T> {
    value: T,
    hash: u32,
    probe_length: usize,
}

/// Open addressing with linear probing and Robin Hood displacement in a power-of-two table that doubles once it is
/// 70% full, like AK::HashTable.
pub struct HashTable<T> {
    buckets: Vec<Option<Bucket<T>>>,
    size: usize,
}

impl<T> Default for HashTable<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            buckets: Vec::new(),
            size: 0,
        }
    }
}

pub type Utf16FlyStringHashTable = HashTable<Utf16FlyString>;

impl<T: HashTableTraits> HashTable<T> {
    const GROW_CAPACITY_AT_LEAST: usize = 8;
    const GROW_AT_LOAD_FACTOR_PERCENT: usize = 70;

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.size == 0
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.buckets.len()
    }

    fn mask(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity() - 1
    }

    fn should_grow(&self) -> bool {
        (self.size + 1) * 100 >= self.capacity() * Self::GROW_AT_LOAD_FACTOR_PERCENT
    }

    /// HashTable::set, which replaces an equal value that is already in the table.
    pub fn set(&mut self, value: T) {
        if self.should_grow() {
            self.rehash((self.capacity() * 2).max(Self::GROW_CAPACITY_AT_LEAST));
        }
        self.write_value(value);
    }

    pub fn contains(&self, value: &T) -> bool {
        if self.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        let hash = value.hash();
        let mut bucket_index = hash as usize & self.mask();
        loop {
            let Some(bucket) = &self.buckets[bucket_index] else {
                return false;
            };
            if bucket.hash == hash && bucket.value == *value {
                return true;
            }
            bucket_index = (bucket_index + 1) & self.mask();
        }
    }

    /// The values in the order iterating an AK::HashTable visits them: by bucket.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
        self.buckets.iter().flatten().map(|bucket| &bucket.value)
    }

    fn rehash(&mut self, new_capacity: usize) {
        let new_capacity = new_capacity.max(self.capacity() + 1).next_power_of_two();
        let old_buckets = core::mem::replace(&mut self.buckets, (0..new_capacity).map(|_| None).collect());
        self.size = 0;
        for bucket in old_buckets.into_iter().flatten() {
            self.write_value(bucket.value);
        }
    }

    fn write_value(&mut self, value: T) {
        let hash = value.hash();
        let mask = self.mask();
        let mut bucket_index = hash as usize & mask;
        let mut probe_length = 0;
        loop {
            let Some(bucket) = &mut self.buckets[bucket_index] else {
                self.buckets[bucket_index] = Some(Bucket {
                    value,
                    hash,
                    probe_length,
                });
                self.size += 1;
                return;
            };

            if bucket.hash == hash && bucket.value == value {
                bucket.value = value;
                return;
            }

            // Robin hood: if our probe length is larger (poor) than this bucket's (rich), steal its position!
            if probe_length > bucket.probe_length {
                let mut bucket_to_move = core::mem::replace(
                    bucket,
                    Bucket {
                        value,
                        hash,
                        probe_length,
                    },
                );
                probe_length = bucket_to_move.probe_length;

                // Find a free bucket, swapping with smaller probe length buckets along the way
                loop {
                    bucket_index = (bucket_index + 1) & mask;
                    probe_length += 1;

                    let Some(bucket) = &mut self.buckets[bucket_index] else {
                        bucket_to_move.probe_length = probe_length;
                        self.buckets[bucket_index] = Some(bucket_to_move);
                        break;
                    };

                    if probe_length > bucket.probe_length {
                        bucket_to_move.probe_length = probe_length;
                        core::mem::swap(&mut bucket_to_move, bucket);
                        probe_length = bucket_to_move.probe_length;
                    }
                }

                self.size += 1;
                return;
            }

            bucket_index = (bucket_index + 1) & mask;
            probe_length += 1;
        }
    }
}

/*

//! The dispatch tables of the interpreter flapc generates from interpreter.flap, which the interpreter runs each
//! executable's frames with.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, Ordering, fence};

use crate::bytecode::instruction::NUM_OPCODES;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;

/// How many entries a dispatch table has: one per possible opcode byte.
pub const DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE: usize = 256;

pub type DispatchTable = [*const c_void; DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE];

// NB: The tables are immutable data in the assembled interpreter.
unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The handlers of the interpreter, indexed by opcode.
    safe static js_interpreter_dispatch_table: DispatchTable;
    /// Every entry checks for breakpoints before running the instruction's handler.
    safe static js_interpreter_debug_dispatch_table: DispatchTable;
}

fn table_address(table: &'static DispatchTable) -> *const c_void {
    table.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// The handlers of the interpreter, indexed by opcode.
pub fn plain_handlers() -> &'static DispatchTable {
    &js_interpreter_dispatch_table
}

/// The handlers of the interpreter.
pub fn plain_dispatch_table() -> *const c_void {
    table_address(plain_handlers())
}

/// The handlers that check for breakpoints, which every executable runs with while the VM is debugging.
pub fn debug_dispatch_table() -> *const c_void {
    table_address(&js_interpreter_debug_dispatch_table)
}

/// The most tables a VM runs executables with: one for each interpreter tier (see `InterpreterTier`).
const MAX_TIER_COUNT: usize = 4;

/// The dispatch tables a VM's interpreter runs with. They start as copies of the tables above, which are immutable and
/// shared by all VMs, so that another thread can stop this VM's interpreter wherever it is. The table a running
/// interpreter dispatches through lives in a register, out of reach of other threads, but what that table holds is
/// not. That makes the interrupt free for the interpreter (see `Vm::request_interrupt()`): a check at every back edge
/// costs tight loops several percent.
pub struct VmDispatchTables {
    tables: Box<[[AtomicPtr<c_void>; DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE]; MAX_TIER_COUNT]>,
}

impl VmDispatchTables {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            tables: Box::new(core::array::from_fn(|_| {
                core::array::from_fn(|_| AtomicPtr::new(core::ptr::null_mut()))
            })),
        }
    }

    /// Makes the table at `index` a copy of `source`, and returns it.
    fn copy(&self, index: usize, source: *const c_void) -> *const c_void {
        let table = &self.tables[index];
        // SAFETY: Dispatch tables have DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE entries, and this only reads the immutable ones.
        let source = unsafe { &*source.cast::<DispatchTable>() };
        for (entry, handler) in table.iter().zip(source) {
            entry.store(handler.cast_mut(), Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        table.as_ptr().cast()
    }

    /// Makes the interpreter call the fallback handler at its next dispatch in every table, which any thread may do.
    pub fn stop_dispatching(&self) {
        const { assert!((NUM_OPCODES as usize) < DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE) };
        let fallback_handler = plain_handlers()[DISPATCH_TABLE_SIZE - 1].cast_mut();
        for entry in self.tables.iter().flatten() {
            entry.store(fallback_handler, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }
}

impl Default for VmDispatchTables {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl Vm {
    /// Fills in the VM's dispatch tables: copies of the debug table while the VM is debugging, and otherwise of the
    /// table of each interpreter tier at its index, with the plain table at every other index.
    pub(crate) fn update_dispatch_tables(&self) {
        let source_of = |table| {
            if self.debugging_enabled() {
                debug_dispatch_table()
            } else {
                table
            }
        };
        let plain_table = self.own_dispatch_tables.copy(0, source_of(plain_dispatch_table()));
        for table in &self.head.dispatch_tables {
            table.set(plain_table);
        }
        for (tier, table) in self.jit.dispatch_tables() {
            let table = self.own_dispatch_tables.copy(tier as usize, source_of(table));
            self.head.dispatch_tables[tier as usize].set(table);
        }

        // NB: An interrupt that came in while this ran must not get lost.
        fence(Ordering::SeqCst);
        if self.interrupt_requested() {
            self.own_dispatch_tables.stop_dispatching();
        }
    }
}

/*
