//! The dispatch tables of the interpreter tiers executables move through while the JIT is on (see `InterpreterTier`),
//! made from the handlers of the profiling build of the interpreter, which only builds with the JIT have.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use super::{InterpreterTier, JitState};
use crate::bytecode::instruction::{NUM_OPCODES, instruction_name_from_opcode};
use crate::interpreter::dispatch_tables::{DispatchTable, plain_dispatch_table, plain_handlers};

// NB: The table is immutable data in the assembled interpreter.
unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The handlers of the profiling build of the interpreter, which collect feedback for the optimizing JIT.
    safe static js_interpreter_dispatch_table_profiling: DispatchTable;
}

/// The handlers of the profiling build of the interpreter.
fn profiling_dispatch_table() -> *const c_void {
    js_interpreter_dispatch_table_profiling.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// The plain handlers, with the profiling build's handlers for the instructions that count the tier-up budget
/// (function entry and loop back edges), enter JIT code (calls), or return to a caller that may run with other
/// handlers (see `InterpreterTier::WarmingUp`).
pub fn warming_up_dispatch_table() -> Box<DispatchTable> {
    mixed_dispatch_table(|name| {
        matches!(
            name,
            "Enter" | "EnterCoercingThis" | "EnterWithOwnEnvironments" | "Call" | "Return" | "End"
        ) || name.contains("Loop")
    })
}

/// The plain handlers, with the profiling build's handlers for the instructions that enter JIT code (calls) or return
/// to a caller that may run with other handlers (see `InterpreterTier::Unprofiled`). Nothing counts the tier-up
/// budget of executables the JIT never compiles.
pub fn unprofiled_dispatch_table() -> Box<DispatchTable> {
    mixed_dispatch_table(|name| matches!(name, "Call" | "Return" | "End"))
}

/// The plain handlers, with the profiling build's handlers for the instructions whose names `use_profiling` selects.
fn mixed_dispatch_table(use_profiling: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Box<DispatchTable> {
    let profiling = &js_interpreter_dispatch_table_profiling;
    let mut table = Box::new(*plain_handlers());
    for opcode in 0..NUM_OPCODES as usize {
        if use_profiling(instruction_name_from_opcode(opcode as u8)) {
            table[opcode] = profiling[opcode];
        }
    }
    table
}

impl JitState {
    /// The dispatch table the interpreter runs the frames of executables in each tier with, with the plain handlers for
    /// the tiers whose tables are not built.
    ///
    /// NB: Executables only move to the warming up and unprofiled tiers while the JIT collects feedback, which builds
    ///     their tables.
    pub fn dispatch_tables(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (InterpreterTier, *const c_void)> {
        let mixed_table = |table: &Option<Box<DispatchTable>>| {
            table
                .as_deref()
                .map_or(plain_dispatch_table(), |table| table.as_ptr().cast())
        };
        InterpreterTier::ALL.into_iter().map(move |tier| {
            let table = match tier {
                InterpreterTier::Plain => plain_dispatch_table(),
                InterpreterTier::WarmingUp => mixed_table(&self.warming_up_dispatch_table),
                InterpreterTier::Unprofiled => mixed_table(&self.unprofiled_dispatch_table),
                InterpreterTier::Profiling => profiling_dispatch_table(),
            };
            (tier, table)
        })
    }
}

/*

//! Entering JIT code, and the calls JIT code makes into the runtime to leave it for the interpreter, which the
//! translator (see `translate`) serves.

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_abi::register;
use libjs_jit::code::SiteKind;
use libjs_runtime_macros::jit_abi;

use super::code::{
    CompileState, EXIT_COUNT_BEFORE_DISCARD, EXIT_COUNT_BEFORE_DISCARD_FROM_LOOP, EntryStatus, JitEntry, JitResult,
};
use super::translate::{self, RegisterDump};
use super::{executable_of, frame_of, frames_above};
use crate::bytecode::executable::Executable;
use crate::bytecode::feedback::tier_up_costs;
use crate::bytecode::{instruction_at, op};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::execution_context::ExecutionContext;
use crate::layout::value::Value;

/// Whether the interpreter should run a new frame of this executable in its JIT code instead of interpreting it.
///
/// NB: Debuggers step through bytecode, so frames run in the interpreter while one is attached.
pub fn can_enter_jit_code(vm: &Vm, executable: &Executable) -> bool {
    executable.jit_compile_state() == CompileState::Installed && !vm.debugging_enabled()
}

/// The JIT entry table's entry of executables without JIT code, which JIT code that calls their functions directly
/// enters like their JIT code with the callee's frame. Compiled code would publish the frame before anything else sees
/// it (see `Op::PublishFrame`); this makes it the running frame and has the caller's runtime run it in the
/// interpreter (see `libjs_jit_finish_direct_call()`).
///
/// # Safety
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM and the frame it built for the callee.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_not_compiled_call_entry(vm: *const Vm, frame: *mut ExecutionContext) -> JitResult {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes its live VM.
    let vm = unsafe { &*vm };
    vm.set_running_frame_in_current_realm(frame);
    JitResult {
        value: 0,
        status: EntryStatus::Resume,
    }
}

/// Calls the entry of JIT code for the frame the way native code does, marking the frame as run by JIT code while
/// the code runs.
fn enter_from_native_code(vm: &Vm, frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>, entry: JitEntry) -> JitResult {
    let frame_ref = frame_of(frame);
    // NB: The frame runs in the interpreter once the code returns other than with EntryStatus::Returned, and is
    //     popped otherwise.
    frame_ref.runs_jit_code.set(true);
    let trampoline = vm.jit.entry_trampoline();
    // SAFETY: The entry is for the frame's executable, whose frame is fully built and running.
    let result = unsafe { trampoline(core::ptr::from_ref(vm), frame.as_ptr(), entry) };
    frame_ref.runs_jit_code.set(false);
    result
}

/// Runs the JIT code of the frame's executable. The frame is the running execution context, fully built, at pc 0
/// with Enter not run yet.
pub fn enter_jit_code(vm: &Vm, frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>) -> JitResult {
    assert_eq!(vm.running_execution_context(), Some(frame));
    let frame_ref = frame_of(frame);
    assert_eq!(frame_ref.program_counter.get(), 0);
    let executable = executable_of(frame_ref);
    // NB: The executable keeps its code attached while JIT code may run frames of it, even if it is discarded
    //     meanwhile (see Executable::detach_discarded_jit_code_if_unused()).
    let entry = executable.jit_code(vm).expect("the executable has JIT code").entry();
    enter_from_native_code(vm, frame, entry)
}

/// Continues the running frame, which the interpreter is running at the loop back edge `pc`, in its executable's JIT
/// code if that has an on-stack replacement entry there. Returns how the code returned, if it ran.
pub fn enter_jit_code_at_loop(vm: &Vm, frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>, pc: u32) -> Option<JitResult> {
    assert_eq!(vm.running_execution_context(), Some(frame));
    let frame_ref = frame_of(frame);
    let executable = executable_of(frame_ref);
    if !can_enter_jit_code(vm, &executable) || !frame_ref.frame_initialized.get() {
        return None;
    }
    let code = executable.jit_code(vm).expect("the executable has JIT code");
    let Some(entry) = code.osr_entry(pc) else {
        // NB: A fixed budget can keep expiring at the same back edge in nested loops, missing the code's OSR entry
        //     forever. Try the next back edge when the code has an entry at a loop this one is in. Frames in other
        //     loops would check at every back edge without ever reaching an entry.
        // NB: Top-level code runs once, so no later frame would enter its code at the start.
        let runs_once = frame_ref.function.get().is_none();
        if code.reaches_osr_entry_from(pc) {
            executable.head.tier_up_budget.set(tier_up_costs::LOOP_ITERATION);
        } else if !code.may_reach_osr_entry_from(pc)
            && (runs_once
                || code.exit_count() >= EXIT_COUNT_BEFORE_DISCARD_FROM_LOOP
                || code.count_fruitless_loop_check(frame_ref))
        {
            // NB: The frame may have exited into this loop, and no later iteration of a loop it is in reaches an entry.
            //     Once the code is detached, a later check here compiles the executable again, with what the exits
            //     taught it and an entry at this loop.
            vm.jit.count_coverage("discard-from-loop");
            // NB: Top-level code that moved on to a later loop recompiles with an entry there, which is progress, so
            //     scripts with many long loops are not refused after MAX_FRUITLESS_DISCARD_COUNT of them.
            //     A function's frame that ran out of fruitless loop checks does not count as progress: every call may
            //     exit into the same loop again.
            if runs_once {
                executable.note_learned_jit_exit_site();
            }
            executable.discard_jit_code(vm);
        }
        return None;
    };
    vm.jit.count_coverage("osr-entry");
    frame_ref.program_counter.set(pc);
    Some(enter_from_native_code(vm, frame, entry))
}

/// Resumes the running frame, a generator's frame suspended at the continuation `pc`, in its executable's JIT code if
/// that has a resume entry there. Returns how the code returned, if it ran.
pub fn enter_jit_code_at_continuation(vm: &Vm, frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>, pc: u32) -> Option<JitResult> {
    enter_jit_code_with_frame_in_memory(vm, frame, pc, "resume-entry")
}

/// Continues the running frame at `pc`, where its memory holds every value live, in its executable's JIT code if that
/// has an entry there. Returns how the code returned, if it ran.
fn enter_jit_code_with_frame_in_memory(
    vm: &Vm,
    frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>,
    pc: u32,
    coverage_key: &str,
) -> Option<JitResult> {
    assert_eq!(vm.running_execution_context(), Some(frame));
    let frame_ref = frame_of(frame);
    let executable = executable_of(frame_ref);
    if !can_enter_jit_code(vm, &executable) || !frame_ref.frame_initialized.get() {
        return None;
    }
    let entry = executable
        .jit_code(vm)
        .expect("the executable has JIT code")
        .osr_entry(pc)?;
    vm.jit.count_coverage(coverage_key);
    frame_ref.program_counter.set(pc);
    Some(enter_from_native_code(vm, frame, entry))
}

/// `asm_helper_enter_jit_code_after_catch`: the interpreter calls this when it ran the `Catch` at `pc` in the running
/// frame, whose executable has JIT code. Continues the frame in the code's catch entry after the Catch, if it has one
/// (see `libjs_jit::builder::osr`). Returns the interpreter's control word: 0 to continue interpreting after the
/// Catch, and otherwise what `control_after_entry()` returns.
pub fn helper_enter_jit_code_after_catch(vm: &Vm, pc: u32) -> i64 {
    let frame = vm.running_execution_context().expect("a frame is running");
    let executable = executable_of(frame_of(frame));
    let next_pc = pc + instruction_at::<op::Catch>(&executable, pc).length();
    if let Some(result) = enter_jit_code_with_frame_in_memory(vm, frame, next_pc, "catch-entry") {
        return control_after_entry(vm, result);
    }
    // NB: Code compiled before the handler first caught an exception has no entry after its Catch. Catches there count
    //     like exits, so that the executable is compiled again with the entry once they keep happening. Handlers
    //     without an entry for other reasons would get none from a compile either.
    if !can_enter_jit_code(vm, &executable) {
        return 0;
    }
    let code = executable.jit_code(vm).expect("the executable has JIT code");
    if code.compiled_before_handler_caught(pc) && code.count_exit() >= EXIT_COUNT_BEFORE_DISCARD {
        vm.jit.count_coverage("discard-from-catch");
        executable.discard_jit_code(vm);
    }
    0
}

/// The interpreter's control word after JIT code it entered in the running frame returned: 1 to continue interpreting
/// the running execution context, negative to leave the interpreter.
pub fn control_after_entry(vm: &Vm, result: JitResult) -> i64 {
    match result.status {
        EntryStatus::Returned => {
            // NB: Like the interpreter's Return, a frame without a caller, or whose caller waits in native code,
            //     returns from the interpreter.
            let frame = vm.running_execution_context_ref();
            let exits_interpreter = frame.caller_frame.get().is_null() || frame.returns_to_native_caller.get();
            vm.return_from_running_frame(Value::from_bits(result.value));
            if exits_interpreter { -1 } else { 1 }
        }
        EntryStatus::Resume => 1,
        EntryStatus::ExitInterpreter => -1,
    }
}

/// Runs the frame that just became the running execution context in its executable's JIT code, if it can, for the
/// interpreter's Call, which found that the executable has JIT code. Returns the control word of the interpreter's
/// `asm_helper_enter_jit_code`: negative if the interpreter leaves, 1 if the code returned (the frame is still the
/// running execution context, with the value it returned in its return value register, for the interpreter to return
/// it to the caller), and otherwise 0, to continue interpreting the running execution context.
pub fn helper_enter_jit_code(vm: &Vm) -> i64 {
    if vm.debugging_enabled() {
        return 0;
    }
    let frame = vm.running_execution_context().expect("a frame is running");
    // NB: The interpreter's Call enters the code before the callee's Enter could bind its this value.
    crate::interpreter::execution_context::coerce_this(vm, frame_of(frame));
    let result = enter_jit_code(vm, frame);
    match result.status {
        EntryStatus::Returned => {
            frame_of(frame)
                .register(register::RETURN_VALUE)
                .set(Value::from_bits(result.value));
            1
        }
        EntryStatus::Resume => 0,
        EntryStatus::ExitInterpreter => -1,
    }
}

/// Called by exit and leave stubs, and by slow paths in inlined callees, with the index of their site: translates the
/// state of compiled code there into interpreter frames (see `translate::exit()`, `translate::leave()` and
/// `translate::publish()`). After an exit, the JIT function returns
/// `EntryStatus::Resume`, and the interpreter continues in the innermost frame.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM, its frame, one of its code's exit or leave sites and the registers it saved.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_exit(
    vm: *const Vm,
    frame: *mut ExecutionContext,
    site: u32,
    dump: *const RegisterDump,
) {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes live pointers.
    let (vm, dump) = unsafe { (&*vm, &*dump) };
    let root = NonNull::new(frame).expect("JIT code passes its frame");
    // NB: The frame's executable keeps the code attached while JIT code runs the frame, also after it was discarded.
    let executable = executable_of(frame_of(root));
    let code = executable.jit_code(vm).expect("the code is attached");
    match code.site(site).kind() {
        SiteKind::Exit(_) => translate::exit(vm, root, code, site, dump),
        SiteKind::Leave => translate::leave(vm, root, code, site, dump),
        SiteKind::Publish => translate::publish(vm, root, code, site, dump),
        SiteKind::Call => unreachable!("call sites are no exits"),
    }
}

/// The frame a call at a call site in an inlined callee of the code running `root` made, from the running frame: the
/// one linked to `root`.
fn call_site_callee_frame(vm: &Vm, root: NonNull<ExecutionContext>) -> NonNull<ExecutionContext> {
    *frames_above(vm, root)
        .expect("the frame is on the running frame's chain")
        .last()
        .expect("the callee frame is linked to the frame")
}

/// Called by compiled code on the generic paths of a call at an inlined call site, which run in the frames of its
/// inlined calls: pushes them (see `materialize_inlined_call_frames()`), and returns the innermost one, which runs.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Compiled code calls this with its VM, its frame, one of its code's inlined call sites and its frame pointer.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_push_inlined_call_frames(
    vm: *const Vm,
    frame: *mut ExecutionContext,
    site: u32,
    frame_pointer: u64,
) -> *mut ExecutionContext {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes live pointers.
    let vm = unsafe { &*vm };
    let root = NonNull::new(frame).expect("JIT code passes its frame");
    translate::materialize_call_site_frames(vm, root, site, frame_pointer, None).as_ptr()
}

/// Called by compiled code when the callee of a direct call at an inlined call site did not return to it: materializes
/// the frames of the call's inlined calls below the callee's frame, and finishes the call in the innermost one like
/// `libjs_jit_finish_direct_call()`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Compiled code calls this with its VM, its frame, one of its code's inlined call sites, its frame pointer and the
/// callee's status.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_finish_inlined_direct_call(
    vm: *const Vm,
    frame: *mut ExecutionContext,
    site: u32,
    frame_pointer: u64,
    status: u64,
) -> i64 {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes live pointers.
    let vm_ref = unsafe { &*vm };
    let root = NonNull::new(frame).expect("JIT code passes its frame");
    let callee = call_site_callee_frame(vm_ref, root);
    let innermost = translate::materialize_call_site_frames(vm_ref, root, site, frame_pointer, Some(callee));
    let pc = executable_of(frame_of(root))
        .jit_code(vm_ref)
        .expect("the code is attached")
        .site(site)
        .frame(0)
        .pc();
    // SAFETY: The innermost frame of the inlined calls is the call's frame now.
    unsafe { super::calls::libjs_jit_finish_direct_call(vm, innermost.as_ptr(), pc, status) }
}

/// Called by compiled code when the native function of a native call at an inlined call site threw: materializes the
/// frames of the call's inlined calls below the native function's frame, and unwinds it like the runtime does for
/// native calls.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Compiled code calls this with its VM, its frame, one of its code's inlined call sites, its frame pointer and the
/// exception.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_inlined_raw_native_exception(
    vm: *const Vm,
    frame: *mut ExecutionContext,
    site: u32,
    frame_pointer: u64,
    exception: u64,
) -> i64 {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes live pointers.
    let vm = unsafe { &*vm };
    let root = NonNull::new(frame).expect("JIT code passes its frame");
    let native_frame = vm
        .running_execution_context()
        .expect("the native function's frame runs");
    assert_eq!(frame_of(native_frame).caller_frame.get(), root.as_ptr());
    // NB: The native function ran in its own realm, which may be another one than that of the frames of the call
    //     site, whose realm the runtime unwinds to.
    vm.head.current_realm.set(frame_of(root).realm());
    translate::materialize_call_site_frames(vm, root, site, frame_pointer, Some(native_frame));
    crate::interpreter::slow_paths::calls::handle_raw_native_exception(vm, Value::from_bits(exception)).0
}

/// Called by JIT code that never created the arguments object of the frame (whose arguments are unchanged) when it
/// needs one after all: creates it like CreateArguments of the given kind does and returns it as a value.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM and its frame.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_create_arguments(vm: *const Vm, frame: *mut ExecutionContext, mapped: u32) -> u64 {
    // SAFETY: JIT code passes live pointers.
    let (vm, frame) = unsafe { (&*vm, &*frame) };
    translate::create_arguments_object(vm, frame, mapped != 0).0
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/jit/entry_table.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The JIT entry table: where calls into the JIT code of an executable go, and who owns that code, outside the GC heap.
//!
//! Every executable the VM registers while the JIT is on gets a slot for its life. The slot holds the entry that
//! calls of the executable's functions jump to (its JIT code, or else an entry that has the interpreter run the
//! frame), the executable it belongs to, and the executable's JIT code. Executables keep only their slot number, which
//! JIT code and the runtime mask into the table and check against the slot's owner. Nothing in the GC heap points at
//! JIT code, so a corrupted executable can at worst name the slot of another executable, which the owner check
//! catches. On Windows, which commits slots as they get used, it can also name a slot past the ones in use, which
//! faults.

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::code::{DetachedJitCode, JitCode};
use crate::gc::defer_gc::DeferGc;
use crate::gc::sweep::Sweep;

#[cfg(all(feature = "address-sanitizer", not(windows)))]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn __lsan_register_root_region(start: *const c_void, size: usize);
    fn __lsan_unregister_root_region(start: *const c_void, size: usize);
}

/// How many slots the table has, a power of two. Executables registered while it is full never get JIT code.
pub const JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY: usize = 1 << 20;

/// Slot numbers are masked with this, which keeps them inside the table.
pub const JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK: u32 = (JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY - 1) as u32;

/// Where the owners start, as a byte offset from the entries.
pub const JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_OWNERS_OFFSET: usize = JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY * 8;

/// Where the code starts, as a byte offset from the entries.
const JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET: usize = 2 * JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY * 8;

const JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE: usize = 3 * JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY * 8;

/// The slot of executables without one. Its entry has the interpreter run the frame, and it has no owner.
pub const NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT: u32 = 0;

/// Windows has no mappings that take no commit charge until they are written to, and every worker would pay for the
/// whole table. The arrays get committed together, this many slots at a time.
#[cfg(windows)]
const SLOTS_COMMITTED_AT_ONCE: u32 = (64 * 1024 / 8) as u32;

/// One reserved mapping of three parallel arrays, indexed by slot: the entries (`*const c_void`), the owners (the
/// address of the owning executable's head, as `u64`) and the code (`Option<Box<JitCode>>`). Its address stays the
/// same for the VM's life, so JIT code embeds it.
pub struct JitEntryTable {
    base: NonNull<u8>,
    /// What freed slots and new executables' slots get as their entry.
    not_compiled_entry: *const c_void,
    /// The first slot no executable ever had.
    next_slot: Cell<u32>,
    free_slots: RefCell<Vec<u32>>,
}

impl JitEntryTable {
    pub fn new(not_compiled_entry: *const c_void) -> Self {
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        // SAFETY: A fresh anonymous mapping, which no one else uses. Its pages read as zeroes until written: no owner
        //         and no code in every slot.
        let base = unsafe {
            let base = libc::mmap(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE,
                libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
                libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS | libc::MAP_NORESERVE,
                -1,
                0,
            );
            assert!(base != libc::MAP_FAILED, "mapping the JIT entry table failed");
            base.cast::<u8>()
        };
        // NB: Pages read as zeroes once committed: no owner and no code in every slot.
        #[cfg(windows)]
        let base = ak::windows_code_memory::reserve(JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE);
        let table = Self {
            base: NonNull::new(base).expect("mapping the JIT entry table failed"),
            not_compiled_entry,
            next_slot: Cell::new(NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT + 1),
            free_slots: RefCell::default(),
        };
        #[cfg(windows)]
        assert!(
            table.commit_slots_from(NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT),
            "committing the JIT entry table failed"
        );
        table.entry_cell(NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT).set(not_compiled_entry);
        // NB: The leak checker does not look into mappings for pointers, and would report the JIT code of a VM that
        //     lives until the process exits (js) as leaked.
        #[cfg(all(feature = "address-sanitizer", not(windows)))]
        // SAFETY: The code of the table is inside its mapping, which lives as long as the table.
        unsafe {
            __lsan_register_root_region(table.code_start(), JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE - JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET);
        }
        table
    }

    /// Commits the next `SLOTS_COMMITTED_AT_ONCE` slots from `slot`, a multiple of that, in all three arrays. Returns
    /// whether that worked, which only fails when the system is out of commit.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    fn commit_slots_from(&self, slot: u32) -> bool {
        [0, JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_OWNERS_OFFSET, JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET]
            .into_iter()
            .all(|array_offset| {
                let offset = array_offset + 8 * slot as usize;
                // SAFETY: Slots are inside the table, and the capacity is a multiple of how many get committed at
                //         once. Committing pages again keeps what they hold.
                unsafe {
                    ak::windows_code_memory::make_writable(
                        self.base.as_ptr().add(offset),
                        8 * SLOTS_COMMITTED_AT_ONCE as usize,
                    )
                }
            })
    }

    #[cfg(all(feature = "address-sanitizer", not(windows)))]
    fn code_start(&self) -> *const c_void {
        // NB: The offset is inside the mapping.
        self.base.as_ptr().wrapping_add(JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET).cast()
    }

    /// The address of the entries, which JIT code embeds.
    pub fn address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.base.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// The address of the slot's entry.
    pub fn entry_address(&self, slot: u32) -> u64 {
        self.address() + 8 * u64::from(slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK)
    }

    fn entry_cell(&self, slot: u32) -> &Cell<*const c_void> {
        // SAFETY: The masked slot is inside the entries, which live as long as the table.
        unsafe { &*self.base.as_ptr().add(8 * (slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK) as usize).cast() }
    }

    fn owner_cell(&self, slot: u32) -> &Cell<u64> {
        // SAFETY: The masked slot is inside the owners, which live as long as the table.
        unsafe {
            &*self
                .base
                .as_ptr()
                .add(JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_OWNERS_OFFSET + 8 * (slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK) as usize)
                .cast()
        }
    }

    fn code_cell(&self, slot: u32) -> &Cell<Option<Box<JitCode>>> {
        // SAFETY: The masked slot is inside the code array, which lives as long as the table.
        unsafe {
            &*self
                .base
                .as_ptr()
                .add(JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET + 8 * (slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK) as usize)
                .cast()
        }
    }

    /// A slot for the executable whose head is at `owner`, with the not compiled entry, or `NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT` if the
    /// table is full (on Windows, also if the system is out of commit for more slots).
    pub fn allocate(&self, owner: u64) -> u32 {
        let slot = match self.free_slots.borrow_mut().pop() {
            Some(slot) => slot,
            None => {
                let slot = self.next_slot.get();
                if slot as usize == JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CAPACITY {
                    return NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT;
                }
                // NB: The next allocation tries again.
                #[cfg(windows)]
                if slot.is_multiple_of(SLOTS_COMMITTED_AT_ONCE) && !self.commit_slots_from(slot) {
                    return NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT;
                }
                self.next_slot.set(slot + 1);
                slot
            }
        };
        self.entry_cell(slot).set(self.not_compiled_entry);
        self.owner_cell(slot).set(owner);
        slot
    }

    /// Frees the slot of the executable whose head is at `owner`, which died, and returns its code.
    pub fn free(&self, slot: u32, owner: u64, _: &Sweep<'_>) -> Option<JitCode> {
        let slot = slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK;
        if slot == NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT {
            return None;
        }
        assert!(
            self.is_owned_by(slot, owner),
            "only the owner of a JIT entry slot frees it"
        );
        self.entry_cell(slot).set(self.not_compiled_entry);
        self.owner_cell(slot).set(0);
        self.free_slots.borrow_mut().push(slot);
        self.code_cell(slot).take().map(|code| *code)
    }

    /// Whether the slot belongs to the executable whose head is at `owner`.
    pub fn is_owned_by(&self, slot: u32, owner: u64) -> bool {
        owner != 0 && self.owner_cell(slot).get() == owner
    }

    /// Makes calls through the slot enter `entry`, or else have the interpreter run the frame.
    pub fn set_entry(&self, slot: u32, entry: Option<*const c_void>) {
        self.entry_cell(slot).set(entry.unwrap_or(self.not_compiled_entry));
    }

    /// The code attached to the slot.
    pub fn code(&self, slot: u32) -> Option<&JitCode> {
        // SAFETY: The code stays in the slot until detach_code() or free() takes it, which callers do not do while
        //         they use the reference.
        unsafe { (*self.code_cell(slot).as_ptr()).as_deref() }
    }

    /// Attaches `code` to the slot, which has none.
    pub fn attach_code(&self, slot: u32, code: JitCode, _: &DeferGc<'_>) {
        assert_ne!(slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK, NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT);
        assert!(self.code_cell(slot).replace(Some(Box::new(code))).is_none());
    }

    /// Drops the code attached to the slot, or moves it to `parking`, whose owner drops it later.
    pub fn detach_code(&self, slot: u32, parking: Option<&RefCell<DetachedJitCode>>) {
        assert_ne!(slot & JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK, NO_JIT_ENTRY_SLOT);
        match parking {
            Some(parking) => parking.borrow_mut().extend(self.code_cell(slot).take()),
            None => drop(self.code_cell(slot).take()),
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for JitEntryTable {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        for slot in 0..self.next_slot.get() {
            drop(self.code_cell(slot).take());
        }
        #[cfg(all(feature = "address-sanitizer", not(windows)))]
        // SAFETY: The region registered when the table was made.
        unsafe {
            __lsan_unregister_root_region(self.code_start(), JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE - JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_CODE_OFFSET);
        }
        // SAFETY: The table's mapping, which nothing uses anymore.
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        unsafe {
            libc::munmap(self.base.as_ptr().cast(), JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_SIZE);
        }
        // SAFETY: As above.
        #[cfg(windows)]
        unsafe {
            ak::windows_code_memory::release(self.base.as_ptr());
        }
    }
}

/*

//! Memory for JIT code.
//!
//! Code is carved out of large chunks that are mapped read+execute, and every write makes the affected pages writable
//! (and not executable) for the duration of the copy: memory is never writable and executable at once. On Linux
//! x86-64 with memory protection keys, the pages are writable and executable, but a protection key, allocated before
//! the process has threads, keeps every thread from writing them except the one writing code, while it writes. On
//! macOS, chunks are MAP_JIT mappings whose write protection is toggled per thread instead. On Windows, chunks are only
//! reserved, and pages get committed when code is first written to them.
//!
//! Every VM has its own chunks, which only the VM's thread writes and runs code in, so flipping the protection of
//! pages that hold other installed code is safe.

use core::cell::RefCell;
use std::rc::Rc;

use libjs_jit::artifact::Patch;

#[cfg(windows)]
use ak::windows_code_memory;

const CHUNK_SIZE: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
const ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT: usize = 64;

/// How much of the start of a chunk holds no code.
#[cfg(windows)]
const CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE: usize = windows_code_memory::UNWIND_INFO_SIZE;
#[cfg(not(windows))]
const CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 0;

const _: () = assert!(CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE.is_multiple_of(ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT));

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn page_size() -> usize {
    // SAFETY: sysconf() has no preconditions.
    let size = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
    usize::try_from(size).expect("the page size is positive")
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn page_size() -> usize {
    windows_code_memory::PAGE_SIZE
}

fn align_up(value: usize, alignment: usize) -> usize {
    value.div_ceil(alignment) * alignment
}

#[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
mod protection_key {
    use std::sync::OnceLock;

    /// PKEY_DISABLE_WRITE from <sys/mman.h>.
    const PKEY_DISABLE_WRITE: libc::c_uint = 2;

    unsafe extern "C" {
        /// glibc's wrapper of WRPKRU for one key.
        fn pkey_set(key: libc::c_int, rights: libc::c_uint) -> libc::c_int;
        safe fn pkey_alloc(flags: libc::c_uint, access_rights: libc::c_uint) -> libc::c_int;
        pub fn pkey_mprotect(
            address: *mut libc::c_void,
            length: libc::size_t,
            protection: libc::c_int,
            key: libc::c_int,
        ) -> libc::c_int;
    }

    static KEY: OnceLock<libc::c_int> = OnceLock::new();

    // NB: pkey_alloc() sets the rights to the key for the running thread only, and a new thread copies the rights of
    //     the thread that creates it. Allocating the key while the library loads, before there is a second thread, is
    //     what makes every thread start out unable to write with it.
    #[used]
    #[unsafe(link_section = ".init_array")]
    static ALLOCATE_KEY_ON_LOAD: extern "C" fn() = allocate_key;

    extern "C" fn allocate_key() {
        // NB: A thread that exists already would keep whatever rights it has to the key.
        if !process_has_one_thread() {
            return;
        }
        let key = pkey_alloc(0, PKEY_DISABLE_WRITE);
        if key >= 0 {
            let _ = KEY.set(key);
        }
    }

    fn process_has_one_thread() -> bool {
        // NB: A directory that cannot be read to its end may list any number of threads.
        std::fs::read_dir("/proc/self/task")
            .and_then(|threads| threads.collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>())
            .is_ok_and(|threads| threads.len() == 1)
    }

    /// The memory protection key of chunks whose write access is toggled per thread with the key instead of with
    /// mprotect(), or None if the CPU or kernel lacks protection keys, or the process had threads when this library
    /// loaded. Threads may write the chunks only while they write code; the pages themselves are writable and
    /// executable. One key serves every VM in the process.
    pub fn key() -> Option<libc::c_int> {
        KEY.get().copied()
    }

    /// Allows (or forbids again) the running thread to write memory with the key.
    pub fn set_writable(key: libc::c_int, writable: bool) {
        let rights = if writable { 0 } else { PKEY_DISABLE_WRITE };
        // SAFETY: The key was allocated by allocate_key().
        let result = unsafe { pkey_set(key, rights) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "pkey_set() failed");
    }
}

#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn pthread_jit_write_protect_np(enabled: libc::c_int);
    fn sys_icache_invalidate(start: *mut libc::c_void, length: libc::size_t);
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", windows)))]
unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The compiler runtime's instruction cache flush (a no-op on x86-64).
    fn __clear_cache(start: *mut libc::c_char, end: *mut libc::c_char);
}

struct Chunk {
    start: *mut u8,
    size: usize,
    /// Whether the protection key guards writes to the chunk.
    has_protection_key: bool,
}

impl Chunk {
    fn map(size: usize) -> Self {
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        {
            // SAFETY: An anonymous mapping has no preconditions.
            let chunk = unsafe {
                libc::mmap(
                    core::ptr::null_mut(),
                    size,
                    libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE | libc::PROT_EXEC,
                    libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANON | libc::MAP_JIT,
                    -1,
                    0,
                )
            };
            assert!(chunk != libc::MAP_FAILED, "mapping JIT code memory failed");
            Self {
                start: chunk.cast(),
                size,
                has_protection_key: false,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            let chunk = windows_code_memory::reserve(size);
            assert!(!chunk.is_null(), "reserving JIT code memory failed");
            // NB: The range starts at the chunk's first code, whose prologue the unwind info then describes (see
            //     `JitState::entry_trampoline()`).
            let unwind_range = windows_code_memory::CodeRange {
                start: CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE as u32,
                end: u32::try_from(size).expect("a chunk of JIT code is smaller than 4 GiB"),
                frame_layout: windows_code_memory::FrameLayout::RbpAtSavedRbp,
            };
            // SAFETY: The chunk was just reserved, so it has no unwind info yet and no code runs in it.
            let added = unsafe { windows_code_memory::add_unwind_info(chunk, &[unwind_range]) };
            assert!(added, "registering the unwind info of JIT code failed");
            Self {
                start: chunk,
                size,
                has_protection_key: false,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", windows)))]
        {
            // SAFETY: An anonymous mapping has no preconditions.
            let chunk = unsafe {
                libc::mmap(
                    core::ptr::null_mut(),
                    size,
                    libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_EXEC,
                    libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS,
                    -1,
                    0,
                )
            };
            assert!(chunk != libc::MAP_FAILED, "mapping JIT code memory failed");
            #[allow(unused_mut)]
            let mut has_protection_key = false;
            // NB: With a protection key, the pages can be writable without any thread being able to write them, which
            //     makes writing code a per-thread register change instead of a page protection change.
            #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
            if let Some(key) = protection_key::key() {
                // SAFETY: The chunk was just mapped with this size.
                has_protection_key = unsafe {
                    protection_key::pkey_mprotect(
                        chunk,
                        size,
                        libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE | libc::PROT_EXEC,
                        key,
                    )
                } == 0;
            }
            Self {
                start: chunk.cast(),
                size,
                has_protection_key,
            }
        }
    }

    fn contains(&self, address: *const u8) -> bool {
        let start = self.start as usize;
        (start..start + self.size).contains(&(address as usize))
    }
}

impl Drop for Chunk {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The chunk was mapped with this size. Every block of it holds the allocator that owns the chunk, so
        // no code lives in it anymore when it drops.
        #[cfg(not(windows))]
        unsafe {
            libc::munmap(self.start.cast(), self.size);
        }
        // SAFETY: As above.
        #[cfg(windows)]
        unsafe {
            windows_code_memory::delete_unwind_info(self.start);
            windows_code_memory::release(self.start);
        }
    }
}

struct CodeWrite<'a> {
    destination: *mut u8,
    code: &'a [u8],
}

/// Copies each code to its destination, which all lie in one chunk, making the pages writable (and not executable)
/// for the duration of the copies, once for all of them.
fn write_codes_in_chunk(chunk: &Chunk, writes: &[CodeWrite<'_>]) {
    let copy_all = || {
        for write in writes {
            // SAFETY: The destination was allocated for the code in a chunk that is writable during this copy.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(write.code.as_ptr(), write.destination, write.code.len()) };
        }
    };

    #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
    if chunk.has_protection_key {
        let key = protection_key::key().expect("a chunk with a protection key has one");
        protection_key::set_writable(key, true);
        copy_all();
        protection_key::set_writable(key, false);
        return;
    }
    let _ = chunk.has_protection_key;

    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    {
        // SAFETY: Toggles the running thread's write protection of MAP_JIT memory.
        unsafe { pthread_jit_write_protect_np(0) };
        copy_all();
        // SAFETY: As above.
        unsafe { pthread_jit_write_protect_np(1) };
        for write in writes {
            // SAFETY: The destination holds the code that was just written.
            unsafe { sys_icache_invalidate(write.destination.cast(), write.code.len()) };
        }
    }
    // NB: Making a page writable commits it, so pages between the writes stay as they are.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let runs = written_page_runs(writes);
        for &(start, end) in &runs {
            // SAFETY: The pages lie in a reserved chunk, and no code runs while this thread writes it.
            let writable = unsafe { windows_code_memory::make_writable(start as *mut u8, end - start) };
            assert!(writable, "making JIT code writable failed");
        }
        copy_all();
        for &(start, end) in &runs {
            // SAFETY: The pages were committed above.
            let executable = unsafe { windows_code_memory::make_executable(start as *mut u8, end - start) };
            assert!(executable, "making JIT code executable failed");
        }
    }
    #[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", windows)))]
    {
        let page_mask = !(page_size() - 1);
        let page_start = writes
            .iter()
            .map(|write| write.destination as usize & page_mask)
            .min()
            .expect("there is a write");
        let page_end = writes
            .iter()
            .map(|write| align_up(write.destination as usize + write.code.len(), page_size()))
            .max()
            .expect("there is a write");
        let pages = page_start as *mut libc::c_void;
        // SAFETY: The pages lie in a mapped chunk.
        let result = unsafe { libc::mprotect(pages, page_end - page_start, libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "making JIT code writable failed");
        copy_all();
        // SAFETY: As above.
        let result = unsafe { libc::mprotect(pages, page_end - page_start, libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_EXEC) };
        assert_eq!(result, 0, "making JIT code executable failed");
        for write in writes {
            // SAFETY: The destination holds the code that was just written.
            unsafe { __clear_cache(write.destination.cast(), write.destination.add(write.code.len()).cast()) };
        }
    }
}

/// The pages the writes go to, as runs of consecutive pages in the order of their addresses, each from its first page
/// to the end of its last.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn written_page_runs(writes: &[CodeWrite<'_>]) -> Vec<(usize, usize)> {
    let page_mask = !(page_size() - 1);
    let mut pages: Vec<(usize, usize)> = writes
        .iter()
        .map(|write| {
            let start = write.destination as usize;
            (start & page_mask, align_up(start + write.code.len(), page_size()))
        })
        .collect();
    pages.sort_unstable();
    let mut runs: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::with_capacity(pages.len());
    for (start, end) in pages {
        match runs.last_mut() {
            Some(run) if start <= run.1 => run.1 = run.1.max(end),
            _ => runs.push((start, end)),
        }
    }
    runs
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct FreeBlock {
    start: *mut u8,
    size: usize,
    /// The index of the chunk the block lies in.
    chunk: usize,
}

impl FreeBlock {
    fn end(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.start.wrapping_add(self.size)
    }
}

/// A first-fit allocator over chunks that stay mapped until the allocator goes away. Free blocks are kept sorted by
/// address and coalesced within their chunk. Chunks that the kernel happened to map next to each other may differ in
/// how their writes are protected (see `write_codes_in_chunk()`), so no block, and no allocation, spans two of them.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CodeAllocator {
    free_blocks: Vec<FreeBlock>,
    chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
}

impl CodeAllocator {
    fn allocate(&mut self, size: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        let size = align_up(size, ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT);
        if let Some(index) = self.free_blocks.iter().position(|block| block.size >= size) {
            let block = &mut self.free_blocks[index];
            let address = block.start;
            block.start = block.start.wrapping_add(size);
            block.size -= size;
            if block.size == 0 {
                self.free_blocks.remove(index);
            }
            return address;
        }

        let chunk = Chunk::map(CHUNK_SIZE.max(align_up(CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE + size, page_size())));
        let start = chunk.start.wrapping_add(CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE);
        let code_size = chunk.size - CHUNK_HEADER_SIZE;
        self.chunks.push(chunk);
        if code_size > size {
            self.free(start.wrapping_add(size), code_size - size);
        }
        start
    }

    fn free(&mut self, start: *mut u8, size: usize) {
        let size = align_up(size, ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT);
        let chunk = self.chunk_index_of(start);
        let index = self.free_blocks.partition_point(|block| block.start < start);
        self.free_blocks.insert(index, FreeBlock { start, size, chunk });
        let adjacent = |blocks: &[FreeBlock], first: usize| {
            blocks[first].end() == blocks[first + 1].start && blocks[first].chunk == blocks[first + 1].chunk
        };
        if index + 1 < self.free_blocks.len() && adjacent(&self.free_blocks, index) {
            self.free_blocks[index].size += self.free_blocks[index + 1].size;
            self.free_blocks.remove(index + 1);
        }
        if index > 0 && adjacent(&self.free_blocks, index - 1) {
            self.free_blocks[index - 1].size += self.free_blocks[index].size;
            self.free_blocks.remove(index);
        }
    }

    fn chunk_index_of(&self, address: *const u8) -> usize {
        self.chunks
            .iter()
            .position(|chunk| chunk.contains(address))
            .expect("JIT code lies in a chunk")
    }
}

/// Installed code: a block of a VM's executable memory, which goes back to the VM's allocator when dropped.
pub struct ExecutableMemory {
    address: *mut u8,
    size: usize,
    allocator: Rc<RefCell<CodeAllocator>>,
}

impl ExecutableMemory {
    /// Copies each code into newly allocated executable memory. Pages that more than one of them go to are made
    /// writable only once. The names describe the codes in /tmp/perf-<pid>.map when `perf_map` is set.
    pub fn allocate(
        allocator: &Rc<RefCell<CodeAllocator>>,
        codes: &[&[u8]],
        names: &[&str],
        perf_map: bool,
    ) -> Vec<ExecutableMemory> {
        assert_eq!(codes.len(), names.len());
        let memories: Vec<ExecutableMemory> = codes
            .iter()
            .map(|code| {
                assert!(!code.is_empty());
                ExecutableMemory {
                    address: allocator.borrow_mut().allocate(code.len()),
                    size: code.len(),
                    allocator: Rc::clone(allocator),
                }
            })
            .collect();

        // NB: Changing page protections is expensive, so code going into the same chunk is written with one change
        //     for all of it.
        let mut writes: Vec<(usize, CodeWrite<'_>)> = memories
            .iter()
            .zip(codes)
            .map(|(memory, code)| {
                let chunk = allocator.borrow().chunk_index_of(memory.address);
                (
                    chunk,
                    CodeWrite {
                        destination: memory.address,
                        code,
                    },
                )
            })
            .collect();
        writes.sort_by_key(|(chunk, write)| (*chunk, write.destination as usize));
        let mut start = 0;
        while start < writes.len() {
            let chunk = writes[start].0;
            let end = start + writes[start..].iter().take_while(|(other, _)| *other == chunk).count();
            let chunk_writes: Vec<CodeWrite<'_>> = writes[start..end]
                .iter()
                .map(|(_, write)| CodeWrite {
                    destination: write.destination,
                    code: write.code,
                })
                .collect();
            write_codes_in_chunk(&allocator.borrow().chunks[chunk], &chunk_writes);
            start = end;
        }

        if perf_map {
            for (memory, name) in memories.iter().zip(names) {
                write_perf_map_entry(memory.address, memory.size, name);
            }
        }
        memories
    }

    pub fn address(&self) -> *const u8 {
        self.address
    }

    /// Overwrites the code at the offset of each patch with its bytes, which the code is not running at the time.
    pub fn patch(&self, patches: &[Patch]) {
        if patches.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let writes: Vec<CodeWrite<'_>> = patches
            .iter()
            .map(|patch| {
                assert!(patch.offset as usize + patch.bytes().len() <= self.size);
                CodeWrite {
                    // NB: The offset is within the memory, as asserted.
                    destination: self.address.wrapping_add(patch.offset as usize),
                    code: patch.bytes(),
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let allocator = self.allocator.borrow();
        let chunk = allocator.chunk_index_of(self.address);
        write_codes_in_chunk(&allocator.chunks[chunk], &writes);
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }
}

impl Drop for ExecutableMemory {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.allocator.borrow_mut().free(self.address, self.size);
    }
}

fn write_perf_map_entry(address: *const u8, size: usize, name: &str) {
    let name = if name.is_empty() { "<anonymous>" } else { name };
    if ak::perf_map::write_perf_map_entry(address as usize, size, &format!("JIT {name}")).is_err() {
        eprintln!("LIBJS_JIT: Unable to write /tmp/perf-{}.map", std::process::id());
    }
}

//! Text descriptions of the feedback the interpreter collected, with every instruction that has feedback slots and
//! what they recorded, for LIBJS_JIT=dump-feedback and the `jit` testing object.

use core::fmt::Write;

use crate::bytecode::executable::Executable;
use crate::bytecode::feedback::{
    CallFeedback, CallFeedbackForwarding, KeyedFeedback, arith_feedback, call_feedback_flags, keyed_feedback_bits,
    value_feedback,
};
use crate::bytecode::instruction::{
    instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes, instruction_length_from_bytes, instruction_name_from_opcode,
};
use crate::gc::class::class_of;
use crate::layout::cell::{CellHeader, Gc};
use crate::layout::function_object::NativeFunction;
use crate::layout::object::Object;
use crate::layout::primitive_string::PrimitiveString;
use crate::runtime::symbol::Symbol;
use crate::runtime::typed_array::Kind as TypedArrayKind;
use crate::utf16::Utf16View;

const TYPED_ARRAY_KINDS: [TypedArrayKind; 12] = [
    TypedArrayKind::Uint8Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Uint8ClampedArray,
    TypedArrayKind::Uint16Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Uint32Array,
    TypedArrayKind::BigUint64Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Int8Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Int16Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Int32Array,
    TypedArrayKind::BigInt64Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Float16Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Float32Array,
    TypedArrayKind::Float64Array,
];

fn append_bits<T: Copy + Into<u32>>(out: &mut String, bits: T, names: &[(T, &str)]) {
    let bits: u32 = bits.into();
    if bits == 0 {
        out.push_str("none");
        return;
    }
    let mut first = true;
    for (bit, name) in names {
        let bit: u32 = (*bit).into();
        if bits & bit == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        if !first {
            out.push('|');
        }
        out.push_str(name);
        first = false;
    }
}

fn append_cell(out: &mut String, cell: Option<Gc<CellHeader>>) {
    let Some(cell) = cell else {
        out.push_str("none");
        return;
    };
    if let Some(string) = cell.downcast::<PrimitiveString>() {
        let _ = write!(out, "\"{}\"", string.to_utf8());
    } else if let Some(symbol) = cell.downcast::<Symbol>() {
        out.push_str(&Utf16View::of_string(&symbol.descriptive_string()).to_utf8());
    } else if let Some(native_function) = cell.downcast::<NativeFunction>() {
        let name = native_function.name();
        let name = match native_function.initial_name() {
            Some(initial_name) if name.is_empty() => initial_name,
            _ => name,
        };
        let name = Utf16View::of_fly_string(&name).to_utf8();
        if name.is_empty() {
            out.push_str("native function <anonymous>");
        } else {
            let _ = write!(out, "native function {name}");
        }
    } else if let Some(object) = cell.downcast::<Object>()
        && object.is_function()
    {
        let name = Utf16View::of_string(&object.name_for_call_stack()).to_utf8();
        if name.is_empty() {
            out.push_str("function <anonymous>");
        } else {
            let _ = write!(out, "function {name}");
        }
    } else {
        out.push_str(class_of(cell).class_name());
    }
}

fn append_value_feedback(out: &mut String, bits: u16) {
    append_bits(
        out,
        bits,
        &[
            (value_feedback::INT32, "Int32"),
            (value_feedback::DOUBLE, "Double"),
            (value_feedback::STRING, "String"),
            (value_feedback::SYMBOL, "Symbol"),
            (value_feedback::BOOLEAN, "Boolean"),
            (value_feedback::UNDEFINED, "Undefined"),
            (value_feedback::NULL, "Null"),
            (value_feedback::OBJECT, "Object"),
            (value_feedback::BIG_INT, "BigInt"),
            (value_feedback::EMPTY, "Empty"),
            (value_feedback::OTHER_MASK, "Other"),
        ],
    );
}

fn append_call_feedback(out: &mut String, feedback: &CallFeedback) {
    out.push_str("target=");
    append_cell(out, feedback.target());
    out.push_str(" flags=");
    append_bits(
        out,
        feedback.flags.get(),
        &[
            (call_feedback_flags::POLYMORPHIC, "Polymorphic"),
            (call_feedback_flags::SAW_NATIVE, "SawNative"),
            (call_feedback_flags::SAW_CONSTRUCT, "SawConstruct"),
            (call_feedback_flags::FORWARDED_POLYMORPHIC, "ForwardedPolymorphic"),
            (call_feedback_flags::FORWARDED_CLOSURES, "ForwardedClosures"),
            (call_feedback_flags::OTHER_FUNCTIONS, "OtherFunctions"),
        ],
    );
    let forwarding = match feedback.forwarding.get() {
        forwarding if forwarding == CallFeedbackForwarding::Apply as u8 => "apply",
        forwarding if forwarding == CallFeedbackForwarding::Call as u8 => "call",
        forwarding if forwarding == CallFeedbackForwarding::Bound as u8 => "bound",
        forwarding if forwarding == CallFeedbackForwarding::Callback as u8 => "callback",
        _ => return,
    };
    let _ = write!(
        out,
        " forwarded by {forwarding} with {} arguments to ",
        feedback.forwarded_argument_count.get()
    );
    append_cell(out, feedback.forwarded_target());
}

fn append_keyed_feedback(out: &mut String, feedback: &KeyedFeedback) {
    let bits = feedback.bits.get();
    out.push_str("keys=");
    append_bits(
        out,
        bits & keyed_feedback_bits::KEY_KINDS_MASK,
        &[
            (keyed_feedback_bits::INT32_INDEX, "Int32Index"),
            (keyed_feedback_bits::STRING_KEY, "String"),
            (keyed_feedback_bits::SYMBOL_KEY, "Symbol"),
            (keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_KEY, "Other"),
            (keyed_feedback_bits::MULTIPLE_KEYS, "MultipleKeys"),
        ],
    );
    out.push_str(" elements=");
    let mut element_names = vec![
        (keyed_feedback_bits::PACKED, "Packed"),
        (keyed_feedback_bits::HOLEY, "Holey"),
        (keyed_feedback_bits::OTHER_ELEMENTS, "Other"),
        (keyed_feedback_bits::MAGICAL_LENGTH, "MagicalLength"),
    ];
    let typed_array_names = TYPED_ARRAY_KINDS.map(|kind| format!("{kind:?}"));
    for (kind, name) in TYPED_ARRAY_KINDS.iter().zip(&typed_array_names) {
        element_names.push((keyed_feedback_bits::typed_array_bit(*kind as u8), name.as_str()));
    }
    append_bits(
        out,
        bits & !keyed_feedback_bits::KEY_KINDS_MASK & !keyed_feedback_bits::OUT_OF_BOUNDS,
        &element_names,
    );
    if bits & keyed_feedback_bits::OUT_OF_BOUNDS != 0 {
        out.push_str(" out-of-bounds");
    }
    if feedback.last_key().is_some() {
        out.push_str(" last_key=");
        append_cell(out, feedback.last_key());
    }
}

/// The feedback of every instruction of `executable` that has feedback slots, one line per instruction after a line
/// naming the executable, or `None` if the executable never collected feedback.
pub fn describe_feedback(executable: &Executable) -> Option<String> {
    let feedback = executable.feedback()?;
    feedback.update_value_feedback();
    let name = executable.name();
    let name = Utf16View::of_fly_string(&name).to_utf8();
    let mut out = String::new();
    if name.is_empty() {
        out.push_str("Feedback for <anonymous>:\n");
    } else {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "Feedback for {name}:");
    }

    let bytecode = executable.bytecode();
    let mut at = 0;
    while at < bytecode.len() {
        let opcode = bytecode[at];
        let slots = instruction_feedback_slots_from_bytes(opcode, bytecode, at);
        let [arith, value, call, keyed, cache_value] = slots;
        if slots.iter().any(Option::is_some) {
            let _ = write!(out, "  [{at:4x}] {}", instruction_name_from_opcode(opcode));
            if let Some(slot) = arith {
                let _ = write!(out, " arith#{slot}: ");
                append_bits(
                    &mut out,
                    feedback.arith()[usize::from(slot)].get(),
                    &[
                        (arith_feedback::INT32, "Int32"),
                        (arith_feedback::DOUBLE, "Double"),
                        (arith_feedback::INT32_OVERFLOW, "Int32Overflow"),
                        (arith_feedback::STRING, "String"),
                        (arith_feedback::BIG_INT, "BigInt"),
                        (arith_feedback::OTHER, "Other"),
                        (arith_feedback::OBJECT_PAIR, "ObjectPair"),
                        (arith_feedback::BOOLEAN, "Boolean"),
                    ],
                );
            }
            if let Some(slot) = value {
                let _ = write!(out, " value#{slot}: ");
                append_value_feedback(&mut out, feedback.value()[usize::from(slot)].get());
            }
            if let Some(cache) = cache_value {
                let _ = write!(out, " value of cache#{cache}: ");
                append_value_feedback(&mut out, feedback.cache_value()[usize::from(cache)].get());
            }
            if let Some(slot) = call {
                let _ = write!(out, " call#{slot}: ");
                let call = &feedback.call()[usize::from(slot)];
                append_call_feedback(&mut out, call);
                out.push_str(" returned: ");
                append_value_feedback(&mut out, call.value.get());
            }
            if let Some(slot) = keyed {
                let _ = write!(out, " keyed#{slot}: ");
                append_keyed_feedback(&mut out, &feedback.keyed()[usize::from(slot)]);
            }
            out.push('\n');
        }
        let Ok(length) = instruction_length_from_bytes(opcode, bytecode, at) else {
            break;
        };
        at += length;
    }
    Some(out)
}

//! The runtime helpers of the builtins JIT code calls without a native frame (`libjs_jit::snapshot::HelperCall`).
//! Each takes the VM, the `this` value and the arguments of the kinds its `HelperCall` lists (strings as values, int32
//! values as `i32`), runs no code, and returns what its `HelperResult` says, in 64 bits: the empty value where it
//! declines, having done nothing observable.

use libjs_jit::snapshot::Intrinsic;
use libjs_runtime_macros::{jit_abi, jit_function_address};

use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::keyed_collections::canonicalize_keyed_collection_key;
use crate::runtime::map::Map;
use crate::runtime::regexp_prototype::regexp_builtin_exec_running_no_code;
use crate::runtime::string_prototype::{StringPrototype, trim_primitive_string};
use crate::utf16::TrimMode;

/// The address of the runtime helper of `intrinsic`, or 0 if JIT code calls it in another way. Every intrinsic with a
/// `HelperCall` has a helper here.
pub fn address(intrinsic: Intrinsic) -> u64 {
    match intrinsic {
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeIndexOf => jit_function_address!(string_index_of),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeLastIndexOf => jit_function_address!(string_last_index_of),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeIncludes => jit_function_address!(string_includes),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeStartsWith => jit_function_address!(string_starts_with),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeEndsWith => jit_function_address!(string_ends_with),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeSlice => jit_function_address!(string_slice),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeSubstring => jit_function_address!(string_substring),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeToLowerCase => jit_function_address!(string_to_lowercase),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeToUpperCase => jit_function_address!(string_to_uppercase),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrim => jit_function_address!(string_trim),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrimStart => jit_function_address!(string_trim_start),
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrimEnd => jit_function_address!(string_trim_end),
        Intrinsic::RegExpPrototypeExec => jit_function_address!(regexp_exec),
        Intrinsic::MapPrototypeGet => jit_function_address!(map_get),
        Intrinsic::MapPrototypeHas => jit_function_address!(map_has),
        Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeApply
        | Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeCall
        | Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypePush
        | Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypeSlice
        | Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypeSplice
        | Intrinsic::ObjectPrototypeHasOwnProperty
        | Intrinsic::StringFromCharCode
        | Intrinsic::StringConstructor
        | Intrinsic::ArrayConstructor
        | Intrinsic::ObjectConstructor
        | Intrinsic::BooleanConstructor
        | Intrinsic::TypedArrayPrototypeLength
        | Intrinsic::MathMax
        | Intrinsic::MathMin
        | Intrinsic::MathImul => 0,
    }
}

/// The string of a value JIT code checked to be a string.
fn string(value: u64) -> Value {
    let value = Value::from_bits(value);
    assert!(value.is_string());
    value
}

/// An int32 result, zero-extended.
fn int32(value: Value) -> u64 {
    // NB: Strings are shorter than 2^31 code units, so their indices are int32 values.
    u64::from(value.as_i32() as u32)
}

/// `string.indexOf(search_string, position)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_index_of(_vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, search_string: u64, position: i32) -> u64 {
    let (string_value, search_string) = (string(string_value), string(search_string));
    int32(StringPrototype::index_of_string(
        string_value.as_string(),
        search_string.as_string(),
        f64::from(position),
    ))
}

/// `string.toLowerCase()`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_to_lowercase(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    StringPrototype::to_lowercase_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string()).0
}

/// `string.toUpperCase()`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_to_uppercase(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    StringPrototype::to_uppercase_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string()).0
}

/// `string.lastIndexOf(search_string, position)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_last_index_of(_vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, search_string: u64, position: i32) -> u64 {
    let (string_value, search_string) = (string(string_value), string(search_string));
    int32(StringPrototype::last_index_of_string(
        string_value.as_string(),
        search_string.as_string(),
        f64::from(position),
    ))
}

/// `string.includes(search_string, position)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_includes(_vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, search_string: u64, position: i32) -> u64 {
    let (string_value, search_string) = (string(string_value), string(search_string));
    u64::from(StringPrototype::includes_string(
        string_value.as_string(),

        f64::from(position),

}

#[jit_abi]

    let (string_value, search_string) = (string(string_value), string(search_string));

}

/// `string.endsWith(search_string, end_position)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_ends_with(_vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, search_string: u64, end_position: i32) -> u64 {
    let (string_value, search_string) = (string(string_value), string(search_string));
    u64::from(StringPrototype::ends_with_string(
        string_value.as_string(),
        search_string.as_string(),
        f64::from(end_position),
    ))
}

/// `string.slice(start, end)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_slice(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, start: i32, end: i32) -> u64 {
    StringPrototype::slice_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string(), f64::from(start), f64::from(end)).0
}

/// `string.substring(start, end)`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_substring(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64, start: i32, end: i32) -> u64 {
    StringPrototype::substring_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string(), f64::from(start), f64::from(end)).0
}

/// `string.trim()`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_trim(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    trim_primitive_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string(), TrimMode::Both).0
}

/// `string.trimStart()`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_trim_start(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    trim_primitive_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string(), TrimMode::Left).0
}

/// `string.trimEnd()`.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn string_trim_end(vm: &Vm, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    trim_primitive_string(vm, string(string_value).as_string(), TrimMode::Right).0
}

/// `regexp.exec(string)`, for a RegExp object `regexp` whose exec runs no code (see
/// `regexp_builtin_exec_running_no_code()`).
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn regexp_exec(vm: &Vm, regexp: u64, string_value: u64) -> u64 {
    regexp_builtin_exec_running_no_code(vm, Value::from_bits(regexp), string(string_value).as_string())
        .map_or(Value::EMPTY.0, |result| result.0)
}

/// The Map a `this` value is, if it is one.
fn map(value: u64) -> Option<crate::layout::cell::Gc<Map>> {
    let value = Value::from_bits(value);
    if !value.is_object() {
        return None;
    }
    value.as_object().downcast::<Map>()
}

/// `map.get(key)`, or the empty value if the `this` value is no Map.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn map_get(_vm: &Vm, map_value: u64, key: u64) -> u64 {
    let Some(map) = map(map_value) else {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    };
    map.map_get(canonicalize_keyed_collection_key(Value::from_bits(key)))
        .unwrap_or(Value::UNDEFINED)
        .0
}

/// `map.has(key)`, or the empty value if the `this` value is no Map.
#[jit_abi]
extern "C" fn map_has(_vm: &Vm, map_value: u64, key: u64) -> u64 {
    let Some(map) = map(map_value) else {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    };
    Value::from_bool(map.map_has(canonicalize_keyed_collection_key(Value::from_bits(key)))).0
}

//! The runtime helpers of the intrinsics JIT code calls without a native frame (`libjs_jit::snapshot::IntrinsicHelpers`).
//! Each returns a value, or the empty value, having done nothing observable, for anything it does not handle; the
//! code then exits to the interpreter, which runs the instruction itself.

use ak::Utf16FlyString;
use libjs_runtime_macros::jit_abi;

use crate::bytecode::executable::{KeyedPropertyLookup, KeyedPropertyLookupCache, PropertyLookupCacheEntryType};
use crate::gc::class::GcCell;
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::object::Object;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::array::Array;
use crate::runtime::completion::Must;
use crate::runtime::ecmascript_function_object::as_ecmascript_function_object;
use crate::runtime::module_namespace_object::ModuleNamespaceObject;
use crate::runtime::property_key::{PropertyKey, StringMayBeNumber};
use crate::runtime::proxy_object::ProxyObject;
