/// The packed-array path of Array.prototype.splice, without coercions or
/// calls of species constructors. All checks precede its observable work.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `items` points to `item_count` live, aligned values on the caller's native
/// stack, outside any object's element storage, for the duration of the call.
#[jit_abi]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn libjs_jit_array_splice(
    vm: &Vm,
    receiver: u64,
    start: i32,
    delete_count: i32,
    items: *const Value,
    item_count: u32,
) -> u64 {
    let receiver = Value::from_bits(receiver);
    if !receiver.is_object() {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    let Some(array) = receiver.as_object().downcast::<Array>() else {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    };
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("JIT code runs in a realm");
    if array.realm() != realm
        || !array.is_simple_packed_array()
        || !array.extensible()
        || !array.length_is_writable()
        || array.shape().property_count() != 0
        || !array.default_prototype_chain_intact()
        || !realm_watchpoints::array_species_is_unchanged(vm, realm)
    {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    let length = array.indexed_array_like_size();
    let start = if start < 0 {
        (i64::from(length) + i64::from(start)).max(0) as u32
    } else {
        (start as u32).min(length)
    };
    let delete_count = (delete_count.max(0) as u32).min(length - start);
    if u64::from(length - delete_count) + u64::from(item_count) > u64::from(u32::MAX) {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    let removed = Array::create(vm, realm, 0, None).must();
    removed.set_indexed_property_elements_to_undefined(delete_count);
    for index in 0..delete_count {
        let value = array
            .indexed_get(start + index)
            .expect("packed arrays have every element")
            .value;
        removed.set_packed_indexed_element(index, value);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps these values on its native stack, which GC
    // scans while allocating the result. Element storage growth does not collect.
    let items = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(items, item_count as usize) };
    array.splice_packed_indexed_elements(start, delete_count, items);
    Value::from_object(removed).0
}

/// The property key of a string or symbol, which converting runs no code for.
fn string_or_symbol_key(vm: &Vm, key: Value) -> Option<PropertyKey> {
    if !key.is_string() && !key.is_symbol() {
        return None;
    }
    key.to_property_key(vm).ok()
}

/// Whether looking up properties of the object runs no code and cannot throw. Proxies run traps, the bindings of
/// module namespaces may be uninitialized, and platform objects may check their embedder's rules.
fn has_ordinary_lookups(object: Gc<Object>) -> bool {
    // NB: Neither class has subclasses.
    let class = object.class();
    !core::ptr::eq(class, ProxyObject::CLASS)
        && !core::ptr::eq(class, ModuleNamespaceObject::CLASS)
        && !object.is_platform_object()
}

/// Whether the object is an ECMAScript function that has the property `key` without having made it yet.
fn has_lazy_function_property(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, key: &PropertyKey) -> bool {
    as_ecmascript_function_object(object).is_some_and(|function| function.has_lazy_property(vm, key))
}

/// Whether looking up the property `key` of the object creates nothing.
fn lookup_creates_nothing(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, key: &PropertyKey) -> bool {
    if has_lazy_function_property(vm, object, key) {
        return false;
    }
    if key.is_number() {
        return !object.is::<StringObject>()
            && !object
                .downcast::<TypedArrayBase>()
                .is_some_and(|typed_array| typed_array.content_type() == ContentType::BigInt);
    }
    !key.is_string() || !object.has_intrinsic_accessors()
}

/// Whether looking up the property `key` creates nothing in the object or in its prototypes.
fn prototype_chain_lookup_creates_nothing(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, key: &PropertyKey) -> bool {
    let mut holder = Some(object);
    while let Some(current) = holder {
        if !lookup_creates_nothing(vm, current, key) {
            return false;
        }
        holder = current.prototype();
    }
    true
}

/// The fly string of a string key, if the string is stored as one already.
fn fly_string_key(key: Value) -> Option<Utf16FlyString> {
    if !key.is_string() {
        return None;
    }
    let string = key.as_string().utf16_string();
    has_fly_string_storage(&string).then(|| to_utf16_fly_string(&string))
}

/// Whether an object whose own string-keyed properties are those of its shape has the own property `name`, from the
/// VM's keyed property lookup cache, whose entries for an own property or its absence this remembers too, or from its
/// shape. Returns `None` for other objects and for array indices.
fn has_own_string_property(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, name: &Utf16FlyString) -> Option<bool> {
    if !object.own_string_keyed_properties_are_in_shape() {
        return None;
    }
    let shape = object.shape();
    let cache = vm.keyed_property_lookup_cache();
    let index = KeyedPropertyLookupCache::entry_index_for(shape, name);
    if let Some(entry) = cache.lookup(index, shape, name)
        && entry.shape_key() == Some(ShapeKey::of(shape))
    {
        // NB: Only names that are no array indices have entries, since the shape does not hold indexed properties.
        match entry.entry_type {
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty => return Some(true),
            PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::MissingOwnProperty => return Some(false),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    // NB: Array indices are indexed properties, which the shape does not hold.
    let key = PropertyKey::from_fly_string(name.clone(), StringMayBeNumber::Yes);
    if key.is_number() {
        return None;
    }
    let metadata = shape.lookup(&key);
    cache.set_entry(
        index,
        KeyedPropertyLookup {
            entry_type: if metadata.is_some() {
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty
            } else {
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::MissingOwnProperty
            },
            property_offset: metadata.map_or(0, |metadata| metadata.offset),
            ..KeyedPropertyLookup::for_shape(ShapeKey::of(shape))
        },
        name,
    );
    Some(metadata.is_some())
}

/// `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` called on `object` with `key`.
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM.
#[jit_abi]
pub extern "C" fn libjs_jit_has_own_property(vm: &Vm, object: u64, key: u64) -> u64 {
    let (object, key) = (Value::from_bits(object), Value::from_bits(key));
    if !object.is_object() || !has_ordinary_lookups(object.as_object()) {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    if let Some(name) = fly_string_key(key)
        && let Some(result) = has_own_string_property(vm, object.as_object(), &name)
    {
        return Value::from_bool(result).0;
    }
    let Some(key) = string_or_symbol_key(vm, key) else {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    };
    let object = object.as_object();
    if has_lazy_function_property(vm, object, &key) {
        return Value::TRUE.0;
    }
    if !lookup_creates_nothing(vm, object, &key) {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    object
        .has_own_property(vm, &key)
        .map_or(Value::EMPTY, Value::from_bool)
        .0
}

/// `key in object`.
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM.
#[jit_abi]
pub extern "C" fn libjs_jit_has_property(vm: &Vm, key: u64, object: u64) -> u64 {
    let (key_value, object) = (Value::from_bits(key), Value::from_bits(object));
    let index_key = key_value.is_int32() && key_value.as_i32() >= 0;
    if !object.is_object() || !(key_value.is_string() || key_value.is_symbol() || index_key) {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    // NB: [[HasProperty]] of ordinary objects asks their prototypes, so every object of the chain must look up its
    //     properties without running code.
    let mut holder = Some(object.as_object());
    while let Some(current) = holder {
        if !has_ordinary_lookups(current) {
            return Value::EMPTY.0;
        }
        holder = current.prototype();
    }
    if index_key {
        let key = PropertyKey::from(key_value.as_i32().cast_unsigned());
        if !prototype_chain_lookup_creates_nothing(vm, object.as_object(), &key) {
            return Value::EMPTY.0;
        }
        return object
            .as_object()
            .has_property(vm, &key)
            .map_or(Value::EMPTY, Value::from_bool)
            .0;
    }
    let name = fly_string_key(key_value);
    let mut holder = Some(object.as_object());
    while let Some(current) = holder {
        match name
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|name| has_own_string_property(vm, current, name))
        {
            Some(true) => return Value::TRUE.0,
            Some(false) => holder = current.prototype(),
            None => {
                let Some(key) = string_or_symbol_key(vm, key_value) else {
                    return Value::EMPTY.0;
                };
                if has_lazy_function_property(vm, current, &key) {
                    return Value::TRUE.0;
                }
                if !prototype_chain_lookup_creates_nothing(vm, current, &key) {
                    return Value::EMPTY.0;
                }
                return current.has_property(vm, &key).map_or(Value::EMPTY, Value::from_bool).0;
            }
        }
    }
    Value::FALSE.0
}

/// `GetIterator(iterable, sync)` in fast array mode (see `get_iterator()` in the interpreter's slow paths): the
/// iterable, if it is an array whose iterator method is `%Array.prototype.values%` of the realm of JIT code and whose
/// iterators have the builtin `next` method, so that nothing can observe the iterator GetIterator would make. The
/// empty value otherwise.
///
/// JIT code calls this with its VM.
#[jit_abi]
pub extern "C" fn libjs_jit_open_array_iteration(vm: &Vm, iterable: u64) -> u64 {
    let iterable = Value::from_bits(iterable);
    if !iterable.is_object() {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    let array = iterable.as_object();
    if array.downcast::<Array>().is_none() {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("JIT code runs in a realm");
    if !realm_watchpoints::array_is_iterated_unobservably(vm, realm, &array) {
        return Value::EMPTY.0;
    }
    iterable.0
}

//! warm, the tier-up policy, and the glue between the runtime and the `libjs_jit` compiler: snapshots of executables

/// Whether this build has the JIT (see `disabled.rs` for builds without it).
pub const BUILT: bool = true;

/// The frame a pointer the runtime got from JIT code or the VM names.
fn frame_of<'a>(frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>) -> &'a ExecutionContext {
    // SAFETY: Callers pass frames that are live on the interpreter stack, which stay live while the reference is used.
    unsafe { frame.as_ref() }
}

/// A field offset as JIT code takes it.
fn offset(offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(offset).expect("field offsets fit in u32")
}

/// The executable a frame runs.
fn executable_of(frame: &ExecutionContext) -> Gc<Executable> {
    Executable::from_head(frame.executable.get().expect("the frame runs an executable"))
}

/// The frames above `frame` on the running frame's chain of callers, innermost first, or `None` if `frame` is not on
/// it.
fn frames_above(vm: &Vm, frame: NonNull<ExecutionContext>) -> Option<Vec<NonNull<ExecutionContext>>> {
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    let mut running = NonNull::new(vm.head.running_execution_context.get());
    while let Some(current) = running {
        if current == frame {
            return Some(frames);
        }
        frames.push(current);
        running = NonNull::new(frame_of(current).caller_frame.get());
    }
    None
}

/// What calls of an executable without JIT code enter through its slot in the JIT entry table.
pub fn not_compiled_call_entry() -> *const core::ffi::c_void {
    libjs_runtime_macros::jit_function_address!(entry_exit::libjs_jit_not_compiled_call_entry)
        as *const core::ffi::c_void
}

/// Which interpreter handlers an executable's frames run with. Each tier's value is the index of its dispatch table
/// in the VM's dispatch tables.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum InterpreterTier {
    /// The plain handlers, which neither collect feedback nor count the tier-up budget. Everything runs on them while
    /// the JIT is off.
    Plain = 0,
    /// The plain handlers, except that function entry, loop back edges, calls and returns use the profiling handlers,
    /// which count the tier-up budget, enter JIT code and switch to the dispatch table of the frame they continue in.
    /// New executables warm up here while the JIT is on, so code that only runs a few times never pays for profiling.
    WarmingUp,
    /// The plain handlers, except that calls and returns use the profiling handlers, for executables the JIT never
    /// compiles: their frames neither collect feedback nor count the tier-up budget, but still enter the JIT code of
    /// the functions they call.
    Unprofiled,
    /// The profiling handlers, which collect feedback for the JIT.
    Profiling,
}

impl InterpreterTier {
    pub const ALL: [InterpreterTier; 4] = [Self::Plain, Self::WarmingUp, Self::Unprofiled, Self::Profiling];
}

/// A compile job running on a compile thread. The VM keeps the executable and every cell its snapshot refers to
/// alive until the job's code is installed or the job is abandoned.
#[derive(Trace)]
pub struct CompileJob {
    pub executable: Gc<Executable>,
    pub cells: Vec<Gc<CellHeader>>,
    pub snapshot_executables: Vec<SnapshotExecutable>,
    #[gc(untraced = "the cells keep the samples alive and in place until the code is installed")]
    pub sample_slots: allocation::SampleSlots,
}

/// With the "stress-install" option, finished compile jobs wait for at most this many tier-up checks.
const MAX_STRESS_INSTALL_DELAY: u32 = 16;

/// The pseudo-random numbers the stress options make their choices with: SplitMix64, seeded from the "seed" option.
pub(crate) struct StressRandom {
    state: Cell<u64>,
}

impl StressRandom {
    fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        Self { state: Cell::new(seed) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn next_u64(&self) -> u64 {
        let state = self.state.get().wrapping_add(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
        self.state.set(state);
        let mut z = state;
        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xbf58_476d_1ce4_e5b9);
        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94d0_49bb_1331_11eb);
        z ^ (z >> 31)
    }

    /// A number from `low` to `high`, both included.
    pub(crate) fn between(&self, low: u32, high: u32) -> u32 {
        debug_assert!(low <= high);
        let range = u64::from(high - low) + 1;
        low + (self.next_u64() % range) as u32
    }
}

/// The JIT's state on a VM.
pub struct JitState {
    pub options: Options,
    /// Where the stress options get their pseudo-random numbers.
    pub(crate) stress_random: StressRandom,
    /// With the "stress-exits" option, how many more checks JIT code runs before it exits. JIT code counts it down;
    /// `libjs_jit_exit()` sets it again after an exit it caused.
    stress_exit_countdown: Box<Cell<u32>>,
    /// With the "stress-install" option, the results of finished compile jobs that are not installed yet, with how
    /// many more tier-up checks they wait for.
    held_compile_results: RefCell<Vec<(u32, u64, CompileResult)>>,
    /// The code detached while drops were deferred (see `defer_code_drops_until_collection_is_over()`), which a
    /// post-GC task drops.
    codes_detached_in_collection: RefCell<DetachedJitCode>,
    /// Whether code that is detached now goes into `codes_detached_in_collection`.
    defers_code_drops: Cell<bool>,
    /// With the "stress-invalidate" option, how many more tier-up checks happen before the next invalidation.
    stress_invalidation_countdown: Cell<u32>,
    /// With the "coverage" option, how often each coverage key was counted.
    coverage: RefCell<BTreeMap<String, u64>>,
    /// The dispatch table of executables that warm up, see `InterpreterTier::WarmingUp`. Only built while the
    /// interpreter collects feedback.
    pub(crate) warming_up_dispatch_table: Option<Box<DispatchTable>>,
    /// The dispatch table of executables the JIT never compiles, see `InterpreterTier::Unprofiled`. Only built while
    /// the interpreter collects feedback.
    pub(crate) unprofiled_dispatch_table: Option<Box<DispatchTable>>,
    /// Where calls of executables enter, and their JIT code (see `entry_table`). Only made while the JIT is on.
    pub(crate) entry_table: Option<entry_table::JitEntryTable>,
    /// The free lists call stubs pop function environments from (see `allocation::FunctionEnvironmentFreeLists`).
    pub(crate) function_environment_free_lists: allocation::FunctionEnvironmentFreeLists,
    /// The memory the VM's JIT code lives in.
    code_allocator: Rc<RefCell<CodeAllocator>>,
    /// The memory the tables of the VM's JIT code live in.
    data_allocator: Rc<RefCell<DataAllocator>>,
    /// The compile threads, started by the first asynchronous compile job.
    compile_queue: OnceCell<CompileQueue>,
    /// The compile jobs that run on the compile threads, by id.
    jobs: RefCell<HashMap<u64, CompileJob>>,
    next_job_id: Cell<u64>,
    /// The addresses of the runtime functions JIT code calls, looked up the first time a compile job needs them.
    runtime_function_addresses: OnceCell<runtime_info::RuntimeFunctionAddresses>,
    /// How native code enters JIT code, generated the first time it does.
    entry_trampoline: OnceCell<(ExecutableMemory, EntryTrampoline)>,
    /// The call stub JIT code shares (see `libjs_jit::codegen::generate_call_stub()`), generated the first time a
    /// compile job needs it, if there is one.
    call_stub: OnceCell<Option<ExecutableMemory>>,
    /// The construct stub JIT code shares (see `libjs_jit::codegen::generate_construct_stub()`).
    construct_stub: OnceCell<Option<ExecutableMemory>>,
    /// The installed code that depends on things staying as they are.
    pub(crate) dependents: dependencies::Dependents,
    /// The id the next installed code gets (see `JitCode::id()`).
    next_code_id: Cell<u64>,
    /// Whether an object with the `[[IsHTMLDDA]]` internal slot was ever made.
    pub(crate) htmldda_objects_exist: Cell<bool>,
}

impl JitState {
    #[cfg_attr(
        ladybird_gc_lints,
        expect(gc_container_on_stack, reason = "the VM makes its JIT state before its heap")
    )]
    pub fn new(options: Options) -> Self {
        translate::RegisterDump::assert_layout();
        let warming_up_dispatch_table = options
            .collects_feedback()
            .then(dispatch_tables::warming_up_dispatch_table);
        let unprofiled_dispatch_table = options
            .collects_feedback()
            .then(dispatch_tables::unprofiled_dispatch_table);
        let entry_table = options
            .enabled
            .then(|| entry_table::JitEntryTable::new(not_compiled_call_entry()));
        let stress_random = StressRandom::new(options.seed);
        let stress_invalidation_countdown = Cell::new(options.stress_invalidate);
        let stress_exit_countdown = Box::new(Cell::new(0));
        if options.stress_exits != 0 {
            stress_exit_countdown.set(stress_random.between(1, options.stress_exits));
        }
        Self {
            options,
            stress_random,
            stress_exit_countdown,
            held_compile_results: RefCell::default(),
            codes_detached_in_collection: RefCell::default(),
            defers_code_drops: Cell::new(false),
            stress_invalidation_countdown,
            coverage: RefCell::default(),
            warming_up_dispatch_table,
            unprofiled_dispatch_table,
            entry_table,
            function_environment_free_lists: allocation::FunctionEnvironmentFreeLists::default(),
            code_allocator: Rc::default(),
            data_allocator: Rc::default(),
            compile_queue: OnceCell::new(),
            jobs: RefCell::default(),
            next_job_id: Cell::new(1),
            runtime_function_addresses: OnceCell::new(),
            entry_trampoline: OnceCell::new(),
            call_stub: OnceCell::new(),
            construct_stub: OnceCell::new(),
            dependents: dependencies::Dependents::default(),
            next_code_id: Cell::new(1),
            htmldda_objects_exist: Cell::new(false),
        }
    }

    /// Whether the interpreter collects feedback and counts down tier-up budgets.
    pub fn collects_feedback(&self) -> bool {
        self.options.collects_feedback()
    }

    pub(crate) fn htmldda_objects_exist(&self) -> bool {
        self.htmldda_objects_exist.get()
    }

    /// An id for code to be installed, which no other code of the VM has.
    pub(crate) fn next_code_id(&self) -> u64 {
        let id = self.next_code_id.get();
        self.next_code_id.set(id + 1);
        id
    }

    /// The address of the countdown JIT code exits at with the "stress-exits" option, or 0 without it.
    pub(crate) fn stress_exit_countdown_address(&self) -> u64 {
        if self.options.stress_exits == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        self.stress_exit_countdown.as_ptr() as u64
    }

    /// Whether the exit JIT code is taking was caused by the "stress-exits" option. If so, starts the next
    /// countdown.
    pub(crate) fn take_stress_exit(&self) -> bool {
        if self.options.stress_exits == 0 || self.stress_exit_countdown.get() != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        self.stress_exit_countdown
            .set(self.stress_random.between(1, self.options.stress_exits));
        true
    }

    /// The results of finished compile jobs to install now, of those that just `finished` and those held back by the
    /// "stress-install" option, which holds each result back for a random number of calls.
    pub(crate) fn compile_results_to_install(&self, finished: Vec<(u64, CompileResult)>) -> Vec<(u64, CompileResult)> {
        if !self.options.stress_install {
            return finished;
        }
        let mut held = self.held_compile_results.borrow_mut();
        for (id, result) in finished {
            held.push((self.stress_random.between(0, MAX_STRESS_INSTALL_DELAY), id, result));
        }
        let mut install = Vec::new();
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < held.len() {
            if held[index].0 == 0 {
                let (_, id, result) = held.remove(index);
                install.push((id, result));
                continue;
            }
            held[index].0 -= 1;
            index += 1;
        }
        install
    }

    /// Whether the "stress-invalidate" option wants an invalidation at this tier-up check.
    pub(crate) fn take_stress_invalidation(&self) -> bool {
        if self.options.stress_invalidate == 0 {
            return false;
        }
        let countdown = self.stress_invalidation_countdown.get().saturating_sub(1);
        if countdown != 0 {
            self.stress_invalidation_countdown.set(countdown);
            return false;
        }
        self.stress_invalidation_countdown
            .set(self.stress_random.between(1, self.options.stress_invalidate));
        true
    }

    /// Where code that is detached from its executable now goes to be dropped once the collection in progress is
    /// over, while drops are deferred. Otherwise it is dropped right away.
    pub(crate) fn parking_for_detached_code(&self) -> Option<&RefCell<DetachedJitCode>> {
        self.defers_code_drops
            .get()
            .then_some(&self.codes_detached_in_collection)
    }

    /// Has the code detached until the returned guard goes away kept until the collection in progress is over, for
    /// the sweep callback of a collection that may still rewrite slots in the code.
    pub(crate) fn defer_code_drops_until_collection_is_over<'a>(&'a self, vm: &Vm) -> CodeDropDeferral<'a> {
        assert!(!self.defers_code_drops.replace(true));
        if self.codes_detached_in_collection.borrow().is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The VM outlives its heap, whose collections run the task.
            unsafe {
                vm.heap().enqueue_post_gc_task(
                    drop_codes_detached_in_collection,
                    core::ptr::from_ref(vm).cast_mut().cast(),
                );
            }
        }
        CodeDropDeferral(self)
    }

    /// With the "coverage" option, counts `key`, which is only formatted then: what compiled code contained when it was
    /// installed (see `libjs_jit::coverage`), and what happened to it ("exit.BadShape", "discard", "osr-entry", ...).
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn count_coverage(&self, key: impl core::fmt::Display) {
        // OPTIMIZATION: Hot paths count, so the check that coverage is off is inlined into them.
        if self.options.coverage.is_none() {
            return;
        }
        self.count_coverage_key(&key.to_string());
    }

    #[cold]
    #[inline(never)]
    fn count_coverage_key(&self, key: &str) {
        *self.coverage.borrow_mut().entry(key.to_owned()).or_default() += 1;
    }

    /// With the "coverage" option, writes the coverage counts into a new file in the coverage directory and starts
    /// counting from zero. VMs do this when they go away; processes that never destroy theirs do it before exiting.
    pub fn flush_coverage(&self) {
        if let Some(directory) = &self.options.coverage
            && !self.coverage.borrow().is_empty()
        {
            self.write_coverage(directory);
            self.coverage.borrow_mut().clear();
        }
    }

    fn write_coverage(&self, directory: &str) {
        static WRITTEN: core::sync::atomic::AtomicU32 = core::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0);
        let number = WRITTEN.fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let mut json = String::from("{");
        for (index, (key, count)) in self.coverage.borrow().iter().enumerate() {
            if index != 0 {
                json.push_str(",\n");
            }
            json.push_str(&format!("\"{}\": {count}", key.replace(['\\', '"'], "_")));
        }
        json.push_str("}\n");
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(directory);
        let path = format!("{directory}/coverage-{}-{number}.json", std::process::id());
        if let Err(error) = std::fs::write(&path, json) {
            eprintln!("LIBJS_JIT: Could not write {path}: {error}");
        }
    }

    /// The results of finished compile jobs the "stress-install" option holds back.
    pub(crate) fn take_held_compile_results(&self) -> Vec<(u64, CompileResult)> {
        self.held_compile_results
            .take()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(_, id, result)| (id, result))
            .collect()
    }

    pub(crate) fn code_allocator(&self) -> &Rc<RefCell<CodeAllocator>> {
        &self.code_allocator
    }

    pub(crate) fn data_allocator(&self) -> &Rc<RefCell<DataAllocator>> {
        &self.data_allocator
    }

    pub(crate) fn compile_queue(&self) -> &CompileQueue {
        self.compile_queue
            .get_or_init(|| CompileQueue::start(self.options.compile_thread_count()))
    }

    /// The compile threads, if a compile job started them.
    pub(crate) fn started_compile_queue(&self) -> Option<&CompileQueue> {
        self.compile_queue.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn add_job(&self, job: CompileJob, _defer_gc: &DeferGc<'_>) -> u64 {
        let id = self.next_job_id.get();
        self.next_job_id.set(id + 1);
        self.jobs.borrow_mut().insert(id, job);
        id
    }

    /// Whether compile jobs run on the compile threads.
    pub(crate) fn has_compile_jobs(&self) -> bool {
        !self.jobs.borrow().is_empty()
    }

    /// Forgets every compile job, whose results are dropped when they finish.
    pub(crate) fn abandon_compile_jobs(&self) {
        self.jobs.borrow_mut().clear();
    }

    /// Forgets the compile job of `executable`, whose result is dropped when it finishes.
    pub(crate) fn abandon_compile_job_of(&self, executable: &Executable) {
        self.jobs
            .borrow_mut()
            .retain(|_, job| !core::ptr::eq(job.executable.as_ptr(), executable));
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_job<'d>(&self, id: u64, defer_gc: &'d DeferGc<'_>) -> Option<Deferred<'d, CompileJob>> {
        self.jobs.borrow_mut().remove(&id).map(|job| defer_gc.cover(job))
    }

    /// The entry trampoline (see `libjs_jit::codegen::generate_entry_trampoline()`).
    pub(crate) fn entry_trampoline(&self) -> EntryTrampoline {
        self.entry_trampoline
            .get_or_init(|| {
                let code = libjs_jit::codegen::generate_entry_trampoline::<libjs_jit::asm::MacroAssembler>()
                    .expect("the entry trampoline can be generated");
                // NB: On Windows, the trampoline goes first in a chunk of its own, whose unwind info then describes
                //     its prologue: native code calls it, and keeps no frame pointer that a stack walk from the
                //     prologue could take for the trampoline's.
                #[cfg(windows)]
                let allocator = Rc::new(RefCell::new(CodeAllocator::default()));
                #[cfg(not(windows))]
                let allocator = Rc::clone(&self.code_allocator);
                let memory =
                    ExecutableMemory::allocate(&allocator, &[&code[..]], &["entry trampoline"], self.options.perf_map)
                        .pop()
                        .expect("one code was allocated");
                // SAFETY: The code is the entry trampoline, with its calling convention.
                let trampoline = unsafe { core::mem::transmute::<*const u8, EntryTrampoline>(memory.address()) };
                (memory, trampoline)
            })
            .1
    }

    /// The address of the call stub for code with this runtime info (whose call stub address is not set yet), or 0.
    pub(crate) fn call_stub(&self, runtime: &libjs_jit::snapshot::RuntimeInfo) -> u64 {
        self.call_stub
            .get_or_init(|| {
                let code = libjs_jit::codegen::generate_call_stub::<libjs_jit::asm::MacroAssembler>(runtime)
                    .expect("the call stub compiles")?;
                ExecutableMemory::allocate(
                    &self.code_allocator,
                    &[&code[..]],
                    &["call stub"],
                    self.options.perf_map,
                )
                .pop()
            })
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(0, |memory| memory.address() as u64)
    }

    /// The address of the construct stub for code with this runtime info, or 0.
    pub(crate) fn construct_stub(&self, runtime: &libjs_jit::snapshot::RuntimeInfo) -> u64 {
        self.construct_stub
            .get_or_init(|| {
                let code = libjs_jit::codegen::generate_construct_stub::<libjs_jit::asm::MacroAssembler>(runtime)
                    .expect("the construct stub compiles")?;
                ExecutableMemory::allocate(
                    &self.code_allocator,
                    &[&code[..]],
                    &["construct stub"],
                    self.options.perf_map,
                )
                .pop()
            })
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(0, |memory| memory.address() as u64)
    }

    pub(crate) fn runtime_function_addresses(&self) -> &runtime_info::RuntimeFunctionAddresses {
        self.runtime_function_addresses
            .get_or_init(runtime_info::RuntimeFunctionAddresses::look_up)
    }
}

impl Drop for JitState {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.flush_coverage();
    }
}

unsafe impl Trace for JitState {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        for job in self.jobs.borrow().values() {
            job.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

/// The name of an executable in logs and perf maps, with the place of its code: "name (file:line:column)" of its
/// first instruction that has a source position, leaving out the file if the source has no name.
pub fn describe_executable(executable: &Executable) -> String {
    let name = crate::utf16::Utf16View::of_fly_string(&executable.name()).to_utf8();
    let name = if name.is_empty() {
        "<anonymous>".to_string()
    } else {
        name
    };
    let Some(entry) = executable.source_positions().find(|entry| entry.line != 0) else {
        return name;
    };
    let filename = executable.source_code().map_or(String::new(), |source_code| {
        crate::utf16::Utf16View::of_string(source_code.filename()).to_utf8()
    });
    if filename.is_empty() {
        return format!("{name} ({}:{})", entry.line, entry.column);
    }
    format!("{name} ({filename}:{}:{})", entry.line, entry.column)
}

/// Defers drops of detached code while it lives (see `JitState::defer_code_drops_until_collection_is_over()`).
pub(crate) struct CodeDropDeferral<'a>(&'a JitState);

impl Drop for CodeDropDeferral<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.defers_code_drops.set(false);
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" fn drop_codes_detached_in_collection(context: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The task was enqueued with the VM as its context.
    let vm = unsafe { &*context.cast::<Vm>() };
    vm.jit.codes_detached_in_collection.borrow_mut().clear();
}

// JIT code compresses and decodes the compressed cell pointers of cells like the runtime does.
const _: () =

/// The addresses of the runtime functions JIT code calls, which every compile job's runtime info has.
pub struct RuntimeFunctionAddresses {
    /// The address of the slow path JIT code calls for each generic opcode, indexed by opcode, or 0 for opcodes
    /// without one (the compiler refuses to compile those generically).
    slow_paths: &'static [u64],
    try_get_by_id_cache: u64,
    try_put_by_id_cache: u64,
    raw_native_exception: u64,
    to_boolean: u64,
}

impl RuntimeFunctionAddresses {
    /// Looks the addresses up in the runtime's function table, which JitState does once (see
    /// `JitState::runtime_function_addresses()`).
    pub fn look_up() -> Self {
        let addresses = runtime_function_addresses();
        let address = |symbol: &str| {
            addresses
                .iter()
                .find(|(name, _)| *name == symbol)
                .map(|(_, address)| *address as u64)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("the runtime has no function {symbol}"))
        };
        // NB: The table holds addresses of functions, which are the same for every VM of the process.
        static SLOW_PATHS: OnceLock<Box<[u64]>> = OnceLock::new();
        Self {
            slow_paths: SLOW_PATHS.get_or_init(|| {
                (0..=u8::MAX)
                    .map_while(OpCode::from_u8)
                    .map(|opcode| slow_path_symbol(opcode).map_or(0, |symbol| address(&symbol.to_string())))
                    .collect()
            }),
            try_get_by_id_cache: address("asm_try_get_by_id_cache"),
            try_put_by_id_cache: address("asm_try_put_by_id_cache"),
            raw_native_exception: if RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTIONS_RETURN_IN_REGISTERS {
                address("asm_helper_handle_raw_native_exception")
            } else {
                0
            },
            to_boolean: address("asm_helper_to_boolean"),
        }
    }
}

/// The runtime info of a compile job for code of `realm`, with what JIT code needs to allocate cells itself (which
/// refers to the cells in `allocation.cells`).
pub fn runtime_info(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    allocation: AllocationInfos<'_>,
    _defer_gc: &DeferGc<'_>,
) -> RuntimeInfo {
    let addresses = vm.jit.runtime_function_addresses();
    let mut layout = runtime_layout();
    layout.try_get_by_id_cache = addresses.try_get_by_id_cache;
    layout.try_put_by_id_cache = addresses.try_put_by_id_cache;
    let keyed_lookup_cache = vm.keyed_property_lookup_cache().jit_layout();
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_entries = keyed_lookup_cache.entries;
    layout.keyed_store_cache_entries = vm.keyed_property_store_cache().jit_layout().entries;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_index_bits = keyed_lookup_cache.index_bits;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_entry_size = keyed_lookup_cache.entry_size;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_entry_type = keyed_lookup_cache.entry_type;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_property_offset = keyed_lookup_cache.property_offset;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_dictionary_generation = keyed_lookup_cache.shape_dictionary_generation;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_shape = keyed_lookup_cache.shape;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_name = keyed_lookup_cache.property_name;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_prototype = keyed_lookup_cache.prototype;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_prototype_chain_validity = keyed_lookup_cache.prototype_chain_validity;
    layout.keyed_lookup_cache_new_shape = keyed_lookup_cache.new_shape;
    layout.single_ascii_character_strings = vm.single_ascii_character_strings_address();
    layout.fly_string_cache = vm.fly_string_cache().as_ptr().expose_provenance() as u64;
    layout.key_concatenation_cache = vm.key_concatenation_cache().as_ptr().expose_provenance() as u64;
    layout.numeric_string_cache = vm.numeric_string_cache().as_ptr().expose_provenance() as u64;
    layout.large_numeric_string_cache = vm.large_numeric_string_cache().as_ptr().expose_provenance() as u64;
    let strings = vm.cached_strings();
    let string = |string| Value::from_string(string).0;
    layout.typeof_strings = TypeofStrings {
        number: string(strings.number),
        undefined: string(strings.undefined),
        object: string(strings.object),
        string: string(strings.string),
        symbol: string(strings.symbol),
        boolean: string(strings.boolean),
        bigint: string(strings.bigint),
        function: string(strings.function),
    };
    let mut info = RuntimeInfo {
        no_htmldda_objects: !vm.jit.htmldda_objects_exist(),
        slow_paths: addresses.slow_paths,
        jit_call: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_call),
        call_forwarding_arguments: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_call_forwarding_arguments),
        finish_direct_call: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_finish_direct_call),
        prepare_construct: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_prepare_construct),
        construct_result_error: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_construct_result_error),
        finish_direct_construct: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_finish_direct_construct),
        construct_stub: 0,
        construct_this: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_construct_this),
        throw_call_stack_size_exceeded: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_throw_call_stack_size_exceeded),
        raw_native_exception: addresses.raw_native_exception,
        push_inlined_call_frames: jit_function_address!(super::entry_exit::libjs_jit_push_inlined_call_frames),
        finish_inlined_direct_call: jit_function_address!(super::entry_exit::libjs_jit_finish_inlined_direct_call),
        inlined_raw_native_exception: if RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTIONS_RETURN_IN_REGISTERS {
            jit_function_address!(super::entry_exit::libjs_jit_inlined_raw_native_exception)
        } else {
            0
        },
        array_push: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_array_push),
        array_splice: jit_function_address!(super::intrinsics::libjs_jit_array_splice),
        store_holey_element: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_store_holey_element),
        slice_arguments: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_slice_arguments),
        open_array_iteration: jit_function_address!(super::intrinsics::libjs_jit_open_array_iteration),
        // NB: Filled in by capture_snapshot(), which lists the cells as embedded cells.
        array_iterator_next: None,
        array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set: None,
        array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set_address: None,
        array_iterator_method_watchpoint_set_address: None,
        jit_exit: jit_function_address!(super::entry_exit::libjs_jit_exit),
        to_boolean: addresses.to_boolean,
        primitive_to_string: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_primitive_to_string),
        helper_calls: HelperCallAddresses(super::helper_calls::address),
        float64_functions: Float64FunctionAddresses(super::calls::float64_function_address),
        to_object: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_to_object),
        remember_vm_cache_get: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_remember_vm_cache_get),
        array_create: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_array_create),
        intrinsic_helpers: IntrinsicHelpers {
            has_own_property: jit_function_address!(super::intrinsics::libjs_jit_has_own_property),
            has_property: jit_function_address!(super::intrinsics::libjs_jit_has_property),
        },
        create_arguments: jit_function_address!(super::entry_exit::libjs_jit_create_arguments),
        object_allocation: allocation.object,
        array_allocation: allocation.array,
        rope_allocation: allocation.rope,
        function_allocation: allocation.function,
        create_lexical_environment: jit_function_address!(super::allocation::libjs_jit_create_lexical_environment),
        realm: CellId(realm.as_ptr() as u64),
        array_prototype: CellId(realm.array_prototype().as_ptr() as u64),
        object_prototype: CellId(realm.object_prototype().as_ptr() as u64),
        array_constructor: CellId(realm.intrinsics().array_constructor(vm).as_ptr() as u64),
        no_yield_continuation: ExecutionContext::NO_YIELD_CONTINUATION,
        heap_region_base: vm.head.heap_region_base.get() as u64,
        heap_region_offset_mask: HEAP_REGION_OFFSET_MASK,
        primitive_storage_cage_base: vm.head.primitive_storage_cage_base.get() as u64,
        shifted_is_cell_pattern: nan_box::SHIFTED_IS_CELL_PATTERN,
        object_flag_is_function: object_flag::IS_FUNCTION,
        offsets: runtime_offsets(),
        layout,
        dynamic_calls: dynamic_call_layout(vm),
    };
    info.dynamic_calls.call_stub = vm.jit.call_stub(&info);
    info.construct_stub = vm.jit.construct_stub(&info);
    info
}

/// Whether raw native functions return their completion in two registers, the way JIT code calls them. Elsewhere they
/// return it through a pointer, and JIT code leaves calls of them to the runtime.
pub const RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTIONS_RETURN_IN_REGISTERS: bool = !cfg!(any(
    all(target_arch = "x86_64", target_vendor = "apple"),
    target_os = "windows"
));

fn dynamic_call_layout(vm: &Vm) -> DynamicCallLayout {
    let entry_table = vm
        .jit
        .entry_table
        .as_ref()
        .expect("the VM has a JIT entry table while the JIT is on");
    DynamicCallLayout {
        object_flag_is_ecmascript_function: object_flag::IS_ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION_OBJECT,
        ecmascript_function_shared_data: offset(ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION_OBJECT_SHARED_DATA_OFFSET),
        shared_data_executable: offset(offset_of!(SharedFunctionInstanceData, executable)),
        shared_data_asm_call_metadata: offset(offset_of!(SharedFunctionInstanceData, asm_call_metadata)),
        executable_jit_entry_slot: offset(offset_of!(ExecutableHead, jit_entry_slot)),
        jit_entry_table: entry_table.address(),
        jit_entry_slot_mask: JIT_ENTRY_SLOT_MASK,
        jit_entry_table_owners: offset(JIT_ENTRY_TABLE_OWNERS_OFFSET),
        metadata_can_inline_call: asm_call_metadata::CAN_INLINE_CALL,
        metadata_needs_environment_or_this_value_resolution:
            asm_call_metadata::NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_OR_THIS_VALUE_RESOLUTION,
        metadata_uses_this: asm_call_metadata::USES_THIS,
        metadata_strict: asm_call_metadata::STRICT,
        executable_registers_and_locals_and_constants_count: offset(offset_of!(
            ExecutableHead,
            registers_and_locals_and_constants_count
        )),
        shape_realm: offset(offset_of!(Shape, realm)),
        object_flag_is_raw_native_function: if RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTIONS_RETURN_IN_REGISTERS {
            object_flag::IS_RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTION
        } else {
            0
        },
        raw_native_function_index: offset(offset_of!(NativeFunction, raw_native_function_index)),
        vm_native_function_table: offset(offset_of!(VmHead, native_function_table_data)),
        native_function_table_index_mask: NATIVE_FUNCTION_TABLE_INDEX_MASK,
        native_function_table_entry_size: offset(size_of::<NativeFunctionTableEntry>()),
        native_function_table_entry_function: offset(offset_of!(NativeFunctionTableEntry, function)),
        prepare_call_environment: jit_function_address!(super::calls::libjs_jit_prepare_call_environment),
        shared_data_call_environment_template: offset(offset_of!(
            SharedFunctionInstanceData,
            call_environment_template
        )),
        call_environment_template_size_class: offset(offset_of!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, size_class)),
        function_environment_free_lists: vm.jit.function_environment_free_lists.address(vm),
        function_environment_size_class_mask: offset(FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_FREE_LIST_COUNT - 1),
        call_environment_template_cell_size: offset(offset_of!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, cell_size)),
        call_environment_template_binding_values_offset: offset(offset_of!(
            CallEnvironmentTemplate,
            binding_values_offset
        )),
        call_environment_template_binds_this: offset(offset_of!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, binds_this)),
        call_environment_template_has_function_fields: offset(offset_of!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, has_function_fields)),
        call_environment_template_words: offset(offset_of!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, words)),
        function_environment_words: offset(FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_WORDS),
        declarative_environment_words: offset(size_of::<DeclarativeEnvironment>() / 8),
        function_environment_binding_values: offset(offset_of!(DeclarativeEnvironment, binding_values)),
        function_environment_outer: offset(offset_of!(Environment, outer)),
        function_environment_function_object: offset(FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_FUNCTION_OBJECT_OFFSET),
        function_environment_this_value: offset(FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_THIS_VALUE_OFFSET),
        call_stub: 0,
    }
}

/// Candidates with at most this many bytecode instructions are always inlined, without counting against the inlining
/// budget.
const ALWAYS_INLINED_INSTRUCTION_COUNT: u32 = 10;

/// Constructors of at most this many instructions are inlined into their constructs (see
/// `InliningLimits::max_construct_instructions`).
const MAX_INLINED_CONSTRUCT_INSTRUCTION_COUNT: u32 = 50;

/// A snapshot with the cells it refers to, which must stay alive (and in place) until the job's code is installed or
/// the job is abandoned.
pub struct CapturedSnapshot<'d> {
    pub snapshot: Box<Snapshot>,
    pub cells: Deferred<'d, Vec<Gc<CellHeader>>>,
    pub snapshot_executables: Deferred<'d, Vec<SnapshotExecutable>>,
    /// The slots of the samples of the closure templates, whose samples are among the cells.
    pub sample_slots: Deferred<'d, SampleSlots>,
}

/// An executable of the snapshot.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Entry {
    executable: Gc<Executable>,
    /// None for the executable being compiled.
    function: Option<InlinedFunction>,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    depth: u32,
}

struct SnapshotBuilder<'vm> {
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    defer_gc: &'vm DeferGc<'vm>,
    /// The snapshot that is being captured.
    snapshot: SnapshotWriter<'vm>,
    cells: Vec<Gc<CellHeader>>,
    entries: Vec<Entry>,
    indices: HashMap<InlinedFunction, u32>,
    /// The function the compiled executable runs, or `None` for the top-level code of a script or of a module.
    compiled_function: Option<Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>>,
    /// The words the compiled executable's frames start with (see `FunctionFrameFields`).
    compiled_function_fields: FunctionFrameFields,
    /// The closure templates of the compiled executable.
    closure_templates: List<Option<ClosureTemplateSnapshot>>,
    /// The samples of the closure templates of inlined functions, by executable and template index, until the
    /// inlining candidates they are get their indices.
    closure_samples: Vec<(u32, usize, Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>)>,
    sample_slots: SampleSlots,
    /// The lexical environment templates of the compiled executable.
    lexical_environment_templates: List<Option<LexicalEnvironmentTemplateSnapshot>>,
    /// The environment templates of the direct calls of the executable whose snapshot is being made.
    environment_templates: Vec<EnvironmentTemplateSnapshot>,
    /// The bound arguments of the call feedback of the executable whose snapshot is being made.
    bound_arguments: Vec<u64>,
    /// For the constructors among the inlining candidates, by index: the shape of the `this` value their inlined
    /// constructs create, whose entries their megamorphic caches describe.
    construct_this_shapes: HashMap<u32, Gc<Shape>>,
    /// For the derived constructors among the inlining candidates, by index: what their super() constructs with in
    /// inlined constructs of them (see `ExecutableSnapshot::super_constructor`).
    super_constructors: HashMap<u32, SuperConstructTarget>,
    /// For the base constructors with fields among the inlining candidates, by index: the values of their fields (see
    /// `ExecutableSnapshot::literal_instance_fields`).
    literal_instance_fields: HashMap<u32, LiteralFieldValues>,
    /// For the derived constructors with fields among the inlining candidates, by index: how they add their fields
    /// (see `ExecutableSnapshot::derived_instance_fields`).
    derived_instance_fields: HashMap<u32, DerivedInstanceFields>,
}

/// The property offset of a literal field, its value, and the shape its definition gives the object if it adds the
/// property, if asked for (see `SnapshotBuilder::literal_field_definitions()`).
type FieldDefinition = (u32, u64, Option<CellId>);

/// The values of literal fields, by property offset (see `ExecutableSnapshot::literal_instance_fields`).
type LiteralFieldValues = List<(u32, u64)>;

/// The number of bytecode instructions of an executable, counted up to one past `limit`.
fn instruction_count(executable: &Executable, limit: u32) -> u32 {
    let bytecode = executable.bytecode();
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < bytecode.len() && count <= limit {
        let Ok(length) = instruction_length_from_bytes(bytecode[offset], bytecode, offset) else {
            break;
        };
        offset += length;
        count += 1;
    }
    count
}

pub(crate) fn ecmascript_function(cell: Option<Gc<CellHeader>>) -> Option<Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>> {
    as_ecmascript_function_object(cell?.downcast::<Object>()?)
}

/// The target of a call site if it is a builtin written in JavaScript that JIT code can inline: a normal function
/// without a function environment of the caller's realm, which already ran.
fn builtin_inlining_candidate(
    target: Option<Gc<CellHeader>>,
    caller_realm: Gc<Realm>,
) -> Option<Gc<NativeJavaScriptBackedFunction>> {
    let builtin = target?.downcast::<NativeJavaScriptBackedFunction>()?;
    let shared_data = builtin.shared_data();
    (shared_data.kind() == FunctionKind::Normal
        && !builtin.function_environment_needed()
        && shared_data.executable().is_some()
        && builtin.realm() == caller_realm)
        .then_some(builtin)
}

/// The intrinsic the compiler knows an object as, if it is one.
fn intrinsic_of(vm: &Vm, cell: Option<Gc<CellHeader>>) -> Option<Intrinsic> {
    let cell = cell?;
    if cell.downcast::<StringConstructor>().is_some() {
        return Some(Intrinsic::StringConstructor);
    }
    if cell.downcast::<ArrayConstructor>().is_some() {
        return Some(Intrinsic::ArrayConstructor);
    }
    if cell.downcast::<ObjectConstructor>().is_some() {
        return Some(Intrinsic::ObjectConstructor);
    }
    if cell.downcast::<BooleanConstructor>().is_some() {
        return Some(Intrinsic::BooleanConstructor);
    }
    let function = cell.downcast::<RawNativeFunction>()?;
    match function.builtin() {
        Some(Builtin::StringFromCharCode) => return Some(Intrinsic::StringFromCharCode),
        Some(Builtin::RegExpPrototypeExec) => return Some(Intrinsic::RegExpPrototypeExec),
        _ => {}
    }
    let address = function.native_function(vm)? as usize;
    NATIVE_INTRINSICS
        .iter()
        .find(|(native_function, _)| native_function.is_some_and(|native_function| native_function as usize == address))
        .map(|(_, intrinsic)| *intrinsic)
}

/// The intrinsics the compiler knows by their native functions (of any realm).
static NATIVE_INTRINSICS: [(&RawNativeFunctionPointer, Intrinsic); 24] = [
    (&function_prototype::APPLY_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeApply),
    (&function_prototype::CALL_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::FunctionPrototypeCall),
    (&array_prototype::PUSH_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypePush),
    (&array_prototype::SLICE_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypeSlice),
    (&array_prototype::SPLICE_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::ArrayPrototypeSplice),
    (
        &object_prototype::HAS_OWN_PROPERTY_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::ObjectPrototypeHasOwnProperty,
    ),
    (
        &typed_array_prototype::LENGTH_GETTER,
        Intrinsic::TypedArrayPrototypeLength,
    ),
    (&math_object::MAX_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::MathMax),
    (&math_object::MIN_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::MathMin),
    (&math_object::IMUL_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::MathImul),
    (&string_prototype::INDEX_OF_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::StringPrototypeIndexOf),
    (
        &string_prototype::TO_LOWERCASE_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeToLowerCase,
    ),
    (
        &string_prototype::TO_UPPERCASE_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeToUpperCase,
    ),
    (
        &string_prototype::LAST_INDEX_OF_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeLastIndexOf,
    ),
    (&string_prototype::INCLUDES_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::StringPrototypeIncludes),
    (
        &string_prototype::STARTS_WITH_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeStartsWith,
    ),
    (
        &string_prototype::ENDS_WITH_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeEndsWith,
    ),
    (&string_prototype::SLICE_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::StringPrototypeSlice),
    (
        &string_prototype::SUBSTRING_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeSubstring,
    ),
    (&string_prototype::TRIM_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrim),
    (
        &string_prototype::TRIM_START_FUNCTION,
        Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrimStart,
    ),
    (&string_prototype::TRIM_END_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::StringPrototypeTrimEnd),
    (&map_prototype::GET_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::MapPrototypeGet),
    (&map_prototype::HAS_FUNCTION, Intrinsic::MapPrototypeHas),
];

/// The builtin `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next` of the realm, if `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%` holds it.
fn array_iterator_next(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<FunctionObject>> {
    let next = realm
        .array_iterator_prototype()
        .get_without_side_effects(vm, &vm.names.next);
    if !next.is_function() {
        return None;
    }
    let next = next.as_function();
    (next.as_native_function().is_some() && next.is_array_prototype_next_builtin()).then_some(next)
}

/// The object the holder of a prototype chain lookup cache entry has in the property the entry describes, if the entry
/// is still valid and the property holds an object (such as a method).
fn prototype_property_object(entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> Option<Gc<Object>> {
    if entry.entry_type != PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain {
        return None;
    }
    let value = prototype_property_value(entry)?;
    value.is_object().then(|| value.as_object())
}

/// Whether the own property an entry reads or writes is writable in the shape of the object, which makes it a data
/// property for as long as the object keeps the shape (see `Object::storage_set()`). Loads of the properties of
/// prototypes always check, as they are guarded by no check of the object they load from.
fn property_holds_data(entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> bool {
    if !matches!(
        entry.entry_type,
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty
    ) {
        return false;
    }
    let Some(ShapeKey { shape, .. }) = entry.shape else {
        return false;
    };
    let mut writable = false;
    shape.for_each_property_in_insertion_order(|_, metadata| {
        if metadata.offset != entry.property_offset {
            return core::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(());
        }
        writable = metadata.attributes.is_writable();
        core::ops::ControlFlow::Break(())
    });
    writable
}

/// The value the prototype of a GetPropertyInPrototypeChain or ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain entry holds in the
/// property, if the entry still applies.
fn prototype_property_value(entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> Option<Value> {
    if !matches!(
        entry.entry_type,
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain
            | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain
    ) {
        return None;
    }
    let holder = entry.prototype?;
    if !entry.prototype_chain_validity?.is_valid() {
        return None;
    }
    if holder.shape().is_dictionary() || entry.property_offset >= holder.shape().property_count() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(holder.get_direct(entry.property_offset))
}

/// The function of the accessor an entry calls: for a GetPropertyInPrototypeChain
/// entry, the getter of the accessor its prototype holds in the property, for a ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain entry
/// its setter, and for a GetOwnProperty entry the getter the interpreter last called.
fn entry_accessor_function(entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> Option<Gc<FunctionObject>> {
    let (accessor, setter) = match entry.entry_type {
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty if entry.key == 0 => return entry.getter,
        entry_type => {
            let value = prototype_property_value(entry)?;
            if !value.is_accessor() {
                return None;
            }
            (
                value.as_accessor(),
                entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain,
            )
        }
    };
    if setter { accessor.setter() } else { accessor.getter() }
}

/// Whether the property of an entry held an accessor: the accessor the interpreter last called the getter of for a
/// GetOwnProperty entry, or the value its prototype holds in the property for entries of a prototype.
fn entry_holds_accessor(entry: &PropertyLookupCacheEntryData) -> bool {
    match entry.entry_type {
        PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty if entry.key == 0 => entry.getter.is_some(),
        _ => prototype_property_value(entry).is_some_and(|value| value.is_accessor()),
    }
}

/// The target of a call site if JIT code can call it directly, building its frame the way the interpreter's call
/// fast path does, and the function environment as libjs_jit_prepare_call_environment() does if it needs one, with
/// whether the site also called other closures of it.
fn direct_call_target(feedback: &CallFeedback) -> Option<(Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>, bool)> {
    let flags = feedback.flags.get();
    let closures = flags & call_feedback_flags::POLYMORPHIC != 0;
    if closures && flags & (call_feedback_flags::OTHER_FUNCTIONS | call_feedback_flags::SAW_NATIVE) != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let function = ecmascript_function(feedback.target())?;
    function.can_inline_call().then_some((function, closures))
}

/// The target of a call site if it is a native function, which JIT code can call directly in the frame the
/// interpreter's call fast path builds for it, or replace with an intrinsic, and the entry it calls it at, if it can:
/// none where native functions do not return their completion in two registers, and JIT code leaves calls of them to
/// the runtime. Function.prototype.call and apply forward their calls, which the runtime does for JIT code.
fn native_call_target(vm: &Vm, feedback: &CallFeedback) -> Option<(Gc<NativeFunction>, Option<NonZeroU64>)> {
    if feedback.flags.get() & call_feedback_flags::POLYMORPHIC != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let function = feedback.target()?.downcast::<NativeFunction>()?;
    let entry = if let Some(raw) = function.downcast::<RawNativeFunction>() {
        if FunctionPrototype::is_call_function(vm, &raw) || FunctionPrototype::is_apply_function(vm, &raw) {
            return None;
        }
        raw.native_function(vm)
    } else {
        function.capturing_call_entry()
    };
    let entry = entry
        .filter(|_| RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTIONS_RETURN_IN_REGISTERS)
        .and_then(|pointer| NonZeroU64::new(pointer as usize as u64));
    Some((function, entry))
}

/// The words of an ECMAScript function its frames start with, which stay the same for its lifetime.
fn function_frame_fields(function: Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>) -> FunctionFrameFields {
    let shared_data = function.shared_data();
    FunctionFrameFields {
        script_or_module: shared_data.script_or_module.word(),
        environment: function
            .environment()
            .map_or(0, |environment| environment.as_ptr() as u64),
    }
}

/// Adds `cell` to `cells`, the cells a snapshot refers to, and returns what the snapshot knows it as.
fn note_cell<T: Extends<CellHeader>>(cells: &mut Vec<Gc<CellHeader>>, cell: Gc<T>) -> CellId {
    cells.push(cell.upcast::<CellHeader>());
    CellId(cell.as_ptr() as u64)
}

/// Adds the environment of `function`, whose address its FunctionFrameFields hold, to `cells`.
fn note_frame_field_cells(cells: &mut Vec<Gc<CellHeader>>, function: Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>) {
    if let Some(environment) = function.environment() {
        note_cell(cells, environment);
    }
}

impl SnapshotBuilder<'_> {
    fn cell<T: Extends<CellHeader>>(&mut self, cell: Gc<T>) -> CellId {
        note_cell(&mut self.cells, cell)
    }

    /// The bits of `value`, whose cell, if it has one, is added to the cells the snapshot refers to.
    fn value_bits(&mut self, value: Value) -> u64 {
        if value.is_cell() {
            note_cell(&mut self.cells, value.as_cell());
        }
        value.0
    }

    /// function_frame_fields() of `function`, whose environment is added to the cells the snapshot refers to.
    fn frame_fields(&mut self, function: Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>) -> FunctionFrameFields {
        note_frame_field_cells(&mut self.cells, function);
        function_frame_fields(function)
    }

    /// Adds `rows` to the snapshot as a list.
    fn list<T: Row>(&mut self, rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = T>) -> List<T> {
        let list = self.snapshot.begin();
        for row in rows {
            self.snapshot.push(row);
        }
        self.snapshot.end(list)
    }

    fn optional_cell<T: Extends<CellHeader>>(&mut self, cell: Option<Gc<T>>) -> Option<CellId> {
        cell.map(|cell| self.cell(cell))
    }

    fn shape(&mut self, shape: Gc<Shape>) -> ShapeSnapshot {
        ShapeSnapshot {
            shape: self.cell(shape),
            property_count: shape.property_count(),
        }
    }

    /// What property lookup cache `cache` of `caller` knows. Of a megamorphic cache, that is the entry for
    /// `known_shape` if it has one: JIT code only uses megamorphic entries for objects whose shape it knows.
    fn property_cache(
        &mut self,
        cache: &PropertyLookupCache,
        caller: &Entry,
        known_shape: Option<Gc<Shape>>,
    ) -> PropertyCacheSnapshot {
        let kind = match cache.tier() {
            PropertyLookupCacheTier::Empty => PropertyCacheKind::Empty,
            PropertyLookupCacheTier::Monomorphic => PropertyCacheKind::Monomorphic,
            PropertyLookupCacheTier::Polymorphic => PropertyCacheKind::Polymorphic,
            PropertyLookupCacheTier::Megamorphic => PropertyCacheKind::Megamorphic,
        };
        // NB: The interpreter caches the properties strings, numbers and booleans get from their prototypes as
        //     properties of those prototypes. JIT code speculating on such entries would check for an object and exit
        //     for every primitive, so caches with them are left to the fast paths, which look these up themselves.
        let realm = caller.realm;
        let primitive_prototype_shapes = [
            realm.string_prototype(self.vm).shape(),
            realm.number_prototype(self.vm).shape(),
            realm.boolean_prototype(self.vm).shape(),
        ];
        let mut sees_primitives = false;
        let entries = self.snapshot.begin();
        let known_shape_slot = known_shape.and_then(|shape| cache.megamorphic_entry_for_shape(shape, 0));
        let slots = match known_shape_slot {
            Some(slot) => core::slice::from_ref(slot),
            None => cache.entries(),
        };
        for slot in slots {
            let entry = slot.get();
            let shape = entry.shape.map(|key| key.shape);
            if shape.is_some_and(|shape| primitive_prototype_shapes.contains(&shape)) {
                sees_primitives = true;
                continue;
            }
            let entry_type = match entry.entry_type {
                // NB: Only the VM's keyed property lookup cache has entries for missing own properties.
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::Empty | PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::MissingOwnProperty => continue,
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty => PropertyCacheEntryType::AddOwnProperty,
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty => PropertyCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty,
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty => PropertyCacheEntryType::GetOwnProperty,
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                    PropertyCacheEntryType::ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain
                }
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain => {
                    PropertyCacheEntryType::GetPropertyInPrototypeChain
                }
                // NB: Like the interpreter, compiled code relies on an entry for a missing property only where the
                //     property is also missing from an unchanged prototype chain, which an entry without a prototype
                //     chain validity can only tell for shapes without a prototype.
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty
                    if entry.prototype_chain_validity.is_none()
                        && shape.is_some_and(|shape| shape.prototype().is_some()) =>
                {
                    continue;
                }
                PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty => PropertyCacheEntryType::GetMissingProperty,
            };
            let prototype_property = prototype_property_object(&entry);
            let cached_value_offset = prototype_property_value(&entry)
                .filter(|value| value.is_accessor() && value.as_accessor().cache_on_receiver())
                .and_then(|value| value.as_accessor().cached_value_key())
                .and_then(|key| shape?.lookup(&PropertyKey::from_symbol(key)))
                .map(|metadata| metadata.offset);
            let accessor_function = entry_accessor_function(&entry).map(|function| {
                let cell = self.cell(function);
                AccessorFunctionSnapshot {
                    cached_value_offset,
                    function: cell,
                    intrinsic: intrinsic_of(self.vm, Some(Value::from_object(function.upcast::<Object>()).as_cell())),
                    inline_executable: self.inline_executable_index(
                        Some(Value::from_object(function.upcast::<Object>()).as_cell()),
                        caller,
                    ),
                    native: self.native_accessor_target(function, cell, entry.getter == Some(function)),
                }
            });
            let row = PropertyCacheEntrySnapshot {
                entry_type,
                property_offset: entry.property_offset,
                shape_dictionary_generation: entry.shape.map_or(0, |key| key.dictionary_generation),
                shape_is_dictionary: shape.is_some_and(|shape| shape.is_dictionary()),
                shape_is_stable: shape.is_some_and(|shape| shape.is_stable()),
                writes_data_property: entry.writes_data_property,
                new_shape: self.optional_cell(entry.new_shape),
                shape: self.optional_cell(shape),
                prototype: self.optional_cell(entry.prototype),
                prototype_chain_validity: self.optional_cell(entry.prototype_chain_validity),
                prototype_chain_valid: entry
                    .prototype_chain_validity
                    .is_some_and(|validity| validity.is_valid()),
                key: (entry.key != 0).then(|| self.cell(Value::from_bits(entry.key).as_cell())),
                key_value: entry.key,
                prototype_property: self.optional_cell(prototype_property),
                prototype_property_intrinsic: intrinsic_of(
                    self.vm,
                    prototype_property.map(|object| Value::from_object(object).as_cell()),
                ),
                prototype_property_inline_executable: prototype_property.and_then(|object| {
                    self.inline_executable_index(Some(Value::from_object(object).as_cell()), caller)
                }),
                prototype_property_direct_call: prototype_property
                    .and_then(|object| self.prototype_method_direct_call(object)),
                // NB: Watching a slot allocates, which collects no garbage while the snapshot is taken. Slots
                //     replaced while watched are checked instead, as invalidated code learns nothing, while the
                //     check learns from its exit.
                prototype_property_watchpoint: prototype_property
                    .and(entry.prototype)
                    .filter(|holder| !holder.shape().was_slot_replaced(entry.property_offset))
                    .and_then(|holder| {
                        holder
                            .shape()
                            .watch_slot_for_replacements(self.vm, entry.property_offset)
                    })
                    .map(|set| self.cell(set)),
                accessor_function,
                property_holds_data: property_holds_data(&entry),
                holds_accessor: entry_holds_accessor(&entry),
            };
            self.snapshot.push(row);
        }
        if sees_primitives {
            self.snapshot.drop_rows(&entries);
        }
        PropertyCacheSnapshot {
            kind,
            entries: self.snapshot.end(entries),
        }
    }

    /// What the global variable caches of `executable`, whose frames run in the realm of `caller`, know about the global
    /// variables of the realm, as far as it still holds.
    fn globals(&mut self, executable: Gc<Executable>, caller: &Entry) -> GlobalsSnapshot {
        let realm = caller.realm;
        let object = realm.global_object();
        let environment = realm.global_declarative_environment();
        let environment_serial = environment.environment_serial_number();
        let shape = object.shape();
        let caches = self.snapshot.begin();
        for cache in executable.global_variable_caches() {
            let row = self.global_cache(cache, object, environment, environment_serial, shape, caller);
            self.snapshot.push(row);
        }
        let caches = self.snapshot.end(caches);
        GlobalsSnapshot {
            object: self.cell(object),
            declarative_environment: self.cell(environment),
            environment_serial,
            caches,
        }
    }

    /// What a global variable cache found, like `GetGlobal` and `SetGlobal` use it, if it still applies.
    fn global_cache(
        &mut self,
        cache: &GlobalVariableCache,
        object: Gc<Object>,
        environment: Gc<DeclarativeEnvironment>,
        environment_serial: u64,
        shape: Gc<Shape>,
        caller: &Entry,
    ) -> Option<GlobalCacheSnapshot> {
        let realm = caller.realm;
        if cache.environment_serial_number.get() != environment_serial {
            return None;
        }
        if let Some(entry) = cache.first_entry()
            && entry.shape == Some(ShapeKey::of(shape))
        {
            let value = object.get_direct(entry.property_offset);
            if value.is_accessor() {
                return None;
            }
            return Some(GlobalCacheSnapshot::Property {
                shape: self.cell(shape),
                dictionary_generation: shape.is_dictionary().then(|| shape.dictionary_generation()),
                offset: entry.property_offset,
                writes_data_property: entry.entry_type == PropertyLookupCacheEntryType::ChangeOwnProperty
                    && entry.writes_data_property,
                assigned: super::dependencies::global_object_slot_may_have_been_assigned(
                    self.vm,
                    &object,
                    entry.property_offset,
                ),
                value: self.global_value(value, realm, Some(caller)),
            });
        }
        if !cache.has_environment_binding_index.get() {
            return None;
        }
        let index = cache.environment_binding_index.get();
        let value = environment.get_initialized_binding_value_direct(index as usize);
        Some(GlobalCacheSnapshot::Binding {
            index,
            mutable: environment.binding_is_mutable(index as usize),
            assigned: environment.binding_may_have_been_assigned(index as usize),
            value: (!value.is_empty()).then(|| self.global_value(value, realm, Some(caller))),
        })
    }

    /// The value of a global variable. Functions are inlining candidates of the call sites of `caller`, if given,
    /// since the code may call them after passing them on, which no call feedback of `caller` records.
    fn global_value(&mut self, value: Value, realm: Gc<Realm>, caller: Option<&Entry>) -> GlobalValueSnapshot {
        let cell = value.is_cell().then(|| value.as_cell());
        GlobalValueSnapshot {
            bits: value.0,
            inline_executable: caller.and_then(|caller| self.inline_executable_index(cell, caller)),
            cell: cell.map(|cell| self.cell(cell)),
            intrinsic: intrinsic_of(self.vm, cell),
            has_instance: self.ordinary_has_instance(value, realm),
            typed_array: value
                .is_object()
                .then(|| value.as_object().downcast::<TypedArrayBase>())
                .flatten()
                .and_then(|array| {
                    use crate::runtime::typed_array::Kind;
                    use libjs_jit::ir::TypedArrayElement;
                    let element = match array.kind() {
                        Kind::Uint8Array => TypedArrayElement::Uint8,
                        Kind::Uint8ClampedArray => TypedArrayElement::Uint8Clamped,
                        Kind::Int8Array => TypedArrayElement::Int8,
                        Kind::Uint16Array => TypedArrayElement::Uint16,
                        Kind::Int16Array => TypedArrayElement::Int16,
                        Kind::Uint32Array => TypedArrayElement::Uint32,
                        Kind::Int32Array => TypedArrayElement::Int32,
                        Kind::Float32Array => TypedArrayElement::Float32,
                        Kind::Float64Array => TypedArrayElement::Float64,
                        _ => return None,
                    };
                    Some(TypedArraySnapshot {
                        element,
                        fixed_length: (array.cached_data_offset() != TYPED_ARRAY_CACHED_DATA_OFFSET_INVALID)
                            .then(|| array.array_length.length.get())
                            .and_then(|length| u32::try_from(length).ok()),
                    })
                }),
        }
    }

    /// How `instanceof` with `value` on its right-hand side runs, if `value` is a function that inherits the
    /// `@@hasInstance` of `%Function.prototype%` of `realm`, which is neither writable nor configurable: its shape, which
    /// tells that while the function keeps it, and where its `prototype` property is.
    fn ordinary_has_instance(&mut self, value: Value, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<OrdinaryHasInstanceSnapshot> {
        if !value.is_function() || value.as_function().downcast::<BoundFunction>().is_some() {
            return None;
        }
        let function = value.as_object();
        let shape = function.shape();
        let has_instance = PropertyKey::from(self.vm.well_known_symbols().has_instance);
        if !function.has_ordinary_get_own_property_for(self.vm, &has_instance)
            || shape.prototype() != Some(realm.function_prototype())
            || shape.lookup(&has_instance).is_some()
        {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: ECMAScript functions create their prototype property lazily, but one in their shape is the one they have.
        let prototype = shape.lookup(&self.vm.names.prototype)?;
        if function.get_direct(prototype.offset).is_accessor() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(OrdinaryHasInstanceSnapshot {
            shape: self.cell(shape),
            dictionary_generation: shape.is_dictionary().then(|| shape.dictionary_generation()),
            prototype_offset: prototype.offset,
        })
    }

    fn inlined_function(&mut self, function: Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>) -> InlinedFunctionSnapshot {
        let realm = function.realm().expect("an ECMAScript function has a realm");
        let executable = function
            .bytecode_executable()
            .expect("an inlined function has an executable");
        InlinedFunctionSnapshot {
            function: self.cell(function),
            formal_parameter_count: function.formal_parameter_count(),
            strict: executable.is_strict_mode(),
            // NB: Arrow functions resolve `this` through their environments.
            uses_this: function.uses_this() && function.this_mode() != ThisMode::Lexical,
            global_this: self.cell(realm.global_environment().global_this_value()),
            realm: self.cell(realm),
            shared_data: self.cell(function.shared_data()),
            super_base: self.super_base(function),
            // NB: Arrow functions resolve new.target through their environments.
            has_own_new_target: function.this_mode() != ThisMode::Lexical,
        }
    }

    /// The base of `super` property access in `function`, if its home object gets its prototype from its shape.
    fn super_base(&mut self, function: Gc<EcmascriptFunctionObject>) -> Option<SuperBaseSnapshot> {
        let home = function.home_object()?;
        let home_shape = home.shape();
        if home_shape.is_dictionary() || !home.has_ordinary_get_prototype_of() {
            return None;
        }
        Some(SuperBaseSnapshot {
            home: self.cell(home),
            home_shape: self.cell(home_shape),
