//! Interpreter feedback consumed by the optimizing JIT, as the profiling interpreter records it. Every instruction
//! that collects feedback carries one slot index per feedback kind it records, and each kind has its own array, which
//! `ExecutableFeedbackHead` points the interpreter at.

use core::cell::Cell;

use super::cell::{CellHeader, Gc};

/// Every executable has a tier-up budget that the interpreter counts down: entering the executable costs
/// `FUNCTION_ENTRY` and every loop back edge costs `LOOP_ITERATION`. A threshold of N therefore means N invocations,
/// with every FUNCTION_ENTRY / LOOP_ITERATION loop iterations counting as one more invocation.
pub mod tier_up_costs {
    pub const FUNCTION_ENTRY: i32 = 16;
    pub const LOOP_ITERATION: i32 = 1;
}

/// Where the interpreter finds an executable's feedback arrays, as offsets into the primitive storage cage, which the
/// interpreter masks every address it forms from them into. The executable owns the arrays.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ExecutableFeedbackHead {
    pub arith: Cell<u64>,
    pub value_buckets: Cell<u64>,
    pub call: Cell<u64>,
    pub keyed: Cell<u64>,
}

impl ExecutableFeedbackHead {
    pub const fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            arith: Cell::new(0),
            value_buckets: Cell::new(0),
            call: Cell::new(0),
            keyed: Cell::new(0),
        }
    }
}

/// The union of the operand kinds seen by an arithmetic, comparison or unary operation, as `ArithFeedback` bits.
/// `INT32_OVERFLOW` means that the operation produced a result that is not an int32 (overflow, negative zero or a
/// fraction) on a path that int32 operands take.
pub mod arith_feedback {
    pub const NONE: u8 = 0;
    pub const INT32: u8 = 1 << 0;
    pub const DOUBLE: u8 = 1 << 1;
    pub const INT32_OVERFLOW: u8 = 1 << 2;
    pub const STRING: u8 = 1 << 3;
    pub const BIG_INT: u8 = 1 << 4;
    pub const OTHER: u8 = 1 << 5;
    /// Equality comparisons where both operands are objects.
    pub const OBJECT_PAIR: u8 = 1 << 6;
    /// Boolean operands of arithmetic and bitwise operations, which `OTHER` does not include there.
    pub const BOOLEAN: u8 = 1 << 7;
}

/// The union of the kinds of values produced by an instruction, as `ValueFeedback` bits. The bit for a boxed value is
/// 1 << (low three tag bits | 8 if the tag is a cell tag), and unboxed doubles use bit 0. The bits that do not name a
/// kind below (reserved tags, accessors and other non-value cells) count as `OTHER`.
///
/// The interpreter does not classify values as it runs: it stores the bits of the last value each instruction
/// produced in that instruction's bucket, and the buckets are folded into these bits when the feedback is about to be
/// used and at every garbage collection.
pub mod value_feedback {
    pub const NONE: u16 = 0;
    pub const DOUBLE: u16 = 1 << 0;
    pub const BOOLEAN: u16 = 1 << 1;
    pub const INT32: u16 = 1 << 2;
    pub const EMPTY: u16 = 1 << 3;
    pub const UNDEFINED: u16 = 1 << 6;
    pub const NULL: u16 = 1 << 7;
    pub const OBJECT: u16 = 1 << 9;
    pub const STRING: u16 = 1 << 10;
    pub const SYMBOL: u16 = 1 << 11;
    pub const BIG_INT: u16 = 1 << 13;
    pub const OTHER: u16 = 1 << 15;

    pub const OTHER_MASK: u16 = (1 << 4) | (1 << 5) | (1 << 8) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 14) | (1 << 15);

    /// A value bucket holds the raw bits of a Value. Only its tag is ever looked at, so it is not a GC reference. An
    /// empty bucket has a reserved tag that no value uses.
    pub const EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET: u64 = (EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG as u64) << 48;

    /// The tag of an empty value bucket.
    pub const EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG: u16 = 0x7ffc;

    /// The bit for a value with the raw `bits`.
    pub const fn for_bits(bits: u64) -> u16 {
        // NB: Boxed values have all of the 0x7ff8 tag bits set.
        let tag = bits >> 48;
        let index = if tag & 0x7ff8 == 0x7ff8 {
            (tag & 7) | ((tag >> 12) & 8)
        } else {
            0
        };
        1 << index
    }
}

/// The callees seen by a call site.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CallFeedback {
    /// The first callee seen at this site. Weak: cleared when the callee dies.
    pub target: Cell<Option<Gc<CellHeader>>>,
    /// `call_feedback_flags` bits.
    pub flags: Cell<u8>,
    /// How the first callee forwarded the call to another function, a `CallFeedbackForwarding`.
    pub forwarding: Cell<u8>,
    /// The number of arguments the first forwarded call passed.
    pub forwarded_argument_count: Cell<u16>,
    /// The tag of the last value a call returned to the site, like the value buckets of the other instructions, or
    /// `value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG`.
    pub value_bucket: Cell<u16>,
    /// The `value_feedback` bits of the values the calls returned, which the value bucket is folded into.
    pub value: Cell<u16>,
    /// The function the first callee forwarded the first call through it to. Weak: cleared when it dies.
    pub forwarded_target: Cell<Option<Gc<CellHeader>>>,
}

pub mod call_feedback_flags {
    pub const NONE: u8 = 0;
    pub const POLYMORPHIC: u8 = 1 << 0;
    /// A callee that is not an ECMAScript function object was seen.
    pub const SAW_NATIVE: u8 = 1 << 1;
    pub const SAW_CONSTRUCT: u8 = 1 << 2;
    /// The calls through the first callee did not all forward to the same function in the same way with the same
    /// number of arguments.
    pub const FORWARDED_POLYMORPHIC: u8 = 1 << 3;
    /// The calls through the first callee forwarded the same way, with the same number of arguments, to other
    /// closures of the ECMAScript function the first forwarded call went to: functions with its code, but their own
    /// environments.
    pub const FORWARDED_CLOSURES: u8 = 1 << 4;
    /// A callee other than the first was seen that is no closure of the first's ECMAScript function: another
    /// function, or a native one. Without it, every callee of a polymorphic site was a closure of the first callee's
    /// function: a function with its code, but its own environment.
    pub const OTHER_FUNCTIONS: u8 = 1 << 5;
}

/// How the first callee of a call site forwarded the call to another function.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum CallFeedbackForwarding {
    None,
    /// Function.prototype.apply with an array-like argument list.
    Apply,
    /// Function.prototype.call.
    Call,
    /// A bound function.
    Bound,
    /// A builtin written in JavaScript that calls its first argument back, like Array.prototype.forEach.
    Callback,
}

impl Default for CallFeedback {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            target: Cell::new(None),
            flags: Cell::new(call_feedback_flags::NONE),
            forwarding: Cell::new(CallFeedbackForwarding::None as u8),
            forwarded_argument_count: Cell::new(0),
            value_bucket: Cell::new(value_feedback::EMPTY_VALUE_BUCKET_TAG),
            value: Cell::new(value_feedback::NONE),
            forwarded_target: Cell::new(None),
        }
    }
}

/// The keys and receivers seen by a property access.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct KeyedFeedback {
    /// `keyed_feedback_bits` bits.
    pub bits: Cell<u32>,
    /// The last string or symbol key seen at this site. Weak: cleared when the key dies.
    pub last_key: Cell<Option<Gc<CellHeader>>>,
}

pub mod keyed_feedback_bits {
    pub const NONE: u32 = 0;

    // Key kinds.
    pub const INT32_INDEX: u32 = 1 << 0;
    pub const STRING_KEY: u32 = 1 << 1;
    pub const SYMBOL_KEY: u32 = 1 << 2;
    pub const OTHER_KEY: u32 = 1 << 3;
    /// More than one distinct string or symbol key was seen.
    pub const MULTIPLE_KEYS: u32 = 1 << 4;

    // Element kinds.
    pub const PACKED: u32 = 1 << 5;
    pub const HOLEY: u32 = 1 << 6;
    pub const OTHER_ELEMENTS: u32 = 1 << 7;
    /// An int32 index that was not that of an element the object's indexed storage holds: beyond its size or its
    /// storage, or a hole. Element accesses in JIT code handle none of those.
    pub const OUT_OF_BOUNDS: u32 = 1 << 8;

    // One bit per typed array kind, starting at TYPED_ARRAY_SHIFT.
    pub const KEY_KINDS_MASK: u32 = 0x1f;
    pub const TYPED_ARRAY_SHIFT: u32 = 9;
    /// GetLength receivers with the array's magical length property.
    pub const MAGICAL_LENGTH: u32 = 1 << 24;

    pub const fn typed_array_bit(kind: u8) -> u32 {
        1 << (TYPED_ARRAY_SHIFT + kind as u32)
    }
}

impl Default for KeyedFeedback {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            bits: Cell::new(keyed_feedback_bits::NONE),
            last_key: Cell::new(None),
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C)]

/// What an ECMAScript function object keeps where other objects have the pointer to their indexed elements. Hardly any
/// function has indexed properties, and those it has stay in a dictionary outside of the cell (see
/// `IndexedStorageKind::Dictionary`), so the indexed storage kind of a function never lets anything read the pointer.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct EcmascriptFunctionFields {
    pub shared_data: NullableMember<SharedFunctionInstanceData>,
    pub environment: NullableMember<Environment>,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<EcmascriptFunctionFields>() == size_of::<*mut Value>());

pub const ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION_OBJECT_SHARED_DATA_OFFSET: usize =
    core::mem::offset_of!(Object, indexed_elements) + core::mem::offset_of!(EcmascriptFunctionFields, shared_data);
pub const ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION_OBJECT_ENVIRONMENT_OFFSET: usize =
    core::mem::offset_of!(Object, indexed_elements) + core::mem::offset_of!(EcmascriptFunctionFields, environment);

impl EcmascriptFunctionObject {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn fields(&self) -> &EcmascriptFunctionFields {
        // SAFETY: The fields are as large as the pointer they take the place of, and no more aligned. They are cells,
        //         like the pointer, which this kind of object never uses as one.
        unsafe { &*core::ptr::from_ref(&self.base.base.indexed_elements).cast() }
    }
}

/// An ECMAScript function object that needs more than most: a method or a class constructor, or a function of code
/// with private names (see ecmascript_function_flags::HAS_RARE_DATA).
#[repr(C)]
pub struct EcmascriptFunctionObjectWithRareData {
    pub base: EcmascriptFunctionObject,
    pub private_environment: NullableMember<PrivateEnvironment>,
    pub home_object: NullableMember<Object>,
    pub storage: EcmascriptFunctionObjectStorage,
}

/// The bits of Object::class_bits of an ECMAScript function object.
pub mod ecmascript_function_flags {
    /// Set on all ECMAScript function objects, which keeps their flags from reading as a builtin.
    pub const IS_ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION: u8 = 1 << 7;
    /// The normal function may not have its "prototype" property yet, and acts as if it had it right after "length"
    /// and "name". Until it gets it, its shape is a chain of transitions from the premade shape it started from, and
    /// the function's own "length" and "name" are the first two properties of its shape, unless those are lazy too.
    pub const MAY_NEED_LAZY_PROTOTYPE_INSTANTIATION: u8 = 1 << 0;
    pub const IS_METHOD: u8 = 1 << 1;
    /// The function does not have its "length" and "name" properties yet, and acts as if it had them, in front of the
    /// properties it has. Functions with this flag have shapes of their own: descendants of the premade shape of their
    /// kind, whose first property is not "length".
    pub const HAS_LAZY_LENGTH_AND_NAME: u8 = 1 << 2;
    /// The function is an EcmascriptFunctionObjectWithRareData.
    pub const HAS_RARE_DATA: u8 = 1 << 3;
    /// The function was given a name other than the one of its shared data, which is the value of its "name" property.
    pub const HAS_CUSTOM_NAME: u8 = 1 << 4;
}

/// Bits of SharedFunctionInstanceData::asm_call_metadata above the formal parameter count in its low 32 bits. The first
/// four are what the interpreter and JIT code decide calls by, and the rest is what else there is to know about the
/// function in few bits.
pub mod asm_call_metadata {
    pub const CAN_INLINE_CALL: u64 = 1 << 32;
    pub const NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_OR_THIS_VALUE_RESOLUTION: u64 = 1 << 33;
    pub const USES_THIS: u64 = 1 << 34;
    pub const STRICT: u64 = 1 << 35;
    pub const FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_NEEDED: u64 = 1 << 36;
    pub const THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION: u64 = 1 << 37;
    pub const MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS_OBJECT: u64 = 1 << 38;
    pub const CONTAINS_DIRECT_CALL_TO_EVAL: u64 = 1 << 39;
    pub const IS_ARROW_FUNCTION: u64 = 1 << 40;
    pub const HAS_SIMPLE_PARAMETER_LIST: u64 = 1 << 41;
    pub const IS_MODULE_WRAPPER: u64 = 1 << 42;
    pub const IS_CLASS_CONSTRUCTOR: u64 = 1 << 43;
    pub const IS_DERIVED_CONSTRUCTOR: u64 = 1 << 44;
    pub const CLOSURE_COUNT_SHIFT: u32 = 45;
    pub const CLOSURE_COUNT_MASK: u64 = 0b11;
    pub const FUNCTION_KIND_SHIFT: u32 = 47;
    pub const FUNCTION_KIND_MASK: u64 = 0b11;
    pub const CONSTRUCT_COUNT_SHIFT: u32 = 49;
    pub const CONSTRUCT_COUNT_MASK: u64 = (1 << 15) - 1;
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct SharedFunctionInstanceData {
    pub executable: NullableMember<ExecutableHead>,
    /// How JIT code allocates the function environments of calls of the functions, once the runtime made one.
    pub call_environment_template: NullableMember<CallEnvironmentTemplate>,
    pub header: CellHeaderTail,
    /// How many properties the objects constructions of the function create get, as far as known.
    pub construct_reserve: Cell<u8>,
    pub function_length: i32,
    pub asm_call_metadata: Cell<u64>,
    /// The [[ScriptOrModule]] of the functions, which is the same for all of them.
    pub script_or_module: ScriptOrModuleSlot,
    pub storage: SharedFunctionInstanceDataStorage,
}

/// The number of words of a FunctionEnvironment: a DeclarativeEnvironment and two more words of fields.
pub const FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_WORDS: usize = size_of::<DeclarativeEnvironment>() / 8 + 2;

/// The environment of a call of a function (a function environment if `has_function_fields` is not 0, and a declarative
/// environment otherwise) like the ones the calls of a function get, with its final shape and room for its binding
/// values in its cell, for JIT code to allocate from the local free list of its `size_class` (cells of `cell_size`
/// bytes, see `jit::allocation::FunctionEnvironmentFreeLists`) and fill with `words`. The words have no binding values pointer, outer environment, function object or this
/// value, which differ between calls: the binding values start `binding_values_offset` bytes into the cell (0 if they
/// are not in the cell), and the call binds `this` in the environment if `binds_this` is not 0. Templates are cells, so
/// that JIT code decodes the pointer to one into the GC heap like any other cell pointer.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CallEnvironmentTemplate {
    pub header: CellHeader,
    pub size_class: u64,
    pub cell_size: u64,
    pub binding_values_offset: u64,
    pub binds_this: u64,
    pub has_function_fields: u64,
    pub words: [u64; FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_WORDS],
}

/*

//! Compressed cell pointers for the fields of cells. A field holds the cell's offset into the heap region in units of
//! the 8-byte cell alignment, which fits in 32 bits because the region is 32 GiB. Locals, parameters and return values
//! keep using the full-width `Gc`, which `get()` and `set()` convert from and to.
//!
//! The slot is an `UnsafeCell`, so that a collector can rewrite it behind a shared reference, and `set()` goes through
//! a write barrier hook, which does nothing for now.

use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use super::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout_forward::heap_region_base;

/// How far a cell's offset into the heap region is shifted right to compress it: cells are 8-byte aligned.
pub const COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT: u32 = 3;

/// The size of the heap region, which a compressed pointer covers whatever its 32 bits are.
pub const COMPRESSED_POINTER_RANGE: u64 = 1 << (32 + COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT);

/// The compressed form of a pointer into the heap region. The region's base is aligned to its size, so the low 32 bits
/// of the shifted address are the shifted offset, and compressing needs no base.
#[inline(always)]
fn compress_address(address: usize) -> u32 {
    debug_assert!(
        (address.wrapping_sub(heap_region_base()) as u64) < COMPRESSED_POINTER_RANGE,
        "compressed pointers only point into the heap region"
    );
    debug_assert!(address.is_multiple_of(1 << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT));
    (address >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32
}

/// The address a compressed pointer that is not null names, which is in the heap region whatever the 32 bits are.
///
/// Makes the compressed pointer live up to this point, and the decoded address from this point on. The conservative
/// stack scan recognizes a cell by its address or by its compressed pointer in either half of a word, but not by its
/// unshifted offset, which the compiler could otherwise keep instead while either is held across an allocation.
#[inline(always)]
fn decompress_address(compressed: u32) -> usize {
    let mut address = heap_region_base() + ((compressed as usize) << COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT);
    // SAFETY: The assembly is empty: it only has the compiler put `compressed` and `address` in registers here.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "/* {compressed} {address} */",
            compressed = in(reg) compressed as usize,
            address = inout(reg) address,
            options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags),
        );
    }
    address
}

/// Where a collector that has to know about stores into cells, like a generational or incremental one, will hook in.
/// It does nothing for now.
#[inline(always)]
fn write_barrier(_slot: &UnsafeCell<u32>, _compressed: u32) {}

/// Ties a member to its cell type. The compressed pointer is the GC pointer, which the member traces itself, so the
/// marker holds none. Like a `Gc`, a member stays on its thread.
type CellMarker<T> = PhantomData<(fn() -> Gc<T>, *const ())>;

/// A compressed pointer to a cell, as a field of a cell or of storage that a cell traces. It is never null; see
/// `NullableMember` for one that can be.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct Member<T> {
    compressed: UnsafeCell<u32>,
    _cell: CellMarker<T>,
}

impl<T> Member<T> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn new(cell: Gc<T>) -> Self {
        Self {
            compressed: UnsafeCell::new(compress_address(cell.as_ptr().addr())),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get(&self) -> Gc<T> {
        let address = decompress_address(self.compressed());
        // SAFETY: The member was set to a cell, which a member keeps alive. A compressed pointer that is not null
        //         decodes to an address in the heap region, which is never null.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(core::ptr::without_provenance_mut(address))) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set(&self, cell: Gc<T>) {
        let compressed = compress_address(cell.as_ptr().addr());
        write_barrier(&self.compressed, compressed);
        // SAFETY: Cells are only used from one thread, and no reference into the slot outlives a call.
        unsafe { *self.compressed.get() = compressed };
    }

    /// The compressed pointer, for comparing cells without decoding them.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn compressed(&self) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: Cells are only used from one thread, and no reference into the slot outlives a call.
        unsafe { *self.compressed.get() }
    }
}

/// OPTIMIZATION: Two members name the same cell exactly when their compressed pointers are equal, so they compare
///               without decoding.
impl<T> PartialEq for Member<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.compressed() == other.compressed()
    }
}

impl<T> Eq for Member<T> {}

impl<T> PartialEq<Gc<T>> for Member<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Gc<T>) -> bool {
        self.get() == *other
    }
}

/// Hashes the decoded address, like `Gc`, so that a member and a `Gc` of the same cell hash the same.
impl<T> core::hash::Hash for Member<T> {
    fn hash<H: core::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.get().hash(state);
    }
}

impl<T> core::fmt::Debug for Member<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "Member({:p})", self.get().as_non_null())
    }
}

/// A compressed pointer to a cell or null, as a field of a cell or of storage that a cell traces. Null is 0, which
/// never names a cell because the bottom of the heap region is never mapped.
///
/// This is its own type rather than an `Option<Member<T>>`, which would take 8 bytes: the `UnsafeCell` hides the niche
/// that 0 would be.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct NullableMember<T> {
    compressed: UnsafeCell<u32>,
    _cell: CellMarker<T>,
}

impl<T> NullableMember<T> {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub const fn null() -> Self {
        Self {
            compressed: UnsafeCell::new(0),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn new(cell: Option<Gc<T>>) -> Self {
        Self {
            compressed: UnsafeCell::new(Self::compress(cell)),
            _cell: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    fn compress(cell: Option<Gc<T>>) -> u32 {
        cell.map_or(0, |cell| compress_address(cell.as_ptr().addr()))
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get(&self) -> Option<Gc<T>> {
        let compressed = self.compressed();
        if compressed == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let address = decompress_address(compressed);
        // SAFETY: The member was set to a cell, which a member keeps alive. A compressed pointer that is not null
        //         decodes to an address in the heap region, which is never null.
        Some(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(core::ptr::without_provenance_mut(address))) })
    }

    /// The cell of a member that is known not to be null, without checking.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The member must not be null.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub unsafe fn get_unchecked(&self) -> Gc<T> {
        debug_assert!(!self.is_null());
        let address = decompress_address(self.compressed());
        // SAFETY: The member was set to a cell, which a member keeps alive. A compressed pointer that is not null
        //         decodes to an address in the heap region, which is never null.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(core::ptr::without_provenance_mut(address))) }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn set(&self, cell: Option<Gc<T>>) {
        let compressed = Self::compress(cell);
        write_barrier(&self.compressed, compressed);
        // SAFETY: Cells are only used from one thread, and no reference into the slot outlives a call.
        unsafe { *self.compressed.get() = compressed };
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn take(&self) -> Option<Gc<T>> {
        let cell = self.get();
        self.set(None);
        cell
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool {
        self.compressed() == 0
    }

    /// The compressed pointer, 0 for null, for comparing cells without decoding them.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn compressed(&self) -> u32 {
        // SAFETY: Cells are only used from one thread, and no reference into the slot outlives a call.
        unsafe { *self.compressed.get() }
    }
}

impl<T> Default for NullableMember<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::null()
    }
}

/// OPTIMIZATION: Two members name the same cell, or are both null, exactly when their compressed pointers are equal,
///               so they compare without decoding.
impl<T> PartialEq for NullableMember<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.compressed() == other.compressed()
    }
}

impl<T> Eq for NullableMember<T> {}

impl<T> PartialEq<Option<Gc<T>>> for NullableMember<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Option<Gc<T>>) -> bool {
        self.get() == *other
    }
}

/// Hashes like `Option<Gc<T>>`, so that a member and an `Option<Gc<T>>` of the same cell hash the same.
impl<T> core::hash::Hash for NullableMember<T> {
    fn hash<H: core::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.get().hash(state);
    }
}

impl<T> core::fmt::Debug for NullableMember<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        match self.get() {
            Some(cell) => write!(formatter, "NullableMember({:p})", cell.as_non_null()),
            None => write!(formatter, "NullableMember(null)"),
        }
    }
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Member<u8>>() == 4);
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<Member<u8>>() == 4);
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<NullableMember<u8>>() == 4);
const _: () = assert!(align_of::<NullableMember<u8>>() == 4);

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const HEAP_REGION_BASE: usize = 0x7a00_0000_0000;

    struct FakeCell;

    fn cell_at(offset: usize) -> Gc<FakeCell> {
        let address = HEAP_REGION_BASE + offset;
        // SAFETY: The tests never dereference the pointer.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(core::ptr::without_provenance_mut(address)).unwrap()) }
    }

    fn hash_of(value: &impl core::hash::Hash) -> u64 {
        use core::hash::Hasher;
        let mut hasher = std::hash::DefaultHasher::new();
        value.hash(&mut hasher);
        hasher.finish()
    }

    #[test]
    fn region_base_is_aligned_to_the_compressed_range() {
        assert_eq!(heap_region_base(), HEAP_REGION_BASE);
        assert!((HEAP_REGION_BASE as u64).is_multiple_of(COMPRESSED_POINTER_RANGE));
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_trips_cells_across_the_region() {
        for offset in [8, 0x1_0000_0000, 0x4_0000_0010, 0x7_ffff_fff8] {
            let cell = cell_at(offset);
            let member = Member::new(cell);
            assert_eq!(member.compressed(), (offset >> COMPRESSED_POINTER_SHIFT) as u32);
            assert_eq!(member.get(), cell);
            let nullable = NullableMember::new(Some(cell));
            assert_eq!(nullable.compressed(), member.compressed());
            assert_eq!(nullable.get(), Some(cell));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_compressed_value_decodes_into_the_region() {
        for compressed in [0, 1, 0x8000_0000, u32::MAX] {
            let address = decompress_address(compressed);
            assert!(((address - HEAP_REGION_BASE) as u64) < COMPRESSED_POINTER_RANGE);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_replaces_the_cell() {
        let member = Member::new(cell_at(0x1_0000_0000));
        member.set(cell_at(0x2_0000_0008));
        assert_eq!(member.get(), cell_at(0x2_0000_0008));
    }

    #[test]
    fn null_is_zero() {
        let nullable = NullableMember::<FakeCell>::null();
        assert!(nullable.is_null());
        assert_eq!(nullable.compressed(), 0);
        assert_eq!(nullable.get(), None);
        assert_eq!(NullableMember::<FakeCell>::new(None).compressed(), 0);
        assert!(NullableMember::<FakeCell>::default().is_null());

        nullable.set(Some(cell_at(0x1_0000_0000)));
        assert!(!nullable.is_null());
        assert_eq!(nullable.take(), Some(cell_at(0x1_0000_0000)));
        assert!(nullable.is_null());
    }

    #[test]
    fn equality_and_hash_agree_with_gc() {
        let cell = cell_at(0x1_2345_6788);
        let member = Member::new(cell);
        assert_eq!(member, cell);
        assert_ne!(member, cell_at(0x1_2345_6790));
        assert_eq!(member, Member::new(cell));
        assert_ne!(member, Member::new(cell_at(0x1_2345_6790)));
        assert_eq!(hash_of(&member), hash_of(&cell));

        let nullable = NullableMember::new(Some(cell));
        assert_eq!(nullable, Some(cell));
        assert_ne!(nullable, None);
        assert_eq!(nullable, NullableMember::new(Some(cell)));
        assert_eq!(hash_of(&nullable), hash_of(&Some(cell)));
        assert_eq!(
            hash_of(&NullableMember::<FakeCell>::null()),
            hash_of(&None::<Gc<FakeCell>>)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn mixed_lookups_find_the_same_entry() {
        use std::collections::HashSet;
        let cell = cell_at(0x3_0000_0040);
        let set: HashSet<Gc<FakeCell>> = [cell].into_iter().collect();
        let member = Member::new(cell);
        assert!(set.contains(&member.get()));
        assert!(!set.contains(&Member::new(cell_at(0x3_0000_0048)).get()));
        assert_eq!(hash_of(&member), hash_of(set.iter().next().unwrap()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn debug_shows_the_address() {
        let cell = cell_at(0x1_0000_0000);
        assert_eq!(
            format!("{:?}", Member::new(cell)),
            format!("Member({:p})", cell.as_non_null())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            format!("{:?}", NullableMember::<FakeCell>::null()),
            "NullableMember(null)"
        );
    }
}

use core::cell::Cell;

use super::cell::{CellHeader, CellKind, CellState};
use super::member::Member;
use super::shape::Shape;
use super::value::Value;
use crate::layout_forward::TypedArrayBaseStorage;

pub mod object_flag {
    pub const IS_EXTENSIBLE: u16 = 1 << 0;
    pub const IS_RAW_NATIVE_FUNCTION: u16 = 1 << 1;
    pub const HAS_MAGICAL_LENGTH_PROPERTY: u16 = 1 << 2;
    pub const IS_TYPED_ARRAY: u16 = 1 << 3;
    pub const MAY_INTERFERE_WITH_INDEXED_PROPERTY_ACCESS: u16 = 1 << 4;
    pub const HAS_INTRINSIC_ACCESSORS: u16 = 1 << 5;
    pub const IS_ECMASCRIPT_FUNCTION_OBJECT: u16 = 1 << 6;
    pub const IS_FUNCTION: u16 = 1 << 7;
    pub const REQUIRES_SLOW_ADD_OWN_PROPERTY: u16 = 1 << 8;
    pub const IS_PLATFORM_OBJECT: u16 = 1 << 9;
    pub const IS_DIRECT_GETTER_FUNCTION: u16 = 1 << 10;
    pub const IS_GLOBAL_OBJECT: u16 = 1 << 11;
    pub const HAS_UNIMPLEMENTED_PROPERTIES: u16 = 1 << 12;
    pub const IS_HTMLDDA: u16 = 1 << 13;
    /// The named or indexed storage is a malloc allocation (rather than inline or a ValueStorage cell), which the
    /// object frees. The flags let a dead object's destructor tell without reading the storage, since a ValueStorage
    /// cell may be swept before its object.
    pub const HAS_MALLOC_NAMED_STORAGE: u16 = 1 << 14;
    pub const HAS_MALLOC_INDEXED_STORAGE: u16 = 1 << 15;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum IndexedStorageKind {
    None,
    Packed,
    Holey,
    Dictionary,
}

/// The bits of Object::class_bits of an array.
pub mod array_flags {
    pub const LENGTH_NOT_WRITABLE: u8 = 1 << 0;
    pub const IS_PROXY_TARGET: u8 = 1 << 1;
}

/// Packed and holey indexed storage keeps its capacity in a header right in front of the first element.
pub const INDEXED_ELEMENTS_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 8;

/// An object starts with the shape and the array-like size in the first word of its cell header, which LibGC leaves
/// to the cell, followed by the rest of the header.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Object {
    pub shape: Member<Shape>,
    pub indexed_array_like_size: Cell<u32>,
    /// See CellHeader::identity_hash_state.
    pub identity_hash_state: Cell<u8>,
    pub state: Cell<CellState>,
    pub kind: CellKind,
    pub indexed_storage_kind: Cell<IndexedStorageKind>,
    pub flags: Cell<u16>,
    /// How many named property values the inline storage holds. It comes right after the object, in the cells of the
    /// classes that make room for it.
    pub inline_named_capacity: Cell<u8>,
    /// What a class keeps in the object: the builtin of a function object plus one (zero for none),
    /// ecmascript_function_flags for an ECMAScript function object, which have the highest bit set, or array_flags for
    /// an array. Zero for other objects.
    pub class_bits: Cell<u8>,
    /// Points at the inline storage until the object needs more room.
    pub named_properties: Cell<*mut Value>,
    /// The packed or holey elements. A plain object has its inline storage start here instead, as long as
    /// `named_properties` points at this word, and moves it out of the way for its first indexed property. Nothing may
    /// read this word without knowing that the object has packed, holey or dictionary indexed storage.
    pub indexed_elements: Cell<*mut Value>,
    pub inline_named_storage: [Cell<Value>; 0],
}

const _: () = {
    use core::mem::offset_of;
    assert!(offset_of!(Object, identity_hash_state) == offset_of!(CellHeader, identity_hash_state));
    assert!(offset_of!(Object, state) == offset_of!(CellHeader, state));
    assert!(offset_of!(Object, kind) == offset_of!(CellHeader, kind));
};

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Object>() == 32);
const _: () = assert!(core::mem::offset_of!(Object, inline_named_storage) == size_of::<Object>());

/// Mirrors the Variant<Auto, Detached, size_t> the interpreter reads: the length first, then the alternative's index.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ByteLengthSlot {
    pub length: Cell<usize>,
    pub alternative_index: Cell<u8>,
}

pub const BYTE_LENGTH_LENGTH_INDEX: u8 = 2;

/// Mirrors JS::TypedArrayBase::Kind, in the order of JS_ENUMERATE_TYPED_ARRAYS.

    pub const UINT8: u8 = 0;
    pub const UINT8_CLAMPED: u8 = 1;
    pub const UINT16: u8 = 2;
    pub const UINT32: u8 = 3;
    pub const BIG_UINT64: u8 = 4;
    pub const INT8: u8 = 5;
    pub const INT16: u8 = 6;
    pub const INT32: u8 = 7;
    pub const BIG_INT64: u8 = 8;
    pub const FLOAT16: u8 = 9;
    pub const FLOAT32: u8 = 10;
    pub const FLOAT64: u8 = 11;
}

pub const TYPED_ARRAY_CACHED_DATA_OFFSET_INVALID: usize = usize::MAX;

#[repr(C)]
pub struct TypedArrayBase {

    pub kind: Cell<u8>,

    pub array_length: ByteLengthSlot,
    pub byte_offset: Cell<usize>,

use core::cell::Cell;

use super::cell::CellHeader;
use crate::layout_forward::Utf16StringSlot;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum DeferredKind {
    None,
    Rope,
    Substring,
    /// The ASCII characters are stored in the string cell itself, and only copied into `utf16_string` when something
    /// needs a string of its own.
    Inline,
}

/// The bits of PrimitiveString::deferred_kind_and_flags that hold its DeferredKind.
pub const DEFERRED_KIND_MASK: u8 = 0b11;

/// The flag of PrimitiveString::deferred_kind_and_flags that says the string is interned: it is the only interned
/// string with its contents, so two interned strings are equal if and only if they are the same string.
pub const INTERNED_FLAG: u8 = 1 << 7;

/// A string value. Ropes, substrings and inline strings resolve into `utf16_string` on first use; the interpreter only
/// reads strings that are not deferred.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PrimitiveString {
    pub header: CellHeader,
    /// The DeferredKind in the bits of DEFERRED_KIND_MASK, and INTERNED_FLAG. They share a byte since the cell has
    /// no other room for the flag.
    pub deferred_kind_and_flags: Cell<u8>,
    pub length_in_utf16_code_units: Cell<u32>,
    pub utf16_string: Utf16StringSlot,
}

/// The most ASCII characters an inline string holds.
pub const INLINE_STRING_CAPACITY: usize = 32;

/// OPTIMIZATION: A string of a few ASCII characters, which are stored in the cell rather than in storage of their own
///               that would have to be allocated and freed.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct InlineString {
    pub base: PrimitiveString,
    pub characters: [u8; INLINE_STRING_CAPACITY],
}

use core::cell::Cell;

use super::buffer::{InterpreterBuffer, ThinSlice};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u32)]
pub enum PropertyLookupCacheEntryType {
    Empty,
    AddOwnProperty,
    ChangeOwnProperty,
    GetOwnProperty,
    ChangePropertyInPrototypeChain,
    GetPropertyInPrototypeChain,
    GetMissingProperty,
    /// Only in the VM's keyed property lookup cache: objects of the shape whose own string-keyed properties are those
    /// of the shape have no own property of the name, whatever their prototypes have. Own property checks
    /// (`hasOwnProperty`, `in`) look for these; property gets ignore them.
    MissingOwnProperty,
}

/// One cached property access. The shapes and objects are not traced; the VM's sweep callback clears entries whose
/// cells did not survive a collection.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PropertyLookupCacheEntry {
    pub entry_type: Cell<PropertyLookupCacheEntryType>,
    pub property_offset: Cell<u32>,
    pub shape_dictionary_generation: Cell<u32>,
    pub writes_data_property: Cell<bool>,
    pub new_shape: Cell<Option<Gc<Shape>>>,
    pub shape: Cell<Option<Gc<Shape>>>,
    pub prototype: Cell<Option<Gc<Object>>>,
    pub prototype_chain_validity: Cell<Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>>>,
    /// The encoded string or symbol Value whose property this entry describes, for the caches of keyed accesses like
    /// GetByValue, or 0 for the caches of named accesses like GetById, whose instruction determines the property. Like
    /// the cells above, the key is not kept alive by the cache.
    pub key: Cell<u64>,
    /// For entries of named accesses that get an accessor property, a getter the interpreter called through the entry.
    /// For an own property, it is the last one, for JIT code to speculate on. A DirectGetterFunction is only recorded
    /// once it returned for an object of the entry's shape. Not kept alive either, and forgotten when it dies. It also
    /// makes entries 64 bytes, so that JIT code finds an entry in the megamorphic tables by masking bits of its hash
    /// (see megamorphic_hash() of the bytecode executable).
    pub getter: Cell<Option<Gc<FunctionObject>>>,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<PropertyLookupCacheEntry>() == 64);

/// The layout of an entry of the VM's keyed property lookup cache (KeyedPropertyLookupCacheEntry of the bytecode
/// executable, which asserts that it matches), for the interpreter, which looks up own data properties in it.
#[repr(C, align(64))]
pub struct KeyedPropertyLookupCacheEntryLayout {
    pub entry_type: PropertyLookupCacheEntryType,
    pub property_offset: u32,
    pub shape_dictionary_generation: u32,
    pub shape: Option<Gc<Shape>>,
    pub prototype: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    pub prototype_chain_validity: Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>>,
    pub new_shape: Option<Gc<Shape>>,
    /// The identity of the name of the property, the word of a fly string, or 0.
    pub property_name: u64,
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<KeyedPropertyLookupCacheEntryLayout>() == 64);

/// How the interpreter finds the entry of the keyed property lookup cache that may hold a lookup: the top this many bits
/// of the 32-bit product of this multiplier and the low 32 bits of the shape's address XORed with the name's identity
/// (see KeyedPropertyLookupCache::entry_index_for() of the bytecode executable, which asserts that these match).
pub const KEYED_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_INTERPRETER_INDEX_BITS: u32 = 11;
pub const KEYED_PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_INTERPRETER_HASH_MULTIPLIER: u32 = 0x9e37_79b9;

/// A tagged pointer to the entries of a property lookup cache; the interpreter only ever consults the first entry.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PropertyLookupCache {
    pub data: Cell<usize>,
}

pub const PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_DATA_TAG_MASK: usize = 3;

/// The tag of a polymorphic cache's data, whose entries are an array the interpreter probes.
pub const PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_POLYMORPHIC_DATA_TAG: usize = 1;

/// The data of a keyed generic cache: the tag without data (see PropertyLookupCache::is_keyed_generic()).
pub const PROPERTY_LOOKUP_CACHE_KEYED_GENERIC_DATA: usize = 3;

/*

use core::marker::PhantomData;

use libjs_abi::value as nan_box;

/// A NaN-boxed JS::Value. Only libjs_rust makes values from bits, as bits can name a cell that is not there. Values
/// stay on the thread of their VM, as cells do.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct Value(pub(crate) u64, PhantomData<*const ()>);

impl Value {
    pub const EMPTY: Value = Value::from_bits(nan_box::EMPTY_VALUE);
    pub const UNDEFINED: Value = Value::from_bits(nan_box::UNDEFINED_VALUE);
    pub const NULL: Value = Value::from_bits(nan_box::NULL_VALUE);
    pub const FALSE: Value = Value::from_bits(nan_box::FALSE_VALUE);
    pub const TRUE: Value = Value::from_bits(nan_box::TRUE_VALUE);

    pub(crate) const fn from_bits(bits: u64) -> Value {
        Value(bits, PhantomData)
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `bits` must be a NaN-boxed value, such as one C++ code hands over, and a cell it names must be live.
    pub const unsafe fn from_raw(bits: u64) -> Value {
        Value::from_bits(bits)
    }

    /// The NaN-boxed bits, for handing the value to C++ code.
    pub const fn to_raw(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Value>() == 8);

/*

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;

use super::cell::Gc;
use super::execution_context::ExecutionContext;
use super::function_object::NativeFunctionTableEntry;
use super::property_lookup_cache::KeyedPropertyLookupCacheEntryLayout;
use super::realm::Realm;

/// The memory that execution contexts and their value slots are bump-allocated from.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct InterpreterStack {
    pub base: Cell<*mut u8>,
    pub top: Cell<*mut u8>,
    pub limit: Cell<*mut u8>,
    pub next_frame_id: Cell<u64>,
}

/// An entry of the execution context stack: a context pushed onto it, and the context that was running when it was
/// pushed, with the current realm of then, which the pop of the entry makes current again. That realm is the realm
/// of the previous running context (the running context's realm is always the current realm), so the collector keeps
/// it alive by tracing that context.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ExecutionContextStackEntry {
    pub execution_context: Cell<*mut ExecutionContext>,
    pub previous_running_execution_context: Cell<*mut ExecutionContext>,
    pub previous_realm: Cell<Option<Gc<Realm>>>,
}

/// How many dispatch tables the VM has, a power of two (see `VmHead::dispatch_tables`).
pub const DISPATCH_TABLE_COUNT: usize = 8;

/// An executable's dispatch table index is masked with this, which keeps it inside the VM's dispatch tables.
pub const DISPATCH_TABLE_INDEX_MASK: u8 = (DISPATCH_TABLE_COUNT - 1) as u8;

/// The part of the VM that the interpreter reads and writes. The rest of the VM follows it.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct VmHead {
    pub running_execution_context: Cell<*mut ExecutionContext>,
    pub interpreter_stack: InterpreterStack,
    /// The lowest address of the stack of the thread that runs JavaScript.
    pub stack_base: Cell<usize>,
    /// The lowest native stack address JavaScript runs at: the stack base plus VM_STACK_SPACE_LIMIT (see
    /// Vm::did_reach_stack_space_limit()). JIT code stops above it, see Vm::jit_native_stack_limit.
    pub native_stack_limit: Cell<usize>,
    /// Advanced at the end of every synchronous run of code (see `finish_execution_generation()`). WeakRef targets
    /// used during the current generation stay alive. Interpreter and JIT code advance it with a 32-bit increment.
    pub execution_generation: Cell<u32>,
    pub primitive_storage_cage_base: Cell<usize>,
    pub heap_region_base: Cell<usize>,
    pub native_function_table_data: Cell<*const NativeFunctionTableEntry>,
    /// Non-null while a debugger is attached; the interpreter then dispatches through its breakpoint-checking table.
    pub debugger: Cell<*mut c_void>,
    /// The execution context stack: storage for `execution_context_stack_capacity` entries, of which the first
    /// `execution_context_stack_length` are on the stack. Only the VM grows the storage, but an embedder may push and
    /// pop entries in place while there is room, and walk the stack.
    pub execution_context_stack_entries: Cell<*mut ExecutionContextStackEntry>,
    pub execution_context_stack_length: Cell<usize>,
    pub execution_context_stack_capacity: Cell<usize>,
    /// The realm TypeErrors are created in while a TypeErrorRealmScope is active, at the execution context stack
    /// length it was created at. An embedder's TypeErrorRealmScope sets and restores both directly.
    pub type_error_realm_override: Cell<Option<Gc<Realm>>>,
    pub type_error_realm_override_depth: Cell<usize>,
    /// The entries of the VM's keyed property lookup cache, which stay where they are for as long as the VM lives.
    pub keyed_property_lookup_cache_entries: Cell<*const KeyedPropertyLookupCacheEntryLayout>,
    /// The dispatch tables the interpreter runs frames with, by the dispatch table index of their executable (see
    /// `ExecutableHead::dispatch_table_index`). Indices without a table of their own have the plain one.
    pub dispatch_tables: [Cell<*const c_void>; DISPATCH_TABLE_COUNT],
    /// The current Realm Record, the [[Realm]] of the running execution context (see
    /// `Vm::set_running_execution_context()`). A frame of an ECMAScript function that the interpreter or JIT code
    /// enters for a call runs in the realm of its caller: they leave a call of one of another realm to the runtime. The
    /// frame of a native function they call runs in the function's realm, which they make current for the call.
    pub current_realm: Cell<Option<Gc<Realm>>>,
}

/// The storage an embedder reserves to construct a Vm in place, and its alignment. build.rs cannot see the Vm, only its
/// head, so these are a capacity that the crate checks the Vm against rather than its exact size and alignment.
pub const VM_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
pub const VM_ALIGN: usize = 16;

impl VmHead {
    /// Starts a new execution generation. The counter wraps around, which at worst keeps a WeakRef target that was
    /// last used 2^32 generations earlier alive until the next one.
    pub fn finish_execution_generation(&self) {
        self.execution_generation
            .set(self.execution_generation.get().wrapping_add(1));
    }
}
