//! Watchpoint sets of a realm that stay valid while some properties of its intrinsics are as the realm made them. Fast
//! paths that skip steps of the iterator protocol rely on them instead of looking up those properties every time.
//!
//! - `array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set`: %ArrayIteratorPrototype% has its own `next`, the builtin of the realm. It
//!   depends on the set that fires when the value of the property changes (see `Shape::watch_slot_for_replacements()`).
//! - `array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set`: array iterators have no `return` method. %ArrayIteratorPrototype%,
//!   %IteratorPrototype% and %Object.prototype% have no `return` property, and the first two keep their prototypes. It
//!   depends on the set that fires when an object of that prototype chain changes (see
//!   `Shape::prototype_chain_validity()`).
//! - `regexp_primordial_properties`: %RegExp.prototype% and %RegExp% have the properties that the fast
//!   paths of RegExp skip reading as the realm made them (see `RegExpPrototype::primordial_properties_are_unchanged()`).
//!   It depends on the sets that fire when either object changes, and when the values of those properties change. The
//!   realm starts watching them when a fast path first asks, since it creates the RegExp intrinsics on demand.
//! - `array_iterator_method`: %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] is %Array.prototype.values% of the realm, so that arrays
//!   of the realm without an own @@iterator are iterated with the array iterators of the realm. It depends on the sets
//!   that fire when %Array.prototype% changes, and when the value of that property changes.
//! - `array_species`: %Array.prototype%.constructor is %Array%, whose @@species is the intrinsic getter, so that
//!   ArraySpeciesCreate makes a plain array for an array of the realm that has no own constructor. It depends on the
//!   sets that fire when either object changes, and when the values of those properties change.
//! - `array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable`: %Array.prototype% and %Object.prototype% have no
//!   @@isConcatSpreadable, and %Array.prototype% inherits from %Object.prototype%, so that IsConcatSpreadable of an
//!   array of the realm without an own one is true. It depends on the sets that fire when either object changes.
//! - `string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data`: %String.prototype% has its builtin `valueOf` and `toString`, and
//!   neither it nor %Object.prototype%, which it inherits from, has a @@toPrimitive, so that ToPrimitive of a String
//!   object that inherits from %String.prototype% without own such properties gives its [[StringData]]. It depends on
//!   the sets that fire when either object changes, and when the values of those properties change.
//!
//! A change of an intrinsic fires the sets that depend on it, also one that leaves what they stand for in place, such
//! as a new property of %Object.prototype%. The next query of a fired set checks whether what it stands for still
//! holds, and if so, watches the intrinsics anew with a new set. Once it does not hold, the realm has no set anymore.

use core::cell::Cell;

use crate::gc::root::MarkedVec;
use crate::gc::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::object::Object;
use crate::runtime::property_key::PropertyKey;
use crate::runtime::realm::Realm;
use crate::runtime::regexp_prototype::RegExpPrototype;
use crate::runtime::string_prototype::StringPrototype;
use crate::runtime::watchpoint_set::WatchpointSet;

/// Starts watching the intrinsics of a realm whose intrinsics were just created. Until then, changes of the watched
/// properties do not matter, since creating the intrinsics defines them.
pub fn arm(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) {
    // NB: Prototype shapes belong to one object each, and have the watchpoint sets of their slots and prototype chains.
    realm.array_iterator_prototype().convert_to_prototype_if_needed(vm);
    realm
        .intrinsics()
        .iterator_prototype(vm)
        .convert_to_prototype_if_needed(vm);
    realm.object_prototype().convert_to_prototype_if_needed(vm);

    realm
        .array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set
        .set(watch_array_iterator_next(vm, realm));
    realm
        .array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set
        .set(watch_array_iterator_return(vm, realm));
}

/// Whether array iterators of the realm have its builtin `next` method.
pub fn array_iterators_have_builtin_next(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    let Some(set) = realm.array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set.get() else {
        return false;
    };
    if set.is_valid() {
        return true;
    }
    let set = watch_array_iterator_next(vm, realm);
    realm.array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set.set(set);
    set.is_some()
}

/// Whether array iterators of the realm have no `return` method.
pub fn array_iterators_have_no_return(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    let Some(set) = realm.array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set.get() else {
        return false;
    };
    if set.is_valid() {
        return true;
    }
    let set = watch_array_iterator_return(vm, realm);
    realm.array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set.set(set);
    set.is_some()
}

/// The set that stays valid while %ArrayIteratorPrototype% has its own `next`, the builtin of the realm, if it has.
fn watch_array_iterator_next(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let array_iterator_prototype = realm.array_iterator_prototype();
    let metadata = array_iterator_prototype.shape().lookup(&vm.names.next)?;
    let next = array_iterator_prototype.get_direct(metadata.offset);
    if next.is_accessor() || !next.is_function() {
        return None;
    }
    let next = next.as_function();
    if !next.is_array_prototype_next_builtin() || next.realm() != Some(realm) {
        return None;
    }
    // NB: A slot that property lookup caches may write to has no replacement watchpoint set. Caches write only to slots
    //     that the runtime wrote to before, so the realm stops watching once the property is written.
    let replacement_watchpoint_set = array_iterator_prototype
        .shape()
        .watch_slot_for_replacements(vm, metadata.offset)?;
    let set = WatchpointSet::create(vm);
    replacement_watchpoint_set.add_dependent_set(vm, set);
    Some(set)
}

/// The set that stays valid while array iterators of the realm have no `return` method, if they have none.
fn watch_array_iterator_return(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let array_iterator_prototype = realm.array_iterator_prototype();
    let iterator_prototype = realm.intrinsics().iterator_prototype(vm);
    let object_prototype = realm.object_prototype();
    // NB: %Object.prototype% has an immutable prototype.
    let chain: [(Gc<Object>, Option<Gc<Object>>); 3] = [
        (array_iterator_prototype, Some(iterator_prototype)),
        (iterator_prototype, Some(object_prototype)),
        (object_prototype, None),
    ];
    for (object, expected_prototype) in chain {
        if expected_prototype.is_some() && object.shape().prototype() != expected_prototype {
            return None;
        }
        if object.shape().lookup(&vm.names.return_).is_some() {
            return None;
        }
    }
    // NB: The validity of the prototype chain of a prototype shape fires when the object or one of its prototypes
    //     changes its properties or its prototype.
    let prototype_chain_validity = array_iterator_prototype.shape().prototype_chain_validity()?;
    if !prototype_chain_validity.is_valid() {
        return None;
    }
    let set = WatchpointSet::create(vm);
    prototype_chain_validity.add_dependent_set(vm, set);
    Some(set)
}

/// What a realm knows of a condition on its intrinsics that it watches from when a fast path first asks about it.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct WatchedCondition {
    /// The set that stays valid while the condition holds, since the realm last found it to hold.
    set: Cell<Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>>>,
    /// Whether the condition stopped holding, after which the realm does not watch it anymore.
    stopped_holding: Cell<bool>,
}

// SAFETY: Visits the one cell a watched condition holds.
unsafe impl Trace for WatchedCondition {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.set.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl WatchedCondition {
    /// Whether the condition holds. `watch` gives a new set that stays valid while it holds, if it holds.
    #[inline]
    fn holds(&self, vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, watch: fn(&Vm, Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>>) -> bool {
        if self.set.get().is_some_and(|set| set.is_valid()) {
            return true;
        }
        if self.stopped_holding.get() {
            return false;
        }
        let set = watch(vm, realm);
        self.set.set(set);
        self.stopped_holding.set(set.is_none());
        set.is_some()
    }

    /// The address of the cell that holds the set that stays valid while the condition holds, if that set is valid.
    fn valid_set_address(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.set
            .get()
            .is_some_and(|set| set.is_valid())
            .then_some(self.set.as_ptr() as u64)
    }
}

/// A set that stays valid while `objects` keep their properties and prototypes, and the properties `slots` of them keep
/// their values.
fn watch_intrinsics(vm: &Vm, objects: &[Gc<Object>], slots: &[(Gc<Object>, PropertyKey)]) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    // NB: Prototype shapes belong to one object each, and have the watchpoint sets of their slots and prototype chains.
    for object in objects {
        object.convert_to_prototype_if_needed(vm);
    }
    let set = WatchpointSet::create(vm);
    for object in objects {
        let validity = object.shape().prototype_chain_validity()?;
        if !validity.is_valid() {
            return None;
        }
        validity.add_dependent_set(vm, set);
    }
    for (object, key) in slots {
        let metadata = object.shape().lookup(key)?;
        let replacement_watchpoint_set = object.shape().watch_slot_for_replacements(vm, metadata.offset)?;
        replacement_watchpoint_set.add_dependent_set(vm, set);
    }
    Some(set)
}

/// Whether %RegExp.prototype% and %RegExp% of the realm have the properties that the fast paths of RegExp skip reading
/// as the realm made them.
pub fn regexp_primordial_properties_are_unchanged(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    realm
        .storage
        .regexp_primordial_properties
        .holds(vm, realm, watch_regexp_primordial_properties)
}

/// The set that stays valid while %RegExp.prototype% and %RegExp% have the properties that the fast paths of RegExp skip
/// reading as the realm made them, if they have.
fn watch_regexp_primordial_properties(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    if !RegExpPrototype::primordial_properties_are_unchanged(vm, realm) {
        return None;
    }
    let regexp_prototype = realm.intrinsics().regexp_prototype(vm);
    let regexp_constructor: Gc<Object> = realm.intrinsics().regexp_constructor(vm).upcast();
    let slots = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    for key in RegExpPrototype::primordial_property_keys(vm) {
        slots.push((regexp_prototype, key.clone()));
    }
    slots.push((regexp_prototype, PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().match_)));
    slots.push((regexp_constructor, PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().species)));
    watch_intrinsics(vm, &[regexp_prototype, regexp_constructor], &slots.values())
}

/// Whether ArraySpeciesCreate makes a plain array for an array of the realm that has no own constructor:
/// %Array.prototype%.constructor is %Array%, whose @@species is the intrinsic getter.
pub fn array_species_is_unchanged(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    realm.storage.array_species.holds(vm, realm, watch_array_species)
}

/// The set that stays valid while ArraySpeciesCreate makes a plain array for an array of the realm that has no own
/// constructor, if it does.
fn watch_array_species(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let array_prototype = realm.array_prototype();
    let array_constructor = realm.intrinsics().array_constructor(vm);
    let constructor = array_prototype
        .shape()
        .lookup(&vm.names.constructor)
        .map(|metadata| array_prototype.get_direct(metadata.offset));
    if constructor.is_none_or(|constructor| {
        !constructor.is_object() || constructor.as_object() != array_constructor.upcast::<Object>()
    }) || !array_constructor.has_intrinsic_symbol_species_getter(vm)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let array_constructor: Gc<Object> = array_constructor.upcast();
    watch_intrinsics(
        vm,
        &[array_prototype, array_constructor],
        &[
            (array_prototype, vm.names.constructor.clone()),
            (array_constructor, PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().species)),
        ],
    )
}

/// Whether %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] of the realm is its %Array.prototype.values%.
pub fn arrays_have_builtin_iterator_method(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    realm
        .storage
        .array_iterator_method
        .holds(vm, realm, watch_array_iterator_method)
}

/// The address of the cell of the realm that holds the set that stays valid while %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] of the
/// realm is its %Array.prototype.values%, if it holds a valid one. JIT code reads the cell to tell whether that held
/// when the realm last found out (see `arrays_have_builtin_iterator_method()`).
pub fn array_iterator_method_watchpoint_set_address(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<u64> {
    realm.storage.array_iterator_method.valid_set_address()
}

/// The address of the cell of the realm that holds the set that stays valid while array iterators of the realm have its
/// builtin `next` method, if it holds a valid one. JIT code reads the cell to tell whether they had it when the realm
/// last found out (see `array_iterators_have_builtin_next()`).
pub fn array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set_address(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<u64> {
    let cell = &realm.array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set;
    cell.get()
        .is_some_and(|set| set.is_valid())
        .then_some(cell.as_ptr() as u64)
}

/// The set that stays valid while %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] of the realm is its %Array.prototype.values%, if it is.
fn watch_array_iterator_method(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let array_prototype = realm.array_prototype();
    let iterator_key = PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator);
    let metadata = array_prototype.shape().lookup(&iterator_key)?;
    let iterator_method = array_prototype.get_direct(metadata.offset);
    if !iterator_method.is_object()
        || iterator_method.as_object() != realm.array_prototype_values_function().upcast::<Object>()
    {
        return None;
    }
    watch_intrinsics(vm, &[array_prototype], &[(array_prototype, iterator_key)])
}

/// Whether `array` is iterated with the array iterators of `realm` without anything observing them: it inherits
/// %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] of the realm, which is its %Array.prototype.values%, and the iterators have the
/// builtin `next` method.
pub fn array_is_iterated_unobservably(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, array: &Object) -> bool {
    if array.prototype() != Some(realm.array_prototype())
        || !array_iterators_have_builtin_next(vm, realm)
        || !arrays_have_builtin_iterator_method(vm, realm)
    {
        return false;
    }
    // NB: The array inherits the iterator method from %Array.prototype%, which holds it as a data property, unless it
    //     has an own @@iterator. Arrays without named properties have none.
    let shape = array.shape();
    shape.property_count() == 0
        || shape
            .lookup(&PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator))
            .is_none()
}

/// Whether %Array.prototype% and %Object.prototype% of the realm have no @@isConcatSpreadable.
pub fn array_prototypes_have_no_is_concat_spreadable(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    realm.storage.array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable.holds(
        vm,
        realm,
        watch_array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable,
    )
}

/// The set that stays valid while %Array.prototype% and %Object.prototype% of the realm have no @@isConcatSpreadable,
/// if they have none.
fn watch_array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let array_prototype = realm.array_prototype();
    let object_prototype = realm.object_prototype();
    let key = PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().is_concat_spreadable);
    // NB: %Object.prototype% has an immutable prototype.
    if array_prototype.shape().prototype() != Some(object_prototype)
        || array_prototype.shape().lookup(&key).is_some()
        || object_prototype.shape().lookup(&key).is_some()
    {
        return None;
    }
    watch_intrinsics(vm, &[array_prototype, object_prototype], &[])
}

/// Whether ToPrimitive of a String object of the realm that inherits from %String.prototype% without own `valueOf`,
/// `toString` or @@toPrimitive gives its [[StringData]].
pub fn string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    realm.storage.string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data.holds(
        vm,
        realm,
        watch_string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data,
    )
}

/// The set that stays valid while ToPrimitive of a String object of the realm that inherits from %String.prototype%
/// without own `valueOf`, `toString` or @@toPrimitive gives its [[StringData]], if it does.
fn watch_string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<Gc<WatchpointSet>> {
    let string_prototype = realm.string_prototype(vm);
    let object_prototype = realm.object_prototype();
    let to_primitive_key = PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().to_primitive);
    // NB: An accessor property holds an accessor, which is not a function.
    let own_property_value = |key: &PropertyKey| {
        let metadata = string_prototype.shape().lookup(key)?;
        Some(string_prototype.get_direct(metadata.offset))
    };
    // NB: %Object.prototype% has an immutable prototype.
    if string_prototype.shape().prototype() != Some(object_prototype)
        || string_prototype.shape().lookup(&to_primitive_key).is_some()
        || object_prototype.shape().lookup(&to_primitive_key).is_some()
        || !own_property_value(&vm.names.valueOf).is_some_and(|value| StringPrototype::is_value_of_function(vm, value))
        || !own_property_value(&vm.names.toString)
            .is_some_and(|value| StringPrototype::is_to_string_function(vm, value))
    {
        return None;
    }
    watch_intrinsics(
        vm,
        &[string_prototype, object_prototype],
        &[
            (string_prototype, vm.names.valueOf.clone()),
            (string_prototype, vm.names.toString.clone()),
        ],
    )
}

/// The parts of a realm the interpreter does not read.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct RealmStorage {
    /// The cell that an embedder written in Rust keeps its data of the realm in, next to [[HostDefined]], which an
    /// embedder written in C++ sets.
    embedder_data: ForeignCellSlot,
    /// Whether %RegExp.prototype% and %RegExp% have the properties the fast paths of RegExp skip reading as the realm
    /// made them (see `runtime::realm_watchpoints`).
    pub(crate) regexp_primordial_properties: WatchedCondition,
    /// Whether ArraySpeciesCreate makes plain arrays (see `runtime::realm_watchpoints`).
    pub(crate) array_species: WatchedCondition,
    /// Whether %Array.prototype%[@@iterator] is %Array.prototype.values% (see `runtime::realm_watchpoints`).
    pub(crate) array_iterator_method: WatchedCondition,
    /// Whether %Array.prototype% and %Object.prototype% have no @@isConcatSpreadable (see
    /// `runtime::realm_watchpoints`).
    pub(crate) array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable: WatchedCondition,
    /// Whether ToPrimitive of a String object that inherits from %String.prototype% gives its [[StringData]] (see
    /// `runtime::realm_watchpoints`).
    pub(crate) string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data: WatchedCondition,
    /// Whether this is the VM's empty realm, which nothing may fill (see `Vm::empty_realm()`).
    empty: bool,
}

define_cell!(Realm, Other);

// SAFETY: Visits every cell a realm holds.
unsafe impl Trace for Realm {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.intrinsics.trace(visitor);
        self.global_object.trace(visitor);
        self.global_environment.trace(visitor);
        self.global_declarative_environment.trace(visitor);
        self.host_defined.trace(visitor);
        self.storage.embedder_data.trace(visitor);
        self.storage.regexp_primordial_properties.trace(visitor);
        self.storage.array_species.trace(visitor);
        self.storage.array_iterator_method.trace(visitor);
        self.storage
            .array_prototypes_without_is_concat_spreadable
            .trace(visitor);
        self.storage.string_objects_convert_to_their_string_data.trace(visitor);
        self.array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set.trace(visitor);
        self.array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// Accessors for the intrinsics CreateIntrinsics creates up front, which the object model asks the realm for.
macro_rules! realm_intrinsic_accessors {
    (cells { $($name:ident: $type:ty,)* } offsets { $($offset:ident,)* }) => {
        impl Realm {
            $(
                pub fn $name(&self) -> Gc<$type> {
                    self.intrinsics().$name()
                }
            )*
            $(
                pub fn $offset(&self) -> u32 {
                    self.intrinsics().$offset()
                }
            )*
        }
    };
}

realm_intrinsic_accessors! {

        new_object_shape: Shape,
        iterator_result_object_shape: Shape,
        normal_function_prototype_shape: Shape,
        normal_function_shape: Shape,
        normal_constructor_function_shape: Shape,
        async_function_shape: Shape,
        generator_function_shape: Shape,
        async_generator_function_shape: Shape,
        native_function_shape: Shape,
        unmapped_arguments_object_shape: Shape,
        mapped_arguments_object_shape: Shape,
        regexp_builtin_exec_array_shape: Shape,
        throw_type_error_accessor: Accessor,
        array_prototype_values_function: FunctionObject,
        generator_prototype_next_function: FunctionObject,
        eval_function: FunctionObject,
        array_iterator_prototype: Object,
    }
    offsets {
        iterator_result_object_value_offset,
        iterator_result_object_done_offset,
        normal_function_prototype_constructor_offset,
        generator_function_length_offset,
        generator_function_name_offset,
        generator_function_prototype_property_offset,
        native_function_length_offset,
        native_function_name_offset,
        unmapped_arguments_object_length_offset,
        unmapped_arguments_object_well_known_symbol_iterator_offset,
        unmapped_arguments_object_callee_offset,
        mapped_arguments_object_length_offset,
        mapped_arguments_object_well_known_symbol_iterator_offset,
        mapped_arguments_object_callee_offset,
        regexp_builtin_exec_array_index_offset,
        regexp_builtin_exec_array_input_offset,
        regexp_builtin_exec_array_groups_offset,
    }
}

impl Realm {
    /// A realm without intrinsics, a global object or a global environment, which
    /// InitializeHostDefinedRealm goes on to create.
    pub fn create(vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Realm> {
        Self::allocate(vm, RealmStorage::default())
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_empty(vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Realm> {
        Self::allocate(
            vm,
            RealmStorage {
                empty: true,
                ..RealmStorage::default()
            },
        )
    }

    fn allocate(vm: &Vm, storage: RealmStorage) -> Gc<Realm> {
        vm.heap().allocate(|_| Realm {
            header: CellHeader::for_class(Self::CLASS),
            global_object: Cell::new(None),
            global_declarative_environment: Cell::new(None),
            global_environment: Cell::new(None),
            intrinsics: Cell::new(None),
            host_defined: ForeignCellSlot::empty(),
            array_iterator_next_watchpoint_set: Cell::new(None),
            array_iterator_return_watchpoint_set: Cell::new(None),
            storage,
        })
    }

    // 9.3.1 InitializeHostDefinedRealm ( ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-initializehostdefinedrealm
    pub fn initialize_host_defined_realm(
        vm: &Vm,
        create_global_object: Option<&dyn Fn(Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<Object>>,
        create_global_this_value: Option<&dyn Fn(Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<Object>>,
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<OwnedExecutionContext> {
        // 7. Let newContext be a new execution context.
        let new_context = OwnedExecutionContext::create(0, 0, 0);
        Self::initialize_host_defined_realm_in(vm, &new_context, create_global_object, create_global_this_value)?;
        Ok(new_context)
    }

    /// InitializeHostDefinedRealm with `new_context`, a new execution context of the caller's, as its newContext. The
    /// context stays on the execution context stack, as the running execution context, until the caller pops it.
    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps, reason = "the operation can throw in the spec")]
    pub fn initialize_host_defined_realm_in(
        vm: &Vm,
        new_context: &ExecutionContext,
        create_global_object: Option<&dyn Fn(Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<Object>>,
        create_global_this_value: Option<&dyn Fn(Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<Object>>,
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Realm>> {
        // 1. Let realm be a new Realm Record
        let realm = Realm::create(vm);

        // 2. Perform CreateIntrinsics(realm).
        Intrinsics::create(vm, realm);

        // FIXME: 3. Set realm.[[AgentSignifier]] to AgentSignifier().

        // NOTE: Done on step 1.
        // 4. Set realm.[[GlobalObject]] to undefined.
        // 5. Set realm.[[GlobalEnv]] to undefined.

        // FIXME: 6. Set realm.[[TemplateMap]] to a new empty List.

        // 7. Let newContext be a new execution context.
        // NOTE: The caller passes it in.

        // 8. Set the Function of newContext to null.
        new_context.function.set(None);

        // 9. Set the Realm of newContext to realm.
        new_context.set_realm(Some(realm));

        // 10. Set the ScriptOrModule of newContext to null.
        new_context.set_script_or_module(ScriptOrModule::Empty);

        // 11. Push newContext onto the execution context stack; newContext is now the running execution context.
        vm.push_execution_context(NonNull::from(new_context));

        // 12. If the host requires use of an exotic object to serve as realm's global object, then
        let global = if let Some(create_global_object) = create_global_object {
            // a. Let global be such an object created in a host-defined manner.
            create_global_object(realm)
        }
        // 13. Else,
        else {
            // a. Let global be OrdinaryObjectCreate(realm.[[Intrinsics]].[[%Object.prototype%]]).
            // NOTE: We allocate a proper GlobalObject directly as this plain object is
            //       turned into one via SetDefaultGlobalBindings in the spec.
            allocate_object(vm, |_| GlobalObject::new(vm, GlobalObject::CLASS, realm)).upcast()
        };

        // 14. If the host requires that the this binding in realm's global scope return an object other than the global object, then
        let this_value = if let Some(create_global_this_value) = create_global_this_value {
            // a. Let thisValue be such an object created in a host-defined manner.
            create_global_this_value(realm)
        }
        // 15. Else,
        else {
            // a. Let thisValue be global.
            global
        };

        // 16. Set realm.[[GlobalObject]] to global.
        realm.global_object.set(Some(global));

        // 17. Set realm.[[GlobalEnv]] to NewGlobalEnvironment(global, thisValue).
        realm.set_global_environment(GlobalEnvironment::create(vm, global, this_value));

        // 18. Perform ? SetDefaultGlobalBindings(realm).
        set_default_global_bindings(vm, realm);

        // 19. Create any host-defined global object properties on global.
        global.initialize(vm, realm);

        // 20. Return unused.
        Ok(realm)
    }

    /// Realm::create<T>(): allocates an object and runs its initialize(), which defines the properties of built-in
    /// objects.
    pub fn create_object<T: GcCell + Extends<Object>>(&self, vm: &Vm, build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T) -> Gc<T> {
        let object = allocate_object(vm, build);
        object.upcast::<Object>().initialize(vm, self.as_gc());
        object
    }

    fn as_gc(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        Gc::from_ref(self)
    }

    pub fn intrinsics(&self) -> Gc<Intrinsics> {
        self.intrinsics.get().expect("the realm has its intrinsics")
    }

    pub fn set_intrinsics(&self, intrinsics: Gc<Intrinsics>) {
        self.assert_not_empty();
        assert!(self.intrinsics.get().is_none());
        self.intrinsics.set(Some(intrinsics));
    }

    pub fn global_object(&self) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.global_object.get().expect("the realm has a global object")
    }

    pub fn set_global_object(&self, global: Gc<Object>) {
        self.assert_not_empty();
        self.global_object.set(Some(global));
    }

    pub fn global_environment(&self) -> Gc<GlobalEnvironment> {
        self.global_environment
            .get()
            .expect("the realm has a global environment")
    }

    pub fn set_global_environment(&self, environment: Gc<GlobalEnvironment>) {
        self.assert_not_empty();
        self.global_environment.set(Some(environment));
        self.global_declarative_environment
            .set(Some(environment.declarative_record()));
    }

    /// [[HostDefined]]
    pub fn host_defined(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.host_defined.get()
    }

    /// The data of the realm that an embedder written in Rust set, if it is a cell of the embedder's type.
    pub fn embedder_data<T: EmbedderValue>(&self) -> Option<Gc<EmbedderCell<T>>> {
        let cell = self.storage.embedder_data.get()?;
        // SAFETY: The slot only holds what set_embedder_data() stores, which is a live cell of an embedder's type,
        //         and the realm keeps the cell alive.
        unsafe { T::CLASS.downcast(cell) }
    }

    /// Sets the data of the realm, a cell that the realm keeps alive from then on. A realm holds the data of one
    /// embedder.
    pub fn set_embedder_data<T: EmbedderValue>(&self, data: Gc<EmbedderCell<T>>) {
        self.assert_not_empty();
        // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the heap that the realm is in.
        unsafe { self.storage.embedder_data.set(Some(data.as_non_null().cast())) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn assert_not_empty(&self) {
        assert!(!self.storage.empty, "nothing may fill the empty realm");
    }

    pub fn global_declarative_environment(&self) -> Gc<DeclarativeEnvironment> {
        self.global_declarative_environment
            .get()
            .expect("the realm has a global environment")
    }

    pub fn string_prototype(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.intrinsics().string_prototype(vm)
    }

    pub fn number_prototype(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.intrinsics().number_prototype(vm)
    }

    pub fn boolean_prototype(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.intrinsics().boolean_prototype(vm)
    }

    pub fn bigint_prototype(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.intrinsics().bigint_prototype(vm)
    }

    pub fn symbol_prototype(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.intrinsics().symbol_prototype(vm)
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/runtime/reference.rs
/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use ak::Utf16FlyString;

use crate::bytecode::property_access::Strict;
use crate::gc::visitor::{Trace, Visitor};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::runtime::completion::ThrowCompletionOr;
use crate::runtime::environment::{Environment, InitializeBindingHint};
use crate::runtime::environment_coordinate::EnvironmentCoordinate;
use crate::runtime::error::ErrorKind;
use crate::runtime::error_types::ErrorType;
use crate::runtime::object::{Object, PropertyLookupPhase, ShouldThrowExceptions};
use crate::runtime::private_environment::PrivateName;
use crate::runtime::property_key::PropertyKey;

/// Mirrors Reference::BaseType.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BaseType {
    Unresolvable,
    Value,
    Environment,
}

/// The [[ReferencedName]] of a Reference: a property key, or the private name of a private reference.
#[derive(Clone)]
enum ReferencedName {
    PropertyKey(PropertyKey),
    PrivateName(PrivateName),
}

// 6.2.4 The Reference Record Specification Type, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reference-record-specification-type
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Reference {
    name: ReferencedName,
    /// The [[Base]] of a reference whose base type is Value.
    base_value: Value,
    base_environment: Option<Gc<Environment>>,
    this_value: Option<Value>,
    environment_coordinate: Option<EnvironmentCoordinate>,
    base_type: BaseType,
    strict: Strict,
}

// SAFETY: Visits the base, the name and the this value, as Reference::visit_edges does.
unsafe impl Trace for Reference {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        match self.base_type {
            BaseType::Value => self.base_value.trace(visitor),
            BaseType::Environment => self.base_environment.trace(visitor),
            BaseType::Unresolvable => {}
        }
        match &self.name {
            ReferencedName::PropertyKey(key) => key.trace(visitor),
            ReferencedName::PrivateName(name) => name.trace(visitor),
        }
        self.this_value.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl Reference {
    pub fn with_base_type(base_type: BaseType, name: PropertyKey, strict: Strict) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: ReferencedName::PropertyKey(name),
            base_value: Value::UNDEFINED,
            base_environment: None,
            this_value: None,
            environment_coordinate: None,
            base_type,
            strict,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_base_value(base: Value, name: PropertyKey, this_value: Option<Value>, strict: Strict) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: ReferencedName::PropertyKey(name),
            base_value: base,
            base_environment: None,
            this_value,
            environment_coordinate: None,
            base_type: BaseType::Value,
            strict,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_base_environment(
        base: Gc<Environment>,
        referenced_name: Utf16FlyString,
        strict: Strict,
        environment_coordinate: Option<EnvironmentCoordinate>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: ReferencedName::PropertyKey(PropertyKey::from(referenced_name)),
            base_value: Value::UNDEFINED,
            base_environment: Some(base),
            this_value: None,
            environment_coordinate,
            base_type: BaseType::Environment,
            strict,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_private_name(base: Value, name: PrivateName) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: ReferencedName::PrivateName(name),
            base_value: base,
            base_environment: None,
            this_value: None,
            environment_coordinate: None,
            base_type: BaseType::Value,
            strict: Strict::Yes,
        }
    }

    pub fn base(&self) -> Value {
        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Value);
        self.base_value
    }

    pub fn base_environment(&self) -> Gc<Environment> {
        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Environment);
        self.base_environment
            .expect("an environment reference has its environment")
    }

    pub fn name(&self) -> &PropertyKey {
        match &self.name {
            ReferencedName::PropertyKey(key) => key,
            ReferencedName::PrivateName(_) => panic!("the reference is a private reference"),
        }
    }

    pub fn private_name(&self) -> &PrivateName {
        match &self.name {
            ReferencedName::PrivateName(name) => name,
            ReferencedName::PropertyKey(_) => panic!("the reference is not a private reference"),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_strict(&self) -> bool {
        self.strict == Strict::Yes
    }

    // 6.2.4.2 IsUnresolvableReference ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isunresolvablereference
    pub fn is_unresolvable(&self) -> bool {
        self.base_type == BaseType::Unresolvable
    }

    // 6.2.4.1 IsPropertyReference ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ispropertyreference
    pub fn is_property_reference(&self) -> bool {
        if self.is_unresolvable() {
            return false;
        }
        if self.base_type == BaseType::Environment {
            return false;
        }
        true
    }

    // 6.2.4.7 GetThisValue ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getthisvalue
    pub fn get_this_value(&self) -> Value {
        assert!(self.is_property_reference());
        if let Some(this_value) = self.this_value {
            return this_value;
        }
        self.base_value
    }

    // 6.2.4.3 IsSuperReference ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-issuperreference
    pub fn is_super_reference(&self) -> bool {
        self.this_value.is_some()
    }

    // 6.2.4.4 IsPrivateReference ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isprivatereference
    pub fn is_private_reference(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.name, ReferencedName::PrivateName(_))
    }

    // Note: Non-standard helper.
    pub fn is_environment_reference(&self) -> bool {
        self.base_type == BaseType::Environment
    }

    pub fn is_valid_reference(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }

    pub fn environment_coordinate(&self) -> Option<EnvironmentCoordinate> {
        self.environment_coordinate
    }

    /// The base environment as the declarative environment the reference's coordinate indexes into.
    fn coordinate_environment(&self) -> &crate::runtime::declarative_environment::DeclarativeEnvironment {
        let environment = self
            .base_environment
            .as_ref()
            .expect("an environment reference has its environment");
        environment
            .as_declarative_environment()
            .expect("only declarative environments report binding coordinates")
    }

    // 6.2.4.6 PutValue ( V, W ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-putvalue
    pub fn put_value(&self, vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
        // 1. ReturnIfAbrupt(V).
        // 2. ReturnIfAbrupt(W).

        // 3. If V is not a Reference Record, throw a ReferenceError exception.
        if !self.is_valid_reference() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::ReferenceError, ErrorType::InvalidLeftHandAssignment, &[]);
        }

        // 4. If IsUnresolvableReference(V) is true, then
        if self.is_unresolvable() {
            // a. If V.[[Strict]] is true, throw a ReferenceError exception.
            if self.strict == Strict::Yes {
                return self.throw_reference_error(vm);
            }

            // b. Let globalObj be GetGlobalObject().
            let global_object = vm.get_global_object();

            // c. Perform ? Set(globalObj, V.[[ReferencedName]], W, false).
            global_object.set(vm, self.name(), value, ShouldThrowExceptions::No)?;

            // Return unused.
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 5. If IsPropertyReference(V) is true, then
        if self.is_property_reference() {
            // a. Let baseObj be ? ToObject(V.[[Base]]).
            let base_obj = self.base_value.to_object(vm)?;

            // b. If IsPrivateReference(V) is true, then
            if self.is_private_reference() {
                // i. Return ? PrivateSet(baseObj, V.[[ReferencedName]], W).
                return base_obj.private_set(vm, self.private_name(), value);
            }

            // c. Let succeeded be ? baseObj.[[Set]](V.[[ReferencedName]], W, GetThisValue(V)).
            let succeeded = base_obj.internal_set(
                vm,
                self.name(),
                value,
                self.get_this_value(),
                None,
                PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
            )?;

            // d. If succeeded is false and V.[[Strict]] is true, throw a TypeError exception.
            if !succeeded && self.strict == Strict::Yes {
                return vm.throw_completion(
                    ErrorKind::TypeError,
                    ErrorType::ReferenceNullishSetProperty,
                    &[self.name(), &self.base_value],
                );
            }

            // e. Return unused.
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 6. Else,
        // a. Let base be V.[[Base]].

        // b. Assert: base is an Environment Record.
        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Environment);
        let base_environment = self.base_environment();

        // c. Return ? base.SetMutableBinding(V.[[ReferencedName]], W, V.[[Strict]]) (see 9.1).
        if let Some(environment_coordinate) = self.environment_coordinate {
            return self.coordinate_environment().set_mutable_binding_direct(
                vm,
                environment_coordinate.index as usize,
                value,
                self.strict == Strict::Yes,
            );
        }
        base_environment.set_mutable_binding(vm, self.name().as_string(), value, self.strict == Strict::Yes)
    }

    fn throw_reference_error<T>(&self, vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
        if self.is_private_reference() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::ReferenceError, ErrorType::ReferenceUnresolvable, &[]);
        }
        vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::ReferenceError, ErrorType::UnknownIdentifier, &[self.name()])
    }

    // 6.2.4.5 GetValue ( V ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getvalue
    pub fn get_value(&self, vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // 1. ReturnIfAbrupt(V).
        // 2. If V is not a Reference Record, return V.

        // 3. If IsUnresolvableReference(V) is true, throw a ReferenceError exception.
        if !self.is_valid_reference() || self.is_unresolvable() {
            return self.throw_reference_error(vm);
        }

        // 4. If IsPropertyReference(V) is true, then
        if self.is_property_reference() {
            // a. Let baseObj be ? ToObject(V.[[Base]]).
            // NOTE: Deferred as an optimization; we might not actually need to create an object.

            // b. If IsPrivateReference(V) is true, then
            if self.is_private_reference() {
                // FIXME: We need to be able to specify the receiver for this
                // if we want to use it in error messages in future
                // as things currently stand this does the "wrong thing" but
                // the error is unobservable

                let base_obj = self.base_value.to_object(vm)?;

                // i. Return ? PrivateGet(baseObj, V.[[ReferencedName]]).
                return base_obj.private_get(vm, self.private_name());
            }

            // OPTIMIZATION: For various primitives we can avoid actually creating a new object for them.
            let realm = || {
                vm.current_realm()
                    .expect("GetValue runs in an execution context with a realm")
            };
            let base_obj: Gc<Object> = if self.base_value.is_string() {
                let string_value = self.base_value.as_string().get(vm, self.name())?;
                if let Some(string_value) = string_value {
                    return Ok(string_value);
                }
                realm().string_prototype(vm)
            } else if self.base_value.is_number() {
                realm().number_prototype(vm)
            } else if self.base_value.is_boolean() {
                realm().boolean_prototype(vm)
            } else if self.base_value.is_bigint() {
                realm().bigint_prototype(vm)
            } else if self.base_value.is_symbol() {
                realm().symbol_prototype(vm)
            } else {
                self.base_value.to_object(vm)?
            };

            // c. Return ? baseObj.[[Get]](V.[[ReferencedName]], GetThisValue(V)).
            return base_obj.internal_get(
                vm,
                self.name(),
                self.get_this_value(),
                None,
                PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
            );
        }

        // 5. Else,
        // a. Let base be V.[[Base]].

        // b. Assert: base is an Environment Record.
        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Environment);
        let base_environment = self.base_environment();

        // c. Return ? base.GetBindingValue(V.[[ReferencedName]], V.[[Strict]]) (see 9.1).
        if let Some(environment_coordinate) = self.environment_coordinate {
            return self
                .coordinate_environment()
                .get_binding_value_direct(vm, environment_coordinate.index as usize);
        }
        base_environment.get_binding_value(vm, self.name().as_string(), self.strict == Strict::Yes)
    }

    // 13.5.1.2 Runtime Semantics: Evaluation, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-delete-operator-runtime-semantics-evaluation
    pub fn delete_(&self, vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<bool> {
        // 13.5.1.2 Runtime Semantics: Evaluation, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-delete-operator-runtime-semantics-evaluation
        // UnaryExpression : delete UnaryExpression

        // NOTE: The following steps have already been evaluated by the time we get here:
        // 1. Let ref be the result of evaluating UnaryExpression.
        // 2. ReturnIfAbrupt(ref).
        // 3. If ref is not a Reference Record, return true.

        // 4. If IsUnresolvableReference(ref) is true, then
        if self.is_unresolvable() {
            // a. Assert: ref.[[Strict]] is false.
            assert!(self.strict == Strict::No);
            // b. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 5. If IsPropertyReference(ref) is true, then
        if self.is_property_reference() {
            // a. Assert: IsPrivateReference(ref) is false.
            assert!(!self.is_private_reference());

            // b. If IsSuperReference(ref) is true, throw a ReferenceError exception.
            if self.is_super_reference() {
                return vm.throw_completion(
                    ErrorKind::ReferenceError,
                    ErrorType::UnsupportedDeleteSuperProperty,
                    &[],
                );
            }

            // c. Let baseObj be ? ToObject(ref.[[Base]]).
            let base_obj = self.base_value.to_object(vm)?;

            // d. Let deleteStatus be ? baseObj.[[Delete]](ref.[[ReferencedName]]).
            let delete_status = base_obj.internal_delete(vm, self.name())?;

            // e. If deleteStatus is false and ref.[[Strict]] is true, throw a TypeError exception.
            if !delete_status && self.strict == Strict::Yes {
                return vm.throw_completion(
                    ErrorKind::TypeError,
                    ErrorType::ReferenceNullishDeleteProperty,
                    &[self.name(), &self.base_value],
                );
            }

            // f. Return deleteStatus.
            return Ok(delete_status);
        }

        // 6. Else,
        //    a. Let base be ref.[[Base]].
        //    b. Assert: base is an Environment Record.

        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Environment);

        //    c. Return ? base.DeleteBinding(ref.[[ReferencedName]]).
        self.base_environment().delete_binding(vm, self.name().as_string())
    }

    // 6.2.4.8 InitializeReferencedBinding ( V, W ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object.prototype.hasownproperty
    // 1.2.1.1 InitializeReferencedBinding ( V, W, hint ), https://tc39.es/proposal-explicit-resource-management/#sec-initializereferencedbinding
    pub fn initialize_referenced_binding(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        value: Value,
        hint: InitializeBindingHint,
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
        assert!(!self.is_unresolvable());
        assert!(self.base_type == BaseType::Environment);
        self.base_environment()
            .initialize_binding(vm, self.name().as_string(), value, hint)
    }
}

// 6.2.4.9 MakePrivateReference ( baseValue, privateIdentifier ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-makeprivatereference
pub fn make_private_reference(vm: &Vm, base_value: Value, private_identifier: &Utf16FlyString) -> Reference {
    let context = vm
        .running_execution_context_if_any()
        .expect("MakePrivateReference runs in an execution context");

    // 1. Let privEnv be the running execution context's PrivateEnvironment.
    let private_environment = context.private_environment();

    // 2. Assert: privEnv is not null.
    let private_environment = private_environment.expect("there is a private environment");

    // 3. Let privateName be ResolvePrivateIdentifier(privEnv, privateIdentifier).
    let private_name = private_environment.resolve_private_identifier(private_identifier);

    // 4. Return the Reference Record { [[Base]]: baseValue, [[ReferencedName]]: privateName, [[Strict]]: true, [[ThisValue]]: empty }.
    Reference::with_private_name(base_value, private_name)
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/runtime/reflect_object.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use libjs_runtime_macros::Trace;

use crate::gc::class::{GcCell, define_cell};
use crate::interpreter::vm::Vm;
use crate::layout::cell::Gc;
use crate::layout::function_object::RawNativeFunction;
use crate::layout::object::Object;
use crate::layout::value::Value;
use crate::layout_forward::RawNativeFunctionPointer;
use crate::runtime::abstract_operations::{call_function_object, construct, create_argument_list_from_array_like};
use crate::runtime::array::Array;
use crate::runtime::completion::ThrowCompletionOr;
use crate::runtime::error::ErrorKind;
use crate::runtime::error_types::ErrorType;
use crate::runtime::function_prototype::is_native_function;
use crate::runtime::native_function::raw_native;
use crate::runtime::object::{
    MayInterfereWithIndexedPropertyAccess, ORDINARY_OBJECT_METHODS, PropertyLookupPhase, define_object_class,
};
use crate::runtime::primitive_string::PrimitiveString;
use crate::runtime::property_attributes::{Attribute, PropertyAttributes};
use crate::runtime::property_descriptor::{from_property_descriptor, to_property_descriptor};
use crate::runtime::property_key::PropertyKey;
use crate::runtime::realm::Realm;

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Trace)]
pub struct ReflectObject {
    base: Object,
}

define_object_class!(ReflectObject, extends: [Object], methods: {
    initialize: ReflectObject::initialize,
    ..ORDINARY_OBJECT_METHODS
});

static APPLY_FUNCTION: RawNativeFunctionPointer = raw_native!(ReflectObject::apply);

impl ReflectObject {
    /// Whether the function is Reflect.apply (of any realm).
    pub fn is_apply_function(vm: &Vm, function: &RawNativeFunction) -> bool {
        is_native_function(vm, function, APPLY_FUNCTION)
    }

    pub fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<ReflectObject> {
        realm.create_object(vm, |_| ReflectObject {
            base: Object::new_with_prototype(
                vm,
                Self::CLASS,
                realm,
                Some(realm.object_prototype()),
                MayInterfereWithIndexedPropertyAccess::No,
            ),
        })
    }

    fn initialize(object: &Object, vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) {
        let names = &vm.names;
        let attr = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
        let define_native_function = |property_key: &PropertyKey, function, length| {
            object.define_native_function(vm, realm, property_key, function, length, attr, None);
        };
        define_native_function(&names.apply, APPLY_FUNCTION, 3);
        define_native_function(&names.construct, raw_native!(ReflectObject::construct), 2);
        define_native_function(&names.defineProperty, raw_native!(ReflectObject::define_property), 3);
        define_native_function(&names.deleteProperty, raw_native!(ReflectObject::delete_property), 2);
        define_native_function(&names.get, raw_native!(ReflectObject::get), 2);
        define_native_function(
            &names.getOwnPropertyDescriptor,
            raw_native!(ReflectObject::get_own_property_descriptor),
            2,
        );
        define_native_function(&names.getPrototypeOf, raw_native!(ReflectObject::get_prototype_of), 1);
        define_native_function(&names.has, raw_native!(ReflectObject::has), 2);
        define_native_function(&names.isExtensible, raw_native!(ReflectObject::is_extensible), 1);
        define_native_function(&names.ownKeys, raw_native!(ReflectObject::own_keys), 1);
        define_native_function(
            &names.preventExtensions,
            raw_native!(ReflectObject::prevent_extensions),
            1,
        );
        define_native_function(&names.set, raw_native!(ReflectObject::set), 3);
        define_native_function(&names.setPrototypeOf, raw_native!(ReflectObject::set_prototype_of), 2);

        // 28.1.14 Reflect [ @@toStringTag ], https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect-@@tostringtag
        object.define_direct_property(
            vm,
            &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().to_string_tag),
            Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_fly_string(vm, names.Reflect.as_string())),
            PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
        );
    }

    // 28.1.1 Reflect.apply ( target, thisArgument, argumentsList ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.apply
    fn apply(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let this_argument = vm.argument(1);
        let arguments_list = vm.argument(2);

        // 1. If IsCallable(target) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_function() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAFunction, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let args be ? CreateListFromArrayLike(argumentsList).
        let args = create_argument_list_from_array_like(vm, arguments_list)?;

        // 3. Perform PrepareForTailCall().
        // 4. Return ? Call(target, thisArgument, args).
        call_function_object(vm, target.as_function(), this_argument, &args.values())
    }

    // 28.1.2 Reflect.construct ( target, argumentsList [ , newTarget ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.construct
    fn construct(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let arguments_list = vm.argument(1);
        let mut new_target = vm.argument(2);

        // 1. If IsConstructor(target) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_constructor() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAConstructor, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. If newTarget is not present, set newTarget to target.
        if vm.argument_count() < 3 {
            new_target = target;
        }
        // 3. Else if IsConstructor(newTarget) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        else if !new_target.is_constructor() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAConstructor, &[&new_target]);
        }

        // 4. Let args be ? CreateListFromArrayLike(argumentsList).
        let args = create_argument_list_from_array_like(vm, arguments_list)?;

        // 5. Return ? Construct(target, args, newTarget).
        Ok(Value::from_object(construct(
            vm,
            target.as_function(),
            &args.to_vec(),
            Some(new_target.as_function()),
        )?))
    }

    // 28.1.3 Reflect.defineProperty ( target, propertyKey, attributes ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.defineproperty
    fn define_property(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);
        let attributes = vm.argument(2);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. Let desc be ? ToPropertyDescriptor(attributes).
        let mut descriptor = to_property_descriptor(vm, attributes)?;

        // 4. Return ? target.[[DefineOwnProperty]](key, desc).
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_define_own_property(
            vm,
            &key,
            &mut descriptor,
            None,
        )?))
    }

    // 28.1.4 Reflect.deleteProperty ( target, propertyKey ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.deleteproperty
    fn delete_property(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. Return ? target.[[Delete]](key).
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_delete(vm, &key)?))
    }

    // 28.1.5 Reflect.get ( target, propertyKey [ , receiver ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.get
    fn get(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);
        let mut receiver = vm.argument(2);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. If receiver is not present, then
        if vm.argument_count() < 3 {
            // a. Set receiver to target.
            receiver = target;
        }

        // 4. Return ? target.[[Get]](key, receiver).
        target
            .as_object()
            .internal_get(vm, &key, receiver, None, PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty)
    }

    // 28.1.6 Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor ( target, propertyKey ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.getownpropertydescriptor
    fn get_own_property_descriptor(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. Let desc be ? target.[[GetOwnProperty]](key).
        let descriptor = target.as_object().internal_get_own_property(vm, &key)?;

        // 4. Return FromPropertyDescriptor(desc).
        Ok(from_property_descriptor(vm, &descriptor))
    }

    // 28.1.7 Reflect.getPrototypeOf ( target ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.getprototypeof
    fn get_prototype_of(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Return ? target.[[GetPrototypeOf]]().
        Ok(target
            .as_object()
            .internal_get_prototype_of(vm)?
            .map_or(Value::NULL, Value::from_object))
    }

    // 28.1.8 Reflect.has ( target, propertyKey ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.has
    fn has(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. Return ? target.[[HasProperty]](key).
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_has_property(vm, &key)?))
    }

    // 28.1.9 Reflect.isExtensible ( target ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.isextensible
    fn is_extensible(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Return ? target.[[IsExtensible]]().
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_is_extensible(vm)?))
    }

    // 28.1.10 Reflect.ownKeys ( target ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.ownkeys
    fn own_keys(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");

        let target = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let keys be ? target.[[OwnPropertyKeys]]().
        let keys = target.as_object().internal_own_property_keys(vm)?;

        // 3. Return CreateArrayFromList(keys).
        Ok(Value::from_object(Array::create_from_list(vm, realm, &keys)))
    }

    // 28.1.11 Reflect.preventExtensions ( target ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.preventextensions
    fn prevent_extensions(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Return ? target.[[PreventExtensions]]().
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_prevent_extensions(vm)?))
    }

    // 28.1.12 Reflect.set ( target, propertyKey, V [ , receiver ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.set
    fn set(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let property_key = vm.argument(1);
        let value = vm.argument(2);
        let mut receiver = vm.argument(3);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. Let key be ? ToPropertyKey(propertyKey).
        let key = property_key.to_property_key(vm)?;

        // 3. If receiver is not present, then
        if vm.argument_count() < 4 {
            // a. Set receiver to target.
            receiver = target;
        }

        // 4. Return ? target.[[Set]](key, V, receiver).
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_set(
            vm,
            &key,
            value,
            receiver,
            None,
            PropertyLookupPhase::OwnProperty,
        )?))
    }

    // 28.1.13 Reflect.setPrototypeOf ( target, proto ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-reflect.setprototypeof
    fn set_prototype_of(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let target = vm.argument(0);
        let prototype = vm.argument(1);

        // 1. If Type(target) is not Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !target.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&target]);
        }

        // 2. If Type(proto) is not Object and proto is not null, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !prototype.is_object() && !prototype.is_null() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::ObjectPrototypeWrongType, &[]);
        }

        // 3. Return ? target.[[SetPrototypeOf]](proto).
        Ok(Value::from_bool(target.as_object().internal_set_prototype_of(
            vm,
            (!prototype.is_null()).then(|| prototype.as_object()),
        )?))
    }
}
