#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Trace)]
pub struct SharedArrayBufferPrototype {
    base: Object,
}

define_object_class!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype, extends: [Object], methods: {
    initialize: SharedArrayBufferPrototype::initialize,
    ..ORDINARY_OBJECT_METHODS
});

fn this_array_buffer(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    typed_this_value::<ArrayBuffer>(vm, "SharedArrayBuffer")
}

impl SharedArrayBufferPrototype {
    pub fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<SharedArrayBufferPrototype> {
        realm.create_object(vm, |_| SharedArrayBufferPrototype {
            base: Object::new_with_prototype(
                vm,
                Self::CLASS,
                realm,
                Some(realm.object_prototype()),
                MayInterfereWithIndexedPropertyAccess::No,
            ),
        })
    }

    fn initialize(object: &Object, vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) {
        let names = &vm.names;
        let attr = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
        let configurable = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
        object.define_native_accessor(
            vm,
            realm,
            &names.byteLength,
            raw_native!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype::byte_length_getter),
            None,
            configurable,
        );
        object.define_native_function(
            vm,
            realm,
            &names.grow,
            raw_native!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype::grow),
            1,
            attr,
            None,
        );
        object.define_native_accessor(
            vm,
            realm,
            &names.growable,
            raw_native!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype::growable_getter),
            None,
            configurable,
        );
        object.define_native_accessor(
            vm,
            realm,
            &names.maxByteLength,
            raw_native!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype::max_byte_length),
            None,
            configurable,
        );
        object.define_native_function(
            vm,
            realm,
            &names.slice,
            raw_native!(SharedArrayBufferPrototype::slice),
            2,
            attr,
            None,
        );

        // 25.2.5.7 SharedArrayBuffer.prototype [ @@toStringTag ], https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.toString
        object.define_direct_property(
            vm,
            &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().to_string_tag),
            Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_fly_string(
                vm,
                names.SharedArrayBuffer.as_string(),
            )),
            configurable,
        );
    }

    // 25.2.5.1 get SharedArrayBuffer.prototype.byteLength, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.bytelength
    fn byte_length_getter(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // 1. Let O be the this value.
        // 2. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(O, [[ArrayBufferData]]).
        let array_buffer_object = this_array_buffer(vm)?;

        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(O) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 4. Let length be O.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
        // 5. Return 𝔽(length).
        Ok(Value::from_f64(array_buffer_object.byte_length() as f64))
    }

    // 25.2.5.3 SharedArrayBuffer.prototype.grow ( newLength ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.grow
    fn grow(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let new_length = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. Let O be the this value.
        let array_buffer_object = this_array_buffer(vm)?;

        // 2. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(O, [[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]]).
        if array_buffer_object.is_fixed_length() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::FixedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(O) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 4. Let newByteLength be ? ToIndex(newLength).
        let new_byte_length = new_length.to_index(vm)? as usize;

        // 5. Let hostHandled be ? HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer(O, newByteLength).
        let host_handled = vm.host_grow_shared_array_buffer()(vm, &array_buffer_object, new_byte_length)?;

        // 6. If hostHandled is handled, return undefined.
        if host_handled == HandledByHost::Handled {
            return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
        }

        // FIXME: 7. Let AR be the Agent Record of the surrounding agent.
        // FIXME: 8. Let isLittleEndian be AR.[[LittleEndian]].
        // FIXME: 9. Let byteLengthBlock be O.[[ArrayBufferByteLengthData]].
        // FIXME: 10. Let currentByteLengthRawBytes be GetRawBytesFromSharedBlock(byteLengthBlock, 0, biguint64, true, seq-cst).
        // FIXME: 11. Let newByteLengthRawBytes be NumericToRawBytes(biguint64, ℤ(newByteLength), isLittleEndian).
        // FIXME: 12. Repeat,
        // FIXME:         a. NOTE: This is a compare-and-exchange loop to ensure that parallel, racing grows of the same buffer are totally ordered, are not lost, and do not silently do nothing. The loop exits if it was able to attempt to grow uncontended.
        // FIXME:         b. Let currentByteLength be ℝ(RawBytesToNumeric(biguint64, currentByteLengthRawBytes, isLittleEndian)).
        let current_byte_length = array_buffer_object.byte_length();

        //                c. If newByteLength = currentByteLength, return undefined.
        if new_byte_length == current_byte_length {
            return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
        }

        //                d. If newByteLength < currentByteLength or newByteLength > O.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]], throw a RangeError exception.
        if new_byte_length < current_byte_length {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::RangeError,
                ErrorType::ByteLengthLessThanPreviousByteLength,
                &[&new_byte_length, &current_byte_length],
            );
        }
        if new_byte_length > array_buffer_object.max_byte_length() {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::RangeError,
                ErrorType::ByteLengthExceedsMaxByteLength,
                &[&new_byte_length, &array_buffer_object.max_byte_length()],
            );
        }

        // FIXME:         e. Let byteLengthDelta be newByteLength - currentByteLength.
        // FIXME:         f. If it is impossible to create a new Shared Data Block value consisting of byteLengthDelta bytes, throw a RangeError exception.
        // FIXME:         g. NOTE: No new Shared Data Block is constructed and used here. The observable behaviour of growable SharedArrayBuffers is specified by allocating a max-sized Shared Data Block at construction time, and this step captures the requirement that implementations that run out of memory must throw a RangeError.
        // FIXME:         h. Let readByteLengthRawBytes be AtomicCompareExchangeInSharedBlock(byteLengthBlock, 0, 8, currentByteLengthRawBytes, newByteLengthRawBytes).
        // FIXME:         i. If ByteListEqual(readByteLengthRawBytes, currentByteLengthRawBytes) is true, return undefined.
        // FIXME:         j. Set currentByteLengthRawBytes to readByteLengthRawBytes.

        if array_buffer_object
            .try_resize(vm, new_byte_length, ZeroFillNewBytes::Yes)
            .is_err()
        {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::RangeError,
                ErrorType::NotEnoughMemoryToAllocate,
                &[&new_byte_length],
            );
        }

        Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
    }

    // 25.2.5.4 get SharedArrayBuffer.prototype.growable, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.growable
    fn growable_getter(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // 1. Let O be the this value.
        // 2. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(O, [[ArrayBufferData]]).
        let array_buffer_object = this_array_buffer(vm)?;

        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(O) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 4. If IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(O) is false, return true; otherwise return false.
        Ok(Value::from_bool(!array_buffer_object.is_fixed_length()))
    }

    // 25.2.5.5 get SharedArrayBuffer.prototype.maxByteLength, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.maxbytelength
    fn max_byte_length(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // 1. Let O be the this value.
        // 2. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(O, [[ArrayBufferData]]).
        let array_buffer_object = this_array_buffer(vm)?;

        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(O) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 4. If IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(O) is true, then
        //        a. Let length be O.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
        // 5. Else,
        //        a. Let length be O.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]].
        let length = if array_buffer_object.is_fixed_length() {
            array_buffer_object.byte_length()
        } else {
            array_buffer_object.max_byte_length()
        };

        // 6. Return 𝔽(length).
        Ok(Value::from_f64(length as f64))
    }

    // 25.2.5.6 SharedArrayBuffer.prototype.slice ( start, end ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer.prototype.slice
    fn slice(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");

        let start = vm.argument(0);
        let end = vm.argument(1);

        // 1. Let O be the this value.
        // 2. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(O, [[ArrayBufferData]]).
        let array_buffer_object = this_array_buffer(vm)?;

        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(O) is false, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 4. Let len be O.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
        let length = array_buffer_object.byte_length() as f64;

        // 5. Let relativeStart be ? ToIntegerOrInfinity(start).
        let relative_start = start.to_integer_or_infinity(vm)?;

        // 6. If relativeStart is -∞, let first be 0.
        let first = if relative_start == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
            0.0
        }
        // 7. Else if relativeStart < 0, let first be max(len + relativeStart, 0).
        else if relative_start < 0.0 {
            (length + relative_start).max(0.0)
        }
        // 8. Else, let first be min(relativeStart, len).
        else {
            relative_start.min(length)
        };

        // 9. If end is undefined, let relativeEnd be len; else let relativeEnd be ? ToIntegerOrInfinity(end).
        let relative_end = if end.is_undefined() {
            length
        } else {
            end.to_integer_or_infinity(vm)?
        };

        // 10. If relativeEnd is -∞, let final be 0.
        let final_ = if relative_end == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
            0.0
        }
        // 11. Else if relativeEnd < 0, let final be max(len + relativeEnd, 0).
        else if relative_end < 0.0 {
            (length + relative_end).max(0.0)
        }
        // 12. Else, let final be min(relativeEnd, len).
        else {
            relative_end.min(length)
        };

        // 13. Let newLen be max(final - first, 0).
        let new_length = (final_ - first).max(0.0);

        // 14. Let ctor be ? SpeciesConstructor(O, %SharedArrayBuffer%).
        let constructor = species_constructor(
            vm,
            &array_buffer_object,
            realm.intrinsics().shared_array_buffer_constructor(vm),
        )?;

        // 15. Let new be ? Construct(ctor, « 𝔽(newLen) »).
        let new_array_buffer = construct(vm, constructor, &[Value::from_f64(new_length)], None)?;

        // 16. Perform ? RequireInternalSlot(new, [[ArrayBufferData]]).
        let Some(new_array_buffer_object) = new_array_buffer.downcast::<ArrayBuffer>() else {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::SpeciesConstructorDidNotCreate,
                &[&"an ArrayBuffer"],
            );
        };

        // 17. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(new) is true, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !new_array_buffer_object.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
        }

        // 18. If new.[[ArrayBufferData]] is O.[[ArrayBufferData]], throw a TypeError exception.
        if new_array_buffer == array_buffer_object.upcast::<Object>() {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::SpeciesConstructorReturned,
                &[&"same ArrayBuffer instance"],
            );
        }

        // 19. If new.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] < newLen, throw a TypeError exception.
        if (new_array_buffer_object.byte_length() as f64) < new_length {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::SpeciesConstructorReturned,
                &[&"an ArrayBuffer smaller than requested"],
            );
        }

        // 22. Perform CopyDataBlockBytes(toBuf, 0, fromBuf, first, newLen).
        array_buffer_object.copy_data_to(&new_array_buffer_object, first as usize, 0, new_length as usize);

        // 23. Return new.
        Ok(Value::from_object(new_array_buffer_object))
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibJS/Rust/src/runtime/shared_backing_store.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The bytes of the fixed-length SharedArrayBuffers of a process, and how a message finds them in another agent of the
//! process.
//!
//! A SharedArrayBuffer never leaves its agent cluster, and an agent cluster never leaves its process, so these bytes are
//! ordinary memory of the process: there is one mapping, at one address, for every agent. A message names a store by its
//! id. The id gives nothing to the process of a receiver that is not this one, which is where a message goes that
//! deserialization then rejects.
//!
//! A message can wait for a long time, and every agent may drop its buffer meanwhile. So a message holds a pin. While the
//! message stays in memory of this process, that is just a count on the stores. A message that goes through a socket can
//! still come back here: BroadcastChannel reaches agents of this process through the browser process, and the ends of a
//! MessagePort can both be in this process with a socket between them. So such a message holds a lifeline instead: the
//! read end of a pipe that the sender's process keeps the stores for. The kernel keeps track of where that read end is,
//! as it does for any descriptor in flight, so it does not matter whether the message is delivered to one receiver, to
//! many, to a process that has no use for it, or to nobody.

use core::any::Any;
use core::ffi::c_int;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, LazyLock, Mutex, PoisonError, Weak};

use crate::gc::capi::GCPrimitiveStorageHandle;
use crate::gc::primitive_storage::{OutOfMemory, OwnedPrimitiveStorage, ZeroFillNewBytes};
use crate::random::get_random_u64;

/// DataBlock::SharedBackingStore: the bytes of a fixed-length Shared Data Block, which every agent of the process that
/// has the block shares. The last agent to drop it frees the bytes.
pub struct SharedBackingStore {
    storage: OwnedPrimitiveStorage,
    id: u64,
}

// SAFETY: LibGC's primitive storage takes a lock, the storage is never resized, and what agents do to the bytes goes
//         through atomics.
unsafe impl Send for SharedBackingStore {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl Sync for SharedBackingStore {}

type StoresById = HashMap<u64, Weak<SharedBackingStore>>;

fn stores_by_id() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, StoresById> {
    static STORES_BY_ID: LazyLock<Mutex<StoresById>> = LazyLock::new(Mutex::default);
    STORES_BY_ID.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

impl SharedBackingStore {
    /// A new zero-filled store of `size` bytes.
    pub fn create(size: usize) -> Result<Arc<Self>, OutOfMemory> {
        let storage = OwnedPrimitiveStorage::allocate(size, ZeroFillNewBytes::Yes)?;
        let mut stores = stores_by_id();
        // NB: An id that a message carries should not be guessable, as a message can come from another process.
        let mut id = get_random_u64();
        while id == 0 || stores.contains_key(&id) {
            id = get_random_u64();
        }
        let store = Arc::new(Self { storage, id });
        stores.insert(id, Arc::downgrade(&store));
        Ok(store)
    }

    /// The store of this process that `id` names, if there is one.
    pub fn with_id(id: u64) -> Option<Arc<Self>> {
        stores_by_id().get(&id)?.upgrade()
    }

    pub fn id(&self) -> u64 {
        self.id
    }

    pub fn handle(&self) -> GCPrimitiveStorageHandle {
        self.storage.handle()
    }

    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.storage.size()
    }

    pub(crate) fn data(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.storage.data()
    }

    pub(crate) fn offset(&self) -> usize {
        self.storage.offset()
    }
}

impl Drop for SharedBackingStore {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        stores_by_id().remove(&self.id);
    }
}

/// The read end of the pipe of a message.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub type SharedStoreLifeline = std::os::fd::OwnedFd;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub type SharedStoreLifeline = std::os::windows::io::OwnedHandle;

/// The lifeline as the descriptor that LibIPC and C++ pass around, which the caller then owns.
pub fn lifeline_into_raw_descriptor(lifeline: SharedStoreLifeline) -> c_int {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        std::os::fd::IntoRawFd::into_raw_fd(lifeline)
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        // AK's to_fd() keeps the low 32 bits, which hold every value a kernel handle can have.
        std::os::windows::io::IntoRawHandle::into_raw_handle(lifeline) as isize as c_int
    }
}

/// The lifeline behind a descriptor of LibIPC.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `descriptor` must be open, and owned by nothing else.
pub unsafe fn lifeline_from_raw_descriptor(descriptor: c_int) -> SharedStoreLifeline {
    // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
    unsafe { crate::gc::shared_memory::owned_from_raw_descriptor(descriptor) }
}

/// A duplicate of the lifeline behind a descriptor of LibIPC, if the system has a descriptor left.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `descriptor` must stay open for the call.
pub unsafe fn duplicate_lifeline_from_raw_descriptor(descriptor: c_int) -> std::io::Result<SharedStoreLifeline> {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees.
        unsafe { std::os::fd::BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(descriptor) }.try_clone_to_owned()
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        // SAFETY: As the caller guarantees. AK's to_handle() sign-extends the int.
        unsafe {
            std::os::windows::io::BorrowedHandle::borrow_raw(descriptor as isize as std::os::windows::io::RawHandle)
        }
        .try_clone_to_owned()
    }
}

/// Something that a message names, which the agents of the process share: a store, or the shared memory of an embedder.
pub type SharedByMessage = Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>;

/// What keeps the stores that a message names.
pub enum SharedStorePin {
    /// For a message in memory of this process.
    Counted(Vec<SharedByMessage>),
    /// For a message that has been through a socket, or is about to go through one.
    Lifeline(SharedStoreLifeline),
}

impl SharedStorePin {
    /// A lifeline that keeps the same stores, if the system has a descriptor left.
    pub fn duplicate_lifeline(&self) -> Option<SharedStoreLifeline> {
        match self {
            Self::Counted(stores) => pin_stores_for_a_message(stores.clone()).ok(),
            Self::Lifeline(lifeline) => lifeline.try_clone().ok(),
        }
    }

    /// This pin as a lifeline, if the system has a descriptor left. Without one, the stores may go before the message
    /// arrives, which deserializing throws for.
    pub fn into_lifeline(self) -> Option<SharedStoreLifeline> {
        match self {
            Self::Counted(stores) => pin_stores_for_a_message(stores).ok(),
            Self::Lifeline(lifeline) => Some(lifeline),
        }
    }

    /// Lets go of the stores, for a message that is destroyed.
    pub fn release(self) {
        if let Self::Lifeline(lifeline) = self {
            drop(lifeline);
            release_stores_of_lost_messages();
        }
    }
}

/// Stores that a message keeps alive, until the last duplicate of its lifeline is closed.
struct PinnedStores {
    /// The write end of the pipe, which only ever reports that the read end is gone.
    // NB: Windows does not poll it yet, see take_pins_nothing_holds().
    #[cfg_attr(windows, allow(dead_code))]
    write_end: std::io::PipeWriter,
    /// NB: Only dropped for what it keeps alive.
    _stores: Vec<SharedByMessage>,
}

fn pinned_stores() -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'static, Vec<PinnedStores>> {
    static PINNED_STORES: Mutex<Vec<PinnedStores>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    PINNED_STORES.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn take_pins_nothing_holds(pins: &mut Vec<PinnedStores>) -> Vec<PinnedStores> {
    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;

    let mut poll_descriptors: Vec<libc::pollfd> = pins
        .iter()
        .map(|pin| libc::pollfd {
            fd: pin.write_end.as_raw_fd(),
            events: 0,
            revents: 0,
        })
        .collect();
    // SAFETY: The array is valid for its length, and the call does not block.
    let result = unsafe { libc::poll(poll_descriptors.as_mut_ptr(), poll_descriptors.len() as libc::nfds_t, 0) };
    if result <= 0 {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let mut poll_descriptors = poll_descriptors.into_iter();
    pins.extract_if(.., |_| {
        poll_descriptors
            .next()
            .is_some_and(|descriptor| descriptor.revents & (libc::POLLERR | libc::POLLHUP) != 0)
    })
    .collect()
}

// FIXME: Find out on Windows when a pipe has lost its reader. Until then, the stores of a message stay for as long as
//        the process does.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn take_pins_nothing_holds(_: &mut Vec<PinnedStores>) -> Vec<PinnedStores> {
    Vec::new()
}

/// Lets go of the stores of the messages that are gone. A message that is destroyed in this process calls this. One that
/// another process destroys gets noticed the next time a message goes out or is destroyed here.
pub fn release_stores_of_lost_messages() {
    let released = take_pins_nothing_holds(&mut pinned_stores());
    // NB: A store that goes takes other locks.
    drop(released);
}

/// A new lifeline that keeps `stores` for as long as it, or a duplicate of it, is open anywhere.
fn pin_stores_for_a_message(stores: Vec<SharedByMessage>) -> std::io::Result<SharedStoreLifeline> {
    release_stores_of_lost_messages();
    let (read_end, write_end) = std::io::pipe()?;
    pinned_stores().push(PinnedStores {
        write_end,
        _stores: stores,
    });
    Ok(read_end.into())
}

/// [[ClassFieldInitializerName]]: Variant<PropertyKey, PrivateName, Empty>. Only whether there is a name matters, so a
/// Private Name is kept as its description.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Trace)]

/// What a function's executable is made from when it is first called, which only one thing can be at a time. A
/// function keeps its payload once it compiled, which it compiles from again if its executable gets flushed.
enum CompileInput {
    None,
    /// The function's source and its row there, which its tree is parsed from.
    Unparsed(Arc<FunctionPayload>),
    /// Freshly compiled bytecode.
    PrecompiledBytecode(Box<PrecompiledInput>),
}

/// Bytecode compiled ahead of the first call, and the payload it was compiled from, if the function has one.
struct PrecompiledInput {
    precompiled: Arc<PrecompiledFunction>,
    payload: Option<Arc<FunctionPayload>>,
}

/// A CompileInput in one word: the pointer, with what it points at in its lowest bits.
struct CompileInputSlot(Cell<*mut ()>);

// NB: The pointers in a slot leave room for its tag.
const _: () = assert!(
    align_of::<FunctionPayload>() > CompileInputSlot::TAG_MASK
        && align_of::<PrecompiledInput>() > CompileInputSlot::TAG_MASK
);

impl CompileInputSlot {
    const TAG_MASK: usize = 0b11;
    const TAG_UNPARSED: usize = 1;
    const TAG_PRECOMPILED_BYTECODE: usize = 2;

    fn new(input: CompileInput) -> Self {
        let slot = Self(Cell::new(core::ptr::null_mut()));
        slot.set(input);
        slot
    }

    fn set(&self, input: CompileInput) {
        drop(self.take());
        self.0.set(match input {
            CompileInput::None => core::ptr::null_mut(),
            CompileInput::Unparsed(payload) => Self::tagged(Arc::into_raw(payload).cast_mut(), Self::TAG_UNPARSED),
            CompileInput::PrecompiledBytecode(input) => {
                Self::tagged(Box::into_raw(input), Self::TAG_PRECOMPILED_BYTECODE)
            }
        });
    }

    fn tagged<T>(pointer: *mut T, tag: usize) -> *mut () {
        pointer.cast::<()>().map_addr(|address| address | tag)
    }

    fn take(&self) -> CompileInput {
        let word = self.0.replace(core::ptr::null_mut());
        let pointer = word.map_addr(|address| address & !Self::TAG_MASK);
        // SAFETY: set() made the word from a reference of the type its tag says, which this takes over now that the
        //         word is gone from the slot.
        unsafe {
            match word.addr() & Self::TAG_MASK {
                Self::TAG_UNPARSED => CompileInput::Unparsed(Arc::from_raw(pointer.cast())),
                Self::TAG_PRECOMPILED_BYTECODE => CompileInput::PrecompiledBytecode(Box::from_raw(pointer.cast())),
                _ => CompileInput::None,
            }
        }
    }
}

impl CompileInputSlot {
    /// Whether the input is the payload of the function, which it compiled from at least once.
    fn is_unparsed(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.get().addr() & Self::TAG_MASK == Self::TAG_UNPARSED
    }
}

impl Drop for CompileInputSlot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        drop(self.take());
    }
}

/// The names of the parameters of a function with a simple parameter list that has any.
struct ParameterNames {
    /// The name each argument index of a mapped arguments object maps to, which is empty where a later parameter has
    /// the same name.
    mapped_argument_names: Rc<[Utf16FlyString]>,
    /// The names of the parameters without the ones that repeat, in the order the bindings of the parameters are
    /// created in the function environment.
    parameter_binding_names: Rc<[Utf16FlyString]>,
}

/// The parts of the shared data of a function that few functions need.
#[derive(Default, Trace)]
struct SharedFunctionInstanceDataRareData {
    /// Owns the source text if it is not simply a range of the source code the function was parsed from, as for
    /// dynamically created functions via the Function constructor, or once something asked for it.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    source_text_owner: RefCell<Utf16String>,
    class_field_initializer_name: GcRefCell<ClassFieldInitializerName>, // [[ClassFieldInitializerName]]
    /// Functions with parameter expressions may have a separate var environment.
    var_environment_bindings_count: Cell<u32>,
    var_environment_shape: NullableMember<EnvironmentShape>,
    /// What the last executable of the function left for the next one, while its code is flushed.
    flushed_code: GcRefCell<Option<Box<FlushedCode>>>,
    /// How often the function was compiled again after a flush, in each `FlushLayer`.
    recompile_counts: Cell<[u8; 2]>,
    /// Whether the JIT code of the function's executable was flushed since it was last compiled.
    jit_code_flushed: Cell<bool>,
}

/// What a flushed executable leaves for the next executable of its code, which nothing that code observes may tell
/// apart from it: the shared data of the functions it creates, which closures created before share with those created
/// later, and its template objects, which belong to their site in the code.
#[derive(Default, Trace)]
pub struct FlushedCode {
    pub shared_function_data: Vec<Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData>>,
    pub template_object_caches: Vec<Gc<TemplateObjectCache>>,
}

/// The parts of the shared data of a function that the interpreter does not read.
#[derive(Trace)]
pub struct SharedFunctionInstanceDataStorage {
    name: Utf16FlyString,

    // NB: source_text_offset and source_text_length are a range of the source code we parsed the function from.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    source_code: Cell<Option<Rc<SourceCode>>>,
    source_text_offset: Cell<u32>,
    source_text_length: Cell<u32>, // [[SourceText]]

    #[gc(untraced)]
    parameter_names: OnceCell<Box<ParameterNames>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    compile_input: CompileInputSlot,
    rare_data: OnceCell<Box<SharedFunctionInstanceDataRareData>>,

    function_environment_bindings_count: Cell<u32>,
    function_environment_shape: NullableMember<EnvironmentShape>,
}

// NB: Every function has these bytes.
const _: () = assert!(size_of::<SharedFunctionInstanceData>() == 88);

/// The most properties that constructions make room for ahead (the largest inline capacity of plain objects).
const MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE: u32 = 16;

/// The last construction that follows the transitions again (see SharedFunctionInstanceData::construct_reserve()).
const MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE_UPDATES: u32 = 1024;

const _: () = assert!(MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE <= u8::MAX as u32);
const _: () = assert!(MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE_UPDATES as u64 <= asm_call_metadata::CONSTRUCT_COUNT_MASK);

// NB: Tracing considers the bytecode for flushing, with state of the thread that owns the heap.
define_cell!(SharedFunctionInstanceData, Other, traced_on: owner_thread_only);

// SAFETY: Visits the executable, the call environment template and every cell the storage holds. While a collection
//         flushes code, an executable that idled long enough is left to what else holds it, and the cells that outlive
//         a flush of it are visited instead (see `bytecode::flushing`).
unsafe impl Trace for SharedFunctionInstanceData {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        match self.executable() {
            Some(executable) if flushing::bytecode_flush_candidate(self, executable) => {
                executable.trace_what_outlives_a_flush(visitor);
            }
            _ => self.executable.trace(visitor),
        }
        self.call_environment_template.trace(visitor);
        match self.script_or_module.get() {
            ScriptOrModule::Empty => {}
            ScriptOrModule::Script(script) => script.trace(visitor),
            ScriptOrModule::Module(module) => module.trace(visitor),
        }
        self.storage.trace(visitor);
    }
}

define_cell!(CallEnvironmentTemplate, Other);

// SAFETY: The words of a template refer to the environment's shape, which the shared function instance data keeps
//         alive, and to no other cell.
unsafe impl Trace for CallEnvironmentTemplate {
    fn trace(&self, _visitor: &mut Visitor) {}
}

/// OPTIMIZATION: Precompute the argument indices that alias parameter bindings. Only the last occurrence of each
///               parameter name is eligible; each arguments object also limits the mapping to its argument count.
///               https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-createmappedargumentsobject
fn parameter_names_of(parameter_names: &[Utf16FlyString]) -> Option<Box<ParameterNames>> {
    if parameter_names.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    // OPTIMIZATION: Going through a few names beats a hash set of them.
    const MAXIMUM_PARAMETERS_TO_SCAN: usize = 8;
    if parameter_names.len() <= MAXIMUM_PARAMETERS_TO_SCAN {
        let has_repeated_name =
            (1..parameter_names.len()).any(|index| parameter_names[..index].contains(&parameter_names[index]));
        if !has_repeated_name {
            let names: Rc<[Utf16FlyString]> = parameter_names.into();
            return Some(Box::new(ParameterNames {
                mapped_argument_names: names.clone(),
                parameter_binding_names: names,
            }));
        }
    }
    let mut seen_names = HashSet::with_capacity(parameter_names.len());
    let mut mapped_names: Vec<Utf16FlyString> = vec![Utf16FlyString::default(); parameter_names.len()];
    let mut has_repeated_name = false;

    for index in (0..parameter_names.len()).rev() {
        let name = &parameter_names[index];
        // OPTIMIZATION: A hash set avoids scanning later parameters for every name.
        if !seen_names.insert(name) {
            has_repeated_name = true;
            continue;
        }
        mapped_names[index] = name.clone();
    }
    let mapped_argument_names: Rc<[Utf16FlyString]> = mapped_names.into();

    // NB: Without repeated names, both lists are the parameter names.
    let parameter_binding_names = if has_repeated_name {
        let mut seen_names = HashSet::with_capacity(parameter_names.len());
        let mut names: Vec<Utf16FlyString> = Vec::with_capacity(parameter_names.len());
        for name in parameter_names {
            if seen_names.insert(name) {
                names.push(name.clone());
            }
        }
        names.into()
    } else {
        mapped_argument_names.clone()
    };

    Some(Box::new(ParameterNames {
        mapped_argument_names,
        parameter_binding_names,
    }))
}

fn source_text_offset_or_length(offset_or_length: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(offset_or_length).expect("a source code fits u32 code units")
}

impl SharedFunctionInstanceData {
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn new(
        _: &DeferGc<'_>,
        kind: FunctionKind,
        name: Utf16FlyString,
        function_length: i32,
        formal_parameter_count: u32,
        strict: bool,
        is_arrow_function: bool,
        has_simple_parameter_list: bool,
        parameter_names_for_mapped_arguments: Vec<Utf16FlyString>,
        payload: Option<Arc<FunctionPayload>>,
    ) -> Self {
        // NB: initialize_after_construction()
        let mut metadata = u64::from(formal_parameter_count)
            | asm_call_metadata::MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS_OBJECT
            | asm_call_metadata::CONTAINS_DIRECT_CALL_TO_EVAL
            | (kind as u64) << asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_KIND_SHIFT;
        if strict {
            metadata |= asm_call_metadata::STRICT;
        }
        if is_arrow_function {
            metadata |= asm_call_metadata::IS_ARROW_FUNCTION;
        }
        if has_simple_parameter_list {
            metadata |= asm_call_metadata::HAS_SIMPLE_PARAMETER_LIST;
        }

        Self {
            executable: NullableMember::null(),
            call_environment_template: NullableMember::null(),
            header: CellHeaderTail::for_class(Self::CLASS),
            construct_reserve: Cell::new(0),
            function_length,
            asm_call_metadata: Cell::new(metadata),
            script_or_module: ScriptOrModuleSlot::new(ScriptOrModule::Empty),
            storage: SharedFunctionInstanceDataStorage {
                name,
                source_code: Cell::new(None),
                source_text_offset: Cell::new(0),
                source_text_length: Cell::new(0),
                parameter_names: parameter_names_of(&parameter_names_for_mapped_arguments)
                    .map_or_else(OnceCell::new, OnceCell::from),
                compile_input: CompileInputSlot::new(payload.map_or(CompileInput::None, CompileInput::Unparsed)),
                rare_data: OnceCell::new(),
                function_environment_bindings_count: Cell::new(0),
                function_environment_shape: NullableMember::null(),
            },
        }
    }

    fn rare_data(&self) -> &SharedFunctionInstanceDataRareData {
        self.storage.rare_data.get_or_init(Box::default)
    }

    fn metadata_bit(&self, bit: u64) -> bool {
        self.asm_call_metadata.get() & bit != 0
    }

    fn set_metadata_bit(&self, bit: u64, value: bool) {
        let mut metadata = self.asm_call_metadata.get() & !bit;
        if value {
            metadata |= bit;
        }
        metadata &= !asm_call_metadata::NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_OR_THIS_VALUE_RESOLUTION;
        if metadata
            & (asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_NEEDED
                | asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION)
            != 0
        {
            metadata |= asm_call_metadata::NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_OR_THIS_VALUE_RESOLUTION;
        }
        self.asm_call_metadata.set(metadata);
        if let Some(executable) = self.executable() {
            executable.head.call_metadata.set(metadata);
        }
    }

    /// Creates the shared data of a function the frontend described, which is strict if `strict`.
    pub fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        description: &SharedFunctionDescription,
        strict: bool,
        source_code: Option<&Rc<SourceCode>>,
    ) -> Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData> {
        Self::create_from_owned_description(vm, description.clone(), strict, source_code)
    }

    fn create_from_owned_description(
        vm: &Vm,
        description: SharedFunctionDescription,
        strict: bool,
        source_code: Option<&Rc<SourceCode>>,
    ) -> Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData> {
        let SharedFunctionDescription {
            name,
            function_kind,
            function_length,
            formal_parameter_count,
            is_arrow,
            has_simple_parameter_list,
            source_text_offset,
            source_text_length,
            uses_this,
            uses_this_from_environment,
            payload,
            ..
        } = description;
        let shared = vm.heap().allocate(|defer| {
            Self::new(
                defer,
                function_kind,
                name,
                function_length,
                formal_parameter_count,
                strict,
                is_arrow,
                has_simple_parameter_list,
                Vec::new(),
                Some(payload),
            )
        });
        shared.update_can_inline_call();

        // Set parsing insights that must be available before lazy compilation.
        shared.set_uses_this(uses_this);
        shared.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION,
            uses_this_from_environment,
        );
        if uses_this_from_environment && !is_arrow {
            shared.set_function_environment_needed(true);
        }

        shared.storage.source_code.set(source_code.cloned());
        shared.storage.source_text_offset.set(source_text_offset);
        shared.storage.source_text_length.set(source_text_length);
        shared
    }

    fn initialize_source_text_range(&self, source_text_offset: usize, source_text_length: usize) {
        self.storage
            .source_text_offset
            .set(source_text_offset_or_length(source_text_offset));
        self.storage
            .source_text_length
            .set(source_text_offset_or_length(source_text_length));
    }

    /// vm.heap().allocate<SharedFunctionInstanceData>(vm, kind, name, function_length, formal_parameter_count, strict,
    /// is_arrow_function, has_simple_parameter_list, parameter_names_for_mapped_arguments, NoSharedFunctionDataList {},
    /// nullptr): shared data that has nothing to compile, such as the wrapper of a module with top-level await, whose
    /// executable the caller sets.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn create_without_compile_input(
        vm: &Vm,
        kind: FunctionKind,
        name: Utf16FlyString,
        function_length: i32,
        formal_parameter_count: u32,
        strict: bool,
        is_arrow_function: bool,
        has_simple_parameter_list: bool,
        parameter_names_for_mapped_arguments: Vec<Utf16FlyString>,
    ) -> Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData> {
        let shared = vm.heap().allocate(|defer| {
            Self::new(
                defer,
                kind,
                name,
                function_length,
                formal_parameter_count,
                strict,
                is_arrow_function,
                has_simple_parameter_list,
                parameter_names_for_mapped_arguments,
                None,
            )
        });
        shared.update_can_inline_call();
        shared
    }

    /// Creates the shared data of one of the functions an executable declares, from what the frontend kept for it: its
    /// description, its class field initializer name and the bytecode it may have compiled already.
    pub fn create_from_pending_shared_function_data(
        vm: &Vm,
        pending: &PendingSharedFunctionData,
        is_strict: bool,
        source_code: Option<&Rc<SourceCode>>,
    ) -> Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData> {
        let shared = Self::create(vm, &pending.description, pending.is_strict_in(is_strict), source_code);
        if let Some(field) = &pending.class_field_initializer_name {
            let (name, is_private) = &**field;
            shared.set_class_field_initializer_name_from_utf16(&name.to_utf16(), *is_private);
        }
        if let Some(precompiled) = &pending.precompiled_function {
            shared.set_precompiled_bytecode_executable(precompiled.clone());
        }
        shared
    }

    /// create_from_pending_shared_function_data() for what nothing links again, which moves into the shared data.
    pub fn create_from_owned_pending_shared_function_data(
        vm: &Vm,
        pending: PendingSharedFunctionData,
        is_strict: bool,
        source_code: Option<&Rc<SourceCode>>,
    ) -> Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData> {
        let strict = pending.is_strict_in(is_strict);
        let shared = Self::create_from_owned_description(vm, pending.description, strict, source_code);
        if let Some(field) = &pending.class_field_initializer_name {
            let (name, is_private) = &**field;
            shared.set_class_field_initializer_name_from_utf16(&name.to_utf16(), *is_private);
        }
        if let Some(precompiled) = pending.precompiled_function {
            shared.set_precompiled_bytecode_executable(precompiled);
        }
        shared
    }

    pub fn executable(&self) -> Option<Gc<Executable>> {
        self.executable.get().map(Executable::from_head)
    }

    /// Also gives `executable` the function's metadata, which calls of it read from the executable.
    pub fn set_executable(&self, executable: Option<Gc<Executable>>) {
        self.executable.set(executable.map(Executable::head));
        self.update_can_inline_call();
    }

    pub fn set_is_class_constructor(&self) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_CLASS_CONSTRUCTOR, true);
        self.update_can_inline_call();
    }

    pub fn can_inline_call(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::CAN_INLINE_CALL)
    }

    fn update_can_inline_call(&self) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::CAN_INLINE_CALL,
            self.executable.get().is_some() && self.kind() == FunctionKind::Normal && !self.is_class_constructor(),
        );
    }

    pub fn name(&self) -> Utf16FlyString {
        self.storage.name.clone()
    }

    pub fn source_text_owner(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        let source_text_owner = self.storage.rare_data.get()?.source_text_owner.borrow();
        (!source_text_owner.is_empty()).then(|| source_text_owner.clone())
    }

    pub fn source_text(&self) -> Utf16String {
        if let Some(source_text_owner) = self.source_text_owner() {
            return source_text_owner;
        }

        let Some(source_code) = self.source_code() else {
            return Utf16String::default();
        };

        let source_text = source_code.source_text_from_offsets(
            self.storage.source_text_offset.get() as usize,
            self.storage.source_text_length.get() as usize,
        );
        self.rare_data().source_text_owner.replace(source_text.clone());
        source_text
    }

    /// Makes `source_text` the [[SourceText]] while keeping the source code the function compiles from.
    pub fn set_source_text_owner(&self, source_text: Utf16String) {
        self.rare_data().source_text_owner.replace(source_text);
    }

    pub fn set_source_text(&self, source_text: Utf16String) {
        self.rare_data().source_text_owner.replace(source_text);
        self.storage.source_code.set(None);
        self.storage.source_text_offset.set(0);
        self.storage.source_text_length.set(0);
    }

    pub fn set_source_text_range(
        &self,
        source_code: &Rc<SourceCode>,
        source_text_offset: usize,
        source_text_length: usize,
    ) {
        self.rare_data().source_text_owner.replace(Utf16String::default());
        self.storage.source_code.set(Some(source_code.clone()));
        self.initialize_source_text_range(source_text_offset, source_text_length);
    }

    pub fn source_code(&self) -> Option<Rc<SourceCode>> {
        let source_code = self.storage.source_code.take();
        self.storage.source_code.set(source_code.clone());
        source_code
    }

    pub fn clear_compile_inputs(&self) {
        self.storage.compile_input.set(CompileInput::None);
    }

    /// Records what scope analysis found out about the function's body, as rust_sfd_set_metadata does.
    pub fn set_metadata(&self, metadata: &FunctionSfdMetadata) {
        if let Some(parameter_names) = parameter_names_of(&metadata.parameter_names) {
            let _ = self.storage.parameter_names.set(parameter_names);
        }
        self.set_uses_this(metadata.uses_this);
        self.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION,
            metadata.this_value_needs_environment_resolution,
        );
        self.set_function_environment_needed(metadata.function_environment_needed);
        self.storage
            .function_environment_bindings_count
            .set(u32::try_from(metadata.function_environment_bindings_count).expect("the count fits in u32"));
        if metadata.var_environment_bindings_count != 0 || self.storage.rare_data.get().is_some() {
            self.rare_data()
                .var_environment_bindings_count
                .set(u32::try_from(metadata.var_environment_bindings_count).expect("the count fits in u32"));
        }
        self.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS_OBJECT,
            metadata.might_need_arguments,
        );
        self.set_metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::CONTAINS_DIRECT_CALL_TO_EVAL, metadata.contains_eval);
    }

    /// Keeps bytecode the frontend compiled ahead of the first call, as rust_sfd_set_precompiled_bytecode_executable
    /// does.
    pub fn set_precompiled_bytecode_executable(&self, precompiled: Arc<PrecompiledFunction>) {
        self.set_metadata(&precompiled.metadata);
        let payload = match self.storage.compile_input.take() {
            CompileInput::Unparsed(payload) => Some(payload),
            CompileInput::None | CompileInput::PrecompiledBytecode(_) => None,
        };
        self.storage
            .compile_input
            .set(CompileInput::PrecompiledBytecode(Box::new(PrecompiledInput {
                precompiled,
                payload,
            })));
    }

    /// Whether the function's executable can be flushed, as the function can compile its code again.
    pub fn can_flush_code(&self) -> bool {
        self.storage.compile_input.is_unparsed()
    }

    /// How often the function was compiled again after its code was flushed in `layer`.
    pub fn recompile_count(&self, layer: FlushLayer) -> u8 {
        self.storage
            .rare_data
            .get()
            .map_or(0, |rare_data| rare_data.recompile_counts.get()[layer as usize])
    }

    /// Counts a recompile in `layer` after a flush there.
    fn note_recompile(&self, vm: &Vm, layer: FlushLayer) {
        let rare_data = self.rare_data();
        let mut counts = rare_data.recompile_counts.get();
        counts[layer as usize] = counts[layer as usize].saturating_add(1);
        rare_data.recompile_counts.set(counts);
        vm.code_flushing.note_recompile(layer, counts[layer as usize]);
    }

    /// Drops the function's executable, which no one else holds, and goes back to the lazy state from which the next
    /// call compiles the function again. Keeps what the next executable takes over. Only the sweep callback of a
    /// collection calls this, through its Sweep.
    pub fn flush_executable(&self, executable: Gc<Executable>, _: &Sweep<'_>) {
        assert!(self.can_flush_code());
        let flushed_code = FlushedCode {
            shared_function_data: executable.shared_function_data_slice().to_vec(),
            template_object_caches: executable.template_object_caches_slice().to_vec(),
        };
        self.rare_data().flushed_code.replace(Some(Box::new(flushed_code)));
        self.set_executable(None);
        // NB: The retained code only costs memory once no executable shares it, which forget_retained_code() checks.
        if let CompileInput::Unparsed(payload) = self.storage.compile_input.take() {
            payload.forget_retained_code(executable.code());
            self.storage.compile_input.set(CompileInput::Unparsed(payload));
        }
    }

    /// Whether the function's executable was flushed, and not compiled again yet.
    pub fn has_flushed_code(&self) -> bool {
        self.storage
            .rare_data
            .get()
            .is_some_and(|rare_data| rare_data.flushed_code.borrow().is_some())
    }

    /// Notes that the JIT code of the function's executable was flushed.
    pub fn note_flushed_jit_code(&self) {
        self.rare_data().jit_code_flushed.set(true);
    }

    /// Notes that the JIT compiles the function's executable, which counts as a recompile if its JIT code was flushed.
    pub fn note_jit_compile(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        if let Some(rare_data) = self.storage.rare_data.get()
            && rare_data.jit_code_flushed.replace(false)
        {
            self.note_recompile(vm, FlushLayer::Jit);
        }
    }

    /// Sets [[ClassFieldInitializerName]] to a name the frontend found, as rust_sfd_set_class_field_initializer_name
    /// does.
    pub fn set_class_field_initializer_name_from_utf16(&self, name: &[u16], is_private: bool) {
        let name = Utf16FlyString::from_utf16(name);
        self.set_class_field_initializer_name(if is_private {
            ClassFieldInitializerName::PrivateName(name)
        } else {
            ClassFieldInitializerName::PropertyKey(PropertyKey::from(name))
        });
    }

    pub fn class_field_initializer_name(&self) -> ClassFieldInitializerName {
        self.storage
            .rare_data
            .get()
            .map_or(ClassFieldInitializerName::Empty, |rare_data| {
                rare_data.class_field_initializer_name.borrow().clone()
            })
    }

    pub fn set_class_field_initializer_name(&self, name: ClassFieldInitializerName) {
        self.rare_data().class_field_initializer_name.replace(name);
    }

    pub fn kind(&self) -> FunctionKind {
        let kind = self.asm_call_metadata.get() >> asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_KIND_SHIFT
            & asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_KIND_MASK;
        match kind {
            0 => FunctionKind::Normal,
            1 => FunctionKind::Generator,
            2 => FunctionKind::Async,
            _ => FunctionKind::AsyncGenerator,
        }
    }

    pub fn this_mode(&self) -> ThisMode {
        if self.is_arrow_function() {
            ThisMode::Lexical
        } else if self.strict() {
            ThisMode::Strict
        } else {
            ThisMode::Global
        }
    }

    pub fn function_length(&self) -> i32 {
        self.function_length
    }

    pub fn formal_parameter_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.asm_call_metadata.get() as u32
    }

    pub fn mapped_argument_names(&self) -> Rc<[Utf16FlyString]> {
        self.storage.parameter_names.get().map_or_else(
            || Vm::of_cell(self).no_parameter_names.clone(),
            |names| names.mapped_argument_names.clone(),
        )
    }

    pub fn parameter_binding_names(&self) -> Rc<[Utf16FlyString]> {
        self.storage.parameter_names.get().map_or_else(
            || Vm::of_cell(self).no_parameter_names.clone(),
            |names| names.parameter_binding_names.clone(),
        )
    }

    pub fn strict(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::STRICT)
    }

    pub fn is_arrow_function(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_ARROW_FUNCTION)
    }

    pub fn has_simple_parameter_list(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::HAS_SIMPLE_PARAMETER_LIST)
    }

    pub fn is_module_wrapper(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_MODULE_WRAPPER)
    }

    pub fn set_is_module_wrapper(&self, is_module_wrapper: bool) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_MODULE_WRAPPER, is_module_wrapper);
    }

    pub fn is_class_constructor(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_CLASS_CONSTRUCTOR)
    }

    pub fn constructor_kind(&self) -> ConstructorKind {
        if self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::IS_DERIVED_CONSTRUCTOR) {
            ConstructorKind::Derived
        } else {
            ConstructorKind::Base
        }
    }

    pub fn set_constructor_kind(&self, constructor_kind: ConstructorKind) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::IS_DERIVED_CONSTRUCTOR,
            constructor_kind == ConstructorKind::Derived,
        );
    }

    pub fn uses_this(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::USES_THIS)
    }

    pub fn set_uses_this(&self, uses_this: bool) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::USES_THIS, uses_this);
    }

    pub fn this_value_needs_environment_resolution(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION)
    }

    /// How many properties to make room for in an object that a construction of the function creates with `shape`:
    /// as many as the objects with the shape ended up with, which the longest chain of forward transitions from the
    /// shape tells (every object a constructor builds the same way follows one). The transitions are looked at again
    /// on the first, second, fourth and so on construction, up to the 1024th.
    pub fn construct_reserve(&self, shape: Gc<Shape>) -> u32 {
        let metadata = self.asm_call_metadata.get();
        let count =
            (metadata >> asm_call_metadata::CONSTRUCT_COUNT_SHIFT & asm_call_metadata::CONSTRUCT_COUNT_MASK) as u32;
        if count <= MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE_UPDATES {
            if count.is_power_of_two() {
                let reserve = shape.property_count() + shape.longest_forward_transition_chain(MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE);
                self.construct_reserve.set(reserve.min(MAX_CONSTRUCT_RESERVE) as u8);
            }
            self.asm_call_metadata
                .set(metadata + (1 << asm_call_metadata::CONSTRUCT_COUNT_SHIFT));
        }
        u32::from(self.construct_reserve.get())
    }

    pub fn closure_count(&self) -> ClosureCount {
        let count = self.asm_call_metadata.get() >> asm_call_metadata::CLOSURE_COUNT_SHIFT
            & asm_call_metadata::CLOSURE_COUNT_MASK;
        match count {
            0 => ClosureCount::None,
            1 => ClosureCount::One,
            _ => ClosureCount::Many,
        }
    }

    /// Counts a new closure of the function.
    pub fn note_closure_created(&self) {
        let count = match self.closure_count() {
            ClosureCount::None => ClosureCount::One,
            ClosureCount::One | ClosureCount::Many => ClosureCount::Many,
        };
        let metadata = self.asm_call_metadata.get()
            & !(asm_call_metadata::CLOSURE_COUNT_MASK << asm_call_metadata::CLOSURE_COUNT_SHIFT);
        self.asm_call_metadata
            .set(metadata | (count as u64) << asm_call_metadata::CLOSURE_COUNT_SHIFT);
    }

    /// The reserve of the last construct_reserve(), without asking for it.
    pub fn current_construct_reserve(&self) -> u32 {
        u32::from(self.construct_reserve.get())
    }

    /// Whether the environment of a call has to answer for `this`, `new.target` or `super`, because something reads
    /// them through the environment. Otherwise a declarative environment does for the function's bindings, just as no
    /// environment at all does for a function without any.
    pub fn function_environment_has_this_binding(&self) -> bool {
        let metadata = self.asm_call_metadata.get();
        metadata & (asm_call_metadata::CONTAINS_DIRECT_CALL_TO_EVAL | asm_call_metadata::IS_MODULE_WRAPPER) != 0
            || metadata
                & (asm_call_metadata::IS_ARROW_FUNCTION | asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION)
                == asm_call_metadata::THIS_VALUE_NEEDS_ENVIRONMENT_RESOLUTION
    }

    pub fn function_environment_needed(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_NEEDED)
    }

    pub fn set_function_environment_needed(&self, function_environment_needed: bool) {
        self.set_metadata_bit(
            asm_call_metadata::FUNCTION_ENVIRONMENT_NEEDED,
            function_environment_needed,
        );
    }

    pub fn might_need_arguments_object(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::MIGHT_NEED_ARGUMENTS_OBJECT)
    }

    pub fn contains_direct_call_to_eval(&self) -> bool {
        self.metadata_bit(asm_call_metadata::CONTAINS_DIRECT_CALL_TO_EVAL)
    }

    pub fn function_environment_bindings_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.storage.function_environment_bindings_count.get() as usize
    }

    pub fn var_environment_bindings_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.storage
            .rare_data
            .get()
            .map_or(0, |rare_data| rare_data.var_environment_bindings_count.get() as usize)
    }

    /// Where the function environments of calls to the function find their shape.
    pub fn function_environment_shape_cache(&self) -> EnvironmentShapeCache {
        EnvironmentShapeCache::FunctionEnvironment(Gc::from_ref(self))
    }

    /// Where the separate var environments of calls to the function find their shape.
    pub fn var_environment_shape_cache(&self) -> EnvironmentShapeCache {
        EnvironmentShapeCache::VarEnvironment(Gc::from_ref(self))
    }

    pub(crate) fn function_environment_shape_slot(&self) -> &NullableMember<EnvironmentShape> {
        &self.storage.function_environment_shape
    }

    pub(crate) fn var_environment_shape_slot(&self) -> &NullableMember<EnvironmentShape> {
        &self.rare_data().var_environment_shape
    }

    /// RustIntegration::compile_function(): the function's executable, from the bytecode compiled ahead of time if
    /// there is some, and otherwise parsed and compiled now. Running out of stack on the way is a RangeError, like
    /// running out of stack in the call that got here.
    pub fn compile_function(
        vm: &Vm,
        shared_data: Gc<SharedFunctionInstanceData>,
        builtin_abstract_operations_enabled: bool,
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Executable>> {
        let source_code = shared_data.source_code();

        let payload = match shared_data.storage.compile_input.take() {
            CompileInput::PrecompiledBytecode(input) => {
                let PrecompiledInput { precompiled, payload } = *input;
                if let Some(payload) = payload {
                    shared_data.storage.compile_input.set(CompileInput::Unparsed(payload));
                }
                // NB: This stays the only reference to the code if nothing else holds the function.
                let executable = Arc::try_unwrap(precompiled)
                    .map_or_else(|shared| shared.executable.clone(), |unique| unique.executable);
                return Ok(Executable::create_with_source_code(
                    vm,
                    executable,
                    source_code.as_ref(),
                ));
            }
            CompileInput::Unparsed(payload) => payload,
            CompileInput::None => panic!("a function that was not compiled yet knows how to compile"),
        };
        let started = shared_data.has_flushed_code().then(std::time::Instant::now);
        let precompiled =
            crate::compile::compile_function(&payload, builtin_abstract_operations_enabled, vm.native_stack_limit());
        shared_data.storage.compile_input.set(CompileInput::Unparsed(payload));
        let Ok(precompiled) = precompiled else {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::RangeError, ErrorType::CallStackSizeExceeded, &[]);
        };

        shared_data.set_metadata(&precompiled.metadata);

        let Some(started) = started else {
            return Ok(Executable::create_with_source_code(
                vm,
                precompiled.executable,
                source_code.as_ref(),
            ));
        };
        // NB: The flushed code stays in the shared data, which visits it, until the new executable holds it.
        let executable = Executable::create_with_flushed_code(
            vm,
            precompiled.executable,
            source_code.as_ref(),
            shared_data.rare_data().flushed_code.borrow().as_deref(),
        );
        shared_data.rare_data().flushed_code.replace(None);
        let elapsed = u64::try_from(started.elapsed().as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
        let stats = &vm.code_flushing.stats;
        stats
            .recompile_nanoseconds
            .set(stats.recompile_nanoseconds.get().saturating_add(elapsed));
        shared_data.note_recompile(vm, FlushLayer::Bytecode);
        Ok(executable)
    }
}
